detailed_description: Your HEALTH is TIME You must KILL to get more TIME A HIGH-OCTANE-ACTION SHOOTER, 90% ARCADE FUN, 10% roguelite. In this future, MAN and INTERNET have merged into a new being. This being needs DOPAMINE every 10 SECONDS, or else it will DIE! • ARCADE FUN! You are MULLET MAD JACK, and you must kill enemies to refill your 10 SECONDS OF LIFE! • Beat handcraft stages at random full of exciting new obstacles at each chapter! • Memorize each room and compete for better times! • Cleverly build your character every FLOOR, in a fully-fledge NARRATIVE with small roguelite elements. • Defeat the mysterious masterminds and experience the ultimate OLD SCHOOL ANIME plot! KEY FEATURES: • Fast Arcade feel full of dopamine rush like the old times • A fully animated campaign with old-school anime cutscenes • 50+ Power ups that change the way you can play the game. • You can play the game forever in random levels on ENDLESS MODE • A CLASSIC MODE with no TIMER if you want a traditional campaign • Unbox a digital/virtual BIG PC GAME BOX from the 90's • 15 trading cards and more than 50 point shop items • Relive the bloodshed from 80's and 90's ACCESSIBILITY: Full controller support, Ultrawide support, key and button rebinding, Mouse sensitivity, Purple blood mode, disable camera shake and flashes, custom AIM options, custom volume controls for sfx, music and voices.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game.MULLET MADJACK is not a rhythm game, even the music gives some strong beats. What makes this game stand out from regular FPS is the health bar is measured by time. You are given 10 seconds to live, to refill it you need to kill before time runs out, a good concept similar to 2011's movie In Time.I‘ve beaten the campaign on normal difficulty, the key point is  . Sure time is limited, but don't forget to keep your pace, try to eliminate enemies rather than escape your way through, because every hit will deduct your valuable time. My advice is take this game as a regular FPS, clean the area (or most of the enemies) before moving on to the next, but in a timely manner. 10 seconds is not that short, you can use a timer to have a good feeling if you are unsure, just do not panic. Good luck.At the end I made it to 30+ floors in the prize claiming section, not knowing it is actually an endless run, and eventually rewarded a sneaker as promised. For the story mode, every 10 floors you will face a boss, the boss fight is easy compared to 10 floors of non-stopping killing. This is intense even if each floor is only 30-50 seconds long, but with the ticking clock and groups of enemies, concentration is required to beat a level, especially a gameover punishing player to restart from floor 1. At the end of each floor you can choose 1 out of 3 temp upgrades ranging from new/upgrade weapon to abilities like double jump, special kill (headshot/crotch kill!!!) for extra time, or environment helper, or boss life deduction etc., this adds a taste of raffle. My favorite goes to that tier 3 Uzi which offers unlimited ammo. This is as good as a cheat to largely reduce the difficulty, because loading takes time, and time is everything in this game.The campaign is 3 hours long, kudos to devs for not extending it into a 9 hours gameplay because after 30 floors there's nothing new, the rest are just refine your skill, repeat each level to prepare the final boss fight on the 90th floor. The campaign ended before I tried out every upgrade and got bored. $19.99 can be expensive for a 3-hour game, but the excitement is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking for a game with killer fast-paced gameplay where your health is time, and time is always running out? Mullet Mad Jack can definitely scratch that itch, it’s unlike any game I have played before. Climb each floor of a skyscraper building killing robots to keep your dopamine rush alive and seconds on your clock. Battle through handcrafted stages with all types of enemies that aim to destroy you. Clear each floor, pick upgrades and weapons to help get you higher and higher. Boss battles are super sick, music is on another level, and the art style is out of this world. After you complete the campaign, you can play through the game again as a boomer shooter with no timer, play forever in endless mode, or you can up the difficulty by playing in challenge or hard mode to complete all achievements. Really enjoyed beating the game on the higher difficulties where headshots and level memory really makes a difference. The music and art style make this game stand out among the few other titles in this newer genre!Achievement Count: 48Time to 100%: ~10hrsDifficulty: ★★★★✩Genre of Game: FPS, Arcade, Boomer Shooter, Fast-PacedFun Rating: 9/10Checkout my YT video review or my

_childDocuments_.review: I saw neon colors everywhere. A women on a small screen screamed orders at me to buy, attack, or die depending on what the people wanted to see. I shot hundreds of robots and other horrors as I fought my way through endless corridors, searching for my princess. Eyes twitching and muscles spasming, I guzzled down liters of fizzy drinks to feed my endless need to be the perfect consumer. I committed acts of violence and horror live for adoring fans as part of an endless quest for likes.  I confronted the moral quandries and hypocrisy of late stage capitalism, and I grappled with the knowledge that I too am just a cog in this machine and if this society ceased to exist then so would I. So anyways, once I got the dosage on my meds adjusted, I started the game and it was pretty great. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is another sleeper hit of 2024 that came out of nowhere for the most. At first glance, it's not hard to make comparisons to Post Void, simply by being a corridor boomer shooter. However, I find Mullet Madjack to be a bit more forgiving, as it’s easier to read the level layout and the patterns of enemies.The game immediately oozes charisma with its highly stylized visuals that transport you into a 90s anime, with lots of references to 90s pop culture and retro shooters. You even get to unbox a big box version of the game in-game that introduces you to the game. Accompanied by a great selection of synthwave tracks, an idiosyncratic sense of humor, and high-octane gameplay, Mullet Madjack achieves exactly what it promises and doesn't shy away from letting you know:YOU NEED THAT DOPAMINE HIT.And, you probably want to enslave yourself to that Peace Corp lady, but that’s another matter.Mullet Madjack has 9 chapters that can be completed in about 2.5 to 3 hours. Each chapter consists of 10 floors, and you have only 10 seconds to reach the end of each floor. Each kill adds to your lifespan, and if you get creative, you get rewarded. It plays like a roguelite: if you die, you go back to the start of the chapter (the first floor). However, you get to keep some permanent unlocks, and they let you keep one of your best upgrades. There is more than enough variety in unlockables (guns, environmental items, and so on) to keep the flow going.The game always has some tricks up its sleeve with twists. While levels evolve with more traps and enemies, you’ll soon recognize the pattern, as it doesn’t change much within a chapter. However, since it only takes about 30 to 50 seconds to complete a level (usually), you get a mental reset soon enough and probably won’t mind that. Bosses are fun overall, and there are some surprise gameplay sequences that are great callbacks to retro shooters. The game also cleverly ties the ending to its endless mode. With the addition of different difficulties for the story mode -if you want to suffer more- and endless mode for the leaderboards, you get fair amount of replayability.All in all, Mullet Madjack is a very clever parody, but above everything else, it is great entertainment. Go kill some billionaires, handsome.★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: is a fast paced boomer-shooter roguelite set in the year 2095.The game is set in the year of 2095 in which robot billionaires have taken over the world and humans are highly addicted to dopamine. The player controls Jack who is a so-called moderator who was hired by Peace Corp. to rescue the Influencer Princess who is being held hostage in a massive skyscraper filled with killer robots. The princess is located 10 floors above you and you only have 10 seconds to reach the exit of each floor, sounds easy right?I played the demo of  earlier this year and it instantly hooked me despite not being a huge fan of boomer-shooters but the fast paced action and the setting itself just made me like the demo a lot when I played it.The game itself was released not too long after I’ve played the demo and I purchased it fairly shortly after the release. The game feels good. It’s fast paced and the gameplay loop is straight forward: Your timer ticks down, killing robots gives time – dopamine goes brr; or something like that.Quite honestly the story itself is okay but nothing special, right? It kind of has the whole Mario vibe. You finish the 10 floors; you defeat a boss and the princess is  on another floor. Despite this sounding a bit whack, the story has certainly its moments, especially the epilogue and the whole premise of the game itself is quite interesting.The gameplay loop is satisfying. The bosses are quite simple but can be a challenge on higher difficulties. Clearing a floor gives you an opportunity to buy new guns or new passive effects and defeating a boss grants you some permanent upgrades – so pretty standard roguelite elements that mix well with the whole fast boomer-shooter gameplay.The upgrades that you get after every floor feel fair and nice. If you have a good gun and some good upgrades you will probably do more than well – especially in the endless mode in which your timer gets reduced by 1 second every 10 floors which makes the game harder after you’ve reached floor 40 since you will only have 7 seconds to complete the level; that means that getting hit and not instantly killing a robot could be fatal.The art-style, the graphics, the music and the overall vibe of the game are great. It’s essentially a retro anime with a beefy male protagonist that yells those 90s action movie slogans every so often.The length of the game isn’t too crazy either. It took me around 3 hours to finish the game which is alright since there is the previously mentioned endless mode in which you can unlock some more cosmetics and if you like to go for achievements there is a few of them that require you to play through the game on higher difficulties and such – so there is replay value for sure. I hope that there will me some more content update in the future though.Speaking of different difficulties: There’s also a difficulty which removes the timer and changes the gameplay from a fast first-person-shooter to a boomer-shooter that let’s you play the game without needing to worry about the timer and such. I personally think it’s a nice idea but it’s certainly not meant to be played like this but it might be fun for some people that have beaten the game already and want to try something new. There’s also an achievement for completing the whole game in that mode. Is  worth your money? Yeah sure. It depends on what you want from a game.If you go after the whole “1 Euro = 1 Hour” thing I’d say that it’s best to buy it on sale if you only plan on playing through it once without messing around with harder difficulties or with the endless mode.For me personally, I bought it with the 20% off deal and I have to say that it’s worth it for me. I will probably mess around with the endless mode a bit and hope that the developers add some more content in the future since it’s a pretty good game that has a cool setting and great aesthetics.There should be a demo available so you could just mess around with that before you decide on getting it or not.“” - JackIf you found this review helpful, feel free to visit my  page.

_childDocuments_.review: It takes 3 hours to beat and you'll be bored by the end of it, because the gameplay is shallow and repetitive. The weapons and upgrades don't do enough to change up the gameplay, and there's a serious lack of variety in the enemies and levels. It's really mindless and doesn't feel rewarding in the same way as similarly fast-paced games like Hotline Miami.I loved the aesthetic and had fun for the first hour or two, but unfortunately the game never really develops beyond that. It's all style and no substance. Maybe get it if it's on sale for $5, but otherwise it's not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished the game, and this should be the moment when I am the most hyped about the game. Instead, I am disappointed.I like anime, I like rougelites, and I like... Variety. And the last is something that this game severely lacks.Have you played the first floor? Congratulations, you have seen about 80% of what the game has to offer. Sure, it adds new enemies, but do not offer much in terms of different approaches. And the environment changes, but not much, and it is not like you will notice the difference anyway given the pace of action. The story is shallow, which is to be expected, but so is the gameplay.Tired of wiping the same looking floors? And they literally look the same, since they utilize a _very_ small number of sections as well as a tiny set of regular enemies. Well, from time to time the game offers a very short one time different gameplay mode - because it does not know how to keep you engaged with its core mechanics. And the bosses are extremely boring: all of them (beside one which is nearly a joke) are made by formula "shoot it until it dies". Moreover, they use a regular shooter format, not the main "shoot something every 10 seconds", so they noticeably break the flow.The left hand consists of a low resolution hand sprite with a higher resolution sprite of phone and fingers. A small detail, but it really irks me.It might be possible that I fell victim to my own high expectations, but I hoped to see a bit more than a flashy attraction. But this is just it, an attraction. Higher difficulty level are dumb, since they change the time balance but not enemy behaviors.If you want this game for the sake of flashy entertainment - sure, go ahead. But be warned that it might run out of steam disappointedly quickly, even before the credits start rolling.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is fast action in its purest form.This is an FPS stripped down to only those intense, frenetic firefights of movement and trigger finger reaction in an endless, glorious loop. The game itself actually mentions Flow State, and that's exactly what it delivers!This is one of those masocore games you play for the challenge. As such, the Attempt - Fail - Reattempt gameplay loop doesn't keep you waiting; you're back in the fight to try again immediately. It's easy to sink hours into MMJ  a good way.Aside from being the tightest action game I've played all year, MMJ also has heaps of style. For a game that outright thumbs its nose at plot, the characters are fun and full of clever dialogue you might miss if you're not paying attention. There's depth here....And do the game's virtual "unboxing". It's worth your time.Going to unwrap another lollipop and get killing! I have a new addiction!

_childDocuments_.review: The amazing art and presentation can't hide that the gameplay loop gets stale quite fast, as you're rushing through the same randomly connected map modules, with the same object and enemy placement. Having the roguelite aspect (select 1 of each 3 random power ups after each floor) allow for deep/amazing/rewarding synergies would be a great way to solve the repetition, but unfortunately that's not the case in Mullet Madjack.Although one of the devs has stated the game is not a roguelite/-like, one of the main features of the game, as being advertised on the page is:  The power-ups are presented in typical roguelite fashion: 3 random 'cards', of which you can select one, yet there are no actual 'clever builds' to make. Being able to create awesome synergies through power-ups would actually make the repetitious gameplay loop a lot more fun & interesting.So, if the game actually distances itself from the roguelite aspect, what's left? A fast paced FPS that feels a bit like a light-gun game, that get's repetitive fast, because it doesn't have the aspects of what makes a boomer shooter good, like Dusk and HROT for example.All in all, and considering the price I can' t recommend. The game just doesn't offer enough currently to keep it fresh, fun and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't see the appeal. Every room plays the exact same, its your average shooter with a 10-second time limit. The style is nice, its very fast-paced, but the variety in upgrades and rooms just killed it for me. I'll probably still finish the game, but its just... very repetitive for what it is. When you find a roguelike/lite you are usually looking for replayability, and good variety of upgrades. This has neither.Also, the game will constantly remind you that you are 1 difficulty higher than standard. It feels like the game is mocking me for dying on the higher difficulty. Every 2 deaths my screen will show this little "Hey btw you are on hard mode you can turn that down". It was fine the first time, but when you say NO to something 5-10 times in a row it gets annoying, almost downright patronizing.Can we have an option to turn off these useless upgrades like "the protag will say some one-liners" because it was funny the first time, but seeing that "upgrade" just makes me take a deep sigh in realizing that I just wasted an upgrade option for nothing. "Mark where the end level door is" really? in the game where you have essentially a single direction to go? "Slide faster on ramps" might be cool but its useless for bosses.Weapon balance is all over the place. Pick up the railgun/uzi/pistol to insta-lose.I really hope that there is more in store for the game, because the core gameplay loop is good. But other than that, you probably won't be playing this game for more than 5-10 hours.Edit: it just gets worse. I went down to "Normal" because I was sick of the constant difficulty reminder, and now its telling me EVERY SINGLE DEATH to switch to a different difficulty. I've unlocked a few upgrades that ruin the visual clarity of the game (add them to the useless list). I don't understand why the developers felt the need to make a main boss turn-based? In this game??? It really broke the pacing for me, and the post-rpg moment was lackluster at best.I've just realized there is no way to turn off the environment-based tips that show up EVERY time you come across an object in the environment. They take up a good 1/4 of the top of the screen, and tell me information I already know. This doesn't change at higher difficulties, why?Do the devs never want you to die in this game? Are you just meant to speedrun through the story spamming leftclick, rightclick, repeat? I don't understand the patronizing. Every second of this game just wants you to beat it without any issue, no learning, just go down to the lower difficulty! It really makes me angry every single time I die. Roguelikes should feel fair and rewarding when you die. It might be fair, but every time I die, I'm being told "skill issue". Its a really simple fix and its a real wonder why it isn't like this before: only show the notification after a streak of deaths. If the player closes the notification, DONT SHOW IT AGAIN.rocket science.Aside from that, there's typos, unfinished upgrade text ("after killing an enemy, boost damage for seconds". How many?), FPS issues at later stages, and visual clarity is a joke. Honestly I can't understand the hype at all.Edit 2: I finally finished the game, and boy, I wish I hadn't. Turns out  Yeah. It's really bad. Why not just have the ending be a link to your Deviantart profile? Doesn't help that the main lady you are trying to save is voiced by the EXACT SAME voice actor as the Peace Corp lady. Also... Rock, paper, scissors. REALLY? I want whatever the devs were smoking when they thought this section was a good idea.This is by far one of the most overrated games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant game held back by a few issues.  To start, this is one of the most engaging audio/visual experiences I have EVER experienced.  Truly, it is remarkable.  The mastery of the 80's anime artstyle is so satisfying.  From the UI to the animations to the menus and even the interactive in-game manual (!!) it is a huge treat.The core game loop is also masterful.  It really is a pure concentrated shot of dopamine and the game is very self-aware of it.  So what's the problem?  Well, have you ever played a game that gave an amazing first impression, but the more you played it and examined it, the more you began to see its flaws?  Unfortunately that is this game to me, so I'll try to go beneath the surface and explain some of the issues I had with it.-Identity crisis-This game is listed as 90% arcade, 10% roguelite.  I'd say yes that is true on first impression, but the more you play, the more you begin to see how the game never fully commits to being either.  The core gameplay loop does feel like 90% arcade (the roguelite perks don't last indefinitely and are minor), but the problem comes more in the level design and progression.  Ironically, in some ways the level design is LESS arcadey than many roguelites.  Most roguelites have you play a collection of biomes and in each biome is a randomized set of procedurally generated arenas/rooms.  This game does not really even do that, but instead, almost every single room in the game can occur at ANY part of the run, and will be repeated over and over at any point, like shuffling through a deck of cards.  Every 10 floors, the game introduces a new hazard such as lava floors or lasers, and sometimes some unique room layouts, but the reality is you will be shuffling through the same rooms during the ENTIRE run, albeit with a few new hazards.  So not only does it not have a level progression of arcade games (a stream of novel content from beginning to end but the same game every time you play), but does not even have as strong a sense of biome progression as in roguelites.  This not only moves the game more away from the feel of an arcade game, but leads to an overall diminished sense of progression during the run.  This issue unfortunately also is exacerbated by other issues.-Pacing-Despite this game being about a flow of constant forward progression, the actual pace of the game feels tedious.  Each floor lasts about 15-60 seconds and there is an incredibly dense amount of player actions that occur in that brief time.  After every floor, the game goes through the standard congratulations, the female character gives you some quips, and you choose your perk for the next floor.  It kind of feels like doing high intensity lifts in the gym for 30 seconds but then pausing for 10 seconds after each set.  For a game being about the "flow state", this creates a less than desirable flow from floor to floor.  This is also made worse by the overall pacing of the campaign.  After 10 floors, you fight a boss then move onto the next chapter, where the game does a "tutorial floor" to introduce the new hazard/enemy type.  At first this setup seems fine, but because each of the 10 floors plays out exactly the same (due to randomly shuffling rooms that occur repeatedly at every part of the run), those 10 floors end up feeling more like a slog and much longer than they actually are, especially due to the constant breaks in between each floor.  By the end of campaign, it really starts to feel like you have been running the same 20 second core game loop over and over for several hours, albeit with a few new hazards.  It feels like the game could've benefited more from a genuine arcade progression by trimming the campaign down in length and also having more of a true level progression system where most if not all the rooms are locked to specific chapters.  I don't think the campaign warrants being 3-4 hours and 100 total floors considering the lack of true level progression, and unfortunately does not make the game an effective arcade game (which typically is cleared within 25-45 ish minutes).  There is also I think a pacing issue with the "side missions" that occur.  Around 3 or 4 times during the campaign, the game breaks into a kind of playable cutscene or a new gameplay type segment, such as a sniper section or car section.  Some of these sections don't have gameplay and consist of walking through an empty house.  While beautiful and memorable, they will inevitably slow the game down for future runs and further move the game away from a pure arcade game.  Inversely, the unique gameplay segments (like the sniper section) do not stay long enough in order to effectively break up the monotony of the core game loop.  I think the campaign could've been shortened, transitions sped up, and these additional gameplay type bits could've been lengthened and expanded on to better break up the monotony.-Difficulty systems/balance-My major issue is that the game in my opinion does not open up in higher settings as the dev claims, but instead the opposite. With most great games, in higher difficulties the strategy and gameplay systems blossom into its full beauty, but in this game, it confines the player more.  For example, in higher settings you literally HAVE to headshot enemies or kick them into environmental hazards to refill your constantly draining time/life meter, because normal kills won't fill it up.  This is a problem, because this new genre of "booter shooters" is about getting into that flow state, albeit through a very "one-track" way of thinking.  Flow state gaming is very satisfying of course, but when it is such a one-track-think dopamine rush, it can quickly devolve into fatigue and monotony.  In other flow state games, you may notice that the most satisfying flow states occur at both a physical and mental level, where you are able to establish that exhilarating synergy between complex strategic decision making and physically executing the strategy with clinical precision.  The flow state in this game in higher difficulties confines the game more into just a blistering pace of rapid, near perfect accuracy of headshots while dashing through tight corridors and rooms that often line you up for the shot as soon as you open the door.  There's nothing inherently wrong with that, but it would have been nice for the higher difficulty settings to open the game up more into both a physical AND mental flow state.  The game just doesn't really have much of any sense of strategic decision making, it is more about being able to recognize what enemy type and room you are dealing with as instantaneously as possible and then muscle memory takes care of the rest.I could go on more, but I think I have started to scratch at some of the ways I think the game will not hold up as well as I'd desire for long term commitment.  I definitely believe the game will be very successful, because I think a lot of what is here is nothing short of genius.  This game I think does deserve and will achieve its high status as a beloved title.  Its swagger, aesthetic, instant gratification, and core game loop are undeniable.  For me, it just happened to be one of those games that doesn't quite hold up as well on further examination.  To summarize, the three major issues for me lie in it neither fully committing to being a great arcade game nor roguelite, its numerous pacing issues, and difficulty systems that confine an already one-track mind game into a corridor racer head shooter game.  I will likely still try and clear harder difficulties, but I think the brilliance of the dopamine kick did start to desensitize too quickly, turning some of that fun factor into a tedious dopamine "ritual".  And the game does break the 4th wall by explicitly depicting video games as functioning as a kind of masturbatory dopamine kick to "consoom" and fill our boredom of our meaningless lives.  I just do not agree that the best games devolve into such.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: This game is fun. Buy it. Do it.Ć̶͓o̴̧̭͌̉n̶̞̊s̷̫̰̿u̸̮̍͆m̶̺̈ḛ̵̯̚For the rest of us, the game is fun! The artwork is perfect, colors are bright and vibrant, speed is your best friend and your best enemy, guns are meaty and satisfying, soundtrack is amazing, the lore is not extensive but it is satisfying, making for a great setting.The good:Levels are autogenerated based off a set of templates, which can create its own set of challenges or advantages. And the more levels you do, the more hazards come into play. Because dying is quick in this game, being able to have not repeat the same level over and over is nice, but there's also the option to not have it being randomized, so you can master a map if that is what tickles your fancy. The timer is a very nice mechanic. You only have 10 seconds to live, even less if you take damage, but you can recover seconds by killing and just... Being badass. You nailed a headshot in midair? You get yourself an extra second to live, on the house. You kicked a robots to an industrial fan? That leaves a mess, but was badass, one more second.At the end of each floor, you can can get one of a selection of random upgrades, which could be guns, upgrades to said guns, speed, of just being more manly. Keeps each run different from the one before, and forces you to a different style of combat depending of what upgrades you get. The Bad:There's not enough! I did beat the game under 8 hours, on the Challenging difficulty, and I could've beaten a lot quicker if I didn't suck at games. Nonetheless, there's the need for more. A sequel, maybe a different character, different guns, new enemies, but still having you killing billionaire robots and perhaps even the peace corp. I even got some names to donate for a potential sequel:Mohawk Johnny RageMildly Angered SalarymanPonytail Chainsaw CarlFlattop Crazzy Frank, with two Z.Finally, the BR dub is just nice. I did only play briefly with BR dubbing, because I'm just so used to have everything in English, I don't consume any BR media these days and living abroad just distances me further from roots, but after reading about it, I gave it a try, and hearing voice actors that were part of my childhood was quite something.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRDoes the game look great? Absolutely.It presents the 90's Old-taku, ultra-violence theme perfectly. The game is fittingly ridiculous in every way. Nothing about the presentation is bad. But this game needed purposefully designed levels and not procedurally generated ones.It's one of those games that works great on paper but I think the biggest problem with it is that it is a rogue-like and as you progress through the game it's mostly the same rooms (a few different rooms are added) and they just add different enemies or traps to those existing rooms.When you have a game that requires as much twitch decision making as this, then I just don't think procedurally generated levels are the best platform for this combat design. You often find rooms being repeated over and over during the same level, some of the rooms really needed more testing, the wallrunning rooms get you killed all the time because you just jump over the walls, or accidentally slide off the map because you were trying to melee something.My biggest reasoning, however, for why I think this needed to be purposefully designed levels is how the sequencing of rooms can hand you a win or get you killed. Sometimes the rooms come together perfectly and your just running forward and shooting whatever you see (possibly how the game is supposed to feel) other times you end up with so many tight turns , corridors and enemies in blind spots that you aren't even sure what killed you. Some of the things they start to add to the rooms also feels like it doesn't really work for this game. The biggest things being the laser mines. You're character does not control precisely, he doesn't need to normally, but the laser mines require precise movement, except when they end up around corners or in blind spots, then you just walk into them by accident.The upgrades also feel wonky, with the biggest problem being the weapons. The railgun is too slow for this game, the plasma gun pushes you back when it fires, making you too slow for this game and I still don't know what's wrong with the katanas but they just don't feel right. You have to charge up the swing for them but that feels very out of place in this game, and half the time it doesn't even kill the enemy and you don't know if that's because you missed or because it didn't do enough damage.

_childDocuments_.review: All flash, no substance. Decent enough game, but not even close to worth the price. It's a game that is almost completely carried by it's visual style/aesthetic; the veneer of which becomes quite thin very quickly. All the levels are pretty much the same. Again, they have a good visual style, but they are extremely repetitive/unimaginative in terms of level design and there is a very small pool of enemies and earned perks. I get that it's supposed to be like an arcade game, but it's not that interesting to play because of these things. Also there is a lot of jank where you get stuck on geometry, which absolutely kills any fast paced "arcade" game. If you want something in this kind of vein but with actual depth, play Neon White instead. Also, the developer is an overly sensitive salty manbaby/babyman that acts really hostile to people who offer polite and very valid constructive criticism on the message board. Earth to game developers on Steam! That is part of what the message boards are there for. If you can't handle constructive criticism, then you're in the wrong business friendo. Sorry you think that anyone who points out the glaring issues in the gameloop just "doesn't understand the game". Nah dude, your game gets boring way too quickly, sorry. This is what I originally wrote on the message board, to which the developer said it was pretty much my issue alone (yet, if you look at the other negative reviews, they say very similar things):Okay good game overall so far (I'm only on chapter 8, however I feel like that is far enough to make this assessment), but there are certain things that (in my opinion) hold it back from being great/amazing. These are things which prevent it from being something that I would fully recommend to my friends who are like me and enjoy these kinds of games.1. Lack of variety level to level.I don't mind the format where there are individual chapters with 10 levels each, but I think the level design needs to have a bit more variety chapter to chapter. A lot of the levels/floors feel very much the same in each chapter except for very minor additions like lazers or giant fans.2. More permanent upgrades would be nice. seems like they cap pretty early on, which seemed a little bit strange to me. I know this game isn't a strict rogue-lite/like, but it would be nice to have more permanent upgrades and ones that are a little more interesting. It makes the game feel very small.3. If I exit the game and come back to it later, don't make me do the tutorial for that chapter again. I actually hate that. At least allow players to actually skip it. We've seen it, we don't need to see it again (and again).4. Make the skip buttons actually work. They don't work, at least for me (perhaps someone can shed some light on this). They somehow work for the full cutscenes, but not for the dialogue.5. If there is no boss fight for that specific chapter, don't include perks that impact boss damage for the perk pool for that chapter. If I am trying the game on different difficulties and replaying chapters, I shouldn't have to remember which ones have a boss and which ones don't when like 85% of them do. Either that, or have a real boss fight for each chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: In a very distant future, humanity has merged with the internet and is ruled by a cruel robot billionaires known as “robillionaires”. Our hero, Mullet Mad Jack, is a robo-killer called moderator with the objective of saving a hostage locked up on the 10th floor of a tower. The problem is that Moderator only has 10 seconds to live and constantly needs dopamine in order to survive. The only way of extending his life is by killing robots, thereby holding the interest of the viewers of a brutal livestream show. The plot is a bit simple, but it’s narrated in a really fabulous way, with a very distinctive ‘90s cyberpunk anime style that is simply gorgeous. There is also a lot of environmental storytelling such as wall posters, graffiti, tv screens and vending machines, but unfortunately you don’t really have time to stop and admire them. There are also some over-the-top moments that take place during boss fights or when you get closer to your objective, with funny dialogues and meta-references. Speaking of which, I recommend reading the in-game digital manual (yes, they still exist) with all the story, characters and gameplay descriptions, which also unlocks a new weapon as a form of thank you for unboxing the manual and legally owning the game.Gameplay-wise, Mullet Mad Jack is a great mix of FPS games like ,  and , but with a distinctive roguelike progression that makes it more similar to , a lesser known game that is equally worth playing. Each level is a race from start to finish as you run, dash and destroy enemies to gain more life time. You start with one weapon and through each floor you can swap between random weapons and upgrades. While you constantly need to check your available time, you also need to take care of your health and quickly restore it by destroying vending machines and getting a drink. Dying means losing all weapons and upgrades, as well restarting the chapter you are playing, which is made of 10 levels (floors). There are 10 chapters in total and each one adds more gameplay elements, such as environmental hazards, new enemies and mechanics (wall running for instance). Overall, it’s a really fast-paced and adrenalin-fueled gameplay structure, with each level lasting around 40 seconds – 1 minute depending on your speed and ability. This can make the game incredibly short or slightly longer depending on your skills, but in my experience the length is adequate, even if the difficulty at the default setting isn’t really enough for someone who loves this kind of games. Fortunately, there are more difficulty options that can reduce your life time and increase the enemy damage, so the game can get really challenging if you want. Speed runners will also have a fun time climbing the global leaderboard, which can be accessed from the main menu. Technically there is a lot of replayability here, including a separate Endless Mode, and hopefully the game will be long supported with updates and DLCs, yet the thing that didn’t entirely convince me is the level design. Despite the beautiful aesthetic of each level, they tend to be a bit too similar, with the same type of generic assets, corridors, doors, vents and acid lava pits. I was also expecting enemies to be more varied, especially during the later chapters, because despite their beautiful cybernetic design the same ones are too often repeated through each level. Boss fights are different and cool enough, but as you can image, they don’t last for too long.Overall, Mullet Mad Jack is a very addictive game that will easily capture your soul with its beautiful anime visuals and dystopian cyberpunk story. It’s an FPS filled with adrenaline, violence and nostalgia for the ‘90s that doesn’t last too long unless you play at higher difficulties or want to test your speed running skills against your friends and the entire Steam community.
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: Way back in the before times (of 2020) a little indie game called Post Void came out that was far better than it had any right to be for how simple it was. Go fast, hit headshots, fill your decapitated head with juice from the blood of your enemies which lets you live just a little bit longer. I'm sure there was games before Post Void that did what it did, although maybe slightly less anti-epileptic than Post Void, but Mullet Mad Jack is the evolutionary followup to Post Void and it ramps up every element of Post Void's core gameplay to 999 with an overload of lights, dopamine, 90s anime aesthetics and crazy ass robo-goons. Any faults that MMJ might have (and there are some) are more or less moot points because of the overwhelming amount of absurd and high quality art direction that you run by at 200MPH on your mad dash to the checkpoint. This is a rare instance of the trailer for a game not accurately depicting how batsh*t insane the game can be especially if you really try gunning it through the levels. A slightly more methodical approach can definitely improve your survival rate but good lord is it fun just blasting through a level like a cannonball. The basic premise for anyone who didn't get it is that you have 10 seconds to live which is granted to you by an I.V. from your phone, you are being livestreamed climbing the tower and killing Robillionaires, and the more the "chat" loves you the more it feeds Jack dopamine through the I.V. which you get from getting kills, headshots, environmental kills and a hundred other things. The gameplay loop is more or less a boomer shooter style mad dash to the exit of each level trying to time your kills to keep as much uptime as possible. I will say that there are a few enemies and obstacles that are a bit frustrating to combat beyond the point of fun (looking at you lasers that can't be jumped through safely without going at turtle speed, although you can just kick people into them to shut them off). I streamed the game on my Twitch channel originally and for the sake of that I had the difficulty on "Normal" and it proved to be a lot because talking and walking is a bit hard, but I finished the game offline (the last like 20ish floors) and was easily able to crank the difficulty up to the hard/challenge zone. I would encourage you to play on this difficulty as it is very fair if the game has your full attention and you're never so far from a checkpoint that deaths are too punishing. The developer intended difficulty was a blast. Words cannot describe how much of a, for lack of a better phrase, dopamine overload this game is. There are some stumbles with some lackluster bosses (excluding the final act), some middling upgrades and some minor bugs, but the off the walls aesthetic that gets shot straight up your nasal cavity every floor is more than enough to make up for it especially at 20 bucks full price. I'm going to 100% this game at some point, picking up the last few achievements I don't have and would encourage anyone who is interested in this game to pick it up. Gotta save that princess, moderator.edit: also there's a demo, if you're hesitant, use it

_childDocuments_.review: Manages to scratch that same itch of an ultra fast paced FPS roguelite with a visual assault on the senses that I loved in Post Void. Despite the maximalist super saturated colours, it is quite readable to make out the enemies and items (to the point where you don't need the enemy or item scanner upgrades), and there are even melee executions like Doom to increase your life. The story is pretty old-school and kind of sexist in using a big-boobed "virgin" damsel in distress as plot motivation for a stoic, 80s style badass hero but she becomes an actual character by the end. However, I did lile the epilogue and plot continuation to the endless mode and your PEACE CORP handler has good voice acting. The upgrades are a lot of fun in that you're looking forward to beating the levels to keep building up your powerups and modifiers to glean more seconds of life and stronger weapons, even if a shotgun, SMG, or katanas can be enough from start to finish. The levels can get very repetitive in their layouts to the point where you can notice the same five variations of the levels and enemy positions, but when you're in a flow state of speeding past the level (because you only have ten seconds to live in a very Crank-like premise), you don't mind just bopping robots in your quest to kill robobillionaires. The cyberpunk commentary is nothing new but the motivation to get a new set of sneakers is very satirical of 80s and 90s toy crazes, and the humour keeps up until the end. Even some of the bosses are gilarious like a turn-based battle or playing rock-paper-scissors with your tamagotchi. The bosses are much easier than expected and the hardest bits are actually the laser obstacles, but the game definitely gets easier as you progress, gaining permanent upgrades such as being able to keep your latest weapon or any upgrade into the next run. I do want to play more of the endless mode and upgrade all the weapons, but also katana-only runs are completely viable much like Superhot. I played on Normal and will go for the harder difficulties for replayability. It's easy to recommend if you're into anime, arcade FPSs, and some of the other games mentioned here.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in-f*ckin-tense! And absolutely worth the $20, in fact I wish I got it prior to the Steam Summer Sale because buying it on sale feels like stealing it...Combat flow is the name of the game here, and goodness gracious does it flow. When you learn the controls and get yourself into a rhythm it's incredibly easy to lose yourself for hours with this game and the level and enemy designs help keep you alert. There's plenty of playstyles for different people here as well, despite the 10 seconds you can be slow and methodical as you clear out rooms, but blasting your way to the end as fast as possible is also viable and actually heavily encouraged. Different weapons will compliment your playstyle in ways you might not even think of. For example I went through majority of the campaign blind firing into enemies with the SMG which was hella fun, then when I unlocked endless mode I ended up picking up the more precision based Rifle, which then led to practice lining up head and nut shots which led to faster and more efficient times. You'll constantly pick up new ways to play and extreme levels of dopamine when you get just a little better.The aesthetic is also amazing, the unabashed throwback to 80's style anime and over-the-top gore that surrounded it in that era is incredibly pleasing to the eye, and the animations compliment it well. There's some questionable CGI at parts that honestly isn't even a negative since it feels like it's a callback to said anime. The one-liners that Jack says sometimes never fail to get a chuckle out of me and frankly The Streamer, aka the Shop Gal, never once got on my nerves as she kinda melds in with the rest of the game and accents it well. The cyberpunk-esque theme is also amazing, and the HUD really shines with the older 80's style take on cyberpunk and the more freaky styled body alterations (for example, the cell phone that has a blood tube connected to Jack's arm.) The music also lands right at home with the rest of the aesthetic, and while it wasn't a large focus for me, due to being enamored by the combat, it still adds to the experience and wraps it up in a gorgeous chrome bow.The story is deceptively simple and yet explores some rather harrowing themes about the modern day... like most cyberpunk inspired stories do. The Streamer and Mr. Bullet do a wonderful job at portraying their sides and both really make you feel like Jack really is trapped in a dystopian future, both due to the writing and their respective VA's work. Depending on your skill level and difficulty choice, the story portion of the game may take you 2-3 hours to complete. I personally played through and Challenging difficulty which is the experience the devs intended you to play on, and while there were some frustrating moments in there, it was mostly skill issues on my part and I was able to power through them.So all in all, this game is absolutely incredibly and I cannot recommend it enough. The aesthetic and gameplay loop is super addictive and is absolutely worth the $20. I would go as far as to ask that you wait for the Steam Sale to be over so that you can buy it at full price because the devs have absolutely cooked up a friggin' masterpiece.So yeah, I'm gonna go back in to kick ass and lick lollipops! Also shout-out to Gianni Matragrano for his amazing work as Mr. Bullet, the way he screams MULLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEET will forever be ingrained in my brain.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is a fun, fast-paced FPS experience oozing with style that ends just as quickly as it starts. The game and its levels are structured like a roguelite, with rooms, enemy placement, and upgrade choice varying randomly between each level and each attempt. Although "vary" may be too strong a word for this game as the possible changes between each level are so minuscule that the game feels exactly the same the entire way through. Granted that constant state is a fun one, it feels good to blitz through rooms keeping up your combo, it looks great, sounds great, but there is no variety in the gameplay at all. Outside of the charming cutscenes that separate the different chapters in the two-hour-long campaign, your experience will not vary. There are additional score attack gamemodes that change the rules of the game and challenge you to make it as far as you can, but it's just not enough of a difference to be worth the time. And for $20 I tried to get as much time out of this game as I could, my playtime that you see now is how long it took for me to get every single achievement. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Received the game as a gift from a friend.That said, at time of writing, I have completed 100% of Steam achievements, though I still have a few more pairs of shoes to get. I've done endless mode up to floor 53 as well.So, as for whether I recommend it: yes, as long as you're a fan of this kind of game. So to start, the positives:The Action: blood pumping, wild, stimulating, my dopamine needs have been drowned. You can approach it a few ways, regardless of your skill level. If you're a button masher that slams the shift key & swings a katana like a one legged blender, you'll be happy. If you've got the reaction time and reflexes of a robot to catch headshots with a railgun as you move at full speed through hallways, you'll love it.The Art: In gameplay, the game is crisp, in cutscenes they have that special old school anime vibe to them that is absolutely perfect. It's that perfect combination of vaporwave, old school anime, and retro gaming vibes that it scratches that something special for me.The voice acting: Personally, I love it. All the Duke Nukem style one liners, the Peace Corp commentary, Mr Bullet screaming "MULLET", its' all just so perfect that it both brings you back in time and puts a smile on your face.The Bad:The Story Length: This is really the only thing I can find any sort of real issue with. I would have liked the story to go longer, but that said, I don't fault the dev for this, because for an indie dev's first game on steam, All of what you get is just so great. So really, my only direct critique is: I'd love to have more (but then again, doesn't everyone).Really, I think the game is amazing. But, I do think it isn't for everyone. Some people like a game to relax with, I don't feel relaxed playing this game, I feel absolutely pumped and hyped. I played it late at night, and when I stopped I felt more awake than I did when I started.That said, watch the gameplay a bit. If after one minute of gameplay (approximately 1~4 floors of the story mode) it seems like the game for you, I'd absolutely recommend it.I sincerely hope to see more of this developer's work in the future (and I hope the robillionaires are willing to throw their cash at him) because if they ever make another game with the same vibes (does not even need to be the same exact type) I would absolutely buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: It was late at night, I had just finished my 4000th playthrough of Mullet Mad Jack, my favorite game of all time. I decided that I was going to attempt to beat my endless record of floor 300, getting my life soda (Actually monster...XD) and readying myself for a long night of playing with zero sleep. As I begin my playthrough, beating levels in under 30 seconds as usual, I start to hear strange noises coming from somewhere outside my house, thought I ignore it. Nothing can stop me from playing Mullet Mad Jack, I have to pay attention to every single item, every single enemy, and keep on top of the game. Floor 20, the noise becomes louder, as if it's gotten into my own home. Though like before, I can't investigate, I have to focus. Floor 30, as I finish mopping up the enemies, I hear my own door slowly creak open. Was it my mother telling me the game volume was too loud? Was it my father coming back with the milk and cigarettes? I look back to see the man himself, Mullet Madjack."Mullet Madjack?", I said in shock, my mouth drooling, "What are you doing here?"He took a step forward, "I noticed your appreciation for my skills, and I just wanted to come in and give you some of my heart because of that."Hearting...my posts? I couldn't believe it. "Oh-thank you so much, I'm so glad-""Not yet, and I didn't meant that kind either." He said, taking off his belt. "On the bed, I can lay down the 'rules' for you."Oh my god, was he being serious? I felt my heart start to beat like his during gameplay, my face slowly warm to the color of a bloodied screen, and with joy I nod. I crawl to my bed as he follows after, us both hopping on."I won't lie, you have grown a beautiful mullet, but it isn't what I'm interested in, bucko." He said chuckling, now stripping down my pants. I anticipated his banhammer, grabbing onto my sheets tightly. Suddenly, I feel my mullet grabbed and my head pulled back, the icon now thrusting deep inside of me. With each thrust I moan only louder and louder, losing my grip and letting him control me to my will. As he's about to climax, I hear him scream,"THIS IS HOW WE KEEP THE FORUMS CLEAN!"My insides are filled with his matrix juice, and my mullet is finally let go, my body going slump against the bed. He hops off the bed, walking to the door."I would love to show my fan some appreciation, but I gotta shadowban myself before I get any views from your mother."He runs off, leaving me filled to the brim with shock mixed with happiness, as well with my mother screaming in horror at what happened to me.On a serious note, what the ♥♥♥♥ is with this trend of locking difficulty achievements so that when you complete a higher difficulty, you don't get awarded the difficulty achievements below it? I shouldn't have to play each individual lower difficulty when I should of just gotten it from playing on the hardest one. That ♥♥♥♥♥ boring, just give them all to me instead of making me go through each.It's a good game though.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - Amazing 3.5 hours Normal	- The gameplay is a fast paced boomer-shooter similar to 'post-void' with story arcade mode and an endless roguelite mode. 	- Designed to test your skills, with every 10 floors presenting additional enemies and obstacles that require strategic thinking and quick reflexes.	- The controls are highly responsive, making precise movements and actions possible, which is crucial given the game's difficulty.	- Rogue-lite upgrades per every level give a sense of variety, keeping the game fresh.	- The story light yet is captivating, with a mix of humour and drama that keeps you invested in saving 'The influencer princess'.	- Dark undertone of 'consumerism', addiction to dopamine and futuristic dystopia.	- Vibrant saturated graphics, with detailed environments and character designs that bring a retro 90's anime feel.	- UI is intentionally loud and obnoxious which may seem like a negative but only adds to the challenge, feeling and style of the game.	- If you're money conscious and looking to play just for story\completion?  It's 3.5 hour story and very light. It's not worth purchase until half price sale.	- If you like the gameplay loop of a boomer shooter and want to do endless runs and focus on getting better with the escalating difficulty? I'd say it's definitely worth it.	- The Difficulty options are honest and explain well which difficulty is right for you to start with. 	- Story mode is very forgiving on Normal mode and has Checkpoints every 10 floors (floor takes approximately a minute).	- The game is hard, so be ready for a tough but rewarding experience.	- The game is meant to be played multiple times in escalating difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: Ooooh yes, this is a great Game!I will keep it quite short here.Mullet Mad Jack is basically Post Void but better. And no, I don't want to hate on Post Void. The idea was great but to be honest, Post Void was a pretty unforgiving Game.So let me explain... Post Void is basically an Ego Shooter where you have a VERY limited time to get through a level. Time goes down if you do nothing or get hit, time goes up if you kill enemies. So it is a VERY fast moving Game. You have to run, shoot, HIT and make it to the next level and if you finish one level, you can choose one of three upgrades.Also it has a very distinct psychedelic look that is quite awesome (U-Comic Style) but in motion it can be very tiring on your eyes.And it is unforgiving as heck.Don't worry, this is not a Post Void Review but I just wanted to mention it because Mullet Mad Jack improves on almost everything that Post Void did. (But Post Void was there first :) )So, Mullet Mad Jack is basically the same but better. Same principle, you have 10 seconds, this is your life. You get hit, seconds get taken away. You shoot/hit/kick/combo enemies, seconds get added.There is enough variety that it doesn't get stale. You have your "typical" Arsenal of Weapons: Pistol (which I played 90% of the Game), Shotgun, Submachine Gun, Assault Rifle, Plasma Rifle, Railgun.All of those feel great to use except for the Submachine Gun which has a little too much recoil.Inside the Levels - which here are floors of a skyscraper (Nakamura Plaza) - you can also find one hit melee Weapons that are a one time use after pick up and they refill your time completely.And there are environmental hazards where you can kick your enemies into or make them explode another way.I don't want to spoil all the mechanics here, actually it is quite simple.So my first experience in my first 20 minutes was: "Oh man, this is as unforgiving as Post Void, I am probably getting frustrated, also I feel too old and my reflexes are not what they used to be."If you have a similar experience, I urge you to press on. Shortly after the Game klicked.It was not about the speed and precision (as the Game even tells you) but more of a flow state that you have to get into. And when you are into that zone, you really flow and it really klicks.Yes, you will die, it's part of the fun. But right after you die, you will want to get back into it."Just one more attempt."By the way, this Game is also basically a roguelike with a handful of roguelite elements.Without spoiling, there are 3 Upgrades, that you can upgrade 2 times each, which stay forever after unlocking them. This is the roguelite element. The Roguelike Element is, that after every floor you get to choose one of 3 upgrades (which you can later re-roll) and those upgrades are lost when you die.Also: This Game has Episodes and Checkpoints, this takes away a lot of frustration. Basically every Episode has 10 Floors and usually a Boss at the end. After each Boss, you get a checkpoint and your Game is saved. If you - for example - die in floor 6, you will get thrown back to the start of the Episode, so the first floor.This Game references the 90s many times, but the vibe is more of an 80s vibe here. The artstyle is very crisp (as you can see from the pictures or videos) and somewhat Anime influenced, don't want to say too much about that, but it looks really cool.Music is also very fitting and does the job well of pumping you up throughout the Floors. Not much variety though but also it doesn't really need it.You can play it in bite sized chunks or just try and push through. Both works fine.Also, of course the Game isn't very demanding so it will run well probably also on older machines. I finished my first playthrough on Challenging in about 5 hours, got 37 of 48 Achievements in that short time. Usually in some Games, I have no interest in revisiting those Games, but Mullet Mad Jack stays on my hard drive.I want to dabble a bit more in the endless mode, also now that I have a grasp on the Game I want to beat it on hard mode as well. So as of writing this review, it's been around 5 hours of pure fun and it will likely be even more.At this Point you probably could've guessed, this is a total recommend from me. I also encourage you to get Post Void as well, so that you can see where this Game stems from. You can get it pretty cheap, way under 5 Bucks on Steam.Btw., I asked the Dev if I could by any chance contribute to this amazing Game (translation wise), so IF that is going to happen and I can do it, I will also edit this review here with a little note, because I don't want anyone to think the positive review is because of that.So yeah, get your Mullet on and violently shoot some robots...Addendum: Right after finishing the review, I jumped straight back in (even missed my Bus) and played Endless Mode until Floor 31. Just wanted to say, this is really addicting and also soooo satisfying with the Headshots (you get a little ping sound, I live for that).Okay, I'm out...

_childDocuments_.review: Sensory Overload: The FPSMullet Madjack is a high-adrenaline romp dressed up in an eye-watering coat of a nihilistic satire of capitalism and 80's-style retro-futurism through an "bootleg VHS 90's anime" lens. The synth music is booming, the nihongo is sugoi-desu, and the violence is ultra-ing.The pace of the game seems intimidating at first, but downtime is minimal, the controls are intuitive, and you quickly find yourself entering the game's frequently-mentioned "flow state" where you start "sight-reading" rooms and proceeding on autopilot.Very short (beat the game on difficulty 4/6 in about 3 hours total), but I'm honestly satisfied with my experience. Hopefully it gets more fleshed out in future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: TL-DR: Very well polished breakneck paced shooter albiet short story length.Pros:+ It has a Demo, that went a long way to get me to decide to buy it.+ The 90's anime aesthetic really comes to life within the game. Character designs are great!+ Fast paced and addictive fun. The games theme of "Dopamine" really fits and they did it justice.+ Multiple difficulties for novices and experienced FPS players alike.+ It's great to play as a gigachad protagonist in a 2024 game. Rare to see these days in modern indie gaming.+ It's one of those games where the gameplay seems overwhelming at first, but then it "just clicks" and you will be blasting and dashing your way through floors.+ Excellent sound design. Music very fitting for the game also.Cons:- Very short story. Completed in 2 sittings on the easier 15 Seconds of life mode. I died way too often on Normal mode in the demo. I am very glad this easier mode is available but you will blast through the story.- Floor checkpoints were a bit too spaced out. I get that each floor takes a minute to beat, but this design choice solidified my decision to play on the easiest mode. I can see it get frustrating to do floors over and over again. - Can't be played for long sittings, the flashy visuals will go for your eyes.Overall, it's a welcome addition to the FPS genre! If only the story was longer, but many will enjoy the "Endless Mode" the game has on offer.

_childDocuments_.review: No-nonsense first person shooter that did what Doom 2016 did - chose a genre and kept everything relatively simple. The game is fast paced adrenaline rush that doesn't leave you much time to think. And that's the beauty of it. You're not supposed to. This game is meant to be played like your very life depends on you moving as fast as possible - which it technically does; within the game world, that is.Right from the start you go in hard and fast; like a macaque hopped up in dozens of different illicit drugs up to its eyeballs with a fully loaded AK-47 in its hands. The colorful aesthetics, the music, and the sounds design are straight up from the '80 and '90 that hits a boomer like me like a 30 ton 18 wheeler going down the highway at 120 mph! The game is visually gorgeous, and any friend of beautiful 2D-art is going to be enjoy shooting, kicking, smashing and slicing their way through this game as the game's dopamine addicted protagonist. As you beat each floor, you get to choose an upgrade from three randomly selected ones, until you beat the a boss at every 10th level, after which you can choose a permanent upgrade before losing the temporary ones. This repeats until you reach the end, after which you unlock the next stage. There is an endless mode for those, who want to keep on going after beating the game or even before it, so fear not - you can still keep the carnage going for as long as you like. The levels are all proceduraly generated, so no two levels should be quite the same.I'm not going to spoil the plot to anyone reading this, what little there exists within the game, but I do have to say it is straightforward but ingenious at the same time. But nobody is going to play this game for its plot. You are going to play it for the gameplay. Though some of the mechanics in the game are bit clunky, like the wall-running that feels like you're grinding your face against the wall while you're doing it, they get the job done and that is all that matters to me in the end.If you're looking for a fast and fun shooter that doesn't require you to think much - just react fast and be quick to aim and shoot - this is the game for you. Clearing a floor takes from somewhere between 30 to 55 seconds, and clearing a stage (10 floors) is around ten minutes approximately - after which the game saves your progress, which allows you to quit the game and come back later. Also, if you die before the boss stage, you get booted back to the first floor of the stage, with all your upgrades lost into the void - forcing you to earn them back as you fight your way back up.All in all, I found the game a fun experience and would recommend it to anyone who is a fan of old '80's and '90's Anime, fast old school first person shooters, and/or just adrenaline junkie.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void goes 80s anime with this one. Mullet Madjack is just straight addictive fun. The perfect dopamine rush to kill a quick hour playing. It doesn't take long to beat, not that it should given the premise, but it's very replayable given the number of difficulty options and endless mode. It oozes style all throughout. You can see all the references to classic anime like Akira, Fist of the North Star, maybe Patlabor? The soundtrack is catchy synthwave which feels appropriate. The takedown animations are quick and brutal. Gives me that DOOM Eternal feel. The art style is really beautiful. It's colorful cyberpunk with impressive animations and campy voice acting. Levels look somewhat different, but are functionally identical all things considered. There's a decent variety of enemies and weapons to keep the experience fresh. The fully upgraded railgun is extremely powerful. It's just fun to power through levels completing them in 20 seconds or less. It's not a very deep game. After playing last year's phenomenal Deadlink, that showed me how to do a roguelite shooter very well. As a roguelite, Mullet is a little light on upgrade options between floors. You see a lot of the same options and they're not that exciting. Bosses are extremely easy. I think I died twice altogether fighting the bosses. This game is easy to learn and easy to master honestly. It doesn't take long to get familiar with the game's pattern for each floor. I still really enjoyed it and I do recommend it if you really liked Post Void. I definitely enjoyed this more. I'd say it's maybe better to get on sale like $15. (7/10)
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: I've said my whole life than I'm a mechanics first gamer. I love cool worlds and good stories, but how a game plays trumps all for me. Even having not remotely finished it as I write this, I can say that Mullet Madjack is one of the mechanically tightest games I've played in years. It'll challenge you (at least on the intended difficulties) but you'll be in flow state the whole time and instantly going "one more run" whenever you die.You should just look at the trailers to get a sense of the game play as trying to describe it won't do it justice. The vibe is 80s anime through and through and the devs clearly knew exactly what style they wanted and nailed it. It's fast, fluid and vicious, laying on new traversal mechanics and enemy types every ten levels, which is when it also checkpoints for future run. This isn't really a roguelite, but it does share some similar elements of that in terms of per-run upgrades with permanent ones added after each checkpoint. Levels are so fast that even if you fail, you don't feel you've lost a ton and at least in my case, I less wanted to be frustrated and more just wanted to jump right back in. I will say that sometimes, you will suddenly die and not realize why as encounters are so rapid, you won't always get clear damage feedback. Some might get frustrated by this, but it didn't happen to me much and I was fine to not worry much about it and just restart.Beyond the campaign, there's also an endless mode and other modes besides you can unlock, with more listed as coming in the future and voted by the community to boot. This is something they clearly intend to keep supporting for a while. There's also leaderboards for those modes, which is another great addition.I'm 45 and games like this show me that I can still hold my own in fast and frantic titles, which is perhaps the best compliment I can give it. This is definitely going to be one of my favourite games of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly short, (I beat it in about 4 hours) but does include an endless mode for continued fun. The story is very cheesy and the dialogue gets a little repetitive, but that's really not what people are here for anyway. The story mostly boils down to: go rescue the damsel in distress because capitalism, dopamine rushes, and evil robots, but unfortunately, you get an unskippable cutscene at the end of the game that feels incredibly pretentious. The game could have hammered its point home through the world building but instead, decided to beat the player over the head with one annoying cutscene that feels completely out of place given how short and skippable most cutscenes in this game are and how fast paced the gameplay is.It's incredibly fast paced, if you avoid the slower weapons. The SMG, katanas, and revolver are all pretty fast paced, as well as the laser rifle, although I didn't really care for that one. The shotgun is a little slow and the railgun slows the game down to a crawl and really isn't viable because of that at the higher difficulties. Most of the weapons feel good. The katanas can be tough to justify due to their inflexibility against almost all of the bosses, but can be swapped out right before a boss fight. They do trivialize the early game levels, as most of the guns feel clunky due to having to reload all the time, something that can be fixed through in game upgrades.The upgrade system is random. You're given a weapons option that can also contain an upgrade to your current weapon, a stat boost, and a hero modifier (most of which are either gaining more time for certain kills or softening the blows from traps) after every level you beat. Sometimes, you get locked in to some terrible upgrades. The laser rifle just feels bad. It doesn't do anywhere near the damage it needs to to feel good to use. Combine that with "talking protagonist" and "silent protagonist" being potential upgrades and some random stat boost like "chance for bullets to pierce through enemies" while you're using a sword, and there are some times the upgrades straight up don't feel rewarding. That being said, some of them feel great. There's nothing like getting 100% ricochet chance and watching SMG bullets flying all over the room or upgrading your revolver to have infinite ammo. The unique life system feels great. While limiting in the kinds of weapons you can viably use (stares at the railgun), it encourages fast gameplay. Did I mention this game was fast? The only issue I have with it is that the game is very vertical and there are some issues with tiny ledges stopping you from falling straight down and sometimes getting stuck on top of enemies that are sprites. The ledges were minor annoyances but usually, getting stuck on top of an enemy meant immediate death, which was rather frustrating. Other than that, the running and gunning is a ton of fun. The movement feels fast and almost all the weapons feel good.The art style is really cool. While it is also a point of frustration due to the sprite art and verticality, it looks like a comic book and works well, well, mostly, with the gameplay and works very well with the cheesy story. The colors really pop and make it easy to shoot at the things you're supposed to be shooting at in a split second and the art is full of detail most people are just going to fly by.This game is a blast and then it's over. I have a few minor gripes, but overall, it's a ton of fun and doesn't overstay its welcome. And if you want to keep playing, there's always an endless mode on offer that will keep the bullets flying

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I highly recommend this game for its price, but mostly for those seeking a fun shooter with an emphasis on dashing through levels, rather than any rogue or rogue-lite where subsequent runs will vary in playstyle like Streets of Rogue. Also Streammer is best waifu (Yes, that is how she is referred to in the art book)Pros: Easy to play, hard to master. Beautiful retro graphics, fun voice acting.Cons: Replay value is limited for a rogue-liteMullet Mad Jack is an incredibly fun and challenging first person shooter with an 80s retrofuturistic design based on 80s anime and rogue-lite elements.Its controls are much like Doom and Duke Nukem, but instead of exploration, it has an emphasis on moving through levels as quickly as possible in one smooth mad dash, using the environment as well as your shooting skills to your advantage. Your countdown is your health bar, with damage from enemies subtracting precious seconds while killing enemies refills your counter. Most levels will be completed in under a minute, and the game is so fast-paced and chaotic that it is easy enough to mistake it for a rail shooter. You kick enemies into fans, explode barrels, use your weapons to annihilate enemies as soon as you enter the room. Besides enemies, it also has a strong emphasis on first person platforming, asking you to dodge lasers, wall run across chasm, and avoid pools of acid and lava to reach the level's end point.Your gameplay will eventually come down to producing as smooth a mad dash as you can muster through a level, using the rogue-lite elements, such as exploding bullets or extra seconds, in order to more easily accomplish that.That all said, it has limited value for a rogue-lite, since levels are functionally the same in terms of your play style. Indeed, most of the weapons operate similarly enough that playing through the game with new weapons will hardly feel worth it. It is strange to say this in a game that features a Katana, a shotgun, and a rail gun, but it is true.Most of the replay value comes in mastering the gameplay more than in varying how you complete your runs.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Graphics and music are good, sound design is acceptable, gameplay is good for 15 minutes and then doesn't develop at all and is insanely repetitive. After about 20 minutes you will see little to nothing that is new or interesting other than some cutscene lore/story stuff with a few different sections. The whole game is basically an autoscrolling shooter. You hold W and dash through the level while clicking heads, occasionally needing to jump, or move to the side briefly to hit a vending machine to heal. There are upgrades but they get wiped every 10 levels so... ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ There are also some perma upgrades but its just ♥♥♥♥ like adding some rerolls and unlocking max weapon level. Enemy variety is horrible, adding an extra enemy after some bosses, but you don't play any different. Hold W, shoot enemies in the way. It's mind numbing, and not in a good way. You don't even get the courtesy of new environments to play in, it's minute differences that change almost nothing, and all looks the same. I was very pleased in the first 15 minutes and then 10 minutes later I was getting lost. Wanted to persevere through it for a full review but idiotically dying resets you to the 1st level of your stage (You die in 47, you go to 41, 37 go to 31, etc). So then you just endure MORE of the SAME tedium. You can't even call it replaying the levels they are so similar, you are basically just given more levels to do. On the Challenging difficulty, the greatest threat to your life is boredom. Both of my 2 deaths were me just zoning out, one during a bossfight that instakills you in melee (he was a chainsaw man I guess), the other because i was just not paying attention to enemies, and the timer killed me because I wasn't killing enough. I don't get all the positivity. it is pretty mediocre. 3/10EDIT: Oh yeah, the price. 20 bucks? Really? Even Dead by Daylight is a better use of 20 bucks, and that ♥♥♥♥ will make you never want to play a multiplayer game again.
