_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal, I am filled with utter joy to see something so neat executed in such a clean way.I'm a huge fan of this type of arcade "try to get as high a score as you can" type of shooter and very few games have scratched that itch for me.Devil Daggers, and Hyper Demon are the only two that come to mind, and while those are great, this is for sure different than those, there's a lot more appeal here for people who aren't coming just to beat their own time.The campaign is lovely, it's a bit short, but only because I wish there was more, it's got a delightfully silly story with a wonderful aesthetic, and it's a great way to teach you if you are looking for that arcade repetition while also having it's own unique content separate from endless.The gameplay itself is fast and simple though with a lot of room for creativity, with plenty of simple environmental methods of killing enemies, and room layouts you'll probably start to remember your own methods for.It's fast, really fast, and that simplicity also helps it escape being difficult to understand in all the chaos.Art is fun, character designs are a highlight for me, really love Mr. Bullets design in particular!Music is really good, although tragically you won't be hearing many tracks play out as you finish most floors in 20 seconds, but it serves the game well for this, I just wanna hear it more.I also wanna touch on how it's updated, because there's something really cool here I don't see often.There have been some changes already that fundamentally change the ease of which one gets a high score, and very often I see this avoided due to it often nullifying high scores. HOWEVER, these changes fundamentally made the game more enjoyable.Most of my complaints with the gameplay on release were changed shortly after and are no longer gripes I have.I for sure recommend it, it's one of the best things to come out this year and it has a lot to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Is there anything better than just stumbling over a videogame that turns out to be awesome? Currently out for the count with Covid, I found myself browsing Steam to add to my ever-increasing backlog, and this anime-inspired gem just leapt out of the screen. Sporting a sexy 80's anime aesthetic (the game says 90's but this looks more like Bubblegum Crisis or Riding Bean to me), complete with VHS-style artifacts, Mullet Mad Jack is an anime fan's FPS dream come true. Set in a cyberpunk future (depicted as only 80's/90's anime could dream of, all neon colours and graffiti) humanity is unemployed while AI robots (Robillionaires) live the good life. Mad Jack is tasked with rescuing an idol that has been kidnapped and must ascend 10 floors to get the girl, while kicking robot ass. However, you start with just 10 seconds to live, each kill granting precious seconds of extra life as you race to the exit utilising all the skill, speed and violence you can muster. The game has an incredible sense of urgency thanks to the pumping soundtrack, smooth graphics and corridor style gameplay. Your can shoot, kick and slide your way past your enemies, using environmental items like fans or electric boards to kill your enemies, or just headshot the robo-thugs for a clean kill. Every level you progress allows you a power up, but die and it's back to the first floor to try all over again. This decidedly brutal reset makes every kill just that bit more important.Mullet Mad Jack's presentation is what drew me in, but it was the adrenaline that kept me hooked all night. The upgrades allow you to customise your play style, kills are immensely satisfying and most importantly, my own deaths were entirely due to my own mistakes (or let's be honest, mad panic as things get hectic and I'm just missing every shot!) so it never feels frustrating despite the punishment of a total reset on dying.A special mention for voice actor Kat Dannes, she's perfect as your sassy operator who seemingly delights in both your successes and failures and just brings the game to life.I think this might also be the first time I've kicked myself for just buying the vanilla version of the game, because the soundtrack by Fernando Pepe and Mateus Polati is superb. I'll be keeping an eye out for a vinyl release because the retro-futuristic smooth opening alone makes it deserving of a place in my collection, but it's all absolute gold. It makes me want to crank it up on the car stereo and just cruise around at night. Ultimately, I adore this game. It runs smooth as silk on the Steam Deck, so good news for blasters on the move. Honestly, I just want more of everything - a physical special edition release, LP, artbook, all of it. It's pure fun and I can't recommend it highly enough. The studio is now on my watch list.

_childDocuments_.review: A wild, thrilling, adrenaline fueled ride.I had seen a bunch of coverage of this game in its earliest stages and thought "Eh, the aesthetics slap, but I don't know if that whole constantly-refuel-10-seconds-of-life thing is for me"And then I noticed they had a demo. I did the whole thing in one sitting and immediately bought the game.Once you get the flow of it (which it is very gentle at introducing), it is basically dopamine reward fueled machine of swift dancing and rythm, and I am here for it.It's fairly short but very replayable given the high variation in builds and difficulty you can roll for. Tuning a game so that it's challenging, but not so ball busting hard that you go URGH and uninstall it on failure is a delicate balance, and I think they've mostly succeeded here.The aesthetics are on point, beautiful art, banging music. It has a Big PC Box Unboxing Experience option in the main menu that is full of fuzzy warm feelings. The Voice Acting is also absolutely on point for circa 1996 Anime OVA English Dub, it's spot on. Some may find the Streamer lady grating, in which case you can mute her immediately from the same screen where she shows up, but I personally love the touch.Man, what an exciting ride. The story mode is fairly short on normal difficulty, it took me about 2.5 hours to make it to the end in a few sittings and retries, but I don't feel like the game is over and can be shelved yet. _childDocuments_.review: Hurry up and buy Mullet Mad Jack if you like cyberpunk, outrun music, 80's / 90's aesthetics, anime of any kind, or indie video games. That's automatic. Read on if you aren't already buying this wonderful game.What's the game like? You're an elder millennial whose mom left him in a mall arcade with five bucks for the next hour and you just put a quarter into Smash TV, Revolution X, and Out Run at the same time. You take a sip of the flat, diluted soda you've been clutching before you stick it on the cabinet with your stash of quarters stacked on the hard, plastic lid. It plays something like that, anyway.How's the story? You're in the story of Quarantine, Doom, Rise of the Triad, and Duke Nukem 3D on a beige CRT monitor with a VGA graphics card on a Pentium II. Your friends are coming over later to watch The Sandlot on VHS but when your parents go to sleep you're going to put on Judge Dredd or Tank Girl. The story's good.Is it worth the money? Well, I don't wear my JNCOs anymore. Those little sunglasses with the small lenses look good on Venjent but anachronistic on me. My CD collection is in the bottom of a box somewhere, slowly delaminating while I refuse to finally throw them away now that Spotify completely replaced everything. But those things were so worth the bygone era they were a part of, an era I was fortunate enough to be a part of before too much of the stuff in those cyberpunk stories came true and the lifestyle of Mullet Mad Jack's weird social media dystopia parody was a little too real.Buy this game. Play this game. It's basically perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: MULLET MADJACK

_childDocuments_.review: The 1990s were a halcyon age of video games.When you bought a game back then, you were getting the complete experience. You weren't tricked into spending stupid amounts with free admission, you weren't convinced that endless grinding for garbage was acceptable under the auspice of it "getting better" as you unlock further garbage, and there wasn't a widespread internet for you to further your stupidity with dumb ideas delivered by loudmouthed hacks convincing you that these predatory tactics are ok.Back then, games needed to be bad ass. Even the games for kids, like Mario and Sonic. In Mario, you're going into another world to shoot fireballs at dinosaurs. In Sonic, you were fighting an army of robots using living creatures as batteries. The exception was Bubsy, those games were anus.But, Mullet MadJack is not anus. Mullet MadJack is awesome. Mullet MadJack will kick you in the teeth for underestimating it. And you'll love it. The premise is simple: You have 10 seconds to finish a level. You can kill robots to get seconds back, you can get pick ups that add more time, as well, but you still need to be moving and killing and putting all these robots into their place. At the end of an area, you fight a billionaire and kill them. These billionaires have enslaved humanity through the use of social media and they need to die. So, remember that the next time you say you get your news from social media; it just means you're a moron that is a slave to robot billionaires. You should have figured that out, though, since most people disseminating news on the internet are just losers, like you, screaming at their phones and acting outraged over dumb stuff that doesn't matter.Mullet MadJack is not dumb stuff, it's awesome stuff. At the end of each level, you pick an upgrade that has effects like slowing time, turning soda cans into grenades, giving more time back for kills, and even giving you a new weapon. Joy is rinsing out hallways of robots with a shotgun using the ricochet and penetrating chance power ups.To be clear, this is NOT a boomer shooter. This is something fairly unique. It's an arcade game crossed with a shooter that has extreme emphasis on movement. It's all tweaked together to perfection and feels outstanding to do just that. Move fast, dash through the air, gun down enemies, stab them, chug down soda, and keep on doing it. Kick them into giant fans, into neon lights, through doors, become the action movie hero you wish you were.That's really what Mullet MadJack feels like; an action movie you get to play. It's Die Hard after a case of Jolt cola. It's Terminator 2 if the T-800 was given a jetpack. It's the Matrix without the insufferable fans who just discovered its core themes are similar to Plato's Allegory of the Cave.Visually? Gorgeous.Action? Perfect.Soundtrack? Flawless. In fact, that's what DLC should be. Let me buy soundtracks.So, basically, if you don't get Mullet MadJack? You're just wrong. You've made a mistake. You're bad. Know how bad? This game is, basically, a Discord moderator's fantasy come true and you can't even handle that. Exactly. That's how bad you are. I don't care how good you are at souls-likes, anyone can read broadcasted attacks. I don't care what you have in whatever skinner box multiplayer vehicle game you play, those are bad and you should feel bad.Mullet MadJack separates the plebes from the patricians.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, MULLET MADJACK sounds simple enough. A kidnapped pop icon princess held hostage at the top of an eight-story tower. You—her mad and mulleted would-be-rescuer—at the bottom, with 10 doors standing between you and the tower’s next floor. Reach the floor’s next door and you’ll receive a new weapon or temporary upgrade. Get through all 9 doors and then kill the floor’s boss and you’ll receive a  upgrade. Die at any point, however, (even seconds before reaching the floor’s final door!) and it’s back to that floor’s very beginning. So far so good, right?   Well, it would be if MULLET MADJACK was a by-the-book cover shooter you could slowly dink ‘n’ dunk your way through as you gradually scale the tower. But Mr. Madjack has a quick trick up his sleeve... or, rather, a syringe up his vein. For you see, in this dystopian robobillionaire future that looks and sounds a heck of a lot like a roided-up 80’s anime, we lowly retrohumans cannot survive without dopamine, and your employer/streaming contractor—the ironically ultraviolent Peace Corp—has decided the best way to keep its viewers engaged (and alive!) is to manually hardwire you into a short-term life support system and stream the results, meaning you only have 10 seconds to reach the next door. Kill something along the way and you’ll get a few seconds back, even more if you kill ‘em creatively. Get shot, however, and you’ll lose a few seconds, and (in case you forgot) you don’t have many of those to spare. Now, if you’ll permit a quick tangent, last August I reviewed a nifty little Boomer Shooter called Turbo Overkill, which I considered to be—at the time—the most fast-paced and relentless combat I had experienced since middle school (those kids were so mean). However, Turbo Overkill, what with its spacious level designs and objectives that demanded occasional backtracking, looks about as fast as freeze-dried turtle turds when compared to the claustrophobic, straight-line, time-sensitive intensity of MADJACK.  But speed isn’t everything, and while MADJACK’s 10-second gimmick goes a long way to creating compelling gameplay, it doesn’t mask  of the game’s flaws. For example, during my 80-floor ascent, I only recall facing a handful of distinct enemy types, and more lethal than their weapons was their ability to get in my damn way by clogging up tight passageways.  Equally repetitive is the dialogue, as after the intro there are only maybe 20 more voice acted lines in the entire game, 10 of which are screamed at you by your manic Peace Corp moderator on every floor, nine of which are Mr. Madjack’s watered down Duke Nuke’em knockoff one-liners about lollipops and soda, and the last of which is the final boss screaming “MULLLEETTTTT!!!” over and over again. There are also a ton of meh platforming sections scattered about each floor, and nothing took the wind out of my high-speed sails faster than killing my way through five minutes of enemies only to barely miss a jump right before the last door and get sent back to the floor’s very beginning. I know, “Get good!” but goodness was this a consistently annoying recurrence during my playthrough.   But, whenever I did get mad at MADJACK, it didn’t take long for the game’s enjoyable visual aesthetic and fun soundtrack to pull me back in. As noted earlier, the game draws heavy stylistic inspiration from the Akira-era of original video animations, and I never grew tired of its bright lights and hyper-saturated gore. As a UI nerd, I also geeked out over MADJACK’s immersive menus and diegetic health bar in the form of your phone, which combines with energetic, arcadey damage notifications popping up all over the screen all of the time to create a mesmerizing, even suffocating experience. I also appreciate the option to increase, reduce, or even turn off your level timer, as each setting can completely transform the way you approach levels and allow you to say, focus on killing everything as opposed to scream sprinting past everyone as I often did.  Everything else in MADJACK ranges from okay :/ to okay :). The boss fights are intense if unspectacular exclamation marks at the end of each floor. Meanwhile, the tower’s level designs have a handful of fun touches, like air duct shortcuts you can Kool-Aid Man your way through, and environmental hazards like poison and lava you can unlock resistances for (or, better yet, just jump dash over entirely). But even as the later floors begin adding lasers to dodge and advanced door locks to disable, the end product still ends up feeling like eight unconnected floors of comparable difficulty as opposed to something that truly builds upon itself. Ditto that for the fast and loose story, which is so busy being silly that it misses an opportunity to expand upon its characters or insane premise in any meaningful way.  But you're not here for serious, unless you’re serious about bisecting evil robots with a giant fire katana. So, for $20 and after adding in the game’s endless mode that’s tied to a leaderboard, I think MULLET MADJACK presents solid value, so I’ll give it an aggregate MEGA score of 3.31/5 (full scoring breakdown from “Plot” to “Sound” available in video form). Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long while since a game managed to disappoint me as much as this one.I wanted to love this game, because I've been a shooter fan since the '90s and this looked promising. But in my opinion it flopped hard.The story is... Terrible. Perhaps the single worst story I've encountered in a video game. Basically, you're meant to save a popular streamer who got kidnapped, and your attempt is aired live as well for everyone to enjoy while the stream's host spams you with dated memes that don't even fit what's going on. You only have 10 seconds to live, but every kill or cool action gives you... life juice or something.It's also incredibly easy. I played on Challenge difficulty, actually died on the tutorial... And that's it. I died once there because I didn't demolish a vending machine (which refills all your HP/Time/survival gimmick) but then I made it all the way from level one to the first boss with no death. Then I quit, feeling... pretty much nothing, which isn't common for me. Nothing makes me want to go back to it. I played literally 20 minutes and beat 12.5% of the game. 5 of those 20 minutes were the main menu and cutscene.And sure, I could try one of the two harder difficulties, but speaking of levels... There are 80 of them, each lasting 30 seconds, and they're "randomly generated" - as in, they're all the same, somehow. And even if they weren't, well, it's not like you can enjoy the scenery -  after all. Besides that, it's also your standard roguelike, and each level gives you a reward, such as new weapons or stat improvements.But really, stick with the default pistol, dash a couple times, spam left click on the first enemy you see, dash again, repeat for the 5-6 more enemies you'll encounter and boom, level completed. That's the gameplay. The bosses are different and you've got extra time for them at least, but they don't save this game. There were better indie shooters released in 2024.And this game is so easy to fix, too: Write a proper story for it, make levels longer and actually different... That'd already make me go from 1.5/5 to 3/5 stars. And honestly, make roguelike optional - among all the memes in this game, its core mechanic is the most tired trend and adds nothing of value here. This game is trying hard to have an identity of its own but simply copied what's been succesful in other indies (and also borrowed the small streamer's starter pack for its visuals).Only play this if you're in love with the vaporwave aesthetic. I guess. I spent more time writing this than I played the game I'm writing about, and this was more entertaining.

Fast paced game play, and a very interesting ten seconds to live mechanic which ensures you keep the action going.It has some roguelite / like mechanics, but I would definitely not call this game a roguelite / like game since there is actual progression and chapters.To summarize the game, 1. Chapters are divided by ten short levels or floors each.2. You have ten seconds to live in each floor, but you keep up the counter by killing enemies.3. You can select an upgrade from a random assortment of three between floors.4. You face a boss on the tenth floor of a chapter, without a timer.5. If you die at any point during a ten floor interval, you start all over with zero upgrades from the first floor of that particular chapter.6. Beat the boss and the chapter is cleared. Move on to the next chapter. Upgrades are reset in between chapters.Give the demo a try if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there, allow me to introduce you to my game of the year: (Here is the link to my YouTube review if you’d rather watch that)Mullet Mad Jack is a rogue like unlike anything you’ve ever played before. Soaked in neon featuring a wild mix of 90s japanimation and synthwave aesthetics, you enter a dystopian future where killing robo billionairs is the norm and it is live streamed to a large audience. Enter Jack, part mullet, part man, part potato and soda lovin’ machine, he is here to traverse 80 floors of nonstop action in an effort to rescue a social media influencer known as “the princess”. The number one robo-billionaire has kidnapped her in order to draw out her virgins blood to summon a god, and Jack is the only person that can save her.   Jack is given a measly 10 seconds to live on this adventure, and he has his handy dandy cellphone attached straight to his bloodline and his heart pumping him full of endorphins and life as he kills enemies left and right. Mullet Mad Jack is a traditional FPS in a sense, you’ll be running and gunning with various weapons, but the twist is every kill and style of the kill gives you seconds back to keep living and keep shooting your way through floor after floor of the Nakamura Plaza. You’ll encounter various enemy types ranging from your typical sharpshooter, to drones, to mecha enemies that will chase you down, and even chainsaw weilding baddies that you have to place a shot on perfectly to get past (please don't get me started on the chainsaw guys, they’re the biggest obstacle and led to more deaths than I can even remember). Jack has to make it through ten floors at a time in which he will regularly flip out screaming “WHY IS IT ALWAYS TEN FLOORS?!”, and at the end of every tenth floor is a boss waiting to challenge your ability to dodge, jump and shoot to victory. The unique thing about the boss fights is you’re not timed by 10 seconds during them, but rather a life meter that starts at 99% and dwindles as you take hits. After every ten floors things stay fresh and the game introduces new enemy types, new traps, and new abilites for you to keep the blood flow running. My one and only complaint with this entire game is that floors and layouts tend to repeat constantly, but in the end it doesn’t really matter because you’re moving at such a fast pace and the action is so intense that you don’t really notice.   The game offers the main campaign, but also an endless mode where you fight through floor after floor until you die to place your best time on the leaderboards against other players. It also offers a slew of difficulty modes ranging from a “boomer shooter” mode where you are not timed and can play as you desire, or others such as easy, normal, and perma death mode which also has a leaderboard. As of review week I’ve already been chasing other content creators scores nonstop and I know its something that is going to keep me hooked for a long time.  So, when it comes to the visuals and sound part of the game, it is purely orgasmic. This may be a bit bias, but if there was ever a game made specifically for me, it would be Mullet Mad Jack. It has a blend of 2D and 3D art style to it, and it’s absolutely beautiful. Invoking pure 90s anime aesthetics crossed with synthwave and cyberpunk vibes and visuals, Mad Jack is a feast for the eyes and the neural synapses. I know we already discussed gameplay, but the end game of the campaign mixed with the visuals and voice acting and everything else going on made me feel something no other game has ever made me feel, and the best way I could describe it is “Emotionally Horny” when trying to talk about the game to friends.  Audio wise Jacks voice actor kicks ass, and there is literally a 90’s protagonist upgrade you can get that makes him spout off one liners nonstop channeling his inner Duke Nukem or Ash Williams. The voice over work for your handler and all the other characters are top tier as well. Synthwave music accompanies you nonstop throughout all the action, and it is truly top tier stuff for the genre. Weapons all sound punchy and hit hard, notably the shotgun, which is one of the best feeling and sounding shotguns ive fired in a game in a long time. This entire game is a sensory treat.  All in all, Mullet Mad Jack is a very strong contender for my game of the year. It features Enticing roguelite gameplay that keeps you hyper focused and wanting more and more, presenting that traditional *one more run* feeling. It has references to so many greats in pop culture, one being Metal Gear which is a huge deal to me. I mean come on now, what game lets you assassinate someone with a copy of your favorite Manga? Not one that i can remember. If you’reconsidering checking out this game, I highly recommend it, you will not be disappointed, and thats a promise. After all, you want to rescue the beautiful princess and claim your prize of badass sneakers, right?

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game that I was able to 100% in about a week. I was able to do all of that in about 12 hours of playtime, so for the price pf $20 I wouldn't say its fully worth it unless you buy it on sale, especially with how quick the game is to complete. It's a nice refreshing experience if you have played fast paced games like Hotline Miami and Ghost Runner.I enjoyed the variety in weapons, upgrades, and enemies for the most part. Though I would say the bosses were lack luster because they were either the same eye blob monsters copy and pasted a few times, or it was a future common enemy that just had beefed up health and shot orbs out of its body. When I saw the boss that was killed by the final boss, I got disappointed because that was the only one that looked interesting (besides the final boss). None of the bosses were really that hard, I just jumped around the room shooting at them and they would die fairly quickly, and that went for all bosses on every difficulty. I have no reason to continue playing this game, I have found all the easter eggs, I unlocked every achievements, and I have tried out every single upgrade and weapon in that span of 12 hours. I did like most of the weapons and for each difficulty I found using certain ones a lot easier, and didn't stick to just one my whole time playing. However, I feel like if there was a larger variety of weapons, upgrades, and bosses, I would put a lot more time into endless mode, but there is just no appeal to me. Overall, this game is a buy, but I would only buy it when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A great, but rather short experience best enjoyed at a sale, I think. It's definitely worth a pickup if you ever have a chance to play it as this game absolutely oozes style through it's 90's anime inspired retrowave/cyberpunk aesthetic with a VHS filter on top of it all to really bring home an authentic feeling experience that makes you feel like you're playing through a 90's action anime -- with all of it's hijinks. So what's it like? It's rogue lite boomer shooter, but I would argue that it's a "puzzle shooter" in a way. A lot of the system mastery of this game comes from the ability to quickly recognize patterns and capitalize on those opportunities via the various environmental death hazards present in each floor.This unfortunately means that mastery of the mechanics will come rather quickly once that pattern recognition sets in, and the only way to really "do more" with the experience is basically be able to interact with these patters quicker. It's admittedly a bit shallow for my liking, and it wears off its welcome fairly fast. For the people who absolutely want to push this game to it's theoretical mechanical limits though, the endless mode is available to give you a more traditional roguelike shooter experience. As for me? I enjoyed it. It was a solid game with very charming visuals, but the lack of meat really keeps this game from being anything over a 6/10 for me personally.

Very pretty game but it really needed to be an early access release so the dev could have feedback on the shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: Here you are, riding your crimson car, waiting for your next call that will send you on your next mission where you will destroy another thousand of robots for the amusement of the crowd. In ancient times, people like you were known as "Gladiators," but now you are called "Moderators." A bloody wire is inserted into your body like a shackle, filling your body with dopamine to keep you alive for longer than ten seconds. Yes, you are truly a   of this eternal coliseum. However, to some extent, your fate is more in your control than that of the young maiden who is captured by a wealthy but twisted robot in search of something beyond reality. However, I wouldn’t take his faith seriously, because he’s just an instrument of entertainment like you, right?Fight in an ever-changing labyrinth against an "iron mass" that seeks to reduce your life timer to two zeros. But, ironically, this "iron mass" is your life source, right? To survive, you must dance this deadly waltz, sweeping from room to room, leaving destruction and death in your wake. Shoot'em in the head (or anywhere else), kick into traps, tear into pieces or simply destroy them all so that the crowd rejoices at this farce and gives you more of this ambrosia called “like”! Fortunately, your masters generously rewarded you with a rich arsenal of chaos. From the ancient sword of honor to a futuristic blaster of control! Also, every tool in your way became a torture device for those machines! So much carnage, and for what? For a pair of fancy boots? And here you are, cut from a network of bloodlust, into the darkest place before your big challenge. Don't you think that is strange? No one can give you that "dopamine nectar" to support your short life, and here you are, still breathing even after ten seconds of silence. Oh, sorry, I forgot that you don't have time to reflect on that trivial topic! Now you have a big bad boss to demolish. Well, you've passed this test and head to the next room, but... what did they say in that old game? "Your princess is in another castle"! And that bloody cycle begins anew. New floors, new deaths, new mockery... Until you've finally reached that so called "ROBILLIONER", ripped his shell and saved that lady called "Influencer"... But is this truly the end of this nightmare? Do you really have this "final goal"? Or is it actually just a false "promised land", and now you are stuck in this cycle until the crowd gets tired of you?Do you actually do all of this just for a pair of shoes? Or do you just want to save that girl you barely know? Or are you just frustrated with this farce, but just can't break free of that cursed cycle and just take it out on these robots to distract your mind from despair?Well, for now, this cycle is unbreakable. The endless maze of violence is still full of iron prey. So take that gun and sink into a dopamine rush! Right now, is the only thing you can do, my mighty Retro-human!"

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a weird game that I'm unable to recommend.The map variety is non-existent and the game is barely legible, the UI is clunky and overdesigned and will often lead to your untimely death by covering up the important parts of the game, the game is not difficult at it's core, it's just not all that playable if played the way it's intended. The hitboxes aren't tight and the level design is samey but not samey enough to be learned by heart. It's a good looking game but that's about all it is. The weapon balance is all over the place and if you're aiming for higher difficulties you'll likely find yourself going back to the only viable weapon in game, the fully upgraded starter pistol which lets you finish levels in a normal amount of time (20-30 seconds) and kill enemies in a speedy manner.The gameplay is horridly shallow and the more interesting gameplay altering upgrades ( such as the grappling hook or environment items) fall short because the game wasn't built to accomodate them. In short, if you've finished the DEMO which is available, you've seen most if not nearly all of what the game has to offer.Compared to other fast paced shooters on the market which fill a similar niche such as Deadlink or Roboquest, Mullet Madjack leaves a lot to be desired, the developer insists that this game has nothing in common with either of those titles but I beg to differ, there's way too much overlap not to take it into consideration. If you're a fan of wild visuals and weird shooters, MMJ might be up your alley, certainly not mine. I decided to embark on a journey to finish the game on HARD and then INSANE but I simply got bored of it, dropped the game for a few months and came back to finish it alongside the rest of my backlog and decided to drop it again. MMJ feels like an early access title sold as a finished product with a healthy dose of identity crisis. I'm not sure where the overwhelmingly positive reviews are coming from because the game is simply undercooked. It falls short in comparison to actual modern boomer shooter such as DUSK, Forgive me Father, ULTRAKILL, Project Warlock, Fortune's Run and many more, I can only attribute the positive reviews to the game's visuals.I urge you to download the DEMO and consider if the free portion of the game ( which is more or less everything this game has to offer) is fun enough to be played through 8 times over for the game's asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I started out loving this game. After finishing it, I still like the gameplay loop, but this game feels unfinished. I’d skip this at full price. The loop is really fun to fly through levels and kill robots while dodging obstacles. The anime style starts out really cool.The bad: The levels never get interesting or frankly even challenging. The bosses are TERRIBLE. Seriously, completely awful. Too simple and easy. A couple are interesting, but there are only 7 (if I counted right) and most are dead brained to fight. The story by the end was grating. It becomes really cringey slop that was very disappointing. They created an interesting atmosphere with a good concept and style, and wasted it on horny nerd garbage. The last chapter and cutscene(s) are by far the most off putting part of the game. It’s some socially awkward 18-year-old boy energy. Awful.At the end of this game, I was really unsatisfied. None of the style paid off and the gameplay never matured. Feels like the game is over as soon as it ramps up.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it on normal lenient difficulty (2s per kill) - finished first 3 chapters on true normal (1s per kill), but reconsidered as I wasn't having much fun retrying whole chapters at floor 8 or 9 and at the time I didn't realize how shallow and short the game is.Fantastic presentation, atmosphere, and absolutely adorable with it's dialogue and story.But the gameplay is severely sub-par. It leans hard on it's speed gimmick because it would not be a good game otherwise.Buy only if you understand that this game is all looks and almost no substance. I decided on a non-recommended verdict because I can't see myself recommending this as a game, only as a general experience.FPS game where you have 10 seconds of life and each level is mostly a linear corridor that takes around 40 seconds to finish. If you were really cool at math you'd know that you're about 30 seconds of life short to finish. That's ok, not all of us will finish before our life ends.But since this is a game and it actually wants you to play it there is a method of restoring your time. You just need to engage in various methods of carnage. Shooting enemies dead, kicking them into doors, explosive barrels, electric fences or exposed wires will all increase your time.After each level you will get to choose 1 upgrade or weapon because this is a roguelike-like. You fight a boss after 10 levels and boss fights don't have the timer. After that you get to new chapter. There are 9 chapters, but last one is just a boss fight and epilogue.The story? You are a Moderator, basically a robot hunter. You have an app on your phone that lets you compete in mercenary work and you current job is to save a female pop-star hottie from robot billionaires who want to use her to their nefarious deeds. Your reward if you complete the task before other Moderators? A new fancy pair of sneakers.There are a total of 7 weapons (that I've seen) consisting of 2 types of katanas, pistol, shotgun, uzi, railgun and plasma gun. You can only have 1 weapon at a time and if you select a new one on level up - you replace the current one. Each weapon also has 3 levels and you can upgrade them by selecting them again on new level.Whole 80s neon presentation is really well represented here. Just look at the trailers, the game really sells itself based on looks. Everything from ingame levels to animated cutscenes are fantastic.Special mention because they are really cool.One thing annoyed me, but the rest of the game works as you'd expect without any technical issues.Speed is a gimmick. It can be enjoyable, but the game around it should have been more than it is.It can be finished in less than 4h even if you die sometimes.And this 4h worth of content is really stretched out anyway. Levels barely change throughout the game, some new hazards are added like laser gates or mines and an odd new enemy sometimes, but nothing crazy is done while progressing through the levels. Only 2 enemies require you to fight them differently and even then all you need is kick them before you can do damage.Item variety is also lackluster. You lose upgrades after each chapter and upgrades are very small % increases to different things. 5% move speed? 10% crit chance? 3% chance of your shots exploding? WOW, what great choices!!! Do you seriously think that 5% movement speed is going to really change up the game?Guns are cool, but even those get old very fast because you still fight same enemies in same way over and over because of the speed gimmick.Each level is also just a glorified hallway, again, because of the speed gimmick. You can't have complex doom levels and keep the speed gimmick.If you land on an enemy, you will slide off them. I died multiple times because an enemy's head would slide me off into a bottomless pit and force me back to the start of the area where I had 0 chances of getting back fast enough to not run out of time.It was the cause of probably like 5 restarts and pretty far into the chapter too.This game really needed something more in terms of gameplay design. Having played through on the lenient mode I have no desire to advance to the harder difficulty because there's nothing here to experience past the presentation. It needed Isaac's style itemization with interesting and powerful combinations and varied enemy types that would require different approach depending on what items you have... oh but that would eat into the speed gimmick, yeah?The speed gimmick is at the center of the problems here. There are definitely people who will be able to enjoy this on a very basic level just for the experience of mastering it's mechanics. But for anyone else this is a very pretty game with a gimmick in place of substantial gameplay.I'd give Mullet Madjack a 9/10 for presentation, and a 3/10 for the gameplayBuy only for the graphics and atmosphere. I can't even fault it for costing pretty penny for how short on content it is because the graphics and cutscenes alone must've cost a lot of money, but I can't just recommend this when there's so little substance in it.Maybe if you're a huge fan of the speedrun-FPS subgenre then you'd have a different opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: one of the fastest-paced games i have played in a really long time, probably since hotline miami, ikaruga, sonic, burnout, or need 4 speed type games. every level is 10 floors per level with weapon or skill upgrades available after each floor which can be finished in a minute totaling to about 7-10min per level depending on your skill. this coming from a 90s kid, it is pretty addicting. im close enough to the target demographic. if the store page gameplay footage appealed to you like it did to me, you will probably like this game. one thing to note, if you quit out of the game mid-floor, you will restart at the first floor next game.oh, yeah, and i could not care less about live streaming, twitch, youtube live, or any of that crap. i prefer to play games, not watch some schmo. the fake in-game live stream thing is not appealing to me. i imagine jack feels the same way, but he has no choice, and neither do i...

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is yet another one of those games that I wish I liked, but... I really just can't. Not a terrible idea at face-value: An FPS runner game, with rogue-like elements and hammy, retro-style anime visuals. But in practice, I've found this game to be kinda blah and un-engaging. I get the appeal of falling into a "flow-state" (HI, HOTLINE MIAMI!), but I never successfully got there with MMJ. Much of that comes down to the chaotic visuals and hud, which makes it more difficult to play than it needs to be. I'm not stranger to crazy boomer-shooters, but these games need to make an effort to design their visuals so you can process the situation at a glance, and I don't think MMJ succeeded in that effort (did they even make one...?).Also, this game likes to think that it's satirizing some kind of 90's anime aesthetic, but really, it's just screaming obnoxious things at you through its hectic pacing and... well, by actually screaming at you over dialogue :PSadly, MMJ is just one of those games that had a seemingly great idea that didn't really pan out in a real-world scenario.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, but has a myriad of little things that all build up to major annoyances.- Chapter transitions are really long and require an excessive amount of text skipping, spam-dashing, or in one case, standing around waiting for a timer to expire.- Skipping text not always consistent.- Combos get you killed in Hard Mode because you need to wait for the combo to cash in before you actually get time back.- A LOT of pointless powerups. Why do you need an exit marker? Or see items through walls? Almost everything is a straight line so you know where to go, and items stand out pretty obviously. Talking protag is just fluff. The powerup that turns explosive canisters into ice ones is a questionable downgrade. Even the Shield Dash and Boss Damage bonuses are useless on Chapter7, as shield enemies don't appear there and Chapter7 has no boss. Too much powerup pool dilution.- The Level3 pistol upgrade says it lets you shoot as fast as you can pull the trigger, but there is a pretty low cap on the firerate. It also loses the damage bonus from Level2.- You will get shot the moment you open a door and there's nothing you can do about it. Enemies have instantaneous reaction and will shoot you the nanosecond the door is registered as open. The amount of runs that end from these is ridiculous.- Kicking enemies into lava/acid/lasers only count as basic kills instead of environmental ones, which means trying to pull off stylish kills in Hard Mode penalizes you instead.- Kicking enemies is inconsistent and does not always flinch them. You will get stabbed/shot in the face a LOT for trying to use the intended combat mechanics. And again, on hard mode this is a death sentence.- One of the chapters gives you a glitch effect on-screen which is extremely chunky and disorienting. There are options to turn off debilitating effects, but not this one. Guaranteed migraine inducer.- The sniper rifle zoom/scope is rubbish and never zooms to where you're pointing. Not sure if this is intentional since it's for a boss/joke fight but it's still very annoying.There are a lot of good things about the game. If you are playing on normal mode or the no-time mode, it's a mostly chill playthrough with some goofs and gaffs. The difficulty spike comes from the very unbalanced RNG, of which the harder difficulties are not balanced around at all.Maybe with time and updates these will get improved, but currently doing the harder difficulties is just a speedrun to find the point where you hit alt+f4.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing review, I want to straight out say that damn this is definitely not worth what it is now, even at its lowest recorded price! It's really hard to recommend this toanybody that isn't already knee deep into playing indie games or loves busting money. Whilst I really do appreciate the unique style and aesthetic, besides that I can't really give it alot of praise. In some cases the visuals in this game is very jarring, especially the 3D animated cutscenes that puts jack in the fore-front. You can distinctly tell, compared to the rest of the scene he is 3D which completely ruins any immersion you have. Even at the game's best selling point it kinda fumbles, which sort of tells you how the rest of it will turn out. I'll chuck dot points cause I'm not bothered writing alot. 1. Generated maps play out mostly the same and often times you see the same tile/set every run with negligible deviations between floors. 2. The game's bosses aren't particularly interesting, and sometimes flat out the easiest part of the game. 3. Guns feel lack-luster or don't particularly stand out. There's more feeling in my imaginary 12 gauge in my mouth than the in-game shotgun. 4. End of floor upgrades were okay, nothing horrid or interesting. Aside from the weapon upgrades or extra time ones they mostly feel negligible.5. Enemy variety is poor. You mostly see the same enemies throughout the game. No visual changes based on the floor either unfortunately. 6. Music is okay. I'm generally open to all sorts of music but this is rather forgettable. The main menu music was kinda neat.7. The game isn't particularly challenging even on the hard modes. A magic monkey was piloting my brain more then I was piloting it. That's how disengaged I was.8. I like the main antagonist's voice I thought he was fun to listen to.9. The meta-narrative about hyper consumerism and 4th wall breaking was a bit cringe sometimes.The overall and lasting impression is faded and fleeting for this one. I thought after playing the demo the game would dramatically improve in a lot of its weaknesses but it didn't. To me, it felt like the demo with a few extra sprinkles on top. Not worth the price, I personally cannot understand the overwhelmingly positive for this one. (08/08/2024)TLDR; Not worth it at all. Just play the demo as you get mostly the same experience there.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a game I had to play for about 15 minutes to understand its premise, and I just don't like it. The game prides itself on being an anime, but feels more like a soul-less parody of anime (like something you'd see on Newgrounds, or that one episode of South Park) than something made by people who actually like anime. The only thing anime about this game is the fact that the protagonist is basically the result of going to an artist and asking them to draw the guy from City Hunter from memory. The only thing that feels anime about it is the absolutely godawful voiceacting, which does in fact sound like the kind of horrid dub jobs companies would crap out for a quick buck. Quick **** you to Vic Ireland. The opening cutscene has the Akira bike slide (HEY GUYS, REMEMBER AKIRA? THAT QUIRKY 80S ANIME FILM?) and a pan over a bumper sticker on the protagonist's car that reads "Shonen", presumably to remind us that a 12-year-old could probably make a more original game than this.Anyway, this game isn't a shooter - it's one of those infinite runner games. You have a 10-second time limit that extends by killing enemies.. except on higher difficulties where only environmental kills count. Even on the lower difficulties, the guns are useless unless you are constantly landing perfect headshots all the time, because otherwise the enemies are bullet sponges who can eat an entire magazine to the chest and not flinch. No, the solution here is to simply spam the "kick" button and kick all the enemies into the giant fans/explosive barrels/exposed electrical panels they're standing directly in front of. On any difficulty below "hard", you can win the game by setting up an auto-clicker on the kick button and holding W. On the harder difficulties, the game is an infinite runner about kicking the right enemies into environment hazards while ignoring everything else. There are also roguelike upgrades, which are for the most part the single most milquetoast thing ever: you can get a whopping 3% chance of one of your bullets (which, on harder difficulties, you are NEVER GOING TO USE) exploding if you shoot an enemy with it, or "up to" 5% faster movement speed. About the only upgrades that are worth it are the ones that give you more time for kills, the rest are so negligible they might as well not exist.The best thing you can do with this game is make like the editorial board at Weekly Shonen Jump and axe it from your hard drive, preferably getting a refund on the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I sure do have the temerity to leave a thumbs down after 15 minutes of play, and I'll leave the comments on (thanks in advance for the awards). Besides the very-fun graphics and Brock Samson vibe (which do a fair amount of work), I found nothing to recommend this game- and if you don't think the first 15 seconds are fun, probably none of subsequent 15 second-fills are going to change your mind. I didn't get it. I like shooters, boomer shooters, and roguelites. This is an arcade game first, which borrows snippets from those genres. It occurs in 15-45-second snapshots of action. They're cool looking, but I don't find them very fun.The game is dead simple- you've got WASD and right/left click - and dash. Sprint, shoot, kick, shoot- and then you died or you accidentally finished the floor (although as far as I can tell, your best bet is to finish the floor ASAP in all cases)The visual expression really is top-notch, but go watch cartoons if that's what you're looking for, because the gameplay is paper-thinWhen you look at a 97% score like this one, that (apparently) falls roughly in a genre-set you like, it feels like a sure thing... but this didn't even seem compelling enough to merit a full hour of play.Not for me, and I'm a little baffled by the over-the-moon reviews. Anyway I've spent more time writing this review than I did playing the game, so time to hang it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fast and fluid game play. _childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had with a movement shooter in a while. Excellent visuals, great soundtrack, satisfying sound effects for every weapon, witty one liners, and MULLETS. The game has it all.There's even a button just for giving the player an interactive experience of opening up a big game box with all the goodies inside as though you were actually in the 90's unboxing your new acquisition, which is a very specific kind of novelty that you'll spend 3 minutes on at best, but one that I appreciate nonetheless.I'd also like to highlight the fact that despite the game being built around randomly generated levels, you can still turn on a switch that makes it so the levels follow a specific order, as well as a general timer for a speedrun, as opposed to having to rely solely on each chapter's individual timer.This game also marks the quickest I've ever aimed for 100% achievements, at roughly 5 days. Though I do have a few criticisms. One of them being that the levels look a tad similar to each other. Even if makes sense that the scenery looks similar, on account of the game taking place inside one individual building, the fact still stands that it IS a videogame, so some rules can be bent. I also think that there should be more enemies in the game, since after a while it can feel a bit too repetitive, specially in Survival Mode and it's variants.I also believe that stackable upgrades should actually stack in the upgrades menu, as opposed to stealing multiple slots all to themselves, which just clogs up the table, and ruin builds.The Railgun and Plasma Guns look too similar to one another, given how distinct every other weapon looks in the game, it irks me that these two in particular are near identical, specially when they both play very differently. I also think that there should have been some more variety between the aforementioned weapons upgrades as well as Rifle, since as it stands, the Rifle is pretty much preferable to the Plasma Gun almost every time on account of both of them receiving an infinite ammo upgrade, but the Rifle benefitting from more damage, as well as a grenade at maximum level (even if I do have grievances with it, as detailed below). Speaking of, said grenade I feel should be set to a button (perhaps middle mouse button, since it serves no function in this game), and not a random timer, as the times it's shot at nothing tend to outweigh the times it's made to actually hit something.I also appreciate the fact the developers have since added more game modes for further replayability, including, but not limited to, making the Sniper segment playable separately, which was a weird ommission from the base game. (The new voice lines are much appreciated as well!)In conclusion, if you like running against a clock that's constantly trying to kill you while you slice, shoot, dash and kick those DAMN robots to the sound of 90's inspired tracks, while pondering about the effects of excessive consumerism on "retro humans" and the commodification of death, then you might want to give this a shot. Just be prepared to die and to be made fun of for it by a sassy anime lady... A LOT.

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MADJACK is a fun, fast-paced boomer shooter, with a very stylized 80's aesthetic. I enjoyed my 9 hours I got out of it, even if I don't think I'll play it again. After beating the game, there isn't a lot of incentive to replay other than beating your high score. There aren't enough weapons and abilities to make experimenting with combinations worthwhile. The only reward to unlock is a new skin for your shoes, something you only see when you kick an enemy. The irony is, the game is not subtle about making fun of the dopamine-triggering gameplay loop that boomer-shooters rely on, yet there isn't a whole lot to keep you coming back for more. It feels like there was supposed to be more to the game that never got fleshed out, and probably never will be. The animations and cutscenes are great. The voice acting is not. I wanted to like the main villain because the character design is neat, but then he opened his mouth. The game seems to want you to take him seriously, so it's unfortunate that his voice actor in particular sounds like a 4chan edgelord with VoiceMod. At the end of the day, I got my $20 worth, but there are a lot of other games I got a lot more gameplay out of for $20. I would buy it in a bundle or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. "Boomer Shooter" is a terrible tag, "Fast-Paced" is what this game is, it is basically Post Void with an 80s aesthetic. Essentially, you get random super-fast paced linear levels, then a boss every 10 floors, and the goal is to always be doing moving and shooting enemies in the head. If you're expecting something like Warhammer 40k Boltgun or Prodeus, you should look elsewhere. This is moreso for people who really like the fast parts of Ultrakill and just want more of that.Gameplay: There are 7 weapons - Plasma rifle, SMG, Rifle, Revolver, Shotgun and 2 variants of the Katana. While I want to really like the Katana, you take damage from touching most enemies, and you need to get close to use the katana. The 2nd or 3rd boss, Chainsaw Guy, is a hard counter to the Katana as well (unless you throw it) which I thought was unbalanced. The powerups are not that well thought out. Especially for a genre like this that is just corridor after corridor of dopamine, I think it should be a cardinal sin to introduce percentage based improvements as powerups. I want more effects on my screen, give me a powerup that shoots a rocket after every 2nd shot or gives me a 1-hit shield every time I kill an enemy. There is no reason for there to be a triple-jump powerup, or a powerup for navigating through the map. It's ridiculous.Soundtrack + Visuals: Great. Not much to add except it is a lot easier to get your bearings than you think. After the first few levels you just naturally lock in.Plot: Not non-existent but might as well be. I will say the Chapter 4/5 stuff does not need to be there. I'm only here to zoom past the levels, the whole "walk around your room while this bar fills up" is a terrible design choice. This is not the genre to tell a deep story. Overall cool game

You can tell the team had a ton of love with what they were making here. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, a game that has a highly repetitive gameplay loop, a single gimmick, and not a lot of variation will get slammed in Steam reviews and fail faster than one of 's levels. But this game makes it all work.There isn't a whole lot of game (git gud and you can reach the credits scroll in 2 or 3 hours) but the tongue-in-cheek humor, fast pace, secrets, and unlocks offer enough to hold your interest and keep the replayability pretty high. Multiple difficulty settings ensure that you're enjoying the game the way you want with maybe some incentives to try a harder setting... but no pressure.Some people will be drawn to the "anime on VHS" style to everything. I'm in that age range where anyone into what was "JapAnimation" at the time only had access to VHS dubs of dubs of dubs of stuff and pickin's were slim. I guess where I am going with this is that, sure, this game gets the feel almost right but it does so upon the shoulders of classic animation that time is about to forget. It's pretty on the nose, too. If you dig the main menu's loop then you'll want to find and watch:- Bubblegum Crisis- Riding Bean- Akira- Dirty Pair- MADOX-01- Dominion Tank Police- Megazone 23- City Hunter- Gall Force

_childDocuments_.review: I have died so many times it's rage inducing. The random layouts just seem to screw you sometimes. It's all part of the game. One thing they don't tell you is that it's a roguelite. It's 9 floors + a boss floor per each chapter. If you die at any point - you redo the chapter and lose ALL your upgrades. There's upgrades you can get which are permanent but they are ok at best. Things like "reroll the shop once per floor". Overall having a lot of fun. The soundtracks so good, even dying means you get to take a new approach. It blends really nicely and makes it feel like a rhythm game. I do NOT recommend max difficulty for first playthrough - even if you struggle through the first part the new enemies will stump you a bit.Get it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MADJACK is an exceptional achievement in what it sets out to do, offering an innovative yet nostalgic approach based on familiar mechanics. It combines the classic style of Doom, the frantic gameplay of Ultrakill, and the strategic depth of Hades, granting the player remarkable freedom to explore and understand their own limits.The fast-paced floor-based structure delivers a highly satisfying game design experience. The Brazilian voice acting is of outstanding quality, and the art style is distinctively unique.Above all, MULLET MADJACK stands as a source of national pride for Brazil.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is a superbly enjoyable game with a strong vision, which easily earns my recommendation. Apart from the high-octane gameplay, I also love the visual direction, the characters, the sporadic humor and references, and the ending.Having said that, the game does feel a bit underbaked in certain areas. I think the environment style and room randomization quickly become overly repetitive, making the later floors not as fresh as I would hope them to be. More level variety, be it more verticality or more creative shortcuts and environmental hazards, would make the runs a bit more varied. Weapon upgrades are also somewhat boring, with many just being "infinite ammo". Having completed the game on hard mode, I am not inclined to play it again, which is a shame.Still, it warrants at least one playthrough!

_childDocuments_.review: pros: - the live streamer "dopaminepunk" setting is unique and kind of cool- the retro anime aesthetic is cool- the gameplay rewards playing stylishly a lot, you rely on stylish kills to stay alive. it keeps you on the move constantly, theres no time to think you have to make quick snap second decisions to try to stay alive.a lot of your success comes down to instinct. very dynamic and fluid. - the extreme commitment to linearity is refreshing compared to most modern games, even including modern fps games. sometimes you dont care about exploring for the nooks and crannies in each stage you just want to run forward, shoot stuff and kick ass and thats exactly what you do here. - gunplay feels very frantic, weighty, intuitive and visceral. it really nails the "kickass" feel of boomer shooters and action games to a t- fun as ♥♥♥♥- fun as ♥♥♥♥cons:- level design lacks variety and makes the game feel somewhat repetitive. each level feels samey, same enemies, same hazards. you do get new types of "rooms" after completing each chapter(like the lava room for example) but the majority of the time its the same corridor with fan hazards, electric vents, exploding barrels and soda can machines. - bosses are extremely weak and dont feel rewarding to beat- there are some balance issues with the upgrades. the triple barrel shotgun overshadows pretty much every gun in late game, turning it into a point and click fest. it is essential for handling the shield enemies. the 3 second slowdown upgrade is basically a cheat code. its almost impossible to lose once you find that as it gives you the time you need to dodge anything and shoot anything in sight within those 3 seconds. if you also get the permanent upgrade that lets you choose which one to keep, you can hold onto the 3 sec slowdown for however long you want. - story had a lot of potential with the unique and interesting streamer/corporation based premise but completely squandered it for a generic mishmash of the "the princess is in another castle" and "the ritual to open the gate to hell will be complete muahuahuahuha" tropes. i dont think this is that big of a deal since this is clearly a very gameplay focused game however. overall, this game is still EXTREMELY fun to play, despite some of these pet peeves i have with it. if you love video games, and if you love action games or arcade fps, you have to play this. i would give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool style and fascinating mechanics. The first thing that I have to mention though is that this game is not as frenetic as it might seem: going super fast and shooting and kicking everything you see will hardly get you anywhere, especially once you're further in into the game. And especially because this game sometimes has a problem of the protagonist getting stuck in the environment.With Mullet Mad Jack you will learn how much 10 seconds are and that you can also take it a bit easy... but also how little they can be. Receiving damage will reduce your time left, so a single mistake could cost you the entire chapter, which can easily be a solid 5 minutes.Key pro/cons:+ Cool style+ Different builds+ Different difficulties for both accessibility and challenges+ Possibility to remap control+ Different challenges+ Good OSTs- A single mistake can cost you many minutes of gameplay- Everytime that you restart after having lost, you will return to the default weapon (a few starting weapons to choose from would be cool)- Cutscenes animations are not always very good- Bossfights are very simple and a bit of a letdown- The UI is a bit too messy, making some important information terribly highlighted

_childDocuments_.review: I do believe the game is really good and provides a refreshing aesthetic of an 80s ova anime; However, the game does heavily suffer from the lack of an interesting endgame. While the campaign may have a lot of redeeming qualities and provides a huge chunk of the appeal of the game, the lack of playable characters and only a handful of guns and lackluster perks, with some exceptions, it really lacks the replay value that has become synonymous with the rogue-like genre. Despite those facts, I would still recommend the game to others that enjoy rogue-likes and/or shooter simply because the basics of the game are still very good. Imo the game is near perfect aside from its aforementioned lack of a compelling endgame and still deserves to be enjoyed and appreciated by others.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game has an incredible aesthetic and is simply addictive. The game focuses on how well you can "flow" and adapt to the gameplay loop and once you have a grip on it, it all flows perfectly together. Each boss fight is unique and can throw you off your flow, so you will have to learn their mechanics. So far the plot has been really interesting and engaging, while being funny and thought-provoking. The aesthetic and addictive gameplay loop are what sold me on buying the full game, but this game has a great soundtrack / sound design as well. Also, plenty of accessibility options if these types of difficult and fast-paced games are not your thing. Highly recommend from my experience so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this is perfect. Its such a rush of dopamine in game and out, while getting to the first set of credits took me like an hour and a half, it will easily be one of my favorite moments in recent gaming memory. the voice acting, animation, models, gameplay, everything is so crisp, refined, and just blatantly fun.  at first going in knowing this was a rouguelite i was shocked that i discovered a build that felt way to broken to be in one, and then i quickly got to see all the upgrades are meant to be fun, and it had me choosing everything just to see what other fun perks were available.  this is one of the only fps games that made me fall in love with a melee weapon, and as comfortable and in love with it as i was i still felt welcomed to check out more of the weapon list too.the unboxing section was alot of fun too with just how genuine you can feel the love put in here. something i also have to comment on is the fact that different timers have appropriate voice lines for them, at no point does someone playing of different difficulties feel shafted out of an experience, and while understandably this isn't any visual settings to help people with epilepsy, it does a really good job at making players of multiskill levels just have fun.  Everything in this little game is just pure fun, and somehow you got me attached to a little tomodotchi at the age of 26.Yall are some cool af people and im so glad i got to experience this game. ill be checking out the endless mode more later on.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Loved every bit of it. The developers took into account that most people hate timers in single-player games and made a No Timer Mode. Hats off to them. The gameplay is satisfying, meaty, bloody - exactly what a game of its kind should strive for. The story is campy, somewhat predictable, but I found it highly enjoyable as well. Feels deliberately made to evoke nostalgia and I say it succeeds in this.The only con I can think of (excluding the timer in most modes, since that is the intended experience) is that there are no true permanent upgrades AND upon reaching a checkpoint the game takes most of the ones you acquired away from you. Overall, absolutely give it a kick! Beware, however, that you, same as I, are likely not one of the handful of people that can rock a mullet.

If you love 80s-90s art and themeing, this is perfect for you-If you love rertowave and cyberpunky songs, this is a banger-Story is real fun. Voice acting is pretty good and the cutscenes are beautiful-Bosses are a good stray away to regular levels. Think 2016 DOOM vibes but without weapon switchingCons:-If you dont like past paced rapid action games, this is very fast paced and rapid action-Can sometimes be hard to re-orient yourself if you get turned around. It only happens if you dash around ALOT-Laser placement can be really wack and is really the only poorly balanced aspectVerdict:If you love boomer shooters and speedrunning, this is a fantastic game for you. It's very stylized, very faithful to retro game and indie game, and is overall a super fun heart pumping time

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game, but maybe on discount or in a bundle. If you like how roguelikes can give you ridiculous builds and combos that can break the game, then this game is not for you. If you like close quarters fps games that a single wrong move is a game over, then this game is not for you. If you like games with endless mode where you really need to try out your best to survive for a long time, then this game is not for you. _childDocuments_.review: ++ Cool visuals and retro-style++ Unique premise++ Very fun gameplay+ Amazing final chapters+ Good music+ Fun "unboxing"-- Way too expensive-- Missing overall varietyThis game is pretty cool, but I really cannot recommend it outside of a sale.The good points are numerous: the gameplay is amazing and just a ton of fun, its fast, brutal, varied and intuitive. The visuals are cool and charming and the music is all around pretty good. The overall premise is very unique and extremely fun to engage with, as it is woven into the gameplay masterfully (10 secs till death). The game goes into overdrive during the last chapters culminating into a great final boss fight.The biggest problem however, and the reason why it is a hesitant recommendation: The story took me 4 hours to complete. F O U R. That's pretty weak for 20 Euros, in my opinion. I would have loved some kind of escalation like in the last chapters, but all you are left with is the endless mode, which is not THAT motivating to be honest. Another big negative point concerns the missing variety: You shoot the same enemies with the same guns, running through the same levels, while getting the same upgrades, which have little impact.Talking about voice lines: the VAs did a great job, no questions asked. Sadly there is almost no variety here as well, before every boss I started spam-skipping the voice lines, as they are ALWAYS the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a great arcade shooter that blends quirky humor with fast-paced action. The game's vibrant pixel art style immediately captures your attention, evoking a strong sense of nostalgia for classic 80s and 90s video games while having detailed environments, characters that pop with personality and beautifully animated cutscenes. The soundtrack is equally impressive, featuring catchy, upbeat tunes that perfectly complement the high-energy gameplay. The gameplay feels great, the guns have great impact and the enemies explode with impact. The timer keeps you engaged and on edge the whole time and they've done an amazing job of keeping the pace high while not feeling overwhelming. I think this is a must play for any fan of shooters.9/10 (Amazing)

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute peak run and gun fun. Mullet Mad Jack brings the retro aesthetic, and arcade-y feeling from the 80s and 90s into a fast paced, non-stop, fun ride, you won't want to miss. It is a game anyone can play and have a great time, but that also brings forth skill expression. The more you play it, the better you'll get at it and the more you'll be able to execute cool combos as you blitz through the levels.The story itself is relatively bare bones, however that's far from a downside. This is a game that embraces the insanity of its CyberPunk Universe. It's here for a great time, not a deep philosophical one, but that is not to say the story has nothing to say, it just won't be the thing that stick with you for a long time.Once you're done with the Story mode, you can dive into the Endless mode and this is where the game fully embraces its arcade-like nature with leader boards and fun that will only end when your skill can't carry you any further.It would be hard not to mention the thematic aspects of the game, since it boldly chose the CyberPunk aesthetic. While the game is by no means breaking any graphical fidelity standards, the way it stylizes itself and uses visuals as well as music is truly noteworthy. For an indie game, it is one of the most beautiful and thematically consistent games on the market. It's obvious the team had a solid vision for what they wanted to achieve and thanks to that it makes many other super realistic games look ugly by comparison. This is a videogame that feels like a videogame and it is an absolute blast.For Hammer95's first title, Mullet Mad Jack is a shot of brilliance and hopefully a great sign of what is to come for the Studio if they keep polishing the talent they already have. Now, your have 10 seconds, moderator. Destroy these damn bots!

_childDocuments_.review: HAMMER95 bravely woke up one day and answered the question "What if Post Void was actually good?" with MULLET MADJACK: ANIME ACTION. The game’s a really fun corridor-shooter roguelite (and roguelike if you play Permadeath) with quirky elements absolutely, absolutely oozing with ardent admiration for both faced paced shooters like the previously alluded to Post Void, but obviously Hotline Miami and 80s/90s series like GitS, Akira, and Gunsmith Cats. It has a lot going for it, but also has a decent number of drawbacks that can be looked over in the grand scheme of things just due to how fun and charismatic the game is as a whole.Pros+ Asthetic: Artstyle and music were knocked out of the park+ Pretty addictive and fun; feels good to play+ Zany and charmingNeutrals/ Pretty costly for the content on display (20 bones for 3-4 hrs) with most of the cost behind "replayability" (which might rightfully not be everyone's cup of tea)/ Hira, kata, and some kanji/JP vocab required to get that “extra immersion” factor (plus knowledge on popular culture but that’s already a given) – imo it’s a lovely touch but might leave some people in the dark/ Rooms can get quite repetitive and "feel same-y" after a while (since you'll repetitively go through them), although this is by design as HMR95 want you to remember the layouts of the room (as mentioned in the difficulty screen)Cons (-) and Nitpicks (・)- Final boss fight can feel very underwhelming and anticlimatic (excluding the outro segment that's just flavor), the dude has like literally 3 attacks and only 1 phase and can be beat in like around a minute or less lol- VERY noticeable audio cut-outs and glitches when things get hectic (to the point of annoyance) - “Seconds gained” popup can block enemies; died due to being unable to see enemies because of this a couple times, felt very cheap- Some upgrades lack info and could benefit from having an “info popup” if hovered over – EX: Weapon upgrades are one of the few things that carried over between checkpoints if you reach the next checkpoint, seeing higher tier weapons requires leveling them up while equipped, what exactly do crits do (double damage?), no mention that the grappling hook heals, etc.- One liners that can be annoying for some; muting LOCKED BEHIND AN UPGRADE for whatever reason??? Really dilutes the upgrades pool, should just be a game setting.- The sniper segment is very discombobulating and a bit nauseating; could benefit from both having a crosshair pre-ADS (to know where you will aim at) and having less "scope" take up the sides of the screen - Screen glitch artifacts effects should be able to be toned downed/disabled in settings (still occur with the “screen flashes” setting disabled)- For a game quite heavy on replayability, lacking a Custom Difficulty option is disappointing (ex: No Timer vs Second Lifespan, kill second reward, max HP, boss/enemy damage, soda/item frequency, etc.)- Katanas feel quite weak (long swing time, lackluster long-range solution, can't benefit from a lot of upgrades)- Some upgrades are just straight-up too weak (You telling me picking up items further and sliding faster is as good as ricocheting bullets and extra max HP? Or laser kills should still only give 1 extra second when head/nutshots also give 1 extra?)- Enemies are a bit hard to see from far away – they appear a bit blurry and low-res (this might just be an engine/artsyle thing but I swear I feel like there’s some post-processing getting in the way here)・Finishers don't mention the free reload (on top of the heal)・Argument can be made to swap the default kick (Shift) and kick w/item use (R Click) binds (this can be rebinded anyways)・Tooltips cannot be disabled (sure need to know to hold W on a slide to go faster for the 60th time)・Life Vest shouldn't take an upgrade slot on No Timer (but instead a side option - it wastes a slot that could've been used on something else)・Art of War passive should be changed to proc at max hp instead (rewards aggressive play instead of passive play)・Railgun should have innate enemy/glass pierce・Endless should show how many floors an upgrade has before it expires on the upgrade screen・Lack of a “quick restart/continue” option (by skipping having to press space at loading screens)・Spelling errors sprinkled in here and there (notably so in the credits and manual)・ Finishes/sodas still show seconds (instead of HP) healed on No Timer (sometimes rarely shows HP healed text in testing)・Wallrunning billboards have an invisible wall behind them, preventing you from climbing over them from behind・If more and more upgrades keep getting added (like they already have been), the upgrade pool are just going to get more diluted and would eventually benefit from something to combat it (ie: being able to choose your upgrade pool and exclude ones that you don’t like – but this might “shift the point of the upgrades being random” and just more of a personal opinion)7.5 - Streamer is my wife; she doesn’t engage in infidelity or polygamy btw

_childDocuments_.review: A stylish, somewhat punishing, but addictive 90s-inspired shooter. It's a short game, but the swift, high-octane nature of the gameplay, as well as the RNG of the levels, provides great replay value. The range of weapons and perks, as well as the randomness of the levels, ensure that no two run feels the same. This game follows Mullet Mad Jack, a character based on the likes of Duke Nukem, who may spew cheesy one-liners or be a silent protagonist (it's up to you) as he shoots, kicks, and finishes off robots to save his damsel-in-distress. You fight through 10 floors, encountering a boss at the end of each, risking having to start at the checkpoint all over if make a mistake. The story is rather bare-bones, but that's fine; it's very much an unapologetic love letter to the video games of the 1990s, and I love that.I highly recommended this title for any FPS-lovers, novice or veteran, and I have every faith this will be remembered as one of the best shooters of 2024.
