_childDocuments_.review: Short Summary: 10/10It's basically a shooter like Duke Nukem but with a bit of a twist and set in a dystopian future with an old school anime vibe.  The story is short overall, but the gameplay is fast and satisfying, with a variety of weapons, power ups, and game modes to try out, all accompanied by a sweet soundtrack.  Absolute blast.  Highly recommended! The Full Review:It's the future, and the internet and AI have evolved to a point that robots have essentially taken over the economy, with powerful Robo-Billionaires owning much of the wealth.  Humans are subject to streams of content and advertising, with the most successful humans being massive live-streamers.  Or, in your case, a MODERATOR.Moderators are tasked with taking down key Robo-Billionaires, and in your case, rescuing the woman known as the "Influencer Princess," who has been kidnapped by one of the most powerful of the Robo-Billionaires. Working through an app/company known as PEACE CORP., you're supplied with weapons and power-ups to complete your mission, but there's a big catch: you only have ten seconds of life. In order to extend the timer, you have to keep your live stream audience entertained; their Likes pump dopamine into your veins, which apparently humans in this future need a constant supply of in order to live. Therefore, you have to kick, shoot, and otherwise dismantle the robots standing in your way, swiftly and with style.The gameplay is very fast-paced, and perhaps too much for those not accustomed to first-person-shooters.  There are A LOT of colors, special effects, and other visual noise flying by as you navigate the hallways filled with robots.  Fortunately, the developers have included a wide range of difficulty settings, including an option that makes the game play more like the original DOOM or Duke Nukem games.  So even if the intended way to play isn't your style, you may still find the game enjoyable on one of those other difficulty options. Regardless of if you play the game in "Boomer Shooter" mode or go all out on Hard mode, I personally recommend that you do give Mullet Mad Jack a try because this game has style.  The soundtrack is a banger and the visuals really makes the game stand out. And while the story is short, I did find it very intriguing, particularly because it feels like it's trying to make a comment on we as humans are so hungry for stimulation and content here in the internet era.  Nowadays we're bombarded with so much media and developing AI to further increasing levels of sophistication, that Mullet Mad Jack almost feels like a satirical take what the future could be.  In any case, the game is hella fun to play.  I love the music, I love the style, and the juxtaposition of the futuristic setting and the old-school anime art direction is just really cool, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for a bit. Gets tedious after awhile... you get a pretty clear preference for weapons after maybe level 40 and each weapon only gets three levels, each of which only unlock the next level by continuing with them, but you do keep that unlock level when you resume, so if you get the shotgun to level 3 it'll always be level 3 in the future. Personally, I found the railgun the primary game breaker, instant kills on everything but kunoichi, super long range (not always a great thing if you're killing stuff at a distance but you move so fast it doesn't matter) and has a blast to take out locked doors. Pistol is reliable til the end if you're good at headshots. Etc. Shotguns don't seem to claim headshot bonus so harder to use in higher difficulties. Most bosses are pretty lame, but I liked one (floor 3 boss I think). Levels have very clearly repeating layouts after a time, so you know exactly how to move in the three "fall to your death" possible areas (forward, don't shoot the glass floors, run on wall, run forward and there's usually a chainsaw guy waiting in the middle of the fork... shoot him and jump across as one example). Game gets real preachy at the end. Most of the time you can skip cutscenes, but if you go through the credits, you're subjected to a solid two minutes of forced clicking to get through a tirade. Meh. The social commentary ain't wrong, but as the one scene you can't skip, it's real lame too. I actually found Post Void in the reviews for this game and probably enjoyed it more from a stylistic perspective, refuses to outstay its welcome. But if you went the opposite direction and you want Post Void, much longer (one set of 10 levels basically the same as the entirety of Post Void) toned down into a more straightforward cyberpunk style with a sassy protag in an anime themed hellscape, this'll keep you busy for an hour or so. There's an infinite mode that lets you try to go zen and kill forever, and that's solid.

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MADJACK is not only a great potential masterpiece of a 2024 shooter but for me personally it's one of the better rogue-likes! The titular Jack is what you get in the form of a Macho anime Husbando if the T-800 and Big Trouble In Little China's Jack Burton did a Dragonball fusion with this Jack being a lollipop chomper like Kojak rather than a stogie chomper like Duke Nukem. Like Duke himself though you occasionally get the option via stage completion pickups to give Jack the ability to spew out one-liners. There also level completion purchases for weapons and weapon upgrades. From shotguns, SMGs, Doom style plasma guns, and even Quake 2/OG Shadow Warrior style rail guns, as well as a weapon or two to unlock after completing the game the first play through. You also have a melee weapon in a Katana sword where with upgrades you can do Scorpion or Liu Kang from Mortal Kombat style fire abilities or Sub-Zero style ice abilities. They're two different achievements that involve shooting enemies in the groin in an obviously more brutal fashion than Johnny Cage simply doing his nutcracker split punch! There is also a Classic Super Mario Bros. style reference when you finish the first two floors after completing the boss fights. Out of the nine total boss fights; three of them are rather unique compared to the rest of the six. The old school anime in a cyberpunk-world atmosphere was another appeal for me alongside me being an old school first person shooter enthusiast. My Steam friend in the YouTube famous Zlimbratski himself recommends MULLET MADJACK as do I!

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is an adrenaline high that's over almost as soon as it starts. Every level is a rush and getting into the flow state feels great, and the passive upgrades have you feeling pretty powerful by the end of each 10-level chunk. My only complaints are that enemies just kind of stand around and the game overall is quite easy. Not every game needs to be a crucible but I wish there was a little more meat on the challenge bones here. It's also  short; I beat the campaign in a little over 2 hours on the "Challenge" difficulty. I'll leave it up to you on whether or not the game's price reflects value. This is possibly the first game whose endless mode doesn't feel entirely tacked on. The core concept of ascending a building floor by floor is the perfect fit for a never ending murder frenzy and I actually enjoyed my time with it. Most FPS in this style that do an endless mode wall off some base levels and vomit enemies at you which I'm never inclined to bother with.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultra-stylish, edge-of-your-seat boomer shooter bliss.Mullet Madjack takes Post-Void's basic gameplay formula, spices it up with some bells and whistles (such as melee finishers and wall running), and packages it all in a neon-soaked, semi-randomized campaign (as well as an endless mode for roguelike purists). The gameplay is fast, and it's hard, with a relentless push-forward momentum that demands you kill to survive. It's ceaselessly exciting, and the devs have included generous accessibility options to make sure everybody can experience the game in a way that's fun for them. Add in a banger synthwave soundtrack, god-tier A/V juice, and copious heaps of personality (including laugh-out-loud one-liners from the player character and a hilarious "unboxing" feature available from the main menu), and Mullet Madjack is an absolute winner. FPS, roguelite, and action fans should be all over this game.  This is a very easy recommend for what is already amongst my favorite games of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: 'If Hotline Miami was an early 90's action OVA.' It definitely captures that same feeling of having to move fast and time your kills to the music. Punishingly difficult when things don't go your way, but a massive power trip when you get everything just right. The mechanic of only having 10s seconds of life (extended by kills) also plays really well into that. Still, similar to Hotline Miami, it also kinda loses it's meaning (at least for me) after you've beaten the story once (took me 7 hours, probably less if you don't suck at FPSes like i do), so keep that in mind. Still, for the time I played, I was completely in awe, and I really think this game is one-of-a-kind in every sense of the word and not just as throwaway figure of speech. The over-the-top and darkly humorous story and setting, synthwave-inspired soundtrack, stupidly cheesy one-liners and the 90's OVA aesthetic all play work really together other and so, I was completely absorbed for the whole of my first playthrough, and the game will likely leave an impression on me long after I've stopped playing it.My only two gripes, are firstly the environmental hazards and jumping, which while not directly fatal, still eat your timer away and I've had so many good runs completely ruined just for walking carelessly into a laser fence or messing up a jump. Thankfully, there's no real downsides in losing and going again until you get it right.  The second gripe, which is the major kicker, is the same as I also have for Hotline Miami, namely that I don't feel much of a reason to play more after beating the story for the first time. For myself, the normal difficulty is already hard enough, the next difficulty above that feels just plain unfair, so forcing myself to beat my head into wall to 'git gud' just does not inspire me.

_childDocuments_.review: A game so dedicated to its retro-80s-gamer-nostalgia aesthetic it has an attract mode (look it up, youngin'). Soon as I saw that and heard the opening theme I knew I was in for a treat. The older I get, the more partial I find myself to tight, focused experiences like Mullet Mad Jack. The synthwave soundtrack, neon-saturated visuals, and fast paced gameplay all make for an enjoyable arcadey experience that almost makes you forget you're playing what is technically an FPS roguelike (as opposed to a meticulously crafted "boomer shooter"). Whether you play for five minutes or five hours, you can feel like you made progress, as the game saves after every ten floors you clear, a process that doesn't usually take more than fifteen minutes. However, because Jack only has ten seconds to live, I often found myself focusing on keeping the ten second timer (that also doubles as a health bar) maxed out at all times, often to the exclusion of nearly everything else; this is a game where you can spend the entire time staring at the timer, and next thing you know, you've blinked and the credits are rolling. Despite these minor complaints, I still highly recommend it, and kudos to the devs for releasing the soundtrack AND and an artbook; not enough devs do that these days.

After each level, there's a sort of roguelike-esque progression where you can change weapons, upgrade your weapon, or unlock different abilities like double jump/nutshots grant you extra time. The colorful graphics combined with the hyper-violent gameplay and the cheesy one-liners of the protagonist (who is about as subtle as Duke Nukem) is perfect. I also really liked the 90s anime-style cutscenes/characters. The story starts off simple (you must save the princess) but actually becomes pretty profound at the end. Beating the game once is pretty quick (I played on normal mode) but there are a few different difficulty levels and an endless roguelike mode. I'll definitely play more of this game at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a fantastic fusion of the adrenaline rush hyperviolent gameplay of Hotline Miami and classic FPS gameplay, all wrapped in a delightful 80s/90s anime OVA aesthetic. It sounds like a strange elevator pitch, but it works quite well overall. If that alone has piqued your interest, I recommend you download the demo and get straight into it.The basic concept between Mullet Madjack is that you have 10 seconds (on Normal) to reach the end of a level before you flatline. Taking out enemies or completing certain movement tricks will give you more time, whereas taking damage will reduce it, resulting a constant need to keep moving and on the offensive. You can jump, dash, kick doors in and use one-off melee weapons to help you in this endeavour, finishing a level/floor results in the roguelite option of picking and upgrade or new weapon from a selection of three. In practice, it's nothing too revolutionary, but it's a solid combination of all these elements together. You complete 9 floors, a boss on the 10th floor, rinse and repeat.The default difficulty, Normal, offers you 10 seconds of initial life and it's a solid entry point to learn the evolving mechanics of the game across the 80+ floors of the complex - not too hard, not too easy. There's lower and higher difficulties for those who want a range of options, but there is one curious and deeply accessible option: no timer mode. Rather than making the game a race against the clock, 'no timer mode' changes the flow to something closer to a traditional boomer shooter, which works quite well as well. Lastly, an endless mode is available if you're keen for a full roguelite experience. A Normal run will take about 3.5-4 hours, but I'm definitely keen to jump back in.This is all supported by a very robust set of aesthetic choices. Mullet Madjack nails the look of 80s/90s anime OVAs and the synthwave soundtrack just reinforces that. The visual and in-game references to things like Bubblegum Crisis definitely brought a small to my face, and I'd argue that the the visual/aural component of the game is its strongest feature.The only weakness I'd highlight is that in some ways, it feels like there could just be a little more to the campaign content and a little extra polish with the weapons. I'm nitpicking as the experience is already quite solid, but an expansion campaign, a few more weapons and a little polishing of some of the weaker weapons could definitely go a long way. The roughly 4 hours it took me to complete a Normal run were definitely all killer, no filler, and the game still offers a fair bit with its alternative modes and the option for endless mode.I will say however, that this game sits in a nice little niche in terms of its contemporaries. I still consider Neon White to be the best of the FPS/puzzle fast-paced games of this era, but this offers something a bit more action-heavy. Likewise, a lot of the aesthetic appeals of Ghostrunner are replicated here, but without the inherent frustration with parts of that game (case and point: boss battles). If this sounds like your jam, you're likely going to have a good time with Mullet Madjack. I still feel that an expansion could do wonders for the game in due time, but it's definitely a great game as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Madjack is a perfected blend of style, fast-pacing and intuitive gameplay in an ultra condensed package.Disclaimer: the game was played on the "Challenge" difficulty, which in-game is represented as the intended way to play the game by the developers.At first, it may seem like this FPS is just press forward and shoot whatever is on the way while you pass through the rooms. But the player will quickly learn that even if a ten second clock is ticking constantly, one must take a moment to assess the situations and take quick decisions about how to clear the rooms effectively (With high countdown number and taking the items to perform executions). Doing this process at first may prove difficult due to how fast the game and the protagonist moves, the constant or immediate reaction of the enemies and the countdown, but after mastering it, it feels just like watching an Action Film, pure awesomeness.The visuals are clear and give the player the needed feedback to take quick decisions on the flow of the gameplay, while also looking awesome on static screenshots, how can this game look so good??? The music also acompanies the gameplay and the cutscenes perfectly, truly a love letter to the era.Even if the game looks daunting or too easy for you, the game offers several difficulty levels that range from "No countdown mode", and the hardest modes which decrease the Countdown seconds, give less seconds as a reward for killing enemies, enemies do more damage, etc...I think the only reason one would not try this game is because he/she doesn't like the aesthetics.9/10 would rescue the princess again.

_childDocuments_.review: *AT THE BOTTOM OF THIS REVIEW IS SOME SPOILER CENTRIC DISCUSSION*Yeah, its pretty ♥♥♥ dope.Had this one on my radar for a while. Gameplay is fast and frantic. I've heard some people describe it as an FPS Hotline Miami. I think thats probably a little inaccurate since the timer-based life system changes the way you play quite dramatically compared to Hotline Miami's one hit kill system. Though the fast time to kill and vibrant aesthetic probably contributes to that comparison heavily. New mechanics are added every ten floors which help keep up the variety. Most of the weapons also feel great (except the plasma gun, not a huge fan of that). The game looks and sounds absolutely gorgeous. It's a very unique style that I still notice despite the rapid pace of everything. I would recommend bumping up the FOV as it made me a little motion sick at the default 60. The game also runs fantastically. A unique detail that I appreciated was the unboxing experience you can find in the menu. It's somewhat unnecessary, but really commits to the bit, is quite funny and surprisingly detailed.I have two points that could be construed as a negative. Firstly, like an OVA, this game is short and sweet. I've not touched endless mode yet, but the main campaign took me around 3.6 hours according to steam. However, this is a case of quality over quantity. There is plenty of replayability with endless mode and the additional difficulty modes. Basically don't be a d**k and refund the game. They clearly worked very hard on this and you're a terrible human if you do. Overall, I think the base game could be a bit longer (which will tie into my critique around the plot), but it absolutely does not overstay its welcome. Despite it's short length, its well paced with its gradual introduction of new mechanics.*SPOILER CENTRIC DISCUSSION*Secondly, I would have liked to see some additional story content as I feel like the story sets itself up for something a little more nefarious, but doesn't really go there. The story probably wasn't central to this game and I get that. But it feels incomplete or that potential is wasted. Given that you see a second building as you progress, the constant fourth wall breaks and the dialogue poking at darker concepts like death, the afterlife and consumerism, I was expecting some twist like, the influencer princess being the villain and the final boss is actually aware of the metaphysical f**kery going on. Or theres additional set of floors like the inverted castle in Castlevania. I'm just spitballing here and there could always be potential for an update or DLC. I could also just be massively misenterpreting the intent. Regardless, the story is still a good time. I like the hidden jokes/gags in the levels and that unboxing thing.*END OF SPOILER DISCUSSIONOverall, despite its short length, I'd genuinely recommend this at full price. It's clearly full of passion, has insanely fun gameplay, has a wonderful audiovisual presentation and does have replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: The exhausting popularity of  “boomer shooters’ has began waning at the candle of creativity. Dripping into this pool of saturation is “Mullet Mad Jack’’  a celebration of nostalgic revery. Naive arcade game-play tributed with two button mechanics (shoot or sprint) predominantly drive the ruthless yet repetitious game-play loop. All ensnared by the vibrant but tiresome cultural aesthetics of 80's. Supporting this feathered frontier is a superficial roguelite system. Upgrades provide mostly banal amendments, lacking creative consequences and development. Maintaining playability remains safely conservative.  The juxtaposition of this rudimentary approach demands more depth. Without any sense of risk, reward or strategy, the arcade gun-play becomes more evidently shallow.  “Mullet Mad Jack’’ is a basic package, indulged by its own bravado rather than developing comprehensive mechanics. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: MULLET MAD JACK is a dizzingly fast-paced, stylish FPS, that, in an age where Retrowave games are not exactly hard to come by anymore, stands out for its adherence to a twisted themepark version of 1980s Anime. It's more Hotline Miami then Doom, easy to pick up, but definitely difficult to master.In the 2090s, humankind and the internet have merged into the flawed "♥♥♥♥ Media", and now literally cannot survive for more then ten seconds without constant dopamine flow. You are Jack, a man with a weakness for lollipops, an itchy trigger finger and a hairstyle that no one before him save perhaps Solid Snake has been able to pull off. Jack is a "Moderator", who's job it is to destroy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ robot billionaires quickly and violently, with your antics streamed live for all to see. Their likes are injected directly into your bloodstream, keeping you alive for a few seconds longer with every kill. Your goal is to rescue the "Influencer Princess", a cute green-haired gal with billions of followers and a strong resemblance to Yui Takanaka of the 80s OVA Megazone Two-Three. She is held captive in the familiarly named Nagatomi Plaza by the bombastic Mr. Bullet, voiced of course by Gianni Matragrano hamming it up as usual.First and foremost, MMJ is FAST. Stages can take less then a minute and the entire campaign took me maybe three hours, accounting for many restarts in the markedly more difficult second half. As previously mentioned, you typically have at most 10 seconds to live (a certain roguelike perk can extend this by 1 second, while in the Endless mode you get LESS maximum seconds every ten floors) Getting damaged tends to take off a few seconds. Kills tend to restore 1 second, while more creative kills- headshots, environmental kills, and even robo-nutshots give more. Drinking Soda restores the full 10 seconds, as does using a finisher kill using items picked up from the environment- knives, pipe wrenches, crowbars, even a copy of (Insert Favorite Manga Here). You start with a fast-firing revolver, and can obtain other weapons between stages, along with a selection of roguelike-style perks. Completing a floor gives you a selection of three perks, and every ten floors you face a boss- the timer is disabled on the boss floors, instead giving you a traditional finite health percentage. After defeating a boss you get a checkpoint, and death will only send you back to the last checkpoint, though you will lose all your perks.SPOILERS FOR PLOT BELOW.Gameplay wise, MMJ excellent. But it has a lot of tonal whiplash and in the end I'm not sure what I'm meant to take away as a message, if it was trying to have one, and it may not have been. A cinematic and intense final boss encounter and genuinely cute ending segues directly into your first endless run and after that is an incredibly bleak Reason-You-Suck speech by the tutorial gal/handler/girlboss character that was honestly rather disheartening. As much fun as I had with MMJ, I don't know at the time of this writing if I would play it again, and this is a game where one of your start-of-level barks is "Let's kill some billionaires!"... but then has a "No billionaires were harmed in the making of this game" message in the credits. Well, why the ♥♥♥♥ not?If that doesn't sound like it would bother you that much, know that MULLET MAD JACK is an incredibly tight, fun and brisk experience and worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Mullet Mad Jack is a first person shooter that gets right to the point: kill robots to get more time and complete the stage. This simple premise is clothed in an eye-popping retro anime artstyle that will grab your attention at every moment.While the basic gameplay is straightforward, the means at the player's disposal are numerous. Various upgradeable weapons including gatling railguns and elemental katanas give you ample room to get creative. Upgrades obtained between stages can be synergized into powerful combinations. For example, one upgrade spawns more explosive barrels, another gives you bonus time when you explode enemies, and yet another gives your bullets a chance to explode. Breaking up the lightning-fast combat are boss fights, many of which require the player to think outside of the box to overcome.Mullet Mad Jack's Endless Mode gives the player a quick way to enjoy the game's adrenaline-pumping action in a more direct fashion and is a great way to play once you complete the story mode. The game is a labor of love and the developers clearly put a lot of care into making it. Having completed Mullet Mad Jack, I find myself eager to keep picking it back up, whether to complete harder difficulties or enjoy more heart-thumping action!

_childDocuments_.review: It's like an ADHD shooting gallery rogue-lite-lite, where you get to pick an upgrade at the start of each level and you lose all upgrades when you die, but here you only go back to the beginning of the chapter instead of the beginning of the game. You have ten seconds to live, getting shot lowers those seconds, but killing enemies gets you seconds back and if you kill them in stylish ways like headshoting them or kicking them into THE VOID, you get extra seconds, and if you just stay still or take too long the seconds keep ticking down to death anyway, so you're constantly ping-ponging between almost death and full health every other room, the level design can kill you almost as fast as the enemies. The trap and enemy variety is great and ups the difficulty ante with each chapter, but unfortunately the bosses sucked, and it sucks there is an upgrade that lowers boss health when half of the bosses are just gimmick fights where the health doesn't matter, it's pretty much a nothing upgrade that wastes a possible upgrade slot on every floor. But otherwise, it's a pretty fantastic game, it's not about going fast so much as about dancing through enemies and level layouts, going from room to room dodging bullets and traps, while fighting the urge to just give in to the ADHD and just mash your way through everything while staring at the pretty colors.So in that sense, it's pretty much an edging simulator. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, if you're a fan of 80's anime, or solid and fast paced FPS action, then just go ahead and get this one and enjoy!The fast gameplay is straightforward with a solid design and focus, with a fun twist to keep things lively and intense without being too annoying or tedious. Plus, the variable difficulty helps one to learn the overall mechanics, while also being available to crank up the scale when appropriate.Major props to the beautiful art and design, as it's a fun and colorful homage to the classic anime of yesteryear. Plenty of fun references to catch without being overbearing. Top notch job with the smooth and detailed animations as well. Also, big points for showing off the "unboxing" experience in all its rendered glory.Gotta appreciate the excellent music as well, with plenty of nice tracks throughout the stages, along with a terrific main menu theme. The sound design is also great, with fitting impact, explosions, and other effects feeling appropriately suited to the action. Also, love the performance from the voice actors, with their characters being appropriately over-the-top and fitting for this setting.As for any major issues or bugs, I didn't really encounter much aside from a few frame rate hiccups between loading screens, and one time when the game refused to let me continue to the next floor. Overall, you won't be disappointed by picking up this title. It keeps things short, sweet, and fun with loads of style, and doesn't rip you off like a modern AAA studio - let's leave that for the robillionaires.

_childDocuments_.review: If DOOM went on a bender and had a one night stand with Hotline Miami, the result would be Mullet MadJack. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's alright!Basically a roguelike with a short campaign that exists to onboard you into endless mode. You have 10 seconds run through a series of randomly arranged pre-fabricated rooms until you reach the exit to the next floor. Getting kills or healing items adds to your time, so you run around blasting robot guys until you pass 10 floors to reach the boss.The gameplay loop is satisfying but starts to get repetitive. The core loop of shooting robots feels great, especially when you get in the groove. All of the guns feel punchy and distinct and the death animations are over the top and fun. You fall into a nice flow state where you're churning through rooms.There aren't enough room combinations, so you can go through the same rooms multiple times in a row. It doesn't help that there's no variation in the visuals. I personally had no desire to move on to endless mode after beating the campaign. Upgrades also feel tertiary. They don't have much impact on your run and there's not much variety.The presentation is solid. The art direction is peak 90s cyberpunk satire. Big neon signs, mullets, and chunky 90s tech smashed together with modern devices like smartphones. Dialogue is hit or miss. I chuckled a couple of times, but some of the satire doesn't hit. Sometimes feels like you're talking to that friend who thinks streamers are more important than they actually are.TLDR; A nice way to kill an afternoon but it's held back by a lack of gameplay variety. Art direction is good though. You'll know if this game is for you from the trailer.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the main story of this, and I loved every bit of it!   While the main game itself isn't that long, it's very action packed!   It's 2D visual anime style really pops out at you in the best way.   The story is you have the rescue the big time influencer princess from the evil robots inside a giant building.   You have to progress through 1 floor at a time and kill robots you encounter as you make your way to the next elevator.  But there is a catch:   You have 10 seconds to live.The main way you get more time to live is by killing the robots.  You can get extra time by killing them in more stylish ways, such as headshotting them, putting a knife through their head, or by kicking them into an electric fan.  Be careful though.   You also LOSE extra time if a robot shoots you too.  When you reach an elevator, you're given the chance to rest and pick a new weapon, or equip a mod that boosts you stats in some ways.   Such as a chance for bullets to ricochet off walls, immunity to acid floors, being able to duel wield weapons for a short time,  and tons more!   But if you die , you lose all of your upgrades and have to start back at the last checkpoint.   There is a certain balance between not being too reckless, and not going too slow either.The good thing I love is this game is very welcoming to players of ALL skill types with tons of difficulties to pick from.   There's the standard difficulty I mentioned, but if you're not as skilled, you can pick an easy mode where you have more time (Or no timer at all if you want)      For those looking for a challenge, you can pick a harder mode where bosses do extra damage and there are less helpful items to find in the levels.   And if you're a real nut, you can play the perma death mode where you have to beat EVERY floor in the game with ONE LIFE.   NO CHECKPOINTS!   But if you can pull it off, you get to be in the worldwide leaderboards!There's some extra stuff you can do and unlock after beating the main game, but I'll leave that for you to discover if you're interested, which you SHOULD be if you love cool FPS.Ready?   Destroy these damn robots!

_childDocuments_.review: This game manages to take a bunch of very well known and familiar genre's, themes, etc and mash them all into one unique experience. Everything going on blends together so well and satisfies the senses in a way I havent seen in many other games. Combat is brutal and buttery smooth, the sounds are pure dopamine, visuals are captivating, and the gameplay is butt cheek clenching madness.My favorite part about it all is that, while it is very fast paced which is reinforced by the 10 second timer constantly ticking away for every second you dont kill someone, you dont have to be a adderall pumping Apex Legends pro to be good at this game. As one of the tool tips explain: "It's not about being the fastest, but to dance and flow through the enemies!". It lets the game be intense and keep you at the edge of your seat while also not feeling too rushed to make something happen and just, as the game says, flow through the levels.I hope to see more from the dev(s) and maybe even an expansion to the Madjack universe. More games starring Madjack, whether this same style or not, would surely be a hit and something I would personally be first in line to try out.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I initially had many issues with this game. The repetitive four different rooms, the predictable enemy spawn locations, the limited selection of like three guns and swords, the few available power-ups, the extremely short levels, and the sound design all frustrated me. However, after playing for more than three hours, I realized I was wrong about most of these concerns.The short levels serve a purpose: they act as checkpoints that give you a brief respite before the kill timer starts again. The repetitive level design, with its close and confined claustrophobic spaces, encourages you to use the environment strategically, maneuver around enemies, or swiftly shoot them to progress to the next room. The consistent enemy spawn locations allow you to anticipate where enemies will appear, saving you from spending too much time searching for them. The limited selection of guns is intended to help you become proficient with these weapons, offering opportunities to upgrade or trade them in. While I still believe the game could benefit from more weapons, I understand the developers' rationale for their decision.One area that still needs improvement is the swords; throwing them doesn't feel powerful enough, even when aiming for headshots. On the positive side, the movement in this game is superb. Everything feels swift and flashy, with each bullet and slash registering impactfully, so you know which hits connect and which do not. The kill timer, reminiscent of the movie "Crank" and the multiplayer game mode in old-school Call of Duty games, is implemented very well here. Speed, movement, accuracy, and precision are crucial and incentivized.That being said, I still think the game is a bit pricey for the amount of content you get. However, it's worth purchasing if it genuinely looks like something you will enjoy. Keep in mind, the story isn't the focus here; in fact, the dialogue often pokes fun at itself and the fact that you're playing a protagonist within a video game. Although the game’s description and doesn't explicitly state this, it’s essentially a roguelike. Make sure you're aware of this before diving in so you don't expect a narrative and linear experience like Hi-Fi Rush. If there is anything I could compare this game to, I would say it's essentially a fps version of hotline miami, with boomer shooter and roguelike mechanics.Overall rating: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: My laptop is certified trash and I'm still able to play this game, which is something I'm very grateful for, so thank you to the devs for that. Also, I am currently on chapter 6 because of the performance issues caused by my own hardware and also by being, as the kids say these days, "bad." I might even swallow my pride and bump the difficulty down so I can finish the game this weekend, might not, who can say? Anyway.As probably a lot of folks might have, a friend introduced this to me via Alpha Beta Gamer and I was hooked on the whole visual aesthetic and gameplay loop. Admittedly, I did not play the other game that's similar to this that I imagine served as part of the inspiration for this and I will have to check that out later, but this is not about that game. Continuing on, I tried out the demo and enjoyed what was available to me, particularly the way the weapons were balanced. The only one I didn't "click" with by the end of it up to the full release was the SMG and that's entirely on myself. I value taking things out very quickly when I'm playing an FPS in general (and this game's central gimmick with the timer values it more so) and the shotgun serves that purpose well and it felt like beaning someone in the head with some SMG fire didn't instantly down them, but then again, the enemies are made of metal.As mentioned previously, I am extremely grateful that the devs have some settings in the options menu that can let my toaster play and I've run into lag spikes only in instances that they would be expected (hi, level 3 shotgun with max reload bonus) and it's been very responsive otherwise. The new enemies and hazards introduced in chapter 3 and beyond are refreshing after spending quite a bit of time with the demo, although the wallrunning prop did take me a brief moment to understand what was being asked of (you just rub against it and you will pop up once you reach the end of the track; don't mess up). Also, the laser traps are dastardly, but in a good way since some players might be all about the speed and it's effectively a speed trap to get you to pause for a second and really think about what you're doing.The new weapons that weren't in the demo, the railgun and the plasma rifle, I've had some fun with. The railgun especially just melts the more irritating standard foes but you have to watch out for the kick because that could invite trouble. The PR, to me, feels like an SMG I can gel with.But my love is with the shotgun and how I can simply turn my brain off (for the most part) and destroy everything in front of me. This shotgun easily enters the top 5 of video game shotguns because it has real range and good hitstun whenever it doesn't instantly destroy the enemy. I do enjoy all the weapons quite a bit, but I always found myself switching back to this thing because it's just so cool.On the story so far that I've reached (up to Chapter 6), I was not truly expecting so much from it, but it's still pretty good given, you know, everything. I do recommend anyone who's played so far to check out the in-game unboxing option because there's even more things to learn about the background that brings some more texture to the world, which I dug.As for things to improve, I've been seeing that some people have been having some performance issues, but I would assume the devs are aware of the situation and will address that in due time. The only other thing I would recommend is perhaps giving a few more concessions to those with photo-sensitivity issues (I am not personally affected by this, but I do have friends and associates who are), but I would want those people to speak up more about that as they would know more than I do on that matter so that the game could have more of an audience, and I do ultimately understand if it proves to be too difficult for the devs to do that considering other things they might want to take care of first and foremost.Bottom line, this game's good if you're able to pick up what it's putting down and as long as you're not at risk with flashing lights, it's definitely worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let's grease up and dive into the absurd world of "MULLET MADJACK," a game that cranks the insanity dial way past 11 and snaps the knob off. This isn't just a game; it's an 80's hair metal album cover come to life, complete with more bullets and mullets than a truck stop in the deep South.Mullet MadJack is the hero we didn't know we needed. Imagine if Rambo stopped taking life so seriously and decided to party hard instead. That's MadJack for you. He's all about spraying bullets with the finesse of a firehose at a cat bath, and his one-liners? They're cheesier than a high school prom in Wisconsin, and twice as entertaining.Now, let's talk gameplay. This no-nonsense FPS is as straightforward as it gets—think of it as a guided tour through a fireworks factory that's currently on fire. With roguelike elements that keep things fresher than a pair of socks straight out of the pack, you'll never get bored, no matter how many times you play.In conclusion, MULLET MADJACK isn't just a game; it's a high-octane, face-melting, mullet-flapping adventure that's as ridiculous as it is addictive. It's a power trip wrapped in anime visuals with the subtlety of a sledgehammer at a glassware convention. If you're in the mood for something utterly absurd and fantastically fun, then buckle up, buttercup. MadJack's got a bullet with your name on it, and it's coming in hot.

_childDocuments_.review: It would genuinely be hard to write this game a bad review.  At it's core it's a very, very simple premise: run through the level, murder everything, get to the end. There's just no fat on the bones here to get worked up about: the game is easy to play, easy to spend a few hours with, and just as easy to put down.For anyone who might look at it and worry it's perhaps a bit too hardcore, the basic challenge is pretty easy, I blew through the normal difficulty with only a small hiccup during Chapter 7 where I kept falling into pits.  It wasn't really the fault of the game, I just kept doing it.  Kicking it up a notch to the developer-intended pain it did spin back around and immediately kick my teeth in so yeah, if you want a soul-crushing challenge you can find it here, but if you just want some light skill-based shooting in a fast-paced package, the game obliges there as well.As I said at the top, it's hard to write anything but a good review for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I was a bit hesitant at first when I heard and saw the game and its older demos. 10 seconds to live?  I already hated timers in games before, because in most games they were just put there for arbitrary reasons that don't usually contribute to the game itself except for the fact to speed up the player and create a fake sense of urgency, with very few of them actually integrating the timer into the gameloop. Mullet Madjack on the other hand, stretches those 10 seconds into pure dopamine as the game puts it.And it ain't lying. The guns feel great, destroying your enemies with speed and precision or obliterating them with the melee finishers or weapons feels amazing. There's very few guns and I feel like some overlap, but thats not the point. All guns are good, though I wish the SMG didn't kick like a mule even with the upgrades.The game doesn't have a lot of content, because its not made to take away your days and nights. It knows what it is: an Arcadey corridor shooter, actually I'd compare this game to Time Crisis but instead of having lifes your timer is your life, each time you get shot it goes down. Its quality is shinning in everything, from the amazing artstyle, to the tight gameplay. It also has multiple difficulties, I personally finished it on the Challenging difficulty as it was the one described "As the devs intended", and even though some levels took me a few tries, they were not impossible. Playing in that difficulty also taught me how to play by using every single mechanic: Shooting, Sliding, Kicking and Finishers.That game is not just the campaign, the game is the campaign and its Endless Mode. Which unlike other roguelikes, here the upgrades you pick are also on a timer: They only last 10 floors. Which I can see myself playing from time to time one or two endless runs when I feel like it.Game is well worth its asking price if you like these kind of indie games, which with games like Animal Well and the like we need more of. Genuine passion went into these by a small group of developers and are worth experiencing!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what happens when you take a bunch of good stuff and throw it in a blender. The fast, unrelenting, perfectionist inducing, loop of violence and general aesthetic offered by Hotline Miami, a hint of Katana Zero in comedic energy and visual flair, and finally, a WHOLE lot of Post Void. (Later referred to as PV) The time mechanic, frantic gun play, and general structure are clearly heavily inspired by PV. I don't think this is any secret or something they're trying to hide either considering the most useless and bizarre upgrade from that game rears its ugly head here too, IYKYK. Just wanna preface by saying no shade to PV, it's a game I haven't finished and have only borrowed off a buddy for an hour or two but I had far more fun here and need to accentuate why that is. If you gotta choose, I'd grab this one but they're both good in their own right.  The reasons why I like MMJ more are mainly stemming from the inspirations I listed earlier, which i’ll discuss later, but the key piece here is the boot. The boot is the best part of this game.  I have an inkling that the developer's knew this considering sneakers are the primary reward. The dash in PV is pretty brief and doesn't have any invulnerability or damaging properties. This works well considering the level design is far more chaotic and difficult to navigate, enemies are built to slow you down and make the time mechanic more of a fear than an adrenaline booster. (At least from my experience and taking into account the more abstract and eerie art direction) I assumed this game would be the same so I spent half of the first floor just kinda tapping sprint for quick little boosts until I realized how you’re actually supposed to play. Now I need to break the thought here to establish something important. It was mentioned earlier in regards to PV, level design. To my knowledge the game is pretty much entirely randomly generated but no matter what the layout is with quick reactions no sidetracking or stuttering is required. The game rewards cooler, more difficult kills with more time. Headshots, nut shots, Doom Eternal style finishers (Made available by picking up items lying around), and most prominently, environmental kills. The way you’re supposed to dash is long strides gotten by holding the button. When you past the peak of your momentum, dash again. Continue this rhythm to make a mad dash towards the exit, mowing down anything in sight along the way. You can indulge in the boot with two methods: dashing into something or right clicking. Dashing into things automatically booting enemies really lets that rhythm cook. Most of the enemy placement is built to condition you into knowing when to shoot and when to boot. Environmentals nets you time, ammo in the clip, and a sweet, sweet dopamine hit. The coolest moments I’ve had in this game are times where I can look at a layout and not even think about an enemy in front of me. I can walk through a corridor knowing who I can just walk into and boot which just leaves nailing what I actually have to aim at. This type of decision making is only encouraged by a later enemy type that can’t be shot. You have to use a finisher or whip out the boot. The rest of the gameplay is solid. I like all of the weapons outside of the Plasma Rifle and MAC-10. Going through them, the swords are good. The main difference between the two from what I could decipher is that  is pure damage and  was able to freeze enemies. Freeze was good for beefier foes from a distance since all you needed was a nice boot to the head to take’em out after but I still preferred being able to just kill from range without needing to run over and finish the job. Biggest boon of swords is taking out locked doors and their upgrades being really solid. The shotgun gets all the positives of a sword from longer range but more tactful reloading is needed since the animation is pretty damn long. Pistol and Rifle are my favorites, putting them in the same category since I don’t have much of a preference between them. They’re the most satisfying to do well with,  The MAC-10 is the easiest weapon to use, it didn’t feel very satisfying no-braining my way through with it. It’s a good weapon and all and at a visceral level feels better after upgrading but still didn’t jive with what I like about the game. The Plasma Rifle slows you down. The game is about going fast so nah. It’s good and all but it’s just kind of a turn-off. If it was a normal boomer shooter I wouldn’t really have complaints about it at all but honestly I dunno why it’s here. The first time I used the railgun was the final boss. It’s fun, I kinda like it, but again it’s pretty slow. If you wanna get better at using the boot it’s a fun challenge though. There aren’t any specific upgrades or anything I feel inclined to talk about. Most of them are pretty good, some of them are kinda useless and I dunno why they exist, some of them are things I wish were there on default. They almost make me wish this game would get DLC to further flesh out the pool, maybe add a new weapon? Compound bow? Chainsaw? The soundtrack is good, not as good as the inspirations I listed earlier, but they’re all easy on the ear, lo-fi, synth bangers with some slick chip-tune tracks mingled in.  Final note on the soundtrack, just thought it was a neat reference, but the song “JankenPOW” sounded a lot like “” to me. Moving on, the visuals are pretty spectacular. There’s some iffy looking stuff in the later cutscenes and I guess I’m not a big fan of some of the voice acting but I like Jack and that’s all that really matters; considering he’s the only one you can’t mute or skip without turning voice volume off. From a surface level perspective that’s all I can criticize. When it comes to stuff I want to praise? Just look at it. The only thing I really wanna note here as a little extra praise is the subtitles. Assuming this is a neat little reference to older anime translations back in the 90’s some of the text just flat out isn’t what’s being said. Same general message, it’s not like Ghost Stories adlibbing, it’s just a little bit off here and there which was fun to notice. It was consistent enough I felt like it had to be an intended decision rather than a bunch of typos.Hopefully you’re convinced that it’s worth your time. One of the few times I’ve seen a game, thought it was cool, waited for launch day, and it was actually good.

What it is, is a fast-pace score based shooter with level randomisation. You end up at the bottom of the building and you are suppose to save the girl who got kidnapped. Twist is, you have only 10 seconds on the timer (more on lower difficulty) and as you kill enemies, you get some additional time - but be careful, getting hit takes the time away. If the timer reaches 0 - you die and return to the previous checkpoint. You get a checkpoint every 10 floors. Completing a floor allows you to pick an upgrade - at the end of a chapter, there is a boss. And that's pretty much it... and yet this game is just so fun to play. An despite what I consider to be a bit high of a price (in PLN at least), the experience was just so intensive with almost no padding anywhere, that I have no problems but to recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: I had a seizure/10I played the Demo and had a lot of fun with it.The gameplay is pretty simply in and of itself. Move forward (with branching paths and shortcuts etc) and kill stuff to refill your life.What had me like the demo so much was the overall quality in presentation.When the game launched, i was at first put off a bit from the quite steep price compared to, for example, Post Void, a game i also enjoyed enough to play through.But then i thought that i liked the demo enough to anticipate the release, looking forward to play more and deeper into the content, so i still gave it a shot.After only 5 minutes i felt the price was worth it.The quality in all areas is top notch. It oozes details and style. But its not just glamour and bling covering up hollow gameplay.It really lives everything it does. It comes with Anime Cutscenes, Synth Pop/Electronic Music and fun, detailed and interesting visual presentation.It doesnt bombard you with pointless effects and lighting to trick you believing its an active game, it places all the effects and details in a way they make sense being there.This is also true for the gameplay.The game offers about 8 or so difficulties, including a permadeath mode, something i wish more games would have (looking at you Amid Evil), as it motivates me to replay once im beyond normal mode (im a pleb).Even if i never manage to beat it.The gameplay itself is deep. You "climb" 10 stages of killing robot dudes. After each stage you get to choose an upgrade, which is a new weapon or an upgrade, adding more time, allowing better combos to gain more time, or more ammo in your magazine etc.The clue here is, which is why i think its great, you can specialize or go broad.I started with a 25% larger magazine and went up to 75% during my first run.But i could also have added other stuff for better combos.Theres also style upgrades, like an upgrade that your protagonist does oneliners.Ending a run, allows you to pick one permanent upgrade (like keeping the last stage upgrade for the next run or adding lvl2 weapons).So theres enough depth and replayability from that alone.The gunplay also is varied, having melee, dash, kick, environmental damage and headshotting.The game features several chapters.I can fully recommend it, at this price, its incredible.It convinced me after just 10 minutes that this is worth the price.Its not just Post Void, its a far more expansive Post Void with 500% increased production value, style and quality.Its a bit less of a drug experience asking you what you do with your lifetime and a bit more content rich.Still questioning my life choices, but with more stable mentality.

name: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions
detailed_description: Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a gamified focus tool, set to a soothing lofi soundtrack. Discover and collect Spirits, customize your cozy virtual space, and facilitate your real-life tasks with a collection of handy features designed to improve concentration and ease stress. CHILL LOFI BEATS AND SOUNDS Soft, soothing lofi music and dynamic soundscapes such as pattering rain and crackling fire provide the perfect background ambiance to relieve stress and unwind. All music in game is courtesy of Homework Radio and fully stream-friendly, perfect for featuring on youtube or twitch as a pleasing background. SHOW OFF YOUR STYLE Customize both your character and your bedroom to suit your mood, selecting from a multitude of fashion, hairstyle, color, and room decor options. From hoodies to horns, bookshelves to boba teas, fairy lights to fireplaces, there’s dozens of options available for you to flex your unique personality and style. ADORABLE SPIRIT COMPANIONS Explore different combinations of room activities, soundscapes, and decor options to lure out the mischievous Spirits that populate the world. Discover and collect them as you focus on your tasks. You'll never be alone with a Spirit companion by your side. And yes, every Spirit can be petted too! BEGIN YOUR PRODUCTIVITY JOURNEY Utilize built-in productivity tools, including a to-do list for organization, a pomodoro timer for focused work sessions, and a habit tracker and journal to foster a healthy routine. Earn XP for practicing good habits, unlocking more goodies over time - from new character & room cosmetics, to hints to help discover more Spirits, being productive has never been so rewarding! KEY FEATURES Listen along to a carefully curated catalog of chill lofi beats, with a selection of themed playlists for every mood and occasion; Stay organized using integrated productivity tools, including a to-do list, pomodoro timer, habit tracker and journal; Create your own avatar. Choose from a variety of hairstyles, outfits, color options, and more to bring to life your own unique Spirit City persona; Spruce up your room to design your ideal cozy retreat, swapping between different wallpapers, flooring, furniture and wall decor; Immerse yourself with interactive soundscapes that change the world in real-time to suit your preferred vibe, from the pitter-patter of rain on a window to the crackling of a toasty fireplace; Decipher hints to lure curious spirits out into the open with the right combination of game settings, unlocking them as your future companions; Earn XP and level up over time, and by using the game’s features to their fullest. Unlock new cosmetics and customization choices as you progress; Stream your sessions worry-free thanks to the game’s fully stream-friendly music library - perfect for co-working streams or as a background on Twitch or Youtube; Expand your song catalog with the built-in web player, providing even more options for the musically adventurous; Enhance your everyday activities. Spirit City: Lofi Sessions offers a pleasing and distraction-free space for you to better enjoy and concentrate on your work and hobbies.
