_childDocuments_.review: Massive improvement over the original game in almost every way. You can tell the devs listened to the feedback of the first game and trimmed the stuff that didn't work while improving on what did work. Blasphemous 2 is how to do a sequel right.I've read some people saying the game is too easy compared to the first. IMO Blasphemous 2 strikes the right balance of 'medium' difficulty for a game of this genre. Most bosses didn't take me more than 5-10 tries to beat and each have visible tells in their animations to let you know how to dodge or counter them. This was fine, as they were still fun to fight and no boss really stood out to me as being bad.Platforming is way, way, way, improved thankfully. There's no more touching the sides of a ledge during a jump and clipping through it. They also removed a lot of the insta death spike sections so when you fall you teleport back to the ledge and lose a fraction of your health. Platforming feels precise and snappy now.Pixel art and music are gorgeous.They also removed the opaque and esoteric relic hunting of the first game. The first game felt like hunting for those relics was just meant to softlock you out of the 2nd half of the game to needlessly pad the game time out but that's no longer the case. You find everything you need to progress much more fluidly by just exploring the world and playing the game.Overall Blasphemous 2 is a very solid addition for Metroidvania fans. 8.7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing sequel, a true successor. Its exactly what a sequel should be, familiar concept but with a new way to play which in turn makes this game have an identity of its own.Blasphemous 2 Keeps the core concept of the first entry and adds new additions to make the gameplay different and fresh. In this game, you get to wield 3 different weapon types instead of sticking to one with each having their own upgrade tree. These weapons are also used for traversing the map and accessing certain hidden areas. Its very neat because in the beginning of the game they allow you to pick one of the 3 and depending on what you decide, it will alter what hidden areas you can access first to get certain collectibles. There are also wooden statues called Altarpieces which give you different bonuses for each weapon as well as bonuses for other stats such as your prayers and even dodging. Depending on how you combine them, they can have the potential of giving you big bonuses that can aid you in combat or traversing the world. The story was just as good as the first one and the theme of Catholicism is ever so present with its harsh tones and brutal story telling, reading the lore of items always felt like I was reading passages from an old time bible. The pixel art is still as beautiful as ever perfectly captivating the whole theme and atmosphere of the game. The map is fun to traverse just as the first one and is also much bigger. There are also new items that you need to find for side quest that test your awareness of hidden walls. This game is HARD, much harder than the first one, I had much more difficulty playing this game then I ever did playing Blasphemous 1. The bosses are extremely fun to fight with some really good ideas but they were so difficult to the point that I spent 4 hours to just beat one specific boss I had a few issues with the game however. There are new enemies that were introduced in the game but I felt like the first game had more variety, some enemies in this game were recolors of others that you previously fought but with a different element or a stronger version of the original, if anything they should of brought back more enemies from the first game since it felt like there were less. I always loved the executions, but in this game it feels like it was half baked. Blasphemous 1 had many different animations for executions with variety depending on the enemy you killed. In this game it was almost always the same animations no matter the enemy with the only exceptions being the old enemies you fight that already had execution animations from the previous entry and only about a handful of new ones (literally a handful, I cant recall more than 5 new animations). What happened? Did they run out of time? Or will it come in later updates? Some parts of the map lacked variety. I feel like some areas looked very similar to one another and didn't have a lot of differences to tell them apart. The same goes for the music, for the most part it was alright but a lot of the tracks felt like they were exactly the same as the others. It was hard to tell if an area had a repeating song or if it was a new one. There is a weird difficulty balance going on with the game. As I stated, this game is much harder than the first one and this is mostly apparent with bosses. You would fight a relatively tough boss for it to be followed by an incredibly difficult almost impossible boss to then go back to just a relatively difficult boss. One specific boss didn't even have patterns, it was random on its actions which makes predictability and learning somewhat useless. I don't mind a challenge but I just think the balancing was a little off. There is more things to collect in the map but this also felt a little lackluster and that has more to do with how interesting the items were . A lot of the times you would collect marks which are used for upgrading your weapon and thats fine and all, but it was sort of disappointing finding something and it contained a mark when you get them by defeating bosses or killing enemies. It was made worse when you find these golden goblets because all that gave you was Tears of atonement or a mark. Overall underwhelming and I feel like the first game had better, more interesting things to find. Which is another complaint of mine, The first game had interesting locations and easter eggs, this one didn't have any of that but that could be due to the lack of updates since from what I understand everything in the first game was added post launch so maybe we just have to wait, hopefully. My last gripe, is the animated cut-scenes. They weren't terrible, for the most part they looked fine but the first game had Animated Pixel Art as the cut-scenes and that gave the game so much character. They were all replaced by standard animations and to be honest that was huge downgrade. Despite everything I really enjoyed the game. There isn't a lot of games out there that tackle themes of Catholicism and execute it so well. The game is made by people that know their stuff and want to deliver a fun and challenging game with a brutal story. I love this game as much as the first and this game is different enough for me to enjoy them both in their own merit. If you were a fan of the first game I highly recommend you play the second and if you never played Blasphemous I strongly recommend this franchise to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 triumphs in what it sets on to be: Blasphemous but better. From gameplay to variety on play styles, level design and soundtrack, it one ups its predecessor. However, something from the OG was lost in translation and the atmosphere of this game, while not inferior, is indeed different.  Personally, my experience with Blasphemous 2 has been wonderful (outside some day one bugs that still remain, but i know the devs will surely fix em with updates), and i look optimistically forward to what the DLCs will offer.The good: The increase in budget shows. Its a beautiful game through and through, with lots of fun to be hadThe bad: In the technical aspect, it remains with some of the clunk and bugs blasphemous 1 suffered of tooLost in action: No more skins like in the OG :(

_childDocuments_.review: A Very Solid sequel with enough to offer! They also serve a purpose in the world so you'll often switch. Speaking of which, Switching is responsive which is a plus because they'll be some platforming involved so its important! One thing I don't like is how a lot of things weren't as "open" as the first. To me i felt that there was a bit of "hand holding" or other things locked behind story progress where you HAD to go to one area to open up another and get power ups and such to back track and find other things. Also the final boss seemed a bit lackluster, especially due to the other boss before it being such a pain. Other than that - I'd say its worth a try, if you've played the first one, You'd enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of graphics and overall fidelity, this is a notable improvement over the original.But in terms of world/story/characters/plot, Blasphemous 2 falls sort of it's predecessor. I'd go so far as to say this feels like the main team didn't have any ideas for a sequel, so they handed it off to a new group.The new weapons add verity, but the one handed sword is still the best due to block and parry windows. In fact, the mace can't parry at all. So even with the extra range I found myself almost never using it.Several animations have been missing since launch. I've been caught in the floor, and had an enemy get knocked off screen that couldn't return. Both incidents requiring me to quit and re-load.And this might be more personal, but if you're going to add a time stop power to your game please make the rules consistent. In short, works on everyone including bosses, but won't stop projectiles even from regular enemies. If the enemy is mostly done the animation, it will still launch the projectile. Sometimes stopped enemies won't hurt you when you touch them, and sometimes they do.Overall, I'd recommend the first one over the second.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same, which is initially enough, but as this drags on, it becomes clear that it's all very phoned in.There just doesn't seem to be much to it. The game's size seems comparable to the original base game, but a lot of the map traversal seems trivial. The game holds your hand so much more than the first, even telling you exactly where you need to go at all times, which completely kills that Metroidvania sense of adventure. Backtracking seems kinda bleh, as while upgrading your flasks is worth it, it doesn't feel like much of a reward overall. Tears of Atonement come in abundance and there's little to purchase with them.Outside that, there's QoL changes in some aspects like easy warping, but they still kept major annoyances from the first game, like the grief system, where you lose max fervor, which basically renders your major spells uncastable, and all this achieves is constantly making you warp back and forth to the NPC that wipes it. Vague, ridiculously named items return, attached to NPC quests and vendors, none of which feel all that rewarding, except this time they are actually spelled out rather obviously in the lore descriptions. Chokepoint enemy battles return to a major degree, inflating the game's playtime because there's just not enough meaningful encounters in this game. The boss battles all have very annoying unskippable intros, incredibly egregious for the later boss battles requiring multiple tries.Speaking of which, the bosses... are interesting in a design aspect, but they're all ridiculously easy, mostly because of the games 3 weapon system and upgrades. If you just beeline the one weapon, you are mostly too powerful for these bosses.Until you're not, which leads me to the finale of this game and the Eviterno boss. Straight up, whoever designed this nonsense should be fired. It's like putting an Armored Core 6 boss into DS2. Striaght up, unadulterated, nonsense.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent. Fantastic metroidvania. A little better than the first Blasphemous, but both are worth your time. I may even re-play the first having beaten this one.Movement is a bit more fluid, so getting around feels better. You get to pick your starting weapons which will change the early game a lot. Later you will get the other 2. Each weapon interacts with a different environmental obstacle so you may even start exploring a totally different area. I started with the fencing gear but every late game boss I fought using the censor.Mark your map up or you will forget stuff. There is also an emphasis on sound cues. There is a very difficult side quest spotting secret marks and using a specific prayer. It's not a big deal if you miss them as it only gives money, but completionists beware. I only spotted 2 myself after I learned about them. They are well hidden in plain sight, and of various sizes.The second ending requires sidequesting along with a bit of a riddle but isn't too much extra especially if you are marking everything you couldn't get and hitting every wall.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review after getting every single achievement like I did on blasphemous 1, I wish steam had a neutral option for reviews because compared to blasphemous 1 this game lacks a lot in, yes the new movement is awesome and a great addition. The good:The first half of the game is magical and really gets you hooked, the environments are beautiful and the music is better than in the first game. The addition of new weapons allow for a slight difference in playstyle that can offer a bit more variety. They removed relics which I think was a good idea since you don't have to go into the menus to swap everytime which is good. To finish, the map is much more interactive and fun to explore and well connected together with more portals for faster travelsTHE BAD:lot of reused enemies and attacks which can be understandable from a lore perspective but from a game perspective it gets repetitive, the new weapons have lacking movesets and don't really become interesting until you pump some upgrades in. The second have of the game felt more tedious than anything and the bosses have been mediocre and even felt like early game bosses. This game also lacks what blasphemous 1 had like NG+ which is a huge part of games like these, they also removed skins and backgrounds in the menu which is really weird because they already know how to code it from the first game. With all this and the game costing $40 I think people should wait for it to be around $20 for it to feel worth it, it's still a really good game but I don't know if I can recommend it for this price.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this far too difficult for the wrong reasons.  Common enemies take off large chunks of your health with one hit, there's no easy way to heal outside of consumables (a la Estus in Dark Souls, so no way to refill without checkpoints).  Avoiding being hit is usually reflex based - so dodging or parrying.Bosses and enemies frequently stun-lock you, so a single mistimed parry means death.  You can't 'dodge' or avoid future attacks because the enemy can do AOE's, or other enemies join in so you're stuck in a lose / lose situation due to not being perfect at parrying.There is no block button, so it's all about having perfect reflexes.   I'm probably too old for this.There are punishment mechanics for dying - so the game becomes harder the more you are having a tough time.  Eventually this completely removes your ability to cast spells.  I absolutely hate mechanics that make the game harder for those struggling.You can remove the 'punishment mechanic' by going to town and spending your currency.  The problem is in two parts: if you're stuck you can't get back to town, and rather than spending your currency to improve you're spending to get back to 'normal'.  I.e. the game is permanently harder, creating a negative gameplay loop.There is a spell to teleport you back to the main town to go and explore other areas, but you can't use it if you died too much on a boss fight since you have no mana left.  Effectively you need to "just git gud" or manually backtrack all the way through the levels again.Common enemies - even the tiny fast ones - take many hits to kill.  With the sword weapon (middle ground between fast daggers and slow mace) takes about a dozen hits for a trash mob.This game I imagine is for people who loved Sekiro over Dark Souls.  That's not me.  I platinumed Elden Ring, and I found Blasphemous far too punishing.My suggestions for improvement:- Remove the mechanic that makes the game tougher if you are dying too often.  I don't know what the devs were thinking but this is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just there to make the player feel like quitting- Tweak - or allow the user to tweak - enemy damage to the player- Tweak - or allow the user to tweak - DPS so common enemies aren't HP sponges- Look to a recovery mechanic - e.g. Hollow Knight's 'heal' button.  The alternative hear means killing yourself since there's no point trying to keep moving forward- Let users teleport from anywhere / add more teleport points like near bosses.  This would remove frustration of being 'stuck'

_childDocuments_.review: Just play the first one. This game is the first but worse in every way, it tries to innovate and it fails. The style is gone, the lay out of the world is generic and boring unlike the first and the combat, while more in depth here, falls flat because its incredibly inconstant. Seriously don't waste your money, its just blasphemous one but worse. The first game is great though, if you want a taste of blasphemous, play the original one.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed this game. It feels for the most part like the game that the developers wanted to make the first time around. Blasphemous 2 overall better than Blasphemous but it has it's own issues. The map to me feels less fleshed out than in the original game but I still had a fun time exploring it. There are also music and SFX bugs in the game. I think the best parts of this game are the multiple the weapons that you can upgrade, the combat, and the rewarding experience for exploring, to find lots of items to help you on your journey of penance. The art and cutscenes are beautiful like in the original and the item lore is very good. I do miss the gory imagery of the first game. This game feels a lot tamer than the original but I wouldn't consider that a negative. I look forward to the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game almost non-stop on switch when it first launched and I was amazed at the improvements: Multiple weapons, More enemy designs, more epic boss fights, fully voice acted, and incredible level design. Looking at the basically completed map at the end of the game put a smile on my face basically being an homage to Castlevania: SOTN excellent map. This game is a fantastic Metroidvania and it seemed to go unnoticed with the 2023 onslaught of games but this is up there with the best of them.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias out there. The combat system has been greatly improved compared to its predecessor. The presentation seems a little weaker but is still light years ahead of most other games in this genre. My biggest complaint would be the buggy quests in this game (same as the first one). I wasn't able to get some achievements and finish some side quests due to bugs in this game, which is a bit of a bummer.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good if you like the first one. Fantastic art and music. Still some audio bugs but not a big deal tbh. _childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best metroidvania games out there.The controls are improved in comparison to the first game. Controlling The Penitent One feels like a Castlevania game.There are more weapons this time, and they are all fun to use in combat, but they are also useful to solve puzzles and for map traversal.This time, all of your relics that give you abilities to traverse the map are equipped automatically.  There was no reason for them not to be turned on by default in the first game.Speaking of the map, it is huge, full of secrets, platforming challenges and puzzles. It is a joy to explore the map in this game. They nailed it 100%, and that's the most important thing you can do when developing a metroidvania: Make the map fun and interesting to explore.In the first half of the game you have a lot of freedom to decide where to go. Then it gets tighter a little, but still you can explore things on your own.I recommend disabling the objective markers, the enemy HP bars and damage numbers for better imersion. But that's a personal preference.

_childDocuments_.review: As a religion-nerd and a Dark Souls-nerd, this game was everything I could have asked for.  My only complaint is they ditched the pixel videos and went with cartoon videos.  I get that the new style allowed for greater detail, but I loved the old videos and was sad to see them go.  I also can't tell if I'm just gitting gud in my old age, but it seemed that, bosses aside, this game was somewhat trivially easy.  I think I died outside of a boss fight all of 3 times throughout.Anyway, 10/10, would keep playing these games forever.

_childDocuments_.review: Finish about 95% of the game after 18 hours. Got to say time well spent. It's a bit tedious finding all the small thing, especially for the ending A. The game isn't that hard if you spend some time gearing up. The finally boss is a bit of a let down in my opinion since the pattern is pretty much predictable. Would love to have a boss rush mode so I can enjoy fighting all the bosses all over again. All and all, pretty solid game just like the 1st.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game as the original was one of my favourites but I can't, especially not to anyone looking for more Blasphemous, this ain't it.The careful and deliberate level design and enemy placement of the first game is gone, enemies feel scattered around just to have them in mostly uninspired maps. This is worsened, and I assume was also caused by on the deign stage, by the fact you have all your generic metroidvania mobility options, such as double jumps, very early into the game. Whatever challenge might be there during exploration you can just skip by jumping over everything, hell even if you are hit, enemy damage is incredibly low with few exceptions and being hit in the air doesn't even flinch you anymore. The danger and thus need to understand your mechanics, the level structure and the enemy's abilities is completely gone.Now one thing that many complained about was the instakilling traps and I acknowledge being in the minority for liking them but not only were they removed, it's just much harder to even fall into them with the new movement options and there's checkpoints absolutely everywhere. There's no tension around failing at platforming, the consequences are basically nonexistant and there's no difficult platforming anymore.Finally the bosses... they're piss easy, a lot of them you can facetank trough for almost the entire fight, they deal really low damage, have very predictable easy to dodge attacks and leave giant windows of opportunities to just bash them.Most of these issues cannot be fixed by releasing dlcs, I hope if NG+ comes that at least manages to offer enough of a challenge to make me have to think about what i'm doing, what build i'm using, how to dodge and when to attack but that is not the case at the moment.In the end, if you want an ok metroidvania with incredible art, Blasphemous 2 is here for you but I imagine most people here came from the first game, this is a relatively generic metroidvania that has nothing that made the first special outside the gorgeous art, at least that's still there.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Insane work on story and lore. Really fun gameplay.Due to the soulslike and metroidvania genre, during the course of the game, you acquire abilities that enable you to reach areas you weren't able to reach in the first hand. So there is a lot of backtracking and searching for those areas to progress further involved, but it never feels tedious and always challenging and rewarding.The Game Kitchen have done a really good job!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable game! I did not enjoy the first game that much, not saying it was bad, it was ok. But Blasphemous 2 seems amazing. I'm glad you have more than one weapon and the combos and abilities are really well thought of. I just unlocked my 2nd weapon, only 4 hours into the game and I don't feel bored at all. The level designs are amazing (as were in the first one too), the enemies are great and finally the penitent one feels amazing too. Not too OP, and the enemies are not too OP either. So far, the game hasn't felt it was being unfair to me and its good to see devs working hard on making a game that is challenging but fair. That is not easy to achieve, so far I've only faced one boss, Orospina Lady Embroiderer and I think I died maybe twice or thrice against her before I memorized the pattern. All in all, the game feels amazing, and I can't wait to unlock more powerful combos and spells as I progress in the game! Definitely one of the best indie games this year. I play tested the last faith (it was only a demo) and well it was quite bland and boring to be honest. So, once again hats off to the devs for making a very engaging and fun to play metroidvania game!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed most of the game even though it was a bit more linear than the first game.(Maybe it felt more linear because of the markers) The bosses where the highlight of the game as I felt that the fights themselves were a massive improvement compared to bosses from the original game as all of the fights felt very clean with little to no cheap moves. Only issue was with the penultimate fight where the boss had two phases one which was very easy and the second being a massive jump in difficulty. Both of these fights I feel would be fine on their own but the combination of both of the fights made me feel like the fight as a whole lost a lot of quality because of this decision. I found that I had to get a lot of health upgrades which I did not previously need for previous fights as I felt i could learn the patterns quite fast with the other fights since you could always jump into the action and the boss would not change up a lot. When it came to learning the penultimate fight it became a cause of frustration because to get to the second part of the fight I would have to wait 1 minutes and 30 seconds just to be killed in like 10 seconds. It's not that the boss is unfair but it can be quite annoying to try to learn it since the fight is so long. The rest of the bosses were absolutely amazing and I thoroughly enjoyed the rest of them. Really happy with the inclusion of a double jump and air dash as it made movement feel a lot better than the first game and the diverse weapon choices was a great decision. I personally started with fencing swords but then transitioned into the normal sword later on as it felt the best to use in my opinion. Overall I would give this game an 8.5/10 I'm sure the developers may add further updates to the game that will increase the quality which may make some of my complaints obsolete but so be it. I would highly recommend this game for people wanting to get into the metriodvania genre as I feel as though it is a game that is easy to pick up compared to something like hollow knight where it is a little less linear.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked the first one, the second isn't gelling with me. It could be the occasional bugs, that the world feels less interesting, the new weapons, or just that I never played the "correct" ending from the original. One other reviewer called this one a very generic metroidvania and I'd agree.I'd recommend replaying the first one and doing all the content there over playing this one until patches are added.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I played the original Blasphemous but this sequel, Blasphemous 2 is a solid game. : This time around, you have three different weapons with their own skill trees for different abilities. I really had a lot of fun trying out the different weapons and each one seems to work better for certain situations. I really enjoyed the Ruego al alba which has mystic abilities and a very strong parry. Overall, the combat gets more entertaining as you upgrade your weapon abilities and it feels fluid. You also have prayers and quick verses along with your weapon combat. : You have a very large map to explore the world, lots of secrets in the game, and it is easy to travel around for the most part. This one is a more linear gameplay with showing the next area for your objective but you can still explore other parts of the map and find secrets, upgrades, other content, etc. : To start off, a lot of the bosses are not too hard and the enemies are fair to fight against. There is a big difficulty spike right halfway through around the sunken cathedral area. I personally had to scout for a lot of weapon, health, rosary, and fervor upgrades. I did not feel like it was a chore to scout out these upgrades as it was enjoyable to traverse through other areas and secrets. A lot of the boss fights were fun to fight against and it did not feel like there was artificial difficulty in the design. There was always a counter that would work against a boss. A lot of people say the 2nd to final boss is too hard but he is one of the 2 final bosses, what do you expect? It took a lot of tries but when you learn his moves and learn how to parry him, he becomes much more bearable. Overall, the enemies and combat feel good and the boss design is fun. They do re-use some of similar enemies from the original Blasphemous earlier on in the gameplay which was a little lackluster. The bosses are interesting and fun to fight against but I feel the original Blasphemous had more captivating and better designed bosses. Also, the final boss for Blasphemous 2 is a little dull difficulty wise : The story felt pretty engaging and it was enjoyable for the most part. I feel a bit disappointed they went with the animation in the cut scenes which felt a bit duller instead of the pixel art from the original game. With the bosses, there are cut scenes which are not skippable which does make for an annoying time. I'm not sure what bugs are in the game but I did encounter one that would not let me get all the lullabies I picked up for a quest along with being locked out of certain achievements if you did not grab certain items for npcs. : Blasphemous 2 is a good sequel to the original Blasphemous. There are some improvements to Blasphemous 2 while also the original Blasphemous performed other parts of the game design a lot better. I would highly recommend playing the original Blasphemous and then playing this sequel if you want a good souls-metroidvania game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: 2d platformer done right! It has been awhile since I have played a game as fun and creative as blasphemous 2, and it's an easy recommendation to anyone who enjoys metroid-vania style games. Only complaint is I wish it was longer! Got all achievements in just 23 hours, going back to the original blasphemous now.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: First Blasphemous was a far superior game in every way possible.Blasphemous 2 is full of bugs which some can  in the hopes that said bugs don't happen again. You have to find some hidden NPCs in order to unlock the true ending which they can bug out when you trigger the event and they disappear forever rendering your 100% run void (happened to me with one of the "Sisters"). Some other players have reported the same thing happening with Cherubs (the little angels). This bug crushed my soul as I was almost done with my first, complete playthrough. Some of my gripes:- The story in this game is a lot mindless mumbling of fancy words with terrible cohesion between events.- Almost all boss fights are hardly a challenge.- There's no NG+ like the first game.- The devs clearly cared more about launching a game title with "Blasphemous" more than they cared for an enjoyable, authentic story. Blasphemous was an absolute 10/10 for me, but Blasphemous 2 was maybe a  so I suggest you buy it on sale if truly interested.(As a side note, TGK programmers should probably take a crash course on unit and integration testing)
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game! Fixed a lot of the problems I had with the first one and was consistently fun up until near the end. I have not had this much fun with a game in a long while. Unfortunately the aesthetic is weaker than the first one especially earlier in the game. Most of the bosses are just guys rather than divine monstrosities which is both disappointing and less fun to play. This is brought to its unfortunate zenith in the penultimate boss who is not fun at all to fight and definitely left a bad taste in my mouth almost alone. The inclusion of different weapons and all the customization helps make up for it though.The maps are cool and the monstrosities are weird. All the areas are pretty fun except two moons which was pretty lame since it used recycled enemies and temperamental walls that reminded me of all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pixel stuff of the first one. One out of many though is pretty good.If you liked the first one, metroidvanias, catholic aesthetic, challenging games or weirdness you'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just left thinking "what happened?" everytime i pick this game up. User @TouchFluffyTale has a review up thats all you need to see about this game. This game feels hollow compared to the first one and how the collision damage mechanic made it to final release blows my mind. Youll run through a mundane environment to just collide with an enemy hitbox- take damage and get knocked back more often than not into another enemy so you take even more damage and knockback. Next ya know youre dead over collision mechanics, fun right? Zero incentive to memorize attack patterns, just spam magic/ranged and youre good every single time. It feels like ive seen all this game has to offer already and i only got my toes wet.. where as i couldnt stop playing the first one. Put like 5 or 6 play throughs, almost 100% the game and all. I hope this game gets to that point through ALOT of patching and enemy/combat rework because as of right now id say buy it if it goes up for 5-10 bucks when its on sale cause 30 is ridiculous
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is packed to the brim with great content that both metroidvania and souls-like fans are going to enjoy, saw a review about this missing the mark and being nothing like the first game but i just don't see it.The lore is easier to understand than the first game but not worse in any manner; the world and the atmosphere, which in the first installment were already great, have greatly improved since; the combat and platforming are outstanding, with 3 weapons to choose from with all of them being viable and unique in their own right; and the customization for your character being perhaps my favorite feature about the game. The rosary now is used to gain defensive stats or various utilities, while the offensive capabilities are moved to 2 different mechanics, one of which is the weapon upgrade system which has been overhauled and has become way more varied and fun while the other is a brand new system in which you can swap different stat boosts and offensive abilities that go in pair to forge exceptionally strong and unique combinations to play around with.This game is seriously so much fun and a great improvement over the first, with my only real complaints being the fact that almost every enemy hit knocks you straight on your ass making a few areas just tedious to get through and the number of enemy types and execution animations being a bit on the low end, but other than that i can't bring myself to think anything negative about this game, it's a great buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: More polished and streamlined than the first game, sometimes to its detriment (cutscenes are too cartoony compared to the grimy pixel aesthetics and some of the bosses are a bit too easy to predict). What I like most is the weapon choice and the traversal options they provide. The world also feels more alive thanks to NPCs and their simple quests. A solid sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Read the full review on Gameffine:Tl;dr-Blasphemous 2 is the perfect sequel fans could ever ask for. The sequel doubles down on everything Blasphemous is beloved for, and then proceeds to add a slew of new features. The result is a beautifully rendered action platformer with challenging combat, varied character builds, rewarding exploration, a plethora of side content and some great music. I would have liked to see more epic screen-filling boss fights, some post-campaign modes and reasonable regional pricing, but I guess the last wish is not up to the developer. Team17, if you’re reading this, fix your prices. Blasphemous 2 is a gem of a game otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. They've retained, for the most part, what made the original game such a good one, although the tone seems not quite as dark and disturbing as the previous entry. Combat feels much better than in the previous one.However, the game has had sound issues for players for at least the past six months, causing areas to lose background music, and even in some extreme cases, enemy attack sounds. Unfortunately this sound bug seems to negatively affect some of the weapons, causing them to get queued and playing even if you get up from a knock-down. Needless to say, this makes the game far harder during these segments, as you can't count on sound cues.And despite the Steam forums saying the issue is under investigation, nothing seems to have happened for the last six months. It is solely due to these sound issues and the team's apparent lack of interest in fixing the problem, that I am not recommending this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptionally good, with a number of notable improvements on the first game. Smooth platforming and great combat, a large variety of interesting items to gather and a very meaningful set of builds and play styles to pursue. The art and music are fantastic, although the boss designs aren't quite as great as the original. Don't listen to the naysayers, if you liked the first game, you will enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is similar to the first in being a Metroidvania but improves upon the last in almost every way. One of the complaints I had in the original was the upgrades not changing the movement or having minimal use and while sure it made it so you didn't need any to beat the game i prefer the sequel's approach, In which you can choose between 3 weapons a lightweight middleweight and heavyweight weapon. BUT each has more then just a unique move set they also act as a upgrade to solve puzzles and locked areas. for example the dual fencers weapon allows you to teleport in the direction a mirror statue is facing which make the upgrades more then the areas they lock like the air dash is multi-purposed, as movement and exploring. And once you made your choice of weapon the other 2 are scattered about to find later. one minor issue with this is depending on which weapon you chose decides which area you go 1st, 2nd and 3rd giving the game too much linearity. and not just the opening act as well! After all weapons have been obtained you still aren't given much agency as to explore you have a set path to go until the end of the game (similar like Metroid fusion). which while the level design hasn't changed to drastically between both i still think that is one of the leg ups the first has over 2.Man blasphemous 2 really isn't beating the ''easy boss'' allegations huh? yeah i hoped they'd be better and to give credit they are (they do more damage) Plus i died to them more. but i think it comes down to the easy boss patterns not truly utilizing the potential (hopefully if there is post launch content it will be improved). i do think the areas are amazing to explore with the immaculate pixel art they really outdid themselves plus the music is even better. the music is Blasphemous 1 was nothing like i had heard before in feel, but each track did kinda blend together in my head i couldn't tell you which music was from what area. Blasphemous two has a more varied soundtrack all the while not sounding out of place.In my original review I didn't touch on the story of the game (the lore is confusing) but comparing the two i would definitely say blasphemous is in a whole other ballpark with the Miracle and high wills story left me blown away with a plot I'd never seen before. with the High wills controlling the Miracle punishing people for doing good and the people wish for suffering. and the second is basically just the first but worse is every way with the miracle (free from the high wills) still making people suffer without a good reason. in blasphemous one seeing all the weird and quite frankly grotesque ways they change. and in 2 since most people don't believe in the Miracle after 1000 years it showing up feels random and that's because it is. The reason for is because some kid wanted the golden clouds to have a beating heart and now that heart has the son of the Miracle.  Not to mention the confraternity of the salt is pretty bland as well. Now for miscellaneous rapid fire points that didn't fit anywhere else. The wall climb is much better. Same with collectibles (the alter pieces and martyrdom marks). The economy is almost perfectly scaled except for the martyrdom points needed you will always be around 15 -20 needed before the game is over because the amount you can get from chests is not the full amount to unlock everything (they can also be gotten by grinding). the rosary beads just copy and pasted with a resistance of little, medium, and large for every damage type. they made hidden walls easier because you will hear whispers when there is one nearby but those are only for the sisters. It's dumb how one and I mean one of the cherubs is in a hidden wall none of the others are. when i played (it could be fixed when you read this) i sometimes got a bug where the music wouldn't play for an area or boss luckily it only happened twice. areas have more creative gimmicks. the weapons have skill trees. the enemies are not stun locked as much.I feel overall this game is better is most respects but I can't help but feel like something was lost along the way. As standalone game it also holds up well. But in spite of this i can't help but feel i had a more memorable time (not necessarily more fun) with blasphemous 1 mainly because I had no idea what to expect going in but as much as I try to be objective I can't deny my judgement is clouded still even so my final verdict is 9.1 Thank you for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is easily one of the best sequels I have played, and definitely one of the best Metroidvanias of the last few years. The Game Kitchen took all criticism that people had about the first game and then reworked most of those and fixed the problems. You have a clear goal and purpose from the beginning, the movement feels very smooth and responsive, the combat is engaging, the exploration and the world are interesting and easy to do due to a very good traveling system. Combining main weapons with exploration mechanics is nothing short of brilliant and refreshing for a genre that seems to repeat itself very often. The world is still dark, sad, and mysterious without being overly depressing. The music is fantastic and every track fits the areas in a very soothing way for the player, and the pixel art is simply breathtaking.Ultimately, I can only recommend this game to anyone interested in a good experience and a very well done video game. If you disliked the first game, you will really like this sequel, and if you (like me) also liked the first one, then you will probably fall in love with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun. Faster game play. Weapons and upgrade system is vast and easy to use. More Metroid than the last. This is going to be a hit, but I prefer the simpler weapon and game play in the first. I also prefer the atmosphere and music in the first, yet some levels with it's music in 2 are more jaw dropping and intense. I had to pause myself and stare at the screen to take it all in. The story isn't sucking me in. He returns to stop what was going to manifest after 1 was completed. It's a bit of an excuse to have The Penitent One return. The game is deep, but only after some time and upgrades. After playing at 56% on the map and getting the double jump, the game opened up enough to revisit areas and find loads and loads of stuff and connecting areas. The dash ability will render levels from annoying to suddenly easy. A win. Just don't like the "caged fights" while getting some items. Ugh! The cartoons too. Not my thing for this game. The artwork is beautiful enough not to use Saturday morning animation (looks like the Castlevania cartoon). I also find it very odd the penultimate boss is ridiculously stronger (took me 3 days until I learned I had a "time stop" prayer) and more difficult than the final boss (took me 20 minutes). I think that is the theme of the game, with the "dragon" being stronger. The ending was also a little abrupt. Great fun, but I might not come back to play the crap out of this like I did with Blasphemous.(edit) ...and the funny thing is that NOW I can't stop playing this on my more portable console. It's growing on me as the better of the two. Get the DLC because it will add a vast amount to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, just a lot harder than the first.Enemies can hurt you considerably easier and can even stun lock you. So if you are too close , they can just pin you against the wall by standing and kill you.The bosses are much harder than before and you need to develop a skill to win. I miss the Mea Culpa weapon, it was much easier to combo , here these skills are divided into three weapons.The art style has taken a different direction, the in game art is very well done and pretty, but the cinematic art feels anime like and not fitting for the game. Overall it's a good game, but I think it's a little quickly executed than the first.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I truly wanted to enjoy this game. The first one is one of my favorites, right up there with the greats like Hollow Knight. This one felt like either a very big DLC or a fan-made game using ripped off assets from the first.PROS:1. Combat is still good. Better, some might argue. The Mea Culpa is back (kinda) and still functions generally the same, along with two new weapons. One's faster and weaker, the other slower and stronger. Different weapons for different playstyles and enemies. I can respect that. 2. Platforming just IS better, not arguably better. The abilities you get in the second half of the game are automatically equipped instead of having to waste a slot in your rosary knot. I think that's how it worked in the first game, it's been a few months, I can't remember exactly.3. The environments are beautiful, and the pixelated art style is still very good. It still adds to the shock of watching an enemy turn into a puddle after an execution.CONS:1. Like I said in the beginning, this feels like a rip-off of the first game, or just a very lazy DLC. The executions were one of the best parts of the first game, because every enemy had a unique one. In this one, the enemies returning from the first game kept their execution animation and most (if not all) of the new enemies have a generic execution. It feels so lazy.2. The cutscenes. if you want to call them that, are completely unnecessary and out of place. They're jarringly HD in this pixelated game, don't serve any purpose besides showing you one thing that's different, and don't last any more than 5 seconds apiece. Compared to the style fitting cutscene in the first game where the Penitent One filled his helmet with blood and put it on, it just (again) feels so lazy.3. DS2 Scholar of the First Sin levels of mobs. They're EVERYWHERE all the time, and you're constantly having to dodge 2 or 3 attacks simultaneously. Not difficult in and of itself, but it makes attacks impossible to get in without taking 1/4th of your health.4. The bosses. This one is my biggest gripe. The bosses in the first game were AMAZING. Stunning to look at, just difficult enough, perfect ratio of "react accordingly" to "maybe memorize this attack pattern". Almost every boss in this one feels like you NEED to learn the attack pattern and you NEED to do it perfectly every time. I'm currently fighting the last boss, I'll update this when I beat it if that's possible. The final boss has 2 phases that I've seen so far (if there's a third, I won't do it), and they're both just some human sized dude, I'd honestly mistake him for a mob enemy if he didn't have named health bar. The first phase has 3 different attacks and they aren't bad to dodge. The second phase also has 3 (unless you count his string of attacks as separate, then he has 5), and every single one of them does at least half of my health bar EDIT: I just hadn't gotten past the halfway point in his second phase. ♥♥♥♥ this boss END EDIT. Even if I had more health, which I'm sure I missed at least one or two somewhere, they'd do at least a third. He puts them together so fast I can only get 2 swings in before I have to dodge and let him run his course. And he's a damage sponge like you wouldn't believe.And this isn't the only boss I've felt this way about. The salt conflagrant or whatever the Hell his name was feels exactly the same, and he just straight up summons mob spawns to annoy you during the fight. Svsona spent the entire fight flying, except when she would come to the ground and 2 shot you if you were too close. None of these fights feel well balanced and the victories never feel well earned. It's never "That was tough, but I'm glad I persevered" like in other souls games. It's always "that was unnecessarily difficult for no reason and I'm glad it's done just so I don't have to do it again."I truly want to love this game. If I'm missing something or doing something wrong, please let me know. As it stands though, this is one of the only games I would not recommend to people. If you liked the first one and are considering getting this one, please use this as a word of caution.FINAL EDIT (hopefully): So the boss I was talking about ended up not being the final boss, jokes on me. I changed up my play style and he was a little easier, maybe that was the play from the beginning. I still can't recommend it, which hurts me so much. I truly wanted this to be amazing. I'll probably still go for the 100% all achievements in the future just because I hate myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is what a sequel should look like to an already amazing first game.  Aside from the true ending Crisanta fight in the first game, the bosses and enemies are notably more difficult and intricate.  Still riddled with bugs, but not nearly as much/as badly as its predecessor.  Weapon variety made not only the combat so much more fulfilling, but also the way their attributes are utilizes in puzzles and secrets is sure to somehow give this game even more replay-ability than the first which I have poured 100 hours into.  The translation of only being able to use a few relics in the first game and now instead just having them as abilities, more unique skill trees for all weapons, the preference variety of combat strength provided by alterpieces- all of it helps to make this a great sequel.  Although the art and cutscenes were beautiful and higher quality and the story being solid- I do miss the pixel art from the first game and do think the story of the original was alot more in depth, interesting, sophisticated, and dark.  This game- while still having its fair share of violent/mature content- definitely also paled in comparison to the first game in terms of things like executions and the deeds of the miracle.  Overall great game, fantastic ending.  Probably one of the best metroidvanias of all time.  Also, please add a hard mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Blasphemous 1, 2 is more of the same. The most attractive new features are the new weapons system, which allows you to use several different movesets and abilities with a quick button press, and the improved movement abilities of the player character.While I do recommend Blasphemous 2, if you want to save yourself a headache, make sure to mark on your map every time you release a trapped cherub. Bizarrely, you need to release all 33 to obtain ending A, and the game does not hint where they are, or even mark the ones you've already gotten, putting you in a really rough spot.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Dare i say better than the first one!? This is a great edition to the blasphemous series, and i hope there are more to come! combat is amazing, with three options to pick from im loving all the spells and chants and finding all the hidden goodies is a good time as well. Very rewarding when i figure out/beat a Big Red Health Bar Boss! Really feels like a seamless transition from the first game !
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Newcomers to the series will probably love it, and Blasphemous 1 (B1) fans may like it a bit less. The common B1 fan perspective that the game is a bit casualized rings true for me.Combat: certainly improved coming from B1. Combat feels good, though the hitstun and knockback can feel dumb at times as you're bounced around. In general the combat is engaging enough. Problem is battles with normal enemies is pretty meh, and the game doesn't throw you into many situations where there's a lot going on, and there aren't unique sparsely-used enemies to keep it exciting. This is part of what made enemies in Symphony of the Night (SotN) so fun - the random crazy monster you only see once or a couple times in the whole castle. Most bosses are pretty fun, but there aren't enough and they're too easy. SotN also had more areas with tons of different enemies colliding and creating interesting clusters of action.Upgrades/metroidvania progression: There are endless NPCs you need to revist after you find x item, so you can get improved gear, health and etc. Cool, and almost required in games like this, but mostly they aren't exciting. There are a few fun spells to play with, but otherwise no improvements are exciting. Most of them are like "10% more damage", or "spells cost less". Again unlike SotN, none of them are exciting especially as you scan over the insane array of fun weapons items and spells to be found in SotN.Difficulty: Way easier than I expected. I may have to revisit B1 to be sure, but this game is easy. Only 1 boss in the whole game gave me trouble. Another boss took me a few tries. All the rest took 1-2 or so. This made me sad because in memory blasphemous 1 was much harsher and I actually had to try. In this, equipped properly, sometimes you can even just tank hits without thinking about it. If you're what I could consider an average gamer, it will probably be only slightly harder than described above.Aesthetic and cutscenes: This is where B1 fans are upset including myself. The art style has completely changed for B2 compared to B1, at least in the cutscenes. They now lack the raw brutish grit of the first game. Instead everything's sort of heavenly and angelic. The artist isn't doing a bad job, but I agree that the new style completely clashes with the gameplay's aesthetic and takes away from what really sold B1. These new cutscenes remove me from the grim world I was hoping for.Writing: The writing is similar enough, but maybe too extreme in its dialect. Maybe it's just my own crappy brain, but the writing is just unnecessarily difficult to read. Much of the time it takes several readings of a sentence to even know what they were trying to say because it's over-the-top wordy. Basically it seems like they should be writing poetry... not characters discussing something that may not be grand at all. Far too grandiose for my tastes and just makes the story annoying to follow sometimes. I like what they're doing but it goes too far to the point of being tiresome to translate.In general I'm a little disappointed because after being in awe of B1 I was expecting a masterpiece. The game is definitely pretty good, but I guess I was expecting too much.  Still, don't get me wrong, I had lots of fun playing. I just was hoping for a more faithful sequel. I haven't found a metroidvania as good as B2 in a long time and this is worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I have decided to change me initial review after having played and completed the game with both endings. I will leave the original review--of which was rated negative--below this review for anyone interested, as I do feel some of those criticisms are present. I think Blasphemous 2 is an absolutely wonderful game, as long as you don't compare it to its predecessor, the original Blasphemous. Blasphemous 2 keeps a lot of the original's elements, such as the metroidvania style of gameplay and the art design and direction, but loses a lot of other core components of the first game. Instead of following a linear upgrade path like the original, you stay at a relatively equal power level from start to finish, only unlocking minor damage boosts through allocating resources to get minor upgrades on weapons and using trinkets to empower specific tools more than others, which makes for a unique system where the starting enemies can be just as dangerous as they were when you first met them, even at the end of the game. On the discussion of weapons, there are 3 of them, each with a unique playstyle. However, I feel that in an attempt to make all weapons equally viable, they make windows for attack easy for even the heaviest weapon, resulting in a system that doesn't make the player rely on the different weapons available to them. I literally never used the rapier & dagger because I found its damage output inferior to the flail. Only on the second to last boss and one type of enemy did I ever even use the sword, and the spells in this game are also vastly superior to any melee weapon available, much like the first game. Upgrades to things like health and mana are relatively easy to find, requiring basic intuition and general exploration to find, with a couple items locked behind more difficult tasks and convoluted questlines, making them much more readily available than the first game, which I personally think is an improvement. Bile flasks are also notably less available in number, and are more coveted in the second game, which makes for a situation where the player is always persuaded to play more carefully with bosses and enemies, however Prie Dieus are much more numerous as a result. Areas do generally feel smaller and more easy to traverse, which is something I personally don't like, as the original game felt more large and daunting, but I could just be imagining things. Areas do tend to feel quite small and quick at times though. Traversal is easier as movement is generally improved from the first game, feeling more fluent and pleasant, and it is also more forgiving, with instant death obstacles like spikes now being completely nonlethal and only doing a small portion of the player's health. Movement upgrades are more linear and are simply added on as the game progresses, unlike the original where a lot of the movement items were locked behind exploration and sidequests, which I preferred more compared to the second game. It should also be noted that the art in this game is some of the best pixel art I've ever seen, and if it hasn't already won awards, it absolutely should with its beauty and depth. The cutscenes were good too, but I found them inferior to the first when portraying characters. When they show environments and scenery, the cutscenes were absolutely amazing to me though. Difficulty is a little controversial, but I found the game relatively easy to complete outside of a few examples. Bosses have consistent movesets with timings that can be quickly learned, making them feel fair, as they can be overcome with time and dedication. Some notable bosses for me included Orospina and Afilaor. I found the Odon fight at Sunken Cathedral to be outright unfair with how he spams his ability to spawn enemies, making the fight downright painful and unpleasant to do. Eviterno's second phase was difficult to learn and keep up with because of his sheer speed and sometimes hard to read patterns, but with enough time I did come to learn his behavior and moveset. I appreciate this game more now, but I do not feel like it is the kind of game I hoped it would be. It feels more like an attempt to mimic the first game while making itself more available to the general public, which I think was a poor move, as the majority of the audience is likely fans of the first game. It's an enjoyable and gun game, but I don't believe it should be held to an equal regard as the first unfortunately. I still recommend it to anybody interested, but don't come in with heavy-handed expectations for the sequel if you are a fan of the elements of the original. If you re interested in further information on my opinion, I highly recommend you read my previous review.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The following was my original review for the game:I will be honest, Blasphemous is one of, if not my favorite game of all time. I know my opinion differs from many others, and I don't think Blasphemous 2 is a bad game to any extent, but I just can't find myself enjoying it the same way I enjoyed the original. Blasphemous 2 feels 'off' in many ways compared to its predecessor. The new cinematics that are drawn in a smooth, clean, and almost cartoonish way are extremely different from the gritty, realistic pixel art cutscenes of the original game, which I feel gave the original a lot of flavor. The subtlety of Blasphemous' figures, lore, disturbing art, and religious portrayal feels like a miserable mockery of its former self, as if they were creating these--albeit impressive and amazing sprites--just for the sake of making weird designs. The same extends to the somewhat overly flamboyant dialogue, which feels complex for no viable reason other than to sound extravagant and mysterious--although that is just how I perceive it. Although, at least for the Spanish voice acting, which is what I played with, it was superb, however the dialogue remained convoluted. Another issue I felt was quite blatant was the apparent brevity of the areas within the game. Most of the areas feel dogpiled within the 2 and a half hours of the game I had played (I now have played around 6 and a half, and my opinion has not changed)--of which I feel I discovered around 7 of based off memory alone. The areas within Blasphemous 2 feel too short-lived to truly capture my attention and interest, as they passed so quickly, I could not fully enjoy their theming and enemies. On an unrelated note, if you are looking for the harsh, unforgiving, and extensive platforming that, I feel, helped the original game stand out a bit more, it is not as apparent in Blasphemous 2, and is much more lenient, with a greater focus on combat. It's a far different experience than the original Blasphemous, although it isn't necessarily a bad thing.Again, I'm a certain type of player, and I hold different values with this game than others. Don't let my comments dissuade you if you feel otherwise, and I encourage you to try this game for yourself if you truly want to, as it could be a positive and engaging experience if you don't emphasize what I've talked about in this review. I will likely continue to play the game, and i will update the review if I come to feel different about the game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The TLDR of my review: Honestly a great game. More of Blasphemous with some more mechanics, polish and story/lore progression. If you are interested in seeing any negatives that might turn you off check the bottom.Now the longer version:Having played and enjoyed the first one quite a bit I was excited to play the sequel. I can honestly say I am quite happy with it.I got the game and in around 20 hours I managed to 100% and get all achievements. This is something I don't usually do unless I really enjoy the game or the achievements are very simple and easy to get. I would say playing completely blind I managed to get map exploration to around 90-93% and achievements to around 80% or so. Finished up with some assistance from guides.Blasphemous 2 is a sequel some people might not enjoy as much as I did. The game in my opinion has done a decent job implementing and polishing up new mechanics in combat and movement, however it remains familiar to the first game. In my case I would say I am happy with that, same way I was happy with Remnant 2. For both games I enjoyed the original game and having a sequel that polishes some rough edges and provides more of the same is exactly what I wanted.Majority of my playtime was on my first save, exploring the world, combat and secrets. Around 23 minutes are on my second save speedrunning to get the speedrun related achievement. For people interested in specific parts I would split this review in a few parts: Combat, Movement, Exploration, Music and Story,First of: CombatThe combat of Blasphemous 2 I would describe as similar to the original with some more options. You are presented with 3 weapons from the get go and picking any one of them only locks you out of the other 2 until you find them while exploring. After you find them switching them happens with a press of a button and is instant, there are no mid change combos but switching being instant lets you play with whatever you want whenever you want. I would say the 3 weapons they went with are a safe but decent approach. You have a heavy flail, quite good range, highest stun chance, lowest attack speed and trading a parry option for the ability to ignite the flail for more damage. The next weapon are dual wielded rapier and dagger/shorter blade. This is the fastest option you have, trading per hit damage for lightning fast attack speed, parry option only if you perfect parry so you don't get knocked back and near zero stun(I might have been able to proc a stun on an enemy once with these weapons). The last option is the middle ground, a one handed sword that plays the closest to the original game, medium damage, medium attack speed, medium stun chance, a normal and a perfect parry option. The sword is the balanced option of the game and the one I used the most as it felt very familiar to the first game.Up next: MovementThe movement was very responsive and enjoyable. There is a good mix of abilities you acquire directly for your character and movement involving some of your weapons. In combat movement usually utilizes the character movement options for bosses and both character and weapon mechanics for combat rooms. All and all a solid movement system.Next: ExplorationI would say the game has pretty good exploration. A metroidvania after all the world is filled with locations you can discover early and return later to access with new abilities. The world is also very well connected and traversal is quite fast combining character movement, weapon movement and unlockable both static teleport points and checkpoint to checkpoint teleportation if you progress the collectibles and NPC quests. Running around felt fast and with enough places to teleport to if needed helped with not feeling lost or bored having to traverse the game.Up next: MusicSome people would turn off music and play with either their own music or no music/sound at all. For me music can add a lot to games. I would honestly say the music in this game is amazing. A lot of the zones have superb music tracks that I would sometimes just sit and listen to as they are very enjoyable. The music is composed in such a great way that I listen to  it even outside the game. Quiet places have serene music compositions allowing you to stop and enjoy the locations and combat and boss encounters have quite dynamic and hype tracks. A great soundtrack all around.Lastly: StoryThe story picks up right after the first game, however it seems there is a significant time gap between the events unfolding as indicated by some places and characters. The storytelling is well distributed between cutscenes, dialogue and of course the staple of soulslike and souls inspired games item descriptions. If you only sit and watch the cutscenes and character dialogue you would still be able to get the general idea of the story. Item descriptions build more of the world and its events. As a lot of the game is still vague you can draw your own conclusions on events and engage with the community in lore crafting and deciphering the meaning of different parts of the game. I quite enjoyed the story and I am happy with it in its initial version. The first game did get DLCs that expanded more of the lore and perhaps the same would happen here. I am eager to see if there is more.The final part would be any negatives or nitpicks that might be important for some people:The only parts I would deem as negative or lacking for some people would be some of the things I find as fine.The familiar feel to the first game, some people like me would see this as getting more of the thing you already liked, but I know some people look towards sequels for new and improved aspects in every department of the game so this is a warning for anyone who is expecting a completely different game. This is still Blasphemous, it feels close to the first game and more of what made the original great, for some it just might be too close.Difficulty - I would say personally I was ok with the difficulty of the game, however I can recognize that the game does have some pretty big spikes at a few points and overall you don't have the situation of feeling like a god cutting down everything and being unstoppable, enemies in later zones scale with you and remain threatening and some bosses do require a fair bit of concentration to get down and figure out. I know some people enjoy starting off weak and becoming near godlike in the end. Here you have your upgrades and you access more and more options but it's far from becoming a walk in the part even with upgrades. The game remains demanding and respects its difficulty and its players.Bugs - I encountered only 2 bugs in my 20 hours, both of which I would call minor and not really hard to fix. Both bugs just needed me to exit to the menu and load in again, taking just a couple of seconds to do and returning me to the last checkpoint so not losing more than a minute or two of progress. First bug was me somehow falling out of the map during one of the bosses. I am not sure how I managed to do it as I never managed to replicate it after that on the same boss or any other boss. The second bug I encountered was my character despawning, I was able to somewhat move and attack as I still heard the noises for it but the camera would not move. This bug happened while I was teleporting and alt tabbed the game. It might have been a bug with the game loading in assets while going in and out of focus, however this bug also happened only once and I couldn't get it to happen again even after alt tabbing a lot while loading. All and all nothing major or game breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've already played Blasphemous, this is an improvement over the original in pretty much every metric.Multiple weapons makes the combat more interesting, with each weapon having it's own gimmicks and style. The boss fights are much better, and for the most part feel more engaging than in the original game.Even if you haven't played the first Blasphemous, the story is pretty much standalone, so you won't lose out by jumping straight in with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I near 100 percented blasphemous 2 and blasphemous 1 so i have spent my fare share of time on each. This game is a wonderful improvement to the already amazing experience of the first game. The new mechanics in combat, movement, and upgrades kept a new feel to the game while not making itself overly complex. The art style, story, and world  are still similar in the first to where while its a new experience its familiar to the fans of the first game without forcing someone to play it to understand key concepts. The way this game utilizes platforming and puzzle solving with the three new weapons is something I really appreciated when playing as it kept me constantly thinking. It ads so much more depth to areas with the story being so intertwined where I always found myself immersed in what was going on. It is just as free to play around with as the first game if not more with the boss order, weapon selection, defensive items, and spells. Everything about the first game that was not spectacular was heavily improved on while keeping parts that already were amazing. Now the one grievance I have is with the boss fights in particular. I really enjoyed the first games boss fights but the second has left me a bit disappointed. I loved a few of the bosses in this game but overall I found them not on par with the first game. This is a bit of a stingy complaint seeing that no boss took me more than around 5 tries but I found some to be quite difficult in concept. Most just felt gimmicky. For example on boss you defeat one phase then a new phase starts a new boss, then the third phase makes you fight both at once. A few bosses are essentially just bullet hell and while these complaints are a bit stingy, I found myself even after beating some just thinking they were a bit unfun due to the sort of gimmicks they had. My only severe issue across the board that would be a caution is hit boxes. The hit boxes on some bosses are absolutely terrible. Lingering hit boxes were a severe issue where they would hit without me being able to approach or bosses would use a move once and then the hit box would move slightly left to the next time they used it. It felt random at times and some hits would stun me into another move and i would get one shot because of odd hit boxes. Apart from my personal complaint about boss design (which wouldn't be an issue for most people  from a mechanics perspective) this game is wonderful. The art, world, characters, story and everything is so wonderful and on par with the first that I just wish I could have found more love in the bosses during my own play through. Definitely recommend for fans of the first or the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A very worthy successor to blasphemous the first and I really enjoyed it. I would highly recommend for anyone who likes action games to pick it up. 9/10 Couldn't stop playing.If the devs read this at all I would suggest a tweak to when the player unlocks the ability to swap between presets for altarpieces at checkpoints to be much earlier maybe at 2 or 3 tools given to the sculptor so that the player can switch easier earlier on in a play-through. The differing weapons is very cool mechanically but often it felt like I wanted to stick to the one I had set my Altar up for and if I had setup for another weapon I still had to go to town to switch preset. The ability to swap the Altar pieces inside the presets could still be restricted to the sculptor until you have given him all the tools but I think being able to swap between presets at the checkpoint would encourage players to use more of the weapons/altar-pieces available to them. Up to you to decide if that is something you want them to do.
