_childDocuments_.review: The return of the Penitence was announced, and here we are again.Sequel obligated, things have both changed and stayed the same.The biggest highlight for me is the completely new weapon system, it makes mastering the combat harder because it is more complex with 3 whole different movesets and equipment types.But it's not too required either since as a whole the game is easier, especially with the flexibility in build crafting through icon synergy.While the game feels easier, that doesn't mean it is easy, and one boss(duo) made me really use different weapons during the battle.I wish it was more explored, but maybe it would've made the game way too hard in average, hopefully we get that as extra content updates! It terms of exploration, it's once again a huge improvement with no more painful inventory swapping of traversal abilities, most are inherent to the three weapons and we get extra movement options as a bonus!The start feels more open, but sadly the second act suffers from extreme linearity, I wonder if it was impossible to make it open and keep the balance.The areas had each their theming and feel, it was pleasant to wander around, especially with the better hazards that aren't instakill anymore.There is a stiffness in the combat and some moves which is familiar. Learning to tame the avatar is part of mastering the game.The death system is less punishing, but you'll frequently stay with a debuff for a while and best to clean it before bosses. I miss the more unique executions, they were great in 1, it felt a little something was missing here with most being generic.The menu UI controls suck, wish it was better configurable.The length is fairly equal to the first before all the post-game content updates, so hopefully we get more of those for prolonged value.Overall a very solid experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first metroidvania I have ever really played.  I dabbled in Metroid Dread before but didn't make it very far.  But I have to say, I truly enjoyed my time with Blasphemous 2.  The "weirdness" in the story and environments as well as the challenging but fair game play kept me engaged throughout.  I'm even thinking of trying another game in the genre now, maybe the first Blasphemous, Ori, or hell, maybe it's time to actually make a solid run at Dread.  :)Either way, if you have any interest at all in metroidvanias I really can't see how you can do much better than this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 elevates the fusion of Metroidvania and 2D Souls-like to new heights, refining the formula with quality of life enhancements and more formidable bosses. It’s akin to the evolution from Dark Souls 1 to Dark Souls 3, retaining the essence while enhancing the experience. Yet, the original Blasphemous, with its raw and unrefined journey, holds a special place in the hearts of many, much like the classic Dark Souls 1. And for those haunted by the Miryim Crystal, its absence is a welcome relief in this sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a "barely recommend". If you liked Blasphemous 1, you'll not like this as much, but still enjoy it. If you haven't played the games, this one being (generally) easier is a good entry point.Good stuff:• Graphics are still some of the best pixel art around; cutscenes much better especially with CRT filter• Platforming is much more interesting this time around• Two types of prayers at any one time are great• Superior customization options for the character• New control scheme takes getting used to, but is tighter than the first• Audio is much better than the first; sound effects really hitBad stuff:•Lots of glitches not present in the first game and still not fixed 4+ months post-launch. Game often crashes at launch, there can be a loss of control of the penitent one as the animation for igniting the hammer/bell fails to load; sometimes, you cannot smash through the people-barriers with the dive bomb attack until you reload, sfx can get caught in loops on boss fights, and most annoying: A persistent glitch in which guilt is not lost at all upon recovering your fragment still hasn't been fixed.• Imbalanced difficulty. Most of the game is substantially-easier than the first, but there are random spikes that are absurd.• Enemies are now bullet/sword sponges, generally. Enemies from B1 that went down in a few swings with even level 3 Mea Culpa now take 6+ hits, and there are not nearly as many weapon upgrades. Despite that, the game is easier, so it's just tedious.• Upgrading health, flasks and fervor is needlessly convoluted now and much more tedious to do.• The sword remains the most useful of the three weapons, and the other two border on useless save for traversal or specific enemies.• Weaker plot, by a lot• They got lazy on executions. In the first game, every enemy had a unique execution. In this one, most of them all get finished in the exact same way.• Although the graphics are better, it has an inferior overall aesthetic to the first game.• Spikes and pits aren't an instant death anymore -_-• Second half of the game is very linearIn a nutshell: If you liked the first game, you will still enjoy playing this one despite its issues, but unlike the first game (which I played through 4 times) this game will have to get some absolutely amazing DLC (and bug fixes!) to make you want to play it again after you beat it.It's just not as compelling as the first game, which I believe is the best metroidvania ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy sequel! Everything is improved when compared to the first game, except cut scenes :(This time it's really a complete metroidvania game.I want to see more content in the future like new game + and platforming challenges, etc. I hope the game kitchen keeps on adding value in this game just like the first one.And thanks for developing this game!Hope to see more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is targeted towards a broader audience, with a noticeable emphasis on accessibility. The gameplay has been made simpler, the storyline is clearer, quest markers assist in navigation, and characters communicate their needs more directly. While these changes are undoubtedly favorable for casual players, dedicated fans of the initial game (myself included) might find themselves a bit let down. Nevertheless, it remains an exceptional game well worth the investment. I can't help but feel a tad disappointed that the developers chose to prioritize wider appeal instead of staying true to the unique qualities that defined the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the first one, but more refined.It had fewer challenging bosses than the first one.Favorite one was the Big Guy in the rain. He was tanky, he hit like a truck, he was an exercise in patience.For those who did not play the first one, this game is a metroidvania/ dark souls like game with a dark religious theme. Dodging is important, especially from the start. The key difference is that this game has three types of weapons instead of one, the upgrade points for the weapons are limited and you will also need the same points for the altar slots. While I began the game with the mace which can't parry, but deals the most damage, while the game progressed I shifted to the sword. The daggers required to much skill from me. I Didn't really focus on spells outside boss battles. It gives you a lot of combat freedom.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game not too long ago, very fun. The combat feels just as good to me as it did in the first game. The campaign felt a bit easier to get through. I don't recall needing to pull up a guide to get through everything, whereas I believe I had to check a few times when playing the last game. They did away with the platforming challenges. Obviously they were optional in the last game, but I never found them to be compelling. As with the first game, the art is beautiful and horrific and the sound track fits the atmosphere? I really enjoyed the first game and find the second one hits that same itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really, REALLY liked the first game. The art style, the gameplay, how subjective and vague the lore was. But this game just feels so lackluster in a few of those components, like small unnecessary changes. I liked the difficulty scaling of the first game, it was difficult in some areas but it forced you to get better at certain mechanics like parrying or dodging. But there are so many enemies that have attacks that you cannot parry, and makes it feel like you have to cheese some fights by abusing a game mechanic or just spamming a single attack hopefully before your life hits zero.The next issue I had personally was the exploration and wondering what to do next in the sequence of the game. The first game didn't give much guidance, but the way the areas were set up make it easier to understand where to go next. Like you could just look and see you have an unexplored part of a region, or go a certain direction based on where you have already explored. Unfortunately, the second game I feel like drags on coming back to areas you've already explored to do a specific puzzle. It's fine coming back to one region to obtain a specific item, but doing it for the story just adds unnecessary time to gameplay. Every region has a good fraction of it you wont be able to access until way later, and it feels like every region was put together with the intention of coming back to it once you get something way later. I just wish it could be a little more direct on where to go next, or have the areas grow in difficulty in that regard once you have more items in your arsenal.These are very minor things that just proved to be consistently inconvenient for me personally. This is in no way is a bad game, I just found things to be inconvenient as it felt like some enemies or regions were specifically meant to slow the progress by an unreasonable amount. Wah wah skill issue. The changes to the gameplay were necessary like the weapon variation combined with the puzzles associated with a specific weapon. Was a fun change of thinking compared to the previous game with various enemies and platforming puzzles. The boss fights themselves were great, I personally loved how some had a second phase and changed their moveset slightly, it made the fights require a lot more attention to what was happening. The new change of scenery with slight reference to the previous game and figuring out the various mysteries in game proved to be more challenging than before which I am thankful for.I don't LOVE this game as much as I liked the first, but that being said Blasphemous 2 is still a good game. In my personal experience playing the game I found enough parts to be overly inconvenient and unnecessary. My personal views lean towards the thought that there could be a couple tweaks and fixes that updates could change in the future. Womp womp skill issue, its a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: An honorable sequel to a masterpiece that is the first game. The platforming and movement are improved. There are more Quick Verses, but Rosary Beads are boring (mostly just resistance stats). There is a plethora of enemies and the bossfights are as cool as they were in the first game. The art style is breathtaking as expected. Locations are very interesting and very well designed, but some are kind of underused, for example Basilica of Absent Faces. When I thought I've seen it all, you still manage to surprise me. I am not that fond of three weapons mostly because they are significantly less interesting than Mea Culpa. Overall, good game. I hate pre-ordering games, but this is a rare occasion where I did and I do not regret it a bit. Cannot wait for the DLCs, especially the new game+ one.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 takes everything great about the original, and provides a breath of life with fresh ideas, quality of life changes, and other improvements. This game is incredible, all of the bosses were fair but challenging, and the penultimate boss is an absolute blast. The weapon system combined with the altar was really fun to play around with. Highly recommend giving this a shot if you enjoy metroidvanias, souls-likes, or both (and even if you don't, I hate Dark Souls, but this game is amazing).Only one minor bug that I found (an animation sometimes didn't play when activating the Veredicto ability, so the character just stood still input locked, not like you would be able to move anyway even if the animation was playing).
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Looks about the same as the first game. Sword has an almost identical moveset, some of the enemies are exact copies. That's not encouraging.Got to a boss that required me to kill one enemy, then a second boss, then kill both at the same time.Now I really am not a fan of gank fights where I'm getting attacked by two people at once especially when one is firing ranged attacks at me while I'm trying to fight something else. Half the time I couldn't even see the little guy's attacks because the big guy's flame tornadoes were covering the screen. The hardest part of the fight was actually seeing what was hitting me at that point.What got my attention was the fact that even though I kept grabbing my body after each attempt my mana kept going down. Turns out the fight was getting harder every time I lost. I was losing mana and defense every death, body recovered or no. If I wanted to fix it, it cost me xp and a LONG ass trip back to town.Absolutely not a fan of that mechanic at all, I'm already losing to the boss why handicap me further and then charge me XP and time for my trouble? If you're going to copy the dark souls formula maybe actually take the time to understand why it works first.The best part was finally beating the boss and my reward was that my defense and mana were still gimped and I didn't even get something useful for my time. Dark Souls knew better than to do that, why don't these guys?
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna kiss every single person that worked on this game, just give them a big ol smooch on the lips. This rivals great metroidvanias like hollow knight and ori and on some aspects completely blows them out of the park.The devs clearly listened to every single complaint from the first game and fixed issues or improved mechanics significantly. More abilities, more areas, more enemies, more bosses. Bosses are actually challenging (the final boss is again a joke, but eh), enemies and areas are slightly less challenging, more responsive platforming sections - EVERYTHING IS BETTER.I love this ♥♥♥♥, man.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off this review by stating that I have not finished the game yet and that I am a fan of Blasphemous 1, this review is mainly for my friends and for anyone else who is thinking about purchasing this game. I also want to clarify that I like this game, and although I was terrible at the Blasphemous 1, I still wanted to give this one a shot, and came to like some of the things the game offered. I say this because this review is going to be mainly negative, so take this as clarification that it is not as if I have hatred towards this game.Into why I’m writing this review, Blasphemous 2 feels like it falls short when it comes to holding up to its predecessor, and feels as if the inclusion of so many things partially drowned the gameplay, especially when it came to exploration and fights. - It is much easier compared to Blasphemous 1, which can be felt when fighting the bosses and when exploring new areas. Bosses are much easier to read and feel much easier to kill (albeit many of them have the ability to two-shot you if you’re not careful), and getting to them is cakewalk. I found myself blitzing through area after area without realizing it, even when I felt as if I was taking my time. The game also feels more like it went down the route of being a Metroidvania instead of both that and a souls-like, as finding new things and running back was more common than finding fights worth your time and skill.- The story is less interesting than Blasphemous 1, and feels very weird to me - Executions felt lackluster in comparison to the first game, where many enemies have the same animation. This is a huge step down in comparison to the first game, as, if the enemy was different, it meant a different way to execute them. I find myself already getting bored of executions, and really only use it for free invincibility frames. This may not seem like a real complaint, but I was looking forward to the new executions, which is why it has its own paragraph.- (I’m not sure if I should spoil this or not but I will just for safety) This is more of a personal complaint than it is a real one, but the exclusion of skins in this game felt odd. In Blasphemous 1, I remember nearly starting all over again just so I can get a new skin. That, and this being its sequel, I expected there to be at least one variant, but sadly no. Of course, you don’t need a new skin for your character in order to play the game, it just felt odd coming from the first game to this without that being a thing.If anything, I’d say just buy Blasphemous 1 if you haven’t yet, and if you really want to try this one, get it for the new stuff they did add and to support the developers. But if you’re looking for story, its souls-like gameplay, or its enemies, I say to please look into a different game, as this may not feel worth your money.(A friend called this the “little brothers’ version of Blasphemous” when talking about it and I wanted to include it but didn’t know where to put it, but that sentence sums up part of the game, too.)
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it a lot, I don't know if I can compare it with its predecessor since I liked both with their differences, beautiful settings, very disturbing and interesting boss design, the mechanics of the new weapons are very fun, the only thing I can have a complaint It's the low level of difficulty, but for everything else, I would play it again. The wait was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: The final act of this game is a absolutely total mess. Not to say the final boss. The most unbalanced and ridiculous experience of gaming I've ever had. Seems that the devs had a deadline to deliver the game and could proper test it.Ishin Ashina of Sekiro should be an inspiration for them, but they decided to go to the Kazio Mario way. It's shame, the entire game was a very pleasant experience. It's a pity the dropped the ball in the finals.

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression is that this is a great game! If you liked Hollow Knight, you'll like this one. _childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: First one is better in pretty much every way, but that's largely subjective.Veredicto still has animation glitches to this day and the game has a myriad of audio bugs that have not been worked out. Solid upgrade in terms of combat choice, but at the cost of pretty much no executions (all a generic animation) and a very derivative / uninspired world/story.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game with both endings.The game is much better than the first one, the only criticism is that the animations don't fit in with the general atmosphere of the game. We also regret not seeing bosses as dreadful as in the first game, but that doesn't stop them from being mechanically interesting.Now do your duty, penitent one
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: It is a really good game with very good ost.There are some downs and bugs that at the moment are still not solved I think.You may get insta killed by some bosses even if you did not get hit.About the controls as I have played with a controller I can see that while using the sword it may attack up even if I did not hold up which is annoying as you try to hit the mob in front of you.I have also faced moments when I try to jump and the character will attack instead.There is damage on touch with the mobs which is really annoying and I am not the only one that will say that this should be removed or addressed in a way as some random mobs can pin you to a corner and kill you.I have also faced mobs that can give you more damage than some bosses, on this it is just me as I do not understand how is that possible.Now lets also talk about the good part.As this is the part 2 and I have played the first one I really like that they have added multiple weapons and more interesting abilities that will help you against bosses and some of these powers and abilities are really good against the strongest bosses.In comparison with 1 I would say this one tended to be easier if you have chosen to explore everything.Overall the game is good and got some flaws that can be solved.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first Blasphemous was actually better. Controls on this release are mostly unresponsive. Switching between weapons is extremely tedious(would have been better to use 3 seperate keys or buttons for each weapon to chose from). Exploration is just cursedly pointless and completely lackluster due to too many overpowering mobs and not being able to improve life gauge at all. When you jump and change direction to attack, you end up attacking the direction you're not even looking at. Sometimes when dodging without pressing anything you end up attacking when you had absolutely no intention to. So far I've managed to defeat the first major 3 bosses and still no way to unlock level 2 weapon upgrades. Most definitely do not enjoy fighting the small ninja mobs since they are they ones that most commonly kill me while im trying to swap weapons in an unresponsive button environment. When Collecting items cannot access pause menu or the map for at least 30 seconds due to being locked out of that function as well. Definitely not enjoying the game currently and it definitely needs work of improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: The scenario is a 10, the music is a 10 the bosses a 9.2 but the executions, the weapons rewards, the lore, the Crisanta dead, are lame, and it is sad because I was waiting for these game for so long, I cannot stop thinking that your goal was to reach a greater audience, and that's the reason why the violence is greatly reduce. I'll give it a final 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first Blasphemous is a soulslike classic and can be a bit too punishing at times. Blasphemous 2 trys to make everything better and succeeds for the most part. The game is more of a Metroidvania than a Soulslike which is really appriciated since most areas now feel more fun than tedious while still presenting a decent challenge. Best part: You really don't need to know anything about part 1, the whole story has been vague and ambigious anyways.

_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this all I have left to do is the final boss. My map is at 99%, I found every cherub, every prayer, upgrade etc. without a guide at 14 hours. 2 of those hours were trying to solve one part of a riddle because I was having a complete mental blockThe game is obviously fun, but it's extremely easy and falls into the pitfall of so many other modern metroidvanias, where all the backtracking is just for money or upgrades you wont use/need. This becomes apparent very early, so really the game is completely linear and after you get all 3 weapons and all 4 traversal skills, you go back to all the areas you marked on your map that needed some kind of movement in collectathon tedium. Don't bother going back until you have all the skills too because most backtracking items need 2 or more, so you'll just waste time if you don't wait. The devs give you every movement skill you need in the same area, so there's nothing like SotN where you had to search for the double jump in a separate area and go back.There were only 2 bosses I died more than twice at and as said before, I didn't even have my health upgrades until the end because they simply weren't needed. The original blasphemous had super easy bosses too but had the worst platforming in gaming on release (if you know, you know) so they improved movement, but didn't accommodate for it. The biggest challenge you'll have is hopping from a few mirror with one weapon, then ground slamming with another.The last gripe is that NPCs are not nearly as memorable as the first. The first game is worth playing just for the art and characters you meet, but they're much more mediocre this time around.I could recommend the game for under $15, but at full price it's really not worth it. Maybe when they add freeLC like in the first game and it has more meat it'll have more value
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Had a lot of fun with the first one, and I enjoyed the second just as much, and beat it just in time for the DLC to be coming out :)Don't speed run, take your time and just enjoy the game and all the areas and hidden areas, also found a little easter egg from the DEVS i really enjoyed! hopefully you;ll find it too.Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is an incredibly beautiful and atmospheric game. Frequently, I found myself just coming to a halt in an area and letting all of the atmosphere soak in. The backgrounds, each oozing character and style, the music, the subtle ambient sound effects... it all comes together to make a truly immersive experience, something which could finally fill the demon's souls ps3 edition shaped hole in my chest.And that is only the atmosphere - underneath is an incredibly fun combat system with more depth than the first instalment, fun bossfights and engaging puzzle platforming. Also, the amount of secrets and optional challenges to discover and master was very fun.Highly recommended to anyone who enjoyed the first game, souls fans and people who enjoy their games with a hefty dose of atmosphere!
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love when a game locks me in a room and spawns like 5 waves of enemies around me, giving me little to no space or time to dodge. I love being juggled around, taking damage because I had the audacity to be knocked back into another enemy. i love fighting enemies that take like a minute to kill because they have ten times more HP than you.Just play the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 1 remains one of my favorite games and I was excited to see what the Game Kitchen Delivered next.The sequel far exceeded the first and my expectations, by increasing the complexity and speed of combat and making the Platform and metroidvania elements FAR superior. The result is an engrossing, hard to put down experience that I blasted through in 3-4 sessions.The art work, as always makes the game as much a piece of art to be admired, as it is a fast paced combat heavy game. Astounding animations, bosses and environments mean this second journey to Custodia is even more exciting than the first. The music by Carlos is as stunning as always, and is one of the few game soundtracks I listen to while I'm working.What else is there to say? It's the iteration of an already amazing game. Better combat with more weapon options, and tying weapons to traversal options is absolutely genius. Cannot wait for future dlc
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias ever made, and my personal favourite. The combat flows perfectly, the world design is incredible. The lore is extremely complex and intriguing. This game never overstays its welcome, unlike many other games which run out of high quality content and cram in a bunch of filler to ensure that the game is long enough, Blasphemous 2 maintains its quality start to finish. 9.5/10, Blasphemous 2 is a masterpiece that anyone who enjoys metroidvanias should play.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a massive fan of the first game and have been for the past few years. So, when I say this game is an upgrade I mean it. There are tons of new mechanics that just make the gameplay so much smoother and the platforming much more enjoyable than the first. I highly recommend this game to anyone who is a big fan of Metroidvanias. You don't even have to play the first game. The only complaint I even have is that they actually animate cutscenes now instead of doing the cool pixelated cutscenes like they did in the first. The animations look sick don't get me wrong, I just prefer the old cutscene style. But that's really the only complaint. TL;DR: If you enjoy Metroidvanias (or even any Souls game) then I highly highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would rate this game neutral.  If there wasn't already a precedent that was far superior (i.e. Blasphemous I), then I might go as far to rate this positively, but since we already know what the series is capable of, this game was a disappointment overall.  The gore and graphical elements, as well as the atmosphere were heavily watered down.  The three weapons added for some interesting dynamics, but found myself only using the mace in most situations.  The Marks of Martyrdom were kinda....not very interesting, and the weapon development felt almost irrelevant.  Lots of backtracking until you can find the warping between save points.  Bosses were far less inspired, and overall character development was lacking.  Overall, I felt this experience to be relatively hollow compared to the first one.  Last boss kinda sucked the big one too.  I beat the game, got both endings, but don't really ever see myself returning back to this one for any reason to be honest.  I'd give it a 6/10. Maybe would be worth it at $15-$20 bucks maximum, but nothing more than that.  Just kinda overall disappointed with the game.  Sure, it was playable.  Sure, it was a typical metroidvania in every sense of the term.  But was it notable enough to recommend.  Not really.  Play it if you must, but know that you're not going to get nearly the type of experience you would expect out of this kinda game, given the original was so fresh and tasty.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a game I kinda didnt expect to happen. I love Blasphemous 1, and was exited when this game was announced. Overall this game was satisfying, but left me wanting a little bit more.Overall I think that 2 is the strictly "better" game. The world design and the gameplay are straight upgrades from 1, and in a metroidvania those are some of the most important factors. The biggest change here is that there is three different weapons, which all play completely differently, and interact with the world in unique was in regards to puzzles/platforming. This game also included a custom marker system in the map which I personally think should be a requirement in every metroidvania.I can't help but feel as if something is missing however. To start, I think the traditional animation cutscenes are a massive step down from the cutscenes in the first game, all thought the in game pixel art is still fantastic. I can't exactly place my finger on it, but something in the spirit of 1 feels missing here. Nothing was as strikingly grotesque in this game in my opinion, and while the lore was still in depth and interesting, it felt slightly too detached from the first game.I did have some issues with bugs, from sound effects and music completely cutting out, to some soft locks here and there, but nothing to ruin the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: PROS- Awesome new movement mechanics- Multiple weapons for different playstyles and situations- Altarpiece system- CONS- Replaced the pixel art cutscenes with anime-style ones- Too few enemy and execution animation variations- Too many arena fights- Story is too derivative of B1The game is great, despite not being a groundbreaking sequel. The Blasphemous atmosphere is ever-present, the music is still awesome and the dialogues are still individual pieces of twisted melancholic poetry. I hope they will release DLCs which will add more content and replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: A soulless cash grab from the studio too afraid to just make another title.A mechanically sound combat experience with excellent frame data and mobility.Both of these statements are true. If the developers had used literally any other world for this game I would love to have added it to my collection. Instead they relied on the name to make sales and ruined the beauty and depth of their own original masterwork.Everything from the writing to the animation feels cheap. Whoever was involved with fleshing out the world and it's qualities/horrors in the first, was not present for this one.The most accurate description of the difference in writing i can think of is thus.The first game was written by an older brother who's been through some serious struggles and overcome them.This one was written by his 8yo little brother prompting ChatGPT to generate everything without any adjustments.You can almost picture it, "I don't like that he doesn't have a name... There's achktually 3 miracles not 1..."The first games introduction was VISCERAL, a guy wearing an outfit matching the mountains of countless dead surrounding him has to kill a giant. then baptizes himself in it's blood by filling his helmet like a cup. That sends a very clear message as to what the player is getting themselves into. 2 is like the PG version in so many ways it's not even the same world. If you want to enjoy a new 2d hardcore metroidvania and you don't have any attachment to the world created by the first this game is gonna be a blast for you. But if you have any love for the first even just completing the introduction will make you wish you hadn't bought it.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a good game? No.Is this a bad game? Also no.What makes this game good? Well, the gameplay is solid, the pixel art is beautiful, and the soundtrack is very enjoyable. There's more metroidvania elements in Blasphemous 2 too, such as a wall jump and weapon abilities.What makes this game bad? The *story*, man. Everything that was great about the first game was just thrown out the window. This game starts off with an egregious mistake. Somehow... the Penitent One returned. This completely takes away from the gravity and satisfaction of the true ending of Blasphemous. When this game was first hinted, I was REALLY hoping you'd play as Crisanta. Her redemption in Blasphemous made her the obvious choice for the next protagonist. Nope. She dies in the opening scene. Wow. But maybe this won't be so bad... right? Nah, the world of Blasphemous 2 shares little to no resemblance to the intriguing and immersive world of Blasphemous. All the delightfully disturbing imagery of things such as trees and ash that was ubiquitous in Blasphemous are just... gone, the new weapons have no relevance to the plot like the Mea Culpa, the setting is nowhere near as interesting, and there are no meaningful side characters to interact with. The only consistent imagery I've seen in Blasphemous 2 is with hands, but giant hands aren't exactly disturbing like a humanoid goat skull tree monster.To put it in shorter terms, in Blasphemous, I really felt like I was experiencing an adventure in an immersive world. In Blasphemous 2, I'm just playing an action platformer with cool art.What a disappointment. This feels like a half-baked reboot rather than an actual sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed the game and gotten both endings, I feel like I'm in a better position to explain my feelings about this game, so I've decided to update my review.I don't have much to say about the gameplay. But, though I would generally agree that it's better than the first, I do have a few complaints: The new weapons are a gimmick. There was only one boss fight in which I found myself switching between weapons. It would've been better to either force the player to use only one of the weapons throughout the game (thus locking them to a certain play style), or to have a singular weapon that we could equip different skills to. Alas, these weapons turned out to be little more than glorified relics. That's not all. Thanks to these things, blocking as a game mechanic, while still there, has become rather unintuitive to the point I almost never used it. Fortunately (unfortunately), outside of a few boss fights, you don't need to block either: enemies have been declawed and most of your battles consist of being swarmed by them rather than focusing on a few, dangerous ones. You'll spend most of your time dodging instead. Overall it feels like combat has been dumbed down, not improved.Art wise, aside from the most obvious issue, which is the cutscenes (they're done in a completely different style to the rest of the game, breaking the immersion), the style has been maintained. The quality, however, has not. The drop is most noticeable in some character sprites, but it also affects the environments, many of which are uninspired and far too bright for the context in which they are supposed to exist. But these things aren't deal breakers for me. Perhaps the most problematic aspect about the art is the fact that there are no execution animations for most enemies, and I'm not sure why. Hopefully it's something that will be fixed eventually, unless they are trying to make the game into a family-friendly experience, for whatever bizarre reason.Something that DLC and patches unfortunately can't fix, though, is the writing. It's superficial at best.I was intrigued by the lore and characters in the first game. Yes, I did die hundreds of times on those stupid spikes and pits, but because I wanted to see more of it, I pulled through, and it always felt rewarding. There's no such thing in Blasphemous 2.The characters are all hollow. They seem to be in a rush to prove just how many big words they know, all with no meaning attached to them. A lot of your time will be wasted by long, overly pompous, pointless sentences that add nothing to the story. This disease has unfortunately also spread to the item descriptions, through which you get to know much of the lore. I read every single one of them religiously in the first game -- here, I just gave up mid game.Some people complained about giving the game a negative review with just a couple hours of play time. Well, let me tell you: even a few minutes of playing is enough to notice how the atmosphere is just... gone. Cvstodia is no longer a dark, twisted place -- the religious themes are toned down, characters are unidimensional, and the plot is just ridiculous. Even the weapons seem to lack any reason to exist, they're just given to you without any explanation. There is no reason to be attached to them like there was with the Mea Culpa. I'm baffled that they resurrected the Penitent One just to make him battle the League of Penitents™. They spent more time giving them cool designs than writing their characters.On the first game, you had a reason to do what you were doing. Your will and that of the Miracle both coincided. Here, anyone could have taken your place.I'm not sure what's gone wrong with the game, since it doesn't seem like anyone left the team. The writing however, is atrocious, and I find it suspicious that no one is credited for it like in the first game. Who wrote this? And why has there been such a change in direction?This game feels like it was made by someone who doesn't understand what made the first one so great. It's a mockery of it, like bad fan fiction.It's extremely depressing to see how nearly every positive review of it never even mentions the writing. I thought that was the soul of Blasphemous... it never occurred to me that I was in the minority.All that aside, that isn't to say that Blasphemous 2 is a bad game, it isn't. And if I had never played the first game, I wouldn't have disliked it so much. But I did play it.Sure, Blasphemous 1 was a flawed experience, but even so, all of its elements worked together in harmony. It was a work of art.Blasphemous 2... is just a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a terrible letdown in every aspect but menu graphics and menu navigation! The atmosphere of wonder and horror is gone, the writing is atrocious (where the first one was outright poetry!), the story pales into  nothingness compared to the first one; Enemy variety is nonexistent: you'll see recolored and reskinned enemies in every area, the best part is the usage of old enemies from part one but all new enemies are boring and terribly animated because of this and of the almost identical ruin backgrounds, that you forget in a day, each location looks and feels the same, whereas in the first Blasphemous you mostly will remember some areas and encounters forever!Music builds no tension and falls flat.The difficulty is laughable - there is no engagement on any level. Compare any frame of the first to any frame of the second and you will notice the difference: this one will not highten your imagination or mesmerize you with it's incarnations of the miracle like the first one did - and even if this is story related, it is no excuse to use all this lazy animated enemies with their poor framecount and a story so far from intersting as they did. Another worst part are the bosses which are amazingly uninteresting: mostly terribly animated human characters straight out of a saturday morning cartoon but even more uninteresting and bland.The violence, nudity and blasphemy is toned down too, the finishing moves are replaced with a catch all thorn animation which is the same for most enemies and covers the execution. It feels like cencorship or cowardice towards the epic store.Then this game gives you 20 or more rooms where you are locked in and have to fight THE SAME spawning waves of enemies till you succeed or die instead of mid bosses or anything interesting and due to the new weapon options and combat you can buttonmash through these encounters which is a shame compared to the first Blasphemous where every encounter had a trick or hint or interaction or pattern to learn. This is just a hollow shell, a shadow of greatness - maybe alll planned with future DLC's in mind, to spread the content - it is a shame and you should not listen to good reviews of this, they are objectively wrong or blindsighted - when playing BP 1 I had to stop and take photos every 5 minutes to show them to friends - I did not make a single photo this time and when I showed part 2 there was no reaction but silence. wWen I presented part one there was awe and joy and interest on the face of the people I showed it. And I am not alone with this experience - reddit and the community forum show the same experience with different people and a strange overly positive review culture that is absolutely not understandable!

_childDocuments_.review: Combat feels amazing in this one, multiple weapons really keeps it fresh I actually don't much care for light-heavy attack combos like the first game and prefer having less to think about and less wasted design space on combos I won't ever use. There are still a lot of eureka moments in this combat system, and the three bosses I've fought so far were fun to figure out once I figured out how to increase my health so I stopped dying in 3 hits. I'm 4 hours in and have all the level 1 upgrades in my preferred weapon and it's great. I did find out that I screwed myself out of a future health upgrade by giving two health upgrades to the health upgrader at once when I finally figured out what the chalices were for instead of arbitrarily sacrificing health in a cup in front of her in between them, which is the kind of goofy game design I remember from getting the true ending in the first game. Map is pretty good too, and I love the first three bosses so far. Definitely going to finish this one. Hope there's a New Game + down the line with the basics unlocked out of the gate.Quite a few flaws though. There's always a weapon that goes a looong time without use outside of platforming(Ruego for me), and there's a really annoying bug with activating Veredicto if you activate the flames while standing. I'd wait for an update before buying outright, I don't think it's really worth full price right now(though snap it up if on a large markdown). I got it as part of Humble Choice.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent follow-up to an awesome title, if I would have to put it in one sentence. But I will nerd out for a bit:For those expecting an equal or more challenge compared the first game, you guys might be slightly out of luck, as I think this is a step down in terms of Boss Difficulty. Take it from somebody who is bad at timing and probably have very slow reflexes -- this game is more forgiving. It won't be a breeze but I think it's easier to get the attack patterns down with this one. I'm not so sure of the quantity of boss fights but I think its a respectable amount considering the first game. Well that's about it for the things that I didn't like. Here are some of the things that I actually loved about the sequel:1. The inclusion of different weapons achieves a lot of things: (1) the selection of weapon varies the path you take on your journey, although pretty minor, (2) it introduces build variety unlike the first game, and (3) it adds the additional traversal challenge. On top of the usual movement upgrades, the three weapons layer in additional movement mechanics making exploration additionally challenging. It doesn't over-exaggerate on platforming challenge unlike the first game slapping on a DLC to repair a mirror. 2.  Speaking more on build variety, the altarpiece mechanic further provides ways to upgrade your preferred play style, including builds that reap off the Guilt System. 3. Quest design is more straight forward and there are few miss-able things unlike the first game. Luckily they aren't tide to any achievements. For trophy hunters going in blind, there is probably just one trophy that you might need a second run for -- too bad there isn't a new game plus yet. Quest design introduces some new mechanics but it also retains some of the familiar once such as Cherub Hunting, Combat Arenas, and such.4. Art and sound design remains superb, though I'm not exactly a fan of the cartoon animations the developers decided to go with here. I'm hoping that they add in those additional graphic upgrades that make the game even more retro.  Pretty excited for the DLC to drop, until then I will probably figure out a way to get that time trophy that I missed in my first run. This is a 9 out of 10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 1 is a weird little game. Is it a metroidvania? Of course. But... It's not got a great emphasis on upgrades, exploration is usually just health and it's clunky and has some jagged sharp edges. But a fantastic first effort imo.Blasphemous 2 is like the devs said 'ok guys, we learned literally every lesson, let's make an amazing sequel'. And they have.Combat? Fluid. It has a small issue or two (I don't like not being able to dodge with the flail if I'm attacking because it's damage does not make up for this)  but past that, having THREE weapons that all play wildly different, and their own skill tree AND unique ability for each... Plus something abilities wise for exploration which I'll get into later... It's good stuff.The npcs, the art, the music? As good as the original. Which is to say absolutely brutal and amazing. From wax filled towers to vistas of a huge lake with candle lit city behind it... From lady's who's faces are stone and matrichical skeletons. To brides in coffins and priest slugs breathing fire... It's great.The exploration? They learned SO much from the previous game. Not only is there a new thing to do on each map screen (or close to. A lot but not overwhelming) WITH your map letting you drop 8+ symbol types on most any square... You're constantly thinking 'oh hey I see a *thing I wanna do* and I can't reach/dodge/fly' up there. I better take a note of that' and the rewards for exploration are, 80%, amazing. Sure you'll get currency or upgrade points but most of the time it's good, important stuff. Items for quests, statutes for massive buffs, prayer beads for passive but substantial buffs... Or, and this is always my favorite, a brand new npc being tortured by the miracle in some gruesome way. Oh and each weapon has its own progression ability. From mirrors that teleport you to bells that reveal hidden platforms and fleshy wooden barriers (wood? Wax? Idk. It bleeds though...) each weapon has a unique ability. So replayability and even which path you take depends on the player. I could start with the sword and end up in the palace. Or I could start with the flail and end up in the sand tombs.... Or even way up in the sky, but not higher than the upper city, unseen but waiting for you to lower it) Overall, it's scratched the metroidvania itch in a way I forgot I needed. This is what I hope more metroidvanias do; refine refine refine. Uniqueness is fun, yeah. Having a weird movement ability or a wacky combat system is great... But if you don't have unique ideas? That's fine. Just make your systems really good. I don't care if I just unlock a double jump and a 'see the hidden platforms ability' in more games... Just make it so it's FUN using the abilities and exploring and combat. Make it good or make it unique.I wouldn't call blasphemous 2 unique. I'd say it's a lot of staple metroidvania abilities and such. But that's not a bad thing. It's a fantastic game and barring the final section being bad (which I'm just about at, I suspect) it's truly one of the greats of 2023, and it's been an INSANE year.Oh. Well. There are some cons. Mainly in a few bugs and a few enemy types stun locking you which is annoying. So... Not 10/10, but few games can be. 9/10, highly recommended for metroidvania fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a very solid sequel to the original game, and for the most part I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. It does of course have a few flaws, but I'll sing it's praises first. Artistically, Blasphemous 2 is gorgeous. The pixel art is so intricate and atmospheric, with every area being incredibly well defined in terms of color scheme, background art, and area design. Character design and animations are also excellent, each NPC is distinct and unique, which characterizes them very well and makes them memorable, which helps significantly when all of their names seem to be a paragraph long. The music was also very solid,  I really loved the background music in the Crown of Towers. Finally, gameplay wise, the actual exploration and combat were generally very, very satisfying. Without spoiling too much, each weapon is pretty well executed in terms of move set, and without too much effort it's pretty easy to make some really unique and interesting builds around the weapons. This makes combat encounters and bosses very satisfying to rip through, especially in conjunction with the brutal death animations. These tight and snappy attacks, coupled with world design chock-full of collectables and upgrades, makes the early-mid game very, very addicting. Unfortunately, the game begins to weaken in the late game, which is where I have a few gripes.For the most part the pacing of Blasphemous 2 is pretty solid, with proper routing it doesn't take long at all to start feeling very, very powerful. Unfortunately, by the late game, however, things stop feeling brutal but fair, and instead feel unjustly punishing. During my playtime I did my best to specialize with a certain weapon, upgrading it and utilizing the available collectable buffs, but by the end I found my damage output still quite underwhelming. Many enemies get really tanky near the end, and the "final area" in particular is deeply frustrating, with only a single save point in an obnoxiously long platforming/combat gauntlet. Additionally, the penultimate boss of the game is a massive step up in difficulty, with an enormous health pool, insane damage per hit, and very minimal windows for retaliation. Additionally, for whatever reason, the late game bosses don't skip their intro cutscenes on repeat attempts, so you have to sit and listen to him ramble before each and every fight. It ultimately really hurt the combat experience at the end, less so for the difficulty and moreso for how sluggish it felt to retry.I also had some gripes with the actual 100%ing experience, for the most part the collectables feel pretty good and are very rewarding. But at the end, when I was looking for ten hidden symbols throughout the world and grinding out the last three upgrade points for the last weapon upgrade, the grind set in and ended up bittering the once sweet taste of exploration. It's a more minor gripe since reaching 100% completion is not required, but the hidden symbols in particular were absolutely unfair without a guide.Ultimately, Blasphemous 2 is an excellent sequel to the first game, and while the experience is soured a bit by some genuinely unfair challenges at the end, it nonetheless is an overall very satisfying metroidvania experience. I'd give it an 8/10, only brought down by a few low points. If you loved the first game, Blasphemous 2 is absolutely a worthy sequel that you should be sure to pick up.(I do miss the skins and NG+ challenges though, hopefully they appear in a later update but I wish they'd shipped with the base game.)
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This review is being made on LAUNCH DAY VERSION. My comments, critiques, and praises may change down the line.Gamplay: 8/10. Feels more fluid than the first, feels more dynamic and free. The weapon variety is a very warm welcome that I really love. Only real issue I will proclaim is that certain enemies can stun lock you from full to dead, and practically all of them can do that if you are touching a wall due to how jank the collision damage is right now, but past that I am loving it so far.Music: 9/10. You definitely get the Blasphemous music vibe from the first. Different enough to enjoy the music differently, but similar enough to make it stand out among other games. It has it's own soundtrack theme that is hard to find work anywhere else and it's a pleasant experience.Graphics: 10/10. I have said it before to my friends with Blasphemous 1 that it is the golden standard for pixel art and animations in games, and they took that for this game and just gave that statement more evidence to support it. I've seen some people complain of the new art style for the cutscences being more of a catoon-y style rather than pixel, but I actually support this choice since the animation looks far better in this than their cutscenes in one. (SPOILERS FOR BLAS 1) The biggest point I have for this is in Blasphemous 1 how you have a cutscene killing the High Wills and the animation in pixel just looks...not good. So while others complain, I find the style change for the cutscenes welcome.Difficulty: 8/10. This is probably subject the change through time, but I find the game to have a good balance of difficulty, even if there are a few outliers of being a pushover or being a borderline nightmare. Not really much else to say other than it feels find so far and feels like a Blasphemous game.Bugs: I have found very very few bugs or glitches, but the few I found where not welcome. The one I found that was the most annoying and consistent is that if you are in hallway encounter and die, there is a 40-50% chance of not being able to recover your guilt fragment since it never drops one. This will be edited accordingly though.Overall: I recommend this game. I still would suggest waiting roughly 2 weeks or so just so that they can iron out the tiny wrinkles, bugs, and maybe balance changes. The only thing I pray they change is the contact damage issues of being infinite stunlocked if you are against a wall and not being able to save yourself. Outside of that, it's a great game that will be worth it when the patch iron is all hung up and finished.

You can fix this eventually though by closing and reopening the map once or twice until it’s right. The big issues is guilt. When you go back to where you died to pick up your guilt, it sometimes won’t remove the guilt on your fervor bar. This forces you to pay to have it removed. It’s been half and half for me. Works half the time and other half the time it doesn’t. Really should fix this soon or it seriously hampers gameplay. Other than that, I am really enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: As an ardent fan of the first game, there is something special missing from the opening hours of Blasphemous 2; something captivating and personal that made you want to see through your journey from start to finish almost immediately upon awakening as The Penitent One. In B2, you're resurrected for reasons, and with little fanfare, undoing the gravitas of the true ending of the original and undercutting the significance of the destruction of the Mea Culpa, your weapon from Blasphemous 1. In return, you get to hunt down three mediocre replacement weapons which serve a dual purpose in traversing the world, signaling more of an emphasis on platforming than combat. Narratively, the story is supposed to take place 1000 years after the first game, yet starting areas are full of several enemies lifted from it, with the same palettes and movesets. After about four hours it all just starts feels like more of the same. I think I'll wait for the inevitable DLC and final updates before jumping back into this one.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR --> Superior in almost every aspect from the first title; faster, more enjoyable to play, with a more varied world to explore, and skills & abilities that make more sense. All of what while being the brutal souls-like metroidvania you're expecting. -----------------------------------------Dear lord, I actually completed the game from start to finish in a single session. So much to recap but let's see.Blasphemous II is finally here, the sequel to the brutal souls-like metroidvania inspired by games of the genre, the Spanish Easter Week culture and many other art references that culminated into a dark, crude world where the designs of The Miracle are above all and everyone. This sequel follows the events of the first game (probably centuries later, maybe even more) and you take control of The Penitent, who silently journeys into a world still ruled by the sacred words and inevitable punishments.This game is basically superior on everything from the first title. So many lessons were learnt, and it shows. I will try to mention the most relevant ones for both newcomers and people who played the first game:- Visually, the game is equally stunning. While we say goodbye to pixel art cutscenes, the new ones are also very good and there are more of them. As for the rest of the game, expect many more varied areas, much more easily identifiable. For some people it might come as a handicap, though, as the game is a bit less dark that the previous game.- The soundtrack is super good too. It still catches on going along with the environment while having that Spanish touch into it. I can see myself burning the OST on Spotify in the following days.- Gameplay is where the game has seen the most changes, for the better. Blasphemous 1, while great to play, felt like Dark Souls 1 in terms of being heavy, stiff and slow. This sequel fixes every of that and offers you a much more fluid gameplay, with many more combat options, as well as easy-to-understand build systems while also keeping the mysterious aura on every item you collect. You can choose between 3 different weapons at the beginning of the journey, which will only matter temporally as you will unlock the rest while progressing through it. Everything just feels faster in the way that it makes sense.- Length of the game is very similar to B1. It took me around 11h to complete, with 98% map exploration. I am very experienced with the genre so I believe the average should be 14h or so, which is completely fine for a metroidvania.- Boss fights are, like in the first game, very good. Patterns are easy to recognize, and fights are fast and satisfying. While the new combat variety might make the game easier, it will still provide a decent amount of challenge.- Exploration is better than in B1, in the sense that it is clear what skill you might be missing in order to reach certain places, and there are also even sound clues in order to find secret paths. You won't escape the classic fake walls though, so there's a high chance you'll keep mashing lots of them.- Spike pits no longer instakill!! Screw that on metroidvanias.Overall, there is a reason why I beated the game in a single session. I just couldn't get enough of it. Every new area, every new NPC I interacted with, every new upcoming boss fight or sidequest, I just had to know where that led to. This is an amazingly faith sequel, with many lessons learnt from a game that was already excellent. Grab this without any fear because this penitence has been great once again.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to the first game.As a good sequel should, it adresses nearly every issue I had with Blasphemous, like annoying instant deaths and a hard to navigate menu, while keeping the gruesome aesthetic and gameplay difficulty in tact.This one will stand up there with the most beloved Metroidvanias!

_childDocuments_.review: Ever got a new SNES game, played it , loved it, forgot about it, then 2 years later, the game got a sequel ?U notice the sequel has the same DNA but the graphics got a boost, the main character especially got more animation, better use of color, a ton more variety in combat and just looks exactly how a sequel should be ?Well, this is blasphemous 2, it reminds me of when a good game came out on a 16 bit console, then got a sequel that made it look even better, think SONIC BLAST MAN 2 and ACTRAISER 2.And still, i can swear on my life, these guys played NOSFERATU on snes one day, and decided to make this, heck, even the enter the door animation is ripped right of that game.I just wish the devs admit it, they were inspired by NOSFERATU, and this is why, i want them to remake NOSFERATU and make us happy.BLASPHEMOUS 2 is the SNES sequel we all knew and loved in the 90s.

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel to its predecessor, with more improvements than downsides. The bosses are generally much more interesting and rely less on RNG-based projectile spamming (although those are still present), forcing you to be more accurate than lucky. The new moveset and weapon system is really cool, and leads to fun platforming puzzles. The art is as great as in Blasphemous 1. There are a few issues, however:1. The previous to last boss has unskippable dialogue not only before the fight but also in-between phases. As the second phase is challenging, you'll need to die at least a few times, and that dialogue quickly becomes frustrating.2. There seem to be two minor bugs: sometimes when lighting Veredicto, the animation freezes. Also, from time to time, the music stops playing randomly (although that's rare), so unless you close and rerun the game, you'll only have enemy and weapon/fighting sounds effects. 3. The cutscenes' artstyle doesn't match the game at all, it looks like cheap, generic, low-budget art that was thrown together at the last minute. 4. Compared to the first Blasphemous game, the lore is almost non-existent.

_childDocuments_.review: Huh.First impressions after beating it--While I have to say, that this is a sturdy and solid follow up to the first game, it is noticeably easier. This could be the addition of ability upgrades in this game, or it could be the content in general. It could also be, that when I played through the first game, there was a lot of DLC that had been added over the years.Whatever the case: that difference in difficulty might determine how much you enjoy this sequel, relative from the first game.Personally, I'm a little bummed that it wasn't challenging enough. I remember feeling like a champ when I finally beat some of the bosses in the first game (Isidora comes to mind). The last boss here was a TOTAL pushover. It took me two tries, and then it was over. The platforming also felt a lot easier. To clarify: the platforming in this game FEELS great, but I think the challenge was less present. Some of the most fun I had in the first game were the timed platforming challenges. Here, they're noticeably absent.All that in mind: it's still a fantastic game. It makes a lot of improvements on the first, and comes out the gates swinging. If you were a fan of the first, you'll most likely enjoy it as well. I just wish I had gotten more of a catharsis out of beating it, like I had before.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some issues, but overall I really liked it.- The game now has cartoon cutscenes which I didn't really like. They don't fit that well with the rest of the style. I just skipped these.- The overall game progress path felt more linear than in the first game. That's not totally bad though.- I mostly played with the mace weapon, which seemed a little too powerful. You might want to not use the mace for a more balanced experience.- The game didn't do a very good job of introducing/explaining the traversal uses of the weapons, so I spent some time being confused about how to progress.- Maybe it was using the mace, but most of the bosses in the game seemed too easy, with the exception of the penultimate boss, which was way too hard (the final boss was much easier). The first game had bosses which were a bit too spongy, so it's good that they lowered the time-to-kill for some of the bosses, but they lowered it by too much. I managed to kill 2 or 3 bosses on my first try, whereas I don't think I first-tried a single boss in the original game. - The penultimate boss was too hard to begin with, but was made extra annoying because it has some short-but-unskippable cutscenes you get really sick of after multiple attempts on the boss. The harder a boss is, the more important it is that you don't waste my time with this sort of thing and make multiple attempts as smooth as possible.- The original game was a bit clunky in terms of traversal, but that also made it more unique. In the new game, you unlock a double-jump and an air-dash, which made it feel a bit more like a generic metroidvania. These powerups feel fun, and they're used well in the game, and it kind of makes sense why every game like this ends up including double jumps and air dashes since they are fun, but this was a somewhat bittersweet change.- I felt that they made the upgrade system a little too complicated. There's now both rosary slots and figure slots for equippable upgrades, as well as an upgrade tree for each weapon, and also both the basic currency and the upgrade token currency you get periodically. It also felt like they left the new rosary setup a little undercooked.- I didn't like how the death guilt system made me feel like I had to worry that if I died to a boss to many times I would have to go grind currency to be able to afford to reset my guilt. I never ended up having to do this, but it still made me nervous.- I mildly disliked some of the new imagery. For example, in the first game almost everything is kind of grotesque, whereas in the new game, your guide character is angelic, which felt wrong to me. I almost felt like she should have betrayed you or something. It's not a big deal though.- I think the music was slightly better in the first game. For example the acoustic guitar piece that the original game plays in the sewer level was really great, and I don't think any of the new game's music was that good. The new music is good enough though.But overall it's still a lot of fun and I would recommend it. It has some changes compared to the first game, and I would say that the changes were on average more bad than good, but it's good that they're experimenting a bit. The changes definitely didn't ruin the overall experience. Tthey did the experimenting well enough that I expect their hit rate for new experiments to improve in Blasphemous 3.It might be good to start the player with all 3 weapons and have a tutorial segment where you had  to use the traversal powers to progress. Then maybe something goes wrong and your weapons get knocked away and you only have the opportunity to pick up one of them before continuing. Then when you later pick up the other weapons, you immediately know how to use them. Or you could just have better hint messages for using each weapon's traversal power once you pick it up, and a comprehension test inside the pickup room where you have to use that traversal power to escape the pickup room.

_childDocuments_.review: Great art. Dark, baroque, sinister and absurd. I don't have the vocabulary to describe it adequately. It was a pleasure to see it all. Technically, I encountered a few bugs: some missing animations, teleportation broke a few times requiring me to restart my game, some small things. Not serious or common enough to prevent me from finishing the game. The combat was overall satisfying, with a few caveats. Contact damage is not ideal when there are some enemies that can spawn directly on top of you (northwest area, you'll know the ones), or glide into you randomly. The trial-and-error in determining which things can be dodged through and which can't is a bit annoying. The pacing and balance is a bit uneven. Weapon upgrades appear at strange periods. None of the bosses are terribly difficult, especially with the massive health and healing upgrades that are a bit too loaded towards the mid-late game. There's a mid-game duo boss that doesn't work very well when you haven't yet acquired some of the defensive abilities that would make it more controllable, and many of the late game bosses have entirely too much projectile spam in lieu of attack patterns (this is perhaps more just a personal taste thing). I do appreciate the general boss and enemy variety. The decision to make the final health and fervour upgrades completely missable based on some minor actions the player can take near the start of the game with little context is foolish, especially in the face of the rest of the quests and items being mostly self-solvable without looking up a guide and acquirable from a specific NPC if they're missed. It stands out as a mistake. There's a little bit too much metroidvania backtracking. I'm glad the map gives you options to mark spots to come back to later, at least, and the final few sweeps are accelerated by all the fast travel options you end up with. Despite the (mostly minor) issues above, I enjoyed the game.
