_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel to a great game. Genuinely felt like a perfect "safe" sequel. "Safe" because this is still undoubtedly just more Blasphemous. Practically everything in the first game makes a return in this direct sequel, but with improvements across the board. You get more weapons, more stat boosting items, more NPC's to be shocked by, better areas, better exploration, better enemies, better upgrades, and the list can go on I'm sure. Easily surpasses the sequelitis for me, I do think this is the better game overall even if the novelty of the original keeps it a close contest.Now to rant about my thoughts on main portions of the game, i'll start with the bosses. They are just about as interesting to look at and learn as they were in the first game's base version. I don't know if the post release stuff from the first game will be surpassed. The individual areas have seen some of the largest improvement in my opinion. The rooms took more interesting shapes and the layouts were more fun to navigate. The start of the game had some really open ended progression but things die down heavily in the mid game where areas start opening up one by one instead of at the same time like I think would have been more interesting. This eventually forces you into following what feels like a pretty defined route. Having three weapons is amazing, especially because you don't have to use all three in combat. You can pick a favorite like I did and just get good with it. The use of all three weapons in traversal is fantastic though and it makes for some of the more interesting movement puzzles. Speaking of movement, it feels very similar to the first game, just better. More consistent and smoother overall. And with the addition of some new movement options it was much more varied than the first ever was. I do miss stabbing the walls to climb though, even if that system resulted in a ton of deaths for me, just felt unique I guess. The combat feels the same way. It's the same, but more consistent and smooth, and of course you have three different weapons to work with. There's also loads of new enemies and better use of enemy variants to kept it fresh for far longer. There is a lacking number of unique executions though which is a shame. The music is about as good as in the first game, overall very atmospheric. The visual presentation seems to have not skipped a single beat excluding two things. Firstly, the world in this game supposedly has a giant heart in the sky but you never see it the background sky box. Thinking about it now that ♥♥♥♥ should be up there looming over our entire playthrough as some sign of the danger to come. Secondly, the cut scenes being in a different style did feel weird, but it's such a non issue for me that I hardly remembered to mention it here. Everything else looks absolutely fantastic. Backtracking was so much better in this game, from the increased density of stuff in every room to the improved layout of the world and placement of fast travel rooms. Much less frustration getting from point A to B and back again. Finally the story and characters. Both were great. The writing is still weird and fun to listen to and the voice acting is a lot better than the first game overall. The characters are all still a wonderful mix of horrifying and mysterious and most were really good. I think the fist game will always have a leg up in this part because of how unique it was when it came out. This game is just as good, it's just no longer the first to do it. There's more I could mention like the improved variety in spells and stat boosters, but generally speaking if the first game had it this game has it too, with some form of improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you told me Blasphemous would have a sequel four years ago, I would laugh at you and ask if you were high or something. And yet, here we are. Blasphemous 2 has been released, and it's more polished, darker and weirder than the first one, and even more gorgeous in terms of art style. It's the same deal with Nioh 2 and Remanant 2: sequels that are basically just the first game but with way, way more content. Blasphemous 2 takes in all the criticism from the first game and improve upon it. I am not just talking about number tweak. The lacking of character build, the annoying platform issues, and the metroidvania identity crisis, all have been resolved in this wonderful sequel. Well, I suppose if I have to say something negative about Blasphemous 2, it would be that if you don't like the first one, you will not enjoy the sequel either. It is still the same game, fundamentally. However, I would still recommend this game to those people simply because of its sheer improvement.Looking back at Game Kitchen's previous works never cease to amaze me. The improvement they have from The Last Door to Blasphemous is phenomenal. From simple background drawn from simple line works, to a full-blown melancholy scenery made with delicacy and wonder, it is undeniable that the studio has out-done themselves over the years. But here comes the sequel. Somehow, Game Kitchen finds a way to improve even further. The background detail of Blasphemous 2 is really something else. Every stage is beautifully crafted. Various degree of solemnity can be seen from each level. The City Of Blessed Name is layered with a warm color of lighting with the doves taking off, conveying a divine and hopeful atmosphere. My favorite scene is probably the starting area of the Choir Of Thorns. It is ominous road to the Crown Of Towers. The dark color and the thorny decoration apply a sense of dread. Once you push pass the shrubs and forests, you are greeted with an open view. A great lake sits calmly in front of you. You notice something different about the lake. The reflection of clear surface seems off. It depicts a night sky and a lively city on the far hill, yet when you look up there’s nothing there. This scene is full of mystery, and at the same time delivers an unspeakable sense of wonder that only Blasphemous and Game Kitchen can pull off.Immediately the first improvement jumps right in. The first game does not have much weapon variety. Mea Culpa is your only sword throughout the whole game. It makes sense lore wise, but I wish there were more. And now in Blasphemous 2 there are three weapons for you to choose. Ruego Al Alba is basically Mea Culpa with a curse sword appearance, but its function is far from identical. With Blood Pact ability, this curve sword can enhance its attack with additional range, damage, and even heal yourselves for the damage you deal. Veredicto is the heavy hitter, a chained hammer made with incense. It has the longest reach and delivers the heaviest punch of the three. It's power is further increased by lighting the incense on fire. Sarmiento and Centella sports a faster attack and a deadly dash attack which is great for repositioning. With repeating strikes, this rapier and dagger can even conjure up some lightning damage. Needless to say, the new weapons are welcoming features. What I love even more is that each weapon comes with one metroidvania style perk. The perk is baked into each weapon's moveset, meaning it can be used to open new areas or cut some hole on your enemies. The human tree trunks can only be penetrated by Ruego Al Alba's high-air plunge attack; Veredicto can ring the special bell to summon the formless platforms and thin the iron doors; Sarmiento and Centella allows you to zoom through the floating mirrors and reach higher level. This is a recent feature which I fall in love with during many years of playing metroidvania, and I am glad Blasphemous 2 jumps on this trend.→Spanish dub has a solemn touch to it, and I love it.→Again, NPCs are intriguingly weird.→Soundtrack is equally good as the first one.→A lot of secrets and collectibles.→That indie games gallery easter egg.→Traps no longer one-shot you, rejoice!→: There are certainly more ways to improve your playstyle in Blasphemous 2. Each weapon has unlockable movesets and some general upgrades in the responding skill tree. Rosary beads have been cut down on quantity and focus on survival and defensive traits. And the new feature, Altarpiece is something worth investing into. It functions similar to Rosary beads, but instead of survivability, it serves as offensive customization for your weapons and prayers. Each figure has different attribute to boost your performance, and I am not talking about a measly 5% boost like the first game. It is 10% and the number can go even higher with right combination. Yes, combination is a thing for the Altarpiece. Combines certain figures together can create some crazy synergies. For example, putting The Anointed One(increases the strength of Veredicto) and The Purified One(Increases Fire damage) together gives Veredicto new attack effect that whenever you attack with the incense active, every swing sends out four fire orbs that explode. There are more synergies that focus on each weapon and even your Bile Flask for you to discover.→: With all these new upgrades also come with a catch. Most of the critics I come across say that the game is a little too easy comparing to the first game, and I have to agree. It is an extremely delicate line to balance. You want to give players the power they deserve, but you also need to keep both the power and enemies' toughness in check to create a balance difficulty. Sadly, Blasphemous 2 is struggling to find that balance. I will be honest. I never feel challenged during my playthrough up until the second to last boss fight.→If two or more enemies manage to run into you when you're knocked down, prepare to take a ridiculous amount of contact damage before you can reposition to safety.→Some descriptions for the puzzles can be cryptic to deduce.中文小簡評→續作出來的比我想像的還快，瀆神2就好比遺跡2和仁王2，擁有一代的基礎但是更多玩意兒！→把一代有的缺點一一改善並且逐一加強，玩過一代你會更愛。→美術風格更上一層樓，每個場景都是充滿黑暗宗教氣息，既神聖又詭譎。→三把武器任君挑選，各自有優缺點，值得一提的是三把武器都各有類銀河系惡魔城的技能，可以解鎖更多區域，又能拿來打怪。→西班牙配音有股不可言喻的肅穆感。→NPC真的是無法想像的怪(讚美。→背景音樂好聽。→諸多隱藏道具及收集任務，各自有相對應的獎勵。→獨立遊戲畫廊小彩蛋。→讚嘆主，陷阱不會秒殺你啦！→本作擁有更多方式來客製化玩法，升級上下限遠超一代，然而這是一把雙面刃，過度強化帶來的是暴力輾壓過關，瀆神2的難度因此比一代低許多。→如果有兩個敵人在你被擊倒時站在你身上的話，除了吃上大量接觸傷害外完全無解。→有些解謎敘述過於艱澀難懂。

_childDocuments_.review: (X-posted to my Wordpress blog, Gunlord500)Not a big review, because it can be summed up easily: A great refinement of Blasphemous 1. Pretty much all the complaints I had about the first game have been addressed: You have plentiful warp points and can upgrade the save points to warp points as well when you get enough secrets, the controls are MUCH smoother, you have actual movement boost abilities (double jumps and air dashes), and there's so much more you can do with your characters. You no longer have 1 weapon but three (basic sword, slow but powerful flail [technically a censer], and swift but weaker and short ranged rapier and dagger) that are really cool, with new moves and everything unlockable. There are also tons of spells you can get that are much more practical and which you can mix and match, because they're now divided into quick spells and heavy spells (the former just press a button to launch, the latter hold down and the cast button). Also, in addition to the first game's rosary beads, you can now equip little statues you find in the game! You can have a max of 8 on you at any one time, and they also have synergies with each other, which can sometimes really affect your playstyle, like giving you enhanced dodges and new moves. There are so many of those combos that you end up having MASSIVE amounts of customization over your build. Also, while I liked the pixel cutscenes in the first game,  they used anime cutscenes for Blasphemous II which I have to admit look much better.What's stayed the same? The masterful pixel graphics, easily the best I've seen since SotN, and arguably better than SotN--the insane amount of detail packed into them, especially all the little tidbits you'd have to be familiar with Spanish culture to notice, awesome boss fights. and excellent music. The OST (consisting mainly of classic Spanish guitar, bit of flamenco) is absolutely superb, although there isn't a song that was Godlike the way Baile de Violetas was in Blasphemous 1. So I'd give the OST a 9.9/10 whereas Blasphemous I was 10/10. But still super good. Finally, the map layout and level design is arguably the best of any Metroidvania ever so far. There's also a REALLY interesting bit that improves replayability: You don't get all three weapons immediately, you choose one and then get the others later. And the thing is, each weapon has different doors it can open or obstacles it can traverse; the sword can slice through certain wooden doors, the rapier can teleport brief differences, and the censer can hit bells that reveal platforms and stuff. So for the beginning of the game there are three different routes you can take through the early parts until you find the other two weapons depending on which one you take. Very neat!I do have some critiques. First, at the time of this writing, there are some pretty serious bugs, like occasionally losing save data and softlocks. More severe and more than I'd like for a game that's been truly released rather than in early access, but still I know the team is looking at all the bug reports so they should have those severe ones fixed in a week or so. So if you're reading this right now it doesn't take anything away from my score, just warning you in case you're buying it immediately.Second and more importantly: The aesthetics are beautiful, but the plot is as incomprehensible to me as Blasphemous 1's was. It seems like every character just strung together a bunch of religious terms (Penitence, Miracle, Sacrament, etc) and that's all. So the plot didn't stick with me or affect me the same way Symphony of the Night's did, or even Ender Lilies (which had a similar, dark souls inspired, 'you need to read the item descriptions and pay attention to the scenery to understand what's going on' thing going). I really hope for The Game Kitchen's next outing they get a writer to look over the script and make it a little less obscure.Thirdly, the structure of the game seems pretty similar to Blasphemous 1 (I'll keep things vague to avoid too many spoilers): After you start, and choose your weapon, you have to fight 3 bosses to unlock a door to the remaining ~70% of the game map, where you have to fight a bunch of other bosses, with the climax being a penultimate fight that's a duel with a character who fights sort of like your guy (although this one has a VERY cool last attack I don't want to spoil at all), and the last boss being a big dude in the background. So Blasphemous II sort of feels, in terms of structure, like a retread of the first game rather than truly original.Finally, as of the time of this writing, there are unfortunately no boss rush modes, NG+ with extra challenges, or alternate skins for your protagonist (the Penitent One) like Blasphemous I had. Maybe these will come out in DLCs (as they did for B1) but their lack is a lil disappointing :<Still, these are very minor caveats, along with some other small ones like contact damage being annoying sometimes. I recommend this with no hesitation, this is a solid 9.5/10 for me, with the only flaws being bugs which will be fixed soon and a confusingly obscure script. Buy it!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is fun, but truth be told, I'm a little disappointed in the sequel compared to the first game. _childDocuments_.review: As other reviewers have mentioned, this game is fun but will leave you slightly disappointed if your are seeking the same feeling the original Blasphemous. Combat is fun and the platforming is interesting- especially with the Mea Culpa DLC. The music is beautiful as always. The bosses are interesting and don't feel like carbon copies of what we saw with the first game.That said...-The NPCs are forgettable. One of the things that I love about the first game are the characters that populate the world and make it feel so much more alive. Gemino, Rendeto, Soledad, just to name a few. This game has very few in comparison, and they don't really expand the lore of Cvstodia. A lot of time has passed since the Penitent One died, surely some lore can be woven into these characters like they were for the first group. But sadly no- they are all very flat in comparison.- Replayability is much lower. In the first game, you could unlock a number of skins which were tied to challenges that, while frustrating at times, kept the play fresh. Once you finish Blasphemous 2, you can start new game plus, but there are no aesthetic rewards for doing so. - This is more of a nitpick, but I dislike the animated cut scenes. They are so jarringly different in style from the rest of the game, it kind of breaks the immersion a bit.Do I think this game is worth playing at least once? Yes.Do I think future DLCs can help address some of my concerns? Absolutely.Do I think Blasphemous 2 holds a candle to the original at all? No. Not even close.

_childDocuments_.review: I played and finished the first. The one lacks its atmosphere, it's cool cutscenes (instead we get some Zelda CD-i lookin stuff), etc. All the enemies are boring and easy and just serve to waste time. Bosses are tedious, with sloppy hitboxes and long phases that makes the fights tedious even when you know their patterns. Movement, especially reversing direction, feels sloppier than the first. Parry is ok timing-wise but inconsistent when it comes to cancelling other move windups and often just doesn't happen when you press RB, leading to some horribly punishing whiffs that didn't make sense. All of the weapons feel bad to use. The death system that punishes you until you *backtrack* (a cardinal sin for Metroidvanias) to go clear out your accumulated punishment, which was a system that sucked in DS2 and it sucks here.I put about 20 hours into the first, which was fantastic out of the gate, but I'm going to refund this one immediately. There are much better metroidvanias out there, and I ignored the generally negative feedback towards this one on reddit and elsewhere because it was on sale, but it's really not worth you time.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first reviewed this game, I gave it a thumbs down, because I had just rage quit it after getting killed by the worst boss ever for about the 150th time.  I have since then finished the game and I have had some time to reflect, and I would say that this game definitely deserves a thumbs up, but the last two bosses did leave a bad taste in my mouth.  The second to last boss is literally the most unfair boss that I have ever played against.  The actual final boss is kind of a pushover once you figure out his patterns.  It would be nice to see a future patch even out the difficulties a little more. But for most of the time playing Blasphemous 2, I was legitimately loving it.  It is a huge improvement over the first game.  Better level design.  Three great weapons instead of one, and each weapon is useful.  The weapons allow for all kinds of different approaches to your enemies, and the game is long enough that you will get to try all of them.  The collectibles are huge in number and high in quality.  Exploration is fun and it helps make the game addictive.  There are more upgrades to your abilities than there were in the first game, and that gives Blasphemous 2 much more of a traditional Metroidvania feel than its predecessor.  Falls into spikes and pits are no longer insta-death (Thank God).  The enemies are also more fun to fight.  The enemies that were the least fun to fight in the first game have been removed in favor of some new enemies that are very fun to fight.  The boss battles, up until the final two, are fantastic – they typify what a boss battle should be in a game like this. Blasphemous 2 is just as wonderful in its art direction and its animations as its predecessor, with the lone exception being that they, for some reason, neutered the executions in this game pretty badly.  The music is top notch once again too.  This game is one of the most improved sequels that I have ever played…. …until that boss.  And if you have played this game, then you know exactly the boss that I am talking about.  The most brutally difficult and punishingly unfair boss that I have ever experienced in a video game.  It is at that point that your 15-20 hours of consistent progress and addictive flow comes to a raging halt.  This boss has two full health bars and three stages on the second bar, with a short cut scene in the middle for good measure.  And by the time that you finally defeat the guy, you will have memorized that cut scene backwards and forwards.  The first time that I played this game it took me, no kidding, maybe 150 tries to beat the guy.  When I finally did, I had maybe two pixels on my health bar and no healing flasks left.  Some of his attacks are so grotesquely unfair that the only way to avoid getting killed by them is to just hope that you get lucky and that he doesn’t use them many times.  It’s truly awful and I’m not exaggerating when I say that this penultimate boss almost singlehandedly ruins what, up until then, is a nearly perfect experience. After you defeat that guy, you go to the final boss, thinking that it must be some sort of epic difficulty confrontation.  And he is al pushover.  Once you figure out his patterns (he only has a few different attacks), you can easily beat him on the 2nd or third try.  I don’t know how you could design a game so near-perfect for the first 98% of it and then stumble so badly with such horribly calibrated boss battles. The final sequences of this game are so profoundly disappointing, and they really left a bad taste in my mouth. The story in Blasphemous 2, like the first game, is largely gobbledygook.  There is, of course, The Miracle.  The Miracle apparently causes nothing but suffering but people still refer to it as a “miracle” for some reason.  You are the Nameless – er, um – The Penitent One, a silent coneheaded guy who is doing penance for some unnamed sin or crime.  An infertile couple is granted a child but apparently that child is diseased or deformed or something, and there is an elevated city above the main city in the game, and a gigantic beating heart there, and you have to defeat 3 bosses to access that city and then beat five more to get five keys to let some birds out of cages – Christ I don’t know.  Like its predecessor, Blasphemous 2 opts entirely for style over substance when it comes to telling its story, preferring to cloak the plot in layer after layer of cryptic dialog and symbolism that makes absolutely zero sense.  There are youtube videos that attempt to untangle this bowl of narrative spaghetti but if I have to watch youtube videos to understand the basics of your plot, then you have failed miserably as a storyteller. Do I recommend Blasphemous 2?  Yes.  Strongly?  No.  In some ways, it is the most improved sequel that I have ever played.  But at a few crucial times, it practically begs you to uninstall it.  For what it’s worth, I have finished it twice, which is fairly unusual for me, so it can’t be bad.  I am hoping for a third game in this series, warts and all.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the first Blasphemous game, but while playing the sequel i couldn't help but be disappointed and angry at how they handled some elements of the game. Apart from the art style the game just feels bland. They completely crushed the "soul" of the first game and replaced it with generic metroidvania elements and for the most part boring level design.The game does improve on some things compared to the first one, like the combat and the fact that you have 3 weapons at your disposal. There aren't any miss-able quest this time around. Also the altarpieces and weapon skill-trees are cool additions. Sadly these came at a cost of making the rosarie beads completely uninteresting and 2 of the 3 weapons having bugs that I found.Due to people complaining about insta-kill spikes in the first game, the devs removed the insta-kill element from them in the second game ( I personally didn't like this decision, but I do understand that people were annoyed and frustrated by the spikes). The problem with this is that it makes traversing the different areas less interesting and tense especially because most of the platforming sections are gone as well and the ones that remain have little to no weight or danger behind them.  The devs tried to fix this by adding more enemies to rooms and imo way too many challenge rooms. This would have probably helped if the enemy variety wasn't so lacking.Obviously some enemies were taken unchanged from the first game (which is totally fine) but the problem lies with the fact  a lot of the enemies are just recolours of themselves with the element of the enemy being changed or them having an extra little addition to their attack. This just makes it feel cheap and recycled. Another part which adds to the laziness of it all is the fact that there are almost no unique executions in the game. I saw like maybe 5 different executions because most  of the enemies have the same boring execution + triggering executions is harder and less consistent. Sadly, even though game has been out for almost a year, common and easily found bugs have still not been fixed. I encountered bugs were in some areas the music cut out randomly and i had to fast travel to get it back. Worst of all, one of the bosses you have to fight has his music AND sound effects completely cut out which you can't fix from what I've tried. Obviously this completely ruins the atmosphere and feel of the fight. Another thing which I noticed is that when you stop time (through the use of prayers or altarpieces), projectiles and flying enemies don't stop, but keep moving in the direction they were moving. This actually led me to being stuck in one of the challenge rooms because a flying enemy went off screen and never came back. Lastly, as stated above, I found bugs with 2 of the 3 weapons in the game. The most apparent  one was with the mace, where there is an animation error when you try to light it while running, this makes the lighting animation cut out and freezes the character in place until the mace is suddenly lit. The second bug was with the rapier weapon specifically with the skills "silver cross" and "cross of the tempest". You're supposed to be able to use the "silver cross" skill anytime you want in the air, but for some reason I had to spend a diamond (Verdadera Destreza) point to use it. Because of this, the upgraded version, "cross of the tempest" which actually had to use a diamond (Verdadera Destreza) point, just didn't work no matter what I tried.Overall, if the game wasn't tied to blasphemous 1 then it would be a decent game. Unfortunately, since it is a sequel that imo for the most part is a downgrade of the original. For that reason i can't recommend the game especially if the developers will continue down the same path and make the series worse. I just can't support that.PS: The final boss has an unnecessary difficulty spike with a couple of lines of unskippable dialogue every time you fight him, which is just annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is not bad, but it is not good either.  The game itself feels unfinished. Spoilers aheadThe gameplay design is fun and new. The weapons were good, although one of them (the rapiers beside the mirrors are basically useless). In the beginning it is refreshing to play. The movement of the character is much more fluid and so is the animation. The OST still slaps, the composers did a really good job.  The slight references to the first game were good to see (although the more memorable characters were left out). Some new enemies were interesting and in the beginning the bosses were exhilarating as well, but by the end they just became unnecessarily hard. Still continuing with the bosses Eviterno does not live up to Crisanta, at all. Crisanta was a genuinely well thought out boss, but Eviterno just felt lackluster.  His moves were not predictable (even after a few deaths) and was just plain...annoying. His first stage is kinda fun and easy, but the second one is just a big no. Items and collectibles. Items lost all the lore they had about them. There was no added information or story to the rosary beads. I loved reading through those in the first game. It added another layer of mystery and worldbuilding. Prayers and chants are really similar to the first game, but honestly they improved in this category. Some of them were really useful (like the one you could travel back to the first Prieu).  The wooden figure and altar system was once again like a fresh breath of air. It was much more useful and customizable than for example the sword hearts from the first game.Cherubs get their own section, cause oh boy was it a mess. I unfortunately have encountered the bug where the game basically locks you out from getting all of them. Went through the map several times, used guides to make sure that I 100% collected them, but the game still only recognised 32/33. (Multiple people had problems with this, as it turns out). This fact will be needed in a bit.The game is littered with bugs. Beside the aforementioned one, I encountered multiple visual problems. Tabbing out of the game while travelling made the sprite of the Penitent one disappear (this happened like twice). Music cutting out during certain bosses and whole areas randomly. Simply put, bugs that should have been already. NPCs felt hollow. In the first game even the smallest NPCs (like the corpses) actually told a story. I remember most prominent ones by name from the first game, but if you were to ask me the names from this one I would not be able to tell you anything. I couldn't get attached to them, couldn't get to know more about them for completing certain tasks and they just felt useless at times. Maybe Yerma is the one that stayed with me the most and only because I was not able to save her in the end  (more on that in a second). NPCs suffered the same fate as collectibles did. The map felt too big as well. The new areas were good to see, but for example I still don't really understand why Mother of Mothers was there? I feel like it would have been better if there was like 1-2 less. Now, for my main grievance. The road to the good ending. In this game to get the true or good ending you need to collect basically everything. All 33 cherubs, the 5 sick daughters, travel 3 times with the Procession of Shadows and the last one you need to hecking buy. First of all and once again this just feels hollow. In the first game to get the "true" ending you needed to talk to multiple NPCs and do genuinely interesting quests. To be really honest, I did not even finish the game after discovering that I got locked out from getting the good ending. Since I got the bug with the cherubs I could not achieve the ending I wanted and just left it at that (plus Eviterno was not worth the trouble).So yeah, it is not a bad game, but definitely does not live up the masterpiece that is the first one. It needs a really big bug fix finally so that it can be actually playable.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 emerges as a refined sequel, surpassing its predecessor in both combat and exploration. The game shines aesthetically, with more detailed backgrounds and a greater diversity of areas to explore. The music is enchanting and perfectly captures the emotion of each setting. A significant change from the original is the shift from entirely pixel-based cutscenes to hand-drawn animations. While this might initially feel off-putting to some players, it effectively details the characters before transitioning to the pixel art graphics.CombatCombat has received substantial emphasis and expansion. Players no longer wield the Mea Culpa, which, while missed for its versatility, is replaced with three new weapons that offer diverse combat options:Veredicto (Hammer): A slow but powerful weapon capable of smashing walls and ringing bells for traversal.Ruego Al Alba (One-handed Blade): Allows for counter attacks and plunging attacks, which also destroy roots found on the ground.Sarmiento and Centella (Sword and Dagger): Enables fast attacks that increase in damage with a higher combo counter and allows the player to dash through mirrors.Additionally, prayers have been greatly improved, offering more variety and being available sooner in the game, allowing players to experiment with them faster.PlatformingPlatforming has been made less frustrating, with spikes no longer instantly killing the player. However, it has also become more challenging, requiring players to switch between weapon mobility skills to access different areas. Although it feels better than in the previous game, the increased complexity will challenge players more.Enemy VarietyEnemy variety is a standout feature in Blasphemous 2. Encounters are generally more difficult than in the first game, with enemies dealing more damage, having more varied attacks, and frequently using ranged abilities. The enemy placement is excellent, making every room feel challenging in the best way.Player Equipment and LoadoutsThe player equipment and loadout system has undergone significant changes. The number of rosary beads that can be equipped has been reduced to five, but the game introduces up to eight equipable altarpieces, which need to be changed at a specific NPC. Although I wish these could be changed at rest points, this system offers more overall build variety, which is a net positive.A major change is the introduction of defined damage types that enemies can resist. This adds more complexity to the system, as altarpieces can alter how these damage types interact with enemies.Boss FightsEvery boss has a short introduction that cannot be skipped, which can make repeated attempts more annoying than necessary. A particular boss, Eviterno, toward the end of the game, is notably challenging and forces players to skip through dialogue each time. This has been a point of frustration for many players and needs to be addressed by the development team.Missing FeaturesNotably, Blasphemous 2 lacks a New Game+ feature, which was a highlight of the first game after an update. This mode imposed specific penalties on the player character, forcing them to interact with the game differently. Despite its absence, the game remains highly recommendable, and I hope the developers add this feature in the future.ConclusionBlasphemous 2 is a worthy successor, delivering a polished and diverse experience. The improvements in combat, platforming, and the equipment system add depth and complexity, while the enhanced aesthetics and music elevate the overall atmosphere. Despite some minor drawbacks, such as the limited flexibility in changing altarpieces and the frustrating boss intros, Blasphemous 2 stands out as a challenging and rewarding game that fans of the series will greatly enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's fun, it's good and it's worth the price BUT the first Blasphemous is superior. If you're thinking about buying this game (and I recommend you do) consider the following first. -Blasphemous has INFINITELY better artstyle, especially custscenes. The new ones seriously don't match the tone of the game and you might think at some point that you turned on Crunchyroll by accident. You can thank Team17 for that, as the animator mainly responsible for cutscenes in B1 was Russian and he left the studio when Team17 forbid distribution of games in Russia.-Blasphemous 1 lets you explore a bit more and is more of a proper metroidvania. This one is pretty linear, you cannot wander into a late game area, because it simply is not there and only appears with progress. You also know where to go at all times, as objectives are now marked on your map.-Eventually you get to posess all three weapons. I thought really hard about choosing my weapon at the beginning of the game, and it turned out to be in vain, as you get all of them pretty early on. Weapon skills from the first game have been divided between 3 new weapons. You liked to have the option to parry and dash attack? Well now one weapon can parry, and the other can dash attack. It really doesn't matter, as you can focus on one weapon and steamroll through the entire game. -No i-frames, contact damage, ridiculous knockback - not only it's really easy to ♥♥♥♥ yourself over by poor positioning, the game tries to ♥♥♥♥ you over in some places. I died more times to contact damage than I'd like to admit. Enemies can spawn right onto you, which wouldn't be that problematic, if not for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ knockback, which can stunlock you right into the corner. This is extremely applicable before you get any upgrades, as a couple of times you get locked in a room with 2 charging enemies that you CANNOT jump over.-Boss balancing isn't there yet. The majority of bosses are REALLY easy and can be taken down in under 3 attempts without tryharding. On the other hand, some late game bosses become ridiculously difficult.-YOU CANNOT SKIP INTROS BEFORE BOSSFIGHTS! I don't know who came up with this, but it's one of the worst things about this game. Let me watch it once and then skip it whenever I want, Jesus it's not that difficult. With some changes, it could be just as good or better than the original. As it stands, it's very serviceable, but not "up there". They will probably drop some DLC at some point, so it has potential. Having said all that, In Blasphemous 2, spikes and falls no longer insta-kill you, so it may be a better game after all lmao.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time for 90% of the game but the second-last boss was a massive difficulty spike coupled with ~40s of unskippable cutscenes. This was very frustrating and my initial review of this was a no.But since I had a good time for most of the playthrough, I'd really like to voice to the devs that cutscenes should be skippable for bosses. And 40s of unskippable scenes for one boss is too much. It was more Blasphemous and I think the combat in this was overall better than in the first. So after having had a few weeks to cool off, I'd ultimately recommend this game, but I do agree with others that the difficulty on bosses can feel all over the place.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome sequel to the first game, although the story was less compelling as the first (I believe it's due to the lack of normal NPC questlines). This isn't necessarily a bad thing, because the additional map size is totally worth all the work into it. I was agog at the scenery and detail, especially in the forest and sheet city areas (iykyk). Like, this game is worth the art alone. I also really appreciate the new ability to mark things on the map which was a huge help.Also, fair warning, the last two bosses of the game are extremely obnoxious and not like the rest of the bosses in the game, so I recommend not sticking to one weapon. Use the whole game to practice different moves, weapons and spells so the end game won't be such a pain. Additionally, if you are going to try to go for all the cherubs, I recommend marking the ones you find on your map as you go through them to avoid the pain of trying to find the last ones in end game as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a worthy successor, that you can still play without having played the predecessor. Lore wise it is similar to a souls-like, you wont understand anything the first time you play it or without looking up some stuff. The second I started playing, muscle memory kicked in and it played just like Blasphemous I. You will recognize a couple of enemies as well. The upgraded art style of the cut scenes was unusual at first and I feared to lose a bit of the grim feel, but it turned out to be not to be a bad decision at all. The things you loved about Blasphemous I you will get more of. I personally loved the little moments when you realize what just happened to the characters and what consequences your decision just triggered. The new possibility to choose and level different weapons is a good addition, especially when the game encourages you to use all of them. Overall everything I expected, with good additional mechanics and lore, so that it does not feel too copy-pasted. The only thing (that I didn't like in the first game as well) is the kind of overwhelming skill and inventory system. It still has its reason and roots in the lore, which is why I still don't think it is that restrictive.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 was amazing. If you liked the first one, getting this one is a no-brainer.It's essentially more of the same, and that's the best thing about it.Gorgeous art, atmospheric music, tight controls, fulfilling combat and varied boss fights. (Although one of the boss fights is WAY harder than the rest, which I found a bit odd. It required very cheesy tactics for me to beat.)There's a lot to explore and a lot of secrets to be found, so completionists get to enjoy the awesome setpieces in some depth.The main difference compared to the first game is that there are now three main weapons which cater to different playstyles. You can also experiment with various builds, as each weapon has its own skill tree with some global modifiers, and there are new equippable items that boost different aspects of the main character, the weapons and prayers etc.The only minus for me was that there were a few bugs here and there, but nothing game-breaking or anything reloading a save wouldn't fix.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.2Compare to the previous game, this game is improved in a lot of way.Graphic - Graphic is mostly the same as the prequel and I think theres's some improvement but not very obvious. Boss design and Enemy placementThe enemy placement are pretty good, some rooms have some crap enemy placement, like two giants with others. that feels pretty unfair and not fun. _childDocuments_.review: I want MORE Blasphemous! In reality, it's a good game, BUT nowhere near as good as the first Blasphemous. Here are some pro and cons.Blasphemous 1:PROS:- Atmospheric world building that connects. Every place you go to seems to tell a story and flows from one to the other. It's dark, moody and you can feel the story seeping through the background.- Violent. It's gory alright. The executions are Mortal Kombat level and are chunky and fun. Even when you are not killing things, everything from enemies to NPCS to backgrounds are violent and gross. Love it. A stark contrast to the Christian imagery and themes.  - Story is awesome. A bit hard to follow but with a little item description reading, everything works out to tell a story rife with guilt, strife, pain and glory. - Animations. Man, the animations are super. From your character sheathing his sword to Boss's simply breathing. Everything is pixel porn. The cut scenes are done in this really janky, dark pixel art style that is so unique. The animators really took their time with making everyone have character. - Multiple endings and more re-playability. After I finished the campaign there was so much more to do, to my surprise. CONS:- It's hard. This game may take some practice. Boss battles are not for the faint of heart.- No customization in looks or weapon. One weapon only.- Something else maybe, but I can't think of it.Blasphemous 2PROS:- Combat is very fluid and responsive compared to the first game.- More weapon customization. - Graphics are better?CONS:- Barely any executions. Like maybe 4. Those gory executions made this game unique. Where did they all go?- Not very violent. Apart with some outliers, this game really toned down the violence. Did people complain and they toned it back? Not sure, but it's not very violent or dark or gritty.- Lack of atmosphere. All the areas and backgrounds are disconnected and do not flow with narrative. Kind of like a Dark Souls 2 situation. - NPC are bland with not personality. Animation has gotten worse with no personality.- Endings stink. They kind of leave you hanging with no real resolution. Also, nothing else to do after the game ends. - No real atmosphere.- Cinematic art style has changed to something softer. No bueno. Maybe the developers plan on fixing these issues later? Blasphemous 1 did release a bunch of DLC that made the game better so maybe that will happen. Again, I like this game, but the first Blasphemous is so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: A well put together mix of 2D Metroidvania and Dark Souls.Aesthetically the Souls influence is obvious. You're nameless armored dude in a grimdark nightmare realm. In this case the motif is Inquisition Dark-Ages Catholicism where everything endlessly bleeds. Statues bleed, enemies bleed, rocks bleed, items bleed, your character fills their 5-foot-tall helmet with blood and dumps it on their head. The architecture is pretty cool though. Fancy cathedrals, monasteries , and sculptures abound. Crypts are suitably creepy looking. NPCs are often screen sized and nightmare inducing. Enemies look grotesque. Bosses are large and imposing.The story? In Dark Souls fashion - it's vague nonsense about "miracles" and "suffering" and "penance" and nothing is explained or makes sense. Every item has a lore section that you could pretty much randomly swap around and not even notice. Bosses babble about standing in the way of your mission which is never explained and doesn't matter. You're not here for the story after all, you're here for the gameplay.Gameplay is closer to Metroidvania than Souls. You have a Castlevania style map you can pull up at any time to track your location and room progress. There's a variety of map markers you can place to track treasures or interesting locations that you can't currently access so you can remember to come back later, which is a nice feature that all these games should have. Like a Souls game, enemies when killed respawn when you rest at a bonfire-type checkpoint. Killing enemies generates soul-ahem, "tears" which are your currency for unlocking upgrades, paying NPCs, and so on. When you die, you don't lose any accrued tears, but until you get to your corpse your character starts accruing "guilt" with each death which saps away at your mana bar and gradually prevents you from earning tears from enemies. So they did a sort of inversion on the Souls formula - you don't lose things when you die, but until you get your corpse back you are penalized at future progression and survival becomes progressively harder. It feels a bit better than the Souls games, and I think it's a clever system.Everything you just read above I pasted from my review of Blasphemous 1, because this game is for all intents and purposes the same thing, again.They made a few changes.  Now you have other weapons aside from just your sword.  You get a big hammer type weapon that's slow and does more damage (it's the best weapon because it also staggers enemies more and has crazy reach) and your fast double daggers (which are useless).  You can switch between them instantly so you can mix and match if you want to (you won't).Curiously they also kind of scaled back on the equip options.  The rosary was downgraded to just 5 beads, mostly because they replaced its functionality with a 8 slot "altar" where you slot wooden figurines for bonuses.  But then they also removed the sword core system.  But then they did add the ability to equip two spells instead of just one.  In the end I'm not sure it was an overall improvement.They did remove having to equip relics - when you get new map traversal skills they are always on.  A no brainer fix there.The level design is pretty similar to last time.They cut down on the failable quests for the most part too, which was the correct decision.  There's still a few puzzles that require walkthroughs to have any hope of completing.The story is still vague gibberish.The first game was good, and this game is really more of the same.  So it loses a bit of luster for being completely unoriginal and not making substantial improvements or innovations.  But it's a fun enough time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is even better than the first part. The developers have done a great job providing a more comfortable experience—fewer exhausting, boring bosses, more challenging skill checks, and interesting enemies.However, I hate the last biome with the red thorns due to its skyrocketing difficulty curve. It took far too long just to reach the final prie dieu. This is the only major issue with the game. That section is unpleasantly harsh and frustrating.Nevertheless, Blasphemous 2 is a great sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a great Metroidvania. I enjoyed the first Blasphemous, but if I were to rate it, I would give it a 7, due to the lack of progression and the 'clunkiness' of the gameplay in some sections. Blasphemous 2 is a solid 9. The developers have taken all the feedback to heart and improved their creation in every aspect, truly commendable. The gameplay is flawless, with a sense of progression that keeps you glued to the screen, and an even more inspired artistic style, with backtracking handled perfectly. I hope the sales have been great because I really want to play a Blasphemous 3!Some minor negatives I feel compelled to add (but very personal):a) Half of the bosses are challenging and exhilarating, while the other half are just frustrating.b) I love trying to complete all the Steam achievements, especially in a Metroidvania, but personally, I always prefer achievements that I can complete in a single run of the game and that I can still achieve after defeating the final boss. I hate having to Google what I need to do to avoid ending the game at 99% because of an achievement that I can't/won't get at this point (true story).

_childDocuments_.review: It's technically a better game than the first Blasphemous, but it also feels like it sanded down some of the interesting edges in the process. It's not as gory or horrific, the cutscene art style is jarring, and the executions feel like an afterthought this time. I also encountered a few distracting bugs a few months after release (sometimes the music just doesn't start in places, and will start playing randomly again while you're in the same area).However, the combat, skill trees, and bosses are all a big improvement. The game also looks amazing. I slightly prefer the first one overall, but this is still a great metroidplatformervania.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as the first; still very good.  Tips I wish I knew going in: Finding 6 of the 9 hidden sisters unlocks fast travel at every bonfire. High priority.Talk to the green girl as soon as you see her every time, and agree to have her help. If you leave the screen before talking to her or say no at any point, you fail her quest. You can still get the item rewards from her quest a different way, but c'mon. "Guilt" is complex now even though it looks the same as the first game. You do NOT recover all guilt when you corpse run. You always accumulate a small % even after you recover. Higher guilt not only eats your magic bar, but also increases enemy damage AND currency drop amounts. Removing guilt with the guilt npc is a questline. I don't like this because it makes repeat boss attempts annoying, but better to know what it's doing than not.You can create synergy effects by combining certain idols in a window. This will create a little symbol between both idols.

_childDocuments_.review: A very strong follow up to the first game which improves and expands upon the combat and movement excellently. The soundtrack and art style is still fantastic and the game doubles down on the metroidvania side this time around. I can't speak to the story in comparison to the first game, as i'm the type of person that loosely follows along with the plot/lore in these games and then heads off to youtube for a deep dive post credits. If that sounds like you, you'll probably be fine with the story here too. 0 Crashes and only one minor bug throughout my 15-hour first playthrough. Here's a tip for new players. USE YOUR MARKERS. the map markers will make backtracking with new abilities infinitely more enjoyable.The ending lets the game down a bit by having a massive difficulty spike out of nowhere for the final boss. Which compared to every other boss in the game is much harder with no real progression in difficulty leading to it. This left a bit of a sour taste after having to watch the same unskippable cutscenes during the act multiple times, this is something the developers should patch and would make the experience better.Still a fantastic game that's one of the most enjoyable games I've played this year and one of the most enjoyable metroidvanias I've played in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 had a lot of quality life improvements over the 1st one that I think at the end of the day, took away some of the charm of it. In the first one every little relic would make your character slightly less clunky and potentially improve your movement, here instead you get defense bonuses against different things. I'm a sucker for bit art, so I was a little sad to see the creepy cutscenes in bit art to be replaced with art (that was great looking) similar to Hades. I can see why some people argue that the 2nd one is "easier" than the first (except a sudden spike in one of the last bosses). Overall, if you liked the first one, you'll probably enjoy this one. My biggest gripe was that finding the cherubs got bugged for me and 2 didn't get properly marked so I couldn't get one of the endings because of that.

_childDocuments_.review: A very, very solid title for Metroidvania lovers. Game-play elements are built on top of what the first part did. The world map is slightly more complicated and bigger than before, but becomes easily accessible for backtracking once you've progressed farther in the game.If you're a seasoned Metroidvania player, this game is not the most difficult of them all. I would say it's of "medium" difficulty when considering a game like Aeterna Noctis to be much harder. Only one boss took more than 5-10 attempts to beat.There's enough "precision" platforming to go around but it's not over done at all.The music is spectacular, the pixel graphics are excellent and the whole concept / theme of the game is very, very, well executed. Hats off the dev for parts 1 and 2. I eagerly await part 3.9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, just not as wonderful as the first.To be perfectly clear. The first was an absolute masterpiece. So the bar was almost impossibly high.The biggest thing to to me is that it just didn't grab me the way the first did. The first was full of stunning pixel art, shocking animation, confronting imagery and so many odd little things to double take at and get lost in the details of the world. The first has pixel art cut scenes, though lacking in movement, the details were spectacular. This has Anime cut scenes that kind of pulled me out of the moment. The first one had me scouring the internet to try and find a physical copy of the art book. This, while still beautiful feels somewhat less macabre and inspired.The new game play elements are good, I like the new weapons, cool to return to some of the old areas. Just a little disappointing. I still recommend it, I'm just picky and was obsessed with the first.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game even though it wasn't perfect, but I can't recommend this one if you're not a fan. There are some things that have changed for good, things that haven't changed and bugs that shouldn't have made it into the full release.It's great that you get 3 different weapons that serve more purpose than just for killing enemies, but I regretted choosing Veredicto (the big bonker) as starter weapon. You barely get to try them before choosing and not being able to parry is kinda a big deal.Jumping off cliffs or into Spikes no longer insta kills you and retrieving your guilt fragment is less buggy. I'm not a fan of the new guilt system, where you HAVE to pay eventually to get rid of your guilt.Enemy ai sometimes stops working, animations aren't playing correctly and one time I got stuck in mid air for no reason.Combat feels okay, but some enemies are to easy to stagger / hammering the attack button is more efficient than parrying. Stun locking is still a thing and hit boxes feel off sometimes. Like in the previous game there is a lot of back tracking and limited options for fast travel.The story is interesting and mysterious, but it doesn't feel as exciting as in the first game. The scenery looks better and like more love went into the design. I do not like the cut scenes, it totally ruins the aesthetics of the pixel art style.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this one is a little bit overhated by the first game's fans. Yeah, it doesn't have the same unique atmosphere as the first one, and plays completely different, but if you cast this aside and decides to evaluate it as what it's, it's a great metroidvania.The combat is far smoother and with more options than first game. The areas are designed very well, and backtracking after obtaining new abilities was fun. The map isn't that big to make backtracking annoying, and it was easy to explore the whole map and get all upgrades. Exploration felt very rewarding and getting new abilities felt very satisfying.The enemies have decent but not great variety and bosses were all fun and offered very good challenge even though I will agree they lacked the creepiness of the bosses in first game. If you like metroidvania genre, definitely check this out. What this game lacks in atmosphere and setting, it compensates in pretty much everything else. Just be ready for a different experience than the first game and try to be open minded about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is a sequel done right. It takes everything that made the first game great and expanded upon it heavily. I played through the entirety of the first game before diving into the sequel and my only real complaints regarding the original were the options for mobility and the lack of weapon variety. These issues are masterfully answered by the new weapons presented in the sequel, which both broaden the means in which you can engage combat as well as providing new means of traversal. The interconnected map is excellently tied together and while there is a range of variety I found no bosses in the game to be poorly designed. Just like the first game the setting is gripping and dripping with personality. I absolutely devoured this game when it came out, I just could not stop playing it. Blasphemous 2 is a master class not only as a modern Metroidvania but what sequels should aspire to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: If Blasphemous 1 was gourmet food with amazing desserts (DLC updates) then this feels like video game junk food in comparison.It's a decent game but it's vastly overshadowed by its prequel and the standards it set. Difficulty is lukewarm at best, Story is hardly present - more of a mediocre excuse for one, not even the NPCs you meet on your journey are particularly memorable at all.The game is -fun- in terms of receiving a constant stream of metroidvania dopamines until you get the 100% map completion, but that's about it. Get upgrades, collect items, explore the map, light platforming, hack and slash enemies with a couple bosses thrown into the mix (out of which even the somewhat challenging one took <10 attempts in total). Before you know it the game's over and you feel like you've sat in one of the many metroidvania treadmills out there rather than something that even attempted to come close to the lightning in a bottle that was Blasphemous 1.Each of my criticisms are things that the original game perfected from the get go, so it's a real shame that this game feels like an AI-created sequel. None of the believable world building or atmosphere has been carried over and neither has the quality of the satisfyingly challenging gameplay.I initially defended the game considering everyone had B1 to get used to the rough game formula so all of those reports of "game too easy" are to be taken with a grain of salt; but after finishing the game and seeing the incredibly lackluster ending(s) I'm inclined to agree that overall this is a disappointing sequel to a dearly beloved indie metroidvania that managed to elevate itself from the rest.This one just feels like one of the many forgettable ones instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the good things before going to the sour part of the game.Good:Pixel art is great, it is truly amazing.The OST is masterfully done, it is really fantastic.The voice acting and concepts of this game are majestic.The wooden prayer bench is a good idea.The prayers and incantations are a nice touch.Some weapons having a special ability in combat is good.As of playing this game I have encountered several game breaking bugs. There is a climbing glitch in the woods of thorns area where you have to crawl in a narrow incline but the game instakills you as if someone coded a spike pit there.There is also a platforming puzzle in the sunken church level, the drowned church with all the ink stuff, where PO refuses to hold on to the cherub ring despite my character even dropping far above it, he simply does not grab on, I had to use a cheat of infinite jumps just to complete this platforming, another soft lock bug if you want to collect all items.Most of the bosses I played I loathed,most bosses I skipped with a one hit kill cheat as I just could not be bothered to deal with the constant stuttering and freezing when your weapon, like the censer, hits a target multiple times and your animations slow down while the boss just goes like Sonic. Also the constant literal freezing glitch that happens when you turn on the fire of the censer has gotten me hit numerous times, I know the devs are working on the censer fire thing but the slow downs and stuttering also happens when doing the rapier flurry attack or the combo from the blood blade because there are too many sprites moving all at once and it messes up my rhythm and flow. So basically I can just not use the censer in boss battles which is a shame as I really like it.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic sequel to the first game, Blasphemous 2 improves on nearly every aspect where the original fell short, while bringing enough new elements to the table to re-invigorate Cvstodia. First and foremost are the QoL changes, such as not dying immediately from a spike trap or pitfall, and being able to unlock traveling between shrines much more coherently. Additionally, the level design feels much more modern than the original, and the dungeons all feel detailed, fleshed out, and fun to explore. The story is also far easier to follow, which is beneficial to casual players.                                                                                                         That said, there are some aspects where the original remains supreme. Noticeable from the opening cutscene, Blasphemous 2 lacks the gritty themes of the original, made obvious by the change in artstyle. The atmosphere feels especially generic and bland when compared to the desolate and plague-ridden environment of the first game. Though this could be attributed to the plot, as the Miracle has been gone from Cvstodia, this in of itself serves for a less interesting premise than the original. There is no more aura of mystery -- nothing to discover in terms of story or lore. I felt far less involved in the world and lore of the game as I played than the original.    Regardless, Blasphemous 2 was certainly a very enjoyable experience. Each dungeon somehow improved in quality, and the excitement upon reaching the final zone was palpable. Although I miss the Mea Culpa, the combat feels smoother than the first game, with more options and unique features. Marks of Martyrdom are also a smart addition, as weapon upgrades don't simply require more tears of atonement. The gameplay improved solidly from the first game, with the exception being the somewhat linear progression. This isn't that big of a deal though for me, as there's plenty of metroidvania in the game already.      In conclusion, I'd definitely recommend this game. The story isn't bad on its own -- it only falls depressingly short when compared to the masterpiece of the original. The gameplay is invigorating and exciting, and it's a fun time all in all.
_childDocuments_.name: Blasphemous 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first one, this is a pretty cool metroidvania with some unique qualities but I just can't recommend it without caveats. First the good: the very weird and disturbing religious tone is still awesome and the graphics are amazing.The combat starts out a bit slow, but it gets fast and fun as you level up. Discovering secrets and new paths is fun. Sometimes you are stumped about where to go next however, but that's how it goes in a metroidvania.The bad: everything feels just a bit worse than in the first game. Story-wise, less is more guys! The first one gave you some space to experience the world in a good pace. This one there is a lot of exposition.The combat is a bit more tedious as enemies feel very spongy. I ended up basically skipping entire screens of enemies as it was just not fun to hack away at them for minutes. In the endgame it improves a lot but that's no excuse, I should want to kill everything that moves because it's fun throughout the whole game, like in the first one! And finally the difficulty: It is all over the place. It felt much easier than the first one at first. Bosses were better as it usually only took 4-5 tries to figure them out, which is the sweet spot for me. But then the final boss has such a large spike that I actually just lost interest in the whole ending. It is not fun to grind a boss for half an hour inching away at his life with fully upgraded gear. If you like this kind of games you will have some fun, but it left a sour taste in my mouth for sure.

The gameplay loop is super addictive and exploring always brings something new, characters are all super unique, weapons feel incredible and movement is fluent and fast. _childDocuments_.review: GOTYBoth this, and B1 are this weird ephemeral sort of game that I can't truly put into words why I love them so. It's the atmosphere and the music and the combat and the voice acting and everything ever put into a game. I could go on and on about every perfect step that both games in this series took.The soundtrack for this game is genuinely beautiful, I'm even willing to argue perfect in every sense. Every area was a new song, and a new 5 minute break from me to just sit there and be marveled at every single instrument and note.The visual designs of enemies never missed once, it was all clear, and crisp. I could tell when they were attacking and the visual cue of an attack was better telegraphed than any 3D combat game I could think of.The voice acting is amazing. Both English and the native Spanish dubs are amazing. It all just sounds so well and each voice a perfect match to what I see on the screen.My only real complaint is maybe the lack of *meaning* behind the weapons in this game. B1 had this insane lore behind the most basic sword that the Penitent One had, made even deeper with the DLC. B2 on the other hand just gives us 3 weapons, and beyond the text blurbs they have in the inventory, and the statue carvings you can get relating to each weapon, it seems not much was actually imporant about them. They're *just* weapons, as compared to B1's Mea Culpa being this insane piece of craftwork that I get even really explain without spoiling that games story.It doesn't seem really fair to compare a game to it's predecessor, but with a game that is a direct sequel like this, it's warranted, at least a little. It's still amazing though, all of it is.10/10 on all fronts

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this was mostly fun though I did like the first game better overall. The level design and most bosses, I actually thought were well made. It seemed easier, especially with the right build (altar piece stuff) - but it was also way more grindy because the martyrdom drops were so random and you needed them for everything like unlocking pieces, upgrading weapons and that was mostly luck based. Because you couldn't see the next upgrade in the path so you might get unlucky and get something you didn't need.Eviterno was an awful boss at that and I'm by far not the only one with that opinion. His attacks are difficult to read because you can barely see him moving anything and his movements all look almost the same. And then he has a ton of health. But the real rage inducing thing is the atrociously easy P1 which still simply takes a long time due to his teleportation mechanic. And then you have to sit through the stupid cutscene. Just start the boss fight in P2 after you have beaten P1 for the love of the Miracle.Also, please do strongly consider removing contact damage from enemies which have regular attacks. It made group fights so stupid to get through. And if you could just unlock the prie dieu port much earlier, that'd be great. Because that single ability made the games about three times more enjoyable.You did improve Blasphemous a ton as you kept working on it, so hopefully the contact damage grievance most people seem to share about the 2nd game might be addressed in the future with maybe a story content DLC. Because I'd really like a NG+ run with more content and a few changes and improvements. The game was pretty good already but it could be truly great like the final version of the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS REVIEW WILL BE EDITED THROUGHOUT MY PERSONAL GAME PLAY As someone that went into this game with the intention to 100% it and being obsessed with the first game, things are not looking good. Speaking on only an hour of game play, so far I am not loving this nearly as much as the first game. The best way I can list my grievances is to, well, make a list. To simplify, it's going to consist of a couple subjects and I'll start with things changed from the previous game, and things that were just straight up removed.Changes>Cartoonish drawn cutscenes that have a jarringly different style from the game itself>Unique executions are nonexistent for some new enemies with most of them sharing the same animation >Movement has a very weird and flighty low-grav feeling while feeling like you have way less mobility>Voice acting and dialogue quality seems to have plummeted drastically compared to the first game where each line felt like it was given by the character and not just someone playing a character>Parrying enemies now has layered timing beyond just one result of a riposte. If done at the incorrect time, it'll only do a partial parry, resulting in you being pushed anywhere between 1 to 5 inches across the screen, this new addition has has resulted in my being kicked out of a room an INNUMERABLE amount of times if the parry timing is slightly off, only a perfect parry will allow you to do a riposte.Removed>Air Impulse/Latern Jumping has been removed from the game! This was my favorite combat/movement mechanic from the previous game and its removal is tragic to me

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 1 was a great game, good bosses, music, atmosphere, etc.  Blasphemous 2 is an even better game and I love it just as much as Blasphemous 1.  The Game Kitchen really learned from their first game because everything feels so much better in 2.  Better and harder bosses, better level design, outstanding area music and art, the npcs were just as creepy and otherworldly as the first game and felt alive (in Spanish, not sure about English).  My only complaint was the finishers were pretty limited, there were probably 3 unique ones total, 2 of them on 2 different big type enemies, and 1 on the candle guys from the first game.  Not a big deal, and the first game added more finishers in later updates so I'm sure the devs will deliver here.  If you loved Blasphemous 1, or you love Metroidvania's definitely play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't too crazy about the original Blasphemous, so I was a bit hesitant to check out this game.  I'm glad I did.  This is an improvement in every way on the original, and the result is an excellent, well-crafted metroidvania that is enjoyable the whole way through.  The bosses are all great, if a bit on the easy side for the most part, the areas are fun to traverse and explore to find secrets, and the puzzles and platforming challenges to get extra experience points, quest items, and other upgrades are satisfying to complete.  As with Blasphemous 1, this game has lore for each item and spell you pick up if you like diving deep into that and getting some background on the story and world.  I have no big criticisms of the game, I think it's excellent at what it tries to do, and overall a very strong metroidvania that anyone who enjoys the genre would like.  There are a few nitpicks I have, such as some animations not playing properly, the music acting oddly at points, disappearing for a bit and then coming back in all of the sudden, and the presence of one major glitch that made it so I had to redo a combat trial for one sidequest twice, but it seems to be a decently rare occurrence,  so most people probably won't have issues with it.  None of these detract from the overall experience in any way that would ruin it, although the glitch can make it a bit tedious on the off chance it does happen.

_childDocuments_.review: I really felt Blasphemous 1 captured the vibe of a sad, aged catholic lady who had a bunch of dark, perverted secret ideas and shame. (I'm not a writer).So far *this* game feels like an action/cartoon game. _childDocuments_.review: Blasphemous 2 is one of those sequels that's two steps forward, two steps back.  The presentation's great as ever; nice animation, good music, very moody ambiance, nice sound effects, the fantastic Spanish audio included from the start.  The minute to minute gameplay is well improved from the first; the Penitent One controls more smoothly, the new movement mechanics are well implemented.  The new weapon trio is great; outside of changing the early game and affecting what secrets and paths you can take contingent on your starting choice, they all have different styles, and let you lean into the parry-and-counter style of the first game, a rapid fire high risk/reward dual wield set, or just ignore blocking entirely and crush things with the censer (which I used for almost the entire game and adored).  Letting you equip a "quick" prayer and a bigger effect together mean a lot less menuing to deal with situations you encounter.  Splitting character "equipment" into altarpieces for general character customization and the rosary beads for general resistances and bonuses is a good way to handle things.  Some of the nice QoL features from the first game's DLCs also show up and make things smooth going as well, like altar teleporting.  B2 is a lot of fun to just run around and fight in.That said, while the specific moment to moment gameplay is a marked improvement, the game also falls apart compared to the first game in some fairly significant and damaging ways.  After a strong opening act, Blasphemous 2 goes extremely linear in a fashion that doesn't live up to the first game and takes a lot of the joy of exploration from getting new tools and upgrades away.  The boss design is fairly uninspired.  A lot of the general creepy religious-monkey's-paw aesthetic and design from the first game is lacking; the NPCs mostly feel like retreads or just imitations of the first game, which means that the sequel doesn't have that same level of oppressive dread that kept the first game going (the animated cutscenes, which are good quality animation, also feel like they're working at odds to the pixel artwork style).  Quest design is abysmal; it really doesn't matter what choices you make in dealing with NPCs, because at the end of the day you can just go buy the other quest reward(s) you didn't get based on your handling and get everything anyway (the only missables I'm aware of are a bonus health/fervor upgrade for dealing with the related NPCs in a specific fashion).  And while the first game's alternate ending (pre-DLC) was somewhat esoteric to unlock, it also didn't force you to effectively 100% the map to get either.I'm hopeful they can elevate Blasphemous 2 with DLCs like the first game, which ended in a far, far stronger place than it began.  I still mostly enjoyed my time with Blasphemous 2, and would recommend it for Metroidvania fans or folks who liked the aesthetic of the first game but bounced off the extreme difficulty curve (or the spiked pits), but as it stands right now I'm going to be far more inclined to go do another NG+ cycle of the first game than play through Blasphemous 2 again.
