_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY like the overall presentation and atmosphere of the game, really dig the visuals, but boy does it feel confused, rushed and plainly unfinished. Despite taking only few hours to complete, only first part of the game feels fairly polished, well-paced and properly designed, with puzzles, despite being fairly easy, making sense and requiring at least some effort to complete. But as soon as you're out of the apartment block, the game turns into a randomly placed monster murder simulator with shockingly bad melee combat, shocking easy ranged combat and shockingly easy progression blockers - I just refuse to call using 3 close objects in a row a puzzle.Melee combat is a travesty, it's broken and somehow both easy to abuse and can screw the player over at the same time. Sometimes you hit twice with one attack. Sometimes the axe doesn't play its attack animations. Some attacks in combo take much longer, but deal as much damage. Some attacks appear to have wider range, but they don't. All attacks feel like hitting enemies with wet noodles. Sometimes you can spam the enemy to death without allowing them to retaliate. Sometimes they manage to put a hit in after your every attack. Things just happen. Stomp is also very hard to aim properly.Thankfully, there's ranged combat. And the game showers you with so much ammo, that there's honestly no reason to use melee at all, there's more than enough to kill everything in the game twice over. Same goes for healing items, on Intended difficulty there's way too many sprays. In general shooting feels fine, but shotgun needs a proper rework: it sounds weak and quiet, somehow feeling weaker than Mica's revolver.There's also an unlimited lighter to burn the bodies, which makes me question its inclusion to the game at all, considering very limited backtracking. It really feels like it's there just to waste your time with menu navigation and finicky corpse hitboxes.Enemy variety is very limited, but considering short length of the game it's fine. Problem is, with how broken combat system is, I never even got to see how non-standard enemies attack. In only scripted scene where the game pits you with a larger enemy in melee range, it got spammed with guitar without landing a hit on me. Another problem is the dogs, they're outright broken. I'm not sure they even have any attack animations, they just keep running into walls.But the biggest problem is that monsters never feel threatening, and the static noises they create make them easy to anticipate during exploration.Then there's a story, which attempt at human drama is irreparably ruined by scary flashing screens, evil laughing mutants and spooky robot voices on the other side of the phone. That's where confusion part begins, because despite creator clearly respecting Silent Hill, the game suffers from things that made modern horror games so despised by the fans of classic survival horror games. Loud monsters crashing through walls are not scary. Why even resort to cheap scares when you clearly understand how to create properly haunting atmosphere, like inside the Church?Also, I have major issues with heart lock puzzle and sewers area of the game. Despite being set in an Orwellian near-future pandemic setting, Mica goes through the sequences that make no sense in such a world. Sure, crucified body with a glowing heart lock and flowers growing inside its chest make a striking scene, but... why? Engine with 4 hands (which were invisible due to a bug, I presume) demanding 4 beating hearts... why? If the answer is "Red Tree did it", then you should probably explain why Red Tree does nothing of that sort before and after the Sewers until the very end of the game. Games like Silent Hill and SIGNALIS can get away with surreal moments like this due to their strong reliance on symbolism and dream elements. Hollowbody doesn't really have that, it feels more grounded in reality and any kind of surrealism feels very out of place. Same goes for final boss, all monsters in the game are clearly local population affected by the Red Tree or whatever created it (AI nano machines mentioned in one newspaper?), yet the final boss is a giant spider... why?And then, there are bugs, glitches, and game's overall lack of polish. Blatant invisible walls everywhere, camera clipping through walls, music not looping properly, enemies without a head dropping one on death, dead enemies appearing alive when you revisit locations, fisheye shader being broken in the corners during signal cutscenes, Mica playing exit animations meters away from the entrance on transition, weird mirrored white textures with black text on some buildings, floor/water in final boss room missing, camera locking up looking behind Mica after going into inventory during the chase sequence, the list goes on and on. These things ruin the only things the game does really well - immersion, visuals, environments and music.It's great that the developer is actively patching the game, and even adding more content, and I'd love to give it another go in a year or two, when it's updated and patched up, but in its currents state it's just not really worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those cases where I'd like a "maybe" option. The atmosphere and ambient music is fantastic up to a point, but to me it couldn't carry the experience by itself. I didn't find the monster design to be particularly unique or interesting. The final enemy you encounter in particular felt like a creature you'd see in a completely different game and was very jarring. The difficulty of the intended mode left me wanting as well. Once I realised how little danger I was actually in, the atmosphere lost its edge. This happens rather early on as well as you're able to run past things quite easily. Yes this is something that happens with most games in the genre, but they usually have something to fall back on to keep you on your toes. Enemies with new and unique behaviours, labyrinthine level design you can get truly lost in, a limited inventory which makes you strategise how to optimise your pathing, more complex puzzles etc. Hollowbody in my opinion has little to none of this.The puzzles are pretty bog standard, the level design is quite plain overall with the best example being front-ended in the apartment building. I was hoping it would expand from there, but it instead becomes more restricted as you progress. The enemies don't do much for me either mechanically and very rarely feel like a threat. In those cases it's usually because I wasn't paying attention.I won't harp on the narrative too much for not wanting to spoil anything so all I'll say is it failed to grip me. I never really got a good sense of the world and what's happened. I never felt particularly connected to the main character either who in one breath would say "oh these poor souls" when looking at a corpse and in another breath would criticise their lack of hygiene in the kitchen. The whole ending felt rushed as well. Rather anti-climactic honestly. I really hate that I didn't enjoy this game. I am glad that it's receiving so much positive feedback from so many people. It just wasn't for me I suppose. Regardless I wish nothing but the best for the devs who made this. Any game that gets shipped is a damned miracle and they should all be very proud of themselves for what they accomplished. I look forward to seeing what they all do next.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is the sort of game that I hate giving a negative review to, because many of its faults come across moreso as a result ambition and the dev's reach exceeding their grasp.  Visually the game nails the PS2 look, and the dilapidated environments are very reminiscent of Silent Hill 2.  Combat is sufficiently serviceable, and going at it with a 2x4 with nails jammed in it is the right blend of clunky, impactcul, and viable that I like to see for melee weapons in survival horror games.The problem is in how Hollowbody's story is the worst kind of impenetrable combined with poor usage of physical space, bad puzzle design, and some very obnoxious backtracking.The game environments are often quite large.  It takes actually quite a bit of legwork before you get to the first real "area" of the game, an apartment building, and many of the identified rooms in said apartment are completely blocked off and  inaccessible.  What rooms that are accessible might only have a some handgun bullets or a medical spray to be found, but between the game's semi-random item placements, the small size of those items, and the overall drab and dark tones of the game environments it can be very easy to miss items.Much of the game beyond the apartment carry on that design philosophy to the detriment of the experience.  This is further compounded by several instances of extreme backtracking, including the fact that, in order for you to get the best gun in the game, the player has to travel from a lategame area aaaaaall the way back to nearly the start of the game.  Heaven help you if you decided to had to then backtrack oncemore because you were doing everything with the keycard too.  Ultimately, the size of the in-game world is to its detriment.Puzzles are also misses far more often than hits.  Due to the corridor-like nature over the overall game world, oftentimes the items needed to advance are near the immediate vicinity of where you need to go and feel more like just something shoehorned in to slow you down and pad out the game.  Puzzles typically come in two flavors: either it's something you pick up that you then use to be able to advance within short notice to keep moving (though there might be used as a piece of some larger puzzle, like using chopsticks to try to get the right power output at a circuit breaker when you have no idea what the actual target amount should be) or you having to run back through the game world again for a noticeable distance.  There is also the infamous sewer section, where there is a completely blatant red herring puzzle that the dev has admitted they threw in just to make the player feel hopeless, overwhelmed, and confused.  The only problem is, at least for me, the game also glitched so that part of that puzzle did not even show up on my screen, which would further increase the likelihood someone would think that it was just a game-breaking bug and give up and stop playing.Lastly I want to talk about the story.  I want to, but unfortunately the entire mess of the narrative is so confusing it's hard for me to really do so.  The opening text crawl talks about a bio-terror attack and the "fall of the Western Cities", and while the actual incident appears to be fairly self-contained (quite literally), some of the word choice (especially about that "fall of the Western Cities" thing) can easily mislead you into thinking the scope of the calamity is far bigger than it actually is.But you play initially as Sasha, some activist trying to get to the bottom of things just outside the walled-off city before she gets attacked by a zombie-like creature, at which point you switch to her presumably SO, Mica who breaks quarantine to go and try to save her.  Going to try to find a loved one is a perfectly solid option for starting a survival horror game, but we don't really get any scenes or dialogue to help flesh out the relationship between Sasha and Mica.  Additionally you don't really get a good sense of what's going on as you play; the game beats you over the head about how this megacorp that moved in and gentrified a fairly destitute town didn't really fix anything and may have either dug up something spooky or done spooky tests on people in the area but the details about that never really come into focus.  At least not without doing the absolutely bonkers backtrack-fest secret questline with the keycards and the terminal, and my patience with the game was gone by that point.If you know what you're doing, you can leave holes in the player's understanding of the circumstances of a game and still not undermine their actual enjoyment.  Games like Signalis and Lone Survivor are excellent examples of having a fairly clear emotional arc even when core details of the game's narrative go unexplained.  You get to know the characters very well.  Unfortunately Mica just... really doesn't have great character moments even in spite of having a few little narrative vignettes and potentially even a companion who will follow her along through the entire game.  You'd think having someone around to talk to and be a prompt for exposition to the player would mean that Mica would be well-positioned to be fleshed out but I essentially know nothing about her by the end of the game.  Her relationship with Sasha remains "this is the person I care about and love".Heck, it's funny how I understand more about Sasha's motivations and desires from the few minutes of playing as her than in the hours of playing as Mica... all because in her brief section she DOES talk to her friend and do a pretty good job of laying out what she was doing and why she was doing it for reasons I can understand.Get it on sale if you really want to give it a try.  It's clear the dev had a lot of ideas for this game but I don't think they really work out well in exectuion.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: They nailed the visual and sound design. The atmosphere and  cannot be denied. Unfortunately as a game it's rather... hollow. There's loads of positive reviews praising these good points, so I'm going to focus on the bad points that ultimately determined my recommendation.Puzzles are few, and brainless.  This is pretty standard, unfortunately. "Puzzles" basically consist of a lock and key which are almost immediately adjacent. It's not thoughtful design. Weirdly, puzzles practically disappear halfway in, and some even appear unimplemented. Combat is blehhh. Clunky, but also too easy. The same handful of enemies repeated and they are all easy to handle. Always have plenty of ammo, so just blast away indoors, and easily run around them outdoors. One great aspect of survival horror games is replaying and optimizing the heck out of them. Planning routes and doing challenge runs. I love doing this on the older RE titles. But in Hollowbody, the puzzles and enemies being so trivial, it doesn't feel like there's much for the player to polish.The voice acting was respectable, certainly for an indie game. Unfortunately the voice acting couldn't make up for how inane and amateurish the writing was, or how underdeveloped the story is. There is nothing that drives the narrative forward, I would forgive you for forgetting why Mica was in this city at all. None of the back story is really explained, you don't get a clear picture of what the monsters are, the game does nothing with it's futuristic sci-fi setting. It's incredibly thin. The documents and radio signals are basically "Things are getting bad here! The corporation is evil!" without details or reasons.I didn't exactly hate it, because the PS2-esque survival horror  was done well, and it's pretty incredible one person apparently did the graphics, music, and sound effects. But the game clearly needed a team to flesh it out and deliver on the concept. I've never played Silent Hill, it's primary inspriation, but it reminds me of Rule of Rose, which also had stellar atmosphere, little exposition, and clunky gameplay. The difference is, Rule of Rose had good storytelling and maintained tension throughout the game.Unfortunately this just isn't worth full price to me. If you're hungry for old school survival horror, wait for a sale.

But the worst thing of all: the writing is pretty bad. The main antagonist of the game - who you have contact with frequently - is an annoying edgelord who can't seem to shut up when I just want to save the game. Once I reached the end, I was sure that I had reached the bad ending. However - spoilers - unlike what the game seems to suggest (by naming your ending), there is only really one ending. The other one is a gimmick which did not add anything to the story or changed it in any meaningful way. _childDocuments_.review: I'd like to begin by saying that it is a  achievement for one person to finish a game of this caliber, especially since Nathan worked on it for only three years. I certainly couldn't have done that! In that regard, this is a fantastic example of the dedication of one person.However, I don't feel this game works for me. I'm a big fan of the genre, Signalis and Silent Hill 2 are some of my favorite ever games, so I had high hopes for Hollowbody. The game certainly evokes the PS2 aesthetic, and the low-poly models are nice and simple. Mica's design is genuinely wonderful, and the Blade Runner-esque tech throughout (especially the UI) are a delight.This retrotech future aesthetic  a little threadbare, more style than anything else. It works well in giving Hollowbody a specific vibe, but I feel relies too much on knowledge of specifically the Blade Runner films to hint at the larger world. No puzzles directly interact with future tech, instead using simple fuses or power redirection, or figuring out the combination of a keypad safe. One could change this setting to the modern day, or the early 2000s, and not have to change much. Despite wall-mounted videophones existing, a lovely bit of retrotech, you still save through conventional dialup or pay phones. The videophones only exist as set dressing.Speaking of the phones, Hollowbody isn't content to hint at its secrets, instead taking every opportunity it can to directly discuss them. The phone conversations Mica has once you hit a save room are  blunt and straightforward. I actually laughed aloud once the voice on the other end essentially discussed exactly what was going on, without any real nuance or thematic veiling. .  there something haunting her past, which this story forces her to engage with? I have no idea. She's just looking for her girlfriend.Really, all we know about Mica is that she's (maybe?) a private investigator (she has a gun? I think she's a PI?), having worked in a bar previously, and is in a relationship with Sasha (who is referred to as 'her friend' at some points, which was awkward and perhaps unintentionally implied a 'gals being pals' rhetoric).We have so little time to get to know Mica, or really, anything at all. Three of the main areas (the apartments, sewers, and station) all clearly evoke their Silent Hill inspirations, but there's remarkably little to do inside them. The apartments in particular felt like a bit of a drag, and a few of the empty units could probably have been removed.As a brief aside, I do genuinely like the . However, even these were slightly too open, and I found I was easily able to dodge basically every enemy that wasn't in an entirely enclosed space.I don't necessarily mind the game being short, but there's so little time to linger and really get to know anything. There's a single NPC in the game, who only serves to affect your ending. . I know nothing about this man, have no idea why he's in the game at all, .And, really, I think that's my main complaint. You can finish a run in 3-5 hours, which isn't bad, but there's so little going on and most of it is references to Hollowbody's inspirations instead of actually using them in an interesting way. .On the topic of bugs, there's quite a lot of them. I don't hold this against the game, again it's only one dev. It does slightly mar the experience, however. Perhaps my favorite one was, again, the , where on BOTH playthroughs I seemingly stumbled onto the way out without really knowing why. I believe there's some intentional spatial ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to disorient the player, however this caused me to completely bypass the  puzzle in my first playthrough.I do, however, slightly hold it against the game that, every time I moved while aiming, and released the aiming button, Mica awkwardly jerked back into her default standing animation. I'm honestly kind of astonished this is still in the game, but I am not a 3D game dev and I can imagine working with 3D models is a nightmare.On the topic of difficulty, this game is VERY easy. Ammo and health pickups abound. Even on the hardest difficulty, I had 30+ ammo for both the revolver and shotgun. I accidentally got the secret ending because I'd only used two repair sprays (and could have easily done a no-hit run if I tried for it). Even on that third difficulty, I never felt the need to actually ration my ammo, either easily running past enemies or gunning them down before they ever got close.I don't have much else to say. The documents and signals all feel somewhat arbitrary, apart from the ones directly hinting at puzzle solutions. In other games, they evoke the main themes or hint at supernatural contexts, but none of Hollowbody's really do. They're all portraits of human suffering in light of corporate power, which is ultimately something of a background detail. Puzzles are largely fine and functional, but many don't evoke anything more than vague gesturing toward Silent Hill strangeness. The  puzzle is interesting, but... doesn't hint at anything. It's just a creepy puzzle.I can say I'd be interested in a sequel, perhaps with a separate writer coming in to tighten the core themes and better engage with larger concepts. As it is, Hollowbody is perhaps a fitting name, given my experience with it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a love-letter to , and even if it can't quite escape the orbit of its inspirations, it's still an impressive little horror title.The pitch is a familiar one, if one with a few wrinkles. In the not-so-distant cyberpunk future, a woman named Mica has lost her friend (quite likely her lover, though it's unclear), Sasha, in the abandoned exclusion zone outside the oceanic city, Aeonis. The exclusion zone houses an old city of tenement housing which was bombarded from orbit decades earlier after the outbreak of some kind of biological contagion; against all good sense, Mica breaches the border of the zone, and thus the player enters the Survival Horror, as the saying goes.The faire on display is delightfully old-school, and long-time fans of survival horror games, especially the aforementioned  series, will slide into the familiar rhythms of gameplay without any fuss. From the systematic exploration of spaces to managing a limited pool of resources to even the option to toggle on tank controls,  revels in the game-flow and mechanics of yesteryear. In fact, I may even suggest that new players try out tank controls before settling on the default option; many of the fixed camera angles feel designed for tank controls in-mind explicitly.Serious praise needs to be given to the game's atmosphere, too, which I can't praise enough. The droning ambience and rhythmic beats that seamlessly fade in during combat evoke Akira Yamaoka without feeling like they're trying to copy his work note-for-note. Similarly, the game's art-direction nails the assignment; the rainy, fog-filled streets drip with menace and hint at the horrors of years past; in its best moments,  feels like the PC port of an older PS2-era game, and I mean that in the most sincere, most enthusiastic way possible. If other indie developers take nothing else from this title, I hope more designers begin to emulate this particular look. Headware Games deserves all the praise it can get on its aesthetic work here.That said, I have reservations; to begin, the plot never quite boiled beyond a simmer. Put the science fiction components of this story out of your mind;  is ultimately a tone piece, and though it contains many interesting disparate elements, they rarely coalesce. In spite of its unique set-dressing,  could easily have been set in modern England without much change.Paradoxically, the plot itself often seems absentee in its obsession with lore and the past horrors of the exclusion zone; as a result, the game suffers with immediacy, more eager to share old vignettes than to expand Mica's story. At only point near the game's middle do things begin to seriously develop, and this is the closest the game comes to a rising action before its climax an hour or two of gameplay later; my kingdom for some active character development. Between the lack of clear purpose behind the science-fiction elements and the over reliance on both lore-dumps and flashbacks, the plot of  feels under-baked.This is all compounded by the game's rhythm and pacing, which though not bad, definitely reveal the title to be a indie project with limited internal review. In so closely emulating the old  games,  inevitably draws comparison, and frustratingly, its level design mostly feels too open and unfocused. In spite of its survival horror, quasi-dungeon crawling roots, level design never feels better than the apartments in the game's opening half, and though it never falls apart either, wandering down linear streets and running into invisible walls quickly wears out its welcome. Combined with a final boss that introduces new, bespoke mechanics, and it feels like  suffers from a lack of focus.But if I'm being too harsh, let me mitigate my complaints with this statement - the fact that this game was largely developed by one person, Nathan Hamley, makes overlooking some odd design choices extremely easy. Game development is not only hard, and for what's on display here, you'd be forgiven for thinking this was the efforts of a larger team. Instead,  is an auteur project to its core, and in this medium, that's not only surprising but also as impressive as it is artistically fascination.I wish I could say I love , but even in the ways it comes up short, there's no getting around that it's still a damn fine example of survival horror in action; should Hamley choose to continue developing this setting or should he choose to take the lessons learned here to build something more impressive, fans of the genre would be remiss not to at least try out this indie gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a TLDR for the impatient readers: It's great, if you love Ps2 style horror games, go get this one, you'll feel at home again.This is exactly the game it was intended to be, a love letter to early/mid 2000's Ps2 horror games but with a modern touch in some areas. Playtime:I finished my first run on the "intended" difficulty in about 6 hours. But I'm also someone who explores all the areas to make sure I don't miss anything. So depending on your play style in might be 4 to 7 hours if you want to find everything and explore all corners.Presentation:The graphics style is very much Ps2 inspired, but with a crispy edge to things. It does have a very specific moody color pallet that evokes a overall somber feeling, so don't expect a very colorful game. It takes mostly place in a long abandoned UK landscape and town during rainy weather nighttime with a few hints of color and light of whatever home appliances, lights and other powered elements are still functional. And because of that light and color stands out a lot more in the eerie darkness. The inventory and map interface are very well done and ties into the Cyberpunk style of digital imagery and scanning technology you'd expect in a 80's sci fi movie.The game also does a fantastic job with weather effects and rainy moody ambiance. The way lightning lights up certain sights of horror in the right moments makes it feel very cinematic in a more classic style of horror.There's also a large amount of environmental storytelling and the world building is very well done. Not all rooms you visit will be essential to your progress, but are extra spots to help paint a bigger picture and you can choose to exploring everything or focus on your main objective.Gameplay:I was using the standard controls (you can also choose classic tank controls) and it played very smoothly, no problems there. Melee, aiming and shooting is very straight forward with an auto target system so you can focus on timing and movement. There's a familiar set of horror weapons but also some special ones to make things interesting.Puzzles are a nice mix of information gathering, switch flipping, item combining and finding the environmental context after reading a riddle. It fits the Silent Hill-style formula very well in that regard.Storytelling:There's some genuinely good voice acting and writing in this game. It's always refreshing to see horror set in a non-American English speaking setting with different natural sounding accents from corners of the world you don't hear in a game like this very often. This gives the game it's own unique voice rather than repeating the same cliche sounding lines we've heard so many times before. It's something different and this is good. The game tackles some heavy subjects and you will encounter echoes of the past that tell some very sad desperate stories of people who are stuck in dire situations. And like with many horror stories these moments echo things people struggle with in our lives. The main plot also did something that I hoped a modern horror game would do. I don't want to go into details and spoil anything, not even with tags, but what Nath did here made me smile since a lot of horror games follow a specific trope but this game avoids it and there's even a bit of dialog addressing it, if you understand what it's trying to say to the player. The end is also very interesting and you should keep watching at the end.Conclusion:All in all, it's an excellent horror game that is crafted with great care by ONE really passionate developer with a taste for intelligent horror, helped by a great cast of voice actors and artists. And I can't wait to see what new project Headware Games will make next.

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointing game. After playing the demo in a next fest I was looking forward to this a lot. Unfortunately, past what the demo had to offer, the rest of the full game was mostly running past enemies in wide open areas. In these large areas there was little to nothing to do other than walk from point A to point B. After leaving the apartment building you have to run down a long road that leads to a park that is way to empty to be as big as it is. And of course you can just run past almost all of the enemies no problem. But once you get to the very end of the park the game tells you to run back to almost the very beginning of the long road. And of course once you do your business back at the beginning you have to run all the way back to the end of the park.After this you have an actually alright area immediately followed by more of running from point A to point B on another long, wide open road where most enemies pose little to literally 0 threat.Then you go into a really short but inoffensive area only to then have a mediocre gimmick boss fight that is really easy and really short and then the game is over.Unless the ending that I got has me miss out on an actually good final boss fight the game has 1 boss and it isn't very exciting.I'm unsure about the combat since I didn't actually have to do all that much of it. The melee combat felt decent enough but in a patch midway through my playthrough the dev seemed to buff the already reasonably strong melee weapons. Making the already somewhat easy melee combat even easier. I swear I was killing enemies in half the hits I previously was.Because I wanted some level of challenge I pretty much just used melee on the base enemies and gunned down the larger ones and the dogs.I had so much ammo for all my guns because of almost never having to actually use any that even when I used ammo I never had to worry that I might run out.At the end of the game I had sooo much ammo and 9 or 10 heal sprays go unused because even going for melee when I didn't need to was to easy.I started NG+ on hard mode to see if anything was different and it was mostly the same from what I have played so far.Enemies do more damage but seem to have the same health and if there where anymore enemies out in the street/park I couldn't tell and I swear there where FEWER enemies in the apartment building.The main difference on hard is using the lighter to burn bodies like in the remake of RE1.This so far seems unimportant since whereas you may go through some rooms half a million times in RE1. HB is really linear and doesn't require much backtracking for much of anything aside from 1 secret note and 1 secret weapon.Honestly most of the game was pretty boring. I love survival horror and was really looking forward to this game since playing its demo. But this just isn't it. I think for me to give the game a positive review hard mode is gonna have to pick up sooner rather than later.While the dev has made efforts to improve upon issues and fix bugs I'm not confident my problems with the game can be fixed by changing numbers. The game is fundamentally flawed in it's boring levels and how little to do there is in so many of them.I'd give Hollowbody a 5ish out of 10 as it is right now. there isn't anything offensively bad, but man I just did not have fun with most of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a frustrating game of threatening to do something interesting. With exception of some of its level design, it almost never does so. If you're expecting hand crafted interesting rooms to explore with some weird thing to give you some sense of dread for daring to explore and find it like the og Silent Hills, you'll get only part of that. The rest of the time, you get long, drawn out practically straight line recreations of a modern British town with some scifi nubbins and cars and black biomass dotted around. Otherwise, average British town circa now.Hollowbody also frustratingly does not much at all with its scifi setting, with the exception of how the main character gets to where they are and one puzzle that tangentially uses the ID system for corpses, it could be changed to modern day setting and nothing in the story would change. The notes, which there are plenty, do almost all the heavy lifting of conveying this takes place somewhere in the future as the story and gameplay certainly doesn't.The writing itself is boring and says all it says in the first couple lines of a scene and then just keeps saying more. Over the course of the game, there are several phone calls with an entity that, for some reason, the main character keeps indulging until nearly the end of the game. The content of these calls is also to just watch as the main character gets goaded by simple childish mocking almost over and over about "what they did" or a phone call calling her a murderer over and over to pad the time. Additionally, the writer either doesn't know what a direct address comma is or hates the idea of them, as every time someone calls out a name (this happens often), it is never given a comma before or after.The notes are the highlight and are realistically written with the right kind of fluff that gives a better understanding of the world at the time and conveys that these notes had a purpose for people in the world, not just the player. There are some badly written notes, a newspaper article stands out as if it was written by a middle schooler, and some posters of nothing that's not apparent are used to unnecessarily pad out the notes too.However, Hollowbody does have some flashes of greatness and understanding of the horror in Silent Hill. An instance of exploring two houses in the British streets is a particularly fun sequence with an extremely well done jump scare. And the sewer level greatly pulls the rug out from under your feet with what it throws at you after collecting the "keys". But again, these highlights are in the middle of long drawn out running around straight line streets that offer zero interesting things to observe or find other than the same 5 classified corpses. There's crashed cars. wow. Biomass. cool. Anything else? nope. So if you do play, just do yourself a favor bee line it to the main objective.Gameplay is also clunky, but passable as it's fairly easy. You shoot the gun, you swing the stick. Hit the thing, stomp the thing down. Not much to it. There's one boss fight that introduces a new mechanic, and that's over in like a minute. I do wish the puzzles got more difficult, but actually get easier as the game progresses. The one exception is the sewer level where the level is the puzzle. If only the entire game were like that.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review by saying I appreciate the work and effort that went into Hollowbody. Being a solo developer and creating something of this scale is impressive and that shouldn't be forgotten. I bought this game for my partner, as he's a big fan of old school Survival Horror, and all of the pre-release info on the game felt really promising.And there are some great moments - The sewers beginning to loop on the player, the UI that aims to capture a cybernoir aesthetic & the voice acting really works. The starting Apartment Building also felt very Silent Hill, with various floors to explore, puzzles to solve & a more non-linear approach to progression.But the moment you leave the apartment, the game becomes this linear romp through very forgettable environments. It never hits the same high as those opening moments, and areas like the Train Station and the city streets just don't feel as complex or interesting as a result. The best Survival Horrors lean into the Metroidvania genre of level design and interconnectivity, of which Hollowbody just doesn't seem to grasp.The only boss fight in the game being the final fight, and it relying on an entirely different mechanic instead of allowing the player to use their weapons collected across the game, also feels like a big missed opportunity. We were playing with a PS4 controller, but for some reason the game never mapped the detonator to a button, so I had to use the middle mouse while my boyfriend controlled with the controller.The camera also feels too sluggish - When you turn, it takes the camera a few moments before it turns to follow Mica, when I think having it turn with her at a quicker pace would feel far more comfortable. Hollowbody feels like a game that has a ton of potential, a ton of great ideas and worldbuilding, but doesn't quite know how to fit the pieces together to create a replayable experience. So while I want to support the developer, I can't, based on the playtime of my partner & I, recommend this game in it's current form. It just feels unfinished.But I urge the dev to continue creating games, because this is a great stepping stone & first experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay... honestly when I saw this game announced... I was already hyped. Little did I know how in love with this game I would be. I had to do it in two streams because sadly I'm not a full time content creator and have to work a regular job... but I literally thought about this game the entire day while I was at work.  This game is a nostalgic masterpiece. It really dives deep back into the late 90's early 2000's era of Survival Horror. It leans more towards the "Silent Hill" side than the "Resident Evil" side... which I of course love because I'm a huge "Silent Hill" fanatic. The game is solid... easily the front runner for me when it comes to my choice for "Game of the Year" in this genre. It'll be really hard for any game to come out to push this one out of my top spot. Not only is this a trip down memory lane... but it's a game that was crafted with love... and you can tell that while you're playing it. So much has went into this game... so much time... so much effort... so much thought. It's one of those games that really shines forth with the "gamers don't care about graphics"... because so many games focus on looking so hyper realistic that they miss the core reason why we play these games... the story being told. I beat the game on "Intended" difficulty my first time through... I'm fully intending to do a second run through on the hardest difficulty now that it's unlocked. Would I recommend this game to other "horror" game enthusiasts?? 100%... with so much praise and assurance that they're going to love it too. Is the $16.99 asking price fair?? Are you kidding?? This game could've literally sold for $29.99 and I still wouldn't have been upset with the value I got for the purchase... $16.99 is extremely generous from the Devs... and shows you that the creation of this game wasn't just for a money grab. They wanted to put out a game that they new all of us fans of the older "survival horror" genre would enjoy. Honestly... I'm hoping that this kind of steers the horror genre in a different direction. We have enough "P.T." and "Visage" clones out there... not to mention the onslaught of "Survival" games that have hit the market. "Hollowbody" has done one thing here that most of the games released in the last year or so haven't (apart from a few like "Song of Horror" and "Tormented Souls")... and that's "Make Survival Horror Great Again"!!!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of classic Resident Evil or Silent Hill games, Hollowbody is a must-play. It immediately pulls you in with its eerie atmosphere, the story telling, and top-notch audio design. This game has heart!The art style is incredible, and knowing it's all made by one person shows just how much passion and dedication went into it. I truly wish the developer success and can't wait to see more from them in the future.One cool feature is after you beat the game, you unlock an FPS mode for New Game+. It changes the whole experience. While the first playthrough wasn't super scary, replaying the game in FPS mode had me on the edge of my seat. It felt like a completely different game — intense and thrilling! Plus, in FPS mode, you get to see the environmental details up close. The attention to detail, the texture work — it's like the world itself is telling a story. The dilapidated corridors, graffiti on the walls, and a lot of other details — it's pure love.That said, there are a couple of things that could be improved:The futuristic setting is really intriguing but mostly appears in cutscenes. I wish there were more gameplay moments exploring the world, maybe meeting up with characters like Tax or even a flashback sequence to flesh out the environment.The NPC following you throughout the game reduces the isolation factor, which dampens the scare factor a bit. Being alone would have made it scarier.After the apartments, the pacing and level design fall a little short. It feels like you just keep moving in one direction without much challenge.But honestly, these are minor things, and they don’t ruin the game at all. I’m sharing this feedback in the hope the developer can improve on these things in future projects. Hollowbody shows a lot of ambition, and I can’t wait to see what comes next!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: If one were to evaluate this just as a solo developed game, this is a very impressive project.If one were to evaluate this as a $16.99 product, this is a big letdown.The start of the game builds up the tension and mystery wonderfully and then does nothing with it. The initial zone, , loses its intrigue and spook factor within a matter of minutes. And I think it might have to do with the lack of actual threats. Combating or evading enemies can be done half-asleep. They pose little to no threat, even on the harder difficulties. And there's almost no variety there either. But the combat isn't really why I and many others play horror games. Story is a massive draw and what stays with people after the game is done. So how does Hollowbody's story go? Not bad. But severely lacking. There's two stories, the story of your character and their journey, and the story of the wrecked British city you travel through. I enjoyed both of them. But I got so little of both. I felt starved to know more about our main character Mica, more about her friends Tax and Sasha and their overall place in this world. I wanted to know more about what they did, what the world was like, and more about what they wanted to do. But we get very little there. I could sum them up in a sentence: Sasha wants to learn what happened, Tax and Mica want to find and help Sasha. Nothing else to discover or connect with.The world reveals more about what happened in the ruined exclusion zone through discovering documents and radio signals which give you a flash into the past. But they only give you some insights into the ruined zone when the world itself seems to be on the brink of collapse. And the insights you get into the zone are bare-bone and leave me with more questions than answers.So overall I can't recommend this game. There's a lot of potential that's not acted upon and $16.99 is way too high an asking price for what is delivered.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect, there still needs to be a bit of polishing done to make it truly sing, but as a project made mostly by a solo developer?  It's incredible.  Atmospheric, intriguing, terrifying...  It's worth picking up if you have any love for the PS2 era of horror games. My biggest issues are the strange visual glitches in the menu and the janky physical attacks with your weapons.  They're all well animated, but the varying attacks can be frustrating to time.  The first three SHs for instance allowed you to tap for weak strikes and hold for strong ones, I think lifting that would help.  And the item menu can be awkward to navigate.  Holding down the directional button doesn't shift through items quickly, so getting from one end of the inventory to the other can be a chore.As for the good, oh...  It's a stellar example of storytelling told through implications.  Piecing together what's happening, what happened, slowly over the course of the entire game was a true treat.  It doesn't explicitly tell you what's happening, you just have to figure it out through context clues and word choice and that's amazing.  This feels like a missing Silent Hill game from a cyberpunk universe and that's just so, so cool to me.Please, if you're on the fence at all over this, give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a really cool game that I was very excited for a while and bought day one. I think the game is still really cool after beating it, but I can't really recommend the game overall. It feels like it's emulating Silent Hill without really understanding why exactly those systems really worked in the first place. It also didn't really deliver on my expectations with the cyberpunk setting, because despite the world being set in a cyberpunk future, the game itself is just another run through a regular dilapidated city, fit with a few retro appliances like CRTs and video phones. The bottom line though is it's not very scary, and has pretty bad combat that boiled down to mashing a single button. I'm not entirely sure why there were any guns in the first place, and I'm also no sure why we can get more than one melee weapon. There's also no enemy variety aside from maybe a few dogs to break up the regular zombies. It all got boring very quick, and the boredom with the combat just made the game even less scary than it already was. I understand a horror game can have less than stellar combat and still deliver a really immersive and terrifying atmosphere (look at silent hill), but Hollowbody simply does not deliver. If you just want a short form horror game for a good price, I still believe this game is perfectly serviceable for a one person developer and recommend giving it a try. But if you're familiar with a lot of horror games, I cannot recommend this. This game will not do anything very different or interesting. The setting could've set it apart alone, but it's underutilized so I don't recommend buying it based on that.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to mess around with the harder difficulty and dungeon crawler mode to see if my opinion somewhat changes but I doubt it since I have quite the core issues with this game.Hollowbody starts out promising enough. Unfortunately no...After the first area you only have to run around the overworld 2 times. The second dungeon you get is just a maze with no puzzles and the third one is just way too linear and light on puzzles again. And that's it. You can finish this game in 4 hours on your first time. Enemy variety is also lacking and they don't pose much of a threat. Hollowbody also tries way too hard to be Silent Hill 2 (2001) at times, losing more from it's identity in the process.There are certainly things to like about this game but overall the experience is unremarkable and not worth the asking price. Play some other indie survival horror games or go back and emulate some of the ps1/ps2 era classics instead.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are itching for a game that will make you remember playing Silent Hill, then fine by me, go ahead, but there isn't much to leave a lasting impression like Signalis and a couple other recent games were way more successful at. By the time I had finished playing all that I had to say was "Wow, I played Silent Hill 20+ years ago. Next game." Searching for a lost significant other: check. Radio messages: check. Abandoned town: check. A complete lack of self-identity: check.Unfortunately, the plot is not interesting and the narrative is pastiche at its best. There's ZERO meaningful development for the main character and everything is dumped in the last five minutes of the game. Early on, you are allowed to make a choice related to a character that at first seems to be very significative, but barely impacted the story or had any effect on the gameplay whatsowhever,  other than a handful of extra dialogue lines for the next three hours and even those felt like an afterthought. However, the voice actors do deserve praise for their work, the acting was decent, if only lacking more interesting lines.I never felt any tension. While the streets of Silent Hill kept you on the edge with a masterful use of ambience, fog and soundtrack, there wasn't much suspense at all to be found in Hollowbody. Everything is somewhat well lit and lacking interesting setpieces, the game could had been greatly improved by simply making everything much darker with a noise filter to make better use of the flashlight. A great amount of my time in Hollowbody was spent crossing empty streets that were as big as football stadiums plus a 95% of locked doors, with plenty of space to run from every single enemy you meet --- from the 4 types I found, the only ones that made me bothered enough to shoot were the dogs that managed to be just a tad bit annoying. There were plenty of dead ends that didn't rewarded the exploration by any manner other than giving me a super dramatic camera angle of rubble and crashed cars.I had a truckload of ammo and restoratives by the time I finished, since there's ZERO situations where you are put in real danger. Melee weapons are a thing, but there's no need to use them either unless you wanna go full psycho beating every single one of those innocent little things that don't pose much of a threat other than screaming "weeeee weeeeeehhh wiigghhhh" while looking pitiful. I was bored waiting for anything scary or freaky to happen, but it never did.All puzzles were really, really easy lacking any form of deeper mechanic. To sum up most of them, the game basicaly holds your hand by locking you in a room with two items then hey, hey psst psssst psssssssssst I WONDER WHERE YOU ARE SUPPOSED TO USE THOSE wink wink wink nudge nudgeThe cyberpunk scenario was nothing but a 2 minute cutscene, it felt both unnecessary and completely underused since the abandoned city you explore got nothing to do with it. Actually, nevermind --- the main character made sure to remind me that this was the future by constantly spewing lines about bathtubs and dirty sinks while exploring an abandoned apartment. My LORD, can you just imagine that people used to SIT INSIDE OF BATHTUBS TO GET CLEAN??? Luckly, she didn't mentioned anything about toilets and seashells.  I do hope that by the year of 2060+ people will have no need to poop anymore thanks to the nanomachines in their intestines. I give Hollowbody a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody serves as proof that it does not take a giant company to create a unique and worthwhile experience, while also standing as a love letter to the 6th's console generation's horror games such as the likes of Silent Hill 2 and 3. Not being without its flaws, primarily that the short playtime doesn't give the game enough time to spread all its themes out to their full potential, the root of the game here is really good! Especially the sound design as well as the voice acting have made this quite enjoyable, even motivating me to start a new game and get all of the three endings. Mica as a protagonist was enjoyable and pretty relatable. She wasn't overly dramatic but always reacts accordingly to the situation while also having to offer some snarky comments about the environment she's in, providing the game with a sense of humor without losing its sense of seriousness. Especially at the end I really rooted for her to find her friend, which given by the short playtime is a feat in itself.My general verdict is that Hollowbody does not redefine the wheel and I am mighty thankful for that. As it stands right now, we have a game here that wants to do one thing and that it does quite well! To find out the whole thing was made by mostly one person inspires me and I sincerely hope that this won't be the last time I'll hear from them. If you like Survival Horror Games, can live with a shorter playtime or are simply nostalgic for the kind of games they made in the early 2000's, Hollowbody is right up your alley and worth the price!Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: By and large, Hollowbody is a solid entry to the Survival Horror genre which takes inspiration from the likes of Silent Hill and other classics of the genre, which for a solo-dev is commendable. You've got your classic formula here such as resource management, fixed-camera angles, and other elements of sadly by-gone era.However, as others have mentioned the game begins to lose pace after the first initial hour or so, replacing the dystopian and grim apartment block with large open streets that are incredibly linear and render the enemy types almost obsolete because you've got so much room to avoid them, and your exploration efforts are greeted with blocked routes despite having an abundance of houses and alleyways that lead to nothing and emptiness. The story aspects never really got any traction either or at least in my view there was missed opportunities. Whilst I won't give anything away, there is a point in Hollowbody where you will naturally think your choices will impact the direction the game will take, but it never leverages it, instead you just have a few additional dialogue lines and a different ending that's it. The enemies whilst initially intimidating are slow walking husks that really don't pose a threat outside of cramped conditions, with the exception of the dog type enemies who were annoying, that from my play-through seemingly spawned from nowhere, (I even reloaded saves to see if I could spot them, and never could). The end "boss" was just shame, I played this on intended difficulty, with the expectation of a big slog at the end to just face something that felt totally out of place and was a cake-walk, I had an absurd amount of heals and ammo at this point as well.Despite it's faults, this is still worth picking up if you're wanting a survival-horror fix but don't expect it to leave you with the same impact such as Signalis. I hope potentially the dev can introduce other segments or additions in the near future, with the intent of replaying this on Punished difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering that this is an indie game, it is quite impressive, but I do have a couple of hangups such as the lacking enemy variety, the not quite stellar story and the clunky movement. However, I found that the atmosphere was quite fitting, so on the whole, it is the quality you might expect from an indie game, therefore a recommendation.  I played with a keyboard, and this takes place in the same setting as , however, the story is completely its own thing.The mainland was abandoned, the United Kingdoms is a ghost town, but Mica must go there, it has been twelve days since Sasha (Mica’s ) has gone missing, and no one is willing to brave the United Kingdoms to save her darling, besides herself. You see in survival horror titles you sometimes have to piece together the narrative yourself, and solve the mystery on your own, and  is no exception, Sasha is there, probably, somewhere, but what happened to this town? What is going on? Or rather, what went down years ago?There are answers, some more explicit than others, and if you have played  you might even start out with a couple of theories, however, that is not a requirement,  is an independent story, all the pieces are within it, you just have to gather newspaper articles, listen to the static left behind by the dead, and scour the town to unlock a computer.This genre is filled with stellar stories, but  manages to be just okay, there is nothing that truly grips me, but it is inoffensive, and calling it bad would be rude and incorrect, so therefore: It has an okay story.There are certainly things I enjoyed about the narrative, the taunting voice on the telephone is one such aspect, it is creepy, especially when it is your only source of companionship, but I am also not completely sold on it, and I am not quite sure why. Perhaps a combination of feeling like it tries too hard, or maybe the narrative contrivance, like, Mica, why do you keep picking up?Questioning it yourself does not make it better if the audience cannot deduce why for themselves. Let us say that she does answer it just to hear another voice… that does not make perfect sense, because there are two routes, and one sees her accompanied by someone throughout, so, she is never  on that route, and the dialogue does not change.I choose to believe that Mica is aware that the telephone saves her progress. Aenois is a cyberpunk city, with certain buildings and cars straight out of , however,  does not take place in Aeonis it takes place in the United Kingdoms, complete with apartment buildings, city blocks, villa streets, and there is even a sewer! Suffice to say that the environments can get repetitive.The enemies are… not actually better, they look creepy, and burnt in a way that might imply radiofrequency radiation, but there is so little variety, and you end up killing so many of them that it gets old, so the main appeal is simply the design implications.However, the monsters have some very jittery movement, creepy moans, and this horrid wheeze that is unsettling, but again, you hear it so often that the novelty passes away.As for the ambient music, I will not complaint, it sets a mood, and it does so brilliantly, it makes abandoned buildings seem haunted and works wonders to build tension. It puts me right there, in the middle of the scene, and it makes it difficult not to be immersed. Unfortunately, there is a bug with the looping, and sometimes you will have this obvious, immersion breaking jump. It is not common, but frequent enough that it might spoil your experience.  As for the voice acting, well, I think it is probably fine for the budget that  had, it is okay, but you easily notice that extreme distress and fright do not come across as intense as they should be doing. I also believe there is an issue with the mixing, but I may be incorrect. It seemed to me that different characters were louder than others, forcing me to adjust my volume on the fly so as to hear what they were trying to say. In this video game, you kill enemies, if you want to, and you do puzzles, that you have to do. It works well,  has logical problems and reasonable solutions, you will never get stuck on something because you are constrained by your sanity, but unfortunately it is a bit too easy.Enemies do not pose much of a threat, even in melee, and most puzzles entail bringing one item to one specific place. I would have enjoyed more interesting problems and encounters, but  is a short title, with a small scope, and all things considered it is an enjoyable experience, however, it does have a couple of issues that I feel are noteworthy.Consider the rest of the review my nagging, or suggestions to consider for future titles.1)	In  you cannot spin around your heel; it is a survival horror title where you cannot spin on your heel, what gives? Ok so you can but tank controls are turned off by default, and movement  it feels awkward and clumsy, there is this really weird forward momentum to turning which makes precise movement more annoying to do, not to mention the sharp turns that happens from a mere tap at the keyboard. 2)	There is also the melee combat, attacks have no forward momentum, what gives? This is actually really annoying cause you have to hug enemies in order to hit them, add to that different attacks with different reaches and different attack speeds you have a system that feels bad to play. I stopped using the second melee weapon because it simply felt less reliable than the terrible starting club. 3)	There is a system in place to burn enemies you kill, if you do not do it a survival horror staple might happen, but it feels severely underbaked. Why have a system like this when we can do it from minute one, and it is not limited in any way? It is simply busywork, something you ought to remember to do, while other titles such as  or  gives weight to it, it adds to those games, while it does not add anything to .4)	Exploration is not rewarding, yes, you do get the secrets, and at one point you can backtrack all the way to the beginning for a new weapon, those things are nice, but they do not outweigh the rest of the game.You mostly progresses through linear corridors with optional paths being either empty or containing one item or maybe a collectible, it is not exciting and I was tempted to just stop exploring.  is at its best in cramped spaces, the apartment building is the best area, and it is the first one you will ever explore, yet even that is filled with empty rooms that feels like a waste of time. 5)	The linear streets have another issue, it is effortless to simple step to the side and run past basically every enemy in the entire game, which is great because I am conserving the ammunition that I will never need to use. 6)	A nitpick, sometimes the game automatically brings up the inventory when you interact with something in the environment and sometimes it does not. Having it consistently open the inventory (or not) would be preferable, the players already know that the solution is an item, so it is only annoying because it is inconsistent.I feel like I need to justify writing all that cause I feel rude,  is a fun game I enjoy it and that is why it sucks when it does not live up to its full potential. A few (or all) of my complaints might be intentional, a part of the artistic vision, but some might not be, either way a customer should be aware of what they are getting themselves into.

_childDocuments_.review: My brain was gleefully counting things that reminded me of Silent Hill and Resident Evil games. Yet at the same time, the setting is very original. Not so long of a story that it outstays it welcome, yet also left me wanting to replay it. I know new game + has some cool little tweaks in it. _childDocuments_.review: I know that survival horrors are supposed to be clunky sometimes. But dear god, this is something else. You see, even if something is intentionally made inconvenient, I still expect it to be . There is close to nothing in Hollowbody that is consistent. You cannot understand if you can walk somewhere, because somtimes you can walk where you don't expect, and sometimes there are invisible walls where you expect them the least.You cannot understand if your melee attack will hit enemy, because sometimes your character does proper range attack, and sometimes she does very short range attack, with the same weapon, without any way for you to understand which attack you get next.You cannot understand if enemy will attack you because they sometimes simply do not telegraph their attacks, and you can take damage immediately just by standing nearby, making it impossible to guess if it is safe to approach the enemy right now (the game also has clarity issues in general, e.g. there are dogs that can charge at you, but, unless you see them, you will never know because they don't make a single sound).I also want to mention camera, because it is definitely not good. I know it is inspired by classic survival horrors, but those classic games still bothered to pick good angles to ensure you always see your character, important objects and ways to other locations. This is not the case of Hollowbody.I do understand that the game is single dev, but I rate experience. And I don't get good experience from the Hollowbody.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game was so close to being great but fell off in many places. A lot of rooms and places just feel useless. A lot of the time they would just be empty. The animations for melee specifically seemed super janky. The story was somehow shallow but also didn't make any sense. Way too many items. I finished the game with around 10 heals, 30 handgun bullets and 15 shells. And one other thing that will probably annoy people that I'm even talking about it but I feel like Sasha and Mica's relationship was queer bait, the way they speak to eachother and Sasha's letter to Mica makes me believe they are girlfriends but Dev got scared and made them friends instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this by saying I think that, from what I've played so far, this game is pretty good. It's a great callback to the PS2 era SH games with fantastic atmosphere and appropriate jank, with a cool futuristic theme thrown in. I'd love to keep playing and it's extremely impressive this is a one-man dev team.However, I've now had the game completely freeze my computer twice, even to where my keyboard, mouse and controller all immediately turn off. The first time was during the intro scenes with the main character, the game hard froze on a loading screen(specifically the loading screen after she gets off the call with the guy in her car). That was annoying but I just rushed through the prologue again and all was well...Until the second time. I was deep exploring the apartment complex, hadn't saved for likely about 15-20 minutes when it hard crashed again. I had just opened the door with the battery acid and was exploring one of the apartments when it happened, for no apparent reason. My computer specs are all fine, drivers are updated, running at 2k on ultra settings at 120fps no problem, no temp issues, stutters, nothing. Everything seems to be fineI can't stand losing progress in games generally speaking, but in a survival horror game where there's no autosaves? I have no wish to continue playing if losing progress is a consistent possibility. I have no plans to refund the game as I really do like it and I want to support the dev, but beware if you get this game right now. Hopefully it's not a common occurence and I just got unlucky, but I'll likely wait for a patch/update all the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody wants to be Silent Hill so badly you’d be forgiven for mistaking screenshots or even brief gameplay footage from the series. The game doesn’t shy away from this fact though. It knows exactly what it is and doesn’t pretend otherwise, and while there are some hard sci-fi elements present, they mostly take place in the background as part of the narrative or UI elements.You’ll be exploring sprawling and confusing areas in severely run-down modern suburbs infested by nightmarish creatures and somewhat obtuse puzzles. The game isn’t very keen on holding your hand throughout the experience and you’re expected to get lost occasionally.While the game is full of mature themes, the narrative doesn’t get nearly as dark and personal as the Silent Hill series. The voice acting is serviceable, but the music and audio design is superb and produces an oppressively haunting atmosphere that never relents.You never feel quite safe, and even as you start to figure out patterns and predict events, the game still finds ways to pull the rug out under you.My only real gripe is that it sometimes feels a little janky beyond what was intended. Some doors wouldn’t update correctly on the map, some data would reset on load and some of the necessary items are hard to see or placed in areas where you’ve forgotten about them once you’ve finally acquired the means to access them.Fortunately, none of these were game breaking in any way and merely served as minor annoyances.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody. I will preface this Review by saying that I almost gave this Game a negative Review. But I want to be fair here even though this Game has MANY issues and problems I barely gave this a thumbs up, but we will get to that.So my first Playthrough took me 6.8 hours (maybe subtract ~40 minutes in which I was in the menu pausing the Game) and 14/20 Achievements were - well - achieved.You can already guess, it is a short Game. But it says so even on the store page, it shouldn't come as a surprise to you, the buyer.With every problem present in this Game, I will always keep in mind that this is an indie Game, MOSTLY by one person whom I followed on twitter for the progress of the Game. But that doesn't mean I won't point out all the issues that I had.Here we go. The Game when you first start feels already a bit janky and wonky but you will get used to it. The Animations are really not that great either but it kind of fits the Playstation 2 aesthetic.I had a few stutters here and there but it was still very playable and they didn't distract much (definitely no comparison to the Silent Hill 2 Remake Stutter Fest iykwim).The Controls are a bit stiff, it is probably for the most part intentional but they could've used a bit "smoothing out".The Camera angles don't always feel deliberate and sometimes change so quick that they can disorient you a little. Also the Camera Recenter takes a bit too long.What I really liked was that Hollowbody takes it's time and builds up suspense, really good stuff here. Also the atmosphere of this Game is really, really good!Unfortunately there were basically only 3 puzzles in the entire Game. I had high hopes, because the first puzzle already made me feel really smart after figuring it out but sadly the other 2 are really easy and kind of disappointing.Sound Design and Music were also really good here.  Though I have to say the Sound was bugging out sometimes, I think. For example I heard loud moaning noises from my left side but there was nothing there. And also the "splatter" sound effect from stomping was "bound" to every second stomp, regardless of where you stomp. But those are just minor nitpicks.Voice Acting was kind of good for a small Game like this.The Combat was okayish, kind of clunky but serviceable. I played my first playthrough on intended difficulty and only died once because I didn't pay attention. Most of the time you will have sooooooooo much ammo left, I didn't use the Pistol that much, the Shotgun only once and the Bow never. Mostly I just used the Melee with a guitar that I found, I think it was kind of OP against most enemies who are then stunlocked and go down after 4 swings and 3 stomps (or 3 swings with a later melee weapon). Enemy variety was not that great, but again: It's a short Game, so totally fine.Enemy "AI" was pretty weird and some enemies were flat out bugging out and running against walls and into corners. The Lock On System was also really bad, especially for the dogs. One just came out of nowhere, hit me and instantly sprinted away to the other end of the map and when I wanted to lock on he was already gone for miles and he did it over and over again. And when you enter an area with a fixed perspective then the lock on would not work at all.Then came a point where I was really frustrated. I got stuck in a little front garden because apparently my character "vaulted" into the garden but I had no chance of vaulting back out again on a knee high wall, which was really frustrating because the save point was kind of far away. The dev could've at least made an open front garden door there like the garden right next to it which was open.After I restarted back to the last save and made my way back there, 2 enemies that were there before were missing which was also weird. I reloaded the area 7 times and checked and it was always kind of a different enemy placement.Then there were some strangely placed invisible walls and the prompts are just plain wrong over the course of the whole game. For example: When it says "Pick Up" you just "Inspect" or when it says "Use" you also sometimes just "Inspect", or it says "Inspect" and then you "Pick Up" or "Use". You got the feeling that this was not tested at all. And there were a few grammar errors but that's totally fine.So overall the Game is just littered with small negatives that culminate in a lot of frustration but I also had a bit of fun. Yes, it was quite easy on "intended" and it was not that scary but the atmosphere and the good sound design really saved this Game  for me to not give it a thumbs down.I was also kind of disappointed by the ending but that could very well be a "me problem".After finishing the Game I unlocked  but even though this may be a different experience for a second playthrough I didn't want to jump straight back in.Maybe some other time. Overall I could at least play this Game (unlike Silent Hill 2 Remake), so that's something.Just don't expect too much "Survival" in this little Action-Psychological-Horror Game and you will probably enjoy it. I give it a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a must-play for survival horror fans. With strong echoes of Silent Hill, it nevertheless tells a confidently original story, dripping with atmosphere, a solid variety of puzzles, great level design, and combat that starts off deceptively rare but will test your resource management skills. It's not a long game, taking four hours at the upper end to beat, but it's well paced and weighty enough to make you feel like you've come on one hell of a journey by the end.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for the PS2-like Survival Horror game that you've been hearing about, this is it. Buy it, it'll do the thing you're expecting from it. You don't need to read further. That said though, while the game *is* very faithful to the look and feel of that era and type of games it is more than a mere-nostalgia trip. This game is a much a love letter to Silent Hill 2/3 as it is a game that perfectly stands aside them as it's own game worthy of praise. It is very successful in evoking that Silent Hill vibe but it doesn't just stop at emulating it for nostalgia's sake. It really adds it's own vibe to the proceedings. I especially love that the apartment block you're exploring in the beginning feels lived in, and I don't just mean the amount of detritus, as lovingly and copiously as that's been rendered here, but the fact that each flat has a story both told in documents strewn around but mostly just the care that's been put in visual storytelling. I Also love that each deceased body you come across doesn't just serve as set-dressing but each has a name. These were persons, people, with lives. Making that 'VOID' readout when you scan the bodies that much more disgusting. It really hits home the message that it's always regular people that are the victims of these cataclysmic events brought on by uncaring megalomaniacsAnd the fact that the Cyberpunk aspect isn't just bolted on for cool aesthetics sake but actually feels proper dystopian is also very commendable. Even the part that shows the bustling cityscape feels proper dystopian and grim in nature. If I have to be picking nits, I will pick this particular nit which is the nit that after finishing the apartment block I kinda expected a memorable encounter. I guess Big Triangle Pizzabox Faceman ruined my expectations since. Well, I guess that's what you get when your protag isn't a sexually repressed self-sorry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. That said, I felt the introduction to the first monsters was quite memorable in that 'Oh ♥♥♥♥... I guess it's on now' kinda way where the vibey silence was broken and replaced with vibey baby moans and atmospheric guttural choking sounds.But yeah, it seems insane to me that this polished full-featured Survival Horror game with an enthralling story and moody vibes is a solo-dev endeavour. On the other hand, it is very palpable as this game just oozes with care, love and attention for detail that you typically associate with a solo dev.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game made even more impressive when you find out it's made by a solo dev. The story was intigueing, the gameplay worked well and the sound and music fit perfectly.Atmosphere is great and emulates the silent hill uneasiness and feeling very well.You can also tell there is a clear uninterupted direction/vision of what every facet of this game should be, but the game does lack some refinement.Puzzles were engaging, albeit a little easy and one puzzle bugged out for me and allowed me to carry on without completing it properly.I love the "tech noir" aspect of things, but it lost it's edge as soon as the intro finishes. It would have been great to see more of that in the environment, but I understand from a storytelling point of view that it wouldn't have made sense. Maybe something explored for the sequel?The world is intriguing enough to want to read every single piece of lore in the game, but I do think some of the stuff felt a little repeated in what it was saying.I did find that the difficulty unatually ramped up towards the train staion parts, but that could be a personal experience, although it would have been nice to been given more of a heads up that the wooden boxes can be stamped on to get more ammo. I missed every ammo box in the apartments because of that and it most likely rippled the difficulty for me later on.I think anyone in love with indie horror or PS2 aethetic horror should play this and I fully recommend it.
