_childDocuments_.review: It would be unfair not to give this game a positive review. Having been developed entirely by a single person denotes a great deal of talent, but that doesn't mean that the game doesn't have numerous flaws.The PS2 aesthetics are recreated to perfection and everything on screen is a visual delight. The music and ambient sound are also very good, but, in my opinion, the game lacks quite a lot in terms of game design and narrative.Large empty and sometimes labyrinthine areas that do nothing but confuse and frustrate the player since numerous times you don't have a clear visual guide of where to go, coupled with a melee combat in which you're going to always end up taking damage make it better to ignore the enemies and sprint around until you find the objective. At a narrative level I guess it's ok, but nothing great, simple characters and leaving the whole Blade Runner / futuristic premise of the game that could have been very interesting to explore to just the cutscene at the beginning.A standard game, with excellent art that maybe with a bigger team, a dedicated writer or a game designer could have been something incredible. Still, a wonderful solo work and my most sincere congratulations to the developer!

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up, my family was much more comfortable around  than . The disturbing stories and focused terror of the classic  games didn't sit well with my folks, compared to the shlocky fun house horror of the  games. So thus it was that I only interacted with  through Let's Plays and video essays, rather than the franchise itself. Fast forward to early September 2024, and a glance at the thumbnail of RagnarRox's newest review was enough for me to get  in prep for the Halloween season; the man is a gold miner when it comes to horror games.I say all this because  is as much an ode to the classic  quartet as  was to . And no matter what I'm going to say about it, it is impressive that this decent spiritual successor was made by one developer (barring voice actors and a public relations person). After playing , I'm keeping Headware Games on my radar for whatever they make next. For a solo dev, they nailed it with the gameplay and atmosphere!For the most part,  plays just like a classic survival horror game; complete with fixed camera angles and the option for tank controls. I say “option” because the game has a more modern movement system that is on by default for the game (a la ), which is why I suspect the game recommends players to use a controller. Since I only have a keyboard myself, this modernized movement became way too finicky when my direction changed on a camera-by-camera basis. Switching to tank controls solved all my movement issues, and I recommend other keyboard users to do the same.The rest of the gameplay is great, and I think it will be familiar to any  vets. That said, the item economy is pretty lenient for a survival horror game, to the point that I wasn't hurting for ammo even on the hardest difficulty. The playtime is pretty short, running at about the same length as one of 's A or B scenarios (i.e. around five hours). This can easily be shaved down to less than two hours if you know what to do and forgo collectibles.  has a focus on replayability, with different endings and a small host of unlockables. All in all, it took me around thirteen hours to get all the unlockables and achievements.’s visuals and soundscape do a great job getting the setting’s grimy, gloomy cyberpunk-lite feel across. Barnsdon is a drab, wet, and dark city, but it did work to wonders in building a steady sense of dread and tension on my first playthrough. My favorite part about wandering Barnsdon’s streets was getting the occasional flash of lightning that illuminated shambling silhouettes in the distance. That, and  was where the game peaked for me in aesthetics and scares. After that point, the game loses a bit of steam in my book. The music, however, was evergreen all the way through. I’m glad I paid the extra five bucks for the soundtrack!And finally, the story. The game wasn’t lying when it described itself as a short story. Stripping out the busywork of traversing Barnsdon,  feels like it has the structure of a short story alongside the length. I think that’s part of the reason why the game loses steam for me in its last third, as much of it feels like padding that could be cut out without affecting the story at all. That’s a shame, because it has a strong start, and is carried by the vibes and the orchestrated scares up until [the end of the sewer section]. The game also expects the player to put the put together the puzzle pieces that is what really happened in Barnsdon. While I’ve seen a couple people complaining about that here and there, I actually liked that angle of handling the worldbuilding. Although I wish Mica shared a fraction of Sasha’s thirst for the truth, as I feel it could’ve helped in supporting that last third of  storywise. On the other hand, Mica’s seeming disregard for Barnsdon’s true history seems to play a role in how the story ultimately plays out.Which brings us to the endings and full-blown spoilers: So this ultimately leaves me pretty mixed with . On the upside, this game is a  foundation for Headware Games, and I’ll be keeping an eye on them come whatever project they come up with next. The scary vibes are really good for the first 2/3rds, to the point of making me pause the game to take a breather at times (in a good way!). The extra unlockables and like are also appreciated. Unfortunately, the thinness of the story and design past that 2/3rds mark left me feeling hollow near the end (pun not intended), and a certain ending needs to be bolstered a bit. The bones are good, but needs a bit more flesh to make it stick the landing. I did enjoy my initial runthrough of  though, and in the end, it did kick off the halloween season in a good way.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna start this by saying if I could give this as many thumbs up, I would. This game is made by a solo dev and man oh man is it one of my favorite indie games EVER. There's something about the PS2 Survival Horror aesthetic that makes me so nostalgic and this really scratches it! Feels very much like the Silent Hill games on PS2 and that is the biggest compliment I could possibly give for something as those are my favorite games ever. The exploration and gameplay is super fun, the story had me engaged throughout the entire game, all the notes, signals, etc are so interesting! This game is basically PS2 Silent Hill games but with a sci-fi noir sort of vibe. If you are a fan of old school PS2 style survival horror you HAVE TO CHECK THIS OUT. Show some love to the developer as well! I cannot wait to see what else comes from him, please do yourself a favor and try it! You won't regret it!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is extremely impressive for such a small dev team, aesthetics, atmosphere, visuals, sound, are all superb. All the important bits are there. Much larger devs with way higher budgets have done far worse. The first 1-2 hours of the game are super immersive, exploring the apartments and streets was really fun and the story is easy to follow, and I dig the characters and moody dialogue. The later areas are more linear so I didn't like them as much, the final boss is also kinda lame. The combat in general is very basic, which I guess is by design since it's trying to capture that ps1/ps2 era survival horror style, just like most of those older titles fighting especially melee is jank and doesn't feel great. Same with the camera fixed camera can be cool and add tension and perspective but often gets in the way of combat and is frustrating/breaks immersion. I liked the puzzles and the enemies design is great, I wish the game was alittle longer, had more buildings in the city you could enter and more/better bosses. In the intro you also kinda get a Blade Runner vibe and I was hopeful for a more sci/fi type of horror game but you don't see much of that after the opener. Overall it's great for fans of classic survival horror games and one of the better indie horror titles this year thus far. 8.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the growth of this game ever since the developers showed off an almost empty, moody environment with merely a player character running around demonstrating it's movement and functions - that was enough to know exactly what to expect, and 3 years later here we are.Hollowbody delivered; it melds together Silent Hill and classic Resident Evil, but in a creative twist, it flirts with a futuristic dystopian world such as Blade Runner somewhere in mid-21st century Britain. I enjoyed the little callbacks to Chasing Static (also well worth checking out).Impressively polished for a game that was put together by pretty much one person on his own, despite one or two annoying bugs and quirks (but nothing game-breaking). Looking forward to New Game+ which has a few neat surprises. If you like classic survival horror and the charm of the PS2 aesthetics, then you're in for a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: If you like old RE or Silent Games, you'll love this.Understand that Hollow Body aims at recreating the gameplay of that genre with it's own twist (if it wasn't obvious from the trailers), so you're not exactly getting modern camera controls Dead Space combat.That said, Hollow Body is an excellent retro horror and atmospheric experience.+ Puzzles with just the right amount of challenge to figure out.+ Emphasis on exploration and scavenging (for tools, ammo, and other supplies).+ Larger backstory gradually revealed through radio transmissions and documents scattered throughout the city.+ Excellent artwork and environments.+ Great soundtrack.- Dogs

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been a fan of this game since its early development and backed it on Kickstarter from day one. Watching its progress has been a great, and it's impressive to see what one passionate developer can achieve.Having played the final release, I'm pleased with the game overall, though I believe there are areas for improvement.Playthrough for reference: Strengths:- Atmosphere: The game’s dark, oppressive ambiance evokes strong Silent Hill vibes, creating a deeply immersive experience.- Level Design: Despite some backtracking, the level design felt natural and integrated well with the storyline, providing a clear sense of progression.- Music: The soundtrack is exceptional, enhancing the game’s unsettling atmosphere and drawing players further into its world.- Multiple Endings: The availability of various endings adds significant replay value, offering players more content and storylines to explore.- Character Design: Both the main characters and enemies are well-designed, contributing to the game’s unique aesthetic and immersion.Areas for Improvement:- Numpad Consistency: There are two instances involving numpads in the game. The first requires entering a code directly, while the second uses a note with the code. For consistency, it would be better to use the same input system for both.- Footstep Sounds: I experienced a lack of footstep sounds for most of the game, I only heard them one time for about 10 to 20 seconds, which diminished the immersion. This might be a bug, but it significantly impacted the atmospheric experience.- Puzzle Clarity: Some puzzles lacked clear prompts, leading to unnecessary backtracking. For instance, the power box switch with chopsticks and the underground station door, which requires a ticket not initially mentioned, were confusing. Additionally, the ticket machine in the station should be more prominent.- Combat: The inability to test or examine weapons' functionality and range without engaging an enemy is a notable limitation. I recommend changing that limitation so players can freely explore weapon mechanics to better understand their capabilities before using them in combat situations.- Camera Angles: Certain camera angles could be improved. At the start, when turning left in the cave, the camera angle makes it difficult to see the character and where to go next.Overall, I’m giving this game a thumbs up. It has a lot of potential, and I thoroughly enjoyed my experience. With a few tweaks, it could be even more compelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a survival horror game that is a mix of Blade Runner and Silent Hill. We play as Mica, a smuggler that is looking for her friend in a walled off city. She'll have to solve puzzles and collect an arsenal of guns and improvised weapons to survive. I really enjoyed my take with this game, it takes about 4 hours to complete, a New Game+ mode, a Hard mode, and has 3 endings. 2 of the endings depend on your choices in game, the last ending depends on how well you do in Hard Mode. Highly recommended for any survival horror fans out there!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: HollowBody is special.Not only does it capture that magic of 2000's horror, it was made by one person. This is a towering achievement, and a role model for other developers.The game is full of charm, passion, and attention to detail with its lore/worldbuilding. Top tier in its genre and well worth the price of entry. The story? very good, engaging, touching, dark with some dry humour from the protag Mica. Nothing comes close to this for me. The best survival horror experience in years.

_childDocuments_.review: It is amazing to me that a game like Hollowbody exists, bar none.I have been watching it's development for some time now, solely because when I first found it, I had realized that  is the game that I've been searching for a long time: an authentic PS2 horror experience. An era of gaming that is often talked about, but seems to have little representation at times.This game doesn't just represent that legendary era of horror game history, it somehow feels  with the games it draws inspiration from. Somehow it feels like I could've opened a time capsule filled with the most influential games from my youth, As if this game, which was developed 20 years later, had been cut from the same cloth as the classics.In my personal opinion, I think that's pretty amazing. I haven't felt  in a horror game in long time.And I think adding a new, unique, compelling story to this "20-years-closed chapter" of gaming history is a pretty special thing.There's a couple of very specific things that kept me thinking about this game leading up to release, and that will have me thinking about this game long after.The #1 thing that brings me back to these classic survival horror experiences is usually the environments. This same thing is honestly what what drew me to Hollowbody in the first place. The ambiance and tone, the pieces of environmental story telling thrown about, every nook and cranny of a scene that's just asking to be explored. These are my favorite kinds of worlds to get lost in. And playing this game, I can easily say I'd get lost in it's world.To be honest, I'm a huge proponent for sound design in video games; Namely, horror games.And many times, sometimes I'm a little let down by how little attention or mind is paid into really cohesive sound design.So with this in mind, I didn't really have much expectations for the sound design going in.But I'm so so happy that Hollowbody just  I played with headphones, and the atmosphere imparted by the sound design really had me on edge at times, and I think that's such an important aspect of horror that is often forgotten.Sometimes the horror and terror comes from what you . I think this game understands that well.~~I also just wanted to take a moment to point out the voice acting. I don't expect much for voice acting in video games, but to be honest I was pleasantly surprised just how authentic and likable the performances were. Mica specifically reminded me so much of Heather from Silent Hill 3, which is the highest compliment I think I could give.Mica felt real, and I cared what she cared about, and that's a lovely thing.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I wanna say that I took part in the beta testing of Hollowbody and now I'm very excited that I can comeback to it again. Even after playing this game for so many hours I'm still having fun with it.As a fan of the old survival horror games from the PS1/PS2 era I really like Hollowbody.It has all the ingredients needed to cook a good survival horror experience. Good atmosphere, good sound design, diferent areas to explore, puzzle solving, item management, backtracking, creepy enemies with creepy noises and fixed camera angles!! Voice acting is also really good.Hollowbody is a must play for all horror fans out there .

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to be the original Silent Hill 2 so much that it picked up the worst things about it.I'm a survival horror fan so I'll admit that this game does tickle some my passion for horror games a little bit but unfortunately, it falls flat on most aspects of what should make a good survival horror game fun.It's not that fun unfortunately and the plot/story just isn't interesting at all.It's boring, flat, repetitive and the gameplay is very rough and not fun.If you want a mediocre PS2 era game then this is the game for you, otherwise, stay away from it. 6/10Now having said that, if this is the dev's first game, it's not bad. _childDocuments_.review: If you’re anything like me, hooked on horror from the early console days, then you know there’s something uniquely special about that era—especially when it comes to the Silent Hill series. I still remember obsessing over the eerie world and mythos of the franchise, pouring over every magazine article, scouring the web for fan theories, and pleading with my parents to rent these rated M treasures. One moment sticks out, clear as day—while on a family trip to Arizona, my dad called to tell us he’d snagged a copy of Silent Hill 2: Restless Dreams. I was beside myself with excitement. The rest of the trip? I could barely think about anything else other than getting home and diving into those fog-drenched streets.Turns out, I wasn’t alone in my obsession. Nathan Hamley, the solo developer behind Hollowbody, shares that same love for Silent Hill. From the game’s Kickstarter to recent interviews, Hamley’s made it clear: his goal was to bottle the magic that made those classic games unforgettable—something he mostly nails with Hollowbody, though there are a few hiccups along the way.The game kicks off with Sasha, a young woman standing on the outskirts of a blockaded city, ravaged by a contagion that wiped out the population. She’s part of a group of activists and scientists trying to piece together what happened. But when she’s sent out to find her missing colleague, Mark, she too vanishes. Fast forward a few weeks, and we meet Mica, a smuggler fixated on finding Sasha, someone dear to her. In a scene that oozes atmosphere, we catch her in a futuristic apartment, surrounded by photos and clippings, staring out at a dark, rain-soaked city, cigarette in hand. Mica eventually gets a lead and heads off, only to crash into the exclusion zone after her electronics malfunction mid-flight. Injured and on edge, she must navigate the abandoned city, radio for help, and find Sasha—no matter the cost.For the next 3-5 hours, you’re left to explore this hauntingly desolate British city—its eerily empty suburbs, crumbling apartments, and ominous subways. And like any great horror game, Hollowbody thrives on three key ingredients: its gameplay, sound design, and that constant, creeping sense of dread.You’ll spend most of your time solving environmental puzzles. Thankfully, these aren’t overly complicated, keeping the flow going without much backtracking. Whether you’re using alcohol from a homemade distillery to burn through an emergency exit or finding a key by rifling through someone’s wallet, the puzzles are logical and engaging without being frustrating.Combat, in true 6th-gen fashion, can be a bit janky. You start with a trusty 6-shot revolver, but soon find a variety of melee weapons and additional guns to help you fend off enemies. Combat is reminiscent of Silent Hill, where you lock onto enemies and unleash a short combo of attacks followed by a couple quick stomps finishes them off—unless you’re playing on the “Punished” difficulty, unlocked after beating the game once on “Intended”. Here, every enemy corpse must be burned to ensure it stays down.And that’s where the game stumbles a bit. By the time you’re tackling Hollowbody on Punished difficulty, you already know the layout, enemy spawns, and where to conserve resources. Enemies don’t resurrect fast enough to make the mechanic feel like a real threat, making it less tense than it should be. You also have no limitations to how often or when you can use the lighter, so you can just spam its use on every corpse after every battle. It’s a great idea in theory, but the execution misses the mark.What Hollowbody absolutely nails, though, is atmosphere. Hamley’s sound design is masterful, constantly keeping you on edge. The soundscape blends industrial hums, unsettling droning, and occasional eerie music to keep your nerves on high alert. You’ll constantly question whether that noise is an enemy creeping up on you or just the groan of an old building settling.The environments only deepen that sense of claustrophobia and dread. You’re hemmed in by towering, decaying buildings, and enemies blend into the shadows, forcing you to stay vigilant. In my first playthrough, I never felt truly safe. Every turn had me hoarding ammo, not knowing what might lurk around the next corner, and the scattered collectibles—like old radio broadcasts or chilling documents—kept me hooked on uncovering the city’s tragic past.At its core, Hollowbody is more than just a throwback to the classics; it’s a love letter to what made those games legendary. Nathan Hamley took the essence of his inspirations and crafted something that stands on its own in the modern horror landscape. If you’ve got even the slightest interest in atmospheric horror games, retro or otherwise, Hollowbody is a must-play.If you are interested in other horror game reviews, please read my review of Darkwood, found on  You can also follow me on Twitter for updates and Instagram for travel photos and in-game screenshots!

As someone whos favorite genre has been horror since RE on ps1 in 96, this game was just irritating, frustrating, and annoying in nearly every way. you walk nonstop, jogging slowly at best, with a camera that controls atrociously and terrible combat. _childDocuments_.review: This game was so close to being a classic but fumbles in a few key areas. The controls just don't feel good, and remapping doesn't fully work. Example, binding quick turn to a button doesn't perform the action. If only the controls stuck more closer to SH2 in terms of movement, stomp accuracy, faster melee, and separate buttons for map and inventory.The story is also far simpler, and because of that, less interesting. Your main companion doesn't have a name, and the MC has very few interactions which expand her character. Because we never really find out what's happening in this world )up to interpretation stuff), the dialogue just doesn't hit for me.Resources like ammo and health refills are far fewer, though I'm sure that was part of the challenge, so it's not a big deal. However when CRITICAL HEALTH flashes on the screen with no way to turn it off, being at low health can get annoying pretty quick. And when the melee combat is as clunky as it is, running around with no ammo isn't fun either.All of these are easily fixable mistakes (besides the story) if there was just a tad bit more polish before release. I really wanted to enjoy this more, but I'm gonna have to give a 5 or 6/10 for this one. It is very possible other survival horror fans will enjoy this more than I did, however, and is worth playing if you're a hardcore fan of the genre. I will give props to the dev for the $17 price (compared to 20 or higher), so it could be a good deal for casual players, but I wouldn't consider this a must-play. Considering all the good stuff I see in this game, this dev has some potential and I'm looking forward to his next project.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is probably the closest experience you'll get to the original Silent Hill 2. Great soundtrack, solid enough combat, simple but effective monster designs, and some decent puzzles. And the best part? Hollowbody almost perfectly mimics Silent Hill 2's somber but eerily tense atmosphere. Only complaint is that I wish it was just maybe an area or two longer to help flesh out its story a bit more. Highly recommend.

Puzzles can be a little simplistic and the monster variety a little generic but it does have a story that makes you want to push forward to find out whats going on. The real thing that impressed me is that this is the work of one man, which given how professional some of this game feels is a tremendous feat.The game isn't very long, took me around 4 hours in total but there are things that make replaying viable, such as New Game+, areas you may have missed on your fist time through and different endings. All in all very much worth your time if you're a fan of survival horror.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly don't understand why this game is so highly rated.I wanted to love this game. I had such high expectations for it going in, and it seemed really promising to start. The graphics are nostalgic and the story was engaging.At first.TL;DR: This game had so much potential to be a great game that uniquely sets itself apart from other puzzle/survival horror games, but fails at every step. The story falls flat, the character you play has no development or personality, the puzzles are extremely linear, if you can even call them a puzzle. The combat is repetitive and the world building wasted. If you wanted to play this game, just go play Silent Hill 2 instead.I commend the developers for trying to recreate what made games like Silent Hill 2 and classic Resident Evils great. But the more you play, the more you realize that the game is just that. A copy of older, and better, games. From the weapon animations to the world building, it near copies Silent Hill 2 sections almost bar for bar. It even has a secret "dog" ending.As I played through the game, I found myself confused as to what was going on. The game gives you nothing to work with and no answers. I'm left wondering where are the NPCs to give me further understanding of the world with dialogue, I'm left wondering what the relationship is between the main character and the person we're looking for, I'm left wondering why things are the way they are. While leaving things to interpretation is all fine and good, there is nothing that engages you into thinking further, because you don't know anything.Why do we start the game in a neo-city Bladerunner setting, but the entire game is spent looking at "retro" items? The only thing that was actually faithful to this was the intro sequence on a hovercar. I was so disappointed in the "tech-noir" description when there was literally no tech involved. Just noir.The tunnel heart puzzle just completely got skipped for me because of the tunnel's randomization mechanic that just thrusted me into the end of it without even solving the puzzle, forcing me into the next section. In fact, most, if not all, puzzles in this game are extremely simple and require no thinking.This is a glorified walking simulator game, except there's nothing that makes you want to keep walking.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but highly effective cyberpunk horror story. People have already made the comparisons to Silent Hill 2, so I'll skip that part ...other than between this game and Signalis, I wonder if Konami wishes it had patented the Ominous Red Square Save Screen.The gameplay feels great moment-to-moment, even if most melee weapons feel a tad lacking in impact, and the fixed camera can act a bit goofy. The sound design is rock solid. Every little background noise made me want to suddenly coat my chair in poo.I highly recommend this game if you ever want to see for yourself how awful is truly is to be British.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: An overall faithful adaptation of the classic survival horror genre in the ps1/ps2 era.+ Choice between modern and tank controls+ A choice between 3rd and 1st person mode, but not immediately (see below)+ Both locked and free cameras throughout the game, to your detriment and to your advantage, depending on the angle of course+ Classic combat for the most part, more closely relating to the Silent Hill series+ Almost fully remap-able controls with invert options on the movement joystick of choice (please note I did not say camera joystick)+ Secrets relating to items, some of which still make no sense to me after finishing the game+ Overall very solid voice acting+ Multiple endings+/- 1st Person mode only unlockable after beating the game. At least they aren't charging money for it.+/- No way to set quick-turn to 2 buttons. Silent Hill it would be L1 + R1. Resident Evil it would be walk backwards + cancel button. I ended up setting mine to the Left Joystick button as all other buttons had better uses.+/- Voice work sounds like the same 2-3 people.- Camera controls at the time of posting this review (09/16/2024) cannot be inverted. The right joystick is used, by default, to look around, just like in the Silent Hill games. I'm an inverter. It made some things more complicated. An oversight I feel.- No dedicated map button, and the quick-menu button doesn't take you to the map, but rather the "main hud" where you can then select the map. It'd still just be nice to have a dedicated map button considering how much it'll be used.- No dedicated inventory button. Again, you can get to the "main hud" and then click the inventory. I know I'm nitpicking here, but it'd be another nice QoL feature.- Multiple EndingsGame is great though. Some minor nitpicks. Didn't crash at all and gave me some challenge. Definitely gave me nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just say that if you enjoy any old RE/SH games, you are going to love this game.  Within the last year I grew a fondness to the older games of RE, like 2 and 3.  I enjoy the graphics, camera angles and tank controls.  I am not in the norm and I realize that.  But this game was just like sitting down and playing one of those old RE games.I first heard of this game through an RE streamer (Bawkbasoup), he said he played the demo but I didn't watch that video when it came out like months ago.  Once I saw his 4 hour play through of this game come up yesterday, I had a hunch.  Instead of watching the playthrough, I purchased the game and figured I'd play it after work that night.  After I started playing, around 5-6 of my friends were watching me play the game until I beat it that same night.Needless to say, this game is truly amazing.  The prologue gives you a sense that something is going to go wrong (it always does) and then after some exposition, walking the lonely roads of this destroyed town, until you enter the nightmare.From what I remember, there's about 7 areas of the game.  The first area is what everyone talks about, and for good reason, the apartment is very ominous and scary.  The puzzle for the safe was so well done, props to you sir, and I didn't even go into room 14 to see what that key was for...Once you get outside up on the top of the apartment, I freaked out cause I didn't realize my choices were going to impact the game.  Unfortunately the worst happened and I had to leave the apartment.  But very well done for that, I wasn't expecting that one bit.The second and third area I feel can be clumped together, the park and the graveyard.  Now let me preface this by saying this was the longer areas for me.  I walked out and saw some dogs, instant nostalgia to RE1, and then they started attacking me.  I'm not sure what happened to the dogs but they would just run past me like they were patrolling and they wouldn't attack me sometimes.  Other times they went right for me, not sure if the AI needs some tuning or if that's intended, but thought I would mention it.  This park/townhome area was very nice looking but I didn't feel like there was much to discover, mostly just enemies in my way, but some very cool lore in these areas.The graveyard and church are a smaller area but I did like the way the puzzle was, it brought me back outside looking at the open graves and I thought that was a cool way to implement a puzzle.  And the people in the church covered up showing them all with a flash of lightning, so cool.  But the sewers were where it got interesting.The sewers were dark and I heard every enemy around every corner, which added to the suspense of the twisting corridors.  When I finally got the pieces for the hands, I turned around and I was running towards an enemy, once I killed him I just kept walking and eventually it lead me to the ladder.  My friend mentioned that this area might be glitched, since that's what he read online.  But I liked the way it just brings you to the winding corridors with a threat following you, I walked forwards for a few minutes and turned around a few times thinking it was one of those, turn around and the exit is gonna show up, but that didn't happen.  This area was also a bit short but had a lot of claustrophobic areas, which I thought was a nice touch and I feel made the area longer than it was.The town area was where I looked at the map and said that's a lot of enemies and ran straight to the gas station.  Might've missed a signal but it's fine.  There wasn't too much to do in this area,  if more shops were open with more stuff to explore and learn lore wise that would've been a great addition and probably would make me want to stay in that area longer than I should've.And then it lead me to the subway tunnel.  Now this is where I died twice lol, both times on the opposite sides stairs.  However, this part was probably my second favorite, next to the apartment.  I liked the whole going into the bathroom with a few creatures to get the tokens and the amount of enemies in this area in general was a lot.  It reminded me of going into the first bathroom as Jill in RERemake.  I also didn't even realize that I had to turn a fuse box on for the turnstile, and in that stair way was where I died.  Luckily I didn't save so I had to do it all over again.  And descending into the hole.Finally getting to the last area, this area brought me back to the underground of the RERemake, with the Black Widow.  Now I wasn't expecting to see a spider per say but I did see the explosives and figured they were for something big.  Once the screen went black and the spider popped up, I ran away, as I was running away there was an option to turn the camera around and that made this fight so much better, cause without it I'd be hitting the button to blow up the bombs and miss.All in all, this game was a wild ride.  It had it's ups and downs like most games do, like some areas weren't as fleshed out as much, but this guy made this by himself.  Just that fact ALONE, puts this game so far up on my list.  Major props to you.  Also I'm hoping that you make more games like this, I know it'll probably be daunting, but you got talent my friend.Now I kinda want to touch on a few things, like the melee combat cause I see that it's a bit of a talking point.  When I was using my club to hit people, (I found the axe to be a little slower and I would get hit a lot more, but that's because I wasn't as used to it as I was the club) I related it to Elden Ring/DS combat.  You got a stomp and then you're able to switch targets.  In a group of 2 of those creatures, I would just hit the one and then swap to the other while the one was stunned.  It wasn't that bad of a strategy until one was on the floor, those creatures will bite your ankles more than a crawler from COD zombies, and they also can pinwheel you just like COD zombies.Also the guns in the game were so much fun, walking forwards in the combat stance while unloading rounds into the creatures was so much fun, I only found the shotgun and the bow and arrow.  The shotgun was very good for the bigger creatures, while the bow actually did some damage.  It's around 4 arrows/shotgun shells to get those bigger guys down.Another thing, is the tank control option.  I turned this on immediately just because I wanted the experience, thank you for even considering adding the option.Now there's really only two things that really just didn't sit well with me, those are the main inventory screen and the quick turn.  I'm upset that I can't hit one button to quick turn, like the RE games.  But honestly after playing through the game, I actually got good with using multiple buttons to quick turn lol.  The main inventory screen is very annoying, I DON'T KNOW WHAT IS GOING ON WITH THE EYE, but it scared me like multiple times cause I thought I was getting hit in my menu but it was the eye going red and then back to normal.  Everything else in the inventory screen is very good, the map looked good and easy to understand.  The item screen was very easy to know what was what and the lore pages were a little annoying switching back and forth while I was reading but that was probably just me moving the stick.All in all, this game was truly an experience.  This is a game that would be an easy contender for a game night.  It's got the old PS1 feel, the old controls, it's perfect for a horror game night.  Highly recommendAlso there's a normal creature, a bigger one that sounds like bees, the same kind of enemy as the second one but it has Iron Maiden claws, the dogs, the crabs and then the giant enemy spider at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a dystopian horror set in an abandoned post-apocalyptic British city. It heavily emulates PS2 horror, particularly Silent Hill 2 Pros- Great Environments - The cityscape is great to explore and look at. Very bleak and disturbing.- Good Puzzles - The puzzles all make sense and things are very clear on with ONE exception- Decent Combat - The combat feels just like a PS2 horror game.- Excellent Voice Acting - Strong performances throughout and well done dialogueCons- Story Is A Little Unclear - Multiple Playthroughs are likely required to paint a bigger picture- Sewer Puzzle - Spent Literally Hours thinking this was bugged before realising it's just insanely obscure and badly put together (and entirely optional) , the one case of bad design in the game.- Easy To Get Lost - Map doesn't update properly (could be a bug?) confusing to find key items at times.- Bugs - Camera often get stuck, visual screen glitches, can fall through the world.Overall despite some flaws Hollowbody delivers a strong tribute to classic PS2 survival horror and while at times it can be a little frustrating particularly in the sewers, the good strongly overwhelms the bad. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:- Graphics are charming in their faux-2000's era poly count. Wish more games kept this style.- Music and sound design is great.- UI presentation is very atmospheric and helps sell the cyberpunk slant to the story setting.- Voice acting is wonderful. I especially enjoyed the static signals you can find which tell small stories of people trapped in the city.- Fun, free unlocks after completing the game.CONS:- Pacing is a bit strange. The game's first area, the apartment building, has many rooms that don't seem to have a purpose and there's a very heavy emphasis on exploration and tense slow build up as you unlock more rooms. After the apartments, everything moves at almost a break neck speed and many areas are over as soon as they feel like they've begun.- Puzzles are lacking. The first puzzle you encounter in the game was amazing, I was very excited to see more puzzles in that vein because it was just the right amount of thinking and context clues I enjoy in puzzle solving without being too absurd. After that initial puzzle, I can't think of any puzzles that aren't simply just "find item, use it here" or at the level of that first one. It would've been nice if there were just a few more brain teasers throughout the game.- Story is... a bit lacking. I wouldn't mind so much if the enemy encounters (another gripe of mine) kept me on my toes and there were some entertaining set pieces to make up for the story's weak spots. That being said, I did think it was cool there's a different ending depending on an early choice you make but the events you see for all endings don't feel satisfying and left me confused in a way I didn't enjoy, almost like I watched 3 different endings with no connection to each other? The static radios are nice for some immersive storytelling but the files and documents you find are very droll reading.- Enemy encounters were a bit of a let down. There's a wide variety of enemies you encounter but none of them feel particularly threatening or that different from each other in how you have to deal with them and even worse is that there are no boss encounters until the end of the game.  I had wasted time conserving ammo throughout my playthrough, wanting to stay prepared for anything that happened and it turns out I didn't even have to use my gun for the last part because it has a built in damage mechanic with a key item the game gives you. If the game had some sort of area bosses after certain zones, it would've helped the pacing substantially.Overall, if you enjoy 3rd person adventure and/or horror games and are nostalgic for PS2-esque graphics, you'll likely enjoy this game for what it is, especially at the price it's being sold. However, do keep your expectations in check because this is definitely not a lengthy, challenging, or deep game and it's probably only good for one or two playthroughs. I'd say it's more of a modern, 3d point and click adventure game with enemies added in. Lower on the scariness rating. 7/10 game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent love letter to the early 2000's era of survival horror. Extremely impressive for a one man dev team. Beautiful atmosphere, environment and soundscape. Exploration and level design were very fluid and felt good to play through. Combat was really well done, not too powerful, not too punishing. Just right for that "Defend yourself in a semi-panicked state" that early era of survival horror has. I've been following this game on twitter for, jeez I guess a year or more? Well worth the wait, and the price tag can't be beat. For <$20, I got way more than my moneys worth of enjoyment and I haven't even gotten to finish the game yet. I don't want to spoil too much about the game but I did want to point out I really enjoyed the world. That sort of late 80's early 90's cyberpunk feel without being too heavy handed on the tech aspect. Plus really neat world building. The only thing I can say might need any sort of lens over it is the camera. For the most part it works really well, but there were a few minor places where I would miss a transition box or something and the camera wouldn't switch scenes when it was supposed to. Extremely minor inconvenience, as it was easily remedied by backing up and walking back through a threshold.All in all, solid 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game until it wasn't. Most recent update broke the final area in the game. I can tell because any video walkthroughs show a completely different puzzle than what is included in the version I bought. Blocked by a bug 5 hours deep.UPDATE: The dev responded the next day by hotfixing the game. That's commendable no matter who you are. Games by solo devs will have bugs, games with million dollar budgets have bugs. Thank you to the team!This game has excellent atmosphere and sound design, nailing the PS2 era to a T. Combat is as stiff as it needs to be to feel like survival horror, but maybe a little easy in the long run. Puzzles are well-designed and won't send you searching for a guide. The first hour was absolutely captivating and had me spinning tales in my head about where the story would go.My only real gripe is that the promise of the story isn't realized and many threads are left hanging when credits roll. There's a good chance I'm just stupid, but I get the feeling the abstract, dreamy feeling is put above direct lore answers and I'm generally not a fan of that kind of storytelling.All that said, this game was more than worth the asking price and made for a great end to spooky season for my girlfriend and I, despite some issues. _childDocuments_.review: It never feels good to give an indie game a poor review, but I thought this was really boring. The story was hardly there. The signals are a cool idea, but they're focused on little vignettes of people getting evicted and not being able to play at parks rather than anything actually interesting or spooky. I felt like the combat had no stakes, was clunky, and there's zero point in even rationing ammo because you get so much of it. Aesthetically, I understand. The PS2 era graphic style looks good, and the environments feel right and the well-done audio design helps as well. That said, it's all wasted when there's zero tension.This game has reminded me to approach indie horror with an extreme amount of caution. This game is getting a lot of praise, and I honestly just don't see why. I can usually at least understand why others like a game that I don't personally vibe with, but with this I really can't. _childDocuments_.review: tl:dr: keep your expectations in check and you'd probably like it enough to go replay some ps2-classics it's inspired by.Interesting lore and setting, intriguing premise ruined by one-dimensional characters and mediocre writting. The game's story just isn't any good, it's barebones and primitive. Hero wanders into spooky forest in order to save the damsel in distress. The dragon is a talking tree. The dragon wins. That's it. Underlying lore, setting and backstory is so good and underutilized that the main story feels agressively boring and weak. Post-credits cutscene adds insult to injury.However, the visuals and sound design are great, combat is as clunky as it gets just in the ps2-era games, the game is fun to explore outside of open areas (which are a long tunnel with copy-pasted everything). If you played ps2-era horror games, you'd feel at home. Also, you'd be disappointed, because this ain't it chief. There aren't any substance to it aside from the apartment building and sewers, which are the best parts of the game. After that it goes downhill up to the point where you need to tap a button on time to kill the most uninspired boss that feels like it doesn't belong to the same game and then the ending. In any case it's fun for a couple of hours, but there is definitely nothing to write home about it, you've seen all this a million times before. And seen it much better. It's not a love letter to ps2 era horror games, it's an imitation. Quite good imitation, but not even remotely as interesting or cerebral. And if you aren't creative - you ain't scaring anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven`t beaten it YET, but I plan to.  My general rule of thumb is, I expect 1 hour of gameplay for every $1/100円 I spend on the game. Give or take depending on my enjoyability.  So far, it has met that expectation, through its storyline, puzzles and atmosphere.   If you enjoyed Silent Hill 1, you will enjoy this game.From what I read, it has some cool New Game+ replayability to it too.  So I am looking forward to that. Trying to avoid spoilers, but from how I progressed VS what I have seen, implies this game is designed for additional playthroughs.  Game is fun so far, although there are still some bugs and balancing I think that needs to be addressed.  Keep in mind, I am playing in "intended mode", so difficulty may be different for you. -Combat is simple. On par with Silent Hill 1, with press "prepare attack" button and then "attack" button. Stun-locking is a thing, so don`t be afraid to go melee with the monsters.- TONS of ammo and health lying around. Never felt like a god, but I was comfortable with engaging in combat.- It seems like choices matter. I failed to save someone, and later got a phonecall, with the caller mocking me for failing them. - Puzzles are pretty fun. You have to be good at some basic information deduction and paying attention to detail, but I wouldn`t call the puzzles I found so far to be "hard".  Plus the answers will always be online, to help our less astute players. - Voice Acting isn`t too bad.  Introduction scene on the beach felt a bit off, but the rest of the game feels pretty good.- While the game is supposed to be "tech-noir"/"cyberpunk", the world feels like what would happen if said area got "left-behind" in the times.  The Tech is still there but feels outdated. Makes a nice atmosphere with the "what happens to the poor people in a cyberpunk world?".- Game feels creepy. I am always on edge, even when backtracking.- Even the "dead-end" rooms will have something to give.  It could be an item, but a lot of times it just adds to the world-building and atmosphere of the game.  A good reminder that I am not just going through random buildings, but that each room once housed a tenant who once had hopes and dreams.-One section,  I managed to skip almost entirely. I collected the 4 objects, which teleported me to the finish area. But instead of using the pieces, I decided to explore some more.  Found a ladder and then left the area.  Items were missing, so I am pretty sure I just skipped over a huge chunk of the game. - The game crashed on me once.  It happened outside the , because I tried to grab an item on the other side of the wall.  Luckily, I saved literal seconds before it happened, so I didn't mind so much. - Not sure, but I think the introduction scene for the first monster glitched out on me.  Camera was panning towards it and then suddenly became a jump scare, with the monster hitting me the second I was given control again.   Wasn`t sure if it was intentional or not.- Movement: I can`t quite put my finger on it, but the NON-tank controls feel slightly off.  They are responsive, but feel weird.  If you are facing left and then press right,  you don`t turn around instantly or even have an animation of you turning around.   Instead, you do this odd little 180 U-turn where you need to move up or down a few steps.  I wouldn`t mind it so much, except the camera is ALWAYS trying to adjust itself to where your character is looking, which makes it feel more sluggish.  It makes it feel feel weird, like you are fighting against the controls.  Luckily, I adapted to this quirk pretty quickly. The  item is far inferior to the  weapon you find earlier.  It does more damage, sure, but only 1-2 hits worth.  It has horrible range (and I mean BAD range) and attack animations compared to the 2nd weapon.  Since most enemies get stun-locked, it is just plain better to use the second melee weapon, instead of the third. Dev either needs to up the damage, or up the range for the third weapon. - There are some "dead-end" areas that don`t reward anything. Item or story-wise.  These may be intended New Game+ areas though.- No idea why we can`t freely rotate the camera in non-fixed camera zones. I think it would help with the non-tank controls quite a bit.  Currently, it just has me spamming the L3 button over and over, so I can at least focus on where I am looking.   Despite its bugs, flaws and balancing issues, I am enjoying the game so far. I will update my review once I finish the entire game, but I would say that, so far at least, I feel like the game is worth what I paid for (with the 10% discount).     You can tell the dev played, loved and understood what made the classic ps1-ps2 horror games so good and wanted to build off of it. You can also tell the developer is somewhat new at programming though.    The game feels rough around the edges, but I can see a real diamond hidden underneath the dirty flaws of this game.   Can`t wait to see what else the developer releases in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the greatest games I've played. Indebted to the 00s horror that we're all so hungry for, Hollowbody proves to be far more than a nostalgia-cash-in. It's at once a love letter and a truly new game of its type, meshing cyberpunkian themes of selfhood and the complications of an identity that's based on the body as well as the mind, with the creepiness of other Weird horror tropes, of a foggy, rainy, forgotten, abandoned town, peopled by pitiful creatures (or puppets) of ill design. The puzzles, the art design, the narrative, the score--all of it is stupidly well made. And, being from the north (which the game is set), it honestly had an extra layer of uncanniness, going around the zerofuturist smashed-window council estates that feel like they've been copied and pasted from the neoliberalist, capitalist-horror reality that we're trapped within today. The game has a lot of heart, and it honestly feels like an outreached hand to these kinds of neighborhoods that have been through twelve gruelling years of Tory rule. Thank you, for this. I feel seen. If you like your horror sad, your visual art morbid, your music melancholic, your protagonist's lonely, and your narrative's devastating, then Hollowbody is right up your street.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, playing Hollowbody immediately brings me back to the days of old. The graphics, gameplay and general game feel lend themselves very well to the PS2-era aesthetic this game was targeting. At times, I literally felt some of the same feelings as I would playing Silent Hill 2 or 3.So, I’ll be splitting this into a few sections.Hollowbody's atmosphere especially shines through. Whether it's exploring a desolate shore in the prologue or the bleak, dark and grungy cityscape - there's always an underlying sense of unease.Whatever has happened to this world isn't just a visual thing - some of the apartment rooms and other areas of the game world have these mini-stories that suddenly make the entire scenario feel more grounded. More real. People's lives were torn apart from this. It helps to make the world feel bigger than it is, in my opinion.God, and there’s two particular sections which absolutely spooked the hell out of me.There’s an area which took me by surprise. Sure, it’s a common locale – but there’s something about the visual imagery presented with no context that really, really got under my skin. After a short puzzle, immediately following that area there’s another one that got me procrastinating on my map. Except it didn’t work as well as I wished either. I’m not really one to be too bothered by claustrophobia or anything of the sort, but this area’s tight, labyrinthine layout + the horrific soundscape going on in the background really got to me. It really felt like something outta Silent Hill 1, honestly.The simplest way I can describe this is an evolution of the classic Silent Hill formula. You’ve got the classic suite of: find items, memos, weapons, maps, and even a few secret things along the way. Just like the old days.Combat included.And trust me, that isn’t a bad thing. The combat feels tight and consistent. To me, it genuinely feels like a smoother, more iterated on take on the classic SH combat. So you’ll still be able to figure out the enemy patterns and fight them with fairly no issue – but I still felt in my playthroughs that I had to use some strategy when it came to different enemy types, and especially groups of enemies. This is doubly-so for the increased difficulty settings, should you choose to play them.As I described earlier, I felt like for me, a highlight was all of the worldbuilding and the environmental storytelling throughout the game, but that’s not to say there isn’t a main story here. (Though, if you're looking for a story that's more in your face - this isn't going to be for you.)Whilst I’ll try to avoid specifics about the story, the main premise is that the world’s gone to ♥♥♥♥, your friend has gone missing – and you’re out to find her. Unfortunately, as you set off on your search – your flying vehicle broke down, and now you’re stuck in the Exclusion Zone.  A place the world forgot about and left to rot.It’s got a lot of sombre notes overall, and some of the endings are so visually interesting – it really took me by surprise.Speaking of which…With achievements, difficulty settings, collectibles, and (a couple of) endings – this game is practically built for replayability.Moreover, it even includes some fun New Game + additions to make the game a little different on your next playthrough – including a first person view, which definitely freshens up the experience if you’re looking for it.For a solo-dev effort, I honestly think this an incredible accomplishment. And if you want something to hold you over 'till the Silent Hill 2 Remake - this is gonna be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 5/10While some of it's ideas were interesting at first, this game quickly squanders the concepts that make it feel original and quickly devolves into a sloppy mess of one part love letter to PS1 and 2 era horror games, and one part mindless slog through overly large and under developed areas. Just as a side note before getting into it: This game was made by a single person. In some ways it's shows, but in others- they've done more here than a lot of full studios with full teams have managed in the past. Make sure your expectations are set accordingly prior to purchasing this title.POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD:I wish there was a 'neutral' option for a review, something that says 'I don't want a refund but I have a hard time recommending this title.'  It's not something I regret playing, but I don't see myself wanting to go back and unlock additional endings. The sound design was decent, using ambient noise in place of music and some decent voice acting here and there helped set the mood for sure.  But beyond that, it's hard to really point to something in Hollow Body as outstanding. This game seems like it really doesn't know what sort of identity it wants to go with as it's 'main theme'- The opening talks of a contagion, a walled off city, and orbital strikes. The main character begins in a futuristic city [complete with her own flying car!] but before the end of the opening cinematic you've crash landed into a walled off city that looks like it could be straight out of suburbia circa 1999. The tech is gone, the cyberpunk qualities forgotten. Save for the voice clearly inspired by SHODAN [System Shock] that comes through on a telephone every so often.Maybe the dev wanted an action-Survival Horror more in line with classic resident evil. The gunplay certainly feels like it slips right in with those games, but the enemies aren't engaging or varied enough to really warrant much attention, and the areas are so very barren you never feel much tension. So maybe, ultimately, they wanted a more Silent Hill approach- hell nearly every major location in this game is lifted from a Silent Hill game  [Apartments from Silent Hill 2, Subway from Silent Hill 3 and 4, Sewers from Silent Hill 1] But to have that, you need to have a character with at the very least an understandable and relatable motivation and someone to connect with. Mica [the lead] never really gets any of that treatment. You're given the most basic of motivation: 'go find and save Sasha'. The problem? We don't know what the relationship here is- are they lovers? Are they friends? Best friends? Does Sasha owe us money?  It's a plot device trope that isn't well executed here because you don't know the stakes beyond "I want to find this person'.Instead what we get is a weird amalgamation of concepts that never really gels. A woman looking for another woman of unknown significance, an evil corporation that walled off a small town it bought up, and  the populace it keeps under military lock down, not giving the residents food or water, and finally a random 'outbreak' of some form or fashion, but none of these is really explored enough to feel like it belongs with the other parts. And there's really no clear connnection between the main character and these events at any point. Oh, and there are some monsters thrown in for good measure. The story, while it has some interesting ideas, is a mess that really could have used a little more time to cook.The level design needed a lot more attention, and several areas are overly-large and little more than tedious jogging tracks. The opening beach, the city streets, and the sewers [my god the sewers..] in particular offer very little in terms of interest or tension, and feel like they exist more so to pad out the game because without those sections you could potentially beat this game in well under the 2 hour time limit and refund. These issues are further exacerbated by never really feeling like you know where you're meant to go beyond- 'I guess I'll go that way'. There are no story telling clues or events that really give you a heading [The church bells in silent hill 1 for example.] That's not to say you'll get lost [except for in the sewers...] because everything is pretty straight forward. That said, I would have loved a better map. One deviation from Silent Hill norms- a pen and paper map that's clearly marked and includes notations of special areas/objects/puzzles is the one thing from those games that WASN'T used here. Sections in the apartments with classic back tracking would have been far better if your map listed room numbers, or even puzzle areas. For a section where you need to find a specific house number outside without really any explanation to how the house numbering scheme WORKS. The map could have been immensely useful. Instead it's a 3D layout of cubes with no discernable features or useful information.  There also aren't really any memorable land marks to get your bearings in the world. You can only use 'the small stack of open brown boxes' as a way point so many times before they all blend together. There's not a lot to find in these expanses of open space either, so instead of being tense or rewarding a lot of exploration, it's more mind numbing and works against the tense atmosphere the game seems to so badly want to create.There were some technical issues of course- namely the game dropping frames randomly, or suddenly being unable to tell how I'm controlling it and refusing to respond to any input while cycling through input prompts for PS5, then Xbox, Then mouse and keyboard on screen in rapid succession randomly for several moments. But the weirdest one for me was in the sewers [The..damned..sewers ;.;...], I found the exit ladder before completing the puzzle of that area, exited to autosave- then promptly all of the hearts needed for the puzzle disappeared from my inventory. I ran through the sewers again just to see if they respawned in their starting locations, but no, they were just gone, that puzzle left unfinished. The fixed camera angles are also misused and mis-aligned in several places. In a game where the camera is behind you more often than not, when you shift to a fixed angle it's usually to highlight something- an item, an enemy- an interesting set piece. But several instances of this just seem like it was done for the hell of it with no motivation or meaning, often focusing on a wall or down an empty alley. The positioning on several also needs to be looked at and tweaked as there are areas outside the bounds of what the camera can 'see' where your character can move around in and not be on screen at all. The elevator in the apartments was the most egregious since I couldn't see either my character or the exit door and just had to mash x and hope for the best. It makes things very frustrating trying to explore and winding up staring at an empty room. The shifting of camera angles in the subways also commits the sin of you have to swap the direction you're pressing on the joystick or suddenly you're running the wrong way, which in my case, lead to taking far more damage than I should have.A little more nitpicky is the lack of puzzle interaction consistency. Sometimes in the game when you approach a puzzle section, you interact with it and it brings up your inventory so you can find and select the puzzle piece. Other times, it doesn't and you just have to try it yourself despite the game not prompting you. Ultimately there were a lot of interesting ideas on display here that with a little more refinement could have made this game a gem of the indie survival horror scene. As it currently is, though, it feels more like a forgettable diversion than a true experience. The creator definitely has a lot of talent, though, and I'm truly eager to see what their future projects wind up like.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, if I hadn't paid for the game, I probably wouldn’t have finished it. I can see how some people might enjoy it, or rather, I understand that there is a lack of games in this genre nowadays, so some people are really craving for this type of experience.My honest feelings are that, that this is mostly an "okay" game that could have been good. It is also very short. While it is relatively cheap, for what it offers, at the same time it feels a bit overpriced.Why do I feel this way? The game seriously lacks polish. There are a lot of bugs and small issues that bother the hell out of me.Some examples:These are just a few examples, but there are a lot of them. I'm sure there are way more I didn’t even encounter. If I were making a game, these things would seriously bother the hell out of me. I definietly would have tried to fix or change them. I feel like just one more month of development could have fixed a lot of these issues.As for the gameplay and progression, it mostly consists of running around and finding stuff. I feel like you don’t even need to fight most enemies because you can just run past them. If you get hit a couple of times, just use a first aid kit, and you’re good to go. I was saving up ammo, thinking there might be boss battles later on, but there weren’t. So, in the end, it felt like there was no real point to having weapons in the game at all.You could say I’m very critical, but when I feel something has potential, I tend to be even more critical of it. This game, in my opinion, had a lot of potential, but in the end, it failed to deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: For the price I don't regret my time with this, but it's a fairly low-mid tier attempt at survival horror throwback. If Tormented Souls was the RE2 of modern throwbacks, this is like one of those dodgy PS2 era Alone in the Darks of modern throwbacks.Big issue really is the content isn't really there. The game starts off with a positive level exploration experience a la Silent Hill being stuck in an apartment block, but after that it's just a linear press through some basic areas. And it doesn't help the sheer amount of rooms you have to unlock to not even receive anything worthwhile or necessary. If you need a Survival Horror game throwback itch scratching, Crow Country, Signalis, Tormented Souls, are all far better.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A game that's accurately PS2 horror in its in roots, to a deep fault. Combat is dreadfully floaty and inaccurate (half the time you won't even see what hurt you because the enemy animations are so stiff). There's a ridiculous amount of back tracking in every area of the game that gets stale real fast. The puzzles are annoying and randomized so you can't even bypass the more excruciating ones by looking up a solution (the graveyard puzzle was especially bad right after the previous section's abundant backtracking). Worse than all of this, the auto save happens so infrequently that you can lose massive swathes of progress. Why doesn't it auto-save after core puzzles are solved or before bosses are fought? The game crashed on me twice and I lost at least an hours worth of progress at one point before throwing in the towel (and no, there were no save points in this area that I could have used to prevent that). The story's also kind of nonsense and predictable the moment you find your first newspaper clipping saying what the local pharmatech company was dabbling in... At the same time the story won't progress much at all for hours at a time either.Unless you're in the mood for a seriously janky, occasionally broken, highly frustrating experience from 2002, avoid this unless later on some of these issues are fixed. Real shame because the atmosphere and setting are absolutely top notch. But this is an example of yet another indie game that put mood and visuals before the actual core gameplay itself
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasure to experience both visually and audibly. They did a really good job recreating a survival horror experience with the atmosphere and style to those of yesteryear. With that said however, beyond looking and feeling like one, Hollow Body falls short with just how hollow it actually is. It was over before I knew it, and I felt like there had been little to take away from the experience. I'll be revisiting it in time and perhaps my take will change after another go but for right now I wouldn't recommend it. Looking forward to future projects by this team however as everything was promising from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Video Review: An excellent little horror game in the style of Silent Hill 2/3, around 2-3 hours long with multiple endings.What it really nails is the atmosphere. It's a slow burn, but around the 1 hour mark I was fully immersed in it's oppressive, lonely tone. This is mostly due to the excellent soundtrack/audio which evokes the unnerving "not quite music" feel of the old Silent Hills. While there's only a few enemies they're terrifying, which I'll be honest usually I find mutated looking humanoids more silly than scary. They move in that uncomfortable twitchy way of that SH franchise, and the game does a great job shrouding them in darkness or under flashes of lightning so their details aren't evident. That being said it definitely has some issues. It may lean a little too much into some of the tropes of the era, specifically going into ten different apartments only for nine of them to have nothing worth picking up or examining. There also is one or two obtuse puzzles, but once I realized every puzzle is solved by items specifically near the puzzle itself it got much simpler. The game is also extremely easy, even on the hardest difficulty, as you can run past most everything which (to be fair) was the style at the time. I also found the story somewhat...lacking. It has some genuine high points and overall great voice acting from the lead, but the ending I got while a downer (I'm into that) didn't do enough to explain enough what was going on . I don't need it spelled out or anything, but some bigger payoff would have been nice. I'll report back once I do the other endings to see if this still stands.tl;dr, if you liked the PS2 style of horror games, this is a modern, bite sized version of that, with all its incredible atmospheric high points and an unfortunate few of its flaws. But for it's low price, it's absolutely worth grabbing if you like horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is very very cool for a single-dev project, the graphics are very interesting and the story has a great groundwork !! the weapons are cool, the concepts behind each character and subject in the game all have a lot of potential - but ultimately , by the end of the game, it all kind of fell very flat ): spoilers ahead in review!starting off with the gameplay itself .. the combat is a little clunky, but forgiveable. but the objectives and their direction was difficult! it felt like there were either very very little pointers telling you where you were exactly meant to be OR extremely harsh directed pointing arrows to the next task, no inbetween. for the most part it felt like I was just running aimlessly through a city or through hallway after hallway not really knowing what to do! the puzzles were relatively simple but progressing was kind of irritating a few timesonto differing topics:- the enemies !! the existing enemies are cool and their concepts are very neat, but there's no explanations for them or what they do or how they came to be or any explanation!! you have the normal guys, and then the big ol weird guys, and then the dogs! okay, cool designs, but there's no reason to give them more than a glance you know!  alongside this, there's only really one bossfight, and there's not really any reason to even use the gun during it. The introduction cutscenes for the first stray and the big ol spikey guy were cool, but even then the gassy enemy is kind of left in the dust; it'd be cool if there was more reason to actually think about them beyond "oh scary figure that I need to swerve around in the street"- there's little to no dialogue with the sidekick you have a chance to pick up on your journey, no thoughtful discussions or character development that you can gauge through small little conversations or anything [] - just walking! he doesn't even get a name throughout the story! it sucked to find that out because I genuinely thought he'd be my favorite character; in reality there's not really much of a 'character' beyond 'wounded man' !! The rooftop scene was incredible and well-done, I loved it, and I really did enjoy his lines past that point - but all I really had to look forward to WAS the brief acknowledgements of surroundings instead of any actual lore-building conversations between him and Mica- the existing characters too, we don't know much of their background - it would've been a lot nicer to have it go more in depth about their relationships, like Mica describing her past with Sasha. the existing bonds with Sasha and Tax would be super cool if elaborated on more! {both of these above points were addressed slightly more with the restoration update recently added, giving more clarity on the story + antagonist; so these (for the most part) are no longer a major point; I do still wish the antagonist got a bit more, but the story is a bit more coherent now !! just have to do a lot of backtracking to get to it, which was mildly frustrating, but worth it!}I usually try not 2 leave very lengthy reviews like this, but the game had a lot of missed marks - I genuinely believe that the dev will go on to make absolutely incredible games if they keep at it, but for now I have to say that I didn't really enjoy playing it as much as I wanted to :')Edit: Went through and got all achievements, edited the review a little bit to keep it up to date - overall, this  game is incredibly worthwhile if you just want a short retro survival horror style type game, but not so much if you want in-depth character-writing and a storyline that you don't have to piece together on your ownEdit 2: after the Restoration Update (the newest patch for the game), i'm a bit too lazy to go back and edit EVERYTHING written here, but the newly added secrets do give more information for the lore and antagonist of the game - which I commend! my other points still stand but I enjoyed the newly implemented puzzles and it was very exciting finally being able to get into the locked room in the sewer and see the notes in there

_childDocuments_.review: The game's pretty serviceable, and the studio did a good job creating atmosphere. Sound design worked well. I was pretty unnerved for a while, mostly in the first building. But once you're past that point, everything sort of simplifies.The story is told almost entirely through documents and audio logs. The level design is very linear for the most part. Enemy design is very simple. I ended the game with plenty of ammo in all my weapons, and never even had to use the shotgun.All of the "character" of the game is front loaded, with the last stages being basically walks through plain, unremarkable hallways. There's one single moment early in the game that defines the ending you get, at it's at the end of the most interesting part of the game.It's not a bad game, and I wholly encourage the developers to keep going and improve on pretty solid foundations. But I don't see myself booting this one up for its New Game +.

_childDocuments_.review: For the price I don’t think it’s worth 20 or even 15 this is like a 6 $ game at most. I liked the UI and the atmosphere of the game bit the really bad hit boxes for the enemies when using melee is so frustrating and annoying it’s just better to just shoot them and call it a day. The game lacks any real depth, it’s very shallow and feels unfinished at certain parts, the story is thrown at you but doesn’t stick at all, I found myself just skipping the text on screen trauma dumps that served no purpose but dragging the game just a little bit longer.
