_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games but I appreciate the effort on this and would like to share some of my criticism in hope for a better sequel. I need to, however, preface it by saying that a full-on negative review doesn't do the game justice, it's more on the brink. I definitely don't regret spending money on it and supporting the developer but the flaws far outweigh the positives so in fair conscience I couldn't recommend it as a complete product. Some minor spoilers included.The best things by far are the atmosphere, the graphics, the feel of the game, the UI and overall presentation, cinematic (some of) camera angles, all of it's top notch. I was engrossed by the ambiance and enjoyed it until the end. However, I felt like some of the homage was a bit too obvious and served as nothing more than fan service to titles like Silent Hill, Resident Evil, Blade Runner and some others.The plot is engaging enough at the beginning to make me act on the decisions of the main character and the finale is dramatic enough to feel some satisfaction about the journey but everything in between lacks cohesion. It's like the game doesn't really know if it wants to be a mystic thriller, cosmic horror, or zoombie shooter. The main mystery remains just that, a mystery. In my opinion there's a significant difference between having an understanding of what the mystery is and carefully removing some pieces to create suspense for the audience and not really knowing an answer to your own question and create confusion to hide the fact, with the latter being a more prominent case for the game.The lore, or rather how it is presented, doesn't make a lot of sense either. The exposition is very brief and the details of the catastrophe are far and wide between with mere hints of some unknown virus arising from a longevity potion, or some booster or what-not. Instead the game is littered with filler text on how things happened prior to the outbreak. You read and listen to stories of people you don't really care about because there's no interaction with them or their environment all that much, and more often than not the story itself would be related to how unjust the society was before the deadly virus got them, which pales in comparison. It's hard to empathize with some water outages when you know these people would've been dead in two weeks or months after that altogether. The stories on the radio are just jarring after one or two and don't really invoke any feelings, which is probably related to some corny acting here and there as well.The worst part is probably the gameplay, or better to say the deterioration of it with time progression. All interesting puzzles are left behind on the first level and the game just really struggles with presenting an interesting loop from there on out. The enemies don't present any challenge whatsoever not only because they are not meant for open spaces, of which there is a lot after the first level, but also because any attack of the character, ranged or melee, staggers them leaving them completely helpless. The ammunition is more than plentiful even on harder difficulties leaving you with three, four times more than you need to feel any tension. The presence of any weapon besides revolver and some melee weapon really seems unnecessary as there's practically no difference in how it acts or is handled. And for the love of all that is saint please never ever use auto checkpoints like it is done in the very last level. It is a capital offense, there's just no other way around it.Despite all that is said above, I still would say to give the game a try when it's on sale or if you want to support people who want to act on their love for games. I simply hope that the author's next project can take into consideration all the flaws of this installment for the sequel, if it ever happens, as I personally would love to return to this world again.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play this game but are not desperate for a horror game give it 6 months to a year so hopefully the dev can work on its problems and fix them. Currently the game has a stuttering problem, running toggle is buggy and it lacks polish as a whole. This game should have been delayed instead of released like this, it feels more like a work in progress than a finished game. the level design is abysmal, you walk lots of rooms that are the same, walk roads that have nothing, face enemies that aren't threatening (i played on intended difficulty)  and do what, 2 puzzles in  the entire game? the safe puzzle was good, it showed the dev knows how to make a puzzle, why is there no more puzzles then?On the good side of things, the atmosphere is good, the combat is quite good for a horror game and the music is nice, but its not easy to be immersed while the game is stuttering.There is an attempt of trying to make a good story, but it failed trying to achieve the feeling of "i want to know what happens next" in me. All the signals and notes just shoves the same thing down your throat over and over, trying to make you care about the town and its people but it doesn't go deep enough into details to make you care really (the signal of the two sisters killing themselves in their own terms is the best one, it makes you care about them, wished the remaining was as good). Also, there's nothing really going on with mica as a character, which is weird since, again, the dev showed he can make a good character with the sasha intro.ps: make the dog enemies make some noise when attacking, it's weird having them mute.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody has single-handedly reignited my passion for not only "indie" games and retro games, but horror games in general.10/10, would get lost in the apartments again.Hollowbody is a very good love letter  to what I'd consider the "peak" era of gaming in my life... the classic PS2 experience. I'd struggled to feel that any game since had really replicated the feeling of playing things like Silent Hill, Kuon or Fatal Frame. Hollowbody achieves exactly that.Not only does it scratch the ever-fleeting feeling of my childhood, but it also is just a good game in general. The story is very unique and interesting, doesn't feel poorly written and even has really good voice acting to accompany it.I don't think I ever heard a single voice in here that I didn't like.Hollowbody also feels like a breath of fresh air because while other horror games are pretty hit-or-miss these days, Hollowbody truly captures what made this genre great in the first place. It's hard to put into words, but there's a feeling that can only typically be found in older horror games and Hollowbody absolutely hits the mark.World-building? Atmosphere? Horror? Intriguing story and gameplay? PUZZLES THAT ARE WELL-DONE?This game truly checks all the boxes to where I'd say it might actually be my personal Game Of The Year.Absolutely give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the dev doesn't really get what made the ps1/ps2 survival horror so good. The staples are all here - tank controls, weird clumsy inventory system, visual health indicator in menu, savepoints... Even less subtle ones like health sprays from RE and  color blinking after save / eye image behind menu screen / radio static near enemies like SH. This game got everything - And it's all unoriginal. There is nothing new and interesting, everything is copied from old games, and all the original stuff (enemies, locations, plot) feels really bland and cheap. The enemies were the main disappointment though - I didn't feel scared at all, just bored. Wallmart version of sh1/2 enemies. In short- If you want to play a good ps1 horror game I recommend Alisa. If you more into ps2 horror - Remothered 1 And Tormented soul. Don't waste your money on this, unless good old school survival horror for you is defined by the option to turn on tank controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond awful. I wish I refunded when I still had the chance.Hollowbody is a prime example of should an indie dev do it all -vs- get some help. While admiral do it all alone it's probably best to outsource some of the development, because Hollowbody really does suffer from being the efforts of one person being stretched too thin. While things like graphics, sounds, voice acting are excellent basic things like movement and combat are clunky, awkward and to be honest no fun to play.I'll summarise:Pros:+ Voice acting+ Ambience/environment+ GraphicsCons:- Basic movement- Controls, even using a gamepad- Camera- Story-telling- Combat, melee and firearms- Everything elseI'm a developer myself so hate to be harsh, but how a game with such basic issues like walking in a straight line can have problems I'll never understand. Pick an angle and stick to it.The camera swings all over the place at the first sign of a change of direction, it makes basic movement tedious and combat an absolute chore. Good luck trying to fight more than enemy at a time, you need to "lock on" before you can fight them!? A very poor idea. I won't say much about melee combat there's plenty of other reviews that go into more details, but it's some of the worst you'll ever play. Zero range and random animations.The story makes no sense, and I was glad to be finished. What happened at the end? Do not care. I won't be playing it a second time.In conclusion:Hollowbody is a prime example of a poor product marketed well, it tapped into the nostalgia of people wanting some classic survival horror and failed miserably. Providing nothing of real substance it's manipulated it's players into accepting  an inferior product when there are so many better games in the genre. 3/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly not really sure about this game.I want to like it, want to love it actually, but it felt heavily of nostalgia bait and, no pun intended, hollow gameplay.In short, I think this is what Silent Hill would feel like without Kojima.The game is pretty short, has very few collectibles, off shoots, or side mission type things. so unless your playing through multiple times, don't expect a long stay for a horror game. The worst part though is that once the nostalgia of older games is gone, there just isn't really much here. Vague writing, uninspired enemies, a weak end boss (though that's pretty par for the course for the oldchool horror games), annoying melee combat, and weird audio and visual glitches, the immersion starts to wane pretty early. It's a nice little game for a run but I really wanted more story there. It doesn't take risks, show anything truly horrific, or really have a reason to exist or tell it's story. Where silent hill was telling the story of man vrs mind, this doesn't have anything nearly that interesting. There is no "hollowbody" baddie like pyramid head or safehead like I was fully expecting. It just a test of patience against standard 6 shot or so spongy enemies with some admittedly interesting puzzles. the worst part is the old game nostalgia also brought with it the wave of annoying problems and tedious pause equip type mechanics those old games had. It makes me wonder if this type of game was simply a product of its time, and there was a reason devs move on to better mechanics in games.Its worth a play through at 15$. But the game really needed a writer who was deeply involved in creating the world, monsters and lore here. It's packed full of good ideas, but none of them really ever really went anywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was in my wishlist for 8 months. Was it worth waiting almost the same time for a baby to be born, not sure, but like a child it's disappointing.It was a bit too short but what really is there more to tell to the story. I got the reunion ending and I'm gunning for the others so I can't point my opinion on those but I felt the reunion ending was lacking, it felt short, the voice over the phone just became almost non threatening with that last phone call, I for sure thought that mother was going to be Sasha, but seems this game didn't go that route. Did we die at the end, did Tax save us? These things don't feel like they get answered and then there is a time skip 24 years later to just a loud sound and a boat?The gameplay is what you'd expect from a Silent Hill inspired game, the tank controls feel responsive, probably because if you hold in run the character keeps on walking so it's not that stop-start tank control movements from the older RE games, also want to say thanks for including the tank controls for the purist fans, the combat feels identical to Silent Hill and there is just way too much ammo, played on intended maybe it's less on punishment, since this isn't my first rodeo with survival horror I was saving that up for a boss fight or for a tough encounter but most of these enemies you can just circle around and the final boss fight, maybe there is a different boss fight for a different ending but the spider fight was a bit of a snooze. You don't even use your guns against it.This game is not bad by any stretch and I really feel that if you are a fan of older style survival horror games especially things like Silent Hill or Signalis this is one to play, if you didn't wait for this game you should be in for a good time. Good Scares, good atmosphere, decent puzzles. Actually get it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a "Very Positive" with 307 review at the time of writing this and I'm happy for the developer that people are enjoying the game. I have to be frank though and say I don't understand how as this game felt like a slog to play.It's very Silent Hill inspired. Everything from the atmosphere to the "save game" UI to inventory is straight out of Silent Hill and that's not a bad thing. They have a very good foundation for being a love-letter to the series but that's about it. The second you start up the game it is a drag. If you took out all the meaningless travel and backtracking you could save about 2 hours out of the 4 hours the game is. I know, I know, Silent Hill also had a lot of meaningless travel time and it could drag out but the difference between this and that is how rewarding it is at the end. Silent Hill is good at dangling the carrot in front of you and giving it to you when you made it down the yellow brick road but here the carrot is rotten and you had to trek through waist high garbage.The only two things I really liked was the first "main" area of the game and the dungeon crawl mode you unlock when you beat the game. Being able to go through that first main area in first person made things very immersive and I felt like I was playing Silent Hill 4 The Room all over again. But once that main area is over it feels like you're thrown into a worse version of Silent Hill Downpour and nothing gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is objectively impressive as a solo developer project. The creator should be very proud of what they were able to achieve here......However, as someone who plays a lot of horror games, both from the indie scene as well as big studios, I've been kinda mystified by the overwhelmingly positive responses to this title. I was quite excited to try this game and finished it in one sitting, but I just don't see what everyone else seems to see in it.The gameplay in Hollowbody is serviceable. It got the job done, but didn't exactly impress me in any regard. Combat encounters are generally either easily avoidable due to some very large & open maps, or entirely required when the game decides that it's time for you to dump your ammo and places you in a thin hallway with 3 to 5 enemies that cannot be evaded in any way. Puzzles range from arbitrarily confusing to elementary levels of easy.The story & writing was mostly /fine/, but just often uninteresting & wrote. At worst, there's scenes like one in which you encounter a suicidal person on a rooftop, which is used as pure shock value and allows you to try and talk that person off the ledge, but seems to imply that it was pointless to begin with. This felt like something straight out of a David Cage joint in the worst possible way.Worst of all, if I had to nail it down to one thing, is that Hollowbody does not seem to know what kind of tone or even genre it wants to stick to. For example: the introductory cutscene of the game (which is modeled heavily after the Blade Runner films) would have you think that there will be a heavy sci-fi element to this game, but every single environment you navigate from that point on would fit right in with modern times, aside from some very slim sci-fi trimmings, such as the electronic keycard locks on the doors of otherwise normal apartments.I'm an enormous fan of both Silent Hill & Resident Evil, which are clearly the 2 games that Hollowbody is drawing the biggest inspiration from, but all I can see in this game is pale imitation, seemingly without the understanding of why the things it borrows work so well in those games. The protagonist wearing an RE4 Leon jacket and your first discoverable melee weapon being nearly identical to the wooden plank wielded by James in SH2 should tell you all you need to know on that front. Most reviewers seem to be more than happy to just be playing another game that /reminds/ them of those classics, and if that's enough for you, then hey, you'll probably have a great time with Hollowbody. To me, In our current horror game renaissance, it did not feel like enough for me to make this game stand out in any notable way.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I've been following its development for a while, I was really interested in it and it ended up feeling... very boring. While in Silent Hill 2, meeting Eddie feels like a surreal experience, leaving you unsure if it was real or not. In Hollow Body, meeting the drifter feels straightforward, going through the motion and leaving me with a companion for no clear reason.Hollow Body captures a lot of the feel and looks of some of the greatest games of all time, unfortunately compelling you to compare it to them.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody: A hot Russian bird's odd holiday in a Dundee junkie council estate in Keir Starmer's Britain, circa 2050.First of all; it's not woke. Don't worry. That seems to be a huge worry for most. There's no political messaging or browbeating the player through anything. The world's politics are limited to the universe it's set within, where a government has increased it's control due to it's own incompetence in handling numerous problems that have gone unchecked, and thus screwed over it's own people to compensate. Hence the top header.Second; it's brilliant. For a solo dev project it's one of the most polished games I've played. Indies are leading the way over AAA these days. There's been no crashes on my end, no falling through the world, and no soft-locking myself. The game has a solid story, mirroring Silent Hill 2's search for one's lover. It's gameplay is decent, there are puzzles that don't hold your hand with flashing bright signs and simply give you all the clues to succeed, and you can kill all enemies or you can avoid most of them. It'll make backtracking an annoyance if you want to pick all the collectables up, so it's best to go full exterminator.Overall, a solid 7/10. 8/10 if and when all the bugs are fixed. It was a bit short and could have done with more puzzles, but that's really the only complaint. Personally, I would like to see some alternative outfit(s) as unlocks for beating the game on the hardest difficulty, possibly an unlimited ammo unlock like with the old Resident Evil games.

_childDocuments_.review: Blade Runner x Silent HIll x Cry of Fear, and essentially one guy made this indie masterpiece! Hollowbody is saturated with morbid atmosphere, dredging up those creepy vibes that so few modern horror games truly seem to nail. The sound design/music is some of the best you're likely to find in a survival horror game, and the voice acting is legitimately on par with a AAA game, or a game coming from a larger development company, with some genuinely emotional moments that hit you right in the 'feels'.  There's plenty of combat, if that's what you're looking for, but you can mostly avoid enemy encounters and simply enjoy the dark journey up until the end. The puzzles are relatively easy, and you have a choice of multiple melee weapons and firearms, including a bow. There's more than one ending, and even some unique unlockables, which all adds to the replay value. In my honest opinion, the dev asking for too little money with this one. Totally worth the bucks, and then some!!

_childDocuments_.review: Ok.... imagine all the classic horror games being remade into a single game. Imagine them with nice survival horror elements and put all of this in a Blade Runner like sci fi universe.Does it sounds like it's too much? Not all, this is a postapocalyptic universe where you go into a mutant/zombie quarantine zone to rescue someone(if they are alive).First 40 minutes were great The game start slow with a lot of grey and not much happening. The game really begins when you crashland in this weird quarantine zone.The game is purely made out of immersion and atmosphere. Gameplay is pretty janky and i feel like the game should have more modern Quality of Life features.Pros: atmosphere is amazing, you see a lot of post-apocalyptic scenery combined with sci-fi themes but you have a trusty revolver and normal modern items.Immersion is beyond words with a lot of attention to the sound and visual design, the rain is almost too loud but when you enter an apartment complex the silence is killing you.Control scheme is what you would expect from the original Resident Evil and with some of the atmosphere of Silent Hill.The price is so low for this experience that it makes me regret ever buying AAA games.It captures perfectly the feeling and magic of the 90s.Dark tones and colors, nothing cartoony wich is so refreshing.Cons: janky, inventory management is bad for today's standards, i would say it leans too much into nostalgia to the point where the young audience will not apreciate it, the start is very slow and i would have started with the sci fi scenes first to draw interest.Map is almost useless beyond seeing how long the corridors are, definetly needs work or at least an option to switch from reto to modern map.Is there any reason not to play it? not really, the only reason people might not like it is because it would feel outdated. Feels like it was made for the Playstation 2 but has a lot of quality control.This is the type of studio that should recive a lot of money to pursue their unique, original and impressive projects. The game itself could be indie game of the year but the limitations of the budget and production quality do show themselves.So yeah, give this studio your money:)

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I had pretty big expectations from seeing the (at the time) 96% review score on Steam and briefly glancing over a review video on YT that seemed to praise it a lot. Ultimately, the game falls short on many aspects. More than half the game is running around unnecessarily large maps of empty streets - littered with enemies that you'd simply run around (only ever inclined to kill them in the few narrow indoor areas of the game) - and the very rare ammo or health pickup on the ground. The game at a later point also required the player to backtrack a loooong way to collect an extra item they'd otherwise miss, which by that point of the game you're likely to never use it. Story wise, little is ever thoroughly explained and there isn't any conclusive answer to the how-and-why as I usually see in other horror titles. Environment storytelling is also lacking. Unless I'm just dense and not observant to the telltale exposition.Game itself is also rather short and would have been 1-2 hours shorter still if the levels weren't so huge to jog around in and without the backtracking.I've also run into a couple of rather annoying bugs; one I could simply re-load the game and avoid the problem action, while the other had to reset my key bindings to default so the in-game hint would actually properly prompt me as to what I should be pressing to perform an action.Overall, I suppose it's "OK" for what seems to mostly be a 1-man project (judging from the credits), and it's probably a reasonable purchase at its generous price point. I'm just feeling wanting for and somewhat disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most important parts of a survival horror is pacing. This game does not have good pacing at all. Things felt ruined by poorly placed notes which hid environmental scares by being in a menu, and bad sound design. The environments are also mostly empty and makes the game feel so drawn out and boring. In contrast, Silent Hill has absolutely no wasted space or time. Time until monster that looks off and represents a repressed memory or feeling of characters in Silent Hill? Like, a minute. In this game? 40 minutes. 40 minutes of me not thinking about anything but where am I going. There are hints of good design here and there, but it all feels more like it was taken from inspiration rather than understanding the idea behind the designs.I really can't go too far in to critique without spoiling this game, or the Silent Hill series, but it feels like a game made by someone who played ps2 survival horror without understanding how harrowing of an experience the games are. It shouldn't take half an hour for horror to even show up.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently finished playing Hollowbody on my Asus ROG Ally (Ryzen Z1 Extreme model), and it performed great on the 15W power setting.Yes, I recommend this game. It’s an interesting and creepy experience, offered at a fair price. The aesthetic is nostalgic, reminiscent of classic PS2 games. While I found the controls clunky, I understand that the awkward combat, movement, and environment interaction are likely intentional to evoke that old-school survival horror vibe. Plus, considering this game was essentially made by a single person, that’s impressive in itself!What I didn’t enjoy was the story. Hollowbody begins like many other survival horror games, but in my opinion, it falters in execution. To illustrate, I’ll compare it to two other games. Crow Country weaves a mystery you slowly unravel through environmental storytelling and notes. Even with its convoluted plot, it offers a clear conclusion, and the journey keeps you guessing throughout. Meanwhile, Signalis starts with a similar premise—you’re searching for someone and gathering information. By the end, you’re left with a complex, thought-provoking story that invites you to piece things together, leaving lingering questions in a satisfying way.Hollowbody, on the other hand, doesn’t achieve the same. The scattered lore pieces fail to be compelling, making it hard to care about unraveling the story or speculating about what could happen next, regardless of the ending you get. It felt to me like the creator had a strong concept but struggled to execute it fully, leaving the narrative feeling disjointed and unsatisfying.That said, the developer has added additional content, which could extend your playtime and perhaps provide more clues to piece the story together. If you’re up for the challenge, it might be worth diving back in!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough and I went from positive-->mixed-->fairly positive thoughts on the game. I really do like the setting of the game with it's tech-noir vibe. I also appreciate it's approach on the Silent Hill style of game, taking obvious inspiration but maintaining it's own unique story. Considering this was made by a solo dev and surely the work that goes into something like this, I give major applause to anyone who takes on a project for others to enjoy. The game itself is neat, has combat, puzzles, eerie vibes, an interesting story, so with that I would recommend it to others who enjoy these classic survival type of games.It's not a perfect game I did have my own small gripes with it, mainly with some puzzles not making sense to me, and enemies/combat feeling a bit lacking. Regardless, those aren't deal breakers to me but I can see where others won't be too interested in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, and super impressive stuff coming from a solo dev! That being said, it is rough around the edges, and feels like it is trying a bit too hard to emulate SH2, at the expense of dubious gameplay and level-design.The good:- The whole aesthetic, the music, atmosphere and visuals are top notch for this kind of game, I really loved this. - Mostly fun puzzles.- Great voice-acting- Has a few REALLY good moments.- Combat is serviceableThe bad:- The enemies are not scary or threatening most of the time. I can count only a few times i actually felt they posed a real danger (but when they did, oh boy). Also, the default hardest dificulty is a walk in the park. This kind of ruins alot of the otherwise excellent vibe.- Some really frustrating level-design at times. A bit too much backtracking in general, and a bit much empty space.  The streets are hard to navigate as of the latest update, as there is no subtle indicators of where to go sometimes.  The park has alot of frustrating invisible walls. - The dynamic camera is buggy, and tends to rotate around alot. The cuts to static camera (while adding to the aesthetic), also feel frustrating alot of the time.- The inventory menu is a bit frustrating, and takes a bit out of the immersion for me, although i totally get the nostalgia value here.- The overall story and endings feel unsatisfying.- I was also kind of disappointed in that the futuristic setting is not relevant for the story at all. Score: 5/10.Maybe buy it on sale. That being said,I am excited for any future game this developer. Very impressive stuff all things considered.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I want to recommend this game because it's made by one person mostly (I think?) and for that it's pretty good but ignoring that I can't recommend it. The futuristic cyberpunk setting is not really relevant to the whole game which is really unfortunate meaning the game could have been set in almost any setting. The puzzles are a bit too simple and some puzzles (for example the one with the ID card that drops into a drainage) require so much backtracking that I didn't even bother anymore because it was very far into the end of the game and I just wanted to finish it. In terms of story the game doesn't tell you much to be honest. There is a bit of background info about how a corporation bought the town to kick out all the people and build something better but somehow things turned bad and you've got the situation where the main character Mica finds herself in. The relationship between Sarah and Mica is also not very clear until the very end because the game doesn't tell you anything but apparently Mica is Sarah's significant other. Level design is also a two edged sword, it's atmospheric and fitting for the game but there is so much unnecessary walking which could've been cut in half at least and the game wouldn't be worse for it on the contrary even.

_childDocuments_.review: Been following this game for quite a while and when I got the chance the purchase it, I was ecstatic! A game that seemed to be a love letter to Resident Evil and Silent Hill while still being unique and original. After my 6 hour playthrough, I can confidently say that my expectations were blown away. Not only did the story and world suck me in, it also has a lot of nods and inspirations coming from Bladerunner 2077 and Silent Hill 2. The game's aesthetic is ripped straight out of the 2000's, with its low poly models and low resolution textures, it somehow managed to be visually pleasing and sometimes I would walk around appreciating the little details. Not only that, the soundtrack enhances the world even more, making it so that the City really feels like its own character. I also have to commend the voice acting in this game. My personal favourite performance would have to be the protagonist Mica Holloway! That said though, I do have my gripes and a fair amount of criticism that negatively impacted my experience or at the very least annoyed me with this game.First of all, the combat in this game is very clunky and while I do like the fixed camera perspective, I usually tend to avoid combat in games like the Silent Hill Franchise. However, in Hollowbody the combat felt flat and honestly pretty annoying. I'm sure that it is intended to be clunky and I know some people like having a clunky combat system but I hated it when I was forced to kill enemies even though I wanted to progress through the story, exploring and solving puzzles. On the topic of puzzles, I feel like the game needed more puzzles. I'm not asking to bloat the hell out of the game but by adding one or two more puzzles would've been more than enough.In the end, it is all my opinion but overall I really liked Hollowbody, every section felt unique and it was a lot of fun exploring them, and sometimes quite tense and scary! (Especially the sewer section good lord I prob ♥♥♥♥ my pants XD) Highly recommend and worth the price!8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a solo developed survival action adventure in the sci-fi horror genre where a young woman crash lands in an abandoned British tenement block looking for someone dear to her. The game sets itself up really well and hits all the tropes of a classic Sony PlayStation 2 game of the same format. Pulled back camera that sometimes is in a fixed position, scarce resources making you think about when is best to fight or flee, puzzle items to find and figure out how to use to progress, hard stencil shadows and lower polygon count models. The soundscape thrums against the ear in the best way, setting the right mood at all times. Combat feels imprecise at times. I wasn't ever really sure how close I needed to be to score a melee hit and sometimes the targetting didn't go where I needed it to for gunshots, but when they land its quite satisfying, the groans and moans and cries of the creatures unnerving me every time.The story and bits of stories scattered over the game feel very sentimental, laser focused on the well being of family and loved ones during hard times. All the logs are stories of families struggling against change, perfectly preventable change, but forced against their will. Its a short and sweet experience, well worth the price. I think fans of survival action adventure horror will feel at home with this one. I'll try new game+ with the first person "dungeoner" mode next spooky season for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: First is review in english.Níže je recenze v češtině.As a fan of this type of games. I've been eyeing this game since Steam Nexxt fest 2022, where I had the chance to play a demo that really surprised me. The atmosphere was amazing and dense, plus being set in a cyberpunk world combined two of my favorite things. Oldschool survival horror, and cyberpunk. I'm just somehow affected by the static shots or camera movements, so that the game has an atmospheric effect. The game really works.I didn't hesitate about the release and immediately bought the day-one with the soundtrack. I like to support developers who make games of this type and even more so when the game feels good and is practically made by one person. After finishing and preparing for the bonus difficulty in new game plus, I still want to continue and find out which other endings are hidden in the game.The only problem I have with the game is its technical condition. Not that it is hacked or poorly optimized. I myself had no such problem while playing. But there are a few other problems. You can see and feel in the game that it is a one-man project, and this is also reflected in the quality of the animations, the combat system and a lot of unfinished business, such as badly looping music, when you can hear a second gap when you start the music again. Enemies go through objects, you keep getting stuck on those objects, when a few minutes ago Mica went twice as big, and every now and then the camera says it's going to stop working and just won't switch. The graphics aren't that amazing either, but that's no problem at all, I honestly couldn't have done it better. Even so, the game's visuals have something in them. The atmosphere of a ruined English city at rainy night, which has really gone through a lot of ♥♥♥♥, is often absolutely amazing, and that's why I'm more annoyed that something pulled me out of the immersion practically every 10 minutes, how the game sometimes practically falls apart during the gameplay. I've had a few times where I couldn't open the inventory and just going back to the main menu and reloading the game solved it. Once my autosave didn't save and I had to do the whole part in the city again. Not that it was such a problem, but it really forced me to close the game a few times.Another thing is the length. Personally, it took me 5-6 hours to complete the game on the intended difficulty. However, there are gameplay videos on YouTube that last a maximum of 2 hours, and with the next playthrough, which I'm doing now, I also have the feeling that it won't last more than two hours. So, if you are willing to survive a completed but unfinished project or the game is interesting to you, because there really aren't many similar games, then give it the green light, the price might be too much for some, but if it supports the developer himself, then I am willing to give twice the price.I personally liked the game and will be happy to return to it. It has a lot of flaws and a predictable story, but the atmosphere absolutely saves it. The number of puzzles is also large, even though some do not make sense, they are all beautifully clear but not simple.  If you are looking for a nice savory with a good atmosphere and an old-fashioned way of gameplay, from the era of PS2 games, even with tank controlls option, do not hesitate.  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Jakožto fanoušek tohoto tipu her. Tuhle hru jsem vyhlížela už od doby Steam Nexxt festu 2022, kde jsem měla možnost hrát demo, které mě opravdu překvapilo. Atmosféra byla úžasná a hutná, navíc zasazení do kyberpunkového světa zkombinovalo dvě mé oblíbené věci. Hororové adventury a kyberpunk. Prostě na mě nějak působí ty statické záběry nebo pohyby kamery, tak aby hra působila atmosféricky. To hře opravdu jde. U vydání jsem neváhala a rovnou koupila day-one i se soundtrackem. Ráda podporuji vývojáře, kteří dělají hry tohoto tipu a tím ještě více, když hra působí dobře a dělá jí prakticky jeden člověk. Po dohrání a přípravě na bonusovou obtížnost v new game plus, chci stále pokračovat a zjistit, které další endingy se ve hře skrývají.Jediná problém který se hrou mám je její technický stav. Né, že by se sekala nebo byla špatně optimalizovaná. Já sama jsem neměla během hraní, žádný takový problém. Ale je tu pár jiných problémů. Na hře jde vidět a cítit, že je to projekt jednoho člověka a to se také odráží na kvalitě animací, soubojovém systému a spousty nedodělků jako například špatně loopojící hudba, kdy při znovu spuštění hudby jde slyšet sekundová mezera. Nepřátelé procházejí skrze předměty, vy se o ty předměty neustále zasekáváte, když před pár minutama Mica přešla dvojnásobně velký a kamera si čas od času řekne, že přestane fungovat a prostě se nepřepne. Ani ta grafika není kdo ví jak úžasná, ale to není vůbec žádný problém, na rovinu bych to lépe neudělala. I přesto má vizual hry něco do sebe. Atmosféra nočního zrujnovaného anglického města, které si prošlo opravdu hromadou sraček je mnohdy naprosto úžasná a proto mě více štve, že mě prakticky každých 10 minut něco vytrhlo z imerze, jak se hra někdy prakticky rozkládá během gameplaye. Několikrát se mi stalo, že jsem nemohla otevřít inventář a vyřešilo to jenom vrácení se na hlavní menu a načíst hru znovu. Jednou se mi neuložil autosave a já tak musela dělat celou část ve městě znovu. Né, že by to byl takový problém, ale opravdu mě to párkrát hru donutilo vypnout. Další věcí je délka. Mě osobně trvalo hru na intended obtížnost projet v rozmezí 5-6 hodin. Na Youtube jsou ale gameplay které trvají max 2 hodiny a při dalším průchodu, co teď absolvuju mám také pocit, že to na víc jak dvě hodiny nebude. Pokud teda jste ochotní přežít sice dokončený, ale nedodělaný projekt nebo vás hra zaujala, protože podobných her opravdu moc není, tak tomu dejte zelenou, cena možná někomu přijde moc, ale pokud to podpoří vývojáře samotného, tak jsem ochotná dát i dvakrát takovou cenu.Mě osobně se hra líbila a budu se do ní ráda vracet. Má sice spoustu chyb a předvídatelný příběh, ale atmosféra to naprosto zachraňuje. Množství puzzelů je také velké, i přesto, že některé nedávají smysl, jsou všechny krásně zřetelné ale né jednoduché.  Pokud hledáte pěknou jednohubku s dobrou atmosférou a staromódním způsobem gameplaye z éry PS2 her, dokonce i s možností ovládání na tank, neváhejte.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is an indie horror game styled around the classic Silent Hill games, although with a more sci-fi narrative and aesthetic. The atmosphere is definitely the strong part of the game. There's a great oppressive feeling as you explore rotting buildings and ruined apartments, picking through the remains both literal and figurative of the occupants lives. The entire world overrun with flesh-like growths, and it only gets worse as you delve deeper into the quarantined city. A+ on the setting design here. The gameplay is also solid. It's what you would expect from a Silent Hill-like, where fights are mainly about ammo/resource conservation and careful spacing around enemies that thrash wildly about. I liked running madly through city streets infested with monsters, knowing that its impossible to fight everything. Naturally, tank controls are an option for the full experience. I will say the narrative wasn't incredibly strong. The ending was really cool imo, but there aren't a lot of standout narrative moments between the beginning and ending. I'm fine with the calamity that befell these ruined cities being mysterious, but I would have loved more audio logs or dialogue about when the bio-threat itself actually started taking over. But regardless, the overall vibes are immaculate, and I've had a blast playing through it on every difficulty, so I heavily recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I should preface this by saying that I give this a  This is very impressive for a one person dev, and I did like the game. However, I felt there were a lot of gripes that left me feeling a bit mixed overall. The game is short, but whether that's good or bad is...debatable. If you're looking for something for this October, keep your expectations low or wait for more potential fixes.Now, I was relatively excited for the game as I thought the premise was pretty neat, essentially Blade Runner theme Silent Hill. To that end, the game ended up nailing the atmosphere pretty well. The protagonist, Mica, has some kind of cybernetic implant, you find an old construction mech, the weapons look futuristic. Its a neat look with the older styled homes combined with retro future tech. The story is simple: go to dangerous place to find missing person, but you get a little SH shenanigans throughout. Not bad, but nothing that breaks the mold. The combat feels like a SH game, which that can be a good and bad thing. If anything, it made encounters feel dangerous.Now...onto the gripes portion. These are mainly technical, but ended up feeling frustrating nonetheless. First thing, the options menu is janky to navigate in general. Not major, but it is a slight headache to wrestle with. Starting the game, the portion that you play from the Next Fest demo is as good as it was when I played, but once you get past this portion, the game begins to feel incredibly front loaded. None of the other areas feel as thought out as the beginning apartment building, where many of the remaining areas are simply long, linear stretches sprinkled with enemies, not to mention you have to backtrack through at least one of these long areas, making it just that more of a slog. Many routes lead to dead ends with nothing but a different camera angle for you, meaning exploration isn't very worthwhile; you'll end up finding plenty of ammo and healing along the beaten path. The puzzles also become more sparse as the game goes on, where many end up just needing the right item for the right object to progress. There's also only a few enemy types that all function similarly, and some of the AI, like the dogs for example, just seems to run around you instead of attack. All of this along with the occasional bug (like audio glitches and enemies being stuck and able to hit you behind doors to other areas) makes it easy for your immersion to get broken.All of that being said, I did enjoy my time with the game, and the visuals are spot on in emulating the PS2 Silent Hill games, but I ended up feeling left wanting as the game went on. I apologize that this ended up being so long winded, but I felt strongly about this about this game and want to see it polished out a bit more., I would recommend waiting a bit in case of more patches and ideally getting it on a sale, as its a really cool project, especially for one dude. If you are looking for something mainly with atmosphere and visuals, this could scratch that itch. However, be warned about the above critiques in case you are looking for something more combat heavy.

_childDocuments_.review: Conclusions first. If you're on the fence about getting this game, it's worth every penny. It's not a very long game, but it nails the vibe of the survival horror games of the early 2000's and it does so in a way that definitely communicates the developer's love for these kinds of games. I love some of the set pieces, the graduation puzzle was sweet and required a little bit of lateral jump. The rooftop was great, the environment in its entirety was lovingly rendered, but especially in the place with the camera, something magical happened, something that I would've loved to see a lot more of. Also I got lost at some point in the game, and it was cool.In fact, if the dev ever makes a Hollowbody II, or something in that vein, I'll buy it on launch day. If anything, this game is a showcase of the developer's understanding of the things that make this specific period of games so memorable. And if they had more time, or funds, I would love them apply their capabilities to a more fully fledged game. It seemed like the dev exercised a lot of restraint in this game, since there's a lot of ideas in the game that are (somewhat) managable for a solo dev, but seem to hint at a chopping block where a lot of ideas still lie that require more hands to realise. One last remark, I played this game on a CRT TV (which makes the game look even more gorgeous), but this made the text illegible. If you ever feel like killing two birds with one stone, a font size knob might be a nice feature that allows for greater CRT compatibility, as well as serving as a accessibility feature for those with eyesight issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm genuinely hoping that this game gets a sequel.  It's a good game!  But I feel like the quality dips over the course of the play-through.Positives: -The start of the game is genuinely tense and my favorite part.  Nathan nails what makes Silent Hill so terrifying in its perversion of the mundane with the apartment complex and the graveyard later on.  -Enemy design.  Save for the end boss, the designs for the enemies are legitimately scary!  The movements, breathing, and subtle radio static give me a sense of dread seeing this.-Well designed fear.  There's a couple of great moments in this game that really spooked me, but the tension was well paced and foreshadowed.  Cons:-The sound designs for the weapons don't feel great.  The shotgun, holy weapon of all survival horror games, sounds light and airy, like I'm shooting a pellet gun.  -There's the potential for getting a character to join you in the game.  While appreciated to have another person be a legit bro, I found myself not being as scared because I knew I wasn't alone.  -Repetition.  Some of the later areas start to look very samey as you play.  There's a distinct lack of character in some of the tunnels you traverse, and while that gives a sense of confusion I feel like it happens enough without landmarks to go past scary confused and back to frustrated confused.  All in all, I very much liked the game!  It's a great attempt at a horror game, and I feel like there's potential for growth and expansion!

_childDocuments_.review: Too short, sadly. It needed a few more areas to explore to really flesh out the gameplay and maybe a bit more monster variety and spooky moments, but what's there is solid and fun. It's not quite what I hoped for in a survival horror that resembles Silent Hill, because of those shortcomings and because the enemies were very non-threatening, and not really scary either. The boss was pretty cool though, if not clunky in execution. I only got the one ending and it seemed to be the bad one. Despite those flaws though, I'll say it did manage to get pretty intense and scary once or twice, because while the monsters aren't scary or threatening, games like these spook you in a psychological way, and this one does that decently at times. I just think it needed more of that. Some of the locales are a bit meh though in design because the apartments, for example, make nearly every room identical and can be a bit boring to get through. It's a small issue though, a nitpick, because the apartments still played out well.Speaking of the enemies, the dogs are very annoying. Mainly because they jump at you, then run a mile away and come back randomly to repeat the process unless you shoot them. Can't melee them, they're too quick. The standard zombie like enemies are okay enough, easily predictable to melee but sometimes they can be a bit inconsistent in their patterns, resulting in some cheap hits. But this wasn't too much of a problem, I just needed to be careful and play smart, so not necessarily a complaint or criticism. You can mainly run past everything anyway unless you're inside where it's harder to avoid getting hit. Overall, I enjoyed it, it's just too short. Needed more moments that build tension and there's too few of that. I'd say get it for a bit cheaper personally, just a bit.P.S. The music is really good and the voice acting is also good, Nice work all around.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really scratches the itch for horror game enthusiasts like me that miss the good old PS2 days of spooky games. (っ◔◡◔)っ ♥ The Good ♥ (aka what I loved):- Immersive environments (think British Silent Hill)- Thematic music and ambiance - Various weapon choices for those that prefer melee to ranged combat- Interesting story beat- Enemy variation(っ◔◡◔)っ ♥ The "Bad" ♥ (aka things I didn't love, but didn't hate):- The environment was sizable but you could only interact with what the game had planned for you (no going into random houses or buildings that would have no bearing on the story or progression, I would've liked a little additional exploration, even if it was only to find extra files/photos/stories about side characters etc) which made things feel empty at times.- Music in some cutscenes randomly gets VERY loud and seems not to respect your audio settings (I had my SFX just above "muted" and it was still blasting mine and my friends eardrums as I streamed it for them). It's unclear if this is intended or not because sometimes it made it feel that tension was building and other times it was covering character dialogue and seemed unintentional in those instances.- There was no way to either retrieve or craft more arrows for the bow after you find it as far as I found on "intended" difficulty. I also didn't find any additional arrows outside of where you originally pick them up in contrast to gun ammo which is widely scattered throughout the game. I'm unbothered by a lack of crafting systems in horror games because it forces you to strategize when to run and when to shoot, but this felt like an odd choice when including a bow and 20 arrows as a weapon option, which means I rarely used it.- Small inconsistencies from beginning to end. For example, subtitles will sometimes say one thing while the voice over says another, often just a word or two swapped around (i.e. "you already made up your mind" vs "you already made your mind up"), and the Makeshift Axe is called an axe when you pick it up and in your inventory, but on the pause screen it shows you have a Makeshift Spear equipped.- Although there were approximately 5-7 enemy types (which I felt like was more than enough for a game of this size), you don't really have to treat any of them differently from each other. I never felt that I was in too much danger around any of the enemies in particular and if I didn't want to deal with them, it was mostly possible to just ignore them. I would have liked to see some differences as far as perhaps type that's slower so melee may be better vs. fast ones that you may want to consider using bullets on, or ones that are slow but vomit on you or will grab you and bite you so getting close and using melee isn't ideal, etc. Overall, the "bad" things about this game did not ruin the experience for me and I greatly enjoyed playing the game. I've certainly played worse games made by teams with far more people working on them. Hats off to Nathan! ((Edited to fix some punctuation and grammatical errors.))

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst positioning yourself as a homage to the horror games of the PS2 era is a sure fire way to burrow your way into my heart, I found myself thoroughly underwhelmed with Hollowbody. Now, I don't want to take away from the evident fact that this is a truly impressive passion of project, but I also can't deny that other games of this style and development history (see: Signalis or Lone Survivor) have manage to pay tribute to Survival Horror games in a way that doesn't feel so artificial and shallow. Whilst others have taken the basic principles of the classic style and added unique twists, Hollowbody is simply content to replicate those elements without much thought for why those mechanics were interesting in the first place. Sure, you can burn enemies to prevent their return, ala the Resident Evil Remake, but with Silent Hill style areas that you never really return to once you've solved them, this is a pointless addition. There's an ending system that harkens back to Silent Hill 2 but with just the one choice to make, it feels forced. Couple this shallowness with rudimentary puzzles, derivative, dull areas, and a meandering story that only barely comprehends that the story has to be moody and abstract without actually having anything to tell, Hollowbody is a bare game that will satisfy a certain kind of itch if, like me, you yearn for the classic days of fixed camera angles and tank controls, but it will last in the memory for only a short while, failing to take root in your mind, if you will.

_childDocuments_.review: - Creepy atmosphere and well made surroundings- Good sound, music, voice acting (except for weapon sounds)- Interesting character- Not too scary, but tense enough- Some light, but well made puzzles- A homage to the great PS2 era horror games - Overall on the short side (I really took my time playing it)- Too many large spaces with nothing to do (run past enemies)- Dull story that doesn't unravel- Weak final fight (very basic)- Weak endings (did not offer a fulfilling resolution)- A bit too much backtrackingAlthough I won't replay this game, unlike for example SIGNALIS, I still enjoyed my time with it. The first half of the game (apartment complex) was really well done, the second part not so much (although I was definitely surprised by the minor twist in the sewer level).Either way, I want to praise the developer who have his mind, heart, time and effort into this game. Even if it wasn't perfect for me, you should be damn proud of what you managed to accomplish. I'll definitely be waiting for your new projects. Kudos!

_childDocuments_.review: a good, not great modern survival horror game.the entire outdoor section of the game is just. really bland, and the game is definitely at its best during the indoor sections.this is mostly because the enemies are not nearly aggressive enough to make fighting them ever worth it in the open outdoor sections, which on paper isn't bad (silent hill's city sections for example didnt exactly make you fight either) but considering i would say a good 30-40% of the game is spent outside definitely makes it a little bit of a disappointment.speaking of enemies, i feel like the enemies are creepy but thats kind of it, and combat is very much just "shoot the monster until it dies" and because the only boss fight is at the end of the game, and is more of a puzzle / chase sequence where ammo doesn't matter it just doesn't make the resource conservation aspect of survival horror exactly shine throughthe story is... good? its not really explained very well especially the finale but not in an artsy way like how signalis is, moreso in a just a rushed ending kind of way. there are little hints as to whats going on in the dialogue from the stranger, but overall it just feels half-baked.mica is a great protagonist, i wish they leaned a little bit more into her funny / snarky side because there are a couple interactions with the environment that show she has that side to her.however the world-building imo is the best part of the game, especially through the use of the radio letting you hear echoes of the people that lived in the city you're exploring.tl;dr: its good, not great. a solid 6/10 for me personally, and while it may not be my favorite of the modern indie survival horror games, it certainly isn't bad and i think supporting indie devs who are keeping this genre alive while AAA devs modernize it to fit wider audiences is always going to be important, and for the price point the game is absolutely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eyeing this game since the first demo came out and I honestly had some huge expectations for this game. When I saw the release trailer, I knew I had to get the game the day it came out, and I did. The game is... GOOD. Damn good. This just screams classic PS2 Horror and that makes the game worth it. Don't get me wrong, the game has issues, but they can easily be patched out. As of writing this, I have just finished it, and all of my issues may no longer be relevant down the road. The game looks amazing for being made by one guy. The world itself just screams Blade Runner mixed with Silent Hill. The dark, grimy world was made perfect, and I found myself on edge on multiple occasions. This game is at its strongest during the quiet moments, and unfortunately, those are few and far between. The game becomes pretty combat-focused immediately after leaving the first area and doesn't slow down after that. The feeling of exploring the empty streets was the exact moment I knew the game was gonna slowly become one of my favorites. I honestly hope the game does well so I can get a sequel and get more lore about the city. I may have missed some documents that explain it, but the ending sort of... Didn't it explain anything? So I'll assume the creator is setting up a sequel or something to continue Mica's story.My biggest issue is the enemies. The lack of variety did lower the scare factor by a large amount. I had already seen everything about 4 hours in. The combat also isn't great. Many, MANY times, I swung my melee weapon on for it to not hit whatsoever, even right up against an enemy. The guns are... Pretty much useless. It takes 6 shots to bring down the most common enemy and they'll stack up in the streets. One encounter had me run through every bullet I had, and I had been saving my ammo since the beginning of the game. Enemies also have this nasty habit of stun-locking you to death. 3 or 4 times, I had waited for an enemy to swing so I could get right up close to swing my melee weapon, and the enemy had immediately thrown out another attack, and stun-locked me up against a wall. This was more common during the late game once you got off the city streets. The ending also wasn't anything too exciting and the boss was quite easy. These issues do NOT mean the game is bad. The game's strengths are world-building and exploration. Just out exploring the streets, I came across a secret weapon, and that thing saved my life so many times. Don't just run through this game. Take it slow. Explore everywhere. Even at my most thorough, I still missed things, and I plan on going back to use the goodies I unlocked to play the game on the Punished Difficulty. I plan on finding everything this game has to offer. I love this game and as of now it is my personal game of the year. Buy it. Play it little sparrow.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s ok. The game really doesn’t tell you much of the lore, and so the area feels like empty set pieces. Enemies are either lil skinny dudes, tall skinny dudes, or dogs. Puzzles aren’t really a thing here minus one early game. That said, it’s not an action game, and it’s not trying to be. It’s a horror game and it has good ambience. Even though the world lacked proper depth, it has a rotten, dead atmosphere. The ending felt out of place. No explanations anywhere. For the price, it’s worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Well written, well developed, and overall just a fantastic homage to the Silent Hill and Resident Evil games of the 90s and 00s. Insane that this is essentially the work of just a few people. It's better than some AAA horror games I've played.There are some bugs and wonky controls that can be frustrating but they're easy to look past. Great game and I hope there is a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a really fun survival horror game. It's like playing a game from the early 2000's but with good-feeling controls. The atmosphere is excellent. The sound design is good. The movement is good. There are fun hidden weapons to find, and beating the game unlocks some cool new modes. The ending I got was ominous and leaves me wanting to find out more. I will be going back and starting New Game+ and looking for weapons and notes I missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I recommend the game! It's got a great aesthetic, the gameplay is exactly what you want from a survival horror, really great voice acting, and the world feels very lived in. The item menu was a delight. Especially loved Beeb and some of the scifi gadgets! And I wanna reiterate, I do think the game is rad and worth checking out!That said, I think it was lacking in the horror aspect a bit. The enemies never felt like much of a threat. And while I do dig the consistency in art direction, the lack of variety in the environments made the game feel same-y. I look forward to playing it again now that I've found out that there's multiple endings and I can't wait to see more from this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollow Body is an interesting concept. You can see where it takes its inspirations from very plainly. Resident Evil fixed camera angles for effect, monster design and atmosphere straight out of Silent Hill, somewhat even gives off Cry of Fear with how the character feels as though they're being pulled towards a destined doom. For all of these great influences I was left feeling as though the game could have been a lot better. It was incredibly short, never really showed how futuristic society is outside of the ruins of the abandoned city. That contrast would have really added to how deep in the ♥♥♥♥ our protagonist has put themselves. You don't get any real information on what caused the infection or how much the shady real estate company that set off the chain of events really was involved. It really left me feeling like I was in the dark far more than I should've been. The combat is incredibly clunky, but you can tell that it's intentional. It can be hair pulling annoying with how unpredictable the enemies movements are. Despite all of these cons I will say that I love seeing this genre of horror making a resurgence. Crow Country was another game that came out recently just like this and it was the most memorable game I've played in a long time. I hope more games like this come out and only improve as time goes on. Don't skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: While I can't say this game is perfect or the type of game silent hill fans have been needing for all these years, this game does so much interesting stuff with its environment and general atmosphere that I'd recommend it to anyone interested in these types of games, especially at the low price, low hour count, and replay-ability.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Just 100% completed this. Some good, some bad... I recommend it overall, but might want to pick it up on sale.- Atmosphere is really good. Spooky and unsettling.- Art direction and music are both really good.- Cinematics felt immersive.- Really appreciated the numerous contributions from voice actors in the game too!- Combat is okay. Melee weapons are annoying, but the game gives you enough ammo where you would rarely use them anyways.- Storytelling was okay. A strong premise combined with somewhat nebulous story development led to an overall story that felt okay, but not gripping.- About the endings... - Puzzles and items were sparse and forgettable. If you find an item in an area, the place to use it is a few screens away, if that. Puzzles are easily solved.- Areas felt pretty empty, and the game shuffled you through too many of them. Would've loved to see 2-3 big areas that you wander and progress through with more variety of things to find / interact with.- Enemies are easily avoided and lack variety. I'm a huge fan of survival horror games, and I feel like this was a solid game in that space. Some polish on the solid foundation will really make it stand out, I'm sure. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A short game that takes around 4 hours to beat.There is some nice surprises in it, but its clearly made by a very small studio & you can feel it.However the inventory system is very nicely made & you're never really stuck at a place for long as the puzzles are not too difficult to figure out.If you're a veteran of survival games you'd know to expect from this.Its a nice twist of Resident Evil, Silent Hill & Blade Runner in the same go with some weird twists of other franchises in there too.There seem to be multiple endings too & the one I got was probably one of the weirder ones.You also have brief dialog options at one point in the game, which I kinda wish you had throughout most of the game.But I can see why it wasn't the case.6.7/10Video gameplay here:
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem for all those who like to take a walk in classic horror game memory lane.It offers not great graphics (in today standards) but the ones that honouring the classics.It has an okay story and fabulous sound design that do the trick.It is a fun and engaging game that takes you on a not long journey with multiple endings.I recommend the game as I am missing those classic games from time to time and this one gave me that same feeling that I was craving for.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! The style and atmosphere are flawless. It took me back to the PS1/PS2 era (think Dino Crisis) but at the same time it modernises the mechanics. This game makes excellent use of mixing the over the shoulder camera with the fixed camera angles. Highly recommended.There is one section that I strongly dislike which is the sewer section. From what I understand the developer has already acknowledged this as a weak section and is already planning a rework. There are also a number of new game plus features which I have not tried yet including "dungeon crawler mode" which gives you a first person perspective. Will definitely play it again at some point to try this out, possibly after some updates from the developer. Clearly a lot of care and love went into the game, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving it a thumbs up because the game is complete, it's enjoyable and it's quite a feat for a solo dev.I just didn't like it, story-wise.Other than that, I enjoyed it, the atmosphere was great, the sound design was eerie and was a perfectly functional videogame made by a solo dev, which is an amazing feat.PS: play Signalis and Crow Country if you liked this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible experience. If you are a fan of Silent Hill, Resident Evil, or just classic survival horror in general, then you will love this game! It's dripping with atmosphere that gives the original Team Silent games a run for their money, and the sound design is downright bone chilling. If you have been itching for a new experience in the same vein as classic survival horror titles then stop reading this review and BUY THIS GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little indie horror with visual and sound design that reminds you of the classic Silent Hill. Storyline is thin and combat is just so-so, final boss is underwhelming but i also kinda like that it's not tedious. Casual players who are usually not into survival horror can still enjoy it because you won't be running around with low health or low ammo, nor do you have to manage inventory carefully. Overall it's a fun experience and well worth your time. Recommended 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is an indie horror gem that all lovers of classic survival horror should play. To give a pithy single sentence summary, it's a British Silent Hill or Signalis, in the best way possible.  Its decaying, dystopian world is oppressive in a way that perhaps only a British game could be, truly capturing the essence of the expression 'the banality of evil.' Even without monsters crawling all over the shop, the walled off necropolis you spend most of the game exploring weighs on you, its empty shell a monument to a history of economic decline, day-to-day hardship, classism and corporate exploitation. The sense of death, loss and waste follows you around everywhere you go. For the (more than reasonable) price, there's simply no reason for fans of the genre to give this one a miss. It's all the more impressive given that it's made by one guy.Pros:- The atmosphere.- No, seriously, the atmosphere.- classic survival horror mechanics updated with modern quality-of-life features- brilliant audio and environment design- great pacing and some neat original ideas that'll really throw you at times.Cons- true to the genre, the voice acting often leaves something to be desired- the plot payoff may leave some players a bit cold- somewhat simplistic combat.8/10 - would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent little horror game! Heavily inspired by Silent Hill, and wears it's heart on it's sleeve. There are some annoyances such as clunky combat, some bugs and jank, but Being that this was made primarily by one guy these things are easy to overlook. Not a whole lot in terms of puzzles but there are a couple that are kind of cool and creative. It's very short even for a horror game but the world itself is pretty interested and I wouldn't at all mind more of it in the future. Looking forward to what more this dev will be making!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Kickstarter backerSolid survival horror with multiple endings with light restrictions. Mica is a solid protag with an interesting story. Enemies with a good variety for a ps1 throw back. NG+ options give a lot of fun and unique reasons to try for the alternative endings..Hints for alt endings: 3 exist. 2 rely on the wounded sticking a round. 1 requires you not heal more than 2 & can only be done in NG+ . the enemies can always die.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: If PS2-era Silent Hill and Resident Evil had a dark-cyberpunk lovechild. It's a bit short and janky at times but the price is right and if you're hungry for some old school slow-burn survival horror you should find a lot to enjoy here. The game is impressively developed by a single developer and ultimately is a really stellar effort, but not without some issues and bugs. All minor and nothing really game breaking, but a lot of little things that start to add up and bring the overall feel down a bit. The 'Use' icon will often be in place when 'Seek' is clearly needed, making you mistakenly think there is an item pickup. Melee weapons will sometime 'unequip' when you enter and exit your menu. Wounded Stranger often gets in your way blocking your path, sometimes during tense combat moments, and doesn't offer much to the overall game experience, he's more of a annoyance. Gripes aside, a very impressive and devoted effort by the solo dev and I'd be curious what would be possible with a larger team. If you go in knowing what to expect you should be satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Good atmosphere and a fun game, but gets a little monotonous in the enemy variety, and how many sections are open areas you can just ignore the enemies in. I spent more time running past enemies and hoarding hundred of bullets than I did needing to actually fight and manage resources.Still, the game oozes style and recaptures a lot of the eerie feeling I got from Silent Hill, which is fantastic. Solid work from the dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: POSITIVE STUFF: A fascinating indie survival horror title that reaches for lofty heights but ultimately left me only partially satisfied. The story was engaging to a degree and the world was amazing to take in and digest, I also liked the characters and being able to make a meaningful choice with The Stranger. Heck, the one really good puzzle in the Apartments was rad, I wish we had more of that! The voice talent on display was another high point. The graphics were also a highlight, I loved the mix of PS2-inspired models and texture-work with modern lighting and effects to really sell the aesthetic. If you want a spooky atmosphere that isn't too scary and a bit on the simpler side, I definitely recommend.NEGATIVE STUFF: My only complaints are that the gameplay was just too simple for me, and a little too linear. I would've been fine with the latter if there was more rewarding and challenging exploration in each area. I loved the first part of the apartments section and honestly thought there was going to be more ways to unlock some rooms or mess with a fusebox, only to be disappointed that things closed off and we'd have to move on to the next 'level', pretty sure I missed a flamethrower and a key that I saw down a hole. That and melee combat felt too risky and clunky for my taste. If that would put you off, I would watch gameplay first and decide for yourself.Overall, I enjoyed my time with the game and don't regret supporting it. The fact this was mainly made by a single guy is a crowning achievement in my books. I would be down for a sequel or interested in other future works by the same dev! Cheers.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: The story and atmosphere are both fantastic. I can see this game becoming a horror classic in the same vein as Signalis.My only knock is that some of the game's maps are very large and explorable, but just result in a dead end. These spots would be excellent for additional lore drops or visual set pieces to delve moreso into world and the people living in it. Even still, I feel this is a testament to how much I enjoyed the game: I still want to know more.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A capsule of the "coziness" of classic horror games. Simple story with enough worldbuilding elements to pique my interest. Great music and sound desing.So pleased with this horror game revival that's happening right now and can't wait to see more from Headwaregames (one person game studio? 😮 insane).
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the atmosphere of Hollowbody and as a fan of survival horror classics, it scratches that itch. It's also seemingly inspired by three of the coolest things of all time: Blade Runner, Escape From New York and Silent Hill. It's not perfect, but few games are. My biggest issue would be the incomplete feeling story along with a minor nitpick: the quick turn mechanic. Overall Hollowbody is well worth your time if you like games like classic RE/SH. Hope to see more from this creator, they're off to an amazing start.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem of a throwback survival horror that unfortunately stumbles due to some gameplay jank, especially a few hours into the campaign.The presentation is top notch and dripping with style and attention, the music and voice acting being a particular high point really bringing the world to life. Though, I would have liked to see more of the high tech sci-fi elements throughout the game, beyond just the UI.Combat unfortunately is where the game suffers and, towards the end, is what you spend most of your time doing. It's where the faithfulness of the games ps2 inspiration is a drawback and feels like an inconsistent imitation of the Silent Hill 2's which itself was the weakest part of its own game.What few puzzles are in the game are superbly crafted and well executed and my only complaint is that I wish the game had more of them.I would definitely recommend this to any fans of classic survival horror but I don't think its quite strong enough to be anybody's entry point into the genre.Regardless, I'm very excited for whatever comes next from this developer whether its more Hollowbody or something else entirely.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say I haven't 100% the game yet but I have completed one play through and I am IN LOVE.  This game is so full of my old nostalgia for games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill while also holding its own unique charm and story that is memorable on is own.  The atmosphere is top notch, constantly making you on edge and feeling uneasy so that when things do happen you are startled all the more.  I also found out there are multiple endings which I think is fantastic for a short game like this and I can't wait to dive back in and get the others.  Amazing game from a solo dev and I can't imagine what amazing things they would be able to create if they had the support of a whole studio.  Keep up the great work.  I'm looking forward to future projects.
