_childDocuments_.review: It’s crazy to me how a game like Hollowbody can be made by just one single person. It’s even crazier that one person can create a game that feels like a AAA horror experience from the PS2 era. But we are getting ahead of ourselves here – spoiler alert: this game is awesome.Hollowbody tells the story of Mica, a young woman living in a closed off city due to a strange almost alien like ‘virus’ that has destroyed much of the world. She is searching for Sasha, her researcher friend who has gone missing while out on a research trip. The game is set in the future – nanomachines and flying cars are a thing in this tech-noir world. Yet it doesn’t feel over the top. It feels like perhaps, just perhaps, this could be where our own world is headed.The introduction of the game introduces us to Sasha and her disappearance, before cutting to a scene of Mica standing at her apartment window. She stands watching the rain as it pelts against the glass and the brightly lit city outside, talking with her friend Tax about going out to find Sasha. He warns her against it, but she is dead set on going. The scene shifts again to a first person viewpoint in a car, flying out from the city in the pouring rain. Of course the car talks, reminiscent of Knight Rider from the 1980’s. But something goes wrong and the car crashes, leaving Mica alone and injured in a desolate and abandoned town.This is where the game truly begins and you are immediately struck by an incredible sense of loneliness. The rain falls as you move Mica through the streets and strange noises can be heard. What is going on? Why is this typical English town so rotting and decayed, covered with a strange gooey like substance? The build up and atmosphere is masterful – it is just you, looking for a way to get to high ground and use your radio to call for help. There are no other human beings – unless you count the dead – and no monsters. You are well and truly alone. In fact you don’t come across monsters for a good chunk of the first area of the game – you are off the streets and exploring an abandoned flat block when you first discover the shambling, once human monsters that sound like they are either laughing or crying. The noises honestly gave me chills. Yet even when you discover the monsters, you still feel alone. Rooms in the flat block are often empty and when you are back on the streets there are stretches where it is just you. This is a recurring theme right to the end of the game. Yes, there are monsters here. But you are alone.Fixed camera angles give you a real retro survival horror experience in Hollowbody and reminded me of old school Resident Evil in many ways. In the same way it felt like a love letter to Silent Hill with the ambience and emptiness. Combat was clunky, but that felt like a deliberate move to make the game feel like the games of yore. Ammo was scarce and oftentimes you found yourself either battering enemies to death with a plank filled with nails (Silent Hill 2 anyone) or simply just running. Combat never felt overwhelming in this, however and if you want to just run then you certainly can from many of the ghouls wandering about. The puzzles in the game aren’t particularly challenging, but a few of them will make you stop and think for a bit. I spent a good while on a safe puzzle in the flat block and the candle puzzle in the church!The backgrounds are visually stunning and incredibly detailed. So detailed in fact that sometimes it’s easy to miss things that you can pick up. It took me ages, for instance, to work out that you can stomp certain boxes to pick up ammo. I was also stuck for a little bit because I hadn’t seen a puzzle item to pick up. This means that you have to be really careful when exploring to make sure you don’t miss anything. The cutscenes too, are beautifully put together, immersing you in the story. I also need to point out just how good the voice acting is in this game – it’s brilliantly done and it feels like you are listening to lines put together for a AAA game.I loved the save system in the game, and how it worked into the story. To save the game, you have to use various telephones. The first time you find them, the phone will ring and you will speak to a strange creature with a robotic like voice. This voice is incredibly important to the story and as the game progresses it will become clearer just what this voice is.Hollowbody truly feels like you are stepping back into the PS2 era – I felt like a teenager again, sitting in my room and playing a horror game that had me wondering what was going to happen next. Whilst there weren’t many jump scares, the game didn’t actually need them. The tension and isolated feeling was enough to invoke a feeling a fear. This is an impressive game from a single developer, and one that I would highly recommend checking out.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game if a little short.Reminded me of Silent Hill 3 in many ways. Great atmosphere that really felt like the setting was genuine thanks to all the little details.The plot needed some fleshing out for me, one of the endings in particular made no sense since there were 2 cutscenes back to back which contradicted each other.It would have been better had there been more enclosed environments, it was a bit to easy to just run around 90% of the enemies, for me survival horror works best indoors.Impressive that it was put together by a single dev, hopefully more to come.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Short but enjoyable survival horror game absolutely carried by its atmosphere and presentation. Gameplay, in my opinion, leaves a lot to be desired, as you get too many resources and the enemies are so easy to avoid that the game feels like a walking sim at times. The outdoor sections mostly consist of huge empty streets to walk past, with no threat from enemies. The indoor areas are not complex but the level design is good. I can't deny, even though I don't think the gameplay is particularly good, I enjoyed my time with the game quite a bit due to its strengths.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those where i wish steam let you give a numbered review. The game proudly wears its influences on its sleeve and the atmosphere is so thick you can cut it. The fixed camera is clearly inspired by classic RE titles but rarely does the game do anything interesting with them aside from exactly ONE cool monster reveal. One issue with those monsters though: maybe its me, but the game just isnt scary despite the excellent atmosphere. The games controls and design is simple but effectively done with modernized controls, making combat easy to grasp (which could be why it loses some of the fear factor). Combat becomes trivial late in the game to where its no longer daunting and just annoying with how random the damage you receive is.The story is...just ok. Nothing really special. Serviceable, but its no Silent Hill or even a Signalis. I guess my biggest issue is that its a struggle to describe Hollow Body outside of any of its influence. Its cyberpunk setting, while initially interesting, becomes utterly pointless to where this game could have easily taken place anytime from the 90s to now. Hollow Body simply lacks an identity outside its influences.considering this was a solo dev game, its actually quite impressive how he managed to put all this together and hes clearly illustrated a love for the genre (despite the flaws). He even cared enough to provide some replay value and even a first person mode.all this taken into account, a more accurate score would be a  6.5-7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, but unlike Chasing Static (the studio's previous game), I think its lost a bit of the wider audience appeal by hewing closer to genre traditions. I grew up on those classics and didn't mind, but if you're coming into this without any retro survival-horror experience it could be a rough ride! The plot, exploration, and atmosphere are all great, but I was a little disappointed at the cyberpunk aspects being pushed to the background so quickly. It also felt weirdly out of time, with old phone booths next to houses next to ruined mechs which gave it a scattershot feel ranging from the 1990's to the 20XX's but not in any convincing or layered way.Finally, it felt like some exposition just.. didn't carry as well, it does a decent job of keeping you guessing, but somehow lacked the feeling of urgency Chasing Static had.  I didn't feel as immersed in it, though I can't exactly say why.Overall it's a solid 6 hours of entertainment, made better if you're already familiar with the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Since my expectations/hopes for the Silent Hill remake are about as low as a gophers balls, I bought this with some high hopes. The screen caps and video looked very promising, and I'm a sucker for these types of games. Overall, for 17 bucks? It's pretty damn good. Pros: -Fantastic atmosphere. The dev (singular, yeah, this was made by one person,) did a great job with nailing the atmosphere that the original silent hill games have, especially indoors. The way your flashlight reacts to the walls and shadows is just so on point. -Voice acting is very serviceable, nothing that will blow you away, but it definitely does not sound ameteur-ish. -As opposed to some of the OG silent hill games, the puzzles here are not overly confusing, IE; if you're paying attention it makes sense how to solve them. You won't have to combine 3 different items to use on a random crack in the wall or something like that. -Graphics look good too, it's not AAA COD graphics, but honestly for these types of games, the slightly lowered res is a plus in my book. -The story here is interesting enough to be invested, but might be a little too vague for some people. This game is kind of like Silent Hill + Bladerunner + Resident Evil. If that sounds interesting, you should definitely pick this up. Cons: -A little too short. About 4-5 hours your first playthrough. There IS a new game+, which has some unlocks and game modes that I'm looking forward to.-A few glitches I encountered, that while weren't game breaking, was enough to break me out of the immersion for a second or two. A couple times you have an NPC following you and they had a tendency to float on trees if they got too close. -There is a puzzle in here intended to confuse the player. Without spoiling anything, some players have reported the progress of solving it causes a bug, although the dev states it is intentional. I personally loved this section, but felt I should at least mention it. If I'm being honest, it seems people are quick to point out a "bug" when something isn't going exactly how it's expected to go. Overall, 8/10. The dev seems to be actively working on this to get some of the kinks ironed out and add additional content as well. Again, this was made by one person. That's an accomplishment of itself. Often times, it's difficult to emulate the spirit and direction of a Silent Hill-esque game; there have been groups of people try to release a game like this and fail.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, get it if you want a ps2 style horror game with heavy Silent Hill influence. But it's not as scary imo. Graphics, controls and story could come straight from 2002 or so. The Cyber-Noir setting is interesting and pretty unique but they don't make much with it imo. Story seemed interesting enough to make me complete the game, I was a bit disappointed in the end though. The game has very huge, linear and somewhat empty areas and your character runs pretty slow. Besides some items and a couple documents to read, there's no point in exploring these spaces. If you want to get an optional secret you have to backtrack all the way back to the first area of the game. You walk around 20 minutes to get it and then the same way back for a third time. Most of the game is just walking. The puzzles are easy but at least you have to think a little bit before the solution becomes obvious. Combat is fine, you find plenty of ammo and health items. Playtime is around 4 to 5 hours. My rating: 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I love horror, but franchises like Resident Evil have become too shooter-based and too intense for my taste. I crave slow-paced horror that sips into your bones, and Hollowbody delivers just that.Do yourself a favor and don't play the story mode. You don't have to fight all the time, which means you'll always have enough ammo.And that's what I love about it. You don't have to fight. The monsters are creepy and there is are different monsters that make it interesting but apart from very tight spaces that are blocked by enemies you can run past them.The atmosphere, sound design, and level design are superb and I really felt immersed in the story and the creepy areas it was all happening in.I haven't played any games in the locked camera angle age, but I love the way it is done in this game. It is a match made in heaven for horror games and I am sad that there aren't any more games using it.As a PC guy, it was weird to hold my mouse and not even use it once, since the game is for made for gamepads, but the controls were intuitive and responsive enough that my right hand finally had a rest.I don't usually write Steam reviews, but I followed the developer's progress on YouTube and the more we supported indie devs, the more great horror gems like Hollowbody we get.If you're still reading this, you know you want the game. Just buy it and have fun for a few hours. It's exactly what I got and the money was well spent.Great job! I'll be waiting for your next games.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: There's a couple thing that make this game kinda annoying to play for me. The backtrack for the heart lock is not that fun. You need walk back for around 10 minutes to find and get the place you need to be. The second one is the sewer level. The sewer level is hard to navigate with the camera constantly changing angle. On top of that no map for that area too and i got lost a lot of time. Other than that, this game is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest survival horror games I've played in quite some time. It has great atmosphere, plays really well, smart puzzles - it's a no brainer for any fans of old school Resident Evil, Silent Hill games. The voice acting is on par, it has great outcomes, the storytelling is quite rich. Really looking forward if there's any sequel. If I had to score it, it would be a 5/5!!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful classic survival horror experience, and a thorough homage to early Silent  Hill entries, but instead of mystical themes, it relies on apocalyptic and bio-horror setting of decadent futuristic Britain, which makes the game quite fresh and intriguing. Length is perfect, gameplay is nice - though the melee is still a bit janky at times. There some good, non-stupid puzzles and a handfull of truly creepy moments - but no banal screamers. Overall, a solid blend of ominous atmosphere, griping plot and melancholic cityscapes. The neverending storm is chef's kiss in this mixture. I was hooked onto Hollowbody from the start to the very ending, and can assure you - it's a must-have for all fans of oldschool survival horrors!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Great classic survival horror that you grew up playing in the early 2000's. its Resident Evil meets Silents Hill. it takes more ques from silent hill 2. If you want a game to help scratch that survival horror itch you been having, and want something to kill the time until Silent hill 2 remake, it's a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a retro-ish survival horror game in the style of Silent Hill.It's a short game, linear game that I can't imagine will take you more than 4-6 hours on a blind playthrough.The graphics aren't amazing, but are more than good enough.The camera can be frustrating at times; it goes between over-the-shoulder with very limited movement and fixed camera angles.There are melee and ranged weapons. Melee takes a little bit to get used to the quirks.The puzzles are logical and you don't get the answer.I highly recommend this game if you enjoy survival horror games.Similar games: Signalis, Silent Hill 1-3, Crow Country.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Neat project by a solo dev, really dig its Silent Hill Blade Runner vibes. _childDocuments_.review: A great throwback survival horror game. If you liked Silent hill or PS2 horror games you might like this one. Amazing atmosphere, great setting and creepy enemies. I had some nitpicks with it like the city exploration, enemies dont give too much trouble because you can just run past them and the streets are pretty boring to explore. _childDocuments_.review: For a solo developer this game oozes with style and eerie atmosphere that transports you back to the early years of the PS2 era. It would've been a masterpiece If not for the combat requiring more polish and the dull enemies that do not match the raw atmosphere of the game. I give it a solid 7.5/10 and I'm looking forward to the developers next project.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Very competently made survival horror game that totally could be mistaken for a title that came out at the start of the PS2 era. The mood is on point.I was quite underwhelmed by the handful of puzzles featured. I also had a hard time connecting on an emotional level with the main character and the story. _childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody nails that nostalgic PS2-era Silent Hill vibe with its atmospheric design and creepy environments. It’s a short 5-hour experience with a simple, effective story and interesting map and enemy designs.The only downsides are the clunky melee combat thats making some encounters feel frustrating and a few pointless corridors that make exploration feel unrewarding at times.If you love old-school Silent Hill, this is a must-play!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a survival horror game in which you play as Mika who is looking for her friend Sasha. It takes place in the future (and also current) dystopia in the UK. Some vague tragedy befell an eastern city at the hands of a big company. This game takes many cues from Silent Hill which will become apparent almost immediately. It follows the same structure as those games. That being : city, enclosed area, city, enclosed area, rinse and repeat. The city areas are easily the weakest parts of the game. The city is extremely samey and boring to look at. There are many points where you can clearly see where the map ends. They're a bit confusing at first, but you quickly realize that these segments are very linear. It suffers from an amateur dev hallmark in the form of thoughtless enemy placement and we'll see this more in one of the last areas. It's an indie game developed by one man, and though that is very admirable, it means we're in for some jank, and this game has tons of it. You can expect the usual, awkward looking animations, clipping through details in the environment and some semi jank combat. Melee weapons are awkward to time correctly, so they're by and large useless. Fortunately, guns work just fine. You even have a dedicated stomp button a la Dead Space which can be a bit tricky to aim with. The game is not without its bugs either. There's a toggle option to auto run and I had this turn on permanently for me. I had to fiddle with the awful option menus to fix it. There was also a house you visit early in the game that had a wall that I clipped through and fell into an out of bounds area, forcing me to reload my save and lose some progress. The graphical settings leave a lot to be desiredIn conclusion, this is a decent game that will scratch the survival horror itch, but it isn't without its faults. If you're a fan of classic survival horror, you'll probably enjoy it. One thing I neglected to mention is that the voice acting in this game is surprisingly very good. I was a bit taken aback by how well the voice actors performed.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: This was a nice indie treat. If you loved the old Resident Evil or Silent Hill games from the older consoles then this will feel like a nice little throw back to that era. I loved the changing angles of the camera, liked the creepy vibe and overall just liked how there were times where I questioned if the game was messing with me. The game does not overstay its welcome and can be completed over a weekend. Much like games of yesteryear, you have little Easter eggs to look for and collect, so you definitely get some replayability with this one. After completing the game it looks like there are a few other endings, so I'll be going back to see if I can get those as well. For an oldschool gamer this is a welcome addition to my library and what makes it even better is that this was put out by an indie developer and you can support them by purchasing this well made game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Just a perfectly wonderful little slice of survival horror.  It wears it's influences on it's sleeve, but that is no bad thing in the case. The atmoshpere, tension, music and emotional resonance all mesh cohesively into a charmingly macabre tale, from a ravaged Britain. Very human, relatable, well paced, and not overly long or convoluted.  If you miss the glory days of a certain Konami franchise, that appears to have lost it's way, or long for your memories of Playstation One era horror, but with gorgeous graphics, and genuinely well placed voice acting, make room in your heart for Hollow Body.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredible callback to PS2 era survival horror. Featuring fantastic graphics for the aesthetic its going for and thoroughly polished gameplay with solid voice acting performances it's easy to mistake this for some hidden gem looked over from that era of gaming. As someone with a lot of nostalgia for the classics of that time I found this game thoroughly enjoyable from start to finish.The only blemishes on an otherwise perfect retro style horror game is the story and some of the area design. Story-wise it's a fine story and well told but very shallow. In the start it seems very focused on world building and telling a more commentative story about the dystopic future the game is set in, but it doesn't really go anywhere with it instead shifting towards a more personal story of our protagonist. This is fine and it's not a bad story by any means, but it does lack the sort of complex character storytelling of something like Silent Hill 2 or 3 (an unfair comparison for sure but many other aspects of the game stack up pretty well to these 2 legendary games).Aside from that, the more open areas of the game are nice aesthetically but create some boring gameplay moments. Especially in one section where the game has you running all the way back across a gigantic park and a few city blocks and then back again just to open a gate. This may be more engaging if you don't clear out these areas before needing to do this backtracking, but in my instance I did so it just felt like filler.On the subject of level design there's a few parts of the game that gate off your ability to return to previous areas. Generally speaking there's nothing wrong with doing this in a game but they happen very sporadically and this combined with sparse save points can create frustrating moments if there's unexplored areas or unsolved puzzles you want to revisit when the game suddenly tells you "nope, you can't go back there".Lastly the enemy design and combat is pretty great, except the AI seems to be a little inconsistent. There were a couple instances where the enemies all clumped together in one spot creating a very frantic situation that was great from a survival horror standpoint, but then when I would revisit the same spot (either after dying and reloading or loading in to another area and coming back) the enemies would be far more spread out and the same exact area would suddenly be a breeze to either pick the enemies off one by one or just dodge them altogether. I don't know if this is some invisible difficulty adjustment mechanic or just jank in the enemy pathing, either way it didn't ruin the game but I did find it kind of odd.Overall though this game is amazing and absolutely something worth checking out if you're a horror fan! The bonus unlockables and alternate endings add that perfect replay value that the retro games which inspired this title utilized.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable homage to the OG survival horror series - Silent Hill and Resident Evil - with its own twists. Sure, combat does feel a little repetitive after a while, but then again - same case with SH/RE. Smart puzzles. Immersive story. Great atmosphere. A true throwback to the PS2 era - gameplay and aesthetic-wise. A perfect way to scratch that survival horror itch in anticipation for the SIlent Hill 2 Remake. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of the survival horror genre, I've had this game on my wishlist since I heard about it, and bought it as soon as it became available.In my opinion, it has some rights and wrongs, but the things it gets right make it shine like the diamond in the rough that it is.Let's start with the not-so-good, if only to get it out of the way as quickly as possible: Obviously, in technical terms it's pretty average. Graphically, I'd compare it to a game from the early PS2 era. Aesthetically, it's rather bland and grey, and while I understand that may be intentional given the setting, I struggled to find any differentiating or unique elements in its design or aesthetics. It also has some problems and bugs (which I'm sure the developer will fix, given the interest they've shown so far). Finally, the combat mechanics are pretty basic, very much in line with what we would expect in a classic survival horror.And now, on to the good stuff. First of all, this is a game that puts a lot of emphasis on worldbuilding. Everything from the audio transmissions you can pick up, the personal subplots that pepper the setting in the form of documents, the design itself... all help to reflect the atmosphere of loneliness, abandonment and deep despair that the game aims to (and in my opinion, succeeds in) conveying. The plot is interesting and contains just the right amount of mystery while leaving enough questions open to keep you wondering after the game is over. The music, sound effects and voice acting are top notch.If you're a hardcore lover of classic survival horror, especially psychological horror like Silent Hill, Rule of Rose or Fatal Frame, give it a try. It's well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where it inspires you to just say, "Screw it, I wanna develop a game too!"Because there's a true passion here to emulate the elements of what makes the older survival horrors work.Even making damn sure that "modern controls" aren't overly powerful allowing you to whip your character around in an instant and instead implementing purposeful clunkiness with a turn radius.It's just one of those details along with the static camera placements that don't allow you to see exactly what's around a wall sometimes that truly recreates the classic horror experience.As things continued on, I learned that overly exploring isn't quite worth it as there can be wide empty areas and to just enjoy the more linear than expected pace. (Although don't leave to the next section shown on your graceful map too soon if you haven't solved a puzzle because there may be no way of going back to finish that puzzle. Unless there's like some huge backtracking moment later on, but enjoying what's here right now!)EDIT: It's a huge optional backtracking moment later onAs long as indie games like this continue to get supported, the health of the survival horror genre shall never die!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is everything I wanted it to be. So that would be a sick as ♥♥♥♥ survival horror experience. The music and sound design is bonkers impressive. With this and Signalis, Survival Horror lesbians stay winning and indies are keeping the genre alive in EXACTLY the way you'd want it to. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a good, short, Silent Hill fan game, this should do it. The visuals, sound and voice acting were very good. Beyond that, personally, I was sadly very disappointed in this game that I've been looking forward to for a very long time. I'd like to point out some things that really jump out as especially not ideal. Hopefully this could be helpful in future projects.-Monster design is very poor. Visually boring, and not connected to any themes or the world itself. Literally any flair or extra detail would have made them better.-Visually the game looks great, but the locations chosen were overwhelmingly boring. It really needed at least some striking, unexpected locations to break up the dark gray corridors.-What's up with all the empty rooms and places that had nothing in them? It really felt like I was getting punished for exploring, by having my time wasted again and again.-The Notes. Why were they so incredibly long? Actual paragraphs. And none of them said anything interesting or informing. It really felt like filler with no substance.-Nothing in the story connects in any meaningful way. The setting is Blade Runner, but it never comes into play beyond the intro. The on the nose allusions to Covid felt really out of place and almost in poor taste. And nothing in the story connects to the interpersonal relationship between characters.-The "demon voice" modulation on the main antagonist - please, don't use it anymore. It makes it sound silly. Just a good actor speaking in a normal voice would have been a thousand times more effective.-Giant Enemy Bug Monster. C'mon, man.Anyways, great job making a game all by yourself mate, that's a heroic achievement either way. I genuinely hope to play more games from you in the future, you got lots of great things going for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Preamble: I am still playing through the game.  This is based upon my impressions of a few hours of play.  I will update as necessary once I complete the title.I must preface this by stating that, unlike a lot of the YouTube reviewers whose videos on this game I watched, I was not a big player of PS2-era survival horror titles back in the day, having at most played about 30 minutes of Silent Hill 2* before getting distracted by other games.As such, I would not say that I necessarily have the same kind of nostalgia for the style that this game uses.  I say that because my personal lack of nostalgia makes the game's effect on me all the more poignant: I may not have played very much PS2 survival horror but I *did* play PS2 and this game unquestionably captures the essence of that era in all of the right ways.  It artifically limits its graphical fidelity to a style similar to the sixth generation of consoles but while doing so it also perfectly emulates the artistic techniques used by the more talented developers of that era to make the most of those limitations and the result is a game that very much looks like it could have been a lost PS2 classic.The story and atmosphere are, to the extent that I have played, appropriately creepy with plot details delivered piecemeal which is standard for the survival horror genre in general.  The game presents an opening premise, a reason for the protagonist to be where she is, and tells the rest of the story about why things are the way that they are through various notes found during gameplay.  The setting itself is not completely novel, being a seemingly abandoned village where something apparently went horrifically wrong some time ago, but the game presents it in an appropriately unsettling style with a decidedly British flavor, being that said abandoned village is in the UK; the intent was to evoke the imagery of older PS2 survival horror settings and it does so admirably (at least as far as my limited experience can discern).  I should note that I do feel as though the Blade Runner inspired setting does not show fully beyond the introduction -- though this may change as I progress further in the game -- as apart from some "retro-futuristic" technology seen in abandoned buildings the overall aesthetics of the game would not seem out of place in the real world.Gameplay is relatively simplistic, but that, too, is a throwback to the old survival horror games of yore going back even before the PS2 era.  Hollowbody is going for the sort of gameplay and combat feel that predated the innovations of Resident Evil 4 and, in that regard, I believe that it manages to accomplish that while offering just enough quality-of-life features to stave off some of the feeling of jankiness of the older games that it emulates.  This is not an action game and it is not trying to be; an argument could be made that the awkwardness of combat controls of the past were a result of technical limitations that no longer exist and thus are not necessary but this game is intentionally trying to emulate the style of those games and it was clearly balanced with that kind of control setup in mind.  Thus, the controls are, to me, fine -- just be aware of what you are getting into, as this is not a behind-the-shoulder shooter.Other than combat, which like in any good survival horror is often better avoided than engaged, the gameplay involves solving puzzles to progress.  These are rarely complex, but that is the nature of the genre -- mentally taxing puzzle solutions are the staple of point-and-click adentures, not survival horror games.Overall, I am having a very good time with this game.  I may not have the same level of nostalgia for PS2-era survival horror or Silent Hill in particular but I do have enough nostalgia for the PS2 generation to see the dedication of the developer in evoking that feel in this title while telling an interesting story in a suitably creepy and unsettling world.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly well made game, especially considering it's made by a solo developer. _childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: An impressively solid title especially for what was a solo dev project.A cool wee callback to the PS2 era of survival horror with mixed fixed camera angles etc with obvious draws from the near perfect Silent Hill 2 and some others too. There's defs time it feels it maaaaybe leans a bit too heavy into its inspirations like how the sound effects, UI, music and overall feel are definitely Silent Hill all over (particularly with the flash to red for saving and how the enemies make a particular radio static sound when nearby) but nothing overly egregious, and I am all for the fantastic soundtrack that captures that mix of melancholy and industrial depression.That being said the game does fall short in some aspects but I'm hesitent to give it the full brunt given truly what is here is remarkable for how it was made and it's not exactly a full priced title or anything. But there are things that feel like needing more polish or that do let the game down in the end if we're to be critical.The story starts off strong enough, intriguing mystery of a seemingly biological disaster, a strange alternative future brittish city now laying in ruins and a desperate dive into a long since quarantined zone to rescue a loved one (though I was dreading a "you were dead all along, you're loved one died here during the actual outbreak" twist the entire time XD). But it doesn't really go anywhere, you'll pick up bits and pieces of what happened through audio logs and such but by the end it feels like there's still at least a third of story missing to really make the "ahhhh" moment, having your dark horror remain in mystery is a tricky feat cause some will want more but some will just feel like they've not been given a complete story.By the end I was genuinely thinking I had at least one last chunk of the game to go all for it to somewhat unceremoniously and abruptly end with a lot of "it's up to you to interpret" vibes. There is environmental story telling, but not much that feels "meaningful".Gameplay is fine, some will say the combat is disappointing but I feel they're desperately in need of a reminder of what combat was like in Silent Hill esque games cause that was kinda the point. IT does granted feel like they're needs to be a tiny bit of rebalancing and touching up some areas, especially since honestly only in the one encounter and 2nd last area of the game  did I ever really feel the need to actually engage in the combat. Enemies are incredibly easy to navigate, even with the cities various roadblocks and debree to block your path, hell even the  were surprisingly harmless to run by that I honestly thought one of them was actually leading me to the next objective.Weapons are a fairly mixed bag also, the pistol honestly is the ol reliable and I wish I just used it more often, by the end of intended difficulty I had something like near 100 bullets left cause I kept thinking I'd need it for something more dangerous, the shotgun feels depressingly weak and barely an upgrade to the handgun which felt odd especially given the ammo scarcity (hell it doesn't even come loaded, who does that XD) and I even learned there's apparently a bow and a flamethrower but I never found those but still felt barely threatened outside of one forced encounter. Melee weapons are all over the place honestly, your starting plank is understandably weak and often leaves you feel like it's a last resort especially cause of how clunkily you wield it, often needing to practically hug the enemy to hit, but then I found the guitar in the same area, a weapon that done decent damage with an actually solid moveset and I never needed another melee weapon ever again. I'm to understand there's a bunch of melee weapons I missed but the only other one I found was the roadsign "axe" and it just as bad to use as the plank so back to the guitar for the whole game.Enemy designs are nice but granted nothing to really write home about nor do they feel like they tell a story or anything but that being said their sound design is top notch and genuinely unsettling.Level design overall is fine, there's many familiar layouts (the first major area being an all too familiar dingy and claustrophobic apartment complex), but it never truly feels like the spaces are being utilized to their fullest, there's lots of dead empty spaces or uninteresting dead ends (especially in the outside city streets areas). It's super nitpicky but there's also some small amateurish mistakes like how the wheelie bins are all scaled far too small, and some buildings the placing of windows and such don't look right in the slightest. The outside city area is definetly a low point though, while I'll fully say hats off to attempting to make so much of the outside area traversable (especially since it feels like there was efforts to make it feel like a believable brittish town) and not have it just railroad you where you need to go like the classic Silent Hill 1 map, but much like the SH1 map, there's way too much nothing to actually find and in some cases it just makes exploring feel like a chore as you plod back and forth making sure you didn't miss anything, and even moreso in one instance that has forced backtracking across a very uninteresting chunk of the map.Hollowbody's strengths definitely lie in the aforementioned sound design and it is drenched in atmosphere, while mechanically I never really felt at threat, the atmosphere does a solid enough job to never really let me feel truly at ease and blending a very realistic British depression with surreal horror is a vibe I can get with. I also love this games diegetic UI, it's so pleasently old school while also leaning into the cyberpunky vibes the game hides at the very corners of it's world building, complete with the little reflection of Micca's eye on the inventory/menu screen. Granted the map could be a bit better (though I found it personally satisfactory enough) and there was a rather common bug where at the very right of my inventory a silouette of whatever the recent item I picked up would glitch onto the screen causing some odd visuals.Puzzles are far the most part harmless but also lack that spark that made Silent Hill games stand out for it more. There's a somewhat decent safe code that took a bit, but then most of them were to the degree of "I need the round object to fit this round hole, if only there was round object in the very next room that fit this description" which isn't a criminal offense but it would have been nice if there were a few more brain teasers. There was one that annoyed me but moreso cause I feel it's solution was obvious . There's also one non puzzle that I loved but I can see it bothering others, I'd actually want to gush about it cause for me it was one of the coolest moments in the game but I feel it's one best left to discover yourself.While at the end of all this I feel I've been very critical I'd still say it's a worthwhile horror title to delve into especially if you're a fan of the PS2 generation of survival horror. Just maybe be sure to temper expectations if you're expecting the 2nd coming of christ or something like some other reviews are making out.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Good. Classic feel. Story weird. Me like. You buy.Pretty good for it's price and plays fairly well. Feels like the games that inspired it. Most bugs are visual (menu, dead enemy location is where they died- not where the model lies, this make burning corpses a little annoying). Was able to 100% in about nine hours. Not bad for a game made by one person. Can't wait to see the speedruns of the game. Should be fun to watch.The story is fairly simple, yet confusing as hell. A lot of unanswered questions. I'm definitely hoping that there will be more in the future. Though once you finish the game, you may not come back to it. Would definitely recommend despite this.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing achievement for a solo developer. Great art that is often just as beautiful and detailed as its main inspiration, Silent Hill 2. It lasts about as long as it should, and the atmosphere is THICC. If you're for some reason concerned about price-value ratio (why? the game is so cheap!) there's also a high amount of replay value, with mode unlocks aplenty. However, it's a fairly flawed game. There's some missing polish in some areas, and I'd say the primary issue is the pacing. About 1/3rd of the game takes place in an apartment building and I was desperate to leave. Too many apartments that served no purpose. The middle is a city section that is surprisingly hard to navigate thanks to another notable flaw: the map is almost useless (but sure does look cool!) Aside from one egregious bit of backtracking, it's not so bad.The last act picks up the pace, but has its own issues. There's a puzzle in the sewers where you have to collect some items in a featureless, grey maze. I managed to find all the items, entered the wrong corridor (there's no map, good luck navigating) and apparently triggered permanent progress and couldn't return to finish the puzzle. This is really, really bad and needs to be addressed. The entire sewer section needs some kind of visual direction. It's way too big, way too samey-looking, and even without the lockout issue described above, it's not fun.The story. I'd like to criticize the story but the game didn't give me one. I have no idea what the setting was, what the antagonist was or what happened during the course of the game. I certainly have no idea what happened in the ending I got. There's clearly things I missed, and alternate endings, but ideally, every path through a game should let you in on some kind of story. Much like Signalis, there's more a vague impression of a story than something you can sink your teeth into, but at least this gives your character some motivation and identity before the ending cutscene, so it's not quite as bad as in that game.Camera. My kingdom for being able to turn the camera with the right stick instead of constantly having to press L3 if I wanted to see where I was going. Right stick is currently pretty much useless, so this is a weird omission.There's a part (being vague here) where you have a conversation with someone and can influence what they do. The only problem is the result feels entirely arbitrary, and then the game mocks you for messing up something important. I don't think the psychology of this interaction makes much sense, and it's frustrating to, I'm guessing, lock the player out of important story elements because of it.Still, absolutely worth playing. Hollowbody understands survival horror gameplay far better than Signalis, but still doesn't quite give me that "godlike indie survival horror game" I've been on the lookout for. To be clear though, it is a monumental effort from the developer. When I saw in the credits that he also made the music, it blew my mind. Dude is hogging all the skill and talent.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Given it's a single person indie endeavor, I can't be too harsh on it;But I do wish it was a little bit longer for the plot to develop properly, less linear, the weapons had some weight to them (which is mostly solved by a little camera shake, to be fair) and with actual puzzles (except for the church one, the other ones are fetch quests), not to mention the last boss was underwhelming.That being said, great enemy design, great environment, great camera work, the voice actors really did a great job, the weapon variety was unusual in a good way.For the price tag and enjoyment I got out of it, I can't be mad at what the game is, but rather at what the Dev could've done with less time/budget constraints
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a banger year for new Survival Horror titles, and Hollowbody is no exception. I know people keep harping on this, but the fact that this is a one-person dev is extremely impressive, and I would have never guessed had I not known. The inspirations from Silent Hill are very apparent, and while I wouldn't say it brings much new into the genre, it pays homage to it very faithfully. The atmosphere, environments, limited supplies, and even mechanical options like a tank control toggle definitely shows a clear awareness of what people want in a game of this genre.Definitely some bugs here and there; most of them were just goofy cosmetic issues like clipping and bad enemy pathing, though there were also a few times when the fixed camera scenes would get stuck while I had to blindly figure out how to maneuver my character back on-screen. Still, nothing game-breaking and I'm sure will be polished with patches. Story is serviceable and interesting, treading familiar ground, but not so closely that it feels like a carbon copy of SH. It is short, you can beat it in a sitting pretty easily, but it's one I definitely can see myself going back to again on New Game+.Combat is...a bit clunky, but appropriate given classic Silent Hill's was too.The ambient music and sound design are solid, even genuinely unnerving at times.If you're looking to scratch the survival horror itch in the lead-up to Silent Hill 2 Remake, this is an incredibly well-made project, and a clear example of a talented fan's passion for the genre. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is tech-noir survival horror game developed by Nathan Hamley aka Headware Games. You play as Mica, a black market shipper who is searching for her partner in a exclusion zone but something ain't right and she has to do whatever it takes to survive and escape the zone.The best way to describe it, is probably Silent Hill with a touch of tech-noir. The focus lies more on the exploration and the narrative than the combat. You will notice very quickly after you leave claustrophobic apartment that the enemies aren't obstacles to overcome and the result is that the game is not really scary. Because the next areas like the park, houses or the Streets are very open so you can ignore and run around most of the enemies. I really liked the first hour during which you explore the Apartment segment, it's really tense and caustrophobic. The voice acting is also pretty solid and the controls are pretty smooth. The Radio static when a monster is close was also a neat easter egg. Parts of Hollowbody are also modelled around developer Nathan Hamley's home town of Bristol which just shows the passion that went into developing this game. But sadly the oppressive atmosphere from the beginning and the tech noir setting doesn't last long which was a bit disappointing. But considering that the entire game was created by just one guy makes it really impressive how well Hollowbody has turned out.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent throwback to late PS1 and PS2 era horror games. Controls and Camera angles might be a bit clunky and awkward to those who never experienced this time period, but it is bang on the mark. First hour had me tense and the remainder of the game never shook its creepy atmosphere, and an unshakeable sense of foreboding. For a one man band, it is a gem of a game and I wholeheartedly recommend it to fans of horror games and those out for a pang of nostalgia. Game is not very long (took me about 7hrs to complete) but I feel this is a good length for the money and there is also some replayability with alternate endings and a secret weapon for those willing to backtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: If you like your Silent Hills, then you'll love this. This is one of the best looking indie horror games I've seen, the UI is better than of those AAA games, the soundscape is eerie and creepy, perfectly fitting the game. The core gameplay loop is simple and easy to understand, as it is usually in games of this genre. The game runs quite well on (older) Steam Deck, FPS averaging 50 (from 30 to 60). I am happy that I backed this game
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a extremely atmospheric horror survival game. Throughout my time with the game I consistently felt an overwhelming atmosphere that kept me on edge. I expected scares in places where there were none and sometimes the horror was done in the opposite of what I would expect. It plays with your expectations and shows that sometimes being scared is actually about what isn't there. The music was pretty well-done. The locations were solid.I would say the only parts of the game that I disliked were some of the end sections and the city itself. A lot of repeating visuals can make the game feel repetitive. Alongside this, the game has a large amount of bugs that still need to be ironed out. Overall? The game was exception and extremely engaging. I do think some of the atmosphere dies out as the game goes on. Would have loved to have seen more of what the first section had. Hearing noises in areas only for things not to be there, visual scares, ect ect. For one person, this was pretty well done and has sparked a real genuine joy in me. I feel like horror has turned into a genre that anyone can dip their toes into but Hollowbody tried to do something old-school that was really refreshing to see. You CAN still make games on the old horror formula and they can be good.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Great throwback to ps2 survival horror. The start is a bit slow but once you are inside buildings exploring the game kicks in and feels good. Some nice quality of life stuff compared to older fixed camera games and survival horror, like letting you know you have an item to use or quickly swapping between melee/ranged or getting into the map.I was hesitant when i saw a 3D map as they can be confusing but it is done very well. Doors you cant access get automatically marked off as you'd want. Will continue to play but just alt tabbed out to give a hearty recommendation to anyone hesitant!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game quite a bit! Considering this is a single dev project, I'm quite impressed. I will say that the game starts off stronger than it ends and that the apartments section is, in restrospect, the strongest one. Lovely graphics, great vibe, I wish there was a bit more content, but it's a solid play. I will say with 7 hours I essentially turned every stone over; the average straight forward run will probably last you 3-5 hours
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished one ending. The game certainly has the spirit of Silent Hill running through its vein but not quite at the same level. I'd be remissed if i didnt say id like to see more from these devs though. They are certainly on the right track, just a bit more refinement needed. Bit more enemy variety, bit more that could be done with the setting, and more ramping in the physcological aspects for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Really amazing that a solo dev can deliver what AAA studios really struggle to do. An intriguing, tight, and terrifying game that knows its genre and excels at it. It wears its influences on its sleeve, and if you're a SH fan you'll feel right at home, but it'd be a mistake to think of it as a clone. It has its own world, its own tone, and it does what it does in a simple but effective way that most big budget titles fail to capture.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: "A bioterrorist attack on British territory forced the evacuation of the so-called “Western Cities”, leaving some unfortunate people confined. Mica goes in search of her friend Sasha, who has not forgotten and seeks justice."A survival horror that is for Silent Hill 2 what Alisa (C. Croes) was for the first Resident Evil, with a conscientious study of what worked in that one and deserved to be updated to the new trends. With a centered 3D camera that constantly gives way to cinematic still shots.The understanding of the sensations that SH2 scenarios transmitted, are here faithfully transferred, making us feel at home to the fans of that legendary title. The same applies to the puzzles, designed with old school flavor.While the design of the enemies is not very varied, they're effective in their context. One that is amplified by documents, radio static and environmental narrative. Combat, however, is kinder to the player.And like all good survival horror games, there are several endings to unlock, as well as a first-person mode and another with higher difficulty after finishing the game for the first time.I can assure you that my 16 year old self would have loved to play Hollowbody for a whole night, but my 33 year old self has tasted every little detail of this work as if it were a fine wine.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A great little slice of horror nostalgia, doesn't quite measure up to it's inspiration however ...Hollowbody is a compelling and engaging survival horror game, aping the golden era of the PS2 generation. Effectively blending cyberpunk aesthetics with traditional survival horror gameplay. Unfortunately for all of it's inspiration it never quite measures up to the standard from your Silent Hills or Resident Evils of the era, the few flaws there are become clear when measured up to them.I don't want to be to negative since the experience on offer here is still well worth experiencing and it shows great promise ahead.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Layers on layers of atmosphere and environment design, SH and Blade Runner fans will enjoy the vibe throughout- Voice acting was pretty decent for the most part- Light and cameras for the most part made a very good experience- Captures the gameplay of the old Silent HillsCons:- Melee combat (Making your weapon cycle animation with no way to control it, that all has different range and timing is awful, and becomes especially egregious when you pick up other melee weapons that have unorthodox animations.- Minor, but lots of typos (even beginning as far as when the controls pop up on screen with 'Swap Taget'), UI glitches when scrolling through enough items, bugs such as pausing when about to change the camera means the camera can be stuck in the previous position. All these things carried over from the demo and was not caught.- While capturing the fixed and dolly style camera that SH employs very well, there's some points where it's frustrating, especially when the enemies are actually quite quiet even up close. RE created tension by not being able to see them, but always hear them - this game lacks that tension.- Cinematics felt half-completed, especially any kind of horror ones.- Map and puzzle design was very linear which made the outdoors exploration boring, just run down a very large open corridor.Overall I would say it was a very lukewarm experience, nothing really stood out, and it didn't feel like it built up a mystery despite trying to.6/10. Still a good game and a huge achievement for one person (Same as SIGNALIS is for a 2 person achievement) - There unfortunately is just much better polished and more ambitious projects out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: So I was turned onto this game because some of my favorite YouTubers launched reviews for it the day of release. Hearing that it was a fixed camera angle survival horror game that harkened back to the PS2 era I was immediately interested. Then after looking up a trailer and watching a little bit more I came to Steam and noticed it had a launch sale price. On my end it seemed like a low risk to give it shot and so I did. I was greeted with exactly what I was hoping it would be. The game is abolutely a love letter to that PS2 style of survival horror gaming and I am all here for it.Positives:The graphics, environements, and creature designs all looked like something that would have come out at the start of the 6th console generation. Throughout my playthrough I had so many kicks of nostalgia. The fixed camera, the character movements, and so on were all reminicscent of those old school games. Also, all the voice actors did a great job as I found the performances solid. I really enjoyed the creature designs and thought they were pretty grotesque looking. It's also a nice digestible game to. Much like those old school horror games a player could easily do a speed run. It was also a good call to have different modes from casual to normal and then being able to unlock a higher difficulty, new game+, and even a first person mode (which I am eager to try next). There are different ways to experience it after the initial encounter warranting mutliple playthroughs. There is also a few different endings depending on how you handle certain events. This for me is a staple of the genre and it is impressive that the creator of this game included that. I also typically enjoy game music and so when I can I buy the soundtrack with the game. Luckily the soundtrack is nice and atmospheric and like the game itself is very reminscient of it's genre. There is also options for changing to tank controls (yes please) if you are really craving that old style of control. Playing this game with tank controls felt like coming home again.Negatives:I can't think of too many negatives as I enjoyed the bulk of the game. Most of it had to do with graphical stuff like occasional glitches such as monsters being dead but still be making sounds, at one point I entered a section where the door got blocked up and after clearing the challenge the blockage vanished. Not in a transitional way it was more like the game was supposed to get rid of it, didn't, but then remembered it was supposed to. It was probably the jankiest segement. There was a monster dog that occasionally showed up during some of the sections and it would always run past me only ever deciding to attack me once or twice but for the most part couldn't care less I was there. Not sure if this is based on difficulty or if something is wrong with the programming. Until it attacked I really thought it was guide dog. I think the story could have used some more fleshing out. I believe I get the gist of it but would have liked to have seen maybe some more cutscenes and the final boss was a bit of a let down.Overall, I really enjoyed this game and for a solo creator his passion for this genre shined through. Every decision came from a place of love for survial horror games and I wish him the best. For me, if he was this good on his own I can only imagine what he could do with a slightly bigger team. I actually hope he makes a good chunk from sales, is able to hire some extra hands, at which he can make a sequel to this and make it bigger and better. The indie developers are what are keeping this old school era of survival horror alive and with devs like Headware Games I think the future is looking pretty bright.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: WOW!  I can't believe this was made by one person! (With voice actor help of course!)This was a treat of a game, and the dev was very aware of what made Silent Hill special.  I liked the use of random sounds and random bits of music popping in at any given moment the same way Akira Yamaoka would execute the sound design.  It was a real treat.I also loved the environmental designs and the atmosphere of this game,  I do highly suggest giving this game a try.. Now.. be prepared, this game is rather short!  But it has multiple endings, so while it's short, the multiple endings give it replayability and the fact all THAT and the music and design of it all is done by one person alone is REALLY magnificent to me.  Worth it, and I hope this game gets some attention, because it deserves it!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: the atmosphere is excellent with the combination of the soundtrack, visuals, and enviroment designs make it very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ creepy to traverse around. the gameplay is a bit lacking (the shotgun sucks so much and it makes me sad) and the main story is lacking a bit. For a one dude dev team, he nails a ton of what makes survival horror games good but when the credits rolled, i felt a bit underwhelmed.  Despite the few gripes i got with it, would still recommend if you want some good survival horror for an afternoon or 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a love letter to classic survival horror games. Not enough bullets, slow melee stance too many monsters. If you enjoyed Silent Hill, Siren, the original REs and modern survival horrors like Signalis you'll find a lot of influences from those here. I liked the story a lot. The world building and environmental story telling was great. The puzzles could be a bit of back tracking I didn't expect. Once I got used to how they were going to be it became easier. There was two issues I ran into that I can actually over look. First issues I ran into is there was some sound issues towards the very end of the game with one of the phone calls cut scene. All the sound was extra loud and I was unable to hear any other audio but ambience/background sounds. Second issue was a bit worse. Game said to use controller. I said okie dokie dug around found my controller. Went to go use melee and it would not go into the stance for whatever reason. Shooting worked just fine but I couldn't melee. So this made the game a challenge for me as having limited bullets and unable to possibly use melee to get out of a jam. Luckily my chat was smarter than me and maybe about half way through the game they suggested I tried the keyboard and mouse. Melee worked like a charm and I became a murdering machine. Honestly I will just keep playing on a mouse and keyboard but I'm a weirdo and play a lot of controller suggested games this way.Great game short sweet creepy as all hell. Will get the other endings soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on kickstarter and am happy with how it turned out. The game is pretty short, like 4 hours for me. For a one person effort though it is a crazy achievement to make a game like this. It nails the vibe it is going for. If you enjoy old school ps1/ps2 horror games, especially in the vein of silent hill I think you would like it. I do wish there were a bit more puzzles. I enjoyed the safe opening one a lot. Also the combat is kind of meh. I realize it is going for silent hill type combat, but personally I dont find the style interesting at all. Support indie devs
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give more time but something about the camera when it follows the character gets me too nauseated to play. I will say tho, after that intro, I really was digging the neo future setting. Definitely Res vibes, and a sure recommend to those looking for a throwback to the good Ole days, just sadly kept making me sick. I refuse to say it's because I'm getting old.. aye yi yi.Great work dev! Here's to hoping I can give another shot sometime and not get nauseated xD
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough! If you've grown up with games like SH and RE, this game is just for you.The atmosphere, lighting, music and even controls bring you back to those old PS1 days (of course with "a little bit" better graphics and controls). A few jump scares got me good! There's a few puzzles here and there, that were not too difficult but also not too easy. Could've had more tbh. I love me some puzzle! Also, the voice acting was amazing! Took me around 6 hours to finish, but I did take my time enjoying everything. I highly recommend this game! One of my favourites this year for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: This was an awesome little survival horror game with some pretty big Silent Hill vibes. It oozes atmosphere, which I feels is super valuable for these types of games (preferable over jump scares, imo). Melee combat feels a bit clunky, but not in a bad way (kinda like in a ps1 era resident evil way). Highly recommended for fans of Silent Hill and Resident evil who want a short little romp that you spend a handful of hours on.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: A depressingly accurate depiction of growing up in an economically deprived small British town in the 80s & 90s. Apart from the guns. We had those taken away in 1996 for some reason. Spot on besides that. -------------------------------------------Pretty damn great survival horror experience. A tad short and lighter on puzzles than I'd like, but more than worth the asking price. NG+ stuff is a welcome addition. Dev clearly knows their stuff and I'm excited to see his future work.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody was A truly mixed experience for me. Easily one of my most anticipated indie games of the year, and Its very impressive for A single dev. But I can't help but feel A little let down by the game overall. While I would recommend this game to anyone who's A fan of survival horror games. Anyone who's not. This game Is most likely not going to do It for you. While the atmosphere, and world look great. It just misses on so many components that make A great survival horror game. Lack of puzzles. Basically no bosses. There's different enemies. But they all function virtually the same, and the street areas feel like they are there for padding out the runtime. Not to mention the size of these areas make the enemies virtually none threats that you can run pass, and this takes away the incentive of killing them. So you have plenty of ammo In moments where you have to fight enemies. So your never stressed or worried about Ammo or even health. Though the brightest spot with the game for me Is the voice acting, and the first person mode you unlock after your first playthrough. The game plays fantastic like this, and really should of been the approach the dev took with the game. The way everything Is presented to the player through this perspective makes the experience 10x better. With that said. I really hope we get A Hollowbody 2 or something similar. Because the dev Is clearly talented, and with A little fine tuning. This experience could become one of the best out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game a good review when I finished my first run but changed my mind after obtaining every achievement and endings. This game doesn't have that much to offer there're only 4 unique enemies and just one boss and the boss fight is very boring, there’re 2 normal endings for this game and 1 special ending which you can only unlock in a special condition in the hardest difficulty. The 2 normal endings are almost identical and don’t leave any impact at all, at first I thought the game ended too soon because I picked a wrong choice which led to a bad ending but perhaps if I had picked the right one there might have more content behind it (ex. omori) but i was wrong I experience almost everything in the first run and the second ending doesn’t change much from the first one and that really disappoint me.In summary, the gameplay and atmosphere during the run are very enjoyable, but the ending feels hollow.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAY: 7/10GENERAL DIFFICULTY: 3/10PUZZLE DIFFICULTY: 4/10SETTING: 9/10LENGTH: JUST RIGHTREMINDS ME OF: SILENT HILL, OBSCURE, RESIDENT EVIL-----------------------------------------------------------------A well done horror game made by one person. Silent Hill 2 is clearly one of the main inspirations but it also reminded me of other early 2000s games like Obscure. Melee combat is a tad clunky to use effectively in my opinion and ammo a little too plentiful for a proper challenge, however I would say the setting makes up for it. The streets of a town in England are effectively portrayed here, right down to the little yellow alarm boxes on the walls of some houses. The puzzles are easy, which is okay with me this time and there seems to be at least one branching path. Story-wise, it's good enough but I would not call it particularly deep. I also do not think it needed to be though. All in all, well done to the developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: a fairly short classic-inspired horror game. the combat and puzzles seemed appropriately challenging for the game. i personally really loved the visuals and sound design. they perfectly captured the ruined town you were exploring, and really added to the experience. it was a really enjoyable game to play. and an incredible achievement for the dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty cool !If you like survival horror games, with heavy "Silent Hill like" atmosphere, you'll love Hollowbody.The puzzles are cool, the story is quite cryptic but I enjoyed my first playthrough. It seems toi have several endings (like SH games). I had a "bad" one, unfortunately, but I will get all of the other ones ! The game doesn't use too much backtracking (except for an optionnal but OP weapon).You have melee weapons and guns, but I didn't see any differences for the melee weapons except for the animation. The damages seems to be the same, it's not important but it could have been cool to make some melee weapons better than the others.Oh, and if you're too scared to play a lesbian character, go somewhere else. It's SO fun that the game is being critiqued about the sexuality of a fictionnal character (wich is not even a real big point of the game nor the plot). It's a freaking game, if you can't say anything about the gameplay, and prefer being homophobic instead, please, keep your mouth shut and stay a silent incel. XOXO.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve already spent my own money on this gem, now it's your turn! Play the demo and prepare to drop some cash - it's that good. Here's why:I’ve been following Hollowbody’s development for over a year, and I’m happy to say the final game is everything I hoped for. Nathan Hamley has nailed the atmosphere, creating a survival horror game that stands out from the crowd.The opening scene really hooked me with its dialogue—workers in hazmat suits casually chatting about how their crumbling world affects their jobs and daily lives. It reminded me of a Tarantino film, where mundane conversation is mixed with the gritty reality of their situation, making it all feel more grounded and unsettling.The game’s fixed camera angles and mood-soaked environments bring back that classic Silent Hill vibe, but with a fresh, cinematic flair. Every scene is dripping with tension, and at 4-5 hours, the pacing is perfect—it doesn’t drag or overstay its welcome.While some puzzles and navigation can get a bit tricky, they’re minor issues in an otherwise stellar game. If you love atmospheric, story-driven horror on the classic survival horror formula, Hollowbody is a must-play. No wonder it’s trending on Steam—this game has earned it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true love letter to Silent Hill 2/3 made by a solo developer and a great voice cast. My first play through was on Intended difficulty and I couldn't put it down, taking about 6 hours and I then realised it was 2 am. Random aside: Sad guy in a grey hoodie, rooms full of Polaroids, jumping off buildings, backtracking to fix subways with fuses... people keep saying Resident Evil and Silent Hill but are we sure that this isn't Cry of Fear?Despite any criticisms that I have, I'm truly impressed by what has been accomplished in a relatively short amount of time and the developer should be proud. It's definitely a game that I would recommend to survival horror veterans.Things that I liked:- The atmosphere is spot on, the sound design constantly had me like someone was in the next room or breathing down my neck. I'm so used to horror games that they usually don't phase me but some sections had me quite tense with the odd effective jump scare.- The world-building is intricate, with gritty visuals and a haunting soundscape that perfectly complements the claustrophobic, dystopian setting.- One aspect of horror games form that era they didn't copy is terrible voice acting. It's actually quite rare to hear regional British accents in video games and they did a good job.- I generally prefer shorter horror games that don't overstay their welcome and the game is short; it's fairly easy to 100% it (including the 3 endings) in 8 hours. - The main character is well written and voice acted and reacts to situations in pretty believable ways.- The 2 true puzzles were good. The are other puzzles but they are mostly just about using the correct item or combining two items. I feel like the heart puzzle should of at least had more to it.- - I was pretty invested in the story and it was cool to listen to the signals/flashbacks and read the notes for more historical context; some of the content was legitimately harrowing.- I wasn't expecting the sewer gimmick and it legit made me feel crazy- The implementation of both tank controls and 'modern' fixed camera controls. I can work with both but prefer the modern style and as I understand it, it's quite difficult to program, so I appreciate how natural it feels.- The first person mode for beating the game is pretty cool and a good incentive/fun way to go through NG+.Things that I didn't like:- The enemies hit like absolute trucks even on the normal difficulty. I died to one of the early enemies and lost 20 minutes of progress because I wanted to explore rather than backtrack to the previous save point and heal items were quite limited at the beginning.- I died once trying to use melee near the start and it felt pretty jank so I just used projectiles for the rest of the playthough. I'm aware that the game is copying to jank combat on purpose from the SH2 era but it feels even worse than SH2. Even using guns exclusively, I ended the game with 100+ pistol rounds, 32 shotgun shells etc because the dominate strategy is just to run away.- The map is 3D and supposed to be futuristic but the maps are very flat so it just makes it harder to parse.- The body burning mechanic is a cool Evil Within/REmake/(Signalis?) call back but given that the lighter never runs out, there isn't limited inventory, it feels like it just adds unnecessary busy work to the hard mode and reinforces the fact that the dominant strategy is just to book it constantly- - - - You can't skip cut scenes. I did replay the game on hard mode to try 1st person mode and get the last achievements but it dragged a bit having to do the prologue again.- The pacing can be a bit weird. It can take up to 30 minutes to get to the first enemy encounter, which is longer than even Amnesia: The Dark Descent which I consider a masterclass in horror pacing and suspense.- It's easy to get locked onto the wrong enemy and get spun around or hit in the back.- The first person camera mode had quite a lot of head bob and be quite awkward; kinda wished it was just c-stick to aim.Bugs that I noticed:- In first person mode if there are enemies in the crawling position and you go in and out of the menu they T-pose before dropping into the crawling animation again- If you finish the game holding a weapon you will start new game+ still holding that weapon- Occasionally difficult to pick up items, requiring you to be right on top of them or a very specific angle. This is especially bad for burning bodies in the hard mode.- When you interact with certain things, the player model can snap awkwardly into place.- Not really a bug per say, but if you lock onto a dog enemy and it runs into the distance the lock-on stays awkwardly.- It feels like the shotgun range doesn't have drop off like it should.- I press the menu button and it selects Options first instead of Resume Game.- I got the Riven ending and the secret ending at the same time on my second play through and I'm not sure if I saw the correct cut scenes. I got given 2 or 3 eyeball key chains too.- Sometimes when burning bodies I got a weird messed up menu.
