_childDocuments_.review: HollowBody is a survival horror that takes inspiration by the great ones from the past like silent hill 2-3 and is mixed with sci-fi vibes. it's also very close to the previous title Chasing Static with little and big references here and there.The combat feels really punchy and satisfying if you know what to do. Maybe i was expecting more from the shotgun with the standard enemies.The ps2 aesthetic is really spot on and it almost feel like a forgotten survival horror from that era.There are a few mistakes and little bugs here and there but i'm sure the dev will fix them. Things i don't really like are the puzzles, except for one in the first area. The others are like find the object, backtrack a little and put it in the right place. Most of the times the solution is in the very same area of the puzzle...like easy-sometimes baby mode(?).Another thing that i heard a lot around, the story is very confusing. And even with all the pieces of informations it's still headscratching. Maybe it need just a few more notes, audio logs or characters conversations to make this story not incomplete...don't get me wrong i like my story to be mysterious and up to interpretation but let's say not like this one. Maybe a lore\director's cut update can fix this. Overall i like the game even with the shortcomings, it feels good and nostalgic but keep in mind that there are some things that keep this one to be great like other modern indie survival horror (In sound of mind, Tormented Souls, Amnesia the Bunker, Signalis, ecc...)It's a solid 7,5. _childDocuments_.review: Here's My Review For Hollowbody. The game isn't very long if you just focus on the story and maneuvering past enemies. I beat it in about a little over 4 hours while reading texts you can find for world building and looking at all the cut scenes. The atmosphere is done really well and the tone of the game suits it very well too. I enjoyed the art-style of the characters and enemies. It was an overall enjoyable experience for me. I very much recommend this game to anyone interested in this genre. The positives: -Gameplay is great for those who enjoy old school horror games. Even includes tank controls-The voice acting is good and serves the story well. -The game has extras like first person mode, big head mode and harder difficulties for replayability. Can see how damaged you are without needing to go into menu to see health.-Some hidden secrets and things to see that you have to go out your way to access but nice addition. The negatives: -Melee did not seem to work correctly. Never got to swing any of the melee weapons because I just couldn't.  -Some of the dialog in the documents you find have some typos or worded very strangely. -Not many, if any, boss battles and very little enemy variety.-have leeches that run along the ground but they don't really attack you unless you literally stand still.  -music will cut out at times but nothing too distracting.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I really get into writing this review I'll just say: buy it. Seriously, just buy it.  Block out like 5 hours, get in a dark room and just go.I'll start with my small list of things that are technically criticisms (but I think could be fixed pretty easily) since I wanna just gush about this already:-There are a few times in the game where it wants you to press A (or E if you're on keyboard) to further the dialogue and then there are times where you'll see the A prompt but then it'll auto continue and it's never super clear why that is. Could be an easy fix, small issue in the grand scheme of things.-There's a few times where a small amount of items/doors can be a littttttle hard to see due to the camera angles, but again another small issue that can be easily fixed.-There are a small handful of items that require a ridiculously precise angle to grab. That can absolutely be fixed with a few tweaks so I'm sure before long it'll be fixed!-The map has the typical red door on the map means locked and blue means good. I would have liked to see red for locked, blue for good, and some other color for doors that are inaccessible. I know in other 2000's eras games they'd mark it with an X, so maybe that?Now my only two gripes:-The combat is a little... clunky. Specifically the melee weapons honestly. Bit of learning curve when it comes to learning how far away you can be to hit enemies, and the act of hitting them looks a bit strange some times and feels a bit strange too. I think the guns are perfectly fine, maybe could use a bit more weight to them in the animations but again totally fine! -My other gripe is the lack of  Spoilered that because some people really don't want to know how many of something there is, just to be safe.  NOW, onto what I really want to get to, the positives!!-LOVE the music. Feels right out of a early 2000's horror game without feeling dated in the slightest. Couple pieces in there that could be real classics down the line.-Nails the blend of PS1/Early PS2 graphically. Looks like someone found a copy of a lost 2000's horror game that never got published till now.-The atmosphere, WOW. From the moment the game boots up I'm sold. Never been across the pond but it looks and feels very authentic and like a real place that could exist. Dark, grimy, claustrophobic at times.-Said atmosphere is backed up by the phenomenal sound design. The pounding rain, the moans of an enemy just around the corner, a baby cry as you stomp out one of the creatures. Great great stuff.-I was not anticipating voice acting so that was a lovely surprise! And another surprise, it's really good! I really enjoyed it, I thought for sure it was going to just be a text filled adventure. Especially love Mica's voice, and the voice over the phone. Had a good time reading the hidden journals/letters/articles spread across the game. Also the signals, cool way to show a bit of the before times without doing something big and grandiose.-I'm always an absolute sucker for horror games that have lots of puzzles that are just "oh now how in the world do I do this/get over there?" and you gotta find random items to get through, some fun ones in here. Hopefully in a future sequel/future horror game you do there'll also be more conventional puzzles, similar to the  puzzle. That was my favorite in the game!That all being said, I give the game a strong 8. Great atmosphere, sound design, story, music, characters, plenty of little puzzles... if you're a fan of early 2000's horror games ala SH2, you'll love it!Playing this feels like getting in on the ground floor of a future star developer, especially since it was essentially built by one person! As someone who spent two years building a decent 4-5ish hour game for my friends in RPG Maker, I'm unbelievably impressed with what you were able to accomplish here. _childDocuments_.review: I found out about this game completely by accident via survival horror Twitter; I wasn't a backer, but I thought it was interesting and was waiting on the release since I played and loved Chasing Static. I've only played through the first part so far, so take my review with a grain of salt - I will update upon completion.I think we gotta remember what this game is - It's an oldschool Silent Hill/ResE 2000s/PS2-worship nostalgia game, with all the associated clunk and cheese - manage your expectations accordingly. We're going for SH dead-wife melodrama with polygonal butts and heavy atmosphere. Leave your raytracing, particle physics, and 200-hour AAA sandbox games at home. I appreciate that they updated the setting with some BladeRunner vibes and a world that isn't just Foggy Sadtown Times With Mr. Sadman (tm)-It's nice to see a game like this that isn't just a bad SH clone and has some creativity in the setting. It feels like it pays a little homage to all the cheesball sci-fi games and B-Movies of the 2000s, which was unexpected but a welcome addition. There are parts where you're running past abandoned mechs or viewing "ancient" future tech and it adds a fun layer on top of the standard horror vibe in most SH clones.I love fixed-camera games and have been thirsting for them to come back, and I think Hollowbody does a great job with that idea and has an overall very pleasing cinematic flair to it. You can tell a lot of stylistic intentionality went into the visual decisions, though I think a bit of functionality is sacrificed at times - such is the nature of fixed cam so I am not mad at it. You can tell visual aesthetics are the dev's strong point and leaning into the SH-style meditative melancholy does the game a lot of favors and hides a lot of blemishes.I don't think it's that much worse to play with a keyboard/mouse either, so if you can't afford a console controller I don't think it's a dealbreaker - you should try the game anyway. It's a little clunky but it feels a lot like the PlayStation classics it wants to reference,  so it feels ok even though it's imperfect. Playing with keyboard reminded me a lot of running ResE on desktop emulators in HS in the 2000s.Hollowbody does feel a little style-over-substance. Once you get done being impressed with how much it feels exactly like a specific flavor of 2000s survival horror game, there's not so much left afterwards - I am not very far in yet but I will say the plot feels a little cliche and limited storywise; from reading other reviews it's not the longest gameplay either. I'm seeing folks saying they are finishing the game in under 5 hours in some cases. It also does feel a bit derivative at times - I know we all love Silent Hill but I also have already played Silent Hill and would love to see the dev get weirder with it. Chasing Static (the dev's other game) was great because it also referenced B-Horror Sci-Fi like The Thing etc so it felt unique while still having that nostalgia vibe we all crave. There was also the whole static-y audio thing taken to an extreme where it went past being a bit and started to feel like another character. Holllowbody doesn't have anything like this so it falls a bit short once you start looking more closely.The world could have more surprises and easter eggs to discover too - not only to build B-plots but also to reward folks who instinctively look under every rock in a game. You gotta know your audience after all, and some of us are gonna be out here trying every door and poking every trash can and corpse, even if there's never anything there. Please respect my mental health diagnoses enough to give me a treat for it.However, again, this is also about managing expectations - a solo dev built this in Unity and it's referencing an era where games had a limited scope and usually one main, often underdeveloped, plot thread. So the limitations do feel stylistic to some degree. That said, when you're looking at things like SH2 or ResE as inspiration, you can still do a lot of implied worldbuilding and story expansion if you write your game well - I feel like Hollowbody lacks a little depth in this regard and isn't quite fully baked. I would also say gameplay things feel a little unpolished beyond a stylistic choice - the HUD for interacting with objects can be clunky and the menu is very Unity 101. Some parts of the terrain block you when there's no reason you shouldn't be able to walk over them, and some ammo boxes, etc are glitchy. Combat is also ROUGH and movement can be a pain- please do yourself a favor and turn on tank controls. I know it's a solo dev but I would think that this kind of thing could be handled with a few more hours of work and testing. I am sure it will be updated over time and I know they wanted to get the game out, but I'd be slipping if I didn't mention it.All said, I think it's very solid for what it is, so again: I'm not mad at it. I came here expecting a diet SH2 clone riding on the coattails of the oldschool graphics nostalgia wave, and Hollowbody delivered an interesting combo of those ideas with a couple fun updates. I'll give it a 6 or 7/10 and will be happy to update that as bug fixes etc come in. It met my expectations and is a job well done, especially for one dude manifesting it out of pure commitment to the bit. Definitely worth checking out - and while you're at it you should check out Chasing Static too. They're both worth the time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is an absolute gem of a survival horror game, capturing the perfect balance of tension and atmosphere without relying on cheap jump scares. From the moment I started playing, I was hooked by its eerie, decaying world. The environments are stunningly detailed, with a gritty, dystopian feel that really immerses you in the setting.What struck me the most is how well the game builds tension. I was constantly on edge, but never to the point where it felt overwhelming or exhausting. The atmosphere alone does most of the work, keeping you alert and uneasy. The puzzles and resource management add just enough challenge to make you think strategically, and I loved how combat wasn’t always the focus—sometimes it’s smarter to avoid a fight.It’s mind-blowing that this game was developed by just one person. You can feel the passion and care in every detail, from the story to the voice acting, and even in the pacing of the save points. I didn’t encounter any bugs, which is rare these days, and it’s clear the developer put a lot of effort into polishing this game.I’d recommend Hollowbody to both seasoned horror fans and those new to the genre. It’s not about shock value, but rather about crafting an experience that keeps you engaged and a bit on edge throughout. I’m genuinely having a blast playing, and I can’t wait to see what this developer creates next!

_childDocuments_.review: I am LOVING this game. Let me explain why;First off, I see a lot of people comparing it to RE1R and such, this is NOT resident evil. Resident Evil has and always will be a bit faster and more action packed. RE1 was def slower, but you still had a lot of combat encounters. There are far few in this game. What this IS is a love letter to survival horror, and the gameplay falls more in line with Silent Hill 2. It is much slower, relies on atmosphere, and likes to use combat encounters when it's least expected. There have been tons of times where no warning, the camera would switch, and I would see an enemy looming over me. The atmosphere is INTENSE. Part of survival horror is knowing how to use sound effectively, specifically knowing where to use silence, and this game strikes that balance borderline perfectly. There are some areas where the only sound is your footsteps and it is HARROWING. The only place I would have suggest to maybe tone down the music would have been outside because when I turned the music to mute, it was terrifying and really drove home that feeling of isolation. The voice acting too is superb. Within the first three hours there was a scene that literally made me cry because of how it was written and the heartfelt and emotional voice acting.The puzzles are pretty hard! The very first puzzle I encountered there was something to throw me off and the second I had to look up a guide because the solution is not something I would just think of, but once I did, it made a weird sense. Some of the puzzles definitely have that "Silent Hill 2 use the can-opener on the can to get a lightbulb" logic.There are not too many negatives I have for this game. There are glitches, such as every melee weapon I have used with the exception of the starting one sometimes glitches out animation wise and will stop swinging in a wide open area, mid swing, causing me to get hit. It also will randomly un-equip my weapons sometimes after coming out of a menu. One thing to keep in mind is this is made by ONE person, who truely understands what makes an emotional survival horror game great.This is an amazing buy, for under $20 USD, even off discount, well worth it. Can't wait for my other playthroughs and to try to 100% the game.Updates after finishing 100%:I would have preferred a few more boss battles like  but overall it blew me away. For $15 we got a game that most AAA developers (or lets be real AA or indie devs since AAA devs have abandoned horror with the exception of Capcom and shockingly Konami) struggle to emulate, let alone create. The ambiance, the feeling of isolation, everything is so well done. I even found myself turning the music down all the way when outside for a bit because the silence and footsteps really drove it home. The puzzles tripped me up slightly, and one even had me pulling my notes app to make note of things. It feels big in a decent way too, the city feeling like the streets are never-ending and you just hope you don't hit a dead-end.Endings discussion ahead:Overall I absolutely loved the game. I'm extremely grateful that 100% it was not insane like for instance, RE1Remake. I played through it 3 times. Once on normal, once on easy (to get all the documents and signals), and once on Punishing for the best ending in the game (there is no argument to that, if you say otherwise, you are incorrect.)My final thought is that after you beat the game PLEASE, PLEASE  it gives a completely different vibe and makes you appreciate the world-building so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a brilliant love letter to a lost era of survival horror. _childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed the 5 hours I spent playing Hollowbody, the atmosphere is pretty good, there are quite a few really good sections, and while it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥, hitting dudes with melee is quite satisfying. The game is also really good to look at, honestly the game looks so pretty, this is what I wish devs would aim for when making "PS2 graphics games" it's really nice. Voice acting was pretty solid too, very british lolNow for the cons, the game has like 2 solid puzzles and the rest are "combine these 2 items next to the thing to open the thing" puzzles, not much engaging tbh. And this might differ from person to person, but I felt like the game was showering me with bullets and healing items, was at like 55 pistol rounds, 16 shotgun shells and like 9 healing items at some point lol kinda makes you lose the feel of "survival horror" at that point but I get it, your average player might screw it up and lose all their ammo and healing items and then give a bad review for the game, understandable but I wish it was kinda toned down a bit cuz I think I finished the game with like 12 healing items and only shot my shotgun twice throughout the game lol enemies are pretty generic without much variation but I guess it's okay since it's going for that silent hill vibes not the RE feel. Also there is a bit of jank here and there, quite a few invisible walls and the music would cut off for a split second I think to reset the loop or something lol I don't mind these things but some might find them annoying. Also the map ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ keeps rotating on its own for no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason it's infuriating lolanother thing that bothered me is on the "free-cam" sections which are like 80% of the game, you have to press the left stick to re-orient the screen to look forward instead of just using the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ right stick cuz the game is so afraid of being labelled a 3rd person action game I guess? I dunno but it felt annoying having to press L3 constantly to fix the camera while moving R3 did ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The endings also suck ass, there was so much potential here but oh well.It might sound like I hated the game but I actually quite enjoyed it, and for the price it's a really enjoyable experience, i'd give it 7/10, really wish some things were done better but what we got is a really good experience that kept me quite engaged throughout, I never felt like I wanna rush to finish the game and be done with it like how I feel with most games these days. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody embodies (excuse the pun) a lot of what you would expect from a PS2-inspired Survival Horror. From narrow hallways to open streets, the environment gives you the feeling of an area long abandoned, but still hiding secrets. Mica must scour this landscape in search of her friend.I think this game handles the genre well, and I only had couple real hangups with the design overall. Firstly, the environments didn't really seem to connect with our main protagonist. It felt like someone exploring someone else's world without any real reflections on the character themselves. Secondly, the design of the sewer "puzzle" left me visibly upset as I felt robbed of the chance to complete what was laid before me, with zero indication if I had interacted correctly or wrongly. It felt miserable to leave that area, unsatisfied.Overall, I still recommend this game. It doesn't take any new strides in storytelling or mechanical depth, but as it is made by a single developer and at a $17 price tag, it's a no-brainer for any fans of survival horror. It has replayability, secrets, and multiple endings that all bundle well into an interesting, if simple, package.You can also find my video review here: Well done, Headware Games. I look forward to what you work on next.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful homage to games like Silent Hill, fixed camera angles, tank controls, feels clunky in a 'good' way. Some derpy camera issues here and there, but nothing game ruining for me. Beat the game in about 3.5 hours, and that was with me getting stuck on a puzzle or two.  None of the puzzles are very hard or mind blowing, but just enough to keep you engaged. I felt the games default difficult was WAY too easy. I also wasn't sure how to actually do melee combat because I missed the first tutorial for it until WAY later in the game when I got it figured out by accident (Basically if you have a melee weapon out and you try to melee without an enemy nearby, your character ALWAYS just stomps. They will only swing their weapon when youre close to an enemy)   I only had to heal 4 times in the whole game, and had surplus ammo by the end. I know I can new game+ the difficulty up, but I don't know that I really want to play the whole game again. I kind of absorbed everything by the end. Also, there is multiple endings it seems, so if you're into 100%ing games, you're in for a treat, and there's an unlockable first person mode to make the game a whole other experience when you beat the game. _childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a fun nostalgia trip to the PS2 era of horror games and one that can be recommended to genre veterans although with some caveats. It took me a bit over 3 hours to beat the game on the "Intended" difficulty on a playthrough that involved a fair amount of optional exploring around so don't go in expecting a long game. That being said there are at least a couple different endings and once you beat the game you unlock NG+ that allows you to select a harder difficulty mode "Punished" along with some other NG+ things so there is some minor replay value there.What does the game do well? I think it often managed to nail the atmosphere especially when it mixes in some psychological horror elements, the derelict city setting is quite nice and the semi fixed camera angles are well implemented.So what about the not so good things then? I think one big point especially genre veterans will find on their first playthrough is that the game is sort of lacking that "survival" part of survival horror as there is plenty of ammo and healing items to go around as the game barely ever forces you in to situations where you need to fight thanks to the easily avoidable and rather passive enemies.Another negative point I would say is that the pacing has some issues especially in the early parts of the game, as well as one section that sort of drags on a bit too long in the latter half of the game. To some degree I would blame the level design and the borderline useless map for some of the pacing issues as well.Overall I would recommend this to fans of the genre if you don't mind some of the flaws / issues listed above.
_childDocuments_.name: Hollowbody

_childDocuments_.review: First off, that this is a single developer game is mindblowing.I'm all about atmosphere in games, and especially in horror titles it's crucial. I'm thrilled ro report that Hollowbody nails it on every front. The lo fi but very effective visuals, the naturalistic but still surreal urban decay, the bits of environmental storytelling sprinkled throughout that help paint the backstory of the dreary setting, the minimalistic but effective music and sound design - they all converge into something really special. It's never diluted, it's densely packed with suspense and atmosphere, and the fixed camera jumps take me back to the late 90s early 2000s titles that scared the living daylights out of me back then. It's a bit of Alone In the Dark and a bit of Resident Evil and a bit of Silent Hill, but actually more than the sum of its influences. Hollowbody is a thing of its own and it's beautiful. Happy to have supported it early. Will help crowdfund / buy anything else Headware puts out there. You can tell when a game is a product of passion, not focus groups and marketing pitches. This is 100% the case.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have any issues with your resolution not being in the preset options, you can set the resolution yourself manually!To do so in Windows you can go into RegEdit/Registry Editor - HKEY_CURRENT_USER-Software-HeadwareGames-Hollowbody and modify the values using decimal the Screenmanager Resolution Width_h and Screenmanager Resolution Height_h entries (not the default ones).The game will likely have your resolution set by default but if you change any settings and it isn't in the options menu, you'll have to refer to this fix! If this doesn't work you might be able to delete the current settings and have it reset to default values. Thanks Nath for helping me with this fix and for giving us this stellar game!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic so far. Loved the playable demo when it came out. Have been looking forward to it since I found out about it and it's definitely not disappointing. Melee combat is crunchy, gun combat is exactly what it should be, targeting has been a bit difficult but that's most likely a me problem.The atmosphere is awesome, the world building is great, all the neat little bits of story you can find walking around this dilapidated city are great.Only issue I have so far is 1280x800 zooms forward a bit so the sides are cut off, running at 1280x720 resolves this issue, but there are the little black bars at the top and bottom of the screen. _childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric throwback to the PS2-era of survival horror games. With a unique world and premise that uses a dystopian scifi setting as the backdrop for a creepy story that almost feels like fantasy at times. Its setting and tone are VERY reminiscent of Silent Hill 2, as well as the gameplay. It is ultimately about the story though, which can be completed in about 4-5 hours. Fans of more involved survival horror may find this lacking in complexity of combat and puzzles, though it does offer higher difficulties, New Game+, and other modifiers upon completion.This game's strength is in its atmosphere. It seems to want you to take your time in exploring, and studying, the sights of the ruined city it takes place in. The darkness, the constant storm, and great soundtrack had me immediately immersed in an oppressive atmosphere that never let up until it was over.

_childDocuments_.review: OMG I love it !! Have been refreshing steam page all day to be able to get it ASAP. You can feel the love the developers put into the it and I'm really grateful that I'm able to experience it instead of watching them youtube videos about it. Really happy to support it at launch and I wish the devs all the best in their future projects ! Gonna try Chasing Static after I'm finished with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I have finished the game and yeah it's a recommendation for sure. It's not perfect, I have some issues with a few sequences (One in particular is just pointless and very much intended to be so () and some definite BS with one big enemy placement near the end of the game that caused me to lose progress. Not too much since the game is fairly short, but it felt pretty BS the way I died. Otherwise I wish the story was a bit more developed. We kinda get to the end in a way that feels random. I wish the game was also a bit longer. It's great, but it does feel like part 1 of a bigger story. Which is to say I hope we see more of the MC or at least the world in general. I am intrigued and want to explore it more!OG Review**************A bit early to say how good the game will end up being, but after almost 2 hours, it has been a pretty good time just taking the time to explore, take in the amazing atmosphere and pretty neat voice acting!It does very much feel like futuristic Silent Hill, but I can't say I mind. Especially when old SH games have not been a thing in ages. So may find it distracting, but I think the setting alone does a good job at setting a different tone for the story.The one thing I'm not a big fan of so far is the melee combat. It feels a 'lil jank. Like it's hard to gage when you can attack without getting hit in response and the first time I got into an encounter, I got put into critical health right away which didn't feel great. Anyway if you're on the fence, go try it! It's under 20$ CAD currently and it seems like some good quality horror game!

_childDocuments_.review: Hollowbody is a triumph of modern survival horror with clear cut inspirations from horrors of the early 2000s. It combines a beautiful story with crisp gameplay and wraps it together with a haunting soundtrack and voice acting that will stick with you for ages.Get your notepad ready for puzzle notes, turn the headphones up and strap in for one of the finest experiences we've seen in horror since the PS2 generation itself. If you're a fan of horror, you'll love this, and if you've wanted to get into classic survival horror but struggled due to the inaccessibility of older titles, this is absolutely a great entry point into the genre.It's time to grab Mica, and go find Sasha.

name: SILENT HILL 2
detailed_description: Deluxe Edition [Deluxe Edition - Contents] ・SILENT HILL 2 ・Digital Artbook ・Digital Soundtrack ・Pyramid Head Mask（pizza box） The mask is a skin that applies to James (the main character) in the game. About the Game Having received a letter from his deceased wife, James heads to where they shared so many memories, in the hope of seeing her one more time: Silent Hill. There, by the lake, he finds a woman eerily similar to her... 'My name… is Maria,' the woman smiles. Her face, her voice... She's just like her. Experience a master-class in psychological horror―lauded as the best in the series―on the latest hardware with chilling visuals and visceral sounds. High-end Graphics and Sound With ray tracing and other cutting-edge technical enhancements, the world of SILENT HILL and its unsettling ambiance is even realer than before. And with the inclusion of new, immersive soundscapes, you'll feel like you're standing in the thick of it. Larger Environments Explore locations and buildings that were once inaccessible, or are newly added in the remake. Enjoy the same acclaimed story, even while you experience the town of Silent Hill with fresh eyes across an expanded map. Over-the-shoulder Camera The remake moves from the original's fixed-camera viewpoints to an over-the-shoulder perspective, putting you closer to what James sees, for a more thrilling, more immersive experience as you explore the town and come face-to-face with monsters. Evolved Combat Gameplay Familiar weapons like the steel pipe and handgun make their return, but now with an updated combat system. Avoid attacks with carefully timed dodges, aim down sights, and more, making monster encounters more engaging and nerve-wracking than ever.

What he finds is a ghost town, prowled by disturbing monsters and cloaked in deep fog. Confront the monsters, solve puzzles, and search for traces of your wife in this remake of SILENT HILL 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This review is a "Do not recommend trying on a Steam Deck"I'm not going to say I don't recommend it to everyone because I tried playing it in a way it wasn't intended to be played. I'm very sad to say I can't get it to stop freezing. I know it was overly optimistic to think I could get it to run on the deck, but I tried. I looked up several fixes and tried them all. Idk, maybe there's still something that would work, but it's not worth 70 smackers to me. Especially when I can just emulate the original. It was actually running fairly well in certain parts, I even got it up to 50fps sometimes, but then it would just completely crash, especially in combat. At one point completely freezing, so I had to restart my machine. It sucks being poor and only having what I have, but I guess I have to wait til I can afford better hardware, or they come up with a deck patch. Until then, I'm suggesting people with Steam Deck don't even try. I've seen that others can get it running, and that's great. But again, it's not worth the 70 dollar gamble of it crashing in crucial parts.I'm leaving a negative review only in the very naive hopes that Bloober will see this and feel pressure to get it working on Steam Deck, because it does seem very close - but not quite there.I will say otherwise I was feeling very impressed with what they've done with the game and I am SUPER eager to play it, obviously. The mood is spot on and the way they've improved upon the old ideas is truly amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure this game received a warm reception because the bar has been set so absolutely low for this series. While the art direction is pretty good, and I do like some of the more minute and style changes, the gameplay is awful due to the addition of verticality as a mechanic. It wasn't difficult to proceed in the original -- your map updates with what is blocked off and not, so either explore somewhere you haven't been yet or figure out a puzzle. With the verticality, your map is updated, but NOT with possible entry-holes, windows you can smash, ledges you can climb... meaning you will be spending A LOT of time either looking through every corner to find out just how the hell you're supposed to get anywhere or looking up a guide only to find out you missed some poorly lit wall you could break with a pipe five minutes in the opposite direction. And that's just not enjoyable whatsoever. It's not like the original was 'fun' necessarily, but I wouldn't call it frustratingly boring either. I got halfway through the game and just couldn't bother anymore. And that's not even getting into the performance issues. Have fun having 5 FPS during a scene with only one prop for reasons you do not understand in a game you spent $70 on. I wouldn't recommend this for a fan. And I DEFINITELY would not recommend this for anyone new to the game -- just play the original ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it still holds up.

_childDocuments_.review: You enter a corridor with a lot of doors. Right before you inspect them - you pray they would not open. If they do not, you can move further with a bit of an ease. However, if they do open, you realize that now you have to go in and face the unknown terror that lies ahead.This game is a horror masterpiece. I've currently stopped at Brookhaven hospital. When I opened the map, I noticed two things - there are a lot of doors and it's only 1F.To be continued.I thought the nightmares I've endured in Brookhaven hospital were going to be the end of it. Is it possible that this game could depict something worse that I had to go through? The moment I escaped the hospital and took walk in the streets of Silent Hill, I was gasping for some kind of relief. Where was that beautiful thick, pale fog that surrounded the town the first time I've arrived to look for Mary. A moment of solitude and shelter was the only thing I wanted. At last I reached the park and although surrounded by darkness I could feel the tension fading. Not until I've entered the Prison. The second time I've exited the underground I felt like a shell of my former self, completely numb, tired. I no longer question anything, it doesn't matter where the boat will take me. I am ready to meet my end.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill is one of the most beautifully crafted games and there aren't ANY games out there that are like it. This game is unique, even the OG games have such an enchanting appeal that will just hook you onto the game in a heartbeat. This game can really call out to you and make you feel connected to it, to the atmosphere.. to the characters and to their pain and suffering that they have gone through. Silent Hill really does an amazing job at capturing you and keeping you engaged within the game. its simply a perfect portrait, amazingly painted to the littlest detail. The horror, sadness and suffering, grief and guilt aspects of the game are amazingly described and shown in characters such as James, Maria and Angela.I am so thankful that the devs have given us such a beautiful, aesthetically pleasing and true adaptation from the original game. Silent Hill 2 remake is truly one of the best remakes of the year. When you get into Silent Hill it will always remain with you and will always be a part of you, a truly unforgettable journey into this psychological horror themed game. Its worth any amount of money

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game since the first debut trailer at Silent Hill Transmission. And I can confidently say that Bloober Team not only paid tribute to one of the greatest psychological horror games ever created, but honouring that legacy and making several quality of life improvements and maintaining the vision of the original game.First play through: 20 hours , Difficulty: Hard, Puzzle Difficulty: Hard, Ending: In WaterGraphics:+Unreal Engine 5 brings the town of Silent Hill to life. Beautiful lighting effects, and textures.+The level of detail in every crack of Silent Hill is masterfully done. From Woodside Apartments, to Brookhaven Hospital are standouts here for me.+The Otherworld was incredible, the various levels of decay, rust and oppressive darkness just increased the tension level immensely. +Motion capture and facial expressions were great. All the characters looked fantastic. Including enemies.Sound Design:+Sound effects and music were top notch, from creature sounds, fire arms, the background music and ambience. The soundtrack is remixed from the original Silent Hill composer Akira Yamaoka.+Voice acting from the whole cast was spectacular. I was very fond of Angela's voice actress performance in particular (Gianna Kiehl) but also (Luke Roberts) as James Sunderland.+The soundtrack is back in all it's former glory, beautiful renditions from the original OST hit me like a nostalgia bomb. Game play and Narrative:+Game play has been updated from it's original Silent Hill 2 (2001) instead of an isometric static camera we now have a over the shoulder perspective. It works incredibly well, the tension is maintained throughout especially with how oppressive the darkness is now. And how aggressive enemies can be. Mannequins got hands(not literally) but they will beat the crap out of you.+New cut-scenes and updated dialogue for Eddie and Angela give an updated perspective on their mental state as it continues to degrade after each encounter. The subtle nuance of Eddie's icy breath and slow deadening of the eyes, to Angela's traumatic experiences.(spoilers obviously)+Boss fights had a much needed tune up. Arguably one of the weakest points in the OG Silent Hill 2 for me. Bosses have various mechanics now, you can actually opt for an all melee strategy now if you choose. They still kept the spirit of the original bosses intact but now with a shiny new mechanical paint job. Abstract Daddy is a big stand out for me. +Easter eggs all over the place, from Silent Hill 2 flashbacks, to Silent Hill 3, and even Silent Hill. Was very clever how they were implemented.Now for some negatives.(Subjective opinion)-During my playthrough I upgraded my gpu from a RX 6600xt to a RX  7800xt as the 6600xt was able to get 42 to 55 fps on med-low settings with FSR 3.0 on. But it wasn't stable all the time. The 7800xt fixed that issue, but ray tracing was still a performance hit of about 30 fps. Without it 100+ fps on max settings FSR 3.0 balanced no problem. Needless to say, expect some stuttering (maybe)-Picking up items or interacting with certain objects can be a bit of a pain, you had to be near pixel perfect to pick up an item or trigger a certain element in the environment. Somewhat frustrating.In conclusion:Bloober Team pays homage to the legacy that is Silent Hill 2. The remake doesn't replace or is inherently superior in every aspect, it just compliments what has been made, and shows just how well the original holds up in many aspects. While modernising other features and narrative points that may have been lacking with great results. Overall you get 9 endings, New game plus, a ton of value for the dollar spent. If you like Survival Horror, Psychological Horror, pick this one up you should have a great time with it. And welcome back Silent Hill, you have been missed.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible modern remake of an all time classic. Whether it's your first time playing Silent Hill 2 or if you're revisiting the foggy town, you're in for an absolute treat. Bloober knocked it out of the park with this one, they put a ton of love and attention in this game and you can tell with all of the easter eggs and callbacks to the original game. The game looks incredible and runs fairly smooth while also having some of the best sound design of any game I've played in recent years (the squelching and squishy sounds of the random piles of flesh and filth around you takes a while to leave your brain). I've played both this and the original and in my opinion this is the definitive version of the game, everything they changed for the remake was for the better and made the experience extremely eerie, atmospheric, and fun for today's standards. I highly recommend giving this remake of an all time great a try!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing "The Medium," I got the sense that Bloober Team is using it as a way to show they deserve to remake "Silent Hill 2". But honestly, I didn't want "SH2" to feel like "The Medium". That would be okay, but it wouldn’t reach the heights of the original. The first trailers made the fighting system look pretty weak.Fortunately, all my worries, including those trailer issues, disappeared by the time the final release came around—except for the framerate problems. This is the first time a "Silent Hill" game has come from a non-Japanese studio, and it’s been a big success.They didn’t ruin anything; instead, they expanded the world and honored the classic locations. I bought the deluxe edition at full price and don’t regret it at all.I can’t wait to dive back into the game and really hope Bloober Team takes on more "Silent Hill" remakes.P.S. Just to add, I’m not usually into scary games, but "Silent Hill" is tied to my youth and laid the groundwork for my love of psychological horror with its complex characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting anything that good. SH 2 is an extraordinary video game experience. Pretty hard and taxing mentally but it left me blown away+ S Tier story with very mature/hard themes+ Insane and disturbing but in a good way+ Looks pretty good+ Except for Angela, the English voice acting is really good. Especially the main character.+ Combat is pretty good especially melee. It's surprisingly technical and feels like a souls like sometimes but very engaging and hard.+ Very good puzzles (on Hard difficulty). Unlike Resident Evil, this game doesn't assume that players have brain damage.+ Despite some trolls' claims, SH2 Remake is DEI free.- Some stutters from time to time but nothing immersion breaking or unplayable- Hardly any unlockables like bonus costumes, weapons or gameplay modifiers. We've been spoiled by the latest resident evils but it shouldn't be that hard to add some content to increase the replay value.- I did get a few crashes- The different endings conditions are totally obscure and requires the use of a guide. Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is well done. The highs and lows of Silent Hill 2 have been honored. Small details are sometimes more, sometimes less appealing.I thoroughly enjoyed the remake. Graphically, with Ray Tracing and DLDSR, it's right up there.What I absolutely dislike and annoys me greatly: Stuttering. To minimize stuttering as much as possible, you need to play with FSR 3.0 Frame Generation. In the Engine.ini (C:\Users\x\AppData\Local\SilentHill2\Saved\Config\Windows), enter the following:[SystemSettings]r.FidelityFX.FI.Enabled=1After that, you have to use FSR 3 in order to enable FSR Frame Generation. In my case, I combined it with DLDSR 1.78, but I also have a 7800x3D with an RTX 4090.There is no other way to minimize the stuttering! However, FSR 3 Frame Generation leads to disocclusion artifacts inside buildings. To avoid these as much as possible, you should play with Motion Blur enabled.In my case, sharpening (Reshade) is not necessary due to DLDSR.It’s a shame that the developers didn’t put more effort into this. And why on earth is Nvidia’s Ray Reconstruction and Frame Generation not supported?

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I approached Bloober Team with a degree of skepticism, not due to doubts about their standing within the horror genre—where their craft is somewhat unique and the reputation is well-deserved—but because I felt they had yet to truly reach their full potential. They didn't have 'it'. While their past efforts have shown promise, they never quite captured that elusive quality that defines masterpieces. Should Silent Hill 2 (SH2) indeed represent their artistic maturation as a process in self-realization, I welcome it wholeheartedly. Nevertheless, I still anticipate an original title from Bloober Team that transcends their previous work, which has often been considered as budget titles. As for KONAMI and SH franchise in general, let's not repeat history. Those familiar with the franchise know all too well the mishandling and stagnation that plagued the series (and the KONAMI itself) for years. Yet, one cannot help but hope that Konami has at last found a way to inject fresh vitality into its veins. Perhaps this is just a stepping stone for KONAMI to get back in the business. Though I was initially apprehensive about the project, I did not believe from the outset that it would devolve into disaster. On the contrary, the director’s comments conveyed a clear sense of passion and expertise, suggesting a deep understanding of what made the original a masterpiece. As Silent Hill 2 is a story that lives in interpretations how it is directed is everything and it only gets only heavier when you realize the topics it tackles. Fortunately, the remake not only preserves much of the artistic integrity that defined the original (keeping all the sinistry and creepiness around the town intact) but also succeeds in modernizing the gameplay. Furthermore, it expands upon the existing content, introducing new areas (which increases the playtime significantly) while implementing QOL improvements that enhance the experience. While the fixed camera was a notable part of the og (and most of the games during that era, defining new approaches to utilize for storytelling) SH2 is also successful with its generic over the shoulder camera. Evil finds new ways to sneak onto you.One thing that is notable with this remake is not only they tried to deliver a sense of familiarity but also challenged it by adding new layers of interpretations. One of them is the bold assumption of that you already have gone through the events of Silent Hill. The only slight issue lies in the performance—microstutters and occasional frame rate dips, which, despite some efforts at fine-tuning, have proven difficult to resolve. This is exclusive to 4K though (in my case). While I was able to achieve 50-60 fps overall, it would tank a lot and sometimes get completely broken and require a full restart (which is frustrating as you know SH2 uses an old save system and that means you need to replay the same stages after the last checkpoint). Nevertheless, the overall performance remains satisfactory and the game is most definitely playable at 2K (above 70 fps, DLSS Quality & Epic presets, 3080ti). A more significant concern, however, is the introduction of a modern health indicator: a red screen (aka low health vignette) signaling the character’s weakened state. I strongly recommend disabling this feature, as it not only disrupts immersion but also conflicts with the thematic intent of the game. In a narrative where the "In Water" ending—one that requires the protagonist to endure significant damage—is largely regarded as canon by fans, this red paint thrown onto your screen feels frustratingly out of place. I can sense it getting worse in the darkness (i.e. most of the game) and especially in the Otherworld. A more organic approach is to monitor James' physical animations, which offer a better immersive representation of his deteriorating condition [don't worry they are explicit and readable enough]. Playing the game without any hint will probably do wonders as you must rely on the visual & audio cues and they did some clever job at that. At its core, Silent Hill 2 remains an unparalleled work of art, a narrative imbued with layers of meaning, all interwoven through the lens of personal turmoil, with the game unflinchingly disturbing the player while conveying its own cognizance of torment and grief and to this very day still stands as a poignant exploration of the human psyche.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the original Silent Hill 2, this remake managed to recapture the same lightning in a bottle. It is a surreal masterpiece that is worth playing for both new and returning fans of the series.Among many others, I was also worried that Bloober Team would dishonor the legacy of the original game, and everything that made it so unique from the other horror games at the time.I am so, SO glad that I was wrong. It is pretty obvious that this remake's goal in mind was to be as faithful to the original formula as possible, while adding new and enjoyable aspects of the game that don't ruin the immersion. I loved the new puzzles, probably even more than the original's. I even enjoyed the combat, and didn't find it game-breaking. If anything, I thought it fit well with how ruthless the monsters are compared to the original. Lying figures can have the upper hand in numbers, mannequins will hide in places you least expect and get the drop on you, and the knife-wielding nurses can easily kill you in seconds if you're not careful.I liked that ammo is a lot harder to find now, however healing items are very common. I beat my first playthrough in standard combat and puzzle difficulty with little to no ammo, but about 40 health drinks and 50 syringes... I didn't die once.The one aspect that I think they EASILY improved on is the boss fights. Frankly, they only really served as a spectacle in the original, and didn't really prove much of a challenge. The ones in this remake are a lot more refined, enjoyable, and at times difficult. The fight with Abstract Daddy is pure nightmare fuel, easily being one of the most haunting moments in the game.Fortunately, the story follows the original almost to the exact detail. However, the game does have two additional endings, and they fit BEAUTIFULLY with the story. I love them. Anyways, saying anything more about the story would be a disservice to letting people experience its beauty for themselves. There are also LOTS of references and easter eggs for the original players to enjoy, and even plenty of small details that are easy to miss, but can speak volumes about the story and the characters, if you know the meanings behind them.The visuals are gorgeous too. Not even exaggerating, I took about 300 screenshots in my first playthrough. I couldn't help it.With returning champion Akira Yamaoka being tasked with the soundtrack, saying it's a masterpiece is a no-brainer. I loved both the remixes of the original tracks and the new ones, and I really hope that an OST is published soon.My only personal complaint is that the cutscenes are locked to 30 FPS. It didn't really bother me, but it would've been nice to see them in a higher framerate, given how well-crafted they are. I also heard some complaints about stuttering issues, but luckily I didn't experience any of that. I played the game at 2560x1440 resolution, medium graphics settings and DLSS Supersampling set to "Performance" and the game ran at about 60-110 FPS constantly. I could see how 60 FPS can be a little annoying to most people, but I didn't mind. Thankfully, I'm just happy to finally play this remake.TL;DR: If you enjoyed the original Silent Hill 2, you'll love the remake. It's true to its original source material, and even has lots of new content that is appreciated. Does it replace the original? No. Is it still very fun, even for those who never played the original? Absolutely.I think Bloober Team knew that they would never make something as good as the original, but they could make something for people to relive its beauty in the modern world. You could tell that they genuinely are fans of the series. This is as good as it gets for a remake. 10/10 game of the year for me.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Love' doesn't feel like the right word.Silent Hill 2 is a bitter, dark, ugly, and beautiful portrait that understands everything that's worth hating and loving in humanity. Bloober Team have done a magnificent job translating the classic into the modern era. Some things are lost; I miss the fixed camera angles, and the cheesy voice acting, but these are facets worth giving up on, in my view, to see Silent Hill live on. Nothing in its substance- its brutality, its pain, its honesty- is bled away in this remake, as I truly expected from something made in a time where people are progressively obsessed with not offending anyone, even themselves. It stands as such a stark contrast to modern game design, where everything is sanded down and simplified. Silent Hill trusts the player to figure things out, to the point where its puzzles becoming bizarrely abstract, yet entrancing all the same. Every aspect of the game is doused in symbolism, in metaphor and purpose, that even the weakest parts act as the soles of a goliath. A singular example of artistic achievement in the medium. It doesn't focus on content for content's sake; the original skeleton doesn't even feel like it was visualized as a product or a way to make money, but as a means of expressing something from the soul. That expression still echoes today.There are arguments to be made about how much merit a remake can truly deserve. At the end of the day, even the very best can only bring an original excellence in line with current expectations. I cannot ascribe the quality of Silent Hill 2's writing or design to Bloober Team, much as I would like to, but, at the same time, I'd like to point at the sheer difficulty they must have faced in reimagining a 23-year-old game. The fact that they succeeded on any level is testament to their capability, and with the degree of faithfulness and reverence they obviously handled this with, I fully look forward to their future work with delight. It deserves the very best praise that I can give it: that it is Silent Hill 2, and not a drowned reflection. One of the best experiences of any year. I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: A remake that in many ways improves upon the original. Silent Hill 2 Remake is bigger, scarier, and looks and plays great. As one of the many people that were cautious about this game, I am beyond happy to say that not only has Bloober Team made a fantastic remake, but they have made a triumphant masterpiece that fully understands what made Silent Hill 2 a classic horror game. Akira Yamaoka's new soundtrack is great, the acting and voice performances are way better than the original, and the monsters are interesting and scary. This is how you do a remake.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game it is a piece of art that stands out in gaming for its storytelling and writing. Few games have had such a tight narrative fueled by symbolism that really keeps you moving through the game and the balance between these two things really sets Silent Hill 2 apart from other media. For a franchise that is famous for its setting I was really driven to complete this game by the strong writing of the characters, the dynamics between them, and the mystery of the main character. James is an excellent POV for this story and is such an amazing vessel for exploring human nature and driving criticism of our modern ways of living. Commentary on death, sex, forgiveness, selfishness, loss and purpose are common themes throughout story telling but Silent Hill 2 makes me feel like I am thinking about them for the first time again. James, Laura, Angela, and Mary will remain in my heart for a long time.

As a fan, I can confidently say this remake is the best thing that could’ve happened to the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time SH fan, I can wholeheartedly recommend this remake. It's not perfect and it will not replace the original, but it comes pretty close. Fact of the matter is that finding a way to comfortably play the original 4 games is a headache, and this remake will be the best option for the majority of people to experience 2. Bloober and ex-Team Silent members managed to overcome all odds, as well as potential meddling from Konami, to deliver a faithful recreation of a masterpiece. It builds on top of what exists rather than changing too much. The actors do an incredible job. The combat is a bit more action-oriented, but you still have to be smart about the situations you put yourself in. The expanded exploration is a huge plus as well with many rewards for people that go off the beaten path. The soundtrack has its throwbacks but all the new stuff is good as well (though I prefer some older versions of songs like Heaven's Night). Audio is fantastic and really adds to the atmosphere. I had my concerns with Bloober heading this project because I did not enjoy 90% of their catalog, but they have proven themselves tenfold. If you are a Silent Hill fan, this is a must buy. If you are new to Silent Hill, this is a great place to start. You don't need to play 1 as it's not really connected to 2's story. Now please remake the rest of them. I would kill for a remake of 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only got 18 hrs played. I normally don't use standby, and I don't know why did this time. But that's why it shows 67 hrs. I didn't play this when it was originally released. Years later I tried it but didn't like the controls. That said, the controls are way better here and the 3rd person view is great. The story is meh. I need to watch an explained video. Because right now I'm like, why even go out there? But since you're here, why not let the girl dance for you? Have some fun in Silent Hill. Are the monsters all in his head? A manifestation of how he sees himself? How are the lady and little girl following him to the underworld? After about 14 or so hours it started to feel drawn out. Combat was ok. I mainly used the pipe. Performance was terrible starting out. I changed some settings, but the main fix was lowering the quality from medium to low. It went from 14 fps to 140 fps, and I couldn't see much of a distance. My pc specs should run this on high settings at 140 fps. I'll put that on the game being poorly optimized. _childDocuments_.review: I’ve just finished my playthrough of Silent Hill 2 Remake, and here’s my take on it. Overall, this is a fantastic return to the fog-drenched world of psychological horror, but there are definitely some areas that could have used more polish.The Good:Atmospheric Graphics: The visuals in this game are phenomenal. The foggy, grim town of Silent Hill feels incredibly immersive and detailed, from the eerie lighting to the decayed interiors. It really draws you in, and every location you explore has a haunting beauty that feels true to the original while benefiting from modern graphics.Sound Design: If you're playing this game, do yourself a favor and use headphones! The sound design is absolutely top-notch. From the chilling sound effects to the background score, every sound is crafted to keep you on edge. The radio static when monsters are nearby, the distant eerie noises—everything adds to the atmosphere of dread.Voice Acting & Story: The performances are stellar. James Sunderland’s emotional journey feels authentic, and the supporting characters—like Angela and Eddie—are deeply compelling. Their stories are heart-wrenching, and the new voice acting really helped me connect with them on a deeper level.Weapon Feedback: The combat mechanics feel solid, especially when it comes to weapon feedback. Both firearms and melee weapons feel weighty and satisfying, especially when you land a hit on the game’s horrifying monsters.Exploration: Exploring Silent Hill has always been a big part of the experience, and I found myself thoroughly enjoying most areas. Each environment is dense with detail, making it rewarding to search for clues and solve puzzles.The Not So Good:Simplistic Combat: While the weapons feel good, the combat itself can feel shallow. The AI is not very challenging, and enemy variety is quite limited. You’ll often find yourself fighting the same few types of enemies, which can make encounters repetitive.Performance Issues: This is where things start to fall apart. Despite having a high-end PC, I experienced frequent frame drops and stuttering, especially in open areas like the foggy streets of Silent Hill. It didn’t ruin the game, but it definitely affected immersion, particularly during combat scenes.Inconsistent Animations: There’s a weird inconsistency when it comes to animations. Sometimes James has a full animation for picking up items or interacting with the environment, while other times actions just happen without any movement. It’s not game-breaking, but it’s jarring and breaks the immersion a bit.Visual Bugs: I ran into a few bugs, including some strange visual effects and clipping issues. While they weren’t game-breaking, it gave me the impression that the game wasn’t fully polished, especially for a title in 2024.Weapons Not Visible on Character: One small gripe is that James’ weapons seem to appear out of nowhere during combat. It would have been great if we could actually see his gear on his body, as many other modern games do.Uninspired Prison and Labyrinth Sections: The parts where you are led into the Prison and Labyrinth were a huge letdown for me. They felt more like forced sections rather than natural parts of the story progression. I didn’t enjoy them at all, especially the labyrinth—it felt disjointed, like I was just tossed there because the game needed me to go. The exploration, which is usually satisfying, really faltered in these areas.Final Thoughts:If you're a fan of the original or love survival horror, Silent Hill 2 Remake is definitely worth your time. The atmosphere, story, and audio design make it an immersive experience. However, be prepared for some performance hiccups, shallow combat, and a few questionable design decisions. Despite these issues, it’s a faithful remake that does a great job of bringing the classic back to life.Rating: 7.5/10Still recommended, but with the hope that patches will address some of the performance and design issues!

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10TLDR: Silent Hill 2 Remake is a gamey game game videogame, its a superficial, spoonfed iteration of its predecessor. Yes, it looks visually stunning. Yes, it's nice to see what a modern Silent Hill can look like. But to me this does not feel like a Silent Hill game at all. The camera angles, the overt combat action, bad mo-cap/flat VA/changes to dialogue and superficial handling of the source material just don't gel well with me. It, as crazy as this sounds; feels like a video game and no longer an artistic experience.For me, personally I wanted a true 1:1 remake, which was never a guarantee I know. But equally I'm not happy with the product that this is. Silent Hill fans are either unhinged, hyperfixated, turbofans like myself who just want another teenage therapy session disguised as a video game, or they are normal people who want a video game experience. Me being the former. Anyway, I'm sure this unhinged review will come across as ridiculous to those who wanted the latter, but if you're like me and wanted the former then I hope this review helps.Where to begin? I'd say this is more of a Reimagining than a Remake. If you're like me and are heavily devoted to the original then I don't think this'll be for you. I was more hopeful for a 1:1 remake similar to Resident Evil 1 than what I suppose comparatively is more Resident Evil 2. As a deranged hardcore fan, I went in knowing that Bloober could either go 1:1 or veer off and do their own thing which is what they did. I knew no matter what they did they couldn't recapture the magic of the first, simply because that is impossible for any game or experience really.So to begin, and spoiler warning for anyone who hasn't played it yet.Story: The story structure remains relatively the same with the biggest differences stemming from the lack of subtly and nuance from both James and Maria as characters. Personally, I think the biggest problem is that there is no longer a conflict between the hope that Mary may be alive, and the suggestion that James killed her. There isn't this back and forth to persuade you of either. James now answers in place of us, the player. Instead of us coming to our own conclusion in place of James, that agency is taken away from us as James now comments on the oddities of the story, and Maria as an entity. Because of this shift in narrative storytelling to completely rends the ambiguity and theory-crafting element from the player.Maria's character is just one-dimensional, flat-toned, and leans on this "evil-succubus" role that anyone with a superficial understanding of Silent Hill 2 would have, rather than being a complex entity whose at war with the innate traits shes inherited, her desire to live, and her need for James as both a fragment of Mary and as as an entity whose survival lies on making James choose her. To me personally, Maria is the poorest performing character in this Remake by far, the changes to her dialogue are just pointless and destructive I just don't understand what it is they wanted to achieve? That combined with the bad mo-cap and atrociously flat voice acting just make this the biggest casualty to one of gaming's baddest b's I've ever seen. Personally, I think Maria was a large factor in the original game's success as a story, and this performance in the remake just brings the whole thing. Like, whats the need to imply she works at Heaven's night when you're just going to have her walk in there, turn all the lights on, get up on stage and spin around the pole, and then get behind the bar and start making drinks? Where is the subtly in any of that? She just comes across as a massive 'pick me' girl, on an almost teen-drama level. It's smarmy, its seedy, and its disingenuine. She comes across as superficial and fake. Which is not what she is supposed to be. All of her scenes really are doggy-doo-doo. All the way to the end, where James confronts her before the final boss and its still shockingly transparent that Bloober failed to understand this woman. For Maria to say "I could give you what she never could." and "I'm better than her" with that sinister Hollywood homebreaker look. Like the original game is right there, shes not this seductress. Shes a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ memory of a dead woman, whose terrified of dying, and whose whole existence depends on winning over a man who wants a different version of her she could never be. Who genuinely loves this man. Shes supposed to be pleading with James to take her on because she subconsciously knows she will die if he doesnt. Don't get me started on the changes to Mary's letter. Anyway onto other matters.Combat: Loved the new combat like James' desperation and the meatiness of it, got stale quick and a bit frustratingly jank with how monsters will hard lock onto you during attack animations. I.e. dodge a nurse's first swing and then do 2/3 dodges back and watch her slide along the floor toward you to chain into the second hit.  Enjoyed the new mob mechanics and behaviours, bosses however were a bit too samey barring the Abstract Daddy fight which I'd say felt like the only real boss fight.Layout changes: Not a fan, not necessary for someone who wanted a 1:1. Problem with traversal was the OTT amount of holes in walls and above-head windows to climb through, just made backtracking annoying and lost the game's original feverdream, completely lost, lemme check my map vibe. Apartments were okay, Hospital just didn't make any sense, and the Prison just seemed pointlessly stretched out and gated behind a superficial door puzzle. Puzzles: Speaking of puzzles, I genuinely did not understand the point in replacing the puzzles entirely where you could just add new solutions. What was to me more insulting was seeing these 'Memories' of the original game placed everywhere. Its just weird to have the memory of the old game be sat inside the new one, and none of it is significant to the story. It just comes across as "heres this thing we didn't want to incorporate in any way.". What replaces the old is now superficial, literal, and cartoonishly camp in a way that would be more suitable in Silent Hill 3 and its overt themes of religion, and mysticism, than in two which present as more innocently a product of humans gone awry.Characters:[!] Actually had to cut this bit cuz this review was too large to post. James: Good VO/MoCap, Maria: Butchered. Angela: Handled well. Eddie: Good. Laura: Those crazy Mo-cap eyes wtf ahaha. They all suffered from bad mo-cap barring James, stuff facial expressions, and fluctuations of flat delivery and unneccesary dialogue changes.Music: Am I the only one that noticed that the music was never fully playing out? It would jump between multiple tracks and never last long enough to help build the atmosphere. In the hospital it is atrocious.And why have we decided to just rearrange the songs away from their original locations? Why are we getting the Toluca Lake boat theme in the basement of Lakeview hotel? The Over the Shoulder camera: I thought it took away from the atmosphere and immersion, personally. I still think they should of maintained the original overhead camera with dynamic cam moments. It just made the whole game not feel like a Silent Hill game to me. No one seems daring enough to try any other perspective out and it frustrates me, Capcom has sold the idea to indie horror devs that horror now needs to sit on a shoulder and I hate it. I miss entering a room and being given a distinct, cinematic, eerie shot/angle and being denied the ability to see in front of me and the only way to know what is there is to move into that space.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what you think it is: It's a very loyal, modern remake/update. Nothing groundbreaking here.There is Unreal Engine jank or optimization that can be done. _childDocuments_.review: I have a confession to make: I never finished the original Silent Hill 2. Back then, I was just a kid who walked into a video game store and picked up a stack of CDs: GTA 3, Clive Barker's Undying, Max Payne, Postal 2, you know, that kind of stuff. And for some reason, Silent Hill 2, yeah. It felt incredible, even though I didn’t have a proper PC gamepad (and getting one to work in the early '00s was a pain in the ass, trust me). The story was gripping, but I hit a puzzle and got stuck. Being from Ukraine, most video game stores sold pirated CDs, and my copy of Silent Hill 2 had a messed up language pack that broke one of the early puzzles for me, it was lost in translation. Since I was just a kid with no clue where to find a solution online, after a few hours of frustration, I dropped it and went back to shooting mobsters and triads in GTA 3 (zero regrets). Years passed. I played Silent Hill 3 (never finished it either, but in my version, Heather had an automatic rifle from the very beginning, which gave the game a whole different, kind of Resident Evil vibe), Silent Hill 4: The Room (yep, finished that one), fell in love with William Bevan, aka Burial (listen to “The Day of Night” by Akira Yamaoka, then dive into Burial’s Untrue album; you’ll thank me later), watched the Silent Hill movie (wow!), watched the second movie (blegh!), played P.T. (I still have a PS4 with it), and here we are.Now, this remake feels just like the original Silent Hill 2 felt to me twenty-something years ago. The only difference is that now I can actually finish it and truly appreciate the story. I was lucky to avoid major spoilers for over twenty years, so I can honestly say this is the best psychological thriller/horror experience I’ve had in recent years. Period. I encountered no bugs except the usual UE5 stutters, but adding -dx11 to the launch options fixed that (thanks, Dmytro!). The pacing felt organic, though I’ve heard some say the game feels bloated. Not to me, anyway. You know, the man’s trying to get out of hell! It shouldn’t be a short and fun ride. The sound design was terrifying in the best way, and the voice actors absolutely nailed it. James feels tired and on the verge of despair, just as he should. And that thick fog? Felt like it was creeping right into my room. Maybe it feels so good because I never finished the original game, but who cares? This remake gave me 30 hours of an ultimate gaming experience, and that’s something.So, what about Bloober Team? Seems like a new star in game development is born, that’s what.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 Remake is nothing short of a masterclass in psychological horror, brilliantly reimagining the 2001 classic for modern audiences while preserving the soul of the original. Developed by Bloober Team in collaboration with Konami, this remake is a haunting experience that will linger long after you’ve put down the controller.Graphics and Atmosphere:The visual overhaul is absolutely stunning. Every texture, from the dilapidated buildings to the eerily realistic fog, feels meticulously crafted. The town of Silent Hill feels alive, or rather, decayed in a way that draws you in and unnerves you at the same time. The lighting system is incredible, with shadows creeping and shifting in ways that make you constantly question what’s lurking in the dark. It’s a visual feast of dread that perfectly captures the oppressive and melancholic atmosphere of the original, while pushing the boundaries of what next-gen hardware can do.Sound Design and Music:Akira Yamaoka’s legendary score returns, enhanced with more nuance and depth. The iconic theme still sends chills down your spine, and the new ambient sounds breathe life into every corner of Silent Hill. The distant echoes, unsettling whispers, and the screeching static of the radio are not just heard – they’re felt. The sound design is so immersive that I found myself on edge even in moments of silence, expecting something terrible to happen at any second.Story and Characters:The heart of Silent Hill 2 has always been its deeply psychological and emotional narrative, and the remake stays faithful to that. James Sunderland’s journey to find his wife Mary is just as poignant and disturbing as ever. The improved facial animations and character models add an extra layer of emotion to the story, making each interaction feel even more impactful. You feel the weight of James’ grief, guilt, and confusion as if they were your own. The supporting cast, especially Maria, is brought to life with even more complexity, making the story’s twists hit harder than before.Gameplay and Mechanics:Combat remains secondary to the atmosphere, but the controls have been significantly improved for a smoother experience. The subtle adjustments to gameplay mechanics – like improved camera angles and more responsive movement – ensure that the remake feels modern without losing its classic survival horror roots. The puzzles are still satisfyingly challenging, but the quality-of-life improvements (such as easier inventory management and clearer objectives) help avoid unnecessary frustration.Enemy Design and AI:The monsters, iconic in their symbolism and grotesque designs, are even more terrifying thanks to the enhanced graphics. Pyramid Head, in particular, is more menacing than ever, embodying the darkest parts of James’ psyche with an unsettling presence. The AI has also been tweaked to make enemy encounters feel more dynamic and dangerous, with unpredictable movements and attacks that keep you on your toes.Final Thoughts:Silent Hill 2 Remake, brought to life by Bloober Team and Konami, is a triumph in every sense of the word. It delivers on the nostalgia of the original while updating the game for a new generation, balancing modern improvements with a deep respect for what made the original so beloved. It’s a harrowing journey into the human mind, exploring themes of grief, guilt, and redemption in a way that few games have ever done before. Whether you’re a long-time fan or a newcomer to the series, this remake is an absolute must-play.Rating: ★★★★★ 10/10
