_childDocuments_.review: I've always considered myself an admirer of the Silent Hill franchise. Never actually played any of the games besides PT (mainly due to being too afraid as a child and never being able to find a copy of any of them as an adult), but absolutely loved the concept, design, lore, story, and world created by Konami and Team Silent. I love horror more than any other genre, and when I heard that Silent Hill 2 was being remade, I was ecstatic. But once I heard that Bloober Team was heading development, I was worried. I had played a few of their prior titles and was very much not impressed by their games in the past. And when trailers first started releasing before the game released, more and more I became worried about what might happen to one of horror's greatest creations. Trailers which in hindsight were not the best at showcasing the game released, which worried everyone. But I was still hopeful. Hoping that despite what could potentially happen, SH2 would still be SH2. And upon purchase, I was blown away.     It's been awhile since a horror game actually unnerved me. Since I've had one get under my skin, make the hair stand on the back of my neck. Probably not since RE7 have I been truly disturbed by a horror game. But immediately upon leaving a rest stop bathroom, overlooking the foggy cliff leading to town, I could tell something was different. After making my way into town, my skin immediately started to crawl. Strange figures darting in the fog, the static of the Radio, the emptiness of the streets save for your own footsteps all combined into one of the best feelings of discomfort and sense of un-belonging I've not felt in years. The more I played, the more I explored the town, made my way through the cramped and claustrophobic halls of apartment buildings, the hospital and back alleys, the more I fell in love.      The sense of dread and uncomfort the atmosphere created was like no other, and thats not even accounting for the fear and terror the Other World gives. The monster design's are top notch, Lying Figures a simple but gross fodder enemy, the mannequins attacking from hidden corners or behind objects, ambushing you as soon as your guard finally starts to lower, nurses acting as dangerous threats all act greatly in tandem with each other. Boss designs are all just as horrific as they were, all challenging endeavors that are fair encounters through and through.      While some changes to the story were to be expected, they're barely changes at all. Mainly additions of new cutscenes for characters like Maria and Angela, or encountering Eddie in the movie theater instead of a bowling alley. And there's even hidden collectibles that act as throwbacks or references to the original game, such as a lying figure's body where you originally fought Pyramid Head. And speaking of the characters, Maria, Angela, Eddie and Laura are all fantastically performed by their new cast. Maria is just as seductive, leading and in need of James as she was, Angela giving a heartbreaking performance, the pain of her past very much still alive inside her. Laura is beautifully shown as an innocent girl just stuck in this town, and Eddie is terrifying, watching the events of his life unfold in his Other World delivered amazingly. And then there's James. Guy Cihi's performance in the original is already great, damn near perfect. But the performance Luke Roberts gives is almost on par IMO, sometimes even surpassing it. Guy gave James a voice that had him with one concern, finding his wife. And Luke is nearly beat for beat with it, but with an extra layer of being tired, exhausted and just wanting everything to end.     The only complaint I can have with this game is the performance as a PC port. It runs sluggish as hell upon launch, and dipping below 50 fps, which it commonly does. Thankfully there are fixes for this that solve the issue. Other than that, I can confidently say that Bloober Team absolutely destroyed any concern I had, and my expectations were completely blown out of the water.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Chugging kombucha/vitamin water to face the daily horrors is a healing mechanic I also utilize in my plight against the horrors of the world (Going to the office).Usually, when I play horror games, I find them thrilling but never scary. This was the exception; I was generally scared to explore the decrepit corners of Silent Hill. A town fully realized to be both a living nightmare and a town I swear I have visited. I would need to take breaks due to this amounting stress. The beautifully acted cutscenes would relieve that stress and replace that feeling with melancholy and intense sadness for each character. The way they matched the movement and the eyes and face to catch subtle nuances in the performance made this an incredible story to see unravel. Looking back on my experience, there is not a single part I disliked or had a problem with. It's a 10 out of 10 masterpiece and my game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who loved playing the original for years despite the clunky combat and other gimmicks as a result of the ps2 hardware, this remake keeps the spirit of the original intact and does something new with it. Do consider that I have about 5 hrs in the game and im still at around what would be the 1:30 hr mark for the original (or grandfather clock puzzle in apartments).There’s new maps and entirely new locations and levels, the level design is made in such a way that allows for new ways to get around that is not just opening some previously locked door, you can also go through windows after breaking them yourself using melee weapons or crawl on your stomach and fit into tight spaces or break walls or even pull a lever that lowers the staircase from one level to a lower one, it’s genius and makes getting around feel like more of a challenge since you don’t know what to expect in each room you’re crawling into and you have little time to react before they see you. Exploration also rewards you for interacting with cupboards and windows, selves, and breaking glass/windows and getting into places you couldn’t get into before THROUGH the window you broke it’s actually insane how much more you can explore this time around and it is absolutely worth it each time if you’re playing on hard, you’ll need the extra ammo and health, because the combat is actually terrifying.The combat in this game is so masterfully done that looking back on everybody saying the dodge mechanic was “unrealistic” and that the game looked bad gameplay wise feels so offensive ? the combat in this feels sooooooo much more engaging rather than the spam button stun fest of the original, you don’t attack at your pace, you’re FORCED to attack at the pace of the enemies, they dodge and sprint and tackle you keeping you on edge of when to dodge and when to attack. It’s such an intense change since every altercation makes it feel like you could really die. Not to mention that there are slight variations in the same monsters, like some lying figures explode on death and others walk faster and feel more aggressive, the mannequins are definitely no joke and 1 bad encounter can end your entire run. I highly recommend to play with hard settings to feel that anxiety when traveling in smaller corridors but i don’t think it is necessary to have a good experience, there’s a lot more to explore and so much more to enjoy that isn’t simply just combat.There’s loads more puzzles too, none of them feel reductive to the experience and if anything make each new area feels unique as it starts to look a lot like what i remember sh1 and 3 looks like when the “otherworld” takes over, significantly more graphic too. The puzzles themselves aren’t too difficult as the game does a good job of leading you the right way and often times will completely change once you come across a new puzzle, the level around you will shake and you’ll hear new sounds with a new track and things will close behind you leaving you in a totally unfamiliar place of the map isolated from the spot you started forcing you to solve a puzzle to find a way to get back.In terms of the va and the character acting i honestly have no complaints. The original felt dreamlike and as if nobody could properly communicate with one another but in the remake it feels like broken people TRYING to communicate but failing miserably, especially noticeable in your interactions with angela in the beginning of the game and its become a welcome change in tone. The voice actors have absolutely done the characters justice and the character acting with the animations is absolutely amazing, you can finally get a sense of who james is as he shows a lot more compassion for the people he meets in the town, this is pre maria though but i don’t doubt they’ve meaningfully dealt with that interaction in a way that will absolutely be worth it. It doesn’t just elevate the cutscenes but also the combat as every kick that james gives the monster you’ll hear his real disgust and hate for that thing, honestly genius it totally changes how combat feels and really drives home the satisfaction of surviving the next level, lore wise i guess it adds onto his character more vs how he remained mostly silent during combat in the original. Overall the acting is extremely solid on all ends and in my opinion will just make the events later in the story so much more miserable and heartbreaking to experience.I’ll also mention that for certain scenes or puzzles or rooms/levels they’ve been moved around, you’ll expect them to happen at the same time as the original but they end up being slightly after or before certain parts and have differences to them but it never feels glaringly wrong or like it is interrupting the flow of the game. The game flows soooooo smoothly and makes sure to never put extra parts that feel like artificial “padding” even with the smaller puzzles since those often have entire sections of the area to their own and with the engaging combat it makes for extremely entertaining and terrifying exploration in confined spaces especially.There’s more to talk about with every small thing they added and things they kept, like james still moves his head independently to alert that there’s some key item or equipment around but there are also things that are different and really fun that add onto the experience, like the blood on james jacket indicating health or being able to actually break glass even if it serves no purpose or how seamless traveling from the outside into some building/room feels. I’ll definitely say that you should not be worried it will “play/look like resident evil” as it has an entirely different feel to it despite the 3rd person camera and the improved combat. There’s also tons of setting to help you change how you want the UI to look so if you want maximum difficulty you can turn off the indicators for low health, low ammo, and indicators for certain items, at a risk that you might miss something but i honestly like it as it keeps it cleaner looking for me with the added satisfaction of finding it all yourself, you can also choose this retro filter to main it grainy and significantly more washed out and honestly i kind of like it that way.Initially watching the trailers when they first released i was also anxious of the quality but decided to have hope that maybe this remake will be really good, i was fine with settling with something to be just “whatever” but this remake is EXCEPTIONAL and impressed me. Highly recommend.Overall so far this is a wonderful remake and deserves that title, it’s not soulless by changing integral parts of its identity and it’s also not boring since it’s not a direct 1 to 1 copy, it adds new things that enhance the experience and changes previously existing things so that it flows significantly better in the story beats of the game, extremely terrifying and the new pacing feels slower in terms of story but faster in terms of combat making for a very high anxiety game, it also feels significantly more grand and makes for new interpretations in the smaller nuances of the actors which is really entertaining to see. I don’t want to rate it out of 10 just yet since I feel that 5hrs might be too soon but honestly it’s looking like a perfect 10 for me, 10 for how much i am enjoying it. I hope everybody can enjoy this game as much as I have and please please judge it on your own merits and think,”if this was released today as its own standalone game, would it be good ? would people play it ?” i honestly believe the answer is yes to both but it really does depend on you as the player, besides if it ends up not being your style after you’ve given it a fair shot, the original is still playable and that’s totally fine too. Still worth checking out and definitely a project worth supporting. Here’s to hoping we might actually get the same treatment for SH1 and SH3 🥂

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. From its stunning art and immersive atmosphere to its impeccable execution, it truly earns a perfect 10/10. What fascinates me the most, however, is its content. This game is a genuine horror experience, not because of the unrealistic creatures, but because of the raw, bittersweet terror it evokes. It dares to explore the darkest corners of the human psyche, confronting players with the ugly truths about the heinous acts we are capable of. The way it tackles taboo topics is both bold and nuanced, making every moment feel unsettlingly real. In my opinion, it’s the best game of the year, not just for its technical brilliance, but for its fearless exploration of the human condition.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about halfway through this game, and I’ve got to say, it’s been absolutely amazing so far! The developers did a fantastic job of staying true to the spirit of the original, and the graphics are nothing short of stunning. The atmosphere and detail in every scene really immerse you into the experience, and it feels like a fresh yet familiar take on a classic. I’m really impressed with how well the game captures the essence of what made the original so great.That said, I do have one small gripe—why did they make Angela Orosco look so different? I hate to say it, but her character design just feels off, almost like they made her look more masculine, which doesn’t quite match her personality or past design. It’s a minor issue, but as a fan of the original, it’s something that stands out.Now, onto the one real negative: the performance issues. Despite how amazing the game looks, I’ve been running it on a 4060 Ti, and I’m struggling to keep a consistent 30fps. There are constant frame drops and stuttering, which really detracts from the experience, especially during intense or cinematic moments. It’s honestly disappointing to see such a great game be held back by optimization issues. Hopefully, they can address this in future patches because it’s frustrating to see such potential bogged down by poor performance.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: Blames Blunderland 2-2: The Returnening.Silent Hill 2 is a 3rd-person survival horror following the classic gaming tropes the genre is known for. Silent Hill was the 2nd biggest pioneer of Survival Horror with Resident Evil being the 1st. You navigate mazes, shoot monsters, collect supplies and solve puzzles. The bread and butter of the genre.It's probably one of the most well-known story in the gaming zeitgeist, but I'll still sum it up for good measure. You play as James Sunderland, a broken man searching for his wife Mary in the town of Silent Hill. James' wife died 3 years prior to the events of the game, however, he receives a letter from Mary beckoning him to meet up in their "special place". Knowing that their "last vacation" spot was in Toluca Lake, James enters this foggy and seemingly abandoned town, searching for answers... Silent Hill was a town dominated by a cult who worshiped demons and devils. A certain event that happened before Silent Hill 1 made the town collapse on itself and was largely abandoned by its residents. It is not a good place to be wandering around alone...On the graphic side, it is a well-produced experience. The town of Silent Hill never looked better. They worked really hard to recreate South Vale. There's a lot of abandoned objects and clutter. Everywhere you go, you can see they looked back twice and added further polish. The character models look really good, both for humans and monsters. The human faces aren't as god-tier as Death Stranding, but it holds up.In the sound department, Akira Yamaoka came back in the fold and remixed some of the old SH2 songs, as well as adding new ones. The OG SH2 soundtrack is basically legendary, so it was crucial to have him back in the remake. The voice actors are great and don't stray too far from the original's emotional scope. Yes, they've taken  liberties at certain parts, but it's still within the given context. The sound effects and ambient sounds are top tier, it's a crime not to play this with headphones.To kick things off, I'll talk about things I didn't like that much.If there's any harsh criticism I'd have for this remake, it would be what they did with the Otherside. In the OG version, the transition to the Otherside was really subtle, except for the hospital. Also, the OG version of the Otherside wasn't a hellish rusty bloody metal landscape. It was mostly just "over-decayed" liminal spaces. In the remake, they took the "mainstream" Otherside of SH1, Homecoming and the 1st movie, and plastered it in places where there wasn't really an Otherside in the original. A quick example would be the Appartment complex, the first "main dungeon". Woodside part is normal, Blue Creek is Otherside. However, the OG version wasn't all that, Blue Creek felt like it was just a very decayed and condemned part of the appartment complex. The original SH2 was a moody, sleepy, dreamy and ghostly experience. The remake has taken the same route as the recent Resident Evil remakes, focusing a little more on cinematic action. The transition from fixed camera angles to forced over-the-shoulder camera further drives in that point. The remake is a lot less "psychological horror" and lot a more "survival action horror" so to speak.You had more freedom of exploration before. Not just outside in the street but on the insides as well. A lot of streets now have sinkholes which block paths that were once open. Main "dungeons" like Appartment or Hospital now have 500% more locked doors. After playing the game a couple of times, these changes become apparent. Still open-ended to some extent, but more linear than the original.To drift back into a positive vibe...They did not butcher the story. It is an extremely faithful retelling of the original. As a matter of fact, they added a little more cutscenes that wasn't there before. I was expecting some things to be removed but they've delivered on this front. The same can be said about the areas you visit. Despite being a little more linear, all areas from the original return and some of these got expanded a little more. I'm actually impressed by that.In the original, the combat was slow, janky and goofy. The combat in the remake is a lot harder, so much so that we now have a Dodge button... Enemies are numerous and aggressive. Unlike the original, getting ganked in the remake can mean a quick death if you don't react accordingly. You don't have an aiming lockon here, so you better make each shot count as you will find a lot less ammo than the original. Also, you can't "pause" the game to recover health, you have to chug your Estus live during combat.I liked how the remake remixed the entire game and made it longer and confusing than the original. They removed some of the old paths as well as a bunch of old puzzles, but added new ones instead. They've been able to shove my expectations aside and keep me surprised while still being faithful to the original's main path.All in all, this remake is a great way to come back from the dead. Perhaps a little too "mainstreamified" for my nostalgia goggles. We've been running on fumes for too long, and finally we got something substantial that I think all fans can like in some way or another, while also disliking it for what's missing from the original or its altered gameplay hoops. It's a great link to the past and it gives me hope for this forsaken franchise that has been stagnating for more than a decade.Technical stuff: Use -dx11 launch command for better performance.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Bloober did it, the absolute mad lads.When I watched the Silent Hill Transmission stream on Youtube a year or two back, I was excited for more Silent Hill but really apprehensive about Bloober making the remake. This was mostly due to not having heard many good things regarding their previous work in horror. I am glad to say however, that I was wrong. Bloober has done a great job remaking a game I hold dear to my heart. It does feel like Bloober did have the same amount of love as me and many others have for Silent Hill 2.My biggest worry from the start was that they'd change the story or mess with its subtlety or themes. The story has been left alone, with only minor changes to dialogue. All the important bits are still there and I couldn't personally be much happier with it. The voice acting has always been a point of contention in the community. I personally always liked the acting in the 2001 version, but the current voice work is still a large improvement over the original. At least for the most part. Eddie, James and Laura had the biggest jump in quality, while I found Marias and Angelas voice work a slight bit lacking at times. Maria especially I felt lacked a bit of the raw emotion that she had in the original. Eddie had the biggest glow up, I definitely felt that he came off more unhinged and scary in this version. The biggest improvement overall outside of voice acting and visuals, was the gameplay. The gameplay won't necessarily wow anyone on its own, especially if you've played some more action heavy horror games like the RE4 remake. But if you look at it from the lens of someone who has played a good amount of the earlier Silent Hill games, its night and day how much it stands above the rest of the series. How much that says about it when the latest mainline release was in 2012, is up for debate. I played the game on hard since I had it recommended to me that way, and the combat could be brutal at the start, especially when ammo is more scarce. Enemies hit like trucks and I got hit a lot since I hadn't gotten their patterns down yet. I still found it enjoyable nonetheless. The camera and melee lock on didn't really mesh well together sometimes. While the enemy variety is still lacking as it was in the original, I do love that they made them distinct from one another with their different attacks and patterns. The music, sound design and visuals are top notch in the remake. I was so glad to hear that Akira Yamaoka returned to do audio design and the soundtrack for this game. I still listen to the original soundtracks when I'm out and about. His work on the overall sound design shines through especially in the overall ambience of the game. However I'm not a huge fan of all of the changes made to the songs. For example, I much prefer the original Theme Of Laura to the one in the remake, but Yamaoka still manages to show me why he is the GOAT. There were considerable differences made in this remake however, so its not a 100% like the original, which is what I was expecting anyways. I liked the new puzzles they added, both the ones I don't remember being in the original as well as the ones they changed up a bit. They kept my brain working a good amount and didn't feel too obscure or hard to wrap your head around. The level design was already changed up quite a lot, resulting in areas feeling a lot larger than they were originally. This doesn't really come as a detriment to the overall pacing of the game though it makes it longer in playtime. There are still a lot of locked doors however. The game is also technically speaking very well done. I didn't encounter any obvious bugs or glitches, other than some weird ragdolls and slight shimmering caused by some of the settings I was running the game on. The game performed alright on my mid-tier rig of a R5 5500 and 1660 Super. Running the game on FSR 1 quality mode with med-high settings landed me an average of 50 or so frames per second. Some areas did cause some tanks in the the 30s but those were few and far in between.If you have a similar rig to mine, you can definitely enjoy the game to the fullest without the frame rate being a detriment. There is FSR 3 available but its hidden in the configuration files and it personally didn't too much for me that FSR 1 didn't already do. As someone who would consider themselves a big fan of the original Silent Hill 2, I'm satisfied with the experience I was given and thats all I feel I can ask. It's not a perfect game, but neither was the original. The remake is very well made and worth your time. I don't know if I'd recommend it necessarily as a way for a complete first timer to enjoy the series as this version might leave them too spoiled to enjoy the more rough around the edges originals, but if you truly can't play the original in any way, this version is a great way to experience the story and get absorbed in to the Silent Hill series.

_childDocuments_.review: Stutter Hill 2 Deluxe Unpatched Edition. Seriously, don't know how the overall consensus of the game is overwhelmingly positive, or how you'd be hard pressed to find any negative reviews online. Buyer beware, unless you have a really high end machine because I have multiple pc's to test this on, it's not worth it at all. The base game is great and what's there is a fantastic framework for a game of the year contender, but it's wrapped up in Unreal Engine 5 stutters for everyone else. Considering how slow Konami has been on rolling out updates for Metal Gear Solid Master Collection, because that was it's own mess, I'm not too optimistic on how fast they can fix this game's problems. So I would wait on this game for God knows how long before you buy. Litterly, there's no benefit of being an early adopter these days, so just don't, unless you want your first playthrough to be a dissapointing mess.Edit: After playing the game more, I would say this game prefers Nvidia graphics cards, so if you have a low mid range PC, your AMD card will absolutely not work. But if you have like a 3060, it should run for the most part but traversal stutters are going to happen regardless. It's playable on Nvidia. AMD? Well just have a beefy one. Still I'd recommend on sale unless you really just want to jump on the bandwagon because I am enjoying the game. To give you an idea, on a lower end AMD card, the game ran like Callisto Protocol on release. With a less powerful Nvidia card, it was an actual playable experience. So if you can wait, wait. If not, take the game as it is, it's still very fun. Gpu's tested are the AMD 6700s laptop gpu (doesn't perform well at all) and the Nvidia 2060m (which had a pretty playable experience), then of course very little problems on a AMD 7900 xtx. Mostly played the game on the 2060m. Upscaling used on all builds with low settings. Sometimes i would come across 15fps for the traversal stutters, and if I waited it would go away (2060m). Ran the game on fsr ultra performance on all builds and on the 2060m I'd usually get around 60fps with dips every once in awhile. There is also a potato mod for this game that really makes it playable on anything, but you'd have to add reshade to make it look decent. 😂 And that mod is called Demake on Nexus Mods.P.S. Oh and last but not least NO CLOUD SAVES

_childDocuments_.review: I remember watching the first trailer and be like "Oh...Konami on their way to ruin a masterpiece again..."Boy oh boy was I wrong, Bloober COOKED, and they cooked HARD.They perfectly captured the essence of Silent Hill 2, the additions are all very welcomes, the changes all make sense, and whetever absolutely didn't need to be changed, didn't.Silent Hill 2 was a masterpiece, not just for its time, it brought a different flavor to the horror genre, while Resident Evil was a carbon copy (and at times clearly plagiarism) to Alone in the Dark, Silent Hill did its own thing, an horror that is a lot more personnal, a lot more psychological, and dare I say, because of that, a lot scarier.While many horror games capitalize on cheap and fradulent jumpscares, Silent Hill has an objective, to NEVER make you feel safe, and it does that through ambiance. The combination of abhorent visuals, and deafening silence is possibly the scariest experience I've had in my gaming life. The game could throw absolutely nothing at your for 2 hours straight and you would still be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ your pants.And yet, while being the scariest game, it's also one of the most beautiful, it's an exploration of what makes us human, the feelings that you wish didn't exist, but they do, they damn well do.Guilt, Anger, Emptiness, Depression, they're all here. The monstruous characters that Silent Hill depicts are always a lot closer to you than you wish. Just to be clear, this is a perfect remake of an already perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: A remarkably strong reimagining. Bloober anchored themselves on the roots of Silent Hill 2, took from it the key ingredients, and wrapped their reimagining in their own prose seemingly without intent to replace the past or gaudily mimic it. In the same way that a book may be adapted to film multiple times and, with each iteration, take on new forms influenced by the creators vision, Bloober's focus here seems to present their own take on the material. Knowing that you could never really, truly replicate the era specific prose, technology, and design language, that both intentionally and unintentionally give Silent Hill 2 its timeless identity, Bloober's vision is the best of both worlds: all the right ingredients to show care towards identifying what makes Silent Hill 2 tick, but confident enough to build upon, from, and into it to make for what often feels like an entirely new experience.And in the end, unexpectedly, we've got two things: a remarkably true to spirit reimagining of Silent Hill 2 in all its greatness, and a genuinely good, fresh, modern Silent Hill game by its own merits.The Unreal Engine 5 warts dampen the experience, and the subjectivity of stutter will differ wildly based on taste, personal thresholds, and hardware. And while I obviously would have preferred strong technical consistency, the engine faults just aren't enough for me to hold back a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely surprised by how good this was as an experience. As an avid fan of Survival Horror, I probably fall into a niche subset of people who play and enjoy Resident Evil, Evil Within etc. but I've never played a Silent Hill game in my life, despite hearing all about how good 2 & 3 are from a friend of mine for years.I was very dubious at first, having seen the original trailer reveal, along with having played several of Bloober Team's past entries such as The Medium, Blair Witch & Layers of Fear, and not having really enjoyed any of those. In the end I decided to watch the aforementioned friend of mine play a couple of hours in the apartments section early on in the game, watching in total silence. I've gotta admit, Bloober Team have done a fantastic job.Not only did the raw gameplay completely turn my opinion around, this has got to be a stellar example of a remake done correctly. In my opinion this sits alongside the Resident Evil 2 Remake, as a masterclass in how to provide a phenomenal experience to both new and old players alike. I've heard things through osmosis over the 20+ years since the original released, but I went in pretty much as blind as possible. I'm so glad I did.The combat is intense and satisfying, the areas are gorgeous to behold, both the scenic and nightmarish locations, and the sound design is simply superb. Multiple times I was given a foreboding sense of dread from the sounds I heard, be it enemies, or ambience. The atmosphere created in this game is phenomenal, and you are truly doing yourself a disservice if you don't experience it firsthand, by yourself.I haven't felt a sense of unease and actual terror like this from playing a videogame in years. I honestly can't recommend this enough to any Horror fans, especially if you have a soft spot for Survival Horror like I do.

_childDocuments_.review: It was nice to see a «Leon Kennedy» but without Face App again. After beating every RE I ran out of horror games and Silent Hill 2 was a breath of fresh air. Sounds are so real, I strongly recommend playing in headphones.The only disadvantage of this game— I couldn't play it for more than 2.5 hours in a row, just because my brain was tired of constant puzzles, scary sounds and a terrifying atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10. If you were on the fence, this is your signal to play it.When this project was first announced, i was very skeptical. As an avid enjoyer of the original, I didnt trust Bloober or Konami to handle the source material with the care it deserves. As more previews were released, i actually got more excited. It looked promising, i was definitely going to play it, if even just to know. Having cleared it once in one marathon, i can safely say Bloober team knocked it out of the park. I hardly have anything negative to say about it. Visually its beautiful, everything feels so alive and real. Even just walking around town, or the park, or anywhere for that matter, is like a religious experience. There's so many small details in both the environment and characters. Those characters feel much more human than before. The voice acting is fantastic, the body language, facial ticks, little eye movements. Even just the little lines that come out when you are wandering with Maria. They feel like PEOPLE, and not just plot devices. The combat is solid. Definitely more engaging than the original, but nothing too crazy. Puzzles and environments have been overhauled, in a way that keeps the spirit of the originals while also maintaining surprises for returning fans. Only thing i can really complain about is theres a section or two that is almost overstaying its welcome, but to be fair, i played it in one sitting..I yap about this game all day. Its really something.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a solid remake actually. There's big revamps to a lot of areas of the game and the boss fights are also improved a lot which is pretty cool, there's a couple of extra cutscenes here and there also and some new areas not seen in the original.The voice acting is pretty good although I prefer some of the line deliveries of the original over this one and even some lines were taken out entirely which is unfortunate, other than that though its passable. The combat isn't too bad, its mostly a lot of dodge timing which can be frustrating when enemies have delayed attacks and taking damage really sucks on hard difficulty, if you really suck at dodging in games you're not going to get far at least if you try playing on hard. The puzzles are quite good I do like how they've improved and expanded upon some of the puzzles in the original and even scrapped some puzzles in favor of better ones so that's pretty good, there are a few challenging ones but the further you get into the game the easier they get in my opinion.Visually it is very nice and impressive looking even on low graphics settings although there can be some odd visual bugs when you're on the lowest settings and have frame generation stuff on. The hair is the main problem for me its so ugly and glitchy looking if you don't have high settings so it does take you out of the experience a bit unfortunately.There are some things here and there which feel a bit like maybe low budget or just maybe not given enough time for more polish which is a shame, some animations and little details are a bit janky which is unfortunate but oh well. The game itself runs sort of okay but its plagued with constant framedrop issues which can be annoying at times, outside of that though it does run a lot better than most new games that are coming out these days, on lowest settings and frame generation I'm able to get between 70-120fps in most areas so its pretty decent compared to stuff like alan wake 2 which I could only get like 30fps on, and this is at only 1080p, I can't imagine how bad it must be at higher resolutions. But yeah its not too bad, could be better but yeah pretty much the main thing that kills the game is the framedrops, they really need fixing. The game also crashed for me twice which kinda sucks, once at the end of a boss fight and once just opening some door somewhere.I do like how they've changed some things around in the game but other times I feel like ah man I wish they would've kept this in. Overall though I definitely think its a very good remake and I am glad that it exists so people who weren't able to play the original can experience the game. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 3 hours of Silent Hill 2 Remake at the time of writing, as well as that I have not played the original game (only seen videos). but I want to talk about this game regardless.This game from a visual standpoint and especially comparing it to the original, is beautiful. It uses Unreal Engine 5 and to give a clear idea on how beautiful it is, in my opinion it looks better than Demons Souls on PS5. There are so many high quality textures, puddles, character models, shadows, and so on. Because of this the game's atmosphere is also incredible and easily my main draw to the game. The original was already known for it's atmosphere, ambience, and tone and in this remake it is no different. In some ways you could say it is better than the original though I don't want to claim that it is. The fog obscuring your vision, the wind sound effects and other sounds effects that play in the background, the colorless-ness of the world, as well as the dark/depressing tone the game gives off keeps you immersed within the town of Silent Hill as you walk around.As for gameplay, much like Alan Wake 2, Dead Space, Callisto Protocol, Resident Evil, etc. it is basically just a Resident Evil clone with different factors in there of course (like no real inventory management) but it's more or less the same fundamentally. It's probably most like Callisto Protocol since that game is mostly melee-focused like this one. Is the gameplay the most disapointing part of the game so far for me? Yes. Does that mean the gameplay is bad? No, far from it, in fact it is really good anyway. So why complain about it if it's good? Well as a person who has played the Dead Space Remake, Resident Evil 4 Remake, Alan Wake 2, a little bit of Callisto Protocol, and other games like those. I suppose I was hoping that since recently alot of AAA horror games have been more or less very similar, this remake would try to be different fundamentally from RE in some way (which I suppose it technically is?) I don't know what exactly I was hoping for but something different I guess. Now once again, none of this means the game is bad at all and im not trying to rail on it by comparing it to RE. After all RE's gameplay is still great to this day so therefore Silent Hill 2's gameplay is still great to me. Plus the overall game in the 3 hours I played (up until the Apartments) is a masterpiece so far. So I don't really have a right to complain about it at the end of the day.I don't have much to say about story and plot, like I've said before, I've only played 3 hours. I'm only almost done progressing through the Wood Side Apartments. But so far the story has been 'intriguing' is the word i'd like to use. I'm interested to see where it ends up. I intend to edit this part and this entire review in general the more I play until I get at least one of the endings (I know there are multiple.)The last thing I'd like to talk about, which is part of the reason I started this review this early on, is the performance. As of right now (10/12/24 or 12/10/24 for most other parts of the world) The game's performance is not too great at all. I had to look up the settings online that I needed to have on 2k resolution (2560x1440p) to maintain a 'stable' 60fps which was fine around the start of the game, but now at the Apartments it's has boggled down to more or less 40fps. It could just be because I'm on 2k resolution but I see plenty of people complain about the performance who are on lower settings and resolutions. So I think in general the game is not optimized well on PC. It's no Jedi Survivor launch performance, but I recommend people who are interested in buying this game to at least wait a week or two before paying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ $70 to get the game. Most likely by that point Bloober Team will have at least rolled out a patch or two for performance.

_childDocuments_.review: SH2 is the remake many of us never thought we'd get - lovingly crafted by a team that clearly adores the original. One that is incredibly faithful to the original but brought up to the modern age in terms of graphics and gameplay. Bloober team definitely cooked, and they should feel so proud of themselves for what they've created. Although I don't think this replaces the original due to aspects I will discuss later, it is definitely close enough to replace it for those who will never get into the original game and I'm glad that SH2 has a chance to be experienced by a wider/new audience.At time of writing I just finished my first playthrough on hard/hard at 26 hours and am utterly exhausted.Pros- Incredibly faithful remake that matches the original almost 1:1, and any puzzles or events that werent included in the gameplay have little throwbacks that will bring a smile to veteran players' faces.- The atmosphere was nailed 1000%. Bloober expertly used darkness, sound and colour to create a truly oppressive atmosphere that was honestly draining to play through (in a good way). The otherworld environments were spot on and I liked how they used the colour red to be both menacing, guiding and a source of safety. Out of the original trilogy I always found 2 to be the least scary, but the remake ratchets up the tension so high (whilst still being SH2) that I honestly don't know if I could force myself through a remake of 1 or god forbid 3.- Combat. I was really skeptical to begin with but the combat is similar to RE2 remake but the addition of a dodge and meaningful melee makes it feel so much better. On Hard the enemies are a real threat which further adds oppressive atmosphere. I dont think I'll ever get over the shock of getting my ass whooped by a mannequin, but the cat-and-mouse dynamic introduced by their behaviour I personally really enjoyed and added yet another layer of anxiety to the game. Mixed- Length. The remake is significantly longer than the original and whilst I enjoyed many of the expanded areas, by the time I got to the  I was ready for it to start wrapping up. I felt the additional areas in that section and the  were overly long without any pressure release , though the final area was just right.- Bosses. Most of the bosses were completely revamped with new forms and phases. For a first playthrough I thought it was really cool, but having finished the game there's not really any bosses I want to fight again. Despite definitely earning it's title as the Dark Souls of Silent Hill games, none of the bosses were especially fun to fight as they were quite long with lots of HP which usually meant firing all your bullets into them and then finishing with the pipe which just felt and looked silly. The peekaboo bosses in particular were frustrating to fight. Honestly I preferred the originals bosses that were over in 5 seconds and were more important just from a story perspective.- "That part". SH2 had quite a few 'ugh that part' parts that I was not looking forward to seeing in the remake. The bad news is that they are allll present, but the good news is that almost all of them have been significantly improved, either through streamlining or making more fleshed out. Unfortunately the remake has quite a few "that part"s of its own .Negatives- Dialogue. A lot of the big moments just didnt hit like i expected them to, especially Maria's.- The areas felt really gamey in that you had this central puzzle that sent you off to each area to find pieces to solve and trigger a world shift or to move on to the next area. Obviously this is how survival horror games work but I swear the original felt a little more natural in how that game loop played out. I think part of this was that there were too many threes... 3 items to collect, 3 sub areas per main area... it became really obvious and I think contributed greatly to the pacing issues in the later parts, whereas they could have just made some areas much shorter like in the original.- DualSense trigger bug. The game supports adaptive triggers but they bug out and stop being adaptive after about 5 mins of gameplay. It's a real shame as it feels super cool whilst it works.This review is getting long so I will wrap it up. Bloober did an amazing job, you need to buy this game and experience it. It is unfortunately not perfect, but it gets so, so much right that the negatives aren't really that big of a concern (and are my subjective opinion, I hear a lot of people really like the boss fights...)Boot it up, pop it on hard and enjoy a week of anxiety-fuelling, soul-crushing terror. Here's hoping we get more remakes out of the team!

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought a game could move me so deeply... As I learned more about its story, I realised how much I resonated with the character of James. Unfortunately, I couldn't empathise with him due to his actions, but I was truly affected by experiencing such a well-crafted narrative. My connection to James and the story is somewhat tied to my personal life, but that doesn't make the game any less impactful; in fact, the way it was executed makes it even more compelling. Looking at the events through the lens of my own experiences, this game wasn't just about James and the other characters confronting their traumas; for me, it was also a confrontation with myself. It turned out that this kind of personal journey was exactly what I needed all along. I may not be as deserving of punishment as James, but I too have made bad decisions that I felt warranted it... In 2019, my girlfriend was diagnosed with cancer. Of course, we weren't married like James and Mary, and I didn't experience the challenges of living together or caring for someone who was ill, but it was still awful. I wanted to help her as much as I could, even if it was a slim chance of her marrow responding. Besides offering psychological support, I felt powerless, and this process was wearing me down. She seemed to try to distance herself from me, and my biggest regret was allowing that to happen. I had grown distant from her; we felt like strangers, and we weren't letting the gap between us close. She made that decision entirely for my sake, and I accepted it, succumbing to my own selfishness. I should have been there for her; I shouldn’t have accepted that I didn’t need to be by her side. This game made me realise that I still can't forgive myself. I wish I could receive a letter from you too... At that time, I couldn’t do anything for you, but I would throw myself into hell for you now.  James and I are both examples of the worst kind of people; don’t be like us.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the Silent Hill franchise, having played the games from 1 all the way to Silent Hill Shattered Memories. I was very excited about this game, and my girlfriend gratefully purchased it for me. Things were promising, definitely captured the heart and soul of the Silent Hill Franchise. The graphics, soundtrack, and sound design were amazing. It wasn't just a cash grab in terms of aesthetics; the story/graphics people really cared.HOWEVER, the game is MARRED with glitches, screen tearing, and random crashes. In particular, when you reach Woodside Apartments (near the very beginning of the game), the game CONSTANTLY crashes when you open the door to the Courtside yard. You can literally not progress. This is the first game I have ever encountered a game-breaking glitch that does not allow you to progress. This is sort of the gaming trend where they rush out a game to meet an arbitrary deadline (i.e. October/Halloween), and then they will probably say "Oh, we will patch things later." It's only been a month since the game was released to the public, so perhaps they will address this soon., and I hope so. But having the audacity to charge 70 USD for a game that you cannot play is a microcosm of the gaming industry. PLEASE wait several months/when they discount this game before you purchase it.EDIT: I finalllyy got the game to not crash every time I opened the Apartment door. What you HAVE to do is 1) uninstall/reinstall the entire game, and 2) under the Steam Properties, add launch flag: -dx11. Apparently this has only worked for some but not a lot.I still standby the review: the visuals were great. The innovation/building from the original game was great. But in the end, it has to be a GAME that is functional, and it is marginally functional at best. I reached the Brookhaven Hospital and randomly,  I've not been able to move at least three times, the stuttering, the clear loading of enemies (when you leave and reenter the area, the dead bodies rise and ragdoll onto the floor). Great visuals, poor gameplay design/optimization.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Silent Hill 2 done by the team that made the Resident Evil 2 Remake.  That's SH2R.  In some ways it enhances the original, in others it misses the mark.  Overall, not worth $70.  Wait for a sale.Ideally, SH2R would have been 5-8 hours long and $40, like the original.  A much more compact and potent experience.  But they wanted to charge $70 (or even $80 for deluxe) so they had to stretch it out.===Changes from the original that hinder the remake:- Combat and the camera make this a more action focused game.  The same thing was done to RE2R.  But SH2 is about atmosphere, which is lost with the new camera.  Don't believe me?  Check out the fixed camera mod for RE2R.  It changes the feeling of the entire game.- SH2R is too long.  I know you can speed run it, but on your first playthrough you want to take it slow, look at everything, let the gloom sink in.  Stretching the game out turns it into a slog.  In the original, you'd finish the game in 5-8 hours and then instantly want to play it again to see the other endings.  In the remake, you'll finish in 17-22 hours and then want to uninstall.  Keep in mind this isn't Parasite Eve, with a ton of unique monsters.  There are 5 enemy types (not including bosses).  Fighting gets VERY repetitive and boring.===There are MANY glitches (but to be fair, the devs are working on these):- The game LOVES to stutter.  There are mods that can fix this.- During combat James can end up on a low surface he normally can't get on (like a bed or couch).  Since you can't jump down, you have to reload.- You can get stuck if you save in the wrong place.- The save/load menu system is buggy.  Sometimes there are multiple rows highlighted.===And some minor nitpicks:- Turning the entire screen red when you're hurt like CoD is dumb.  It completely ruins the immersion.  Luckily, there's a mod to fix this.- There's a weird issue with model scale.  Like old cars that should be giant instead barely coming up to James' chest, or newspaper boxes that are as tall as James.  Seems the asset teams weren't communicating world scale very well.- SH2 takes place in 1993 (or possibly early if you go by what the original devs say).  Yet every rundown old car has modern seat belt latches.- The dog ending is missing the slide show, so the growls in the song won't make sense.- The shadows look bad, even compared to the PS2.  They don't react correctly to your flashlight.  This happens with or without ray tracing.- I have never seen a VHS player pull in a tape like a slot load CD player before.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not in a good mental state, I highly recommend avoiding this game for now. Even though I had played the original 2001 version and knew what to expect, I can honestly say that it affected me psychologically.Silent Hill 2 is undoubtedly one of the masterpieces of the video game industry; it’s not just an ordinary game. This installment confronts you with your deepest fears, offering a deeply psychological narrative that explores themes of guilt, loss, and redemption. The way the story unfolds is masterful, with shocking revelations and twists that keep you guessing and fully engaged.One of the standout elements of the game is the sound design and music, significantly shaped by the legendary Akira Yamaoka. His unique blend of haunting melodies and unsettling ambient sounds creates an immersive atmosphere that enhances the emotional depth of the story. Yamaoka's music not only sets the tone for the game but also intensifies the feelings of dread and despair, pulling players deeper into the narrative.The characters, such as Eddie, Maria, and Angela, are also masterfully crafted. Their body language and behavior carry deep psychological meanings, which I found to be impressive.Overall, I’m truly grateful to Konami and Bloober Team for reviving this amazing franchise. I sincerely hope the game sells well, so they’ll consider remaking more titles in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 is a game that is very dear to me. Though I did not have a PS2 to play it, I remember staying at my friend's place to play the game circa 2001 (wow, time long gone). It was a game that came out after 9/11 and made a massive impact because of how bad that month got.	How does the Remake hold up to the original? Well, a quick summary of the original is needed.	Silent Hill 2 follows as a sequel that can also work as a standalone game. You don't need to know about Silent Hill 1, but having it makes the game all the more attractive due to the town's history and dark undertones.It is a game that is not focused on combat (save for exceptional instances or boss fights). It is a psychological horror and a slow burn at that. It builds; it hints at secrets held within the town and James' (protagonist) past.	For first-timers, the game provided multiple endings based on unknown actions that the player performs, more so with the New Game+.	While James has access to weapons and firearms, he isn't the greatest, and that is okay. As a character, he is just an ordinary man, nothing special, nothing grand: not a special forces member, not a space marine, but a guy. This lack of polish in his combat style adds to the tension, to the fight or flight aspect of what makes us people.	Do we go ham and bash everything we see, or avoid them and find our Mary?	The voice acting and the animations were very stilted, purposefully, to add to the surreal nature of the world. Of course, some things do feel a bit like "Twin Peaks" in terms of how cheesy they sound. Animation involved the use of motion capture, which further led to the odd nature of the character's emotions.How does all of this come together in the Remake?SH2R, to keep it short, does a decent job of utilizing the Unreal Engine to give us a gorgeous game. The landscape is imposing, and the re-imagined designs of the creatures look spectacular, thanks in part to having the original creature designer of Team Silent helping to assist - (Masahiro Ito)	This, coupled with the incredible sound design of yet another Team Silent member - (Akira Yamaoka) - which can be heard in every object breaking, every footstep, not to mention the music and ambiance, all come together to make for a tense atmosphere.	When it comes to the creatures, Blooper Team gives us a few additional variations of each of the creatures. These creatures are generally faster and more aggressive. Many will close and grapple with James and horribly disfigure this poor guy.	Many of the bosses have had adjustments made to them to take them from the simple, plodding sods that they were and turn them into genuinely frightening creatures hunting after you.	Unfortunately, with all of these changes made to the Remake comes baggage.	Graphics—While gorgeous, the game is undoubtedly unrefined for many people. Even I, with an AMD and 4080 graphics card, had game crashes, major stuttering, and odd graphical glitches. Fixes have helped in some places, but I had to resort to modifying the engine in order to keep it smooth. Typically, I've had no trouble running the game at Ultra, but again, certain moments suddenly stutter, most likely due to something z-fighting in the distance or such.	Combat- James has more freedom of movement and a dodge function, but as you run into the more aggressive enemies, this can become extremely difficult. The enemy's speed and numbers can quickly overwhelm you; this is most apparent in the Otherworld. Blooper did try their best to provide a level layout that gave us the ability to squeeze through cracks and escape or even trap these creatures. Still, again, you run into so many of them that it can become a wild circus of you trying to zip between the enemy just to make some breathing room. The 2nd variation of creatures is faster and meaner and often will grapple you and punish James horribly, and in greater difficulties, it leads to a lot of game-overs since the camera's sluggishness tends to fight against you at the worst times.	Boss Fights- Most of them are generally fair, but you will find yourself in at least 2 of them where the enemy's speed and actions can often catch you off guard and scrambling to try and reload your weapon(s). Now, I didn't mind it, but I can see this becoming aggravating for others, and take into account that I play casually for fun, not for achievements.	Character models—Yes, I will include this because certain aspects bug me as a 3D artist. Angela and Mary, while the body models are fine, I have issues with the pudding faces because, for one thing, that isn't precisely how the anatomy works, plus it takes away from the fact that they are supposed to be alluring. Angela's beauty is tied to her tragedy, while Maria's beauty is tied to James's history.	I'm mixed about James himself. On the one hand, he is a little too Leon Kennedy-looking. Honestly, I prefer the look of the original James, as again, it felt like an every-man. I do give credit to the team for providing small details to James as the game continues, such as looking tired, having dirty hands, etc.	Audio- Honestly, I really can't say anything against it. I really enjoyed the re-imagining of the soundtrack and how faithful it is to the original. Again, that isn't really fair since the original artist worked on it. The ambiance and foley effects are fantastic, and honestly, I feel I can leave it there.	The biggest sin of this game, for me, is that it comes to a moment where it really begins to overstay its welcome. The change in enemy numbers and combat ends up becoming a speed bump that gets in the way of the story's momentum, and that is what troubles me most. The story provides you with fantastic depth, and you want to move on, but then a lot of combat begins to filter in between you and the next bit of the story. For me, it was when I got to the hospital's Otherworld that I started to get exhausted from fights, to the point that it slightly mired my thoughts with the Prison, which took a moment to set aside my thoughts on the hospital, the Prison introduced a new variation of one of the enemies that I both loved and hated. I loved it because of the use of the creature, and I hated it because it was designed for a character that reacts faster and doesn't fight the camera to aim at this thing.Final Thoughts and Future InstallmentsHonestly, I give this game a fair B- to B+. Certainly, it isn't the original, and when it is at its best, it hits that B+, but at its worst, it gets that B-.	It is a great game, and Blooper did an outstanding job, mainly translating a game that so many of us loved for its atmosphere to 2024. I do feel that they could have allowed this game to bake just a little longer in the oven.	In the end, I would give Blooper a chance to bring us a refined Silent Hill 1, and if that does well, Silent Hill 3. I hope that they will perhaps try to put more emphasis on the player's progression from story elements to story elements, as opposed to enemy/boss fight to enemy/boss fight.Final Final ThoughtsThe Endings get a C- for not giving us the proper goofy joke clips in the Dog Ending. Seriously, it goes straight to credits. You couldn't even just rip the old silly ending slideshow for us?

_childDocuments_.review: The original game was my favorite for ten years now, wasn't thrilled of an idea of a remake but I was positively surprised to how faithful it is to the original, Bloober team's efforts are definitely noticed, they went beyond everyone's expectations to bring this carefully crafted game back to life.Unfortunately, I did find this game to be extremely more combat oriented which strays from the originals feeling of "not winning fights but rather surviving them" It did feel like this game is made more for the next generation of "fast paced combat enjoyers", which is again, not the SH vibe. for comparison, I remember the original having no more than 100 kills in total at the end of the game, in this game my kill count was 380 that consisted of the three same enemy types.Despite other little nitpicks like removed scenes, I still consider this being a work of art and greatly recommend this game for those who don't mind a slow burn and MANY PUZZLES (I hated most of them but that's because I'm too dumb to solve them), beautifully crafted, dream-like atmosphere and the best soundtrack ever created, this game is quite the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, it's pretty good.I have a few things to address :As per usual, some people lie about performance.Sure there are a few stutters but barely.Performance is okay otherwise.With settings on mid, the game runs well, i noticed (because of an fps counter) a drop to 58fps for a second or two. That is not 10-25fps lost very often as some pretend.All my specs are on my profile. Some of this folks, of course, have a far better rig than i do and supposedly get faaaaaaaaar bigger issues, far more often than me.To be polite, i'll call... nonsense on that. Konami having killed one of (if not the biggest) stealth franchise is no excuse to lie.--------------------Story remains faithful enough to the 2001 classic.However, we are getting a new ending. Maria is a bit more slutty and Angela is far more believable.Portrayal of characters changed a bit in a good way. They feel more alive.Gameplay has been massively modernized (ik, it sounds scary). What i mean is that it is closer to the Resident Evil 2&4 remakes (not like the utter disgrace Resident Evil 3 is). You don't have an added upgrade system, you are not getting boring fetch-quests... Nothing of the sort. The new dodge and melee is snappy and accompanied by a very satisfying feedback in both the visual and audio department. Difficulty is satisfying thankfully.Graphics aren't mindblowing but they do the job quite well. The dynamic fog is not bad but less thick than in the OG. I think it should have been thicker... on the other hand, it looks more realistic. As i wrote in the story section, characters are mostly improved, partly with new facial animation mostly on point. Maria and Angie still have their distasteful haircuts though.However, it is not a perfect remake :Performance is okay but a few bugs remain.UE5 may not have been the go-to but bloober team still did decent work.The game is quite demanding, a bit more than i expected...Framerate is stable once you find the right settings.One final note, this game might not be what it seems.Play the 2001 PS2 version before this. It will help you formulate your own questions bout the nature of this entry.Story : 10/10Gameplay : 9.5/10Graphics : 8.5/10Performance : 6/10Total : 8.5/10While a good remake, i will not consider it for awards.First off because of Konami's actions and this being a remake.Be thankful for the money and f*** off.Keep up the good work Bloober Team.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 Remake stands on the same pillar that the original Silent Hill 2 had created. Personally cannot choose one over the other which is a good thing. Atmosphere, Music, Story it's all there. Biggest change that is very clear to see (as well hear) other than some additions to map layouts with some added elements that enhances the experience is the combat and new voice cast. Combat is subjective but I enjoy both the original and new combat not much for me to really complain about. It's been little over 23 years of differences that yes objectively the new combat is better, but the charm of the originals came in it's difficulty curve managing all the mechanics intended or even unintended in post game Ending's grinding and 10 Star Run's especially.We already heard the anew voice cast in HD Collection already it was terrible in context to the original Silent Hill 2. Silent Hill 2 Remake's cast is beyond solid the major highlights for me personally other than James Sunderland was Eddie Dombrowski.Overall for those wanting to replay Silent Hill 2 in anew light or never been able to play it at all with how the original console games prices have skyrocketed this is a very beyond solid way to experience Silent Hill 2 with a fresh coat of paint.With that being said, it's a small personal gripe I personally have that many may not pick up on. There is a personal void after accomplishing extra playthrough's on Hard Combat and Hard Puzzle while also getting all the achievements, your Score Screen essentially not mattering other than bragging rights. Hope that this game will get some sort of updates (other than general performance patching) to possibly add in Born from a Wish DLC Campaign as well adding in to make the Scoring System matter to earn the same/similar reward like the original. Also add in more achievements like for full Hard Mode playthrough's and more would be extra good replayability.Overall Score: 4.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: JC Kitan (experienced consumer of the survival horror genre)I can imagine the painstaking stages the Blooper team had to go through to translate a work of art like Silent Hill 2 (Jurassic one xD). Moreover, it was too big a bite, but did the result remain the same as the original, or even better... To begin with, I must say that I had a phenomenal experience and the development team honestly SUCCEEDED in translating the old format!Of course, like any product of modern horror in gaming, this remake suffers in terms of deciding how to transfer the older masterpiece to modern players (I mean the generations born after the nineties). The sufferings of this remake are not so much on the artistic level (visual, sound and narrative), but more on the level of playing the game itself (the so-called gameplay). Is it that important, it definitely is, because unlike the movie, we set the plot, we decide which direction to go, we are the curators of the story...I will carry out this review quantitatively and based on crucial parameters, I will present the initial evaluations as well as the explanation of why I think so. At the end, i will give a final CLIMAX rating that will surprise some. All in all, even though it is a remake of a masterpiece - of the masterpiece of the same name - I feel obliged to give an opinion about the game outside of scholarly discourse.1. Narrative overview / Rating: 8.0/10Synopsis of the story: The story begins three years after the questionable and painful death of the wife (Maria) of James Sunderland (the main character of the game). James receives a mysterious letter from her inviting him to return to their "special place". Visiting that special place (the city of Silent Hill itself) it becomes obvious that this is not the city he remembers - it is mysterious, dangerous and disturbing, full of various creatures from nightmares that constantly follow him. His search for Mary leads him to face not only the horrors of the city itself, but also the darkness and secrets within himself.Such a blasphemous attempt to describe the synopsis of the story without simultaneously creating a "spoil" is rare. Overall, the story holds up very well, and it's clear from the start that the developers are experienced connoisseurs of the original story and all the potential repercussions that the characters in the game face. Dramatically, the remake begins identically to the original and keeps the "old school" treatment, but at times, speaking of the technological development of video games, it tries too hard to modernize certain scenes, which loses the basic charm of the most important parts of the game. The problem lies not in the way of monologic and dialogic, or even diegetic narration, but in the way of framing the scene. Previously, scenes had so-called "dutch" corners and totals were present (in the context of the film plan). The remake does not allow that risk, and forces more close-ups (than those mentioned), which loses the surreal magic and even the Lynchian spirit that the Japanese forced in the original game. Of course, there is everything that I criticized, but not in the places where it should be. Given that it is a remake and therefore an extended experience of storytelling and playing the game itself - the new inserted scenes look phenomenal and fill the gaps of the original, and sometimes they also problematize and create a bigger QUESTION about what is happening and in which direction the mystery will go.In addition to the narrative, it is important to mention the acting. The actors did a phenomenal job with their characters. The main character James Sunderland has never looked better than he does now. The other characters are wonderfully reimagined, as well as the way they are set up - in opposition to the main character. The acting is on point! The direction is not...I know that for some it sounds pointless to analyze film grammar in a game, but this is a game that responds as an undisputed multimedia work. After all, all games nowadays strive to have phenomenal direction. However, whoever directed the original scenes went too far. At times it seems as if the director, i.e. the game director didn't know if he wanted to force a surreal spirit or a psychological foreplay between the characters. The combination of multiple genres in the SH franchise is not a bad thing, but it is awkward in terms of direction, because you don't know exactly if something is purposefully poorly executed, because it is not moderated with the remaining scenes that are super done. It is important to note that the Japanese are extremely awkward when it comes to storytelling, so their original games had that charm, but when a westerner remakes a Japanese game, it becomes very difficult to understand whether the author refers to his own style or tries to combine original and your own, create a new result. Certainly a very difficult task, but I am satisfied if nothing else.2. Atmospheric (un)opportunities and perfect visuals / Rating: 10/10In terms of graphics and the visual atmosphere itself, the game does not make mistakes. In this parameter, the remake was given an honorable place to be better than the original itself. The way the fog and hail concept has been improved is mind-blowingly killer! Most of them, mostly as I write, criticize some aspects of the atmosphere, like it's too dark a game or something like that - NO! It's not dark, increase the brightness if you use HDR. Adjust the brightness based on your monitor. I'll just say it.The stage space has been filled with new details, from where you can clearly see that the space was once alive and filled with details of a past life. There are a lot of psychological attributes in the stage space that play with the main character, testing him. A GREAT job again!3. Soundtrack/Sound Design / Rating: 8.5/10As someone who has been emulating SH music and sound design for years, I have to be critical here. Let's start with the sound. The sound is completely school-made, precise and designed in the spirit of the original. So what's wrong... Well. The incorporation and relationship of SFX and music is wrong. Whenever there is no music, the design is at its best, however, when the music starts, the way it's mixed, I can barely hear it. Is it school - it is... However, SH is a pure improvisation of the relationship between sound and music, and here it is lacking. If I were to analyze the sound separately from the music, I would give the sound a 10/10 and the music a 6-7,Music - khmm... I wonder why there was a need to remake the music itself. Honestly! Let's be real! Where the problem arises - in the music... Listen to some of the main tracks, like Laura Theme, Null Moon or Heaven's night. The instruments are almost missed, it sounds identical, but the uncanny experience that was present in the original is missing due to the so-called trip/hop lo-fi arrangement. 4. Game design/Level design/Puzzles / Score: 10/10There is no need to write so much here, because this is a unique experience, both for new players and for people who have crossed the original many times. The way the world is designed from a gamer's point of view should be the basic manifesto for any new survival horror game ever, especially if someone decides to remake an older game. So, the levels are full of creepy (un)opportunities, new but at the same time improved puzzles. It's a truly unique experience and kudos to the Blooper team!In this section, another compliment to the developers - "Congratulations, you did a better job than Capcom with the remakes of the Resident Evil franchise"!Conclusion:All in all, Silent Hill 2 - Remake is a great game - RATING: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: After Kojima's Silent Hill was canceled, Konami faced a lot of criticism because, first of all, Kojima is a genius, and secondly, the short demo P.T. turned out to be incredibly successful (I liked it as well). I had little doubt that Kojima's Silent Hill would have been great. But Kojima and Konami parted ways like ships in the night, and the project was shelved - until recently.Konami decided to entrust the game to Bloober Team, the studio responsible for games like Blair Witch, Observer, The Medium, and Layers of Fear. Interestingly, I liked each of these games in its own way, but to be honest, they were all B-tier games, and they even had performance issues. (The Medium, for example, would cause even powerful graphics cards to struggle when it had to load textures in two worlds simultaneously.) Overall, it’s hard to call their games masterpieces or extremely popular.However, the game turned out to be awesome - almost perfect, but not quite. It’s clear that resources weren’t unlimited, but it’s also clear how carefully and diligently Bloober Team worked with what they had. There aren’t a ton of enemies or enemy types, but I think they’re well-made and thoughtfully designed. The same goes for the bosses. The locations are often maze-like, reminiscent of Resident Evil, but what I really liked were the puzzles, not all of which were super obvious or as straightforward as in RE.Things got worse when the first gameplay trailer was shown. It featured clunky, jerky animations straight out of 2008, which fueled doubts about the game, and everyone started expecting a disaster.Even though the game keeps you on edge and really captures that Silent Hill vibe, by the end, you start getting tired of the formula: shoot something, find an item, solve a puzzle, repeat. The game isn’t too long, but this repetitiveness makes it feel longer than it actually is. There are also some issues with freezing, but as Digital Foundry explained, this is related to Unreal Engine 5. Even if you lock the framerate at 30 FPS and the frames remain stable, there are still noticeable stutters. (For some reason, I didn’t get the claimed 60 stable FPS; I had drops to 40 FPS and, at one point, even to 30.)In conclusion, I think everyone got exactly what they were expecting: the game has great puzzles, decent action, and a thick atmosphere. I really enjoyed it, and for those who are still undecided about buying it - I highly recommend it.I hope the sales will be good, and we'll be looking forward to the next remake from Bloober Team!

_childDocuments_.review: The “Silent Hill 2” remake breathes new life into a beloved horror classic, delivering an updated experience that stays faithful to the original while adding a fresh visual and auditory polish. The story remains untouched, allowing players to step into the shoes of James Sunderland as he journeys into the town of Silent Hill, haunted by a letter from his late wife. The remake retains the original’s psychological depth, capturing James’s personal torment and the symbolic monsters that represent his inner guilt and sorrow.Graphically, the remake is stunning. Leveraging modern hardware, the developers have amplified the fog-filled, desolate landscape of Silent Hill, making the setting even more oppressive. Detailed textures, realistic lighting, and facial animations bring a new layer of immersion to the characters and environments. The iconic monsters, including Pyramid Head, are as terrifying as ever, now with a more horrifying level of detail.In terms of gameplay, combat and controls have been modernized. Movement is smoother, and combat is more responsive, which enhances accessibility without sacrificing the tension of resource management and survival that defined the original. The updated mechanics make it feel more fluid but still faithfully difficult.Sound is exceptional, with Akira Yamaoka’s remastered soundtrack adding depth to the atmosphere. The audio cues are expertly designed, enhancing the horror in subtle ways that keep players on edge.Rating: 9/10. The “Silent Hill 2” remake revitalizes a classic with updated visuals, refined gameplay, and incredible sound design, offering both old fans and newcomers an unforgettable horror experience.

There were so many parts I just wanted to get it over with because I was so scared.The combat is very basic, same with the enemies and boss fights.I really enjoyed the puzzles and just walking around these creepy and beautifully designed environments.I went into this game expecting something similar to dead space or resident evil.It's very different to both.
