_childDocuments_.review: I want to be upfront that I experienced some near game-breaking stuttering off and on throughout my playthrough. Despite that, I kept playing all the way to the end.Survival horror is my favorite genre. While I haven’t played any of the original Silent Hill games, I’ve gone through all the recent Resident Evil releases, so I was excited when I heard this was being remade. Some things in the gameplay trailer made me a little nervous—the animations looked clunky, and knowing Bloober Team’s track record, I wasn’t sure they’d pull it off.I was wrong. This game is awesome. I found the combat to be super fun and addicting, even if it’s not quite as deep as Resident Evil. While the melee is pretty one-note, it stays challenging. The atmosphere and characters are what truly make this game shine. The setting and music elevate it to another level. From the very beginning, when I first heard the music, I knew there was something special here. I didn’t expect to be so moved by this game, and the acting—especially for James—is some of the best I’ve seen in a game.If you’re a fan of Resident Evil, this is a must-play. I would say this game scratches the same itch but is on the complete opposite end of the horror spectrum in tone.I really hope Bloober Team can resolve the stuttering issues so that everyone can enjoy this game as it was intended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be so great if it wasn't for the terrible optimization and stutters. It destroys immersion because the game stutters every 5 seconds or has a super low framerate. My PC is due for an upgrade but it's still a decent rig: Ryzen 5 2600x, 3700ti, 16gb of 3200mghz ram. I can run Resident Evil 4 remake at high settings on 1440p and get 60fps no problem. On this game I get anywhere from 20-100fps and it has no rhyme or reason as to why the fps is what it is at the current time. It generally stays in the 40s-50s and gets worse as progressing through the levels. I have tried every known fix (run with dx11, turn off steam overlays, turn off vsync, validate game files) and nothing changes. I can run it on high or low settings and still get the same framerate. I can run it on 1080p low settings and the framerate still stays the same. That proves that there is something inherently wrong with the games optimization! Even changing the resolution percentage in the advanced settings does nothing to change the framerate. I can raise it or lower it and nothing changes. I can honestly say I've never played a game that was this poorly optimized. I've been trying every new Nvidia driver in hopes that would do something, and no it does not. I have been slowly playing through the game and hoping for an update to fix it, which hasn't happened. At this point I am sad I wasted $70 on this game after seeing all the great reviews and I don't understand how it is still overwhelmingly positive. I have made it to the prison and really want to see the end of the game, but sadly I guess I will put it down for now and play something else in the meantime in hopes they actually release a patch to fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a faithful remake of one of my favorite games ever. Even though it removes the Dutch Camera Angles, they still make the game feel claustrophobic and tense with the third-person camera. The story largely stays the same, with a couple of the story beats fleshed out or put in a slightly different order. The original game had a very Japanese feel to horror, where most of the characters are in this numb sense of reality, while the remake feels much more Western, where most characters seem like they are actively suffering and in emotional distress. Overall this is my game of the year. I didn't think Blooper team could do it, but they over-delivered. If you've never played Silent Hill 2 or you grew up playing it as I did, this is a great way to experience the horrors of 2001 on modern systems.
_childDocuments_.name: SILENT HILL 2

_childDocuments_.review: So I have never played Silent Hill 2 before, I've seen the occasional video essay and definitely knew more about certain plot elements going in than I probably should have but, just know that if you're looking for a comparison by someone who knows the game well I cannot provide that. At the same time I'm also not a huge horror fan, while I have found enjoyment from action-horror titles like Dead Space 2 I am just not the biggest fan of loud jumpscares at the camera and being helpless and all that... Horror is sometimes tricky for me...I say all that because this game really captivated me, it was the kind of horror that got under my skin, made me feel the hairs on my body stand up, and a couple of times made me pause because a sound was so unsettling that I needed to recenter myself... But it never went too far, it played the longer quieter games of horror, even its more intense sections were rooted in that quiet kind of horror, where the creeping sound of something you don't see is infinitely more powerful than a loud jump from something you do.If you go into this seeing the 3rd person camera and expect the Resident Evil style of combat and action, this isn't that, combat has a clunkiness to it but also a satisfying sense of weight and pure desperation in every swing that, even though very basic, serves its purpose well enough but Silent Hill 2 isn't known for its combat, it's famous for its themes and story and atmosphere and as far as I'm concerned this remake has definitely lived up to the reputation I've heard about this game for so many years.The story and acting is dreamy and weird but honestly great, the music and presentation and sound design all work together to make absolutely nightmarish soundscapes that occasionally turn genuinely beautiful or reflective and melancholic; and the visuals, while definitely fighting the hardware for frames sometimes and with the occasional stutter and overly harsh DLSS smear, still creates a phenomenal sense of dread; darkness and fog can make the imagination do a lot of the work of the horror for you and this game seriously knows that.If like myself you're not a jumpscare fan this game is seriously light on them, it's more creepy and tense than downright terrifying and screaming at you all the time and that really worked for me, and I honestly found it was all the more memorable for it; there was a bizarre sense of immersion that I found from it all that just had me absolutely absorbed into the whole experience, and it's one I genuinely am actually looking forward to turning the puzzle difficulty up and doing again some time. It's a kind of horror that made me "get it"; I am very much not a horror fan but, I guess I am at the very least a Silent Hill 2 fan now because this game's restraint and willingness to sit and stew in a moment or feeling was far more powerful and chilling to me than any screamer ever will be.In my dreams I still find myself going back to that place, it's a terrible nightmarish haunting place, and I won't forget it for a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game since the news of a possible remake of the legendary series have appeared in the Internet. Unfortunately, I didn't play the original game when it was released 23 years ago and I was very excited when I found out about the serious development on this remake! This particular game will appeal to both fans and those just getting to know the series. If you are looking for the game that have a special, unique atmosphere that will be remembered forever, then I definitely recommend this game for purchase.I am a fan of the Silent Hill series and my favorite parts are the first 3 parts. I also believe that these 3 parts are the best example of "psychological horror" genre games. Silent Hill is: depth of plot, psychological insight, quantity and quality of raised problems, interesting characters with tragic stories, heartbreaking soundtracks...Oh yes, let me say a special word about SH soundtracks. Akira Yamaoka is a God of music! His compositions brought this series to life. I was happy to find out that he's also working on the remake. Soundtracks from the 2nd part are my favorites and it wouldn't be as emotional and exciting journey if it wasn't with his music.So, now specifically about the game. There is a generally linear game divided into different locations, where you can fight enemies with different types of weapons (melee weapons, pistol, shotgun and rifle) and avoiding their hits, have to look for items or solve puzzles () to open access to the next levels, but you will also have a small opportunity to walk around the city/current location without any problems (except for the doors that are locked at certain stages and, well, enemies you probably don’t want to face). After all, every time I passed another house or room, I wondered, “who lived here and what really happened?” No matter how dead this city is in the story, its streets are still alive with all of those details and that is beautiful in its own way! . There are several types of enemies in the game with their unique “features”, which you get used to over time, but sometimes because of the number of enemies it is very easy to miss a hit or even a few and end up dying. That is why in this game it is important to watch the enemies' movements and calculate timings correctly. This series was never about a cool combat system, but the developers managed to get rid of the old, sometimes quite funny mechanics and make something of their own, which most of the time looks not very impressive and dynamic, but which is very suitable for Silent Hill series as a whole. In addition to the usual enemies, there are few boss fights, which, from a story perspective, look good, but they are not too challenging especially with a lot of resources you have.. Those who are not familiar with the story of the original, then if briefly and without spoilers I will say that the main character receives a letter from his wife, who asks him to meet at a “special place” in Silent Hill. Silent Hill is a small town, which used to be a popular tourist spot, until a terrible tragedy happened in it. Unfortunately, the second part gives us very little information about the origin of the town and the creatures in it, this information is in other parts of the game and there will be spoilers, so I can only say that the tragedy is associated with people who for the sake of their goals went very far and in the end because of them a lot of people died...Anyway, throughout this particular history we encounter enemies and meeting several characters who either just talk to us about their problems or accompany us like Maria did. In the original series, Maria has never caused me any sympathy, but developers did smth that really got me attached to this character. There are 8 endings in the game, so your actions and your "play style" will be important if you want to achieve one or another ending. At the end I can say that the SH is a very complicated and completely untypical story, especially in the genre of horror. So whatever your experience, it will be in your memory forever.. In my opinion, this game is not as scary as the Outlast series and there are few jump scares, but there are other types of horrors. For example, each location has its own tragic story and the horror you see there, is on the surface/in the enemies or in the details that you have to find around. In addition, some locations were creepier, especially in the dark as there are all these creepy and sometimes unexpected sounds and enemies that only add an atmosphere of horror. There is another frightening element: the boss fights or chases where you have to think and do smth very fast and try to not die. of the game is great and walking around the city, making a bunch of beautiful and atmospheric screenshots is normal reaction. I am also exciting to try the “90’s” graphic mode during the second play through, but there are more modes in the settings. However, there is one minus and this is an optimization. I do not have powerful computer and unfortunately, I had to find a combination of settings that would allow me to play with a smoother picture and more FPS. For the overall picture of the game, it is a minor minus, cos my game has never crashed or freezed at important events/fights and I think that developers will solve important problems with the new patches.To those who say that the remake turned out to be bad, I can answer that it is very difficult and even wrong to compare the remake with the original (), because the original part came out more than 20 years ago and at that time people felt completely different emotions playing games. No matter what, I can never imagine a better remake of SH2 than we see now from the Bloober Team. I could go on forever about how great the Silent Hill series is. Thank you so much Konami and Bloober team for all these emotions, I am looking forward to the next remakes of SH1 and SH3!P.S. I thought that Digital soundtrack from Deluxe Edition contained more music tracks :( I hope we will get more in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are stunning, thanks to Unreal Engine 5. The way the fog rolls through the town and the sharp lighting make every dark corner feel dangerous and alive. The audio in this game is phenomenal. From the eerie soundtrack to the subtle sound effects, every sound deepens the unsettling atmosphere, making you feel like something is always watching. The controls are smooth and intuitive, which is a relief in a horror game where tense moments and quick reactions are key. Exploring the world and dealing with enemies feels natural and engaging. Even though this is my first time playing Silent Hill 2, the story had me hooked. The psychological depth and character development are incredibly well done, with twists that left me thinking long after I stopped playing. Unfortunately, the game does have frequent but not constant micro-stutters, which seem to be an issue with Unreal Engine 5. While they don’t ruin the experience, they can break immersion at times, especially in such a tense, atmospheric game. Hopefully, future patches can improve performance.Even as a first-time player, Silent Hill 2 Remake blew me away. The chilling atmosphere, compelling story, and fantastic visuals make it a must-play for any horror fan. While the frequent micro-stutters can be a bit distracting, they don't overshadow the overall gripping and intense experience. I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: : this game is an absolute triumph, a worthy remake/retelling of SH2, incredibly faithful to the tone and intent of original but with modern updates and sensibilities, extra world building and expansion of areas that were less fleshed out in the original game, and even includes the addition of some story exposition that was not present in the original game but has been discussed over the years by Team Silent, which is a wonderful touch. Bloober Team clearly made this remake with a lot of love and respect and it shows.Nearly every odd detail you can remember in the original game is preserved and retained in some form, to the point where I was absolutely delighted whenever things I remembered/expected to happen actually happened, and I was genuinely surprised when things that were not part of the original popped up, but not in a bad way. Even the original soundtrack is kept thanks to Akira Yamaoka returning with updated takes on the music you know and love; when I finally finished the game and heard Theme of Laura at the end, I was basking in the pure joy of it, and it was a bit like the feeling you get when you reconnect with a long-lost old friend you haven't heard from in years. : Silent Hill 2 has no strong ties to the other entries in the original series--it essentially can be treated as a standalone title in my estimation--so you can hop on in and enjoy one of the best if not THE best entry in the series; there's a reason why nearly every modern SH title has tried to emulate aspects of SH2, and you can experience why firsthand in a contemporary way. I highly recommend it if you've ever been curious about the series! On the other hand, if you are someone who needs to play this game with a SUNNY FOGLESS SILENT HILL(tm) mod... keep walking, this isn't the game for you. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to put into words just how much I adore this game. I am enamoured with it.If a remake can make you feel exactly how the original felt then you know it has done something right. This made me feel that way and so much more. Silent Hill 2 is a heavy game - it's nearly impossible to walk away without having felt something. To go through these emotions all over again is a privilege and a testament to just how hard Bloober team clearly worked on this title.From the get go the performances from the new actors are nothing short of stellar. The real star of the show is Luke Roberts' and his portrayal of James. His performance is one of the best I have seen in any game. His eyes and body language speak a thousand words when the dialogue offers nothing but silence. For a game laden in metaphor and interpretation, to have an actor this good takes everything to the next level. From the very start of the game right through to the end James comes across as ultimately a much more complex character than the original could ever portray.I also have to commend Salóme Gunnarsdóttir's performance, specifically as Maria. The new Maria is vastly superior to the old. So much more sinister and haunting. I'm not entirely sure how I feel about her Mary, however, as I think the original had so much more of an impact especially in her reading of the letter to James.I'm a huge fan of the gameplay side of the remake and not just for the modernisation of the combat. I played this game with the HUD completely turned off and I'm so glad I did. Nearly everything in this game is diegetic - it doesn't require HUD indicators to tell you about key pieces of information. James' jacket will become increasingly bloodied as his health lowers, and his movement animations will clearly show how close to dying he is.The audio design, which is easily some of the best I've ever heard, will tell you everything you need to know about your surroundings. Where enemies are and when they're about to attack is very clearly telegraphed in the audio. When I played the original Silent Hill 2 I couldn't believe how good the audio was, and now I think the remake has surpassed it in almost every regard.Almost. As much as it pains me to say it, the newly composed soundtrack from Akira Yamoaka is not as good as the original Silent Hill 2. A lot of the most iconic tracks have received a lot of love but ultimately lack the magic that the original score had. I also think these tracks are placed way too far back in the mix during cutscenes to make them as impactful as the original game. Music during gameplay is much better than those found in cutscenes, and the more industrial and haunted tracks are still as oppressive and impactful as they ever were.When listened to in isolation, the music does have a little something else to it. The new compositions are laced in nostalgia and a sense of longing that is perfectly fitting for a remake over 20 years after the original. Everything is almost a little sadder, a little more sombre than the original score, and it complements the remake and its overall themes and tones so well... I personally just love the original score that little bit more.I played through the entire game on Hard/Hard and I have to say the pacing felt excellent throughout. Combat often felt terrifying and the puzzles were engaging. I was a little worried puzzles would carry some of the crazy noughties puzzle logic that can be found in older games, but I'm happy to say they were absolutely fine and really enjoyable in most cases. There was very little friction despite being on the hardest difficulty, and every level of Silent Hill had really fine-tuned pacing.I'm sure I could gush forever about this remake. It's by no means perfect but it is ultimately a fantastic companion-piece to the original. The fact that there's debate about which one is better goes to show just how good this game is and how much of an impact is has already had on the franchise.I really have to commend the developers on this one. Not only did they understand what made Silent Hill 2 special, they have also understood why and how remakes can be so much more than a simple re-treading of old ground.

_childDocuments_.review: Like maybe, my faith towards Bloober wasn't there. I thought they would fail to improve on the Masterpiece that is Silent Hill 2. However to my surprise they expended the game, improved the gameplay and added 1 new boss.Pros- Expended city and exploration- Kept all the OG endings + added 2 new ones- melee combat and dodge system- Music remixes- James VA- Kept Action and Riddles difficultiesCons- Terrible performance issues (Traversal stuttering and FPS drops)- Lack of features such as (DLSS 3.5 , FSR 3.1 , Frame generation , 120/165/240/360 FPS cap , Vignette on/off , Chromatic abberation on/off)- Cutscene in 30 FPS (there's a mod that fix that however it should be there vanilla)- Born From a Wish (missing at launch)(paid DLC in the future probs)- End game is very barebone ( No hyper spray , no ranking system , no unlockable concept art / costume etc...)- Janky animations (which are never gonna get fixed)The ranking system is a big deal for me, i liked the challenge of the OG. Which award you with an OP weapon when you reach 10 stars. Could be something cool in the remake but they completely remove it and that's a huge downgrade for me.However thanks to Konami to release that masterpiece. People that trash talk the remake clearly never played the OG. Sure they censored a bit of content and some janky animations but the quality is there 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mostly great remake. Looks great. Good audio. Wonderful fog effect. But I wouldn't recommend this at its current price. Maybe $40? If you're here to relive 'the good ol days' then pay whatever you want for it, but if Silent Hill 2 is 'new' to you, maybe wait. Bloober did good with everything, except combat and game performance. Ya know, 2 of the most central things to a game. Unreal engine 5 is a trip because some games look great and play like butter, other games look great and are choppy and suffer constant hiccups. This is the latter of those two. As for combat, sheesh. Enemies constantly will break their own move sets, timers and limitations just to f**k you. Oh you've beaten enemy 'A' 100 times? Well THIS time its acid spray is going to go about 2 feet further and will have a linger effect that if you walk over the acid within 3 seconds of it being sprayed it'll hurt you, yes we know it's NEVER done that before and who knows when/if it'll happen again, we added that to randomly screw you to ensure combat is never reliable! Oh enemy 'A' missed you when you dodged? well now it'll go into laser guided missile mode, the normally slow enemy will now move at high speed following you until in a clearly locked attack animation until it gets within distance and then it complete the attack animation and it WILL hit you, we capitalized that because the decision was made when the enemy started the attack, all dodge/run abilities and capacities have be negated and damage is now assured because FuN!?If you were hoping Silent Hill 2 would come back like Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 4 or Dead Space did, I am sorry but this isn't it. It's very close, it's better than nothing. And because SIlent Hill shouldn't be allowed to die, regardless of how much Konami wants to suck at making them, it should still get your purchase because it ISN'T a bad game. It's just an imperfect game. It's a solid survival horror game, but it's combat system is whack. You'll be having a blast battling enemies one after another and then suddenly an enemy type you've beaten 100 times will suddenly just defy everything and will just suddenly do an attack instantly without a cooldown or even animation cancel out and override attack you. The game is DESPERATE to hurt you to the point of breaking its own rules. That's bad game making 101 right there. But if you here for the puzzles, exploration and horror, it's great. If you want a game thats super fun to play, try Resident Evil 2 or Dead Space (remake), because this feels like a chore to 'play'. If you want a fantastic story in a visually stunning world, well the other games I mentioned also work but this one works too.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 Remake holds the reins of the original while losing its grip in quite a few spots that, although they don't ruin the experience, hinders its enjoyment from the source material. It does a great job at recreating the environment, atmosphere and tension the original brings right down to its core. Silent Hill has never been more eerily beautiful with its blood smeared streets, pockets of puddles and abandoned, barricaded stores littering the town. The sound design is incredible with the original sounds from the strange creatures, the radio spiking in its frequency when so much as a cockroach is munching at your feet, and the exploration and discovering the neat little nods/flashbacks to the original stating "We didn't forget!". Bloober has managed to be faithful when it comes to exploration and gathering your next key item, with some slight mix-ups for puzzles and solutions thrown around that may or may not intrigue people who have played the original. But, while I want to say the game is perfect, it's not.The voice acting ranges from absolutely horrible to generally pretty good, and personally I think the fault is with the original script. Any time Maria and James are interacting with each other, it feels fake. The original has very cheesy, borderline terrible voice acting that managed to be very charming for the time. Trying to replicate that in 2024 sounds bad, real bad. It isn't natural, it feels like they're reading directly from a paper in front of them and it manages to make me cringe at how off it feels. But, shortly after the initial meet-up, you're thrown into a brand spanking new cutscene of Maria talking about letting yourself be loose as you enter Heaven's Night. It's entirely new dialogue with nothing to go off on, and it shows. It's clear, its showing emotion, exploring Maria's character as this sexy, easy going personality that will stop at nothing to gaslight you into paying attention to her more. It feels as manipulative as the original without needing to copy her and I love it. But it's a "damned if you do, damned if you don't" scenario. Change it too much and people will whine its not like the original. Keep it the same and people will question why you should get it in the first place, and that feels like a lot of what the remake is. They played it fairly safe without changing the story beats but adding new ones in to try and squeeze a bit more out of the little time you already get from existing characters without it being too overwhelming. I adored those cutscenes when they came on [even though I think the casting of the characters were a little off], and I wish they showed off more considering how much longer the game overall feels. Combat is another damned if you do. The original had some terrible combat issues with it being too basic. Swing, swing, swing, stomp. Shoot, shoot, shoot, stomp. It got the job done and allowed you to explore with ease aside from key bossfights. The remake improves on it, but not enough. Adding active dodge frames, meatier hits, and aggressive enemies, even more so if you're in the Otherworld, are great additions. But throwing in almost quadruple the enemies, multiple at once in tight corridors or rooms can feel like a hectic mess. I was shocked when I was in the middle of the apartment building and already achieved a trophy to kill 75 enemies with melee. That's nearly as much as an average player will kill in the original in less than 3-4 hours! To me it feels like padding in some areas when you walk into an area with corpses, only to grab an item and have them revive and sometimes be forced to combat them. Nothing in the game was overall hard, as the dodge gives so many iframes it's difficult to be whacked the second you learn a pattern. Most of my injuries were the Mannequin Legs creeping around corners or beside items that I was too impatient to notice before grabbing said item. The combat became too rock-paper-scissors too fast for me personally, as most enemies followed the same patterns the next time you fight them. Swing, swing, swing, dodge, dodge, dodge, swing, swing, stomp. It boiled down to being too basic too fast, but Silent Hill never had good combat to begin with. I'm not sure if I prefer the original or the remake's combat, but they've done their best and I suppose that's all I can ask.Bossfights may have gotten the biggest improvement over the original, though! Pyramid Head is as slow and deadly as ever, Flesh Lip breaking out of his rustic bedframes to use them as appendages was a real shock, and the rest of the bosses continued to surprise me in ways I was pleasantly okay with. It's hard to get into too much detail without spoiling them, but I'm happy with the direction they took.Overall, the remake doesn't replace the original for me. The original has better voice acting, heart wrenching moments that do a great job at making you sob, something that the remake doesn't. The reading of the entire letter, James & Maria's separation, James' frustration at doctors being unable to cure his wife. The emotions are raw, heartfelt and very real emotions people in these situations. The helplessness and loneliness of sadness and impending doom. They managed to fail at these parts heavily but created new ones that I think will stick with me regardless. The remaster has better exploration, the graphics are superb and the sound design is something I haven't heard in a game yet, and it's gorgeous. They're both good games on their own, and I'm happy to be wrong about this game. The second I saw Bloober's name to be revealed as the lead developer on the project, I was a cynical person. But they proved that once in a blue moon, they can make a good game.And obviously, Akira Yamaoka ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocked the show. Absolute legend.

_childDocuments_.review: i was extremely excited for this game when i first herd about it about a year ago so i bought it hoping it was going t be amazing and it is in some areas but falls flat in others, lets start with the positives PROS:-Graphic are amazing and look great (but that's not something unusual for an UR5 game)-the story is great and very immersive (not something the should be unexpected for a remake of a game already wildly loved)-the puzzles in the game are excellent and take me back to the classic horror games from the early days-i love the new behind the shoulder camera view, defiantly the best update of the game -the voice acting is defiantly a huge improvement compared to the original with most of the dialog unchanged seeminglyCONS:performance of the game is not optimized at all. I have a RYZEN 7 7800X3D and a RTX 4080 SUPER and even running on DLSS i am getting a lot of stutters and frame drops -the cut-scenes seem to be locked at 30 FPS and sill have stuttering as well, I've looked in the settings but cant find anything to change the cut-scenes frame rate-The melee animations bot look and feel bad, even from the game play footage i always taught the melee animations looked weird (especially when swinging at the ground) but is also does not feel great in game-character facial expressions seem flat and sometimes emotionless (this one might just be my opinion)-weird shadow/lighting, when you shine your flash lite on objects like bats or hand rails the shadows look really weird, like the are floating in the air rather than actual projecting to the walls or objects behind them.most of the negatives can defiantly be fixed in a patch, but these are just some of the things I've noticed in my play time so far. Im going to continue playing it since i already spent $87 on it, but i defiantly wish i waited for reviews and for them to fix a lot of these issues before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Early development footage and trailers didn't do this game justice as to what we finally ended up receiving!Though I still think it was the right choice holding off till release I have nothing but respect for Bloober and still very little towards Konami (Haha....)The gameplay is quite intense, James has little room for error in combat even on the Standard difficulty as he can only make a few mistakes before succumbing to his injury's.James is not a Action Hero or Super Cop like the protagonists from the Resident Evil series.He is as Human and Fragile as the person behind the screen is controlling him.With practice and good decision making he can become formidable.Exploration has become a lot more open ended if you find yourself being strained during fights. A fair amount of health and ammo can be found if you take the time and look for the details of whichever environment you find yourself inThe game itself is gorgeous and really adds to the immersion besides the occasional stutter (Bloober pls fix.)The remake is not one for one as many of the different scenarios/puzzles have been changed or replaced. Some of the old puzzles are left as references and easter eggs and the new additions are lovely and will make it a fun return for both new and old players entering the town.New voice actors deliver an amazing performance and some of the dialogue has been rewritten to either flesh out some of the characters which I personally see as a positive making me either like or understand them better Never thought we would ever see a Silent hill game again let alone a good one.Definitely worth checking out,Now let's see some more, Yeah?

_childDocuments_.review: Very different start than the original game.  Combat style is different.  Now can break open windows to get places.  Almost an entirely new game, definitely will not be disappointed if you're a fan of the 2001 Silent Hill 2.[Update] After playing through 3/4th of the game it is a very new experience from the original.  Songs are updated versions from the original soundtrack, which only consists of 10 songs from the original 30.  Story is pretty similar but maps are much different from what I remember.  Brookhaven was a completely different experience with a few similar events.Things I do not like so far:1. Character faces, like James for example looks as if he now has a bowl cut.  Script modifications are not bad but the acting is.  2. A big part of combat is now finding the hidden leg monsters and shooting them before they start moving.  Also dodging is annoying because you sometimes have to dodge twice in a row not to get hit.  You get three melee attacks and if you do not knock the enemy onto the ground with the third, you're guaranteed to take damage.3. Using a controller has been very awkward, it feels like the game was meant to be played as an FPS using AWSD style.  Combat using a controller has been especially awkward when switching guns.4.  Soundtrack only has 10 songs out of the original 30.  No "Theme of Laura" which was like the main song from the original game?

_childDocuments_.review: (spoiler free!!)This remake stays entirely true to the spirit of the original, changing things very minimally, and adding so much fun to the overall experience. Many smaller moments have changed from the original 2001 release in a way that is extremely satisfying - often I found that my instincts and memories of the original game were used against me, tripping me up and leading me to scare myself just a little extra! This was never done in a malicious way though, rather, any time that happens, it feels respectful and loving. After continually getting burned by more recent releases from this series, I didn't know it was possible to feel this amount of love for Silent Hill from the new games, nor did I really expect to feel like Silent Hill was BACK in full force.My first playthrough clocked in at around 19 hours - I spent a lot of time exploring VERY thoroughly. My efforts to leave no stone unturned truly felt rewarding - I'd often find small notes and helpful items tucked away, or even just little environmental things I appreciated seeing. The puzzles were all beautiful and satisfying, with just the right amount of difficulty - I can't wait to complete my first new game + on hard riddle difficulty! The combat is genuinely fun - several enemies that I would previously write off or ignore in my many playthroughs of the original game are now an actual legitimate threat that you cannot ignore, and yet it is SO satisfying to kill them now. Mannequins especially I have a new love for after playing this game - they're the perfect mix of being able to actually jump you and mess you up, but also being kind of charmingly goofy if you happen to spot one before it spots you.The pacing of the game, although longer than the original, does not feel like a slog, or like I'm being forced to do things that aren't enjoyable or necessary for the story. I really and truly enjoyed every moment spent in each location, and I cannot wait to finish enough playthroughs that this becomes as much of a comfort to me as the original 2001 release.I am endlessly thankful that Bloober Team was able to take criticisms of the writing from The Medium especially, and handle the stories of the characters in this game in such a profoundly touching and respectful way. They really knocked it out of the park. Additionally, Akira Yamaoka's music is incredible through and through (always has been, but WOW. I cannot stress enough how well the soundtrack highlights the game.)Although on release, there are minor issues with stuttering, I have not personally experienced anything that truly affected my enjoyment of the game overall. I wholeheartedly recommend playing as soon as you can! I may be just slightly biased though, because Silent Hill 2 is my all time favorite game. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is, without a doubt, the best game I have ever played. A breathtaking and disturbing horror spectacle, Silent Hill 2 is a masterclass in storytelling, atmosphere, and design. I simply cannot overstate how incredible the sound design, world-building, and character and monster design are. Every element works together to create an unforgettable experience.The story is utterly captivating, and I genuinely grew to care for all the characters with my whole heart. I’ve never played a game like this before—one that kept me on edge, scared and nervous almost the entire time. For the first time in any game, I found myself eagerly reading all the notes and books I stumbled upon, desperate to figure out what I had gotten myself into and to uncover every possible detail about the world and story.Visually, the game is simply stunning. Whether it's the eerie, fog-filled streets or the oppressive interiors, the level of graphical achievement is nothing short of phenomenal. I regret not playing the original, but after this experience, I feel like I’ve made up for lost time. Now, I’m even more motivated to explore every corner of this world and fully 100% the game.I’m dying to uncover all the endings, and even with my ADHD, I refuse to spoil them by watching videos. I want to experience everything firsthand.In short, this is a truly magnificent game. It easily earns an 11/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Against all odds, this is a fantastic remake, and should easily satisfy even the most pessimistic fans of the original.That said, it's not without its flaws.Like many others, I wasn’t completely sold on the remake initially. Even though I’ve enjoyed Bloober Team’s past works for the most part, remaking such an iconic game is no easy feat, especially for a studio that, whether you like their games or not, has a lot to prove. Judging by the trailers, it was easy to conclude that Bloober managed to nail the atmosphere and visual side of the remake, but many others questions were yet to be answered. Especially considering the trailers seemed to sell the game as more combat-focused compared to the original—combat which, in the trailers, didn't look particularly good.The good news is that the combat is solid, but there’s definitely room for debate regarding how much of it there is. On one hand, the combat is enjoyable, and the enemy AI is one of the highlights of the remake. Some enemy behaviors are so beautifully unhinged that they made me smirk several times. Because of this, enemy encounters kept me on my toes, never knowing what would happen next. However, the sheer amount of enemy encounters is definitely excessive. I think even the atmosphere of the game would benefit from reducing the sheer amount of encounters.Of course, translating a game over two decades old to modern mechanics and control schemes is no easy task, and it comes with both upsides and downsides. As a survival horror game, it struggles in some key areas. The biggest issue is that there’s simply too much medical supplies, and on normal difficulty, the game is simply not well-balanced. I finished the game with over 60 medical items, the medical items are so plentiful that it detracts from the survival aspect. By the end of the game, your character feels like a living incarnation of a medical basement. The same can be said about ammo. While not as excessively easy to come by as medical supplies, there’s still too much, which again hurts the survival aspect of the game.This sadly isnt helped by the fact that the game is easy.  I didn’t die a single time during my playthrough, and I doubt many others will either. Even when caught off-guard by bunch of enemies, the game gives you plenty of space and opportunities to heal. So, while the general gameplay is fun and dynamic, the survival horror elements leave much to be desired.The second biggest issue is the performance, which is absolutely horrendous. The base performance wouldn’t be as much of a problem if it weren’t for the constant stuttering. It’s everywhere, all the time, to the point that I would classify some sections as nearly unplayable. It was so bad I had to take breaks twice because the stuttering was downright nauseating.The final criticism I have is the soundtrack. Despite being composed by Akira Yamaoka again, I felt the music was a downgrade overall. Some of the changes made to the tracks felt unnecessary and seemed to be different for the sake of being different.Thankfully, nearly all other aspects of the game hit the mark. The atmosphere is top-notch, and the general vibe is on par with the original. The characters and mood recapture the uncanny feel of the original quite well. The graphical presentation, especially in terms of the environment, is phenomenal, though some character models could use slight improvements.The puzzles strike a great balance—they’re not so easy as to feel trivial, but not so difficult that you’ll need to look up solutions on YouTube. I also think the changes made to the environment and puzzles were, in most cases, the right call.The biggest improvement, without a doubt, is the boss fights. We all know the combat in the original was pretty bad by all accounts, and the bosses were somehow even worse. So, it’s hard to overstate just how big of an improvement these are, especially considering the low bar set by the original. Each boss fight is actually good now, and some changes even make more sense from a story perspective. It would be shame to spoil any of these encounters, but they are great.The audio design is also very good, all sorts of sounds, creaks, screams will accompany your journey all the way through, but its bit of a shame that if you have good headphones the direction of the audio occasionally doesnt correspond the actual direction properly, but not a huge issue on its own.Lastly, I have to praise the developers for their incredible attention to detail when it comes to the original. Even some of the more obscure events and elements were included in the remake, things I never expected to see again. It's clear this project was made by people who deeply care about the original, and I couldn’t be happier.Overall, it's one of the best horror games in ages. Whether you've played the original or not, if you're a fan of horror games, this is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute masterpiece. From the story, acting, music, to the gameplay—it’s all perfect. As a huge fan of the original it's clear from playing this game that Bloober Team truly understood Team Silent’s vision. there is so much passion put into this game it makes me want to cry. It was so important that Bloober team got this remake right to bring Silent Hill 2’s story and characters to a new generation of gamers, and I genuinely believe they did it justice.The original will always hold its own, but this remake captures everything that made the original so so amazing and brings it to the modern age.This is horror done right. I’ve played horror games for years, to the point where I’m desensitised to gore, jump scares, and un-killable enemies, but the Silent Hill 2 remake had me jumping out of my chair at several points and each time it was unscripted, regular gameplay. The enemies are soo creepy and unsettling that you always feel on edge when you know they are nearby. Never have I felt so tense playing a game. For the best experience, I highly recommend playing on hard mode.The sounds and music in this game is just the chef's kiss that really brings everything together and make this game the masterpiece it is. From calming and melancholy to down right hostile, the sound design in this game deserves it's own separate review.The story telling is on point but you really have to read between the lines to understand what's happening. New players are going to finish the game with a lot of questions, but once you do some digging and read up on everything, upon a second play-through you will pick up on so may little details you missed the first time. Whether it's the placement of items, the symbolism behind the monsters or even just noticing subtle shifts in the characters movements and facial expressions when talking with each other, once it all comes together you will be blown away (and likely chronically depressed). subtlety is lost in a lot of horror these days with the monsters and mystery getting explained to the viewer but with this game, all the information you need hidden in plain sight for you to figure out and interpret yourself. This game touches on some very heavy themes but handles them with a lot of care. Does a perfect remake exist? Yes. It's this. It took me 35 hours to complete one play through because I just kept stopping to soak in the atmosphere and sounds of this beautifully bleak and sombre town. I hope this remake inspires and moves people for the next 20 years, just as the original did for me. It’s a 10/10 experience and a must play game for lovers or horror.

_childDocuments_.review: The very art director and creature designer from the original Silent Hill didn't want this to exist.That was what set the alarms off for me. I agree with him, I wish Konami would let this franchise alone already before making it worse, but we now have this remake (something that never happens in this day and age). Those saying it is faithful are either paid actors or lying through their teeth willingly.Puzzles. It becomes a chore. Solving it/finding a key does not feel good after 7 hours straight of doing the same thing over and over again. I was an avid horror fan in my teens so I have plenty of experience with horror games using puzzles as a resort to fill a very very short story. But this is simply excessive.The 'horror' aspect died, if it even lived, extremely quickly for me. The scenarios don't look all that scary when you can't see anything because it's just so dark and the flashlight is quite the mandatory standard for a horror game: small ball of light barely shining. It suffers from using realistic graphics, the old ones added to the feeling of being in the 'wrong place'. By now, we've seen this type of otherworldy places ad nauseam and somehow, they feel far more underwhelming than I expected for being used to it. It is rare when you find yourself with more than one monster and you can still manage to defeat them without issue. In that term, yes, it is faithful; But if they keep throwing enemies at you, one by one with a combat system that has swift movements and no fatigue, it just has no effect. This remains true for a very large portion of the game, which allows you to save bullets and become Terminator when you do encounter larger groups of enemies. As per the sound aspect, then again, I find no outstanding features about it. The noises and ambient music only become obnoxious when they constantly loop; They're not a 'surprise' as in the original and they don't have that awful screeching noise that pierces your eardrums (yes, I'm saying it's good that the original gives me headaches). The enemies whose only purpose is to jumpscare you are easily noticed due to the modern camera and bright color, to which must be mentioned that the ''looking at objects of interest'' feature from the original becomes useless. James' head always moves when you move the camera, so it's very easy to miss when he is actually looking at something. Most objects are at eye level anyway.Almost every door can be opened or find your way inside. Plenty of rooms are useless too, only two bullets or a drink waiting for you.I already despised the OG's story, so I can't talk much about that. Good ol' ''Something happens to a woman, how does the closest man to her feel about it?''. Don't even make me mention Angela. Horror writers stop writing about men hurting women challenge. I'm utterly convinced that if James was a woman and Eddie had Angela's backstory, people wouldn't praise it as much.Still, it is to be noted that the character's personalities are extremely watered down in the remake. Plenty of good dialogue has been modified or completely cut out. Do NOT expect the same camera angles, you'll be deeply disappointed. Basically, they took a piece of passion and turned it into a product that could be easily digested by the masses instead of finding its own niche like it did 23 years ago.More changes, the one that pisses me off the most: Pyramid Head's first battle. In the original, the Otherworld is build up very slowly. Weird stuff in toilets, water on the hallways' floor, etc. In the remake, it's quite black and white, the apartments do suffer a very noticeable change. When you first defeat Pyramid Head, he goes underwater and it gets drained. You know, a fantastic parallel to that one ending? Yeah, it's gone. The water theme is misunderstood to the point of making me wonder what this team was thinking when changing so many crucial points.Weird object combinations (strand of hair + bent needle) are gone.No 'Born From A Wish' scenario. Can't say I didn't expect this.I will now mention what I did enjoy: The combat system is easy to learn, the dodge button is the same as Resident Evil Revelations 2 (controller) so whoever played it will be thankful. I have my own button mapping for Resident Evil 4 for speedrunning and the running button is also the same so, basically, the controls are perfect for me. Toluca prison has been my favorite part. No boring, repetitive puzzles with clues hidden in documents; You build your way out by slowly advancing. Good stuff.Overall, I do not like it and the replay value is close to none for me, especially due to the excruciating first eight hours having explored every corner. My main issue is that it feels like a completely pointless game. They couldn't expand on the story (lacking the original creative minds and Masahiro Ito probably didn't want to do add to it either) so the extra hours are merely white noise between cinematics you already know, but... honestly, worse. The lightning in that iconic Maria scene (''Don't you want to touch me?'') doesn't hit the same. Lacks contrast. Plenty of elements are absent which decreases the feeling it's trying to convey. It explains the 'creative differences' between Ito and Blubber.If I want to experience this story again, I'll simply boot up my ps2 to play the far superior version with the side scenario. And I'm gonna say it: The acting in the remake is awful. My recommendation is not to buy it and let Konami rot with their greediness and disrespect to what should've been a good trilogy, the way the original team wanted, and nothing else.

_childDocuments_.review: Even 2 years after the first Silent Hill Transmission it still feels surreal that this game even exists. Not only is this a return to the Silent Hill franchise that Konami has left dormant since that god awful HD collection and the tragedy that was the cancellation of Silent Hills and its subsequent de-listing of PT, but it's a remake to arguably the best entry in the series. And if that wasn't enough, it's a remake made by Bloober team of all studios, which they have had a tenuous track record of releases. So how is it that in spite of all the odds, Silent Hill 2 Remake is not only a good horror game, but an incredible remake that succeeds in nearly every category? So first, how is the game itself, just based on its own merits outside the original? Well unsurprisingly it feels pretty modern, yet familiar if you've played the classics from this genre. It's a third person OTS action game with an emphasis on exploration, combat, and puzzle solving. The game is split up into multiple indoor areas you will be exploring, not unlike dungeons in Zelda, and the town of Silent Hill acts as the hub area which connects them all together. Each dungeon-like area will consist of exploration and puzzle solving, with a good amount of combat thrown in, but they will also contain cutscenes which progress the story. Some of these areas will even cap off with a boss fight at the end, which strengthens the Zelda dungeon comparison. Since this is a survival horror game, exploration is a necessity since most of the the health items and ammo you find lying around is hidden off the beaten path. Outside a couple of boss battles however, I never found myself too low on ammo and health, and its abundance did hurt some of the tension this game otherwise builds up very well. Puzzles are another core pillar of the experience, and I'm happy to say they're well designed and hold up to past entries. Many of them did challenge me to think outside the box, but I never found them too obtuse, and that's a very fine line to tread so I respect the effort the designers put into them. Then, there's combat. And let me say this one surprised me. Horror games in the past have had a reputation of poor combat systems since they were never integral to the experience, and I went into this game expecting no different. But that's not the case here, the combat in Silent Hill 2 Remake is surprisingly fun! It's not as polished as something from a AAA game, there's still some jank. But even after 16 hours in I never found combat boring, and that's thanks to the newly introduced dodge mechanic. James can now dodge enemy attacks like he's in a souls game, and enemies will telegraph their attacks, while also keeping their patterns varied. There's a real skill curve to the combat, and over the course of the game I got better at consistently avoiding taking hits. I jived so much with the combat that unless I was low on health I always chose to confront most enemies instead of avoiding them. You might argue this clashes with the intent of a horror game being to make you feel vulnerable, but the Silent Hill series always relied on its atmosphere to scare you instead of trying to overwhelm you with enemies. It's roughly twice as long as the 2001 original and while that might be a good thing for most players, the third act of the game starts to lose some of its momentum, though not to the extent where I felt it was outstaying its welcome. Story is as strong as the original, and it is for the most part pretty faithful. You take control of James Sunderland who returns to Silent Hill after receiving a letter from his wife, Mary, to come meet him there. Not too unusual, until you account for the fact that James's wife has been dead for 3 years, and you're here to find out if she's really alive and waiting for you. Along your journey you will encounter other characters who were "called" to Silent Hill, each for their own reasons. Silent Hill 2 doesn't shy away from challenging topics like abuse, suicide, depression, and mental illness, and I find it handles them quite tastefully while also never being too explicit about it. This game hides its themes behind a heavy use of metaphors just like the original, and it's largely this reason the 2001 game has endured such a strong legacy as a cult classic in survival horror. The remake respects the source material in this regard, but never plays it too safe, and isn't afraid to take slight artistic liberties in its character designs. Slight spoiler ahead, but there's even a scene showing an interaction between Maria and James at Heaven's Night, which is wholly original to this remake. The interaction is not just a bit of fan service showing us a more intimate interaction between James and Maria which we haven't seen in the original, but it also serves as a bit of character development for James. I want to avoid specifics, but if you've already watched the scene you'll know what I'm talking about. Overall, Silent Hill 2 is a strong remake and a great Silent Hill game that is faithful to the original, but also isn't afraid to modernize the parts that aged and expanding on what worked. Bloober team obliterated everyone's expectations through what I could only internally rationalize as them making some kind of deal with the devil, and I guess that's at least partly true since Konami did publish them. We know more Silent Hill is coming down the pipeline, whether those titles come to fruition or live up to even half the quality of the remake is impossible to determine now. What I can say for sure is that we finally have Silent Hill 2 Remake, and if that's all we ever get, then as a longtime Silent Hill fan who's been burned by high expectations for years, it was well worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: The Silent Hill 2 Remake is a masterpiece that brings new life to one of the most revered horror games of all time. The developers have done an incredible job of preserving the original’s haunting atmosphere while updating it with modern graphics, sound, and mechanics that make it feel fresh and immersive.From the moment the game begins, you’re enveloped in an eerie, oppressive ambiance that pulls you right back into the desolate, fog-laden streets of Silent Hill. The visual overhaul is breathtaking: the enhanced graphics allow for more detailed environments, nuanced lighting, and shadows that add a layer of realism and dread to every location. The infamous fog has been beautifully reworked, making every encounter feel as though it could hide something terrible just out of sight. The audio is equally mesmerizing—Akira Yamaoka's score has been re-recorded with a modern polish that retains the original’s haunting melodies but feels even more resonant and chilling.One of the standout elements of this remake is the character work. James Sunderland’s story remains as psychologically complex and tragic as ever, but the updated facial animations and voice acting add new depth to his emotions, allowing players to feel more connected to his journey through guilt and grief. The other characters, too, are portrayed with an intensity that makes every interaction impactful and every storyline twist hit harder.Gameplay mechanics have been modernized in a way that respects the original game’s pacing and challenges but feels smoother and more accessible to new players. Combat has been refined, making it more responsive without sacrificing the tension and vulnerability that make the encounters so terrifying. It’s still more about survival than action, and every enemy feels like a genuine threat, especially with the enhanced AI and disturbing redesigns of classic monsters like the unsettlingly iconic Pyramid Head.Silent Hill 2 Remake is a love letter to fans of the original and a perfect entry point for newcomers to experience one of horror gaming’s greatest stories. It’s atmospheric, deeply emotional, and terrifying in all the best ways—a testament to what a remake should be. It’s hard to imagine a more respectful and effective update, and it firmly establishes Silent Hill 2 as a timeless piece of horror history. This is survival horror at its very finest.Thank you so much!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a new player reading this and you're interested in playing the older Silent Hill games: DO IT. There's a post on the /r/silenthill subreddit on the best ways to play the old games (you'll find it through Google easily). This remake is really good, but it lacks some of the essence of what made the original game special. It's not necessarily the developer's fault - the OG Silent Hill 2 is the definition of lightning in a bottle. It was a product of it's (technical) limitations at the time and that's part of what makes it so charming. The ending performance of Monica Taylor Horgan (Mary/Maria) alone is a big reason to play the original. That's why I advise you to experience the original game(s) first hand. This remake doesn't replace the original Silent Hill 2 - they both co-exist with another.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh. I kind of feel like ♥♥♥♥.It might have to do with the fact that I pounded energy drinks until 4:00 so I could finish this game. I couldn’t help it, though: I had to see this thing through.I forgot how much I  . I mean, a lot of the early games in the series hold a place in my heart. But it was  that I obsessed over. I loved recounting the story for people who would never be able to stomach actually playing the damned thing. I even used to have a plot analysis I printed off from GameFAQs that moved with me from state to state. So, even when I couldn’t access my PS2 to play the actual game, I could read over the plot analysis. I’d steep myself in the plot beats, sinister twists, secret endings, fan theories, source materials… Like tonguing a sore tooth, I’d find some ill-begotten solace in this.Because that’s kind of what  does, isn’t it? It gets caught under the player’s skin like a shard of glass that breaks off and is impossible to remove without digging. It is synonymous with illness and ending. Lust and corruption. Terror and beyond.Yeah. I feel like ♥♥♥♥. But I’m happy to feel this way again.We old folks were cursed to look on in horror as Konami degenerated into a pile of dog puke in the 2010s. And, though I’m less familiar with the circumstances, I know Bloober Team has had their share of issues as well. So, when the  project was announced, it was met with much gnashing of teeth. Konami had already bungled a remaster of the game in the years before the announcement, so there were very few people who had any faith in this project. The players had every right to feel this way; the original  is, without exaggerating, a cornerstone of horror (not just in games but in the genre ) and every attempt to recreate the magic of the original game has fallen on its face.But, somehow Konami and Bloober Team have found a way to hit that vein again. Even as a guy who just wanted to replay  after all these years and had my fingers crossed that it would be good the entire time, I’m floored by what I just experienced.They’ve managed to capture the feel of playing the original game while modernizing everything about it. The oppressive atmosphere always keeps the player on edge – even with updated combat mechanics, there is no guarantee of safety here. Every staircase, every room, every corner is an opportunity for Silent Hill to strike at the player. Whether it’s an enemy waiting for James behind a cardboard box so it can spring out like a trap or the environment suddenly, inexplicably collapsing further in on itself like a singularity, this is a long, crushing trek through a world that hates you and wants to see you suffer… just like it’s supposed to be.All of the ingredients that made the original stand tall like a looming behemoth are here. The sound design was the first thing that caught my attention. I think it says something that the music that plays as James first explores Silent Hill got my heart racing and set me on edge. It’s that beautiful dissonance of exploring a quiet, misty town while discordant music thunders through the speakers, landing squarely in the player’s gut. Skittering that makes the skin itch, crashes from nowhere and everywhere, mumbling voices when no one’s in the room with you. It’s all here and it’s all perfect.And every character has as much punch as they did in the original. Or, dare I say, even more so: I don’t remember Eddie making my skin crawl as much in 2001 as he did in 2024. Some of it is his model, sure; his constant sheen of sweat makes him appear unwell and gives the player the impression that he reeks of something putrid. But it’s his pointed taunting and teasing that truly seeps into the player. And they completely nailed Angela’s transformation. As the story progresses and her dreamlike dissociation begins to peel back, her cold defensiveness comes forward. The tables turn: she’s no longer trapped in a room with James, James is trapped in a room with her. And the player feels it.One of the things that had people worried before the game’s release was the combat. PlayStation released a “combat reveal” trailer that sent a lot of people flocking to their keyboards to share their outrage that Konami and Bloober Team turned the main character into a monster-killing-machine. You see, the combat in the original  intentionally felt awful. James isn’t a trained soldier – he’s a guy who finds a two-by-four on the ground and is using it to survive. But fears about this aspect of the game turned out to be unfounded; every encounter has the potential to be the last one if the player is caught off guard. A little more fluidity helps ease things along without making the monsters feel like cannon fodder.Of course, the story is one of the game’s greatest strengths and much of it remains untouched here. None of the minor changes made in this version detracted from the story whatsoever. The one thing that might be missed that is tangentially related to the story is the original’s fixed camera perspective. The over-the-shoulder camera in the remake works great, but the exemplary camera direction is now mostly limited to cutscenes. It’s unfortunate, but it’s a necessary change.I don’t count it as a negative, but this game is  compared to other modern horror games. Considering the price of admission, I didn’t mind the extended playtime at all. On top of that, I think it was handled extremely well. In the original  games, it felt like at least half of the doors the player came across were locked with no way to unlock them. In the remake, however, a lot of those locked doors are now unlockable from the other side. This means that, as the player progresses through the environments, they are opening shortcuts they can use when they need to backtrack later on. What starts as a meandering trek through the hospital (or wherever) turns into quickly zipping from place to place to solve puzzles as the level progresses.Honestly, I think the length of the game adds to the oppressive feeling of the environment itself. Sometimes it feels like it’s never going to end… and I think that’s the point. You, the player, begin to lose hope that you’ll ever find refuge, right alongside James.That neatly brings me to the most important question anyone should be asking: is the game scary? And, um, yeah, it scared the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. There are multiple parts that are going to linger in my mind for far longer than is healthy. Without getting into spoilers, there is a scenario at the beginning of the Labyrinth that had my pulse pounding and left me short of breath. The final stage was so eerie that it ruined the color yellow for me. And scouring the desolate locations around the town felt so realistic that it reminded me of the times years ago when I explored abandoned buildings and retroactively made my memories scarier. This game is just as devastating as the 2001 version, if not more so. not only managed to retain the feel of late-90s/early-2000s survival horror games while bringing it up to current standards, but it also managed to dredge up the feelings of true terror that, I think, only comes from horror games. So, yeah, I recommend this game. I recommend it so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard. It quickly and handily became my Game of the Year. However: if you’re thinking about pulling the trigger on this one, keep in mind that this game is not fun. It’s not supposed to be. If you don’t like the idea of being subjected to pervasive, creeping dread that will slowly burrow into you until your insides feel wrong and your own skin doesn’t feel right on your body anymore… maybe skip it? It might make you feel like ♥♥♥♥. But, if you’re like me and you’re chasing that feeling, buy it right now. Do not hesitate. Jump down the hole.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must buy.For new players, a modernized retelling of one of gaming’s most mature, tragic, and symbolic stories. For experienced players, a love letter that is made by a team that clearly respects this game and worked hard to work in little Easter eggs and moments that make you DiCaprio point at the screen.Atmosphere, sound, graphics, gameplay. All superb. Areas and puzzles expanded in clever ways that mostly work.My recommendation: take your time. Try to absorb everything you can because a lot of the presentation is about the finer details. In my playthrough, my sprint button was dusty because I never touched it. I just walked and soaked in the first experience. If you play Iike I did, you should get about 20 hours worth of gameplay. And that’s only for one ending out of 8.Warning: this game does have heavy topics that may affect some people with different life experiences. That is part of the ethos of the game, but it handles it with deft.Bloober team also made some changes that paint some characters and their actions different. For long time fans, they will either love these changes or completely disagree. However, the beauty is that different people with agree or disagree with different changes, which leaves room for different interpretations and perspectives.One point to be aware of. This is not a criticism, but just something to be aware of. Unreal 5 is taxing for systems. So don’t be surprised if in some areas outdoors you started chugging with lower spec hardware. Cap at 30-40 FPS and you should be fine.Lastly, for my Steam deck brethren, don’t be put off by the “Unsupported” rating. It works absolutely fine for me, similar to how Black myth Wukong works. Just cap your fps to 30, low graphics settings, and your good to go 👍 Silent Hill is waiting for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 has always been more than just a game to me; it's a journey I’ve walked for over a decade, through foggy streets and broken souls. Today, stepping into the town again with this remake, I’m utterly stunned. The gameplay is this magical blend of the clunkiness we loved from the PS2 era, that gritty, raw feeling of survival horror, but with the modern fluidity of over-the-shoulder mechanics. It's nostalgic yet refined, capturing the soul of the original while giving me new ways to experience it. Every angle, every corner of the town I loved feels alive with details I never knew I craved, details that scream ‘this was made by fans, for fans.’I’ll admit it, when Blobber Team was announced as the ones driving the remake, I was skeptical, reactive even. Silent Hill 2 isn’t just a game to me; it shaped my entire career. This was the game that pushed me towards the creative path I walk today. The soundtrack? It was the reason I picked up a guitar in the first place, the melodies echoing through the highs and lows of my life. The idea of someone else touching something so sacred? It felt wrong. But damn, was I wrong.Blobber has surpassed even my highest expectations. Every scene, every bit of atmosphere they’ve crafted feels like a love letter to the original, but amplified. The tension, the dread, and most of all, the emotions, they’re all there, but with an even sharper edge.Yes, there are some micro stutters here and there, but they haven’t broken my immersion one bit. The way they’ve handled the new dialogues? It’s like meeting old friends again, but now they’re flesh and blood, living and breathing in ways they never quite did in my memory. And while Silent Hill is, of course, a horror game, this remake has reminded me just how much drama and melancholy it carries. The sadness, the deep, somber tones of the original—it’s all back, only somehow… better.Silent Hill 2 isn’t just horror—it’s heartbreak, it’s grief, it’s the human condition, and Blobber Team captured it perfectly. If you loved the original, prepare to fall in love all over again.Our franchise is back, waiting for you, in our "special place".Welcome back to Silent Hill.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exceptional remake, Bloober absolutely knocked it out of the park with this. There were 2 main things I had gripes with on the original, the combat was boring and the acting was just not good. This remake improves on these two things exponentially. Combat actually takes thought now instead of 'see enemy, aim gun, spam button to shoot until they drop, stomp'. Well-timed dodges are your saving grace, but it's not to the level of the enemies throwing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ combos with 30 attacks like it's Dark Souls. Enemies also seem to learn from how you fight, so you're encouraged to mix things up which I like. The boss fights are also significantly better, overall the combat is just a massive step up from the original.Another thing that's a massive step up from the original, the acting. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the acting in the original was bad. It's been improved in every single way, the line delivery, the mocap, everything. The story feels so much more impactful when the characters actually feel believable.I only really have 2 issues with this remake: the performance and the mouse input. The performance is just not good. I have a 5800x3d, a 4070, and 48GB of RAM and dropping to 40-60 FPS was not uncommon. It's definitely more difficult to stay immersed when I go from ~100 FPS to suddenly being at 50 FPS during a boss fight. Hoping this gets improved with updates though. The mouse input also feels.. not great. It feels like it's just emulating a joystick, and can sometimes make hitting shots on up-close enemies a lot harder than it should be. Not a massive issue, but still something i'd like to see fixed.Overall, if you enjoyed the original or want to get into Silent Hill 2 in general, just play this version. I genuinely believe it's an improvement over the original in pretty much every single way, the only reason I would recommend playing the original is so you can see the changes they did in the remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Superb adaptation. Takes everything that made the original game great and expands and improves on it in every way possible. As much as I love this game, however, I must add a word of caution: If you are considering getting this game and you are someone who has experienced abuse or tragedy, be forewarned that this game pushes some pretty deep emotional buttons and will take you down some pretty dark psychological paths that you may not be ready to go. _childDocuments_.review: First off, I must admit I had serious doubts about this remake, much like many other longtime fans of the series. I couldn't imagine Bloober Team successfully handling such a monumental title. I've always held the first three Silent Hill games close to my heart, with Silent Hill 2 standing out as the best of the trilogy.The Silent Hill 2 remake by Bloober Team delivers an impressive take on James, with his character design and voice acting standing out as exceptional. The game's visual fidelity is stunning, bringing the eerie world of Silent Hill to life in ways that surpass expectations. Akira Yamaoka's music and sound design are masterful, once again creating a haunting atmosphere reminiscent of the 2001 original. Though the fog isn't quite on par with the original, I personally found it to be far better than anticipated and a great addition to the remake’s overall atmosphere. I also found the redesigned UI to be sleek and incredibly customizable, a nice touch for modern players.However, it's important to note that this is not a flawless remake. My biggest issues lie with the character designs for Angela, Laura, Maria/Mary, and Eddie, which are far from satisfying. The voice acting, too, is a major letdown, which nearly detracted from the overall experience for me. These two aspects alone could have brought any other game down to a much lower score, but because Silent Hill 2’s story remains so deeply compelling, they don’t drag it below a 9/10 in my eyes.Bloober Team exceeded my expectations, and despite my gripes, I enjoyed my 101 hours with the game.
