_childDocuments_.review: “In my restless dreams, I see that name. Konami.” Ask anyone who plays videogames which franchise had a rough past decade and many are likely to bring up Silent Hill, Keiichiro Toyama’s beloved brainchild and interactive adaptation of Jacob’s Ladder. After several disappointing third-party titles and the serious contender for “industry fiasco of the decade” award that was P.T.’s cancellation, things were looking grim for the series. Fans were certainly displeased when announcements of the Silent Hill 2 remake would be handled by Bloober Team, a Kraków-based developer with a spotty track record. In defiance of all criticism, the Silent Hill 2 remake is an excellent title, and many (including myself) need to sign the Bloober Team apology form. The town of Silent Hill has never looked better. The urban decay of the fog world and the hellish rust of the otherworld have a level of visual fidelity that’s the best in the horror genre. Environments are crafted with a meticulous attention to detail that induces feelings of claustrophobia and discomfort. One wrong step and James will require a tetanus shot. Backing up the environment are Masahiro Ito’s iconic monsters with their glorious grotesqueness in full HD. The combat has been improved as well, going from an auto-aim system to similar to Resident Evil 4. Don’t be fooled, James is no Leon Kennedy. The tension of the original’s combat has been skillfully preserved in this iteration, and best of all is there is no frustrating menu management now that reloading and weapon swapping is in real-time. One cannot review this remake without mentioning its sound design. Bloober’s rendition is nothing short of hellish, with a cacophony of sounds ranging from rusty saws to violin strings being brutally drawn. The original Silent Hill 2 composer, Akira Yamaoka, returned with high quality remasters of the original’s classics, as well as several new tracks that serve as welcome additions. The utilization of the soundtrack is subtle but does a great job of eliciting emotions from players such as fear, anger, relief and sadness. For series veterans, the remake introduces several gracefully done easter eggs which refrain from breaking immersion. While some may not be pleased with the removal of a certain voice line, the changes between the original and this iteration are interesting enough to warrant a playthrough from even the most dedicated of fans. For newcomers, this is an excellent gateway title that will hopefully lead them to experience Silent Hill 1 and 3. There is one remaining issue: the remake struggles heavily while loading. The stuttering is immense and makes the game unplayable for several seconds. This leads to a frustrating cycle of players letting James idle in place upon entering a new section though if you experience this while a monster is nearby the dread is palpable. Despite this, this title is a worthy entry in a famed series that is past its prime, but hopefully this success story leads to a revitalization of the franchise as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start? Ignoring the entirety of the issues presented by UE5 itself, the game was great and I enjoyed its storytelling, even if I had to play the entirety of it at 30-45 FPS on 75% resolution scale. Completely ignoring performance issues since that's a me issue, the story remains faithful to the original and captures most of the emotional sections well. The combat is fun and engaging and enemies have attack patterns and telegraph their attacks, giving you time to react accordingly and dodge instead of the combat devolving into just pressing the attack key over and over again like in the original. The voice acting is fluent and organic, the VA's did a great job in the more emotional sections. The environments are faithful, and those that go out of their way to be different still capture the spirit of Silent Hill 2 well. However, the game is not without its faults.The combat, as I said, is fun and engaging, it makes one-on-one encounters awesome to fight, the problem is, there are barely any one-on-one encounters. It gives you the feeling that they were too proud of how they designed it so they tried their hardest to force you to use it as much as possible by having a bunch of enemies everywhere. On top of that, some of the enemies are faster that you are and will easily catch up to you, so even if you don't want to fight, you might just not have a choice, it's not as easy running around them as it was in the OG. One more combat-related gripe I have is the radio, what's the point of it? In the original its purpose was for it to let you know there was an enemy nearby that you couldn't see due to the locked camera angles, and it did its job quite well, in this game it feels more redundant than anything, on top of that, it doesn't even make any noise when there's a posing mannequin close by, which defeats its entire purpose, rendering it useless.The voice acting, as good and as organic as it is, is not my thing. The voice actors did an amazing job and I hope they got compensated accordingly but in my opinion it doesn't quite capture the feeling the original Silent Hill 2 had. The charm of the original voice acting was that it felt unnatural and awkward, it make you feel like something was off, wrong. Made you question if the people you were talking to were even real, albeit quite funny at times.The ambiguity and subtlety of Angela's story was completely thrown out the window, which seemed like an odd decision to make regarding the storytelling since the original was left ambiguous on purpose and is honestly not my thing.When it comes to graphics and cutscenes, it feels like the developers and writers focused a lot more on showing off the engine and making the game look as pretty as possible a lot more than they should have. Some of the camera angles feel forced and unnatural and sometimes outright unnecessary. It's a remake of an almost 20 year-old game, as good as it looks, it feels excessive. Yes, Unreal Engine 5 is a stunningly-beautiful engine with great capabilities, but it has its issues, and those issues happen to be pretty big, basically denying a huge portion of people the opportunity to play a game that both looks and runs good. But like I said, performance issues aside since that's on the personal side.The game is great, despite all the little gripes I had with it, overall it's faithful to the original and the worldbuilding and storytelling are stellar. Despite being almost twice as long as the original, it remains fun and engaging all throughout, making it feel about the same length, probably even shorter. That said, would I play it again to find the different secrets and get the different endings? ♥♥♥♥ no. Would I recommend buying it? Yes, but I'd also recommend playing the original Silent Hill 2 first to have a good idea of how Silent Hill was back when it was first conceived before playing the remake.Overall, loved the game, solid 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was genuinely worried that Konami was going for another cash grab, seeing how they wronged the franchise on multiple occasions in the past. Not to mention, the development team assigned to the remake had a spotty and questionable track record. Being a big fan of the original, I was very very skeptical. I am pleased to say that this is one of the best remakes to have come out in the past decade. Truly redefining the survival-horror genre, this remake not only stays true to the original source material, but updates the game to stay current in 2024. Similar to Capcom's remakes of the Resident Evil franchise, this game certainly takes inspiration from them. However, while there may be arguable comparisons, this game implements mechanics and features not found in those remakes. I never played a game before where I had to clear corners, slowly progress through corridors and hallways so as to not be blindsided, and meticulously search every nook and cranny for finite health and ammo resources. Even with the original, I was not super tempted to do another play through on new game plus. But with this, I want to 100% everything. I really hope they continue to remake more of the Silent Hill games, and of course, retain the same quality and production value that this one had.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the Silent Hill franchise since I was a kid. This series means a lot to me. Initially when I heard that arguably the best game in the franchise was getting remade I was sceptical. However, Bloober team have pulled of the unexpected. This is quite possibly the BEST remake I have EVER played. Game play wise this takes what was great about the original Silent Hill 2 and RAMPS it. The atmosphere is great, the fog and darkness always leaving you wondering what's just around the corner. The fighting system was also a great improvement, I always felt that the fighting in the original silent hill was a tad too easy if you knew what you were doing, in this the timing you need and the precision as well is a welcome addition. The puzzles have all been good. I won't say mind numbingly hard, but at the moment I've only started a medium/medium play through and the puzzles have all been straight forward to an extent and certain twists on classic puzzles from the original were a very welcome addition.The sound design and music has been a massive highlight. The sound design adds so many different layers to this. Akira Yamaoka is known for going above and beyond within this franchise and he has done so again. The general atmospheric background tracks really do help escalate your emotion throughout it and at the correct moments the tense feeling you should be feeling when you are exploring such dank horrible places. The classic tracks that have been remastered and re-recorded too are a very welcome addition. It points when you're feeling tense it brings a sense of nostalgia but with the new arrangements a whole new level to familiar but different. Overall I would rate this game as a MUST play for any die hard horror game fan. Even if you've never played a Silent Hill game before I would even go as far as to recommend this as a really good starting point.

_childDocuments_.review: this is damn good, damn good!!! as someone who didn't grow up with the OG, but having played it for the first time in my 20s, i enjoyed the OG as having a PlayStation past but also a deep infatuation with the lore, music, sound design, world design, etc. of silent hill that i had learned of from external references. i played it, and loved it, really with no complaints considering the point in time it was made. when this remake was first unveiled, my excitement was profound because i love this franchise so much - even if this game was bad, i still would have enjoyed it - but too bad... it was perfect. i think that someone who hasn't played the original will want to compare it to resident evil, and likely complain about the lack of enemy variety - but even with a 25+ hour playthrough, i still wasn't fully evading enemies and taking damage (they hit hard on hard difficulty! which is good!) - but even then, if you remember a certain corridor enemy that also appears in SH3, you will be pleasantly surprised with what Bloober did with that enemy here! So enemy design, awesome - combat is super punchy (i love the sound design of curb stomping enemies, James' voice actor did great) - and combat was fun, fair, and had no instances of me screaming "BS" to some hitbox shizz. Atmosphere and music, sound... more oppressive than the OG, i was scared out my britches the whole dang time, and all the homages to the OG triggers/scenes were a nice touch. I love what they did with Maria, her dialogue was a nice tension relief between the Apartments and Brookhaven, It's hard to view this game without the lens of the original (which i think is pretty much perfect) - and with even that considered, i thought this was a perfect game (A LOT OF GAMEPLAY compared to the original, looks beautiful, great combat, oppressive atmosphere, etc.) but even as a standalone without the legacy of the original game, this definitely stands on it's own with things that it does even better than Resident Evil Remakes with the sound design, combat (i think this game's combat was great... and combat, even if it's not the premise of the game, should still be good obviously) - Bloober team needs the blessing to get us Silent Hill 1, 3 (PLEASE), and 4 remade as well, because it can only get better from here. This was a great game, and i wish i could forget it and play it again. It really blew my balls off, really good stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: James SunderlandBoy oh boy where do I even begin. James Sunderland.. honey, my pookie bear. I have loved you ever since I first laid eyes on you. The way you dive into your trauma and strike fear into your enemies eyes. Your silky smooth touch around the toilets, and that gorgeous pale face. I would do anything for you. I wish it were possible to freeze time so I would never have to watch you die.You had a rough childhood, but you never gave up hope. You are so amazing, you're a great husband, sometimes I even call you dad. I forever dread and weep, thinking of the day you will one day die. I would sacrifice my own life it were the only thing that could put a smile on your beautiful face.You have given me so much joy, and heartbreak over the years. I remember when you read that letter and its like my heart got broken into a million pieces. But a tear still fell from my right eye when I watched you suffer over your wifes death, deep down, my glorious king should be happy. I just wanted you to return home. Then allas, you did, my sweet baby boy came home and I rejoiced. Mary's death was a hard time for us baby, but in time you made history happen. You came back from Silent Hill and I couldn't believe it.I was crying, bawling even, and I heard my glorious king exclaim these words, "This town is full of monsters, how could someone sit there and eat pizza?" Not only have you changed psychological horror games and the gaming world forever, but you've eternally changed my world. And now you're getting older, but still the goat, my goat. I love you pookie bear, my glorious king, James Sunderland.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic REMAKE, don't come into this game looking for a REMASTER as they have changed numerous parts of the game. However don't be alarmed as in my opinion I believe the changes only proves to enhance both the environment and story telling of the original.    Many players are quick to point out the almost bare bones combat system but I believe Bloober team made the right choice in keeping the style simple and somewhat stiff. If you think about it, an in depth combat system would ultimately only take away from the story telling and atmosphere as it would shift the overall feeling from dread to action thriller as seen in the western produced Silent hill games. Now I can guarantee the current combat system can be improved upon and tweaked in a way to still feel satisfying while also keeping the hopeless tension both you and the protagonist should feel, but in my opinion I'm just glad the original feeling of Silent Hill is still maintained. If you're anything like me and have been hoping for some good Silent Hill news after the whole PT thing, or if you've been craving that distorted and twisted feeling your gut tells you whenever you think of Silent Hill, I'm glad to say this game won't disappoint

_childDocuments_.review: I finally played the Silent Hill 2 remake, and I don’t even know how to feel anymore. This game isn’t just scary; it’s emotionally draining. The oppressive fog, the distorted echoes, the way everything feels like it's rotting from the inside—it’s like being trapped in someone’s nightmare, but you can’t wake up.James... man, he’s more broken than ever. Every step he takes feels heavier, like the weight of his guilt is crushing him in real-time. The story hasn’t lost its punch either it’s still a tragic spiral into grief, regret, and madness. I didn’t think it could get any darker, but this remake finds a way.And the music... haunting. Soundtrack feels like it’s scraping at the edges of your soul, reminding you that there’s no happy ending here. Only the silence and the void.If you're looking for a game that leaves you feeling hollow in the best way, this is it. The atmosphere, the story, the sound it all comes together perfectly, dragging you down into the depths of despair. And honestly? I wouldn't want it any other way.

it.the progression through the town has added quirks and there are new areas to explore.the notes are similar if not exactly the same but there has been many alterations to the themes of the major "dungeons" its not a large margin but it is slightly different in tone and ascetics. i could write a 10 page essay on all the things i love about this remake and there is a lot to appreciate but... it also has its problems. if you want a detailed analysis on that wait for the myriad of youtubers who will no doubt break it all down my recommendations being FUNGO and NubZombieas someone whos beaten the original more times than i could count or remember as well as the original being one of my all time favorite pieces of fiction (though not my favorite silent hill, that would be 4... i know im weird right?) there are a lot of nuances and thematic changes in tone voice acting as well as all the way up to the atmosphere with background tracks i have a loooot of gripes... but those gripes while many arent enough to say this isnt a VALIENT effort by team bloober in fact the quality of this remake is so great as a hardcore looooong time fan (i played silent hill 2 in 2005 after my uncle bought it for me at GAME CRAZY!) i can choose to look past these gripes... some of which only a hardcore fan like me would get annoyed by.the first hardcore fan gripe is that the track "a world of _childDocuments_.review: I was very anxious about how this game would turn out. From Bloober's inconsistent and questionable quality to Konami's blundered handling of the franchise for literal decades, the  remake was always going to be something I cast a very critical eye on as a massive  lore geek. Even if the original game was not my favourite of the Team Silent titles, I am well aware of how monumental the original's reputation was and how well it was earned. Now I have officially seen all of the content the remake can offer with its endings, changes, and overall gameplay, I think I can make a good judgement on the game.In short, the  remake is the best game the series has had since 2004, by a  margin. But it being better than the original? That's not as clear cut an answer to give. There are a lot of things this game does better than its source material, but there are many important things it does worse.First, the positives. The gameplay of the  remake is easily the largest improvement aside from Bloober's obvious talent for stellar visual detail. The game adds some nice modern polish to dated combat mechanics of old while keeping the risk and reward of such systems intact. Even with a dodge at his disposal, James is easily punished for missing swings or wasting ammo if players aren't paying attention, and the limited supplies to find call back to when resource management was key to survival in the genre. Despite easier and more fluid controls, you never feel safe or powerful, which is how it should be. This is especially clear in the much improved boss fights, which are challenging with mix-ups that veterans might not be expecting, but just as fun to tackle.The puzzles of the remake are also a warm return to the days when such puzzles didn't insult a player's intelligence. Whether based on riddles, environment manipulation, or exploration, they are well constructed and require being thorough in order to solve. Any found clues make the solutions more than manageable with just a little bit of thinking, but without making the answers too easy to work out. Though I am slightly disappointed that number combinations aren't randomised each playthrough like the original (as helpful as that is for speedruns), the initial process of working them out was very enjoyable.Of course, the art direction, sound design, and music is some of the best I have seen in a horror game in a long time, with obvious props having to go to Bloober's art team and the incomparable talents of Masahiro Ito and Akira Yamaoka. The environments are fantastically well rendered in detail and layout and the nightmarish Otherworld variants are a wonderful blend of the incarnations seen in the original  and its sequels to keep things cohesive. The monsters, and all of their variants, are much more threatening with their aggressive behaviour and subtleties to their visual designs, and the new soundtrack boasts a nostalgic blend of the original ambience and industrial cues alongside new renditions that elevate what made the original score so beloved (though, your mileage may vary based on personal tastes).However, there are not-so-positives to be had here despite my praise, and they're on very important things. The  remake is still a remake in a long running franchise at the end of the day, and so it has to match the source material at minimum and offer a new perspective or improve on it at best, especially in regards to character and story. I unfortunately don't think it manages to pull off the latter beyond trivial reasons of nostalgia.The new voice talent is an overall mixture of good and bad. James and Eddie are both incredible and more believable portrayals of their characters, surpassing the original presentation in a lot of ways from the inflections in their voice and general direction with slight tweaks to lines. James in particular is the star of the show for good reason, with his performance being the best out of everyone. Angela is mostly good outside of one or two moments where her performance seems a little muted, and Laura is about on par with the original.Unfortunately, as one of the most important castings in the game, the new Mary/Maria falls flat. While the characters out of intense moments are fine, they both severely lack the gut punch emotions in the key scenes where they need to nail it. Though new scenes highlighting an almost gaslighting nature to Maria are nice, most of her dialogue ends up coming across as generic NPC-companion worthy for most of her appearance. And the pivotal scenes for Mary do not come close to the original in terms of weight and delivery, not by far.There's also the long running franchise problem of flat out ignoring the existence of the other Team Silent originals outside of scant references. There is a reason that a "2" is in the title of this game and the 2001 original was an exploration of what the town had become in the wake of the first game. It had pieces of lore and town history to connect the games together to explain  the town does what it does, as well as adding context to the events that happened prior. But, as has been the case since the release of , every subsequent game after this simply takes the face value premise of  as the basis for the entire franchise, and the remake unfortunately doubles down on this. Key pieces of lore, such as the Book of Lost Memories that outright explain the town's power, have been completely omitted in the remake (the book can be found, but not read) and all other references to the occult and the cult of the town that used to be in places such as the prison and the symbology throughout the Otherworld have been severely toned down or removed entirely. The original  felt like an expansion of what had come before, but the remake makes it hard for any newcomer to understand  things are happening or why this is titled as a sequel in the first place. As a bit of a lore nerd about this series, it's really disappointing to see the continued enforcement that  is the only game that matters and exists to most people when the remake itself is actively omitting information that connects it to the other original three.If I was judging the  remake solely as an adaptation of such infamous source material, the game is neither an objective improvement across the board, but also not a downgrade in the same way. I treat it more as an alternate version of the same story rather than a totally different interpretation ala the  remakes or a simple copy+paste of the original's plot. Its character performances are simultaneously better and worse, the environmental storytelling is simultaneously more detailed and less connected to the franchise as a whole, and the overall horror and disturbing nature is simultaneously way stronger in some locations and a lot weaker in others. But reviewing this as an actual survival horror title, the  remake is a very enjoyable experience with a lot of incredible visual details, disturbing implications through visuals and sound thanks to veterans of the original team, and a gameplay loop that feels both refreshing while also a solid callback to old school survival horror mechanics.As a standalone game, 8/10. As a  title, 6.5-7/10. Still better than the last six games that came before it by .

_childDocuments_.review: A great remake. And yes, I want to mention one tragic situation in my life that happened 2 years ago, when the remake of Silent Hill 2 was announced on October 20, 2022.My house burned down by 80% on October 30, 2022 at 23:11, and I was in Silent Hill for a long time in a state of shock, but I came out of it after I got sick. Thank God, none of my relatives were injured, and I've been waiting for this game for 2 years. 2 years later, I bought this game and it was perfect. Thanks to the BLOOBER teamI melted. I'm a big fan of the original, but the last time I went through the original was 3 years ago. I managed to forget some details. And this remake gave me new and at the same time familiar emotions. In general, I am as happy as a LION who was given not only a bone, but also a whole hefty piece of meat. This is literally what the original SH2 looked like in my childhood memories.  The Bloober team, well done! Separately, I would like to mention the reworked sound and soundtrack of Akira Yamaoka, they are artfully recreated in the style of the original and create the same atmosphere. Silent Hill 2, which we deserveYes, this is the original that was masterfully recreated by the Bloober team, and the good news is that this opens the way for other remakes or re-releases of old parts on modern platforms.  We are waiting for new Silent Hill series games.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely solid experience.Expectations were not high given the state of Konami for the past decade and Bloober team's previous releases.However.It's hard to not say that this game has managed to not only stay true to most of Silent Hill 2's appeal, but also build upon it in a very respectful way.Visually the remake is incredible.The general atmosphere of the exteriors and interiors are absolutely fantastic from start to finish.There doesn't feel like an area that was slept on in the slightest. It's gorgeous. Especially Lakeside, probably the most pleasant earned reprieve after trudging your way through Silent Hill and all its dark decrepit horrors.The gameplay ended up being more than serviceable, despite how everything looked from previews.It simply works. Health items may be over abundant even for Standard difficulty, as I ended my "Leave" playthrough with 57 health items to spare!Though the biggest peeve as to why that is, is because the dodge mechanic was also gifted with the modern appeal of: An egregious amount, that with any amount of patience.. Your combat encounters should never trouble you.I don't believe it is a bad mechanic. It actually allows combat to feel fun and rewarding. But it is noticeable how generous the devs chose to be with its i-frames.The acting manages to not only respect what already existed, but flow in such a way that it still retains that semblance of weird characters in foggy town.Everyone very much "talks" to each other and everyone feels quite natural, except for the one certain character you'd expect.None of the visual design changes to certain characters felt distracting by the time I got hands on with the game and Angela still comes across like Angela, despite some changes.. She is a mess. It shows. It's far more on the nose as to why.Eddie is done well.Maria is insufferable for all the uncanny reasons.Laura has far more character, with her artistic storytelling revealing her mental state throughout James' journey.Mary is wife. Seek wife.Sunderland is probably handled the best.The town and interiors have been truly fleshed out.No cut corners in the way you could gripe about Resident Evil 2RE or (especially) RE3 remake.It very much provides you a Silent Hill 2 experience with some extra meat and seasoning to each environment you'll stumble upon.Whether the intense build up of most interiors or the brief respite of returning to Silent Hill's outdoors, it all feels like alot of consideration and love was poured into these spaces, which is truly blessed.Enemy variety in Silent Hill 2, compared to SH 1 & 3 has always been quite tame.James' inner turmoil aside, the remake did a good job of spicing up the encounters with what already exists:And then there's the variants.Each main enemy has an additional variant that adds some extra spice to their encounters, but I think that's worth seeing more than reviewing. They were handled quite well and keeps the game from being too repetitive, combat wise.Puzzle difficulty is still a choice when you start your playthrough, which I was surprised to see.Very cool.Only experienced Standard so far.They've all been handled quite well.Visually, some of them are quite creative.It still feels like you're playing a Silent Hill title, rather that some silly people got a hold of an IP and just tried to do what they think a Silent Hill puzzle would look like. Some are quite remarkable in their format, others are very standard.I'm genuinely shocked to see a title of this calibre remade in 2024. Retain multiple endings and not just feel as if it is preying upon nostalgia for a quick penny.It's a game.That's nice to see.While the world and game dev isn't always such a simple place.. I genuinely would not mind seeing Bloober Team handle a Silent Hill 1 remake, if it is anything NEAR as close as what was produced with this Silent Hill 2 remake.Playing through this not only felt fun.I actively felt inspired to load up Silent Hill 2 again. The original. I've always loved  and I will always prefer 3 when thinking of: Though I like that this managed to spark some new interest in revisiting the original Silent Hill 2, as it was my least favourite of the original 3 Silent Hill games.Very cool experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, no use in beating around the bush. I honestly don't recommend this game, at least not at full price. This is really disappointing to me as everything I read and saw regarding this remake looked very promising. What I found however is another developer trying a little too hard to "improve" the formula and refusing to recognize when something they designed does not work, or at least not well.What am I talking about? Well it's the combat. No, I am not wearing rose tinted glasses, the original Silent Hill 2 also had some pretty lack luster combat, it was there, it was serviceable, but it was bland. The remake however, goes to far in the opposite direction by trying to make combat a primary focus of the game, if not THE primary focus. My gripes are as follows:1. Enemy aggression is way too high. Enemies in this game are ACTIVE. I mean really active, there is no more sneaking or playing it safe. You are fighting, and you better like it, because it's the majority of the game.2. So many enemies. If Bloober wanted to make the combat encounters intense, that could be fine, if it weren't happening constantly. There are so many enemies now, it just becomes desensitizing.3. The actual combat system is a clunky mess and the game does a very poor job of teaching what you are actually supposed to do. There seems to be this cat and mouse system where you are supposed to hit an enemy a couple times, then back off, rinse repeat.... except when that is punished for...reasons? Sometimes enemies just have input reading levels of response time where they use an instant follow up attack after you perform a single swing. I don't want to say it's unavoidable, but the game does nothing to teach you how to avoid it. From a new player perspective, it just feels like they wanted to back in intentional damage as part of the game. This is kind of silly because in a survival horror game, it's all about conservation of hard to find items. Now it has become more of a smoke if you got em scenario, just chug healing drinks and fight through the awful combat. Also, the whole system seems to be about movement, but you are constantly fighting hyper aggressive enemies in tiny spaces where dodging and running don't really work. Makes no sense to me.Overall, Bloober seems to be very proud of their combat system, as they force you into it as often as they can, however, it just isn't enjoyable to me. I like that they tried to improve things rather than do a 1:1 remake, but I would prefer eve the old bland stiff combat over this mess.The most painful part of all of this is that the rest of the game design is quite good. The atmosphere and sound design is superb. Graphically, it feels right for the most part, and the game does a good job of capturing the old feeling of each of the memorable areas from the original. I know there are some complaints of performance, and yes, there is stutter here and there, but it is nowhere near as bad as people are making it out to be. I am high susceptible to any kind of stutter or frame pacing issues, and this game doesn't really bother me.That being said, I really hope there is some plan to tweak the combat, as it's just a little too clunky and forced for my taste and is fouling an otherwise great experience. Some have suggested that I put the combat to easy, but I honestly don't find it difficult, it just feels cheap, so doing so would be more of a bandaid than a true fix.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good remake. Game and character art is amazing. It's true to the original. I'm giving it a thumbs up because of these reasons.However, I'm starting to question peoples tastes in games because the original game design doesn't really equate to anything "fun". It's 10-15 hours of doldrums with only a few truly action packed fights and amazing jump scares. Most of the game just follows the main character as he runs after the same kid, distracted from his real quest of finding his wife, through building after building of locked doors. He must unlock every door in the building before he can be transported to a "hell" version of the building, that we call the "other world" version. Then, after unlocking more doors, and doing a puzzle or two, he fights a mini-boss that are all unique, but consist of spamming the same dodge and shooting or whacking the thing until it's time for a cut scene to end the fight.While the game is true to the original, I'm left with the question: why? They certainly could have spiced it up a bit while still saying true. Additional dialogue and cut-scenes would have been nice to help flesh out the backstory of each character, instead of feeding it all through newspaper clippings and random notes that make you fill in between the lines. The wiki has 1000 times more content on each character and mini-boss than I ever found in the game notes.I enjoyed a lot of this game. Especially the first parts, where I was still getting introduced to the spookiness of Silent Hill again, and going through the shifts from normal to other-world. But that doesn't justify the complete boredom that set in eventually, as I trudged through room after similar room and unlocked door after similar door for hours on end.This game is a testament to the differences between games from two decades ago and the action-packed-never-a-dull-moment games of today. Neither really do gaming justice and this remake was a chance for Bloober to blend between those two extremes to make something that is more than just nistolgia.Also, there's major stuttering on PC that you need mods to fix. You can find them on Nexus Mods.I rate this game 4/10.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Silent Hill series, I went into the remake of Silent Hill 2 with very low expectations. The trailers didn’t impress me, and I was skeptical about Bloober Team’s ability to handle such an iconic title, given my mixed feelings about their previous games. Despite all this, I decided to buy the game, driven by my love for the series and the hope that it might surprise me.And it did, in the best possible way.From the moment I stepped into the eerie town of Silent Hill, I was blown away by the visuals. The graphics are stunning, enhancing the atmosphere while staying true to the original’s haunting mood. The fog, the lighting, and the character models are all meticulously detailed, creating an experience that feels both nostalgic and fresh.But it’s not just the visuals that shine—gameplay-wise, the remake is incredibly engaging. I found myself hooked and unable to stop playing. I have to give a huge thank you to Bloober Team. Despite my initial doubts, they managed to deliver a project of such high quality that not only met but exceeded my expectations. As a fan of the series, I feel relieved and grateful that this remake didn’t disappoint. Silent Hill 2 is a masterpiece, and this remake did it justice in a way I didn’t think was possible.

_childDocuments_.review: A complex, well thought out dish, somewhat ruined by being too repetitive and overseasoned.As it stands now, at the price they want for this game, I have to give this a thumbs down, even though my opinion on the game is mixed. I really want to give this a neutral score, but it's either Thumbs up or down and I cannot quite give this a thumbs up.This is not a replacement for the original Silent Hill 2.This remake is its own animal, and it is not shy about letting you know that. If you’re new to Silent Hill 2 and this happens to be your first experience with the franchise, you are going to see a lot of cutscenes that feature broken objects, and you will likely have no idea what they mean.However those who have played the original Silent Hill 2 will see these scenes and go “I see what you did there!”The developers know that veterans of the original Silent Hill 2 will go to certain places, and look for certain objects, and they put those cutscenes in to say “Yeah we know why you’re here, but we’re doing it a different way!”And do it a different way they did. Some of the changes I like, other changes I don’t like.(THIS IS WHERE THE SPOILERS BEGIN)I like the scene in Neely’s Bar where you repair the record, and listen to a song that reminds James of Rosewater Park. I think this was a nice addition, and a way to start easing you into the fact that there are going to be more puzzles.And more puzzles there certainly are. On top of that, puzzles from the original game now have extra steps that are needed to solve them. Even with puzzles set to Light, these are not easy to solve. Though, they are manageable. I don’t consider myself to be great at puzzles, but I was able to beat the game through trial and error without looking up a walkthrough.Graphics wise, I love having full control of the camera, and seeing all the little details, like the fact they made an error with one of the television models, giving it two VHF knobs instead of a VHF and UHF knob like you’d expect to see on an old TV. I have one complaint about the graphics. They made too many areas, like the bathroom at the start, way too dark.Character design wise, I think they did a good job overall. I would say the human characters have a believable apperance that matches who they are.This gets into my main complaint about this remake. Bloober threw subtlety out the window. I’m going to be talking about this a lot, because it pervades the entire game.The original Silent Hill 2 was great, but it was a subtle, slow burn. You could think of it as being a dish that was well made, but slightly underseasoned, and a bit undersized. It left you wanting more. You don’t *quite* get all the answers as to what’s really going on. You don’t know how much of what you’re seeing was caused by other people, or something supernatural. You don’t know how much of what you’re seeing is James’ warped version of reality. As a result, you play through the game over and over again in order to get every morsel of lore and gameplay that it has to offer.In the remake, the supernatural elements are so blatant that there’s an achievement for the first time you cross over into the other world, and it happens far sooner than Brookhaven. Bloober overdid it here. It’s the gaming equivelent of adding too much seasoning. A pinch of salt will make a lot of things taste better, however a tablespoon of salt will ruin pretty much any dish.Bloober overdid it on the monsters, and they overdid it on the gross scenes. In the original game, James stuck his hand into a hole in the wall, *once*. That was all that was needed. In the remake, this happens multiple times and quickly loses its impact. By the 5th time, it’s just annoying.Also, the infamous scene of James sticking his hand in the toilet was optional in the original game. This time it’s mandatory. In the original game, you did it to get a safe combination to get extra ammo. It was a decision you had to make, as in, how desperate are you? How badly do you want that ammo? Bad enough to stick your hand into a gross toilet? You had to make that decision.Speaking of ammo, this game starves you of ammo. I think the survival horror element of scrounging for every last bullet you can find and agonizing whether to use up your precious ammo or try and get by with melee attacks works well for a Silent Hill game, but it really should be reserved for higher difficulty levels. If you’re playing on easy, the game should be more generous with the health and ammo.The monsters far more plentiful, and far more dangerous. You’d think this would translate into a more scary experience, and at first it did. But now it’s like “Oh, another mannequin.” or “Oh great, another spider mannequin” or “Oh, another nurse.” I’ve encountered so many monsters in this remake that I’m just annoyed by them.Part of what made the original Silent Hill 2’s monsters work so well is you could go a while before encountering one, kind of half forgetting that they existed. You let your guard down a little bit, then BAM! The game reminds you! General gameplay wise, yep, this feels very much like a Silent Hill game. Meaning that on your first playthrough, you will be spending a good 45 minutes wandering through the same set of rooms, looking for the ONE THING that you missed! That one key. That one cracked section of wall. It’s a staple of the horror genre to have literally only one option that works. It’s made more aggravating here in the remake, because James can hop over various waist high objects. Yet he’s stopped cold in his tracks by a random bucket or branch that he could just realistically step over.This remake has some interesting mechanics not present in the original, but again, they overdid it.James pushes a cart over to a spot so he can climb over it to reach a vent.James breaks a wall.James slides through a narrow hole in a wall.James crawls through a hole in the bottom of a wall.All of these would be good game mechanics, if they were used sparingly. However they are used so repeatedly that they lose all impact and become just another nuisance. Breaking a wall with your melee weapon happened in the original game, when you got trapped in the bottom of the well. However, here in the remake, the scene at the bottom of the well loses all impact, because the wall breaking mechanic is well established at that point. In the original game, you likely had no idea you could use your melee weapon to break the wall, and likely found out after desperately trying everything else. That scene sticks with you, because it was done only once. Once was all that was needed.And then there is the iconic scene where the Lakeview Hotel reveals its true state after James watches the video. The problem here in the remake is that the hotel starts looking run down and flooded well before the big reveal, and that somewhat spoils it. You could argue that this is because James’ delusions are starting to unravel, but it lessens the impact of the big reveal. That’s a shame, because the hotel’s run down state was executed very well here in the remake.Reality shifts happen in the original Silent Hill 2 as early as Brookhaven, but they were done with no fanfare, and no special attention drawn to them. That makes the big reveal in the Lakeview Hotel so much more memorable! You’ve spent time exploring what appears to be a fairly normal looking hotel and then: WHAM!! The game hits you with everything it’s got! One massive burst of pure flavor and intensity right before the end!I got the Leave ending here in the remake. I think that’s appropriate, because I don’t think I want to go back for a second helping. I mean, it wasn’t outright bad, and I don’t regret buying it, but I think I’ve had enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 (2001) will always be praised for being, objectively, one of the best video games ever made. Two years ago, we were given the somewhat controversial news that Bloober Team (creators of Layers of Fear, The Medium, and Blair Witch) were given the impossible task of remaking this classic with the same coat of paint as the Resident Evil and Dead Space remakes. I was honestly never doubtful of this project and thought all the trailers leading up to its release looked great, and I'm happy to report they exceeded my expectations!This is an incredibly faithful remake, or rather, re-imagining that literally copies some cutscenes one-for-one and adds a few extra story beats. It doesn't completely overshadow the original, but it's such an obvious love letter that was handled with extreme care. Each of the six main characters were well written and performed extraordinarily well. It feels like they studied the source material, but were still able to create their own version of each character that still fell in line with the original.Every area you know and love still remain but are completely fleshed out. Even the town of Silent Hill has more spots to explore in the opening hours of the game and sets the tone for the type of puzzles you'll be dealing with throughout your journey. The town feels very 'lived in' and the fog is just as intimidating. Each enemy type is still here and even some new ones show up every now and then. The boss fights feel MUCH better, when compared to how cumbersome they were in the original.With all of this praise comes some small gripes - while I do LOVE each area and puzzle has been extended, Silent Hill 2 Remake comes with some pacing issues that I really couldn't look past. When the story beats are few and far between, you'll be traversing an area for about 2 hours with absolutely zero dialogue or cutscene that adds to James' story. It's really not terrible and might be more of a preference thing, especially considering the nature of this games story and underlying meaning. Speaking of story, I also think maybe one or two story elements weren't quite handled the way I would have wanted, specifically one of the final scenes in the game. Again, it's really a preference thing after years of watching retrospective videos on why some cutscenes were directed the way they were, so it's a bit sad to not see them handled the same way here.I played this game pretty slowly and clocked 18 hours in my play through. With two additional endings and a new game plus, I can absolutely see myself playing this for years to come.Silent Hill 2 (2024) is a very faithful and modernized re-imagining of a beloved PS2 title. I think Bloober Team took its critical response to heart and spent some much needed time polishing something they probably could have released a few months after the first trailer. Combat and boss fights have been completely transformed and are much more engaging. I do feel like parts of this game were padded out a bit too much so it would have been nice if a few of them had been a bit more streamlined, but this was such a fun experience and an almost must play for fans of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I have indeed already recommended this to others. I will say that I loved the original SH2 (Not the HD collection either, that one can go die in a dumpster fire)This game returns you to our favorite nightmare town. Yes some things changed (such as placement of some monsters but they do give a call-back to the things that changed in the form of an Echo which is pretty neat.) With things that were changed I didn't have a problem with for the sheer fact that they called back to the original.The character designs are fine, especially for Angela. I really feel that 1) she now looks her intended age and not only that she feels true to her story. This said in the original, she looked like she was in her thirties and cracked out. Instead of feeling like a victim/survivor of horrific trauma she literally just seemed... crazy. Like personally in the original I could tell what she was dealing with but the original just didn't do any justice to the character or her story. In the remake she feels more true to herself, her story and her trauma. They did a very good job this time around conveying it through the story telling.Maria looks more like her original concept art. She is still Maria. The OG voice actor was the best, however, the one they got for the remake is also good. Like Maria feels more Maria than a projection of James if that makes sense.Eddie and some of the way his lines are delivered are where my gripe seems to be as far as characters go. But it's only one line in particular that I prefer the original delivery of vs. the new one. Combat wise: The combat is a step up from the original. It flows better I feel. If I have any gripes here it is that there is maybe a little too much combat in some areas. I don't remember as much fighting in the original although with the change and the fact that after you've "killed" some monsters... they will on occasion stand back up needless to say even if I pass by one that seems dead... I hit it again with the pipe or the chainsaw. I feel like it adds to the tension some though in an odd way. I do get some stuttering when loading into areas but it's nothing bad or game breaking. Changing some settings would likely fix it if I'm honest, but I tend to forget to do so because for me it's not something that detracts from my overall experience.The atmosphere is great. To start, I'm hard to scare or make uncomfortable period. This game does not scare me however it is very easy to get lost in the atmosphere and the sounds... especially if you're an insomniac and you haven't slept in a couple days and decide I'm going to jump back into it. Then the sounds alone can really start to play with you. _childDocuments_.review: After exploring the streets of Silent Hill and the narrow spaces of the Woodside Apartments, I wrapped up my session at 4 a.m., feeling my initial faith in Bloober Team remains intact and I'm essentially convinced they have accomplished something truly remarkable. I found their surreal and abstract horror in Layers of Fear intriguing, while their approach in Blair Witch was not only terrifying but also emotionally resonant - a faithful extension of the original film.Initially, Bloober Team demonstrated a clear passion, respect, and understanding for the delicate source material that made the original an indisputable masterpiece in 2001. Moreover, they approached the remake with great care, remaining responsive to critical fan feedback and implementing tangible changes over time.The remake maintains a great deal of the artistic integrity that defined the psychologically pioneering original while also impressively modernizing the gameplay. The existing content has been significantly expanded and altered, establishing new locations and added narrative elements, implementing various aspects that undoubtedly enhance the overall experience.Silent Hill 2 appears to be a remake executed admirably; it might very well be considered the remake of 2024, potentially even the top horror game of the year. And frankly, it's about damn time the stagnated and mishandled Silent Hill franchise finally reclaims its rightful place at the top of the hill.

I've seen them in other games and I just absolutely hate everything about them. I spent way too much time backtracking trying to figure out if I missed something before finally looking up a guide and realize I needed to complete the puzzle that I thought I didn't have all the items for. Or I would get to a puzzle and find flaws in it that because of my interpretation made it completely impossible to complete.There's one section with a bunch of coins where you have to solve a riddle and place the coins in the correct order to complete the puzzle. The first part suggests the direction that the woman coin is facing is important but then the second part tells you the woman should be running away from the man but you have to place her facing backwards like she's running away backwards. That makes no sense at all.Honestly, if it wasn't for those puzzles I'd probably have really enjoyed the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I had serious doubts that "Bloober Team" would be able to handle such an ambitious task as the remake of Silent Hill 2. The pre-release trailers only added to my skepticism about the final product quality. But fortunately, and to my great surprise, they managed to get almost everything right. The atmosphere, sound, and graphics are all done at a very high level. However, there are also some drawbacks. For some reason, all the cutscenes are only in 30fps. The combat system in the game is frankly weak and serves a purely functional purpose. I also can't help but mention the extremely mediocre optimization and the presence of stutters on absolutely all platforms. As soon as the stutters are fixed, the Silent Hill 2 remake can confidently claim the game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: The lights are flickering above me, and I'm squinting so hard my eyes might as well be shut. It's quiet now save for my heavy breathing - the stabbing sensation in my side is a constant reminder of why I give people a wide berth.  I came here - I'm not sure why, if I'm being honest. Compelled? Captivated? Coerced? It really doesn't matter now, I suppose. My time here is running short. I just wanted to see her one last time, just to tell her... just to tell her I'm sorry.Silent Hill 2 (2024) is a remake of the critically acclaimed game of the same title, way back in the forgotten, fog-shrouded time of 2001. And it's excellent. It's pitch perfect. Bloober Team had a Sisyphean task, and they somehow pulled it off - staying true to the source material, modernizing it, and dare I say improving on some antiquated game design of yesteryear. There's reverence here, for the original: throwbacks to lines that didn't quite fit the new voice direction, puzzles that were guilty of moon logic relegated to glimpses of the past, etc. And this title wouldn't be so excellent if not for the work not just of Bloober Team, but the original Silent Hill Team... Virgils guiding their Dantes. Do I have any issues? TEENSY, baby issues that I'll lay out here, right now: OPTIMIZATION, and I don't care for how enemies lock on to James like they're enemies in the original Demon Souls.That's it, really - I was a little frustrated on the last boss because sometimes it's a pain in the butt to pick up consumables unless you're looking at them just the right way, but those are my gripes, and they could all be addressed in due time.From the moment you start this game, it feels like such an intimate journey... it almost plays like a film, with the art direction and scene direction. Slowly, deliberately, the town of Silent Hill unveils itself to you - brimming with mystery, with horrors, and with lost souls. It's such a narrative game that I struggle to say much. Yes, it's two decade old piece of art, but I hope people are able to go into this as blind as possible and just experience it for the first time.This is more gush than review, but... the way James updates the map is just so damned immersive. I love the sound design - it is OPPRESSIVE, like there are insects scurrying and skittering around in your head. I hated myself for rushing around a corner, spying a health item I desperately needed, only to get clocked by an enemy just waiting around said corner. The town is rich with assets, notes, storytelling through environment, vistas that are breathtaking, claustrophobic depths... it feels, pardon the pun, alive. Dirty, desolate, depressing, but very much alive.I played it on the highest difficulty, myself - and if you're a seasoned survival horror vet, I would recommend it. By the end of my, like, 18 hours with the game I was as exhausted as my James. I was HURTING for supplies, and every little health item or bullet I found usually came with the caveat of 'I got this, but at what cost?' But there's nothing wrong with playing on a lower difficulty and just enjoying the story, for the story's sake. You won't be locked out of anything, as far as I'm aware.In summation, imagine being tasked with - I don't know, recreating Guernica, in the spirit of Guernica, in 2024? Or being told you have to rewrite 'The Exorcist' for a modern audience while remaining true to what made it so memorable, so iconic in the first place? Picture having to improve upon something so tight and refined and consummate that it just isn't really possible; whatever the time, the budget, the talent... you are probably not going to improve on 'the wheel.'Bloober Team did just that. They took a 23-year-old game, inserted it into some kinda Willy Wonka device, and managed to make the essential version of a beloved, survival-horror classic... which is selling them so incredibly short on my part. I wouldn't go so far as to say it replaces the original, but it is certainly the best way to play this game now, for a modern audience with modern devices. If I were to force a comparison, Bloober Team did for Silent Hill 2 what Peter Jackson did for The Lord of the Rings. Are people going to be disappointed? It's 2024, there's someone furious right now that a hurricane wasn't a destructive as was promised. That doesn't take away from the fact that this is a twisted, beautiful nightmare I loved beginning to end - one I'll carry with me, always.... It also helps that I took an embarrassing amount of screenshots.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill 2 came to me when I needed it the most. It was, without any exaggeration, a life-changing game for me. The art was unlike anything I'd seen. The audio was revolutionary. The narrative was heartfelt and extremely engaging. Everything about it has made it one of my favorite games ever made, and it changed my outlook on life and video games as a form of art. It has a permanent place in my heart.And this is a passion project created by people who respect, understand, and love it as much as I do. That is the highest praise I can give it.I'm a very anti remake person and, especially for video games, I feel like the notion of needing to remake an incredible game just because it doesn't live up to "modern standards" is really arrogant and completely disrespectful to the idea of games as a creative medium, an art form. Things like the Resident Evil 2 remake throw out so much of the original simply for the sake of changing things and making it feel "new" and "remade." Games like Yakuza Kiwami 1 and 2 change the tone and devalue the source material's narrative so much that I consider them greatly inferior to the originals. This game, while still being very transformative and different, avoids doing anything like that. In fact, I'd say it builds on things in places I didn't even realize could be built on. It knows it's an adaptation, and understands that it's different. It doesn't want to replace the original at all. This game is built out of unconditional love for the source material. It's a celebration of it, not a copy.Please, if this game interests you, play the original. Enhanced edition is very accessible and a fantastic way to play it. Then, once you understand its status as a masterpiece, come celebrate it with us.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is an atmospheric bukkake and I'd recommend it on that alone. Every area you enter will either be hauntingly quiet, or have an atmosphere soundtrack that sounds so otherworldly and make you tense up to the core. It's unlike anything I've listened to or played before. Every footstep, water drop, door creak, wind gust, paper flap or light flicker will always make you second guess if you're actually alone in the room or not. James' voice acting and performance is so great and adds to the already great atmosphere. He will breath uneasy when scared, limp when hes hurt, pull his weapon out when he knows a monster is near, grunt and swing at enemies as if his life depended on it (because it does.) I was never interested in Bloober team before, but now they are definitely on my radar from now on. Atmosphere is super important to me in video games, and I gotta say, they absolutely nailed it in this game. Not to mention, I ACTUALLY feel scared and uncomfortable playing this game for long periods of time, which I haven't truly felt towards a game since the original Dead Space back in 2008. I can officially add this game to my list of best horror games of all time (that I've played), competing with Dead Space and Resident Evil. I really do hope Konami lets Bloober remake more silent hill games as I have not played a single one before coming to this remake. If they bring the same passion for horror they had for this game to their future titles (Cronos/any future silent hill game), then we are eating good af

_childDocuments_.review: First the map layout for building is bonkers.  The hospital has no operating rooms but a pool, with the locker room two hallways away.  Instead of signs pointing to radiology, oncology, orthopedics, etc.  The signs are for the cafeteria, stairs, lounge, pool, etc.  The non corrupted buildings are nonsensical which then doesn't make the corrupted buildings feel more confusing and profound.  It never feels like your exploring the town and falling down a rabbit hole.  You feel pushed to the next objective, that never feels strong enough to warrant your character putting himself in this much danger.  Through the original game you keep pushing on trying to figure out the central mystery of your wife.  In the first Act James decides his wife isn't there and this was pointless.  The enemies with target you without having seen you.  The enemies also appear from nowhere.  I checked a wall to make sure there was nothing hiding behind it.  I was blocking the door and went back thinking I had missed a first aid box and now there was a monster waiting where there hadn't been 3 seconds before.  The game encourages you to learn how to take lower enemies down with melee, where as the first game it encouraged you to run, because James isn't a skilled fighter/killer and you were very short on supplies.  It puts white fabric strips around places you can progress without a door.  However the Hospital is covered in White fabric.  At one point it go so dumb I just had to start laughing.  This games is just not that good.  It's a C+.  If we hadn't had our expectations so low with bloober team than more people would be seeing the flaws.  But everyone's just so happy it's even in a playable state that they're treating Bloober like they built a masterpiece, and all they did was not take a c**p on it.  Sigh.

I'm not 100% sold on some of the changes to voice acting and character designs but I don't hate these changes either. As someone who played the original SH2 many times over, I absolutely love this remake!

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill has always been my favorite videogame series, with Silent Hill 2 being my absolute favorite horror game of all time. Bloober COOKED here.  It is very obvious they were all huge fans of the OG and wanted to re-create that atmosphere and story, while adding a modernized touch.  They did this 10-fold.  If you are a fan of the original Silent Hill games, you NEED this.  If you have never played Silent Hill, but love psychological horror, you NEED this.  Even if you hate horror games, you should give this a chance, because the story is truly a GOAT.  THANK YOU, Bloober.  Now remake the 1st and 3rd game, and I can die happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely perfect remake. It knows exactly when to be faithful, and when to freshen things up, and when to mix things up. All without ruining the spirit of the original, or trying to replace it.This game has the atmosphere of silent hill down. Easily the creepiest it has ever looked. The fog is thick and mysterious; hiding dead ends and creatures from view, the shops and buildings are laid out almost exactly how they were originally, and the locations have been expanded to make silent hill feel more real than ever. And don't even get me started on the "Other world". It's just perfect. dare i say, better? The original had one flaw that i was always aware of, and it was that the "Other world" wasn't as rusty and industrial as it was in the first game. I missed that a lot. But, now it's back, and scarier than ever. metal grated floors, opening up to an endless void, metal fans, walls peeling, and of course, lots and lots of rust.Starting to feel like a broken record, but that is how i feel so far. Currently in the prison and, oh boy, I've been having to take a lot of breaks. This game has my chest hurting after a bit. I love it, but holy hell it's scary!

_childDocuments_.review: They killed it with this remake man. As someone who played the original game twice and loved it both times, this just straight up elevated what worked in the original while taking away the few things that didn't. The combat was intense and the split second decisions you had to make about how to handle an enemy encounter kept me on my toes. The story and characters are all intact and in some cases actually better in my opinion such as characters like Laura and Eddie especially. What really shocked me though was just how terrifying this game was. The original Silent Hill 2 is scary but scary because it builds up a sense of paranoia, making you think something is out there in the dark waiting for you, but in all honesty isn't there in most cases. I expected that similar thing in the remake and while it does do that in several ways that pay homage to the original, the scares here build up a sense of paranoia and act upon it. You're suspicions are often correct and there often is an enemy or hostile creature trying to get the jump on you.  All in all though it's a great game only ruined by performance issues on PC, (which were mostly patched) and the fact that James doesn't break it down in the bathroom with Pyramid Head cheering him on.

_childDocuments_.review: After years of anticipation, Silent Hill 2 by Bloober Team is finally here, and as a fan of the franchise, I can say that the remake truly does justice to one of the greatest psychological horror games of all time. This is a faithful, haunting, and utterly mesmerizing reimagining that hits all the right notes — right up there with the Resident Evil remasters. It’s clear that Silent Hill 2 was handled with care, respect, and a deep understanding of what made the original so iconic.Bloober Team stayed true to the heart of Silent Hill 2’s narrative, and that’s where this remake shines. James Sunderland’s tortured journey through the fog-laden streets in search of his deceased wife is as heart-wrenching and chilling as ever. There’s something timeless about the psychological weight this story carries, and the remake doesn’t shy away from embracing that dark, emotional core.Where the game could have innovated a bit more is in James’ character development. Don’t get me wrong, his arc is still compelling, but given modern storytelling techniques, there was an opportunity here to add layers or new perspectives that could have deepened our connection to him. However, this is more of a nitpick—what we get is still a masterful portrayal of grief, guilt, and psychological torment.Here’s where the comparison to the Resident Evil remasters becomes more evident. The combat and exploration are refined without losing the slightly awkward, clunky feel of the original, which only enhances the horror experience. The survival mechanics are tight, with Bloober Team giving just enough control to feel capable, while still leaving players vulnerable in tense moments. One thing I missed? The original’s fixed camera angles. While I understand that the updated over-the-shoulder camera is essential to appreciating the game’s stunning graphical overhaul, there’s a part of me that longed for those static shots that made navigating the fog feel so disorienting and terrifying. However, the freedom to explore Silent Hill with a more dynamic camera does allow you to fully take in the oppressive beauty of the world. Silent Hill feels as mysterious and dangerous as ever, and the game’s pacing is executed beautifully. From tense encounters to eerie, quiet moments, there’s a constant push and pull between calm and terror. My only minor criticism here is that the puzzles, while iconic, haven’t been modernized enough to fully challenge today’s players. A few more intricate puzzle designs would have been a welcome addition.This is where Bloober Team truly excels. Visually, Silent Hill 2 is a masterpiece. The fog-drenched streets, the decaying environments, the oppressive darkness—it all comes together to create a world that’s both beautiful and nightmarish. The characters’ facial expressions are more lifelike, which makes James’ emotional journey hit even harder.But if I had to single out one thing that elevates this game to greatness, it’s the sound design. Akira Yamaoka’s eerie soundtrack and the impeccable sound effects immerse you so deeply in the game that the line between reality and nightmare starts to blur. Every creak, distant cry, and unsettling melody lingers in your mind long after you’ve put the controller down. Sound of this game is real masterpiece!Bloober Team’s Silent Hill 2 remake is a triumph, blending nostalgia with modernized gameplay and breathtaking visuals. It’s not just a love letter to the original; it’s a revitalized experience that’s haunting in all the right ways. As a long-time fan, it was a thrill to see this masterpiece brought to life with such care, and I believe it holds its own among the best modern survival horror remakes.Sure, there were a few areas where I would have loved more—like the ability to toggle the classic camera or a bit more complexity in the puzzles—but these are minor issues in an otherwise fantastic experience.For fans of the series, this is a must-play. For newcomers, it’s the perfect way to experience the eerie world of Silent Hill for the first time.A beautifully crafted remake that does justice to the original while standing tall as a modern survival horror masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: The original is *the* game I point to as a perfect video game.I think this is in the same realm as the Resident Evil 4 remake. SH2R is a damn good game so far, aside from some relatively minor technical issues, but now, because of the influences of the game it's recreating, it's just that -- a damn good game. _childDocuments_.review: OPTIMIZATIONI've lot of the times problems with optimizations, even in games most people don't have even if i've a mid-high end pc (4070ti i5 13600kf). But this UE5 game have drops from 45 to 60 fps on 1440p max settings native, microstutter but not freeze i had on other games, at least for my experience with new games is not that bad, hoping they will optimize more in new patches.COMBATSilent Hill 2 specifically is not famous for his combat, so how this remake does it? i've not yet a gun, but melee attacks are a bit faster than original sh2, the only bigger mechanic is a dodge in 4 directions: it's more action for sure, but you still feel in danger, you can't parry or quick time actions, so for now it's still pretty survival (i remember hating silent hill 3 combat, in 2 i beated all enemies without problems, a bit spongey).AS A REMAKEI heard already they changed some lines, so purists of the original game would hate some of those, i'll see in the future, but for now feeling visuals and dialogue resembles a lot the original, the big difference you feel is the obvious over the shoulder camera.UPGRADED REVIEW AFTER FINISHING THE GAME: as a remake, is great, no questions, it's very good, still mantains what made original good expanding on locations and still feels sh2, way scarier and still sad.OVERALL, ONLY CONSIDERING THIS NOT ONLY AS A REMAKE BUT AS A STANDALONE GAMEStory is not complicate but told well during the game, not a full action game but still satisfying (i not like horror games where you only need to run), a lot of puzzles, good game lenght for a game of this type, multiple endings. _childDocuments_.review: Walked into this one with very tempered expectations. I was never the biggest fan of Bloober, I found their games to be very hamfisted, and not the kind of horror for me, and like many others, when they were chosen for this remake, I was skeptical. I am very happy to say, they knocked it out of the park. It's faithful to the original, balancing modernization and nostalgia, but parts of this game even eclipse the original for me. The additions made to the base game help flesh out the side characters, and make the story feel more involved, deepening the emotional weight of it all. One of the new endings, "Stillness", has become my favorite of all, and most importantly, the game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scary. Hats off to Bloober, if they're willing, I think further remakes would be in good hands with them. Hell, after this, I'm convinced they could make a whole new mainline SH. In the year of our lord 2024, I never thought I'd say this, but Silent Hill is back baby.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original Silent Hill 2, I was excited to see how a modern remake could update the classic for a new generation. Unfortunately, the developers seem more focused on pushing a "diversity, equity, and inclusion" (DEI) agenda than preserving the unique atmosphere and characters that made the original so special.One of the most obvious changes is the redesign of the characters, and it’s not for the better. It feels like the developers intentionally "uglified" the cast to fit a certain mold of inclusivity and realism. Characters who once embodied a troubled yet intriguing figure, now looks like a bland, unappealing. Other supporting characters have similarly undergone awkward visual overhauls, often making them less distinct or memorable. Instead of enhancing the narrative through character design, these changes feel like an attempt to tick DEI boxes, with the focus on representation rather than on staying faithful to the original vision.This push towards modern ideals also affects the game's tone. Where the original was a masterclass in subtle, psychological horror, the remake seems to sacrifice this for messaging that feels more in line with modern social issues. The depth and nuance of the original storyline, which focused on personal guilt and torment, now seems diluted, with the inclusion of themes that feel shoehorned into the narrative.It’s unfortunate that in catering to DEI trends, Silent Hill 2 Remake loses much of what made the original a masterpiece. Instead of elevating the story through thoughtful modernization, the game feels like it's trying too hard to be politically correct, and as a result, it alienates fans of the original who were looking for an authentic, haunting experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully done remake. Graphics are incredible, performances are stellar, atmosphere is sublime, ambiance and score are legendary, and gameplay is perfectly awkward & befitting of James' predicament. Areas have been massively improved since the original in terms of emphasis for exploration, well designed horror/scares, and balance between quality-of-life improvements, new gameplay elements, and respect for the preexisting lore and design. New endings are awesome too, and completing NG+ with the chainsaw was absolute joy. My favorite areas & moments definitely include the heart-wrenching havoc of Brookhaven Hospital, the trepidatious trek through South Vale's Otherworld, and of course the lamenting and laborious lengths of the abyssal Labyrinth. Overall, excellently done. I can't wait to see if Bloober Team get the chance to remake other additions in the Silent Hill franchise, and if so, I'm definitely gonna preorder!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remake, beautifully executed and follows the original source material faithfully, with only minor stylistic and route changes. Graphics 10/10, this game really captures the setting of the 2001 game perfectly and brings the spooky setting of Silent Hill to life really well. The over the shoulder camera position works well in this game as opposed to the RE remakes where I think it fell short a little. All together it gives you the feeling of being there. Sound 11/10, the OST from the 2001 game has been remastered and brought to this.. it honestly gave me goosebumps, UI sounds are identical too. Definitely use headphones for the full experience. The voice acting was actually done amazingly, nothing over the top or overly dramatic, which helps lend the vibe to these just being ordinary folk ^~^Controls 5/10, I know it recommends to use a controller.. but for these style games i want to use a M+K.. my only issue is i have to remap most of the controls to be able to work with my Colemak setup.. In game (the walking and combat bits) works perfect.. however the movement key changes don't translate to menu navigation which for a puzzle game where you're using your menus a fair bit can be a bit frustrating. But i dealt with it. This isn't the only game to have this issue though so its not the end of the world.Linux Compatibility 10/10.. not problems at all maybe a little issue with the shaders especially for the hair gave a weird bokeh effect but with shadows? not sure.. but worked straight out of the box. Only thing i did was use VKBasalt to add a little sharpness and AA as temporal AA always leaves ghosting which just distracts the hell out of me lol.Overall 9/10 Well worth a play and i hope that Konami give Bloober team the reigns for the next remake (which should be SH1) Great work to everyone at Bloober team and Konami, my favourite game of the series got an amazing remake, I can't praise you guys or the game enough <3 and I'm waiting to see what you guys have next for the series!
