_childDocuments_.review: Redemption Reapers has made me mistrust 'mixed' averages on Steam, forever more. The developers of Ender Lilies got done dirty; by the harsh initial reception AND their £40 price point. 'Tis is a strange case given the negativity over technical & difficulty woes made myself and numerous others averse. Has been patched so now runs well, with better balancing in terms of loot/abilities + an easy mode. Thus, I very much recommend going by the most recent reviews. Played on the Deck, after purchasing on sale for £20. Took 25hrs to finish, others likely will in 18-20hrs. Had two crashes; both levelling up skills. Auto-saves on menu before, thankfully.  Only issue in battle had was a temp save not loading. Cutscenes put the fan into overdrive, and given a SRPG opted limit to 40fps. Plays fine at 60. Text a tad hard read.I did not think it was TOO hard, aside from one big difficulty spike at the mines where you're suddenly underlevelled vs new tough enemies that oneshot. If you played Triangle Strategy, that was harder, for me. Positioning and marking enemies - esp suicide shamblers - is key as the AI will punish mistakes. That and grouping up to combo, which is a simple yet immensely satisfying mechanic that the game is built around.Weapon durability is easy to deal with by not doing as I did and selling old weapons, as you can switch weapons in battle. PS: Don't use the legendary weapons till need them.Money is somewhat limited and repairs/upgrades expensive, but as long as you get the loot to sell in missions, you'll be fine. And if not, can replay via skirmishes.Reapers has a straightforward battles -> cutscenes -> menus flow, without fluff. There is however a very nice touch in the form being able to move your units freely before committing to an action (similar to Valkyria Chronicles). I would describe it as the opposite of Fire Emblem Engage, in a good way: no garish colours and running around a 3D homebase pointlessly. Despite being initially rather basic, the more you play and unlock, the more flexibility you get. I was especially impressed with the customisation allowed via accessories. For example, I gave my archer two specific  accessories, one that let her do more dmg if first on a turn, and one if at full health. I had my main tank have an accessory that recovered health killing. And, skill wise, you have to prioritise: do you want to attack first when attacked, or more dmg output? Etc. Some of the skills really change the way you play, such as sentinel stance negating dmg to counter once, but only once. Whilst the Mort are pretty much just unexplained LotR orcs, I did care about the cast by journey's end as they struggled thru a grim (but not grimdark) dark fantasy world, seeking redemption; with a powerful and wonderfully choreographed final cinematic hat caught me offguard. As someone else said, the cutscenes here feel like high budget rewards for progress. Regarding the story, it isn't until the end that the oft mentioned events at Troden 2yrs prior are explored, leaving it with less depth at the start than by the end. Also, in two scenes - the pre-title cinematic with heroine and an early scene with commander/lieutenant - the writing seemed off, ie "it does brighten my day a bit" regarding killing. Rest was fine, and voice acting mostly very good.Going from a metroidvania to a SRPG with lots of cutscenes/dialogue clearly resulted in a few mistakes, such as no way skip or ffward enemy turns (can only make them move faster via a setting I recommend putting on very fast), but it had a lot of love put into it. Maybe there should've been 6 characters, with a spell caster, to let you split your group up more evenly. It also peaked somewhat midway, with the until then varied enemy types growing a bit stale, before picking back up for survival battles at the end. But, overall, 'tis a great game with an addictive loop.Recommended to anyone that likes preset characters in SRPGs, with tactics built around them, as well as people looking for the opposite of FE: Engage.That, or fans of Ender Lilies: some wonderful, if a tad overused battle themes. The soundtrack is one of the best things about the game; so much so that you will stay for the music, if not the game itself, as another reviewer mentioned. Maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: Redemption Reapers

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Fire Emblem but much easier, your characters are offered a lot of tools that can be really powerful if you use them effectively. They are also pretty balanced so you won't bench any of them.The difficulty curve is stable, I finished the game in Normal without grinding and I barely encounter any frustrating situations, a really good game for people who want to get into strategy games.It might gain a better reputation if its UI is better polished (for a game relying so much on counting grids it doesn't have an option to always show grids), and could have more character interactions to make you know more about the five characters you use from start to end.Pro :+Versatile Unit Controlling+Satisfying animation feedback+Great soundtracks and atmosphereCon :-Bland cutscenes-Flat storytelling-Weak character development (story wise)-Level designs are consistent so every level kinda feels the same
_childDocuments_.name: Redemption Reapers

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, they changed the store price from $50 to $24.99?Absolutely recommend for that price. It's a well put together, extremely nice looking tactics game that kept me enthralled enough with the systems to push me to the end of the game.  It doesn't do anything crazy, but it does offer a sort of grim dark hopeless situation story and what we do if we find ourselves in such a circumstance.Combat was entertaining enough and learning how to chain assists made combat entertaining enough. A lot of the reviews are from people frustrated given the full release price of the game.  Notice nearly all of them say things along the lines of "if it was half price, yeah absolutely."Well it is half price now. Go get this game and encourage developers to make more. Quality turn based tactics games are at a premium still IMHO, especially compared to some other genres.

_childDocuments_.review: Redemption Reapers is a rather generic interesting take on the tactical turn based genre. The game itself is less tactics and plays more like a SRPG then a TRPG. Instead of the turn system you get Action points that you can store up and that increase as your characters kill enemies in the map gaining you more points. The game does have replayable missions despite reviews saying it does not. And you can swap weapons mid fight. Now on to the general mechanics, redemption reapers has a cast of 5 characters and the idea is that the battle is comprised of you taking these characters and their active/passive abilities to the highest level you can get them and allowing them to work at their best. It's not your typical TRPG in that one or two characters will get super broken and run through every enemy. It's more about taking advantage of each characters strengths, sometimes going backwards to go forward, and letting players compose themselves before jumping into each group of enemies to think of strategies. The biggest challenge and the turn off for people may be that there isn't a skip animation and that you only get one heal with one or two springs on maps to regenerate that healing for one teammate. This can make losing a map more frustrating then when you finally win it but I found it enjoyable. The story I hear stays pretty bland for the first few chapters and for the 4 hours I played I can agree, its not enough to turn me away but its enough to definitely challenge a few others for whether they should stick around. The voice acting is comprised of notables from other fire emblem titles but just done badly and with lacking emotion obviously with the games dreary tone. Soundtrack is nice and adds a level of something to like in the game. Like most TRPG's though nothing game changing as far as the story plot development. And after beating the game the ending was ok but not satisfying that you felt the journey was worth it.Tl:drRedemption reapers isn't a very noob friendly RPG. And its a rather bland take on the genre that can be fleshed out better. The combat stays very simple and generic for the a good few chapters until you get enough skill points to start specializing your units in what they can do best. Whether that be dodge tanking, one shotting enemies from a distance or just soaking damage. The game opens up around the halfway mark with more options then just lining up units to link attacks off of eachother. The story and characters miss the mark and ultimately it ends up feeling very generic and bland. This is a game you could give a 7/10 to or easily give a 4 or 5 out of 10 to.Gameplay 7/10Story 6/10Soundtrack 8/10Replayability 6/10Overall I'd give it a solid 7/10. If it was 40 or 30$ it could probably be a 8 or 9 for what its asking but at 50$ it falls into just a good game with a sadly bad port to PC.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get the negative reviews for this game at all.  It's a challenging, unique tactics game set in a medieval post apocalyptic world.  It looks great, the story and banter are good, the animations on point, is devoid of fluff.  More importantly, the fighting system is very good.  It does requires spending some time with it and thinking seriously about each move, but once you do, it shines.  The game does exactly what it sets to do with panache without overstaying its welcome and the price has dropped to 30 dollars, which feels right.  Excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this game if you're concerned about the value you'll get for the money you spend. Overall, it's just not worth it. However, I'm giving it a positive review for some aspects.You won't find anything new here. All of the gameplay mechanics can be found in other games too. Leveling up, battling system, weapon stats, accessories, and even the skirmish mode are all pretty standard. Grinding is a pain.I like the graphic design, especially during battles. However, the animation is lacking. If you've played Mass Effect Andromeda, it's even worse. After building up a lot of sad scenes, the facial expressions ruin it.The music is fantastic. It perfectly captures the emotions of sadness, war, final bosses, and survival.The story is a little unique. I usually play games with a happy ending or something, but this game takes you on a slow journey towards redemption. Although it's a bit weird, it's like battling a supervillain with no superpowers. The enemies can cast magic, but we can't even cast a fireball.You can't play this game on Steam Deck, which is a disappointment considering the price. I had to install it on my laptop instead. It's a small issue, but it's a big deal for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend for non-SRPG veterans. I'd also recommend e.g. FE Emblems before this; this game is really for people who really like SRPGs and are out of games to play. There isn't really a plot or characterization worth playing for here in what is ultimately a shaggy dog story.That said, the way the support attacks work and how crucial they become in more difficult missions are pretty fun. It makes each round into a mini-puzzle where you have to work out the positioning and the turn order of your units beforehand. While the battles do get same-y, the way supports become literal force multipliers makes it feel good when you find elegant solution to what seems insurmountable. This is, however, pretty much the only real innovation here; everything else is pretty standard FE-clone stuff.The main issue is that the game is quite unforgiving, even at the normal difficulty (the only one available until you beat the game). Non-tanks will generally die after two hits or so, and while there isn't permadeath, losing a unit when the entire point of the game is to chain support attacks with your units is pretty crippling. The game isn't all that difficult if you are familiar with the sort of game, but it doesn't have much tolerance for errors, and the RNG tends to make you (or, well, me) play conservatively in case you get a miss at an inopportune time.Hard mode is kind of silly. It's the unforgiving nature of the game turned up to 11. The very first mission in hard mode essentially has one solution that you have to follow, or you lose (or you restart until you get a lucky dodge). The second mission is arguably even more difficult, though it's also slightly less scripted since you have more options.Still, it was fun enough for me to play through to get into hard mode. Just don't expect anything groundbreaking, or beginner-friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is actually an interesting take on the turn based genre.  It's not redefining by any means, but it's not bad.  Here's some things I noticed for better or worse.Looks like it was developed for the switch or ps4No graphical options above 1080p (perfectly fine for Steam Deck).  Play windowed if you use any resolution above that.  It will make the game look tolerable, though it's still not bad.A lack of options to be honest.  There are very minimal things you can change.Music is pretty good IMOVA isn't bad, but I think the direction and script hold it back.The story is serviceable, but it's not going to win any awardsThere's combo attacks when other characters are either opposite side of the enemy or adjacent to an allyOn Level up, stats can increase; str, dex,, spd, endur, faith - you also gain sp (which is used to level up skills) when leveling up.You can upgrade weapons Weapons have durability ala FEYou can trade between characters in maps and still have turnsMovement feels more like xcom and gears tactics; there are some positioning advantagesNo opportunities of attack or advantages of attacking from behindIt can be difficult to tell your team members apart since they ALL are black and gray.Spears can attack from two spacesBased on how you many turns (and another factor I can't remember) you finish a map, you ear extra xp that can be distributed to your team at battle prep, which is basically your between map campNo map rotation, but I haven't found it necessary like in some games with this perspectiveThere's lore to go through as well if you're into that sort of thingRuns fine on my 10700k, 32gb ram,  rtx 3080I've played less than an hour, but so far I think it's better than your average indie tbs game released here on Steam. _childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this as a rather competent SRPG with a fairly high production value.  The game plays well, has plenty of strategic depth, and has a decent enough story.The game consists of 30 unique battle maps, split into 28 chapters, a finale, and an optional skirmish.  Almost every main mission map can be replayed via a skirmish mode, with some exceptions due to events in the story itself.  But for the most part, skirmish (grinding) is entirely optional.  I did replay a couple maps to test out some new skills and tactics though.In terms of difficulty, there is an Easy and Normal difficulty (with Hard and New Game+ unlocked after you finish the game once).  I played on Normal, which gave a decent challenge.  As is typical for this type of Fire-Emblem-like game, each character has a relatively low health pool compared to damage input/output, so it is always important to play tactically.  As you play, new challenges are gradually added in the form of different enemy types, buffed enemies, and extra reinforcing waves.  But you are also given plenty of new skills to use along the way.This game also tries something different regarding primary equipment, by giving each item durability and forcing you to spend your (limited) gold repairing them between battles.  This design choice leads to some interesting gearing, since your starting weapons stay relevant throughout the entire game by virtue of being the least expensive weapons to use.  For example, a starter weapon can be used 50 times for the same repair cost as using an end-game legendary weapon once.  (As I neared the last few climactic fights, I had 6500 gold in stock, but a single hard fight where I used legendary weapons liberally cost me 2/3 of that stockpile!)  And by giving each character room for 5 weapons, you can often balance cost and damage output as needed (i.e. if an extra +5 damage will kill an enemy).  I appreciate the system (although it would be nice if the game told you in advance how much each weapon costs to repair).Lastly, I felt there were some obvious omissions.  The game lacks any graphics settings besides Vsync and resolution.  In many cutscenes, it would lag quite a bit (but the battles played pretty flawlessly).  Many stats are unexplained (although there is a tutorial page telling you what they do, that tutorial is never displayed in the normal course of the game; you have to look for it in the menus).  In retrospect, I'd consider these somewhat minor negatives and I still enjoyed the game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to talk too much about Fire Emblem because I think the game stands perfectly fine on its own, but FE is the main tactics game franchise and the game balance guy on this game used to do FE. So, what I will say is that this is clearly an indie game and can't be as sophisticated as something like the Jugdral games, but it's quite fun and you can pay 50 dollars for this and have a good time or you can pay like 90 dollars to play Engage how it was intended to be played and feel profound embarrassment and disgust about all the pubescent screaming girls in that game.Putting that aside, presentation is quite nice. The character models feel a bit lacking like they don't have big enough pores or something, but are perfectly okay to look at for over a dozen hours. The colors are good, I think the characters should have more colors, but not brighter colors. Their clothes are usually dark grey with light grey when it would be better to have something like dark red or green to see better. The first few monster designs look bad, like something out of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Chinese mobile game, but after those first few there are some really fun designs. Music is very solid, it feels like some of the better tracks from FE:PoR. I know Japanese, so I switched the language and VO to Japanese an it is really nice. There are ad materials for this game talking up the VO cast and it always points to the English cast, but they sound boring and idfk who they are. The Japanese VO is good with some rather prominent talent and everyone doing a good job of acting like they are in a fantasy world. Story is serviceable. The antagonists are unintelligible monsters, so no interesting villains. The story more so wants you to focus on the background of your characters and they are quite interesting. There is even a very bad thing that the characters did in a war that they constantly allude to. So much so that the game would have been much more interesting if it was about that stuff, but I guess it would have been too much for an indie team to develop a war like in large-scale FE maps. They also like to deliver story through item descriptions and notes that you can find in the stage. I honestly think it's a cool idea and like that more than trying to incorporate all story into what is voice acted. I know many people complain about reading in games, but it's way more interactive than watching a movie.I think gameplay is super solid. You have a maximum of five characters, so they map sequential attacks of four characters to four buttons and the fifth character can add an attack via skill. Because you have five characters they don't die, they retreat and they do a good job of theming that into the game world. You have weapon durability like Genealogy of the Holy War and they do make it hard to repair a completely depleted weapon. Depleted weapons aren't terrible though as all their stats go to 0 because weapons don't have any handicaps, so you won't necessarily be caught with your pants down. The big thing is the AP meter. At the start of every turn it recovers by a percent, I believe. It is locked to 10 points which is good because it lets you be locked and loaded to do something valuable at any point in the campaign. With enough actions a unit can gain up to four extra points, but you likely won't hit that point and get a special move that can be used at 13 points that is very helpful. There are many complaints about characters being too fragile, but I really haven't had that issue; I can place some characters in the way of up to 4 enemies and will come out on top if I pay attention. There aren't real classes but each character has weak points and strong points that fit class archetypes, so you can tell just by looking at enemies and characters who is strong against whom. Truthfully, the strategy of trying to use your points in conjunction with your skills and your team attacks is outright fun. If you play your cards right you can take out over 10 enemies on one turn. Difficulty is rather low; they do try to keep the enemies dangerous by keeping damage high which is much better than letting enemies survive way too many rounds so they can bully your glass cannons. Ultimately, if you went through Thracia 776 or any of the hard modes of GBA FE you are set. However, I don't mind it being easy because it is 1, very fun and 2, not part of a genre that has ever really been that hard. I will say some end game maps try to slow you down which is not so much fun.Length is perfectly fine. I think people think that because it is an indie game they should have a worse pricing scheme than AAA companies, but there is about as much content as FE Echoes and that game sold for 40 dollars. With inflation and higher development costs per worker it is a perfectly fine price. There is also this really cool thing where, since the game is fun, a year down the road you can just play it again. If they add a hard mode then even more replayability.It really bugs me to see this game being rated so poorly when it seems like a big issue is people not being very good or expecting indie games to be priced absurdly low or wanting lame things like fixed growths.In conclusion, it has a lot of indie jank, but it is fun and I will replay it so you can probably tack on another 10 hours to my play time. It also has a lot of heart and soul with how the characters and world are crafted.I wrote this right before the final stage and after beating the game there is a hard mode, so yeah quite replayable.

_childDocuments_.review: --Game played on version 1.4 and the recommendation is based on buying the game on discount.--This game seemed to have a rocky launch, but as of the latest update, I played through all the game without encountering any bug.This game is what happens when you take Fire Emblem, remove the "great war" plot, all the anime tropes, all the filler characters and hardcore deaths. Then replace it with a plot focused on survival, a grim dark setting, a small cast and 5 unique controllable characters. I have to say that when I started the game I was a bit put down by the setting and theme, everything is dark, everyone wears black, nothing good happens to anyone... you know, typical grim dark fantasy stuff. But the gameplay hooked me in, and I ended up getting invested in the characters and plot by the halfway point. The core of the gameplay is that the Ashen Hawks, our black wearing cover team, can gang up on enemies to make follow-ups, these follow-ups are free, unlimited and don't use Action points, so the game really wants you to use these tactics, bait enemies and gang up on them... but for the love of god, don't rush into enemy groups because while the Hawks can give out a good pummeling they certainly can't take one, just a couple of hits and your guys will be out for the chapter. Action points (AP) is another mechanic to balance the different skills of our characters, as they level up they will unlock new attacks or support skills and these skills have different AP costs, so while your normal attack will cost 6, you can get powerful attacks that cost 10 AP or weaker attacks that cost 4 AP, AP management is not that big of deal, but if you want to use the most powerful attacks when you need them, you will have to pay attention to it every once in a while. Outside of that, the game takes a lot of design cues from Fire Emblem, a character can carry multiple weapons, but each character can only use one type, these weapons wear down with each use and need to be repaired. The starting weapons are weak and cheap to repair, while the more powerful weapons became more and more expensive to repair, this makes choosing when to use a powerful weapon a costly choice, since gold is not plentiful. Don't get me wrong, by the end of the game I had a lot of weapons upgraded to the max level, and plenty of uses of all of them, but outside of keeping the cheaper ones at full uses each chapter, the gold I was getting was just enough to keep going. Now you can do Skirmishes to train and get some extra resources, but if you spend more than you earn on those, you can get forced to sell extra weapons or equipment pretty fast to keep your weapons in good condition...On the story, the game has a small cast, and they make good use of it, and you are present with different choices through the game to get to know the background of each party member, the dialogue tends to be short, but their story is expanded in the archive with more details. The archive is a bit of hit or miss, most of the lore of the game is there, each time you pick up a "relic" on a map, it goes to the archive and unlocks some lore, it can go from a lost love letter to a full diary of a town mayor describing the days prior to his death. While it's great that all that info doesn't slow down the story or the game, by the time I was invested in the plot, the amount of stuff piled to read on was just a bit much for me to actually do it, but if you like lore, you're going to like the archive.Overall the game was some pretty decent 24 hours of tactical RPG gameplay, and it ended right when it should because the last few chapters were being a bit too big for a 5 member party and while you can suspend the game, you cannot save mid-battle, so if you lose at the end because you got cocky... back to the start of chapter with you.The game also has a hard mode and NG+ that you unlock after beating the game, some nice additions if you want the extra challenge or another run to complete all the entries on the archive.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; The game isn't worth the asking price, but better than alot of the reviews and reviewers give it credit for.The game gives me exactly what I wanted from it: a solid, good looking SRPG.Pros:Combat looks really goodLevel design is goodThe game looks really good in terms of themeI enjoy the world building through collectibles and some item descriptionsControls are lacking a bit, but overall very easy and intuitive to navigateCons:PriceApparently has some issues with the stream deckVarious bugs that will most likely be addressed as the game hasn't been out that longHard Mode unlocked through New Game+I honestly think people are being too harsh, with the majority of early reviews crying in 4k and every other Reviewing video complaining that the characters are bland (ie not taking into account the art style of the game and wanting characters to take a page from FE Colgate protag) and that they're getting stuck/ its too hard (cant change their weapon when there's a very clear option to change weapons when hovering over a character).I don't think this game is for people expecting something similar to modern FE Games.I DO think this game would potentially appeal to fans of the older FE and maybe Tactics Ogre games

_childDocuments_.review: The game has solid fundamentals, the follow-up system feels pretty well though out (though I donno why there needs to be a timed combo thing in an otherwise turn-based game), the accessory/weapon system is basic but gets the job done, there's some minor customization with the skill points, all units having a single self-heal to use the makes you really consider your moves, there are systems which reward quicker play and not relying on suicide strats, all good things.However where I feel the game fails is with its use of the "Elite force of five" instead of a full party, sure you get to rely on each units specific strengths and all that but especially once I made it to Chapter 7 the game really doesn't feel like it was built for such a small party, the maps are massive and teeming with enemies, and with such a small party, limited healing and reliance on the team attacks you really cannot afford to split up too much to cover up more of the map, I'm expected to spend hours scouring every freaking dead-end corner of this map just to get the treasure all the while the "kill boss" objective is there just taunting me, just make it a rout at that point. Which the game so far hasn't given me anything outside of the starting 300 gold which was good for all of one basic weapon from the shop, and a few weapon repair on weapons that weren't completely totaled, sure I missed two chest total among the few maps before, which I would assume at least one of them might have had something to help the finances, and if that is the case then I'm not really so keen on the idea of the collecting the treasure on the maps as being mandatory for the sake of not going bankrupt.I'm guessing also that one of the reasons why I would at least assume they went with the "elite force of five" instead of a larger party was to give everyone more interesting characters and all that, well for my money so far these character about as uninteresting and bland as they get, which does also go for the story and the world, The entire premise of fighting these mindless zombie-goblins instead of actual villains with character doesn't work for me at all.The game has potential and it's hardly the worst I've played and it does have good ideas, but it's just not interesting enough to continue with and I do agree with the general consensus that it's not worth its default price at all.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Redemption Reapers is a tactical game centered around a small group fighting an unending horde and trying to redeem themselves from their black past. If you want a comparison, it would be Fire Emblem-ish.  8/10The music is really good, with a sorrowful theme that accompanies you through the campaign and reflects the situation the characters find themselves in and their past. The sound effects are decent enough. Voice acting is a pleasant surprise and for the most part enjoyable.  7/10I enjoyed the character and enemy design for the most part; while enemies were repetitive for the most part, I think the biggest offender is the map design. Unfortunately, most of the battles are on multi-stage maps, where you go through different sections of cities, wild or in-between. 7/10Fire Emblem meets X-Com tactical missions might be a good idea of what to expect. You have a small team of 5 warriors who face a horde of enemies constantly. In this sense, each of your units covers specific weaknesses and strengths, which means that each battle is a constant use of this to manipulate the enemy into certain attack patterns.The gameplay itself is a loop of this, with the ability to visit the merchant between battles and choose different skills for your characters to improve. Every now and then you are given the option to choose what one of the characters says, but it doesn’t lead anywhere at all, so that was strange. For me, the game has 3 big weaknesses; maps follow the same pattern always: kill all enemies; then you have weapon durability which I have never been too fond of, and even more so here where gold is severely reduced, and lastly, you have only 5 characters to use, where you could have added one or two more to explore more skillsets and expand your options. (Plus, story-wise you are called a brigade, and it seems an odd choice of name for how few Hawks are presented throughout the game).  7/10The story in itself isn’t bad, but I think it could have been explored much more. A mysterious horde of monsters has appeared and destroyed every country in the world and is threatening humanity with extinction. You follow a small ragtag band of misfits who try to do what is right, as the story progresses you learn more about the stories.I feel like there could have been more exploration with survivors from different countries, more characters that appeared, and interactions with citizens, and refugees. Especially in the last third of the game which seems a bit rushed and some characters are introduced, and it doesn’t seem to go anywhere. Similarly, through the story the characters carry this shadow, this regret that taints them, and by the time it is shown what happened, it doesn’t seem like it was really such a big deal, yet everyone vilifies them for that.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the grim aesthetic of this tactics RPG and while it might seem difficult for some, just have to treat it differently than others in the fact that there is no OP unit like Ike/Seth to carry your entire playthrough when you start feeling challenged/make mistakes. Regardless, skirmish exists for when you feel stuck so difficulty can be avoided. Figuring out the ideal formations and then having to readjust when they throw out the different Mort units/reinforcements that can bypass/break your formations at times is EXTREMELY satisfying. Feels way more like a strategy game compared to other titles where you just send your OP unit out alone and farm XP with the occasional enemy hitting their 1% crit rate on a character you're leveling --> soft reset/save scum.Game is not hard, it's just different so need to treat it differently. Each chapter feels like its weening you perfectly into developing new formations to deal with the new enemy types and by the end of the game, it feels like you mastered it even if you really didn't. Also, Ender Lillies.

_childDocuments_.review: Moody, somber atmosphere with an amazing soundtrack. Gameplay is quick and fluid, voice acting for the majority of the cast is superb. Cannot stress how good the soundtrack is, so I'm saying it twice. Maybe this is why it's reminiscent of NieR? Or maybe it's the "weapon stories", which are attached to accessories in the game. Really like those.And here is the first caveat: The story is very simple, and compared to how rich the stories of collectable letters and books are, is a bit of a disappointment! Stuff like a kid poisoning an entire church to "save it from suffering" is wild, and only the tip of the iceberg. The main story has nothing along the likes of these. It's just... going around, fighting a lot... not bad, but expected way more. Some of the sidestory characters are more fleshed out and deeper than the main cast!On the gameplay side, keeping your units together is important, since that way many can attack the same enemy at once. This mechanic kind of makes your army move together and leaves little room for strategies about splitting up. Maps aren't too large, but some have splits - dividing your army or keeping them together is a tough decision.Regarding technical details, graphics settings are quite barebones. Some more resolution settings have been added in a recent patch, which is very welcome! Really wish we could disable motion blur, moving the camera is similar to Final Fantasy Type 0 HD pre-patch. Most of the story is told in static visual novel scenes, and lip-syncing is pretty much non-existent even in the animated ones. Cutscenes are pre-rendered and are not the highest quality.Thankfully chapters have varied objectives, it's not just "KILL EVERY LAST ONE OF THEM!!!". Gold is very tough to come by, every piece matters. Fighting extra skirmishes is not advisable before you unlock ones which reward you with an ingot to sell. Otherwise you could end up with nothing but broken weapons and no way to repair or buy more. Recent patches added more resources to skirmishes, which is a very welcome change.Stat level-ups are random, you can either take no damage from everything for quite a few chapters, or you could die in a hit. Growth rates seem low and that's concerning. You won't do enough damage unless you surround enemies either! It's hectic, but fun early on. Mid-game, not having the right build or weapons or having weak characters hampers you a lot. There are no new RNG-proof characters to help you out unlike in other tactics games. Tried and you can savescum for better level ups at your base, and I'd actually advise you to if you can spare the time. Better than being hard stuck forever.All in all, probably not worth base price unless you like the tone of the game, but if you can look past these flaws, it's really good! Haven't regretted jumping in day 1.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a game that is a bit similar to the older Fire Emblem games, but with a grittier tone, and a smaller cast of characters, that is basically this game, It relies more on each character's unique abilities compared to Fire Emblem as well. The game can be brutally difficult however on Normal difficulty. The newly added Easy Mode is great for people that want to be a bit more chill, and I'd recommend casual Fire Emblem players to play on Easy mode to start with. If you do that, you will enjoy the game a lot more. I'd give it a solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a blast playing this game, if you're a fan of the fire emblem franchise; you might want to check this game out!I think most of the negative reviews comes from people who never played a fire emblem game. This game aims to emulate the formula with a gritty, more mature twist to it. The moment I fired it up, I felt right at home with the stats, mechanics and approach to battle; everything is the fire emblem formula.Where it veers off is that you control only a squad of 5 mercenaries. You have your typical archtypes covered with the fighter, the rogue, the archer, the berserker and your mid range spear wielder. Each character is locked into their own unique class which do not promote. They however unlock new skills every few levels that you can further improve with skill points. So you can build synergies with your different team members which affects how you will position and use them on the battlefield.The difficulty is fair for me. It's the type of game where your squad of 5 needs to overcome an army of 30+ enemies. Healing is limited so you need to use your abilities to bait out the enemies where your team will have the advantage in every encounters. It's important to check the enemy range and damage to plan who will be able to 'tank', so you take as little damage as possible and negate the possibility of counter attacks.I've always seen this type of tactical game as a puzzle to solve and the game does a good job of giving you the tools to overcome the challenges it throws at you. So far, the game stays fresh because they always throw a curve ball at you that will change how you approach battles. Every time you think you found something that works, you can expect a new mechanic that will challenge you to up your game.I like the graphics, they're very detailed for the genre. I like the atmosphere and the more serious approach. It is very linear and railroaded, but I don't see that as a negative. I'm always looking forward to the next map to see how I can use this new skill to develop new strategies around.Overall I'm happy with the game. The mechanics are simple, solid and efficient. It doesn't reinvent anything but mashes different styles of the genre and it works well for me. If you like squad based tactical rpgs and fire emblem games, you'll be right at home with this title.It gets a solid 8/10 for me and I'll be on the lookout for more title from this company.*Bonus points for allowing japanese voice overs and english subs

_childDocuments_.review: Just came around to buying this game.It is a gloomy apocalypse story japanese manga style in a low magic fantasy world.No lightning spamming sorcerers as hero for you!;-)That being said the game is decent and fun.The characters are unique and have their own role. Also quite some background.The missions are hard as you struggle to keep your squad alive and your weapons in good conditions as well as level up.Round based combat is solid and the missions open up more and more later on as for area size and enemy diversity.Crafting, upgrading and unlocking skills are all vital parts of the game.With the latest patches there was a easy mode included.I would rate it "normal" as for how the game plays. You can still lose a squad member during missions in easy mode if you are careless.With the patches the game has gone through there is now plenty possibility to go XP and gear material farming with the inclusion of "skirmishes".You can go through every old unlocked card to earn money and crafting materials as well as some hidden lore if you go through it at least one more time. You can go for specific skirmish missions giving you crafting mats for your axe/sword/dagger/bow/spear and can do them several times.Also to farm XP if you feel you are underpowered.Squad members downed in mission do not die but are not availabe in the mission anymore meaning you need to manage without them.Mission objectives may change slightly depending on who was downed.Skirmish mission can get monotonous but are fast.They are closed at certain time during story missions then wiped and reset with the continuation of your story in another part of the country. So  be sure to save.As for the save game:It is a bit annoying that if you save the save does it at the point right after the mission.Meaning reload leaves you AGAIN with same repairs/skill level ups to do etc.That is pretty annoying and too much console like.Why say SAVE when it is actually just a SAVE POINT?Needs clarification else you rush into the mission again and have not repaired or leveled up you guys.There are some "points of no return". One around level 14-15. You will have several missions before you can use the skirmishes to farm XP or materials again.And then only after the point of return with then unlocked mission areas.There are quite some difficulty spikes at some points so it might be wise to reload and grind some skirmishes.The first foray into the mines is one such point.Difficulty ramps up quite a bit there.For some reason the intro stutters tremendously almost to the point that you fear the game does not proceed.Sequences later run more smoothly but still have some little performance hickups spoiling a bit of the nicely made sequence movies.Definitely needs some polishing in the video parts. If that would greatly enhance the game feel.As for the asking price:Picked the game up at 50% off and it is well worth the 25 Euro.I would not say it is worth the 50 Euro it normally costs.Too much "normal" round tactic stuff and good but not great combat.What pushes things is the story and the good voice actors and the very good soundtrack of the game.So I give it a 7 out of 10 total.For the discounted price. Full price would be too much for what is offered.So if you are looking for some decent fantasy round themed RP-Squad game with a bit of a gloomy apocalypse setting - go for it!I am having fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun and great game the got buried at release with a barrage of negative of middling reviews and that's really a shame.At the moment of writing this review the game has been thoroughly patched and the price was permanently cut in half which really makes this game an easy recommendation for anyone who was on the fence when it released.It's a grim dark game TRPG with Fire Emblem mechanics while forgoing the relationship aspects of that game and focusing more on the strategic gameplay.It's about a small mercenary group fighting against all odds and reflects that in it's gameplay.Resources are scarce, your weapons degrade and the amount of enemies just keep icreasing.Rarely can you drop an enemy with one hit which requires from the player careful positioning so you can chain attack with an adjacent unit to make the most if your squad. Combined with various skills you can upgrade and an expanding selection of weapons this makes for an really engaging game.I'd recommend the game to anyone who likes a bit of challenge in their TRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game for ppl looking for a dark story or who enjoy gridbased tactics style games. As a disclaimer, if you're expecting this to be 3D FFT it's nowhere close to that deep. What it IS is a slow-burn style dark tacticalRPG with generally cool looking combat effects (although they do get a bit repetitive). The story was fine, some stuff doesn't really get fleshed out super well, but it wasn't hot garbage like so many modern games. I would say if your bar is set by late 90s early 2000s RPGs, the story is average, if your bar is set to modern times the story is above average, nothing phenomenal, but solid. For people saying the combat is super hard, they clearly didn't take the time to read skill descriptions or pay attention to the enemy move distance, I played this first on normal then on hard, the game literally lets you toggle on enemy move/attack range and you can easily use that to bait towards your tanks and work your way through pretty much every map.It does not require grinding if you manage your main story combat well and keep your characters evenly leveled, however if you want to get every item and most of the skills high or maxed, then you'll want to do some of the side "skirmishes", these also help with extra gold and resources so you're not babying your higher power weapons (since all weapons have relatively limited durability).The main protagonist is technically Sarah, so if you want a female lead this DOES have that, that said it's really more of a story about the whole group and while it's told from her perspective, it doesn't really have the limitations that would normally be associated with a single POV, which is good because she's actually the most bland of the characters aside from maybe Urs.TLDR, decent game, nothing amazing, but also above average for what it is, manages to find a middle ground between triple A (not quite as pretty or polished) and Indie (cool concepts but limited resources).For people that are trying it out: ACTUALLY LEARN THE COMBAT SYSTEM, IT'S NOT HARD, LOOK AT ENEMY MOVEMENT/ATTACK AREAS, LOOK AT HIT %s, BOTH OF THESE ARE MADE SUPER AVAILABLE BY THE DEVS, DON'T COMPLAIN IT'S HARD IF YOU'RE LITERALLY DISCARDING THE FREELY GIVEN TOOLS OF THE COMBAT SYSTEM, ITS A TACTICS GAME SO USE TACTICS LOL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is linear in every way.-No side missions (unless you count "skirmishes", which is just replaying previous maps). -No character choice. You use the same 5 characters throughout.-No tactical variation - the same tactics are what you will use for pretty much every map. That is my main gripe, I wish combat had more variation.-Dialog choice is there, though it makes no difference in the story. It does impact whether you unlock character codex entries, so be aware of that if you want to see all of those.-No spoilers, but the story is quite straightforward, no real surprises. I did enjoy it at least. Especially the ending. A lot of people hated the ending, but I wish more devs had the balls to end games like that.-No real gear variation, you get weapons as you progress and the selection is fairly standard. You can miss certain weapons if you do not A rank maps, so be aware of this if you want all of them. The camp menu has a prominent x/255 inventory capacity text. Which I always found very funny, because even if you got every weapon, accessory, and item, you would not even use half of that space. I think they added it because it looks like Fire Emblem lol?-The achievements are straightforward. I played the game without any grinding or trying to get achievements, and I ended up missing only two of them, which would have required probably 5 hours of grinding (no thanks) to get the lvl 40 achievement.-Not really very difficult. I went through the game on Normal (you unlock hard after beating the game) without needing to do any skirmishes. I lost only once, and only because it was a protect the NPC map where the dumb AI NPC ran into enemies. I got A rank on almost every map. So the game is not too hard once you figure out the optimal tactics. I do think the game walks a nice line on difficulty. They should have let hard difficulty be selected from the start, I have no desire to replay the game on the harder difficulty.-Gameplay and abilities are simplistic. Nothing new here whatsoever. There is not any sort of weapon triangle or other exploiting weakness systems as far as I can tell.-The enemy and NPC AI... pretty awful. Just bad.-The graphics are the high point. It feels like a mix of modern graphics, and PS2 era CGI somehow. Character models are pretty nice IMO. Though they clearly reused the model and face for the two commanders in the game, Rowen and some guy at the end I can't recall. It is easy to see, especially when they talk to each other,. Not sure how that was let through considering how good and varied the rest were.I would not pay more than 20 bucks for the game (I think I got it from a Humble Bundle or Choice). I finished it, and don't regret my time, so I suppose I recommend it. But it is a close call - if I had reviewed it before the first half was done, I probably would have not recommended it.The game could have been a great one if they had variation. Especially character, combat, and skill variation would have really put the game over. Too bad, it feels mostly like a missed opportunity

_childDocuments_.review: Took a look at  AD-globe creation Redemption Reapers, published by Binary Haze. What I liked, what I feel needs to improve. Let's get to it.What I enjoyed:Animation: Wonderful cut scenes and terrific action sequences that fit the genre they are doing. Good startAesthetics: Nice layouts, controls, utilizing classic game design. Sounds: Professional voice acting, music, sounds, and sfx. Straight Forward: a direct sequence that is pretty easy to follow. Giving you goals, sequences, and easy line of sight of what you should do. Controls: Not awful, move, attack, change gear, switching characters are easy that any teen can follow.Dark Fantasy: Look zombies, Undead, whatever, the game does fit the genre it presents, in its classic anime designed characters and enemies.Isometric: A standard for the past 40 years that has become a mainstay in gaming. (BUT)Gear: Upgrading, resources and combination sequencing in your chess moves matter.Brigade: Despite individual movements, this is about combination set-up for the entire brigade.Challenge: The difficulty settings will punish mistakes. What I feel needs to improve:Nothing New: Dear god, how many times must I say it, Isometric is fine, but learn from what has been done. Mordheim made a while back continues to be the prototype of turn base games in that it puts you into the action in war-band game-play using the setting as your experience. All this work and your not even part of that action. ShameVS system: Done to death bringing nothing new to turn base mechanics. Skill tree abilities is merely enhancing point damage differentials. Keeps the player at a distance: Grow or die. All this work on cut scenes, actions, yet you in battle is kept at a huge distance. Learn from Mordheim, third person turn base using the environment settings so the player feels they are part of those cut scenes. Let down for me. Durability: Its wasted here, and not really necessary. Neither is the merchant.Upgrading system: Not diverse enough, very bland.Blood: If you are squeamish to even fake blood, a caution on the splatter end moves. Doesn't both most, but to some it might. There should always be a no-gore option in games. They never learn My final thoughts:Redemption Reapers joins a long list of turn base games that really does not bring anything new to the genre. I applaud the hard work and the execution for it does a lot right than wrong, but is that enough anymore as we see these types of games constantly released. If your going to invest in such a game. Make it truly innovative. Its not that think Mordheim is some wonderful game, it has many flaws, but getting players in Third Person, using a great developing environment that puts the player in the action, climbing, jumping, making you feel you are those characters is something no one is picking up in turn base mechanics. Its foolish. You must grow beyond isometric. The point is a lot is lost in Redemption Reapers that keeps you at a safe distance. Reapers will come and go with no real impact and many games are like this. A wonderful fantasy turn based genre that does give you the mood of what they are creating, but the game play is redundant and boring at times. A positive thumbs up for all the moving parts in this game work and work well, It is a good game, and its lack of creativity missed out on being a great game. See the video game-play to see if this game is for you. My score 3.2 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: Redemption Reapers deserves a wider audience than the one I feel it has gotten. This is a solid and for the most part excellent TBS RPG. The combat once learned becomes second nature, positioning your team to maximise the synergy and number of attacks between all 5 of the Ashen Hawk Brigade per round. Combat has a cinematic flare at times and the whole game plays out like a slick Japanese anime. A game about fighting an unbeatable foe.It has its issues, mostly for me with the weapon degradation and high repair cost, mixed with the tight economy that at times is taken away from you throughout the story. Leaving you fighting against the games systems as well as the games enemies. The RPG elements are partly out of your control lessening the RPG aspect a bit.All in all though a game i would recommend if you liked games like Othercide or X-com.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a solid game. Story was dark and straight forward. Game play was nothing ground breaking for the genre of Strategic RPGS but maintains the solid core game play of the genre. Music is very fitting to the theme of the game. Voice acting for the game was really good. It becomes more apparent as the story progresses and you see artistically why the characters are the way they are. AI of the enemy is smart enough to know if it can eliminate a unit. It won't hold back either if it can kill a unit it will.  So don't think you can bait it with injured armored units to ignore the less defensive ones. Units however don't suffer from perma death however if you loose a unit some scenario objectives change. For example if you were originally just suppose to get across to a bridge or a location as the objective loosing a unit changes it to enemies have to be defeated as you need to ensure the lost unit can safely be moved. The semi difficulty of the game is its weapon system which is punishing at times if you don't stay on top of repairs and maintenance. My suggestion is to ensure each character has three weapons at any give time just in case. It might be a down side for some but the thing to keep in mind is that this game is a story first and foremost. Character customization doesn't exist and each character has a specific play style attuned to them and their background. Its not like other SRPGS that have job systems or you can build a character different from its portrayal. Personally I didn't see this a draw back as it helps may you more understanding of the characters on a personal level as well as better understand why they have the conections/reliance on the characters they interact with.If you are into SRPGS then I would suggest getting the game. If its on sale then it is a definite pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an artfully crafted game that is a whole lot of fun. _childDocuments_.review: Great game so far. I've seen some pre-release critics about not being possible to replay older missions or maps, but that's not true. The game has a skirmish option that lets you play previous maps to earn extra XP and whatnot.The story and characters are indeed a bit generic, but the same can be said for any Fire Emblem entry and they never get that same level of scrutiny.As for the strategy aspect of it, characters have moves that shuffle enemies across spaces, as well as the ability to gang up on an enemy if they are adjacent to an attacking enemy. I haven't got too many skills so far, but I expect that there will be more skills that interact with the map and tiles in that way. I really liked that because i feel positioning is sometimes under-explored in tactics games.I've played with japanese voice-over so far, and the va is very good. I'm not sure if the English VA was the one they lip-synced for, but it sometimes the lip-syncing looks a little weird in japanese.Stats are easy to understand(although I would like to have a button to explain what each stats do), you can see the forecast of what increasing a certain attribute will improve in your character stats.I'm interested to know what will happen in the story, and what kind of upgrades my characters will get for them. The pricing might be a little high for some people(I think shaving 10$ out of it would make people much happier and permissive to its shortcomings as it isn't an AAA game by any means), but there's local pricing for Brazil which makes it 30% cheaper than in PS4 or XBOX.

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent, but rough around the edges with an ugly generic font used for much of the text in the game, voice overs lacking much emotion, semi-decent but cheesy cutscenes, and a story that avoids giving details that would be meaningful to the player until far too late.That and it's a REALLY shameless rip-off of fire emblem with a huge amount of its mechanics ripped straight from the FE series. _childDocuments_.review: *VOICE ACTING*: One of Redemption Reaper's few redeeming qualities is the vocal talent it employed. It's amazing that a game like this somehow managed to land the triple-A cast of David Lodge, Lucien Dodge, Allegra Clark, and Kyle McCarley.*DIALOGUE*: Awful and abundant. Takes itself way too seriously. Lugh and Karren's endless diatribe of snide remarks made listening a chore. I found myself skipping dialogue after four or five chapters. Reminder to all aspiring writers out there that the Sasuke Uchiha character has been utilized several thousands of times more than it needed to be across all media. Think of something else. Writing a character this way is lazy writing. Same goes for writing wimpy characters like Naki whose entire character is 'My Dad Died in the Zombie Apocalypse.' That sucks, but you're in a Fire Emblem rip-off, kid. Everyone's dad is dead. Grow up.*PLOT*: Why is any of this happening? Events are poorly explained, which compounds with low-effort writing into more incentives for the player to just hold the B-button any time any character opens his or her mouth.*CINEMATICS*: Appealing to the eye, but lacking in foundation due to poor story-telling, world building, plot, and character development.*GAMEPLAY*: Zero attempts made to deviate from or transform the Fire Emblem formula. Ordinarily, I would not compare one game to another so readily, but since this is a blatant case of *'you can copy my homework but try not to make it look like you copied my homework,'* I really have no choice but to criticize in this vein. Choices imposed on the player (such as prioritizing chests/pick-ups, utilizing veins, etc.) are completely risk-free. The player is seldom punished for making mistakes. Legit Fire Emblem Heroes with zombies. Soloing Sacred Stones with Seth requires better mechanics than Redemption Reapers. Dodge tanking the game with Sarah by Chapter 3, anyone?*MAP DESIGN*: Not compelling in the slightest. 90% of enemies do not aggro until you step into range. Play the zone, bait enemies with a tank, reduce damage using Martyr so even enemy berzerkers do 1 damage on their initiation, kill everything on player phase, rinse and repeat. Most objectives are rout or kill boss. Ambush spawns are not thoughtful in placement or timing, and usually do not pose a significant threat as a result. I am convinced that no one at this studio bothered to play-test the game.*OTHER THOUGHTS*: Don't buy Redemption Reapers unless it's on sale for 60% off minimum and you have nothing else to do. Purchasing for $50 would be a waste of money. Redemption Reapers had a lot of potential, but I feel the experience fell short due to lack of polish and play-testing. Disappointing because I had anticipated this release for some time.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few hours in and I'm shocked that this game has mixed reviews. It's fantastic. Mechanically, it is one of the freshest tactics games I've played in a long time. It uses an AP economy system, but strips movement from it. This means a character can always move a set distance (pending on how fast they are) per turn. Along the way, they can spend AP on actions. As they level up, characters gain new actions. In practice, this means your characters are moving through the battlefield, stopping mid-movement to do something (attack an enemy, open a chest, use a special move, etc.) and then continuing their movement after. Coupled with a mechanic that allows for allies adjacent to the enemy to take attacks of opportunity, It creates a real sensation of momentum that other turn based games frequently struggle with. You have a unit charge a weakened enemy, finish them off, then still slide into position next to another enemy while your next unit lines up a swing on that foe, allowing the first unit you moved to make a follow up attack there. Its deeply satisfying to execute on these kinds of combos.The narrative themes of the game are also reflected in the mechanics, which is always nice to see. Even within each individual character, who they are is well codified mechanically, as well as that character's inner conflict. I particularly enjoy Lugh, who has one possible skill choice of being a "lone wolf" where he gets a damage bump when not adjacent to allies and also a "martyr" power, which allows him to protect characters near him. The fact that you have an early choice to throw points into either of those skills is not only an interesting choice that will change the way the character is used as a unit on the battlefield, but its also deftly communicating something about Lugh as a person.  Narratively, there's some flatness/clunky exposition to the writing in the early-going, but the characters are interesting, the voice acting is elevating the material more often than not, and the overall concept opens up a lot of possibility.Redemption Reapers also straddles a really interesting line between being a "puzzle" tactics game like Into the Breach, and a more classic tactics game like Othercide or XCOM. So far, it seems to be getting the best of both worlds. If you enjoyed the score on Ender Lillies, the music here won't disappoint either. Difficulty wise, the game is keeping me on my toes without dipping into full throated frustration. It feels well tuned on that front, with money being scarce and equipment being hard to come by and fragile. My one nitpick is that the game is clearly designed for console/controllers, making the mouse/keyboard UI feel a bit off. The follow up attacks is where this is most notable, but this is an easy fix (I just need a PC controller that works lol.)I'm seeing plenty of the less generous reviews based around price point. My copy is a review copy but I'm considering a double dip to have it on console. I think its well worth its current price, and price point isn't really what we should be judging a game on anyway. The work exists outside what is currently being charged for it.I'll be putting more time into this and sharing further thoughts on the Gamers With Jobs Conference Call, Episode 855. That'll drop March 1st. Thanks all, hope this is helpful for folks.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: Generic and uninteresting.Characters: Bland and unimaginative. There's only one archer and the rest are melee fighters. Few characters. For a brigade, this unit has very few soldiers. It's a team, and not even a platoon (two teams or more). Controls: Terrible with a keyboard and mouse. Have to use hotkeys instead of clicking on mouse for most actions. Can't escape battles to go to the main screen to save. Also, can't zoom in on characters or rotate the point of view. For a strategy game on PC,  that's as bad as it gets. Gameplay: Repetitive. No cover system, no flanking, no shields, no 3D terrain, no blocking, only dodging. I do, however, like the combo system and positioning of units that gives extra attacks from your other teammates. Graphics: I expected better. They should have focused on the maps, character stills and gameplay animations instead of uninteresting cutscenes. The graphics settings could have been higher. UI: Simple layout, but still clunky, especially for levelling up and inventory. I don't like the font or aesthetics either. Sound: The music is good, but the feeling is mostly moody and melancholic. It has a depressing feel to it. The voice acting is extremely generic. Has little passion. The voices themselves are pleasing enough. The writing is run-of-the-mill. Conclusion: I do not recommend purchasing this game at full price. I wouldn't entirely avoid the game, but it's quite boring compared to what I thought it would be. The trailers fooled me, to say the least. Also, I'm just desperate for any good tactical, turn-based squad game.Disclaimer: I haven't played the game as much as I should have for a review, but the game just has not captivated my interest at all. I might try it out again, but not for now.

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Cut-scenes are good; visual novel elements are good; character design is good (although it's not going to win any diversity awards); really no bugs I noticed.The bad: The AI is limited.  It will always go for your weakest character (DPS), which means you'll just go slower with your tanks in front, which results in very slow and predictable game play.  The Glenn character is given a first-shot-invulnerability skill early on which just means you will always run him in front.  The meh: The story is okay (anyone who's seen GoT is going to wonder why these ppl are whining about one bad battle from 2y ago every step of the way - like once or twice gets the point across).  The economics (weapon repair absorbs a lot of money) which doesn't add much.  The crafting is okay, but you end up w/these brittle 1-shot weapons at the end, but they're so expensive to repair you won't use them unless you... grind.  I don't feel like grinding as a mechanic is necessary in 2023+ or particularly fun.  I'd prefer to have a chance without it so it's an option rather than a requirement.Net-net: This is probably a good time-passing Tactical TBS to play on your steam deck while you're killing time.  Otherwise there are better options for those seeking a more tactics from their TBS.

_childDocuments_.review: When my friend mentioned that Redemption Reapers was directed by Masayuki Horikawa -- the same guy who directed Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance and Shadow Dragon -- I immediately put it on my wishlist. This was definitely a good choice! I think in some ways, RR is on par with the likes of Path of Radiance or Shadow Dragon. It's proof positive that great SRPGs are still being created; the genre isn't dead, but you just need to know where to look.Redemption Reapers is a very competently-designed SRPG at its core. Its battles are all filled out with lots of side objectives and challenging enemies. The battle system is clearly what you'd expect from a classic SRPG, but it also does its own spin on things like team attacks, weapon upgrading, character-specific abilities, and the like. Resource management is finely-tuned, forcing the player to actually budget their gold and materials intelligently -- this is more than you could say of Path of Radiance and its ridiculous amount of free money that it gives to its players. When it comes to gameplay, RR has a lot going for it.On the presentation side, the game features good voice acting, cutscenes, graphics, music, and a polished UI which you'd expect of a AAA game. It's all great, making for a gritty game with a grim and bleak atmosphere. I did find one bug, which is that if the game freezes or crashes, there's no "autosave" feature which allows you to return where you left off. This was a bit frustrating because it forced me to redo the entirety of chapter 9; my game froze right as I was about to fight the boss.While the gameplay has many great things about it, I had one fundamental disappointment: namely, that the entire playable cast consisted of only 5 units. This one problem, in turn, caused several other minor ones. For example, several chapters feature NPC units with downright moronic AI. This is a 2023 SRPG -- has AI really not gotten any better since the 1990s? Another relevant question is, "why couldn't we control these NPCs ourselves, especially given the dearth of playable units?" Certain chapters in the late game are way more challenging than even the final boss, and the main reason for this is that the game doesn't give you a good way to counter magic. Again, this problem could've been solved by giving us more playable units, such as a magic-oriented one. Among other things, the game also lacks the replay value of Path of Radiance or Shadow Dragon, due to its paltry playable cast. Even when compared to its contemporaries like Lost Eidolons or King Arthur: Knight's Tale, the number of playable units here is pitiful.There was also one big problem I had with the storytelling, which is that the game never really tells you about where the Mort came from, or what their goal is. I get that the devs were going for a survival horror, zombie apocalypse themed atmosphere. That's cool, but it shouldn't detract from the story. The Mort are the ONLY enemies for the ENTIRE game, so their impact on the story -- both on an emotional and worldbuilding level -- is dulled due to their unexplained nature and motives. Sure, The Walking Dead did this too, but it's equally lazy storytelling there. Redemption Reapers probably could've done well to be more like Resident Evil, which features zombies and survival horror as the main focus, but still provides context and lore for those who are interested. ...So it's not perfect, but that's fine. (Path of Radiance was far from perfect too, yet I still consider it a classic.) Likewise, Redemption Reapers is a great SRPG. The entire game took me 16.5 hours (including some idling) to finish the game on normal, then another hour to fill out the achievements on a Newgame+. Next, I'll have to finish the game on hard. That should be fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Yep, definitely an tactical RPG game.For me, this genre can be split into two categories: one where it is fun to figure out a OP combination of team setups to break the game, and the other being focused more on survival, where I am barely scrapping by each chapter. This game falls under the latter.You're given a finite amount of resources and different ways to spend those resources. It's fun trying to weigh the pros/cons for each option to find out the best one to help survive.To list some examples of what I mean:There's a lot of inspiration from FE Path of Radiance/Radiant Dawn here so if you like the gameplay loop of those games, I think you'll like this game too. The soundtrack in this game was surprisingly pretty great too.Character level ups work similar to FE. Each character has a specific growth rate for each stat and rng decides if you get a +1 in the stat on level up. Fortunately, booster items that give +2 stat do drop pretty frequently so it can help cover for poor rng.The story started off pretty interesting but kind of just ended near the end leaving me with unanswered questions with the lore. Honestly, don't expect much from the story. There was literally no character progression as well.The team size is very small. I was kind of expecting the usual FE mechanics where you can recruit more characters and decide which character to deploy on each map. Unfortunately, you're stuck with a total of 5 units for the entire game, and that really takes out some of the strategy in deciding who to bring for each chapter.The AI of guest NPCs are terrible. On chapters where you need to protect and escort them, it can be pretty frustrating to babysit them while still trying to finish the chapter quick enough to get the bonus EXP and also grabbing every loot on the map. It would have been nice to be able to influence where they move via direct commands or changing their generic tactics AI.They've patched in a NG+ mode, but there isn't enough incentive to make a 2nd play-through worth it. For reference, I've played through 3/4 of a NG+ run, and I haven't seen any new cutscenes or different routes. There are no new weapons or items that changes the combat up too. Once I got the last of the achievements, I just stopped.Overall I did enjoy my time with the game. This game is definitely hard. I'd say the difficulty is a tad bit easier than a maniac mode in FE game. It was very rewarding when I got through a chapter without losing a unit. The music was great, but I feel like they ran out of time near the end to properly resolve the story.I'd give this a solid 7.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is "ok" if you buy it at an discount (got mine for 30 Dollars). I feel thats a fair price.However, i must say that the "follow Up" System is kind of strange.  It seemed like a nice concept in the first missions, but as i progressed, it got really clear that you MUST use this as your only tactic with every enemy    a l l   t h e   t i m e ...  LEt me explain :What this System does : When you attack an enemy, and another of your Heroes is in Attack Range, he will get one attack for free. Which means, that in the best case you can attack a unit which is surrounded by up to 4 other heroes, and all will attack. (Some Weapons have longer Range too, and your heroes have unlimited "follow Up" attacks which means they can attack multiple times during a turn.This sounds nice, but is SO DAMN STRONG that every other tactic you might consider is useless compared to this. Also, there is no "Zone of Control" , limiting your tactics, due to the enemy AI which is very predictable. As long as you stay outsite of their attack range , they wont move unless they are scripted by the story to do so.  If you move inside their range, they will move and attack you. Which is incredible exploitable...  The Game was said to be really difficult according to the reviews, but i had really not a single difficult situation during my playtime up to now. I think thats because i was using the "obvious" tactic : Sent you "Tank" within attack range of the enemy, and make him "defend" (he can even counterattack doing so). If you skill him "right" with damage reduction , he will pretty much not take damage doing so.  Well, and then let the enemies come to him, and move your other heroes who waited 2 tiles further away in attack position and just murder more or less anything with the follow up system.  And repeat this with EVERY enemy, it gets boring really fast...Also the "item" system is strange.  I get what they where going for, with durability and stuff.  But it makes no sence :D There is NO reason to equip a weapon that does 5 damage and has durability of 50, when you can use one that does 9 damage (and might oneshot an enemy) and has 30 durability. (usually you have, with the right Skills, more than 100% "ToHit" with both weapons. Both will last for the whole mission, and you have to repair them anyways....All this does is make you replay some missions to get enough money for the repairs. Classic "TimeWaste" mechanic.What that game really needs , should there every be a "Part 2" (beside the "grind mechanics" to me removed ^^ ) are more "decisions" in combat. (which skill to use, where to position your units, how to protect certain units and so on... )  As it is now, there is one obvious tactic that overshadows everything else and makes every other tactic uselessStill, its an "ok" game, but i would wish it was a little bit deeper...  I give it a positive review ( IF you can get it at a 50% discount, 50 bucks is WAY to much) , but its not exaktly my cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: Still not worth 30 euro.So this game got a lot of backlash on release because it was initially overpriced at 50 euro. Now it's on sale for 30 euro and people seem to warm more up to it. I still think 30 euro is way too much for this game and honestly 20 euro would still be a lot to pay for it.The big selling point is the squad-based combat that is seen as hardcore and requires you to spend a lot of time to understand. My gripe is that even though the combat is definitely the best part of the game, it still have a lot of issues which I am going to explain in the following:Eventually you'll have 5 characters in your team, each with their abilities. You have a stoic frontline warrior, a dodgy knifeuser, a strongwilled archer, a cringeinducing but powerful spearwielder and the team-leader, another frontline warrior but who's not nearly as strong as the other.When a battle starts, all of your enemies are scattered across the map. You'll have to organize your team so you can take each of the smaller groups one at a time. The trick to the combat is that if one of your characters attack an enemy, allies will get follow-up attacks, if they stand within the enemies reach. That's a nice way to make the combat a little challenging, and if you can figure out how to get your spearwarrior within melee range and then have someone else attack the enemies, he'll be able to clear the field eventually.My gripe with the combat is that the follow-up mechanic, seems to be the only thing it really has going for it. There is nothing in regards to seeking cover from archers, no attacks of opportunity and so far my archer haven't gotten an overwatch ability either (may come later as I haven't finished the game) - I don't demand those abilities in all tactical games, but at least have something interesting going for it. In my opinion, the biggest issue the combat got is, that you get to engage each group of enemies one at a time. You enter a map where you are apparently at war with the supposed orc-like enemies but your team gets to kill 2-5 orcs at a time, while the other orcs are twiddling their thumbs and looking at their enemies getting hacked down until it's their turn. Not only does that take away from immersion, it also makes the combat feel less hardcore than all the yay-sayer make it out to be.With this game having nothing but the combat going for it, I really can't recommend it, especially at 30 euro. If you want a fun squad-based game then purchase The Dungeon of Nahelbeuk. Not only does it have more interesting combat, there are also way more entertaining characters and a more interesting story - and you can get that game right now at a meagre 12,24 euro.
