_childDocuments_.review: I quite like the game. It doesn't have many graphical options but it does support up to 4k on PC unlike the other review stated. Turn on VsynC because its locked to 60 anyways and it does tear. Part of the difficulty is knowing how to position your units properly to use their skills rather just pre building them to be unstopable like the more recent FEs. Your builds impact what type of positing will work best for you. It really feels like you're an elite force fighting against an unending horde. I quite like the setting too, where most everything is ♥♥♥♥ most of the time. Some people might not, but I adore that kind of atmosphere. The voice acting is a little bit of a mixed bag leaning heavily towards good. All the talent is great (including Geralt and Dorathea from 3 houses voicing two of your 5 party members), and do their roles well. Believe I heard 3 houses' felix as a character as well. The problem is sometimes the voice direction is just a bit off making them say things that don't match the situation. 99% of the time this happens during cutscenes. Characters talk quite a bit as just static images or during combat and all those lines and delivered perfectly. One particular character's (not one of your party members) voice just does not match his body/face at all, and can be a bit overbearing at times but its nothing too bad.I'm a bit sad this game isn't getting the recognition it deserves via sales or reviews so maybe watch some gameplay before deciding. If it looks interesting to you, give it a shot if you can, at least on sale. It hits the right spots for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Still new to the game and like others, I'm writing this more in response to the oddly bad reviews for this, its 50 bucks yeah, but it has great visuals and atmosphere, I love a good gothic/dark atmosphere,on top of the great music score.I don't understand the hate.Like I see once person negatively compare this to fire emblem engage,this is better than engage,  easily for me.It's lacking in some of the qol, but has other areas it innovates in,its darker, shows blood,  and keeps a consistent tone.if you want a good tactical rpg, without the goofy add ons this is for you.edit:5 hours in found my first issue, what the heck is this balance,5 of us, against 12, ok fine.in this fight they get not 1, not 2, but THREE WAVES of reinforcements!?!i can take extra actions after attacking which is cool, but I never have enough gauge to attack again...On top of my ranged unite having apparently half the range of the enemy range units,having to get within 3 tiles to engage and not even enough mobility leftover to get out of their attack range.I can't  attack more than once per turn 90% of the time, I can't out run thembecause they move just as far as I do, and theres effing 20 against 5.its a tactics game,  I'm supposed to play smart and leverage my advantages against the enemy.  YOU NEED TO GIVE ME ADVANTAGES.some gimmick or mechanic I can use,give me a regular attack that doesn't take ap/skill points,let me rest to heal a small amount, on turns I don't engage w the enemy,don't let the enemy move just as far as my fastest unit. give me SOMETHING!and the healing portal, let that refill the entire team draught not just the person that gets it!I can't get the character that needs it most to the portal, they obviously can't move freely.this could be an amazing game but we need more than this.triple edit:I still recommnd this btw,  had to babymode chapter 5but the following story was interesting.quadruple edit:ok so clearly I raged a bit, at a section that forced me to take things slower than I like,but  after I raged I went back in, beat it, and played for like 5 more hours.I'd give this game a 7 out of 10.if they give it some qol love with some patches, and they do it right I could bump it up to a 8-9.I bought this game yesterday with both hope and some reservations going into it,and I've put in close to 20 hours in the 2 days I've had it. lolThere's a lot of potential in this game, and clearly a lot of heart as well.Final edit:ok after the 24 hour mark and I can't honestly recommend this game.Before it was at a level where, yeah it had issues, but none that impeded,ability to play the game or enjoy the game.But the system balance is BAD.its clear they ran out of money or time, and that would be fineif it was complete/up  to standard.but while it isn't a problem early on, the balance is horrendous.at mid game, enemy levels jump up like 5 levels between stages.While your exp gain doesn't keep up, my team is lvl 10-12 against lvl 20s,that one shot half my team one on one.now here's the issue, that alone is wouldn't be an issue,IF it was possible to grind for levels, but the non story grinding modeoffers little benefit.In addition you have a weapon durability system, that is 1 to 1. -_-30% equals 30 attacks, when it takes multiple to take out most enemies.and it costs gold to repair it.  fine. except...you can't get gold in skirmish mode, you also can't get the bonus reserve exp,that you receive from completing a level in story modeSo   skirmish mode is the only way to get more exp,  but it costs you severely to grind it, as your best weapons will become unusable and need to be repaired.But the mode doesn't give you the gold you need to make said repairs.Also exp gain  from on level or lower level enemies is TINYcompared to what you eventually need to level up.These problems compound to make skirmish mode COMPLETELY irrelevant very fast, while its meant to supplement the player its actually more of a detriment.So you need levels or strength but are unable to get it, making it functionally unplayable. and that's not even touching on the bad merchant system...`I've thought about it extensively and I just have no way forward anymore, I can't get through the stage.  I could grind for 10 hours, but then all my weapons  would be dustedI can "PROBABLY" scrap together enough gold after the fact to repair just 1 main weapon for each character but I shouldn't have to do that, I'm NOT going to do that. I enjoyed the honeymoon phase, it has good points, but everything weighing it down,makes the game literally unplayable once you progress far enough. I TRULY hope they fix this, because everything wrong with it has relatively simple fixes,it just needs time and effort.  But until those things are fixed I cannot recommend or even play this.another edit: ...I tried again and beat it.I give up on trying to categorize this game, it has issues, it has difficulty,I can't tell how much of the rage is bad balance or carefully crafted scenarios that will force your brain to the limit.I just don't know,.....ok it has  non-static stat growth on level up unlike fire emblem engage,and you're able to suspend battle and pick have it auto save and pack up right at the turn you left.I feel like Im starting to understand this game better.you can pretty much fully customize your  characters playstyle that way,seems very much an old school type of trpg....I'm thinking this is actually a good game.the core gameplay feels very good, and I've been complely unable to put this thing down.and now that I know I could have been min maxing my growth I almost feel like starting a new playthrough just to see what I can do.....ok it doesn't have a quit button, so you can't actually min max stat growth,they really need to add that, it'd improve things a lot.and a confirmation on the restart  button so you don't accidentally restart.

_childDocuments_.review:
Descending suddenly on the world, the macabre Mort armies destroy nation after nation, leaving humanity decimated in their wake. Among the forces resisting the Mort is a small band of mercenaries known as the Ashen Hawk Brigade.

Redemption Reapers is a dark fantasy simulation game set in a medieval world. Be immersed in the tale of the desperate struggle between the Ashen Hawk Brigade and the terrifying Mort legions.

With despair looming as the menacing Mort horde marches ever closer, help your small resistance defeat the enemy masses by bringing together a rich variety of character builds and a meticulous strategy. Experience the exhilaration as you rise up to overcome the odds and achieve victory!

name: Once Human
detailed_description: Join our Discord! About the Game [Version 1.3] NEW PVE SCENARIO Survive Together, Thrive Together! Version 1.3 introduces the new PvE scenario 'The Way of Winter.' A new survival mechanic, Temperature, makes survival more challenging than ever! Collaborate with your friends to build and upgrade the Thermal Tower. Team up now to explore the new map, face mighty bosses, secure new deviations, and discover even more exciting content! The apocalypse changed everything. Human, animal, plant… all are infested by an alien creature – Stardust. As a Meta-Human, you can survive the contamination and use the power of Stardust. Play alone or join others to fight, build and explore. When the world is in chaos, you are our last hope. Survive in the wilderness You wake up in the middle of nowhere. You'll have to brace yourself for the cruelty of nature (from monsters to lack of food); however, Stardust's influence does not restrict to living things, it also affects the soil and water. Eating polluted food and drinking dirty water will reduce your Sanity. When your Sanity drops, your max HP would drop accordingly. To eat or not to eat, it's a question. Fight against monsters Battle numerous enemies that are once human, and challenge bosses from another dimension to gain powerful items and ease Stardust pollution. You are not only fighting for yourself, but also fighting for the survivors. Customize weapons With about 100 gun blueprints divided into seven categories for you to collect and craft, every loot grants you something new. Did I mention accessories and gun perks? Right, they are the heroes here. If our current weapon cannot satisfy your need, you can add different parts and perks, upgrade your firearm to your heart's content. Build territory Use Territory Core to build a house of your own. You can keep a practical style, jamming everything needed in a small room; or you can design a townhouse with a patio, kitchen, garage… The best part is, you can relocate your territory any time you want! Find out the truth Delve into the truth of Stardust, find out where it came from, and what it wants. In the journey of seeking truth, you may feel alone, but you are never alone. There are several factions in the world, some can be violent and hostile, others might be friendly and helpful. Explore human settlements to learn their stories or exterminate bosses without leaving a name for survivors to praise, the choices are yours.

short_description: Once Human is a multiplayer open-world survival game set in a strange, post-apocalyptic future. Unite with friends to fight monstrous enemies, uncover secret plots, compete for resources, and build your own territory. Once, you were merely human. Now, you have the power to remake the world.

_childDocuments_.review: As an enthusiast of modern gaming technologies, I was very disappointed to find out that "Once Human" does not support ray tracing. While the game offers an interesting survival horror experience in an open world, the lack of realistic lighting and shadows detracts from the overall impression. The graphics are decent, but without ray tracing, they seem outdated and fail to utilize the full potential of modern hardware. If you expect top-notch visuals, you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a Veteran beta player for this game and decided to wait a few days after release before posting a review.It's sad being in the discord and seeing people say they're going to come here and review bomb if they don't get their way on something just to come look and they actually did it. All of these negative comments are from people who didn't read the notes put out about the game and didn't communicate with their friends before jumping in. Now to the review. I. Am. In. Love. With. Once. Human and it takes a lot for me to like a game and to stay engaged. After a day of Open World games like this I tend to get bored but this is not boring. Yes, in every town it's the same objectives. Find the crates, find the mythical and mystical chests and so on but what makes it fun is the unknown of the area. Between Gus the Bus stomping around everywhere, random Deviants floating around that you can try to catch, little deviated critters around every corner, small mini games like the piled up cars all over the map, a GIANT WALKING HOUSE that has a minigame/puzzle on the inside. This game is FULL of little fun things like this, people are just trying to rush through and they're completely missing out on the immersive part of the game. The devs of Once Human listen to their players. On the same day of release we didn't have multi-character creation. People didn't like it and on the same day as release, they fixed it for us. They -are- listening to their players and they always have since the beginning with the betas. People are just being impatient and that's why they are becoming upset.Right now the only PVE servers they have are Seasonal and this current season wipes in 6 weeks. You get to keep your base build, you get to keep ALL of your blueprints you collected in the previous seasons for guns, armor and whatever else, you keep game currency and you keep whatever items you payed real money for as well if you bought skins or whatever. It's practically a "character itself" wipe of knocking everyone back down to level 1 and you grind for mats and everything again but what's fun about this is every season will be a brand new map, new objectives, new seasonal deviants, new story line. They ARE coming out with Eternal servers if you do not like the thought of "seasonal" game play. Eternal isn't out yet but I would assume they are trying to push it out pretty quick and yes there are separate PvP servers as well ♥If you like open world survival games with crafting, cute creatures, co-op, zombie/monster killing, gun customization, neat monsters that roam around the map, mini games, puzzles and things of that sort then just try the game out for yourself. Don't let the current negative reviews steer you away from playing because those reviews are from impatient people who didn't communicate with their friends nor did they read what they needed to do before jumping into a server.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was at "Mixed" reviews when I started playing and now sits at "Mostly Positive". I'll be honest, I don't really understand most of the negative reviews. It's a free game, and a decent one at that, of course there's going to be a limit on servers. Even though I have complaints, I understand that it's a FREE game and I'm not expecting perfection. I think the game is fine as it is now and something I could see paying around $10 for or $20-$30 if the bugs were smoothed out.Pros:Game is pretty similar to most other games in the same categories. The things that stand out to me are the monster designs and the lore. The basic monsters are pretty much just zombies with a few bug-like here and there but the bosses and events are really cool and unique. The lore is really nice too, I thought it was a good change for these types of games that isn't "zombie apocalypse" or "mutants are invading Earth". It still is monsters evading Earth but at least there's a reason why. I do like how easy gathering resources are and you can capture monsters to do that for you. My friends and I have been playing it together and have really been enjoying it.Cons:I will say, the servers being limited to a certain number of people is annoying. If you change from one server to another, you have to start over completely. It's frustrating wanting to get your buddies on the same server with you but if your server is full, then starting over is your only option. I heard there was private servers that they got rid of, which makes that even more frustrating. There are a few bugs I've encountered but they're really not that bad, mostly funny. I did experience one where my character picked up an exploding barrel and it got stuck floating around me. I could pick up other barrels and teleport and it would stay. It would also block all of my bullets if I was shooting enemies. I could do damage to it but it never did anything to it other than show how much damage I was doing. I logged off and logged back in and it was fixed. There's also an issue where people can put their bikes or whispers in places that can prevent you from moving forward. Whispers can be turned off but bikes stay there unless they're recalled by their owner. At one point, it was blocking the way out of an important mission. You could fix it by travelling back to your base but I still wanted to explore and collect the loot around the area.I'm editing my review to add that, like many public server games, there are trolls. There's a specific event where you must grab exploding containers and shoot them at an enemy, but for some reason, the other players can shoot it and explode it when you grab it or are holding it. I spent 20+ minutes on an event that should've taken five because this donkey decided he and and a friend wanted to grind XP from the event instead of just completing it. Like I mentioned before, people are also putting their bikes in spots to block players from being able to complete storylines too. I really really just want private servers back.My biggest gripe is the UI. None of it makes much sense and I'm usually just clicking around until I find what I need. It could definitely use an update. I would be pointed in the direction of a story mission and then get there and be severely underleveled. At one point I was level 8 going into a mission that was level 18 because it was the only marker on the map. I didn't realise I would have to manually active the side missions, even right after you get them. I think there's also just WAY too much on the screen at one time. Getting rid of the global chat helps but even then, it's a bit overwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: The start of the game feels nice. Then about a hundred hours in, you start to realize that there's nothing more to the game than what you've already played up to that point. You max out your gun, the unique armor that boosts it, a 4-setter and a single offpiece. You build another gun. Then another. You end up having an optimized loadout for all content in the game. And from then on, the only thing you can do is make the easy game easier. You travel to a Hard server seeking some level of challenge. You get nothing but HP bags, and faster-ticking satiation and water meters. Your house breaks for the 8th time after a random update. Your truck vanishes when it was doing nothing else aside from making alcohol for you next to your house. Your vending machine vanishes with everything in it, and you get nothing back, not even an apology. Support ignores your tickets. Your house breaks again.Maybe there's new content. You sign up for this cold wilderness survival map - to find the content-filled map you started with is now replaced with swathes of empty space with more verticality. Now instead of driving for 3 minutes to access 15 minutes of looter shootering, you drive 15 minutes to access 3 minutes of looter shootering. The guns you built in your first playthrough are still the same guns, still ideal. You've rebuilt your house at least 3 times across 3 servers at this point, and you stare at the half-done construction site. You realise you're going to build it again, everything you build will be deleted again in 4 weeks, and something will inevitably break again. The only thing that will surely work well in the future is the next RNG cosmetic box, from which you most likely will not get anything at all, unless you pay enough money to purchase Fallout 4 eight times over.You give up, purchase the Fallout series, and finally get a storyline and changes in gameplay, and then look back. Has the experience in Once Human really been worth the time you spent in it?And you realise you knew the answer all along. Only the first 100 hours was ever worth it. _childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of things right about this game, but the bad things about it make the game a lot more unfun than fun.Server Lag and Desync issues are rampant, when the servers are loaded you will feel like you're trying to play your game through someone else's remote desktop.  It feels like a slide show most of the time when you do something big like a PvP War.Your weapons and armor will constantly break.  Many times you won't be able to run even a few dungeons before you have to go spend a bunch of resources to repair.From a PvP perspective there are many balancing issues and overall bad design choices that immediately drove most of the PvP population away.In PvP, there's several  cheese builds that don't reward skillful play, not that this game allows skill expression to begin with.  There are many builds that can kill players in 1-3 shots shooting their toes, no headshots required. Even the "headshot" marksman build has an item that gives you guaranteed 1 shot headshot damage by shooting someones toes.  Combined with laggy servers this makes a frustrating experience. Deviants are overwhelmingly powerful in PvP and are outright unfair in many situations.  A player can sit in stealth and call upon a samurai deviant that teleports behind you and one shots you.  When getting shot by a player there's no indication or even audio of when and where you're getting shot from.  A lot of times you just end up on the floor not knowing how or where.In PvP Chaos mode you have a chance to drop a random piece from all your gear, including the ones you fully calibrate and spend a lot of time and resources on with unique calibrations.  The players who get these weapons can't even use them very long because they cannot repair them.  It feels bad for both sides.  Especially when you can get 1 tapped by a previously mentioned samurai deviant.In PvP Frontier Wars, it feels like a disorganized zerg fest.  If you are equally geared against the other team but outnumbered, good luck.  PvP feels more like a numbers game.  Your weapons and Armor will degrade within a few deaths as well.  Players with lower end PCs can and will phase through your base because the base doesn't load for them fast enough.  This makes some players able to reach the target they're supposed to destroy without going through a team's defenses.  In PvP Frontier Wars the attacking team can use their semi-trucks to grief your defending area where you're supposed to build a base to defend your resonator.  These semi-trucks do not disappear even if destroyed and do not phase away when the war starts or ends.  They are essentially there forever and the only way you can move a truck is if you ram into it with multiple players' vehicles, even then they may only move an inch or get stuck.  Your only choice is to build around them.The enemy players can also use these trucks as RESPAWN point... To respawn inside the area you are trying to defend and build upon.In War, attacking a fortification is a breeze because if you don't have natural terrain to defend your base you can get RPG'd from the attacker's spawn with spawn protection.  The RPG has no drop-off to damage and will always fly in a straight line.  If you're up close, a C4 which is easy to obtain will obliterate a wall with one bomb.At endgame, there's no real content, you farm the same dungeons over and over to try to min-max RNG substats on mods you put on your weapons and armor.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a free game. It works remarkably well. The EULA stuff is overblown as every company with some amount of online support stores the data you provide it and unless you live in China, no one cares or wants your gov ID.The problem is the storytelling. The first 15 mins (which is what I played of it) is a tedious exposition dump. I don't care about your world, its people, or the amount of stuff you are trying to shoehorn me into caring about. This is a survival game, first and foremost. Give us a mysterious facility that answers 0 questions, makes 0 asks of you, and is just the basis of your escape to fulfill your destiny afterward. I got a shady government organization, a talking celestial parrot named after the protagnist of Cyberpunk 2077, and an anime waifu that is obsessed with butterflys vying for attention to provide the most inane yet plot-heavy dialogue as quickly as possible. I would snap my fingers to find a way not to be given this as the first treatment.All this to say, stop doing this, game devs. Allow the environment, things the players choose to do on their own time to arrive at their own conclusions. I should arrive in a broken down facility with things trying to kill me. There should be almost 0 dialogue and 0 reports I can find willynilly hanging out on the desks. We live in 2020s; every piece of tech you come across has a password or some sort of lockout procedure. No one is printing out classified reports and letting them roam around freely in their facility, even post something catastrophic. That said, if you can get over the narrative equivalent of the T1000 from Terminator 2 ramming your head with industrial equipment grade exposition, I am sure there is a pleasant game somewhere in here.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I enjoy Once Human? Yes.What do I like about Once Human?Well... I guess I should start off by saying that Once Human is a survival game that feels different from other survival games. Even though it has the usual stuff like needing to drink, eat, and avoid getting sick, it somehow feels new and interesting. I believe this is due to the grind not feeling repetitive and feeling a sense of progression in everything you do.As someone who doesn't enjoy survival games at all, I feel that Once Human has changed my opinion on survival games and has opened me up to try others in the future.There's a lot going on in the game which I have enjoyed, such as it's post-apocalyptic setting, it's interesting season mechanics and proposed changes for upcoming seasons, along with the interactions between players (i really like that I can interact with my friends house and help them progress). The dungeons are another notable mention as some of the end-game bosses have very interesting mechanics which is reminiscent of intricate Raid Bosses in a MMORPG.However... it's not without it's flaws.  The game relies on loot boxes for the best-looking cosmetics, and the ones in the cash shop aren’t that great. The localisation isn’t very good, and the voice acting is either bad or missing in some parts. The building system, while expansive, can be finicky and would benefit from further refinement.Overall, I believe Once Human offers a compelling and innovative experience and that at least for me, stands out from other survival games.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... 317 hours of playing and i really enjoyed the most part of them to be honest. So why the heck am i giving this game a negativ recommendation?!?Simply because of the season system.This game has so many great things to explore, to discover, and ... to fall in love with. But it also has a great neckbreaker. The current season system.You're spending a month in order to level up, to get the epic gear you've aimed for, in order to build your perfect home, in order to tame your desired creatures during the current season. You've also spend hours in order to farm the needed and "allowed" ressources in order to completly rebuild your house just like they've promised.But than... the season change occurs and the most important thing you'll get... is a new unofficial title and name."Sisyphos". You know that poor ancient greek king that treated on Zeus and was forced to push the same stupid rocks upwards to the pitch only in order to watch them rolling back down and had to start all over again and again?Well welcome while walking in his shoes...You'll get a total of 20k points in order to tranfers items from your last season, to the new season.Things like weaponblueprints, blueprintparts, mods, furniture formulars and so on will carry over for free.But what doe's that actually mean?Nothing else that you have to start over again from the scratch in order to be allowed to use them again. All things that you've allready earned before within the game.Let me explain this a little bit more in detail.You've managed to really get 3 legendary weapons and a full set of of epic / legendary armory during your season. Now, you have 20k points available in order to transfer all these items and all the other stuff you own to the next season. Nice thing so far.But... transering only a single legendary weapon to the next season, will cost you 10k of these points.Do the math, 3 weapons, 6 armorparts. 10k each and you have a max of 20k. Also, every other single ressource, deviant, and so on will cost you points. To make it even more worse... even if you carry over these items, you won't be allowed to use them unless you've leveled up again to lvl 40-50. Same, count's also for your weapon and armor blueprints. You are not allowed to use and craft them, unless you've achieved the required level again.So basically, you're forced to waste a good part of your next season only in order to be allowed to use those things again, that you've allready earned. It's getting even worse. If you keep in mind how much ressources you've allready spent in order to raise their calibration level. Cause don't forget... if you carry that blueprint over, manage to upgrade it via the wish machine... it will have no affect on your current weapon. You'll have to build and upgrade it again from the scratch. Same counts for armor parts.Same count's for housing and taming creatures. You've spend so many hours in order to get the things right the way you want them to be. Only in order to see, that you are not able to carry them over par on par just like promised and you wanted to. Actually, you are forced to play with a "wannabee house" untill you've earned all those memetic shematics again -wich you allready had- in order to get your "real" house back.So actually, i still think that Once Human is a nice game worth of a shot by everyone during your first season of your personal gaming. Also, i think that this game has great potential to last on the market as one of the best f2p survival games.But as long as they are not willing to change the current season system, or come up with alternative servers that allow you to carry over all of your achievements, items, level and so on... this will be a very tough run for this game. And... i won't even speak 'bout the  policy problematics we have to deal with here.So after 317 hours of actually playing this game, my conclusion is... Netease did a good job on presenting a new survival game. As long as you are willing to accept all those strange policy agreements regarding personal information 'bout yourself and all the people you are connected with via, Facebook, Instagram, Discord and so on...You'll get a very good game during the first season you participate in. But right after that, you are simply forced to waste hours and hours again only in order to be allowed to use equipment, weapons, armor and housing installations again, that you have allready gained and earned...So... no matter how sorry i'am bout it. but i simply can't give this game a positive review right now.I see the potential, i see all the lovely work that has been put into details and i really appreaciate it.But as of now, it's literally a one season wonder cause many people... will turn their back upon this game after the first or second season change the've been forced to.

_childDocuments_.review: The $25 USD Battle Pass being tied to each character, rather than to the account, feels like a cash grab, especially when players can create up to 10 characters. A more reasonable approach would be an account-wide Battle Pass that resets to level 1 for each character per server.The game itself has some bugs and glitches but offers a fantastic storyline and is especially enjoyable with friends. However, the current map design and limited exploration opportunities encourage creating multiple characters to see the full map. A year-long, server-wide season that utilizes the entire map would solve this issue and enhance gameplay.While the game is fun and free to play, the high cost of the Battle Pass overshadows the experience. Developers could easily generate revenue through their existing in-game currency and cosmetic purchases without charging $25 per character for the pass. Overall, it’s a good game, but the monetization model needs adjustment to be fairer and more player-friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorta torn on this one, as it's a really good game that was well thought out with lots of content on the surface... However underneath that shallow surface there is really nothing to do other than just grinding for better stuff to upgrade your gear to carry over the next season...First con, is it's very laggy even with my 5 gig fiber connection, sometimes unplayable... And like I said Its a really great game during your first season until you learn how everything works and the community is very helpful, but in your second season you realise that wasted your time in the first season and you can skip half the content or building since all you really need to do is just grind for equipment frags, deviants, starcrom or calibrations (stuff that matters) to caryover to the next season and repeat this over and over again.The gear selection is very limited and it's a standard blue, green, purple, gold system that's in every game now, so the only thing you need to do is upgrade your choice of damage type gold gear to 5 stars and synergize your armor and calibrations with that damage output, so If you know what you are doing and good at first person shooters, by your 3rd seaon you are fully equiped with the best gear for at least the top 2 DPS builds and can solo virtually everything in the game even at the highest difficulty... Basically, Is it a good game? yes, is there any reason to continue playing more than 2-3 sesaons or playing after you max out 1 or 2 of the limited builds? no. because after 2-3 seasons it just becomes a boring repetative grind fest trying to get better calibrations and deviants or helping others do the same...Also there is really no point in wasting time building an elaborate base as the only thing you need it for is to store stuff and defend your filter against very easy territory purifications so there really isn't any point in stockpiling lots of resources other than what you need to upgrade your gear as all those resource don't carry over to the next season and just get stuck forever in the eternaland void ...I mean it might get better if they add more content, gear selctions damage types or things to do other than just grinding silos (dungeons) and Prime wars (public group events) for things to upgrade the very limited amount of gear options they offer.... They should also increase the cap of what you can pull from eternaland at the begining of each seasan or remove that mechanic completly and just give us everything we wasted time on in the prior season... I litterally have 200 biomissles and thousands of resources stuck in eteraland hell from my first season that I will never be able to use again other than destrroying them for those pointless eternaland points...Overall It is %100 a must try and fun past time game that will keep you entertained for hours, with some questionable "what is the point of that?" game mechanic based flaws...

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from wanting to play World of Warcraft in the past, and being a fallout 76 Vet. This game caught me and became my new day to day game. This is one of those games that you can literally grind for anything you want. Whether it be farming, fishing, silo raids, or even designing homes or bases. You will be hooked in this game. At first when you play it may seem a bit confusing especially if your trying to join off your friends right off the bat. But a lil bit of time and chatting around I figured out how to meet my friends in game after going through a teleporter in the same game and connecting to the same world #. Don’t get me wrong it’s very confusing when you start out but treat it like riding bike. The more time you have on it the smoother it gets. One thing I love about this game is the fact you don’t have to “Pay-to-win” at anything. Most stuff even the design blueprints to make objects at home are shareable with friends. So even if you buy something in shop with real money such as territory sets it can be shared up to 4 people in your squad. It brings a sense of community cause even if you don’t have money you can share your “wealth” with others and leave iconic items at there homes. As for cosmetic items for your character they can’t be shared but the legendary outfits will most likely make the fits for you character rather then the paid outfits. In terms of combat this game gives me nostalgia to many other games. Think of pubg camera with FPS POV as choice mixed with 3rd peson POV. Your able to use  almost anything from guns knives to RPGs and cannons in this game. When leveling up you may feel powerful but each boss has its own elements and phases which keep you on edge. Each update changes the difficulty as the game progress to keep every player alert. I personally love this game and if you read my lil review this far I hope you love it too.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has potential, it really does, but it's got some problems that it doesn't really tell the player upfront.  It's not REALLY a survival game, as you can't die from not eating or drinking, you just have a slight debuff, and with water and food so plentiful, you'll never want for either.  Me personally, I enjoy that style of system, but I don't refer to games that use it as survival games.However, the problem I have really hits with the fact that the game is going to be running on seasonal wipes.  Nowhere in the betas did they talk about this game having seasonal wipes.  Yes, you keep your cosmetics and 'some' blueprints, but that's not really the problem here.  It's that if I have to start over every 6 weeks and do the same fights over and over, then the only way there's room for different content in the future is to remove old content.  At best this system results in a Destiny type of content vault which nobody likes, leaving the game size bloated for no reason other than the veterans will have access to things that newer players have no way of getting.The other problem with seasonal wipes, is not only does that super insensitive the FOMO aspect of what you can earn, but progression of certain aspects of your character will only unlock later in a season.  This means that to get the full experience of each season and what it offers, you MUST log in every week and do the new content.  Week after week, season after season.  Life got in the way and you are JUST starting at the end of week four?  Do you scramble to try to get through everything you've missed?  Or do you put the game away for another two weeks until the next season starts?Lastly, the six week cadence.  While future seasons could be made longer to match up with other games that have seasonal wipes much akin to games like Diablo 4, it does not have other game mechanics bogging down users playtime such as building and crafting towns/supplies for progression, nor does it limit the player who wants to dump 40 hours in two weeks into a season and finish it.  Six weeks is just a short enough time for it to feel like crunch for a player who can't chunk out the content at their own pace.It's ALSO not enough time for Devs to put out any sort of solid or meaningful content on a consistently decent timescale.  If every season is going to have more than a single new flashy re-colored base game outfit and one new bland weapon skin for a player to earn?  Then development and testing for the story updates they promise for each update is going to be nowhere near competent enough to follow through with a solid product.  So, while it's speculation on my part for now, I foresee that updates will either be VERY limited in what's new, with only a single new quest and activity or so per season, or it will be a whole new quest line fraught with bugs and issues in a game that's already got a slew of performance issues.  The former defeats the purpose of wiping the game every season, and the latter is what most Devs go for these days to keep the money rolling in.  Either option we get, you can bet that their cash shop will continue to push out new recolors and basic outfits regardless of whatever each season brings.  But hey, one bonus is that it IS all just cosmetic!This game has promise, it could be good if the Devs change some things around!  The core loop is quite fun!  I picked it up last night and played through 8 hours without finding myself bored.  But given how they've chosen to set up the game long term, I have little hope that for people like me who are seeking to get immersed in a long term game world they put their time into.  And that if I stick with it and follow this cadence from season to season, it will get me little back to show in 6 weeks for the effort it took to get there.But if you don't mind the idea of wipes, and you just want something you can pick up every few months and start over again, then this is for you.Edit: Given the responses from the devs, I've decided to continue giving the game a chance for it's first season.  Will update this review once more once it's over depending on how the season transition actually turns out.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT DOWNLOAD! [Rant]Whilst playing with my friends on a PVE server, I was banned after fighting the third main boss, or as my friends and I call her "Spider ♥♥♥♥♥". This ban was due to prohibited behavior, and due to me not cheating or altering my client in any form or matter, I obviously sent an appeal, however, this was mistake one. The so called "customer support" is a bot, that gives you no contact to an actual human, all it does it forward your message to an employee, which then reviews you report and then says yes or no. Through me trying to resolve this ban I was waiting for an upwards of 2 days, with no other contact or information, and just this morning I woke up to see I received a message from the bot stating that I will not be getting my account ban removed. You may say "Why not just create another character?" and my poor fellow shell with a soul in it, you don't understand, my friends and I have only played on one server, and have spent an upwards of 10+ hours total grinding to reach the final area, doing side quests all the while. This means that I will also have to do everything again, but this time without a friend, and will have less time to enjoy everything like everyone else. I would also like to add that I searched through Reddit and other forms of media to find that all false bans had the same problem, PROCESS HACKER, which is a tool that is used as an alternate to Task Manager on Windows 10, because they for some reason couldn't implement searching into Task Manager until Windows 11. I would also like to add the response to my ban was bad, they did not include further info for my ban just stating what was already known, saying I had an unfair advantage, which I obviously did not, especially in a PVE server. One last note I would like to add is that the bot also responded with this "... please note that behaviors that do not alter game data or disrupt the balance and fairness of the game environment will not lead to suspicion of player accounts and subsequent bans." So they even stated that I was banned for no reason! Then they had the audacity to ask me to review their service. Don't even bother. [Rating/Review]The game play is boring, enemies are extremely easy, the six week time limit is wack, world lacks detail, the game overall is mid. 4/10[More in depth review]Starting off with the world, it is extremely bland, and some areas feel like there is almost nothing in it sometimes, being compared to other mobile and PC games like Genshin Impact or Honkai Star Rail. Textures are downright abysmal in some places, albeit better than when in beta, they still look terrible. Enemies are dumb easy to kill, they only have a few attacks or only one for that matter, so all you have to do is Run at them with a baseball bat and kill them in two hits. Combat is lame, you might as well be using melee the entire time and make it into a souls game, because  you at least get some enjoyment out of that. Time management is a pain in the ass, only being able to do so much in an exploration game within six weeks is annoying and downright awful, at least double it. [Controversies]Also I would like to add, do not listen to anybody saying they're "stealing" your information: First, they are not, they do what every other company does, which is only take relative data required in your country, and they only get your social media if you link it. Second, regarding government ID's, this is for countries that have time limits, such as China. Third, the "spyware" is for players who live in countries with time limits, this is so they can either kick you off, or lower your rewards for going over the time limit.Fight me in the comments if you have anything to say, I got all day.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put this as a negative review, but honestly, for a free game, it's decent. I'm only keeping it negative so the Devs can work on these issues:My friends cannot join me on my server because there's a max amount of players that can join a server, ever. Even if my server were to die and have no active players, my friends would still not be able to join me because the spots have been taken by players who have quit.Cosmetics, battlepasses are not account-wide. They're player wide. I bought the battle pass for $20, but joined my friend on another server, only to find I'd have to re-purchase and earn all the battlepass rewards once again. That is the most scummy practice, I've ever witnessed in a PC game, even if free. Once bought, it should carry over to all of my characters.The AI is ridiculously dumb. I'm able to shoot an NPC and another NPC who is 1 foot away, witnessed me killing the other and doesn't care. In my opinion, things like that should alert enemies to my location and have them come at me, unless I've used a silenced gun.The enemies are also fairly easy. At level 20, I was still using gear I got at the beginning of the game (level 3-5) and was killing enemies that were 10 levels above me, easily. Sometimes 1 hit killing them. That should not be the case. I should have a reason to want to upgrade me gear, maybe grind to be at level for the content I am fighting.The other thing to add to this is, the enemy is very easy to 'cheese'. There is a boss who shoots a giant laser beam at you, and you have to take cover. But, if you crouch, even though 50% of the rest of your body is showing, they cannot hit you. So, I can kill the boss with 0 worries and not take any damage while not having to care about any mechanics, all because I crouched.PVP servers are still PVE servers. When you join a PVP server, you still have to get to level 11, and then you can OPT into PVP if you want to. We should be OPT from the start. I don't mind having a buffer level and not being able to get  into PVP until level 11, so you can gear. But once you hit level 11, you should always be in PVP mode. We agreed to PVP by joining a PVP specific server. It's just strange being in a PVP server where 95% of the people you run into are in PVE mode and cannot be attacked and cannot attack you.

_childDocuments_.review: Please be careful when buying paid currency in this game!Game is decent, especially for a F2P game. I honestly would have recommended it, if it weren't for the amount of bugs I've been encountering adding up, which is slowly being exacerbated by each new patch that comes out. It unfortunately reminds me heavily of Destiny 2 in that sense.Current examples include audio settings not sticking unless you select another tab before leaving the menus, monsters hitting you through walls or attacking you from underground, animals changing colors at a distance, what I suspect is a memory leak which is far worse on DX11, and textures either not loading or loading incredibly slowly despite being on an SSD.The big breaking point for me was using a 1-time free character editing token that otherwise costs something like $9, only to have my character come out having changes that I did not make to her face. I've uploaded screenshots of the preset I chose, which had minimal cosmetic changes (eye color, makeup, etc) and what I saw when I finalized the changes.Conveniently, there's not  but  Reddit threads that are now over a month old that show the exact same problem, one with the exact same result as me. Inconveniently, it seems neither never received responses regarding their tickets, nor were either reimbursed for their tokens.I contacted their Discord's support bot and was of course met with your typical automated apology and hollow assurance that if it's a bug they'll fix it and to be patient. I'll edit if I get an actual human response, but I'm not holding my breath.I was already unimpressed with the studio's handling of the bug with their paid store in which players were given extra paid currency only to have them revoke it and ban you if you stayed in the negative - this is just the icing on the turd cake for me. Silver lining is at least I can hopefully prevent others from consuming their tokens and regretting it, should they stumble on this review. I feel in particular people paying to change their character only to have something like this happen are straight up being scammed.

Dev responses to the issues in the last scenario. In Prism Clash, a 3 week pvp scenario, players were tasked to capture ‘Pokémon’ or Deviatons that appeared after events. Lag issues, griefing and exploiting were all rampant. Devs have addressed griefing and exploiting, but some issues remain. A lot of the players were affected by these issues, resulting in a poor user experience. And the rewards at the end of the scenario? Instead of the expected unique faction cosmetic items, useless tokens for a tiny cosmetic shop full of crap that no one wants. I feel like we were punished for a poorly thought out beta-test. I fact, the actual beta test for this game had better rewards (a unique cosmetic set on release).Devs, you were told this was going to happen multiple times, at least acknowledge our concerns.I cannot recommend this game because I am concerned for the direction it is going in for the future. It does not respect player time or investment.Update: Customer Support is done exclusively by a discord bot. Meaning you'll never get a real person to read your issue, never mind respond.November 2024 Update : Customer support simply does not exist. It's very much a case of 'buyer beware' if you choose to spent money on this free to play game. No one ever answers the support bot. There are multiple reports of players who have bought items and not received them from the shop or been double charged. I cannot verify these accounts myself, but I can confirm that a support request has been ongoing for over six weeks with no reply.Late Nov 2024 Update: An actual human responded to my ticket and said the following before closing the ticket without letting me respond:"Thank you for contacting us. If there is an error with character binding, we are unable to reissue or transfer any related rewards. We also advise you to be cautious when binding characters in the future. We hope this does not affect your mood, and we appreciate your feedback.Please feel free to come to us whenever you have questions in the game. Appreciate it a lot if you could rate our service. Wish you a good day."This was their mistake, their problem with reward systems that caused me to have a phantom character with the same name as my main that received rewards in my stead.

General rambling notes below.+ You can build a house that actually looks decent.- The worlds are littered with boxes and empty foundations + You can fast travel and use vehicles.- Actually driving in this game is pretty bad.+ The monster design and general art direction is pretty good when it doesn't clash horribly with itself. Some of the body horror is brutal if you take the time to really examine the bigger monsters. - Unfortunately the overall vibe doesn't make it past "we have Geiger at home" - Sweet baby mode is this game easy. MMO tutorial area easy, which kind of completely destroys any point to early game gear because your starting machete is fine for the first 5 hours of content. - Most interesting/challenging content is time gated. _childDocuments_.review: Played 400+ hours. The game has great potential, but at the moment I can't recommend it. The performance is insanely bad, and you can find a new bug every 10–15 minutes.- The build system is really bad. You never know why you can or cannot build something in a specific spot.- The parts snap everywhere except for the point you want them. Big bases are not supported due to placing limitations.- PvP does not truly exist because of the desync and performance issues. You get to oneshot ppl you dont even aim at or   be killed not even seeing someone cause they shoot at you 5sec ago.- PvE is mainly "balanced" or made "more difficult" with genshin impact scaling: More HP and more damage from the   enemies.  No exciting new mobs, and the mechanics bosses have, which could be good, are even worse because of   telegraphs that already counted you as hit even when you dodged. On top, some builds are good for every content and   some are so niche that it's a waste to even try them out.Common Bugs:- Interface bugs where you get stuck and have to force quit or icons overlap.- Vehicle bugs where you can't place it or drive it sometimes lead to crashes or you need to force quit.- Crafting and building where you can't place something anymore that you've placed 10 sec ago, so you have to replace the   whole base. You can't craft items you have the materials for; you can't stop a running craft because "storage is full"   appears for no reason. You can't receive the items you crafted.- Gameplay bugs where you can't gather or loot items. Enemies bug and hit you even though you can't see them. You can't   revive mates because they are not in the place that the game shows you. Animations bug where you can't move, aim or   shoot properly.  Stunlocks from enemies that have no animation. Instakills from attacks that have done 5-10% damage   3 sec ago.And these are just a VERY few bugs i've listed. THERE ARE WAY MORE! On 6-14hours play sessions, I had days where i encountered all of the mentioned bugs and more MULTIPLE TIMES.The performance and bugs are still not even worked on becuase its more important to release a 599,94€ car skin. And yes, if you are not lucky, you will pay 599,94€ for that skin (to be fair, I have to mention you get everything else in the pack too, like character skins, weapon skins, and some other cosmetic stuff, but if you only want the car, be prepared :D).Like I said, the game has great potential, and someone with casual playtime can still have fun with the game in its current status. As for me, I cannot recommend it due to the problems I mentioned before.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything feels like the most memorable and interesting moments in Once Human, from meeting all the characters, to capturing deviations, and exploring locations, building my house, i even built my house right next to my dad's house! And the game can have some amazing surprises, like when my dad found a whole couch in the garbage can, or when i found silver ore right next to my house even though there was only gravel and copper ore there! It's a game if you want a challenge or chill in the low level areas. The best part is that it's a co-op game so you can play with friends or family! And it's free! so i hope you try, and enjoy, Once Human!

_childDocuments_.review: In short:  This is an amazing example of how to make a free open world survival game MMO, and is a great choice for f2p players who have some time to sink into a game. Plus, it's fun with friends.The combat and story are a bit basic, but are both still good. There are so many things to do, and the game is very generous with the resources it rewards you with. It has base building, bosses that you can fight solo or with a party, events, leveling up, a tech tree, cooking/crafting, mechanic where you can have different "deviations" fight, gather resources, or generate their own unique resource for you, and 2 different types of servers (pvp or pve) for people that want to play in different ways. And best of all..... you get to do everything for free! You pay for cosmetics, and that's about it. There are so many things to do, QOL mechanics, and a great overall sense of progression. Better yet, you can play it with friends. And even better yet, the devs (at least so far) are quick with fixing various problems with their game. Like recently, where they made it so you can invite friends to the server that you're playing on even if it's full (a server's limit is based off of how many people have characters in it, rather than how many people are currently playing on it). If you have some extra time, or the game just looks fun, I recommend giving this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Once Human is a game that honestly doesn't seem to really know what it wants to be. It borrows elements from many types of games, but doesn't seem to incorporate them well. Stuff like food/water are in no way scarce and you'd be hard pressed to need to "drink dirty water" for example. Most resources aren't scarce either, except for those things that are used in a lot of recipes, such as acid, may require a bit of farming at the lower levels.There are tons of menus and sub menus to find rewards at, which is a bit annoying to navigate. However, this isn't as bad as the several different currencies that are in the game, some which are just apart of normal game play, and others which are for purchasing different cosmetics. I'm not sure why there was a need for 5, 6, 7 different currencies (there are several, so it's hard to keep track of.)For building mechanics, overall it's not horrible and I've seen some cool designs, but sometimes things don't snap together right or walls or floors face the wrong direction. The rotate feature doesn't seem to rotate it and instead moves it to another snap location. Raising and lower foundation doesn't seem to work right where if it snaps to a previous foundation, you can't just lower it, for example. Sometimes trees will still spawn inside my base as well.However, I will say it's nice you can move your entire house around the map if you'd like, which is helpful as you level up and move to higher level zones. Combat isn't difficult, with most enemies being cool only for the first time you see them and then you get bored pretty quick fighting the same old enemies. There are occasionally that random one that pops up and adds a little "something new" in the moment, but those seem a bit rare. There are several enemies that are just different colors of previous ones or in some cases, just the same enemy but scaled up larger than the smaller version. I've been able to solo all bosses I've done so far, which honestly is nice. There are a couple of world bosses I've joined in on, but the world bosses are difficult because they require crazy amounts of explosives. This can be ok, because we probably don't want to see the bosses downed easily, but there was so much lag that it made fighting nearly impossible as I kept dying to things I couldn't see. There are a lot of bugs, but so far, none have been game breaking for me. For example, I have had some of my captured deviants get stuck in my floor... multiple times.The story itself can have interesting moments, but I don't really feel invested in it. Most of the characters you meet don't stand out and it's easy to just move through the story without really knowing why you're doing anything that you're doing.Since the game is free, if you're bored, give it a try. But overall, if you are playing something else, you can probably skip this. While I don't recommend it, I will still play it for now, but long term, I feel like I'll fall away from it as other games on my watch list get released.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:Mechanics & Control: The game offers a vast map and diverse crafting options, encouraging hours of exploration.Challenge & Fun: The current enemy AI is too simplistic, reducing the challenge and impacting the fun factor.Innovation: While the open-world concept isn't new, the execution with various crafting options keeps it interesting.Graphics and Audio:Visual Quality: The graphics are detailed and impressive, especially the lighting effects and environmental design.Soundtrack & Sound Effects: No specific mentions; the soundtrack and effects are adequate but not outstanding.Story and Characters:Narrative: The plot has potential but is described as rather superficial for now. More depth could be added in future updates.Multiplayer/Community:Online Modes: Not extensively tested yet, but there are reports of connectivity issues that could disrupt the multiplayer experience.Value for Money:Cost-Benefit: Given the open world and numerous interaction possibilities, the game seems to offer fair value, assuming technical issues are addressed.Conclusion:Once Human is a game with much untapped potential. It offers an intriguing world and appealing graphics but suffers from technical shortcomings and overly simple AI. It might still be worth a look for fans of open-world survival games, especially if future updates tackle the existing issues.Overall Rating: 7/10Pros: Vast open world; impressive graphics; engaging crafting system.Cons: Weak AI; technical issues; lack of depth in some areas.Recommendation:For players who appreciate a rich and visually stunning open world and are willing to overlook some technical flaws, Once Human might be a worthwhile investment. _childDocuments_.review: What we have here is a weird mixture of various other games with some unique ideas thrown in. The problem is that it all feels really just slapped together. Your character isn't overly responsive and feels like he weighs 8 tons while you're moving around. The general combat is okay though, its nothing amazing but its a very solid foundation that they can build on.The building is terrible, its just bad. The basics are all there but the building itself is uncomfortable and very very finicky. They at least have a free move building camera and that does help but the snapping is troublesome and not intuitive. Having to get the exact right angle on something like a roof panel is cumbersome and it took me about three times as long to just get a roof over my head than it should have.There is a decent variety of things to build and you've got pretty free range to build as you see fit. However the build radius itself, at least where I was at in the progression was very small so I felt very limited. Placing things works well enough, easy enough to rotate things around and there is a decent tech tree to work through.Resource gathering is more or less painless and its what you would expect. Hack at trees to get wood, go find copper or whatever else to mine. Nothing felt like it took too long to amass if you just spend a few minutes doing it. I do like the crafting queue feature at each of the crafting stations, frees you up to go do whatever while you wait for it to do its thing and nothing took all that long to complete.The skills system itself... is a bit confusing. There is this whole what I am guessing is like a pokemon type of system. You can obtain new little critters or deviants I guess they call them to put in your backpack and each has its own skills to use. I only found 2 during my time, the butterfly and a little jelly guy. The butterfly was just some extra dps that would do it when you toss it at something, the jelly guy could turn into cover or act as defense. I honestly forgot I had them most of the time. I got to around level 12 and only fought one thing that put up any sort of resistance. The first rift boss, big thing with some basic mechanics that I was able to match make into..It wasn't hard or anything, had some bare minimum mechanics and it fell overEvery other enemy I came across wasn't a threat.. like at all. The general zombie like guys you see everywhere all are dead before they even know you're there. Couple of weird big cat things with a tarp over their head? They also die easily all you need to do is back pedal while you fight them and they can't hit you. the AI is on a level of PS2 games. Although i genuinely think some PS2 games had better enemy AI than this gameCouple of other larger creatures, couldn't even tell you what they do because they all just fell over dead with nothing but the basic pistol you get shortly after the tutorial. Most enemies seem to have 2 or 3 different attacks that they just spam at random and very slow.What bothered me the most was that you could just see everyone's structures.. everywhere.. you can't go anywhere without seeing someone's little base or forward respawn point. Its just urban sprawl on an active server.. stuff built everywhere and it just was goofy to see. I mean I get it, its going to happen in a game where you can build if its a public server but this was just obscene. Anyone who had played something like old school starwars galaxies know what Im talking about.. houses.. houses as far as the eye can see concentrated around the major areas. It just.. feel bad and sorta takes me out of the whole thing. There is no point in finding a cool place to build or even a unique base design because there is just stuff everywhere and everyone's place looks more or less the same. Im sure that gets better in the later areas but its just a pretty big turn off for me.Graphically, its pretty good. No real complaints. Game looks and ran great. Its not the best visually but in the genre its in, its a good contender for good visuals. No real visual glitches or anything weird happening. Very solid on that front.I might give it another go later, but I think I saw everything I needed to see. It just didn't grab me, For a free game? Seems okay, but there is just too much competition out there that do what they're trying to do but better. Since its free, id say pick it up if your curious, but don't expect something that is just gonna draw you in and make you want to keep going. I lost stream really quickly on it and its a real shame, had alot of potential but alas. Not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Once Human is an excellent game that scratches an itch that few other games do. I am a big fan of survival games. I enjoy collecting resources, gear crafting, base building, all that and a bucket of chicken. This is Looter Shooter Survival that is well balanced and does a great job at all it tries to do. Maybe not perfect, but well worth the price tag (FREE!) The game is great about giving you free cosmetic items though they are limited in number and a bit plain. Such is the curse of F2P, but it does have some really nice and affordable outfits in the cash shop, and after playing the game for a few months, I dropped a little money on an outfit. I am still getting more than my money's worth from the game. Sure, you will probably hear about crazy people spending hundreds on loot crates to get a new car, or something similar. But if those people have the money to burn, that's up to them. Everyone else can get a complete outfit for the price of a fast food order, without loot crates, and be happy. The only thing this game really lacks is danger. I started on Novice server, and quickly found that was a mistake. After first couple weeks, my friends and I decided to move servers because it was too easy. So we skipped Normal difficulty and went straight to a Hard Mode server. This was unfortunately still too easy. The only time it gets difficult is in later phases when you can select Hard or Pro mode when entering a "dungeon". There is very little in the way of difficult mobs in the wild. While there are lots of enemies about, they are mostly isolated to their bases or settlements, and you don't have any wandering up to your front door. Maybe this is partially due to the fact that you can place your home practically anywhere in the game world, which is a very large sandbox. Only place you can not build your home is inside an enemy bases or the survivor towns. People still build right up against these locations for easy access to loot runs, or NPC vendors.You decide you want to move your home to a new location? No problem! Find a new spot your home will fit, open build menu, select Move Territory, and you can relocate the entire home you have built, and all of it's contents, and everything else you placed around your home. you can do this as many times as you like, with a 10 minute cool down. This alone is amazing for someone who likes to build but wants to move their home as you progress through the story, missions, and character level based areas. Want to be a real traveler? The game offers both a small pickup truck, and a large semi truck, that you can actually build a home on, making your home a mobile home, and allowing you to take everything with you as you travel around the map. Find a nice scenic place to park, or even attach a vendor to your mobile home, and park near busy towns to sell the items you gather, or craft, to other players.The game does have a few bugs here and there, but nothing game breaking, just minor inconveniences, and it is obvious that they are fixing the bugs, as they are becoming fewer and fewer all the time. I think the issue is that the game was released before all bugs were squashed, and the player base are beta testing in live servers. The devs are well aware of the impact of issues on players, and they offer occasional gift packs via the in-game mail, anytime a bug has caused trouble. Once Human is well made and loads of fun to play with friends. All of the people I have met on the PVE servers have been super nice, helpful, and sharing. Great community. I recommend the game to anyone that likes Looter Shooter games, Survival games, MMORPG games, and a touch of the twisted!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit2: Over 1k hours now and only behind 7D2D and Ark in my time spent playing a game. That said, I have to complain a little bit about the Way of Winter scenario. There are a lot of areas on that map that had clearly been intended for something (the oil rig, the giant trees, the fortress at the top of the mountain) but are completely empty; no salvage, no mobs, nothing. I'm hoping that these areas get fleshed out and the map in general has more to do, but it feel unfinished. If you're playing for the first time, start in the Manibus scenario.Edit: So after 589 hours in game, I'm still having a blast. The community is great and friendly (at least on my PVE server) and the reset mechanic that everyone was worried about was actually a lot of fun and gave us all a chance to run through the scenario again and pick up things we might have missed on our first play through. I've spent WAY more than I've ever spent on cosmetics in a game before, but I don't regret it at all and it's not like anyone forced me to or it gives me any advantage in game. Looking good is it's own reward! TL:DR great game, it's free, give it a shot, maybe you'll like it too. Old review below:Honestly, I'm having a blast. You can make a new character on multiple servers and you can even claim the event rewards separately for each character so you're not stuck playing a character on a server that you don't particularly like. The worries about privacy are overblown. If you're not going to play this game because you're worried about the TOS, then you shouldn't be on Steam at all. Another review goes into it in detail, so I won't rehash it here.For a F2P game, it's monetization is really fair. I haven't seen anything that is P2W. Things you can flat out buy are all cosmetic. Anything that would actually make your character more effective is bought with currency you can only earn in game by playing. The 6 week server wipe isn't even all that unusual for the genre. Nearly all survival crafting games have server wipes. Yes, 6 weeks is shorter than average, but you aren't starting from scratch each time, unlike most other games and you're getting a new map with each new season (or so they say. We'll see how that goes in 6 weeks)Gameplay is nothing all that innovative. You have a pet capturing/taming system which is alright. The way it works is a little like Palworld but that's about as far as the comparison goes. Its fair better than Ark's or Smallands at least to the amount of time it takes with about the same amount of utility as Palworld's pals but in some ways more specialized. The building system is pretty standard, though it's nice that you can relocate any piece you put down and if you demolish it, you get most of it back (all? I honestly haven't noticed exactly how much you get back). The crafting system is pretty standard as well, though it's nice that crafting from containers is the default so there's no running around from crate to crate grabbing stuff to put in your inventory before you can craft something. Go home, go unload, craft and then head back out. The crafting system doesn't get in the way of other aspects of the game.POI design is good, boss fights are kind repetitive but with enough tactical variation to be entertaining. Looting is looting and reliant on RNG but that's the way all games are. You can grind for currency though and flat out buy the blueprints you want if you don't want to gamble on the Wish Machine or scrounge for mystic crates and hope you get the blueprints you're looking for. Long story short, I highly recommend this game. It combines everything I like about survival crafting games and MMOs. I would literally pay a subscription to play this game, I like it that much. I might even consider buying the battle pass (though the paid battle pass is all cosmetics which I don't really care about other than I want to support this game).

_childDocuments_.review: Once Human: A Witty Review of an Outlandish Adventure!Character Creation: Sliders Galore!Ever wanted to create a character that truly represents your wildest dreams or nightmares? In Once Human, the character creation is as deep as the Mariana Trench! With enough sliders to rival a fast-food joint's condiment bar, you can tweak, twist, and turn every aspect of your avatar until they're perfect. Or hilariously imperfect. The only downside? Hair colors are as limited as my dancing skills. Seriously, there's like five options. Rainbow Mohawk, where art thou?One Character, One Love...Until Now!Initially, Once Human allowed you to create only one character. One precious, singular being to pour all your hopes and dreams into. But fret not, my fellow gamers! The devs heard our collective groans and quickly pivoted faster than a cat spotting a cucumber. As of today, you can now create multiple characters across different servers. Yes, that means you can finally experiment with that blue-skinned, red-eyed monstrosity without deleting your main!A Letter from the Devs: An ApologyIn a heartfelt message that reads like an apology letter from your dog who just ate your favorite shoes, the devs said: "Based on player feedback, we have urgently opened up the functionality for multiple-character creation. You can now create characters on any server and embark on adventures with your friends. Our initial decision to close multiple-character creation was due to the imperfect experience of playing with multiple characters. We had originally intended to update it after perfecting the multi-character play function by August 1, but unfortunately, it led to a poor gaming experience. We sincerely apologize for this."It's a refreshing, quick and humble response, admitting that the initial decision led to a subpar experience. Kudos to the dev team for listening and acting swiftly.Gripping Storyline: The World AfterOnce Human isn't just about creating the most outrageous character imaginable. No, this game drags you kicking and screaming into a gripping storyline set in a post-apocalyptic world where enemies can be anywhere or anything. From mutated creatures to rival survivors, danger lurks around every corner. It’s like your favorite dystopian novel, but you’re the star of the show!Open World, No Tab-Targeting: Pure ImmersionForget tab-targeting; Once Human offers a completely open world experience where you must aim and attack manually. It's like playing an action movie where you control every thrilling moment. Wander through desolate cities, explore eerie forests, and scavenge through abandoned buildings in search of resources. The freedom is intoxicating, the danger is real, and the adventure is endless.Final Thoughts: Adventure Awaits!Once Human is a PVP/PVE MMO that's got the bones of something great. With its incredibly in-depth character creator (minus the hair color faux pas), engaging gameplay, and now, the ability to create multiple characters, it's shaping up to be a wild ride. The storyline is gripping, the world is immersive, and the enemies are as unpredictable as they come. So grab your sliders and get customizing, because the world of Once Human awaits your unique touch. And hey, maybe we'll get those extra hair colors in a future update. One can only dream...or slide.
