_childDocuments_.review: I'll give it one thing: It's a fun addicting grind. However.This game's lack of effort put into making sure certain features work without flaw is frustrating:- Mailbox Links - You collect 3 items in an area to get a new unlockable item from a mailbox. Great idea. Collect 3, put them in and oops! You only have 2! Womp womp. Go find the other one (even though no third exists).- Lava! Be careful in this area! (boss area/town) - Sounds fun, right? No. Certain areas have incredibly high heat for no reason, Your HP will drop randomly and that's that. You go underground at a stage in this Level 50 zone using an elevator into the belly of the volcano! How exciting! Wrong. Half of the air has the same hitbox as the lava from above you. Walking aorund you'll randomly find a pocket of instakill. You'll drop half your important items and need to return to pick it up. The closest place to come back is a short walk away - But don't worry! The AI in this "Level 50 super dangerous zone" respawn every 5 seconds,, so on your way back you have to do EVERYTHING again. Enjoy. You get back to where you die, step forward and have a 50/50 of walking into this same invisible hitbox and dying, leaving more loot that you have to come back to somehow pick up,, or you get your loot to continue.- Server locations: I get  160-200 ping from South Africa. I usually get 120ish to EU West servers. I have no idea what networking issues you have but the EU west servers are sometimes so laggy it's unplayable. Half of the shots dont register, you can stop shooting and the enemy will just randomly die in a few seconds becaause while you're reloading you somehow do more damage that comes through late -- or there's Fire enemies that use flamethrowers to melt you. Cool, right? Sure. But with high ping you avoid the fire just to be standing and shooting later on and the fire just happens to be underneath you - even though it's not visible at all, you melt and die.This game is a series of mismanaged questlines that often end up in softlocks that you need to watch guides to get around, or other niche but incredibly frustrating issues. This game appears polished at a glance but there are so many small issues that it's less of a fun grind but a mindnumbingly annoying endless Sisyphean task to complete. - Especially in the "late game" which comes after the first week of content is completed in a season and you're going for completion, doing sidequests and more.The more you play the more super annoying small issues you'll find, leading to less want to play the game and eventually just giving up on the season. _childDocuments_.review: The game started off pretty solid—it was fun to play, and the graphics look good. But then the issues started to pile up. The game is really poorly optimized. Even though my ping was around 43ms, it constantly lagged like I was on a server halfway across the world. It completely kills the experience.As for content, there’s just not enough. Most of the new stuff they add is cosmetic or furniture, and the best-looking items are all locked behind loot boxes that you have to gamble real money for. What they do add into the game without loot boxes looks terrible. The free cosmetics and furniture are so badly designed they make your character look like a hobo. It’s like they didn’t even try with the free stuff, which makes it feel like they’re pushing you to spend money just to avoid looking ridiculous.On top of all that, the support is awful. After one patch, loads of people got hit with game-breaking bugs, and the devs did absolutely nothing. They just ignored everyone’s complaints, which is honestly unacceptable.In the end, "Once Human" is a perfect example of "a good idea gone bad." It could have been great, but between the terrible optimization, lack of real content, and non-existent support, it’s hard to recommend. If they actually fix things and stop being so money-hungry, maybe there’s hope, but for now, it’s just disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: After 25 hours of playtime, I feel like I've gotten a decent enough feel for this game to write a review.Conceptually, it is great. I've always been a huge fan of the survival horror genre, and this one hits that mark solidly.Visually, it is beautiful. The contrast between the peaceful nature elements and the twisted horror elements creates a really unique aesthetic that isn't often seen in this genre.Mechanically, it is fun. Gameplay-wise, it has its quirks, but everything works at least most of the time (which is more than some online AAA titles could say).The one major hiccup this game suffers from is the optimization. After a lot of experimentation and tweaking settings, I finally figured out how to get it to run consistently on my machine (Ryzen 5 5600, ASUS Prime X570-P motherboard, 16GB of Corsair Vengeance LPX @3200MHz, EVGA 2070 Super). Firstly, make sure your game is installed on an SSD if possible. If it isn't and you try to run it in DX12, the game experiences a memory leak where performance steadily gets worse as time goes on. Aside from that, set the textures to high, and cap the framerate at 30. Trust me, I know it sounds counter-intuitive, but that's how I've gotten the most consistent performance from this game.Overall, I think if this game was better optimized, it would be fantastic. That said, I'm still having a lot of fun with it.

There's usually like 10 enemies total in an entire compound and they die instantly. I spend 90% of the time looting. Enemies need to be faster both in movement speed and in reaction to the player. I shouldn't be able to casually walk up to gunmen. Imagine if going to a compound was actually threatening and scary. The indoors have a lot of enemies, more risk, but more loot. I should be worried about dying if I'm going indoors and there's a bunch of zombies around. I can't recommend the game in it's current state because it's utterly pointless. The progression means nothing if there's no challenge. Rewards mean nothing of there's no challenge. _childDocuments_.review: I ignored a lot of the negative reviews here assuming that they were just fearmongering, however, since installing this game, I've noticed 2 new mysterious apps in my startup programs (Which have been disabled now) that have no file location. So this game gets a negative review for making me fear now for my PC's security after installing it (It has been henceforth uninstalled).EDIT: I've received comments on my profile asking what these files are and how to remove them. The startup files are a single digit number, and a string of hexadecimal numbers/letters.Now apparently these are non-malicious are are just it keeping track of your installs of their programs and your ID on their systems, but it's done in a super suspicious way so, for people like me who are worried about having this stuff on your computer, I got rid of it by doing a full system restore of my computer to before I'd installed Once Human.You can apparently also get rid of it at in file explorer at Computer\HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Runby deleting the AF_Counter and AF_uuid, but that path didn't lead anyway for me when I tried it, but if it works for you, great, and apologies for not adding this addendum sooner.

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually a really decent game, especially so for a f2p game. Given that your privacy is already lost once you've used any social media site, you might as well enjoy the game. It's got a voiced main quest line with great looking cutscenes, decent base building (at least the clipping isn't like craftopia), fun exploration with plenty to see, and huge interesting boss fights. I had to dance to lower the defenses of a giant discoball enemy, what's not to love? The combat is cookie cutter shooter with random weakpoints (99% it's the head), and you upgrade your gear through loot which you can find everywhere and break down into crafting materials. Honestly I didn't expect so much polish for a f2p game, but here we are.Oh and if basebuilding isn't your thing you can just use pre-built houses from the devs.Edit if you're worried about privacy policy:

_childDocuments_.review: "Minus Crystgin" Legal Concerns and Fair Resolution Regarding Once Human In-Game Currency Issue.DearStarry StudioI am writing to address the recent issue involving the erroneous crediting of in-game currency in Once Human, to highlight both legal concerns, and to emphasize that this situation is not the fault of the players. The current approach to resolving this matter unfairly penalizes those who acted in good faith. Furthermore, I want to raise concerns about the possibility that this incident might have been more than just a simple mistake.The Situation:Erroneous Credit of In-Game Currency:Recently, many players, including myself, noticed that our Once Human accounts were unexpectedly credited with additional in-game currency. This occurred around the time of a new loot crate event, leading many players to reasonably believe that the currency was either a reward or a refund.Importantly, there was no communication from the developers regarding this sudden increase in currency. This lack of transparency left players to assume that the extra coins were intentionally provided as part of an event or as compensation for previous issues.Spending the Currency in Good Faith:Given the timing of the currency drop alongside the launch of a new loot crate event, it was entirely reasonable for players to assume that the currency was a legitimate reward or refund. Players have no obligation to second-guess or question the legitimacy of in-game currency that appears in their accounts, particularly when no warning or explanation accompanies it.As a result, many players spent the additional currency on loot crates and other in-game items, believing it to be legitimate. For those of us who have invested significant amounts of real money into the game, receiving extra currency as a reward seemed entirely plausible.Sudden Reversal and Account Defaulting:Days after the currency was spent, the developers announced that the extra coins were credited due to a "bug." Without warning, they defaulted players' accounts to a negative balance to reclaim the value of the mistakenly credited currency.This action effectively penalized players who acted in good faith, creating a situation where they are left with a negative balance. While access to the game hasn’t been limited yet, the Terms of Service (TOS) 5.3 clearly state that this could happen if the negative balance isn’t resolved. This possibility now hangs over players’ heads, creating stress and uncertainty, especially for those who have already spent significant amounts of real money on their accounts.Not the Players’ Fault:It is crucial to emphasize that this entire situation is not the fault of the players. Here’s why:Reasonable Assumption:Given the timing of the currency drop, alongside a major in-game event, players had every reason to believe that the currency was legitimately theirs. Players are not expected to question the legitimacy of in-game rewards or currency, especially when no communication suggests otherwise.Lack of Notice:Players were not informed that the currency was mistakenly credited until after it had been spent. The developers' failure to promptly notify players of the error left them in the dark, through no fault of their own. Players made purchase decisions based on the information available to them at the time, which indicated that the currency was theirs to use.Unilateral Error by the Developers:The erroneous crediting of in-game currency was a mistake made solely by the developers. This was an internal issue, a failure of the game's systems or management, for which the players bear no responsibility. Any financial or operational burden resulting from this error should be absorbed by the developers, not passed onto the players.Legal and Ethical Concerns:Violation of Consumer Protection Laws:UK Consumer Rights Act 2015: Digital content must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose, and as described. The sudden imposition of a negative balance after spending what appeared to be a legitimate reward fails to meet these standards.US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Guidelines: The FTC prohibits deceptive and unfair practices. Providing currency without explanation and then penalizing players could be viewed as both deceptive and unfair.EU Consumer Protection Laws: Under EU directives, misleading and aggressive commercial practices are prohibited. The developers' actions could be considered both misleading (by not informing players of the error) and aggressive (by defaulting accounts to negative balances).China’s Consumer Rights Protection Law: This law emphasizes fair trade and transparency. Failing to communicate the mistake and penalizing consumers may violate these principles.Punitive Measures Without Due Process:The unilateral decision to default accounts to a negative balance without prior warning or explanation constitutes a punitive measure taken without due process. Players were not given an opportunity to understand the situation, return the items, or even dispute the issue before their accounts were negatively impacted.Terms of Service (TOS) and Legal Limitations:While the TOS may include a clause stating that a negative balance could lead to restricted access, this does not absolve the developers from their obligation to act fairly and transparently under consumer protection laws. The TOS cannot override statutory rights that protect consumers from unfair and deceptive practices.Possible Motive:Given the timing and the way this situation has unfolded, there is a possibility that this was not merely an accidental bug but a deliberate tactic designed to exploit players who are heavily invested in the game. Here’s why:Timing with Loot Crate Event:The extra currency was credited right when a new loot crate event was launched, encouraging players to spend the coins on these crates. The coincidence raises questions about whether this was an intentional move to stimulate spending and later claim that it was a mistake.Reliance on Player Attachment:Many players have spent significant amounts of real money on Once Human, creating a strong attachment to their accounts. By defaulting accounts to a negative balance, the developers may have been banking on the fact that players would rather spend more money to restore their accounts than lose access to their hard-earned progress and items.Manipulative Tactics:It is possible that the developers knowingly issued the erroneous currency to stimulate player spending during the loot crate event, only to later reclaim that currency by defaulting accounts. This tactic could be seen as a way to increase revenue at the expense of player trust, relying on the fact that players who have invested heavily in the game would be more likely to pay the balance rather than lose their progress.What Should Have Been Done:The appropriate and lawful response to this issue would have been as follows:Immediate Communication:Upon realizing the error, the developers should have immediately communicated with affected players, informing them of the mistake and outlining the steps that would be taken to rectify the situation.Reversing the Transactions:Instead of imposing a negative balance, the developers should have simply reversed the transactions made with the erroneously credited currency. This would have returned the players’ accounts to their original state without penalizing them for an error that was not their fault.Offer a Fair Resolution:In cases where items had already been used or consumed, the developers could have offered alternative solutions, such as partial refunds, in-game credits, or other compensatory measures that do not unfairly disadvantage the players.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of potential. It is not a bad game, per se. The way the game is laid out, needs re-worked. However, for a free to play game.. it is built fairly well, and does NOT shove money down your throat. Which, is a plus. The games phase system locks you out of higher level areas on a week by week basis up to 6 weeks.It is fairly obvious that most of the effort went into phase one (forested areas) of the game where you start. As you progress farther into the game, it shows less and less content. The desert area of the map I can sort of understand. But not so much other areas.The mod system for weapons/gear needs to be better.There are bugs in the game that mix with not-user-friendly content that more often than not, leave you asking what the heck is going on (usually having to go OUTSIDE of the game to figure things out).The biggest drawbacks to the game are 1) the overly limited way you gain 'skill tree' specializations called memetic specializations. There is a very large list of specializations you can get, but you can only have 10 of them. And you can NOT choose which. As you level, you get an option of 5 to choose from. After you pick one, you have to use a SUPER LIMITED item to "re-roll", again on a limited list of 5 you don't control. You only get 5 re-rolls per SEASON, and you have to earn the reroll items in that season.2) Seasons are a huge drawback. There is no long term server. All servers (other than being PVP or PVE) are 6 weeks long and reset.3) The build system for your base is buggy, and does not always work. Its like fallout 76, but both better and worse at the same time. At times, you have to build, to unbuild, to build, to unbuild, to build, to unbuild just to build something simple.That is just a quick glimpse into the game...4) If you don't get the right specializations, you are SCREWED. Period. One such perk type is for acid. if you don't get one of them, you are going to hate life. End game is ALL about acid. you need it to craft practically EVERYTHING. and without said acid perks.. you are stuck fighting enemies to get acid like 3 at a time to whatever number you require.If you get the right specializations, you are done with the weekly season grind in one day. Otherwise, you don't get far at all. There is no mid range.The game has a wide range of things to do. Has a good amount of content. Decent boss fights. Lots more. However, there are some very strong negatives that make the game a one season game that many will stop playing very soon. Oddly enough, even though things like acid are a severe pain, there are no ways to pay real money to get it. Sure, for acid specifically, you could go to a contaminated area and pump acidic water. Then convert it to weak acid you need to refine.. but that requires more perks that if you don't have them, you will hate life.I want to recommend this game, but I simply cant. The way the game is laid out in its current form, just leaves you wanting to beat your head on a wall and give up (unless you are love solo grinding and just don't care about the drawbacks, or you are in a group of friends sharing resources to make up for the deliberate game bottlenecks that make no sense).Fix the building bugs, fix the lack of content, fix the specialization crap, and a few other things. People will play the game for a lot longer. After this season is over, if I manage to complete everything or not.. I am unlikely to return. If things are changed, then yes. Absolutely, i would return. Not much needs changed either (though, some of the changes might take time to code properly).

_childDocuments_.review: Best word to describe this game: "jank."I don't care about the season thing and I'm not worried about spyware, and my rig can play it (although still with performance issues, obvs), so I'm not saying "not recommend" for any of those common reasons. The game itself is quite beautiful and very unique. It mostly kinda works. It's free. It's jammed with content (a lot of it is repetitive but still, lots there). And whoever did the enemy designs deserves an award - seriously. The problem is that the game is just... janky. Here are a few examples:- Combat feels like you're fighting underwater, all the time. Everything is sluggish, nothing is responsive, everything is just a little bit too slow. This is true of the controls all the time, but you really notice it in combat.- The physics reminds me SO MUCH of Goat Simulator. It's like nothing is polished, everything was just sort of slapped together quickly and then stuffed with content and pretty designs so you hopefully wouldn't notice.- Dialog is laughable, especially because half the time I'm talking to a floating hair and boots. Stuff loads in painfully slowly and I'm often looking at half of a building or NPC for up to 30 seconds before I see the whole thing. Sometimes quests don't complete when they should, and all NPC dialog requires repeated triggering with lag.- The user interface is the worst interface I've ever seen in a fully released video game. Period. It's like they actively don't want you to learn how to play the game. There are 50 million menus, many of which are hidden inside other menus. It's so bad there are like a dozen keyboard shortcuts just to get to some of the menus, and of course some of these don't actually function. Over 10 hrs in and I'm still not sure how to get to everything that I've previously found. Try setting up your emote quick wheel: I dare you. There is no reason for this game to be so hard to use, and it makes everything take longer and feel slower.- The survival aspects are cool ... until you realize it's sort of the same thing over and over. Many survival games can be like that (wood then stone then metal) but this game is like: the exact same thing, over and over. First you get rusted parts, then standard parts, then better parts. You just need to be in a different area and then you get the next tier of part. It's that simple.- Some of the jank is disguised as gameplay, which is honestly kind of clever. For example: you don't pick up individual items, you just hit "F" and everything sort of flies to you like a badly done physics game. Your vehicle is impossible to find, so you just summon it to you whenever you want (even though it's also in your garage somehow). Sometimes random crap is floating in the air: is that intentional level design, or is that a buggy item placement? Who knows! The enemies have 100% accuracy with some of their attacks, regardless of distance or hit boxes: balance, or jank? You decide!There's a lot of potential here and the core gameplay is still interesting, but between the insane NPC load-in times, the sluggish controls, and the indecipherable menus, it's just so hard to actually play the game with this much jankiness going on. I think people are enjoying it right now because the game can be hilarious with all its jank + the insane weirdness of it, but I suspect the season thing is in place because the designers know there really isn't much of a game here: so starting over again and again is the only way to keep people hooked.You're better off skipping this and paying for a well-designed survival-craft game instead. Maybe one with an interface you can use.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Unique Twist on Survival Games!Rating: ★★★★☆ (9/10)Review:I've been playing Once Human for a few months now, and I have to say, it's a refreshing take on the survival genre! The game's post-apocalyptic world, overrun by alien-infested creatures, adds a unique twist that keeps things interesting. As a meta-human, you get to explore, build, and fight your way through this bizarre world, and it's a blast!The crafting system is deep and satisfying, allowing you to create a wide range of items and customize your weapons. The combat is straightforward but fun, with a variety of enemies to keep you on your toes. The seasonal updates add new challenges and content, which helps keep the game fresh.The seasonal phases keep the gameplay interesting, with each phase bringing new challenges and rewards. Building and protecting the thermal towers has been a fun and engaging activity, especially when collaborating with other players. The new content feels well thought out and adds a lot of replay value to the game.One of the best parts is the ability to build and customize your territory. I've spent hours designing and upgrading my base, and it's incredibly rewarding to see it come together. The community aspect is also great, with friends to explore and fight together.While the game isn't perfect and has some occasional lag issues, it's still a fantastic experience overall. If you're a fan of survival games, I highly recommend giving Once Human a try!I hope this helps! Have you had a chance to play the game yet?

_childDocuments_.review: Hi, I want to review this game without bias."Once Human" is quite interesting. Let's start with the basics:1. The gameplay isn't terrible, but it gets repetitive. You'll encounter most enemies  early on with nothing new and find that many characters in the story are pointless and are very bland.  The best parts are the cinema-tics and boss fights.2. The phase system is frustrating. If you're grinding and progressing to fast and hit the end of the quests before the next phase, You have to wait for the next phase to progress. Otherwise there will be a giant pink border you cant go into otherwise you'll die.3. Base building is cool but buggy. It needs work compared to games like V Rising and Fallout 76. You earn metric points from leveling up to buy upgrades and structures, once you hit a  certain threshold you cannot upgrade passed a certain point until the next phase so you want a better generator? oh too bad gotta wait until the next phase, oh you want to build more of the same of what you have? oh too bad theres a cap limit.4. Seasons reset every 6 weeks, sometimes longer, which isn't clear. If you enjoy base building, losing everything except blueprints and formulas after a reset (especially in PvE) seems pointless. PvP makes more sense, but private servers aren't even allowed.Overall, "Once Human" isn't terrible, maybe a 6.5/10. People make excuses because  it's free-to-play, but that doesn't excuse its shortcomings. With community feedback, it could improve. For now, if you play other games, you might want to skip this one, but if you don't mind everything i just said knock yourself out!.

_childDocuments_.review: Once Human promised an immersive open-world experience in a post-apocalyptic setting, but unfortunately, it fails to deliver on many fronts. The game’s visuals are lackluster and lack the polish one would expect from a title in 2024. The environments feel generic, making exploration feel more like a chore than an adventure.Gameplay mechanics are clunky and unrefined. Combat often feels unresponsive, with hit detection issues that can lead to frustrating encounters. The crafting system, which could have added depth, feels overly complicated and is plagued by repetitive resource gathering that quickly becomes tedious.One of the most frustrating aspects is the six-week reset mechanic. This arbitrary timer not only disrupts progression but also feels like a forced attempt to keep players engaged. Instead of fostering a sense of achievement, it creates anxiety and resentment as players feel pressured to grind through content before the reset hits. This design choice detracts significantly from the overall experience, making it hard to invest time and effort into the game.The story is another major letdown. What could have been an intriguing narrative is bogged down by uninspired writing and poorly developed characters. The dialogue feels forced, making it hard to connect with the plot or care about the outcomes of any of the characters.Multiplayer elements seem tacked on rather than integrated smoothly into the game, leading to disjointed experiences that lack cohesion. The matchmaking can be frustratingly slow, and once in-game, coordination with teammates can be a hassle due to poor communication tools.Overall, Once Human is a missed opportunity that falls short of expectations. It’s a game that feels more like a slog than an engaging experience, leaving players longing for a more polished and innovative approach to the genre.

Where the game truly shines is in fun and simple combat, with a wide variety of bizarre enemy types and bosses. It's gorgeous to look at, and the visual effects, particle effects, etc. are top-notch. Story's interesting enough. I can't speak for PvP as that's not really my thing, but in PvE I think this game is a solid 8, maybe 8.5/10. I highly recommend it, especially considering it's free. Hear me out, let’s say you spent a month grinding for your deviations and was even lucky enough to get atleast between 3-3 to 4-4 on them, only to lose each and everyone due to the server wipe. _childDocuments_.review: This game started out well and was getting better, but the recent changes aren't doing it any favors.  I was very much enjoying this game, 550 hours of play time, multiple builds and servers played on.  This is about normal difficulty servers as most of these issues are going to be even worse on Hard mode servers.  Serious balance issues are being ignored in favor of placating the whining pvp players.  "That build is broken (because I didn't pick/like it or I'm not good enough to play it), it needs to be nerfed." Starry Studio answer? Nerf it so bad for everyone that the build is useless for PvE.  Durability is a MASSIVE problem in this game. 20 minutes (at best) of combat play and you have to stop what you are doing, return to your base and repair all your gear?  How is that even remotely balanced, much less fun?  You want us to expend resources repairing our gear? Great! I agree! Increase the cost to repair but decrease the durability loss because 20 minutes worth of dungeon running and having to stop is terrible.Players whine that boss fights are too tough or bosses have too much hit points, or do too much damage because they are too lazy to learn the mechanics? Starry Studios answer: Nerf the bosses but ignore that the problem is the hordes of monsters spawned that make the fights beyond the average player. Lastly, most real challenges in the game are a matter of numbers.  Hordes/groups of monsters rushing you while trying to fight a boss or get through a mechanical phase.  You clearly need multi-target damage output, but there are only three (3) builds for that.  Two of which are so bad and under powered that they are useless for anything more than trash monster clearing, Bounce and Frost Vortex.  The other is literally The Build because you pretty much have to play it. Once Human started as a really fun game that had some low stress stuff to do and still had some real skill challenges, but their new direction seems to be appeasing the whiners who just quit the game anyway. Sorry Starry, but catering to the lowest common denominator does not make for a good nor fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was eager to try this game because my friend seemed to be enjoying it a lot. My friends had just finished a season and transferred everything to a new server, so they told me it was a good time to jump in. I let the game download the day before, and on the big day, I started it up, prepared to enjoy a new experience.To my surprise, the game has its own internal patching system. Despite Steam reporting that everything was "Ready to play," I had to wait for an additional 10GB patch to download and install in-game. No biggie, just a little annoyance—let’s move forward.Then came the main menu. The music started blasting so loudly that I couldn’t hear my friends. I’ve encountered this in other games, so I figured it would be an easy fix: go into the options, lower the music volume, and that’s it, right? Wrong. Apparently, there’s a bug in the current version of the game where, after launching, the sound-related options in the main menu don’t save. You exit the options menu, and the changes are reverted.Thankfully, a quick Google search revealed the hidden arcane knowledge: in order to save the volume settings, you have to make your changes, switch to another menu (like Graphics Options), and then exit. Annoying, but I found the solution fairly quickly.Time to select a server and create a character. While the character editor is nice, it seems that the only way to save your character is by exporting a picture with a QR code. I wanted to see if this feature worked, so I tried importing the created QR code—but it failed, giving me an “Invalid QR code” error. If you value the time you put into character creation, I recommend taking screenshots of all the submenus.After creating your character, it’s time to give it a name. This is where the "little annoyances" started pushing me past my breaking point. The game doesn’t support spaces in character names. Normally, this wouldn’t be a huge issue if the game warned you when confirming the name. But instead, it just removes the space and combines the first and last name into a single word."No problem," I thought. "I'll just delete the character and start again." Wrong. You cannot delete characters you’ve created—something I've never encountered in any MMO before. Alright, let’s Google how to rename a character. There must be an option for this, right?Oh, there is. Apparently, you can purchase something called a "Renaming Card" for €5, which allows you to rename your character. Suddenly, it makes sense why the game doesn’t alert you about spaces in names and just mashes them together. It feels like a deliberately predatory business tactic.I have no problem paying €5 for something worthwhile in a game I enjoy, but this? This is pure greed. Reading through other negative comments and learning about the doubled premium currency bug further solidified my disinterest in giving this game a fair try.Avoid this game like the plague.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin by saying although this is a positive review, I would still ONLY recommend it at least for a week's worth of fun, if I could post a neutral review I would, Warning, WALL OF TEXT, TLDR at bottom.Firstly, the whole journey from 1 - 50, it's great, exploring new areas, completing town anchor missions, looking for morphic crates and doing silo/boss missions, all while learning new things to build your base up and activate the defense part to defend and earn starchrom, all amazing, haven't played a game so much in a long while, this really captivated me and I even lost time and sleep over it, super fun.But that's where it mostly ends, everything else late/end game I find is just super bad or just so limited and time gated it feels more like one of those facebook city building games where you wait 15 hours for single upgrade to mostly achieve nothing, i'll make some bullet points with issues I have with the end game in no particular order.1. Prime Wars - Needs an overhaul, the whole scoring system to get your chests is a pain, resulting if hundreds of spammed wall structures (They need to be destroyed for you to score), the silver shield on every boss that stops all damage that isn't explosive (Very expensive, especially Biomass missiles) and then to top it off, if you fail and waste biomass rockets, you get nothing and if you win, you still need controllers to open the chests otherwise the loot sucks.2. Controllers, an item needed to get full loot from every single Silo, Dungeon boss, Prime war chest, basically anything worth while needs controllers, they're way too hard to get, a low chance on low spawn rate public events just isn't good enough, at a minimum they should be x1 - 3 per public event 100% of the time.3. Starchrom, ah yes, the currency you need to get blueprints through the gacha system, and the ONLY way to get any good blueprints, extremely limited currency, you'll get a bunch at first but then it'll come down to barely 4 - 8k per week, mainly from your cortex base defense but that's limited to 40 per week (4k starchrom max), keep in mind, you can outright buy blueprints (8k for a single legendary BP) and that's just to get your base weapon, there is TONS of blueprints to get and it costs even more blueprint/frags to upgrade them all, it would literally take hundreds of thousand of starchrom to get everything, and you're limited to 4k or so per week, with no other way to farm it, feels awful, you can't try new builds out or test any new weapons, so if you find your build you made during 1- 50 isn't working your basically boned.4. Dropped Legendary Weapons, useless, no other use other than a few materials and it's calibration, you can't repair dropped weapons because they don't belong to you, so any hype or excitement dies straight away upon finally getting a drop, they need to rework this system, make them way rarer but let us repair them.5. Acid, A dropped material, except almost everything worth while late game needs acid, from ingots, gunpowder for ammo and many other things, you simply don't get enough off it and takes forever to farm.6. Durability, Goes down way too fast, do a single prime war or a dungeon or 2 and your off to repair, isn't so bad a first but you soon realise it burning through your materials, really needs to be tweaked so I'm not repairing every 10mins, this also applies to your car/bike, this thing is made of paper, you'll be repairing this CONSTANTLY, even trying to drive safely, the roads are janky and you can't avoid damage.7. All there is to do END game once you're 50 and have done your base is basically MOD farm, all dungeons, silos, bosses result in more mods, worsened by the fact you need controllers to open any crates/crystals for loot at the end of the dungeon thus limiting how much you can do when it's the ONLY thing to do at the end.8. Specializations, You get these every 5 - 10 levels, can't remember exactly but getting them is complete RNG, some of them are trash and some are BEYOND broken, these can literally make or break your life in Once Human from making gold ingots to having the ability to make Acid without the need to farm, there's no way to reset these outside of a highly limited once per week reset and there's ALOT of them, needs to be changed so we can reset with Energy Links (In game normal currency)9. Seasonal Resets, yes there's resets, it will reset your level and wipe your base/map/materials farmed while keeping things like blueprints, on a survival game, really doesn't suit being there, hope it gets tweaked later.TLDR: It's a amazing game held back by way too many limitations and time gated content, it's amazingly fun for your first 7 days or so depending on your pace but then it dies off end game, without almost nothing to do you will be stuck waiting on weekly timers and resets to get anything meaningful done, highly advise you play it very sparingly and hope they change some of the games biggest issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be long, so my apologies in advance.OH is one of those games that have TREMENDOUS potential, but certain bad decisions will ultimately cripple it.  The Devs have stated that there are "Scenarios" which are content blocks that progress through seasons.  When the last season ends, a specialized reset occurs.They give you what is basically a contrivance, called Eternal Land where things you've accumulated over the seasons gets moved.  Blueprints, Deviants, Mods, currencies, and other items are moved, and the player is given a allotment of resource points to move them back into the game world.With that said, the player is reset to level one, their base is destroyed, and their skills (called memetics) are reset.  In the case of houses, I have a particular example, since this is sort of a MMO/survival hybrid.my house in game, has a 1200 build rating.  I have all advanced benches, 2x furnaces, 2x refineries, 8 water pumps, the kitchen set, 2 brewing barrels, 6 advanced biomass generators, each with a electric eel,  4 regular synthesis benches, and one advanced synthesis bench.  I also own a Trailer Head, a pickup truck and the "Jeep" with maxed out components and all  the extras like front and rear bumper guards and the wheel guards.When you make a blueprint of your base, you are given the option to pick one structure or all of it.  Selecting all, apparently produces a blueprint where all of the above is stored in the blueprint, hence the build rating.When the "reset" occurs, you return to level one, and materials like engineering plastic, automatic and specialized parts, etc are simply beyond your ability to acquire at a low level, and no amount of "Resource Points" will be enough to move enough raw material from Eternal Land, their contrivance, to cover these issues.The end result is that you build basic benches since you lost all your memetics, rebuild your vehicles from scratch, even after maxing one or more out, and spend an inordinate amount of time just getting your house blueprint completed.The Devs have tried to paint the resets in a positive light, saying that's how new Scenarios (content) is delivered, but the mechanics in place are not being given due consideration.  Even if you move guns & gear into the Eternal Land contrivance, you will need crystals to repair them, which you will either need to stockpile in Eternal Land, or level up to a point you can gather them over again.More frustratingly as well, by the time you play for a bit at 50, you will have a refined set of memetics picked which support your character and your subsequent playstyle.  The "reset" removes ALL of that from you.  On top of that, if you do not move furnishing items (not formulae, but the items themselves) you've found in the game world into Eternal Land, you will lose those as well.And then we come to Deviations(Similiar to Pokemon). They do get saved in the Eternal Land contrivance, but they are PROHIBITIVELY expensive  resource point wise to remove.  You get 20K points to use, you can certainly gather many more than 20, and to remove  them from Eternal Land is 1K per Deviation.In the end, you potentially have access to a lot of the stuff you once had, but the actuality of the situation is that you really did just lose it outright, and will need to spend the time to recover it all over again. The Devs have received enormous feedback about this, and even delivered a survey in game.  However they have been utterly silent about player feedback, essentially ignoring a large chunk of the playerbase that doesn't want to be reset.And as many MMO players realize, you do not need to reset a character to level 1 to introduce new content.  EQ1, EQ2, WoW, FFXIV, et al. are obvious examples.This is the reality of OH at the current point.  If they actually address this mistake positively I will most certainly change this review.  But as a longtime MMO player from EQ1 day one onwards, I cannot honestly recommend Once Human.

It's just the same enemies over and over again and they literally might as well just be puppets. They're so easy to handle, die fast, there's just absolutely no threat or difficulty. Seeing how PVP is offered in the game, ya might ask if it's pay to win and honestly I have no idea. I spent an entire night running around a "populated" pvp server and didn't see a single person. The most fun I had was with the building system, it works well and scratches your brain just right. Materials aren't ridiculously tedious to gather and you'll quickly have enough to build an entire mansion on a mountain top like I did. _childDocuments_.review: This game has many positives and negatives after playing for close to 1k hours. im just gonna list em below.PROS:gunplay/ character building - the main point is to shoot things, and the variety of which you have to do so is pretty excellent.variety - this game provides variety in a few ways. new servers open up new maps and mechanics, lootable furniture, clothing and blueprints and mods allow you to really flesh out your experience, and constant updates to add new or update existing mechanics and features.community - this game inspires communal gaming like i havent seen in many. you WANT to talk to your neighbors, trade, borrow, and team up. content - while a slow burn at first, the content continues to fill in with different server styles. and i know this is controversial, but the 3-6 week wipe. while you have to start over, you keep the parts that you work the hardest for, and with proper planning, you can go to the next server with a pretty great head start. CONS:Microtransaction priority: while this game doesnt use its microtransactions for pay to win methods, it does offer an insane amount of skins and costumes for a fat price. the currency purchasing amounts dont line up with the amount needed to spend, most likely to squeeze more money out of you. it almost seems like they put more effort into this portion than any other part of the game sometimes.bugs: because this game is producing new content at an insanely fast rate for a game company, it produces a ton of bugs too. while most of these are inconvenient, for some they have been breaking points.  building system: while i enjoy the building system, it is rife with bugs and unnecessary enforcement of sometimes arbitrary rules. it also misses several building pieces that other games with base design fill well. if a pretty base is what you want, this game is not the most suited yet.pvp: i may be alone in this, but the pvp for me was the worst time ive spent in this game. the world chat is toxic, the gameplay is filled with exploitation and glitching, and the way people can build can be super frustrating to counter or fight against.communication: the devs have a way of dropping mechanics and concepts without you knowing, leading to things like loss in progress because you didnt know your base could be wiped by people or this monster. they will usually only add such things after the player base complains for a bit.all in all, i still think this game is incredibly fun. i have found friends and community here, and will probably be playing many more hours to come, i just hope the devs flesh out a few more things in the coming months and im happy

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly a really fun game. But they limit the number of total characters that can be made on a server instead of limiting how many players can be on the server at once. This creates a huge problem long term.Not only does it mean you can NEVER join your friend's server if it hit it's character limit. It also means if anyone quits, like the tons of people who check out a F2P game then bail after a couple weeks, they all continue to count towards the server character limit for every server they made a character on (up to 10). Those servers will still be considered "full" even if they only have 3 active players who don't even share the same playtime.Eventually all current servers will be dead servers that are filled with people who no longer play or who switched to other servers. New servers will need to be made for the influx of new players and you'll have to keep switching to those servers if you want an active server. But once you've made characters on 10 severs you'll never be able to join another server again. And those 10 servers will all eventually be dead servers.This will especially be a huge problem in a couple of weeks as the gaming tourists, who are trying a game cause it's free and new, eventually wander off and leave a slew of dead servers on their way out.I really, really like this game and think it has huge potential. But until this issue changes I can't recommend the game unless you just want something short term.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a review from someone who has played the game for 870+ hours logged on Steam.The game start off good after the initial release, mainly during the first server. No major game breaking bug, mistranslation here and there, but forgiveable for a newly released game. No significant lag except for Prime wars.But the overall direction went to a totally different direction with major lag in all part of the game. Prime war? still lag. Silo, monolith dungeon? Lag. Solo Silo, Monolith? Lag as well. Running around the map? Lag as well. Some build is not viable due to significant lag. More and more translation error as well.All while these major issues are still in game, the dev release 3-4 paid loot boxes. Note that the game are only in the 2nd round of the season and a season only last for 6 weeks. Don't get me wrong, the gameplay is fun, hence the 800+ hours, but I wouldn't recommend anyone to start playing it in the current state. Despite the lootbox, it's not a P2W game. The theory crafting in the game is fun, and albeit locked behind the Starchom in-game currency (can't buy with real money), you can still make a number of different builds, which I have tried at least 15-20 possible builds.The base building is fun, but it's also one major reason for the lag, as mainly noticeable in the Blackfell area due to the trucks and the building on top. So, overall, it's a good and fun game, I would not recommend anyone to start playing it at the current state. You'll lose interest quickly with all the lag, and will definitely have bad impression with the mistranslation and the frequent bug. Watch the dev/community reaction on the lag issue, and see if it has been solve before trying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: About 2 weeks in 2 days from now, I've been playing the game since Day Numero Uno and I want to make a few things clear.NO, THE GAME IS NOT SPYWARE*It IS Spyware in China, but every game allowed to operate in China is Spyware there, that's how their government works, nothing we can do to stop that. HOWEVER, IT OPERATES LEGALLY BY THE STANDARDS OF EVERY OTHER REGION IT IS OPERATIONAL IN. ONCE HUMAN DOES NOT STEAL YOUR CANADIAN, AMERICAN, EUROPEAN OR EVEN AUSTRALIAN DATA! I understand nobody reads the ToS, but I went out of my way to, and it clarifies this in the ToS itself. People see one thing they don't like, stop reading and immediately go to cry about it.With that out of the way, the game.In my opinion it's a very fun communal survival game. It doesn't work in the same vein as Rust or ARK, rather it has a story you're set onto, like every other player, and you progress through that story while levelling, looting, crafting and killing. It's a fun loop that gets broken up frequently with other activities, grinding, exploring and side quests. It doesn't get all that tiring honestly.There are seperate PvE and PvP servers in the game but don't be so hasty there, buckaroo. If you're a PvP fiend you'll have to understand this game is PvE first. That's not a knock against the game I just don't think they planned out PvP interractions all that well.At the time of this review my warband is about to participate in the first War. A PvP centric event where it does kind of play like Rust in the sense that one team builds a base in a locale, and has to defend their core [the TC, in Rust terms] while being attacked by an enemy who bid on the chance to go to war with them.Aside from War, there's PvP zones and voluntary PvP, as well as Chaos Cortexes. All three of these follow largely the same rules.PvP zones are oil digs where your Hive [a group of players smaller than a warband] can claim a pump and defend it to get good rewards. The entire area is PvP and people can attack you, destroy your defenses and unclaim your pump.Voluntary PvP is just that. You and other consenting players murder eachother.Chaos Cortexes are drops that come by every so often. When you pick one up, you get forced into PvP and have to transport it home. Other players will be made aware of your presence nearby the same as voluntary PvP and can choose to try and kill you to claim the Cortex.Other than that the game plays a lot like a MMO in the sense that your main progression is going to be story dungeons and bosses.  Thankfully the gunplay is pretty solid and fun to handle, although simplistic. The melee combat is lacking so that wasn't a focus, clearly. Melee weapons just have preset combos, a shoulder bash you can do while sprinting, and heavy attacks. They usually do truckloads of damage but put you precarious situations sometimes.Weapons and armor can be enhanced, modded and upgraded but only if you've crafted them. Dropped weapons and armor can't be repaired, but you can throw mods and accessories on them at least. I'm not sure how I feel on the repairing front, I think you should be able to personally, maybe for a increased price compared to crafted weapons?This game plays very uniquely, but some readers may have been waiting for me to get to a certain point, and yeah. Here it is.It's a contentious topic among the community. Seasons in Once Human only last 6 Weeks and than everything is wiped. You keep your blueprints but your level, progress, house, memetics, and so on all disappear and you have to do it all over again, maybe even on a new map which I can't imagine going well. We've hardly seen most of the map and we're already about a quarter through the season. Players may feel it's too late to get into the game just a week from now. In my opinion, this cycle is far too short. It doesn't personally ruin my fun but I can see how others could be upset by this. It's not a good model.Overall this game is a lot of good fun, especially with friends, but you may run into an issue trying to play with your friends as plenty of servers are at max player capacity right now, and there's nothing we can really do about it until August. August will supposedly bring a invite feature, allowing friends of yours to join you on already full servers. But August is a ways away. This game is having the same issue Helldivers 2 did at launch. They undershot their scope, and now they need to find a way to fix it.I'd rate the game 7/10 for now. I do recommend it, please give it a shot! But I understand if you don't want to given the many negative circumstances. Maybe I'll come back at edit this review sometime in the future after playing Once Human more.

_childDocuments_.review: The concerns regarding NetEase's terms and conditions are partially justified, as they allow for the extensive collection and use of personal data. However, such practices are not unique and can also be found at other major game providers. Both NetEase and other game publishers must adhere to data protection laws such as the GDPR in the EU and the CCPA in California, which contain strict requirements for data collection and use. EA, Microsoft, Apple, Epic Games etc. pp collect similar amounts of data. If you care so much about privacy and control over your personal data, then switching to Linux and staying away from big tech companies could be an excellent solution. I think the game itself is great so far. A successful release.

_childDocuments_.review: Once Human has been quite a mixed bag. On the positive side, the game offers a plethora of items to unlock, and the blueprint system adds a strategic depth that's both engaging and rewarding. The deviant system and gunplay are well-implemented, making combat enjoyable. However, the game has its fair share of drawbacks. The player-made buildings often clutter the landscape with uninspired designs, mostly consisting of simple boxes or foundations. Despite the abundance of custom content, the game feels somewhat soulless, as if it's been pieced together from store-bought assets. The six-week resets are a tough pill to swallow, and it's uncertain how this will affect the game's longevity. NPCs and characters lack depth, making interactions feel generic and uninteresting. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the stuff about them stealing data, and/or installing programs on your computer are TOTALLY FALSE. It's nothing different from games like Pex Legends or other free-to-play titles. Cosmetics and season passes, no pay-to-win.The game has excellent visuals and sound. While not being the biggest thing in graphics this decade, it does a good job of delivering a quality experience.The base gameplay mechanics are solid as well. The animations, actions (harvesting, etc.) are smooth and fairly fluid. The combat could use a little more fine tuning, but it's by no means "janky" or clunky.There are MANY things you can do to earn XP and progress, from crafting to building and of course combat. If you like the gameplay loop of games like Conan Exiles, early ARK, and others, this will be somewhat familiar and enjoyable.The game's story and style feel like a combination of Fallout, Resident Evil, with some Silent Hill/Secret World thrown in there. Some of the "deviants"/pets do feel a little misplaced and don't jive with the rest of the overall style, but it's not off-putting. If anything, it adds an element of light-hearted fun.There are directly purchasable cosmetics, and there is a $10 "season pass" that let's you unlock a lot of things as you progress in the game. Each season, a new series of events will begin, but you'll keep access to your previous unlocks.I highly recommend giving this game a try. Put in a few hours, and I think you'll find you don't want to put it down.

Similar to many other games out there, but with a development team that actually seems to care what the players think, and works to fix issues in a relatively time-sensitive way.There is tons to do, in 3 different (at this time) scenarios... each with its own flavor. The different systems for customizing playstyle are both easy enough to learn quickly, but sophisticated enough to keep veterans coming back for supertweaking of their toons. _childDocuments_.review: The post-apocalyptic world is creepy and beautifully designed. Walking through the abandoned cities and forests gave me chills, especially with the sound design adding to the tension. The monstrous entities you encounter are genuinely terrifying, and the game does a great job of keeping you on edge. I spent a lot of time scavenging for materials and enjoyed building up my arsenal. There’s a nice variety of weapons and tools you can create, which adds a lot to the survival aspect. Teaming up with friends to take on hordes of monsters or exploring new areas together is a blast. It definitely makes the experience more enjoyable and dynamic.However, the game does have its flaws.  I also encountered a few bugs here and there, which pulled me out of the immersion at times. Hopefully, these will get patched soon. If you’re a fan of the genre and don’t mind a few hiccups, it’s definitely worth checking out.- Incredible atmosphere and sound design- Deep crafting system- Fun and dynamic multiplayer- Can get repetitive- Occasional bugs

_childDocuments_.review: So many of the negative reviews do not understand what a roguelite is. The server resets after 6-8 weeks, you lose seasonal items, but keep all blueprints, equipment modifications, and can carry resources and items from one season to the next. Even if you play a few hours a day, much of the progress you achieve will be retained and put you on better footing for the next season.Starting my second season now, I am able to make the desired set of equipment I had unlocked from the last loop, and put in my endgame modifications making the equipment better than it would be otherwise. More over, I know what I am doing more, know how to counter enemies, and know better what is and is not worth focusing on or developing. It feels like rolling an alt in any other MMO, but with the benefit of having some things that carry over to give a boost or set the tone for how I approach the season. The gameplay loop is entertaining and I find myself just trying to loot everything I can, even when I know I don't need it. Harder difficulty dungeons focus more on adding additional spawns and mechanics instead of just boosting health pools. This also encourages group play since a single player can quickly become overwhelmed. For best results, be social, don't be a ♥♥♥♥, loot everything, but be willing to pay attention to guides and external sources when something doesn't make sense.

_childDocuments_.review: Per usual, there's nitpick and ganging up over the smallest of things in reviews without people reading into it or actually taking the time to experience it. There's pros and cons, like any other games.This is a Free to Play. I am astounded by the character customization that we get in comparison to games you have to buy. There's a decent amount of content and places to explore and fun little things to collect - a LOT more than many of those "early release" games you buy can claim. This game isn't completed in just 6 hours or less and new content continues to be released at a decent pace before you can finish the current content (or at least for me). It's enough for me to comment to myself "This is a free game?" with each new feature that astounds me. Better yet: it's not pay to win.Now.. The enemies are a bit easy in the starting zone, which can make the pace feel slow or the combat a little dull. The base building could also use some touch up in how the pieces snap together (i.e. the curved crescent shape snapping to  the underside of ceilings), but otherwise has been enjoyable once you can move your base away from the first zone (where everyone is heavily crowded). I am also a little iffy with the seasonal resets, as my play is so limited between work and family and I feel I might not reach the end before reset happens.Maybe I've been a little starved for a finished game, tired as hell of all those paid "early release" with slow moving promises. But this is still a breath of fresh air and worth giving a chance.

name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition
detailed_description: Relive the glory of Stronghold, the original BAFTA-nominated real-time strategy game, with this new definitive edition of the classic 'castle sim'. Witness the game that started it all, carefully rebuilt using the source artwork, remastered music, returning voice talent and veteran developers of the first entry in this legendary series. UNITE A BROKEN REALM Welcome to the fractured, war-torn frontier of medieval England. With the King betrayed by his treacherous lords and a realm on the brink of collapse, take control of scattered forces and reunite your kingdom against the monstrous Rat, Pig, Snake and Wolf! Strike down each villainous Lord in missions ranging from breaking sieges and capturing enemy castles to building epic fortresses and repelling enemy assaults. Test the limits of your strategic mind with castle assaults and grand banquets in military and economic campaigns. Dive into classic RTS and city builder gameplay now elevated with remade graphics, community requested features and remastered music from series maestro Robert L. Euvino. Gather resources, construct mighty castles, protect your townsfolk, manage your gold, raise armies and wage all out war! A LEGEND RETOLD Building on its 20 year legacy, Stronghold: Definitive Edition features two classic campaigns told across 26 missions, alongside fresh single player content in the form of a new narrative campaign designed by Firefly Studios founders Simon Bradbury and Eric Ouellette. Exclusive to the definitive edition, this new 14 mission campaign sees players march across the devastated English hinterland in search of Sir Longarm's captured kin, before venturing beyond the story in a challenging new historical 'Castle Trail' of 10 unique scenarios. With remade artwork, a higher fidelity soundtrack, full Steam multiplayer support for 8 players, Steam Workshop, modernised gameplay and more, Stronghold: Definitive Edition is the ultimate way to experience the game that started it all. Your kingdom awaits! NEW FEATURES ZOOM INTO NEW VISUALS remade by the original artists with improved animations, textures and lighting. REMATCH CLASSIC VILLAINS as you hunt The Rat and The Snake in a challenging new 14 mission campaign. BATTLE OLD FRIENDS on Steam with 8 player multiplayer support and extra maps on which to wage war! RELIVE HISTORY in a new Castle Trail with 10 challenging siege scenarios and famous historical fortresses. LOSE YOURSELF in a remastered soundtrack, with fresh recordings from some of the game's original voice actors. CREATE, SHARE & ENJOY new Stronghold community content with Steam Workshop support.

_childDocuments_.review: It's 2001, you come back from school. It's Friday, so you have a free evening. You launch Stronghold, the new game of the little-known company Firefly Studios. The game runs with 20 FPS at best on your Pentium II 233 Mhz. Sometimes it's 15 FPS or lower when there are more units on the screen. But it doesn't matter, the important thing is you can just run this great game on your computer. And now, 22 years later, the magic returns. For me, it's a perfect remaster. No big changes, some small QoL improvements, a new campaign, new maps, improved textures, flying cows in high resolution, improved map editor. And integration with Steam Workshop, which already become a source of nice new maps (anyone else remember this site for original games?  And more FPS this time. The finished remaster (looking at you Konami) with already announced updates for a reasonable price (looking at you Konami again). Totally worth buying. And already waiting for Stronghold Crusader Definitive Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played Stronghold 22 years ago on its debut release, and as I sit here now reviewing the Definitive Edition I can’t help but feel immense pride to see Firefly Studios still actively flourishing – in the first 72 hours of release it had sold 100,000 copies and had a peak of 9,672 concurrent players on Steam.Firefly was originally conceived in 1999, consisting of just two co-creators Simon Bradbury and Eric Ouellette, who spent their first two years together creating a game that aimed to merge both the City Builder and Real-Time Strategy genres. They accomplished this in 2001 with their first release – Stronghold, which released to critical acclaim and commercial success. The game became a surprise hit and due to its popularity led to several sequels including the fan favourite Stronghold Crusader in 2002. Both of these titles use a 2D isometric game engine which is comfortably the best way to experience the series, the Definitive Edition uses the Unity engine as a wrapper for the original game. The Stronghold series has been tried and tested over the years through different pathways, however sticking close to the original blueprint is what makes it (in my opinion) most grand. A blend of British charm and replayability made this series such an instant hit, combined with innovative castle building and visuals. The Definitive Edition enhances the original experience with remade artwork, modernised gameplay, high fidelity sounds and workshop support. The visuals are so crisp and smooth, like rewatching an 80s/90s program in HD. It’s absolutely fantastic. I will never tire from watching routine work processes in Stronghold – let’s take the art of making bread: watching workers harvest wheat crop, who then move the wheat to the keeps stockpile. The young workers then take the wheat from the stockpile and transfer it to the mill. Once flour is milled, the young workers take the bags of flour back to the stockpile. The bakers then pickup the flour and transfer it back to their bakery, where you’re able to watch them create food for the castle, before being placed into the local granary for storage/consumption. What I’m describing is the absolute charm of the game: watching the beautiful synchronisation of routine jobs throughout the castle is nothing short of scintillating and it is through this charm that makes the game richly excel. The Definitive Edition includes a new 14 mission campaign, along with a new historical ‘Castle Trail’ which sets 10 unique scenarios to delve into. The campaign itself was fine, I preferred the Castle Trail as it proved to be more challenging (I’m looking at  Heuneburg) nonetheless my entire experience so far has been incredibly rewarding. Now that I’ve attained 100% completion, I look forward to the post-release schedule - at least two major free updates coinciding with paid DLC.  is set to contain new economic missions and maps, and will release alongside the  DLC.  will include a new Castle Trail and maps, and is set to release alongside the  DLC.Buy it. It’s brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: For more than 20 years, Stronghold has held steadfast to its RTS niche amongst the Starcrafts, Age of Empires and Command & Conquers of the world. Thus it is only fitting that it, too, now finally enjoys the luxury of a definitive edition.For many of my generation, this was one of their first real PC games and the franchise is still beloved to this day. Playing it is ageless fun.I can't really comment on the MP side of things (Coop, Bots, Skirmish) because I was never into that. However, I don't really see how something that was never part of the original game could warrant a negative review.From what I can tell, Firefly Studios are dedicated to adding more content in the future which is very much welcome. At the time of writing I've already finished the new Rat and Snake campaigns which I thoroughly enjoyed. Looking forward to the Pig and Wolf DLCs!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a definitive edition done right!As a Stronghold veteran since day 1 (I started playing Stronghold  way back when it came out in 2001) i can only say that this is an amazing remake. The graphics are very clean and were upscaled so you can see much more details as in the original, but the visual style of Stronghold is still preserved. Several quality-of-life updates make the gameplay more comfortable, like seeing a small arrow as an indicator if your popularity changes, or enabling right clicking orders for the troops.Essentially, this is Stronghold 1 with all its contents and some more, like new campaigns, workshop support, achievements. Definitive Addition has high hopes, but if FireFly Studios wants its gamers to make use of the Steam multiplayer features it's included - you're going to want to add AI. _childDocuments_.review: Look, it's a pretty old game. I'm writing this review for you guys - not the game or devs. I'm writing it in the hopes that on those days when you just don't feel like playing the latest AAA (or indie) trending game, you might consider giving this classic a try. It really is worth the chance, and if you can get it for under 10 bucks, it's a steal. And I truly think most people will like this one a lot.Like strategy games? Like City/castle builders? You need to buy and play this if you never have. And if you've played it in the past, you owe it to yourself to play it again. Is it the type of the game that will be your top ten favorite? No, probably not. But it absolutely will give you dozens to hundreds of hours of fun. It's virtually bug free, being from the era when games were completed before they were released. Everything works. Maybe the UI isn't super modern, the graphics (although updated since the original release) are mediocre, and the music is... the music is better not mentioned. The story line is lighthearted/silly and relatively simple. You're not going to find any masterpieces of story writing, or outstanding characters that you think of fondly 10 years from now. That's not what this game is, and it doesn't try to be.What this game is, is a very straight forward city/castle sim and strategy game. You gather resources that you use to build your defenses, your industry, train troops, and keep your peasants happy. Nothing is super complex about the systems. There's no research trees, or requirements you need to reach to unlock things  (though the campaign unlocks new buildings, resources, and weapons as you progress). Build wood or stone walls towers and gates in any design you wish. Make multi-leveled defenses, and employ designs that are segmented and redundant to help fend off waves of enemies. Train archers, spear men, mace men, pike men, crossbowmen, swordsmen, and even mounted knights to defend your castle and settlement. If that's not enough break out the siege weapons like catapults, trebuchets, ballistas; and traps, boiling oil, and war dogs.Some of the missions have you go on the offense, taking a limited number of troops and engines and assault the enemy, but for the most part, you're the one building and defending (in the campaign.) Additionally, there are some extra campaigns that add some newer features, buildings, and challenges - new maps, new tactics, and dozens of more hours of game time. If you decide you just want to design and build your dream castle and throw endless enemies at it to see how your design fairs, you can do that too. I hope that if you decide to give this one a chance you find it as much fun as I did. It really is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Some of you could define "Stronghold: Definitive Edition" as a nostalgia operation, trying to resell the same copy of "Stronghold" over and over again (Skyrim docet) and probably you are not wrong. Of course there are plenty of new quality of life improvements (autoselling/buying, rally points, keybindings, a more dynamic camera, steam workshop), nothing really necessary but still appreciated. What about the new Campaigns? Despite being really challenging (especially on very hard), they are not really adding anything interesting or engaging.So, why did I buy this game? Because replaying a game which defined my childhood and hearing "Castlejam" after 20 years, is priceless.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the original game, then you will probably will be buying this. But would I recommend this game to a newcomer? Absolutely not. And here are the reasons why:The good:* Original campaign in its full glory is still good and unique, every mission feels different and the new textures made it even better.* Auto market got added to the game, which is massive QOL improvement.* Troops can now be trained more than one at a time with ctrl and shift clicks, which is really good.* They added additional animated character for DLC campaigns.The bad:* DLC campaigns are done very poorly, the story does not progress in logical order. One of the first missions in rat campaign gives you all of the units you want and then you start going backwards from there. And it surprisingly felt that way for all of the 4 DLC jewel campaigns. They did not listen to their playerbase feedback about it.* DLC campaigns lack cinematics of your opponents, the enemy troops just keep coming without any taunts like in original campaign, missed opportunity.* The scripts in DLC campaigns are bad, because there is none...* DLC campaigns did not take into account replayability. The maps are small and your castle can't be placed on different locations, which makes the games play exactly the same all the time.* Lots of the maps in DLC campaigns were actually running from point A to point B, it was overused and miserable experience. Putting hundreds of wolfs on the map while they are bugged and your troops wont even attack them is not considered fun.* New maps felt unbalanced and untested, mostly dull and boring, that you don't even want to play again through again.* New economic missions are actually really heavily combat oriented. They did exactly the opposite of what they were supposed to do.* Bugs from original game are still not fixed and quality of life improvements from crusader are not brought over. For example, you still can't click on items on your stockpile to easily open market.* No skirmish mode. They told from the beginning, that they would not make one for this game, but they should have, even if it took longer and would have made the game higher in price.* Multiplayer is literal 1/10 experience, don't even think about buying this game to play with friends.* No new additional items added to the game, everything is exactly the same from gameplay wise. They could have added some new items only for DLC and kept the original campaign as is for the sake of keeping the gameplay exactly the same for it.* Second castle trail maps were done in a way that you actually can't go through the walls at some locations, which is clearly because of laziness. Instead of making some weak points harder to attack, they simply played with terrain so that you can destory the wall, but can't go in from that location. It was used in multiple castle trail maps.* The newly added animated character always had the same animation, made it dull. And he was used mostly in the begging of the mission at the same time when you are told "Place your granary", which overlapped and felt like another untested product of laziness.* Still no hiscores in the list of missions, so you have no idea how well you did in them afterwards.
