_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasure it was to walk down memory lane with Stronghold: Definitive Edition. Even more refreshing to see the game with improved graphics. High definition indeed.Those familiar with the first need no lengthy explainer. As a veteran Stronghold player, I make note of some of the changes made which are either an improvement or hindrance (in my opinion) to the game.For starters, the mass train/buy/sell at the barracks/market using click+Shift is a handy tool, as is left click+Ctrl to copy+paste existing structures. Similarly, zooming in/out with the mouse wheel saves having to right-click all the time. The option to magnify/minify the minimap is another good addition to S:DE. It is only a pity that you can't zoom in the game up-close, so as to better appreciate the remastered sprites, as they are quite well done.Perhaps the best feature is the doubling of the unit/building limits. Firefly mentioned they might (fingers crossed) increase it even further. Still, some things remain unchanged, and I'm not referring to the game mechanics. The AI still takes a while to respond with taunts or insults after defeating them in the campaign. We should also have been able to click+drag for the killing pits as we do with the pitch ditch, since individually clicking can become annoying.Firefly also ought to have enabled building when paused, which, although not a feature in the original Stronghold (instead first introduced in Stronghold Crusader), would have been useful instead of having to slow down the game speed.Speaking of, I noticed that S:DE's game speed, even at 90, is comparatively slower than the original game. Whether this is due to the reworked system or otherwise, I cannot say. Meanwhile, I was amused to discover that Firefly removed the old bug (for a lack of a better term) wherein if you have full tavern coverage which gives you 8 popularity, you can still retain peasants without food/taxes as the no food penalty was -7.Concerning the DLCs, I must say they are excellently designed, and the pricing quite affordable, even for those whose currencies are not as strong as the pound. The missions to capture the keep or to reach the flag at the other end of the map are especially challenging. Even holding against enemy sieges can be nigh impossible. The only drawback is that save for one mission, you can't build moats, while training knights are limited to two or three missions. I gather that S:DE has been well-received, and moving forward, I hope that Firefly will eventually be able to include maps bigger than the current maximum size of 400x400. I imagine that for a game over two decades old now, this should not be too much of an issue.Though they've said they won't be providing mod support, considering that this is a Definitive Edition, perhaps some modders with the know-how can do so of their own volition. Most importantly, many players, including myself, fervently hope that a Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition may come to pass. Perhaps with the Extreme version included as well. But only time will tell.

_childDocuments_.review: Not long ago I was talking with a friend and the name Stronghold came up in conversation, and no more than a few days later Stronghold: Definitive Edition was announced. Our surprise was tremendous, and of course I had to play this edition. FireFly Studios once again puts us at the head of a kingdom, in this strategy and castle sim game, with robust and polished mechanics over the course of twenty years, which in my opinion stand out from the rest of the titles in the genre. This version adds a new game mode, an additional campaign, Steam Workshop integration and multiplayer, among other things. Honestly, it's a great game, and if that wasn't enough, they already have content planned for the future.Starting with the classic campaign, we’ll be located in a fictional medieval Britain, and we’ll be put in the role of a feudal lord fighting for the unification of the country. We’ll face a series of missions of progressive difficulty, and the plot will be told to us little by little. Among challenging and varied objectives, we’ll be introduced to the iconic main enemies: The Rat, the Snake, the Pig and the Wolf; and overthrowing them one by one will be our goal.On the other hand, the new campaign is recommended for veterans of the franchise, and will take us through the fields of a devastated England while we seek to free a fair maiden. This story presents us with new and challenging missions that will test our tactical and resource management skills. Perhaps for some it will be interesting to see the difference between the old and modern direction, and I can say that even separated by so many years they feel very cohesive; as far as I saw, of course, because the truth is that this campaign is pretty difficult for me.On the gameplay and accessibility side, the game has modernized some things, like controls (blessed WASD) and quality of life aspects, but beyond that there are mechanics and details that, for me, make Stronghold stand out and separate it from its peers. For example, here it’s not enough to just build barracks and hire units, no; in this game you have to hire blacksmiths and fletchers to prepare the weapons, then take them to the armory and then hire the relevant unit. It seems a bit complex and can be a bit irritating under pressure, but it's a bit more realistic and I like it a lot.Another thing that I have always found wonderful is that stone walls not only serve to protect our buildings from enemy armies, but our units can also climb them and defend from the heights. Ballisate can also be built on towers, bracers can be placed for archers to rain fire on infantry as well as to ignite the pitch fields, and we can even place units with oil pots to burn alive those unfortunate enough to get close to the walls. As you can see, the game revolves a lot around sieges, so there are not only measures to defend these fortresses, but also to attack them. There are units that make it easier for others to climb the walls, such as soldiers carrying ladders or siege towers, classic catapults, or trebuchets that can even throw cows and leave a very lethal cloud of pestilence (and a very beloved detail of the franchise, as strange as it may sound). It's a game that really provides an experience focused on the conquest and defense of castles, very tactical, and it feels great.For those who are already familiar with the saga, this edition also has a new game mode: the "Castle Trail", a chain of ten missions of siege or defense of historic castles, and extremely challenging. We also have an improved map editor, Steam integration for multiplayer (which I admit I didn't get to try, because I couldn't find a group the times I tried), and the Steam Workshop to download maps created by the community. I downloaded a very cool one of Minas Tirith! Although I was beaten to a pulp.I can't leave without talking about the audiovisual section, since they made an effort to give it a more modern and detailed look, like the interfaces, but without losing that "old school" vibe so special of the saga. And the music was updated with higher fidelity tracks, which I also appreciate since I really love the melodies that have adorned these games over the years. I understand they also brought back vocal actors from the original Stronghold, a very nice touch.In closing, I wanted to say that it has things that really stuck with me from the first time I played it, who knows how many years ago, and Stronghold: Definitive Edition took me on a nostalgic journey that made me relive those moments, back to when I played it on my brother's PC and in simpler times... but I'll stop there before we all get depressed. The charm of Stronghold is back stronger than ever, and it shows that it was a good game twenty years ago and still is today. I think it's a nice entry point into the RTS genre, and certainly recommended for fans of the genre.

Skirmish matches came in crusader (which I desperately hope gets the definitive edition treatment, the HD is just zoomed out), so sadly as far as I know you can't skirmish against the AI. There are plenty of scenarios and battles which are essentially near enough to a skirmish that I find it satisfying. The graphics are obviously dated but incredibly charming. It's that late 90s early 00s 3d-like sprite art style that doesn't so much look ugly as it does stylistic/dated (you can tell the map poly counts are very late 90s lol). I think it looks good. I haven't even touched any of the community stuff yet. Suffice it to say there's more than enough content here for the money. If you have nostalgia for the game, it's a must buy imo. If you're just an RTS fan, you might enjoy it. Like I said it's very slow paced compared to most RTS games I find. If you like castle builders than you'll probably enjoy this, but it is heavily combat focused in most modes. It's a good game. If it at all looks interesting to you from the screenshots and gameplay trailers, go for it. You won't regret it (and if you do you'll realize long before the refund timer is up I'd guess)

_childDocuments_.review: Only get this if you don't have any of the other Stronghold versions already on Steam. Even then, this is a hard sell. I have been playing Stronghold since I was a kid, when Stronghold first came out. I understand the mechanics and have played the campaigns a few times, particularly the economic one. In this "definitive" edition, some of them are pretty much impossible. The problem is the devs railroad you into almost unwinnable situations, to the point you essentially have to cheese the game and/or use glitches to finish some of the missions. For whatever reason, the devs set the game to bombard you with random events every couple of minutes like pestilence, plague, thieves stealing food, etc. The issue though is these happen every couple of minutes, are (at least in early missions) completely unpreventable, and can literally lead to your entire stronghold failing due to a spiral of popularity and people leaving that is near inescapable. For instance, early on in some missions, plague will affect your town. This has a MASSIVE impact on your citizen's happiness, but because the devs lock most of the buildings to progressing through missions, you don't have access to an apothecary which would address this issue.... so there's literally nothing you  can do besides watch as everyone leaves the stronghold you spent the last 15-20 mins building up simply because the devs don't want to give you the tools to fix these problems early on but clearly didn't think about how often they set them to occur. On top of that, the devs never really do anything when they re-release these old games. Like, there's a couple of improvements, but it feels like they kind of take the Skyrim approach and re-release their games every couple of years. Anyway, yeah, don't get the game if you want to play a fair and balanced campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold has since I was a child been one of my favorite games. I've never really been to interested in RTS games but this game has always had a place in my heart. I've been playing this remake now for quite awhile now and I can happily say It's a really good remake! There are some small things here and there that could be improved upon and I hope the devs keep on updating this game as it's a really good game that really deserves their attention. Some of the flaws that I've noticed is the following: - Zooming is a fixed zoom and not "free zoom" if that makes sense. I would love for it to be so that you can zoom as much as you want or as little. The default zoom is either too much or too little, would be great with a middle ground or "free zoom". - Dialog can at times be hard to hear. I know you can adjust the music / dialog volume but it feels a bit off at times. - Enemy troops can enter the castle in walls that doesn't make sense for them to be able to enter. There is a gap that you cannot see and this is usually is around hills and rocks. I've lost a few battles because they've been able to enter when I thought it was closed. - When you are fully zoomed out there is very much aliasing, maybe some AA would be beneficial to add? I've noticed that this also applies for stone walls. Other than what I've written above I'm really happy with this release. It's not only good but actually really cheap compared to other remasters I've seen. It's basically the same thing you get with the HQ editions but you also get improvement on features and updated graphics plus more campaing and an updated multiplayer! If you're a big stronghold fan then this is the remake you've waited for!

_childDocuments_.review: I have no words to describe how incredible this game is. After 20 years, seeing an improved version of this game released and being able to experience it is a reason for great joy. Only those who really valued the first Stronghold know how perfect this game is now, and how wonderful to play it is. Every detail of the game is enchanting and you spend hours admiring and playing that you don't even realize how many hours you spent. That phrase you hear when you're playing: "It's too late Sir, aren't you tired?" It never made so much sense. Seeing the people working on the beauty of the castles, the details of the animals, the swaying of the trees and being able to fight against the most feared enemies is fascinating. This is the best game in the history of games. Thank you Firefly for this gift, thank you for this work of art. Being able to experience and be part of this is a reason for great gratitude, thank you, thank you very much!

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE stronghold, I have logged loads of hours in the HD edition and hundreds of hours in my childhood and will always have fond memories, and think everyone should try it. Saying that I CANNOT recommend Stronghold Definitive Edition and that is really upsetting.From the start the opening movie is now wide screen but stretched. In fact nearly all the movies and character portraits are stretched to the point they are badly disfigured and pixelated.There is no skirmish/bot mode. The new "castle trail" campaign which looks like the campaigns in crusader, is more invasion/siege maps with a map style menu. In my opinion, the new main menu has lost a lot of the charm the original one had.The newer visuals are nice, though all the effects from the buildings makes the screen too busy when you have a big city. The models of the soldiers look stiff and plastic, especially against solid backdrops like marsh. The zoom and updated controls are great though.The weakest point of the original Stronghold was the troop tactics. No formation, grouping, bad pathfinding etc. Which was fine in 2001 but nothing has changed in over 20 years and there is a big push for the multiplayer which will make it struggle against other RTSs.Old maps are still here which is great (though they are dated 2023 for some reason) but this includes the one titled "user created map" which looks odd. Maybe when the new campaigns come out this be worth the time, but (to me) it feels like Firefly hopped on the remaster bandwagon and tried to stick something together and the title Stronghold: Definitive Edition is just that, a title, and does not represent a defining quality of the game. I think it should be the "steam addition" more than anything. Stronghold HD is currently £3.49 on steam, unless you want to support Firefly Studios (which is great!) I would recommend starting there and maybe "upgrading" for the multiplayer when you have completed the campaign.   P.S change the default look of the scribe on startup, no one likes the new one.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to recommend this game, because I love the original and seeing this made me insta-buy because of nostalgia, I won't. There are some glaring gameplay bugs in this version, and I think Firefly could have easily playtested  this before they released to solve them. The fact that they didn't, AND the fact that they've already announced the 2 latest parts of the campaigns to be behind a paid DLC (making me have to pay more to get the entire story), makes me see this as a fast moneygrab and not worth my attention.First the good:2 new campaigns, awesome! I loved the new variety, and the scripted events on some "make your way through this map" missions were a fun addition to my stronghold experience.Steam multiplayer looks like it works. This is a nice addition, but frankly, I loved stronghold for the singleplayer aspect so I didn't care much about this one.Now the meh:There are new sounds in this game. They are nice, but volumes are all over the place. Additionally, sounds are stereo by default. One of my ears is deaf, which means that if I play this game with a headset, I will not hear the announcer say that I am being attacked when my keep is to my right on my screen. Very annoying, but I get that they didn't put up this accessability as a priority. Sad though, that I didn't have this problem in the original game.Click-Hitboxes of units are all over the place. it's harder than in the original to put units closely next to eachother, because you will probably select a unit you didn't want if you give a move order near it. This can be alleviated a bit using the new "modern" rts control scheme, where your RMB and LMB commands are shuffled a bit, but I shouldn't have to evade ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hitboxes by changing my controls.Improved visuals are nice in theory, but they look so much similar to the old visuals that there is not much reason to prefer these over the stronghold HD ones. Now the ultra-bad: There are some very dumb programming mistakes in this game that were not in the original.First off, in the Jewel campaign with the Snake. They wrote some new AI for this game, making them prioritize gatehouses above "the weakest part in the wall". Unfortunately, when I do not build a gatehouse at all (because why would I want to walk to my signpost?) the AI... does not prioritize anything anymore. The enemy soldiers just stand still. If they feel REALLY motivated, MAYBE they will decide to stand still under your walls while getting pelted by your archers. Means I can win almost all "hold out until last battle" missions if I just wall off the signpost area. Very easy to spot bug, very dumb that they didn't catch it, very gamebreaking.Additionally, there is a bug in the siege mode. If I select a map, then switch to attacking side, then back to defending side, and then start, I will have no army attacking me and I will instantly win the map. Probably the attacking army gets set to 0, because you can select a custom army now as the attacker in a siege. This means that at least it not unplayably broken, because if you do not switch between attacker/defender, the attacking army will be there like normal. Still, very dumb bug. Come on, firefly programmers, you can do better than this.All in all, new campaigns are nice, but Firefly ffs hire some proper software testers.

_childDocuments_.review: No campaign co-op, neither single nor multiplayer skirmish mode, the map size is still limited to what it was in the 1990's for no logical reason, multiplayer very frequently crashes and has other extreme bugs that make it unplayable (EG 8 players will be in a game, you can confirm you're all in-game via a video call & screen sharing, but the game only detects 1-4 of you), etc.The issues go on, but perhaps worst of all is how the toxic community excuses all of this with, "This is *the* definitive way to play the game, so of course it's okay that there are almost no improvements to the gameplay whatsoever! You're all so dumb for thinking the 3rd release of the same game should have significant improvements to justify making and selling it as if it's a new game, rather than a small update to the 2nd release, Stronghold HD!" But in fairness, as of now I'm seeing fewer toxic fanboys in reviews and forum discussions calling others dumb for rightfully pointing out to FF Studios, "You've had over 20 years to learn from your successes and failures. When you release a product, could you improve upon it in the ways that players enjoyed the most, please?"On the bright side, this fiasco taught me about the Stronghold Europe mod and Stronghold mods in general.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game now, i played a bit but the input lag is still there. Also i found it hard to navigate with the zoom levels being still unintuitive to use: (e.g. i can't put it to a resolution where i can zoom fast and see the map without having the issue of noisy textures and hard to see units).There are many little bugs, like e.g. the moonwalking troops, that break the immersion.It is not only visually unpleasant to view, but also the hitboxes of the units and buildings aren't aligning with the visual art.On that note: Many of those things were already present in the demos, and have been voiced by the community,I've also taken a look at the campaigns, and from the things that i've seen, i find them lackluster in their storytelling as well as their mission and gameplay design. Especially compared to the community content collected on Heavengames over the years (its not even close,...).I like the bugfixes as well as the steam MP implementation, but i think they don't justify buying the game for its price (sometimes MP doesn't even work properly).I would expect some more QoL stuff from a DE like hotkeys from Crusader. Or at least feature parity with the original, like the v mode. I think this is not the standard that was set by the original games back then, with lots more attention to detail.I am sad to say, that i ll return the game after playing for just 50 minutes :frowning:I had good hopes.... now i am disappointed.**I beg you FireFly**, if you ever want to work on the Crusader Definitive Edition you need to change your stance on how you work with the community. This whole project could have flourished from outside input, other indie studios have managed to pull it off too! And with Community, i mean those creators and modders who have catered to the audience of these games for the past 20 years and kept it alive for this long. _childDocuments_.review: Stronghold: Definitive Edition is Stronghold 1 we all love, but vastly remastered in many ways to fit the modern standards. Refreshed visuals (they look gorgeous, by the way) and music; new features; Steam Workshop; multiplayer integrated with Steam; a lot of quality of life improvements; and many more... All of that without affecting the core mechanics of the game itself and, of course, its brilliant atmosphere that surely made a lot of older players fall in love with this game back in the day. Not to forget the fact that the game works like a charm.This is clearly the best way to play and experience Stronghold 1. It doesn't matter if you played the older versions of the game in the past, or perhaps you may want to check out this fine classic at last. "Definitive Edition" is truly worth its name. It also reminds us that Stronghold 1 is not only the first video game of the well-known Stronghold franchise, but also that - even after all those years - its gameplay holds up as a great classic castle building simulator. And like I mentioned earlier, the Definitive Edition's improvements and new content, really make the difference, if compared to the older versions of the game. They allow players to experience Stronghold 1 in all its glory and in a pleasant way, fitting the modern standards.Thank you, Firefly Studios, for remastering this game in such a fantastic way!

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, life in the old castle.Let me preface this by saying that I've played Stronghold since I was 4~ years old when it came out.There is so much to say about this game, I'll try to say as much as possible while keeping to the point. I am a massive Stronghold fan, always have been, I think I've bought 5-6 or so copies of the game, be it for different Steam accounts, or gifts for friends, or buying it also on GoG etc. etc. I've always enjoyed and loved this game and it's a game I keep returning to and always will keep returning to.Finally after 20 or so years Firefly have finally made the sensible choice of returning to their one working games in their IP. The thinking is sound, you iterate on the old product and you offer improvements in order to offer a more attractive product and get sales.What does this remaster offer this time around? A new campaign. It's pretty good. The campaign itself does not warrant the price though in my opinion, so wait for a sale if you can. Part of the reason why I think it's not good enough is the fact that I find the level design to be lackluster at times. Stronghold is a game often described as "castle sim," revolving around building castles, but annoyingly enough I feel like most map designs heavily encourage people to just build a wall or set of fortifications between point A and point B to defend against enemy attacks, which to me does not encourage much strategic depth and thinking. It truly is a shame because the maps themselves often look great but the gameplay does not differ much from map to map when the only difference is "build a wall and some towers to block off this cliffside," "build a wall and some towers to block off this peninsula" or "build a wall and some towers to block off this mountain pass." I get that this might come off as nit picky but I can't help but feel like I expect more when we're paying for the development of this remaster.New remastered graphics. I'm torn on these. This is subjective, but in my opinion the new graphics fail to capture the charm that the old game has. It may very well be due to the nostalgia of having played this game for 20 years, but it just doesn't feel right to me personally. However a point on the graphics that is not subjective is that they have not done a great job with the animations for some units. For whatever reason they chose to replace/slightly change the graphics of the swordsmen and the knights, which is fine (though me personally I thought the old ones were more charming, but again, that is subjective,) but what really stands out with them is that the framerate of these two units is simply way too high, and the movements of them completely lacks any sense of weight. I strongly prefer the look that the old swordsmen had for example, because they felt more powerful simply because they looked like they were heavy. The new swordsmen almost sort of look like they are sliding across the surface. The knights as well look like they are moving way too fluidly and unnaturally, and also they weirdly lean back into their saddles.This remaster has multiplayer support. That's a big plus. Get it if your friends are nagging you to play with them, if you want I guess. If you can disregard the other points that I've already made.This remaster also introduces a few new bugs. That is to be expected of course when the game is remade in Unity, but it's just a bit disappointing to see both your melee units ignore battering rams that could have been destroyed before they reach your walls. Same way that it is also disappointing to see a siege tower get destroyed, but still see enemy units use the "destroyed" invisible siege tower to scale your walls in a completely unfair way and kill your lord.For these reasons I simply can't whole-heartedly recommend getting this game. I still recommend people to get the original when it's on sale, but if someone asked me "should I get Stronghold: Definitive Edition?" I'm probably gonna say no.

_childDocuments_.review: I really was excited about this game. I also actually played the first of the new campaigns. It's really not that special, but it is more optimized for new computers. No need to mess with the resolution. I also haven't really seen that many bugs aside from a few annoying ones like a rock being here, or not being able to build on top of bushes, but I now think the latter is intentional. The best parts of the "definitive edition" is that you can adjust more things control and hotkey related. They also changed other things like the main menu and designs of certain things. Most of the time, I don't even notice the difference between the improved designs of buildings and whatnot. The original campaign is basically the same, but the colors look like they were too defined and bright; however, while I prefer the original look for the cut-scenes and character portraits, I'll admit that the new look doesn't look terrible. It is strange how Sir Longarm and Lord Woolsack's portraits have a golden hue to them, but all in all it's not so bad.      The best things about this remaster is that you can zoom in and out more freely, adjust hotkeys as you like, and a grouping mechanic which is actually quite helpful- but don't use the number 9 option because you'll get those units stuck in that slot without being able to adjust it. I suppose they apparently added the Steam Workshop and such; but honestly, as a game, it's not much better, and the new content isn't worth it.   There were times I would be in annoyed wonderment; like, why the heck can't I build stuff other than quarry's on top of the stone reserves? Where did such a dastardly idea come from? Why doesn't a Cathedral or Church add a small bonus like before? How come the new maps weren't that well refined? I can't build something in a perfectly well-enough sized spot because of a single-dot of uneven ground, rock, or bush? When was it that you couldn't build on top of bushes? Not trees, bushes of all things. How come my ranged units require so much micro-management at times? The original stuff is still just about the same or as good as in the original, but some stuff makes the game annoying.    I finished the first part of the new campaign, but it's more of a pain than anything fun and engaging. The story is extremely lackluster, unfortunately the VA's performance is somewhat lacking, and the missions themselves are terrible. The maps used are more of a pain than not as well. The fighting on said maps are annoying because of the enemy troop placements, like they have two or three missions where you go through this maze-like map to get to the end. The first one wasn't so bad, but there was one where I almost wanted to just stop because of how bad the design and arrangements were. To be clear, the maps mostly weren't hard, they were just tedious and tiring. They say the new campaign is made for "veteran players", but it was such a pain and nothing like the original campaign. If you like more modern and adjustable, and maybe like anything and everything new from Firefly even if the new missions are just a pain and wearisome, then you probably won't care for this remaster's shortcomings. I would recommend just getting the original because it still has a lot to offer which is what most of this one is anyway, and it's quite a bit cheaper. I almost want to fully recommend it, but I didn't particularly enjoy everything that's new. More of a painful experience than a fun one regarding the new content, but I can't say the same for the original. I will always be glad for the original content. I wish I could give it a 3/5 stars kind of rating, or a neutral one. It's good, but essentially only because of what was already established beforehand. Some of the new stuff are nice, but not the campaigns.

_childDocuments_.review: I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LOVE this one. The old Stronghold was already one of the favourite games of my childhood and this DE version honors it incredibly well. _childDocuments_.review: It is not easy being a stronghold fan.For over 20 years now we watched Firefly trying to capture even a glimpse of the brilliance they captured with stroghold and stronghold crusader, the latter of which released in 2002. Fore two decades we bought title after title hoping they would have returned to that original spark that put their studio on the map, only to be disapointed time and time again. We have experienced everything from from buggy titles, ugly graphics, dysfunctional clients, broken AI and unfinished releases and compared to all those set backs stronghold definitive edition is at last a step in the right direction. However Firefly chose to call this remaster a definitive edition, yet there is precious little definitive about it. They had 20 years, 20 years to get this right and yet we are still confronted with the same frustrating bugs, from units disappearing to broken AI, on top of gaining an entirely new issue on the side of online functunality, which is practically none existent. Compared to the features and improvements of other companies definitive editions, which they deliberately invited comparison too when they labeled it as such, this is a sad excuse for another round of cashing in on Stronghold Nostalgia.This game is perfectly serviceable as a remaster, it is an accurate to the original and makes notable improvements in areas  like aspect ratio. So I am not gonna tell die hard stronghold fans not to enjoy it, after 20 years of worse and worse stronghold titles, this game must appear like drops of a water in the uncaring desert, but for anyone that looks for a deeper  truely defintiive experience they are probably better off just playing a modded version of crusader or just save the money and keep playing stronghold for what little this game offers in extra content: two very short campaigns and a campaign trail, which is again more frustrating than fun due to broken AI. But then again maybe you just appreciate the slightly prettier pictures, although if you want to see how far the love and dedication has fallen just look at what they did to your poor advisor (and yes I know you can turn his appearance back to the old version, its just sad that I felt the need to do that, which again I find runs contradictory to what a definitive edition should stand for).

_childDocuments_.review: The low entry point of this Definitive Edition doesn't quite justify the low effort put into the "Remaster" part of what this Remaster was expected to be. This episode is the exact same 20-year-old Stronghold with a few more-than-welcome (but how could it have been otherwise?...) quality-of-life features and slightly updated graphics to suit modern monitors, with a few more Siege maps and a (short) secondary campaign.Those who expected Firefly to seize this opportunity to redesign the game by adding a Skirmish Trail, co-op and economy tweaks based on the Stronghold Crusader experience will get none of that here, with the developers stating clearly this will never happen. Subsequently, there are only 2 stances left. If you're merely happy to delve back into your beloved "childhood RTS" with a tad more content, then definitely go for this Definitive Edition. If you expected a Stronghold 2.0, you should avoid it instead as you'll feel the devs are just trying to milk an old cow playing on players' nostalgia. Both points of view are equally valid in my opinion so your choice should solely boil down to your level of expectations and fandom.Since Steam doesn't allow for a Neutral review, I'll personally lean slightly towards the Negative side as I expected more from this Remaster. But as stated previously, your mileage may vary greatly. To put things into perspective however, I still rank the original Stronghold Crusader as the best episode in the whole franchise, including this latest addition.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally! Some good food!If you've followed FireFly up until the release of Stronghold DE, then you'd know that they had delivered on pretty much everything they've promised, and for a very reasonable price too.I'm pretty sure that everything from the original title is here, with an extra bit of polish. _childDocuments_.review: This is a graphical remaster of an old RTS game that clearly shows its age as this game lacks many features that would become well known in the genre not too long after Stronghold came out. Things such as being able to select a group of units and then having a little box show up detailing each individual unit, allowing you to click on specific portraits to give commands to one guy without having to hunt for them in the crowd. This makes ordering wounded soldiers off the frontline an issue, compounded by the fact you can't zoom in far enough to be able to reliably click on one person in a group, often getting two or three per click.Another thing to note is the game is not entirely clear where deficiencies are. Low food production can sneak up on you, as there are no flashing numbers on screen to let you know what's falling behind leading to many instances of running very low on bread. The only way (that I'm aware of) to see how many unemployed pops you have is to click on the barracks which will detail it there for you. Lastly, I've had to restart many missions because it turns out there was a tiny gap in my wall that I couldn't see.Now, while it's understandable some may get upset at this lack of creature comforts I personally love it. There is a time and place to remaster a game, and a time and a place to remake a game and I think the devs made the right call on remastering this instead of remaking it. A game like Dark Souls 1 absolutely should have been remade in order to fix the game's pacing and level design post Lordvessel, but I can't help but feel adding new creature comforts to an old game like this would've been a dis-service. This game is a look into the past on what RTS games used to be and I'm all for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the original Stronghold 1 and crusader titles, they are the first RTS games I ever played and up to this day I am able to get back into them and enjoy myself thoroughly, 20+ years later.The DE version however still needs work, a lot of basic features don't work anymore. I cannot use laddermen to mount on walls with crenelations.The ultrawide support is nice, but when you can either fully zoom in or fully zoom out, in both cases it makes it kind of hard to play, there should be a 50% zoom option. The music volume decreases when units talk which is very distracting, it's like i'm in a skype call or something. The double clicking of units with the "modern rts controls" also doesn't work properly for me, most of the time it doesn't actually select more units.Quite frankly I don't understand why they only put one developer on the project. This game is really special and it needs to be given better treatment to be able to speak to a new audience.These are all complaints of things they actually said they would fix or issues that are new, I would have also loved to see bots in MP, for that I hope they will also make a crusader rerelease. It would also have been nice to get some redone soundtracks like they did with Age of empires DE.It's still worth the money if you haven't had the chance to play the original, but it needs some polish still.

_childDocuments_.review: STONE NEEDED ME LORD!! Been playing Stronghold since I was like 8 years old. I'm 32 now. This was the game that started my love for RTS games. Plus, the original, or rather, Stronghold HD held up really well. And personally, I have never been a big stickler for graphics so I wasn't sure if a "definitive edition" of this classic game was necessary. But man this is DEFINITELY worth it!For starters, the graphics and animations are all updated and they look great. So thats all well and good, but what really got me excited was all the new content and modern quality of life features! A whole new campaign (I forgot the name of) A kingmaker trail! Which was a mode that was introduced with Stronghold Crusader. I haven't tried it yet, nor the new campaign but I am very excited for their inclusion. Another update for this version is Steam Workshop support! The workshop support has done a lot for Stronghold Warlords and I can't wait to see some of the content that people come up with for it.On top of what was there before, we get all this new content plus a road map with a lot of exciting stuff planned! And these guys have had a good track record of sticking to their plans (At least they did with Warlords when it comes to the roadmap). All in all I would highly recommend! Especially for the price, its a solid RTS and a legendary classic, only made better by new controls (WASD camera control/ Q&E rotating screen) that you can choose between "Classic" and "Modern" controls, which was very nice to see. Only issues I have found so far are audio issues. When you get a "Message from your scribe" and the message proceeds to play at the same time. Which is a minor issue that will probably be patched soon.I would be lying if I said I wasn't sad to not see a skirmish mode V AI. The original didn't have it until Crusader, but there is a lot of new content that wasn't in the original game already so I am very excited about that. Even though they don't mention skirmish v AI in the road map, I am still hopeful, and again, excited for what is coming in the road map.TL:DR If you are a longtime Stronghold fan and love the original game GET THIS ONE! It has everything you use to love with even more content and planned DLC for the Pig and Wolf with the original Voice Actors! Very exciting stuff. If you are new to Stronghold this is a great place to start with the updated graphics and modern controls and QOL features! Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game now as the multiplayer is worse than in the original game with Game Ranger. The game lobby is very bugged. Most often you cannot see yourself and mark that you're ready to play. This itself is enough for me to justify the negative review. There wasn't a lot done feature wise for this release so if they cannot get the bare basics of the multiplayer working then I think it shows just how much they care about this project. Just to prove how bad it is, it took us 20 minutes of recreating lobbies and rejoining games to get the first game to start.The second problem are the clear expectations that were not met. From the moment that this project was announced people were very vocal about the skirmish/bots in multiplayer feature. The developers were clear about not intending to add that but then what is the point of spending any time on the remaster if the improvements are just going to be cosmetic and clearly ignore the demand. IMO the price point does not justify the feature set and whenever I want to feel the nostalgia I can get it from the original game. As for playing with friends we mainly do it in Crusader and better bots from UCP so this edition does not tick any of those boxes.I bought this game just because I want to encourage Firefly to properly remaster Stronghold Crusader and I know that it won't happen if this project is not at least moderately well received. However, after seeing how little attention and resources were put into this project (judging by the state of the game at release) I feel like there is no hope. Perhaps the studio is no longer capable of releasing something decent that will also address the key issues and needs of the player base.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the best remaster, but neither the worst. All of the most annoying problems of Stronghold are still present here - the maps are still too small to have proper building freedom in multiplayer, any tower can still be manned with absurd amounts of soldiers by exploiting unit clipping. Townsfolk still annoy you by constantly blocking placement of buildings and walls. Mod support is still not a thing - Steam Workshop is for custom maps only. AI Skirmish isn't there as well, though the game has enough content to replace it, so the problem is not that critical.Even though the remaster is not what I really expected, it still is the one and only Stronghold - a great game with lots of high quality and unique mechanics, wonderful art, sound and music and fantastic atmosphere. The campaigns are great, the siege / assault / economic missions are a very entertaining challenge.All in all, a wonderful game, a must-have for sure. If anyone reading this haven't ever played Stronghold - you should definitely start here. The remaster doesn't change much but the core still is as great as it has always been. For those, who have already been playing Stronghold, however, I would advise to think before buying - even though the changes in this remaster are quite welcome, 99% of it is still the same game. If you are short on money and you already have Stronghold HD - I would not recommend it, buy something else instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give thumbs down to this because I like the core game so much, but this is a very lazy remaster. I know the original inside and out -- fantastic game. The sound has issues and is unbalanced, such as wolves growling in the distance sounding really off. The map "pull down" feature (hotkey V) from the original was removed for some reason, which for many situations was more useful than the "flatten map" feature they did keep. The targeting reticle is much smaller and non-adjustable. I don't understand any of this at all. It's a downgrade in so many ways.The only reason to buy this would be to explore the new campaign. It also introduces custom hotkeys which is great if that's your thing -- I certainly appreciate that. But if I had bought this for more than $15, I'd have felt ripped-off. _childDocuments_.review: The classic strategy game is back, and in a good way. For those who never played it - its a medieval real time strategy with a focus on castle on castle siege combat. Its quite compact and easy to understand with its basic production chains and simple units, but has good skill expression through optimizing speed and position of everything you manage. There is no tech tree ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or special ability showdown. All players have access to same tools.Its very atmospheric and charming despite its simplistic isometric visuals, with lovely Medieval England aesthetics, great music, sound design and voices. There is a decent variety of content and challenge - you got the main story, siege missions, economic missions and free build. There is no PvE skrimish setup like they had in Stronghold Crusader, but they never said it would be added, so its just a bit of a shame.Regardless, now that its plugged into Steam Workshop, for just 15 bucks you get a great RTS experience that can be great fun for either those evenings after work or gathering friends for some PvP on the weekend

So it is quite important to come up with a manageable building schedule. The scale of the game is simply groundbreaking for a game this old. Truth to be told, the DE really manages to bridge the time gap as the game looks and sounds really fresh! Onwards to glory!

The short campaigns (not featured in the original title) feel much more challenging than the main campaign, yet some of the missions felt a little unimaginative (run through a map wide canyon and reach the flag. But the regular "build up your castle and defend it" missions were guaranteed original Stronghold quality, only more challenging (had to lower the difficulty) but this is nothing but a good thing.Definitely recommendable for the current price, especially if you have played Strongholds before but also for the newcomers, don't be afraid to jump in.

_childDocuments_.review: For what is a relative pittance (15 bucks is very affordable) Stronghold DE brings Stronghold back to modern hardware, the graphics update makes the game look crisp without ruining the original aesthetic and does an excellent job to translate it into the modern era.The game looks as it does in -my memories- and not the jagged pixillated reality that loading OG Stronghold would do.The modern control scheme for someone who hasn't played a while is nice as well, and if you've played any sort of sim or rts, you'll probably find it easy to pick up and play with minimal translation error. Also, you can play Fullscreen, borderless windowed -and- windowed without hassle. A problem which plagued HD, meaning you can now have a second window open, which in a world where most PCs have a dual screen setup is much appreciated, also the 3k unit limit is awesome.At this price point with these quality of life changes, I would already consider Stronghold DE well worth the money, but now with proper Workshop support, a functional multiplayer and entirely new campaigns. Not only do you get the joy that is the original Stronghold, you get fresh content to go with it as well.After playing for 9 hours, I had no major issues, no crashes, not CTDs, it ran smoothly and I was just castle building like I did when I was a wee pup.Here's to hoping that Stronghold DE will pay off enough to convince Firefly to give Crusader the same treatment. So the people with lapsing memories of what is in which game will be able to play skirmish.

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly believe that such an approach to remastering should be more commonly practiced. What personally appeals to me a lot is that, besides refreshing the legendary production, new campaigns have been added, with more planned in the future. This means the game hasn't lost its flavor, and furthermore, we have the opportunity to delve deeper into the story. On top of that, multiplayer has also been added through which you can connect via Steam, and the price for the game is really attractive. It's possible to make the childhood game even more enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: A great REMASTER of the good Stronghold game.Improved graphics, music, animations, mechanics, etc.New campaigns (with more coming soon), focusing on both economic and military aspects. Split in multiple categories you can play the economic ones or the military ones.There are also separate missions (both economic and military).There are sieges and invasions, where you can assault and/or defend historical emplacements (castles from all over Europe).-- YOU CAN CHOOSE WHETHER TO ATTACK OR DEFEND IN EACH ONE.--- MOD SUPPORT. For example, invade Helm's Deep from The Lord of The Rings.The Sandbox/Freeplay is still here, and made better through additional parameters you can configure before playing AND DURING YOUR PLAY (PRESS F1 FOR THE MENU).Your name is spoken on launch once set (and can be changed later-on. For example I am welcomed with 'Good Morning, Lord Daniel'. Depending on time of day it changes which is amazing.-- They also have that for voicelines during missions and actions such as 'Surrender, Lord Daniel?' when I wish to surrender in a match.DOWNSIDE: There is no skirmish in Multiplayer (yet), so you can only do PVP, not PVE.UPSIDE: Singleplayer there is Freeplay, siege, siege that, invasion and custom maps.Multiplayer works flawlessly now, you don't require Hamachi anymore because it is steam steam multiplayer now.Built-in Map editor, with upgraded functionalities etc.Built-in Steam Workshop support.New unit: Monk. Imagine macemen but Religious.~~~~Difficulty:The game is made by veterans, for veterans. The missions are already challenging on Medium Difficulty. This is done by changing starting units and resource amounts, or additional random events or enemy mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not happy to write this review, since it is the first time I give a thumbs down for a Firefly title (Well, SH3 was bad, but this is quite obvious!). After playing both demos and looking through the missions of the final release, I am not satisfied with SH:DE. The game requires much more polishing regarding mission design, story telling with regard to the new campaign as well as bug fixing. To provide some examples: There are UI elements that are disproportionate, some textures lack details compared to the original release (e.g. wooden walls), the scribe seems to be less vivid when it comes to commenting on events throughout the campaign... and crashes are also a thing! Several bugs that existed for 20+ years now have not been fixed yet. But most importantly, I am not sure, if the level design is intended the way it is. Mission 1 plays a bit like mission 13 of the original: Move your crossbowmen, so they can shoot the enemy, wait for enemy units to be killed, repeat... I hope that Firefly is going to improve SH:DE with patches to come. I continue to be faithful, since SH1 is a great game in its core, which is why I recommend to wait with the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I love the original Stronghold, bought the HD version and immediately this one too. I spent countless of hours, enjoying the previous games, but this one is definitely a major letdown. At least, objectively speaking. The original game is almost a quarter century old, and always had some shortcomings. Glitching issues, pathfinding problems and such. In the early 2000s we easily overlooked this, but it's shortcomings became painfully obvious when I played the game again.Which means, that FireFly Studios didn't really do anything meaningful with the game, just gave it a graphical facelift and that's all. I didn't expect major overhaul, fully expanded campaign and such, but to be frank, not even minimal effort was put into this game.- Unit pathfinding is still abysmal and seemingly at random, especially in larger groups.- Moat filling is still annoying, units stretch out as wide as possible, exposing themselves to danger.- Even with aggressive setting, archers/crossbowmen sometimes fail to shoot at targets, you have to micromanage them.- Last, but not least, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mission design stayed. Hello Mission #15, Carving the Path. Here, you can only cheese your way through, exploiting AI and map design like in the originals. _childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible! While I never played the original, I have always been a huge fan of Stronghold Crusader and moderately a fan of the other Stronghold entries. It's the most like Crusader, and I mean this as a huge positive, both games have similar/same animations, characters, units, and music. The feel this game, and Crusader, capture is unlike any other game in the genre. You do not get games with this much charm, unique and smooth gameplay, or music as good as this. This is Stronghold done right! I love the updated graphics and how smooth this game runs!I am hoping the positive reviews and success of this definitive edition show Firefly that Crusader would be just as much, if not more of a success! I also hope it highlights how much Stronghold 1 and Crusader features are valued while they create their next big Stronghold title.I do have some complaints:1.  No Skirmish mode - The original also did not have this mode, but this mode is arguably the mode that keeps players playing the longest and allows more replay ability, especially for those who don't like playing against real players online.2. No AI in multiplayer - There is no option to face AI in a multiplayer match, only real players. This just stopped at least 2 people I know from buying the game. I wonder how many others? As I mentioned above, there are players who do not like playing against real players, and having AI in multiplayer would have allowed the game to reach a larger audience and as well add more replay ability.I love this game, I can't wait to complete the campaign and all the addicting challenges Stronghold is so good at, but coming from Crusader, which had skirmish and the option for AI in multiplayer matches, I felt disappointed that I will inevitably complete this game and have little reason to return once I finish the missions. Whereas if it had those features, I'd play this for years with my sister. I am hoping they update to add one or both of these features, but I do not have my hopes too high.All in all, it's a great and true remaster of Stronghold 1. If you're a fan of the original and/or Crusader, pick this up and play! Show the developers your support for this incredible gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆Pros:-The classic stronghold with higher resolution and several improvements.-Achievements add an extra layer of challenge.-The inclusion of automatic trading is a significant plus, streamlining economic management.Cons:-Disappointed by the absence of cooperative play in multiplayer.-Expected the return of the original narrators and a new campaign with their iconic voices.Unfortunately, the new campaign features only one new narrator, narrating the story through journal entries before missions, which can get monotonous.-The missions in the new campaign, however, introduce a fresh format, such as navigating from one side of the map to the other while rescuing units along the way, adding a new dynamic to gameplay.Overall Impression:Stronghold Definitive Edition is a nostalgic journey with enhanced features, making it a worthy experience for both returning players and newcomers. While there are some missed opportunities, the new campaign's unique mission format adds a refreshing twist to the classic gameplay. Looking forward to future updates and improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Good morning, Your Lordship!The moment has come for a classic strategy game to return in its rejuvenated form – "Stronghold: Definitive Edition". This game does more than just invite us to revisit childhood; it immerses us in a world of medieval castles and strategic battles, now refreshed with updated graphics and high-resolution support.Graphics and AtmosphereThe “washed” graphics retain the familiar visuals but now appear more vibrant and detailed. Enjoy the stunning landscapes of your settlements and watch battles where every sword glistens in the sun. The soundtrack complements this atmosphere, transporting us deep into medieval adventures.Strategy and SurvivalDon’t forget about cheese – it’s a crucial part of your strategy and economy! Whether you focus on military actions or economic development, remember: a good stock of cheese is essential for your army's survival.Multiplayer and New MissionsThe multiplayer now functions flawlessly, allowing battles against friends and other players. New missions add freshness and challenge, prompting you to make innovative strategic decisions.Nostalgia and NoveltyFor those who remember the original game, "Stronghold: Definitive Edition" offers a dive into nostalgic memories. New players will discover a fascinating and thrilling world of medieval strategies.ConclusionAnd, of course, I must mention our faithful servant, always ready to report the latest events. His voice now sounds even clearer and more realistic, thanks to improved audio.Verdict"Stronghold: Definitive Edition" is not just a reissue; it's an opportunity to experience a classic strategy in a new light. This game combines the best of the past and present, creating a unique gaming experience.Rating: 10 castles out of 10.Message to FireFly Studios: Your efforts are appreciated, Your Lordship. We invite you to a world where every decision you make can change the course of history.

Their accessible map tool with so many triggers, effects, conditions, etc... has given SO MUCH single player content for anyone to enjoy after they've already finished the base game or wanting something different. Firefly needs to take a page out of their book because more community tools is so good for games like this extending their life. If not this game Firefly, consider this in future games. You guys like money right?Lastly as of now, there are still bugs and issues. (Especially multiplayer) but they have seemed very prompt to acknowledge and fix things in a timely manner. They have been communicative and upfront about their development, which is more than can be said for many other developers these days.All in all if you enjoyed the original Stronghold and would like the new graphics, quality of life, new campaigns, future updates along with cheap DLC, and accessible multiplayer without going through gameranger or whatever else. _childDocuments_.review: Stronghold, the original BAFTA-nominated RTS castle sim, returns in a definitive edition that aims to recapture the essence of the classic. Set in medieval England, it offers a blend of strategic military campaigns and city-building elements. Despite its promising premise, the remake may not entirely live up to the expectations of fans of the original.Overall Score: 6.5/10Graphics/Visuals (7/10):The updated graphics are a noticeable improvement over the original. However, while they are good, they don't stand out as exceptional. Sure, the fire looks prettier, but thats not exactly adding a lot of value when the game is missing features that were in the original (looking at you, skirmish mode).Sound & Music (8/10):The remastered music, returning voice talent, and the contributions of series maestro Robert L. Euvino are notable highlights, adding depth and nostalgia to the gameplay experience. The sound is honestly the best part of the remake.Story & Narrative (7/10):The storyline, with its focus on medieval England and the challenge of uniting the kingdom against various lords, remains engaging. However, it doesn't bring much new to the table in terms of narrative innovation. The new campaign isn't all that great as it lacks the castle building elements in a majority of the missions. It just gives you a set amount of troops and says "Good Luck!". The main feature of the game is all the building elements, but it shoots itself in the foot by giving you missions you can't use it.Gameplay & Mechanics (5/10):While the gameplay stays true to the original's spirit, the absence of the skirmish mode is a significant drawback, especially for players seeking a single-player challenge. If you aren't playing multiplayer, there is no way to simply build and fight another kingdom, which was the funnest part of the game.Replayability & Content (6/10):The game offers a decent amount of content with its military and economic campaigns. However, the lack of variety in game modes, particularly the missing skirmish mode, limits its replayability significantly.Innovation & Originality (6/10):While the game attempts to bring classic RTS gameplay to a modern audience, it doesn't introduce substantial innovations or improvements over the original, making it feel somewhat dated. While I get thats the point, when you bring an old game back with less features than it originally had, its gonna be a bad time.Technical Performance & Optimization (10/10):The game performs just fine. No issues.Value (6/10):For fans of the original, the game might hold some value at $15 USD, but the absence of key features and lack of significant updates may not justify the purchase for new players or those looking for a comprehensive RTS experience. You are better off purchasing a previous installment in the series. I can't help but feel like this is a bit of a cash grab.Final Thoughts:The definitive edition of Stronghold nostalgically revisits the classic RTS, but it falls short in delivering a fully satisfying modern remake. The absence of popular features like skirmish mode and the lack of significant new content make it a mixed bag. It's a game that might appeal to die-hard fans of the original for its nostalgia factor but could disappoint those looking for a something more. If I could give it a mixed review, I would, but I can't recommend the game in its current state.

This is simply a blatant scam and a pitiful attempt to capitalize on fans of a game that has already been a maximum disappointment to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold Definitive Edition: 🏰 A Castle Worth Storming Your Wallet For! 💰I recently embarked on a medieval journey that left me craving more chivalry, strategy, and just a touch of insanity. Yes, my fellow gamers, I'm talking about the Stronghold Definitive Edition. If you've ever wondered whether a castle siege simulator could be worth its weight in gold, let me tell you, it's time to grab your catapult and aim for the drawbridge! 🏹🏰From the moment you load up Stronghold Definitive Edition, you're greeted by a jester-like advisor who appears to have had one too many goblets of mead. This character alone is worth the price of admission. His quirky humor and penchant for making questionable strategic decisions will have you giggling through the entire campaign. Who needs a sensible advisor when you can have a manic jester leading the charge? 🤪🃏The game's graphics might not be cutting-edge, but they carry an undeniable medieval charm. You'll witness armies of tiny, pixelated peasants scurrying about, diligently working to build your dream castle. And by "dream castle," I mean a ramshackle collection of wooden huts, surrounded by a perilous moat filled with more crocodiles than the Florida Everglades. Trust me; it's your very own "Deathtrap Manor"! 🏡🐊The soundtrack, if you can call it that, is a collection of merry minstrels playing catchy tunes on their lutes. It might drive you to madness in the best way possible as you try to fend off waves of marauding foes. Battle drums, siege engines, and the screams of your besieged citizens will keep you on your toes, or at least, on the edge of your rickety battlements. 🎶🥁Speaking of battles, the AI in Stronghold Definitive Edition is something to behold. It's as if the opposing lords have undergone rigorous training at the School of Inexplicable Siege Tactics. They'll attack your heavily fortified walls with a handful of archers, then offer to surrender while your castle is still standing strong. It's an AI rebellion of epic proportions! 🤖🏹Stronghold Definitive Edition boasts a multiplayer mode that will have you and your friends competing to see who can turn their castle into the most spectacular disaster zone. It's the ultimate test of your strategic prowess and your ability to withstand the relentless banter of your fellow players. 👫🎮In conclusion, Stronghold Definitive Edition is the ultimate medieval madness package. From the deranged advisor to the perplexing AI, and the musical stylings of our minstrels, it's a game that's worth every gold coin in your digital purse. So, go forth, noble gamer, and conquer this castle simulator. Your jester awaits with open arms and a catapult loaded with laughter! 🃏🏰😂💰

_childDocuments_.review: To start with, Stronghold is an amazing game. It was 20 years ago and still is today. That is... If the design works for it. The Definitive Edition mostly leaves intact what made the original game so outstanding, and the new visuals are definitely nice for the most part. So far so good.The lack of a Skirmish mode like a lot of users pointed out isn't really the issue here. While it's nice to had it backported from the sequel Stronghold Crusader the game could easily do without that provided the Singleplayer content excels over it. And here's the thing. The real problem is what got added into the game, or what which didn't get changed.The main campaign of 21 missions is awesome... But it has 3 awful missions in it centered around you commanding forces to take over a castle. While the missions aren't really that hard on Normal and still fair and doable on higher dificulties it's just an annoying nightmare to deal with those 3 siege missions even on Easy. They're totally not fun in the slighest and you're going to have to rely on an insane amount of saving and loading to get through (in comparison the rest of the missions can just be easily cleared without saving). It's completely out of contrast. While that was always part of the original game too it's a missed opportunity the devs didn't do some proper playtesting. How about considerable more troops, or fewer traps and forces for the opponent on Easy. That's what Easy is for.There's also the economic campaign. It's fine and fun in it's own right, but it has some extremely annoying design going for it. Most hurdles thrown at you come in the form of events, like fires in the fourth mission. Not only erases it all your building in a blink of an eye, but your popularity just nosedives below 50 in a matter of seconds, meaning you have no way to get back up. Especially if your grannary goes out of stock too. The thing is... These are events. You could build water wells to quench the fires but it has to be one of the most useless buildings there is. Forget about trying to clear out the fires in time. Since the events occur at set intervals you keep making saves, and optimize for the best outcome prior to the fire starting. Bandits are fun too. Not because the bandits itself are that much of a hassle but because they obviously have to impact your popularity too. And they raze every structure in your path, and you can forget about your own forces making it in time unless you already had towers and walls set up in time.Speaking about bandits... There's a two new smaller campaigns added into the Definitive Edition... And I feel mixed about it. When it's just a normal mission, it's fine for the most part, but I don't get for example why they rely so much on the economic-style campaign events such as bandits and fires as well. The original campaign didn't do that. And to make things worse, about one-third to half of the missions are siege missions... Yes... The exactly kind of missions you hate so much. It doesn't help that Stronghold doesn't have the cleanest gameplay to control your army with. There's no Attack Move for example like in Age of Empires II. Melee units don't tend to position them in front of your archers. Stuff like that. While none of this was an issue for me during the regular campaign, it does become an issue when mission design makes it it's core.The two new campaigns also lack the same interesting storytelling the original campaign had. While the storytelling was nothing groundbreaking, it was charming with figures such as Sir Longarm, Lord Woolsack and the four villains. Showing the map of England (thank goodness my language sticks the default England map) shifting it's balance of control was already one of my smaller pleasures when playing Stronghold back then. The new campaigns? Forget all of this. Just a background with some scrolling texts. You don't even get to see in the mission overview which new features you got access to in that mission. It just links to the guide now instead. This was another one of those smaller things that added up to the experience.Half of the original campaign is mostly focused on these invasion missions where you build up your fortifications and hold out for like 3 or 4 waves of attacks. And while these type of missions are generally fine and fun they generally don't last long enough in the 2nd half of the campaign. Don't bother trying to set up a whole infrastructure. By the time you done so the final wave has already started. The problem is that once you reach the second half of the campaign your ability to make more complex infrastructures increases too, yet... These missions last just as long, except with stronger and more enemies. It's best to just focus on the essential, boosting your popularity through good things, raise the taxes and buying the weapons from the Market. Producing them yourself just takes too long in missions this short. Maybe this was always the case, but I felt like the original campaign could have been rebalanced here and there. Especially with the mission you have to defeat the Snake you notice why there isn't a Skirmish mode in this game. The AI controlling the Snake is practicially braindead and all challenge in that mission mostly comes from invasions from the Pig at set intervals.There's also some other stuff here and there that doesn't make sense. Why aren't Black Monks recruitable anymore from cathedrals? Did I miss something? Was boosting popularity through religion always that useless? Even with a dozen chapels you barely boost it. Do the townfolk always get in the way when I want to place buildings? Why are minor obstacles on the terrain such a problem now to build structures upon? Especially if you get into missions with barely any space to build. Why do my towers and gates instantly tear down when a new invassion happens if I build them too close by? The game already prevents you from building too close to signposts, so why do they get torn down instantly when I am allowed to build?It's just a shame the original Stronghold couldn't had been better than this. You probably don't want to buy the two new DLCs if their quality is more of that of the new Jewel campaigns in this versions. I feel like a Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition would have gotten away much better with it even if it had the same lack of polished fine-tweaking in some areas and meager new campaigns. It has a Skirmish mode at least and given they keep things as they are, even if only for the Skirmish Trials it would had been an absolute positive.Before I end this on a sour note. I really love Stronghold, and for the price this Definitive Edition is sold at you can't really go wrong with it (even better when on sale). What's there to love about Stronghold is still there, and even if it's only the original campaign it's still very much worth it (if you can resist slamming your keyboard trying to do those siege missions that is). You just need to know what you're getting into: a singleplayer campaign experience, which is perfectly fine. I just wished some more attention was given to the new content and the game was a bit more rebalanced. Some missions are simply too easy. Others too short. Others completely sucks. And others are just too frustating through it's events.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold: Definitive Edition is kind of a mystery to me. I understand why it exists (the developer needs money and had to crank out something cheap and relatively low-effort) but at the same time I really don't. There's already an HD re-release of the original Stronghold, and Definitive Edition really doesn't add much that the HD re-release didn't already have. The biggest question I have is why the developers didn't improve the camera at all. I understand that they wanted to keep it as close to the original as possible, but.. the HD port already exists. It's not like you need to go through some complicated DOSBOX setup or extensive patching to get it to work. The problem with the camera is that the entire game is isometric, and you can only view the game world from four camera angles. On top of that, the game doesn't allow you to move the camera even partially off the game's map, which means that each camera angle cuts off a corner of the map. Hope nothing important's going on there.Along with the camera problems comes the fact that the game's main mechanic is kinda broken. Most of the campaign maps rely on the idea that you have a small force against a larger invading force and use walls and fortifications to make up for the difference. The problem is that building walls isn't great - walls can be built in eight directions (including diagonals) but all wall improvements (towers, gates) can only be built in four directions. This wouldn't be a problem if the game had, say, a hotkey that would make it so that walls snap to straight lines - only as far as I can tell, unless it's not listed in the game's key bindings, no such hotkey exists.The game also makes it hard to tell whether a wall will be effective or not. On one map, I built what I thought was a complete wall only to find out that the wall had a hole in it that the camera would not allow me to see no matter what angle I set it to. It's also hard to tell if an enemy can traverse a given piece of terrain.All of this pales in comparison to the game's unit AI being a buggy mess. Units in this game will try to hit enemies even if they have no chance at doing so, sometimes to absolutely laughable effect, things like the enemy AI's catapults aiming into cliffs because they can see your walls on the other side. Unfortunately, this is a two-way street in that your units will also try to hit anything they can see, even if they can't actually see or hit it. I'd say avoid this until the bugs get patched out. Buy the HD re-release (Stronghold HD) instead at a fraction of the price, or better yet buy Stronghold Crusader HD which people still play online.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like how firefly keep slapping RTS label on their titles, when they lack the fundamental features of an RTS game. (and no, i am not talking about skirmish being missing.) Where is the camera grip, the replay feature, the multiplayer balance?Do not get me wrong, i like the core gameplay of Stronghold, even with its lacking RTS features. It's a nice castle sim with some RTS elements, the king of the hill is fun to play (largely thanks to the backstabbing opportunities it creates) and all.I don't like how the glorifyingly advertised features are broken at launch, (looking at you, multiplayer) even though i expect it to be fixed in coming updates.I don't like how they are about to put a price tag on content that can never hold a candle to the existing, free, and superior content already available online (looking at you, upcoming DLC campaigns). If you are going to put a price tag on anything, do Robert some justice and put the remastered soundtrack as DLC(assuming there is one, maybe my ears are defying me and not allowing me to notice the difference)I don't like how established QOL gets destroyed in a new version of the game(button Z cannot be used for both zooming in and out anymore!, you cannot click on the message video skip it and restore the minimap anymore!, V button is gone, although thats a rather minor one)I don't like how some of the newly implemented QOL is lacking in common sense (who the hell would want to point and click on a flag button for unit rally point and not use the inarguably better method of number hotkeys, which was the implementation for the followup title to the original stronghold)UI being stuck on corner is annoying, it's like windows 11 forcing the centered taskbar items (which they later realised should have the option to put it back to corner again)The visual upgrade overall nice, but even that has some drawbacks, be it in terms of reduced texture moddability, or reduced discernability of certain elements.The added hotkey mapping, and "click to select" mode on building hotkeys (which became the default behavior on future titles) is good.But the ACTUAL good thing that came out of the remaster is the newly added map editor features, because that will allow mapmakers to make more interesting maps. Basically more tools to play with = good. Nice job on that one, the sole programmer of SH:DE!Dealing with firefly is like having  in family, that no matter how many times he messes up, you cannot help but love him and care for him.
