_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I've heard such good things about the series but for some reason it always passed me by. I've tried to play some of the re-releases over the years but could never get them to run properly. So I was excited to try this out.UI is super important to me in games, especially anything to do with strategy or building. And this is... not good. I have to click on my granary to see how quickly my food will run out. Placing gates within walls is painful - you can't rotate buildings, instead you have to choose one of 4 possible orientations in the building menu. And aligning them to my walls was a process of trial and error. There's no way I could find to speed the game up, so the early parts of missions run super slow while you build up your stockpiles. There's no control groups for units. The final straw for me was when my woodcutter walked halfway across the map to chop down trees, instead of walking to the forest right next to his hut, and got ripped apart by wolves.If you played this back in the day then you'll probably love it. It's a handsome remaster in many ways, and you'll probably feel right at home if you're already used to it's quirks. But it didn't do enough to hook me in and the frustrations quickly piled up.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy only if you have a modern PC. It looks like a potato can run it, but for some reason you still need a modern PC for this version of stronghold to work. Had to learn that the hard way LOL.tactics;game mechanics at their core are the same as the legacy games (SH 1 and ST Crusader), but arrows feel like they are nerfed somehow; an archer/crossbow army is not the answer to all problems in this game as it used to be in the legacy games, so be careful of that in your tactics. By consequence; Macemen just became a whole lot scarier Lol; a unit of crossbowmen can no longer stop an equal force of macemen without breaking a sweat; no, the macemen will tank the crossbow bolts long enough to get to the crossbowmen and they will club them.Spearmen are now actually useful and they can actually hold their own against better melee units when they outnumber them like 5 or 4 to 1. Can no longer just wade throw hords of enemy spearmen with a very small force of armored units like the legacy SH versions. In general: it gets some getting used to, but it feels more.. right. each unit in the game has its uses now. The Leather Army tactic (crossbowmen and macemen only) still worms well, but other tactics are just as viable now.Economy: much more limited on where and how you place your mines and quarries, so a mining economy is impossible on most maps now. Ale is maxed out at 4 popularity, and religious buildings are all but useless and are now actually a hindrance as the peasants will "demand more" without you gaining any extra popularity out of it, and you will actually lose popularity if you delete them to switch economy later on, so just don't bother. Max tax is capped at 20 now, so no more 24 tax and max popularity perfection builds.In general; the economy feels more limited and slower, but it is much more agriculture based, and this feels more realistic for the middle ages

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the Stronghold Series since 2006 with the original box set of CDs.Defining games as "Classic" is tossed around a lot these days, but this is a genuine classic. Genre defining of a game it may be, FireFly has yet to release a project after Stronghold & SH: Crusader that could even hold a torch to said games in terms of quality, atmosphere, and general enjoyable. If you are to ever play any Stronghold game, this is the one. If you really enjoy it, pick up SH: Crusader for all the flavor it adds through trails, new unit variety, new terrain (Desert game-play), new lords to interact with and of course skirmishes. FireFly has done what most hardcore fans would expect of this gem, alter little and letting the fans have more content to screw around with (Campaign material focus). If that doesn't sound like much from the developer end, see what they have done to this series over the last twenty years. I really do mean it when I say there hasn't been a good a SH game since this and Crusader. Veterans will understand the value of simplistic alteration and run with it.  Side review: Reviews should primarily be for green players who have never played a FireFly game before. Here is a quick tip when navigating reviews already posted. DO NOT get hung up on negative reviews pointing out the lack of "Skirmish mode". This mode of game-play refers strictly to player vs A.I. in a custom lobby set up by the player. This game originally did not and most likely could not be re-programmed to have skirmish mode due to the lack of A.I. lords available outside of the main story line. If you really like to battle A.I. on your own accord, do so by playing SH: Crusader, the only worthy successor game that has a built-in skirmish mode. Please do not play any of the modern "SH games" (SH:2, SH: Legends, etc, etc.) If you do, do so at your own peril, veterans of SH would easily tell you the 3-D games are a different beast without many positive aspects to them unless you already have nostalgia for them.

_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: True gem as we know from the originals, perhaps the only childhood series that remains engaging and so much fun. My main con is related to the multiplayer (which is otherwise flawless) games can completely freeze, forcing you to leave. Very frustrating, especially far into a match. Unfortunately proves to be a rather consistent occurrence resulting in just a sense of wasting time. They should find a fix more urgently, otherwise love this game to bits.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very faithful modern port of the original game. It runs very smooth on modern systems and it hasn't lost any of it's charm. More importantly there is a LOT more content and the increasing difficulty of the new scenarios is pretty challenging. The missions are also much more diversified in their approach compared to the rinse and repeat model from the crusader path.It is good to see that Firefly is returning to what made them big and it seems that they got the message. Thus far they stayed true to their words: they create and improve the content of the game and communicate transparently. I wholeheartedly support them with this approach and I am really looking forward to what is yet to come.The pricing is really fair considering it is a complete port to a new engine. Fingers crossed they get the resources they need to implement a skirmish mode in the new Unreal 5 project or maybe even in this installment.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic modernization of an iconic game. If you enjoyed the original, this is incredibly money well spent. The developers are proactive and receptive to feedback, extending the life of the game with new content and even more improvements. If you haven't played the original, but like a good RTS with the best castle building/siege elements in any game ever, this is absolutely for you. Take it for a spin, you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Great castle sim. What it isn't: magic, dragons, elves, orcs, or anything fantasy. What it is: build castles, have a functioning economy with food production and resource gathering, and fight over said castles - sometimes defending your castle and sometimes sacking an enemy castle. Two big thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: "You want me to send this review Scripture to the King Sire? Very Well."Playing this game has been an absolute blast in its remastered glory. This game to me is just pure nostalgia from way back when I was still single digits. (Which is a huge chunk of time ago now let me tell you) The Music is iconic, building your Stronghold into a (almost) impenetrable fortress feels rewarding, the game play is great and the remastered visuals uplifts this 2D venture into the modern era to stand alongside other strategy remastered classics like Star craft and Command and Conquer. I think what makes Stronghold for me though are the cheesy panto-esk villains that you fight your way through one by one. I love those briefings. So if you like classic strategy titles, you love games based upon the medieval times, then catapult this game into your games list, you'll have a blast if you do. Tiberius.8/10my only suggestion for improvement is that the game is crying out for a fast forward button for the odd mission where you have no choice but to just wait for a objective to be met or maybe a gate / tower to be destroyed by a slow but methodical siege etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: if you're a fan of the original game as well as the HD versions this is worth the nostalgia and plays much better with quality of life and visual updates that make the game just as enjoyable now as it was when it first came out.  and if you're familiar with all the tricks to edit save games into map files, it just opens up sooo much map editing goodness that allows you to do your utmost best to make your favorite castles of real life or fantasy as close to the real thing as possibly can be done with this games engine. which was good in it's heyday which tells you how good of a map editor it has.  take your time, play around with it, heck even google things to see what you can do with the editor, there was once a community i'd found online back in the day called "stronghold heaven" which may still be up that had LOTS of user made maps and some of them so well and faithfully done to the source and reference that they had that it's beautiful to see the work that was put into the map they created.  there were several lord of the rings based maps that again were well made and crafted by the users that made them. if you have ANY of those old maps or ones you yourself have made you can use the "sav" to "map" trick just by editing the end of the file name and move it to the appropriate folder and enjoy. i just did that with a few myself as well as moved an old map i made into the DE map folder and i can once again enjoy a map that i spent hours making!!!

_childDocuments_.review: A great castle builder. You can marvel at how your castle functions as every part of it moves around like a cog in a machine. The food that you will mainly eat comes from the wheat that must be processed first into flour before being fully transformed into edible bread. The position of every building also matters, as the worker needs time to go to the stockpile to fetch materials and return to their workshop. This will make you min-max the placement of every building (except for houses). The unit control itself is very simple, with only 3 behaviors that you can set a unit into: standby, defensive, and aggressive. What it lacks in unit complexity, it makes up for in scale, as controlling hundreds of archers is a normal occurrence. They also have a lot of options for combat outside of unit type. Elevation is important because your ranged units have better accuracy when placed higher; moats are important because you can better defend against sieges; oil pits are important because they could allow you to defeat far superior units using a lowly archer firing a burning arrow. Some of the RNG could be annoying, though. If you want to use either a catapult or trebuchet, just pray to God that they can destroy the target before emptying their magazine.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I’d absolutely recommend Stronghold DE to returning Stronghold players and new players alike. But before I write anything I want to address the elephant in the room; skirmish. There is not skirmish mode in Stronghold DE. There wasn’t a skirmish mode in the original stronghold, because there was not a Skirmish AI. The developers have said that is was unfeasible to create a whole new AI, and would instead focus on remastering graphics, animations, music, voice acting, multiplayer functionality, and adding new content. I get that. I forgive the game for not having skirmish mode, although I am admittedly disappointed like the rest of us. Even without skirmish, Stronghold DE offers a great amount of content. I’d wager if this game is successful, they will remaster Crusader, which had a skirmish mode.The “remaster” aspect of this game is apparent. The animation and graphics quality has greatly improved. It offers a refreshing visual and audio experience for those coming back to the game, and realizing all the small details you may have missed due to the old graphics is a joy for those of us who grew up on Stronghold.  I’d recommend the game for this aspect alone, especially at the game’s low price point. It’s also worth mentioning the QOL improvements like barracks rally points and new hotkeys that modernize gameplay. There is ton of content. Not only do we have all the content of the original game, but we have a new military campaign and castle trail as well. Mission creation tools allow for community maps and missions to be shared, adding content. The road map promises two cheap DLC’s in the future, adding new campaigns for the cost of a cup of coffee. Stronghold DE offers the perfect opportunity to relive this classic game, and adds more than just a new coat of paint.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Will preface this by saying I've spent literally high hundreds to thousands of hours playing Stronghold and Stronghold Crusader.  Starting in my childhood, through teenage years, university and now still as an adult.  I have basically done all there is to do in these games.  For those of you who will be returning to this franchise, the redefined graphics, animations, framerate updates and overall re-make make this feel like a brand new game.  I found myself falling back in love with the micro-management of setting up a city, growing your resources and armies, and then just sitting back and watching the people of your castle work.  The reasons that I fell in love with these games in the first place decades ago.  There is so much familiarity with the setting, gameplay, soundtrack and animations that it feels right at home, but the upgrades make this feel new and exciting. If you are new to Stronghold this game will be an absolute treat, and I envy the feeling of experiencing this wonderful world for the first time.  It provides just enough to learn how to play the game, but requires the ability to micromanage economy, resources and military in order to really thrive.  In about 25 hours I managed to wrap up the new Economic and Battle campaigns at Very Hard difficulty, and I found a few of the missions quite challenging.  If you are new to the game, they will be difficult!  But the ability to scale the difficulty makes this game great for all ages and skill levels.  Just enough challenge with a massive sense of reward at the end of every mission.  I took my time and just enjoyed the environment, the hustle and bustle of your castle. The only complaint that I have is sometimes when commanding troops to move or attack, you loose your troop selection when telling them to move to a location and have to reselect them and try again.  I don't remember this happening in the older games.  A very minor detail that doesn't effect the gameplay overall.  I'll be able to spend another 20-30 hours on this game without feeling game fatigue or repetition setting in, meaning it is a 20-hr game for a seasoned vet looking to rip through just the new campaigns, or a 50+hr game for someone just looking to enjoy all of the options that are available: starting on the old campaign, continuing into the new campaigns, playing the Castle Trail, and enjoying the world builder and Castle Builder modes.  I hope this convinces you to buy this game, as it is 100% worth it!!!  PLEASE MAKE A STRONGHOLD CRUSADER DEFINITIVE EDITION!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The graphic improvements are noticeable, but not drastic or jarring, the original charm is retained.Original voices (50% of what made me love this game as a child) are still there.The controls feel good, but unit patching is a bit hit & miss, AI are even more hit & miss.The new content in the form of two short campaigns was... okay? Not terrible, just not very in depth.One mission requires hitting several objectives quickly as regular 'easy' attacks from various signposts will be followed by one that will be very difficult to survive - even on the lower difficulties, and impossible if you weren't prepared for it (I wasn't, and I'm not sure the game really warns you about this well enough)The two campaigns focus on the Rat & Snake's counties, but with much stronger unit comps than they seem to have in the original campaign. New intros & voice acting supports the new content.Multiplayer as a built-in is nice, can be iffy with connectivity (Still easier than the old way), but lots of player made maps and a couple of updates have improved it so far.If this is your first Stronghold game, this version is probably the best option as it's a little easier to play. Stronghold Crusader is often referenced as a better game - largely because the AI can build their own castles, which they CAN NOT in this game. The strength of Stronghold is the narrative campaign - which Crusader doesn't have.A series of well sculpted missions with excellent writing & voice acting in their intros. The military campaign starts of easy and learning, introducing new elements, weapons and units in line with the story progression. It hasn't aged perfectly as a game, but I feel the main campaign holds up very well, even after years of re-playing, I didn't skip the intros, and thoroughly enjoyed them. The economic campaign sucks, but individual 'Invasions' and Economic maps are pretty fun, the sieges are cool, especially if you're familiar with the castles.Many players of the original are disgruntled that this version hasn't imported features from Crusader, but that doesn't make sense to me personally, I got more or less what I expected, a polished, more playable (and OBS capture) version of the game from my childhood.I do love Crusader, the skirmish missions, mercenaries and variety of AI lords, but can only hope that the success of, and support for Stronghold DE will lead to Crusader DE in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Very good remaster.  Lots of functional improvements, such as better AI for your own troops, peoples paths don't go around for no reason. If you zoom in though, the details on the sprites are really detailed.  For example the tavern, you can make out each patron and the bartender in updated graphics.  Campaign has been good so far.  Levels work their way up to being difficult.  Makes you learn the mechanics until one level you need them all to survive.9/10, imo.  But I loved the original so I am biased.

_childDocuments_.review: - Compared to HD, the graphics don't look that much better. Moreover, after 15 minutes of gameplay, you completely forget which version you're playing. I deliberately opened both HD and the Definitive Edition for comparison. There's no noticeable difference, except HD costs 1 euro, and the Definitive Edition costs 15 euros.- Furthermore, HD feels even better because the animations in the game are quite clunky. It's understandable for that time and that image quality. In the Definitive Edition, they slightly improved the image quality, but the animations remained the same, now they look out of place.- The quality of the game environment is questionable. If before everything was clear - where the cobblestones are, where the trash is, and where the impassable cliffs are, now eyes hurt from mixed up picture. The environment now lacks consistency. It seems as if it's stitched together from assets of different games.- Gameplay-wise, it's the same game, with the same bugs and the same imperfect engine. The game has quite a few bugs, although they are not critical:-- Soldiers clip through the tower into the jagged wall and remain stuck there forever.-- The stone quarry storage sometimes spawns on an inaccessible cliff next to the quarry.-- Sometimes food producers don't see the granary and consider it inaccessible - you have to delete and rebuild it.-- Another bug - order archers to shoot an area. When they have their bows drawn, order them to shoot at single enemy. If before they couldn't reach him or shot at him in the general area, now all arrows fly precisely to the target. Cheese as it is.-- If you want to overcome a cliff and are allowed to build - construct a wall cell right on the edge - now you can build a staircase on both sides of the wall. And your farmers no longer need to make a detour through half the map to get to the warehouse.That is not all, just what I have quickly recalled.- The controls in the game are a kind of torture. You won't be able to select one unit from a crowd from a bird's-eye view - always 2-3 fighters will be highlighted. And selecting all units of the same type with a double click in this situation becomes impossible. If you're controlling a group of siege weapons - you'll often accidentally move engineers out of them because exiting the weapon and moving are done with the same right mouse button.- Another topic is the game engine and the way range is calculated. As a player, I NEVER understand where and from where my archers can shoot. Sometimes I calmly shoot beyond the towers, sometimes I don't reach the point where I should theoretically hit.Quality of the New Campaigns and Gameplay in General.- In short, the new campaigns are like a slap in the face. The missions feel as if they were made by a child. Some missions are simply long and disrespectful of the player's time, while others are absurdly simple and feel like a joke. Out of the two campaigns, there are 2-3 missions that genuinely spark interest. The rest are unclear fillers.- I'll note a positive point here - missions where you have to first capture a castle and then hold it are a good addition.- I want to address the developers - you should prohibit engineers from pouring pitch while standing on the ground. Because any mission where the player has access to pitch turns into a circus. Just place 3-4 engineers with pitch near the sighpost, and the entire enemy army will burn obediently while the AI is on timeout.- The AI in the game is generally weak. Stronghold is not a game about castle building. It's a game about building 3-4 large towers right next to the sighpost. While the AI is on timeout, archers destroy any army. The solution to this problem is simple - allow the construction of defensive structures only within a radius around the bastion.All the negativity outlined above is not really the fault of the developers but rather the legacy of the old game. We love Stronghold for some of its bugs and cheesy mechanics. However, in the updated version, I would expect more than just improved graphics.I'm glad I got to experience this iteration of the game, but I don't believe it's currently worth the money, especially considering you can buy HD for 1 euro. What would I expect from a refresh of such an old game?-Overhaul of the engine regarding range calculation.-Display of shooting range.-The ability to set formations for squads. Try stretching your archers into a line now - it's not an easy task.-Improve the AI; it's currently a sad sight.-In multiplayer matches, add the option to play against AI + the ability to complete multiplayer scenarios.However, I have a feeling that the developers simply wanted to quickly make some money, so we may never see these improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold was the first game I ever played on PC, and I am very passionate about it. Whenever I went back to it I was sad about the fact that the software is rapidly aging, and is technically no longer on par with other titles in the genre.You can imagine my pleasure when DE was released. It fixes this exact problem, keeps the game very close to the original, and adds a lot more content and quality of life improvements, all at a considerably very cheap price point.If you're a fan of the old Stronghold, you will enjoy this. If you're a fan of RTS games and are looking for something unique with the feel of a 90s indie game, this is for you. If you're a fan of medieval history, if you like economic simulations, or a great historical soundtrack, this game is also for you.However, if you expect AAA quality release or the revolution of RTS gameplay, this game won't satisfy you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty neat. There are a lot of good UI improvements (autotrade makes managing your economy slightly more streamlined without ruining the fun of build planning) and the new half-campaign is decently challenging. There's a lot less sitting around and waiting in the new missions, which will appeal to new RTS sensibilities.I do think the marketing campaign around the new missions has been a bit misleading. They've been advertising the new missions sets as being themed around our old favourite villains of the series, but they're not really. The villains were characterised by their difficulty, their VA's fantastic performances, and the units they threw at you during the campaign. None of these internal consistencies have carried over. Just a personal bone I'd like to pick, the missions are still good (the Peninsula castle build was a highlight).Have fun placing your castle.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the only real changes are graphics (which is rather irrelevant tbh, the old graphics were beautiful), built-in multiplayer lobby and autosell. Many crucial changes remain untouched:- still you can't personalize rules in multiplayer games. You can't choose banned units/buildings, you can't change cost of buildings, set limits for certain types of units etc. If they want multiplayer to thrive, they must provide such solutions- no balance changes - the game is as broken as it used to be, which, combined with the previous point, makes multiplayer unplayable mess of catapult armies- most of old bugs remain, opening the list with overcrowded walls and towersSolution to these problems is simply letting players balance the game by allowing a very in-depth personalization of rules in online matches. Let players set such rules, export them and share via lobbies, just like they share maps. Examplary rules to be set by the lobby host:- cost of units and buildings- stats of units: hp, attack, attack multiplier against other units, movement speed- what units/buildings/siege equipment are available- what are the limits for each building / unit (for example a player couldn't make more than 3 catapults)- what are specifically starting resources / units- what are the prices on the marketplace- strength multiplier for units of given player (to balance matches between players with different skill who still want to play together and have fun)I guarantee - this is what stands between the current state of the multiplaer (aka catapult hell) and real competetive multiplayer with respectable and enjoyable, evolving meta.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original way back when it released (and some of HD version since).The game always had great campaign and gameplay.The new campaign, more missions, steam multiplayer support, 4k support are all great things, and I think they warrant rebuying the game at current pricepoint.The only reason this review is negative is to the get devs attention - the pathfinding bugs are baffling and really irritate. Also the issue with ambiguity which fields are traversable leads to rage-inducing issues with imprecise walling - especially close to the map edge. The AI is also weirdly exploitable (it seems that once the AI orders units somewhere it will calculate path once, and won't recalculate it regardless of what happens in the meantime)There wasn't this much pathfinding issues in the original (I don't recall the state of AI, so no argument for comparison here). The readability always was an issue, but I feel it could've been solved (or improved) in the remaster.All in all if you like the fantasy of building and sieging medieval castles, it is an excellent game to pick up - but it does show it's age in the abovementioned ways so have that in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, so many years have passed, but to this day the Stronghold series of games is one of a kind, in no other game you can build your fortress from scratch, every square meter of the wall, carefully plan your defense, cleverly develop the economy, and then think up a plan for how to besiege your enemy (who, by the way, has also been busy with his fortress all this time!) and bring it to life.With a small number of tools available, the game offers a great variety of tactics and possibilities. There are only 7 basic units, but each of them occupies its own niche and plays a role, there are no useless ones (even the spearmen, whom everyone hates, can, for example, dig a ditch!). Every siege weapon is useful, of course, most players love catapults, but a siege tower is useful for quickly clearing a wall with archers, and a trebuchet will help destroy an enemy barn or armory that is well covered by walls to break their economy. In defense, you will also find variety and room for adaptation: if the enemy likes to use slow swordsmen or crossbowmen, the oil ditch is effective against them, catapults on the walls will protect you well from siege weapons, and mangonels will protect you from fast, but not well-protected groups of enemies (for example, from the macemen). Every time you play against different players, you have to think about what to do in this situation.As for this remaster, the game now has nice graphics and animations. You can now play multiplayer without using any programs like GameRanger. Modern controls have been added; the camera can be zoomed out using the mouse wheel, for example. This made the game much more convenient. Steam Workshop support allows you to easily and quickly view and download maps, without having to download them from any sites. And new campaigns are just nice.But there are also disadvantages:1) Unfortunately, the developers did not add a game mode with bots, although this is very necessary and I really don’t think it was difficult to do. I often play with a group of three friends, and we would like to arrange 3v3 or 2v2 battles, for this we could add a couple of bots, but unfortunately this is not available. There are four characters in the game (Rat, Snake, Pig and Wolf), they are just asking to become bots with their own difficulty levels, but no. It's a pity.2) Before starting a multiplayer battle, the game does not allow you to set starting positions for each player (like you can do in Crusader), which seems a little strange, I hope they just do this in some update.3) You still can’t play historical battles online :(4) There is no support for larger maps! I would like to have maps one size larger than they are now.Please note that the things I listed above are very easy to fix!

_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This was my First Strategy game. I found it in an old Office supply store and got hooked the moment I loaded it up. If you ever played Age of empires or a city building game you'll enjoy this game for its combination of battling, defending, siege and economic building.  Same as original, good way to get back into Stronghold to enjoy it and learn for the first time. AI is as devastating as before, I managed to beat every level EXCEPT one (The Pig Siege) on Normal. One of my favourite modes where you play levels created by the developers themed around either defending or attaching complex Kingdoms. With the addition of Workshop you'll pretty much never run out of these. Sim City Builder game mode, LOTS of fires, LOTS of Plague, LOTS of Rabbits. Fun, Casual fun whilst also difficult without a strategy at times. Laggy, Doesn't show servers after updates (last time I looked it was fixed though)Ignore and Pass. The Definitive Edition adds a number of new things that old players will enjoy and enjoy like coming back for another round such as new graphics which look AMAZING, Entirely New Campaigns and workshop capabilities for endless scenario's which I will outline separately below.Two small campaigns with around 7 missions each. These are Campaigns where you fight the Rat or the Snake and there are different themes to these levels such as Build and Defend, Siege or Survive, free captured troops and get to the objective. It's fun and new. This is a series of 10 Siege or Defend the Castle levels with no time limit like the campaign.It's effectively a playlist of the Siege/Invasion game mode levels with a text introduction of a real world event.

_childDocuments_.review: Good and bad at the same time.Graphics: When I first played the new version, I did not see that much difference to the older versions. But then I started the HD-version: Oh my, what a difference! Crystal clear graphics instead of blocky ones. It also workes on Ultra Wide displays without black borders!The gameplay is good and bad at the same time:  Building a castle is fun and the economy works as intended without much flaws. But the fighting system? If you select archers and an enemy just out of reach: They don't go to him, no, they just say "I cannot reach him". This is mediocre, but ok when defending a castle, but attacking one this behavior breacks your balls. As well as the spearmen etc. If set on aggressive, they attack walls first bevor attacking the enemy. So if you breached a castle, they will not go after the attacking foes on the towers, they will attack the next wall. If you manually select them to attack a foe, they might kill him and even then, they start hacking the walls. This is so frustrating!But year, if your focus is more on defending than on attacking, this game is still one of the best.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly faithful update to the original. It's maybe a little TOO faithful of an adaptation. Because they wanted things to be compatible with the old engine there's definitely a fair number of things missing you'd really expect in an RTS. There still are not unit formations, although control groups and rally points improve things a little bit in terms of giving you more control over your units. The addition of autosell/autobuy is enough to probably make this THE way to play Stronghold from now on, no more mashing to buy wood 5 at a time or having to check your stockpile every 30 seconds. My biggest complaint is the new campaign is full of the "siege an enemy with limited troops and/or time" type of mission, which is just the worst. I do not want more missions like end of the pig. The story of the new campaign is also very much in the tone of the original missions, which you may like but I'm not a fan of. Being the young captain just doesn't give you the same plain thrill when you aren't a single digit number of years old. There are also less callouts from the characters when you are under attack or you defeat an enemy wave, which is a shame because the ham and cheese voice lines of the rat is what I'm here for. The graphics are all faithful to the original spritework, but the update has left some units harder to read than before and there's a kind of... blur to the battlefield I can't really explain but that makes things look a little clunky. I have not tried the multiplayer and I don't intend to, this game isn't really balanced well for it and like the original it lacks skirmish mode against the AI. Apparently there are a lot of connection issues, but any game on launch is going to have those and they are patching it so your mileage may vary. All that said, it's an extremely faithful adaptation of Stronghold and hopefully Firefly recognizes that they should be putting more than one guy on this thing with how they're shattering their original expectations. Worth buying at launch, but if you're on the fence skirmish mode against the AI is not planned and the devs have been very transparent about that so wait for SHCDE if that's what you're into.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold came out at the tail end of the golden era of RTS, right before developers stopped caring about adding meaty well paced campaigns full of personality to their games and started just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ out games trying to be the new hot e-sport, until MOBAs took their lunch money, and the rest is history. So yes, Stronghold has a great campaign worth revisiting. As a game, it's more like a laser guided missile. Build. Demolish. Build in order to demolish. Plop down some farms. Man your walls. Man your siege engines. Go nuts. It is very focused. Its biggest success is that it has incredible depth, while simultaneously being super easy to control. Also, your units actually go where you order them to go, another craft that apparently got lost to time by RTS developers in the last 20 years. The remaster gives it a very welcome facelift, while adding a new campaign that's kicking my ass, so that's great. It doesn't add skirmish and co-op, but personally I don't mind. That's not what Stronghold is. It's you and your walls against carefully scripted and balanced challenges, at least for me. It's being offered at a reasonable price, and most importantly, it has aged well and is still worth playing today.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold Definitive Edition is a nostalgic trip back to the classic castle-building real-time strategy (RTS) game from 2001, and it's a delightful experience for both returning fans and newcomers. The game retains the essence of the original while offering significant improvements in graphics and controls.One of the standout features of Stronghold Definitive Edition is its attention to detail in recreating the medieval atmosphere. The improved graphics breathe new life into the game, with intricately designed buildings, lush landscapes, and charming character animations. The visual overhaul makes it clear that the developers put a lot of effort into modernizing this classic title.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The game now appears better than it ever has thanks to a minor visual overhaul. However, I don't believe it is the same, particularly with the current campaigns. It's feels just like playing Stronghold Crusader's map editor, placing tons of units on top of one other and seeing them fight to the death. I preferred the brief classic missions, but they didn't do much with the actual cut scenes with the remaster, resulting in monstrosities that don't match the frames for conversation. People are moaning about No Skirmishes, please shut the hell up. The original had none, and AI conflicts were conducted through particular mission campaigns and side scenarios this is how the original has always been, they made absolutely no mention of planning to release such a feature. I'd just play another game if I wanted AI skirmishes.These types of players are behaving like a friend of mine who wanted to play PvP with me but forgot that I was a major fan of the original and understood a number of methods that made it tough for him to achieve much. Rush with Crossbows made short work of him and he uninstalled and refunded the game and demanded there be skirmishes so that he could what I presume not get his ass kicked by someone who knows how to play against actual players? I understand. It sucks that some of us prefer to try hard, and that a single player mode vs AI is often the better option, but isn't that why you play Crusaders or anything that has that feature already put in? This is not a remake. It's a partial remaster to fix some issues and to also bring nostalgia. It's a pretty tall order to want developers to add in tons of content to a game that is many years old, when all they plan to do is add in a few new campaigns with... ehh... voice acting and ehh... game play you get what you paid for which is more than reasonable.  Good nostalgia, though I don't see myself playing it for a very long time because while it was fun to hear the voice actor from the original. It didn't sound the same with the new campaigns.It's reasonable as hell with the pricing, and the child inside of me had a blast listening to all of the catch phrases he grew up with and still remembering a lot of it.Aside from nostalgia, the game was still enjoyable to play if you enjoy the type of gameplay that consists of completing missions in the allocated timeframe or surviving attacks / defenses. However, if you're like half of these mindless sheep seeking for their next 4X or micro-management Age of Empires II sort of gameplay, you should go elsewhere.

It looks really good on a modern screen with the animations and static images looking both faithful to the original style but also very smooth for modern 2D look. _childDocuments_.review: Like most longtime players, I have a very love/hate relationship with Madden. I love it because it's football and a few months help me forget how grumpy I got at the previous iteration. I hate that it's a repackage of the previous year with a couple new features, a few missing features that should've been kept, and more bugs than the previous year. I had a pretty low threshold for EA's quality control when it came to Madden, especially for Connected Franchise but I'm impressed at how well they've outdone themselves this year. I'll forgive a lot for the sake of a fresh Madden skin but I can't forgive how abysmally poor the menu interaction is. They are slower than molasses and I ignore big chunks of the experience simply so I don't have to deal with the headache of waiting five minutes after every button press. This should be one of the simplest parts of the game and yet it still manages to be one of the worst experiences. How does a AAA game screw up menus?!And since I've gotten this far in my tirade, hire a UX designer, listen to them, and manage scouting better (among every other area but this one especially has bothered me lately). I have the memory of a goldfish and should be able to:- Sort & filter draft prospects. We all know Madden franchises are all about the spreadsheets. Let me have a spreadsheet view by golly. I want to be able to sort by age, speed, or strength without having to go three levels deep for each and every candidate. Especially when the menus are such trash. It takes 5 minutes to find a piece of information that could easily be bubbled up.- Hire and assign scouts on the map. I can't remember which zone had which positions which correlate to a specific scout when I have to go through three different clicks to assign a scout.

_childDocuments_.review: I am mainly an offline player so take this review with a grain of salt. So far Navigating the menus has been painfully slow. In superstar mode something as simple as hitting "advance week" takes 10-15 seconds to register, than it does the sim of the other teams games, than another 10-15 second wait while it appears to just lag, than the week will finally start. Every menu you try and open, ie. settings, roster, upgrades, also have a massive delay after trying to enter them. This doesn't seem like much when you are used to games that navigate quickly or just don't feel like letting time just sitting there looking at a frozen screen add up it can be quite aggravating, especially with the price tag this game came with. The gameplay is more of the same from madden. When you hold A to skip through scenes you also end up sitting there waiting at a minimum of 20 seconds, which is almost not even worth it to hold A at that point. The screen freezes so you're basically watching a still frame of something for almost 30 seconds. If they could find a way to fix this lag I would say this is a decent step up from previous years but right now it just seems like more of the same from the madden franchise. Another thing I would like to bring up / complain about is that when your team accepts a penalty, the announcers will say really weird stuff like "Why would they accept that and give the ball back to the offense", when the penalty was like a pass interference on the defense and the context of their sentence makes absolutely no sense. I also had the announcers tell me that "The Ravens are coming into this game after their loss to Baltimore last week" which... I don't even understand how that happens. I also heard that "The Cowboys defense did an excellent job against the run last week against Dallas". On another side note in superstar mode it says that all of my stats are 1st in the league on the stat hotbar, however they are definitely not first in the league. ie I have 32 catches at this point and both Travis Kelce and Cooper Kupp have more than 32 catches but it still says I'm first in the league in receptions. I'm sure if I wanted to author a book I could sit here and give more reasons why I am yet again disappointed with madden and its single player experience but this was enough of a rant.I will happily change my stance if some of these issues get addressed but I know madden has a history of not listening to the community or fixing problems that don't adhere to them making more money so not holding my breath.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve trialled this on EA Play and want to offer an objective, sensible view rather than the review bombers.I’ve used a 3080/i7 10700 system with 16Gb RAM and the game on a hard drive. Windows 10, 1080p monitor.- firstly, no problem with the EA anticheat and no need for the “BIOS edit” fix. Lucky me.  I’d probably refund if I’d bought it and got that, and not bought it again unless they fixed it properly. - I set all graphics to max and played some matches.- pregame load in was a bit sluggish - took about 20sec I think. This would be slashed if installed on my SSD.- The game looks fantastic and is fluid, save for the rare single stutter which only occurred pre-snap. Not ideal but completely tolerable.- gameplay is all there and in line with the PS5 version. So the gameplay things that p*** off the console players (like annoyances like the lack of EDGE terminology etc) are still there but crucially the PC hasn’t been hit by the lastgen console version. That’s important.- Franchise is the same new improved version that’s on the current gen consoles. Summary? It’s the current gen console version of the game on PC, ported to PC. I think it looks like that’s also the root of some of the issues - if you’ve an older machine that ran last years game easily, perhaps not the best optimised port means that it’s not as slick as it should be. The issue needing a bios tweak is bulls*** from EA - it’s unacceptable and they need to fix it. I would say it you have a machine that comfortably meets the min spec or exceeds it and you want to play the latest and best version of the game on PC - go get it. Maybe try the EA play trial first, will just cost $5 for US gamers.  Hopefully they will fix the issues and the game will be great.Good game, needs the anticheat fix sorted by EA and some optimisation tweaks.

Although it was a mix of just the game being poorly optimized it seemed because as soon as I broke into the game more and season two came out, I saw a boost in my FPS boost to upwards of 20 and 30, but an upgrade to my pc would probably be needed to make it overall better but that is besides the point.Some specs for people who careComputer is on Windows 10 ProAMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core ProcessorNVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 (4gb VRAM)64-bit operating system/x64-based processor16gb of RamFor Ultimate Team, I know EA is known for being cash hungry when it comes to the shop and I can obviously see that with the offers they have, enticing you to buy them. Does that mean you can't have a good team if you don't buy those packs? Absolutely not. I have been able to build a pretty good team without spending a dime on the special currency. Yes it requires you to grind out challenges and the pass but for me, that makes it fun to an extent. I will admit I am a noob and I don't really enjoy playing head 2 head as I am always outskilled and out framed but I find ways to enjoy ultimate team nevertheless. There are some things I wish the game taught me earlier but I have been able to work around it.Franchise is the mode I knew to an extent already and I got what I expected. It obviously takes time to get decent at but I have had a decent amount fun for the hours I have played on it,Do I recommend this for computers on the lower/older end? It would depend your specs and what not. I have old ass  and low vram on it so that contributes to the lag but as I mentioned earlier I have worked around it and it has been made better. I can not recommend waiting for a price dip and if it's worth changing from 23 to 24 because as I said, this is my first ever madden game. Although to end this off, I do overall enjoy the game contrary to some of the reviews. Is the game still buggy and needs fixes. _childDocuments_.review: Introduction:Madden 24, the latest installment of the renowned Madden NFL video game series, has left many fans feeling underwhelmed and dissatisfied. While the franchise has had a long-standing reputation for delivering innovative and immersive football gaming experiences, Madden 24 falls short in multiple aspects. This essay aims to explore the reasons why Madden 24 fails to meet the expectations of its ardent fanbase.Lack of Significant Improvements:One of the primary issues with Madden 24 is the lack of significant improvements compared to its predecessors. While fans eagerly anticipate each new installment, hoping for groundbreaking features that enhance their gaming experience, Madden 24 fails to deliver in this regard. The developers seem to have merely focused on superficial changes, such as updated player rosters and improved graphics, rather than addressing the core gameplay elements that need attention.Repetitive Gameplay Mechanics:Another notable drawback of Madden 24 is the repetitive nature of its gameplay mechanics. It appears that the developers either failed to introduce fresh ideas or were unable to successfully implement them. As a result, players are left with a sense of monotony as they find themselves performing the same plays, executing identical strategies, and encountering few challenges in their gameplay journey. This lack of variety and innovation ultimately fails to engage and captivate fans, leaving them feeling disinterested and frustrated.Artificial Intelligence (AI) Flaws:Furthermore, Madden 24 proves to be a disappointment due to significant flaws in its AI system. While realistic AI plays a crucial role in maintaining the immersive nature of sports video games, Madden 24 struggles to offer a competent and believable AI experience. Players frequently witness unrealistic behaviors from both their teammates and opponents, ranging from nonsensical decision-making to inconsistency in their performance. These AI flaws profoundly impact the overall authenticity and enjoyment of the game, leading to considerable disappointment among fans.Neglected User Feedback:A crucial aspect contributing to the dissatisfaction surrounding Madden 24 is the apparent negligence of user feedback. Developers typically rely on input from the community to identify areas of improvement and address glaring issues in subsequent releases. However, it appears that the developers of Madden 24 have overlooked or disregarded many valuable suggestions articulated by the players. This failure to actively listen and incorporate user feedback has resulted in a game that disregards the desires and needs of its dedicated fanbase, further cementing Madden 24 as a lackluster addition to the franchise.Conclusion:Madden 24, sadly, fails to live up to the standards set by its predecessors and ultimately disappoints fans. The lack of significant improvements, repetitive gameplay mechanics, flawed AI, and the overlooked user feedback collectively contribute to the overall poor reception of this game. As fans continue to seek authentic and innovative experiences in their football gaming endeavors, Madden 24's shortcomings highlight the need for the franchise to refocus its efforts on delivering engaging, immersive, and intelligently designed gaming experiences that satisfy the expectations of its loyal fanbase.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, overall a pretty good game if you’re into football and wanna experience it yourself. But if you start playing and go deeper into playing you’ll start to notice all the things that’ve gone wrong with the programming. When you play Superstar WR Mode (without Home Field Advantage) on Pro it’s way to easy, nearly every 2nd catch is a big one and you get TD after TD while winning every game 35:12 or something. But when you put it one Difficulty up to All-Pro it becomes hell, because then it gets unplayable. Not because the defense is better or is blocking you better, but because of so many unrealistic things that happen again and again that make you wanna quit the game. Your QB starts to throw an completely unrealistic amount of Interceptions (Mahomes threw 5 INTs in the first half to my other teammates, the other QB of course threw not even one). Your teammates seem to drop the ball every two seconds in the redzone too, if it isn’t an interception in the first place. And you lose the ball every two seconds because it’ll get knocked out of your hands or your QB underthrows the ball a couple of yards and just hammers it into the ground in a direction you weren’t even running, like he badly miscalculated the ball. So at the end of the game I had 350 passing yards and one TD because of 5 INTs in the redzone (and a missed field goal and extra point), the other team had 80 passing yards and won because of two TDs and a field goal. Also you miss like 50 or 60 Percent of your Field Goals and Extra Points, while the enemy team barely misses anything. So instead of making the defenders just do a better job they make your QB throw complete ♥♥♥♥ to stop you that way, like they want to mess with you and make you angry. And I didn’t even mention all the times your teammates just ran into you and were stuck with you for a couple of second, so you couldn’t catch your ball because of errors in the programming. I still recommend the game because it is a lot of fun playing, but only if you get the difficulties and settings right.

In previous Madden games, even on All-Madden, I was able to run up the score on the CPU, so I had to adjust the sliders to a ridiculous level. When I first launched this game and started a franchise, I set it to All-Madden, assuming I'd be fine. I lost 62-7, and it was my fault, not a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CPU picks. I feel like the game genuinely took a step forward. If you're not a chronic complainer and you just like Madden, at worst, this game will be fine for you. Even the FOTF replacement, Superstar Mode, is actually fun.Also, if you notice, the vast majority of negative reviews have less than 5 hours of gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Hmm where to start... Overall the game is more playable than recent years, there are still kinks that EA needs to address. Defensive coverage mechanics being the first that comes to mind. Receivers can often get bumped by covering defenders, which is fine, however the game does not have an animation for this sometimes. This leads to the ball being sent to where the receiver SHOULD be, based on their route, but does not account for the models colliding. This almost always leads to an interception, or just missed pass (labeled perfect accuracy). It is extremely frustrating in close games where every down counts, too many games have been lost due to this bug. Also, there are still plays and schemes that allow defenders to breach the line of scrimmage unimpeded by blockers. This obviously makes sense when the defense sends 5-7 on a blitz, but there is some scheme to have a free rusher when only sending 4... Breaks the game honestly, and it's usually brought out by cheesers at the end of a close game because it's a wincon.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not write a lot of steam reviews, in fact this may be my first one. The reason I feel a need to write one for Madden 24 is I have never felt more conflicted about a game. I currently have 404 hours this Madden, it being my second one. I would like to tell anyone looking to buy this game why I would not recommend it even after a large sum of hours.To start, I do not play online. My review has nothing to do with multiplayer metas, pricing or player toxicity. Most of my time is spent in franchise mode because I find it the only viable way to play the game solo. Which leads me to my first topic, super star mode. OH BOY HOWDIE is it bad. I've played a lot of games that very little depth to them but super star mode is a new low. Basically there is a fundamental issue where all the fun was front loaded into the first few hours of playing this mode BUT one would think the idea is to raise a stud into the second coming of Mahomes, Derick Henry or something. After you are drafted you will receive two or three major events and then its just you and a hand full of instance events ever so often. There is no drama like beef with teammates or competition for the starting roll. You can get traded to another team but this seems to happen at random times as I hard carried my team to the playoffs, lost the super bowl and then was traded right after a record setting season. FFS it was like score 40 points a game or loose and I made it to the super bowl. Anyways, Madden's leveling system and game play mechanics really are not deep enough to keep me playing for hours on end and that kitty pool depth only gets shallower the further one strays from the quarterback position. There are no user player traits, level caps in alternate stat categories, and height and weight really only matter when it comes to speed. All of this culminates into a mode that is supposed to follow a self insert football player's career, but sadly is only tolerable for 3 seasons and that is if you are playing quarterback. It would be very easy to improve and add mechanics that would make this a viable way to have fun but a pure lack of effort and creativity is present, spoiler alert this is a running theme with every EA product. Franchise mode is better but feels rushed at best. My main issue with this mode has to do with the best thing about franchise mode funny enough, the drafted rookies. While the simulated draft is my personal favorite part of Madden as a whole I can not help see the infinite ways it could be improved. To start player personality is not in the game. You know the most important thing about sports besides the sport itself. Like would it kill someone at EA to make some traits that make all players divas, team players, saints, or anything other than models. For anyone who has played this mode imagine if a player had a tag that allowed him to never be affected by negative moral even after a huge loss streak. The inverse could also be a fun example, where the player is super good but he constantly drags down moral. This lack of personality extends to the draft itself. In real life people have fun watching chaotic pick swaps and crazy out of pocket picks in the draft. Maddens draft only allows your team to wheel and deal in the draft. Which is so boring. The only spicy thing that can happen is a team randomly taking the WR you wanted when they have 2 super star WRs already. And that is more rage inducing than fun due to lack of realism. I could spit ball ways to make Franchise mode amazing but I would be here all day if I did. Some minor issues are: Players signing long term low paying deals, Draft pick cheesing, teams making illogical roster decisions, free agency either being super exciting or a snooze, drafted players being way to easy to evaluate, no stopping mechanic for stacking draft picks to the moon, ass instance events, boring stadiums. But hey at least there is more to this mode so I can actually play it for more than a day.Lastly gameplay and glitches.... Yeah no I would be here for a year but I will list a few of my least favorite: The O line, defenders have instant acceleration, can jump like Jordan and can turn on a dime even if they are a 70 overall, the new aiming system while cool leads to jank moments all the time, WRs not climbing the ladder ever( no joke after 400 hours ive seen it happen a hand full of times), MY PLAYERS TAKING BRAIN DEAD ANGLES TO TACKLE ALL THE TIME.I sorta ran out of time to give my full thoughts but i hope this enlightens someone to not buy this game and instead give that money to a company that actually wants to make a great product. With how much money EA makes this game should be the elden ring of sports games but it is a giant disappointment start to finish.Edit: So i wasn't going to return to this but it seems to have gotten more than a few likes. Thanks to all of you! In this edit I would like to cover some of the issues with the core game play, Who knows maybe it will inspire some modder or ea dev to actually tackle the issues. Or i'm huffing copium lmao. So when talking football the game is built in the trenches and defense. Fundamentally madden struggles with this. O-line men are drafted high in real life due to the position being vital to the offense, everything runs through them and the qb. The O-line really needs a revamp because blockers get lost all of the time. Most of the time they either line up not blocking an edge rusher or glitch out and do not engage the blocker as he runs by to gift your qb an er visit. They also have real trouble blocking runs on the move because running backs seem to go a little to fast for the designed play to work correctly. When it comes to defense everything besides D-line is a little messed up. In real life offensive plays are designed to trick defenses into opening holes in the field and defenders are supposed to make the right decision. In madden this happens some of the time but most of the time it is literally coincidence. Dbs really need a coverage rework and mlbs need to be more aggressive when zone covering a shallow crossing route or something. Shallow crossing routes are just too free without audible calls. I would rather my defenders make mistakes as opposed to afking and making a tackle/breakup after catch 9 out of 10 timesNext I want to talk about something weird but I think its important, Playbooks. I just feel like they do not reflect team identity enough. Like whats the point of lamar existing if the ai runs like two read options a game. Just make the play books more unique or up the frequency of some types of plays FFS because making a mesh with more squiggly lines aint it. Like a red zone play called the philly special would be so sick, I haven't played as the eagles but I will eat my words if it is already in the game but I would bet 1000 dollars it isn't.That concludes edit 1, Ill rant more later as it is 4 am and i'm a deranged human for writing this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unplayable. An embarrassment for EA, making a game 70 dollars just to make it worse than every madden to ever be made.      The actual gameplay is terrible. Passing is terrible, and throws are about 20 less mph than real life. If you bullet pass it into an area withing 10 feet of a defender it will get intercepted. Blocking is worse than its ever been. Blockers will miss assignments right in front of them simply because the animation doesnt happen. Speaking of animations, nothing will go right with a 100% animation based game. Countless in game bugs, like players kicking the football 50 yards, or failing to pick up a ball on the ground 10 times. Dbs in this game are also worse than ever before. In the NFL, the best of the best completion percentages are just under 80 percent, which is incredible. Quarterbacks will average 80 percent against you in this. Drag routes are uncoverable in man, along with slants zigs C routes, which are all extremely basic routes even college Dbs can cover. Jump balls always seem to go to the defender unless its you defending. Tackling is impossible, when playing on all madden you have about a 15 percent chance of an open field tackle, no matter who the players, even when secure tackling. Movement behind the line of scrimmage is terrible, you cant do anything but run, despite numerous qbs being known for maneuvering around the pocket with ease. If a defender is coming to sack you the only thing you can do is run away or throw it. Throwing the ball away is stupid, the qb usually has about 10 brain cells when trying to do it. fumbling is terrible, despite it happening almost every game, regular tackles never seem to force fumbles ever. throwing is stupid, and overly complex. players look like woody  when they are running, and speed is nothing like the real nfl.    Now, outside of the actual gameplay, there is unsuprisingly numerous issues. First, overalls are always stupid, but thats just a madden norm now. Keeping old players like Chandler Jones and Eric Kendricks high overalls with abilities despite underperformance. The servers are down just about once a day it seems. But my main issue that i am extremley upset about is superstar mode. First of all, it took me about 20 hours to actually get into the mode, because when I click start career it sticks me into a blue loading screen, continues to play music, but never loads despite how long you wait. This happens about 90-100% of the time. Then, sometimes when you are trying to reenter your current career, it just keeps bringing  you out of it. This alone makes superstar career basically unplayable. But I am not finished. I made a running back career and got put on the Bengals. The Bengals have an excellent qb incase you dont know. Well I got through about 4 games and Joe Burrow already threw 16 interceptions. I dont know why the AI does this, but it makes the actual gameplay  extremely frustrating. I also made a qb career, and for some reason it is extremely laggy when i actually play the qb games, and i basically never lag outside of that mode. Another slightly but less important thing is that there is no setting to turn off manual play calling in career mode. I feel it would make the whole you are a player not the whole team thing more real, but that isnt that important. Another issue is just the bugs in general. I wont dive deep into this but there are numerous, numerous bugs.    In conclusion, for a 70 dollar game, the most expensive its ever been, to make an unplayable game is inexcusable, and Madden needs to be boycotted. DO  NOT BUY THIS GAME DO NOT BUY IT UNTIL THAT MAKE IT PLAYABLE( NEW ENGINE, NO ANIMATIONS, NO BUGS, NOT PAY TO WIN, ACTUAL FUN MECHANICS, REALISTIC). this game gives me low expectations for the new college football game they are making on the same engine.

_childDocuments_.review: A step in the right direction from previous seasons but still massively lacking in comparison to the "golden age" of American Football games. Just because it is a 4/10 compared to a 2/10 does not mean it is a good game. I still cannot recommend unless you really need a football fix. Madden neither does well as an arcade or simulation type football game. It exists in a weird middle ground between the two worlds. It is not Blitz nor NFL 2K5. Pros:- They finally upgraded the Madden engine for PC. Sports series are notorious for prioritizing console users over PC users in terms of updates, engine upgrades, etc. I imagine Madden on PC is still behind console but the gameplay is truly a little better.- Superstar mode has potential. It has taken years to even get to a skeletal point but there is a somewhat enjoyable Superstar mode at hand. It is still nowhere near NBA 2k's myplayer (which is its own nightmare) but it is an improvement over year's past. - They finally updated the playbook menus.Cons:- Superstar mode is missing essential features such as a real practice mode, depth chart/substitutions, yearly stats for players, role playing aspects (choice based narrative, relationships/rivalries, history of draft picks by team), and more. For example, there are a few minor video clips of the Pivot podcast crew discussing your Myplayer's performance over the season. It is so lackluster compared to earlier football games. Madden 05 used to have an entire in game radio broadcast with fake headlines based on the season. NFL 2k5 would have a Chris Berman-led ESPN broadcast which even showed highlights from other matchups that were not yours. It is a long rant but what I am getting at is presentation in contemporary football games is completely lackluster.- The soundtrack is one of the worst licensed soundtracks out there. Madden soundtracks were never my favorite thing but it should be a simple formula of Sam Spence music, arena rock/metal/pop, hard rap, and then throw some random genres/whatever you want. Instead they find the most cursed rap music. The music is so bad it makes Lil Uzi Vert seem like a modern genius.- Physics/flow of game are absolutely off. Plays like the Marshawn Lynch run against the Saints, Josh Allen throwing Kyle Van Noy into the ground, Derrick Henry stiff arming Josh Norman, rugby scrums, and other physically dominant plays are not possible in Madden due to its animation based gameplay rather than physics based. What I mean is that it doesn't really feel like you are throwing your weight around. A player with an X under them will just win every matchup because their numbers are higher. Your X (superstar) players will dominate the game but it feels more bouncy than punching if that makes sense?- Simulation stats have always been awful for Madden. Their stats are stuck in 1996 where every team gave an RB 300 plus carries. QB rushing yards and receiving yards in general are lacking in year end stats compared to real life comparisons.This game is slightly better due to minor upgrades in gameplay and superstar mode but it is not nearly enough for what a 2023/2024 American Football game should be.

_childDocuments_.review: Observations after most of an exhibition game:Good:Graphics have improved - ultra settings look better than ever IMO.Playcalling - Texans vs Chiefs - believable play calling.Animations / Tackling - ImprovedReplays - There are less and they didn't show a replay of a kick going out of bounds inside the 20.Bad:When a team scores, before kicking off to the opposing team - WHY is their offense and opposing teams defense shown huddling on the field? Why does it last for 30 seconds or so? If KC scores - their offense should be on the sidelines - but nope, they're out on the field yakking for 30 seconds. Immersion breaking. Plus, regardless of who is on the field - seriously, 30 seconds or so - let's get on with it!  Scoreboard celebrating 1st down - on 2nd down.After a play, the ball is observed with the player's hand stuck through the middle of the ball.Music - turned off immediately. Rap / hip-hop is as divisive as you can get. The little that I heard was "better" than previous Maddens, but so is sticking pencils in my ears.Graphics - Yes, they look nice - but there is pretty significant stutter when camera is switched from time to time - my hardware isn't quite top of the line - but it should never stutter like this.Commentary - Does EA pay again for reused voice lines? Also, not every play needs color commentary - it's just too much IMO. Maybe watch a few games with Madden / Summerall to see how it's done properly. Also, quite often the commentary doesn't match the play - commentary talking about how Kelce was wide open / green grass during a 75 yard play when, in fact, he broke 2 tackles almost immediately after catching the ball.Replays - Nice that there are less - too bad that it doesn't replay the big plays (interceptions for example) but will replay a 6 yard run.Heavy Rain Game - Bright and sunny. Holdover from Madden 23 - you couldn't even fix this EA?Starting the game - WAY too many "Ultimate Team" and whatever ads - just take me to the damn menu, thanks.Controls - Same as last few years - controls are entirely favored for controllers, not mouse / keyboard. Had to close the game from desktop as no matter what keys I tried on the keyboard the game wouldn't stop (and I tried everything that made any sense at all).Understand - I rarely "play" Madden - I tend to WATCH Madden. For me, it's about immersion - does it feel like I'm watching an NFL game. Replays should be shown when it's appropriate, commentary should be limited to where it is interesting and adds to the experience, teams don't have their offense on the field after scoring, etc. Oh, and have to have a commercial break every 3 minutes (okay, thankfully that isn't part of the game). I'm sure I'll come up with more. I don't think it's as bad as some of the reviews would have a person believe, and I see potential once the game is patched (assuming it actually addresses the issues). It needs "polish" - it really gives me the feeling that it was rushed for the PC version - as in the PC version is an afterthought (not comforting as I'll never have a game console). I'll say that it's recommended but I would completely understand if folks wait until some patches come out as the game could use some serious polish.Edit: After further review, cannot recommend this in its current state of "optimization". Madden 23 ran on ultra settings on my laptop, peaked CPU temps at about 72 degrees. Madden 24, running on medium settings, CPU temps hitting 89 - it's not using the GPU as it should. This game is currently not optimized for PC and seriously needs a patch ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: Madden NFL 24: A Football Fix, But Not Much More (6/10)As a football fan, Madden NFL 24 scratches that familiar itch. Madden NFL 24 is a solid fun experience but I wouldn't purchase it every year. Those who are expecting a revolutionary leap forward, you will be disappointed. The core gameplay remains similar, and some lingering bugs and design quirks hold it back. If you're a Madden veteran, consider waiting a few years before upgrading. But if you need your annual football fix, Madden NFL 24 will get the job done, even with its issues.Here's the breakdown:The Good (+):+ Visually Pleasing: Player movement and animations are solid/good, making the game more immersive.+ Playbook Paradise: Playbook variety offers more strategic options and keeps the gameplay fresh.+ Franchise Mode: Has it's issues but I've pumped hours and hours into this mode and i'll likely come back for moreThe Not-So-Good (-):- Franchise Fatigue: While I appreciate the stamina feature in Franchise mode, the illogical AI decisions regarding player rest during the regular season and playoffs are frustrating. It feels like a bug rather than a strategic element.- Face of the Franchise Fumbles: The revamped Face of the Franchise mode (replacing the story-driven Superstar mode) has potential, but it lacks depth and story variety. It feels like a missed opportunity.- Technical Hiccups: A few glitches and odd-looking player models can take you out of the experience.- Menu Maze: The clunky menus require too many clicks to navigate. A more streamlined interface would be much appreciated.The Neutral (+/-)+/- Can't comment on the online playability since I don't do these games online for the most part

_childDocuments_.review: It's Madden. Not much else I can say. We are essentially paying for a roster update, as we have been for years at this point. Though I will point out that with next gen finally on PC, we are heading in the right direction.     I'm really only interested in franchise, so I can't comment on any other game modes as of this writing. I do appreciate that they seem to be TRYING to improve, with certain aspects of franchise mode upgraded. As far as a franchise/sim experience goes, I would say this is the best in many years.    As for the gameplay- meh. It's vastly improved from 22/23, thanks in large part to the next gen features. However, it still leaves much to be desired. The sliders take some SERIOUS tweaking to even make playing the game enjoyable. Running the ball is fine- passing, however, is virtually IMPOSSIBLE. If you like throwing 40 interceptions in a season, this is for you.     The new passing mechanics, while I appreciate what they're trying to accomplish- are just bad. One of the reasons I feel Madden has been in decline the past decade or so is because they always seem to be "fixing" things that aren't broken. Give me classic, simplistic gameplay controls, and put work into features that matter to make the game more engaging. Just my opinion.    Overall, if you're a longtime fan of the series as I am, and particularly just enjoy burning time managing a franchise, it's worth the money if you can get it on sale. Here's hoping it's a step in the right direction and they continue to improve.

_childDocuments_.review: A couple things right off the bat:I had Madden 19.  Just got Madden 24.  Madden 24 has better player control.  I like the slowdown mode when QB passing.  Graphics and overall play (tackles, blocking, hits, catching, interceptions, etc.) are way more realistic.  I am convinced these are the reasons for the bad reviews:1.)  The game requires 20GB RAM for ultimate performance.  I have 16GB, gameplay is fine.2.)  I have a 2.5GHz machine.  Forget what the minimum is.3.)  My hunch is the negative reviewers for this game don't have a machine capable of running this game.4.)  Secure boot - if you're getting the "secure boot is not enabled for this machine" error, your motherboard and/or CPU BIOS aren't up to date.  First, check if "secure boot" is "off":4a.)  Type "msinfo32" in the search bar.4b.)  Under "system summary" on left pane, look for "secure boot state" on right pane.  It's about halfway down.  It probably says "off".  To fix, try the below (Win 11 in this example):4c.)  Type "settings" in search bar4d.)  Under "system" on left, click on "recovery", then click on "restart now".  4e.)  Machine reboots.  On restart, click "troubleshoot", click "advanced options", click "uefi firmware settings".  Click "restart".  Machine reboots again.  Your system should now read "secure boot = on" (see 4a., above).  Hopefully this saves people time, and from going down the rabbit hole of trying to find BIOS update files that need to be booted from a floppy disk (A: drive).  For those of you who may not know, floppy disks were invented by dinosaurs.UEFI is Windows firmware updating utility, Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI).  It's baked into Windows and saves us from the dinosaurs.  That's the 2 sentence explanation (for you purists out there), but one thing's for sure, if you don't have UEFI, get a new machine, it will save you the frustration in the long run.
