_childDocuments_.review: Having played Madden since the Super Nintendo days, I get the hate. I've been there too. This one isn't bad. There are some ridiculous moments...The kickoff hits the crossbar on the goalpost and hits the returner in the head. The game treats it as a touchback but the announcer is yelling about how the returner's muffed the kick. Meanwhile, his two closest blockers run into each other, one gets knocked to the ground, and the other raises his hand like, "Sorry, man! Didn't see you there."But there is a very playable game here. I'm not multiplayer or MUT or any of that. I'm a franchise player through and through. And it's... not bad. The AI isn't brilliant and it's impossible to set the gameplay sliders to simulate an NFL experience. Essentially every game I find myself thinking, "This is the one I lose," as the AI keeps it close, competitive, and exploits my team's weaknesses out of the gate. The first quarter ends (I play 60 minute games) with my opponent up by 3. But then it falls apart and I win by 50+. But that winning by 50+? It's actually fun. Each play is contested, at least a little. If you try the same play over and over - offense or defense - the AI will adjust. Are there problems? Heck yeah! You have to adjust the gameplay sliders to compensate for an AI that will basically teleport defenders into pass coverage, spin and juke through a wall of defenders, and complete passes that defy the laws of physics. (Running hard one way, throwing the ball 50 yards the opposite direction without turning, stuff like that). The AI has no idea what Intentional Grounding is. There's a long list detailed by other reviewers.But if you aren't trying to recreate the Sunday NFL experience, if you treat it like a video game, it can be fun. I have 137 hours in at this writing and I'll probably add 137 more. Should my experience suddenly tank or I end up deciding I hate it instead, I'll change my review. But for now, should the hours played never change, it just means I found a game I enjoy more and moved on...

_childDocuments_.review: Madden 24 had me hyped up, ready to hit the virtual gridiron and dominate. But let me tell you, folks, this game is an absolute disaster. It's like they took everything that worked in the previous titles, chucked it out the window, and said, "Let's see how badly we can mess this up!" Where do I even start? The gameplay feels like I'm trying to control a herd of turtles stuck in molasses. Every move, every pass, every tackle—it's all so slow and unresponsive. And don't even get me started on the AI. Half the time, my own teammates seem like they're actively working against me, running in circles or just standing there like statues. And the glitches? Oh, the glitches. It's like playing Russian roulette every time you fire up the game. Will the ball suddenly disappear mid-air? Will my player decide to moonwalk through the field goal post? Or maybe the game will just give up entirely and crash to the desktop. It's a surprise every time!But what really grinds my gears is the lack of innovation. I mean, come on! We're in 2024, people! You'd think by now we'd have flying cars and football games that actually work. Instead, Madden 24 feels like a lazy cash grab, with developers more interested in slapping a new coat of paint on an old jalopy than actually fixing what's broken.Sure, the graphics are decent, and yeah, it's got all the official NFL licenses. But what good is all that when the core gameplay is about as enjoyable as a root canal? Save yourself the headache, folks. Unless you enjoy screaming at your TV in frustration, give Madden 24 a hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Take all the negative reviews with a grain of salt. They make decent points, but today there is a culture around bashing developers because a game isn't perfect. EA is EA and we know where their priorities in developing games. Unfortunately, nothing will change unless they lose the NFL license and get some competition. I'm a firm believer that the blame should not be placed on the developers, as most of them simply want to make a good game. This is undermined by a lack of consistency in the dev team, money-first decisions from higher-ups, and EA's complacency knowing NFL fans will buy it simply because there are no other licensed options. Welcome to 21st century capitalism.Is the game buggy? Yes. Is there still missing features that were included in Madden games 10+ years ago? Also, yes. Its not ground-breaking by any means, nor will it be remembered as a good year for Madden, but if you enjoyed played any of the recent Maddens and are excited about finally getting current gen features and graphics on PC, it is still fun.

name: Mercenaries Wings: The False Phoenix
detailed_description: “Mercenaries Wings” is a tactical simulation RPG where you level up, equip and command a group of mercenaries to fight through the stages. Character design is by the illustrator Raita Kazama, who has spared no effort in detail to make each character expressive and alive. 【About the Game】 ・Command your units on a quarter-view battle map and bring them to victory! ・Unit positions will affect Action results in battle. Whether your units are positioned in the, front, back, or side of the enemy, and whether they are on higher ground compared to the target are all taken into factor how effective their actions will be. ・Spend Skill Points (SP) to change character classes! By leveling up your character, they will be able to unlock Intermediate and Advanced job classes. Each class has its own set of skills you can learn. Special classes can only be unlocked by using certain items. Build your own balanced team! ・Spend SP to learn new skills! Depending on the class you choose, your characters will be able to learn skills that can heal or buff allies, and debuff or inflict status abnormalities to your enemies. ・A new “Leader Skill” function has been added. Depending on the leader you choose for each battle, you will be able to gain special effects unique to the character to help your team. For example, you could choose a leader that increases movement range for wide maps, or a leader that increases the HP of ally units for melee intensive fights. Choosing the appropriate leader for each fight could make or break the battle. ・The story has a multi-ending. Your choices directly impact the fate of your team. ・The extra difficult “EX stages”are sure to satisfy even the most skilled strategy experts. 【The Story】 Situated on the northern continent lies the Kingdom of Dryden, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign nation. It is said that a hero, blessed by the Phoenix, cut through over 1000 foes to establish the kingdom. As if personifying that violent legend, the current king, Harold, has been warring with neighboring countries ever since he ascended to the throne ten years prior. The desolation caused by continuous conflict has caused dissatisfaction to peak among the populace. They now rise up, led by one Earl Iscariot. One day, when the Royal Army was invading another state, his Rebel Army attacked the under-manned Royal Castle and captured it. And so the Kingdom of Dryden now finds itself caught between a civil war from within, and war with the neighboring Collingwood. King Harold, unable to move his army away from the Collingwood frontlines, decided to hire mercenaries to be his army in fighting against the rebels. One of the first mercenary bands to respond to the call was the Crimson Birds. This up-and-coming band is led by their commander, Kane the Crimson Flash, and vice-commander, Jeremy the Phoenix.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, it's not a great game.  It's a bit generic, but I would recommend it to people who really miss Final Fantasy Tactics if you are willing to play a 6/10 version.  The translation is rough,  the combat is exactly the same as the previous entries.  Probably a literal copy and paste from them.  All this being said, I enjoy it as a simple FFT-like.  It has a decent job system.  The game is as if AI made FFT and I'm OK with that.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the first two in this series to basically ng+ and the previous iteration being almost exactly the same as the first. I am failing to see any difference between this one and the other two. I searched on google for an answer and all I can find is this one adds a leader function to the game. Thats it. Aside from that its the same leveling system, same classes, same skills, same items, slightly different maps and story. Talk about milking it. I dont get why they havent added anything in two gamesUpon further digging, this isnt even the more recent version. They gave it a random name so you cant tell this game was released two games ago.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the other titles, you will likely enjoy  as well. It changed little in terms of mechanics, but it does have major changes in its presentation, some of that is better and other things are worse, which is fitting since the same can be said for the quality of the game. My actual issues with the game are unrelated to the gameplay, so if you only care about that then I guess this would be a recommendation.  keyboard only The kingdom is in yet another war, and now it is swarming with rebels. The Crimson Birds are one of many companies hired to assist the monarchy, but King Harold might not be as noble as they thought, not only are their pays delayed but when they get them, they are less than what they would like. As if that was not bad enough, the King decides to give mercenaries the right to plunder liberated towns something that goes against the morals of a mercenary, apparently. Does he really deserve your loyalty? The premise is about as interesting as previous titles, a few hooks and some engaging ideas but not executed as well as I had hoped. They are definitely more ambitious with , trying to develop more natural characters and relationships, I would say these characters are better if only because of the effort to make them seem more human but some of them are very suspect which was never the case in the  games. Take Cecil, the main character, she is in love with Jeremy, who is her dead sister’s boyfriend, her boss, and her foster brother who raised her. Does he reciprocate? Take a guess. There is also Anemone, she should probably be in jail. On a positive note, I am very pleased to announce that you do not have to serve a tyrant, in fact you are given a choice a third in which sets you in your route, I like that. Yet there are also moments that feel far more contrived than in earlier titles, especially in the “Breakaway” route, and that is disappointing because it is the route I recommend. If you do not pick that route you enter the darker timeline where you find out whether or not Jeremy reciprocates Cecil’s feelings. Maybe just skip that.Most of the changes introduced by  are related to its visuals or its audio. All environments have received a face lift looking more detailed and clearer; however, the character sprites remain in the old, pixelated style which creates an odd disconnect. At least it is very easy to see your enemies, I guess. There are also the portraits, these are a lot more detailed, which is good, and they lean more into an anime style, which I am neutral on. I do think it is nice that we get some expressions that can be used during dialogue to give us some sense of mood and emotion, but um character design? What even is this? The men typically look alright, maybe a bit overdesigned for mercenaries, but then you have the women. Dear lord. Take Anemone as an example, you can see a screenshot of her on the store page, does not seem very practical if you ask me. And pretty much every other woman has the same sort of fanservicy design. If my choices are this, and what we had in the  games then I pick the latter.  Every  game I have played has the same issue. They blind the player with a white flash each and every time anyone gets a critical hit, as well as when other specific things happen. Glad to see that  keeps the tradition alive.So the soundtrack is a more engaging than it has ever been, but I am not sure if it is actually good. I do think that I like the majority of the track, and I like them a lot, they fit the mood of the Chapter or are otherwise nice rhythmic songs that goes well for the combat, but then there are other songs that I just do not understand what they were thinking. I asked myself "what is this? Why is this here?" which is not something I should be doing. It is certainly a memorable soundtrack, but probably not for a good reason. All sound effects have been redone, as far as I can tell, and some of these are better but the level-up is a noticeable downgrade. There is this very clear windup to it and (others) that sort of ruins the mood and turns something that should have a bit of pomp into something anticlimactic and disappointing.  Combat has received one new mechanic, some balance changes, but is otherwise identical. You kill your enemies before they kill you, you use positioning to your advantage, and you check the store between every battle just in case it has a good item.The new addition is the leadership mechanic, one party-member is designated as a leader, and you get a buff depending on their class. Some have per-turn healing, others simply boost your health or your stats, and some are more interesting. One of Cecil’s skills lets you move even after taking an action which can be really useful to take advantages positions or to quickly move to the next target.  features several combat encounters that are interesting, sometimes your enemies will come at you in waves, spawn all around you, and at a few times you will need to guard someone lest you lose the mission. You also get to use your entire party, that can be a good thing because you can try them all out and you have more options in every fight, but it can also be a bad thing, because it means you will have the same party every playthrough.There are also a number of encounters that are  interesting, especially the first few fights. They seemed uninspired, did not try anything worthwhile, nor did it try and push me with any sort of specific challenge. It mostly felt like filler that was necessary to keep the story at an okay pace, which is not exactly an excuse, because previous titles did try harder for their filler. I think the combat is enjoyable enough, so it is not like I hate these encounters, they are just very very bland and forgettable.   While not as grind heavy as , it is likely that you will need to play scenarios to increase your level and unlock new skills, otherwise  can turn into swamp. These missions are repurposed from the campaign; however, they pull from Chapters of each route meaning you will be able to play maps that would otherwise be inaccessible to you. Yet it is possible to completely skip the free-battles, since the campaign gives you a number of Puzzle-Pieces to unlock new classes or rare items and since the secret items are no longer hidden, you can always see them so there is little excuse to miss most of the good equipment.

_childDocuments_.review:
Mercenaries Wings: The False Phoenix, blends turn-based strategy, old-school aesthetics and a tale of war, betrayal and magical forces!

Mercenaries Wings: The False Phoenix challenges your tactical nous across a lengthy and challenging campaign. The Kingdom of Dryden has an incredible history thanks to the story of a Phoenix facing down enemies generations ago; now, buoyed by that legacy, King Harold continually seeks conflict.

Follow the tale of a band of mercenaries, working for coin but then challenged to consider whether their actions, and those of King Harold, are what is best for the land. What follows is a story of war, betrayal, magical lore and redemption for a nation!

A tactical RPG in the finest traditions of the genre, Mercenaries Wings: The False Phoenix requires you to carefully utilise varied units and their abilities. Set Leaders to change the flow of battle, level up your units, change classes, manage equipment and make the key choices that will be the difference between victory and defeat!

An adventure that will take many hours to complete, Mercenaries Wings: The False Phoenix will challenge even the most careful strategists.

Features:

* An all-new standalone story in the Mercenaries series, this adventure offers many hours of entertainment.

* Carefully crafted tactical RPG action.

* Choose a Leader for each battle, level up units, change class types and pick the right equipment.

* Follow the twists and turns of the tale that includes war, magical beasts and leadership challenges!

* Featuring character illustrations by Kazama Raita!

name: Bud Spencer & Terence Hill - Slaps And Beans 2
detailed_description: MORE GAMES FROM TRINITY TEAM About the Game Bud Spencer and Terence Hill are back again! The new game is a sequel to the first game and just like a movie saga. The story picks up where it left off at the end of the first Slaps and Beans. Our heroes will experience adventures in new places with new events and will also meet many new characters along the way. Slaps and Beans 2 returns as a scrolling fighting game with a retro gaming, co-op or single player look with a platform mechanic that allows the player to control Bud Spencer and Terence Hill in a revised and improved version of the combat system. Brand new environment dynamics that progressively add enemies as the difficulty increases and of course again with lots of funny quotes. New mini-games that can be played repeatedly in a dedicated party play area for up to 4 players. And finally the dubbing in four languages that immerse the player even more in the real Bud Spencer and Terence Hill ambience. The main features of Slaps And Beans 2 are: - 80s pixel art graphics - improved Bud and Terence-style combat system - cooperative mode - minigames in 4-player party game mode - voiceovers in 4 languages - lots of slaps and lots of beans (double at least, of course!)

_childDocuments_.review: Fun.It is fully voiced. Voices well reflect the type of dialogues those 2 and their belligerents can have.There is plethora of interactions between the 2 brawlers themselves and with their environment. The anthological slaps that you probably know from one. And the flying circus from the other. Bud will break a lot of things.It comes with a bit of puzzles.It references the movies quite well.It also comes with mini-games such as eating everything including the meal of the ones sitting next to you at the table. Scenes that you will play like a dance game or a QTE.On the darker side, it lacks of variety of sounds. The audio atmosphere could have definitely been better.The fights are also sometimes lacking of dynamism. Yes, the punches, especially from Bud were slow and heavy, but still. A bit faster in the game could have been appreciated.It is also a bit clunky at times. Pushing a box for example could be a bit hazardous.Anyway, if you like Bud and his pain in the neck of Terence, if you liked the previous opus that I believe a bit better, you should like this one.It won't be the game of the year, neither the best beat'em up, but it is funny enough and may bring some nostalgia.Double hands smash with both thumbs up for me. Followed by one last hammer fist from above.

_childDocuments_.review: I played it start to finish on Medium difficulty, and it was all I expected as an old fan of the duo (and the first game). Hilarious dialogues, a silly but somehow still kind of threatening villain, great soundtracks, fun minigames and occasional puzzles breaking up the pace of plentiful brawls. The english voices are great, hats off to the actors (say, was Terence's voice misspelled in the credits or "Mattew" is a variant?). Also, nice easter eggs overall (Doc Brown's lab especially made me laugh out loud)!On the criticism side, though... I often mistook Terence for a mook in bigger fights because he didn't really stand out. The hovercraft minigame could use a clearer health indicator, it took me a while to realize that their "bumpers" serve as such. Finally, there was a puzzle (unfortunately I can't remember where) where the two got separated too far from each other and I couldn't really see what I was doing. Since the camera didn't zoom out, I guess it wasn't supposed to happen.Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend it. It's a solid beat 'em up, and a trip down memory lane to fans of the duo. Nice work!

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun! Both story and gameplay wise. Lots of great humor, music, voice acting and great monkey island-like graphics. I didn't mind these hiccups much though, the game is still extremely original and miles more enjoyable than 99% of the boring clones out there today. A must try imo!

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is just about recommendable, but only to people who have heard of the two protagonists before and are not looking for the next break-through title in the side-scrolling beat-em-up genre. At its core, this is basically the same game as the first Slaps & Beans - it is still difficult to lose in combat, as Bud and Terence slap their way out of even the most overwhelming situations with their trademark non-chalant approach. However, this entry seems less buggy, the AI-controlled partner does not need to be revived all the time (though he still occasionally gobbles health pick-ups off the floor when he does not really need them), and the game's ridiculous story is fully voiced this time around.The second game also features traversal puzzle sections which require using each character in turn to help the other along: this usually goes along the lines of Terence scaling an obstacle to knock a ladder down for Bud. In terms of combat changes, the charge move can no longer be spammed and is now only occasionally useful, and Terence can now aim his throws at otherwise inaccessible enemies. He can also pick up a stick to bat items thrown towards him to take enemies out. That said, most encounters will likely be spent mashing the heavy attack button, and unfortunately there still does not seem to be much point in mixing light and heavy attacks. In addition to basic enemies, there are lanky, kung furious guys; fat, tanky, charging guys; fit, tanky, blocking guys; hypnotic-telekinetic androids who can only be damaged during windows of opportunity, and even one woman who has to be neutralised in an apropriately non-violent way!The achievement for stealth (in one scripted section) is more difficult to get this time than in the first game due to tighter timings on security cameras, and the introduction of new noisy obstacles like chains on the ceiling and metal trays on the floor. It is not clear they are interactive until you touch them, and the alarm goes off. The achievement for winning the vehicle mini-game while going in reverse only also makes a comeback, and I was actually able to get it after only a few tries - something I was not able to do in the previous title - probably because in the second game the mini-game is not a race, but a boating demolition derby match.Some levels towards the end throw a little too many enemies at the protagonists, which is a bit irritating because the combat is not particularly deep, but the game ends before it gets too old. It took about the same time to play-through as the first - around five hours with plenty of movie references along the way.

detailed_description: Buzz Celebrate one year of Ghostrunner 2 with the final Ghostrunner 2 DLC, the Anniversary Pack! Complete your katana collection with three all-new swords, paired with 3 flashy hand skins, and a sleek new motorcycle skin to slash your way through the cybervoid. EDITIONS COMPARED GHOSTRUNNER 2 BRUTAL EDITION Ghostrunner 2 Brutal Edition Includes: Ghostrunner 2 Game Ahriman's Katana Sword and Hand Skin Modern Energy Sword and Hand Skin Molten Blade Sword and Hand Skin Gothic Blue Sword and Hand Skin Hand Hologram with Username Aqua Animated Sword and Hand Skin Design 24A Motorcycle Skin Ghostrunner 2 Season Pass ($19.99 Value) GHOSTRUNNER 2 DELUXE EDITION Ghostrunner 2 Deluxe Edition Includes: Ghostrunner 2 Game Ahriman's Katana Sword and Hand Skin Modern Energy Sword and Hand Skin Molten Blade Sword and Hand Skin Gothic Blue Sword and Hand Skin Hand Hologram with Username About the Game Blood will run in the highly anticipated hardcore FPP slasher set one year after the events of Ghostrunner. Adventure through a post-apocalyptic cyberpunk future that takes place after the fall of the Keymaster, a tyrant who ruled over Dharma Tower, the last refuge of mankind. Jack is back to take on the violent AI cult that has assembled outside Dharma Tower and shape the future of humanity. Featuring incredible katana combat mechanics, a deeper exploration of the world beyond Dharma Tower, nonlinear levels with complex motorbike sections, exciting new modes, and all the action you loved about Ghostrunner. Take on challenging, new enemies as you traverse interactive environments including exploding barrels, destructible walls, helpful neutral entities, and countless improvements that keep combat exciting and fresh. Can’t get enough? Dive even deeper into the lore and plot with the new dialogue system. Sounds of the Cybervoid Save humanity in style as you decimate your opponents while listening to the captivating synthwave soundtrack featuring new music from Daniel Deluxe, We Are Magonia, Gost, Dan Terminus, and Arek Reikowski.

_childDocuments_.review: So Ghostrunner 2. Like many other studios, fell into the same trap of going too big in the sequel without really understanding what made the first game successful. Bigger is not always better. There are a total of 18 stages, of which 4 are very, very long stages that are semi open world that take about 3-4 hours to finish, which is something like 1/3 of the game. Not fun at all, half of the time will be traveling on the motorcycle from point A to point B. It feels like they added mini-tasks to prolong the game artificially unlike the first game which was very short and to the point.The plot is unclear and boring, there is really no auditory twist. They have now added a hub world between the stages where you can talk to the NPCs who will comment on what is happening in the stages themselves which again the acting of the voice actors is mediocre -. I wouldn't really happen to even play these games to simply read text into the microphone.I would happen to it even playing these simply read text into the microphone.The graphics are much better but optimization for PC is bad. Especially in DX12, even in the first game there was the same problem that seems not to have been addressed by the developers. Full of frame drops, stuttering, the AI ​​doesn't always respond correctly, the game crashed at least 4-5 times during the 10 hours it took to finish it.The mechanics themselves are more or less the same as the previous game, the enemies are identical to each other. The skills/progression does not feel significant at all, you can not touch the skill tree from the beginning to the end and the experience itself will be more or less the same. Because the game is mostly based on one hit death mechanics for both enemies and the player. The game starts with the Dash\slow time skills and like the previous game you get 4-5 new skills that...surprise. It's exactly the same skills from the previous game!All in all a good and fun game but for what I already played in the first one, I wouldn't pay full price but wait for a significant discount. They didn't take any risks with it and went for the safest and most boring thing that could be as a sequel.5/10The cost of the game is $40, which is apparently a standard price for AA, but Pierre, I wouldn't pay more than $15-20 for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only putting my review as negative because this game could have been better, this does not mean the game is hot garbage tho.Biggest gripes had to be the absolutely god awful performance. Had at least 5 instances where the map wouldn't finish loading and would get me stuck in the geometry or enemies just spawning in waaay too late.      Other gripes would be the open areas with the bike and the hub area. The bike should have been used way more sparingly and only in tight corridors to avoid as much jank as possible. The hub area also felt so unnecessary with its weird bethesda style dialog options and at times mixed voice acting. Would definitely say go play GR1 and the Hel dlc before you play this one and only get it when its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer: (no spoilers until the end, spoiler section marked)Ghost Runner 2 is a proper sequel in my opinion. the gameplay has been expanded upon from GR 1 and Project_Hel. Though I did get quite a few frame drops in large set pieces even after cranking my graphics all the way down, it didn't distract from the greatly expanded combat, new and upgraded utilities, amazing level design, and quite enjoyable story the game has to offer. if performance is what you're worried about I would say maybe wait for a couple of patches before purchasing, but definitely play the demo. But the game is a solid sequel and I cant wait to see what they do next.  8/10Long answer:The combat has seen the greatest improvement. abilities blend together to make fun combos, the new enemies  have very unique attacks that go alongside great with others causing you to not feel overwhelmed by everything going on. the new upgrade system, though lacking the charm of the first games tetris like system, allows you to form Jack to the ghost runner you want him to be, also aiding in exploration due to the upgrade chips being hidden on every level and there being a lot of them. The parkour and movement are good but lacking compared to GR 1. The overall movement speed feels slush in comparison to the first. this is, from what i can tell, done so the combat could be more fluid. Movement in combat feels great (running speed, dash distance, bullet time movement), but the parkour segments outside of combat feel a little slow overall. the removal of multiple dashes is what hurts me the most. the new stamina bar the game bases dashes/blocking/parrying on limits jacks overall movement as now you have to decide between blocking, or dashing towards the enemy, chewing up the same bar. also meaning that if you block bullets you may not have enough stamina for that dash you though you could do, leading to your death. overall if the dash system from the previous game was re-introduced (while the stamina bar was used for only blocking and parrying as i do enjoy the limits on that) i would have no gripes with the how jack feels to control... besides for the games momentummomentum conservation in this game is very strange. certain object give you ridiculous speed/height while dashing or jumping off of them, but as soon as you dash or slide for a second all that momentum is lost. bhopping feels bad in this game due to how slow it feels and that jack cant keep any of his speed doing so unlike GR 1. If the game allowed even just a wee bit more fluidity in jacks momentum it would do wonders.The level design is wonderful. Inside Darma you are treated to bright neon-dystopian visuals like the first game but with so much more flare. Once you reach the outside, the post-apocalypse world took my breath away (as it also did to my frames). The games signature techno-style blended amazingly with the outside environments and the things you run into out there. the game doesn't recycle the same gimmicks too often and comes up with new and interesting ways to do the same thing you've done already. the new sections of the environment you can manipulate add a lot more options in combat and movement.  my biggest issues come with the extreme frame rate drops in some sections, in one section i had to run passed all the enemies as my game was running at about 15 frames and i couldn't do much in the way of fighting. i had many issues with the bike jumps where i would either get too much/ not enough height and crash, or get glitched inside the floor after landing and have to reset. Launch pads are great fun but the hit box could be a little taller for them as i would attempt to jump into one and flight right on over it to my death. the layout of every level was great besides one level where you have to do long drives on your bike from one objective to another without much to do in between.The bike is a great addition when used properly. every bike-only level was the most action packed, edge of my seat gaming experience I've had in a while. each level with the bike is even cooler than the last. shooting with the bike can be a little frustrating as the guns auto holster after a couple of seconds and over heating so fast you have to tap fire to get any real use out of it.SPOILER SECTION:the wing suit has to be the most amount of fun I've had in a long time with a movement based game. the open arenas and parkour segments cause me to almost forget about my issues i have with the game. but you only unlock this ability for the last few levels of the game. making a nice send off to the game but leaving me wishing they added a couple more levels with the wing suit in mind.The story, though not amazing, its great fun to listen to as you're hacking up cyborgs. the main plot was compelling enough for me to be compelled to find hidden tapes to learn more about the lore.  The extra world building put in with the collectibles helps paint a picture of what life is like in this world. the added touch of the descriptions being from jacks POV is a cute touch. the new characters are great fun to listen and chat with though Zoe is a massive step down from her character in the first. Though i didn't care much once Kira and Rahu took main stage as Jack's besties.on top of that, more Rahu. PLEASEOverall the game is a great sequel though the toning down of the movement is a disappointment. the new more open level design is great and is kept very fresh with unique arenas and enemy variety.  the movement could use a couple adjustments but i am very pleased with this game and i cant wait to see what happens next.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 - I love the art style, the music and similar to the first Ghostrunner when the game clicks its awesome. But unfortunately this game has the exact same issues the first one had and then some. The game is inconsistent as ♥♥♥♥: you jump up to a wall to do a wall run and then just randomly fall off of it, you want to grab a ledge and the game decides to just wall run along the edge instead even though you are perpendicular to it, and I could keep going with this stuff... A game that requires you to be very precise and puts you into difficult situations cannot be this inconsistent.Apart from the issues I mentioned the platforming is pretty good in this game, I like that part of it the most. The combat is mediocre tho, it also has inconsistency issues, projectiles hit when its not even close to you, enemies pixel shot you, they boderline pre fire to where you will be the next second and kill you instantly so you have to pre meditate every move you make to the point the whole thing becomes a memory game. Some people might like that, in this case I am not a big fan. The semi open world bike section seems like some major new thing Ghostrunner 2 has, nah man, its just there to artificially extend the playtime, and it also has god awful controls, weird sense of speed, glitches all over the place.The game plays out important story conversations while you are doing difficult platforming sections, good luck listening and following that... Why the ♥♥♥♥ would you design it that way? Makes absolutely no sense whatsoever. The parts where you go back to the headquarters and can talk to people and stuff doesnt belong in this game, it feels like its also there to just extend the playtime due to lack of meaningful gameplay content.The game also has a bunch of the good old Unreal Engine stuttering, FPS literally cuts in half with a massive frame time spike when entering new areas, can even happend during some longer platforming/combat sections and when it happends in the worng place its usually means insta death.The game is still decently good overall but with a few tweaks and fixes it would be much better, it has way more potential that is simply not realised in its current form. I think I liked the first Ghostrunner more.

_childDocuments_.review: Overview: We have on our hands here game with a great gameplay loop and a great atmosphere, but not a whole lot else. Ghostrunner 2 is a very cohesive and fun-to-play cyberpunk samurai simulator. it nails the cybperpunk atmosphere and makes you feel super badass by showcasing super smooth and fun gameplay. 	       It is totally worth.a purchase on sale, and if you’re super into the cyberpunk setting and can really crank those graphics, then I would maybe say its’s even worth a purchase not on sale. But this is not worth its full price, at least in my eyes. The experience is relatively short, as I clocked in at around 9 hours. It has great, fun, varied gameplay that doesn’t get old particularly quickly (but it eventually does). It also has a great atmosphere and killer visuals, with minimal bugs. Is that all Ghostrunner 2 has going for it? Yeah, kinda. 	            In the first game, the story was not very prevalent, which I viewed as a good thing. I didn’t need a story in a game like this. However, in Ghostrunner 2, they lean FULLY into the ‘we have a very important story to tell and we will spend a solid chunk of your gameplay making you experience it’ vibe that has created some of the best game experiences of all time. Ghostunner 2 is not one of those games though. It is not ground-breaking in a single facet of its design, MUCH less so the narrative/story. The narrative is incredibly boring, drawn out, predictable, and coming from someone whose 2nd favorite game of all time is RDR2, has some of the worst-written, most cliche, and least likeable characters in almost any game I have ever played. After only 2 hours, I had completely turned off the game audio and was only listening to music, rather than listening to the incredibly cringe, boring, and bafflingly poorly voice-acted banter between the characters. No hate to anyone who enjoyed the story and the characters, but Jesus, not for me.  	           The difficulty and pacing was also very, very weird. Some entire encounters, I would beat without breaking a sweat, while others (specifically 2 of the boss battles) made me want to pull out my hair, having my clock in 30+ attempts. Thank god for mid-boss-fight checkpoints… I also just couldn’t stand the pacing. I think part of this came as a result of me being so incredibly disinterested in the story, but I feel like the balancing between fighting encounters and just those ‘easy platforming while characters talk’ felt super super off. That one open world mission in the middle was also way too long and repetitive… I reckon most of thee issues could’ve been pretty easily mended by a commitment to game testing, so that they could get real feedback and implement it into the game. I’m not sure how much of this they did.  	           Overall, this experience is totally worth your time, though. It is much better than the first game, to begin with. The gameplay amps it up to a whole new level, and the badass potential is a lot hgiher. The game also goes on pretty crazy sales for having released so recently, so you might as well add it to your library during one of those sales. It has some good aspect, and some bad. As any mid game does. Just get a good playlist ready so your don’t have to listen to the god-awful dialogue/Sights and Sounds- The world and atmosphere are incredibly constructed- The set pieces look awesome- Running it on my steam deck limited my graphical capacities, but it still looked so sick- Sound design and music were fine, but a couple hours in, I decided my ears would be better off listening to music- The acting was piss-poor, unfortunately.Gameplay- Really snappy and responsive- Innovates a bunch on the first game, switching things up- Makes you actually feel like a cyberpunk samurai, badass as hell- Consistently introducing new gameplay mechanics like the biker    - Not particularly incredible additions, but really fun nonetheless- The consistently new game mechanics were quick enough that they didn’t really get old- The difficulty was very poorly balanced. I flew through some missions, while I had to bash my head against some enemy encounters because they felt so bullshtNarrative- I’m going to choose not to comment because I don’t want to seem like a hater (I hate it)- Like its so bad and uninteresting even though its trying so hard

_childDocuments_.review: Would you like to practice rapid parkour on a mostly broken system? Now go play this game.This seems like a far cry from the incredible first game. Even down to the pointlessly open regions and NPCs that are always yapping in your ear, it seems like an attempt to imitate high-budget games. This totally destroys the mood that the first game so expertly cultivated, and it's obvious that "more" is more essential than "better."More adversaries, more tricks, more projectiles, but at most slight improvements to the poor hitboxes, poor enemy design, and omniscient enemy AI that makes the game more difficult to play than enjoyable. Additionally, there seems to be less fluidity in the movement. Let's not even forget how they lied about something about the future of gameBut to me, it really comes down to the reality that we won't have anything as basic as steady frame rate and ray tracing. In response to the game's issues, One More Level has gone "Lalalalala" and stuck their fingers in their ears. Their player base is of no importance to them; what matters to them is the money they made at launch. This is further demonstrated by DLC after DLC that barely modifies the game, and the constant barrage of unfavourable reviews for the follow-up to one of my favourite games.To be really honest, I don't give a damn about Ghostrunner or One More Level anymore. Because of the way they handled this game, they have completely lost my respect, and I no longer have faith in them to update or improve their games before release. They stole the money after selling a flawed, incomplete product and passing it off as the final item. They just care about the money they can make off the hype, not the community or the state of their game.Furthermore, to use the words of the Ghostrunner developers "a future optimisation patch would be beating a dead horse," WOW.

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird. Definitely worse than the first game, but I wouldn't have it any other way.It's like the sophomore album that's following a great first record -- it's trying new things, and it succeeds at creating some of the best moments between the two games...and the absolute worst levels imaginable. Credit where credit's due, they definitely weren't resting on the success of the first game -- and I can't help but respect that.  Pacing is the biggest issue with this game (and the first game); there is simply too much filler between the killer.If you liked the masochistic death counter + parkour of the first game, you'll find some fun in this one too, alongside some surprises both great and awful. Soft recommend if you're craving more from the first, but don't expect an improvement in all the right places.

_childDocuments_.review: When it all clicks, nothing feels quite as good as GR2. I did not play the original since it's release, and I was surprised that so many of this game's new mechanics, such as blocking, permanent shuriken's, etc, weren't in the OG because it feels so natural to have them (I love parry mechanics). If you can get into a flow with GR2, time will just fly by. The game operates on the rule of cool, and it's concerned only with whatever seems badass, even if it's setting and themes are derivative. The game definitely has problems; The hub is completely unnecessary and while I wouldn't call the writing bad, I don't care to enough to have narrative only sections. Additionally, while many bugs have probably been ironed out since release, this game is still full of them and it can be frustrating to have an amazing performance in combat ruined by clipping into yet another wall. Still, I don't find these flaws distract from how fun the game. It's additionally really great that the sequel does not invalidate the first game, containing enough different mechanics and flow to create a small franchise with two thrilling cyborg-ninja experiences. Don't skip this one!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than the original but it has growing pains from being a larger game. PROSThe game play is a good bit more complex, leading to some very satisfying "THINK FAST!!!" momentsThe enemies are a good bit betterThe bosses are an order of magnitude better than the original game'sThe motorcycle is amazing and some of its set pieces are the best levels in either game. CONSThe game is a little too long for me, this issue seems to stem from the last third of the game being weakerThe open world section is not good in my opinion, no one plays this game for thatThe open world combined with the motorcycle is even worseThe late game platforming is mired with these platforms you have to pull and wait for, they slow down the game and that's bad The final boss is just bad, none of the other bosses rely on a quick time event

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute Cinema, Peak Game, 10/10 fighting is sleek and fast. Beautiful characters like Zoe. I love this game with all my heart. I wish more games existed like this. The cut scenes are amazing, jack leaving dharma for the 1st time with the motorcycle gave me chills. Little bugs, not game breaking. _childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: GR2 is a fun game but I will have to recommend the 1st one if you're new to the series.GR2 adds more elements to the mix but doesn't really improve all that much. Levels are  bigger but don't flow as nicely, you can interact with NPC's face to face unlike the first one but it has no meaning. They barely say anything to add to the narrative and you don't get quests or anything from them to add to your gameplay experience. The half section of the game dabbles in some semi open world style bike riding that gets a little boring. And the bike riding controls aren't the best around. The bike has no weight to it. It doesn't feel like you're driving a vehicle. I enjoyed my time with the game and feel like I got my money's worth. I hope that these little additions that we saw in this entry are build upon and polished so the next release from One More Level can really elevate the series.It's a fun game, if you buy it I'm sure you will enjoy your time. It's just not as captivating as the first one and feels completely skippable.

_childDocuments_.review: gameplay wise this game feels the same as its predecessor, however i would even say the movement feels cleaner and faster which is great.There is some performance issues, my PC specs are roughly equivalent to the recommended however i cant run the game at anything above minimum settings without having frame by frame stutters, perhaps its my hardware issue i wasn't bothered to look into it but i know others are having stutter issues.The story is mediocre at best, but still a good sequel, only 7.4 hours to finish the main story however which was...disappointing - however i do plan on doing 100% achievements.dialogue is not as good as ghost runner 1, nor is the the Upgrade UIsoundtrack is solid and there are some interesting new challenges within the story and enemy types. The parrying system is Terrible (although i just played sekiro which has the best combat system and parrying in gaming history so i shouldn't be surprised).The boss fights are cool but kinda rng based, i do prefer the parkour type boss fights.game lacks polish and seems rushed almost, but again its still solid. just not worth the full asking price.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - A great sequel, but not as good as I thought it would be. The story is ok for me, it's not perfect but ain't bad either. _childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good game that is overcharging at 40$ unless you are very much into replaying the same game on a higher difficulty. A step up from the first in so many small ways, but it's pretty tough to recommend unless you wanted more from the first game with a stronger story.++PROS+++ Much better plot than the first game that is consistent in hype and tone throughout.+ Voiceacting is well done, art direction is pretty. Not much to complain about.+ Performance on my system was almost perfect throughout the entire game.+ Lots of small QOL improvements that make the game a lot more fun to play and a tad bit easier.+ ACTUAL upgrade system that gives you strong upgrades throughout with lots of build potential.+ A roguelike mode that is... Fine, it's not great but it's fine.+ Still LOTS of collectibles and they show up in your little HQ to gawk at in person this time.+ ACTUAL BOSSES even if they are a tad bit repetitive, although the bike boss is the best one in the entire series if you ask me, just wild fun.+ A fun open-world level that makes me wish the whole game was designed in that way, where you basically go from level to open section to level.--CONS--- Both Bike and Glidesuit are added too late into the experience to justify being shown off as heavily as they are. The two levels you get with the bike are fun, the glidesuit is wonky but in an arcadey fun way. The Moto-Bike DLC is just not worth it in earnest unless you sincerely want to just blitz through an endless runner scenario.- The wallrunning, wallclimbing and railgrinding can be pretty wonky even after the first game. This has absolutely caused me many deaths for no particular reason other than the game's own design not always working the best.- Some objects have really, really bad collision.- 60~ish gigs of harddrive space is not a typical complaint I'd put down, but here I'll make the exception as it's a pretty big leap up from the first game without necessarily being better. Small nitpick here for sure.Overall a good game, but unless you REALLY LOVED the first game, I only recommend on sale, and I wouldn't recommend the cosmetic DLCs unless you wish to support the dev further. I'd love to play a 3rd game, but if that has the same wonky issue with wallrunning and wallclimbing I'll be a bit annoyed as that'll be the 3rd game in a row to have that same issue. Otherwise the increased budget really shows in these awesome setpieces and some REALLY well done arena levels, but in other places it makes me question why the addition say the bike and wingsuit were needed and why they were done so late into the game, effectively making both feel just slapped in there.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: So...I've played and I believe even beaten the 1st GR game on hardcore, and as annoying as it was. It wasnt usually a fault in the game that made me fail a mission. It was simply myself getting too impatient. Now, GR 2... how is it that the always seem to make the mechanics that made the 1st game good, feel like complete dogwater dooky poopoo stuck on the side of the lid awful. 1. Parrying, a seemingly more and more common mechanic to see in games ( not a real fact, just personal speculation, or from my own experience) which can either be good, or atrocious to play with/ gimmicky or jank. The first game, though I haven't played it in a while, I recall having excellent parry mechanics in that for one, if u click the parry button trying to get perfect timing( which I personally do as most games with parry I play are tap a button or 2 and it instantly parries and will parry an attack within the X amount of frames the game gives u. This game though, though I'm not far in yet, just feels unresponsive and delayed occasionally. I do intend to get further, and ideally beat this game, but so far, just the combat mechanics seem less fleshed out compared to GR1.2. The combat as stated by others, is not really anything new, very few new enemies, etc. having fought the first actual boss...It's not looking to bright imo. Attacks that I know for certain I shoulda blocked or parried via literally seeing my character pull the sword up into the block animation, only to still get hit and killed.Getting killed by an attack you can at least see, and understand, albeit annoying, is what I want from combat in such a game as this and GR1(which mostly succeeded), instead I get killed randomly, even if I appear to be blocking. Now, I will admit that there maybe is just a different play style than in the first game, but judging on the limited reviews I read, consensus seems to be that this game sucks.TLDR: Sequels always remove what was fun in the first game, so just stick to one and done.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel I'm being very generous leaving a technically positive review with the caveat that this is not a $40 game. Buy it on sale.in short:- Game has performance issues in any of the open world segments (most of the game after the first few levels) which is ridiculous, because this game doesn't look any better than the first which I could run at max settings and literally not once have I had issues with it.- The story is more annoying and more intrusive than the first game. Zoe is still incredibly annoying and whiny and fights with the new character that I actually *do* like who takes her place. Most levels boot you back to a hub where you have to go talk to someone to start the next level, you can also talk to the other characters which I did not do a single time. I liked the villains (and their voice acting) more than any of your friends.- The ending is so self-serious and has this monologue about whether Jack is a man or a machine and how "being a ghostrunner is a difficult line to toe" I'm sorry One More Level, this is beyond bad writing. You cannot make me play as a killing machine that exclusively kills bad people and does good things for 6 hours and then go "hrrrrrm I'm so edgy and conflicted" and expect me to believe it because you said so.- I like most of the new combat stuff and upgrade systems- The motorcycle is pretty fun when I'm racing people and not driving around a giant open wasteland in my linear action game- The bosses are significantly better than GR1- All good games have a grappling hook, even better games have a  which this game does, and it f****** rocks.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is a modern gaming masterpiece that is the middle finger to typical AAA titles that have nonsensical stuff in them. Gameplay may be trial and error, but it feels so good to be a cyber-ninja after learning how to play with upgrades that will benefit your experience. With its electronic music soundtrack and the depiction of a dystopian world, the game is a piece of cake.I strongly recommend this game to anyone who wants a true video game with little cutscenes that don't drag on for too long to the point of trying to be a movie.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: So many decisions they made for this sequel make no sense to me and seem to go against the entire ethos of what made the first game so fun and replayable. I could go on for hours and the music is 10/10 but the combat, level design, and weird rpg elements are 2/10. The amazing flow of the first game feels absent and the pace much slower, cant recommend this if you enjoyed the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED the first Ghostrunner, but it seems like they completely missed the mark with this one. The missions seem way less cohesive and the story is SUPER bland with terrible characters that it just makes you wish there wasn't any at all. I felt like the first game was primarily focused on combat with some puzzling here and there but that's not the case with 2. It kinda feels like the whole game is puzzle after puzzle with combat sprinkled in. The bike was cool but then it came to a weird "open world" part where you have to get off the bike after every little section in order to progress further. I also ran into several bugs where I either clipped through the map or completely fell through it while playing with some performance issues and hitching when loading into a new area. I also for some reason feel like this game is WAY more annoying when dealing with enemies when I didn't necessarily feel that way with the first. So overall, I feel like they had something great going with the 1st game and then they just decided to try and over achieve with the 2nd. I do not plan to finish the game after waiting for it to come out if that tells you anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat game. The sequel kinda regressed in some ways and I beat the game in around 6.5 hours. This includes listening to all the dialogue and finishing all rogue runner stages. So probably 5.5 to 6 hours excluding that.Some bad things first:- Too much focus on the story- The hub is unnecessary and kills the flow of the game- Too many map puzzles- Movement feels a bit slower- Why can you easily block with the right mousebutton?- The bike get stuck on everything and feels bad to control. I had to kill myself multiple times to reset the bike- The outside is kinda bland (I mean it makes sense, but it wasn't very interesting and Ghostrunner never needed open world parts)- I had 2-3 absolutely insane frame drops down to 15 FPS or so- Game could use a little more polish. I got stuck in the ground and traversing felt a little inconsistent at times- This stupid robot you can pull towards you is ♥♥♥♥. It's just confusing because everything other object pulls you towards it- Hair looks super bad on the characters. No matter if AA is on or not- I felt kinda lost at times- Idk if I'm expecting too much, but I wish the game was a little bit longerPositives:- Graphics are even better. It's eye candy- Game ran at 200+ fps most of the time- Slashing these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is so satisfying- Soundtrack is neato- New mechanics are being introduced frequently- Some cool looking bosses. I think most fights were decent too- OG enemies (they also look cooler) + some new onesNow, the amount of negative points might make it seem like the game is bad, but it is not. It's still a good and enjoyable game but replaying this game is going to be annoying due to the hub and slightly drawn out open world part etc. I suggest you get this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is an okay game but not a great one it takes what made the first Ghostrunner great and expands on it. But these inclusions are not really a welcome change. The gameplay is still great but it's much slower than the original due to a strange decision the developer made thus making the game much harder and infuriating if you played the original for 100 hours with these mechanics. That's not to say it's bad, but the level design in this game isn't as creative as the original. Overall Ghostrunner 2 is an okay game but there's issues with stuttering and many bugs and glitches that I have encountered in this current state I cannot recommend it. Maybe in the future when fix the game and during a price drop the game will be worth it. To this date there isn't raytracing in this game... The developers have promised it's been months now.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: The downfall of an indie game is when it tries to be AAA and loses all its charm.I enjoyed this game for the most part but the cons far outweigh the pros, it feels very unpolished and I don't see myself coming back to replay it. They slowed down the pace of the game, enemies are more spread out and the movement feels heavy. The level design is all over the place, there is no way to tell what can be parried and what can not which resulted in a lot of unfair deaths, and the worst part about this game is the story, the character writing is unbearable, it's much better to not have a story than to have one as annoying as this one.There are some exciting sections like the motorcycle levels and the bosses, but it feels like they only come around once in a blue moon.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a huge step down from the first game which was amazing. It comes off like an attempt to mimic big budget games, even down to the needlessly open areas and NPCs constantly yapping in your ear, completely destroying the atmosphere the first game so perfectly cultivated. The movement somehow feels a bit less fluid as well, which was really the last straw. The first game was one of the best games in the year it came out but I didn't even finish this one. Writing this negative review makes me feel so bad I'm gonna go write a positive one for the first game.

_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: More Polish equals less polished (all respect to Polish people, though. Kurwa bober).The game is great, and I enjoyed a lot of it.However, it's way more clunky and way less charming, especially the music, which is still nice, but not as memorable as the absolute bangers from the first game.The character writing and their voice actors are both equally fantastic. Their performances, the humour and the new characters really made the story stand out and really enjoyable.Speaking of... The story is good, but again, not as striking as the story from the first game. The great aspect of this one is the expanded lore and the whole  thing. But the main plot is kinda anti-climactic and doesn't really lead anywhere. While in the first game you were discovering more about the voice in your head, who you really are, and all the stuff that's happening and has happened in the mysterious city of Dharma...Here the main plot is: "ooh, some new bad guys have come up, gotta stop their mischiefs, go go power rangers!" segway...The whole semi-open world wasteland, a.k.a. , is a wonderful addition.It really matches the classic , and now the game can appeal to both BladeRunner and MadMax fans.The motorcycle too, is a very fun addition changing the gameplay a big bit.There are also some other new things, but these two are the most recognisable, and those that really change the ever going stale gameplay, because as fun as it can be, after some time it can get very repetitive.You can clearly see that heart and soul were put into makinf this game.However, as much as I respect that, and am very pleased to see, it doesn't change its quality.The game has very mediocre overall.The most obvious signs being the animations, some models, and other graphical elements.But those don't matter to me. They are not making me rip my ass hair out, out of frustration.What is, is the nerve-cracking, sometimes barely functioning, and unbalanced gameplay and its mechanics.Some upgrades either don't do ♥♥♥♥, or they have such minimal effect it's unrecognisable (like the shield breaker or the guided stars).Some levels are horribly balanced, where the distances between objects you have to access, or the speed at which deadly elements are moving, is way out of proportion.Examples:The challenges being the biggest nuisance and the most broken and unbalanced part of the game. They're just very poorly made and not even fun to play.And most motorcycle levels, which is just constant crashing into stuff, because the map layout isn't correspondent to the motorcycle's capabilities.The frustration from playing can exponentially increase, with a computer "not powerful enough" for the game. Which is exactly my case.For the record, I still surpass the minimum requirements, and being able tu run way more complex games with way fewer struggles kind of indicates the state at which this game is.The voice lines, enemies, and sometimes the whole level itself many times load after you're already experiencing them.Which means that sometimes enemies appear randomly and kill you on the spot.I've got stuck into unloaded objects, fell through the map, and crashed way more times than I am comfortable speaking about.The endless lagging, whenever a new place loads, or some effect happens (like using your abilities or when shooting occurs) is a very detrimental disadvantage to the proclaimed "fast-paced gameplay."I'm saying proclaimed, but there are some levels that if you try to play them "fast", you'll get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the ass.The biggest downgrade has to be the enemy variations.I miss a lot all the different enemies that were in the first game.Here, the enemies are mostly the same throughout the whole game, and they just get a re-skin halfway through.There are some new enemies, of course, but very few. Other than the changing environment, the combat can become easily repetitive.As I've said before, the game is good, and I enjoyed its good parts as much as I could.However, I'll choose the first game any other day ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is nice. There are aspects to it that I like more than GR1. But that's pretty much where the good stuff ends. On to the bad stuff!The story makes absolutely no sense. Granted, it's been some time since I've played the first game. I also didn't get the DLC for the first game. From what I've experienced so far, though, I guess remembering everything that happened in the first game  the DLC is necessary to get what is going on at all. Nothing makes sense and it just seems you're expected to know things from the first game. Yeah, it's a sequel, okay. But even then, I think giving it its own story that isn't dependent on the first game would've been the correct move. Go find any game with sequels. In almost every single one, you can just start from whichever game you feel, and you can still get the general gist of the story.It's very easy to just run in circles looking for the route the devs want you to take. Indicators for what is the correct route are minimal, and quest markers are used sparingly. It's very easy to get lost in bigger areas.Frankly, the game is a buggy mess. Enemies can get stuck on the skybox, some will just never attack, and hitboxes are terrible. In the first boss fight, after it had gone through an entire attack animation, I dashed up behind it to get some damage in, and just died out of nowhere. That's just naming a few that I've encountered in my first 45 minutes of playing the game, and more have been popping up. It's just an absolutely buggy mess.Just... don't. Unless you are willing to put up with really stupid bugs and you don't care about story at all, then just don't get the game. It's embarrassing how much worse this game is compared to the first in almost every way.

But it is less grounded than the first, its either you like it more cause of the changes or you expect it to be too much like the first and you'll be disappointed.Either way its a great addition. I loved it like I did the first and can only recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: Only the most lethal can survive in Dharma City.This sequel is a very bold and highly creative successor to an already impressive original game. When the first Ghostrunner game came out, I was blown away by the movement, the fast combat, and the enjoyable challenge that it presented. The movement was slick, the environment looked really cool, and the gameplay was top-notch.Ghostrunner 2 takes everything that's great about the game and turns it up a notch. There are some seriously mind-blowing moments in this one, and the action gets really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane at times. They added a lot of new stuff, and most of the new mechanics are super slick and satisfying. Ghostrunner 2 is still fast, lethal, twitchy, and utterly enjoyable.However, it's not without its flaws. The Devs took a very experimental approach with this one, which I was initially surprised by. I expected them to just refine the original formula, but I'm actually glad they ended up introducing all these new mechanics. Some of them, like the  aren't as polished, but they're still fun. The  is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AWESOME though. The  was neat here and there, but ultimately I didn't end up using it much.However, I'm glad that these devs are not complacent. They're willing to take risks in a world where AAA game companies refuse to. I will always cheer on a passionate team like this, and I will always continue buying these sort of games.By the way, the game also has a more detailed story than the first one. However, I unfortunately didn't care for it much, as I'm just here for the gameplay. Your mileage may vary though, as there is definitely some interesting stuff there. While I still prefer the overall polish of the first game, Ghostrunner 2 is still a very enjoyable, fast, and at times, over-the-top ride. I highly recommend both the original and this new sequel. Bravo One More Level!Now, I'mma go back and grind hardcore mode
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that this is a disappointing sequel. It has some good impovements, but a lot of downgrades too.The first game was a game that knew what it was, a 3d platformer with combat and AAA graphics. Focus was on speed and finesse, which is why every level ended with time and deathcount leaderboards. This game tries to actually be a AAA game, and that's IN NO WAY A COMPLIMENT. A hub where you just talk to people, an open world section, long and tiresome cutscenes, all of that is "Why?!" This supposed to have a focus on speed, why so many levels are well over half an hour long. The pacing is just truly atrocious.There are some good sections, like the action bike levels (not the normal bike levels), the glider platforming, generally the platforming sections felt good, as well as many combat encounters.About combat encounters, they did not learn their lessons from the first game. In the original out of 4 abilities you would ever use just Tempest because it replenished fast and was easy to use, other abilities just were too situational, too risky, too costly, and too unnecessary to ever use. It was a problem.In this game, it's basically the same thing, but now it's the Shuriken, compared to which all other abilities are trash. Not only is it your only ranged ability, and is also the cheapest, it counters every single enemy you might struggle against, to the point there might as well not be the other abilities. The others are not as trash though, and sections where you need to quickly switch them are cool, but to make them usable you have to upgrade them, and you might as well just upgrade the shuriken because it's the one you will use regardless of the situation by just how strong it is.Ultimates are there to be those extra costly things that you will basically use once per level. And you wouldn't exactly want to use them that once per level, they are in a way "skip the encounter", because of the countdown you want to use it basically on the first encounter of the level to have two uses, and most of them don't even sound cool, experimenting with them is especially prohibitive because of their cost. You would think you would be able to experiment in the all new and important hub, but outside of the roguelike minigame you cannot. Great design.That rumble was to illustrate just how the game doesn't feel like an upgrade, a sequel, but is just different. The cool parts are cooler, but the bad parts of the original are transferred directly and expanded upon at most leaving the same issues, at worst amplifying them.Have to mention the open world level, it truly killed the pace of the game and made me see the negatives. In particular want to mention how the motorcycle is great at the action sections, but especially on the open world level it's utter trash, can't look around on it, it gets stuck everywhere and stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say the game is better than Ghostrunner 1 but GR2 is still a good game in its own right. New to GR2 comes an upgrade system which helps make the movement more smooth and allows you to change up combat a bit. The build variety here is a definite upgrade over GR1, and for casual play there are many ways you can build that feel good to play. Overall, I liked what they were going for in GR2, but the movement feels worse in GR2 than in GR1 and that's mostly what I care about.GR2 also did story better than GR1 I think, but frankly I did not pay that much attention to story in either game so take this with a massive grain of salt. _childDocuments_.review: An improvement in every way from the original, which was already amazing. 3D Katana Zero, with a deep but not overwhelming combat system, and all the tools you need to overcome it. Enemy variety is decent, but it is disappointing that besides two or three units, all three of the major enemy factions feel basically the same. Cybervoid, and parkour in general, is much improved, and the two major level-dependent mobility tools feel wonderful,  The game suffers a little on the technical level; my rig is a bit frankensteined, but it's no joke - 48 gigs of RAM and an AMD 5700. Still, I had *severe* frame stutters in very odd locations, and always during combat arenas or parkour segments, where a few frames of reaction time is literally the difference between success and a restart.  Overall:10/10 Gameplay10/10 Music - seriously, it's perfect7/10 Story - while there might be some translation issues, sometimes characters would discuss new information as if it had already been revealed, and the main threats of the game felt vague and unimportant at times. Still don't know why Mitra was doing anything. Still, though, the dialogue is well-written and characters feel unique, especially the two former Keys. 8/10 graphics - Art design carries this game hard, it's beautiful.
