_childDocuments_.review: In general it was a somewhat fun game for the most part. But compared to the first part and project Hel it just cannot scale up to them and the expectations that came with them.On a basic level this game did deliver a lot of the things i was hoping for - a sequel to a game i really loved with some nice stages and some fun additions to the abilities. The Bike was a good bit glitchy but overall did bring a nice touch and did break through some of the more repetitive feeling. The story was okay, definitly not a masterpiece, but it was somewhat consistent. The graphic was nice, the abilities fun to play around and especially the first few levels really managed to capture the feeling you had throughout the first game. The hub was a sweet addition that a lot of people complained about, but i'm honestly not completely sure why. Most of the dialogue is fully optional and even the needed dialogue can just be skipped through very fast. So it really just provided some easter-eggs and some dialogue for everyone who wanted to see more. But to be honest, that was really where the positives ended, at least in comparision to its predecessor. One of the things i loved most about GR 1 was how smooth and bug-free it is.This game is everything but that. I've encountered more bugs than i could count. From falling through the map, the bike getting stuck, enemies seeing me through invisibility, upgrades/bonuses not working, dialogue and sound cutting out, my gap jammer deciding to quit its job, falling down from walls/not being able to run on them which worked just fine a second ago, or enemies getting stuck and me dying for no reason, it really had it all. The bugs got especially consistent in the later stages and the new "simulation"; which is, as a concept very cool, but nearly rendered impossible due to glitches for me. It just feels like the developers got rushed a lot in the later parts which is such a shame, as the potential is there.The one thing this game really, really did not need though was the one "open-world" - level it got. It was possibly the most bugged, inconsistend, far too long and confusing level it had. Really, the game would probably greatly improve just by removing that level.In total i'd say - it's still a decent game. While it has a good bit of issues it is enjoyable and fun for the most part, especially if you do not aim to get 100%. I struggled a lot on if i would recommend this game not, but i think in general it doesn't really need more hate than it already gets from some people. I would not get it for the full price, nor would i recommend getting it as any of the special editions as of right now at least. If you're looking for a game that feels as polished and great as GR 1 - just stick with GR 1. That game was so insanely good it just set insane expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Immensely rough around the edges, especially for the type of game that it is... but it is fun as long as you play it casually.When I finished Ghostrunner 2 I noticed I was fairly close to 100% the game's achievements, so I figured I may as well go the extra mile. That's where GR2 was at its absolute worst and the lack of polish was even more apparent than my initial playthrough. Sloppy hitboxes, various instances of awkward geometry, questionable level design, erratic enemy response time...And that's without getting into how inconsistent performance is, sometimes working *fine*, sometimes tanking to 50FPS and even below. Especially in the 2nd half of the game, where any sense of optimization is out the window.It's fine if you play the game just to finish it, but going for 100% achievements includes finishing any 5 levels (not back-to-back) without dying. Obviously, player skill plays a part in how painful (or easy) that might be, but it's far from the only factor thanks to the game's everlasting inconsistency.Sometimes you'll dash past a corner and an enemy will take a second to react and shoot, other times they'll be ready to blast you the milisecond you stick your head out. Sometimes you'll manage to connect a jump to a jump-pad just fine, other times you will randomly snap into a wallrun on said jump-pad platform instead. Sometimes you'll counter-attack a Shinobi and all will be well, other times you might randomly clip through the floor once the animation is done and fall to your death.I'm not trying to boil it down to "if you care about achievements, you'll hate this", not at all in fact. I'm just mentioning this in the context of GR2's whole goal. It's meant to be a perfectionist's wet dream, with "trial and error" being the name of the game. But the game has no business attempting to achieve that with this many quirks that constantly thwart your efforts, regardless of your skill level and quick decision making. When you overcome a tough segment in GR2, more often than not, it feels like you got lucky rather than got through it with skill, and that's a shame.That said, I still enjoyed GR2 way more than I have the first game.I thought the first game was an even bigger mess, which offered nothing but frustration. (Slipgate Ironworks's involvement is REALLY felt in that game)I had a bit of hope knowing Slipgate isn't involved in GR2, like maybe it'll have more of a chance to be a more polished game. Sadly it's still broken in a lot of similar ways, but I feel like the gameplay loop is much more refined here.Where GR1 would constantly hit the breaks on your playthrough with boring cybervoid segments, GR2 often makes those a bit more engaging by letting you platform\do combat instead of just walking\jumping basic corridors listening to exposition dump.The bike has been a pretty solid addition in my opinion, but it understandably received a mixed reception. I think the bike in itself is a fun gimmick when used right, but some of the level design really does not flatter it. In fact, the worst level in the entire game involves the bike, so that's another knock against it.A level with a huge open desert where you just meander around between 3 very distant locations in order to get through a bridge. It's butchering the pacing and is not a good time. The more linear segments with the bike are where it shines imo, when you're going full-speed and dispatching threats on the go, while periodically jumping on and off the bike, varying between ground and vehicle combat. Pretty good stuff mostly.I could give two sh**s about the story in these games, but I will say that this game's automatically better for not having the Architect, who was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying, a pompous snot constantly babbling god-complex nonsense in your ear as you try to get through GR1's BS levels. GR2 still has an annoying character (Kira's awful) but it's far less overbearing than GR1's dialogue, where it felt like no one would STFU for a second - which can be an issue in a game where your focus is essential.So, TLDR, Ghostrunner 2 is way more fun than the first game imo, but it is yet another game that demands perfection from the player, but rarely extends it the same courtesy. If you're a perfectionist, the game will rarely reward you for it. It has a lot of rough edges to smooth and has plenty of issues that I'm absolutely shocked are still there so long after it launched. It's jank city, but it's fun if you don't try to play into the perfectionist trap.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Don't buy the game unless you want to be heavily dissapointed.Cons:Gameplay Design Choices - The devs decided to NOT fix the bugs/physics inconsistencies from the first game, made deflect into a seperate button from attacking, downgraded tempest to not kill enemies (now its just shoving them away???), made blink into a VERY-rarely-available skill and have a weird three-step activation (instead of point-and-click, you now have to point, click, then press the skill button again), and just decided to slowed down the combat gameplay in general. New Skills Design Choice - Sure its nice to have the shurikens available for combat, but when you never know if the enemy can be killed or is only stunned, or when the enemy outright dodges them, it teaches you to not rely/use them at all due to how much it messes up your tempo when a result u dont expect happens. The other two new skills are useless in combat, and I'm not joking. The game forces you to use those skills for parkour, but are otherwise unused/unusable.Enemies - Instead of making the terrain play in your favor (as is in GR1), it now plays in the enemies favor, where they are given a wide open area to watch you dodge and squirm with amusement. Doesn't help when there are enemies that can target you with long range projectiles from across the map. Doesnt help when you no longer have blink, surge and a lethal tempest at a reliable availability.Motorcycle - The motorcycle part was the worst, if you can't make physics be consistent at a "running" speed, how on earth would a high-speed obstacle-avoiding motorcycle chase be controllable (I'm on MnK), much less enjoyable. Not to mention theres a COUPLE of levels in which you spend 90% of the time driving the motorcycle just to from point A to point B to point C to.............what happened to the game designs principles from GR1 like seriously ?Sound - Its VERY clear they reused sounds from GR1, which is not an issue given that the sound matches the object. Unfortunately thats not the case, as the beeping sound from a falling drone is used for multiple airborne enemies of various designs, which doesn't make sense for them to make that kind of noise.Music - The music used matches the gameplay: dull, tedious, and you get sick of it real quick. GR1 soundtrack is energetic and hypes u up, whereas in GR2, it becomes some sort of background noise that mildy distracts you. Boss Fights - Gone is the very precise and well-timed parrying and attacks to kill a boss (e.g. Hel, funny elevator shaft). Now its just mindless hacking with the occasional dodging. The worst part is you are supposed to be fighting other ghostrunners, which should result in fights similar to Hel's. But nope its just seldom attacks to you while you can slice them up mindlessly.Character design - GR1 made Jack into an aloof badass, Architect an arrogant but brainy and cunning villain, and Mara a compelling i-do-what-i-do-because-i-have-no-other-choice villain. GR2 made Jack into an obnoxious guy who tries too hard to be cool, introduces a quirky scientist who makes fun of Jack for not knowing pop culture references, as well as a random leader who gets killed one-third of the way into the campaign.Conclusion - Just so many design choices that goes against the combat flow made me question if this is made by another dev team. For comparison, ID Software did a terrific job making DOOM Eternal improve upon the combat system and gameplay flow from DOOM 2016, whereas GR2 somehow has a slower, clunkier gameplay than GR1. Pros:New Lore - Aside from continuing the story after GR1, you get to learn a bit of history of the world by interacting with other characters in a RPG-game way (with dialogue options and free roaming).*Update: Finished the game, utterly anti-climatic ending with the most cliche cutscene and cringe monologue.Challenges - Wide variety of challenges. You have timed parkour courses and enemy elimination, target shooting (with tempest skill), arena minigames.Conclusion - Not enough Pros to make GR2 a more fun/enjoyable/better game than GR1, but the lore kept me going.

_childDocuments_.review: Nah...just nah!This game is just so much worse than GR1.Where exactly?The Boss fights in GR1 where really fun. Exhausting, but fun. Here? Not so much, since "hitting it until it dies" is just not the type of fight that GR is made for. I guess they were trying to take a page out of Dark Souls but they just did it poorly. If your in first person you dont see the animation coming and since the rotation of the enemies is kinda randomised you can predict it either.Some mechanics were fun, especially Naga was a cool Idea imo and the 3 different forms from whats-his-name with the green one healing him was kinda cool aswell.Really? Why? To what purpose?The amount of times I had to restart from checkpoint because I gliched through the floor on my bike was higher than the amount of deaths I had at Hardcore TOM in GR1. Same goes for the Bike being stuck on a pebble, cuz I rode 2cm further to the right than the devs had anticipated.Also the amount of oob area you can reach by just walking is insane, it feels like no one ever checked if the game was ready.Without spoiling to much (even tho I dont recommend playing anyway) the characters motivations are kinda vague and really not that relatable. Everything is just added on top of already closed story-strands of GR1. You could have made a good story if you just didnt desperatly try to get the same story vibe as in GR1 but with all of the changes that you made  was the one where you tried to stay as close, or rather closer than possible?The voice acting and characters reactions tried to make you care about the people, but there is just no build up, no exitation or anything. The last Boss just screams about "JUST LET ME ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ KILL YOU!!!" but his motivations are never made clear. Did I miss some story sequence or smth by accidentally skipping a part or why should I be able to sympathise with this guy?All in all despite this game surely taking many hours to make, it  lazySecond parts are often worse than the first and this game is sadly  an exception

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent and well polished game that stays true to the vision of its predecessor while only building on the gameplay elements. The maps are larger, the combat combos are more complex, and the number of solutions available in the levels are endless. Each time you replay a level you play it different, which I find to be incredibly fun. The sound design is as good if not better than the first game and, just like the first game, there are plenty of reasons to play the game over and over again as you try to beat your previous score. And just like the first game, finishing the level with a perfect run is incredibly satisfying. I love the in game collectibles because they aren't essential to the games core mechanics (ie, you don't need them to win at all) but having them makes the game more fun. Overall: 10/10 great game and absolutely worth the money to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is annoying, I wish Steam had an in between for thumbs up and down, because that's what I'd give this game, a mixed review. I'm editing my review because they added Hardcore Mode. Play Hardcore Mode if you have the game, it makes things better, but problems still exist. Apologies for the bad news.This is a very good game, but the reason I'm giving a thumbs down is because I cannot recommend it when GR1 is just so good in comparison. I've seen a few people saying its better than GR1 and that's awesome, I'm glad people are having fun! These are all our own humble opinions and I respect that... but GR1 is 100% better. If you've never played either I can't recommend this over the first sadly.I saw someone say GR2 is more refined and I strongly disagree, its actually dumbed down. GR1 feels 100% more fluid, faster and difficult.Hardcore mode makes things much better in GR2, but some of my biggest issues like the game's approach to enemies and abilities still exists and I know they won't go away. I can only hope for GR3.Areas: Many of us agree that the outdoor areas severely break the flow of the game. Also going back and forth through areas in this game is not a good move. I understand the necessity of reusing an area, but here it feels very cheap. GR1 you basically moved forwards the entire game, a true sense of progression and a "I'm coming for you" feeling that I absolutely loved. Overcoming Enemy Types: Now this might be subjective because this is how I like to play, but I make it a goal to only use the sword as much as I can help it. No shuriken or any ranged ability on enemies. It just doesn't feel right to me, cheesing it almost. I find it MUCH more satisfying to take down every enemy in the area by viciously dashing and slicing through each one to the next, getting right in their face in the blink of an eye. Shurikens being used to activate things in the environment is fine, but I want to tackle my enemies the way I choose to. GR1 lets you do that, player choice is a wonderful thing.Now for GR2... There are certain enemies that you MUST attack in a SPECIFIC way. E.g. Shurkien first and then attack... no acceptations. I really don't like this. Enemies like that are boring because every encounter is now more predictable. I love GR1 because pretty much all the enemies you can attack at any time, so long as you can get close, and overcome in interesting ways that are discovered simply by playing the game a lot. E.g. For some enemy types not all attacks need to be avoided by going left or right, you can slide at the right moment or dash up into the air to get more height if your legs are about to be lazered off.They also added a block button. This'll be the first time I've said this, but NO BLOCK BUTTON PLEEEEEASE! I know in a melee game a block button feels like a must, but the way blocking/parrying worked in GR1 feels SOOO MUCH BETTER. Its a click, cannot be held. Its way more risky and scarier, therefore IT FEELS BETTER. GR2 blocking is like, "oh, Im being shot at, hold button until stamina depletes....... ooooooo..."GR1 blocking is like, "oh god, here it comes... aaaaaand NOW! BAM!" Way WAAAAAAAY more satisfying. Playing GR2 I literally never used the block button, disgusting lol I only parried which I'm happy you can still do, but get rid of the hold blocking I beg you.One last note on enemies... I swear they made all the enemies easier or slower. Very sad. I feel like the leaping enemy takes an extra second now in the air. THATS A LOT for a game like this. Totally messes up my timing because I've gotten so used to that enemy that I dont slow time, I wait for him to leap at me then I step to the side and slice him in the air. Doing that in GR2 now I can feel the extra time it takes for him to get to me.Devs, I love Ghostrunner, GR1 became one of my all time favorites, but please do not hold back on your players. Do not make the game easier, we like how difficult GR1 was. Not everyone liked how tough GR1 was and that is a good thing!!! Its good that you have a community of dedicated players who want the thrill that comes with an intense game like this. What you DON'T want, and is what you're currently going for, is an easy experience that many casual players will play, but DROP so fast you won't believe. True fans of an amazing game stay with it FOR LIFE if they can help it. Final note, stop offering me skills and abilities that make me invincible at any moment in the game. Stoooooooop. If I get hit by an enemy THEN I'M HIT and I am okay with this. I will adapt, do not make me "invincible while successfully blocking", "invincible when dashing in the air..." AHHHHH this was probably one of the biggest things I hated to see. Not only do you make the overall gameplay experience easier, but you give the player unlocks/skills that make the game EVEN EASIER. Don't do this next time please. Look back at what your fan base loved about the first and stick to that if you want GR3 to be the game. No unnecessary cheap Fallout dialog interaction with characters, no HQ, less annoying characters in your ear, no open world sections, no dumbing down the experience. In GR1 not everyone is going to "feel" like a badass Ghostrunner because it's difficult and they give up... But those who stick with it TRULY FEEL like this deadly machine because they knew a section was legitimately hard and overcame the situation. The final kill is always so sweet... I get chills.In GR2... everyone is a badass cyborg ninja... when everyone is a badass cyborg ninja then no one is.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is a solid game in many ways, but unfortunately, it fails to live up to its predecessor’s reputation for various reasons. The most important reason is the open world-ish maps that come with the second part of the game. It plays like the original Ghostrunner up until the level called “Licking the Wounds”, then we get a solid, adrenaline-pumping bike level that has been carefully designed around the bike, and then it takes a huge fall by introducing open world-ish levels that force you to use the bike a bit too much to get around. I can understand that they wanted to make use of the new gameplay mechanic they added, but this is not how it should’ve been handled. The huge maps are way too buggy to be enjoyed and appreciated properly; furthermore, they basically don’t work with the Ghostrunner’s gameplay style due to the fact that they completely eliminate the fast-paced gameplay and turn it into a slow, sluggish mess. Add shader completion issues that eventually lead to low performance into the mix, and we got ourselves a mess of a game. The only redeeming quality of those levels is the bike’s handling. It’s quite easy to learn and ride the thing without having to deal with the adaptation process. But wait, it’s not over. Almost after every single level, you get to this hub area where you can interact with other characters that have basically nothing useful to say. I felt like the only purpose of this addition was to completely destroy the pace of the game. If that’s the case, they succeeded. Another thing that bothered me was the constant introduction of new mechanics very late into the game and not making use of the formerly introduced mechanics properly. After the bike levels, we get huge levels that are poorly designed around the new wingsuit mechanic. Just like the bike levels, they are extremely buggy and hard to navigate most of the time; furthermore, it’s quite easy to get lost in those levels if you’re going after the collectibles. Speaking of collectibles, apart from swords, audio logs, and artifacts, we have memory shards to collect to expand the memory of GR-74 so that he can use more skills. The old, unique skill tab is gone, instead, you place them in their designated areas. They also have unique combos that give significant boosts to that specific skill, at least that’s something. There are also Ultimate skills that you can use that are very useful to deal with lots of enemies. However, Blink is part of the Ultimate skills in Ghostrunner 2 and as you can easily guess, it’s not that useful. Overlord is also an Ultimate skill, and I can say that it kind of deserves to be there with the enemy variety in this game, but considering the huge cooldown time, it’s still not worth it, unlike the rest of them. Tempest is a regular one, but it doesn’t kill enemies unless you place that specific skill that causes it to kill enemies on your skill tree. Another useful skill that I used a lot is the Shuriken one. It’s the first one you get and boy, oh boy… isn’t it extremely useful. If there’s one thing I love about Ghostrunner 2, it’s Shuriken. Here's the questionable part of the game: Its story. The first installment gave off the impression that it was going to be a one-shot game. The story basically ended with the first one, but I liked what they have come up with, nonetheless. There are some rogue GRs that formed a cult and trying to create a new race called Scions and make Dharma their new home by eliminating or enslaving the human race in the process. The main antagonist, Mitra starts out as a very interesting character who also happens to be the very first Ghostrunner, but goes into full edgy teenager mode in the end. Rahu is another interesting character that I have a feeling that will have a huge role in the upcoming game and the rest? Not that interesting or worth mentioning in my opinion. Allies are also not interesting since they are all cliché characters with cringe-worthy dialogues. The only slightly interesting ally was Adrian Bakunin. Yes, he’s alive after the incident in Project_Hel. That guy has the biggest plot armor I’ve ever seen in any game. GR-74 or Jack is still the same as we know with a lot more emotion this time around. However, the boss fights are reduced to being regular bosses that you hit until their HP depletes except for Naga which is the only boss that has unique gimmicks. They also added blocking which is an unnecessary addition since deflecting was already better for a game like Ghostrunner. Thankfully, the soundtrack is still a banger. However, they are a lot more atmospheric compared to the first one. Before I forget, Roguerunner.exe and Hardcore Mode are great gameplay modes, but Hardcore Mode makes you think outside the box a bit too much, especially in the last two levels.You may ask why I recommend this game if I mention lots of negative things about it and the reason is quite simple: It’s still a fun game despite its flaws. This is also neither a positive nor a negative review. It’s not what I expected, but it’s still a solid game. I expect Ghostrunner 3 to be closer to the first game with a lot better optimization, though. Trying to blend in RPG and open world elements where they don't belong just doesn’t work. An underwhelming and unoptimized sequel to the original Ghostrunner that fails to live up to its predecessor's reputation most of the time. The bike is a great addition, but the open world and RPG elements are not. It takes one step forward, but ten steps back. It’s still a solid game, nonetheless. Be sure to use DX11 if you want to have a smoother experience since DX12 is literally unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely don't understand how people can leave this game a negative review. I'm by no means saying its perfect. There are bugs, sometimes you die in a frustrating way that wasn't your fault, and sometimes if you try hard enough you can get yourself out of bounds. Also, the story line and characters are kind of basic and not all that exciting. At the same time, this doesn't distract from how immensely fun and fast paced Ghostrunner 2 is. The movement is some of the best of any game I've played and the combat compliments this so well. It's quick, easy to learn and so satisfying. The soundtrack is also incredible - there were times I felt genuine goosebumps as the music swelled. The culmination of that is Dharma feels immersive and that dystopian feeling is captured perfectly. Additionally, I didn't spend much time if any looking for collectables or exploring and the story still took me 10 hours to finish. Considering how fast paced the game is, the fact you don't even see half the assets in the game for more than half a second, and the fact this isn't a triple A title, I think that's a really great runtime. I think it's also well paced and doesn't outstay its welcome. Yeah the whole open world desert level wasn't perfect but that's the only time they got the pacing wrong, the rest of the game is action packed non-stop and never leaves you feeling bored. I genuinely couldn't put the game down until I finished it.Overall, I highly recommend it to anyone, and I'd say don't listen too much to the highly harsh reviews. This isn't to say those reviews are wrong, but they shouldn't persuade you not to buy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is definitely a well deserved sequel. You can tell the development team put a lot of care into designing the feature's. There isn't a big gap between the tools and abilities that you learned from the first game put into this game. Most of the abilities you learned from the first game are unlocked in the first level. This help paved the way to have "Jack" learn more abilities throughout the game. If you are looking for a story driven, SUPER HOT, runner type game this would be a definite buy. It is even a plus that the game isn't priced at 59.99 or even 69.99 as most games are nowadays. There are some negative's that do need to be talked about but they may be ironed out over the games lifetime. At the moment of me writing this review, I have 100%'ed the story and achievements. There were some things that I experienced over the course of the game that weren't joyful. When you unlock the motorcycle parts of the game, I would occasionally hit random bumps on the road where there was nothing at instantly explode. Other times my motorcycle would spawn in weird positions if it had to be respawned. On the later levels, I experienced a lot of frame rate drops to the point that it made the game unplayable unless I somehow made it passed a certain area or restarted the game. My setup currently is running a 4080 so frame rates below 10 aren't expected. Especially that the next feature, RTX, seems to be missing from the game. It seems that Ray Tracing was removed from the release of the game because it was buggy and would cause people to crash. Finally, the Wing suit was a cool addition to the final stages of the game but it seems like the map wasn't properly finished or created for those levels. I was able to go around many corners accidently skipping the main path and skipping ahead in the story in certain areas. Overall, this game is definitely a must buy. The Indie developers have done it extremely well and are always taking feedback from their community to make it better. Ghostrunner 2 also is much easier compared to the first game if anyone stayed away from the games because it was too difficult. The base game takes a little longer than the base game of Ghostrunner 1 + its DLC. I am really looking forward to see what the future holds for Ghostunner 2 and possibly a Ghostunner 3 coming down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few times you'll see a sequel do pretty much everything better than the original. Ghostrunner is a great game. Ghostrunner 2 is even better. I'll keep it simple: if you liked the first game, you'll love this. The mechanics are there and improved, the level design is terrific (best I've seen since Titanfall 2's campaign), the various game mechanics layer on top of one another beautifully and, by the end, it's a masterpiece. The story is good too if a bit formulaic. I enjoyed the characters, there interactions were good. A little cliche but you care about the characters enough to still be invested. The ONLY issue I had with the story was there were two specific themes they explored but didn't finish. It felt about 75% of the way there and then the story ends which makes it... a little unsatisfying. But don't let that deter you from buying the game. I'd still give it a 9/10. If the story was just a LITTLE more developed, it would have been a slam dunk 10. You'll still enjoy every minute you play this game. No doubt about it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything I wanted and hoped for.  The upgrade tree is better than the last game, but I would still like it to be so that you didn't have to pick and choose only *some* upgrades. I like the memory chip mechanic, as it is way to make you work for the progress, rather than just grinding XP.   The gameplay is somehow even better than the last game without it changing drastically. I especially like the block mechanic. Rather than timing a slash to block a single shot, you can block a whole bunch, which costs stamina.    The bike is an amazing way of travelling quickly in larger levels without changing the game's fast pace, and I love how they still involve some parkour aspects too.There is so much more I'd love to say about this game, but that belongs in an essay, not a little review forum.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: GR2 is a solid sequel to GR.It boasts a tight level design, just as its predecessor did, however there're two levels that are quite open and non-linear in the way you tackle the objectives.So if you prefer the tight and curated level design of the first and dislike non-linearity, this may dampen your experience.If you don't care, it'll be a nice change of pace (I like the bike sections).There are some micro stutters, however I wasn't plagued all to much by them (a notable exception is the Phase 3 final node battle, which stutters and lowers FPS when certain conditions are met).The music is good, but I personally prefer GR's music over GR2's.The story basically continues from the first game and is mainly about rebuilding life after tyrants have been disposed off; however a, or several, new villain(s) rear their head(s) with a past with those tyrants and a thirst for vengeance to boot.There are a couple nice twists, too.All in all, if you liked GR, you'll probably like GR2. Therefor I can recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first ghostrunner game, I still go back and play it all the time, it is one of my favorite games. I REALLY wanted to love this second game but I can't say I've had a great time with it. My first issue is the bike. I think it could have been a good idea but I CAN'T STAND riding it. First, most of my deaths on levels are from crashing the bike and not being able to control it cause it's goes at such high speeds and is difficult to turn without slamming into a wall, making it a pain in the ass to use. Second, there have been times when I have gone off the road and therefore getting my bike stuck and I am then unable to use it. I've tried walking without the bike but ofc there are areas with me needing a bike to get to, therefore having my only option being restarting the level. Maybe there is a way to get my bike back but idk. Also for whatever reason this game doesn't feel as smooth as the first in game imo. One thing I did like that they added was the shrunkens, I do really enjoy using those. If your gonna get this game get it on sale, I think it isn't horrible but it feels definitely worse than the first game. Maybe I will change my review as I play more of the game, but I've gotten through 10 levels and this is what I have thought of the game so far and I don't really know if I have the patience to keep going.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the most enjoyable games I've ever played...and I haven't played much of it yet, because I know it's not an intensely long game, but it's a speedrunner's wet dream, and I love the challenge. It's so fast paced, so when you do complete a level, you'll feel accomplished. Wallriding, sliding, grappling, hacking and slashing, and deflecting projectiles with your giant katana, feeling like an absolute badass by vanquishing everyone who has 1hp...but you also have 1hp. Get hit once, and you die. But...yeah....I feel like I'm going to actually submit results to official speedrun site for this game. Just, once I get better at it. I read reviews of people who died like 255 times during a single level when they first started out. It's not that difficult, especially if you've played the absolute crap out of any fps that has wall riding capabilities, or you played surf in counter-strike, or bhop maps in cs.This is just more  short bursts. I mean, it's very fast paced, so it will just drain your epinephrine from your body until you have to stop. At my age, that happens quickly. But...the game just makes you feel like a god when your movement is perfect. Just...so satisfying. Worth buying and keeping in your library for when you need to vent out some frustration. I mean, you could potentially get frustrated playing the levels, which I did once (one guy killed me with some sort of phaser rifle and then I got the tutorial tip of "press shift whilst in mid air to dodge"), so I got mad that it told me I could dodge after I died. Still though....really good fun. If you liked the latest versions of Doom, you'll like this.

Definitely a worthy sequel to GR1. However, there are some things you need to be aware of before purchasing:1. It's somewhat short. It took me 9 hours to complete. Now this is a bit longer than the first game (about 7 hours) but i was hoping for more. Especially for $40.2. It starts out slow. Lots of boring NPC dialogue that could be removed entirely without really taking much away from the experience. However about halfway through the story you start having a lot of fun with new mechanics like the motorcycle, and wing suit. (personally I feel like they should have given you the wing suit earlier because I was having an absolute blast with it and wish I got to use it more.)3. It has a lot more puzzles than the first game. Now this may just be my personal opinion, but if you're gonna drop me into a world where I'm a cyber ninja with a sword, all I'm gonna want to do is run around doing parkour and killing things, not solving puzzles. Now I will say the puzzles are never very difficult (There wasn't a single one I got stumped on), but they just feel like a tedious task i need to complete before I get to go back to being a badass samurai robot.4. The God-awful NPCs. The little hub area you go back to between missions is definitely my biggest complaint about this game. I understand what they were going for, trying to add more story to the sequel, but the dialogue gets really boring really quick. It also just feels very disconnected from the rest of the world since you just kinda spawn away from it at the start of each mission, and spawn back there at the end. Not to mention the models for the characters feel very lifeless and almost out of place graphics wise compared to the rest of the world, when I'm there, it almost feels like I'm playing a fan game.Despite all this, I really can't say that I don't recommend this game, because if someone would ask me if they should get it, I would most certainly say yes. The sheer fun you have playing this game definitely outweighs the flaws. The motorcycle, the wing suit, leaving the tower and traversing the world outside of Dharma tower, not to mention the bad ass chase from the giant robot worm, all great stuff. High hopes for a potential GR3!

_childDocuments_.review: - Story is worse than in GR1. The antagonists are flat and unimpactful. It feels uninspired. - You'd expect the combat to be determinstic but it honestly isn't. The optimal way to go about ecounters is very linear but even then it feels random all the time. Often the same movement gets you killed while other times it gets you further (Even when respawning at checkpoints). The lack of consistency keeps be from even trying to no-hit a level. I remember GR1 to be better in that regard also.- The open levels are a step backwards. When I play a ninja I want to go, go, go and slice enemies up as I go and move further through the tower.- One of the powers somehow bugged out and the shuriken-blink stopped working for me with no way to fix it.- The upgrade system is uninspired compared to GR1. - The friendly characters are a waste of space. You wont care much about them or for the dialogue. It suffers a bit from millennial writing.- Movement feels worse than in GR1. It feels more janky and it takes you out of the experience.- While the bike was a fun idea, it's clunky and oftentimes horrible to control.- Half of the abilities are a waste of space and because nobody would use them.I was excited when I heard about GR2 but ultimately it was a big letdown

_childDocuments_.review: i really, really, really love the ghostrunner franchiseand that's exactly why i'm having such a tough time recommending this gamedon't get me wrong, i had a blast playing this game- there was a somewhat interesting story, slightly worse than that of GR1, but enjoyable nonetheless- i particularly enjoyed being able to learn more about the lore of the Ghostrunner worldthe game doesn't fail at providing difficult challenges that go beyond simply completing the levels- the motorcycles, although feeling a bit janky at times, make a great adition to this game of fast and violent traversal/slaughter- the permanent addition of shurikens (among other things) to your skillset was a great ideaif you liked GR1, you will probably enjoy this game as well!HOWEVER- as already mentioned, the motorcycle levels can feel quite janky at times and in addition to that, some of them don't even really feel like ghostrunner levels, and moreso like levels out of an unrelated racing game- a lot of the enemies already move around a lot from the start, which chips away a little at providing a flowstate sometimes- the upgrade system is far worse and far more bland and uninteresting than the upgrade system of GR1, especially because some upgrades are locked behind going the extra mile. if you want the full roster of all upgrades, simply progressing through the game is not enough. in most other games this would not be an issue, but in this instance it takes away some of your versatility which might be required if you're stuck in a section- there are some attempts here and there at open world sections which are simply put terrible- the boss fights measure in no way, shape or form up to the bossfights of GR1all in all, i was very torn right after i completed this gameafter a few days of sitting with the experience i had:if you liked GR1 and want more, then buy this game, you will most likely enjoy itthis is definitely a step-down from the first game, but only because the first game set the bar so incredibly highi'm excited to see what the developers do next

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start with this review by saying that I loved the game's story and new systems. This was a fun sequel, and I loved most of it. The level design was great. The motorcycle missions were a wonderful addition. It reminded me of the swoop bike racing that was in KOTOR. This game reminds me of KOTOR a lot and gave me a sense of nostalgia when I played it. I do think this game is worth the purchase if you enjoyed the first game.My one and only problem with this game is the boss fights. With the exception of the second boss fight, which is mainly parkour, the boss fights weren't fun. The bosses are damage sponges. The idea of this game is everything dies in one hit, even you. I understand bosses needing more health. Hel in the last game had three chunks of health, and when you hit her it felt satisfying. When fighting the first boss, you have to keep swinging into him. It feels like I'm hitting him with a foam nerf sword. It would've been better that every time you parry or stun him that your hit takes a chunk out. Instead of hitting multiple times. The third and forth bosses have the same problem. All in all, this game is really fun, minus the bosses. Despite my one complaint, I do think this game is worth the purchase. Thank you for reading, and have a nice day.Edit: I've 100% completed the game. My opinion still stands. Fun game. Bad boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really feels like a husk of itself. They pushed an uninteresting story and new mechanics that you use once and never again. I beat the game in 7 hours but realistically this could've been completed in probably 5 or less. The level designs were rough and they focused on padding out a lot of it with the shoddy motorcycle gameplay. As a fan of the first game and the idea of a fast paced first-person action game this game really struggles to satisfy what the first game did right. The HEL DLC in the original was rough because of how it altered the gameplay and became clunky and it feels like they doubled down on that feeling for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If sequels should be bigger and better, than Ghostrunner 2 shows, how to do it. It expands over the first title, adding new mechanics (to the very last level) and improving already existing ones. There are levels which feels like more of GR1, but there are also levels consisting of completely new elements, like bike and semi-open world (and few others which I do not want to spoil). And that semi-open world feels fresh and it's not overused. Like in GR1 feeling of movement is amazing, it's fast paced game and sometimes it's almost overwhelming. But it's a good thing, as it fits overall idea. For me, there's only two downsides: 1. occasionally performance can drop, usually in the same places (and this title performance should be a priority). It's nothing game breaking, it's not a level of other titles from this year, but it can be annoying. 2. Levels are too long, during my first playthrough, for some missions I needed 30-40 minutes to complete, which I think it's far too long. Other than that, it's an amazing game and if you enjoy the first Ghostrunner, you shouldn't hesitate, Ghostrunner 2 is worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Literally unplayable. When I say unplayable, I don't mean I ran into performance issues and glitches, I mean the game doesn't work. You'll get past the logos and then stare at your reflection on a black screen until you decide to task manager yourself to reality.Before you have any doubts about my issues maybe being due to a bad system, let me state that I'm running a 12th gen i7 and an RTX 3080, so I'm not short on hardware power. I have 6 hours in this game because I managed to open it 2 or 3 times by closing background processes such as wallpaper engine and trying several times each attempt, but each time I thought about playing the game I would hesitate because I knew I would have so many problems just trying to open it. I decided to try to give it one last go today and make a push to finish the game, and I could not open it for the life of me. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start this review by asking 2 very important questions:Did Ghostrunner 2 really need to exist? Did it add anything worthwhile to the franchise to justify its existence? Unfortunately, the answer is "No" to both those questions..I'll be honest with you, by the time i started playing GR2 i didn't remember the first game all that well, except that i loved the graphics and aesthetics of it, and although it was hard, it was still fun to experience. I don't ever remember disliking it and wanting it to just end halfway through, something i can't say about this sequel sadly..I don't really want this to balloon into something too big so i'll try to list the things i disliked briefly:- The graphics seem worse somehow, the NPCs look so dated, some of the levels outside the tower don't look that good either (the city still looks good though).- The cutscenes (if you can even call them that) aren't great with 2 exceptions, the GR1 recap & the ending cutscene (i honestly don't remember if there was another animated one at the beginning, so maybe 3?), i would've liked to see a lot more cutscenes of that style even if the story isn't the main focus of this game.- Traversal & parkouring is much worse in this game compared to the first one, it's much jankier, and with some very few but super annoying parts with major difficulty spikes sprinkled between long stretches of easy/meh sections, so even though those super difficult parts are rare, they more than stand out compared to the rest of the game (i feel like more than 80% of my deaths were due to the janky traversal instead of the 1 hit kill enemies which doesn't sound right).- The bike sections add nothing to the game, and don't even feel good to drive, feels more like something that was quickly tacked in to try to justify making a sequel.- The hub is so boring and adds nothing of value to the game, i'm someone who tries to exhaust all dialogue options with all NPCs i encounter in games to try to experience as much of the story & lore as i can, but gosh darn if they didn't bore me out of my mind in this game, they look so bad, there are no decent animations or cutscenes for them to make them remotely interesting, the dialogue itself is super meh and the hub overall grinds the flow to a halt, now that i finished it i wish i just skipped 90% of NPCs dialogue and just went straight back to the action ASAP.- Way buggier than the first game, i got stuck in the floor multiple times, sometimes enemies refuse to spawn so you're stuck unless you restart (thankfully you only have to restart to your last checkpoint instead of restarting the whole level), the game also completely froze for me at least once when i tried to switch skins late in the game, and more annoyingly it refused to save my remapped keys & kept reverting back to default each time i closed it..also the audio for one of the ultimate abilities (Flux) kept randomly glitching & playing non stop driving me insane unless i restarted my checkpoint (btw, restarts count as deaths in the game), i probably encountered even more little bugs & glitches but this is all i can remember off the top of my head.I just want to point out that even though it may seem like i hate this game i really don't, i did enjoy some parts of it, the story was meh but it did pick up a bit by the end, the city still looked beautiful & was cool to experience (i'm a sucker for cyberpunk futuristic aesthetics), and the game still knows how to make you feel like a badass when it wants to.But that doesn't change the fact that it pales in comparison to the first GR in almost every single aspect & even goes as far as making many parts worse instead of building on them & improving them, making you question why did they even bother making it in the first place, and for that i really can't recommend it to anyone except on a deep deep sale.Such a shame..

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner (1) sweat here, 3 hours into GR2. At first the gameplay felt a little off, like I was missing a limb. SDSJ's don't seem to work so well anymore, or maybe the timing has changed and I'm slow to adjust. Otherwise, the movement is just as fun, even better in some aspects. I like the new upgrade system (and the new upgrades) more than the last game and the BOSSES... the devs have massively outdone themselves. GR1's bosses were extremely mediocre but the second GR2 boss is already one of my favourites of all time (not difficult from a gameplay perspective but incredibly visually appealing)The characters have certainly improved over GR1, now with physical presences in between levels rather than being disembodied voices. The dialogue in the Hub is a bit awkward with pauses between sets of lines, but this will likely be polished up in the future and it's still engaging for now. The dialogue in mission is pretty funny, I'm enjoying it so far.I really like the setting and background of Ghostrunner. It's rare for me to be absorbed into lore but GR2's story so far is quite interesting.Also, the soundtrack slaps on GR2. The tracks in the previous game weren't very memorable, but they were good and I did keep them on over playing my own music. However, I can see myself listening to this OST outside of the game.Overall and thus far, GR2 improves on its' predecessor (which was already a favourite of mine) in every single way. I waited for a sale to buy it because I'm broke but if you can afford it, support the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the only game I have preordered in my life, and I'm glad I did, because it is amazing. Ghostrunner 2 improves on just about every issue that the first game suffered from. The combat flows extremely well and the new ultimate abilities are amazing. New sword inspect animations are incredible, and the boss system is much better.In the previous game, boss fights were just about dodging or parrying the attacks and then slashing them when they're vulnerable. GR2 doesn't do that, and instead opts for a proper damage system, constantly striking your opponent while dodging their attacks. The levels flow very well, and the perfect parry takedowns are a little janky but still pretty cool. There's also a sort of home base that you can explore and interact with in between missions, talking to characters in the game, upgrading your skills, ect.There's a bunch of new skills to experiment with and have fun with. The game looks graphically amazing as well. The cutscenes feel much better compared to GR1, although the facial expressions of some characters in game feel kind of lifeless and they just stare into your soul while talking to you, but other than that they're great.And there's also the bike levels and the levels are kind of more open rather than directed. I won't spoil anything but I will say that the bike is a blast to use and is probably the most fun I've had in a game for a long time.Yes, the game is difficult, just like the first one. There is no denying that. One hit and you restart at the last checkpoint. (there's alot of those thankfully) But if you can get the flow and movement down and learn to use your abilities in unison, Ghostrunner 2 is so much fun, and considering that most AAA games are $80+ these days, this game is definitely worth the price

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2: Fast, Fun, Frustrating at Times ⚡️Just sliced my way through Ghostrunner 2, and here's the rundown:Super Speedy Ninja Action: You're a cyber ninja who dies in one hit, just like the first game. Parkour, wall run, slash enemies in half – it's all about lightning-fast reflexes and stylish moves.New Tricks Up Your Sleeve: Motorcycle sections! More gadgets and abilities to play with! The core gameplay is familiar but feels even more exciting this time around.Beautiful Neon World: The world is gorgeous, all neon lights and dark alleys. It's a cool backdrop for all the slicing and dicing.Died a Lot (But Kept Coming Back!): This game is HARD. You will die. A lot. But the restarts are super fast, so you can just jump right back in and try again. (Unless you get super frustrated!)Open World? Not Quite: While there's more exploration than the first game, it's not a wide-open world. Still lots of cool levels to conquer though.Overall:Ghostrunner 2 is a blast for fans of the first game and anyone who loves a fast-paced challenge. Just be prepared to die a bunch (and maybe rage quit a few times). But if you can master the flow of combat, it's a super rewarding experience.   (Thumbs up, thumbs down to represent the love/hate relationship some might have with the difficulty)

_childDocuments_.review: This is one I'd really like steam to have a maybe option for. Ghostrunner 2 is very good but lacks is certain areas I can see being gamebreaking for some. The motorcycle is very buggy, and you wont encounter it until halfway through the game. The motorcycle can slam into objects and get stuck forcing a restart. The game in general can be lacking of polish at times. I dashed out of the environment 3 or 4 times to my death in the void because of collision detection errors. I noticed 3 or 4 instances of being able to see straight through the ground or walls into the void. For a game that's very hotline miami esc, it can be irritating to have to redo sections because of collision errors with the bike/player. Ghostrunner 2 continues the series' difficulty in a good way. I would say it was slightly easier than the first, but not a noticeable step down. The level design has taken a step down in quality. I mean there is a point where you are breaking colored crystals in line with what the game says to do for basically no reason. It's not hard, it's not fun, and it doesnt break up the gameplay cause it's inherently set to a 25 second timeframe. There are no moments of me admiring the levels for how interconnected and well made they are. Part of this comes down to the increased number of collectible items in missions and general gameplay's less involved nature. There is less than 5 new enemies. There's the wheel zombie thing that involves dashing to avoid and then you kill it. There is the sandworm that spits acid. The zombies are kind of new visually, but are mechanically just reskins of previous enemies. They replaced the warden with the shinobi. That's it. As far as cut enemies... They removed the wreck. They removed the turrets. They removed the sniper. They removed the splitter. So for every enemy they added, they removed one from the original that provided a unique gameplay challenge. This really is so hard to recommend with all of these elements, but I still do. The bosses and gameplay are fantastic. The music is excellent. The story was very mid, as expected. But the good parts of this game are so worth experiencing. So go into this game with hesitance, and just get ghostrunner 1 is you're curious about the series. And, I believe Ghostrunner 1 is longer as well.TL;DR1 is better, and this one lacks new enemies and the amazing level design we saw from the first game. If you dont have 1, get it instead. If you already have 1 and liked it. This one's good, with more problems than the original. But fun nonetheless.

Absolutely insane.Worked fine with my XBox controller in ultra-wide resolution (21:9). Compiling the shaders took a few seconds. I use the beating soundtrack now while I run in the morning.Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, this is pure adrenaline.Crazy-fast, bloody hack'n'slash orgy in a cyberpunk city.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. I see lots of people complaining about the open world bike section but I honestly thought it was pretty fun. I do like racing games though so that might affect my viewpoint on it. The inclusion of the bike in general was sweet. I do wish you had more time to spend with the final upgrade and that it persisted into the Hardcore mode, but I can understand that it might break some things. Still, it would have been a fun inclusion.The story is pretty good, characters are decent, gameplay is awesome as ever. It is unfortunate that it stutters so much due to what I can only assume is lingering shader compilation and traversal stutters, even though the game compiles them whenever you launch it. There were a few times it did get me killed. Luckily the game is fast enough that it doesn't matter a whole lot. Just reset after death to a few seconds ago and no more stuttering for that part.If you liked the first game, you'll definitely enjoy this one. I thought it was about on-par with the original and I enjoyed it quite a bit. I can imagine that some people may like it more or less, but that's typically how sequels go anyway.There is one issue with the keybinding... I really wish I could scroll through the Shuriken, Ghost, and Tempest abilities with the mouse wheel instead of clicking 1/2/3. It would certainly make things easier in combat and in platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: **Ghostrunner 2** is the sequel to the original **Ghostrunner**, building on the fast-paced, first-person action and platforming mechanics that made the first game popular. Released in 2023, it expands the story and gameplay elements in a richly detailed cyberpunk world.Key features include:- **Enhanced Gameplay Mechanics**: Building on the original's fluid movement, **Ghostrunner 2** introduces new abilities and combat options, allowing for even more dynamic gameplay.- **Expanded World**: The game features larger and more complex levels, offering players a chance to explore new environments and face diverse challenges.- **Upgraded Graphics**: With improved visuals, the game showcases a more vibrant and immersive cyberpunk aesthetic.- **Narrative Continuation**: The story continues to delve into the lore of the Ghostrunner universe, focusing on themes of freedom and rebellion against oppressive forces.- **New Enemies and Boss Fights**: Players encounter a variety of new foes, each requiring different strategies to defeat.The game maintains the intense, one-hit-kill combat style that fans loved while introducing fresh elements to keep the experience engaging. If you enjoyed the first game or are a fan of action-platformers, **Ghostrunner 2** is definitely worth checking out! Are you interested in the story, the gameplay, or both?

_childDocuments_.review: Some other reviewers go as far as not recommending the game for a reason that the game focuses more on the story than fighting arenas and other game mechanics. While this might be the case I do not feel it should result in not recommending the game as the game is amazing, just bit different than the original. It is very apparent that the devs want more open less linear experience and I feel like they nailed the balance between limited resources for an indie game and big plans and ideas. It is still very linear experience (~which is not a bad thing~), but inclusion of HQ and more open big locations with multiple tasks that can be done in any order makes it feel like a more living actual world. This is something that I missed in the original game, where the game aesthetically was amazing and as someone who loves cyberpunk I missed not being able to interact with the world more. This certainly helps. When I first entered HQ I sat in the office for few minutes just looking out of the windows at the world around.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:Ghostrunner 2 takes everything we loved about the first game and dials it up to eleven. The way you move, the way you fight – it's all a symphony of precision and speed that'll have your heart racing. They've thrown in some fresh abilities and challenges that keep you guessing, making every encounter a white-knuckle thrill ride.Graphics:I can't even begin to describe how jaw-droppingly gorgeous this game is. The cityscapes, all lit up in neon, the futuristic backdrops – it's like stepping into a cyberpunk dream. And the characters, they're so lifelike, it's almost eerie. The art direction here is nothing short of a masterpiece, setting a whole new bar for eye candy in the gaming world.Replayability:Ghostrunner 2 is like that gift that keeps on giving. With different paths, hidden spots, and a boatload of challenges, every playthrough feels like a fresh adventure. It's all about pushing your limits, mastering those moves, and finding new ways to tackle each level. Whether you're chasing speed records or perfecting your combat, this game keeps you coming back for more.Story and Worldbuilding:While Ghostrunner 2 shines brightest in gameplay, the story isn't just an afterthought. The cyberpunk world they've built is a character in itself. The plot unfolds with twists and turns that keep you hooked, and the characters... they're mysterious and layered, adding a whole new dimension to the experience.Soundtrack:The music, oh boy, it's like they plucked it from the future. The beats and synths, they sync up with the action in a way that'll give you chills. It's like they hand-picked each track to amplify the intensity. The sound design is on point, and it's a crucial part of what makes this game so darn immersive.In Conclusion:Ghostrunner 2 isn't just a sequel; it's a leap forward. The gameplay is tighter, the graphics are jaw-dropping, and the replay value is off the charts. Hats off to the devs for crafting something truly special. If you're into high-octane action and diving headfirst into cyberpunk worlds, this game is an absolute must-play. It's a wild ride from start to finish, setting a whole new standard for the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is a great action game but it has very little in common with the first game. It's more open, lacks structure, doesn't care about enemy placement or patterns and most of all prioritizes accessibility above improvement. If that's what you wanted, great, but it was already available in the first game through assist mode. Now it's forced on everyone with projectiles being slower, enemies being less accurate and enemy attacks being smaller and easier to dodge. It takes away from what made the first game fantastic.I have replayed all levels of the first Ghostrunner multiple times on both regular and hardcore to improve my time, have fewer deaths or find all collectibles. While I enjoyed my playthrough of Ghostrunner 2 I find very little reason to go back to any specific level. Partly because there is no feeling of identifying patterns and improving your run, partly because of the size of the levels. While most levels in the first game were 15-20 minutes, many here are much longer with some reaching an hour to play through. It feels bloated. As does the pointless mission hub world and the open bike levels that no one asked for.Lastly I have to question what One More Level did on a technical level. The game looks significantly worse than the first game at a much higher hardware cost. A clean, almost cartoony design replaces the grimy neon cyberpunk from the first game  and many levels suffer from consistent frame drops in the exact same area regardless of settings or resolution. Going back to the first Ghostrunner after playing Ghostrunner 2 feels like going to the future on a technical level.With that said, I still recommend Ghostrunner 2. The story is interesting, the movement is more smooth overall. The abilities bring some variation to the fighting and the Cybervoid levels are actually fun this time around. If I didn't expect a game like the first Ghostrunner I would probably find this an amazing action game and one of the better ones this year, it's just very different from what I loved about the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first ghostrunner the combat is fast, flashy and very cool. adding a motorcycle to the formula naturally makes it even cooler and thats definitely the best aspect of this game. However, they decided to put a much bigger emphasis on the story and dialogue in comparison to the first game which could be cool in concept except the story is very basic and the dialogue is just straight up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. everyone talks like an extremely corny character in a marvel movie and they just dont shut up, everytime you get dropped into a new enviroment/ level the great atmosphere is immediatley ruined by someone calling you to tell you about a backstory you couldnt give 2 ♥♥♥♥♥ about. After a while it just seemed like the developers were scared to go 2 minutes without talking so they just let the characters ask each other questions that dont expand the world or lore of the game at all. This is a game where you play as a badass robot samurai that goes around a post-apocalyptic cyberpunk world slicing peoples ♥♥♥♥♥ off with a katana, thats already awesome enough, you dont need a crazy story if even a story at all. All they had to do was make him say some cool one liners every now and then and let the gameplay do the talking for the rest of it. Besides the story there's also a couple things that make the game just not as smooth as you want it to be, like weird hitboxes and mechanics that don't fully work sometimes. The game also introduces a lot of new mechanics in every level but ends up utilizing them in that level only, making them feel kind of dissapointing, especially when its a really fun mechanic that you wanted to see more of in other levels.  I really wanted to like this game but these flaws make it just kind of underwhelming, especially since i really loved the first ghostrunner game. The gameplay is still very fun but i feel like it could have been expanded on way more from the original. Making this game kind of underwhelming in my opinion

_childDocuments_.review: I have to call this "recommended" because I do think it is a decent game and I did enjoy it (hence why I not only finished the campaign but also spent the time to get all the achievements), but that recommendation comes with a lot of caveats. Performance - Playing through the campaign was mostly fine other than a couple of brief single-digit-fps moments out of nowhere. Playing the rogue-lite mini-game was infuriating with so many slideshow moments or just completely freezing for a few seconds (all the more noticeable in a mode where lives matter).Bugs - The enemies would jitter around objects, or just get completely stuck in terrain. The grapple-hook was not reliable, and I would often not go anywhere if I so much as stubbed my toe on a pebble. Towards the later part of my playthrough I frequently found myself sliding forward even when not pressing any keys (a hazard when waiting for a platform to materialise). And when replaying levels for achievements I sometimes found enemies would not spawn, blocking progress.A greater focus on story - I would consider this as a negative, because to me it just feels like the wrong kind of game to be standing around having a chat with your allies. Larger but emptier levels - This was very clear in one of the later levels where you have a motorbike. I imagined the motorbike levels to be high-speed chase kind of sequences with lots of obstacles and needing to pull all sorts of stunts to get by. There were a couple of sequences that lived up to that, but far too much time on the bike was simply following roads with minimal obstacles. The game then gave a massive open area with collectables to find, and yet the location was drab and empty, and there was no fun gameplay in driving around looking for them. But even the levels on foot felt like they were lacking something, even just some background decorations to give the locations more life. Too many interruptions to the flow - What I enjoyed most from the first game was that sense of flow as you chain together abilities to pull off amazing stunts. Somehow I didn't get as much of a sense of that here. The path didn't always seem as clear, or platforming sections wouldn't last as long as I'd expect. Then there would be a minor puzzle to find a switch or push a block. Or I'd have multiple objectives in different directions. All of that would have been fine in small amounts, but ultimately I started to miss the more linear focus of the first game. They even put extra challenges in the levels themselves (races, timed kill challenges, that sort of thing) which not only broke the flow of the level you were on, but also seemed out of place because if you wanted to retry them, you had to replay the entire level up to that point. Easier than the first game - Now this could be a positive or a negative depending on my mood. I certainly didn't die anywhere near as often as I did in the first game. The addition of the block in combat really simplified dealing with many enemies. It is something of a relief to not have a 100+ death count on some levels (I may not be very good at these games!), but at the same time I am left feeling there was a lack of challenge to the game by the end, for both combat and platforming actually. There is hardcore mode of course that I didn't try, but given my other issues with the game, I think I'm good, thanks. I know that is a long list of negatives, but to counter that: you are a cybernetic ninja that can wall-run, dash through the air and insta-kill someone with one swipe of your sword. At that most basic level, this game is still immensely satisfying to play. Also I love the music! TL;DR: If you enjoyed Ghostrunner 1 and want more, and don't mind a less-good version of the game, this is worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolutely mess. Janky controls that only sometimes work and a very janky world that sometimes you'll get stuck in, sometimes you won't. Sometimes you'll stick to vertical surfaces you should be able to run on, sometimes you won't. It really does depend on what the game is feeling in that moment. Sometimes you'll deflect a bullet, sometimes you won't. And then there's also the abysmal performance issues. Many many bugs, collision detection issues, random clipping or getting stuck in the world etc. There are also many instances where the fps just randomly drops. The first half of the game was good, great in fact. I was actually thinking halfway through that this game was way better than the first. But the second half is when it just absolutely breaks and the aforementioned issues start to show up. Absolutely do not recommend in its current state. The first game had a lot of these issues but to a lesser extent. Well, rest assured, for this sequel they completely stopped caring about any issues. If you still want to play a Ghostrunner game then I recommend going back to the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a downgrade, how so?Imagine you are watching the entirety of the MCU Phase 1 - End of Infinity War, Phase 1 Iron Man is the comedy guy when paired up with other heroes but his comedy usually leads to a purposeful outcome that further develops someone else, in fact it even lends to his fighting style such as distracting Loki in the 1st Avengers movie. Hulk is Naive and acts like most of us when in highschool "a timid nerd" and is tricked by Loki (I think), And then you get to Thor Ragnarok and now everyone's throwing out one liners and jokes like we are all Iron Man.That whole description is what you might feel when you reach the outside world segment, I like how they used the open environment levels to be more puzzle based for the secrets but that's really all it was good for and how it is introduced is pretty awkward.Every game doesn't need to feel like this but REVillage & 4 I think did it best where you can come back if you really want the x10 pistol ammo but here it becomes a chore to sift through for the secrets since what you'll be doing is driving a kinda janky motorcycle around looking at your GPS and trying not to hit someone's Prius which will insta kill you if you're trying to do a no death run, that is what your 1st or a clean run through will feel like, 2nd run through you just ignore everything and go to A B & C.In terms of extra side content though the challenges were my highlight since it provided a outlet and use for the open environments.Terms of Music blending into the COMBAT, I honestly do not remember any level being my favorite save for level 1.Level 1 has everything you loved about Ghostrunner 1 since you're still inside the Tower, the music tempo is fast and you are immediately introduced to iconic enemies such as Machinegun man, Pistol boy and Baton runt who all still die in 1 hit. But you also realize that pressing attack to parry no longer parries it does a 'free' block that renders the projectile useless and that to parry you now have to hold right click at the right time but it is also a dedicated defense button.Yes you read correctly there is a dedicated defense button it's okay since it blocks bullets and uses your dash stamina but why is the parry button chained to this as well? It ruins the flow of combat in the outside levels where you end up fighting guys with guns more often than not and if your build was focused on moving fast it feels awful. Speaking of I don't even remember the music of the outside, I think it was a quieter slower pace track but if it did ramp up I do not remember.Side note though Bisecting a guy with a High-Frequency sword feels slightly off, I think it has to do with the fact that the gameplay ideology was changed to defensive options (Parry, Block, Shadow & Shield from flow) over speed & offence.Bike levels though they're a fun addition and don't really over stay their welcome but it's missing the FFVIIRE addition of other guys who chase you either by flying with jetpacks or another bike, you don't see that until the end of the game and there just isn't any rush, feels like a Sunday drive most times specially considering you can jump off and grapple back to your bike.Boss fights absolutely horrible only fun one could maybe be Naga the worm but I think Madhu wins it out for me but it involves spamming attack as their health bar depletes.Ahriman (first boss) is boring he has a big sword and wants to do his best Hel & Guts impression by launching sword waves (or Surge if you're Acktually like that) at you as well as AOEs while you cut away at his life.Mitra (final boss) is SH!T he's doing a Throfinn impression and spams this move a lot; throw 3 knifes which pulse and if you touch it you die, it is boring having to grapple 3 knifes that pulse and if he doesn't pulse he's running away and using more sword waves. He also has a cloak move BUT never does a quick slash into a cloak it is ALWAYS GOING TO BE Cloak into 'Surprise' slash you need to parry and I will give him this he has 2 variants for follow ups after the Pulse attack or the Surge. Other than that the way he is killed is kinda creative for someone who hates fighting in the air like it's a DMC type game.Naga is the Worm section in Gears 2 gut his hearts open during your drive-by.Madhu though is THE best boss fight since player urgency and skill can come into play. it's hack away at his SHIELD (takes about 6 hits) while getting repulsed away (yes you can chain and bait this move) then hack away at his health which has a clear telegraphed attack you can parry for big damage which will then push him into a regeneration phase, while regen is active you MUST turn around see where the tower spawned and kill everyone guarding it and destroy the tower. Repeat shield & health phase to see there is now 1 more tower, repeat 3 times & boss is dead. If you're fast enough you can spawn camp the adds & beat him in 3 volleys with the chance of having to do this maybe 5 more times since there are 6 platforms & he needs 1 to heal, it's possible but I AM NOT GOING TO TEST THAT it sounds like running 2km without shoes.It is a Ghostrunner game though just that it is the Dark Souls 2 of Ghostrunner where half of us will be fighting the other half like the Console Wars. I'd buy on sale though.In terms of style I liked when GR76 (or Jack) used his sword in 1 hand you FELT like a ninja not some kinda samurai type like Hel.Also in a audiolog that hints at another Ghostrunner why couldn't we fight him as a secret boss on the outside in the old 1 hit kill fashion it would've been interesting, there are problems with it such as how long has the recording been there but VR simulation maybe?Parkour was okay but janky at some points the Wingsuit though would've been a blast earlier on and you only get it for 1 level.
