_childDocuments_.review: After playing through both the Ghostrunner games I'd consider this game as a worthy sequel to the first one. It's a game that sacrifices some of the more hardcore elements of the first game for a more fun experience while still retaining the challenge of the first game. Below I've written what i find is the good, bad and ugly of Ghostrunner 2. The Good:- Just like GR1, the mix of parkour and combat feels really good.- The game adds new mechanics such as blocking (which is a little too forgiving, maybe it should eat up more stamina) and my favorite, the wingsuit.- The story is just as great as the first game, I know some people don't care about the people in the hub but I personally enjoyed it. I felt that the characters gave more depth to the setting and insight to what the world looks like from multiple perspectives. - Just like the first game, the level design is (for the most part) really good. Even the linear bike levels are decent, unlike the open world one...- The sequel also fixes some of the gripes I had with the first game. One of which was the akward timing in order to parry a melee attack in the first game. Here it actually feels responsive and in sync with the enemies attack.- The bossfights are far better than the first game. In GR2 it actually feels like you are fighting a boss instead of dodging their attacks for an eternity until the game says that you win. - One of my favorite aspects of the game is the how alive the game feels when it comes to characters. Everyone has their own personality and you can really see this in what they say and how they talk. The dialog between the characters are coherent and make sence and are even funny sometimes. By far my favorite is the chit-chat between the two guards at the hub area. There's even dialog between Jack and some of the characters when you go around and find secrets. The Bad:- As I said earlier, most of the levels are good. However, when it's bad it's really bad. And yes I am talking about the open world bike level... I've got a lot of gripes for this map. Not only is it the only map that looks weird and really unpolished but the map is littered with random tiny rocks that completely kill your momentum. And if that isn't frustrating enough the map also makes no sense to navigate. There aren't any signs that tell you were to go apart from the 3 dots on your hud, which don't help.- The bike isn't great either since it's handling feels really weird. Whenever you move slow you can turn around but whenever you cross a fixed speed threshold it abruptly lowers your turn speed. This feels really akward and clunky. A better system would've been if the bike could adjust its turn speed relative to your speed instead of whatever the current system is. - Just like the first game, the grapple feels too stiff. Whenever you grapple on to a point you move in a completely straight line height-wise. You don't have a slight arc towards the point which would help it feel more natural. You do atleast have the ability to move perpendicular to the vertical axis. The Ugly:- Your keybinds . I've tried everything and found no solution. A lot of people managed to avoid this issue by not pressing Enter when entering the game but this didn't work for me. I also tried to boot in DX11 and DX12 to no avail. You have to rebind your settings on every startup and I'm pretty sure it's been the case since launch.- The only bossfight I hated was Madhu because of a few reasons. Unlike all the other bosses, Madhu's attacks when he is using a scythe are basically instantaneus which is extremely frustrating. Not only that but if you try to dodge his dashes then some of the time you'll still die even though his scythe is nowhere near you. It's like the damage box stays for a few seconds instead of moving with his scythe.- The little platform bots that you pull are really bad. I've died so many times because I expect them to have a timer before moving back to their original position (just like how every other game does this) only for it to instantly move at the speed of light the second I even graze the bots. This was the most annoying part of the platforming of this game, and thankfully the only one.Rating: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for July 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before August 6th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A wild ninja ride. Ghostrunner 2 is a continuation where the players once again run through levels, eliminating enemies with a sword and a couple of slick powers. There’s a strong focus on blocking, parrying, and using a mid-air dash move that when done right will make you feel like an invincible ninja. However, when you struggle, and I struggled a lot, it can be a little brutal. I don’t know if the levels are weaker, or if I was just missing something but I do feel it was more of a user error than bad game design. In addition, there are supposedly performance issues, I didn’t have any that I noticed, but I do recognize that’s a strong constant criticism of this game, and know people who had those issues. I’ll just throw out that I run everything off an M. 2 SSD, and maybe that’s why I’m ok, but I have no clue.Pick this up if you like the original game, some fans didn’t enjoy this one as much but it’s still the same fast-paced combat. It’s a game that makes you want to retry, and even as the first boss destroyed me over 50 times, I felt like I was learning the fight. I may have just shoved my face through the difficulty wall, but I did eventually beat him. _childDocuments_.review: A disappointing sequel to one of the greatest Hotline Miami successors out there.Ghostrunner 2 aimed to go bigger and jump higher, that much is clear. What's missing, however, is the initial sharpness of the formula that made the original click in the first place. It was tight and snappy, calibrated to strike right at the target, one adrenaline shot after the other.Now, with vast levels, complicated enemy patterns, dozens of situational skills, perfunctory puzzles, and story beats that break the momentum, it's as if Ghostrunner no longer wants to be Ghostrunner. It strives to be many things at once, from Turbo Overkill and DOOM Eternal to even Half-Life 2 at times — which are all great comparisons really, just not for this game. A lot of new ideas simply don't go well with the core "live fast, act now, die, repeat" concept, eventually diluting it so much it gets annoying. And when replaying a fight feels like going through motions, you know something is very, very wrong.There are some redeeming qualities, sure. The overall presentation is pretty solid (apart from some wonky-looking NPCs), fundamental combat and traversal mechanics can be fun in the more concise encounters, and the bike is the single best addition to the mix. So good, in fact, that it managed to make the worst level in the game somewhat enjoyable. Yeah, keep the bike, it's cool.Still, I can't remember the last time a short adventure like that was such a chore. Ghostrunner 2 did scratch that very specific cybersamurai itch for a bit, but if I knew what it had in store for me, I would have replayed the first game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As a GR1 fan, I played the first game through dozens of times because of the movement and combat, killing an enemy was satisfying and abilities were more fun to use, not being able to use them all the time was a good counterbalance too, the story was alright, but the gameplay loop was CRISP. GR2 seems to throw all these aspects out of the window and double down on the weakest parts of GR1: the dialogue, story and cutscenes. It also has very buggy enemies and gimmicky levels.I really wanted to make a list right after a session of GR2, so here is the stuff I found disappointing:-Crashes-combat is more dependent on juggling abilities compared to the more streamlined system in GR1.-timed jumps/parkour, not very skill expressive and destroys the flow of movement.-less freedom of movement compared to the earlier title (many walls that you can't wallrun anymore).-way buggier than GR1.-Long cutscenes and cringeworthy dialogue disrupting gameplay.-The hub world being completely useless timewaster. -The music is very bad compared to the earlier title.-Worse layouts on the combat arenas.-Cookiecutter story-Makes me want to play GR1It baffles me how the fanbase literally told them why they love and play the game, and then the devs just ignore it, or worse yet, try to improve it by throwing ♥♥♥♥ at the wall and seeing what sticks. There is a lot of useless fluff in this game, they added fat into an already lean and working system.TLDR: Buy GR1, if you are a fan of GR1, go play GR1 again. This will not be a step up or more of the same. I got it for 7€ and idk if it was worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: The fluidity of the gameplay in Ghost Runner I was one of its standout features. The parkour system, characterized by swift movements and precise controls, The sense of speed is palpable, and the combination of wall-running, dashing, and slicing through enemies creates a rhythm that’s both thrilling and addictive. While Ghost Runner I excels in its narrative depth and fluid game play, Ghost Runner II takes a completely different approach with narrative and gameplay mechanics. the addition of a bike introduces a significant change to the gameplay, adding a new layer of mobility and exploration. While this new mechanic offers fresh opportunities for high-speed traversal and combat, it also highlights the game’s technical shortcomings. Once you step outside the confines of the Dharma Tower, the lack of polish becomes more apparent. The bike mechanics, while promising, sometimes feel clunky, and the open-world areas can reveal inconsistent performance, visual issues and glitches that detract from the overall immersion.Additionally, one significant drawback is the limited key binding options. Despite the game’s release two years ago (23-26-OCT), players are still restricted to rebinding only the WASD keys, although you can rebind all the keys but the game won’t save it….So on each reboot you have to do that again, which can be a major inconvenience for those who prefer or require alternative control schemes. This oversight suggests a lack of attention to player customization and accessibility.The game also suffers from inconsistent frame rates and occasional bugs that disrupt the otherwise smooth experience. There are also moments where the game's design choices such as level layouts or enemy placement can cross the line from challenging to frustrating. The difference between difficulty and annoyance becomes clear when these design elements impede progress rather than enhancing the challenge. Despite these issues, Ghost Runner II remains an exhilarating ride. Its fast-paced action and innovative mechanics have a lot of potential, but the game’s lack of polish and technical flaws are hard to ignore. If you’re willing to overlook these imperfections, there’s a lot of high-speed fun to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game as good as the first one, that in many ways improves on the first game, with some additions that might prove more love it/hate it.Pros:+ Still a great cyberpunk visual-style, both inside Dharma and outside.+ Same good gameplay-loop of parkour and one-hit-death combat. As some people say, don't mess too much with a good thing.+ Refined combat with new upgrade-system and blocking-ability.+ Motorbike is incredibly fun and fits very well into the Ghostrunner gameplay-style.+ Amazing soundtrack. While Daniel Deluxe only returns for two (ableit great) songs, the additional artists bring great stuff, with We Are Magonia and Dan Terminus standing out in particular.+ Voice actors from the original game and Project Hel are back and bring good perfomances.+ Improved boss fights, being more interactive and using the existing Ghostrunner mechanics.+ Improved Cybervoid levels, being more parkour-levels instead of slow puzzle-levels.+ Most of the more open-ended sections are pretty good. I was worried that the developers at One More Level were biting off more than they could chew when they mentioned that there would be levels that are more open-world-like. Fortunately they serve more as extended levels that don't break the pace. One level does however break the pace, see below.+ A valiant attempt is made to expand the world and characters is appreciated, though the execution will be more hit-or-miss for some people.+ RogueRunner.exe is a very nice addition, bringing some replay-value to the game.Cons:- There do appear the occasional bug with clipping through environments. This happens mostly with the motorbike-gameplay, where you get stuck on terrain.- The Climber-characters in the hub-areas have an unfortunate case of Bethesda-face in regards to animation during non-cutscene dialogue-sequences in the hub.- The really big open-ended level (Pillars of Creation) is longer than neccessary. Could have been broken into smaller levels.- While being able to interact with the Climbers in the hub is nice, it does not really add anything to the core gameplay-loop. See mixed-point below.Mixed:+/-: There is a hub area that is going to either be a nice addition to expand the story, or a major pace-breaker. Opposed to the first game that was basically level-level-level, in the first half of Ghostrunner 2, there will be a lot of level-hub-level-hub. While I enjoyed the hub and interacting with the characters, finding the dialogue entertaining and humorous, I can see how it can be seen as superfluous and breaking the fast-paced gameplay for a lot of people. Being able to meet the Climbers face-to-face (Zoe in particular) was a very requested feature by fans (including myself), but I do understand why the hub can be annoying, as it only exists as a reason to talk to the characters. This is not helped by the aforementioned Bethesda-face that the Climbers-characters have, something the villains avoid due to their more over-the-top cyborg-appearance. While I'm no game-designer, maybe briefer cutscenes like the ones in the trailers could have been used instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Just noticed this review, and I hope someone sees this when I clarify that the smart access memory function for my motherboard had played a role in the stuttering issues. With it enabled, the DirectX11 version of this game suffers from the stuttering more than the DirectX12 version. Once I found someone's post discussing this in the steam forums, I fixed the game to my setup and it has been running relatively smooth ever since.The game itself takes a few steps forward and fewer steps back, as I think the first entry is sharper in delivery. There are more features and sections to look forward to in this game, but most of it feels a bit under-baked. There is a larger story with more characters, but the game slogs through unskippable "hub-sections" that just has you skip through character dialog to move the playthrough along. There are larger missions, including a few open-ended ones, but some of them start feeling like slogs to play through as a result. There are more abilities that you have at your arsenal, but are held back by a few downgrades. For example, you are able to dash as many times as you want without a cooldown in this entry. However, its held back by a stamina bar that is not only tied to the dash but to a new block ability. The block is helpful, but compared to how swiftly you can move through levels in the first Ghostrunner by doing the dash -> slide -> jump -> dash combo as indefinitely as you can keep a rhythm, the sharpness of the movement takes a hit. That sharpness also takes a hit from other areas. For example, there is much more graphical detail involved in this entry, and although beautiful to look at, sometimes plays against the flow of gameplay as you can get caught in the levels' physical geometry. With something as demanding in difficulty as this game, this is a serious detriment. During bike sections, one little rock can kill you're deathless run.This game has things to like, including the flexibility of the arsenal, a good and more varied soundtrack, the bike segment :) For some, the rogue-like minigame this game offers can give a bit more value (although it can seem under-cooked at times, too). I also liked how the story expanded on the games universe a bit and explored areas described in the first entry, like a sequel should.Although I do come back to this game every now and then, I'd see myself coming back to the games previous entry more due to how much better it flows than this one, despite the respective hiccups that this entry fixes. This one doesn't replace the first in the slightest.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good continuation of the first game, GR2 picks up where the 1st left off in the story in a seamless way.Pros:The platforming and combat are just as good, with the former outshining the first in creativity and depth.The platforming segments will introduce a mechanic, such as a simple rotating door you can stop from a distance, and then quickly add on to the door with previously learned parkour mechanics, which causes the player to quickly learn how to adjust to the new door mechanic and use it in conjunction with other mechanics. This gives the parkour a nice flow to its increasing challenge and makes the game much more interesting. the blending together of mechanics is done masterfully, to an even better degree than the first. The platforming alone is incredibly enjoyable, and when it is combined with the combat it makes for very enjoyable albeit punishing gameplayCombat is the same as the first game, with some new abilities such as shadow and a time slow ultimate ability, among others. Still one shot for you and the enemies. The combat didn't receive many changes from the first, still very fluid.there are more boss fights, increasing from 1 combat boss and 2 platforming bosses in GR1 to 3 combat bosses and 1 platforming boss in GR2. New mechanics such as the wingsuit and the bike are very fun and enjoyableExcellent graphics and beautiful areas, especially with the more open portions in the 2nd half (no spoilers :3 !!)Characters are somewhat interesting for a game not focused on dialogueI encountered no glitches and only got stuck on terrain once (dashed up a flight of stairs, just crouched and was unstuck)Shares some enemies with GR1, but introduces a few new enemies that are interesting and unique enough to warrant inclusion and can spice up combatStill just as frustrating as the first, but it is easier than what I remember from GR1Cons:Like the first, the focus is not on the story. whether or not that matters is debatable, but if you are looking for a story based game look elsewhere.Is very difficult, so if you want a casual gaming experience look elsewhere.In some levels, the platforming can get a bit stale, but a majority of the levels aren't long enough for this to be a concern.Character models are good but it is obvious that the ghostrunners got more detail than the humansRating: Gameplay: 9/10Graphics: 9.5/10Story: 5/10 (while not bad it is very limited)Worth it at full price

Let's start with good things:-Bosses are a soild improvement. I'd say that only T-073-M holds up to the bosses from GR2. -OST is still god tier. I'd say it is equal to the GR1 OST. Daniel Deluxe, We are Magonia, Gost, Dan Terminus and Arkadiusz Rejkowski all have made a solid piece of art.- are a nice addition, although you'll use them max. once in a deathless run. Maybe with exception of the level , because of how long this level is.-I personally find the bike to be very fun. However it can be clunky due to strange collisions. -Characters are all well made. -Graphics are beautiful. However keep in mind that if you play on low quality, characters faces can turn into a light bulb.-They kept the Slide-Jump mechanic from GR1 <3-The finishers are satisfying to do - is something I didn't expect. Although I didn't like it at first, it grew on me after playing with it for a bit.-Basically everything I liked about GR1 is in GR2-Challenges in levels are also a welcomed addition, but man, F#ck the one in . _childDocuments_.review: I beat the game, but at the cost of me now hating it. Stamina meter in a game about being a robot ninja (how do you run out of stamina when you don't have lungs?) is a stupid mechanic. Grappling is majorly bugged, which it wasn't in the first game. Most of the time using it would completely throw off my momentum and result in me dying or it would stop short of what I grappled to and I would fall to my death. Rail riding is also bugged in the sense that you'll land on them and sometimes you just won't go anywhere. Other times, it'll send you in the wrong direction and you'll die. The bike was a cool feature, when it wasn't getting stuck and causing me to have to reset to my last checkpoint. Bosses were either stupid easy or stupid unbearable. For instance, the last boss is just a punching bag that recycles the same 3 attacks the whole time. I died more times to the environment than I did to the actual boss. Other bosses introduce stupid gimmicks like 3 health bars that they can switch between, and, guess what, one of those health bars causes the other 2 to be healed. So, in a game where you always die in one hit, you have enemies that can heal themselves? Stupid. Most dialogue feels like it was written by an emo teen. The last boss literally throws a tantrum when you start beating him.  Other bosses sound too smart and smug for their own good.  The main 2 of the supporting cast are bickering between themselves for 95% of the time they're interacting, then suddenly they're all chummy with each other out of nowhere. There were also issues with areas loading in. My rig is at/above the recommended specs and it's installed on my SSD, but I'd have to wait outside of some rooms while waiting for it to load in. But if I was rushing and I ran into an area like that, I'd just infinitely fall through the floor until I reloaded from the last checkpoint. All in all, if you liked the first game and still haven't tried this one, just stick to the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want the quick version this game is better in almost every way compared to the first. From gameplay to story to exploration to progression but its not for everyone that enjoyed the more simple direct linear approach the first game had. Just go play it this game is really good!Before moving on to the review. THIS GAME NEEDS A GLOBAL LEADERBOARD IN GAME. Fastest times, lowest deaths, etc. Would instantly be 10x more re-playable as players would compete for positioning on the leaderboard.Now for the more detailed scrambled thoughts...This game takes huge leaps in a lot of ways exploration story and game play. But takes a step back in a couple ways. One of the games step backs is in terms pacing there's a lot of times where it feels weirdly slow. Where the first game was just go go go this game asks you to stop look around and think and slow down at times not all the time but some of the time. Another direct correlation with this is the music it overall bangs just like in the first but in the open world section which last for about 3-4 hours they are just playing dark slow depressing apocalyptic type music this heavily made it hard for me to power through as slow moody depressing music playing for a few hours is not what you play ghost runner for you want to be adrenaline induced head rocking to fast paced music plowing through everything so that was questionable.Unlike most reviewers i feel most just skipped through the story bit straight to the objective however this games narrative is actually very interesting and if you pay attention and talk to the npcs between missions you'll be rewarded with a pretty interesting story ill admit at first it was generic feeling but once you get the motivations of the characters and back stories of some you start to grow a bond to some of them. So i did enjoy that aspect. Because the first didn't really have much in terms of character and world building.In terms of the progression in the first game it was very gimmicky and in this game they simplified it but added more skills and passives. So that aspect was pretty well done but id like to see more on this end still would be cool to have maybe modifiers or trinkets for the swords or gloves to give even more variety for freedom of play but overall progression was better then the first but not by much to be fair.Another thing i see people hate on is the level design in the first it was so linear it felt pretty good going through them fast but way less rewarding to find collectibles or swords in this one the levels are more open giving you more freedom to explore i felt it was overall way more rewarding finding a sword or a collectible in this game compared to the first just because its a little more open you had to go out of your way to find that sword or collectible which was a good reward and feeling for exploring.Bosses as well are overall better and there's more of them you actually get to fight some of them in the first game i wouldn't really call them boss fights but more just puzzles with a health bar so its cool to see this being improved. In this one there's actual boss "fights" where you actually swing your sword at the boss and it does damage to the boss crazy how that works an actual boss "fight" and not just a glorified puzzle with a health bar. So overall bosses are better.One aspect that kind of lacks in the second game in comparison to the first is puzzles the first game had unique rewarding puzzles to get a skill or get to the next area it was very rewarding and unique figuring them out took some thinking this game it just falls flat it attempts the same puzzle trope in some segments but they aren't really puzzles in most cases its just common sense that takes half a second and 0 effort to figure out so that kind of sucks that they couldn't match the same level of witt and smarts and thinking it took to figure out the solution in terms of puzzles that the first game had.In terms of graphics obviously the second is better then the first although slightly harder to run in terms of performance i had to turn DLSS on after that no more issues with fps and was smooth as butter. In terms of animations this is hit or miss they try to make every animation look smoother then the first but doing so it loses its snappy direct quick feeling the first game had this is most notable in the grapple hook in my opinion in the first it was way more snappy this may just be in animation and on paper it might be the same speed but it doesn't matter if its the same speed if it doesn't feel snappy it doesn't feel good.I saw some people say it doesn't feel as fast which is just not true they might have tuned it back a tad to make space for some of the speed modifiers you can find with some of the upgrades and skills you can get however you definitely go way faster then you ever could in the first game with these skills and upgrades but the fact that they force you to get that speed through the progression system with the skills and upgrades might leave a bad taste on some people its still overall really fast base level though.Also another side note the motorcycle is a pretty fun section but the most fun i had was with the wing suit glider that section is very fun in my opinion flying through the air combining that together with parkour and combat that's when the game felt it was at its best for me and that's towards the end of the game. Also the side mode which is basically a rogue like kind of mode is much improved here the first game had this mode too but it was pretty poorly done in the second game every stage is different and forces you to make tougher decisions the first game tried to do this mode too but wasn't nearly as unique stage to stage or rewarding for making tough choices on what abilities or what path you take. The mode is much more improved for anyone that enjoyed it in the first game.Overall this game is better and i enjoyed it will play through it again on hardcore for sure and grab any DLC that comes out however i can see why its not for every one. Most fans of the first game liked the linear simple less story driven go go go straight forward experience and although you get some of that here in the second game it is very much different and tries to be more open and expansive in every way which some fans of the first game might not care for. Overall better gameplay more progression more story more complexity more open levels more bosses more enemy types along with the same ones from the first this game. Ghost runner 2 is better then the first in almost every way despite a couple draw backs that in reality come down to preference definitely give it a shot. I would highly recommend the game to anyone.Edit: After playing hardcore for a bit i can say its easily worth another play through almost every obstacle is changed and harder now. Enemies feel about the same to kill kind of easy to be honest however boss fights feel harder i think theres extra moves sets added but i cant tell. Another HUGE note some obstacles are physically impossible in hardcore depending on if you have certain skills equipped or not so keep that in mind. I think it was a missed opportunity to not add extra collectibles and swords exclusive to hardcore but regardless it does feel fresh and more challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh yeah, I love this game. I loved the first one, too, and this scratched all the same itches. Cons? idk, there's a few glitches, a few invisible walls here and there, and sometimes I just feel like it's a bit too forgiving. But that's just me as a massive fan of the first one. It's not something you'll notice if you're new. It also seems way less focused on completion speed, which I appreciate, since "shaving off a few seconds" sounds more like homework than fun to me. Buy this game unless you were a snob about the ultradifficulty, but in my opinion you'll still find plenty that's hard here and plenty to love. If you played GR1 til you hit that lasertower and gave up, you're gonna love GR2. GR2 doesn't require meth to complete any of its levels.  Start here. You're gonna love this. It's what the first should have been, in my opinion. Can't wait for the ever-based devs to put out content here and there so I have a reason to come back. Hard recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just.. not good.I really loved the original Ghostrunner, it was one of the best games I've played and it was incredibly fun, and pleasantly challenging (a little bit easier than a soulslike, but the deflect mechanic was really fun to master)It was just the right difficulty and a fun weekend. This game though, I'm less than half an hour in and it's not good. If you're expecting more of Ghostrunner 1, that's not what you're going to get here. The graphics are slightly improved, but the character models took a hit. The swords are not as unique. The leveling system lacks the uniqueness that Ghostrunner's puzzle system had. The story is not as good. Jack lost the dry humor that came with being a robot, and is now too human, and it feels like he's trying WAY too hard. It really feels like this game is just trying to incorporate Cyberpunk 2077 aspects, and it just doesn't work. The level design is worse, the movement is worse, the combat is worse. I don't know why the blocking mechanic was added other than to artificially make the game easier. Ghostrunner 1's timing system was frustrating at first, sure, but it was worth it to learn. And THE BUGS. In less than half an hour, I've fallen through the floor twice and fallen off the wall three times while wallrunning. Oh, and the stamina. It just sucks. I want my old dash/sensory boost meter back.I got this game from the humblebundle and I don't think it was even worth the price I paid for that. If you're coming into this game from Cyberpunk 2077 after searching the Cyberpunk tag on Steam wanting that feeling again, this will give you a hollow replica of that. It won't be nearly as good, but it might just fill the void until Project Orion comes out. But if you're coming into this from Ghostrunner 1 you will not be satisfied, not even a little bit. Overall, I think if this game retained the mechanics of Ghostrunner 1 and they toned down Jack's snarkiness just a LITTLE BIT, it would be perfect. Something happened between the release of Ghostrunner and Ghostrunner 2 that caused it to fall apart. Probably greed. Ghostrunner 1 Hardcore is more of a sequel than this will ever be.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 delivers on many fronts, enhancing what made the original great while introducing a few new elements. The graphics have seen a significant upgrade, and the soundtrack is even more immersive, making every moment feel larger than life. The combat has been rebalanced, which may appeal to some, but I found it made the game a bit too easy compared to its predecessor.Combat, which was a highlight in the original, has been overhauled to feel more balanced. However, this balance comes at a cost. The thrill of the fast-paced, unforgiving combat from the first game is somewhat diminished. The battles, while still engaging, lack the intensity and challenge that made them so satisfying. The skills, like Shuriken and Shadow, are well-integrated and add more variety, but the overall experience feels toned down, with enemies that are easier to dispatch and scenarios that are less punishing.The boss battles, unfortunately, still don’t hit the mark for me. They’re too short, forgiving, and predictable—after 10-20 tries, you can easily get the hang of them. The bike and wingsuit sections were interesting additions, though the wingsuit felt gimmicky and repetitive after a while.On the positive side, the skills are more integral to gameplay, offering more strategic depth. However, despite all these improvements, it feels like Jack is only using a fraction of his potential—anything below hardcore mode just feels too easy.The story and characters were another letdown. The narrative felt too linear, lacking the mystique of the original. Most of the characters felt flat and egotistical, except for Bakunin, Saul, and Zoe, who brought some substance but still fell short of leaving a strong impression. Jack seems to carry the team 90% of the time, which makes the group dynamic less believable and engaging.Despite its flaws, Ghostrunner 2 excels in maneuverability and the sheer freedom you feel while playing. The upgraded graphics and level design add to the overall experience, making it a solid but not groundbreaking sequel. If you enjoyed the original and are okay with reflex-heavy gameplay, you’ll likely find this a worthwhile experience.Overall, I’d give it a strong 7 to a weak 8 out of 10, and I definitely recommend playing this with a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: : Since this review is trending on top, I want to add that this game is actually great for the people who couldn't beat Ghostrunner 1, or the people who found it to be too hard to enjoy. GR2 is a  for newcommers or casual players. This review is from a perspective of a hardcore-difficulty enjoyer. And while flawed, it is still an good experience overall.Unfortunately they've made a mistake that Doom Eternal as a sequel has avoided. GR2 is too focused on the story instead of gameplay. And as a result pacing and combat become far less interesting compared to the first game.- Combat arenas are too open with large gaps between enemies.It makes all encounters easy and same-y.- Arenas do not involve using parkour and environment to your advantage. Parkour is used only to navigate to the next enemy.- Arenas do not have any advanced level design. GR1 had a lot of great arenas that always challenged their player and required different approach. Like the 5 swordsmen moment. All GR2 arenas have the same approach, kill all enemies and hold block button between the kills.- The Block button makes game too easy, and less fun a result. It acts like a crutch for a bad play-style. I think they should've kept as a part of easy mode and let hardcore players parry with left mouse button just like before.- Enemies were replaced with grey, voiceless zombies that are hard to distinguish from a distance. This goes completely against game's formula, enemies should be easy to read, not memorized.Overall combat is treated poorly with the game doubling down on platforming. Which has also a couple of flaws, but fun and engaging in general. - The new robot platforms are a  decision. They cannibalize the grappling hook point and often I just die because I can't distinguish them. You can also wall-run on a side of them which will result in an unfair death.- A lot of of levels do not have proper death zones at the bottom of arenas. As a result I get stuck on geometry and don't get an insta-death to restart the arena.- All outside sections are lifeless and boring. Replacing colorful charismatic city with green and orange desert was a huge mistake and a blow to the pacing of the game. - The music choice didn't help as well it just adds to the boring feeling of the location.- Bike gets stuck on a geometry all the time.- Replacing charismatic colorful enemies with dull grey zombies that all look the same. It makes combat more punishing because you don't know what type of enemy is in front of you until it shoots.- 3 of 4 levels you spend outside the Dharma Tower do not improve gameplay and only serve the story.While it provides fun soundtrack, good story and amazing environment  design, the game is too short. It's not designed for replayability like the first game and combat design went from advanced to basic. I am looking forward to more additions to this franchise but I feel like developers either do not understand what made the original fun or they've rushed the sequel and didn't experiment enough.If you are a hardcore fan of GR1, replay the game on the hard mode and get the sequel on sale. It's fun but a step back from GR1.

_childDocuments_.review: For a platform game, it's great. Unfortunately, that's where the good parts end, because for everything the platforming gets right the combat ruins. Where do I even begin with the combat? For starters, no difficulty scaling, so for those who want a more casual experience, forget it, because you have to sweat every second to progress. Then we have the boss fights, what a clunky mess, it would probably be fine if you could use your ultimate abilities but no, apparently your character who is a literal cyborg samurai just forgets how capable he is within a boss battle, how convenient. Then the impossible split-second decisions you have to make are unbearable, it would be fine if I was invulnerable while in mid-blink, but instead, I can still be hit with a stupid stray bullet from an enemy who I can't even see. Don't even get me started on the dumpster garbage abilities that barely even assist you in battle, in the first game, it felt like my character received sizeable buffs for the difficulty scaling throughout the game, but in this "sequel," the only progress you receive is pretty lackluster character boosts. Honestly what a disappointment considering how amazing the first game was. My advice is don't pay more than $10 for this junk if you want to try it, otherwise, I'd recommend just playing the first game which is a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: **Pirated the game, finished it, then bought it.**I will separate this review into story and gameplay:Story: 6/10*No major spoilers for GR 2, but some spoilers for GR 1.*The story in GR 2 falls short compared to its predecessor, GR 1. While GR 1 didn't have a complex narrative, its diverse and well-defined characters brought a lot of interest and contrast to the game.In GR 1, we had the architect—smart, capable, and successful. Zeo was a passionate freedom fighter and revolutionist, while Jack was a cool-headed, efficient military type. This diversity made the story compelling. Even the enemies were distinct, with gangs relying on numbers and tower forces on technology.In contrast, GR 2 lacks this variety. Characters have been homogenized—Zeo is now more cool-headed, Jack more thoughtful, and the other characters similarly blend together. The enemies also feel undifferentiated, diminishing the story's impact.Despite these shortcomings, the story is still adequate, which is why I rated it 6/10. More then fine, but only in a very small way.Gameplay: 9.5/10The game doesn't run smoothly on my system, despite it feeling cool that, even my computer can't handle my speed. It is more annoying then cool...Gameplay in GR 2 closely mirrors GR 1, which is a positive aspect. There are few speed games that can compete with GR 2's mechanics. The game introduces interesting new elements to the already solid core gameplay.However, not all new features are well-integrated. The bike, for instance, feels disconnected from the main gameplay. It's like playing a different game when using the bike, which was disappointing. On the flip side, the game is full of exciting action moments.The game truly shines when you unlock perks that allow you to go full speed. It's an exhilarating experience, making you feel entirely in the zone—this alone makes the game worth playing.*Spoilers for gameplay ahead*: A late-game addition, the gliding ability, integrates beautifully with the core mechanics, offering a fantastic gameplay experience. It's a shame it appears so late, but it still gets its moment to shine. *End of spoilers*.Conclusion:If you enjoyed GR 1, you'll likely appreciate GR 2 as well.* I used gpt to make it more readable, English is not my native language.

_childDocuments_.review: I was given a key via the 505 Games Creators Circle but not paid to review/play the game, I have only played the first GhostRunner game one time and that was relatively recent.Graphically, the game is stunning, I have moments where I see texture popping in at the start of levels but I think that may just be my PC having issues.The Gameplay feels smoother than Ghostrunner 1 but it still has a couple of issues where I would not clamp onto a rail to grind across or I would run the wrong way on a wall and get stuck on some geometry below the map stopping me dying. Again could easily be me doing something wrong but still something I came across while playing.They added a new mini game called Roguerunner.exe and its one of my favourite additions to the game, it is used to unlock cosmetics for your character, first one being new colour scheme for your hands/arms. The way it works is simple, you have no powers but you pick a 1 of 3 starting point with the goal of choosing your path to get to the end mission. Along the way you can pick up 1 of 3 random upgrades or extra lives from doing a Parkour or Area mission and a shop where you can spend lives to get upgrades. When you get the end mission it is always an Area fight.The sound track is amazing as always, I am a sucker for synthwave music. It would be kinda nice to have background music when looking in the upgrade shop and motherboard config bit, maybe just very quite but something would be nice.From what I have played, the bike stuff is really fun, being able to jump off it and grapple back onto it is so cool.I am not sure how long the game is, I have currently beaten 2 bosses and finished the first mission with the bike and currently 5 hours into it. I have not been actively looking for all the collectables but if I saw one I would give it a good try to get it, I do feel like I am just getting into the meat of the game tho so  hopefully it will last a lot longer, even if its for another 5 or 6 hours, I would be happy.You do not need to play the first game in order to play this, there is a "Recap" of the major plot points of the first which you can access on the main menu under "Extras". But of course I would suggest playing the first just so you can experience how much this game improves on it.Overall, I am loving this game and would recommend it to anyone interested in it. If you need instant gratification from games or you dont like games where every new area presents a new problem that you have to spend time learning and solving, then go play something else. Just remember it is okay to not like a game because one mechanic frustrates you, but that doesnt mean hate on that game. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and I want to say from the start IS HARDER THAN THE FIRST ONE, But the game was good, since I have played the first game a long time ago (~ 2 years I believe I got it for free on other platform and I have played it there) but I know the first game since before was released I have seen a Facebook add with it, and it thought, it was a mobile phone at first, and I was surprised on how good it looked and how good it was optimized (not like this one, I will talk about it later)Starting with the graphics, it looks good no comment there, but the optimization is not that good, I had a lot of stutter and some fps spikes (and I don't think ryzen 7 5800x3d 32gb ram and RTX 4080 should have any problem running the game smooth) but after locking the fps to 165 in RivaTuner it did not fix anything just after turning on DLSS it stopped stuttering even if my GPU can run this game easily on 1440p ultra 200+fps native rez.Gameplay it felt harder than the first game, some boss fight was annoying as hell  and another annoying boss it was the  except those tow everything was ok. Audio I feel like almost everything is recycled from the first game and that is a plus, the voice actors were good. As pc requirements, I believe it can run at maximum settings 1080p according to the Steam Hardware & Software Survey: February 2024 maybe even 1440p.The game in my opinion is not that difficult, is hard to master it require significant brain usage for some puzzles, some timed actions it is guaranteed to fail a few times on some puzzles or to get lost but for a little attention you can figure it out.The story was average, not that insane to remember for your life, but it was decent, the grind in this game isn't necessary to progress, but it can make the gameplay easier and some of them are just extra audio files, collectables and some sword skins.My opinion about the game, I give it a solid 6 out of 10, the story was good but for the price of 40 euro I can't recommend it at all for 8h of gameplay if you don't go for achievements and collectables. I will recommend getting the game when it will be on sale for ~ 5 to 10 euro

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying your fast-paced, adrenaline pumping rhythmic game? Time to stop and go back to a hub that could have easily been a menu. The developers added dialogue options, but the only options are to listen to more boring and cringe dialogue — and the order you hear it in; or just leave. I opted to leave. All the dialogue could have been trimmed down and fed to you as radio communications instead.This really leaves me puzzled, they took all the best elements of Ghostrunner, and slapped arbitrary elements on top of it. Open world segments (boring), stamina-based blocking, time trials, a tacked-on rogue-lite game, ultimate abilities... I'm shocked they left out romance options.I'll give the devs props on the atmosphere and the music, but this game leaves me nostalgic for the first game with levels that are tightly designed, adrenaline pumping missions seamlessly leading into another with no downtime at all. Ghostrunner 1 felt like I was dancing a deadly ballet across a chessboard; Ghostrunner 2 feels like dancing the Macarena, fun for a minute, but you wont get 5 hours of enjoyment out of it.I'll be cautiously optimistic for Ghostrunner 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is an action-packed sequel that offers more of what players loved in the first game along with filling in some blanks along the way. The brand new hub offers a chance to chat and meet the characters you speak with face to face and the latter half of the game provides an exhilarating way to get around the open areas with the new motorcycle. Although combat retains its singular sword as your primary weapon, it is opened up with the expansion of a new combo meter and unlockable abilities to suit your playstyle. If punishing difficulty and a willingness to adapt to an extremely fast play style sounds exciting, getting a grasp on these mechanics will provide a thrilling experience not many other games can offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game...it hurts so good.  That last boss fight was punishing and I didn't even know if I could finish the game.  It took me longer than I'd like to admit to get beyond the first stage.  the motorcycle addition was fun, but it would have been helpful to be able to use the mouse to look around especially with the transition from wall riding to the ground.   The number of times I drove into an obstacle because I was outrunning my field of vision.  The music is great and really helps with immersion because, if your like me, you will end up dying and it keeps it from feeling too repetitive.  The controls are surprisingly intuitive and the cyber void sections where you have control over the environment really tested my multitasking abilities.  the movements are really fluid and despite everything that's going on, its really satisfying when you get the timing right and things just flow.  The story has some interesting plot points and some interesting characters.  I think one has to be kinda masochistic to enjoy a game like this or irrationally stubborn I suppose.  This game will invite you into a battle of will.  It was designed to beat you.  It wants to beat you.  Interested?

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy sequel to GR1 that improved on the game in nearly every way. There are new enemy types, platforming mechanics, and abilities that really freshen up the gameplay. I'm going to take a counter-stance on the limited "open world" section that lots of others are complaining about. These sections were not only fun, but they also made GR2 feel more like an action/adventure game with a flowing story. By contrast, GR1 - while incredible - was segmented in a room-after-room gameplay loop which made it feel more like an arcade title.The soundtrack slapped as expected and the story had some compelling new characters, despite not necessarily being the focal point of the game. Performance-wise it ran very well with only a few hitches here and there over my 10hr playthrough. This title is just a bit different, but it retains all the fast-paced charm of the original.p.s. I want to have a beer with the two guards outside the main office
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostrunner 2

_childDocuments_.review: A fast paced 1-hit death cyberpunk slasher/platformer you won't forget!Although it doesn't fit the [1 hr gameplay = 1 dollar spent] criteria, it's  worth the money for the standard edition at least (and an even better deal if you get the brutal edition on sale).Similar to the first game, the fun lay within the wallrunning, jumping, and grappling introduced in the first game, now with added motorcycle! Slashing through enemies while avoiding certain 1-hit deaths is fun beyond compare, an experience tailored for high-skill gamers. This sequel adds new as well as heavily improved mechanics, notably the parry/deflect system, (endgame) flight suit, several motorcycle racing style levels, as well as cleaning up the old game mechanics like the abilities system. High skill, high reward!Short and sweet, half the achievements are challenging and fulfilling, requiring you to put your skill to the test. None of the achievements are particularly tedious if you keep in mind that you must search for collectibles before starting. This time, there's a built in radar for collectibles, so there's no excuse not to get them all! The most challenging achievement is finishing 5 levels without dying. Think it's easy? Think again.Massive improvements over the first game in several areas. First, you can actually see who you're talking with over the radio face-to-face this time! Voice acting has improved leaps and bounds with quality dialogue and meaningful content. While I don't feel particularly attached to any of the characters, there is the groundwork laid for future games. They certainly don't lack in personality, now they just need time to marinate on the player.Very little to hate about this game, but the introduction of new mechanics will always pose issues/fixes that need to be made. As such, only 3 notable problems occurred; 1) The motorcycle feels extremely floaty, and the lerp applied to the camera makes it hard to take sharp turns which are sometimes necessary 2) You can't move the camera while driving, which also makes it difficult to see where you're going at times3) On the motorcycle stage in which you are chased by a large entity, if you die around the beginning of the chase, then you become stuck in a loop in which you can't boost out and the slow speed causes you to repeatedly die. A simple solution might be having the boost accelerate in faster burst initially, or reduce the lag on the boost input.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially gave this game a negative review, after just 2-3 hours of playtime. I wanted badass cyber ninja gameplay and that's what I got in the end, with some levels being big and open, allowing multiple approaches, which I found refreshing.I like that the developers experimented with new mechanics and tried to push the franchise further, and I am looking forward to seeing what is next in the ghostrunner adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: It was an enjoyable experience overall but it feels little more than an extension of the first game and falls short of deserving it's own title (and £35 price tag). Even though I had fun with it, it was hard not to compare it negatively with the first game in most scenarios. The upgrade system is seriously underwhelming and half of the upgrades are almost useless, although the way to piece them together and maximise their effectiveness, similar to the first game, is engaging and provokes some degree of thought. Though in reality it has very little affect.The hub world was probably the worst inclusion that they introduced since the first game. Where Ghostrunner had a continuous flow where the events and plot flowed through conversations had whilst you were playing, 2 now stops you to listen to in a meaningless hub world which only contains (other than characters to talk to) a machine to buy, not even apply as that's done in a menu, upgrades and a machine to play a short mini-game.There was one main inclusion however which I really enjoyed and that was the cyberbike! It provided a break to the core game-play loop of running around and slashing in a positive way which preserved the tempo of the game, unlike the hub world. It was something new to learn and fit the pace of the core game-play which then allowed them to be used together later on in the story.Overall I think if you enjoyed the first game, this is a no brainer as they are almost the same game, although this installment is far less of a challenge. However, it is also for this reason that I cannot recommend enough that you wait for a sale. 100%ing all the achievements took me under 14 hours which for a £35 game, especially one that is a near identical sequel, is atrocious.

_childDocuments_.review: absolute banger of a game, if you like this game, or any of these games, you should try them all:Turbo OverkillQuakeDoomHotline MiamiUltrakillCruelty SquadKatana ZeroRuinerGhostrunner 1All of these games are great, as for ghostrunner 2, its quick if you play though it quickly, but I definitly plan on replaying it in the future. Plus the game itself is a very feelgood game.Went and did a second playthrough and it was super fun as well, it lets you keep the stuff from the first playthrough as long as you use level select, and I enjoyed trying to beat my previous times, find shortcuts, and minimize deaths.Edit: after an update, they added hardcore mode! a super fun mode honestly, I just finished it, took me ~2 or so hours, but im definitly going to replay the hardcore mode many times just like i have the main game to get deathless runs on many of the maps.One of the only features I think the game is missing is a restart on death system. Its really annoying to have to die and then open a pause menu and restart the map, when the game could just place you at the beginning. Great game though!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the embodiment of cool. Cyperpunk samurai parkour mincing baddies while hacking AI ghosts. Great mixture of action, puzzles and story. Had many moments that took my breath away, including amazing motorcycle sequences at breakneck speed, precise hack and slash combos, and thrilling frame perfect jumps. Solid storyline and gameplay so far, highly recommended. They still need to work on bugs, by pushing the game engine there are times when it seems the game doesn't register a move or more frequently a "catch" onto a surface, which can be frustrating. The graphics look beautiful, but NPC animations look dated, clunky and mechanical. The awesome environments and gameplay more than make up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad this game is so short, but even so IT'S THE NEW AND IMPORVED GHOSTRUNNER 2 BOIIIIIIIII, and it's just awesome. For a bonus you get to have a motorcycle, which is even more fun than before even though I had a really hard time controlling it (seriously it slides too much). There is a lot of quality of life changes compared to the first game, such as the stamina bar and the upgrade system, I find that very sweet. The hub and the gaming chair additions are pretty cool too.The game comes with some semi-open world levels that are super neat, and even in general the levels are bigger and offer a lot of ways to destroy your enemies...  the problem is since they have god-like accuracy you get destroyed as well. The giant space you get tends to be a disavantage sometimes since you just focus on an enemy and another one snipes out of nowhere, so you ought to be on the move all the time and check your surroundings real hard in some situations.The parkour is a little strange sometimes and I am not saying that the parkour sections are bad, they are EXCELLENT, but one instance Jack won't stick to the wall and you fall and die, and then Jack sticks to the wall when you don't want him to and you still fall and die. But I guess that's a skill issue, even though I think it can be improved, maybe like press space to stick to the wall or something as an optional feature you can toggle in the menu. In addition to the bike, you get a GLIDER, and what's sad is you can only use it for one level when the gameplay with is is just AMAZING. I felt kind of bummed, but then (I still didn't test this) you can go back in previous levels and maybe use it, which would be a big thumbs up.Anyway, I'm gonna give the game a solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun and very cool. Aesthetics are great and the core gameplay is extremely engaging.But similar to the first, the game suffers from huge replayability issues. The cybervoid sections are better this time, basically being actual levels now, but there is still so much downtime in the game which you can't skip. The HUB area would be fine if you could choose whether you wanted access it or not. But being forced to run around and talk to multiple characters in order to get into the actual levels feels like such an easily avoidable design flaw. _childDocuments_.review: Heartbreaking, but I'm chopping this up as a miss. I loved the first game, but something feels amiss with the second.People have made the claim this is easier - and while that may be true in combat I found  to be the majority of my deaths. These are typically sections of games that you breeze through with the right inputs. Something was chronically wrong with the spacing of travesal objects that I would often fall short, or jump over, things. The swinging poles are a great example; something felt so off (possibly aspect ratio/field of view issues?) where as I jumped towards them I  like I was positioned correctly so that Jack would be able to grab it, but he falls instead. Out of shear paranoia I found myself dashing to each pole, to which felt like if I was viewing the connection in third person, I'd see Jack hit the pole with his shins. Something so very not right with the detection here.Ghostunner implements a 'Hub' between missions (at least in the early stages of the game that I've played). When adding additional features to a sequel the big question is "does this add or remove value". In my experience, it removes. Ghostrunner 1 was a continuous series of back-to-back missions unfolding in a linear fashion. This leaned favourably to the game's pace, as while the combat is fast, so is the feeling of your progression. Being pulled from missions to a safe, at-my-own-pace, Hub area was jarring, and removed the sense of urgency the first game expressed. It's possible that the Hub provided a better opportunity for story expression, but since the story is nonsensical to me, and not the strong point of the series, I think it's ultimately better to abandon thoughts of improving player access to it (if it's ultimately going to hurt other areas). The open area was actually an interesting change of pace, and despite my desire to want the game to feel 'quick', I didn't find it tedious. I would criticise the first section and it's overall game time - significantly more (double?) than the missions prior. There's 3 distinct areas to go to, maybe these could have all been individual timed missions? It's also hard to feel a sense of urgency towards your own game-time (if you're aiming to finish missions quick) when you're driving around an open map where everything looks similar, and efficient pathways are indistinguishable against the wider landscape.Also, and I don't know if this was my aspect ratio and field of view, but the view from the bike was . Half my screen was bike, and that was worsened any time I was going up hill. Some sections require you to go up walls and I was essentially guessing. I was guessing the right path and, if it didn't work, adjusted next life. Absolutely terrible. Naga was probably an amazing sequence for everyone else, but I couldn't help but rack up the deaths (and the frustration) with running trial-and-error blindly. All and all this has the combat that I enjoyed from the first game, but I feel the additional aspects they've added hurt the sequel - and something went terrible wrong with spacing traversal elements considering jump/dash distances.I feel bad to some degree. I liked Ghostrunner 1 so much - but this just isn't feeling fun and it's made worse that I can objectively break-down why.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: This is an LSD trip that last for a day similar to Katana Zero and I dig it. This game is the direct sequel to Ghostrunner (2020) and it improves a lot of features while also introduce some new issues that kinda lower the overall quality of the product. Nevertheless, this is a solid game that fans of the first game and fans of hack-n-slash games will definitely enjoy, give it a shot.*Positive:+Graphic is nice, has clear visual style and very details in Dharma tower+The combat is *chef kiss*, well-crafted in term of visually and sound design, every slash is brutal+While some people may dislike the toned down difficulty, this is actually my positive point. The game is still hard, but not brutally hard anymore+Extended RPG system with new skills, upgrades and ultimate skills, making the game highly customizable for any playstyle player wants. TL;DR making the game easier or harder on choices+The soundtrack on its own is not very good, but for the pace of the game, it did a very good job*Negative:-While the game has many options for setting, one thing persists is the stuttering no matter your setting might be, which can be annoying-The story is serviceable but not very memorable, most characters except Zoe and Kira are blank-slate boring, the theme and setup is very interesting but fall flat due to pacing issue-The game is a little bit short, around 6-7 hours to finish a playthrough, recommend increase to 10 hours-The  is heavily under utilized, almost no feature to back it up due to most features are collectibles and chip upgrades. If they plan to expand this in the next game, recommend hiring someone with  and mission design expertise.*Final score:-Critic score: 6/10, a very flashy roller coaster with many bumps on rails that need fixing or improvement-User score: 8/10, two step forward, one step backward, and leaves to desire in the end like the bittersweet of a bloody chocolate

_childDocuments_.review: Glad the developers got the greenlight for a sequel. Really enjoyed this one. I haven't had to many stutters like many players here, or maybe I'm just used to them. The game runs buttery smooth for the most part, unless there's over 10 enemies on screen, some of the best arenas in the game, slow my game quite a bit and has plenty of stuttering. But that's completely understandable on my computer running a i5 4670k (10 year old cpu) and a gtx 1070 installed on a sata SSD.I kind of enjoyed the ease of using the block button in GR2, with a stamina meter that depletes if you use it too often. You can even upgrade your motherboard to the point where your able to block the mech horizontal lazer rays, and use a shriken to instantly stun and blitz to a tough enemy for an easy kill. Heck you can even use one of many over powered ultimate abilities if you want to completely destroy an entire crowd with ease.With the block button mechanic readily available, it seems like the developers heavily nerfed possibly one of the most highly skilled mechanics in the game. Remember in the first Ghostrunner when an enemy was firing shots at you, if you timed your sword attack at the exact time the lazer shot just about touched you, you could deflect the shot right back at your enemy. Yeah now when you swing, the lazer shot disappears but doesn't bother to deflect anymore. You have to use the block button to deflect the shots. This is especially noticeable in the 2nd to last stage where your using the wingsuit and there's a bunch of enemies firing shots at you all at once. You are unable to block while gliding in the air, but you can attack and use your special abilities. The story is just as laughable or even more so than the first game, which isn't a bad thing at all. The main issue here is Ghostrunner 2 tries to present its horrible story in cutscenes and loads of dialogue in the hub between missions (good thing you can skip most of it if you like). Although some of the dialogue and voice acting gave me a good laugh. I think keeping the story mostly in dialogue channels as you're exploring the world makes the most sense.If you enjoyed the first GR, you'll probably like this one. Even with OP abilities and blocking, I've died quite a bit in all the missions. This game can be quite a challenge for players who aren't used to playing fast paced first person parkour games.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute banger of a sequel to the first game and a fresh spin on an already fun genre. New ways to find collectibles are boggling my mind, exploring vertically and OPENLY, going wherever I want to. Wanna go slow? Take in the gorgeous environment, take a photo or two. Wanna go fast, like, really fast?? Hop on the bike and go full Mad Max road warrior on those enemies. There is a freedom to poke around that wasn't in the first one and it feels REWARDING. There's all kinds of stuff you can find and I enjoyed finding small easter eggs hidden throughout the environment. Don't get me wrong, the difficulty is tough--it feels harder than the first game--but it remains fair. There are tools at your disposal to deal with particularly annoying enemies and different routes to clear a room more easily. I don't feel hindered by the layout or the design of the enemies at all. The story is engrossing and the characters feel like they have more personality than in the first one. The world-building is great so far and I am growing attached to new characters purely because I get to see them more often and see how they develop throughout the story. Highly recommend if you are an adrenaline junkie and like brutal FPP combat. The soundtrack is excellent. The environments are breath-taking. The SPEED???? PHENOMENAL. 10/10 so much freakin fun holy wow awesome

_childDocuments_.review: More Ghostrunner but with much more refined and improved mechanics. The visuals, game play, and music just screams cyberpunk, a genre I absolutely love. The first section with the bike was pure adrenaline for me as you're zipping through tunnels and down Dharma tower needing to make split second adjustments to avoid slamming into your death.  The sections after it though seem to slow down a bit as it opens up to open ended mission design. It definitely takes away from the previously mentioned as you're just driving down open landscapes to get to certain arena type set pieces where there really isn't much in-between to worry about.Nonetheless, the positives absolutely outweigh the negatives for me. One More Level improved upon the first game while experimenting with a different way of challenging the player with it's fast paced, one hit death style game play with the bike. Definitely looking forward to any potential 3rd installment, they have a great universe here.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game, and while I don't mind this game, I'll say one huge gripe I have with this game. The parts in between levels where you're in the hideout are the most boring, stupid idea. The last game had non-stop action, with almost all the exposition being told to you while you play, which made the game constant action. Why would they change that in this? Sure, you might say, "They still tell you exposition while you play," and yeah, while that's true, I shouldn't have to dread ending the level due to boring slow-paced, mundane ♥♥♥♥. Oh, it is more than just slow, mundane, and boring; it also looks BAD. When you talk to characters, there are almost no animations to them. They strike one pose and stand in that same pose the entire time they talk to you, and their faces BARELY move at all when talking to you. It's mouth movements and maybe a slight eyebrow twitch, WOW! That being said, all the dialogue is skippable in those parts (thank god). I'll also add that the big open levels are cool, but at the same time, things are far too spread out, making it slow-paced, which again doesn't feel good. People have been complaining about glitchy things happening to them, and honestly, I've had that happen, too. Still, none of it is game-breaking, just sometimes awkward, funny or a minor inconvenience. Besides that, it's still an excellent game, and I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is... Well debatable for me. It's not good, but its a WHOLE lot of fun. I'll be honest here, my review is going to focus on the bad. I don't want to drone on about what everyone else already has. The game is crazy fun. It's as simple as that, but these 3 issues for me got in the way SO much, I almost did not leave my review as recommended:There are so many spots that are blatantly hidden areas with some secret inside, until you realize they actually aren't, and  this area is just not meant to be explored. It feels like the developer just forget to place the collectible inside. I get its not that kind of game; exploration is NOT to be encouraged here, but it sure does look like it is in game often times. When there IS a collectible, it's in an area that is easily accessible, and not at all off the beaten path, AND marked on your map.Dying sucks. Often times, falling off the path into the abyss takes WAY too long. Some levels also have you ascending upwards, making your fatal descent even longer. Even worse than this though, is how you can often just get completely stuck. You'll fall off the path, get yourself jammed between some of the bars, props, and meshes below the level, leaving it to you to find out how to hop around just right to escape it and finally face your actual death. Frustrating.The upgrades are boring. There's only 1 in fact that genuinely gives you an ability of sorts. I imagined this upgrade list would be packed full of changes to the player's maneuverability (being that the game is entirely focused on movement), but instead they are just plain, often scenario-specific, boosts. This really hampers down the excitement I got from picking up all the not-so-secret collectibles and earning enough money to keep the upgrades coming. In fact, I dismissed the upgrades entirely less than halfway through my play through.Level design (not visually) is... meant for maybe another game. This is not going back to the secret rooms with no secrets. This is something a bit worse. For just one example - there's SO many platforms (that you must run across to proceed) that are ridiculously large. The maps in general are just often WAY too large for their own good. I feel like we either need to crunch these down to remove all of the boring fluff, or make the player's base running speed WAY higher. Genuinely, there were so many times I stopped running across a huge bridge of sorts just to double check I couldn't actually run any faster, or there wasn't a "cooler" way to maneuver passed this section.I think all in all, Ghostrunner 2 failed in level design and execution. There are several other points I could nitpick, but they're not big enough a deal to even mention, so level design and execution is what damages it for me. The REST of the game however is, as you'd expect, a heart pumping blast to play, and the addiction to running is just as strong as ever since Ghostrunner 1, even when it had me running when and where I shouldn't have been far too often.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostrunner 2 is the definition of what a sequel should be. It improves upon all the tenants the first game set up and expands the world and gameplay in ways even fans weren't expecting.Visuals in this games are a subtly better than the first intallment but unfortunatelly there is no ray tracing support at the time of writing, with promises of full support in the near future. The game already looks good without it, it can only improve with its addition.Sound and music go harder than the original in almost every level, there are some supreme bangers in this game save for 1 or 2 stages you will be adding almost all of them to your music playlist no doubt.The gameplay includes everything you already knew from rail grinding and wall running to dashes and slowmo but it also adds new trinkets such as a gliding suit, ways to create new jumping points for your gap jammer and much more.There is also the element of story here which is greatly expanded. Characters are given time to breath and show their own personalities but this not being the focus of the game or having enough budget to allow for true engagement, you will find yourself yearning for the next "standard" level pretty quickly. Fortunately these stage are as short as can be so they function more like little add-ons rather than anything else.9/10. Great enough to stand up on its own against behemoths like Zelda and Spider-man at the game awards.

_childDocuments_.review: The first Ghostrunner game is far better than this one. Ghostrunner 2 is more focused with the maps than the combat. I've spent more time solving map puzzles than actually fighting enemies. That is, when the maps are loading properly. I've gotten stuck and fallen into the sky box multiple times. This is especially true on the desert maps, which are already extremely boring to play on because of the excessive size and dull gray color scheme. It's no surprise so much time was put into the over-designing of maps because the combat itself is lacking. The block feature is by far the worst addition in Ghostrunner 2. Players can lazily press a button and block barrages of bullets. The original Ghostrunner player could only block one projectile at once and it required good timing. This made the gameplay more fast paced and exciting as dodging and dashing were more important. The second game also has a lot of emphasis on the secondary abilities as they charge way too quickly and are necessary to complete the endless map puzzles. This would be less of a problem if ultimate abilities weren't added in. All these extra abilities make the sword play seem less important, which takes away from what made the original combat interesting. There is also too much emphasis on the story of the game. Ghostrunner was able to implement the story into the gameplay through in-game dialog. The story existed to enhance the gameplay, but Ghostrunner 2 feels like the opposite. The story takes priority, even if it negatively affects the gameplay. For example, the game is constantly being interrupted with safe hub scenes so the player can have boring conversations with boring NPCs. The deserts scenes are also proof of this. The writers really wanted Jack to leave the city without thinking about whether or not this would be good for gameplay. As a result, the game is now filled with extremely large, buggy, and dull desert maps which are not nearly as fun to play as the city maps.Then there is the inclusion of the motorcycle. Let's just say driving this motorcycle makes driving in Cyberpunk feel easy in comparison. Overall, Ghostrunner 2 is an alright game, but the original is much better. Overall, Ghostrunner is more exciting, more fast-paced, less buggy, and overall better designed than its sequel.
