_childDocuments_.review: I was introduced to the Persona franchise through gameplay of the original Persona 5, and had very fond memories of it, including its masterful aesthetic, memorable characters, and emotional storyline. However, fast forward a few years, and I've forgotten much of the details of the game I used to like so much. So when Persona 3 Reload came out, I was debating whether or not to begin this new game, or revisit a title I enjoyed in the past.I was very unsure about many things. I wasn't sure if I'd like the aesthetic, the story, and most importantly, the characters of P3R. I had seen many complaints about its shallow social links, or the boring Tartarus exploration compared to its more popular successor. But nevertheless, the story was new to me, so I gave the game a go.***P3R was the first and only Persona game that I fully played through, seeing as I merely watched P5 and then P5R. It's a game where being invested in the characters will drive you to see the game for its full potential. I was immediately interested in the protagonist for his unique, yet relatable personality, coupled with his memorable, even if not fully unique appearance. The theme of the game is by far its best strength; it explores a subject that everyone has questioned in their life, and as the protagonist and his friends grow, they become closer to their fated answer to this big question.Personally, I found its theme so profound for the reason that the characters fight for something so humble, compared to the grandiose goals of the P5 characters. And while I only became invested in a select few characters, they all contribute their own, each and individual importance to a grander meaning in the big picture.***The critiques online that I was initially concerned about never bothered me when I played through the game. I don't exactly have a gameplay background in other Persona games to compare the social links, but even though Tartarus was not hand-crafted and unique like P5's palaces, I still enjoyed it quite a lot. It never became too monotonous that I felt unwilling to explore.However, Tartarus began to feel a little grindy when I approached late game, before the final battle. It was then when I had to spend a few hours merely farming, but like the rest of my P3R experience, the monotonous gameplay led to something that made my grinding worthwhile. P3R often had interesting plot points between regular gameplay, and the ending was able to maintain both its hype and peaceful conclusion. Much like the calm after the storm, in a way.***I played through the game once, and the 130 hours was worth the experience. I enjoyed the game a lot, and more importantly, I enjoyed its story and characters a lot. If I were to pick between P3R and P5R, I'd say that P3R has a stronger protagonist and overarching theme, whereas P5R has a more memorable cast, with its striking aesthetic and exciting plot arcs.

_childDocuments_.review: An astounding story and an otherwise remarkable remake ravaged by a masterclass in anti-consumer practices and incompetence.'Episode Aigis', which serves as an epilogue to the base game and is a major component of the story that Persona 3 has to tell, is locked behind an additional paywall of £28.99. Furthermore, the game is riddled with DLCs which, in truth, do not contribute anything at all to the experience and you can get by just fine completely ignoring their existence, but slapping these on top of the already exorbitant £59.99 price tag for which you would expect to get a full game? It is akin to being spat on.The release itself is utterly pathetic, being riddled with performance issues, and outright preventing some individuals (myself included) from playing the game on PC. At the time of writing this review, It has been 8 months since the game has released, and these issues have yet to be addressed; safe to say, they likely never will be. (As a side note, there is plenty of troubleshooting discussion on Reddit which has led to some individuals successfully finding ways to fix some of these problems. However, these fixes are all obtuse 'band-aid' workarounds, and are not guaranteed to work for you).Circling back to the DLCs while we are still on the topic of incompetence, the actual implementation of most DLCs is inexplicably out of touch. Forgetting for a moment that they should just be a part of the base game, let us analyze the DLCs from a gameplay standpoint. The Personas start at random levels, often above where you currently are, instead of beginning at Lv.1. This is a very poor design choice seeing as the average player is not interested in trivializing parts of progression. The amusing cherry on top of all this is that these files are available in the base game files, making it possible to simply mod them into the game.What was supposed to be a faithful recreation of a timeless classic should have not been squandered like this. Persona 3 captured the hearts of many, inspiring them during their formative years by having a beautiful story to tell about the value of life and the importance of seizing every moment. Seeing it reduced to being just another victim of corporate greed and what is likely rushed development enforced by unreasonable deadlines, is greatly disheartening.Praying for the return of video game industry to a state of simply being a labor of love, where providing a complete and polished experience is prioritized above profit margins.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an improvement over the original persona 3, fes and portable in almost every single way. Better and more interesting combat, though it does remain largely unchanged (which is good). Direct control over your party which 3 and fes did not have. A more fleshed out story, slight adjustment to some of the social links, full voice acting for all social links in Japanese and English and not to mention the 'link' hangouts with your teammates which are basically just social links that don't actually level up. As a remake I think it succeeds on every level besides some very minor things like some goofy looking 3d animation in cutscenes. But in a 80 hour game that's an extremely minor nitpick. However I do think that persona 3 has some inherent issues that are pretty much engraved in its core so they were never going to be resolved with a remake. As opposed to persona 4 and 5 I think the world can feel quite empty. There often isn't much reason to go out and try many different ways of increasing your social stats for example. Once you have found the optimal ways to get the most points per time slot, there isn´t much of a reason to diverge. This is also true for other persona titles, however in persona 3 you get way less to experiment with and not many new things get added during your playthrough. This repetitive emptiness is also reflected in the dungeon design. While I am also not the biggest fan of persona 5 dungeons I do think tartarus is a bit too reliant on the (admittedly very solid) turn based combat. If you do not enjoy the turn based combat you will not like tartarus. This is also an issue in persona 4 but that game does a lot to make dungeons feel more distinct. Tartarus has a change up every block but otherwise it´s basically the most basic way to make a player grind. As a result the game is not very difficult. Even on the highest difficulty, merciless, most people who are familiar with smt games would not struggle much. This makes sense because of the inherent ´grindy´ design but it is still true. Surprisingly the addition of 'theurgy' which initially seemed to me like it would be way too strong ended up being quite well integrated and overall pretty balanced and enjoyable to use.The social links in persona 3 have always been a topic of debate among fans. As long as I have been a persona fan the general consensus among fans has always been that persona 3 has the better story while persona 4 has the better characters. Ofcourse ever since the introduction of p5 which achieved success beyond any previous persona entries combined this discourse has become more skewed towards p5 but I still think that the comparison of p3 and p4 makes more sense. Back to the social links themselves I think that some are absolutely fantastic while others leave something to be desired. I do enjoy the darker tone of most of them. I like that persona 3 is willing to have character's that are morally grey or that have problems that aren't resolved. However this is somewhat offset by the clunkiness with which some of these plotlines are written.Something I realised when playing reload is that I actually quite like the way the antagonists are written in this game. While I do not think it's always entirely intentional, the way they are portrayed leaves it up to the player to decide on where they stand. While over the top they are sympathetic figures, for the most part. Whenever they say things I am never fully convinced of their faults and while actions speak louder than words, I do think that their words could make up for it given the situation, narratively speaking that is.As for the story, I think it is conceptually very strong, but I have always felt that there was a lack of engagement. For me it never really felt gradual and I am glad to say that I do not find this as prevalent in reload. At helps that the world feels more lively purely because of the higher graphical fidelity. I understand criticism from people that wanted the femc option back from portable and I do think it should have been there, but as a persona 3 remake I can also understand the decision to not include it as some of the links are questionable at best and translating something that purely exist in a psp game would likely be quite a different task from looking at a PS2 title.Overall I would say that as a remake this game is near perfect, I haven´t even really mentioned it but I also really enjoyed the nnew soundtrack for this game. As a game I think persona 3 is great but not quite on the level of persona 4 and 5 though I do think those games feel a bit too goofy or cartoony at times. but that´s a different can of worms.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't planning on buying the game to be quite frank since I already own it on the PS2. In the end, I decided to get it since my partner was interested in it. So I ended playing with it myself and I have a couple of things to say. Firstly, I think ATLUS is extremely greedy to charge $94 CAD for a remake that doesn't have new content in it. Even when the game was on sale, it took me some convincing to decide to get it even though it wasn't for me initially. In the end I think it was a bit overpriced even if it was on sale. Secondly, the copy I bought 45$ back then on PS2 included the FES segment with Aegis. To my surprise, I've realized that now this part of the game that was included with the base game is now a $47 CAD dlc. So, in reality the remake costs $140 CAD. That's absolutely insane. I remember a time when I started to stop liking Squaresoft as a company and started considering ATLUS like the new golden standard for rpgs. Now, I'm starting to see ATLUS the same way I used to see Squaresoft back then. Don't get me wrong, it's nice to see this game with improved graphics, but those graphical revamps don't justify the insane price ATLUS is currently proposing. On top of that, they propose dlcs for costume. Yeah, it's just cosmetic in the end, but when your single player game that is a remake of an old game is already over 100$, maybe you should take a chill pill on the dlcs. Another negative point is that you have to deal with denuvo. Additionally, I personally think the soundtrack was better in the previous versions. This might be nostalgia, but I don't like the small modifications they've made on some of the tracks. Nothing game breaking, but it's a bit annoying. I wish there was an option to select the old ost in the options. Really, the worst aspect of the game is the insane greed of ATLUS. If you don't mind denuvo and if you really want the game, wait for a sale; it's clearly not worth paying full price.

Even for $100 for the premium edition, you're easily getting 100+ hours of gameplay. At 1 dollar per hour, you're more than getting your money's worth. Atlus has struck gold again, and now I'm hoping for a remake of the original 2 games (as well as a new game in the lineup).

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload leaves me conflicted.On one hand, it's undoubtably the worst Persona game I've played. The combat is fun, although very easy and stagnant, as you find yourself fighting the same bosses and enemies repeatedly in Tartarus. Say what you will about the ups and downs that were Persona 5's dungeon design, or even Persona's 4 mind-numbing floor layouts; at least those made me feel something. Tartarus made me feel nothing but boredom and complete frustration. You just go up the exact same floors that are only differentiated by a new code of paint. It's tolerable when putting on a podcast or something, but on it's own, it's only saved by the combat system being again, still very enjoyable. Aside from the combat, the other half of this game and any other Persona game is the day to day life of a highschool student. Here, I'm feeling like bored as well. There are some incredible social links, like Akinari and Maiko, but a good chunk of these social links involve some whatever characters. It's also stupidly easy to max out your social stats halfway through the game, and you're left with not much to do. There's nothing you can do to aid in bettering your teammates in combat in the overworld (like the darts in Persona 5 Royal) or even some stupid activities like the small-time vibes that the activities in Persona 4 Golden had. You can either level up a social link, level up your stats, or go to Tartarus. Again, it's mind-numbing. None of this was helped by a pretty weak soundtrack. The new songs added to Reload all sound amazing (Color Your Night my beloved), but the redone soundtrack sounds underwhelming and fails to capture the spirit of the original tracks from what I've heard on YouTube and such. I won't go further into comparing this to the original since I haven't played any other version other than this, but I will say the visual style in Reload, as stylish as it is, does seem to lose some of the edge the original had. On the other hand, I think what really saved this game was the themes and the incredible story. Persona 3 Reload has, by far, my favorite Persona story and characters. Hell, this is one of my favorite stories ever told in a video game before. I can't do it justice here, but the fear of death and the urge to continue on in face of that are masterfully done here to create such a gripping and emotional story that masterfully executes and explores these themes. The main cast are all lovable, and I looked forward to every full moon where I could see them interact more. The ending is one of the rare instances I cried my eyes out during anything. It's just all so well done. Seriously, this narrative is incredible and absolutely shot this game from a 6 to an 8 for me. The gameplay, on the other hand, ranges from enjoyable at best to boring at worst. This is still a heavy recommendation if you like Persona at all, obviously. Just don't go in expecting the level of complexity 5 or even 4 had gameplay wise.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 FES was the first game that got me into the Persona series as well as mainline Shin Megami Tensei. I had enjoyed the narrative the most while also appreciating the more unique gameplay compared to both earlier and later entries (I am a rare Persona fan that has actually played Persona 2, but not rare enough to be a Persona 1 player.) I had my gripes with the original in the form of more janky game mechanics like downing enemies and bosses being very clearly overpowered for chain-stunning, party members having very inconsistent viability when your only method of control was the tactics system (aside from having direct control on the main character), not much development for nearly half of the party because they lacked social links (unless you played portable, which would still have the same problem anyway just with the same gender as your MC of choice), the fatigue system as a whole (even if it became irrelevant in the mid-game and onward), and the lack of presence some antagonists had.Persona 3 Reload has fixed just about all of this for me. I'm still going through the game (currently in September, so I only have a few months left in the game) but I feel I can confidently say that P3R, even without The Answer, is the definitive way to experience Persona 3. While I wish The Answer was in the Reload from the get-go, despite the very controversial status it holds due to its quality in FES, I feel that the main story of Persona 3 with FES and Portable's QoL changes are more than enough to make the game stand on its own. Maybe Atlus will just give us The Answer as DLC anyway. I can actually mix and and match my team without concern of, say, Koromaru being near worthless in FES because his skillset is primarily Dark magic so he'd miss his instakills when I want him to use Fire skills or whatever. In Reload I can actually make use of Koromaru as a mixed Dark/Fire magic user and support with crit boosts and increasing my team's physical damage output. I can actually go at my own pace and take a moment to grind if I need money or extra EXP for my lower level party members without fear of the fatigue system just ruining the pace. Direct control on all party members does have the side effect of making the game generally easier, but I think this is worthwhile to actually have enjoyable gameplay and shifting the difficulty around having actual coverage as a team than just on your main character while your party members are forced to play support. Even then, if direct control just isn't the way, the tactics system is still there. It's watered down though which is a shame, but it at least is usable. And for what it's worth, playing through the game on Merciless has still brought a surprising amount of challenge for me despite having direct control on all my party members.

_childDocuments_.review: "Persona 3 Reload" by Atlus is a highly anticipated remake of the classic "Persona 3," a game that originally set the foundation for the modern Persona series with its innovative blend of JRPG mechanics and life simulation. "Persona 3 Reload" aims to bring the beloved game to contemporary audiences with updated graphics, enhanced gameplay, and additional content, all while preserving the core elements that made the original a cult classic."Persona 3 Reload" follows the journey of a group of high school students in Tatsumi Port Island who join the Specialized Extracurricular Execution Squad (SEES) to combat Shadows, mysterious creatures that appear during the Dark Hour. This hidden hour occurs between one day and the next, where ordinary people are transmogrified into coffins while the members of SEES battle against the supernatural threats.The protagonist, a transfer student named Makoto Yuki, discovers his ability to summon Personas, manifestations of his inner self. The SEES team comprises various memorable characters, each with unique backgrounds and personal struggles: Yukari Takeba: A classmate and initial ally who is haunted by her father’s mysterious death.Junpei Iori: A jovial but insecure member who provides comic relief and depth.Akihiko Sanada: The disciplined and strong senior with a tragic past.Mitsuru Kirijo: The stoic and intelligent heiress of the Kirijo Group, deeply connected to the Dark Hour’s origin.Aigis: A humanoid robot with emotions who develops a profound bond with the protagonist.The core gameplay of "Persona 3 Reload" retains the hybrid nature of dungeon crawling and social simulation but introduces numerous enhancements to streamline and modernize the experience.The central dungeon, Tartarus, is a massive, ever-changing tower that players must ascend. Each full moon marks a significant plot progression with a major boss battle. The remake introduces quality-of-life improvements such as enhanced navigation, streamlined battle mechanics, and better AI for party members, addressing some of the original game’s criticisms.The turn-based combat system remains strategic and engaging, with players managing their party's Personas, exploiting enemy weaknesses, and executing powerful All-Out Attacks. New features like revamped skill systems and improved enemy behaviors add depth and challenge to battles.Outside of Tartarus, players engage in daily life activities such as attending school, participating in clubs, and building relationships with Social Links, which are pivotal for Persona development."Persona 3 Reload" introduces more nuanced interactions and additional Social Links, providing richer narrative experiences. The calendar system, which dictates the passage of time and availability of activities, has been refined for better pacing and accessibility.The remake boasts significantly improved graphics, with high-definition character models, environments, and animations that bring the world of Tatsumi Port Island to life. The game’s signature dark, moody atmosphere is enhanced by these visual upgrades. The soundtrack, composed by Shoji Meguro, is a standout feature, blending J-Pop, rock, and orchestral music. New tracks and rearranged classics maintain the original’s essence while adding freshness to the auditory experience."Persona 3 Reload" includes new story elements, side quests, and character interactions that expand upon the original narrative. These additions provide more context and depth to the game’s lore and characters, making the experience more immersive and rewarding.Numerous quality-of-life improvements have been implemented, such as more intuitive menus, auto-save features, and enhanced tutorials. These changes make the game more user-friendly, especially for new players who may be unfamiliar with the series’ mechanics."Persona 3 Reload" successfully revitalizes a classic game for a new generation, combining modern enhancements with the core elements that made the original beloved by fans. With its compelling story, deep characters, strategic gameplay, and atmospheric presentation, the remake offers both nostalgia for returning players and a fresh, engaging experience for newcomers. Atlus has crafted a remake that honors its legacy while setting new standards for what a modern JRPG can achieve. "Persona 3 Reload" is a must-play for any RPG enthusiast and a testament to the enduring appeal of the Persona series.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried my best to come into this remake with  as open a mind as possible, especially being someone who has played both P3 and P3:FES many times... But this just feels like Persona 5 with a blue/Persona 3 skin. This remake is painfully easy. The Tired system being COMPLETELY removed is just a tragedy because it ensured that you either could not get to checkpoints in Tartarus or you would just a somewhat difficult time getting there. Junpei never annoyed me but now he sounds hyped on too much coffee sometimes. Yukari isn't a b*tch now but any time she gets slightly excited, it's like her voice wants to peak whatever headset I'm using. And the singer... Like, she's not bad or anything. But these songs clearly aren't made for her voice type. Hers feels more like a quiet cafe scene. With the guitars and overall "get up and rock" vibe from the originals, her voice simply falls flat for me. I went and looked her up and like I just said, for other music, she's good. But this isn't P5. This isn't a chic game. More powerful vocals would have paired better. But whatever, when I'm in Tartarus, I just have the sound off now, as I have no interest in listening to P5 themes while playing (since apparently that's an option). The game is too... polished. Saturated in flashy crap. The roughness and edge has been watered down considerably.And finally in Tartarus... Just. let. me. grind.  there's just too much talking. Random conversations about literally nothing. I liked the separation of "hehe haha school life" in the day and "let's get down to work" at night vibes from the originals. As soon as I turn a corner, "HEY, THERE'S A CHEST OVER THERE. MAYBE WE SHOULD--". YES, team. I have eyes. I am not 5 years old. Let ME explore the game. It's the same problem I had with P5. I just feel like the players' mental capacity is heavily underestimated the further along the series goes. Classic case of needing more "SHOW, don't tell". Just let me play.I planned on not even writing a review at all for this game but with Persona 3 being in my top 10 games of all time, I kind felt like I had to. Unfortunate, but I doubt the series will go in a different direction. And that's okay, I guess. I've still got my old PS2 for when I want a real experience again.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is a breathtaking re-imagining of a beloved classic, bringing a new layer of depth and complexity to an already great game, a story so connected with reality and filled with raw emotions. It manages to stay so grounded for a story about exploring the human psyche despite its existing in a medium that tends to be chosen for stories that are the complete opposite in that they are as far from reality as you can get. Every Character, Yukari, Junpei, Mitsuru, Akihiko, ♥♥♥♥♥ and Aigis get their own character development throughout as well as having to face the reality of Persona 3 Reload's finale and how they will choose to live on after these events. A soundtrack that is so well written and composed that many consider that you are buying a soundtrack with a game rather than vice versa because it is that good with remakes of old tracks from persona 3 that sound new and fresh and new songs that fit in perfectly such as "Color Your Night." Social links are a staple of the persona series and they don't disappoint here, with a rich cast of side characters as well as having additional scenes for the cast that weren't in the original game, giving you a break from the tower of Tartarus which has had many quality of life changes added helping the flow of the game and keeping it from becoming stale. A masterclass example of a remake done right.it’s an unforgettable journey through the depths of the human psyche and learning to face death... a must play for any fan of the series or those looking to start.

In terms of 2024 releases, this is my GOTY and I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ what you say.While i do prefer Persona 4's social links, Persona 3 owns up for that in story and Aigis (without giving spoilers) has one of the best social links, not just in Persona 3 but in any Persona game. Makoto (The Protag) is the biggest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I absolutely love him for that and he's also my favorite Persona Protag hands down. The music is absolutely great but songs like Mass Destruction is just butchered and lose a lot of charm of what made the original great. I've listened to both of them back and forth and the original is just better in every single aspect. But Color Your Night, Memories Of You, Changing Seasons are absolutely fantastic and I will continue to blast it to death in my free time.The story is just fantastic. I've never been the type of cry at video games. I've teared at games here and there but only 2 games have made me full out break down, which being Red Dead 2 and now recently: Persona 3 Reload. Everything from start to finish, you don't want to put that keyboard (or controller) down for a second! Every character is fleshed out and makes it hard to spend your time with one specific person. You'll know people's strength and weakness and that's what makes this game hit harder. And it's all worth it in the end. I'm not going to spoil the ending of Persona 3 because it's worth going in blind but what an ending i'll never forget. It has a beautiful message about life and death and I'll take that advice forever and ever.Combat is the biggest weakness outside of music. Persona 5 has the best combat in the games with it's interactions and guns but Persona 3 Reload's combat isn't bad in the slightest! Just not really appealing compared to Persona 5's but.. Persona 3 Reload's combat has the best combat UI though.Overall: Persona 3 Reload is a absolutely fun and a gorgeous remake and has entered my top 3 video games of all time. A fantastic game that is an experience everyone should enjoy. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game genuinely saved my life, it taught me how to recognise I have OCD which pushed me to experiencing Derealization episodes (Which is where you believe life isn't reality, pretty much it's like living through hell itself).I was deadset on unaliving myself the next time I had a Derealization episode, there are 2 characters called Takaya & Jin throughout the course of the game taught me that I suffered from intrusive thoughts as apart of my OCD and ways to calm it down. I still do struggle with my OCD, but ever since I played Persona 3 back in 2022 I haven't had a Derealization episode since. Even though most people dislike Takaya and Jin because they lacked depth in the original, the minimal interactions I had on this game are the sole reason Persona 3 holds a special place in my heart. If you struggle with intrusive thoughts or OCD, I believe this game is worth a shot to see if they'll resonate with you. Here's one quote in particular that is spoken by Jin that stuck with me the most: "Don't be bound by the past, don't look to the future. Simply live in the moment". I applied this quote to myself, instead of fixating on my intrusive thoughts I opted to just focus on what's happening currently in the moment and it actually calmed my OCD down. I didn't know I had OCD back then, but for some reason unknown to me at that point it calmed me down. After in-depth researching regarding OCD I now know why. You push out intrusive thoughts, they'll come back harder. If you try to argue with the intrusive thought itself, you make it stronger and worse. So why did this quote in particular be the thing that got me to deal with my OCD? Because you have to fight the thought with a specific thought that doesn't dissect the intrusive thought or ignores/pushes it out. So let's say I have an OCD impulse that goes like "I have to check every reply to hate me", by telling myself to not fixate on the future and just simply live in the moment I have dealt with the thought in a way that hasn't strengthened it. I don't argue with the contents of the intrusive thought and just deal with it as a concept, if that make sense. There's plenty of other quotes that stuck with me because of these 2 characters, I am forever grateful that this game got remade to breathe new live into these 2 new characters. While people still aren't a fan of Jin, some people have became a fan of Takaya. Having my #1 comfort characters being liked by people is honestly one of the best gifts to ever been given.

_childDocuments_.review: 🎮 Gameplay 🎮☑ Great🔲 Good🔲 It's just gameplay🔲 Bad🔲 Awful🖥️Graphics 🖥️🔲 Great☑Good🔲 Decent🔲 Bad🔲 Awful☠️ Difficulty ☠️🔲 Insane🔲 Difficult🔲 Easy to learn / Hard to master☑ Average🔲 Easy🔲 Shut off your brain⛏️ Grind ⛏️🔲 Bring over night snacks.☑ Average🔲 Easy🔲 No grind👨‍👨‍👦 Audience 👨‍👨‍👦🔲 All☑ Adults☑ Teens🔲 Kids🎵 Audio 🎵☑ Great🔲 Good🔲 Bad🔲 AwfulBugs☑ None that I encounted🔲 Minor🔲 Some🔲 Infested📖 Story 📖🔲 Great☑ Good🔲  Average🔲 Awful🔲 No Story🕓 Game Length 🕓☑  Never ending☑  Long (20-60 hours)🔲 Average (8 - 20 hours)🔲 Short (3 - 6 hours)🔲 Very short(0 - 2 hours)💰 Price 💰 🔲 Free☑  On sale🔲 Worth the price🔲 Avarage🔲 Not recommended💬 Comments 💬Description:Persona 3 Reload retains its core hybrid of traditional role-playing and social simulation gameplay, but is overhauled aesthetically, graphically and mechanically to integrate systems and features that have been introduced to the Persona series since the original Persona 3's release, specifically deriving from quality-of-life improvements first implemented in Persona 5 (2016). In addition to foundational overhauls, Reload refines numerous elements of its graphics and interface to reflect the updated presentation of subsequent entries. For story-sensitive tasks, objective descriptions have been added below the display for the date, time of day and moon phase that list actions that must be performed to progress the narrative, which is functionally similar to Persona 5's heads-up display. The map display has also been improved in function and form over the original Persona 3, having been expanded in size in addition to depicting more intricacies about the surrounding environment, and now placing markers on important locations that need to be visited for story purposes, much like Persona 5's map.The ability for the protagonist to run through areas has also been added.Positives:If you prefer turn based and not time based or free for all then you'll enjoy the remakes combat system. Normally in persona games you feel rushed. It makes you feel as if you need to go into the midnight hour asap. However in this persona game you don't feel that way. It feels more focused on the story and social aspects of the game which feels less stressful. The game has a lot of replayability. Choosing different paths, relationships, persona's each time.Negatives:If you're like me and set camra sensativity on max like a crazy person then the camra speed may be a little slow for you. While you can set the sensativity it doesn't seem to change it very much. However if you're not insane keep it default in most games this wont be an issue.I couldn't relate or enjoy the personality of most characters. Except Junpei, but in a VERY bad way. IMO one of the most annoying characters I seen in a video game. There were only a small amount of characters I did like.Final Thoughts:The game is nice for those who played the first Persona 3 and great for those who have never played it. It takes you back to a time before the changes to the series like Persona 5 Royal and focuses more on the social aspects of the game. I bought the game while it was on sale and it was more than worth it. I would recommend getting it while it's on sale but I'd be more than willing to buy the game at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews for games, but I feel like I am obligated to, as it's the first game to ever make me cry and genuinely help me realize something in my own life as well.I never finished P5R so I felt like I had to finish this one and since I wanted to play the original, then I had no reason not to. I heard that a lot of the issues in the OG were fixed or made more enjoyable and it shows as Tartarus is a blast to explore, social links really make you feel for the characters or cheer them on, and the slow realization that in the end, even if there's a happy ending, sacrifices must be made, and if you play the game you'll see what I mean.The real reason this game grabbed me so much was the main character, he's a blank canvas, despite other Persona protagonists feeling that way, this one made me feel like I was answering to things to my decisions, that *that* would be the option I would've made if I was actually in his shoes. My social links felt like actual bonds and the emotion was poignant, I haven't had the most decided or balanced mental IRL and a lot of the meanings or themes of the game hit hard, it made me think about what I was doing with my life and how I should deal with it myself but not with the feeling I was alone. I romanced Mitsuru in my playthrough, despite being aromantic, I still felt the love form and how since it was my decisions, it felt like that love was mutual between us, now I know that sounds a bit weird but it's a genuine thing I felt and even if it's weird, screw it, I was weird the moment I came into this world. This game made me re-think my life while I still had the time to, and made me feel such poignant emotions I hadn't felt in years since my Grandfather passed away almost 4 years now, I urge you to give it a try, even if you don't like it, I don't want to spoil it for you.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion the definitive way to play Persona 3. (No spoilers)As a huge fan of the franchise, I heavily recommend this game to people who want to try a Persona game for the first time. For reference the only other version of Persona 3 I've beaten is Portable. Even without the playable female protagonist, the base game includes all the content from Portable and adds new scenes, side quests and voiced dialogue for every social link scene. I loved this game so much I'm going to buy Episode Aigis when it comes out in September. Don't be discourage by my play time, you can beat the game in roughly 80 hours if you mainline it. I just spend extra time grinding to kill optional bosses. Also the game runs perfectly on Steam Deck. The biggest flaw with this game is the flaw from the original game; Tartarus. Don't get me wrong, this version is way more fun than Portable's version of Tartarus. However, it is still very repetitive and can get boring if you spend too much time grinding in the dungeon. To explain, Tartarus is a procedurally generated dungeon where you fight shadows in turn based combat to level up and acquire new personas. There are hundreds of floors in Tartarus and more floors unlock as you progress through the game. I really recommend exiting Tartarus if you feel you are getting tired of dungeon crawling. The game is designed to break up the monotony of Tartarus by going on dates, hanging out with your favourite characters, or even walking your dog. If you like this game, I heavily recommend Persona 5 Royal as it's my favourite game of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: - Graphics are great. (Basically P5R but updated)- Tartarus Dungeons are less of a slog (Still tedious, but much better than FES)- Quality of Life improvements from P5R - Social Links are improved.The Bad:- The new bright artstyle and lighting brings down the tone of the game and goes against the atmospheric suspense the narrative is trying to paint.- Certain FES features removed (ability to choose between multiple clubs, characters commenting on outfits)- Bad DLC practices (locking art and soundtracks behind an application, selling digital deluxe package and not including the Answer, combining bgm tracks and outfits to the Answer to inflate the cost and not giving option to buy separately.)- Voice direction (This one is a bit of a hit or miss, some voice lines sound great, while others are less than stellar. Notably Akihiko comes to mind as sounding like a gruff 20-30 year old, and some social link dialogue having bad voice direction [Hanged] where the animation and dialogue doesn't match up.)- Bad DLC Implementation (If you use the BGM tracks from pre-order, it overrides all P3R tracks, including boss tracks).- Lack of music variety (this is a bit of a nitpick since it's a preference thing, but I found the variety in P4G and P5R much more diverse.)This was a hard game to decide on whether to recommend or not, since I just finished FES before jumping into Reload. If this is your first experience with Persona 3, I do recommend Reload over FES due to the quality of life improvements. If you're coming off P5R and expecting more of the same, don't, the pacing of P3R is a lot slower and it's closer to the original P3 than newer titles.Wait for it to go one sale before grabbing it, it's certainly not worth the $70. Avoid the DLC like the plague. Reviews are Mostly Negative for a reason.

_childDocuments_.review: A generation-defining title, properly remastered for 2024.This reload feels like Persona 5 repurposed for Persona 3. You can see it through the 3D cutscenes, the NPC models running around the school, or the 3D models of personas; it is as if they directly threw in P5 assets into this. I was somewhat disappointed by the lack of effort, if not redeemed by P3R designing one of the most aesthetically pleasing pause menus that you'll see anywhere.But it is also due to that very utilization of these P5 storytelling techniques, that P3R is not only a faithful remake of Persona 3, it elevates the delivery of Persona 3's story. Many pivotal scenes that were recaptured with animated films and/or 3D cutscenes give it so much more emotional heft to the moment, that even as someone who has relived the moments many times in previous iterations of P3, still brought me to tears. The addition of "Social Link Episodes" provides deeper connection to the important storylines such as establishing a direct connection between Makoto and  tying loose plot points such as the aftermath of , and simply to get to know better the SEES members that are not part of the regular Social Links. P3R through the above, managed to make what was already a sharp, focused narrative of P3, even sharper. Persona 3 is using its story to convey a message, a message that anyone playing it can perceive  and resonate with its profoundness: the "answer to life".In an effort to make these "Social Link Episodes" rewarding, they reward players with an unlocked persona ready to be fused upon completing them. I have my past qualms about the end-game persona rosters in P3, especially with how there's a scarcity of strong personas between Levels 60-75. Locking more of these personas through these episodes makes the whole fusion process towards the end game even more rough, which was definitely felt in my playthrough (note that the persona roster for base P3R is exactly the same as the original P3). Not detrimental, but the lack of the usual progression curve of swapping personas every month or so was palpable, as I stuck with personas with the base level of ~55+ for far, far too long.And for some godforsaken reason, P3 Reload removed triangle fusions. Why limit the creativity and art of persona fusion for no reason, we will never know. Major minus points.The plus side is bringing in P5 modernization, which means a whole slew of passive skills to play with, and reworking Dark and Light elements to P5 standards, which massively improves the viability of two party members. The Theurgy gimmick is a welcome addition, and an overall balance and power adjustments in phys/magic and the skillsets of some personas makes for a more smooth and balanced game.Though I may lament the rehash of P5 storytelling techniques, P3 Reload does in fact, have completely remade VFX of its skills, to mixed results, if I may add. Vorpal Blade and Black Viper may be the some of the best remakes, but basic elemental magic and things like Megidolaon even, lacks the oomph from past iterations of the skill.Tartarus, the crown jewel of lazy level design in Persona 3, received overhauls that make the climb less monotonous. Redesigning the blocks with different models, increasing the number of random events that could occur in each floor, alongside repurposing Monad and shuffle time, was some of the key changes done to achieve so.The reloaded OST is a mixed bag for me, "Color Your Night" is an excellent addition, lukewarm about "It's Going Down Now", and "Memories of You" is irreplaceable to me. I will be the first to admit that I let my nostalgia bias affect me, particularly because "It's Going Down" significantly reduced my chances of listening to "Mass Destruction". What I do notice and appreciate from the reloaded soundtracks however, is the addition of the "Memories of You" leitmotif to a lot of the soundtracks, similar to what they've done with the start menu of P4, which really hit hard upon realization. Doing it the P3R way is a subtler foreshadowing that is more ubiquitous, which is a nice little enhancing touch to the experience.I want to reiterate that Persona 3 Reload is  definitive way to experience Persona 3 at the time of writing, and the fact that it shares many familiar elements to Persona 5 is perhaps a deliberate choice to ease in players who first played Persona 5. Whether you are playing Persona 3 for the first time or reliving P3 from past memories, Persona 3 Reload is a title worthy of celebration.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my second mainline Persona game after playing Persona 4 Golden back in 2020. P4G is one of my favorite persona games, and I did find myself constantly comparing this game to P4G, even if I didn't mean to. The activities in Reload weren't as extensive or exciting as in Golden, but the key parts of any Persona game were all here, all of which I loved. There were times that exploring Tartarus felt a bit like an unnecessary grind, eventually I got into a pretty good rhythm and enjoyed all of my ventures into its many many floors.The biggest strength of this game is its cast of characters, which have to be one of my favorites from any game that I've played recently, possibly even more than Golden if I'm completely honest. I genuinely enjoyed all of the time that I got to spend with all of the characters on this game, which culminated in one of the most beautiful and bittersweet endings that I've experienced in a game in a long time. I know a lot of people that said they bawled their eyes out at the end, and while I didn't personally cry, the feelings were very real in me. Overall, i would recommend this game to just about anyone, be they newcomers to the series or series veterans.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 FES is one of my favorite games of all time, first played it all the way back in High School and have been a fan since. So I had a lot of expectations going into Reload, what I was expecting was a faithful yet definitive edition of Persona 3. After 30 hours I think I'm confidant enough to say yes, with some minor gripes that are not going to bug the casual player.Almost everything from the original P3 makes it in here, Social Links, requests, same story, same characters and only one main dungeon throughout the entire game. If you're going in this game from Persona 5 please remember that while systematically it is similar, the game's entire structure is different. But this is great imo, because the structure still works great for me 14 years later. The battle mechanics and Social Link mechanics have been vastly improved and modernized. If you were turned off by P3's aged combat and Social Link system, fear no more. If you are familiar with Persona 5's combat and Confidant system, you will feel right at home. My only gripe with Reload is the decision to not include the Female Protagonist option from Persona 3 Portable, including this inclusive and loved feature would vastly improve this game's quality and replayability immensely, this would make this the true definitive way to play and experience Persona 3. This doesn't downgrade Reload's overall quality but it's a feature I still wish they included. Overall, If you want to experience one of the most unique and emotional JRPG's of all time, I highly recommend this if you can at full price, or get it first thing it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR the new coat of paint is brilliant and it's still the best entry in the series.Persona as a franchise is unabashedly the best and worst of anime. It's painfully heavy-handed with its messaging, but also refreshingly sincere. P3 was my first foray into the series and remains my favorite. I played the original release with the awful dub being the only option. Fortunately, the JP audio is available on this release. The translation quality however, is still typical of Atlus. For some bizarre reason, they've decided to keep some of the quirks of the original dub script. One that immediately stands out is Junpei referring to Yukari as "Yuka-tan" even though he says "Yukaricchi" in the audio. There's just no good reason for it.For me, the life-sim parts are the enjoyable parts of the game. I play every Persona by blasting through the dungeon section in one visit as far as the game will let me go, so I can maximize the time spent on the narrative. I started on normal difficulty, and the game gives you an option to lower the difficulty whenever you die. At some point I ran into a boss I couldn't steamroll, so I went down to the lowest difficulty and never looked back. Peaceful difficulty gives you infinite full hp/mp res on death, so you can never lose. There are no penalties for lower difficulty. No Persona game is short, so it's a significant investment for anyone looking to dive in. But I think P3 has the strongest cast and the most interesting setting. Between the original, P3P, and Reload, it's an easy call to recommend Reload. Taking it a step further and putting P3 Reload against P4 Golden and P5 Royal, P3 Reload is still my recommendation. They're all great games in their own right, but I've never been fond of the boonies setting in P4, nor the "adults are bad" theming of P5. The only caveat is you might want to wait for the inevitable DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve finally managed to experience the game for all it has to offer, and I have a lot to say. My journey into the Persona franchise started back in 2019. 	I was rambling on about JJBA to a friend of mine when he whipped out his phone and showed me a gif of the MC from p3FES shooting himself. I thought it was the funniest ♥♥♥♥ ever and immediately wanted to know where it was from. After being told about the game, I immediately went looking for a way to play it. The only ps2’s in my house were both Japanese, and I didn’t feel like learning another language just to play a game, nor did I have the time. We also had a ps3 lying around, but I was a broke high school student so its not like I had money to throw on games. Leaving me to settle with the only choice I had left, emulation. It got the job done. I was playing p3FES in all of its low res, polygon glory. 	It was nothing like I had ever experienced before, sure I had my fair share of turn- based combat before, Mario and Luigi Partners in time, Chrono Trigger, but nothing to this extent. The way the personas emerged from each character was simply enthralling. Its combat was fun and engaging, even though I had a rough time understanding it at the start. The social school / sim aspect was something also new to me. Going around the city, talking to the other characters, learning about their goals and aspirations, wants and needs, desires and fears, absolute peak. I remember being introduced to Kenji, dude was something. Took you out to grab a bite, then started, with no filter, telling me how much he loved older women…from that moment on I knew that this character was the best, and I immediately went about ranking him up, he’s my very first max social link I completed in the entire franchise. Bro knows what he wants and has great taste, what can i say, he’s just like me fr. 	Sadly my little zoomer brain could not be entertained by the game for long, i found most of the plot dumping boring and even the combat, as much as I loved the animations, got tedious for me.Finally after the Chariot Arcana boss fight I dropped the game. It wouldn't be until the winter of 2020 that i would return to the Persona franchise, but not to complete p3fes, I had a new entry that caught my eye, the pc port of p4g, currently only playable on the ps vita. 	I spent hundreds of hours in that game, combing over each and every character, min maxing my personas, grinding out social links or simply just listening to the amazing soundtrack as I explored the town of Inaba. That game changed me, and as silly as it sounds, gave me a reason to keep on living. I don’t cry that often, I'm not fond of shedding tears, I don't like the mess they cause and the feeling I get in my chest as it tightens. However, as “Never more” began playing over the final credits of p4g, I couldn’t stop the waterfall. Since my completion of p4g, I have played through:P2 IS P4 AUP5RP5 StrikersPQPQ 2Which leads me to now, the remaster of p3, p3Reload. This game is amazing. I feel that since I've had the chance to both grow and mature since originally starting p3fes, I have come to love the dark and somber tone of this game.It’s made me reflect on how I use and spend my time. We all have a clock ticking, and once it reaches zero, it's over. Maybe you believe in the afterlife, maybe you don’t, but in the end we all run out of time. That doesn’t mean we should fear the end, but embrace each and every day that we have. Meet new people, try new things, connect with those whom you may have not seen in a while, call your parents, go and see them, that’s the message I got from p3r, go out and enjoy life. tl:dr Go out and touch some grass.

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT something that has any business being released as a full-price game in 2024, nevermind the separate add-ons.Sure, a LOT of work went into this. The graphics are OK (if you enable VSync), performance is fine, the soundtrack catchy, and the game does a good job of explaining all its mechanics from the ground up, which will not only help you with this title, but also all other games in the genre.However, main gameplay is just plain repetitive and boring. Grind social stats day after day, grind a procedurally generated dungeon night after night, grind your way through combat with blandly generic enemies (even on the hardest level, it's always the same: figure out their weak spots, if any, employ the right attacks, heal a bit, rinse, repeat). That soundtrack? It's good, but waaaay too short to cover all the boredom.The apparently highly-rated story unfolds very, very slowly, and, other than being PAINFULLY cringe at times, could have been told in 20% of the time. In 2009 (the year this game nominally takes place), you might have gotten away with that. But we've, like, progressed waaaay past the point where this title is worth your money, unless you're the SEVERELY nostalgic type.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are using a gamepad, the Key Configuration is useless. In short, the only thing it can achieve is swap A and B.There are 2 important rules: 1. You cannot assign one key for two function, no matter whether they use the same key by default. 2. The custom setting cannot be saved if any function does not get its key.By default, "Common -> Scroll Page (Right)" and "Field/Dungeon -> Auto-Recover" shares key RB, while "Common -> Scroll Status Screen (Right)" and "Field/Dungeon -> Dash" shares key RT. I cannot swap the key for Auto-Recover and Dash. If I set "Field/Dungeon -> Dash" to RB, by rule 1, both "Common -> Scroll Page (Right)" and "Field/Dungeon -> Auto-Recover" are cleared. Vice versa, setting "Field/Dungeon -> Auto-Recover" to RT clears "Common -> Scroll Status Screen (Right)". Trying to set those two functions under "Common" to RB or RT will then clear "Dash" and "Auto-Recover". In short, based on rule 1, any key by default serveing more than one function cannot be changed unless you can assign different keys for them.Even worse, assigning some keys causes a deadlock. For instance, "Event/Movie -> Next Message" is by default key Y and it does not allow customization. That is fine. However, you can assign Y to some other function, which will clear "Event/Movie -> Next Message" leaving it empty. Further, "Event/Movie -> Next Message" does not allow customization, this means you cannot assign it with any key, you cannot even assign Y back. Based on rule 2, this setting cannot be saved or fixed, the only thing you can do now is discard change and quit setting.I am not saying I cannot play a game with its default key config. I just wonder how can such a Key Configuration system, showing incapability in logic, appears in a game at this price.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is nothing short of a masterpiece! From the moment I dove into this reimagined classic, I was captivated by its stunning visuals and the seamless blend of old and new elements. The art style is breathtaking, and the character designs are more vibrant than ever, breathing fresh life into familiar faces.One of the standout features of this game is its incredible soundtrack. The music is truly inspiring, perfectly capturing the emotional highs and lows of the narrative. Each track enhances the immersive experience, making battles and exploration feel exhilarating. I often find myself humming the melodies long after I’ve put the controller down!The incorporation of cutscenes from the anime adds a brilliant touch. These moments not only enhance the storytelling but also provide a nostalgic nod to fans of the original game. They’re beautifully animated and perfectly timed, making pivotal moments even more impactful.The gameplay mechanics have also seen an impressive overhaul. The turn-based combat is engaging and strategic, allowing players to experiment with different party compositions and tactics. Each encounter feels fresh and rewarding, keeping you on your toes throughout your journey.Overall, Persona 3 Reload is a triumph that successfully honors the legacy of its predecessor while introducing exciting new elements. Whether you're a longtime fan or new to the series, this game offers an unforgettable experience. Big thumbs up for a remarkable revival that’s sure to leave a lasting impression!

_childDocuments_.review: What I Loved:Stunning Visuals: The graphical overhaul is truly impressive. Character models are expressive, environments are richly detailed, and the overall aesthetic is vibrant and stylish.Engaging Combat: The turn-based combat system is as addictive as ever. Exploiting enemy weaknesses and utilizing different Persona abilities keeps battles strategic and exciting.Compelling Narrative: The story of Persona 3 remains powerful and thought-provoking. Exploring themes of loss, friendship, and the meaning of life, it's a narrative that resonates deeply.Memorable Soundtrack: The music perfectly complements the game's atmosphere, blending catchy J-pop tunes with more somber and emotional tracks.Minor Gripes:Familiarity Factor: While the improvements are undeniable, those intimately familiar with the original may find some aspects a bit too familiar.Content Omissions: The absence of certain elements from Persona 3 FES and Persona 3 Portable, such as the female protagonist option, may disappoint some fans.Overall:Persona 3 Reload is a must-play for both newcomers and longtime fans of the series.  It's a faithful remake that captures the essence of the original while offering a visually stunning and engaging experience. Whether you're drawn to its stylish presentation, strategic combat, or thought-provoking narrative, Persona 3 Reload delivers a truly rewarding RPG adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a young man in his 20s, taking the full brunt of school as a full-time student with a part-time job. Just this past month, I was diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder, and in this past year, I have been attending therapy. The series as a whole has changed my life, and brightened so many dark spots that hovered over my childhood. When I play games, I play to have a great time. For a small moment, I expect that I will experience a work of art that will ultimately brighten my day. And after finishing Persona 3 Reload, I can say that it has left me more than brightened and shattered. It has left me with the outlook that life is brighter than it looks, and that Persona 3 Reload is a great ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.I cried at the ending. I cried at the small, and profoundly heavy themes that Persona 3 Reload tries to convey to its audience through its characters, and ends up wrapping up at the end. For old fans, Persona 3 has been remastered, modernized, and has been given so much love from its developers. It keeps the old feel of the game, and yet, keeps a new focus on how rather frail life really is as a whole. P3R lets you know that outside of its experience: you have one life. That small life matters, and with the people around you, ordinary or unique - they too are special in their own way. Although the game brings this up plenty of times, many of us are also still trying to figure out who we are. You see, in many ways, Persona 3 Reload brings up the question of how we can be ultimately happy. Many attribute it with success, and a personal goal, but with the way Persona 3 Reload tries to answer this; to guide how one can be happy...The game urges its players to do one thing. Find something/someone to care about. It makes a point that if we can learn more about one another with our own types of kindness, and to understand that it doesn't have to be displayed in a grandiose manner - we will find a purpose. You spend around half the game kicking ass, and the other listening to others. A good majority of these characters will help support this theme by having them FEEL human through spectacular writing and voice acting. And a lot of these characters never fall into the neutral category, as you either like them or hate them. There are fights in the game where you must think before you act, and especially on harder difficulties, rewards those who plan accordingly. But aside from that?Get Persona 3 Reload. Get yourself a game that will be both really cheesy and also really heartfelt. I have never, EVER played a game in my entire life that has made me want to touch grass - and made me want to become a pretty boy who points a gun to his head and yells Persona just to send someone to hell, and then to go on a date with a girl the very next day like nothing happened. Please. 10/10,

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload brought me back to one of my favorite stories of all time, and I enjoyed every second of it. From the visuals to the gameplay, I can tell how much time and love was put into this remake. Overall I would give this remake an 8/10, and would recommend it to any Persona fan and really anyone in general open to playing it. Where it loses 2 points is the lack of the Female Protagonist and the egregious DLC prices versus content.1) I understand completely why the Female Protagonist was not included in this remake. Including her would be the equivalent of making the game again, which would be far too high of an order for an already bustling experience. Still, it's something I have to consider when we take into account that there is no definitive version of Persona 3, and unfortunately this remake cannot be considered the "definitive," and rather the "best" version to play. Persona 3 Portable's steam port I cannot say in good faith is a good substitute due to the port quality and its many issues, as well as the stripped down gameplay due to hardware limitations at the time. Ideally the Female Protagonist would've been included, but I understand why she wasn't. Nevertheless, I will still dock a point for this.2) Egregious pricing for DLC is nothing new for Atlus, and I was hoping it wouldn't have affected this game, but who was I kidding. The prices for this game's DLC is abhorrent, especially for what essentially bottles down to a few Persona's from future titles, BGM sets, and costumes. They are simply not worth the price for what is essentially cosmetics and things that can easily be modded in for free. The DLC on day 1 is simply not worth the price and you should NOT buy it if you're expecting to get anything huge out of it. The second part of the DLC which docks points is the (as of writing this) recently announced Expansion Pass, which is a whopping $35 for BGM sets, 1 costume set, and a story expansion called "Episode Aigis." After recently experiencing "The Answer" in the original Persona 3 FES, I cannot say it is worth even $20 unless Atlus majorly overhauls and improves not only its gameplay, but also its story. The Answer is a very controversial epilogue and I understand why now, because for how long and grindy it is there's not much story aside from adding more context to base game events and expanding on why a certain thing happened, and the answer's provided may or may not be satisfying to players. I am holding out hope that Atlus will remedy these issues in Episode Aigis, but if not then the negative reviews the Expansion Pass is currently garnering is completely deserved.TL;DR: DLC is overpriced and not worth your money, taking another point off the overall score.Now while I know this review has been mostly negative, aside from these two major issues I have with the game, everything else is amazing and I cannot recommend this game enough. If you're wanting to play Persona 3, this is the version you should play. If you'd like to experience the Female Protagonist, unfortunately you'll have to make due with the terrible Persona 3 Portable PC port. For Episode Aigis, if it ends up being just like the original The Answer, I would recommend just watching a video of all the cutscenes or reading a summary, because actually playing it at that point would not be worth your time and effort unless they fully rework it for Episode Aigis.Overall, Persona 3 Reload is an 8/10 remake with worthwhile base game content and a story that I consider the best in the series. As of writing this, I'm aiming to 100% each game, which I might add is not too hard for this remake compared to past titles like P4G and the original P5.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Like Persona? Play it. Never played Persona but like RPGs and collecting funky looking creatures? Play it. BONUS: DOG.Bonus++: DLC with the female protag and appropriate storylines would be cool, but it's not a deal breaker to not have it. As a female gamer, kinda used to games not having a female protag and it doesn't make a difference to me at this point - the game is still stellar.My introduction to the Persona series was with Persona 4, and then I played 5. They were all both enjoyable experiences that I might attempt to reexperience at some point in time, more so after starting my playthrough of P3 Reload.Right off the bat, the opening music is an absolute BANGER and I never use that word. The UI is not only smooth, but pleasing to look at as well. I know there are some people who played the previous iterations of P3 and would prefer the old UI, animations, etc, but as a newcomer? Oh, I love this.$70 is a bit steep for a game, but it doesn't bother me too much as at some point most $60 games will be boosted to $70 to adjust for inflation and what not. I think a rule of thumb is if you can at least get 30 min to an hour of gameplay for every $ spent, it's worth it if you're having a good time. Bonus if you get more hours of gameplay from it.I read that the previous iterations had a female protag and it does suck to miss out on that, but it can't be helped. The battles are smooth with features to speed through under leveled enemies and everything looks like it's been paintedf with that  Persona 5 coat. I'm enjoying the voice acting from the cast of characters, even with Akihiko deeper voice.I definitely recommend playing the game for that good ol' Persona playstyle. But god, I wish the school questions weren't so ODD, this game makes college exams look like vocabulary quizzes.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very solid/faithful remake with a lot of great QoL changes. Aesthetically, it's great - the menus, shop interfaces and new portraits all look beautiful. The new voice actors have done an excellent job and you can tell they really love the series. The remastered music is also excellent. I was surprised to see complaints because I think the changes are fairly minor and the newly added songs fit in nicely, despite being a little closer to Persona 5's soundtrack.(One thing to note on the soundtrack - DO NOT buy it as DLC. It's in a convoluted format only playable via its own (very dumb) Unity player so you end up wishing you'd just pirated it.)I would've loved to see the feMC route in the remake, but they've utilised several elements of her social links from P3P, and the additional hangouts with all the SEES members is refreshing compared to the original/FES. I don't feel quite as saddened because they've breathed a lot more life into the main cast. I do have to say that, as expected, they've leaned into the Flanderisation a little too much; particularly with Akihiko. It's probably not as bad as it could've been, but a lot of his new voice lines are training/protein focused which is disappointing. It's one thing I wish they'd lifted a bit more from feMC's route for.My only real complaint is that it seems way too easy compared to the original games. I started out on hard and it feels like easy mode. It's super easy to max stats, battles are easy unless you're completely ill-prepared, and after maybe the first 50 floors of Tartarus, I've always seemed to be flush with money and crafting materials, etc. If you're not new to the series, I would recommend starting on hard or merciless to at least have a bit of challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m playing on Steam Deck. Runs perfectly solid at 60fps for me once I turned off the high res reflections. A perfect SD experience, in my opinion.I’ve been so intrigued by this franchise for the last ten or so years. I tried P5 on PS4 and couldn’t get into it, tried it again later after the PS5 came out and still struggled. But I loved the style and the way it approached its exploration of the topics it was commentating on. Enter P3R. I heard it ran well on Deck and I was sold on trying the series again. And I’m so glad I did.The story so far (and I feel like, despite my ingame playtime hovering around 38 hours, I am still very early) is very intriguing. The mystery of the Dark Hour and how each individual the Player Character meets is connected to it has been so fascinating. I appreciate how it approaches Social Links and skill leveling in a way that feels achievable while still keeping you busy. I don’t feel like I need a guide open to navigate all the time management this game throws at you, which was a big negative of Persona 5, for me. I actually think, after playing a chunk of this game, that I better understand how the series works, and am looking forward to trying P5 again.Combat is fast and fluid and not overly encumbered with itself. Battles, though turn based, are quickly resolved and very satisfying. I know I’ve been hesitating too much when I hear more than a minute of one of the various battle themes.Speaking of — the music is great! It has been living in my head. I play it at work as background music while I wait to dive back into Tartarus. Very catchy stuff here. All in all, a beautiful game with an intriguing mystery and a satisfying game loop. I would particularly recommend it to people who, like me, love turn based RPGs but have tried and failed to be gripped by the series with other installments. Serious fun and thinking to be had here.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly, nothing could have prepared me for this. This game is a punch to the gut, in more ways than one.Yet even so, this games reflections on its core themes are so poignant and beautiful - from flavour dialogue from NPC's all around the island, to Akinari's social link - this game has a lot to say, and it delivers it in such an astounding way.There is a lot here to love, the UI is stylish and brings so much charm to the gameplay experience. The fun little hidden scenes you can choose to partake in, such as taking Koromaru for a walk always resulting in some new interaction with your social links or nice little ties to the main story with your teammates. The way the colour palette of the game adapts as time goes on. There is so much to partake in, and this game has so much life.The dungeons didn't really feel like a slog as I thought they did in P4G, not having to spend extra time to grind once I'd reached the objective really helped the game progress more naturally for me.Overall, it would be hard for me to put into words the full impact of this game, I might not even have them, but this game is a masterpiece through and through, and just another testament to how obsessed I am with this franchise.

The remake is missing a few things, such as FeMC and the answer dlc, and while many may have opinions on their additions in their respective games, I do believe bringing them all together would have created a "definitive" edition of persona 3, rather than leaving it a bit fractured as is. however if you don't care about either then this is probably the perfect version of persona 3 for you haha.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review by saying I enjoyed Persona 3 Reload; however, I can’t help but feel somewhat let down by this release. This game oozes style, and has an amazing soundtrack which really enhances the core gameplay and experience. These aspects lift the game up significantly, and they carry what I believe to be the greatest shortcoming of the game which is the difficulty, and by extension Tartarus.  In a combat encounter the player is given multiple mechanics that can either deal immense damage, or can completely change the course battle. These mechanics, some old and some new, help give the game some variety in combat, and can give the player the sense that they are truly playing as an elite squadron. The trade-off is it the player is almost always overprepared and is constantly rewarded, and rarely punished. Each character in the party can use theurgies to deal immense damage, or provide support and utility. The one more system grants an additional action when striking an enemy weakness, and when paired with baton pass the play can create long combos. Striking an enemy from behind in Tartarus allows the party to use all of their actions before the enemies. These mechanics are great, however when used together they can completely trivialize any combat encounter. I found this to be a detriment the farther I got into Tartarus, especially on the higher floors where I felt like I was going through the motions trying to get to the next story beat as I wiped each encounter within seconds.  While I found the combat and by extension the dudgeon crawling to be too easy, this game excels in regard to its tone, style, presentation, and plot. I was thoroughly engrossed in the plot, and enjoyed seeing each social link play out. This game deals with some relatively heavy themes through its main plot and social links, but also contains many uplifting moments. Each character has some form of struggle, and as the game progresses you watch as they grow and overcome the obstacles presented to them. This makes a large majority of the characters be likable, and I found myself to be actively rooting for them along the way. The characters and plot, while great on their own, are complemented by the general presentation. Emerging victorious from a Tartarus encounter plays a slick animation that exudes the feeling of being a badass. Character and enemy designs are interesting and sleek. Even the transition to the next day is stylish, and this is all accompanied by some of the best soundtracks you can find in a game.  Despite my perceived shortcoming with Tartarus and the slog it can become due to a lack of challenge in battle, the rest of this game is superb. Persona 3 Reload didn’t manage to exceed my expectations that were probably unfairly high, but I was entertained a majority of the way through. It’s characters, charm, style and heavy plot make this a game I would recommend to anyone who is a fan of the JRPG genre, or is looking for a plot that can uplift despite its grim themes.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface: I have a history already of playing the older versions of P3 in the past, so I might be a bit biased in favor of this game already but oh well.For a time, I used to have Persona 3 ranked a little under 5 for a while due to the now “dated” gameplay of being unable to control party members. In hindsight, I was only really placing it in that position from that one factor alone. Coming back to Persona 3 so many years later with Reload has reminded me why I enjoyed the game as much as I did in the past. I’d even argue to say it’s left an even bigger impact on me than it did during my initial experience on the PS2, as it left me in my own head reflecting and relearning about how to appreciate the little things once the credits started to roll as opposed to only getting into my feels.From the new amazing voice cast, to the look and feel of the game alongside the already fantastic story, I had such a hard time putting the game down that I would get so much more invested than I thought I would. The story beats hit me like a truck and are still more than enough to bring me to tears all the way up to the end. I can only imagine how it’ll be for any first time goers who may bother to read through this little tangent. Dungeon crawling feels a lot better as Tartarus both visually looks a ton more appealing and is a lot of fun to actually explore through each floor. The new battle gimmick, theurgy, is a nice flashy addition, similar to “showtimes” and “fusion spells” from P5R and P3F respectively, and makes combat have a refreshing feel to it. Even if at times it may eliminate a little bit of extra challenge, it’s still something I can appreciate and am more than happy to have included (if difficulty really feels too easy, even on hard mode, just play on merciless. There definitely is a spike in challenge there and will catch you off guard if you’re not prepared)There's so much more I could say on the game itself and its personal impacts on me once the game is closed, but I think it's better from here to go through it on your own and buckle down for the ride! If you haven’t experienced Persona 3 and are considering it, I’d say go for it. It’s totally worth the ride. For those who have in the past, I’d say the same. Not only is it just a new way to experience the title, but a new way to remember what’s already an unforgettable journey, the way I see it.
