_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is an HD Remake (not remaster and not on the switch apparently) of an old beloved playstation exclusive game for modern day consoles. There are a few things missing from portable and FES that may be included in the feature, and otherwise: *HD Graphics for all aspects of Persona 3 Reload- including the environment, buildings, characters, and especially tartarus.*Shuffle time makes a return from Persona 3 FES and Persona 4 Golden, with beautifully resdigned tarot cards and arcana burst features. *Link events for the male party members*All major social links have voice lines that weren't included in the original (and other re-releases)*Theragy attacks (which affect the protagonist too) allowing for super flashy and strong attacks that provide beneficial boosts in combat. *Oracle will boost your team's performance and ability to survive; only buffs, no debuffs. *Shift/Shifting, a new tactic in battle similiar to baton pass from persona 5 / royal enabling you to change to another party member after striking one enemy weakness, allowing you to diverse and fully utilize your party members on the battlefield for an all out attack- most of the time.*You're no longer fatigued in tartarus, but the reaper is coming for you in every single floor*Special bonuses for Merciless difficulty game play finished in new game plus+*The arcana is by which all means are revealed...*And many more featuresIn short, 9.2/10; the story hasn't changed and is about faithful to the original, tartarus, the environment, and combat have been improved significantly with 3D Graphics. There is just the issue of the missing answer dlc content, the framerate does rarely flicker, fusion attacks are gone with the multiple protagonist theragy abilities. Honestly, this is one impressive remake of an existing game, and I hope they do improve on missing issues.-It costs $70 for a HD remake of an existing game?! That might be one of the major turn downs for P3R. The dlc adds in unique personas, costumes from other games, soundtrack and artbook as other applications included with Persona 3 Reload that don't even have a quit option (alt + f4 to leave).

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 is a game that a lot of people hold very close to their heart, and I'm one of those people. It's a great RPG with wonderful writing and a bittersweet sentimentality that lends it a surprising amount of weight. The game has had many rereleases over the years, and Reload has firmly become my personal favorite version of the game. It's a great starting point for anyone interested in Persona or Megami Tensei.Reload is significantly different than the other versions of Persona 3, and while other versions have their own good things going for them, I think the additional story content added to Reload makes it my favorite. The life sim elements in the Persona games tend to exhaust me, but I found Persona 3 Reload to handle them the best out of every title so far. My only real complaint with Reload is that I think it's absurdly easy. While the game is overall very engaging, the combat never really feels very challenging on any difficulty. The optional superbosses are hard, sure, but most of the game is a cakewalk.I'm surprised by how nostalgic this game made me. Especially towards the end, the art direction for the final environments of the game and the wonderful guitar rifts used in the music, really brought back the spirit of PS2-era Atlus.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an analogy for . Don't play the game if you are not in a good mental state, or maybe the game is just what you need to push through those trying times.Out of the 3 Persona mainline entries I've played (P3R, P4G, and P5R), this game has the most mature theme out of the three. A more appropriate comparison would be to  (IW) whose main theme is also Kiryu battling cancer. P3R does a much better job at creating the atmosphere of dread and inevitability while the main characters try to remain hopeful and resilient. To be fair, IW's mainstay is its signature silliness so it is extremely difficulty to mix such a serious theme with the gameplay. I must give kudos to P3R developers to actually , unlike IW's developers who . There was one jarring moment where a character important to the main characters dies, but then the next day the protagonist just goes to school as usually with cheery music in the background, so P5R handles these pacing pieces a bit better.Mechanically, this game is probably the worst out of the three, maybe a little bit above P4G if you can't live without Baton Pass (called Shift in this remake). I very appreciate the developers bringing over many of the P5R improvements such as adding Light and Dark elements, because by around 40%-50% into the game, the Personas start to look the same due to the lack of elements, not to mention you are going to start seeing the same Personas over and over. In P5R you also have Nuclear and Psy so the Personas have a lot of variety, making strategy and planning more fun. In P3R, you will soon start to realise that higher-tier Personas just have the same set of skills but at higher tier so there isn't much room for experimentation. On the other side,  means you can't just  your way through the game anymore so maybe that isn't a bad thing. Nevertheless, the mechanics of P3R just really makes you want to play more of P5R.The way I play mainline Persona games is this: the first playthrough is whatever, I'd try to max my social stats but not too worried about social links since I know for a fact you're not supposed to be able to max everything first time. On my second playthrough, this is when I want to plan out some min-maxing in order to battle the superbosses. But having seen how impactful the ending is, I think I will give the game some time to settle first so that its impact is not diluted by the time I start the second playthrough. Maybe I'll even wait for the September DLC first.

_childDocuments_.review: loved the absurdist themes in the game. if you dig deep enough, you'll be able to find plot holes you can poke through, but i think that takes away from the game a fair bit.the use of death as a recurring motif works well with the message the game tries to bring across. the death arcana represents loss, death, and more importantly: renewal. the characters in this game experience loss, grief, and after the MC interacts with them via their social links, they have a newfound resolve to live.death, in the practical sense, is finality. everything that lives is designed to end. with such a realisation, it is easy to take a defeatist approach and sink into despair. what is the point of living if it's going to end? the game says: life contains value exactly because it is finite.it works, because existential themes are universal; they are a reflection of the human condition. there are many different responses, but the struggle to find meaning is shared. camus once said something along the lines of: there is but one serious philosophical problem, which is the decision to kill yourself or not. if anything, this game serves as a potent reminder of that.my eyes feel heavy.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10, cautious recommendation, I guess I like it more than not. Spoilers for the story unless you've played P3 and the Answer.I have played this game, P3R, it's new game plus, and now episode Aigis, in their entirety, with 300 hours in, and I feel I can write a review.  hmmm, as a persona fan captured by the greetness of P5R, and went on to play P5S, P5T...I had high expectations for P3R, knowing of its reputation among P fans. Some of my expectations are met, some fell short.The writing is perhaps the greatest strengths of any Persona game, and certainly it was the peak of P5R, and not the silly "pokemon" gameplay, nor the well crafted yet not really groundbreaking dungeons. (Oh, the crafted dungeon is only in P5, I thought they might add new dungeons in P3 remaster, but nope, its all randomly generated ones)The "RP" is more important and is better than the "G" in Persona games. The story and message is far more important than the gameplay.In P5R, I loved every single confidant (well maybe except one) and many other characters. In P3R...most of the social links are...meh, mid, generic, forgettable. Very few characters outside the main cast is very interesting, nor their stories exceptionally well written. Even in P3 team isn't that friendly to each other compared to the P5 cast. I really liked some of the P3 team, but certain others I don't really have strong feeling for. Some character's stories in P3 are great, but most of them pretty meh.Also, if you thought that most of the confidants in P5 occupied the day slot and not enough for the night slot, this is even worse in P3. With most social links being students, it has to be daytime, weekdays, no holidays, and no scripted events. I think there's only 2 night time links. Some social links only appear on Sundays! Oh, and you better make sure to do the linked episodes ASAP as well, cause they can expire really quickly. It's very difficult to go in blind and max out all confidants and character stories in your first run, before you have foreknowledge going into new game plus.Speaking of which, there's barely anything new story-wise in NG+ plus either, just some minor scenes in the first day of school, and I don't think any other scenes afterwards. I think its only there to fix up your mistake of being able to max out all confidants during your first run. Even P5R had more NG+ exclusive scenes/content. (Lavenza)As for the story of P3...I'm not impressed. I generally don't like downer stories, and it felt the MC's final sacrifice was kinda forced. I don't really like "everything is fated this way" kind of stories, I feel it's bad and forced writing. The final bass is supposedly killable, and we only know this from a very skechy and biased character. A character that is NOT Omniscient. A character that LITERALLY is the final bad boss you can fight. And after this boss fight, MC literally abandons the team to become Persona Jesus. Hmmm...I thought I was supposed to form bonds with other people and overcome the impossible together? Nope, cast them all aside in the last moment, I the MC knows best, and won't even think of trusting my friends to achieve victory together... (In Persona and most JRPGs we kill gods all the time, STFU about Nyx being any different)As for episode Aigis...for something calling itself "the answer', does it actually gives a lorewise or emotionally satisfying answer? The OG P3 ending was at least hopeful and vague enough for me to cope that MC might not be dead. He might just be passed out or just have had a metaphorical "death". "Nope", said EP:A, MC is hard dead and becomes...door-kun. Yup, tens of hours of boring not-Tartarus dungeon crawling...just for this lame revelation. Oh...and Nyx wasn't that bad all along and its actually Erebus, the "grand manifestation of humanity's grief and negative emotion" that needs to contact Nyx to end the world...somehow? What the ♥♥♥♥ ret-con is this? It makes the whole story make less sense. Door-kun will never come back because he needs to stop Erebus now, as an eternal door that cockblocks Erebus from Nyx...Unless Elizabeth from P4A is canon and succeeds in her quest to find a way to put down Erebus permanently...yeah...the OG ending was vague and good enough to need all this baggage.But I guess I'm being unfair to Reload. The mistakes in writing was done decades ago. It's nearly impossible for Reload team to fix that. I was foolish and hoped the team can retcon the story a bit, but I guess they can't. Or fix the social links into confidants quality. P5 shows the Atlus had become better over the years, and their games have evolved over time, in both writing and game QoL improvements. Some of the QoL from P5 made it, but a lot didn't, and I guess I wished for a "story QoL improvement" as well lol...Oh, and the music has always been a highlight of P games, but here it's mostly just remasters of the OG P3/P3:Fes soundtrack. I think there just only 3 original new soundtrack in the base game (Color Your Night/Full Moon Full Life/It's Going Down Now). As for Ep:A, only two new songs (Disconnected/Don't). Color Your Night is especially good. The others are...decently good. But that's all the new original music content.P3R is perfect for those that just want P3 modernized into P5R, and graphically a little bit post-P5R. But for some that wanted and expected a little bit...more, temper your expectations. P3R is a faithful remaster, but did not fix the all the flaws of P3/P3:Fes. But on the bright side, at least Atlus has been impoving over the years, showing clear evolution from P3 to P4 to P5. Not all the evolution can be brought back into P3, but they did brought a lot of it. Yes, this would probably be the best introduction to P3 for new fans, but I don't think P3 itself is as good as P4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to reccommend this for its world, characters, and gameplay, the package it was given in is not ideal, and despite the fanbase being very clear on what they were hoping for with this rerelease for years and the ball being perfectly set up for them to achieve this, they somehow still fell just short of the mark.The good: If you loved Persona 3, this is the same game but prettier, remade in the engine of Persona 5, with quality of life improvements to rein in the more annoying aspects of combat among other things and make it handle closer to the more recent entries. If you haven't experienced this game yet, I would highly recommend it, it's easily one of the best jrpgs out there, now with the most annoying aspect of its combat system fixed, making this as close to the ideal way to experience it as we currently have.The bad: The epilogue chapter that was part of the extended cut is being sold as a DLC and there are no plans to make the option to choose your characters gender, opening romance options for several new characters, part of the game despite this being a feature in the portable version. Only reason I can think is to avoid having to record new versions of almost every line to refer to the main character as a female, which is honestly a pretty lame excuse. Also they recast all the voice actors for some reason and I'm a bit salty, because I loved some of those voice performances, and now they sound like alternate reality doppelgangers.Also, very annoyingly, this game has a DRM that seriously hampers my ability to play it because Im running it on Steam Deck, but often only have time to play once a week, and if I forget to run the game before leaving the house, the DRM won't let me start the game. If you're new to this franchise/entry in it, I would 100% recommend this. The story and characters are top notch, and this has most of what makes Persona 5 Royal's combat my gold standard in JRPGs. If you're a veteran, know that this still isn't the perfected, truly complete edition we were hoping for, but now that it's on pc, there's hope of mods completing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The core story is still the same, but everything is brought up to the production quality of the later games in the series.  This adds a LOT of new scenes that you can play through with your friends and party members that bring the world to life.  The core gameplay is much improved by updates such as being able to issue direct commands to the party like the later games allowed.I haven't played it since P3P, so it was good to see everybody again.  Akihiko's voice actor felt a little jarring at first, but he finds his voice once you get past the first couple of layers of bravado.  Honestly, that was the only one that jumped out at me, and I played through FES and P3P twice each.Still bitter that they aren't planning on including the Female MC playthrough.  I'm saving my clear data for a NG+ after the modders have done what they can about that.Still, I'd recommend it for nostalgia replayers and for latecomers to the series who might have picked it up with one of the later games but want to see where it's coming from without needing to settle for PS2 era gameplay and graphical standards.  Probably don't bother with the DLC personas though, honestly.  They make it harder to resolve Elizabeths fusion requests by more than they make it easier to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is still good. If you liked P3 before, you'll like it again. It's also pretty faithful to FES. Skip the DLC or wait until sale, it's a disgusting money grab. With that in mind this is more a list of changes they've made instead of a review, and written assuming you don't care about spoilers since nothing plot-wise changed that much. Most important change: the rewind feature. All events that take time now create an autosave, up to 5(ish) at a time. No longer do you need to remember to save before every social link in case you screw up an answer, the game did it for you. These are per save, so if you, say, underestimate your academics stat and need to go back even further than an old save, you can use rewind on the old save and go back an extra few days.Second most important change: you no longer hard need a guide for 100% on new game. You can wing it and be fine.Combat: In general it's P5 combat, minus psi/nuke, and overall a touch easier IMO. This includes baton passes, giving ♥♥♥♥♥ some panic buttons you can press, direct character control (the ailments on bosses nightmare is over), direct damage light/dark spells (Ken is still a bit too specialized though), new ailments and other goodies, no fatigue system (thank Masakado!), and giving you retry options instead of kicking you directly back to the load screen on death.They also added theurgies, which are limit breaks. Fill gauge, do severe piercing damage to one enemy (for the most part, anyways). What fills the gauge varies from character to character but all characters will fill some amount if they hit a weakness. Gives Yukari something to do when she's not hitting the mediarama button, kinda makes the 2nd block a little too easy, overall a neat change.When exploring Tartarus, there are some new points of interest. Locked chests exist, but it's the P5 lockpick system, rebranded as twilight shards. Instead of crafting the picks, you now get them in... a lot of ways, but mainly from Elizabeth for quest rewards and when you level social links. You also can find a fixed number in the overworld and occasionally in Tartarus itself. Fixed boss floors have locked chests that are worth your time, but I have been less impressed by what's in the randomly generated ones (2 shards for a Maragi skill card? Really?)Shards can also be used to full heal, including SP, your party at the clock in the Tartarus lobby that used to be a save point. Costs 7 shards, but helps a lot if Yukari runs out of heal juice.One final use: if the game thinks some of your party is super underleveled (Hi Ken!) it might spawn a clock that will catch 3 party members up to your level for some shards.They added breakable objects like in P5 into P3, but they respawn a lot and are just goodie boxes. At time of writing I have 50 life stones from hitting those things. Also, no animation, you just hit them. Helps with cash flow, some of them have twilight shards too!A few months into the game, you'll also get tasks to rescue people who wander into Tartarus. I like the concept, but they stagger who wanders in on different days. This encourages people who try and one-and-done Tartarus to wait until right before the full moon to climb, since otherwise you'll need to go back whenever somebody new wanders in. They also will send a few social link characters in there, and if you don't save them the link dies, which makes it a little less optional. The rewards are generally whatever, honestly. It will also generate cats for you to save, but those just get you twilight shards from Elizabeth... and the game explicitly says the cats will be fine either way. Shuffle time is back but is a lot easier. They removed inverted cards, so only positive results, and you just pick the ones you want instead of playing a shell game. They also added major arcana to shuffle time, which have all sorts of effects. You can only acquire a limited number of major arcana per Tartarus visit, and when you hit your limit, it +1's all the minor arcana for the rest of the visit, so you always want to pick major to fill the bar if you can.The biggest change is Monad doors, which are just bonus minibosses you can clear for goodies. Some are fixed spawns on certain floors, most are random as you climb. The random ones you have to do before you leave the floor or they become inaccessible, but mainly have gemstone rewards that aren't that important. The fixed floor ones have real nice stuff(including the extra fun female outfits), bonus dialog, and some lore scraps. This is where they put some of the extra fun dice!I want to say they tweaked some character skills, but I'm not getting out the spreadsheet to check.Story:Major change: Everyone is less of a ♥♥♥♥♥ to each other. Yukari is rather noticably nicer the entire game, to everyone! Junpei got hit with the Stupei stick hard and honestly got done dirty. Until Chidori he deserves what Female hate he gets for the most part, and I'm not sure why they did that besides bring him more in line with P4 and P5's male sidekick characters. Rest in peace my king.Also, no sign of Mitsuru's whip, but her Persona still has one. None of this affects the major story beats, it's just a tonal change.They added link episodes, which are mini social links for the team. You can watch movies, read, cook food, garden, and walk the dog together. Most of these give a social stat boost and eventually a combat boost, so they are worth doing even if you otherwise don't care/hate Ken and want to avoid him.The social links themselves haven't really changed, except for chariot your only option is the track team. That's really all I can think of.One thing they did not import from P5: you cannot date your teacher. I guess if you could it'd make the Magician link a little weird. Sorry!They even gave link episodes to Takuya, AKA Shirtless Jesus revolver guy. I can't say they add a ton to his character but they are there. Jin gets nothing though.They changed the beach event. Personally I forgot it existed until the internet reminded me, but you may have noticed I'm more combat focused... The love hotel bit is the same. Haven't made it to the onsen yet.I'm only in September, so no idea if you can save Chidori and Shinjiro yet. My guess? Probably.Update: Chidori is still savable, Shinjiro will wait for the P3P DLC I guess.Other stuff: It is way easier to grind social stats. I have 6/6/5 in early September. The game does make it less clear how much each activity is worth, but in general stick to 2 pip activities and you'll be fine. The new music is good, except the "Moon is reaching out stars" remix where the new backup vocalist is not hitting her "OOOOOOOH YEAH" the way she used to.The timed Elizabeth requests are way easier to complete, and the overworld map has !!! markers for where you can get the quest items.Rumor has it they will add the Answer as DLC. Time will tell?

_childDocuments_.review: God bless you all for taking your time to read this. I recently found my son playing a video game called "Persona 3." I was doing house chores while he was playing it in the living room. It seemed like a child friendly and educational game at first. The characters were at a school and learning math. The next thing I know, they were shooting themselves in the head! The characters had what looked like guns and they'd put them up to their heads and shoot. I got worried, so I did some research on the game. The guns are actually "evokers" used to call upon a "persona." I'm worried that my son will one day find a gun and try this out, or try to evoke evil spirits in other ways. I learned that there is a sequel called Persona 4 where the teenagers call a "persona" by using tarot cards. This goes against the Lord. As I kept doing research, I learned that these games are a part of a bigger series called "Shin Megami Tensei." What I learned about this series is horrifying. There are games called "Devil Children," "Devil Survivor," "Devil Summoner," and "Digital Devil Saga" that are part of this series! This got me really worried about what my son was playing. In these games you summon and fight "demons." These demons look really similar to what my son was summoning as "personas." What can I do? I'm scared that if I take away the games, he might try preforming these things in real life and rebel. But if I don't take them away, he'll be felling into the hands of the devil! _childDocuments_.review: Menu: gorgeous, fast, responsive, blue theme is perfect.Music: Remix is good, but i still prefer original. Both are great btw.Gameplay: fast, slick, more enhanced. New attack pose and finish pose for each character.Art: beautiful.Voice: perfect for every character.Dungeon: new design make Tartarus much better than original.World: more crowded than original.Overall, Reload is great JRPG game and great remake for Persona 3. If you love original, Portable or FES, you will love Reload. I haven't finished Reload, but i already finished Portable 2 times and finished The Answer - FES. For me, Persona 3 is the best JRPG game and help introduce me to Persona series. Also, Persona 3 have one of the most memorable ending in JRPG games. And Reload, a remake with many upgrade, will bring to you many moments you never forget.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game that explores the theme of death and loss. There is a main tower dungeon one must rise through to get to the end game and it can become quite a bit of a chore. The characters are very human in their dialogue and interactions.The only negatives I can give is the ending which came out completely contrived to me and the ridiculous power inflation slant that all Japanese stories tend to manifest towards the end of their stories. Otherwise the rest of the game was good.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Shin Megami Tensei Persona 3. The excitement I felt when my relative had told me how interesting the story was, when I was a child and couldn't help but be invested on the idea how people transmogrified into a coffin when Midnight Hits. "Would you believe me if a day consists more than 24 hours?" I was Intrigued.  This was also the beginning of knowing Shin Megami Tensei (SMT) and it's challenging battles! Challenge indeed received, with its amazing Voice Acting, battles, plot, great/funny events that involve around the characters along with good, simple character developments, and twists. A Legend to my eyes has returned on my desktop this time. atlus has indeed kept it true to it's story, excellent music as always, side with extra content involving more of their characters. I felt like a kid again playing this first play through on Merciless, a smile to my face when I had the same experience mostly involving the "floor bosses" as usual, yes the CRITS were insane but it has always kept me excited and never bored! However more extra content that now involves "Monad Doors"! The hours kept going! 10/10 Of course I'll be playing NG+ as there are more content to get into! (also you receive an interesting "key item" after beating Merciless for the first time! I'll leave it that.. I am hype for the future!)
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you do a remake. Fairly true to the original with modernized systems and graphics. Aside from the steep price tag for the base edition, which unfortunately is not even the "complete" game as The Answer is being included as an expansion, this is a solid recommendation for anyone looking for a good story that still holds up almost 20 years on.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Having played Persona 5 as my very first Persona game, I didnt feel like Persona 3 had quite the same level of charm and character as Persona 5.  That being said though, the gameplay was the same addictive turned based game play that Persona is known for, the life sim and social link system is just as nuanced, tight, and addictive as you'd expect, and the story, while it can drag at times, is still heartfelt and incredible.  Overall, I had a blast playing through this game, and would recommend for any JRPG or Persona fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game, basically released at the same time I've finished Persona 5 Royal.The visuals took a bit of getting used to after P5R, but they are gorgeous, and it made me appreciate how much work has went into making this a great game.I wholeheartedly recommend this masterpiece of a game to anyone interested in JRPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is a very well-executed remake. I haven't run into any major bugs, it's nice to have the 3D environments again, the new music is great and the new voice actors are totally fine. I'll be sinking a lot of hours into this game. The question isn't if P3R is good. The question is if it's $70 USD good.And the answer is no, not really.Not when Persona 3 Portable is also on Steam for $20, and has features they could've added to this game but just chose not to. Once the price comes down, I'll probably turn around and change this review to positive, because it IS a good game, maybe even a great game. But I can't in good conscience tell someone they have to play it RIGHT NOW, rather than wait for a price drop or a Steam sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's practically loved Persona games, clocking in hundreds of hours on 4 Golden and 5 Royal, both original and extended versions, diving into Persona 3 Reload was like coming home after a very long time. I'll admit, I never quite finished the original Persona 3, but this Reload version had me hyped up from the startIf you haven't played 3 yet, this is perfect! It's sad not having FES (the extended version) included, but overall, very recommendable
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best game in the Persona series, a much stronger entry than both 4 & 5. Here are some of my thoughts as someone who played FES back in 2014-2015:- The cast is very strong, and all go through character development without simply being pushed to the side or having it only forced through social links (which is a common issue faced throughout 5 with its party members, with it being less prevalent in 4 due to how well the characters bounced off of each other). - Some are upset that we don't get the female protagonist from portable, and that The Answer isn't included (with a high chance of it being later DLC, which is good news) but I say that even without that this is 100% the definitive experience that Atlus said they gave us. - The soundtrack is still excellent, despite being remade renditions of all the songs from nearly 2 decades ago (all hail Shoji Meguro) and with very few songs that are forgettable or downright bad. - Even without the male party members having social links, their linked episodes managed to give us plenty more interactions to bond with them in comparison to the older games where you could only do so with the female protagonist.My only real criticisms with the game:- It's almost impossible to 100% it without a guide unless you're a god at time management or have good enough prior knowledge from the previous versions of the game to have a fully laid out plan of how to do everything (which can still be messed up due to the addition of Linked Episodes). - Some linked episodes can lock you out of fusing some of the game's ultimate personas, even if you were able to complete all social links. This doesn't lock you out of an achievement, but can still be frustrating especially if you were planning on using Orpheus Telos for the superboss.- Even on Merciless difficulty, the game itself is not that difficult. At best, it was either frustrating or annoying but not too tough save for a small number of fights. Said fights were very enjoyable, but I would love for more fights that try to keep you on your toes. Of course, this is a personal issue as someone who has been playing the Persona games for around a decade and is only recently getting into SMT (of which Persona is an easier spinoff entry of).In the end,good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very very good because Persona 3 is very very good. They make some really nice gameplay adjustments and the character models and portraits are gorgeous. I think they played it a little too safe though, because it feels too similar to the original Persona 3, but I don't mind because Persona 3 is great!I like the linked episodes a lot, but I am still really sad Makoto can't be gay/no FeMC but that's okay Atlus I will just play portable instead :))
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the 70$ price tag slow you down, this isn't a stereotypical remaster. It's fully remade from the ground up. The only thing the original crossed over is characters and story. This is like Persona 5 gameplay with the Persona 3 Story. I simply cannot wait for the others to be done in this fashion.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game already decided that I probably wouldn't like it more than Persona 5 Royal, ohhhhhhhhh boy did it break those thoughts. The story and characters and music are so incredibly good. Tartarus is mid as hell don't get me wrong, Palaces were the right direction to go in, but damn. Just damn.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best way to experience Persona 3, as long as you don't overpay for the Episode Aegis DLC. Charging $35 for that at launch because its forcibly bundled with two other dlcs that people may or may not care about is a very annoying business model on top of the $70 remake. I'd say wait for a sale to get both the base game and the Episode Aegis DLC for a good price.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played the three newer gen personas (3 - 4 - 5) around the release of each original version - this one is easily the best remake. I'd argue this is the best game in the series in Gameplay, story, and environmental design with the reworks to Tartarus. Its not nearly as easy as 4 and 5, but it does have its downfalls in difficulty about halfway in when you finally get enough party members and you are no-longer bottle necked by SP.If you have played Persona 4 or Persona 5, Persona 3 Reload will be no different. You fight shadows to level up and fuse personas to make crazy new combination. Unlike 4 and 5 though, in the original release of this game, you could  control your party members, or which persona abilities were inherited during fusion. This was changed in the PSP version of Persona 3, and thank goodness for that.My only gripe with the gameplay is how cheesy it gets later into the game. With no spoilers - once you start getting certain physical type personas, the game becomes a joke. I played this game on Merciless (hardest difficulty) and I hardly hit the game over screen except for a few times in the beginning. I will say however, this is not like Persona 5 where enemy and ally weakness' are amplified by 3x. You deal less damage and take more, good change on that end. Its done really well in this adaption, its easily my favorite of the 3 different versions of Persona 3. The new voice actors (especially Junpei my god) really nail their characters, and I love how they added the og cast back as some side characters. Its especially hilarious when some of the VA's from the OG game start talking to their newer counter parts. The areas are given new life through all the graphical enhancements in this engine, plus all the social links are voiced and helps sell that individuals story. My one and only problem with all of these enhancements is that we do not have female protagonist. If not female protagonist, then at least giving the male team members of SEES their own social link stories.Holy moly did they ever up their game with this adaption. Tartarus used to be an absolute copy and paste dungeon in the original (and FES) + PSP Persona 3. They have since gone the direction of Persona 5 and really given some uniqueness to the blocks in the games dungeon crawling area. Each block, you will encounter small, medium, and large spaces that have similar designs and are randomly generated each day you are in Tartarus. What you find on floor 50 will not be the same the following in game day.Outside of the dungeon space, the outside city is really brought to life in this game. The areas in which a lot of your social stats and social links will be undertaken has included a lot more depth than the original games. The PSP game took a bit more of a visual novel approach to the over-world, you would not even see your character model traversing these spaces. The club in the mall area is also given more life and actually has people in it (from my recollection - in FES this area was barren with absolutely no one around). There's a lot to do with so little time, and it was a blast to sit and watch.If you enjoy turn-based JRPG's with a hint of visual novel flair, Persona has always been the series for you. In my honest opinion, this is the best Persona game Atlus has ever conceived. You are doing yourself a disservice by not playing through this masterpiece if you can afford it. If you enjoyed Persona 4 and/or Persona 5 - this game will be right up your alley. You will find something you enjoy, there's a little bit of something for every nostalgic JRPG nerd who hit their teens in the late 2000s.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game through and through. When I originally tried playing portable on xbox game pass it never really was my cup of tea I vastly preferred 4 and 5 but Reload was an absolute Joyride. As someone who was dealing with the loss of a loved one recently this game really hit home. Would reccomend.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: For those who never got to play the original P3 because they like P5 too much or those that couldn't get their hands on a PS Vita, this is for us. It can't replace the charm of the original but it's a nice coat of paint and accessibility point for new fans (me). Still the same great story and actually a better handling of the characters this time around. I mean that's the only reason I'm here. If I could play just the slice-of-life portions I would simply because grinding is a chore to me. And hey, what's Persona if not for the Personas?
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 3 Reload

_childDocuments_.review: Before I bought this game, I have NEVER played Persona 3, as It was mostly locked to the Playstation 2 and P3 Portable was the only release of OG Persona 3 that was re-released. So, Since It was on sale during the summer sale, I picked it up. And boy, Atlus did not disappoint me one bit.Soundtrack was AMAZING, Characters (Especially Junpei) are AMAZING... This game is an example of how video games can be classified as art.

_childDocuments_.review: HD graphics and controllable characters do not fix the abomination that is p3. played through fes 3 years ago and it was a train wreck yet somehow this felt worse than the original(s).the story is an average end of the world scenario where at years end the world come to its end. this is supplied to the player through a kid no one else can see which of course leads the man character to not investigate or really care until the last few months of the game. at the same time you meet SEES a group has discovered an hour that exists between 12 and 1 called the dark hour. during this hour all people are unknowingly stored in coffins and entities referred to as shadows prowl the island. people have slowly been waking up during this hour, however, and been attacked and killed by the shadows. those who have awakened to a persona have the ability to fight back against the shadows. SEES uncovered the fact that these shadows have been escaping from a building called tararus that forms over the school on the island. Each full moon a Massive persona embodying an arcana escapes tartarus and you are tasked of taking down the shadow before it causes damage to the world. while setting up an interesting premise, the events that occur between the breakdown of this situation and when ♥♥♥♥ actually happens is incredibly bland. strega exists as organization that opposes what you are doing but they really are not threatening nor do they provide interesting characters. the game tries to get you to feel surprise, helpless, scared, when its revealed you are forwarding the end of the world but this info is *supplied at the start* and you never act on it.tartarus acts as the bulk of gameplay within p3 and it was bad for its time while rooting itself into the plot making its removal or change nearly impossible. tartarus consists of over 250 (more than double the combine total of all the floors in p4g) floors of Procedural generated mazes. each floor flat with an occasional ramp, consisting of shadows and the stair way to the next floor. each chunk will have a different aura and tweaked edition of the man tartarus song. R attempts to address this by making each floor more 3D as it cant remove the tower itself. but hey there are the full moon missions which contain gameplay outside of tartarus. they start off fine but then slowly progressing into lazy additions such as descending down five loading zones underground in a straight line.the character writing is atrocious and these characters intended to tie you to the world and take up your day to day life. the game has 3 good links two of which reoccur in the franchise while the rest of the link are, simply put, bad. your best friend (magician social link) spends his time in each link talking about how he wants to date the teacher, while you encourage him to do so. the chariot social link wants to keep running but if he does he runs the risk of never being able to walk again and of course you have to encouraging him to keep running. despite the fact the party members living in a dorm together the party members could not feel more distant. junpei attempts to be your bud without any one on one time. he is given praise for the love formed between him and chidori, but when the game dialogue are *actually read* it comes down to a few cringy encounters that leaves one feeling unimpressed. when combing through the game to find a reason to give a ♥♥♥♥ about any of these male characters, the best the game can offer  is monthly security footage. this footage provided the only experience that made me care about shinji as a character.  no game should definitive edition of a game should require playing another edition of said game to get the full experience.art wise the charm of the p3/p4 games is dropped for the generic unreal engine 4 effect.  i cannot recommend this game or even the older editions of it. _childDocuments_.review: A very good remake with some outdated mechanics that hold it back, though only slightly.The first, and perhaps most important thing about this game is that it practically oozes style from the seams. The art, music, lighting, and graphical overhaul this remake received should absolutely be praised. The look of the game has been rebuilt from the ground up to fall in line with it's edgy modern cousin, Persona 5, while still maintaining the comfy jazzy feel of the original (albeit with a remastered soundtrack which just sounds downright amazing).However, the most glaring issue is that, at it's core, this is still a remake of a game from 2006. It can be extremely repetitive at times, and some bosses are just straight-up damage sponges with no real weaknesses. This isn't to say that it's all bad, though. There have been a litany of QoL changes which truly make some of the grindy parts of the game more palatable. Some of these are brand new, while some have been borrowed from P3P, but all of them are welcome additions. I've tried on several different occasions to get into the Persona/SMT series and it's never really stuck until this game. Safe to say, I've now been bitten by the bug and will be moving on to Persona 5 while patiently waiting on the rumored Persona 4 remake.Side note: Runs at a dang near flawless 60fps on Steam Deck, as long as you have reflections turned off.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is an amazing "remake" of the game that defined why the SMT Persona series has become wildly successful.The story, characters and setting all remain the same but a few of the more modern changes presented in Persona 4 and 5 have been applied to Persona 3 here. One of the greatest changes is being able to directly give your party members orders in combat as well as the introduction of "Theurgies" that act as special attacks that each party member can activate. These Theurgies each charge faster based on individual settings/requirements for each party member. The basic Persona combat structure of matching weaknesses to enemies and triggering "1 More" attacks to chain downed statuses to go for All-Out attacks remains in place.The game's style still looks amazing and the menu work in these games remains second-to-none. No one makes stylish menus like Atlus does.A few negative remarks, mostly surrounding sale practices or removal of content that I'm personally not as upset about :"The Answer", which was added to the FES version on the Playstation 2 is going to be released separately at cost as DLC. I'm not as upset about this as others given the amount of additional work that needed to be done art and asset wise to the base game. If that practice doesn't sit well with you, I would say you should wait for a "complete edition" or a sale on both.The Female Protagonist and all associated social links/interactions from the PSP re-release of Persona 3 is not an option here. I also understand that it would've been a significant amount of work to add this in as an option and it would be nice if it would be released to this version so it can be the "definitive" version of Persona 3 going forward, but there has been no indication this content is coming to the game.Overall, for the price, I still think this game is a great way to either re-experience a classic JRPG in the modern era or experience for the first time where most of modern Persona owes its legacy, charm and style. I recommend the game wholeheartedly.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal remake of one of the greatest games ever made. Definitely the version I'll be playing from now on (unless I REALLY want to play as FEMC... but that mod project is already looking promising, anyway...). From a sheer gameplay standpoint, this is now my favorite Persona. They just keep honing it in all the right ways. I also loved what they did with Tartarus. I only heard a little about it before jumping in, and I expected it to be FAR less overhauled than it was. Yes, it's still procgen, but at least there are now major structural differences in the pre-made parts that match the aesthetic of every area, as opposed to everything being just built out of grids and tiles like the original (And P4's dungeons!)The only disappointment remains to be some of the decisions Atlus has been making recently with the challenge bosses in the series. They give you all these neat toys and ways to break the combat system down to its core, but then... take all of that away and gate what you can and can't do on the challenge bosses. Maybe, I dunno, find a way design them specifically around the systems you've already made instead of taking some of the player's options away to artificially enhance the difficulty? Maybe? It was annoying in P5R, and it's annoying here.W/R/T the Answer/ Episode Aigis stuff: I couldn't care less. Never cared for the Answer. There's some writing that is good in it (Yukari's feelings are VALID, dammit!), but a lot more that's just bad, in my opinion. And the gameplay is a slog. So I'm more than happy to just ignore it, and enjoy the original ending as it is as I always have. It's really scummy to charge for it like they did, but in my opinion, it should've neither been included in the original release OR been made as DLC. It should've just been forgotten. But hey, that's just me. So I will continue ignoring it and not wasting money on it. Maybe just, like, watch the cutscenes on YT or something.But yeah, 10/10 game done justice with this remake, in my opinion. Only really have minor quibbles with it (mainly some vibe/tonal/aesthetic stuff), but I have AT LEAST minor quibbles with EVERY Persona game, so welcome to the club. Unabashed recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: this is peak persona right here. 100% it on my first playthroughi first played p3fes back in summer 2019, and i was pretty ambivalent about it. for every thing i loved, there was some nitpick or strange design decision that held it back in some way. i ultimately came out of it thinking "the story was amazing, but the gameplay was such a slog". kinda the opposite of persona 5 to me where the story is just decent but the gameplay is fun.welp, now that this remake exists, pretty much everything has been improved, and i can definitely say that this has all i want in a persona game. great story, gameplay is actually fun now, and the presentation is top notch.my only real issues are the game balance (i played on hard mode, but it was still way too easy at points. theurgies are busted and should have been heavily nerfed), and the quirks from the original that passed down (some social links aren't good, some aspects of the story aren't amazing, strega is still kinda cringe).characters were rewritten to be more accurate to the original japanese script, but i feel like that made some characters lose some of their spark. i.e. yukari is nicer, akihiko is less geeky and more obsessive with training (probably a result of them sticking to their flanderization), etc. i gotta say tho, i came out liking some characters a lot more in this version like koromaru, ken, and even takaya somehow. my lads junpei and aigis still peak tho !!ultimately, based game. recency bias is probably at play here, but this is probably the best persona game and one of the best SMT games.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Persona 3 Reload was really just my goal to tie out finishing each of the modern Persona games in some form. As a big fan of Persona 5 Royal and decent enjoyer of Persona 4 Golden, it was at first a box to be checked, and I thought it would be around the same level of "well, it's pretty good I guess" that P4G was for me. The $70 drop was difficult but I thought it would be worth it to get in on the action.It was more than worth it.Persona 3 Reload became far more than a box to check off for me and quickly surpassed its price tag in worth. It absolutely has the best social links in all the games, incredible music, fun combat, a mind-boggling engaging story, and characters you'll never forget. Their arcs and the game's ending share a message that will stick with me forever. I don't cry a lot over fiction, but, well... let's just say whichever characters you attach to, no matter how insignificant of a social link they may be with a mere ~10-12 scenes, or how significant of a party member from the start of the game they are, all will give you absolutely gut-wrenching emotions. And if it hasn't happened yet, just wait. It kind of all comes crashing down.I loved this game so much. I'll never forget it. (And I'll never forget you, Bebe.)

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMENDEDA solid remake full of Quality of Life changes and a bunch of upgrades to graphics and lighting. On PC its a buttery smooth 120fps with no frame drops with 2-3 rare instances of crashing during my 100+ hours playthrough. Persona 3 Reload is one of the best JRPGs released this year. Like any other Persona game, you can expect a great cast, a good story, great music, a simplistic but excellent turn-based battle system, and a year in a Japanese Student's life (romance option included). _childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload LasagneIngredientsFor the meat sauce3 tbsp olive oil2 celery sticks, finely chopped1 onion, finely chopped1 carrot (about 100g), finely chopped3 garlic cloves, crushed140g cubetti di pancetta500g beef mince (we used 10% fat)500g pork mince or British veal mince200ml milk2 x 400g cans chopped tomatoes2 bay leaves1 rosemary sprig2 thyme sprigs2 tsp dried oregano2 beef stock cubes500ml red wineFor the lasagneabout 400g dried pasta sheets50g parmesan, finely gratedFor the white sauce (béchamel)1.5l milk1 onion, thickly sliced3 bay leaves3 cloves100g butter100g plain flourgood grating of nutmegSTEP 1First, make the béchamel sauce. Put the milk, onion, bay leaves and cloves into a large saucepan and bring very gently just up to the boil. Turn off the heat and set aside for 1 hr to infuse.STEP 2For the meat sauce, put the oil, celery, onion, carrot, garlic and pancetta in another large saucepan. Gently cook together until the veg is soft but not coloured.STEP 3Tip in the beef and pork mince, the milk and chopped tomatoes. Using a wooden spoon, stir together and break up and mash the lumps of mince against the sides of the pan. When the mince is mostly broken down, stir in all the herbs, the stock cubes and the red wine, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 1 hr, stirring occasionally to stop the bottom catching.STEP 4Uncover and gently simmer for another 30 mins-1 hr until the meat is tender and saucy. Taste and season.STEP 5To finish the béchamel sauce, strain the milk through a fine sieve into one or two jugs. Melt the butter in the same pan then, using a wooden spoon, mix in the flour and cook for 2 mins.STEP 6Stir in the strained milk, a little at a time – the mix will thicken at first to a doughy paste, but keep going, adding milk gradually to avoid lumps. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring constantly (if you have lumps, give it a quick whisk). Gently bubble for a few minutes until thickened. Season with salt, pepper and a good grating of nutmeg.STEP 7Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Spread a spoonful of the meat sauce over the base of a roughly 3.5-litre baking dish. Cover with a single layer of dried pasta sheets, snapping them to fit if needed, then top with a quarter of the béchamel. Spoon over a third of the meat sauce and scatter over a little of the parmesan.STEP 8Repeat the layers – pasta, béchamel, meat and parmesan – two more times to use all the meat sauce. Add a final layer of pasta, the last of the béchamel and remaining parmesan. Sit the dish on a baking tray to catch spills and bake for 1 hr until bubbling, browned and crisp on top.Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played the original but, from what I've seen on YouTube, it's a great remake. Especially the anime cutscenes in FES look like they're drawn by kids in kindergarten, to be honest.Apart from aforementioned improvements, what I liked the most about P3R is having 3 party members from the get-go, starting to be able to go out at night very early in the game and the boss fights being assigned to certain dates instead of pushing deadlines on players. Especially the last one is a blessing when it comes to the overall time management. When it comes to visuals, everyone claims that P3 has finallly reached P5's graphics. However, P3's graphics actually look so much better than those of Persona 5 to an extent that it started to make me thinking that P5 actually started to show its age. The OST is a tiny bit weaker than those of 4 and 5 but it's still great.Combat wise, I'd say it's somewhere between P4G and P5R. It's not as easy and dumbed down as Persona 5 but, it doesn't contain tons of shenanigans like Persona 4 either. The reason is that on top of successfully blending the Baton Pass from P5 ("Shift" in here) and the Shuffle Time from previous games, a new game mechanic called Theurgy is introduced. Therefore, they all make the combat quite enjoyable. Thankfully, the game doesn't require you to do any extra grinding on top of discovering Tartarus at your own pace. Seriously, I died only once in the whole game and that's because a random boss in Tartarus used a dark instakill on me and it surprisingly hit... However, I must admit that Theurgy is an OP mechanic which literally breaks the game when used.Speaking of Tartarus, I agree that it can be repetitive. However, I don't know how but discovering Tartarus never gets boring despite that. Just like Mementos in P5R...When it comes to increasing stats and social links, P3R is the easiest one by far, compared to the other two. Working at Chagall Café is the most effective when it comes to increasing Courage and Charm while for Academics, eating ramen is the most effective option. Besides these two, spending time at arcade also helps a lot to increase a certain stat on a certain day. Thanks to all those 3 options, I could manage to maximise all stats by the end of summer. This is important because Courage is required for ♥♥♥♥♥'s, Charm is for Yukari's and Academics is required for Mitsuru's social links. While the social link system is exactly the same, if Odagiri didn't waste my time and if the game didn't start the social links of Mitsuru and Aigis too late in the game, I would have been maxed out all of them. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you, Odagiri... The only thing bothers me in this section is the lack of Valentines' Day, to be honest. The hilarious dramas on Valentines' Day has been my sole reason to build my own harem in Persona games and not seeing that in here too disappointed me a bit.When I try to look at the down side, the only things I can think of are: "Why there is a smartphone in 2009?" or "How can Koromaru summon a persona as it can't use an evoker?". But, are these really enough not to mark Persona 3 as a special game? Definitely not.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I am a bit mixed on this one....Don't get me wrong - it's a good game, mainly due to the fact that the original persona 3  was a good game and players, who haven't experienced the original will have a great time, hence the reccomendation, but.....i just felt like going through the same game with sanded off edges.For those uninitiated, you're playing as a transfer student, who joins SEES and their mission to unravel the mystery behind something called dark hour (the hour between one day and another) and the tartarus that during it stands in place of their school. You fight shadows with the help of your persona and you summon it with a gun shaped device called evoker. It's RPG/high school student simulator, where you ascend Tartarus by night and by day you try to socialize. The story still holds up. There are scenes that will definetly tug at your heart strings and character have a lot of depth. the themes of death are very prevelent, if you couldn't notice with the coffins everywhere during dark hour or characters giving themselves massive head trauma with the evokers, which oddly enough never feels tastless. There are some added scenes, that flesh out some of the characters more and social links remain the same and that includes the lack of ones with your male companions, instead of that, they added linked episodes, which are time limited. Honestly, it would be better, if they had regular social links, but it's not bad and they do the job. The RPG aspect, has been refined and reworked. They got rid of the fatigue system and you can control your party members, unlike in the original, where somebody had a bright idea of AI doing that for you. they added theurgies, which are basically fusion spells from the original, but now they just need to fill up, kind of like limit breaks in final fantasy. You get more special attacks as you collect and fuse persona in velvet room. One change that i didn't apreciate, is that some boss fights feel more scripted - like i do one of the special attacks, only for health bar to not move - it turns out, that i had to wait for bosses turn to change or pull of something - this i find pretty annoying, especially on the repeated playthroughs.visually it looks great, but it is also kind of downside. Like it's obvious how they tried to recreate persona 5's suave and energetic visuals, but the problem is that this is not persona 5, that game has completely different tone, so the new clean cool look and, for the lack of the better word, stylishnes clashes with it. the other thing that got a facelift is tartarus and while there is more visual variety, it still gets quite monotonous after a while.The soundtrack is great as always, but new versions of the old tracks have some weird elements or changes that i didn't apreciate. Like that weird drill-like synth on mass destruction or the fact, that the chorous isn't as punchy as it should be. On the other hand, the new songs New Moon, New Life, Color your night and it's going out now are great additions.To sum up - i'm conflicted. Part of me feels like buying portable is better option, seeing as that one is like 50 dollars cheaper and has option to play as femc, but also i don't think it's a bad way to play P3. It's just another version - one step forward, two steps back. In a better world, we would get remake with everything, including Kotone. what is likely going to happen is that  we get a full priced Femc version of the game. Knowing atlus and their DLC fiasco, i wouldn't be shocked.

_childDocuments_.review: Since it is Persona 3's Promised Day, I would like to write a review on this game."(Cause) we're living at the mercy of pain and fear, until we dead it, forget it and let it all disappear"There is a timelessness in this game. Memento mori, as the game starts with, as it constantly reminds, as it provides us with other meanings through characters lenses, and as it tenderly closes with. I have grown to cherish the most sincere messages and the way they are framed through conversations that the protagonist has whether he's experiencing normal school life, wandering through the city during evenings, or between SEES teammates, or rather the "extracurricular" club.The music is well-composed and timely placed, whether that be alleviating an awkward encounter, a mischievous deed, or even where words cannot be put together. I'm glad they brought Lotus Juice back in the studio and he really burned it down with the amazing-as-always performances. In terms of graphics, Atlus took what they did well with Persona 5 Royal and perfected the craft even more in this as there are different shades through different school semesters. Once the game is finished, combining with the new loading music, the game provides you with a different loading screen and this alone plays and pulls some of my heart strings.While old English VA's are presented in the game with other roles, the new voice cast has done an amazing job at delivering such unforgettable characters.Persona 3 Reload delivers such a remarkable story that has withstood the test of time of the JRPG genre, for many remakes and many gaming console generations it has provided. For my first 90-hour playthrough, sometimes, just like in life, the hardest part of ending is to start again.March 6th, 2024 update: Atlus confirming the epilogue after Promised Day is one hell of a move.

_childDocuments_.review: Characters don't feel like they revolve around you as the main character. All of the party members grow on their own as the story progresses and it kept me interested in them throughout the whole game. SEES easily tops both P4 and P5's casts due to their own individual character arcs throughout the story. Junpei goes from the classic anime protagonist's best friend troupe to a determined teammate who keeps the mood light after serious events. Never losing the shine of his original personality, but growing into the new responsibilities he now has. All party members have a similar sort of evolution as the story progresses. I love both P4 and P5 but very few characters in those games truly grow out of their gimmicks.Combat is basically the original P5 combat copy pasted. Baton Pass (now called Shifting) allows for your whole party to combo their abilities in one turn to hit enemy weaknesses. The new combat ability in this game is the 'Theurgy' system. Basically an ultimate attack that all your party members will passively charge as a fight goes on (but can be kept between fights). It's neat. They have beautiful animations, but they're WAY too strong into late game. Like, one-shots most bosses strong. Offensive Theurgies stack with Charge / Concentrate spells + standard buffs and debuffs + Boost and Amp passives if it matches the Theurgy element. Did that make combat boring? Not really. You're not playing a Persona game to experience challenging combat. You play to stack overpowered ♥♥♥♥ and see how high the numbers go. And the numbers go high.Moving on to the other half of this game, Social Links are still as good as ever. I enjoyed all of them, but that's completely subjective. However they objectively don't fall behind P4 or P5's stories. Encouraging a classmate and fellow athlete who refuses to accept help for his clearly failing body, helping a dying man find meaning in his last moments, comforting a child through her parents divorce, listening to an anonymous woman rant about her daily life through text chat in an MMO. The many choices are varied and you will most likely find a character you relate to, or just really like. Sadly (and predictably) this game keeps the long-since outdated system in the original P3 of the male party members not having a social link. There are special events where you can hang out with them, and you even unlock new personas at the end of them, however they are not attached to a Social Link and will not give the usual Arcana Burst benefit from it.Tartarus begins just as dull as you'd think from a randomly generated series of floors. However, Shuffle Time events after combat give you permanent stat boosts and exclusive bonuses through the Major Arcana cards that show up. Then as you climb further up, you unlock new Major Arcana cards that provide new unique bonuses as well. The dungeon evolves and new doors, treasure chests and special shadows start to appear, all of which provide valuable items and advantages.Persona 3 has the best story of the three hands-down, with all of your main characters tragically involved in the main plot someway or another. It may not have the recognisable antagonists of P5, nor the unique draw of the TV world in P4, but the Dark Hour (and the mysteries surrounding it) surpass the other two games with its twists. Obviously I refuse to spoil any of it. I miraculously avoided spoilers until I finally got to play this game and I want nothing more than for others to have that experience too. Story is always going to be subjective, but I've played all three of these games and this one kept me locked-in the whole way though.Party members in combat all gain special passive bonuses by hanging out with them in the dorm. Yukari gets reduced costs on her recovery spells, Junpei gives your whole party bonus crit chance, Aigis gives your whole party bonus physical damage etc. Really gives your party their own identity in combat rather than just being there as human shields for the MC.Not a real issue honestly, but this game is shorter than the other two. P5 on a first playthough took me ~90 hours, P4 around 80. This game I clocked in 65 hours to finish it. A decent amount of that time was spent either AFK or unnecessarily min-maxing persona fusions too. So I'd estimate maybe 55-60 hours actually playing. Still a long game, but I felt the need to mention it just in-case an assumption was made that this game was as long as the other two.Party level imbalance became a massive issue as I went further into the game. There is a system that is supposed to fix this. There is a chance that a magic clock thing can spawn at the end of a floor that will give your lower level party members XP, and give them a boost up to the MC's level. Issue is that this only does 13 levels at a time. When I'm at level 60, and poor Junpei is chilling below level 20, I'm not going to use this system due to it requiring multiple uses of this clock to push him up to my level. Me, Yukari, Misuru, Aigis. For the whole game. I enjoyed my harem squad but I would have liked to try my other party members out at some point. The game even suggests to you multiple times to swap out party members to account for enemy weaknesses, but I cannot do that without getting boned by the massive level disparity.Now for actual party imbalance. Yukari and Mitsuru are super busted, Mitsuru was literally out-damaging me for a decent portion of the game (if you've played another Persona game you'd know how insane that is). Yukari's healing allows your whole party to live every attack, and also allows her to spam her Theurgy multiple times per fight due to her healing giving her a huge amount of charge. On the other side, both Ken and Koromaru are too risky to actually use due to them having weaknesses to Curse and Bless respectively. Mudo and Hama insta-kill spells are kind of common among shadows in this game. So although the idea of having a dog and a literal child in my squad crossed my mind at some points, it was just never worth it.Opening the main menu at any point forces the game back down to 30fps. Not a big deal or anything but it takes a few seconds to get back up to a normal frame rate even after unpausing. It made pausing the game for any reason feel like a chore when I got back to the gameplay. Again, only for a few seconds, but it turns out you have to whip out the menu a lot and it got old real quick.Good game 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload... I'm late on the review here, however now that all content has been released for it, I can give a fullfledged opinion. As someone who's sunken in numerous hours into this series, I can safely say that this game is EASILY the definitive way to play P3 now.Let us start withTHE JOURNEY:We begin the journey once again with our lovable, blue-haired, emo protagonist as he transfers schools after going from place to place-. Yadda yadda yadda, I explained all this in my P3P review, so I won't go into detail of the plot for the Journey. Simply put, mysterious big tower needs to be explored with the help of your party.The gameplay in this game is VASTLY improved over the original. It more closely mirrors the gameplay of P5; which makes sense. That game set a new standard when it released for the Persona series. That being said, I found this game more difficult compared to P5. Not that that's a bad thing, I love games that give me a challenge!The mechanics as a whole are what you'd expect from a persona game. Using a combination of physical and elemental skills to exploit weaknesses and get the upper hand. The presentation of this game was shot up to 11 and it shows. Another new mechanic to bring up is the use of theurgy's! Brand new abilities that allow anyone in the current party to unleash a powered up skill that can provide an advantage on the battlefield! One thing I also want to bring up. The voice cast. Normally I wouldn't but it's no secret that P3 received a recast of all the main party characters, among a few others. It's jarring at first if you're used to the original cast, but they still do a phenomenal job! Oh! And of course, FULLY voiced social links too! That one REALLY surprised me! It made me care for the social links a lot more, as the voice acting added a new layer of personality!EPISODE: AIGIS (THE ANSWER):Much to my excitement, they added the answer into the game through a paid expansion pack! (35 bucks is a bit nuts, but I'm not gonna complain about that. There are already enough people that complained.)Either way, The Answer in FES was a fairly nice addition to add more play time to the game, and this? I think for the most part, it did everything BETTER compared to the original Answer. And once again, the voice acting was superb. Without getting too into it, it's a solid addition to the game.Oh, and the music BANGS like always.I will highly recommend this game, and I will continue to sing it's praises into the heavens. Atlus truly cooked with this one!I give it a 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good remake but there is one massive issue with it: Party AI doesn't work.I will change this review when/if there is any improvement on this issue, or at least a proper workaround.It starts off with small things that you notice:-Junpei won't use fire attacks when it's clearly the critical weakness of enemies, opting to use physical attacks instead...But fine, one offs can happen. However, gradually the more glaring issues become noticable:-Shift: Party members cannot use shift or rather, will not use shift in battle. Why? This was possible in Persona 5 when the AI would somehow make a decision based on equipped Personas, adding a great flow of battle. This is unacceptable.So what does this mean? It means that a party member will often just fire the same attack over and over until his or her turn is over with.-Theurgy: Love this added component of battle, a nice added alternative of the combo attacks from Persona 4 and Persona 5... Fatal flaw? The party AI will rarely if ever use it when available. I have seen it used, however it's very rare. Currently I have a party where all 4 members have maxed the theurgy bar but just will not use it, even if they've run out of SP.... What is the point of this?Basically if you play with party AI on, you are forced to switch to manual control to force them to use theurgy skills. A big step down from Persona 4 and 5 when these attacks would happen randomly.If these features have been built in, then the AI should be designed to use them properly.Apart from the awful Party AI, the game has other annoying issues:-Dying and reloading: If you die, you are forced to go through the usual dreary ending screen. THEN you are not given an option to reload, but only to restart from when you first entered Tartarus. Likely, you probably regularly saved each time you went back to the entrance and therefore have a save that is more recent than that.... So when you die, you're forced to either go back to the main menu or to your first entry, and manually reload that save. It's 2024 Atlus! How can you bring in a save system as bad as almost 20 years ago?-I am getting performance issues, occasional skipping on PC. But not that often and not that major.Sorry, this is not good enough, especially for a P3 fan who spent 100 euros on the full edition.. Polish your game, and above ALL. fix your party AI, Atlus.

_childDocuments_.review: TL; DR: I've played the original game as well FES, and I can say for certain that Persona 3 Reload improves everything the original title got right.__________________________________Persona 3 is one of my favorite games ever, and to this day it's been the only game to ever make me cry like a little kid at the end. I have a strong emotional connection with this title, its characters and especially the music. It was THE game that put Persona's name in the map and it was the last game in the series that still had a bit of the Shin Megami Tensei flavor with its story and themes.✅ A faithful 1:1 remake of the original game in every single aspect.✅ A simple, yet very engaging storyline with interesting, well written characters. In a weird way it reminds me a bit of Evangelion, somehow.✅ Combat is also fundamentally simple but carries a lot of depth with the elemental affinities and Personas. The party members have been completely rebalanced and got new abilities, called Theurgies (essentially Specials), as well bonus passive skills. Pretty much every character is viable now (though sadly Mitsuru fell behind compared to the rest of the cast).✅ Tons of quality-of-life changes from the original game across the board. Way too many to listen, but it makes the whole difference.✅ The soundtrack is absolutely stellar, as you'd expect from Shoji Meguro. The re-arranged tracks sound as good as the original, and I dare to say this is Meguro's magnum opus; his use of leitmotivs for Persona 3's soundtrack is outstanding and unmatched.✅ Both the EN and JP voices are great. The EN cast really nailed the role and they sound even better than the original cast from the PS2 era. Also, Tara Platt, Yuri Lowenthal and Liam O'brien return as support cast to voice secondary character (Platt reprises her role as Elizabeth).✅ This game has an impressive attention to detail in the smallest things. Such as every electrical object being seen connected to an outlet in the dorm. Or how idle animations of the party members in the dorm are filled with personality.✅ New activities and fully voiced events with party members.✅ The stylization that Persona 5 brought to the series is reflected in this game beautifully. Menus and UI are gorgeous to look at and still inject the vibe of Persona 3 without looking too much like Persona 5.✅ The celshading is pretty spot on to give the whole game this very anime feel.✅ Koromaru best Persona mascot ever.❌ Very limited, nearly non-existent graphics customization settings. Also, there is no way to remove motion blur, and turning on reflections will overheat your GPU if it doesn't support raytracing.❌ Graphically speaking this game is a bit of a mixed bag. While the main character models and renders look really nice, many backgrounds lack detail, use low-res textures and look a bit bland. In addition many of the models used for the Personas look a bit unpolished. The simplification fits the artstyle, as it's not trying to achieve realistic graphics, and I'm perfectly fine with, but I can't help to think this game sometimes looks two generations older.❌ As much as I adore this game I think it should've been 60 USD; it's not worth the 70 USD to be very honest.❌ Paid DLC on top of the already high price tag is a bit insulting. Sure, the DLC consists of Personas and costumes from other games, but the fact those aren't instead unlockables leave a bad taste in your mouth. SEGA just being greedy.❌ This game doesn't include The Answer, which was a "sequel" to the main story included in Persona 3 FES. Knowing SEGA, they'll probably make it as DLC and overprice it too, and then re-release the game 2 years later with The Answer bundled, Persona 5 Royal style. Edit: Atlus just revealed that The Answer (AKA Episode Aigis) is on the way as DLC for September 2024, as we guessed.__________________________________Overall, even with my peeves, I absolutely loved this remake from start to finish and got my money worth. The ending hit me as hard as it did playing the original game; I cried like a little kid.I've seen a lot of people complaining about the removal the female protagonist, but I'm personally okay with that. Her exclusion doesn't hinder the experience and makes the male protagonist stand out a bit more compared to the ones from Persona 4 and Persona 5.If you liked Persona 5 you'll definitely enjoy this game, even though it's simpler in execution. It's not as flashy and stylish but it has consistency and very relatable characters.
