_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 specifically is a very memorable game to me. I first played the Portable version on PSP and, even with a lot of downgrades of the original (and some QoL from Persona 4), it managed to affect me in a very emotional and thoughtful way of many different aspects of my life.Because of it, I followed this franchise from that point on and played many other Persona and SMT games, most of them were indeed a great time/experience, but not a single one managed to hit me like 3 did.But even with my personal bias and attachment to it, I will try to give at least an honest to good review about positive and negative aspects of this "Remake". Please take all of it with a grain of salt.Pros:-The models are amazing. They really did polish everyone, not only Soejima's Art style improved, but his anatomy as well. If you compare to Persona 5 models, the new ones are less uncanny than the previous game.- The Soundtrack is top notch. Atsushi Kitajoh managed to create not only beautiful arranges from the originals made by Shoji Meguro, but  with the return of the legendary Lotus Juice on the rhymes, they managed to outclass Mass Destruction. It's going Down is perfect in a way that hits you with a dopamine rush when you hit shadow advantage and, if you time it correctly, hit an all out attack at the peak of the song. Color your night still gives you a "Persona 5" vibe, but you can still "feel" it belongs to Persona 3. The entire soundtrack likes to work on small leitmotifs here and there to make you feel attached to the atmosphere of the game, and when you hit the final part + the credits song you get a kind like "nostalgia" punch on your gut together with the really emotional ending.- The Battle system is even more balanced and comfortable than the previous Persona games. The party members skills got buffed, the addition of Kouga and Eiga spells balanced the Light/Dark elements. The Navigator system AND Baton pass equivalents got balanced/nerfed to improve the all in all experience of the game, not to mention since you're fighting shadows, you can't have a spoiler of their weaknesses from the Velvet Room fusion/Recruiting them on ambush.- Tartarus got a INCREDIBLE revamp. The original and portable versions made Tartarus only looks the same thing with different color schemes each Name Floors, but on Reload each one has it's own vibe/environment/random seeds to make the Immersion and experience way better- The addition of Link episodes with party members and, even with some story relevant characters made the experience even better for newcomers and P3 Veterans. They even added some special situations that were exclusive for certain Versions of the game (one from P3FES and another from P3Portable FemMC route only)- The addition of Theurgy Skills made the gameplay even more interesting, putting the Fusion Spells the protagonist had on Theurgies (and not requiring you to have the Personas on the party all times) not only balanced the use of it, but also made it even more interesting to complete the Compendium- You can now choose to date a female Social Link or not. Compared to the original, you were obligated todate the girls and even had the risk of getting a reverse arcana if you got caught cheating or ignored them for a long time- Reverse Arcanas now are way harder to get, In my entire gameplay, I didn't get a single one, so I think the only way now is purposely choosing a rude/stupid option on the Social Link interactions, which brings me to the next topic- Voiced Social Links improved the Visual Novel part of the game, making you feel more attached to them.- Better HUD/Aesthetic design than the previous games.Now with the Cons:- The game feels way more easy than compared with the original and other Persona games, sure, it takes more time to "break" than Persona 5, but the few cases I got a game over were on two specific battles and against the Reaper because a friend on Discord kept insisting for me to beat it on level 35~50. Even with all the QoL and balance on some mechanics, Theurgies really help to mitigate or even brute force some bosses/challenge battles. - You can't change Tartarus Theme like the FES/Portable Version, which is a shame because after a while it gets really boring to hear the same arranged for more than 200 floors.- The game does gives you more options, but you still have the same time limit from the previous games, so, unless you follow a guide or is a veteran, you can pretty much fail to get all Social Links on the first play through(Veteran's Advice: focus on the School Social Links since you can't do them on weeks before exams, exams and school vacation+near the ending)- The Social Links are a hit or miss for the community. Either you hate them, or you love it. So I highly avoid discussing about that online.- Some Link episodes are miss able and even unlocks some specific Personas to fuse, so if you don't make them or lose one, you're pretty much screwed.- Not having the "Answer" and "female MC" route makes the fan base debate if this could really be the definitive edition of Persona 3, but they already confirmed on making a future DLC for The Answer Episode, so, only time will tell.- Tartarus has few Designs for each Floor Section and some are either extremely short, or stupidly big with a big NOTHING on them, so after a few times, you just ignored them and just look to the HUD on the left side.- The Artbook and OST DLC's are a scam. You cannot access them unless booting up the game SPECIFICALLY for each one, meanwhile Steam has a built in MP3 player for games with Soundtrack for years already. This is probably a terrible decision from Atlus/Sega to avoid people from pirating it or spreading on the internet.I highly recommend this game for both Veterans and newcomers, and I can assure that this game was a test/base for the future Persona games (possibly 6 or another 4 Remaster)Elizabeth's Megidolaon out of  10 would cry for the 7th time with Memories of You playing in the credits

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a remake and updated version of Persona 3. Among the new-gen Persona games, 3 is my favorite, and I had a good time playing it, although I already knew most of the story. + Main story that keeps the players on their toes as it unfolds.+ Fun JRPG battle sequences with a mix of daily life balance.+ Stylish UI, Art direction, and music.+ Some parts of the story are updated and so is the gameplay's quality of life compared to prior versions. - The Dungeon exploration can be repetitive (but still doable for me.)- I said earlier that some parts of the story are updated but only minor details and non-major interactions are added. The majority of the story is the same as the older versions. Returning players may find it repetitive aside from updated graphics and visuals.- DLC selections on costumes are not as varied as Persona 5. And the choice of bundling some miscellaneous DLCs with episode Aigis is questionable.For the first-time players of the Persona series, I would recommend the 5th game more but if you like a more sad and serious theme or want to explore more of Persona games or just JRPGs in general then I would totally recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Life and death are the same, but on different ends. Now, you are looking at your own life, thinking what is the meaning behind it, searching and grasping for answers. Storytelling is quite important for a medium to be good and P3 Reload did it perfectly with bringing back original story, but adding few tweaks and tricks here and there.  I had chance to play original, but due to bugs, I wasn't able to finish it. Yet now, I have finished it with huge enjoyment, plentiful of laughs, immersive story and characters, at the same time, a story filled with sorrow, loss and a bit of depression. Persona 3 story in this refreshed state feels as it should, very real. Even though it is just a video game.If you have never played Persona game, you should start with this one, then move either to older titles or newer ones. You will enjoy it quite well. As for me, I am tired of grinding, but that's just me trying first run on highest difficulty. That's why I have finished main story around 150 hour mark. Don't be like me, dumb. Play on easier difficulty and enjoy really well made game. Many other AAA studios should learn by now, that majority of people don't want multiplayer games and wanna come back to solid singleplayer stories. Thanks and until we meet again. On Aigis laps this time.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this for a couple of reasons.First, is the game generally feels very cheap.  There's a handful of well crafted and artistically beautiful scenes and animations in combat with an absolutely slapping soundtrack, but they are used over and over and over to the point of exhaustion.  That wouldn't be so terrible if the game wasn't $70, with a "premium edition" at $100 barely giving anything extra but a couple of costumes.  Not to mention they misled people into believing they would get the expansion pass with that and now they're finding out that its an extra $30 for it.  Overall, this is just price gouging on a level I find to be fairly disgusting.  I bought the game on sale and even then I feel like I overpaid for the quality that is actually here.Second, is that the story is extremely drawn out and boring.  Dig a bit deeper on the forums and you'll see similar complaints, followed by fanboys saying things like "it gets good after the 60 hour mark".  My reaction to that is an astronomically large yet calmly delivered "how about no."  While I loved the opening month or so, eventually that excitement drained and the game lost its spark.  I am at the 25 hour mark as of this review and am literally dying of boredom.  Doing the same things over and over, with social link stories as dry as the Sahara which are supposed to be its main selling point.  (Spoilers, I guess (but is it really?)) My favorite example of this was the track team social link, its story was a teammate going like "ow I have a bad knee" 10x times in a row with absolutely no payoff or tie to the story at all.  It just ends.  Horribly unsatisfying.Look, maybe the game DOES "get good" at the 60 hour mark, and maybe I'll try to slog my way through some more if I manage to find the energy to, but my time is more valuable than anything these days and if you can't bring me in on just a decent premise by the 25 hour mark, then I'm just going to tap out.

_childDocuments_.review: Should have been a definitive edition but otherwise a great remake of Persona 3Ignoring the problem that persona 3 still doesnt have a definitive edition (and by result the best social links are locked to Kotone's route of Persona 3 portable) this is an extremely well done remake of Persona 3, and I'd definitely recommend it to anyone who hasnt played the original trio of games (though you should 100% go and play portable afterwards to get the best experience in terms of other characters) the game has the perfect combat that comes from Persona 5 with a much more balanced system, admittedly the music is absolutely awful here, the main fight theme "Mass Destruction" was utterly ruined in this remake, as was most of the other songs, and the bosses are definitely weaker than the ones in P4G and they dont even hold a candle to Persona 5's, with that said this is still a god tier story with some amazing characters. Just avoid buying the DLC at any cost, it's a huge rip off and you can get all the DLC stuff for free anyway by using the mod menu on gamebanana

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Persona series, this one is a fantastic installment. I played Persona 5/ P5Royal but hadn't played the original P3 so this review is a holistic view of the game not just reload's changes. The combat is engaging and satisfying, though Tartarus gets a little grindy. All the social links started off as relatively uninteresting to me but then had a twist that totally changed my opinion. I haven't yet finished the game so I can't comment on the ending but so far I like the setting and the direction of the story.If you want to play for the dating/ romance sim aspects, I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for that, though I think the romance adds a little enjoyment. I wished there was more romance in p5 too, though, so I think its par the course for this series. Last, my biggest critique is that I know the original allowed the MC to be female but this version does not. I wish they kept that, for replayability at the very least. Solid 9/10 though.

_childDocuments_.review: While I recommend this game 100%, I would disclaimer this review with I would not recommend it be your FIRST persona game. While the game I assume is much updated from the originals (never played them), I would say Persona 5 would be the most newcomer friendly entry into this series. If you were in your young adult years during the end of the 2010s, this games theme is going to be nostalgic, a lot of the cultural feeling is very reminiscent of those times, from the style, to the music. Personally I love it, even if it makes me feel like an old man. Overall highly recommend to anyone who enjoy's coming of age stories.

_childDocuments_.review: If I included P5 this would be my 5th time going through a Persona game and it’s crazy how comforting going back to the series was. The first 40 hours flew by like nothing.The game kind of gets slow at parts, especially in the second half where the dungeon sections get longer but the story is still spaced out the same. It makes it feel more dragged on than it is I think. At least they continuously add new social stuff with party members to keep things interesting during this section.Reload added a bunch of stuff that seems to streamline and punch up the gameplay and kind of makes it easier. I got really into Persona fusing for the first time, almost completing the whole compendium.P3R is right up there with P5 for me as one of my favorite games. It has the best story of the three and its weaknesses with half of its party members was “fixed” this time around with the link episodes. The social links were more misses than hits for me this time around and the pacing can be a bummer sometimes (though this is a Persona problem in general). I can also talk about the role playing aspect has kind of worn off on me, like how the player is only rewarded for being a “yes man” or how inconsequential the dating sim part is to the story (even Sakura Wars for the Saturn did this better). But I don’t want the negatives to feel like they overshadowed the positive experience I had. It’s been something special playing and beating this game right after Final Fantasy X. Both games deal with similar themes of death, inevitability, responsibility, inheriting the past generations’ sins, and the end of youth in varying degrees. And because of that, I guess I’ve had a lot of those things rattling around in my mind the last few months. I did not tear up at the end like I did with FFX, though I can’t say I wasn’t extremely moved during the end of the game. And of course during the monologue the day after. A or 9/10105 Hours4/29/2024

However the game is definitely incomplete in terms of its content. It has some improvements that were included in the Persona 3 FES version of the game, but it cuts out The Answer. _childDocuments_.review: Although if tends to change depending on the day you ask, I would say Persona 3 is my favorite game in the Persona series, and one of the best games the Megaten series as a whole has to offer.  I grew up with it, it introduced me to the larger SMT series as a whole, and it's left its mark for over a decade. When I found out it was finally coming to modern platforms as P3P, and I saw how terribly Atlus had treated it,  I lost any hope that I'd see Persona 3 brought to it's full potential. Then one day, a trailer for P3R leaked on Atlus' Instagram.I had no faith in this remake at first. The trailer looked nice, but with a lot of disappointments back to back from Atlus, (and the gaming landscape at large) I refused to get my hopes up, keeping my eye on it from a distance. I went in with low expectations, expecting a butchered cash grab, but within the first few hours, I was suprised.There's no need to exposit further, Persona 3 Reload blew me away. While I'd still hesitate to call it "the definitive version of Persona 3" It absolutely stands up with FES. The team went above and beyond here, from the presentation, to the game play improvements, both big and small QOL. The new voice actors to a magnificent job, with all of the social links hitting so much harder than they did before, and SEES translating perfectly, feeling perfectly like themselves, even with the new content. If I had to go for minor complaints, I miss the tired system. It was fun trying to minmax your time as much as possible, and if you knew what you were doing you could exploit the positives and negatives that came with it. And while now your Academics feels a bit harder to max out than it used to with the extra study time, the sizeable upgrades and reworks to Tartarus make up for it. Honestly, I'm just happy to have gotten to experience a fully realised version of a game that is so fundamental to me. If you haven't experienced a Persona game before, this is a perfect starting place, and if you've played them all before, I can't recommend a revisit enough. Persona 3 Reload is a brilliant diamond in the unfortunate sea of remakes that make up most of gaming's release cycle now, and I couldn't be happier. Here's hoping this shining mark of quality continues into Atlus' future releases. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Before giving this game a go, I got like, 3/4 through the game on P3P, but stopped for some weird reason.  But I'm really glad I came back around and tried this game again.  It's excellent.  The new additions bring up the overall quality of life a lot and brings it more in line gameplay-wise with Persona 5.  Both the turn-based combat and the daily life gameplay are very good.  Near the end of my time with the game, I loaded a save after realizing I wasn't going to get all of the social links in time, but I'm glad I did.  After re-prioritizing what to spend my time on, I'm happy to say I just barely made it.  The stories attached to most of the social links were really well-written, it was great to see them all pay off in the end.  I feel like I was attached to these social links moreso than in the other 2 Persona games I've played.  They were really cool!  I do wish that I could have formed proper ones with my male party members, but it's not too big of a deal, I guess.  And dear god, the music is 100% the best part about this game.  I think I legitimately spend like, 80% of my time playing this game bouncing along in my seat to it, it was awesome.  While some tracks I think were better in the version of the game I played years ago, I think the majority of these re-recordings are a lot better.  I don't know why people would buy Persona 4 and 5 music DLC when you have music as awesome as this.Anyway, play this game if you're interested.  You won't regret it.  I'm crossing my fingers we get The Answer, since I never got around to playing that as well.

The best thing remains which is the narative and unlike with the original I now have no problem recommending people to play this due to the better pacing and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: "Persona 3 Reload" is not just a game; it's an experience. Atlus has outdone themselves in revitalizing this classic, infusing it with new life while staying true to the original's soul. The game seamlessly blends elements of traditional Japanese RPGs with a compelling social simulation, creating a rich, multifaceted world that is both engaging and emotionally resonant. The most striking improvement in "Persona 3 Reload" is the visual and audio overhaul. The graphics have been updated to stunning HD, making every scene more immersive. The character models are more detailed, and the animations smoother, bringing the world of "Persona 3" into vivid clarity. The soundtrack, always a highlight of the series, has been remastered, with some tracks re-imagined, adding depth to both the battles and the more poignant moments of the story. Gameplay-wise, "Persona 3 Reload" maintains the series' challenging turn-based combat but introduces refined mechanics that make battles more strategic and rewarding. The addition of new Personas and the ability to directly control party members adds layers of strategy previously unexplored in the original. These improvements make combat encounters feel fresh and invigorating, even for those familiar with the original game. At its heart, "Persona 3" has always been about its story and characters, and "Reload" enhances these aspects beautifully. The narrative is deep and engaging, touching on themes of friendship, mortality, and the struggles of adolescence. The expanded dialogue and additional scenes provide further depth to the already well-developed characters, making each of their journeys feel more personal and impactful. The Social Link system, a hallmark of the series, is expanded in "Reload," offering more opportunities to explore the relationships between characters. These interactions not only provide insight into the characters' backstories but also affect gameplay, influencing the strength and abilities of your Personas. "Persona 3 Reload" is more than just a nostalgia trip; it's a testament to how a classic can be transformed into something new and exciting without losing what made it special in the first place. It's a game that will resonate with newcomers and long-time fans alike, offering an experience that is both familiar and fresh.In conclusion, "Persona 3 Reload" is a must-play title that beautifully balances its RPG elements with a compelling narrative and character development. It's a rare gem that reminds us why we fell in love with gaming in the first place.  My only complaint is that Atlus removed Junpei's classic line

_childDocuments_.review: Rather than a negative review, this is more of a mixed review.I was a bit skeptical of the remake, so I wanted to hold off my excitement of reviewing a remake of one of my favourite stories in a game of all time to have an objective review. I waited till I finished the final boss and experienced the good ending before I said something. You can tell this was made by people who genuinely care for the Persona 3 IP and not some soulless remake. The conditions for social links are still strict, the themes and stories are still very much the same, the gameplay and everything has been given a lot of quality of life improvements, though in the case of Tartarus I haven't quite felt it was really that big of an improvement. There is a lot of mention about Tartarus dialogue and all that, but it's more akin to Persona 5's mementos chatter than the interactions that you could have in Persona 3 Portable (talking to the members by interaction in Tartarus).Gameplay wise, I have no qualms. In fact, it surpasses previous iterations of Persona 3 in that aspect.However; in terms of the story, I feel differently. I very much disagree with a lot of the story elements. The soundtrack was done by an apprentice of Shoji Meguro. Yumi Kawamura isn't returning for vocals (she's pretty old so I don't blame her for not being able to hit the same chords as she used to) and they have a new singer named Azumi Takahashi on board. But I personally don't really mind that as they both have proven to be able to make songs when they are new content. (eg. It's Going Down Now)Not to also mention Lotus Juice, who has the midas touch when it comes to Persona music.I mention the soundtrack is due to the fact that although it sounds fine as it is, it does not have the same impact as the original version. When fighting the final boss of the game, the music is a lot more... muted as compared to the original soundtrack. I can't go into much into specifics out of respect for people who don't wish to be spoiled. In fact, I'd go as far as to even say it feels more 'persona 5-ish' in the newer tracks, which I know some people are fine with. I'm unfortunately the annoying crowd that prefers the old J-pop feeling of Persona 3. I like some of the remixes, but some of them are just not... for me, which is the nicest way of putting it. Not only that, but in the ending, there are flashbacks to the whole game as if the game was spelling it out for you that this was your journey. In the older iterations of Persona 3, there was no flashbacks and simply just an intimate scene where there is only dialogue. In my opinion, that's more effective as it makes the player think of the journey they had rather than having the game spelling it out for you. Next, I can mention without much spoilers is the MC awakening his persona scene. When he awakens his persona, the shots are too clear as compared to the chaotic angles and shots of the original and FES. When another persona appears from inside Orpheus; in the original version he tears out of Orpheus like a beast, while in Reload, Orpheus literally deflates like a balloon and is stretched open. I'm not going to say which is in my opinion more interesting, but you can infer my feelings pretty easily on your own. I'm of the opinion that small attention to details always add up to the bigger picture. It matters to me how things are presented. In my opinion, this seems more in the direction Persona 5 has in its art direction and storytelling style. I understand that it's to get new fans into Persona 3, but I feel like this made it lose Persona 3's individuality to cater to them.To spell it out like Persona 3 Reload; the remake, while telling the same story as the previous iterations of Persona 3, doesn't have the same impact and effect as the originals in terms of story due to changes like these. It's a little bit forgivable as they do not have the old team on board as they're on board working on Metaphor: ReFantazio, though this led to the original vision being muddied in between despite having the apprentices, in my personal opinion.Due to this, it's also hard for me to recommend this game narrative wise to a person who wishes to enjoy Persona 3's story for what it is, it's not worth it at $70 dollars if you are like me and care about the story. But, if you're not iffy about things like that, go get the game. A review like mine won't stop you from getting it anyway. TLDR: It's a remake done by people who care about the original IP, but the original people who made the said IP aren't on board. The impact of the story and everything about it is lesser than previous iterations. I find it quite hard to recommend it to people personally because of how much the previous iterations of Persona 3's approach to their message about finding meaning in life that resonated with me. The impact of the message, however, isn't there in Reload. So, if you want to experience Persona 3 at its best(in terms of presentation), I'd recommend playing FES or Portable (even doe people call it the cheap mobile version of p3 or even p3 the visual novel).----After a bit more deliberation, my review is catered towards those who deem P3R as a definitive edition. I do not think it is. There are added scenes that add a lot to the game, which I didn't mention; but I do not think it would replace the originals. I'd still recommend you play FES( (or even portable) over Reload.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Persona 3 so obligatory 10/10.Ok so my negatives: FES is still the best version in terms of artistic direction & storytelling, and also wish this kept the gameplay mechanics that made it so unique. It's like they were split on keeping this a faithful remake but then modifying things to be less impactful than the original. It's a good game, just not a good remake imo. The changes in some of the characters kinda sucked, whilst others are good. Akihiko sucks now but I played FES & P3P so its ok I still like him. Ken is pretty good though. The cutscenes also sucked ass I'm sorry. Can we stop with the 3D model replacement cutscenes, and the actually animated cutscenes everything is so stiff and lifeless I almost prefer the 3D bc at least they show EMOTIONS. (Hey chat how did that one cutscene of them gearing up make it to the final cut that was ASS). Also everything was a little too easy and VERY easy to overlevel. Once you unlock a certain theurgy, you can literally instakill the reaper. I didn't even mean to overgrind, but the final boss fight was such a snooze; genuinely the first boss was the hardest and it went downhiill from there. Dare I say it was easier than P5R.  Positives:ANYWAYS, yeah the story is peak. Despite my problems with art direction, there were bits of it I loved. Seeing all the characters in their updated models was great, and the world looks pretty. The new songs they added are AMAZING STUNNING SHOWSTOPPING BEAUTIFUL. Color your night went straight in my playlist; sorry for being a cornball but yeah. I liked all the new little bits of characterization, and Tartarus was really well designed map-wise for every floor.  Oh also the Aigis RRyoji cutscene was REALLY well done. Just a very chill (lol) & pretty game.If you haven't experience P3 yet, I'd recommend playing FES first for the best story & cutscenes, then P3P for the Female Protag route and a better quality of social links than FES, then play Reload. Reload works at its best when you treat it as its own version of P3; NOT as a remake. I'm such a negative nancy & have a lot of problems with it, but I still had a lot of fun with it. I know a lot of people who've played it and  loved it. So yeah, try it out but I'd recommend to do so after first experiencing FES; or even P3P and just watch the cutscene stuff from FES.  Yeah. Still my 2nd favorite story in Persona games; so I just had a great time re-experiencing it again. Ok I'm done yapping now.As a remake: 4/10As a game: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 3 Reload is a game that takes the concept of the series and perfects those aspects to it's max. This game, I think, could be picked up by anyone, no matter their experience or taste in RPG's and still have a blast with it. As any persona game, it makes you really care about their characters, you want to see them improve, and seeing them get out of their personal struggle is something quite satisphactory and wholesome most of the time. And to be honest most of the characters in this game are more fleshed out than most in other games in the series, also because they don't solely depend on you to become better, other people will help them or even they themselves will come to a realization, just like in real life. Oh and the new activities you can do with your team just improves what I already had said, it shows you their normal life, just acting like normal, real people. Oh and the animations of the characters are stunning, when they are eating you can see them actually eat, unlike the lifeless automatons most NPC's in videogames tend to be. Also the facial expressions are insane, I thought P5 was the peak of how characters could express themselves, but looking at the characters here, specially in battles, is amazing.The graffics and UI are some of the things I most enjoyed in the game, and as a matter of fact is kinda what sold me on the game to begin with since the trailer first released. Many times I would just pause the game and watch the menu, just thinking how cool it was and how the managed to make something 3D look so much like 2D. And I think they perfected P5's aesthetic here; if you barely noticed it was 3D, here you have to actually stop and analyse if it's actually 2D or 3D. Also, the transitions between battles or the times of day are amazing, they improved compared to what we had in P5.The music is also one of the best things of the game (As in any persona) That hip-hop-y feel the original had, mixed with the instruments that P5 uses made one of the best videogame OST's of all time. Also the new additions to the soundtrack are amazing, being "Full moon full life" and "Color your night" my favorites of the game and the series overall.I might have to give it some time to cool down but, as far of games I've played of persona, overall my favorite would be this one. I enjoyed this game to the last single second and I'm already excited to begin my next playthrough. I would recommend this game to anyone who is interested wholeheartedly.

name: Strayed Lights
detailed_description: Strayed Lights is an immersive action adventure set in a wordless, dreamlike world of corruption and shadows. You are a nascent light on a journey to free yourself from the grasp of shadows surrounding you. Key Features of Strayed Lights: Battle endearing creatures deformed by their emotions, shift your colors to repel their attacks. Experience a tightly-crafted cinematic experience through art and emotion, with not a word of dialogue. Explore the fractured lands of Strayed Lights, from luminescent forests to canyons, caves and lands of bewildering mist. Scored to a haunting, atmospheric original soundtrack by Austin Wintory. RESTORE YOUR LIGHT Play as a newborn flame torn by shadows. Progress in a hostile world on a quest to restore your light by facing your inner demons and helping beings along the way. Unlock new abilities as your light brightens. PACIFY YOUR ENEMIES Find your siblings who went rogue, each deformed by a specific emotion. Battle these monstrous forms and pacify the emotions that control them. Face your inner demons taken form to hinder your progress. SHIFT COLORS TO FIGHT Face creatures torn by shadow in fluid and rewarding combat. Repel their attacks while shifting between blue and orange to match their color and overcome them in vivid finishers.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the first three areas as of writing this. Amazing atmospheric game with challenging combat. You match colors with the enemy and parry their attacks. The games platforming elements are solid, but when you jump on a latch it takes a while for your character to pull himself up which breaks the pace of the otherwise fast running. Loads of collectibles which actually make your character stronger so they're an interesting initiative for everyone and not just completionists. The boss battles is where the game really shines though, Shadow of the Collosus/Asura's Wrath vibes, which I absolutely love. Soundtrack is mostly atmospheric with some upbeat music during boss battles. The game follows a set formula. Cutscene points your character in a certain direction? Turn around for a collectible. Two or more different paths to take? Check them all out for collectible. At the top of a jumping puzzle? Gives you view of a collectible so better jump down to get that first. My absolute biggest gripe with the game is that the sprint button is on a face button of your controller, B by default. This sucks because the movement feels great but you constantly want to turn your camera for, you guessed it, collectibles. This makes you play with a claw grip and I don't wanna relive my 2000s Gears of War days. I'm getting old and my finger hurts.

The combat system was somewhat fun, but barebones as you do not get any new combat abilities throughout most of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Strayed Lights' issues are difficult to describe; it's not a bad game per se, and although I enjoyed the combat, so many of its features feel hollow and lack substance, so much so that I often felt I was playing for the sake of completing it rather than because I wanted to. Whether it be the boss finishers relegated to QTE-riddled cutscenes, the unimaginative, linear level design, or the story that provides little to no direction or context for my actions, I never felt drawn in or engaged by the world, instead mindlessly trudging through skin-deep environments, not entirely understanding why.Combat is, to its credit, entertaining and unique; enemies attack wreathed in different colours, and for the strongest parry, dealing damage and restoring health, you must receive the attack matching the colour, swapping between blue and orange with the press of a button. Unblockable purple attacks force a dodge instead, keeping you on your toes throughout an encounter. However, Strayed Lights is a cripplingly easy game: enemy damage is non-existent, and the amount of health restored on a successful parry is absurd, failing to follow through on the intensity this combat model should invoke.Nevertheless, combat is varied: alongside the parry, you have access to a basic dodge and attack, with a few unlockable abilities down the road, all providing substantial depth to an encounter. It plays great too; with each action, particularly the dodge, providing a tactile and responsive feel. However, the parry is both your primary defence  offence so, in practice, much of the expanded moveset doesn't offer enough to be worth using; for example, bosses tend to end a flurry of attacks some distance away, and by the time you've closed the gap to get some basic attacks in, they're ready to go again with another combo.Bosses are the highlight of the entire experience: despite their movesets lacking much variation, each attack chain can be surprisingly complex, mixing up all colours of attacks into a tight string of blows. Learning the patterns and perfectly dealing with the assault, parrying each strike with the right colour and dodging when necessary, gives rise to a riposte, offering immense satisfaction when executed. Unfortunately, these encounters are sullied in their conclusion: upon ending a fight, you're presented with an awkward cutscene in which you watch your character deal a climactic finishing blow with accompanying, equally awkward QTEs. The key word here is "watch"; although I'm the one pressing the buttons, the disconnect created by using a cutscene completely takes me out of the moment, leaving my opponent defeated, but a sour taste in my mouth.The quality of combat encounters is far from consistent: basic enemies litter the landscape, and with their 2 or 3 attacks that never change or evolve, there is almost nothing worthwhile about them. Furthermore,  enemy shares the same visual motif, including the bosses, and you wind up feeling like no enemy feels particularly unique to fight because they don't  unique. New variants of enemies show up now and then, but a groan always escaped my lips as I saw another skirmish come into view. As far as the story goes, Strayed Lights gives absolutely nothing: I couldn't give you a synopsis even if I wanted to. Stuff , and things play out on screen, but with no dialogue to contextualise anything, I couldn't make heads or tails of what's actually going on; "stuff" and "things" become the only words I can use to describe it. Yet that doesn't mean an attempt at a story isn't made; the first hour or so is just  with 30-second cutscenes literally every few minutes, though they don't say or show anything worth seeing.Now I imagine you think this doesn't matter; it's an action game, right? But it needs  and it bleeds into every aspect of the game; why am I fighting this thing? What am I looking at? What is my character's goal? If I'm asking myself these questions, I can't become invested in the epic boss battle. I don't bother looking at the scenery, however beautiful it may be. If I know these questions won't be answered, why bother asking them at all? And therein lies the problem: if I don't care about the world and characters around me, the whole experience becomes soulless, it becomes monotonous and it becomes forgettable.I wish I could tell you that there's environmental storytelling, but there's almost nothing to speak of. Each distinct area is visually very appealing: the composition is pleasing, the colours are superb, and the positions of the moon or a mountain behind an eye-catching centrepiece are all executed well, but again, without context of any form, there's no deeper meaning between the brushstrokes. Suddenly all the beautiful art lacks intent. I don't look at the space and wonder how it came to be; it's  a forest, it's  a tower in the distance, and I never found myself compelled to care.The playable space consists of two small hub areas leading to five moderately sized areas, each housing its own boss and making up the majority of the playtime. These locations are almost entirely linear, however, with very little room for any exploration; the most you get are occasional, slightly hidden side paths that lead to nothing more than an optional enemy or a collectible. Brimming with empty corridors, slow crawls along ledges, and far too many repeated enemies, these spaces feel like their only purpose is to slow you down. It's easy to tell that the intent during these long walking sequences is to give the player a moment to take in the views, although they only present as mindless slogs due to the narrative reasons outlined earlier.With only two types to find, the collectible economy is scarce and essentially not worth bothering to engage with: the primary of the two improves the speed of "energy" buildup, the bar that fills up with successful parries and attacks, ending the fight once full. This buff, frankly, isn't felt at all; not once did I feel I was dispatching enemies faster, to the point that I'm not entirely sure I've correctly understood what it does. The other collectible is somehow less interesting: found in the hub areas, you can take them to a large shrine to unlock what is essentially concept art and more of the first main collectible. Added to the fact that both of them are easily missable, due to multiple unexpected points-of-no-return locking you out of finding them all, the whole system feels more like a checkbox than a properly implemented feature.To reiterate, this is not a bad video game, but it's far from exceptional either, and in an indie scene awash with life, individuality, and personality, I feel that Strayed Lights failed to leave much of an impression on me. There are glimmers of an excellent game buried in this, and I think that Embers should be proud of what they accomplished in their debut title, but as it stands now, completely ignoring the £20 price tag for a four-hour game, this is not an experience that I can recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this but I can't shake the feeling that it's wasting my time.  All the core elements are really solid, great art direction backed by a wonderful colour palette, interesting core gimmick, largely well-designed bosses and enemies, I want to emphasise that I like what this game is doing!The problem is that it feels like the map was scaled up to twice its original size at some point in development, and I don't mean the breadth of its scope, I mean in the scale of its literal geometry.  The bulk of my time in the game so far has been consumed by holding B to slowly traverse ridiculously enormous stretches of empty space, an emptiness so enormous it makes the player character feel bizarrely tiny, with no fresh scenery to take in, extremely sparse collectables to find, and no enemies to fight.  It feels padded, and considering I've heard it's quite short, it's possible that is actually what happened.  I might return to it at some point but right now I've got a lot of stuff to play and I really don't want to spend this much time running in a straight line toward a rock that might or might not have something behind it.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, very pretty....And that's it.Parrying and matching parry colors is the game's general combat premise, but it feels... so painfully flat. No, I didn't get lost at the start. I'm not unfamiliar with the vagueness of the soulslike genre, and parrying is one of my favorite playstyles, with Sekiro shooting up to one of my all-time favorites. So I went into this feeling hopeful, and I found my way to progress pretty quickly, and... there's just no impact or excitement to anything going on. For one thing, I don't mind the choice to eschew vocals in favor of visuals and interpretation, but, that doesn't mean you forget about sound design altogether. Traversal felt uninteresting, like I'm playing a walking simulator, supposedly swept up in the environment to notice that I've been just holding B for fifteen seconds to get to the next mini-encounter. Each encounter is, itself, like a checkpoint where you throw yourself at what amounts to a puzzle sequence of parrying, dodging, and hitting until you use your fancy execute button on the whole pack a-la-Sekiro or die and restart that specific encounter. And this feels like I'm being railroaded, and the options and tools that I'm given to work with are not diverse enough to make up for this linearity. Yes, I just started. The skill tree showed me an entire two other (beyond the first freebie) unlockable powers to look forward to, yippee. Making a heavy attack is also a skill tree unlock, taking up one of the four or five slots on the "lower" tree. The same half of the tree that has health upgrades as one of the slots, yes. It's not promising. And, for all the emphasis I've left to give to the visuals... the game starts you out in some pretty bland, one-color environments. The screenshots show promise, sure, but if you were hoping to hook people on sightseeing, you won't get there early enough before it's time for a refund.This game feels like it's REALLY banking on its color-parry gimmick to grab you, and it's just insufficient. I made it to the first boss on Hard, gave it a fair try, and after chasing it around as it leapt across the arena like I was fighting Elden Beast again, it flattened me mid-parry combo with an unblockable purple poomf of near-silence, my character playing their same exact "fall over slowly and die" animation they do against everything else, and I realized that I just felt utterly bored with the experience. Want to see a really cool and exciting, parry-focused, soulslike AA game? Try Nine Sols.

_childDocuments_.review: A short, straightforward, and visually-pleasing experience. Strayed Lights is an wordless, atmospheric action game about growing up and confronting your inner demons.The key combat mechanic involves color matching your opponent while parrying blue or orange attacks, which heals you and fills your energy bar. Purple attacks cannot be parried and must be dodged. Combat is at its best during boss fights (which all feature a single opponent), but falls short on the two-mob trash packs between bosses. I found myself playing much more aggressively on the trash packs than the bosses just to take one of the opponents out of the picture quickly. The boss designs were all unique and flashy.The environments are beautiful, and poking around in corners rewards the player with an energy boost. I found that it ran fairly well at high settings, with only occasional framerate drops.  (Ryzen 9 5900x - NVIDIA RTX 3080)Not a perfect game, but an enjoyably contained 7-hour experience on the Standard difficulty for me (there are also Story and Challenge difficulties). There are Trials available after completing the game for those who want to revisit specific bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it worth 20 bux?  I'd say so.I mean, a lot of work was put into the game, obviously.  The music and visuals fits into a coherent theme.  Every camera angle  during scenes could be captured in an artful screenshot, and the level design is very well thought-out.  Like the cut scenes, the every piece of monument and architecture -- what little there may be in the lost civilization apparent in the game -- is placed with visual purpose.The gameplay is the right amount of challenge.  If you're familiar with action games, it's a bit of a slower-paced combat; so it's a lot of waiting and timing, but it is fun.  For me, I'd say it's basically a game if you find From Soft games to be total bull, this one's a good alternative.  Not a long game at all, but I think $20 suffices the visual work put into this game. The developers deserve a commendation for the beautifully crafted natural world in the game.Players equating the pricetag to game time really need to kinda shut up, and realize despite the play time, the game had a LOT of thought put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: A small and enjoyable experience, exactly as long as it should be. The color-swapping is an interesting addition to the usual dodge/parry mechanics, and while they it was a bit of a struggle for me to get used to juggling both, once it clicked it came very naturally. The controls also were very tight, which is something a lot of Soulslikes fall prey to, especially from indie developers.Combine that with fun bosses with neat mechanics, gorgeous character animation and environmental setpieces, and Austin Wintory's compositions, and this was a great way to spend an evening.Some small critiques include some frame drops in certain foliage-heavy environments which suggests it could use more optimization, and that while the quicktime events didn't bother me (as setups for fun and flashy finishers), the icons indicating button presses having the BLACK space be the button to push was strange and not very intuitive. I would recommend inverting or changing the icons so the button to press is highlighted in white and not black.To end on a positive, I very much appreciate how the devs added in a colorblind mode to make sure the mechanics are accessible to colorblind gamers. While I didn't personally need it, it's vital and all too often left out of games where color is such a focus. Well done, Embers, for keeping your game accessible.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this is a solid showing if it were a solo dev or a student project or whatever. But I just couldn't have fun with this. The tutorial is extremely slow, taking 20 minutes to show you how to walk, walk walk, crouch, walk, jump, walk, run, run, run, parry, parry, parry, parry, parry and parry. The opening was bizarre - Your negative/upside down guy split your ember brain into shards and sent minions into the multiverse? What?Levels are quite linear once you start down a path, only broken up by combat rooms, which are okay (oh and by the way "souls-like" here really means parry mode). But most of the time is spent walking. What finally broke me and made me return the game is that your camera gets hijacked constantly to pan out vistas that are...fine. Or to look at a monkey, which walks near you. Really riveting stuff that requires a 15 second disconnect of the controls to fully appreciate, I guess.Also, it feels like the game was done, then someone just said, "lets' increase the size of the world by 400% so that it takes longer to get everywhere and increases game completion time". Even the big baddies don't fit in the world right. The massive world scheme works in games like Shadow of the Colossus and Praey for the Gods, because you actually fight behemoth baddies.The world looks decent, movement feels good, enemies seem varied. But the whole product just didn't come together in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Strayed lights has a very unique and abstract story, simple but very beautiful visuals and an interesting Sekiro-light and fun combat system. The enemies have exciting combos that have quite a steep learning curve and the main character is pretty and adorable. The game has some similarities to the Ori series which are very pleasant and the environment reminds me of a surreal, beautiful place that you see, when you meditate.  However, I can't help myself but have the unbearable urge to scream so loud that the developers can hear me. It seems to be a trend to not finish a game before releasing it nowadays. Strayed Lights doesn't feel polished at all.I get random fps drops from 60 to 20 or sometimes even 2 frames per second. You can imagine how terrible that feels in a fast paced combat design. The game randomly freezes in the middle of an attack and the next frame I get hit without being able to do anything about it. That is becoming very frustrating to a point, where I just want to pause the game and take a break. Changing graphics settings doesn't have any noticable influence to the framedrops. As I am playing on challenging mode, I die pretty often due to enemies changing their pattern rather quickly. However, that is very fun to learn and I enjoy such hard challenges. The problem is that it seems like everytime the game reloads a save, it gets more and more broken. The stutters increase in frequency and become more persistent, letting the happening freeze for a couple of seconds in the middle of a battle. It goes up to that point, where I'm even unable to restart the game and close its window. I once had to force reset my computer to even use it again. What it also does is crashing my Steam app, when it tries to close the game. Really, something like this just must not happen with any game.Strayed Lights unfortunately, is very poorly optimized. I just can appeal to the developers to finish their game. Just give it another year, if that's necessary. But please, stop ruining player's experience in releasing a game too early, completely unpolished. I can only imagine how it runs on the Nintendo Switch. I hate to give the game a thumbs down, but in its current state it's a laggy impertinence.Please finish your game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a joy to play this game. The music atmosphere was lovely, thought a tad quiet at some points. _childDocuments_.review: Im going to start off by saying that I think the dev team has a lot of talent and I cant wait to see how they take their experience with this game and use it to make something in the future. The art team especially went crazy in this game, and it is beautiful as a result.However,This is not a game that I can in good faith recommend to anyone else. Let me explainThis game suffers from a number of serious issues that i will go into belowThis Should Have Been A Boss RushIn my opinion, this game should have been a boss rush. The most enjoyable parts of the game was seeing the environments and fighting the bosses. If you have played games like Eldest Souls, both are pretty achievable, and this game would have benefited from it, because the worst parts were finding the collectibles(of which I couldn't find all of them) and fighting the small enemies, whom of which not a single one were enjoyable to fight. The Sound Design Is All Over The PlaceWhy the F does a regular non perfect parry have nearly the same sound as getting hit? How do I learn what moves are giving me trouble when I have to stare at the screen and not the health bar and cant hear what the game is trying to tell me? This would have been such an easy fix too. This is especially bad in the final bossMissable AchievementsThis game came out in 2023, its not really excusable for half the achievements to be entirely missable.Inconsistent Telegraphing, Parrying And trackingWhy are some moves unreactable for no reason? Why cant the final boss track me like at all? Why do some of my parries still work when I missclick by a million years, but others feel like accuracy to a couple frames is necessary? The boss fights are the highlight of this game, and they should have had longer to cook. Standout fights were butterfly phase 1, forest monkey phase 2, and final phase 1. Most of the others had a serious downside that made them less fun to fight.This is a short game for the price. Tying back to the boss rush comment, this game could have had twice the bosses that took twice as long to fight and were more polished, and it would have been way better. the bosses are always either getting utterly steamrolled or winning, there is no middle ground, because once you half learn like 2 attack patterns you can always heal the mistakes easily. Also, the achievement to no hit a boss not being available in the section where you can just fight the bosses makes little sense. Why be able to attack when most of the bosses take little damage and just run away when they aren't attacking? Why the quick time events that take away from what could have been incredible cutscenes? Why is there no way to track the meet again achievement? Why does playing on a lower difficulty make it so you cannot get the unlock all skill achievement because it reduces the amount of NON RESPAWNING enemies which have a vital resource tied to them? These are questions I kept finding myself asking and not finding answers. This game is just a really really beautiful series of major game design and playtesting issues, but has the foundations to be awesome. I hope the developers take this feedback into account when designing the next game they make, because I fully believe they can make something awesome. If anyone would like to talk with me further about possibly improving the game or more in depth discussions about these issues, you have my email, I reached out to support 5 days ago.TLDR this game has serious game design issues and I would not recommend playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Strongly recommend this game. Strayed Lights enjoys a wild color palette, strong soundtrack (shoutout Austin Wintory), tight combat mechanics, and a surprisingly zen atmosphere. The two-color parry system is both unique and intuitive, lending itself to some blistering combat encounters. Story is pretty minimal here; come for the action and not the plot on this one.Strayed Lights is primarily a boss rush (a few brief levels serve as interludes, with minor enemies to practice against). Each boss is memorable and has a strongly differentiated vibe and moveset. I played on Challenge Mode for my first playthrough, which was only recently added to the game, and I'm given to understand that it is significantly more difficult than the normal mode, where combat is more relaxed and meditative.True to its name, I found Challenge Mode to be extremely tough: boss combos come at a relentless pace, they flip between colors rapidly and dish out punishing amounts of damage, and the telegraph windows for each combo are pretty severe. The payoff here is that once you've figured out a boss's moveset, countering each combo with a perfect set of parries is massively satisfying, and I felt like an absolute champ dancing around each of these encounters, similar to mastering a boss fight in Sekiro. Having perfect parries restore a bit of health was also a great design choice, adding a bit of a tug-of-war element to each fight.Strayed Lights and a fairly rudimentary upgrade system, but my only real complaint here is that some of the upgrades feel way less helpful than others. For example, the "hold the parry button and release for a stronger parry" upgrade actually worked against me. Enemy combos come quickly enough that you'll never really use this move, and I would regularly prep the "charged parry" without meaning to, throwing off my timing and leaving me defenseless. With no way to respec or undo upgrades, I came pretty close to restarting my playthrough just to get rid of this disadvantage (in the end, I worked around it by training myself to only ever very lightly tap the parry button).I thought Strayed Lights was great, and I'm excited to see what Embers puts out next. For anyone else plowing through Challenge Mode, I strongly recommend picking the upgrade that lets you do a powerful riposte after perfect-parrying an enemy's full combo; it's probably the most satisfying maneuver to pull off in the entire game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not for me. I loved Sifu and I mostly liked Sekiro so I'd say I enjoy difficult combat games. However it seems like the devs looked at those games and thought "Hey, let's make it so you have to push another button to matchy match a color while parrying/blocking to get the max benefit." Just seems like an unnecessary and not particularly fun mechanic to me. I also found dodging to be very unintuitive in that some things I thought I could easily dodge I would end up getting hit by while other times I'd be surprised I didn't take damage. There is also the issue I hate with games where the pause before a heavier attack from the enemy is super exaggerated and then the animation plays at almost the normal speed of a normal attack. Another more minor complaint is that I'm not sure why they felt the need to have a sprint mechanic when that should just be the default run speed. The sprint button should be a "move slower" button for the parts that require you to walk carefully areas so you don't fall.Also, there should be a level of difficulty between the mid and hard difficulty. Mid was easy and Hard I was a little ridiculous with the time given to switch colors properly and parry.I'd say try it out if you like fast combat games because you might like it, but I just think there are much better options out there and I don't the this brings anything new to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a fantastic little journey with some obscenely beautiful environments and amazingly animated and unique boss encounters.The game is pretty easy, with a very forgiving parry window; the hardest fights will be against two enemies at once instead of any of the bosses. This game would severely benefit with some modifiers and difficulty options (parry window adjustment, health/damage adjustments at a minimum. New attacks would be amazing, but even just those simple options would create replayability).There are some... Issues with the release, the biggest being that the devs compiled with the SteamVR enabled at runtime which is a hallmark of bad developers, but I am proud to say that the game itself isn't in the terrible list of other games that do this. The game also does not offer proper Playstation controller support. However, both of these things are fixable; for the PS controllers just run DSX or DS4 as an Xbox controller, and to disable SteamVR booting on launch just right-click the game in your library, choose properties, and type "-nohmd" in the launch options box under the first general tab.The game is very short; any veterans and people familiar with parrying in games will be done in around 3 hours, 3.5-4 hours if fully exploring the limited areas but... I still absolutely recommend it as a purchase. It was worth the money for me at full price for the journey alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Lets start with the good things about this game, The graphics are phenomenal. A beautiful and colourful world with adorable characters that are unique and likeable.No chapter/world is the same, with each of them having a unique feel to themThe boss battles are all different and keep you on your toes for the entirety of the battle. Even if you restart the fight after dying the boss is not guaranteed to hit you with the same move first during the second attempt. There are plenty of collectibles in this world for the cleptomaniacs like me. I thoroughly enjoyed traversing around hidden paths in order to find all of the collectibles.The fighting mechanic is unique with me not having seen this specific concept in any other game that I have played before.There are plenty of abilities and skills that you can choose from and upgrade as you like in order to match your playstyle.Now for the bad, Even though I praised the fighting system above it must be said that it is rather repetitive  and not particularly challenging. Now I don't know whether thats because I played the game on story mode but it is simply just clicking the mouse button at the right time and occassionally pressing E when needed. No other inputs are particularly needed and with each successful mouse click you heal up a ton. This is great for a casual player like me that enjoys the story of a game far more than the challenge of a battle, however even I found that there was little reward that came with the defeat of the bosses. All in all its a great game and I am happy to have had the chance to play through it. With 4.6 hours of play time I was able to 100% the achievements purely because i had to restart from the beginning again in order to get the intact achievement. Fair warning to fellow completionists that there is a missable achievement in the game where if you don't do particular things before you proceed to the second half of the game, you will miss out.

_childDocuments_.review: First two hours gameplay: It's one of those games that could've been a really good recommendation, but unfortunately as a whole package I can't recommend it. I played almost 2 hours and it seems based on other reviews game is less than 4 hours total which for $25 game is not a fair price.Visuals and the world are really cool and beautiful, very simple but effective art style. Visually it reminds me of Ori and the Blind Forest a lot but in a simpler form. The combat for me was not really interesting and engaging, mainly you have to parry attacks to gain health and kill enemies, you have attack ability but it's secondary and very weak and simple (also attack was assigned to right mouse button which took a long time for me to get use to it), so it's mainly blocking and counter attacks. It might be good to update the UI for mouse buttons in game, it was really not clear which button to press in time!Enemies are good but not that great, I encountered maybe 3-4 enemy types so far, but I really liked the boss fights, they were cool, fun and engaging. _childDocuments_.review: This was such a treat to play and also an absolute “how to” guide when it comes to making video games. I picked it up a while ago in a humble bundle, but only just now got around to actually playing it. Lemme tell you folks, this is absolutely my favourite game from that bundle.I always find myself b*tching in these reviews about excruciating cutscenes and long sections of reading in what should be a game. Ya know… not a book? Well to my absolute delight, every bit of storytelling done in Strayed Lights is done exclusively through visuals and gameplay. There’s a boss fight early on where you can see that the monster is just trying to play with you and all it’s attacks feel bouncy and playful.That brings me around to the combat which feels pretty well tuned. For funsies, I tried to see how far I could get without upgrades and the answer was surprisingly far. I was playing on normal difficulty and found it maybe a tad easy? That being said I’m so over the trend of soulslikes adding difficulty in place of making fights fun an interesting. Even when the combat wasn’t difficult, it was still engaging and entertaining to figure out. If you’re looking for a balanced challenge, I would suggest avoiding specifically the health upgrades as your starting health pool is pretty generous and there are no attacks even late game that will knock off the whole thing. Having the slightly smaller amount just gives a sense of jeopardy and forces you to think harder about risky plays.I’ve been told that the combat is inspired by Sekiro, although I have no experience of Sekiro, and nothing meaningful to add to that. For what it’s worth it’s functionally a rhythm/parry game where you need to match the colour of your parry to the colour of enemy attacks. This flows really well and makes for a delightfully tactile combat system. Oddly enough, it kinda reminded me of the action command system form Paper Mario TTYD, but maybe I’ve just still got that disappointing remake on the brain.The story is also beautiful and spoke to me in some surprising ways. There’s so much love and effort gone into this game. It feels like something someone cared about and put a lot of thought into. The world feels intuitive to explore and I rarely felt lost. Travel times between locations can be a bit of a drag, but the game doesn’t outstay its welcome.I finished it in about 6 hours, but I reckon you could probably do it in 3 if you weren’t stubbornly avoiding upgrades. That sounds short, but it’s exactly as long as it needs to be.Overall, if you’re curious about soulslikes but feel a bit daunted by the idea, I strongly urge you to give this a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives: It took about 3 hours to beat this game on its Normal/Intended difficulty. (I'm sure it may be completed much faster)The parry mechanic was quite interesting and I enjoyed learning/mastering it throughout the play-through.I think for what it is, the game is quite enjoyable. The art is definitely the selling point of this game for me. HUGE props to the artist. I took many screenshots on my journey. I hope to see more of this world in the future. Perhaps with co-op to explore it with your troubled siblings. Negatives:Playing the game on the highest available settings, and native 4k resolution I encountered many "lag" spikes when the world was rendering in or loading the mobs. That said, I didn't find it too distracting. And I was able to complete my play-through without any crashes. There is also some "jank" in a couple of the animations (namely the jump recovery and crouch recovery). This didn't affect me but may impact others. As many other reviewers have stated, 3 hours is quite short. While she story concludes quite nicely, it does leave the player wanting more. I believe that is what the second game mode you unlock after your play-through is intended for. While this will add a little more play time, the mainline story content (though enjoyable) still leaves the player wanting more. Verdict: Should you by this game? $25 retail is quite steep for 3 hours of mainline story content. Yes the world is beautiful (subjective) and the game play quite enjoyable (also subjective) this only leaves the player wanting more from it. Hopefully a DLC will follow, or a sequel/prequel to add to this world. I believe many will enjoy the game for the right price.

_childDocuments_.review: Strayed Lights is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. The scenery is 10/10, it's immersive, it's colorful, it's grandiose, it's peaceful... granted it doesn't have AAA graphics, but it really doesn't matter. The game also never holds your hand. No minimap, no "GO HERE" texts, nothing. Just you and a beautiful linear world to explore. But don't worry, you won't get lost. The game still does a great job making the way clear.Story wise, it's a fully voiceless game that lets you interpret it's background without telling you anything about the world via text or voice. It's all visual. I must admit I'm not good at figuring out these kinda stories, but I still have some idea of what the game wants to say, and it's pretty cool. Gameplay wise, it is very simple but very challenging. The gameplay loop is very very engaging and it's one of the few games I can confidently say I never got bored with. I played in max difficulty, which tests your reflexes and your patience, as this game is heavily based on parrying. You have basic attacks, but you can very well not use them ever if you don't want to. I guess you could say this game is kind of a souls lite, though it didn't feel like a souls game to me. In souls games, I can get very frustrated in those times when you die over and over again to the same enemies. In this game, I genuinely never wanted to close the game because an enemy was beating me up. And they DID beat me up plenty.Overall, if you love magical and atmospheric visuals, this game has some of the best in the market. Really, it's surreal how beautiful this 10 hours journey was. If you like engaging and challenging gameplay, with very satisfying mechanics and colorful fights, this game has it. And if you like to interpret vague and deep stories and figure out what's going on in a mysterious world, then you will be pleased.Loved this game, definitely worth it's price! If you don't mind spending what it's worth, I'd encourage to go to their website and buy it there to support them. I unfortunately didn't do this, which I regret.

_childDocuments_.review: Strayed lights is an unbelievably underrated game that deserves so much more recognition than it gets! It has super unique and creative core mechanics which lead to some of the best bosses i've ever had the pleasure of fighting whilst looking and sounding absolutely wonderfull. Even better is that, thanks to the 3 difficulty options, strayed lights can be played by absolutely anybody. Those less profficient at action games can enjoy the easy difficulty while the average joe (that's me) can try normal. For the most hardcore soulslike fans there's even a challenge difficulty which i will certainly try my hands on later down the line. I enjoyed this game so much that i'm willing to try it at it's absolute hardest, something which i only did for ori and blasphemous before this. I hope this is enough to convince you but if it isn't i'll go in some more detail below to try and get you in on this amazing game!The combat in strayed lights has a certain rythm to it. The core mechanic is that your avatar can switch between blue & red flames to try and parry attacks in the right colour. Parrying in the wrong colour isn't punished as you still block damage but blocking in the right colour heals you and damages your enemy. This simple mechanic is a stroke of genious because not only are you trying to get the timing right on the parry itself, you also have to constantly adapt on the fly to maximize your output. For the enemies & bosses start of simple with the colours but by the end they mix and match constantly pushing you to respect the game's mechanics and engage with them! The fact that parrying in the wrong colour does not punish you is also brilliant. This game really does want you to succeed and such positive reinforcement is really refreshing within the souls genre. I can only hope more developers adopt this method of positive feedback.If that was all the combat had to offer than it would already be tons of fun, but the addition of purple unblockable attacks is that finishing touch. Purple attacks require a dodge roll at the right time, which is harder than it seems. Later bosses can throw in a purple attack into the middle of their combo, and timing this right after a few perfect parries feels incredibly satisfying. You really do get into the rythm of parrying and dodging the bosses attacks after a few attempts, making it almost feel like a dance. There's also light attacks, heavy attacks and special attacks you can throw inbetween enemy attacks to really push the game to it's limits. For regular enemies, of which there's only a few, this is already pretty fun, but when you face one of the game's several bosses the combat shines. You fight most bosses several times throughout their level, each time with new or alterred moves. This natural progression really does make you improve rather quickly to face their final form. Each boss and their phases are unique in their own ways, so rarely do they feel similar. None of them felt unfair and none of them were boring. Even the least fun fight in the game was miles better than 90% of the games i've played or seen. I'm not exagerating when i say that these are some of the best bosses i've ever faced. One of them would even make my top 10 bosses of all time list. Needless to say the bosses are the highlight of the game for me, and already reason enough to play the game. But that's not all the game has to offer.There's also a gorgeous world waiting to be explored, and while the path with each level is mostly linear you get to chose which order you tackle the levels in. These environments are varied and jawdroppingly beautiful. From lush forests to dark caves and towering ravines. From ancient ruins to spiraling crystals and waterfalls. I just got lost wandering around in this world, entranced by serene vistas and a mesmerizing soundtrack. Austin wintory delivered another brilliant OST for strayed lights, and while the music wasn't as exhilirating for the bosses as some other games, it fit the exploration before said bosses perfectly. All in all the game is a treat for the senses as much as it is for the brain and reflexes.Lastly then narrative and performance. Strayed lights' story is pretty vague, but the imagery is beautiful and the symbolism is elegant. It's up to interpretation but not so obtuse as to not make any sense. Every individual can give meaning to it in their own way, which is nice as it makes the game more personal. Strayed lights is also incredibly well polished. The game runs silky smooth at maximum settings and i didn't have a single bug in my full playthrough. The only unintended thing that happened was an enemy dodging into a cliff once or twice, which was hilarious and a true halmark of a proper souls game. As far as i'm concerned there's no real negatives to this game. Sure i'd have liked some more variety for regular enemies, or a deeper upgrade system but the game doesn't overreach its scope. It knows what it wants to do and does it incredibly well. I'd have liked more of this goodness as well but the game doesn't overstay its welcome. For some the lenght might not be enough but the quality is high enough imo to warrant a purchase. If not at full price than certainly at a discount. Please give it a shot, it's really REALLY good :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of souls-like games, but it was really enjoyable experience. It just get's tiring and boring playing against bosses that take a long time to beat. Luckily for me, the hardest boss for me only took about 30min. (And that was mainly because the color-blind issue I mention below.) I was a bit anxious to play it since it was outside my comfort zone, and the screenshots made the game feel pretty same-y. (I was happily wrong)Maps are linear, but there are hidden collectibles around the corners to power yourself up. (Encouraging some kind of exploration, but not mandatory.) Music was quite appropriate for the levels and fights. I played the game with a controller like it recommended, and it was great. Some enemies have some questionable timings, but overall everything is fairly memorable. There wasn't much to the story other than you physically growing up and getting stronger by beating all the bad guys. Graphics were decent without being demanding, but sometimes lacked some textures to really give some definition.My only gripe with the game is having to turn on Color-blind mode to see a couple bosses switch elements easier. The light blue they used is quite similar to the purple they use, especially when the enemy is switching back and forth. (Blue and orange you can parry and swap, purple you cannot do either as it is an enemy corruption element.) The boss that gave me the most trouble had a predetermined string of attacks that kept switching between blue and purple and then an orange to keep you on your toes. Now that is fine and all, but the boss was super aggressive and changed element per action, AND the background was all blues and purples that matched the color of elements. I just had to put the time in to learn his attack strings, and better my skill level a bit. Which I really didn't have to do against any other boss. (There was an elite type enemy that attacked similar to this boss, and by the end level of the game it was VERY common) Final boss was actually fairly easy compared to the 2 bosses before it, which includes the one I mentioned before I had trouble with.Game has plenty of scenes where the build-up is nice and refreshing when it comes off. And also a built in camera mode for all the pretty and great scenery you'll be going through. I give it an easy 8.5/10. If you can get it on sale like I did, then I would push it upto a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art style, immediately engrossing.Intuitive, tight and exciting combat and emotion that invokes Kena/Journey vibes all the way through.
