Multiple Enemies at once was a bit problematic when the A.I. was clipping through eachother or being out of line of sight and still acting as if they're the main focus, but not enough to deter the quality.Austin Wintory killed it, as usual, on the score. Beautiful music that is always undertone until it takes forefront and it shines then fades happily back to the emotion behind the visuals.Genuinely an awesome experience that didn't muddle its own systems too much just for the sake, but did what it does well and kept the experience the size it needed to be.

_childDocuments_.review: While there is a lot I like in this game, there is also a lot that I don´t enjoy. I applaud the creators for trying to make a game with no dialogue and no written words. It is very rare and they did a decent job in trying to capture many of the emotions of the "light creatures" that you meet throught the game. Especially the boss that acts like a giant gorilla. You can see his character and also understand, why his actions are wrong, even though in a basic matter, they are completely normal and understandable.The issue I have with the game though is the combat system. There is beauty in simplicity, but the game has no way of making the fightings of the general enemies in any way entertaining. I hate that they are forcing you mainly to try to parry all the attacks (since that is also the way your character heals), because it gets incredibly stale very quickly. Dodging is much harder than it looks (most of the time I got hit anyway), the timing of the parrying sometimes feels broken and when you face 2 enemies... it gets incredibly hard (if you don´t pick the right skills). The attack button here feels mostly more like a formality, because you don´t actually get much stronger in your attacks (or at least you don´t feel stronger), there are no interessting combo attacks, and you get hit much more often. Boss fights are better, as they are much more dynamic and less frustrating, but even those can not save the combat system in its own. I just don´t like it. And sadly that is a big part of the entire game.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend Strayed Lights to any fan of action-adventure game :- the art direction is simple but beautiful, and the animation work is outstanding : the world and all the characters feel alive even if there's no talking involved. Mastering it feels really good and it never feels unforgiving.- you can see the influence of many classic adventure games such as Soul Reaver and Shadow of the Colossus but Strayed Lights manages to have his own identity.

They felt like scaled-down bosses with how crazy some of the attacks are and how often they change colors during chains. At some point I just skipped all the small guys just so I can get to the boss.- Fighting two enemies at a time was difficult (admittedly some skill issues on my end). It relates to how often they change colors + having to parry w/the right color. Maybe a difficulty option can be given so that pairs of enemies will only take one color each.- Having the Ability Points (AP) replenish based on 'enemies defeated' doesn't work with boss battles . _childDocuments_.review: Strayed Lights is a stunningly vibrant action platformer with environments and a world that feel as soothing as Journey's, but with challenging and rewarding Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice-style combat. Developer Embers asks players to control a small creature of light who must find their lost siblings across otherworldly regions corrupted by shadows. Players will grow stronger, more beautiful and gain new abilities as they explore Strayed Light's vivid environments and battle dark creatures with a simple and fair parrying system.The story of Strayed Lights is told with no dialogue, and Embers manages to craft a compelling tale entirely through environmental storytelling and character actions. After waking up and emerging from a strange pod, players start as a small creature of light who eventually grows into a pseudo-mystical entity that can control firey red and bright blue powers. Fellow siblings of light are waiting to be found, and a mysterious shadowy energy has even corrupted some. Defeating enemies and bosses unlocks new abilities that add depth to Strayed Lights' combat, and it's the game's parrying and color-coded combat that sets it apart from other action titles.Exploring the lands of Strayed Lights can be a relaxing experience, but corrupted enemies lie in wait throughout the adventure, which should take between seven and nine hours to complete. While players and enemies have standard health bars and attacks, both can use color-coded red/blue attacks. If players can time a parry with the corresponding color of an enemy's attack, damage is negated, and some health is restored. Any well-timed block still blocks damage, but the many epic bosses will challenge players and switch modes rapidly. With the right timing and color coordination, winning can feel as rewarding as beating FromSoftware's best Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice bosses, a game that's combat feels like an inspiration for Strayed Light's mechanics.Besides the game's stellar visuals, Strayed Lights' music accentuates each of the game's areas with a soundtrack that reflects the mood each area's creatures are feeling. The atmospheric music can feel tranquil and pleasing or hauntingly mysterious in the game's shadowy regions illuminated by few rich light sources. Austin Wintory, the Grammy award-winner composer behind one of the PS4's must-play games, Journey, has worked on the game's composition, and it meshes well with the already impressive visual cohesion of Strayed Lights. Each area feels more unique with its moody soundtracks while pumping up the excitement during boss battles.Strayed Lights is perfect for players who do not have much time to invest in a game that demands dozens of hours to complete. However, that is also to its detriment. There are a small number of collectibles to discover and a minimal amount of lore that feels like a tease for a world that is so interesting to look at and explore. While each boss is unique and requires different tactics to defeat, generic enemies throughout the map can start to feel repetitive with a lack of varying enemy types.Still, for Embers' first game, this is an especially impressive showing. Strayed Lights is a visually pleasing game with epic bosses and intense combat that any fan of action-adventure platforming games should check out, even if it's over before it really manages to create something unmissable.
_childDocuments_.name: Strayed Lights

_childDocuments_.review: I found Strayed Lights to be a really enjoyable game that strikes the right balance between fun and challenge. The game's visuals are incredibly vibrant and colorful, reminding me of Ori and the Blind Forest. The combat mechanics are reminiscent of Sekiro in that they rely heavily on parrying and timing, which adds a rhythmic element to the battles.One of the things I loved about Strayed Lights was its beautiful and moving soundtrack, composed by Austin Wintory. The music fits perfectly with the game's visuals and adds an extra layer of emotion and depth to the overall experience.Overall, I would definitely recommend Strayed Lights to anyone looking for a visually stunning game with engaging combat mechanics and a great soundtrack. Whether you're a fan of Ori and the Blind Forest or Sekiro, you're sure to enjoy this game.

name: Howl
detailed_description: Reviews About the Game Howl is a turn-based tactical folktale set in medieval times. A sinister 'howling plague' has ravaged the land, turning all who hear it into feral beasts. You play a deaf heroine plunging into danger in search of a cure. Plan up to six steps in advance to outmaneuver your opponents: wolfish creatures filled with hunger and rage. Various types of fiends are lurking in the shadows, each of them possessing different abilities and their own levels of vitality. So, you need to consider carefully the strategy that will bring them to their knees. Not only do you have your wits to rely on while plotting your attack, you also have an array of abilities at your disposal. As you slay more wolves, you acquire skills like Vault, Smoke Bomb, and Piercing Shot. Venture forth on your journey to upgrade your skills and unlock more Action Slots and Undo Round Points. As you plan your moves, you will also shape your own prophecy, composing a dynamic work of scripture as you fight. Howl's visuals are created through 'living ink', a flowing art style that paints the story as you play. Carve your way through a dark, fairy-tale world made up of obscure yet magical places where you fight and write to rid the lands of the plague. Foretell the actions of your enemies in tactical, turn-based combat Beautifully illustrated in a unique, living ink artstyle Outsmart the different wolf species, from fast predators to enormous pack leaders. Unlock and upgrade new skills like Shadow Step, Exploding Shot, and more Save villagers from the claws – and howls – of the wolves. Play through 60 levels in 4 chapters Plot your route on the world map to uncover new skills and secret paths

_childDocuments_.review: Positive review, but with grounded expectations about what you're getting.This is more a puzzle game than strategy. The AI is completely algorithm-based and will have the same output for a given input. The sole exception is the final level where there is (very annoying) RNG that will determine how many times you're clicking Restart. While each puzzle is entertaining to figure out, there's not much replay value.I've got pretty sizable experience in this type of game (Incredible Machine, Into the Breach, etc.), so I was able to easily reach the end in about 3.5 hours without trouble. Going back and wrapping up all the Steam achievements took an additional 3 hours. Your mileage may vary if puzzle/strategy is difficult for you.The graphics have a very pleasant and unique "hand-drawn" art direction, like you're looking at mobile ink on paper. It's not high-fidelity, but the artists knew what they wanted to do, and I respect that.I was not impressed by the story. On each level, the narrator says a couple sentences about what's going on. The problem is, almost all of it can be summarized as "The Prophet is going to this place now," or "People are scared of the Howl," or "Civilized areas are in disrepair." Without spoiling specifics, the ending had one sentence and then a brief art sequence depicting one of the most "esoteric happy endings" I've seen in a long time. It's the kind of ending that makes you react: "Really?"For the low price tag, it was still a fun bit of puzzle solving. But absent any surprise content updates, I'm probably not ever going to pick it up again.
_childDocuments_.name: Howl

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Into the Breach and the XCOM series, I feel right at home here.The puzzle aspect to the tactics are fun and engaging. All with wonderful narration and stellar art that compliment one another perfectly to create a super charming storybook atmosphere. The voice of the narrator is calm and soothing, while the art is alive and gives everything so much character, especially the wolves, who have so many little dynamic expressions that constantly shift to telegram exactly what action they're about to make. The music perfectly suits the vibes of the game, the faint strums of guitar strings are exactly the kind of music I want for a puzzle/tactics game like this.Having the hero be a deaf woman in a world overrun by werewolves whose very howl's turn you into a beast is a story set up I absolutely adore. Representation by itself is important and needed, but representation as a key element of the plot - a crucial part of the story which cannot be removed or else the story falls apart - is masterclass.I've only just made it to Chapter 2, but as you can see i'm really into it so far!

_childDocuments_.review: I fired up  for the first time after a hard day’s work. The main theme on acoustic guitar and cello soothed my mind. The folk tale atmosphere drew me in as the player character’s letter-writing voice-over narration set the tone for a dark adventure. It took me back to reading the original fairy tales as they used to be, before they were censored and infantilized by modern books. is a relaxing game with a minimalistic turn-based combat gameplay that rewards elegant solutions. The aesthetic and the setting work well together to carry the gameplay, and the soundtrack and narration keep you interested. This not an elaborate strategy game, but it is challenging in terms of finding the correct, intended solutions. If you go in with that in mind,  is fairly compelling.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little puzzle game. All of the enemies movements are 100% predictable, so the goal is to plan your movements in response and kill all the enemies / get to the goal in a certain number of turns without getting killed by the monsters. You unlock a few potential powers to give you additional options. The levels are all hand-designed.There's not huge amounts of depth here, but there's enough to spend an enjoyable few hours. Similarly, the story isn't super deep but it's sufficient to add some narrative bones for a few hours. Ultimately, I enjoyed the time I spent with Howl, and I think it accomplished what it was trying to do without overstaying its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little game with turn-based puzzle combat (a bit reminiscent of Into the Breach). Probably on the simpler side and not too long (it took me 5.5h to complete, doing all missions, but not trying to achieve 100% everywhere). The story is relatively straight-forward, but nicely narrated as if it was as bed-time story. The visual style is great and fits this decision. Overall, I would recommend it and I think the regular price of ~10€ is fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Howl

_childDocuments_.review: Howl is a short and sweet little game with a very interesting story premise: a plague that turns people into beasts if they hear another beast's howl. So the hero is deaf making her immune to the plague. The game has a great art style, music, and narration. Each level presents a map where you move across a grid trying to reach an endpoint. This is complicated by obstacles, beasts, and people you need to rescue. Each level has 2 (possibly 3) goals: get to the end under a certain number of turns, kill all beasts, and rescue all the people if there are any on the map. The pace of the game is great; Howl does exactly what it sets out to do and doesn't overcomplicate things just for the sake of checking boxes.
_childDocuments_.name: Howl

_childDocuments_.review: I immediately liked the game's storybook visuals and was intrigued by the promise of challenging tactical gameplay. As far as promises and trailers go, they can be hit and miss, so I appreciate there being a relatively comprehensive demo. It lets you play about 70% of the first chapter and made a good case for the game. The early levels seem a bit more restricted and puzzle-y, especially considering that enemies are acting deterministically, i.e. they follow a known set of rules, no randomness involved.However, after unlocking the first couple of skills, the player's options really open up and levels generally feature a number of enemies that will make it feel properly tactical and less puzzle-like.I have yet to complete the full game, but the number of side-paths on chapter maps and the challenge of 100%-ing each level seems pretty substantial to me. Speaking of acing levels: I found myself flush in "Confidence & Skulls" (the currency for unlocking and levelling skills) pretty early on - Whatever skill I want, I can usually get right away, without having to actually work towards it. I'm guessing this is hard to balance without frustrating more casual players, but I thought I'd mention it.Super-minor, but I enjoyed the game properly recognizing the Switch Pro Gamepad I use on PC and showing me the correct button-prompts, even adopting a sort of Switch-style assignment of confirm/cancel buttons. It's not mentioned on the store page and might not matter to most, but I thought it was a neat touch worth mentioning.Presentation-wise, it's best not to expect anything crazy. Story presentation is pretty simplistic, but I think it fits the style of the game and all the ingredients (visuals, writing, audio, voice work) blend nicely. Reminds me of SNES-era games, before everything had to be a twenty minute animated cut scene. If you dig that, definitely check this out! The game is pretty to look at, offers a solid challenge without feeling tedious or stressful.

name: DRAGON QUEST MONSTERS: The Dark Prince
detailed_description: Overview DRAGON QUEST MONSTERS: The Dark Prince comes to Steam®! Compose your very own team of monsters from across the DRAGON QUEST series and engage in thrilling battles against your foes. Recruit monsters from the wild world around you and combine them to synthesize new creatures as you see fit. With over 500 monsters to choose from and a revamped synthesis system to explore, you can mix and match to you heart's content to create your favorite cute critters and dastardly supervillains, as well as brand-new additions to the monstrous roll call. Your quest to become the greatest monster wrangler of all time starts here! Story Psaro is cursed and is unable to harm anything with monster blood. Now, he must become a Monster Wrangler to create an army for battle. The hunt for high-ranked monsters takes Psaro through the ever-changing seasons of Nadiria and its unique environments, with rivers of bubbling lava, mysterious ancient ruins, and soaring towers of cake. Along the way, Psaro meets the kind-hearted elf, Rose, who joins his adventure to seek out ever-stronger monsters. The key to Psaro's success lies with synthesis: the ability to combine two monsters and create a stronger offspring. Each new creation brings Psaro one step closer to his goal of becoming the Master of Monsterkind. (The network mode Online Battles from the console version, where players battle one another in real time, is not included.) Game Features - A Wondrous World Awaits As time passes in Nadiria, so too do the seasons change, with different weather conditions tempting new monsters out of hiding and revealing paths to undiscovered areas. The Circles of Nadiria are sure to provide a fresh experience every time you visit. - Over 500 Unique Monsters With such varied environments to explore, you can expect them to be inhabited by a plethora of monsters. While many can be recruited in battle, occasionally a defeated monster will ask to join your team of its own accord. Befriend as many monsters as you can, then combine them to synthesize new creatures and build a unique party to your exact liking. - Enjoy All the DLC from the Console Version The Steam® version includes the DLC packs from the console version: the Mole Hole, Coach Joe's Dungeon Gym and Treasure Trunks. Make the most of their unique features to enhance your adventure. - Test Your Might in Quickfire Contests Register your team for the network mode Quickfire Contests to participate in automated battles against the party data of 30 other players. Once a day you can earn stat-boosting items as a prize, and the monsters from any team you defeat will be added to your roster (up to rank B monsters only).

name: Trinity Trigger
detailed_description: Trinity Trigger Deluxe Edition This Deluxe Edition includes the Trinity Trigger game, the Extra Episode Set DLC, and the Weapon Set DLC. Will the power of three defy destiny? About the Game Step into the world of Trinity Trigger, an all-new action role-playing game combining the look and feel of iconic RPGs of the ‘90s with a modern emphasis on fast-paced, customizable combat. As Cyan, a young man burdened by the gods with the mantle of Warrior of Chaos and an inevitable clash against the Warrior of Order, players will set out on a grand adventure to defy fate and save Trinitia. Cyan and his companions Elise and Zantis are accompanied by strange creatures known as Triggers that can transform into eight types of weapons, and players can switch freely between the three characters to implement a solo combat strategy, or team up with up to two friends for local co-op. Together, they will write a new destiny. Master the Weapons of the Gods Solve puzzles and defeat enemies alone or with friends in local co-op as you traverse the dungeons of each Arma, towers made from the fallen weapons of the gods. Seek Out Trinitia’s Mysteries Reveal hidden passages by exploring every last bit of Trinitia’s diverse biomes. Chat with townsfolk for clues to uncover the heavily guarded secrets held in these forests, deserts, snowfields, and more. Change the Tide of Battle Make expert use of the Weapon Wheel in battle to change between eight weapon types on the fly. Every enemy has a weakness—finding and exploiting it is the key to victory. A Generational Role-Playing Epic Trinity Trigger was inspired by the iconic RPGs of yesteryear, but its accessible and rewarding gameplay incorporates modern flourishes to make it an exciting new adventure for players of all ages.

short_description: Caught in the middle of a divine clash of epic proportions that has left gigantic weapons towering over the landscape, Cyan and newfound allies Elise and Zantis set out on a quest to save the world…and defy the gods. Claim your fate in this fantastical adventure inspired by classic JRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise is that divine weapons crashed to earth after a war between the God of Chaos and Order, drastically changing the realms around them. These swords represent a multi-story building/dungeon, countless floors high. The main dungeons of each area are also sections of fallen armories of former divine grace, and they are now filled with monsters that guard the sacred altars within. So-called Bringers will summon spirit beasts known as Triggers to serve as both mates and weapons, and then seek out these altars to expand their Triggers weapon-forming abilities. So one of the goals of the narrative is therefore the exploration of dungeons, helping townfolk by doing quests, and the acquisition of new Trigger forms.The other goal is the continuing clash between the God of Order and Chaos, fought in the mortal world by two champions who are destined to meet in an epic showdown that will decide the issue once and for all. In previous iterations, the issue was settled by an outside group's assassination of one of the champions before things even got that far. This does not seem to please the protagonist Cyan, who happens to be the reluctant Champion of Chaos. The flow of the storyline is a steady line from dungeon to dungeon, with only a few distractions left and right. There could have been more variety in the area layouts or more areas not directly related to the weaponry and alteration.In terms of gameplay, Trinity Trigger is still very much an homage to Secret of Mana, with better attack chaining, action gauges, and special moves. All party members can eventually gain access to every weapon type by exploring dungeons, but they all have their own expertise. Cyan excels with the sword, Elise with the bow, and Zantis with his axe. There are a few puzzles here and there, but they're never really demanding. The game is presented in an isometric view with real-time action combat and is ultimately very straightforward and beginner-friendly. Attacking consumes stamina, which refills itself by waiting a few seconds. All of the healing and status effects—like being poisoned—are done via menu, so I found myself navigating through the menus a lot during battle. The only downside is that the AI is pretty useless in group fights and will blindly follow you into enemy traps on the ground, causing you to use far too many healing items for your AI partners.One gimmick of the boss fights is that the large monsters will always have some sort of shield that has to be worn down before they can be stunned and become vulnerable. In most cases, this shield has one or two specific vulnerabilities to certain types of weapons. While this is a good idea in concept, it doesn't come together very well. Certain bosses escalate into a "Rock, Paper, Scissors" kind of combat with enough shield to take multiple times their total hit points in damage before they are defeated, and that can definitely be annoying.A lot of flavor is actually added by the voices of the characters. The music is appropriate for the respective area, even if it isn't a big highlight, and the anime-like cutscenes fit perfectly into the story.The game definitely has its interesting and, especially gameplay-wise, nice moments, but unfortunately, they are somewhat overshadowed by the simple JRPG cliché of an amnesia story that only gets better halfway through. It's definitely a serviceable JRPG. It takes about 16-20 hours to finish the game, and this includes >50% of the side quests. It really needed more from everything: more optional stuff, more types of enemies (especially among the bosses), and a generally better handling of the plot points. I still had a lot of fun with it, and I hope that FuRyu will continue to make this kind of videogame in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr; you miss absolutely nothing by side stepping this one, or to say you gain nothing by playing it. I played it so you don't have to.I've finished the game in 15 hours with all the side quests available before the post game.  Final boss is a tedious cancer after which you unlock some post game content, which is infinitely more tedious.It is as mediocre as it gets, with all the dungeons being reskins, companion AI being brain dead to the point where I believe they would die less if they stood in place, lest they run into every possible hazard. They'll register the red indicators for enemy attacks, run to the edge of it and still get hit. Story is, I don't know, there, your usual "teens save the world", toppling literal gods and stuff. I digress, but there is this one section where you get to a town where everyone is driven mad by the nearby relic and there is no cure (doctors who attempted to find it were equally driven mad), and then the very first side quest in the said town is a woman asking for some herbs that are keeping her from going mad(?).Combat is casual attack/dodge/get stunlocked or hope the enemy is weak to the axe in which case you facetank everything since you don't flinch while being hit. 8 different weapons in total with two sets of selectable combos and a unique attack. There is a nice touch where the weapons visibly change form as you level them up.All in all if you REALLY need to scratch that Mana itch, Oninaki is currently on PS Plus Extra, an equally mediocre experience. Wait for a sale :D

_childDocuments_.review: Also yes, it runs very well on Steam Deck but some minor aspect ratio issues.For what it is, Trinity Trigger is a great JRPG for those who love 90's RPG like Secret of Mana or Illusion of Gaia. While the story is short and somewhat generic, it does a great job at delivering simple but classical feel of an Action RPG with PS2-like graphics.However, it's quite expensive for what it is. If you want an action RPG where you can turn your brain off, wait for a sale on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: the game has been given to me via Daredrop for streaming purposes.that being said, these opinions are entirely my own.1st of all let me mention that the game does have good parts too it. it's creative and has some cute looking characters and good looking art.the character designs are quite nice and the story is ok.i must sadly say tho. that after streaming this game for 3 days, i don't actually like the game.i had to think long and hard about it and as much as i'd love to see it succeed. has some glaring issues to the game.the game will unlikely get any updates, if it did. i might recommend it.but like i mentioned. it has some glaring issues. like a whole laundry list of issues.so let me get started on it shall we,1, repeated voice lines. over and over and over and over and over and over again. like endlessly repeating voice lines.i noticed this problem early on when you unlock the 2nd character. as she constantly repeats the same 3 attack voice lineslike a broken record. at some point you go numb too the voices to then suddenly hear it all again.it's so mind bogglingly annoying that it's obvious that the sound department didn't co-ordinate with the development department, why? because it's not just the characters. the menu's the creatures EVEN the g darn merchants repeat the voice lines over and over and over and over and over and over again. you buy 1 item (mainly blueprints) and with every single purchase they repeat their 1 of 2 voice lines. you open a menu or quick menu. and you're spammed with voice lines.you upgrade a skill and another voice line repeats. it's so stupidly annoying that i hate it. i would mute all the voices if i wasn't streaming the game. and honestly. i think it impacted the viewer experience as well.2, the ai is absolutely terrible. your allies won't attack enemies unless you attack them 1st. they will often run out of an enemy aoe only to run back into it, they will often times stop attacking altogether. eat hits or not even avoid the attacks.your best bet is to place them all on range and keep your main unit as melee. just to hopefully prevent needless damage.allies can't use status recovery items. only healing items to heal themselves. not even helping allies. 3, the spam of ailments and terrible healing items.i don't know who's idea it was to give 90% of the enemies the ability to poison you. it's a good thing u can carry 20 antidotes as you will go through them constantly. at the point it's permanently fixed to your quick menu. this combined with point 1 is terrible. as every time you open the menu you hear the same voice lines again.then whats with the potions? seriously they should have been % based potions. you can only carry 10 of each type and honestly it's stupid how often you have to recover health. due to the bad ai on point 2 you're constantly spamming potions to heal your allies. recovery with "manatides" is ok but only situational and often times doesn't help your other party members.4, mimics mimics everywhere!o m f g dark souls could take a page out of this book over here. mimics absolutely every friggin where. seriously you can't turn your butt without being attacked by them. and you need to beat them for their gems (that be a point to mention later)gods these things are everywhere! not only are they stupidly strong, they poison you and just soak up a needless amount of damage. 5, too many weapons, too little innovation. so you obtain a excessive amount of weapons which would be the selling point of this game. unfortunately you only have space for 4 weapons on your quick bar, no way to quickly change weapons on your party members, and constantly have to switch out for weapons that are "effective". ontop of the fact that each weapon has their own loadout. (which we will also mention later) there is simply a needless amount of fluff. honestly the amount of weapons would be fine if you go with the damage type style of blunt/piece/slash/magic kinda gameplay. instead everything has upto 8 different weaknesses or strengths related to a weapon. which is stupid. not to mention that your characters have an "element" yet there is absolutely nothing in the game related too it. o he's fire, she's water? woopti do! does it give any benefits? non at all!5b combat becomes a messdue to point 5 having a needless amount of weapons and a lack of switching around properly. the combat becomes a complete mess. bosses are needlessly tanky due to their "shield" bar which drains faster if you have their weapon weakness equipped i guess. but due to the fact that each weapon has it's own loadout, you're reluctant to switch out weapons.while also some bosses constantly change their weaknesses. making it a complete mess to fight. suddenly the boss isn't weak against swords. but against your fists! great. but i never leveled up these weapons! (o welp another point to mention i guess, guess i'll mention it now)5c weapon upgrading/skillswith as many weapons there are. they sure as hell lack allot of depth too them. each weapon has a 3hit combo, a special and another special. gods if i know what they are called.the 3hit combo can be reconfigured each combo stage has 2 skills to chose from (unless you bought the dlc for whatever fluffin reason) so effectively each weapon has 6 attacks. some objectively better than others.you then have a skill you can use when your weapon glows and another when your charge bar is full. that's the full extend of combat honestly.yet they also added skill upgrades. where u can upgrade your weapons to make the attacks stronger. but the TP required for it is shared between ALL the character's weapons. meaning you have to either spread out your points. or do like me and focus your points into the skills you like to use on your favorite weapons.you can see how 5b conflicts with 5c as you end up having to switch weapons too often to focus on anything.5d weapon loadoutswhat? you thought we were done ranting about weapons? gods no.each and every single weapon of a character has 3 attack and 3 armor slots. each used for gems.attack slot gems can only equipped once while defense slot gems can be equipped 3 times.if you want to slot every single weapon with better or the best stuff, you would need roughly 150 gems!while you can only carry 300 gems. mind boggeling to me honestly. this is not helped by the fact that there are ALLOT of different tiers of gems, as well as different rarities.effectively i ended up slotting only 2 or 3 weapons per character as i could not be bothered with it anymore.the whole of point 5+ ends up being. you switch out weapons too often, have to slot too many gems and have to farm too much TP level up the skills. after 3 days of streaming the game, i only maxed out 1 maybe 2 weapons per character.6, needless amount of gems.so i mentioned earlier that gems are used to slot into your weapons.each and every single gem has at least 5 different types. each can have 3 different rarities. this in itself would not be as big of a problem, but as you need so many of them for your equipment you end up juggling gems from weapon to weapon until you have enough to slot everything.and let me tell you, there are allot of gems that are not even worth looking at. the best thing they could have done is to give each weapon the same kind of armor slots are they did with attack slots.the attack slots can only have 1 of each type equipped. so only 1 gem that increases attack ect ect.as the armor slot you end up just slotting in mass amount of exp bonus (in my case) honestly i didn't see a reason until late game not to equip exp as obviously having a higher level is more important than +5 flippin defense.---did i cover everything? think i did. i think.anyway.what they should have done is to give every character x amount of weapons, limit the repeated voice lines and tweak the allies so they don't just stand around doing nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that was build on inspiration from 90s era rpgs and it does pay homage to the childhood memories of that time to some extent. However, it does fall short in the sense that it cannot rival classics from that time. This is a game that most jrpg lovers will not play because there was hardly any marketing for it and the overall reviews for it will not have it standout from the sea of games released this year.As you progress throughout the story, you be moved to different areas quickly but the story progresses very slowly. Add to it the fact the story did not draw much my attention. You control a character named Cyan born with the mantle of Warrior of Chaos meaning he is destined to fight the Warrior of Order, his sister. He along with characters to some extent just join you traverse throughout the land of Trinitia in an attempt to defy the fated duel. These three "Bringers" in the story will summon spirits known as Triggers that will serve as their destined teammates and their weapons in combat.The battle system is rather simple. Each Trigger serves as a multitude of weapons that will unlock as the story progresses,  enemies have weakness to certain weapons being used against them. There is even a feature that allows you to equip your weapon with certain things that makes them stronger. There is also charged up single attacks for each character and a group attack. You can change weapons and companion to control at any moment during battle. The battles are real time and fast paced; however, the companion AI is stupid. They literally run straight to danger while you move along with the other character which makes some battles harder than it should be. The music does blend in with the environment and it does complement the artstyle with each character along with the voice acting. To me along with almost if not every reviewer agrees with is the direction on the artistry the developers embarked on. For a game that came out in 2023, there are little adjustments available in the menu.  Very few graphical settings, no difficulty adjustments, and texts move slow.Having said all that, I do not recommend this game. Whether there is a good reason for the price tag along with the dlcs, that is debatable. This is a game in which its developers should have dedicated more time in adding more features to make the game more enjoyable and flesh out even better what was already presented.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: It's a 15-hour minimum (basic story) game with evocative to old-school handheld gameplay. In which you spend a few hours leveling up your heroes and unlocking progression. A time sink. Sure, visually. Most people are turned off by it because they want the greatest, most realistic 8k quality graphics and eye candy from studios like Ufotable. That will not be found here. It's a Japanese role-playing game. It is more concerned with grind and story/character development. Because it is usually the dialogue that is to be focused on, visuals are usually given less priority and that is perfectly fine with a lot of fans of the genre. My negative view of this game isn't that the game itself is bad, but I don't warrant the purchase of this game as it is. You have roughly 20 maybe 25 dollars worth of gameplay here. It's a lot of fun and might help you pass the time if you don't have anything else to do. However, it is not on par with other games in its price range. The only thing I can say is that if you like xSeed and their other published games, yes, purchasing the game will more likely result in more games being published to Steam, but this is generally bad practice because it will continue to raise the prices of games that are not worth anywhere near $60-100.It's not worth the price tag. Buy it on sale and you've got yourself a pretty decent game.The AI is complete garbage. You're better off killing them all and controlling one player or getting friends to control them, because they will absolutely eat damage for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to point out some glaring issues with this game is that looking at the controls layout with a keyboard and controller will softlock you in that part of the menu. You have you kill the program on task manager to get out of this to restart. buttons can't be remapped to a mouse and keyboard buttons cannot be rebound. For a game at 50 CAD MSRP i expect basic keyboard and mouse support, but this game does not provide it. While the game is not terrible he story thus far is pretty generic and uninteresting with passable gameplay. So a mediocre game with a mediorce price point won't sell. On steep discount (> 60% off) the price point is okay if you just wanted a mindless action-JRPG meant for young kids, but be aware of the issues i pointed above with keyboard support.Another dumb thing is that the game resolution does not support beyond 1080p. And for those of you who have an 21:9 Monitor the game does not have utilrawide support.PS: The post game after makes me regret my purchase and i wish i never bothered to play this game. The ai companions are so badly programmed that they will opt to suicide into the post-game final bosses attacks. Not only was this infuriating, but the final 3 bosses are essentially copy and paste of one another with a different colour and the attacks become a bullet hell game with very little visual screen clarity making this a very unpleasant experience. For a game that had very little grind for the in-story gameplay the end game is a grinding nightmare for materials for slot in bonus stats gem crafting.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Continuing the fine (?) tradition of FuRyu games that offer similar experiences to popular JRPG titles of yesteryear, Trinity Trigger doesn't attempt to innovate or stand out (and in fact is rather ugly for a game whose lead platform is the Switch...graphics are on par with Alliance Alive, a 3DS game-very odd considering the star power behind the game's creation) but it plays well enough and the characters aren't repulsive. Music, provided by veteran composer Hiroki Kikuta, is pleasant, but not the most memorable of his discography. One mark in the game's favor is that multiplayer is an option here, for those that were disappointed that the Trials of Mana remake lacked it. Another positive is the inclusion of customization of your normal attacks to an extent, something that should be focused on if a sequel is in the cards.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing this as a full price title I can only give a thumbs down. If this were a 2-man indie passion project, it would be a different story. The soundtrack is good, everything else just feels cheap and lackluster. To give 1 example: All dungeons are just reskins of each other. They look the same, they feel the same and it's the same plain corridors over and over again. If you are looking for an action RPG as good as the Trials of Mana Remake, this is not it. Buy it for 20 bucks but not full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Trinity Trigger feels like they wanted to make a game similar to Secret of Mana or Trials of Mana, but didn't put nearly enough love into it.I recommend picking up Trials of Mana instead if you haven't already played it. It is a much better game. However, if you have already played Trials and Secret of Mana and are looking for something else that is similar to fill that gap, then this game may be for you.I don't feel like the $49.99 or $59.99 price tags are warranted however. The quality just isnt there. This should have been a $39.99 or even a $29.99 game.--------------------------------------------PROS+ Combat feels like a modernized Secret of Mana.+ The weapon system. There are 8 weapon types to unlock. Customize your attack combo with each weapon on each character. Lots of weapon options to taylor to your playstyle.+ The crafting system is nice once you get used to it.+ Japanese voice acting is decent (can't vouch for English, haven't tried it)+ The music is pretty nice. Most of the sound track is written by Mana composer Hiroki Kikuta, so the music really does give that Secret of Mana vibe. There are a few standout tracks that are especially good. The final boss theme was great and really reminded me of the Flammie fight theme from Secret of Mana.+ The Manatite system, which is similar to Materia if you've played FF7. In this game it replaces armor entirely. You can customize a your traits with different combos of Manatite+ There is A TON of post game content. Extra sidequests, dungeons, bosses, and weapon upgrades galore open up after you beat the game. --------------------------------------------CONS- DAY ONE PAID DLC!!! I got the Deluxe edition because I wanted to try the extra side quest DLCs. On the plus side, they were short sidequests that fit well into the midgame. They had good rewards and added just a little bit more character to each of the characters involved.. But they SHOULD HAVE BEEN INCLUDED IN THE BASE GAME. They were like 10-15 minutes of content each! There was no reason these short sidequests should cost an extra $10 for the 4, much less $20 (4 x $5 each) to those who didn't buy the deluxe edition. This was a ridiculous cash grab trying to take advantage of 'the fear of missing out'.- World building was done poorly. Zones are thrown together haphazzardly and they make up flimsy excuses in game as to why things are that way.- The lore seems thrown together and feels half-assed.- Character development is minimal- There are some clashing art styles. NPC models for example look comically lower quality compared to the models of story characters.- There are no magic or abilities. All you have is weapons and items. All attacks come from your weapons. All healing and buffing comes from items, with some minor exceptions. It feels somewhat shallow.- Level design. Sometimes the maps feel very VERY cheaply put together. Not every map/level is bad, there are definitely good ones in there. But the ones that are bad are really immersion breaking. The Aldo Desert maps are some of the worst examples, made of clusters of blocky square sections. Heres a screenshot: - Multiplayer is locked until a few hours into the story.- Starts slow. I had a hard time getting into the game until a few hours in. --------------------------------------------KNITPICKING* There is no option to display HP as a number instead of a bar in the HUD. I liked seeing my character's growth in Mana games by seeing the numbers go up over time. No such luck here.* The number of different kinds of fodder drops you can find everywhere can be overwhelming at first. * Not enough monster variety
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is good.... when it's working.  Gameplay is fun, combat is engaging, music is pretty good, story is decent.That said, I can't get this game to run properly under Windows...  The graphics are great and seems to run fine at my monitor's 144Hz rate, but all the animations and movement just at 50% speed.I have dual 144Hz monitors, and an Nvidia 3090 GPU.  Something is just wrong with the game.It DOES seem to run fine on Steam Deck, but ONLY when Graphics Quality is set to "Low".  On high, I get the same thing:  Good framerates, but all the gameplay runs at half speed.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than I expected, but it may only appeal to people who look back fondly on .  is an upgrade in gameplay compared to the SoM remake, but it's not a totally modern game.Dungeons and areas tend to be pretty small, but significantly larger than SoM.Combat is still stamina-based, but you can attack around 6 times before being out of stamina. That's compared to attacking once in SoM.The difficulty is also similar to SoM. Getting stun-locked for several hits is the most dangerous part. However, enemies can't be as easily stun-locked in , so it's better in that regard.The progression is similar: explore an open area, get to the next town, get through the next dungeon, get some new weapon or power, and repeat. Especially in the early game, this can feel repetitive, but the game throws some twists into this formula by the middle.The story is pretty simple, but not as simple as SoM.The music is by Hiroki Kikuta, who did SoM and other Mana games, including the recent . I felt the soundtrack was pretty weak early in the game, but it gets much better; there are some great tracks.Stamina-based combat, a dodge roll (with iframes, I think), somewhat limited healing, dungeon crawling, bosses, moderately-paced combat.Is  a proto-Soulslike? By modernizing the combat slightly,  comes so close to being a Soulslike that I can barely tell if it is or isn't one.It's not as difficult as most Soulslikes, and it's a lot more colorful. But there are some optional bosses that are very difficult, and you have to be constantly upgrading your weapons and Manatite to keep up with the enemies.Is this game much different from  or ? I really don't know.I hesitate to say this game is "great," but it's a real step up from . It's very good for what it is, but it might not offer the complexity that modern gamers expect.But I really like it. On sale for $20 for the Deluxe Edition, I felt it was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay but I'd wait for it to go on sale. Can't recommend it at full price.Plot progression seems kind of slow despite moving through different areas quickly but overall the characters are likable and party banter is decently written. Combat is simple but interesting enough. AI is a little dumb so this is probably better to play with friends than solo but you have to unlock it after a couple of hours of playing solo. As it is, the AI gets damaged 5x as much as me and I'm not necessarily good at the game. Generous amount of potions and other recovery items/abilities sort of compensates for it. My only real complaint is that there's no vsync setting in game and without it, there's a ton of screen tearing. Can enable v-sync in graphics driver settings to fix it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: It feels aweful... There is little to no feedback when hitting enemy. Feels like hitting air. Lack of sound design. Bosses are just bullet sponge slug fests. Your companions will make no effort to avoid attacks and will consistently die, so you'll end up alone fighting a battle meant for 3 people.The music is pretty fine. It feels like generic JRPG music and it does the job it's supposed to do.While I like the design of the character sprites. What I'm getting tired of however is the Visual Novel esthetics, that every conversation takes place as a visual novel mini show. I am just tired of this. It takes me out of the game world that the devs crafted.Standard JRPG fair: find crystals, and then kill god (I assume, haven't finished the game yet, not even sure I will).No option to rebind my keys/buttons?It's obvious this games tries to be like Secret of Mana, even replicating the multiplayer that unlocks 3 hours in, which was dumb then, and even more dumb today. But even then, Secret of mana wth all it's flaws, was a pretty good game IMO. Trinity Trigger is not. And that is mainly because the combat feels so bad. And combat is everything in these types of games. You could have no story at all, but if the combat is fun, you have a game. But have an excellent story with aweful combat, and people will just go watch masochistic playthrough on youtube. I really regret paying 90$ CAD for this very mediocre experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: The story is uninteresting, characters lack real development, antagonists are underwhelming. Gameplay is a very simplistic ARPG with boring map, outdated graphics, forgettable music. Most weapons are worthless, I completed the storyline without having to change weapons much. The party AI is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid and will soak up all of your healing items, even the co-op isn't enjoyable either. 4/10. Not recommended for 50 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly fine. There are few points I don't really like in general, though. The arms type resistances of all enemies force you to swap weapons constantly and make fights more energy consuming but not difficult nor interesting. The last dungeon is quite typical for jRPGs, but being classical does not make an excessively long trivial labyrinth any better. The AI of NPCs is unbelievably dumb, and while PC companions seem to have damage mitigation, they are completely useless in encounters with environmental hazards, namely, the last boss becomes a one on one brawl with your miserable team dying indefinitely in the background.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Rating:7/10I would only recommend this game when it is on sale!You play as a party of 3, 2 are controlled by AI and let me tell you. Its there to make certain boss fights with obstacles a living hell for you. If you don't attack and run around trying to dodge attacks, they just stand still and watch till you start hitting again.Wish they didn't gate keep the potion after a paywall as I have 2 mil coins sitting in my wallet but instead I have to go and farm.The leveling up system is useless as the only stat you gain is health, would have been nice to see a variety of stat boosts.However even with all these cons, I still enjoyed this game. Even though it got repetitive sometimes and the AI was frustrating. The art/graphics were beautiful, the story was well worked, it could have used some finishing touches, but I don't mind an open ending. It was also very fun to use all kind of different weapons which you usually can't do.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Whole lotta fun as far as combat is concerned, good voice acting and lots of it. Deeper story than you'd expect, and really good side quests. Weapon systems and skill upgrades work at a fair pace. Definitely recommend!P.S. The extra weapons are a nice helper if you're not usually good at these types of action-RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Top notch character art+ Amazing voice acting+ Very cozy+ Decent musicCons:- The story isn't very interesting- The sound fx during combat are pretty much non-existent, making it very unsatisfying when landing hits or big attacks- The final dungeon is pretty lameOverall, this isn't some epic that's recreating the wheel. It's a casual and fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Secret of Mana, this game is inspired by it.The combat is very similar where you can only attack so often. Attacking costs meter so when your meter is empty, you do minimal damage. The meter refills over time. You can attack up to a three hit/chain in a combo. Like Secret of Mana, you can unlock and have access upwards of 8 different weapons. Each of the weapons also have upwards to 3 different moveset for each string so you can customize your weapon's attack style. Unlike Secret of Mana, each of your party members can equip the same weapon at the same time. You also have a buff you can activate when you have full aura meter and a super/charge attack along with a big team attack. Instead of armor, this game has a gem system that you can slot into your weapons to increase stats, resistance or gain extra passives.There is no magic spells like Secret of Mana in this game.The music has a very similar tune/feeling to Secret of Mana.The difficulty can vary depending on how you play the game. You can get by with fairly well if you keep your items relatively full each time you venture out.Some cons/nitpicks-your attack animation is kind of slow which makes you prone to getting hit very often-the enemies, especially the smaller general mobs, have fast attack animation and will interrupt your attack strings-enemies don't flinch therefore you can't interrupt them-you have no invincible frames so getting stun locked to death isn't a rare thing-the bosses have a guard break mechanic (you have to delete their guard meter before you can do damage)-multiplayer doesn't unlock until you get all three party member-your ai party members are fairly dumb, they will only stand in a single place and spam attack, very very rarely will they dodge-every single weapon type for every single character has it's own set of slots for the gem system, meaning by the end game you have to probably mess with 144 different slots which is a hassle if you just want to play the game, Luckily you can get by with few gem slots.It's a fun game but you can't play the game recklessly or aggressively due to how harsh the combat is towards the player. Like most multiplayer able games, you'll have more fun playing with others.EDIT: Now that I've beaten the game and the post game finale, this game is a very difficult to recommend. The enemy designs does not complement the game play design, you are ALWAYS at a disadvantage. There is a particular build that helps mitigate some of the problem but being required to play a specific way doesn't help much with the overall impression. I still stand that if you're playing multiplayer, you'll have a fun time, single player however might be less enjoyable until you have that build.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game was ok, the dungeons were very generic looking and was a copy and paste throughout. What really made me not pursue the game further was the inability to play coop during remote play sessions. I thought it was my connection at first, but when I tested other games in coop using remote play (Ex. secret of mana and Portal 2) they worked fine. Every time i attempted to play in coop mode (Trinity Trigger) using remote play the game slowed down significantly as if the game switched to a slow motion mode. It didn't seem like any lag I experienced from network connectivity. After a couple of attempts and some changes to the settings in both the game and remote play, the game just didn't run smoothly in remote play coop.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Story is fun and the characters being voiced really helps in maintaining interest. The combat is good but sometimes (i play on keyboard) as I went into the end game I got really annoyed with the a.i allies just dying all the time, especially on bosses. Feels like a jrpg for the ps2 era. It has its flaws but still like'able.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Game is alright so far. Multiplayer with friend would probably up my enjoyment of the game. The music to me is just mediocre, the story is meh, combat feels great. I guess that is how i feel, the game is just average so far. The boss fights and even the harder optional ones are not really hard, they usually do 2 or 3 patterns that are easy to dodge around and it is just hitting a sponge for a while. If their is one thing I wish to really beg for is to turn off combat voice. they literally spam the same dialogue and yeah you can turn all voices off, but need a toggle of the for battle voices. Overall I think the game has potential with harder difficulty options and some qol changes. I will recommend the game because I am having fun, just would like more complexity, I am a long time secret of mana fan, and this has yet to capture that charm for me. for 50$ tho I am not sure, I would maybe suggest waiting unless you have a friend or two to coop with

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommending purely because its way to expensive for the experience. So far so good. The game not bad. The price is WAY too much (I got if half price).I will say my main distaste for this game is the npcs you have following you. They die....a lot. They are not very good at dodging boss mechanics. I wish instead you could have them not follow you but still swap to them in combat. (I hope that made sense.) It would be easier to keep them alive if the bosses aggro stayed on the person you are controlling but instead it kind of randomly picks someone to focus on and then swaps people every now and then. Also having the npcs auto use their big skills would be nice instead of having to swap back and forth to use it which can be a little disorientating.Over all not a bad game.WAY TOO FREAKING EXPENSIVE! _childDocuments_.review: It's definitely not the best game or JRPG you can get here, but it's a cool little one. Yeah it's not amazing in any ways, it can even be frustrating as the other 2 characters played by the AI are so dumb they can't jump out of an attack, but it's still a fun little ride.Story is OK, but messy. Characters are sympathetic. Monsters are cute. Dungeons are repetitive (but that's a japanese game)... Still, I liked it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Trinity Trigger has some bad and good things. The story is certainly interesting. Even if the dialogues are sometimes generic. I found that the 2d conversation animations, lack expression. The fighting is fun but having to pause to switch weapons is just a core, in the long run. I dislike a lot, the fact that all the characters can have all the same weapons and powers. In that sens, your party is all the same. You decide which one can have that power or that weapon, but if it's not into the game, it makes every upgrades an after though. Some bosses have a difficulty spike. The color system that block a weapon on a boss is especially aggravating. Since switching weapons or characters in fight is tedious, you can imagine how those fights become frustrating and story blocking. Yes there is some good production value, and you might get 20 to 30 hours before hanging the game. But that won't be because you complete it, you might get bored or angry before that. I give it 65%. Mainly because the base is there, but the structural decision around the game seems weak to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY AT FULL PRICEIt's a fun enough game, it has a typical JRPG storyline, though feels a bit rushed in the story telling.  The side quests are fun in helping out learn more about your character and teammates.  The art look great and the voice acting is enjoyable.  The areas look nice, and are fun to explore.  There is some crafting in the game, but only to make potions and supplies, which I don't mind.The combat is rough, but doable.  While I enjoy the free movement, the AI for your teammates isn't the brightest and seems to have a mission takes themselves out on enemy attacks or environmental hazards (watched one ping itself off spikes all over a room until it keeled over).  There is no magic in the game, just different weapon types to chose between and upgrade, and abilities you can attach to them.  The dungeons are relatively simple, and so far, have easy enough puzzles.  The bosses are meant to have you choose your weapons once you've learned which on they are weak to, but honestly I didn't notice much of a damage difference between a normal and buffed attack.One of the biggest draws that I looked forward to was the coop feature to play with friends, but it is only for local coop and using Steam's online local coop feature ended up causing too much lag for us to actual get anywhere.  It was a big letdown after spending almost 3 hours to unlock it.Overall, I do enjoy the game itself, even with some of its quirks.  I am glad I bought it on sale though, and highly recommend anyone looking to get it to wait for a similar sale.  While it is fun, I can't say it is $50-$60 fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game if you're looking for a very casual action RPG. I beat the main story and all non-post-game side quests in 20 hours. This game is intended to be in the spirit of Secret of Mana, and it is, although there is no magic system and at times I did miss that. The story is fairly simple, and falls apart a little at the very end, but I didn't really mind.If you're looking for a masterpiece, this isn't it. But if you go in with modest expectations for something casual to scratch a particular genre itch, you'll have a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much potential, but was all over the place. The partner AI felt like it was actively trying to kill themselves. The story was generic and basically substituted tropes for actual storytelling. It definitely felt like the game wanted to do too many things at once and did none of them well.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Trigger

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed playing this game. All throughout my time playing, I got mad 90's RPG vibes à la Trials of Mana and the like. It's a really cosy, albeit a little short game that's perfect for chillin'. I haven't had the chance to use to use the co-op, only ever played single payer. I've played the game for roughly 30-ish hours by this point and I'm very close to completing the achievements, with only 5-6 left. A lot of the achievements are basic grinding or story element related, nothing particularly difficult.  That being said, it isn't perfect game by any means; the game for some reason will stutter a fair bit, which is annoying at best, but still annoying. A far more frustrating grievance is how bad the AI companions can be at times, especially during boss fights -- repeatedly walking into lava, or spikes for example. Sometimes the true boss fight is keeping your AI companions alive rather than the boss itself. Overall, good game. I would play it again and encourage others to try it. 8/10. TLDR; Pros: + Decent story. Nothing amazing, but certainly something to chill to. + The character art was really well designed IMO. Big fan of all character's designs. + Amazing voice acting. I played with the English audio and it felt the voices really matched the designs. + Music complemented the individual areas quite well. Cons:- The frame stuttering. I eventually got used to it and ignored it, so it's not unbearable, just annoying. - The AI can be really, really frustrating at times. Biggest problem with the AI is during some fights your companions will voluntarily walk into hazardous elements and kill themselves. When you have a limited supply of healing, this becomes a problem.

And where will we be without Elise? She is the true hero here. She saves Cyan, gets him on mission. Gets every weapon form before everyone else. And just overall CARRIES. But its cool. Cyan gets Great game imo. Only downside was hearing the attack voice overs, over and over. Bullseye!

_childDocuments_.review:
Trinity Trigger is an all-new action role-playing game combining the look and feel of iconic RPGs of the '90s with an emphasis on fast-paced, customizable combat.

Players take control of three young heroes as they attempt to defy fate and save the continent of Trinitia. Accompanying them are the Triggers, strange creatures with the unique ability to transform into eight types of weapons that players must master if they hope to be successful on their quest.

Whether playing alone or with up to two friends via local co-op, explore diverse biomes and dungeons, strategize to exploit enemy weaknesses, and change your destiny!

name: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader
detailed_description: Explore the Koronus Expanse. Begin your adventure aboard your personal, giant voidship, traveling between the multitude of systems within the Koronus Expanse, a barely charted and incredibly perilous region of space. Despite being considered a backwater of the Imperium, this region encompasses an enormous stretch of the void, filled with dangerous creatures and prodigious opportunities for profit and exploration. Gather your crew. Rogue Traders never travel alone. Gather your retinue of righteous heroes, twisted psykers, and perfidious xenos. All of them are ready to follow you into the darkness between the stars. They will offer you counsel, aid you in battle, and allow you to amass ever more power. In return, you can guide them through their own personal journeys, changing their destinies forever. Your decisions matter, Lord-Captain. During quests show your subjects mercy or disdain, stay faithful to the God-Emperor, or consort with enemies of Mankind - your every decision and every act, even in character creation, is changing the in-game open world and those who inhabit it. Plan your actions carefully. Slaughter the enemies of Mankind in a fully-fledged isometric turn-based tactical combat. Take advantage of cover, the environment, and careful positioning to overpower your enemies. When that is not enough - use your companion`s powerful abilities to turn the tide of battle and achieve victory even in the direst of situations. Our video game adaption of the classic Rogue Trader ruleset allows an enormous number of possibilities for you to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Warhammer 40K game. I am not that invested into lore as some people. But I still enjoy the game. As far as I have reached in game, the story is good. Lots of reading to do as there is not much voice acting. Skills are not that straight forward and would take multiple play throughs to understand(at least thats what i felt). There are ship combat too. You have to do choices that can effect the ending.I am playing coop and it works nicely too. But there are issues though. Lots of loading screens in game. Combine it with your friends who live in different parts of the world with different internet connection speed;  you get the idea. But still its not that bad. Only the host can make the choices in game. Dont expect Baldurs Gate 3 type choice for each character. But your friends can do skill checks in game. So thats a plus. There is friendly fire too so positioning is important.So my verdict, I like the game. If you enjoy turn based combat, story heavy game, chances are you would too.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, but.The closest comparison I've played would be the Shadowrun games by Harebrained Schemes, the X-Comish style and story delivery, with a great deal more quantity of story than any of the Shadowrun games.But the state of play right now is frustratingly broken to the point where I'm going to pause playing and sit back to let it get patched a bit more. I'm in the midst of Act 3 right now and managed to dodge any of the main quest breakers that others have. However, my side/companion quests have been a mess. I had one companion quest introduction get interrupted mid-dialogue with a sudden break to a main quest scene in a totally different room, thus losing that companion quest altogether. I just finished another one (an obnoxiously fussy stealth quest) only to have it abort without explanation at the final conversational step, apparently taking the companion with it.If you enjoy the setting, the vibe is right there. The moral complexity of a universe were doing the ethically right thing may result in horrifically bad outcomes is very much there. There are plenty of lore easter eggs, the soundtrack and visuals are excellent. But playing right now is a slog wrestling with the functional state of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I finished the game finally and overall I had a blast, but it has many issues.Note, there may be some spoilers.I'll start with the good. I really liked the story set-up. I have very little experience with W40K lore and knew nothing about Rogue Traders (RT) at all except for the name and a few things people mentioned here on the forums. The set-up is very clear and allows for an immediate understanding of where you stand. Owlcat have also been doing their little tooltip popups for the past games and those have remained there for further information. There's even a codex which contains further details on concepts both within 40K lore and the game itself.The story itself doesn't start you out as anything special and I thought it would take a bit longer to become the RT, but it's almost immediate essentially, which is both good and bad as it allowed me to step into those shoes and learn as I go. I found the story to be quite enjoyable overall, but it had certainly had its highs and lows, with most highs being frontloaded. For example, the game starts you off deciding which planets to go to first to investigate what is happening. Each decision has consequences on the other planets. They were really obvious and subtle at the same time. That was really well made. They carried this into Chapter 2 as well well, but then it felt like they lost track of funding as those choices started petering out... Overall, I would still call it a fun story, which carried me through most of the game and I did always want to find out more. It's a shame the second half is not as good.The quests were fun, both main and side quests had a lot going for them, interesting characters and contained a set-up, a body and usually several endings. Many of the quests had dependencies, based on what choices you had made earlier into the game, which means you could easily replay this game at least 3 times with very different outcomes, and probably several more times with some more minor changes to the game too.I think the majority of the characters were quite interesting too - bar a few. I found some characters a bit over the top, but within my playthough I always had my main characters I was happy to bring along and a few I didn't mind bringing along on their sidequests. The only two exceptions were Argenta and Marazhai, both because they were simply too extreme for my playthrough. I believe that if I did ever play again with more dogmatic or heretical characters, they would fit into those playstyles better. So although not amazing, I do understand they would have a place in game.The combat was pretty good, overall, but I found the majority of fights too easy (except for a few minor examples). I played on Daring. I also actually enjoyed the ship combat and although it doesn't come to the level of really good, I had no issues with it at all. Now the bad.Most of the bad is related to mechanics. First of all, and I mentioned this in the What Are You Playing thread, is the amount of leveling needed. We are talking about 55 levels with a minimum of 6 characters (but actually more), so you spend 330 levels' worth of looking at menus in this game. This is madness. The majority of levels are minor changes and the ones that do make an impact take ages to decide on because the recommended skills are mostly useless. For example, if you have a psyker, it doesn't even recommend leveling up the psy rating, which is like not a warrior not leveling up their STR in DnD. This needs a full overhaul in my opinion and should be limited to 25-30 levels that have larger impacts.I also believe itemisation to be something that could have been amazing, but with the inventory being so unmanageable it makes it difficult to navigate. Many items provide unique benefits to characters, but sometimes only if they have a particular skill. However, it doesn't show me if my character has that skill. I don't remember all the skill names by heart, so I would have to review each and every item and each and every character. Instead those items were never used. There are also many filters missing in my opinion, such as - can my character even use it ? No, just shade it red and let me scroll through 100 items for no reason.Another issue with this game is the amount of loading screens. Some maps are pretty large and it makes me wonder why others are so small with so many unnecessary transitions. It's probably too late to fix now, but I really can't understand how they did not think about this. Go my bridge to room, load screen, back to bridge, load screen, to map, load screen, visit planet, load screen, walk for 3 mins, load screen, walk back, load screen. This was a major annoyance and my loading didn't even take long. I can't imagine how it feels for people with slower PCs.The final issue for me is that the bugs are still obviously there. This game is really well cooked for the first two chapters. I could barely see anything major, but from chapter 3 onwards, there are many bugs. Quest-breaking bugs, visual bugs, dialog bugs,... They should have beta-tested chapters 3 and 4 at least too to allow for some of the main ones to be picked up on. I feel like they haven't learned (enough) from their first two games.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried multiple times to get 'into' this game. Especially after Space Marines 2 came out, I found myself hankering for a deeper dive into Warhammer 40K. And I consider myself a fan of the genre: from BG1/2/3, Icewind Dale, Pillars of Eternity 1/2, Tyranny, D:OS 1/2, Pathfinder: Kingmaker and Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous. I want to scratch that itch.This game just isn't it. It's in my view the worst of Owlcat's major releases, and I'm tired of pretending otherwise. It's narratively a disjointed mess, its classes are superficially complex but dull to play, its approach to turn-based combat is asinine. Seriously: everyone familiar with this game will agree, it devolves into "get Heroic Acts and wipe the map", there's no sense of dynamic play/counterplay.Frankly, I'm throwing in the towel with Owlcat. They're a ♥♥♥♥ developer. Their games are notoriously buggy on launch (everyone will advise you to download Toybox to fix your saves, like that's somehow a normal thing to do for a full-release product), their combat is always second-rate (Pathfinder's pre-combat buff cycles weren't 'good gameplay', just tedium to overcome stat bloat; RT's meta is arguably even worse). In this instance, the story isn't even that riveting and the writing is not half as good as people make it out to be: often, needlessly verbose. There's a fine art to brevity in dialogue; here, all-too-often it's heavy-handed and expositional.Right now a lot of people will tell you "dont buy DA:Veilguard, don't support practices you disagree with". I'm going to borrow that principle and apply it here: developers will make the games we agree to pay for. If you're cool with consistently buggy launches, maths-heavy but actually inelegant, dull combat and hit-and-miss storytelling (I considered WoTR excellent, but KM and this, not so much), pay for Owlcat Games. If not, stop buying their crap - indefinitely.
