_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to do this review justice, I put 400 hours into the beta and almost 600 hours into the full release. I'm obviously a fan. And I'm now waiting for the DLC's to drop. So: Setting - Gloriously well done!Voice Acting - They are adding more voice lines as they go along. The acting that is present is very very on point but if you've played OC before you know there is a lot of reading, its not Vagras but yes you do need to read and you are rewarded by the quality of the writing and immersion. Music - Everything you've come to expect from an Owlcat Game!Stability - Everything you've come to expect from an Owlcat Game! Seriously though on that point, it will get better as it goes, the complexity of the system mapping behind the game is scary. No OC game is good on release....or for a year after. I will testify that its significantly better than it was and the team behind it has done a lot of good work. Progression - Excellent, complex - you need to engage and learn. Save often. I never looked at the internet builds. I just did my own. Here's a hint, if you just blow through the main campaign and don't explore the setting, your weapons and your characters starter build stats (as some of them are broken if you actually look at what you can do with them and their custom character specific classes - hint hint), you will find the end fights almost impossible. If you do explore like a....Rogue Trader? Looking for every deal and advantage in a story rich setting and even pay half a mind to your party's synergy with each other. You will greet the ending in hails of bolter fire and joy.....or evil laughter. The game is long and takes as much investment of time, energy and thought as WoTR or Kingmaker, I might even describe it as close to Kingmaker in the shear levels of: Oh God I'm fighting what now?! It has the same difficulty ramp too. The difference here is, its not DnD or Pathfinder. Its not so familiar but don't underestimate the lower choices of classes, the variation and options available - It will catch you out if you do and the game released with respec options, free the first few times. It's expected the you will make mistakes and catered for. I will echo that one point of frustration though, for all that, and how much I don't regret backing this from early beta. Pick whether you want to be: A True Heir of the Imperium and Vanquisher of the Mutant, the Heretic and the Zenos (Lawful Good to Lawful Evil) - Dogmatic.A Free Thinking Hero of the Oppressed and Openminded Explorer of the Uncharted (Neutral Good to Chaotic Neutral) - Iconoclast. A Total Monster and Thorough going Psychopath (Neutral Evil/Chaotic Evil) - Heretic.Then play it all the way through, you get no rewards for being a jack of all outlooks and you will softlock your progression by deviating even alittle. If anything this game really hammers into you, stick to your principles and embrace the consequences. All paths are rewarding but yes if you try to roleplay by your own out-of-universe current day conscience, or play the hero - whatever that means to you, you might have problems. Immerse yourself in 40K. Put one foot in front the other, change what you can within your destiny and forge a path forwards where none existed and the sector will change with you within a setting that is dark and you are surrounded by superstition, peril and arrogance. Where salvation is paid for in lives, yours, your subjects, your enemies and where collateral damage isn't really a thing. Thought for the day: "There is no such thing as innocence, only degrees of guilt."

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader is a masterful blend of deep storytelling, tactical combat, and the rich lore of the Warhammer 40K universe. Developed by Owlcat Games, this CRPG offers an immersive experience that will captivate both long-time fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.From the moment you step into the shoes of a Rogue Trader, you’re thrust into a universe teeming with intrigue, danger, and opportunity. The game’s narrative is compelling, filled with well-crafted characters and morally complex decisions that truly make you feel like a powerful and influential figure in the Imperium. The writing is top-notch, capturing the grimdark essence of Warhammer 40K while also providing moments of dark humor and satire.The tactical combat system is another highlight, offering a challenging and rewarding experience. Each encounter requires careful planning and strategic thinking, making every victory feel earned. The variety of enemies and the use of cover and space add layers of depth to the battles, ensuring they never become monotonous.Visually, Rogue Trader is stunning. The gothic architecture, detailed character models, and atmospheric environments bring the Warhammer 40K universe to life in breathtaking detail. The sound design and music further enhance the experience, immersing you in the game’s dark and gritty world.While the game does have its share of bugs and technical issues, these are minor setbacks in an otherwise exceptional title. The sheer scope and ambition of Rogue Trader are commendable, and it’s clear that Owlcat Games has poured their heart and soul into creating a game that honors its source material.In conclusion, Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader is a must-play for any CRPG enthusiast or Warhammer 40K fan. Its engaging story, strategic combat, and rich world-building make it a standout title in the genre. Despite a few rough edges, it’s an epic adventure that shouldn’t be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Owl Cat's Rogue Trader provides an exceptional embodiment of a Rogue Trader in the Warhammer 40k universe. I am an avid fan of the 40k universe and have always been drawn to the mystique of the Rogue Trader class. It is abundantly clear that the Owl Cat's developers share my affinity for Warhammer 40k. The story, characters, and environment all speak to Owl Cat's attention to the nuance of 40k's grimdark universe. Unfortunately, it fails to capture the visceral combat found in 40k novels and captured previously in Dawn of War 2. Nonetheless, This game is as close as a 40k fan will get to interfacing with the dark future of the 41st millenium as a Rogue Trader.I do not how broadly this game will appeal beyond 40k fans. If this is your first foray into the 40k universe you are selling yourself short if you do not have the Warhammer 40k wiki open and accessible in your steam overlay. I was pleasantly surprised by the depth of lore hidden in obscure corners of the game. Owl Cat took creative license in introducing new aspects to the lore, which is a must for a universe as large as 40k. The volume of reading available to the player in this game is extensive. Whether it's a character interaction, journal entry, or new ability you will be constantly beset by tool tips or dialogue boxes. I found the ability selection upon leveling up to be intimidating at first. I did not want a sub-optimal character, however, I also have zero interest in doing any of my own research on formula based abilities. This ultimately proved to be a non-issue, and my role-playing heart prevailed. I narrowed my ability selection criteria to those that sounded in line with how I envisioned my party and was able to remain well ahead of the difficulty curve. I eagerly await perfectly calculated builds from meta-gamers, but in the mean time, I will have no trouble progressing further (with great violence, and through waves of heretics).I have only encountered one nearly game breaking bug. My camera became fixated on an enemy despite the character turn rotation. After some experimentation I was able to rectify this with a lighting bolt through the aforementioned enemy.  I can easily recommend this game to any 40k fan. If you are new series I would caution you that your upcoming adventure must also include a trip to 40k wiki and at least a handful of Black Library Novels (anything by Dan Abnett is a guarantee).

The story is great and the choices are nerve-wracking.  I have had to restart from saves a few times because I didn't really read or comprehend the decision I was about to make and lost a crew member.  It seems like at every turn you are given the option to kill off a member of your crew.  They really capture the Grim Dark of the 41st Millennium. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; great game, buy it later when the bugs are fixed.Good: Great story, great characters, great gameplay. I was immersed and invested immediately. These points alone make every hour worthwhile. I enjoyed exploring and reading everything I came across in the game. For people unfamiliar with 40k, there are links in the text the give lore tidbits so you can understand what's being spoken about without there being unnecessary exposition for 40k nerds like myself.Meh: Reputation and the rewards tied to it aren't balanced well. If you spread the rep points instead of focusing on 1 faction the gear you get will either be the same as what you have or obsolete. It takes way too much rep to get anything meaningful and takes a large amount of Profit Factor (currency) to get good items. Space combat while done well, is more unforgiving than the standard combat. It gets better once you have a second ship to help out and soak some hits, but by the end game it will usually be dead after 1 or 2 turns because you can't upgrade it or control it. If it was controllable and could be upgraded it would perform better.Bad: This game was not finished. Broken quests and links in item/skill descriptions. These kinds of bugs are completely unacceptable because you find them just by playing the game, they are not obscure occurrences. Some people have complained about game breaking bugs, but I never encountered any. The ones I encountered were related to side quests tied to companions which soured the experience. The issues were the quests not even firing or not completing when finished. A minor annoyance is the party you last disembarked with is the "party" you are using as you fly through space. This affected Yrliet's quest early on because even if you recruited her if she wasn't in your party when you disembarked, it would bug the completion of her side quests which were resolved in space.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool setting and really nice that there is a complex set of rules behind the game - but:A turn-based game depends on the rules working flawlessly. - the calculation of initiative in the turns is completely arbitrary; the associated skill “agility” has no influence. As a rule, the majority of opponents act before your own squad, regardless of whether they all have agility 20 or 100. If you then reload the battle, the initiative is completely different and cannot be redistributed in a comprehensible way...- If I manage to debuff an opponent in such a way that he's actually just a drooling statue, I'm surprised that this same opponent turns completely free in his next turn and actually acts normally. Also incomprehensible and very frustrating.-Sometimes the battles start and my squad has no ammunition in its weapons/passive stacks are simply not awarded-The localization into German is really bad in many parts; sometimes the dialogues completely lose their meaning.Nevertheless, I give it a thumbs up - a C+. Unfortunately still an F5-F8 massacre due to the many small bugs concerning the combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is very much a yes, but... review. Rogue Trader absolutely nails the atmosphere grimdark 40k Universe, with convincing dialogue options for those that inhabit it. It perhaps could grate a little with those that want to be the Lawful Good Paladin that certain other CRPGs require.Graphics and sound are effective; music is excellent. DLC is pointless so far - may improve.Combat is, initially, satisfying on normal difficulty settings. The first boss fight (spoilers not hard to find at this point but I'll spare you them) will be utterly infuriating. There is an argument that said opponents SHOULD be infuriating, but as backtracking to re-tool and re-equip is not an option, I would hazard a guess many players will simply slash the difficulty dial at that point. This is not terribly good fun either, a walkover in a turn based game is not entertaining, it's just a grind. It rather spoils the illusion of having options that allow you to tactically beat an opponent, as opposed to doing it by wargear and character build which is realistically the only way to win that boss fight - and many of the later ones.That's the next major grumble. The myriad of character options is both a boon and curse, and you realistically will need a playthrough to figure out what composition you want in your squad; as well as advance knowledge of the wargear. Knowing 40k isn't enough; the game mechanics are such that a MeltaGun "nominally, a very powerful, short range heavy weapon" you would expect to have certain characteristics. But in the workings of the game, they won't necessarily meet expectations.The old FPS gaming trope of giving you a level where you lose all your equipment is also present, and presents a similarly frustrating challenge to the first boss fight. And again, no opportunity to backtrack barring savescum to rethink.So, not without criticism, this was still worth a play-through once for the story. And even then, the final chapter is lazily written, but thankfully over relatively quickly. So as I prefaced this with, it's a yes.... but, review. Treat as such!

_childDocuments_.review: Typical Owlcat Games nonsense--tedious character stat bloat with innumerable superficial, redundant stat choices and 'optimisation' masquerading as meaningful and 'fun'.Bugs, jank, bizarre voice actor choices and occasional grade-school calibre grammatical errors in dialogue (i.e. "then" being used in place of "than") are typically groan-inducing, though much improved on their dreadful Pathfinder counterparts.Also for your amusement:- T-posing.- Reloading causing quests to break (due to the game randomly reloading an incorrect state).- Enemies running into/through walls and causing combat to remain active.- The UI leaving a black square overlay after closing it (character screen/journal/whatever).- Voiceless dialogue cutscenes that cannot be skipped through, leaving you to wait an age before it moves to the next bit, or you skip the entire cutscene.- Few opportunities to simply return to your ship. Traversing a number of maps to get back to it is *tedious*.All-in-all, it's up to the usual Owlcat Games standard--if you don't look too closely you might be fooled into thinking you're playing something more than the sum of its parts.It is, however, a Warhammer 40K RPG. And in that alone it deserves a fair bit of an applause. Pity that in that regard it's more 'Pathfinder' than Dragon Age: Origins, Witcher 3, Planescape: Torment, Knights of the Old Republic, or anything you'll ever remember with fondness or as 'a classic'.Also, this isn't a living world. You simply walk from one confrontation to another, and so on and so forth. And that right there is the sum of the game.All stats, very little substance, and very little meaningful 'world' to immerse in.

_childDocuments_.review: Review after finishing the game. I want to keep it as short as possible. Overall I would rate the game a 7/10. In its core it is a good and enjoyable RPG, and for sure the best WH RPG there is(competition is not that steep). Partialy very well written Characters that make you interested in their Background. Enjoyable Core Gameplay Mechanics. And certainly a love for the lore of the WH40k Universe was felt.Things I would have loved to see improved in the game though:-More Consistent Voice Acting, Only your Companions and Like 1 Enemy got ... some voice acting. The very few Characters in the game that got Voice Acting barely get some spoken words.Maybe 1-2% of the game is voice acted to be realistic and only ever in the first Act it seemed like they even cared. Even more immersion breaking was the fact though,that sometimes in the same Dialogue one sentence was voice acted , just for the next one to be not voice acted again. In myopinion a huge Immersion killer and the game could have been an easy 8/10 with proper voiceacting for some of the maincharacters and opposing figures at very least.-Non Existing Choices: Besides Dialogues slightly altering. I did not feel that any of the choices you do or take, change the actual course of the game, it always pretty much plays out the same with most people having this "whatever" attitude around you.-Non Existing Soundtrack: 95% of the game is just some small ambient noises in the background. I really missed ... like anything. If i compare this to something like the Adeptus Mechanicus game there is a lot to be desired.-Ingame Cutscenes are pretty wonky. Maybe due to engine boundaries,but they often look more comical and make you giggle,when they should have a serious tone.-Main Story is a bit all over the place, without wanting to go into more details to prevent spoilers.Overall the game is very well written, but sometimes it gave me a feeling of short stories smashed together with only some very,what feels like, forced string between them. The thing that kinda kicked of the game and also interested me the most, in sense of why and what,how. Is allready not being talked about anymore shortly after beginning of the 2nd act....-Ingame descriptions of Skills can be confusing,especially at the beginning you feel overwhelmed.I think with some of these Points being improved on the game could be a solid 8/10 even for a brighter audience and a proper 9/10 for warhammer fans

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It has its issues. As of this moment, I would say a mostly positive rating of 75% is probably mostly appropriate (as of this posting, February 2024). If lower than I think it deserves, we are all products of our times, and our times are full of disappointments in terms of game releases, so a brutally critical fanbase is to be expected and therefore a lower score than it probably deserves. This game is no Cyberpunk at launch, I'll just put it that way.What I don't feel is appropriate is some of the content of the negative reviews. There are many bugs. Some of them are game breaking. But they are being addressed at a frankly surprising pace. Yes, they have quite a way to go, but progress is being made. My own experience involved an unequippable item I never equipped equipping itself anyway. That bug has been fixed. Was it longer than I wished? Yes. Was it done quicker than I could reasonably expect? Also yes.This game has bugs. They are being addressed pretty seriously. Underneath them is a surprisingly fantastic game that is well worth the time of any fan of crpgs and 40k especially, the dedication to lore is very surprising. Definitely worth your interest at the very least. Should you wait? Maybe. Should you just pass? Absolutely not. This game is a rough but gleaming gem in need of love and polish, and it is getting the polish.GW abandoned Dark Heresy and Rogue Trader. FFG did a number themselves with a barely edited set of rules, but it was still able to be an amazing TTRPG. Owlcat is trying to keep it alive in another medium and doing it justice. They deserve patients and time. Maybe wait if you don't want bugs. But revisit it later because its definitely worth it. We have Rogue Trader again, folks.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a labour of love to the IP of Warhammer 40k, a modern RPG with familiar gameplay elements set in a grim-dark universe 40,000 years in the future at the very edge of the canon timeline where the Galaxy has been 'split' by the Warp intruding into our universe, severing trade routes and plunging entire merchant dynasties into Chaos (literally). There's a lot of tongue in cheek over the top dialogue options due to the setting of working under the Imperium of Man and having to manage absolutely ginormous shipboard crews and planetary settlements, with your dialogue choices weighted with the fate of millions. There is ample lore and attention to detail such that even newcomers to the Warhammer 40k franchise will not get lost - you can indeed use modern day diplomacy to try and appease the 'greater good' (cough!) but the plot characters will be advising you of the consequences of being 'too nice'! The storytelling is splendid and sucks you into the universe and you can build characters the way you prefer them to be. Or you can just sit out every combat engagement and just pass orders to subordinates and mercenaries :D As a space RPG its loads better than other offerings in the market, ironically as a space exploration, settlement building game Rogue Trader is exactly what I hoped Starfield would be. Also you get cute companions each having unique and diverse voice acting that's a riot - one of them gives me strong Firefly/Serenity universe vibes. After having been chaperoned through the first chapter and all the smooth transition to ever more complex gameplay mechanics, it's time to carve out your own dynasty amongst the stars in the way you want it.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to be as clear as possible. I love this game. It is good, it is great, it is amazing. I have wanted a game like this for a VERY long time, and I was hyped to know that Owlcat was on the job!But the game needs fixes. A lot of them. A few changes as well to enhance the experience. And more accessibility with Mercenaries that you can get as non story based allies. Here is my current review, and here are my suggestions on how to improve it. I hope that this review will assist you in your choice of whether this game is worth your time.To Start, the game has a very good story telling, as a story writer myself, I found my time engrossed in everything I was seeing, not a single piece of information has gone unread so far. However, it was quite disappointing that much of the story goes without voice acting. The Actors Are Amazing! They capture these characters and their quirks SO WELL! I have played both King Maker and Wrath of the Righteous, and it goes without saying that this game has made it hard to dislike any one of the companions.The parts that are voice acted are amazing, each word feels like it has impact, each moment puts a importance on the situation by hearing the finite tones of each character. I however fully understand how difficult it is to actually voice at a full game, I am no stranger to such trifles. However, it would be a strong upgrade to have the game fully voice acted. It is the type of game that would have a legendary dialogue.Moving on from that, a more needed to be addressed issue. The Camera and the Animations. These two go hand in hand for 3 different problems.Starting off, the camera cannot be fully freely moved. You can go up and down, left and right, but you cannot change the angle of the camera which poses an issue in some cut scenes such as being on the bridge of your ship.Second, there are quite a few bugs with this one, but during some missions, your character will move off screen, or in a direction towards a location (my primary example is when you have to deal with a certain unnamed rebellion). A part where you can choose to execute the rebels, the camera does not follow you, so you just wander off and kill 3 or 4 of them and then combat starts with the rest of the group. This creates a very awkward and unprofessional event. Obviously this was not intended and has to be a bug of some kind.Thirdly, animations... Now I do like many of the animations, especially the chaos monstrosities you encounter. However there is a big issue that seems to float about, 2 of them to be specific, both are obviously bugs or oversights.First of all, when in cover and using a ranged weapon, there is a high chance your character will play a very bugged stiff as a board crab walk out from cover while your body acts like a stone holding the gun (pistol, rifle, or other) as a rifle, then shoots the target. In some cases, you won't even be looking at the target when this occurs and it is clearly a error between loading the animation and identifying they are in cover, because I can assure you, the traditional animation look far more appropriate.Another animation issue is that when you enter combat while there are enemies performing an animation of some kind, they will continue to do their jobs even during battle. However this causes them to not move for a good 20 seconds to a whole minute just toiling away until teleporting closer to your team and continuing their jobs, in or out of cover. This most certainly is not normal behaviour, if they were worshippers of Tzeench, maybe, but everyone? I doubt it.Now for the forth, well, not PROBLEM, but something that seems odd and should defiantly be updated.In conversations, your Origin affects your response options a little bit. If you are a commissar, you act like one, if you are a noble, you get choices to act like a noble. It's quite cool and feel unique and right to the atmosphere! However, with the "Morality" system, or perhaps better known as the "Alignment" system, you can choose to be for the Emperor, for the People, or for Chaos. Why does this matter? Because if you sit in your chair on the ship, and someone speaks up about how you are just fresh blood and that you might lead them to their deaths, that it is hopeless, you have a few options. Let him be, he has had a stressed day surviving the horror of 40K universe, which gives you a + to your Humanity, becoming apart of the Iconoclast Alignment. This means that you value human life. Another option, is that you can have your men execute him for his outburst, which gives you a + to your authority, making you more Dogmatic, for the Emperor and all that.BUT as a Commissar, you have a 3rd option, to execute him yourself, as a Commissar would. However, this does not give you any bonuses at all. If you tell other people to execute him, you get +2 Dogmatic, but if you do it yourself, you get +0 Dogmatic... and yet both those options fall under a Dogmatic Alignment...My opinion is to add Alignment bonuses to each potential Origin Response. It would make more sense, it would encourage being true to your nature, while still giving an alternative option. I mean, I want to be a Commissar, but not if it means I don't get to be true to the God Emperor... and yet... it doesn't make sense as to why it wouldn't considering the all.Lastly, Mercenaries. Or to specify, Mercenary Origins. Many of the Companions have unique Origins, one being the Space Wolf, and another being a Tech Priest. I personally don't like Space Wolves, I'd rather have a Dark Angel, Black Templar, or a Blood Angel. Black Rage, Unyielding Plasma Weapon Tactics, Bannerman Shield wielding Blade Bearer, and all that jazz.Now I know that they are "Mercenaries", but a easy solution could be to have it where once you unlock the companion, you can unlock their origins. This would make a great addition for the Space Marine and Tech Priest. Like how you can choose "Home World Variants" for the Forge World. This would be a good way to make a Engineer Tech Priest versus the Pasqal one or something else, and instead of a Space Wolf, you could get a different Space Marine. This would only change their origin ability to suit those changes, even different kinds of Sisters of Battle would be cool to see. It would add a interesting aspect to Mercenaries and give you more to look forward to when actually unlocking them. This would help people who might not like certain companions, make a version of that companion they actually like without missing out on certain content.Warhammer has so many options, that it would be cool to see those differences.With that said however, this game is really still in the making. It was released perhaps a bit too early, and patches and QOL changes need to happen.Aside from that, I would recommend this game.EDIT: I have noticed a new issue... when you do cutscene involving your main character, anything that involves your Main Character walking to a new location, your other allies do not go with you. This means that if your party is on one end of the hall way or around a corner and your main character walks off during the cut scene, your main character is abandoned and alone wherever he ends up for a turn or three. This returns to the previous camera issue where it doesn't follow you during these scenes. It also makes it so that you have to actively position your party near you whenever you end up opening a door with enemies behind it or something of the sort.It should get fixed as it, one, looks super unpolished and weird that your character would just walk off to do that while no one would follow, and two, the way you can fix it is by adopting Divinity Original Sin 2's method, where if allies are outside a certain range, they aren't in combat and can still move around to reposition. Why this wasn't thought of before, I don't know, but it certainly would improve the weird and senseless party members being left behind.

_childDocuments_.review: ***Second playthrough Update: Did a heretic run which is REALLY more half-baked than the other routes. Like the other routes there is still a lot of background text chaos things you can do but active on-screen corruption with companions is really only reserved for one of them (three other just become a tiny bit more aggressive to match your jerk energy, not corrupted) and it's the most painfully obvious one. Additionally, you still can't change companions official alignment which is annoying. Also, while I don't mind a couple of loyalist companions getting cold feet, but their leaving could use more interaction (maybe even fighting them when they leave you). The Heretic route also a lot more bugs than others, usually in the form of dialog that randomly drops mid-conversation and stops you from completing the quest. Finally, it became more apparent this round how bad the pacing is in the last two acts cus storylines (with companions or antagonists) just suddenly end in Act 4/5, not that they need new complicated quests but just a couple more conversations would go a long way.  So, since the baseline game is still fun, I'm barley keeping my thumbs up here, but Owlcat *really* need to add more story bits and fix bugged questlines in Act 4 & 5.****** First playthrough Update: finally finished the game and, imo, most of everything below still applies here except a few things: the story, variety, and game balance does take a hit when you reach Act 4. The ending parts, while not bad per-se, feels like they didn't have enough time to fully develop the stuff they wanted. However, I still had fun overall and If Owlcat adds more meat to the final sections then this would be a great game ***It's a incredibly fun RPG where you can live a lot of 40k roleplaying, but does have some limitations. Which, if you're thinking that this game will have the same scale as BG3, you will be disappointed (tho tbf, BG3 a level of budget and scale most can't/shouldn't reach)The main highlight is the story and dialog, which a lot varied paths (and not just basic good and evil choices) and fun comments you can make. Want to play "good" imperial but still want to be the pompous jerk imaginable, you can do that. Also the companions are really well written, their limited voiced dialog is really well acted, and has stories that can engross you into the grimdark worldThe graphics and cutscenes are not groundbreaking (also cutscenes do have a warcraft 3 quality, which may or maynot be charming to you) but the art direction is amazing to look at, with rich and very varied settings you can explore.Combat if fun, but it does have a big learning curve (especially if you're not too familiar with TTRPG's that this is based off of), tho the turn based space combat is a blast.Now this game is *not* bug free but we already seen Owlcat squashing quite a few with a very fast update and I haven't yet encountered any major game breaking bugs (tho i did have a close call one time)

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best 40K game.I used to be a console player/handheld gamer, so most of my life was spent playing turn-based RPG's (Devil Survivor and other SMT games primarily). Since moving to PC in 2019, i didn't play many RPG's for a very long time. i was VERY excited to try Baldur's Gate 3 and had played divinity 2 a bit before then, and came to find after 30 hours or so from each that they're some kind of feminist comedy game for laughs? i dont really understand the appeal of those games. Moreover, i find it difficult to roleplay or get immersed in "generic fantasy setting", and this game made me realize how I wish ALL RPG's were licensed games based on huge serious properties that you're familiar with and can learn more about. i do not know or care about a single thing happening in divinity or baldur's gate, and 99% of the characters are jokes and don't care either. I hope owlcat one day makes a Star Trek TNG RPG or something using this engine, it's perfect for it and it'd blow baldur's gate out of the water, too, because of the weight of the setting alone.I cannot find the credits for the writers, but i am wagering that it has an all-male writing team, PLUS Games Workshop oversight(who are rebranding 40K into a very much serious direction lately), making for a game where you actually care about what's going on because there isnt a joke every 20 seconds, and no party members making feminist Marvel quips every time you interact with someone. I don't even know anybody who likes comedy and wants comic relief. I don't know who the target audience is. I think they might do that stuff so much in video games because then twitch streamers can scream and overreact when the cat makes a funny feminist poop joke!!! in baldur's gate 3, and then scream again when your all-gay party members quip about it.There is nothing like that in rogue trader. The canon is respected the religions are respected and everything is handled very professionally. This kind of serious writing is nearly nonexistent nowadays, and I'm so, so happy with the way Games Workshop is managing their IP now. If you liked the writing in New Vegas then this game is for you. Everyone including and especially the antagonists have reasonable points of view and explain their positions eloquently.I think Rogue Trader's gameplay loop is bordering on plagiarism of divinity 2, in all of the best ways. Which is why I keep mentioning those games. Rogue Trader is what i wanted those games to be (the stupid puddles AoE spam is not present here however. you and enemies dont spend every turn thinking about puddles. i got bored of that in div2/bg3 after the 3rd or 4th fight).  Content in rogue trader is dripfed and you'll have an entirely new game mechanic to try out every 10 hours or so, which is largely whats keeping me so hooked. i love the space ship and the space battles and have never seen turn-based combat like it before. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up my economy because i was so excited to try every weapon class i recruited 10 mercenaries.I'm playing on Normal difficulty which feels very fair and balanced to me. I don't think I'd enjoy playing on anything harder because of how this genre abuses hit-chance stuff for artificial difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: It's slightly annoying how the setting's fallen victim to its own popularity and I wish I could experience this game without knowing a thing about the setting.I was quite excited about this one. Owlcat Games is one of the few remaining 'we will try to put as many contents as possible in our games' developers and I like them. I also used to play Warhammer 40k tabletop. So really, this is the ideal combination. The world of Warhammer 40k is a world where saving one might actually doom billions all the while countless billions are being doomed by the second for no reason but the paranoia born as much out of human cruelty as the harsh reality. It's a good dynamic and right here you can see the potential for a choice-centred game, right? Essentially, the over-the-top grimdark setting solves the traditional RPG problem of 'if you are a Paragon character then the narratively right choice can be way too obvious' itself. Pen and paper Warhammer RPG got a cult following til this day for a reason.This game is mostly just that, pen and paper Warhammer 40k RPG on a computer. It's quite good. It's just that it would be so much better if I did not see most of the twists/consequences coming ten miles way...Now I am not your well-read Warhammer lorebeard. I kept up with the campaign books and novels until around 2010s, then I just moved on. I don't know what happened then with the lore. But I do have your basic start pack and I saw just about everything coming. It's slightly annoying. After all the efforts put into the story, the plot, the level design, scores, atmosphere and everything by the developers, you are just left with a sudden realisation that 'oh, I know where this is going' or 'I wish I am playing a certain Estonian game set in a world I know nothing about.'And the developers did put lots of efforts in. You have all the good old 'your choices matter' designs here and I'm all in for it: You rarely have enough clues to make a well-informed choice, in the beginning the game can feel like Mass Effect 1 or Fallout 1 in Junktown; time matters so you are permanently on a Telltale/Persona timer; you have a colourful collection of factions with moral convictions like New Vegas or Disco Elysium; your choices have consequences in gameplay and can be very punishing, closer to Frostpunk than Bioshock or Witcher contracts; and your choices can also be futile so there's also a conversation between Life is Strange and Planescape Torment. It's good. Quite good.I just wish I could experience it like something new and unique.

_childDocuments_.review: You can have an enjoyable experience roleplaying in this game. You can even make a ogryn type character work if you at least try to read some of the ability tooltips. You will have to interact with fanatics, xeno (filth) and other unsavory types. The game gives you freedom to chose your own path. The game revolves around you being a 40K character so expect swarms of mindless low HP minions with the occasional mini boss. It was completely fine until the later chapters where you either are in a horrible position in every fight or the battle is unbalanced to the point that your party will be wiped if you do not meta game.The space combat in my opinion is not all that interesting but not horrible. At some point it becomes easy. The main issue with it is that the difficulty of the space battles depends on how many enemies there are. There are next to no tactics involved. There are abilities that are seemingly always on cooldown, and if the Emperor blesses you with access to one of them, the encounter is all but over. It would be nice if something was added to the battles such as positioning, charging attacks etc. to make them more engaging. The reputation system is alright. It would have been nice if at the end of the game you had more loot to trade and get higher levels but I don't see that changing any time soon. I looked in every crate and safe and yet I did not have enough loot for the truly awesome stuff they have at the end.Exploring the Koronus expanse was fun but by the end of act 2 you have seen 95% of places you can visit in the game. They have about 60% of the map empty for future expansions. Unless you visit a system on your own you cant get the extractors back and good luck remembering where you littered. Some resources have value, other only have a perceived value. I though that by having a lot of something would entitle me to some benefit but the game revolves around 2 concepts: 1. Have x number of A resource to get benefits2. Trade x number of resource A for y number of resource BYou don't need to micromanage anything. At the end of my exploration anything remotely exotic was mined. Profit factor ties closely to the things you can buy from the factions. Unless you focus on one faction (except the navy) completely your profit factor is irrelevant. Your protectorate does not really give a lot of room to role play. Same goes for the contracts the game gives you. All planets eventually become hellholes. It would have been nice if there were projects that were tied more closely to you reputation but at the end of the day you are only looking at what a project or event will give your party and ship. Resources are irrelevant, and to my knowledge so are the colonies stats. They are nice but not necessary. The game is nice and fun until act 3. At that point I believe that the fun of the game takes a back seat for the narrative. Until that part of the game is changed (if ever) enjoy the guides and try to survive the horrible game decisions that were made. From act 3 onwards expect bugs (some game braking), unbalanced encounters, having your hand forced and performance issues.I have encountered dialog issues, areas where once you enter you are stuck permanently, mechanics that should lower some resource actually increases it, etc. There is no telling what bug you might encounter during your playthrough. The game gives you a tip to save if you are unsure about something. You might as well follow the advice as it is your only life line if you encounter something game braking. The game is plain and simply unfinished. I gave it a benefit of a doubt and expected issues when I bought it but I did not expect to be unable to finish the game due to the bugs. I regret buying this game on release as the experience with its unfinished elements has tainted my opinion of it. If not for the horrible state of the game I would have sung its praises but the scrap code has done its damage.As the toaster hoarders in red would say: An opportunity wasted is a sin preserved.

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game with a lot of important caveats:Even after waiting for it to be patched I still had abysmal loading times, which are very frequent.Crash to desktop was very common, like at least once an hour of play.Chapter 2 was fun, Chapter 3 was some of the worst game play I have experienced in a while.  It was so not fun I don't know how to explain it other than it was a terrible slog with lots of trial and error.The rest of the game was very much busy work and didn't feel great.The ending was full of contradictions and barely made any sense.With all that said, for immersing in the world of WH40k this was the best game to date, but only for that.  There are better crafted, better games that do a better job and don't crash every 20 minutes or so because you accessed something and it freezes and chokes out.If you can stomach all of that, it is passable as a game minus chapter 3 and chapter 2 was actually fun.  If you love the universe you'll enjoy immersing yourself in the game.  But again, with all the crap that goes with it that really takes away from the experience.There's no doubting the game was just rushed/unfinished and it needed a lot more to bake properly. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of owlcat games, despite trying to love all of them. Judged by this metric this is the best of the bunch (at least I did finish it), but there's still too much that annoyed me to recommend it.While art direction, as well as music and the character concepts are very good, the game itself gets worse every chapter. The cutscenes were a big disappointment. Most of them have the models just standing around while text boxes appear over their heads. It was far from engaging.Annoyances like the random warp encounters are only made worse by a combat system that rolled over and died in the middle of the game (as I was able to finish most encounters in a single turn without min-maxing).Leveling becomes as annoying as the random encounters causing you to level. Reason being the archetypes offering to many option with +x% and not enough new (character specific) abilities. It feels like the game is losely based on Dark Heresy/Rogue Trader. While those games also have a lot of small ability increases, the classes at least offer more variety.Colony managment sounds like a good idea on paper. In practice this means traveling back and forth for miniscule decisions, only two of which actually justify you having to be there in person.With that much sand in the gears and a story that felt like it could have ended much sooner, I was happy to finally be done with it.

I've got 10+ hours here and it just feels like what I'm picking with my character levels just isn't significant or exciting. I think part of that is from how much detail is involved with all the abilities. When I'm looking over a selection of 30+ perks, I can't be bothered to read over every description for every level of every character. What's more is there is a lot of like... "Warp Blast does 2x(BS+WP+1/2FP)% damage - enemy armour+wp"???? Dude, is that like 9 damage? Or like 14? Okay, fine I'll do some quick math here.....Ahhh hah! It's 13 damage... Right so that's less then a sniper rifle so I won't be using my 1 attack per turn on warp blast, okay so what about this next ability?.... Times 30 abilities or perks to look over, and that's every level-up, on every character.I think more then half of all the enemies I've run into die in 1 or 2 shots anyway, so I feel like a lot of this level of detail is lost on me. _childDocuments_.review: This is the second revision of my review. I have completed the game and I tentatively recommend this game as of January 24. You might want to get it on sale though and check the status of bugfixes at this point because there are a lot of bugs.Ultimately, Rogue Trader is a compelling and immersive crpg that has been let down by being released before it was finished.First off, Owlcat have really done a great job of capturing the essence of the setting. It feels lived in and makes Warhammer 40K seem like more than Space Marines and the adventures thereof. The atmosphere, the characters, the music and the abundance of lore, all come together to weave and intricate tapestry that is amazing to explore.The first half of the game is pretty tight, good pacing, a wide array of side content and choice based quests and narrative with good reactivity. The game really shines here and is really enjoyable to play. But it is most definitely front loaded. This level of polish (by Owlcat Standards atleast) does not persist throughout the game. Not all is well, mind you. There are features in the game that don't function as intended or minor bugs but it goes unnoticed in the early game as the important stuff works.Then you get to Act 3 and beyond. Unfortunately, it is here the game is marred by a multitude of broken mechanics and systems. Entire  side quests don't trigger or completing this side quest or that, doesn't register that it has completed. Companion quests are quite buggy, in-game events don't fire properly. Character feats don't work or work contrary to descriptions. Even the ending slides are a bit of a mess, not reflecting accurately the choices you make in your playthrough and some people don't even get most of the slides at all. There are reports of game stopping bugs in the 4th Act, though I was fortunate enough not to experience those myself. They do exist.Add to this that Act 3 really interrupts the flow and pacing established in the first two acts. You get whisked away, a literal prisoner of circumstance that is unavoidable for plot reasons. There is really only one path through this act, you can decide who comes out the other side as your allies and who comes out dead, but it doesn't really feel reactive or impactful the way choices do in the previous acts. This is compounded further in the fourth and then final fifth act, where there is a distinct drop in content and the quality of that which is there. The 4th Act has us return the the Koronus Expanse but there isn't much left there to do. Especially if you were diligent in developing colonies and pursuing side content in the early game. Act 4 feels a little barren in comparison. The showdown with the primary villians from the prologue and Act 1 feels anticlimactic and depending on the choices you make, very lacking in fleshed out reactivity. There are unexpected companions you can pick up here, but they wind up having next to no dialogue or real engagement with the player or the narrative. It feels unfinished and the potential unrealised. Which is a real pity.The final act is remarkably brief and enemy encounters become incredibly spongey too, with massive health pools that are a pain to whittle down. The brisk and fast paced combat of the early game can become bogged down and mired in the usual Turn Based slog.There is so much to enjoy in this game and yet it is held back by a sense that the game just wasn't finished and was rushed out the door too soon. The patches to fix bugs just haven't been coming fast enough and I have no doubt it damages Owlcats and Rogue Traders reputations no end.If you love Warhammer 40K, if you love CRPG's and have to play them all, if you are a dogged fan or Owlcat, by all means get this game.If however you are more discerning, do some research. Check the status of bugs and bug fixing at time of purchase and check the discord and Steam forums for opinions. Maybe buy it on a sale. As of the time of this review, be sure you really want this game. I've enjoyed it and I am a huge fan of Owlcats previous game Wrath of the Righteous, but even I found this hard to get through because the sheer volume of bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing this game (and not recommending it) is somewhat frustrating for me. I've always loved the setting and the lore, and Owlcat did an excellent job with that. I don't think it's a BAD game, but there's a lot of things that someone could give it a bad review for and I wouldn't blame them. I want to love this game so badly but man, I keep hitting things that make me want to go play something else.The dead horse of "so many bugs" has already been beaten to death here. Will Owlcat fix them? Probably. There was even a tiny update on Christmas morning (it may have been pushed out the day before) that fixed all of my visual tiles/layers/icons that were missing. But how long will bug-quashing take? I could see people waiting for a future sale and only buying it then, well after the bugs are fixed.But what has made me want to quit multiple times are only what I might call 'potholes'. They're things that you hit (or see other people hit) and you end up sitting there wondering what is even going on. One of the first ones was the notorious Derelict Hulk. I think it was well made and overall was a fun encounter, but running into that very early on was an eye opener. Was it a conscious choice? Was it just an early game party and build check, maybe? Or was it just overtuned for when people tend to run into it? I left and came back much later, which seems to be what a lot of other people did. But I had no idea until I Googled a number of discussions about it, and saw I wasn't alone.The mechanics behind Navigator points...I thought I understood what was going on under the proverbial hood...up until I hit the mission where I had to find a path to a system without a pre-existing path, and I had no navigator points left (you need 3). Once again I was off to Google, and found myself combing through various threads and discussions to try understanding what was going on. Did anyone else happen to notice *THE LITERAL FIRST TIME* they moused over a system, and seeing a message explaining how to create paths and such? Because I certainly don't remember seeing anything, but a number of people online insist that it is there but it only shows up ONCE. So in the end I learned about some random orange/red encounters giving out navigator points, reloaded a previous save where I still had a couple of points left, then warped back and forth until I got such an event (this took a while) and was able to reach that system. But none of this was obvious from within the game...it took some searching online to find a solution. The most annoying for me was Act 3 and trading a stimm (?) for a pistol I did not need (it's a completely blind dialogue exchange where you don't know what you will even get anyways, or that you will need the original item later) and then playing around in that general area for hours before wondering why I couldn't manage to rescue a specific character. If you don't have VERY GOOD specific stats you can fail 2 dialogue checks (I was at a 0% chance to pass either of them, with Argenta who was also zero help), leaving me my only option...to use the potion/stimm that I had traded away hours earlier, and hadn't found more of...so that option was grayed out. So off I go to Google YET AGAIN, and sure enough...you can lose certain characters permanently in that part of the game. And of course I didn't save between all of the cutscenes/dialogue and trading that stimm away, sooo...I had to reload all the way back to before that storyline even picked up. Is there another solution? Maybe? But I didn't find anything and I 100% didn't want to just up and lose a character PERMANENTLY...so /golflap to Owlcat for that specific design choice.I ended up talking to a few friends who by this point have all quit playing, and there seemed to be a somewhat common thread in the game for everyone: they all hit certain things that either weren't well explained, they were forced to reload and had to go back more than 30m, or were hit in the face with something that came completely out of the blue, and they all literally just exited out and went off to play other games instead. And FWIW, almost all of them have beaten BG3 (at least once) as well as having played all of the Pathfinder stuff. Now add in all of the bugs, especially in the later acts, to ship combat that's really just a minigame (that not everyone likes, though I kind of do) along with a skill system that is just a rats-nest of junk that encourages premade cookie cutter builds for certain characters...and I don't know if I can honestly recommend it, even if I will likely go back repeatedly and stubbornly keep playing. I'll change my review to 'recommend' at a later date if Owlcat goes back and fixes a lot of stuff, but at this point in time I'd tell people to just hold off until it's either on sale (next Christmas, maybe?), or Owlcat fixes a lot of the issues people are currently having.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review, I am technically 50h since I played the technical beta for an extended period of time. However, despite the lengthy sessions of fun i had with the game I can´t recommend it in its current state. I am hardlocked in chapter 2 with 3 different bugs preventing me from progressing the game. There is nothing left for me to do since all 3 mainquests goals are affected. One does not progress despite killing the npc the game told me to kill, one does not spawn the necessary npc for me to talk to progress the story and one is locked behind space combat, which is near impossible for me to beat due to the ship post UI bugging out preventing me from accessing this feature. I am unable to use ship skills, which makes ship combat tedious, unfun and very hard. Now the game has lots of other softlocks and hardlocks affecting not only me but also other players, which leads me to believe there is a serious problem with how flags for quests work or in this case do not work. But wait, that’s not all. Animations are straight up missing for some abilities, like the molten beam ability for psykers, some items are missing effects and stats, menu and UI elements keep bugging out so you have to reload the game and lose progress to be able to access those features again. I am sure they will fix those issues in time with patches but currently I am unable to draw a positive conclusion about the game. Rogue trader is a great game with lots of lore, quests, secretes and features to explore. But in its current state I can´t recommend it.I am just sad now. Please fix this game so we can enjoy it in its fullest. This review will be updated when the issues are resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, what an amazing experience was this game, it is an absolutely most if you love the WH universe, it is such an immersive experience that you will for surely enjoy, the story, the enemies, the weapons everything is just... perfect.Building your character can be a little bit confusing for the first levels as the system allows you to take a LOT of paths, it may take you a couple of levels to understand what does what and if it's truly what you need, you can always make a respec. which is greatly appreciated, and as with any RPG games make sure to diversify your party. All the characters are just awesome and their voicing is perfect, the voice of Ulfar it's just amazing and really makes you fee you are hearing an space marine, the only "bad side" is that not all the dialogues are spoken and in some cases i could have made a better impact on certain scenes. The combat mechanics just hit the spot, and very entertaining, each fight has it's own challenge and with the exception of the raids due to warp travel they all feel different, making you think on how you till face certain challenges and the space battles are extremely fun, such a shame there are so limited encounters but it seems in the next DLC there will be more on them,Talking about combat it was nice to fight against almost every mayor faction of WH, but is such a shame they missed ork, which I hope they add on a next DLC. As every game it is not 100% perfect and the main issues I had were with bugs, some of them weren't that game breaking, however others were really painful making you reload a lot, (and remember F5 does a quick save, always press that button after a fight) , the team is working actively on patching the bugs which is nice.To summarize Rogue trader is an amazing game, made with love and dedication which can be seen in every small detail that the team did, I don't have any doubt that it will soon became a reference for Warhammer gaming just like Spacemarine did a while ago, definitely a must have if you love RPG's.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader

_childDocuments_.review: While it has more than it's share of bugs as of 12/23, this is one of the first CRPGs to hold my attention to the end that I have played in over 20 years. I've started and abandoned many of the most popular titles of this genre, so I have to give kudos to the one that kept me coming back.I am a huge fan of the setting and this game does a great job of letting you see it from a different perspective of the common space marine variety.The combat can be wonky, with plenty of abilities and powers that seem redundant but still enjoyable. Especially when it involves a Sister of Battle melting the opposition with a power axe in one hand and a flamer in the other.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the fence with this one, it's a good game but it has a lot of issues. I love the attention to detail, everything from the music, setting, atmosphere, dialogue, lore is just a faithful adaptation...Except for the Edar/Dark Eldar romance options i felt that was a little out of place, but hey i'm not knocking it. Can't romance the sister of battle either....which is pretty weird all things considered.The plot is fantastic until you get to Act 3. Things just become more and more broken as you progress, cut-scenes don't function, quests break, progression is blocked...The plot itself becomes inconsistent with severe pacing issues during and after act 3. Combat is down to preference, some people will like it, others wont. For me personally i'm split down the middle, on one hand it's fun and engaging and on the other it becomes a slog with inconsistent difficulty spikes. So, i'm on the fence and once again annoyed that steam doesn't have a mixed review option. I'll leave it as recommended because this isn't a bad game, it's a faithful adaptation for the most part and there's lots of genuine enjoyment to be had here...OwlCat really need to start QA testing and actually learning from previous mistakes though because the gamebreaking bugs are inexcusable at this point.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. Not great, but pretty good. Combat is fun, the first chapters are pretty enjoyable, good characters and it's fun to be "the main character". Everything revolves around the rogue trader, and that's real fun.BUT...The last chapters seemed... Rushed. You spend so many time on a drukari ship and after that it just felt... Empty. I was more motivated by finishing the game just so I could play something else. The combat, if you don't change the default difficulty, becomes trivial, most battles just requiring 2 or 3 turns max, because the navigator is so OP the enemies are just obliterated.With all that said, it's totally worth the time. It's not a perfect game, but I look forward for the DLC's.

_childDocuments_.review: On going review: will update as I goI'd like to start with saying i'm not a massive Warhammer super fan, i know the basics: divine emperor, giant supersoldiers in tank armour, demonic gods and some different races that are mostly futuristic versions of fantasy races (space elves, Space orks etc). what I am a fan of is turn based tactical games which Warhammer happens to have a few under their belt, this is their most recent as far as I'm aware. so far I'm only just past the first Chapter which mostly acts as a tutorial/introduction of some of your crew and I must say I'm very invested: the gameplay is fantastic, the world expansive and the characters unique. Fair warning you're going to have alot thrown at you if you're not as familiar to the lore of 40k, i knew a bit and in my 12+ hours have become much more familiar, this is helped along by text in bold being able to be moused over to give background context so if you don't know what The Golden Throne is don't worry a quick highlight will give you some context, which is a great addition for a lore heavy universe that spans decades. I got it half price and would say if you're in the market for a solid turn based tactical you could do much much worse even if you're paying the standard price. Fair warning you'll be doing alot of reading because theres a good chunk of information you're getting pretty much from the start so if you're more a skip the text and amble through you'll likely struggle here (especially with the first chapters final boss, i'll not spoil but it will take everything you've learnt leading up to the fight if you intend to survive the encounter). i will leave it there for now and updated as I progress.The Emperor Protects!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well-done 40K game that really captures the essence of playing a Rogue Trader.  The story is very well-written with plenty of opportunities for character development and companion interaction.  Most NPC interactions offer several choices, while every decision has consequences.  The Endeavor system from the books has been implemented in a novel way.  Likewise the colony development and exploration mechanics.  If you enjoy the Rogue Trader tabletop game, this is the CRPG for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I have a limited knowledge of the warhammer universe, I am not going to comment on the specific settings / lore. However as a fan of turn based RPG, I am totally recommending this game, especially for those who enjoyed Wrath of the Righteous. The replayability is quite high, based on all the choices / consequences and builds possibilities.If you, like me, disliked the amount of loading screens and clunkiness of crusade management in Wrath of the Righteous, I can say it is much better in Rogue Trader. While you can still have some loading and interruptions while warping and discovering planets, a lot of management can be done in the map with menu screens that dont require loading.As with the previous owlcat games, initial release contains some bugs but in my 33 hours of play so far, I have not encountered any game breaking bugs and not a single crash. It is mostly pathing and dialogues issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge 40K fan and have thousands of points worth of models in the tabletop. I've read most of the horus heresy series and many 40K books. This is a great 40K game. It is a planet where I cannot leave due to some warp magic (fine).Yet the bug does not allow me to speak to the quest giver for the main quest to progress. I am literally stuck and all my quicksaves/autosaves are on this planet. (google Hunting Grounds quest if you're curious, multiple posters have the same issue)Let's say load an earlier save? Well, my earlier save is 10 hours past, PLUS there is a chance I get to the same planet and suffer the same issue. (This is a MAIN QUEST. The worst bugs I've had in cyberpunk is cars exploding randomly and the worst bug I've had in BG3 is people catching me as a criminal from far away when looting a body (big whoop).BUGS THAT BRICK YOUR SAVE AND RUIN YOUR PLAYTHROUGH ARE NOT EXCUSABLE!Not to mention the forced ship combat which can drag endlessly and weird reputation system (The high level items require upwards of 80,000 reputation when I'm in Act 4 and only have about 30-40K. _childDocuments_.review: Tentative recommend. There isnt a game out there that understands 40k as a setting like this one. The writing, as is to be expected from Owlcat, is superb. Also to be expected from Owlcat, the game is loaded with content and systems. There's colony management, there's space combat, there's warp navigation, there's probably more stuff I haven't found in my 20 hours of playtime. Unfortunately, as is to be expected from Owlcat, the tooltips are atrocious. Just user unfriendly. Yes I can do the math of "this ability does 3x (Willpower + Ballistic skill bonus)" but could you maybe show me in the tooltip what my willpower and ballistic skill bonus is so I dont have to close the ability tool tip and open the character sheet? Its especially annoying on a level up, where you have to close the entire level up screen to see your character sheet. Some tooltips are wrong, an ability said it stacked 6 times in the description, the actual UI said it stacked 3 times. And sometimes abilities are not shown on a tooltip or sheet at all. I know that pink horrors split into blue horrors on death because I played 40k back in the day, the game does not tell you, it just happens. I know that when a plasma weapon overheats it damages you, the game does not tell you this, it actually just says it cant be used again on this turn, nothing about it damaging the user or how much damage it causes. Why didn't my attack damage that enemy this turn? They have zero armor, it was a hit, even the dice roll log doesnt show me why. Just minor frustrations every single combat encounter and they simply dont need to be as frustrating as they are. I play the game for the characters, the writing, the worldbuilding and the story. I tolerate the combat.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr still too buggy, leave it a few months. context: I'm a 40+ with a  demanding job, I only get a few hours to spend on games a week (although I was sick for ages which helped here...!?)I was part of the beta and really enjoyed the first two acts which were (mostly) in there other than some new sidelines. The additional acts and sidelines which weren't in the beta have a lot of bugs which can make for a very frustrating experience. There are, I think, too many complex battle systems which without spending 100+ hours (like I did) they feel overwhelming when upgrading. I became frustrated by the final battle in Act 3 where most folks either need an overly powerful character (which I was avoiding building as it makes most of the game too easy) or lowering the difficulty to the bottom. Given all the bad reviews of Act 4 that's where I left this game. I probably won't return to it as in 6 months I won't recall all the character systems and don't have the time to spend to re-learn complex systems unless I spend unholy amounts of time in a game.Feels like a shame, could have been an amazing game, was just ok and I'm disappointed I won't get to see the story play out.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed this experience and give it a solid 4/5 stars. It stands apart from so many other similar games in that you are uniquely positioned in society. I really got a kick out of the experience, and I like the way the game really brought home the results of so many of your decisions in the epilogue. The Chapters each had their own arch, and the story driven battles remained fun, characters ramped up in power dramatically over the course of the game. You feel a sense of progress for most levels, well into exemplar before you stop feeling like it matters as much, which is excellent.IF I were to label one criticism - the game really drags in chapter 4. Not because of the narrative, but because the random encounters have all been seen before at this point, and it just turns nto a grind. I found myself thinking "Oh, this fight, in this same map, with these same monsters, in the same positions again". It was particularly egregious if you were heading from a colony on one side of the expanse to the other and encountering the same fight twice getting from A to B. These same fights were exciting in Act 2. Being a bit stingy with your navigator points could prevent some of that grind, as you could then create SAFE paths from colony to colony, but without knowing that ahead its easy to over spend before you really need them. That one blemish, while glaring, is the only major negative i have against it, and every rpg has some of that, so I think this game is worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, want to say that I LOVE this game. It is well-crafted story wise and there are a lot of cool decisions that you can choose that is very similar in vein to the Pathfinder series. The characters are great, the story is great, the voice acting is AMAZING, but the biggest downfall for this game is its absolutely massive amount of bugs. Weird animations, both in combat and in other scenes, exits to different areas sometimes not popping up, the inability to see if you have an extractium on a planet or not, and enemies will freeze in combat sometimes causing their turn to take forever to resolve. There is also an issue with your allies getting frozen as well when using a ranged attack from cover that takes even longer for the game to eventually catch up but sometimes the attack doesnt even damage the enemy, it just acts like you attacked and you spent the AP to use the ability to no effect even if it was a guaranteed hit. I do not recommend this game in the current state it is in due to the fact that I made it all the way to Act 4 and after a certain point in Quetza Temer, there was no exit from the jungle area after a particular fight. I had encountered the bug before in a different area and reloading the save fixed that one, but alas, this time was fruitless and no matter how many times I reloaded the save, the button to leave the area would not pop up and if there is supposed to be a cutscene, it did not activate like it was supposed to. I have submitted more bug reports for this game than any other game that I have played, and thus I implore you, avid reader/buyer, to wait until they fix this game before you buy. If you can truck through a lot of the things I mentioned above, on top of a few other bugs that are small and I can't think about right now, then by all means, this IS a good game with a lot of potential, but it is insulting that it was released in the condition it was in, they should have let it bake for another month or three to fix a lot of the glaring issues.EDIT: A lot of the problems have been fixed, and I concede my earlier points. The game should have released in this state beforehand, but it is a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: After a bit of a rough launch, this game has quickly turned into my 3rd favourite warhammer 40k game. I do not do table top, but im into the lore and books. The developers really tried to en-capture the environment of 40k and bring it to life. I actually have a better visual interpretation when reading the books now. The characters in the story are exactly how they should be, the inquisitor is a fanatic, the sister sororitas is a religious fanatic, albeit the eldar could have endured some better writing... so the game is not without its flaws. The RPG elements are nailed perfectly, and resembles a turn based combat style that is well executed. The story was engaging, and I enjoyed the multitude of choices of dialogue options that can re-direct the story somewhat. Playing the first time I went in the middle of heretical and iconoclast, and realised too late in the game that i should have only chosen one. The game is created so you have to stick to the direction you have chosen, otherwise if you don't go full heretical, or full iconoclast, there will be certain items and characters you cannot use. This also limits your choices in a way, as you cant use the space marine character to its full extent if you have chosen the heretical route. I wish they stated this in the introduction so i knew. Even with the choices, i feel the replay value of this game is limited, I will probably play it 2 more times just to see how powerful the other choices are. If you are a warhammer fan, you will like this game no matter what, honestly its a must play for us fans. However, for the scope of the game, i do not think it should be a full 65$. Half that price i think would more reasonable, and if youre not a warhammer fan, buy baulders gate instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a better CRPG that BG3.(Ive played tabletop 40k for over a decade, although I dont know too much about rogue traders themselves) Its an Owlcat game at release but its pretty stable so far (playing on steam deck), some hiccups but its very playable. I actually like having like 50 levels to work with, feels like an interesting mix of a D&D style 20 levels and a jrpg 100 level system. Certainly better paced than bg3s 12, i dont feel underleveled playing the game on normal. Character customization feels good, even though I dont understand how to build characters well yet. I vaguely know the TT its based on but i didn't play the Rogue Trader one itself. Theres less choice paralysis than their pathfinder games and the recommended level up path seemed rather effective. So far the story and writting its pretty good, on par with early WotR, not quite Pillars or Tyranny levels but interesting. I legitimately did not expect a plot point that happens early on,  and im interested to see how this turns out.Combat is good, plays abit more like xcom than the pathfinder games but I think it works. Id like a way of speeding up animations but its not too bad so far, partway through act 1. They have a cool hologram system so you can see LOS and such after your move. Every game needs a system like this, if a knock off gangster xcom could 10 years ago everyone should have it. It seems a bit finnecky but im going to play around with it more that might be user error, i skipped the popup for it and havent bothered to look it up yet.It feels extremely 40k. The way environments (so far) all look like gothic cathedrals, using some cinematic camera shots to show off the grandiose locations is effective, especially in a crpg. The way characters talk drips with atmosphere, especially when characters talk differently from each other to constrast their points of view. So far my biggest annoyance is that the toggle interactables keeps turning off, happens in WOTR too tho. The UI is slightly clunky on steam deck, more than Wotr but less than kingmaker or bg3. I havent had any real bugs so far, aside from a few minor graphical things, if those get worse as the game progresses I will update.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like something from an alternate reality where the RPG's of yore evolved correctly, independent of boardrooms. It's admittedly a bit slow to get started. But once it gets going, and you start to get the hang of it, it's so big and good! There's a lot of reading involved - it's like a grimdark novel with lots of worldbuilding. Characters use multi-syllabic words. Situations are complex. Not everyone is nice. You don't have to be nice. If you're literate and an adult you'll be pleased to find that, unlike some modern RPG's-gone-bad, it's not made for 13-year-olds by devs with the minds of 13-year-olds. Great RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I 100% recommend this game.However, I do have some complaints.    -The foremost is that  can only be romanced by a female mc. Most characters can preform MANY actions in a turn. *This can become combersome in solo play, but I would actually list this as a positive for multiplayer. When each character in the party is controlled by a different player, it is easy to feel accomplished with you turn, without being overwhelmed with learning the actions of every single character.     -A lot of abilities really need to have their descriptions clarified/cleaned up.   -Lastly, there is a LOOOOOOOOT of reading. Obviously this could be negligible to those who don't mind reading. As a slow reader myself, I don't exactly mind but it seems like a core chunk of game time is spent reading. I personally love the large number of game actions and have built my mc to  However, I am playing multiplayer and don't enjoy playing games solo. The story is actually really interesting. Much much better than BG3 in my opinion, and I'm typically a much bigger fan of fantasy. I can see that Owlcat has learned a lot from their digital Pathfinder games and I am glad to see them improve upon their formula with Rogue trader. I can't wait to see what they do in the future and would love to see a game based on the other factions in this universe.
