_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Rogue Trader. The story was fun, despite all the bugs and niggling issues. It achieved what I expected: delivering an interesting narrative, memorable companions, fun gameplay, and capturing the atmosphere of the Warhammer 40K world.Often when playing RPGs, I settle on the usual squad of companions I like. However, this game and Baldur's Gate 3 left me wanting to explore each companion's story and get to know them more. All of them felt interesting, and I genuinely felt sad when a few of their endings were bittersweet or sad. It made me really want to replay the game and make sure I got their stories right. However, I will wait until expansions and bug fixes are finished.I would have enjoyed exploring the world and my companions a lot more. The main three critiques and things that took away from the experience for me were mostly the lack of voice acting. All of the actors delivered excellent performances, and I was left wanting to hear more from all of them. It would be wonderful if in a future update they were fully voiced, perhaps in a special edition. I'd also like the other major characters to get voices, like Theodora and the inquisitor. Additionally, maybe having a narrator to read the in-between character voice lines, as seen in other RPGs?My only gripes are mostly bug-related, and the ending arc felt a little rushed. I would have loved to explore more of the world. The conclusions and stories for some characters, such as Sister Argenta, Abellard, and Idira, felt underdeveloped, which is a shame because they were some of my favorite characters.The last point is about the combat and leveling, which felt rather underwhelming. I got very overpowered very fast, taking away from the challenge. I think the class system and leveling were a slight downgrade from other RPG games that have come out before and could use with an expansion and rebalance. Other games like Pathfinder and Baldur's Gate handled it a lot better i think.Overall, I highly recommend the game, and it's definitely one of my all-time favorite RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Sublime cRPG goodness.After finishing the game, this is one of my favourite cRPGs.  Yes, there are bugs in act 4/5 (no more game breaking ones fortunately) and the writing/pacing does take a quality dip, but it's still 8/10.  And the early acts are damn near perfect.  My only other complaint is the balancing needs work (right now it's heavily in the player's favour to become unstoppable, unlike their other games).Once the definitive edition is out and all the DLCs are complete, I can see Rogue Trader being a top cRPG for all time.  Even if you have no exposure to WH40k lore, you will find this game incredibly fascinating over its 100 hour run time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great potential, sadly unfinished.At the time of writing I have just about finished the second act. The Game is great and I could not have asked for a better studio to make a 40k CRPG its a match made in heaven.But the game isn´t finished. In about 20h of Playtime I have been Soft Locked at least 3 times. The Amount of jank is impressive and QoL is basically non existent. Companions get stuck on terrain and stay in the instance you´ve just left. Meaning you can´t move from the instance you then find yourself in because your party inst complete.More than once have i had to kill my officer because one of their abilities prevented anyone else from using their turn and essentially gave them infinite moves.One other example being, to enter a district of a station from your Hub you go through one loading screen. To go Back you must usually go from the district you´re in to the start district of the location and then back to your Hub.Other things are for example: You can´t go on certain tiles if your camera is facing the wrong way, or better said not facing a specific angle from the character to the point you wanna go.Generally terrain barely works, Try casting an AOE on stairs. Abilities what usually have enormous depth now only affect one step. Animations break almost every combat. What abilities do and when they are in action is seldomly explained. And often times they dont work? Maybe thats an issue on the user level but if an ability states "Targets in zone die if they take more than 10 dmg in an Attack" but the bugger still stands after eating 15, well thats ´frustrating.That really is the best word for it, Frustrating. The game breaks your immersion very often, objectives are often not explained while other stuff is overexplained.As in: Why do you have a hand holding tutorial that explains what clicking does, but no even a simple introduction to what skills are necessary for what class while building your character? Owlcat have delivered great games with Kingmaker and WotR, I have no doubt they will polish this game to their usual standard given time. And in a way they acknowledge that the game is rushed, the bug report feature is permanent on screen and hotkeyed.If you want a good first playthough experience wait a month or two until the first update is rolled out.Also why tf do you force me to use LMB to move and dont offer an alternative WHILE MAINTAINING RMB MOVE IN THE MAP?Will update review once QoL improves.EDIT:The first big patch dropped with some fixes. Some major ones remain broken and I´ve heard the infamous "Dont play past act I" a few times now. I am currently hard locked in an unskippable sequence because of the "Seize The Initiative" Perk. I have infinite moves but cant do anything, I cant attack or interact I cant even end my turn because it just pops me right back to the top of the list. Really wanna play but i simply cannot.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 40k even a little you should play this game. Getting to walk around in 40k like this is a dream come true for me. I love Dawn of War and Space Marine, but this is so much more than those.Fair warning: 1) I encountered two pretty rough bugs around companion quests in Act 4, I don't remember any bugs before that point, and there weren't any issues in Act 5 either. Hopefully these will be addressed in future patches, many other bugs already have been.2) The game kinda railroads you a bit for the first 5-10 hours. If you are feeling bored in the beginning just stick it out, once you are done on Footfall it gets so much more fun3) There are sooooooo many skills and talents. Making builds is fun, and it feels amazing when you discover something that's so strong it's practically game breaking, but a lot of the time when you are leveling up 6 characters at once it feels like you've been taken out of the action. If I were going to play again (which I definitely will at some point) I'd just keep a note of all of the talents I liked on all of the characters so that I wouldn't have to keep rereading everything every time I leveled up. But yeah, all of those complaints are nothing when held up to how awesome the whole experience of playing the game is. _childDocuments_.review: The game is very well versed in making you feel part of the warhammer 40k universe, but gameplay wise it still needs improvements. I love the game and my hours in it shows that it has plenty potential, but just needs some more tweaks. Pro:- You feel the power of being a rogue trader in the 40k universe. - Each faction feels unique in fights.- Character details and backstories are well done.- Plenty of exploration options once you get your own ship. - All the chaos gods and their minions are featured instead of the game focusing on just one of them.- Chance to become a champion of the dark gods and turn the imperium against itself. - Sometimes making morally right choices have dire consequences.Con:- Boss fights as you get further in the story become increasingly unfair for the player as you play 2-3 boss battles back to back with no means of removing your character trauma's between battles, leaving them ever weaker with each battle. Hell, I switched to story mode difficulty just to keep going and I'm still getting my butt handed to me with final act 4 boss.- Voice acting is well done, but confusing. Not every line has audio for it and it feels weird when an audio file will suddenly kick in out of nowhere instead of the entire conversation having audio. - Constantly having to return to your ship to fix trauma's is frustrating and kills progression. I know there are items that can fix some, but there are far more that require you to return to your ship for treatment. - There are bugs with conversation prompts are sometimes missing blocking you from taking certain actions.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is buggy.  There are quite a few game breaking bugs that will waste your time and completely end your enjoyment of play.For example, in combat on a character's turn, you will select the movement and actions you want to take, and then the game just has a mental breakdown trying to execute it. Then you're hung on that character's turn, forever.  You have no choice but to load a save point to get it unstuck.  The UI still functions during this freeze - you can select other characters (but can't control them, because it's not their turn), access inventory, interact with everything in the UI, but you can't progress because it's stuck on a hung character's turn.I'm going to put this game down until they work out the kinks.  It's too frustrating to have to reload the entire game 4 times just to successfully get through a single combat encounter, and it's a giant waste of time besides.Also, it annoys me that developers would release the game in this state - with game breaking bugs - and expect the playerbase to PAY them to beta test it.  Because that is exactly what I think the state of this game is currently: Beta.  AKA not ready for release.  Yet, I paid for the game, and have to deal with bug testing for the devs.  Last I checked, devs pay QA people to find/eliminate bugs.   QA people don't pay devs for the privilege.Edit:  After looking through the other owlcat games, all of the above seems par for the course.  I'm uninstalling and requesting refunds. _childDocuments_.review: [Updated now that I finished the game] The game that should’ve been made a decade ago; and one of the best space piracy simulators available.  It's classic fallout; mass effect and boulder's gate in the 40k universe. Surprisingly engaging; with a lot of mechanical depth and roleplaying options. Combat is genuinely good; Space combat is solid and the quest writing is good – great. It's the first 40k game where not only do the Eldar feel relevant but makes the universe feel textured and nuanced in a way that most games don’t do. As an exploration of complicity and the moral grey; it succeeds. The Companions are great too; even if i wish they had more wholesome interactions. Unfortunately the main quest is badly paced as you get to the 4th and 5th acts; collapsing under the weight of under-developed plot points and a drowns in a flood of deep lore.  Animations break all the time; there’s way too many loading screens and there are some nasty difficulty spikes that are just inexcusable from a design point of view. This thing can feel cheap at points. Its REALLY BAD at points; basically un-playeble without mods. However; I would still reccomend this. Not as good as BG3; but still one of the best 40k games and enthralling for most of its run.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game as it is. Have some positives and negatives to say. Like to preface that I've been into the hobby and the lore of Warhammer for over a decade at this point. Haven't played much of Owlcat's other titles besides WotR briefly and that game is very tight in mechanics and writing. Positives first; I'm blown away by the attention to detail with the lore as well as the environments. If you are a Warhammer 40k fan you're going to thoroughly enjoy this one. The way the game presents itself with it's writing and setting is on the spot. I'd like to point out that it is very friendly to people who have no idea what the hell a God Emperor of Mankind even is. You get to ask questions during the game and have lore explained to you by characters that are *in* the setting, which is a big plus if you ask me. I already know enough lore to fact check and found nothing wanting. Great game to get into the Warhammer 40k setting with. The game play can be very tactical at times. Certain enemies require your attention to their monster sheet because of their abilities. Sometimes it can be a slog to get through fights because of the size of mobs or the scenario, however getting your character and party abilities to a point where it's just as unfair for the computer as it is for you is satisfying to say the least! Late game Soldier/Master Tactician is brutal fun. Tooling your party to match your play style is a must and very enjoyable to see in action.    Party characters are likable because how they are written into the story. Their companion quests make sense and don't linger too long. Most are tied to the main story line and help move the plot forward which is greatly appreciated. Whenever the game decides to include voiced interactions it is always a treat. The voice acting and direction are very good and I'm almost wishing there was more in the game. I know how time consuming and expensive that is to do but I wouldn't mind a few extra sermons form Sister Argenta.  Now the negatives; The game can be buggy at times. I've encountered a good number of visual and character model bugs. A few favorites have been the T-Posing servitors throughout the game or the Wacky Waving Inflatable Arm Flailing Tube Citizens in a cut-scene on your home-world. Though funny they aren't game breaking in the slightest and of those bugs I have none to report. Had to reload a save once because of a camera issue but that was it in the 100hrs I have logged. There is a bug report option and seems to be very thorough, use it!Although the writing is solid most of the times I have issues with some of the character decisions and motivations in Chapter 3. It did not eject me from the story but made me question the writers intentions with certain characters and how they expected the player to react. Very strange choice but nothing a few plasma shots didn't deal with easily. I won't go further into details for spoilers sake, however there are other aspects of the writing that did not line up with other earlier statements or encounters - every one being minor slip ups it seems. Forgivable but I noticed whenever it happened. "Wait, didn't you just say X? Why are you saying Y now?" sort of stuff. When the game ends there is a still slideshow of what happens in the Expanse due to your actions. Everything seemed to be out of order. NPC characters died but in a later slide it explains what they were doing in other places. Seemed jumbled and I'm unsure why. The jumble soured the ending for me but did not ruin it. A good take away from some of these endings is that the Warhammer 40k setting is brutal and uncompromising. I take a point off for the fumbled presentation but I was satisfied nonetheless. TL;DR If you enjoy the Warhammer 40k setting as well as Owlcat's other titles (Party based RPG's) and have approx. 100 hours to spend, buy this game. It is buggy at times and has its flaws like everything else but well worth the cash and time value. We don't get good Warhammer games very often. Happy to say this is one of the better ones.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:After playing for quite some time I can now very clearly illustrate why this game is at best a middling CRPG made by a clearly stubborn developer that simply can't do anything but story and setting.Pros:- The story is decent, if trope laden-ed as all 40k stories are.- In general the set pieces are amazing. Battle maps are detailed and world maps are intriguing if small. This is not a AAA game in scope but the art details 40k in a way few have achieved.- The music is very good, and the sound is very satisfying with excellent voice acting. Listening to Argenta's joy at murder inspires the Khornite in us all.- The class builds can feel very good, but only because they can become very broken. Perhaps this is the intent but it feels like serendipity got them there, not design.Cons:- The game is extraordinarily buggy, and some of these bugs should have been caught during beta. The devs didn't do ANY bug testing beyond the volunteer work they charged others for. Some of these bugs are as simple as a proof read. Seriously go read the description of the Magos Biologis and Dark Magos buildings on Janus. These are very clearly switched. There are bugs in your favor, there are bugs that will have you reloading every space battle. I haven't run into any game breaking bugs, only bugs that made me have to reload several hours.- The cutscenes are extremely underwhelming and animated at snail speed.- There is heavy reliance on some sections of story being done with theater of the mind. They are almost entirely text with some highly stylistic ink art that... is serviceable but extremely underwhelming.- Colony management is a nothing. The buildings are more puzzle pieces that need to be fit together and you have nearly no clue ahead of time how it will work, because events pop in and adjust your numbers. There is almost no tracking of these events beyond the "stories of the protectorate" which provide almost no information on what happened. Stat changes from these are tracked as "Captains Decisions" but not linked to which ones so even understanding where you screwed up requires save scumming and writing numbers down. The first decision on Kiava Gamma can lock you out of a very important building unless you build another building (which locks you out of another choice) in a different colony. This is typical CRPG fair where "management" side is about as exciting as an advent calendar. The entire UI is pretty atrocious. Colony management again exercises the weird circle fetish the UI intern whipped up. There was next to no thought put into this system, efficiency and complacency buildings are all over the place, and some buildings feel like they took 0 look at the ending result and said just gave a build 30% bonus to something like 3 profit factor the entire colony generates. Just so we are clear all this is for at best a rounded up +1 profit factor in a game which has some things costing over 100. You get 4 colonies? 5? I can remember who cares.- Ship stuff. The combat is fine, and enjoyable, but the communication of the great "circle" of skills terrible. Just show me what I am working with and what is dependent on what so I don't stumble through the interface. Can you guys just not group things in a relational diagram? Did skill tree's do something to your children that you thought skill wheel fixed? Why can't I respec my ship like classes when you put even less effort into making this interface usable?- The class skills are a collection of garbage with some gems that may or may not be functional. Fortunately you are thrown enough levels to make anything work eventually though some secondary classes will have you. Some skills will add like 1 damage or 1 deflection (a pointless trap stat) for a round. Others will add 6 damage for the remainder of combat. Some classes are simply too much trouble for the time put in. Operators or whatever they are seem very lack luster. Sure you could stack a ton of observations on enemies, that might be reasonable against the few big bosses that can stand up to the other classes (are there any) but in reality the game can be played without them, so why convolute when you can hand out free turns and action points like water to much simpler murder machines? Ultimately Soldiers and Officers simply take the cake for starting classes. Officers have some very lack luster secondary classes. Grand strategist is fine, and perhaps if you are absolutely generating gobs of morale or whatever you could use their ult (which can be made repeatable, but max once a turn) as a outlet so you aren't "wasting it" but what fight even lasts more than 2-3 turns (playing on second to hardest difficulty)? Frankly Vanguard and Tactician should be your choices for officer with Tactician being awful until you can hand out the stacks to others in the form of +damage until the end of combat. Officers are incredible though for giving people additional turns with no attack limit. I made Cassia into a Vanguard and my character into a Tactician. Melta weapons don't use BS for area attacks just FYI, so you can dump points into your support stats add some backup melee attacks of opportunity.Ultimately this is every other B tier developer's CRPG. Janky, but built with passion and a mostly well spent art budget. It's not revolutionizing literally anything, as every attempt it innovation is completely devoid of logic. Buy it on sale after a 1 year beta period post launch and check comments to see if this stuborn dev even bothered. I won't be buying any of their other games.Original Review:Their insistence, even after receiving the information through their beta survey, on sticking with their character interface for leveling, is mind blowing.The hell is wrong with the design team here? I mean the character classes are mediocre, there are certainly interesting builds but there is also a huge lack of choices for certain levels. There is a warning that if I am not familiar with the RT table top game I might get confused but this game has NOTHING to do with those systems. Which is all the more reason why a clear character level up screen is needed, since you are introducing new builds and fresh strategy.But the layout is essentially one long unsorted list, with a lot of the core abilities at the very bottom. There is some strange sorting based on class component done on some lists, but not all?You made a wheel though. Good job with that. Really great design choice. Send the intern home please...The game is really well done otherwise, certainly trope heavy and SOMEONE has a mutant fetish. So much so that mere moments of rescuing her you are presented with a cutscene with dialogue offering to bed her in almost every dialogue choice... Sometimes 2 different dialogue lines in the same set of choices! I get it you want me to date the spoiled fish lady!I can forgive campy writing, it's 40k and it's still very charming. The settings are lovingly crafted and bring the world to life and the voice acting is really quite good.A shame I won't be changing my review simply based on such a bizarre and unintuitive UI element. I'll give it one play through, but exploring builds would be stillborn with the character UI, even if I thought the classes have potential, which I don't from what I have read in the "lists". The only accolade I can give the character design so far is it does try VERY hard at looking like it has meaningful options (the lists are long!).I wish some of the skills worked properly. The voidborn perk that swaps Fellowship for Intelligence doesn't update the UI properly. I think it is working but I am not sure if it is working for the Ship positions for instance. It's odd because sometimes it's very good about alerting you to things and other times it's just not. I feel like they just never figured out the character classes and did they best they could and hung up the towel.

This review is still positive, but I believe I will not play further than I have(1 hour). I just appreciate universe and quality of everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: This might just be my favourite WH40K game to date. In short I can't add more than what almost everyone notes, the story and scope are mindblowingly great, but bugs aplenty spoil the fun. I really didn't expect to finally get a heavily, well written, story based game in this universe. It becomes more obvious as you progress, however, that the devs had to scale back their ambitions by a lot.They still managed to complete the game in a presentable manner, but it is undeniable that things are missing, or incomplete. Some plot points and character developments have to be guessed more than experienced. The localisation in my case was atrocious, like google translate would have done a better job, and full of spelling mistakes.Balancing of battles is mostly fine, I won't complain about too easy ones, as the underlying system is so complex, it seems impossible to make every fight equally challenging for everyone. But then there are at least two battles that I would call objectively unfairly stacked against the player. The whole system with the wounds and traumas unfortunately is also something that seemed to have been planned as more integral, but was abandoned half-way through development.Most of my complaints will hopefully be fixed with future patches, and I'd love to see more content released as well. Count me in for an expansion, although I'd also like to see some of the missing content restored and patched.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game... It needs some updates though.I'm not 100% convinced that this isn't a beta release...Is it fun and immersive? Yes.Can it be tedious and long-winded? Yes.It has a good story so far. I've been playing Warhammer 40k since the 90s across all mediums. This game absolutely confuses me. I often have no idea what I'm doing, not because of WH Lore... But because the game doesn't explain things well or offer hints.There doesn't appear to be a waypoint system, so you have to just wander around to figure out where to go for the next objective.I've picked up upgrades for weapons or armor, but have no idea how to apply them.But taking all of the above into consideration, would I recommend this game? Yes I would. Because despite all that they did Good by the Warhammer Lore.The combat is thoroughly enjoyable, it is alive and the sounds of the weapons are spot on with how they should be.The character customization, abilities and items are beautifully done. You have the choice between several archetypes and can customize your characters to suit your play style exactly.The only real issue I have with the game is the dialogue. Sometimes it's voice acted, sometimes it's not.Now obviously we could easily say they only voice acted the main characters and any random NPC you talk to doesn't need to be voice acted, that is fair. However oftentimes you will be talking with a main character and only a portion of their dialogue is voice acted.It's like if the dialogue you're in has to do with the main story then they voice acted it. If the dialogue that you're in is just you making idle chit chat during a mission or when you're on your ship in downtime, then it's not voice acted.I would like to see a major update where every single solitary bit of dialogue in the game is voice acted. Especially considering the dialogue you have with NPCs can be Pages long. It's like reading a miniature novel. So far I have only spent about 20 hours in game. I'm quite certain 18 of those hours have been reading dialogue.If that's your thing, then you'll love it.Because of that I give it an 8 out of 10 across the board.

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's been a solid meh, a huge step back from Pathfinder WOTR in almost every regard.Will continue playing hoping it gets better, but so far it's been little to no fun. Pros:- Writing seems solid if a bit humdrum and trite. Mind that there's a lot of it, even for a cRPG. - The Momentum combat mechanic is an awesome experience the first twenty fights. - eeer, that's about it I guess.Cons:- Environments are bland, repetitive and boring. It's all enclosed spaces and tight corridors, not a great fit for an isometric party-based RPG. Exploration is cumbersome and unrewarding.- Levelling up and skills in general are boring. +(x + 1/2y)*z % to some skill or a talent, woah so exciting. And you level up basically every other fight.- No option to auto-level up your companions or pick a set archetype.- Not enough classes for a party of six. Roles and kits overlap quite often.- Itemization is boring. 95% items is a vendor spam. - Combat encounters are overdrawn, repetitive and - yet again - boring. With the game being turn-based-only they should have focused on good encounter design. Less is more etc. Instead it's just trash fight after trash fight, all in slow-mo, all painfully samey. No memorable encounters so far. It's also surprisngly easy (for an Owlcat game). - The novel Momentum mechanic (along with all its combos and synergies) gets super samey super fast. Survive the first two rounds and kill as many weaklings as possible, thus building up momentum. Then obliterate the battlefield in a single turn. - Game mechanics in general do not seem to be working as intended. Enemy AI just keeps killing its own units. Line of sight is confusing. Some skills are clearly OP. - The plot does not seem interesting, maybe it will pick up later on but so far it's rather run-of-the-mill meh evil cult doing evil things kind of story (~40h into the game).- Companions are bland, nothing like WOTR. They do not seem nearly as reactive as they were in WOTR too. - Voice acting ranges from average (Heinrix, Abelard, Idira) to laughably bad (Cassia, Jae, Pasqual). Another step down from WOTR.- Animations are embarrassingly bad, a third of your actions do not have any animations of FX at all. Enemies sometimes float in a locked pose, with no animations at all.- Same goes for in-engine "cinematics" - boy does it look like 1999. Hilariously bad. I know it's a cRPG so graphics are not that important, but why create these shoddy cutscenes at all? The book parapgraph thingie with some hand drawn illustration works better for narrating set pieces in these type of games if you're on a budget (WOTR did it as did Pillars of Eternity). - Even the OST - something they nailed in both their PF games - is just... there. Nothing spectacular, nothing as memorable or as powerful as 'Mythic Power' from WOTR. - Jank & bugs. Some skills are bugged and do not work as written. Some texts disappear. Some in-game settings reset on their own or do not work at all. Some animations are bugged. Loading times and optimization are both abysmal.Basically, it's a mediocre averageburger. The only good thing about it are the dialogues (not all mind you, some are just plain exposition dumps or some generic drama - and it's pages upon pages on end), but then it's supposed to be a game and not an interactive novel. Right?All in all the game lands way below Kingmaker, miles below WOTR. A big disappointement, especially with WOTR being imo one of the best cRPG ever created. This just feels like a bootleg Owlcat, I dunno, Team B effort or something.It's a decently written WH40K novel attached to a painfully average cRPG. Not a bad game mind you, just... average.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a warhammer game, but owlcat made a CRPG so here I am. Excellent use of cover, fights (even on the unfair difficulty) offer a good challenge, but always one that can be overcome.The first boss took me three tries, each time i learned something new and adjusted my strategy for the next run. On the third try, I lived with one hit worth of hp left and had saved a guaranteed hit attack to last hit the boss.Also one of the coolest implementations of burst fire i have ever seen, and definitely the best cover system in a game to date, especially since levels have been designed with cover in mind.Thank you Owlcat!Edit: post game editI loved every minute of my time in this game. Some parts outshine others and that makes the parts that are less polished stand out. A big issue with the game is that once youre into your second archetype a bit, combat will be over in one round unless you are not optimized. The whole cover mechanic goes out the window.Enemies should have probably 10x more hp or some of the talents should be toned down. Even on the hardest difficulty 1/3 of my burstfire could kill most enemies.Overall the combat is still fun because of the way mechanics work, and you are never only hitting the attack button for one character.

_childDocuments_.review: So i finished the game after 140 hours.This is a great CRPG, the game overall is great. It lacks in some departments. Can it hold up to the graphic fidelity of Baldurs Gate 3 ? no it cant. Same with the voice acting, which in itself ist good but only very few core scenes are voiceated, mostly with your NPC companions. most other stuff is not. So there will be a lot of reading. however what you read is well done. Quests, Story, just normal lore Stuff all great and fitting in the 40k Universe. Overall this is a great 40K game in terms of Lore "accuracy" and also a good introduction into the W40k universe.The D100 System and general leveling system takes some getting used to. There are an almost overwhelming amount of option when leveling, you can respec as well. However once you get a grip on the system you can make some truly game breaking builds.As for the game itself Act 1 is a good tutorial, introducing basic game systems and the whole of 40k pretty well.Act 2 Introduces the rest of game systems, and expands the story.From there on out your have 3 more Acts of varying length.After Act 1 you can fly around small part of the universe the game is set in. kind of like Mass effect explore systems scan planets for resources and point of interests. besides main quests you have, companion quests, can follow up on rumors you collect throughout the game, dialog etc. some might be fruitful and lead to more quests or loot, some might be duds. while running around the planets you might encounter some puzzle which can be fun.Bugs: Rumor has it that after ACT3 the game becomes noticeably more buggy that the first 3 acts. Not in terms of the random T-Posing character but broken quests etc. Personally i havent encountered any of that, or at least i didnt notice, but that doesnt mean you wont too. The game has loads of branching quests and permutations in the story depending on your decisions. However the devs are patching the game constantly and fixing stuff, might take a while to get it iron clad though. I think its known that the game was a bit rushed and stuff got cut, but that might be reintroduced later. In that process some stuff got broken. like the "moral" System has 3 "flavors" with 5 ranks each but i think on some of the flavors you cant reach max level.Balancing: in the beginning you are fairly weak and with a lack of understanding for the level and skill system you might struggle a little. However the higher level you climb the more gear you aqquire the stronger you get. There are some game breaking builds and combinations of gear/skills/classes etc that make loads of fights trivial even on the hardest difficuty. might get patched, might not. If not i recommend have some fun with it and when you get bored with it respec your character(s).For PC users there is a mod called "Toybox" that allows for some tweaking if you run into some bugs.TLDR:Overall the game is very good, sound and music is good, voiceacting too but sadly only few scenes get that treatment. Graphics are OK the style and art is good but it lacks a bit in fidelity. However you will only notice when zooming in. The Story is great and has room for several different playstyle and repeated playthroughts. It has some rough edges but is good enough that i put 140 hours in to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly enjoyed my time with this game. It's really solidly written, though I'd imagine for someone not as interested or experienced with 40k it'd probably be a bit harder to get in to, but even then they provide enough information that I don't think that should be a major problem. I'd say it's probably about a 7 or 8 out of ten.However,The technical quality of this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ abysmal. It is infested with bugs in a way that was never truly game ruining for me (though I did have to manually complete the occasional quest step utilizing mods as it would sometimes just not progress and you'd be stuck), but rather it just truly made the moment to moment experience of playing it really frustrating. I really enjoyed the game's story and character, they weren't perfectly written at all times but it was clear the writers had a lot of respect and care for the setting they were working in, and they did a really good job. Despite that I can't recommend it as this game feels like it needs so much more extra work on the technical side of things that I highly doubt it'll ever getIf you like 40k, AND are willing to put up with a game so rough around the edges that it should never have been released like this, get it on sale. Otherwise, stay away and do not bother. It's a real shame that is the case though, because this really could have been something really really great. All the pieces are there, good story, solid characters, an interesting combat system that is stupidly easy to break in half (turns out extra turns are really good), but the technical side is just so so so bad that it ruins it. What a waste of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's go over the good stuff in the game.Story:It's a good, compelling story written by people that understand the universe of Warhammer. Characters aren't grating to interact with and are true to the world they live in.Art style and models:Beautiful locations, beautiful models. Development team clearly put love into visual fidelity of the game, especially character outfits and location.Sound Design:Good soundtrack, amazing narration (where it's present), good sounding weapons. It's not making you tear your ears out, and quite opposite, is pleasant to listen to.However, the downsides... There are many and they are atrocious.Animations:Absolute, awful mess. Buggy to no end. Ladder climbing animation doesn't exist at all. If your character shoots from around the corner they turn into a crab that awkwardly sidesteps and shoots the gun (mind you, any gun, including bolters) from their chest. In-game cutscene animations are so lacking it's insane. You begin the game and first thing you're greeted with is your character doing a 180 turn while standing on perfectly straight legs towards the person talking. Whenever you pull out a gun mid-cutscene it looks extremely disappointing. There's a platform in the game which you reach via small elevator that goes up like 3 meters. From one platform to another. You can clearly see the platform. When you enter the elevator it black-screens you and teleports you to the top of the platform. Except sometimes blackscreen doesn't kick in on time and you can see this entire thing happen and that they just despawn the elevator model and spawn a new one.Game Design:Despite all the beautiful locations, you don't get to explore them a lot, no. You're always thrusted into combat. For instand, Rykad Minoris landing pad. You land, talk to a Imperial Guardsman, walk 10 meters and you're in a fight. This ABSOLUTELY doesn't tie with the narrative of the situation. "We're holding out in the space port, holding a part of it." That part is just a single landing pad. A SINGLE. LANDING PAD. And when you engage the enemy all the soldiers standing on the pad just... Keep standing. They don't do ♥♥♥♥ except for 1 trooper and the sergeant you talk to.Combat:Grating and boring. It's a slog-fest of shooting things dead. Skills don't grant you unique attacks or anything. They just allow you to hit things harder or more times per turn. Some abilities plainly make you invulnerable to damage. Stack warrior's Endure and Officer's Brace for Impact and you get a damage reduction of like... 7-10 pointsIn conclusion, this game is absolutely not worth its 50 dollar price tag. Genuine trash, if you ask me. For the same price you can get BG3 and pump out more enjoyment out of it due to the sheer amount of content they put into each location.So do community a favour and let this developer starve until they fix the game.

_childDocuments_.review: After all the patches and with DLC out, this is now a great game, with authentic and deep W40K atmosphere and lore.If you are interested in Warhammer 40K lore in any capacity, THIS IS A GAME FOR YOU, do not skip it. Yes, it is a turn-based party RPG with classic vibes, but it's very fluid with engaging combat and plot to keep you entertained. No other W40K game offers so much insight into the peculiarities of life in the grim dark future of 41st millennium.Custom-made RPG system is very deep (there are classes that will make you regret missing math classes) and deliciously balanced towards kill-or-be-killed strategies. Stacking the deck with extra turns, tight knit builds and active-use gear feels great and rewarding for steeply growing encounter complexity, especially on higher difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: But it had to be release before Christmas, right ? riding on BG3 hype as fast as possible uh?The game is frontloaded. 5 acts, but the 2 first one makes up for more than half the game. Starting from act 3, story and content take a nosedive. Also this is where most of the bugfest start (companion quest trigger not working, a good portion of talent not working...)+ Good atmosphere and writing at least until act 2.- Bugs, talents bloat, (it will takes months to sort that out because there are so many)- Combat was fun at the beginning, then you realise that the balance is wack. Tactic is all about giving turns, momentum turn stacking the same buffs and debuffs to broken level. Then you finish in one turn. There are so many mechanics breaking the balance that I'm not even confident it will be possible to fix it.- Animations. Guns effects are well done. However most buff and Psyker powers are uninspired at best, lazy for most. It consist of your character standing up from cover and pointing toward your ally or enemy.Remember how I said combat was all about buff debuffing ad noseam before shooting ? You spent each fight looking at you characters standing up and pointing a direction 10x, then shoot.Pyromancy psyker ? Point towards the enemy and watch the debuff dot appear under him. Firestorm ? same deal but aoe.wow.It bothers me because they clearly could have done better even if they are not ubisoft sized.Take on sale in a few months.

_childDocuments_.review: As this is an Owlcat game freshly released, there are a lot of bugs. I'm used to it, I was prepared for it, and I'm going to overlook them for the rest of this. (That being said, if you want to dive in without waiting, the Toybox mod will save your sanity and your save file.)Rogue Trader is in my top 3 40k games (Competing with Space Marine and Darktide), but is at the bottom of the three Owlcat games. That isn't to say it's a bad game, but Kingmaker and Wrath were much more emotionally engaging on a lot of levels.That being said, the writing in RT is up to Owlcat's usual great standards. Characters have a distinct voice in how they're written, their actions have sensible motivations, why they are the way they are makes sense. I know that seems to be an obvious thing that should happen, but there are no end of games that ignore basic things like this.  I never wanted to stop playing because I wanted to keep engaging with the story, the characters and what was going on. Even some minor side characters without so much as a character portrait I wanted to learn more about and spend more time with. A short dialogue questioning someone dying in front of you, their personality came across so damn well that I was genuinely upset afterward that I just met this fascinating person who is now dead. Also overall they really do -get- 40k. The Imperium is awful, humanity is garbage, aliens are garbage with shinier toys, and being a good person is a trial that might just make everything worse. It's a crapsack universe and the writers know it. Mechanically, the system RT uses for combat took some adjusting after getting so used to things with distinct Dungeons and Dragons DNA in their way of things, but in the end I came to really dig it. I definitely will up the difficulty the next time I play, as once I figured things out there was seemingly no end to the crazy BS combos of talents I could throw together, especially when some new item enabled a whole new wacky and broken idea. If you like breaking RPG systems you're going to have a lot of fun with RT. Ship combat is a nice side activity. Not terribly complex, not a ton of customisation you can do, but it's fun enough. Though I do wish it was expanded upon, made more complex, maybe let you control a full fleet, etc, etc, but for what it was it was decent. Basic game stuff...Looks fine, aesthetic is perfect, sounds feel great, music is pretty good. But eh, it's a CRPG that isn't Baldur's Gate 3, so that's not really what I play for. I want the story and the combat. My only major complaints is that the game feels...small. It's by no means -short-, but it felt like events unfolded quickly. I can summarise the plot in my head far too easily then I'd really like. Engaging with the colony management system or working my way up the vendor reputation systems I felt like I got all these cool toys and then had absolutely no time to enjoy them before the game was over. tl;dr An above average CRPG, a -way- above average 40k game, and the least good Owlcat game, but since all 3 of their games are damn good one of them has to get the bronze.  Enjoyed my time with it, wish it had been longer.

You will take on the role of a Rogue Trader, a scion of an ancient dynasty of daring privateers, that reign over their own merchant empire and explore the fringes of Imperial space with the blessing of the Emperor Himself. 

Exploration will bring the protagonist to mysterious lost and forgotten worlds as well as numerous planets claimed by humanity - from lush Agri-Worlds to steel-clad Forge Worlds, all of them ready to be claimed for your burgeoning merchant empire or plundered for their riches.

name: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy
detailed_description: Apollo Justice's Legal Journey Begins Anew! Join rookie attorney Apollo Justice and his mentor, the legendary Phoenix Wright, in this collection of 3 games! This title features the 14 episodes of 'Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney', 'Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies', and 'Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice', and the 2 previously DLC-only Special Episodes for a total of 16 episodes! Also included is a mountain of extra goodies that's sure to satisfy any Ace Attorney fan! Orchestra Hall - Listen to the in-game background music and select orchestral arrangements! Art Library - View illustrations, design specs, commissioned pieces, and even the special Spirit of Justice Prologue anime! Animation Studio - Play around with character animations and recreate your favorite scenes! This collection supports Japanese, English, French, German, Korean, and Traditional and Simplified Chinese. Mix and match to play in whichever languages you'd like! Immerse yourself in this beautiful collection as you shout 'Objection!' in these newly renovated halls of justice! Some of the contents of the games in this collection are presented as initially released to preserve the games as originally created.

_childDocuments_.review: The Ace Attorney franchise quickly became one of my personal favourites the moment I wrapped up the first few cases of that initial game. Its iconic presentation, smart scripts and nuanced characters made binging the re-issued franchise utterly effortless from start to finish. Needless to say, my expectations for this third collection were very high, and I hoped I would find plenty to love in spite of the fanbase’s more mixed reception of these titles. Thankfully, I found much of this trilogy to be a great continuation for the series; while this is the most inconsistent collection, it offers plenty of intriguing cases and characters to make these games worth experiencing. As this collection consists of the 4th to 6th mainline entries, I’m going to assume you know the gist of what to expect from an Ace Attorney game, as there’s nothing here that significantly deviates from its established formula. Let’s start by looking at the trilogy as a whole. While the other two collections deliver a more singular overarching narrative, this trilogy largely opts for standalone narratives with three major plotlines that carry through each game: the development and backstory of the eponymous Apollo Justice, the disbarment and resurgence of Phoenix Wright, and this idea of “The dark age of the law”, which paints the picture of a murky legal world where the finding the truth is secondary to conviction. I think these latter two plotlines are handled well; Phoenix has compelling reasons to be present past his initial development, and the dark age of the law is used to derive distinctly fresh character motives and plot elements, even to a satirical degree. With Apollo Justice, I unfortunately think that this loud yet unwaveringly passionate character is largely mishandled. He never steps out of the spotlight of Phoenix at any point during the game named after him, he mostly takes a backseat in Dual Destinies to focus more on Phoenix’s return and the character of Athena, and it’s because of these two games that his development in Spirit of Justice is quite rushed, even though I love where he ends up.The underdeveloped nature of Apollo’s character is a large part of why I feel his eponymous game, the last mainline entry released for the Nintendo DS, is the weakest in the franchise by a good margin. Despite it being angled as a soft reboot to the series, Apollo and his new partner Trucy are largely overshadowed during crucial plot moments. Which is a shame, as this new pairing has great chemistry that only improves as the story progresses, but they don’t get much of a chance to prove their abilities unassisted in the courtroom. I also find the four cases on offer to be rather average; their writing largely lacks the punch and tension that the other collections consistently delivered so well, and I was ultimately left underwhelmed for most of their runtime. However, this writing style does not apply to Klavier Gavin, who is a breath of fresh air amongst the prosecutors for being surprisingly likeable, to the point where his presence carried much of the trial segments for me. Separately, I also really enjoyed the expanded gameplay offerings; most evidence can be thoroughly examined in three dimensions, the forensic minigames offer a nice change of pace during the investigation segments, and Apollo’s perceive mechanic, which allows you to zoom in and identify nervous habits of the witnesses, leads to some varied progression in the trial segments. Ultimately, there’s a good amount to enjoy here, but it’s the only game in the series I cannot see myself coming back to.Then we have Dual Destinies, the first 3D entry in the franchise, that thankfully survives the transition from 2D graphics quite well. While some of the models of the returning characters take a bit to get used to, all of the new ones look fantastic, and their animations ooze even more personality than ever before. Of the six cases on offer, I’d say all but the second one are consistently intriguing, ranging from a murder surrounding a detonated bomb, to a stabbing amidst the launch of a rocket, to…defending an Orca? It’s all as over the top as you’d expect, yet somehow feels more grounded than the original trilogy, steering around spirit channelling as a plot device to explain the killings in more ‘realistic’ terms. Athena Cykes makes her debut in this game in style. She’s the rookiest of the lawyer trio yet sets herself apart with a bubbling personality, a shockingly dark backstory, and is the source of the new gameplay mechanic of Mood Matrices, where a witnesses’ emotions are questioned to help draw out further testimony. While I think there is untapped potential with having more segments that require you to decide between assessing emotions or testimony, the presentation and theming of this mechanic easily makes it my favourite addition to the formula. Separately, Blackquill and Fulbright, the new prosecutor and detective respectively, are brilliant additions, in part due to their personalities being polar opposites, and the returning characters are handled excellently. Overall, it’s a really solid entry from the get-go, allowing me to get over that disappointing first game rather quickly.That leads us to Spirit of Justice, the most recent mainline entry to date. Taking place primarily in the fictional kingdom of Khura’in, this title seems Phoenix take on quite literally his most vulnerable cases yet, as the Defence Culpability Act threatens to make him face the same fate as the accused, should his arguments fall through. Matters are further complicated with the addition of Divination Seances, which allows the courtroom to have a glimpse at the victim’s final moments, ultimately damning the accused very easily if this evidence is not questioned further. It’s the most complicated mechanic in the series, but once you understand how the contradictions are usually found, it leads to some very satisfying revelations.Part of the game also takes place back home, largely serving to give Apollo and Athena more time in the spotlight. While Apollo gets one of the best standalone cases in the series, Athena is given arguably the most boring case in the whole collection, killing the great pacing up to that point. Thankfully, all of the cases in Khura’in are excellent, alongside the epilogue case which is a nice throwback to the original trilogy. However, this game undoubtedly stars the worst prosecutor in the series, who very quickly becomes an irritating catchphrase machine that is not deviated from until the end of his final appearance. Despite this gripe, Spirit of Justice is my favourite entry in the trilogy because of how well it executes its intriguing premise and develops most of its characters.I really enjoyed this trilogy overall. While it never reaches the consistent heights of the other collections, it nonetheless has plenty of great stories to tell, nuanced characters to meet, and satisfying objections to obtain. Clocking in at a beefy 80 hours, with a few nice art and music bonuses in the extras menu to boot, it’s hard to argue against the value for money on display, even if some cases fall flat for you. I can see myself fondly revisiting a large portion of the 3D entries, and I hope that the next mainline entry doubles down on everything these games do well, whilst also not forgetting why the original trilogy is still highly revered. But while we wait for that, an Investigations 1+2 collection needs to happen, and I hope to not be lying coldly on that for too long.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a no brainer purchase for any ace attorney fan that's out there. For everyone else I would suggest to start with the original trilogy first prior to playing this game. It's runs great on steam deck, I finished all 3 games on it and never had any issues. The transition between games is very smooth and save files are kept separately.Apollo Justice has only 4 cases with 3rd being the worst in the franchise so if you can manage to skip it then you would enjoy all the others. The music is the best in this trilogy IMHO. Dual Destinies starts really slow with 2nd case being garbage and then slowly getting better towards the end of the game. It's worth playing for getting to know Athena and Blackquill and absolute banger of a last case. This game also has the best bonus case.Spirit of Justice is a hit or miss for most of the people. I did enjoy it even though it felt pretty long and some cases felt like being out of place completely. Overall great games, hopefully more ace attorney will come in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDW: the games are good but the series discards too much of Apollo Justice (Ace Attorney 4) to ignore completely.The good part of this trilogy is that it's got all of the engaging mysteries, fun character interactions and excellent music of the previous games, and if you like those aspects these games are absolutely worth playing.However, as much as I'd love to say it's as good as the PW trilogy I can't, mostly because of the more disjointed feeling between the games. Apollo Justice was a game which thoroughly changed the status quo of the series and the problems with the trilogy mostly stem from Dual Destinies trying desperately to ignore those changes. A good example is Phoenix Wright's character whiplash (don't worry, I'm not going to spoil anything).In short, in AA4 he is slightly too different from his T&T self, while in AA5 and 6 he is too similar.In long:In Apollo Justice, Phoenix is presented to be much more confident and clever, thinking things through much more thoroughly than in his previous games, however other aspects of his character are unfitting even for a more jaded and bitter version of the Phoenix we knew.While his character change is drastic, it is justified decently well, the problem is that Dual Destinies undoes all of this development, he loses any bitterness or distrust, as well as losing a lot of his cool confidence; the best (non spoiler) example I have is that Phoenix doesn't overreact to being surprised in Apollo Justice at all, however in Dual Destinies he overreacts to pretty much any setback using his surprised sprite.

_childDocuments_.review: I have waited years for these games to finally be ported to something that isn't an iPhone or Android device.This collection of games were such a vital part of my teenage years, I am so happy to be able to relive these absolute classics on an HD screen! Dual Destinies may not be the best Ace Attorney game in the franchise, but I have so many great memories anticipating the 3DS release of the game. From the web based Japanese demo that I would play over and over to the trailers that were so good at making the wait for that game almost unbearable! Dual Destinies is what helped get my foot into making YouTube videos with my old Music Compilation videos. I owe a lot to Dual Destinies, and it's about time that it leaves the 3DS and Mobile Phone landscape of gaming! I still cannot believe that Dual Destinies came out 11 years ago!!! I have a lot less memories with Apollo Justice Ace Attorney, I've only played that game once on my DS, and Haven't returned to it since then. That's not to say it's a bad game! I still love every single AA game that's been made! I WILL, however, say that whoever was responsible for Spark Brushel's armpit tell... you know what you did.Spirit of Justice is the best game out of the whole collection, without a doubt. From the long awaited return of Maya Fey (side note, genuinely where is our boy Gumshoe!?), to the infamous clown girl...... to the gut wrenching final case that finally let Apollo shine in his own trilogy. I truly believe that Spirit of Justice will go down as a highlight for this franchise.I really want to say thank you to Capcom for not letting this franchise die with AA6. Thank you for giving us more updated versions of the Original Phoenix Wright trilogy, thank you for translating the Great Ace Attorney games and letting us finally play those amazing titles in English. Thank you for giving us Apollo Justice Ace Attorney, Ace Attorney Dual Destinies, and Ace Attorney Spirit of Justice on modern platforms. This series has meant a lot to me, and I cannot wait for what is next for Ace Attorney. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Great games, IMO the original trilogy is still better but these are still excellent titles.By the way, if playing on Steam Deck, go into the game's Steam Properties and set the Game Resolution to 1920x1200, and turn on "Set resolution for internal and external display" (if this doesn't show, exit and re-enter the menu). After this, go to the PC Config section in the game, and set the resolution to 1920x1080. This removes jagged edges from Apollo Justice. This also works for the original AA Trilogy on Steam Deck (I'm unaware if this has any effect on TGAA).

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this in case anyone reads the negative reviews because of a bug I was experiencing. If you are on windows 11 and the game wont launch, first check task manager, and close any instances of the game that are "running." Just search task manager for "gs" and close any instances of the game still running. Then, go to the games install folder, there should be a file in there called "CrashReporter.exe" Just delete that and the game should work. Anyhow, as for my actual review of the game, I'd say its pretty solid, but not as good as the first trilogy. Still a lot of good fun to be had throughout however.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm super happy these games came as a three pack to Steam finally. _childDocuments_.review: As of this writing, I've finished Apollo Justice and am on Chapter 3 of Dual Destinies. I've played Apollo Justice before, but that was over 10 years ago on my DS. I've never played Dual Destinies or Spirit of Justice since I didn’t have a 3DS. I appreciate that all the Ace Attorney games can now be (legally) played on PC instead of requiring old retro consoles.Objection! That said, I can’t say I love this trilogy more than the original Phoenix Wright Trilogy. There was a certain charm to the first three games.Maybe it’s the sprites? There was something endearing about the hand-drawn art of the Phoenix Wright trilogy. I don’t love the 3D sprites they started using in the newer titles—they didn’t age well, in my opinion.Maybe it’s the pacing? The text scroll in the Apollo Justice trilogy is slow, and you can’t adjust it. I read faster than the text appears, but you can’t just press "A" to skip because you risk also skipping sprite animations, which I want to see. When the game dictates your pace, it can get a bit frustrating.Maybe it’s the wacky gimmicks? The Ace Attorney series isn’t known for its realism, but the crimes became more outlandish and harder to follow—they completely lose me at times.Hold it! It’s still a fantastic experience for anyone who loves the Ace Attorney series, and is a series worth recommending. If you're itching for more after the original trilogy, this has the Ace Attorney formula that you can come to expect.
_childDocuments_.name: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second installment for the Ace Attorney Trilogy that Capcom brings to the steam store. While the first one revolves around Phoenix Wright, this Trilogy (as the name already suggests) follows Apollo Justice to some extent.Since 2 out of 3 games are ports from the Nintendo 3DS this collection is a tiny bit more hardware hungry/needs better graphic cards as the first one. Now lets come to the meat of it: The game itself. As typical for Ace Attorney games you have a WIDE range of characters and many are fleshed out to be deeper than "I am bad guy doing bad stuff". The background music always completment the situation and accentuate sudden shifts in tone, let it be funny or dramatic. The graphic is much more polished for the first game and nicely scaled for the 3DS ones.The controls are well ported over, but since many of the forensic minigames were just DS/3DS gimmicks it obviously is not as engaging as they used to be. But they are still fun to do, dont get me wrong.Apart from the normal stuff we got on the handheld there are also PC only additions like art books and music/sound sampling. As things that we take for granted but takes a bit of optimisation: The loading times.I tested it and from hitting "start" on steam to my loaded game save it took only 7 seconds. SECONDS! I know, its not the hardware intense game there is, but some other games dont even have their start loading screen up after 7s.I did not talk about the story? Come on, its a no brainer. The Ace Attorney games are always riddled with plot twists and nice character arcs.But I also have some not so nice things to say (so I dont look like a total fanboy):By god, I forgot how annoying most people are in the first game (Apollo Justice). Maya was already sometimes hard to get around but Trucy takes the cherry with lacking all common sense and sometimes being downright criminal (ofcourse without any repercussions). In addtion this "Phoenix Wright being transformed into a hobo" never was my favorite plotline as it does my boy really dirty. Gladly its not permanent, but we will never forget. Also it does not help that everything is VERY constructed. Some problems or even murder could be prevented with some normal human interaction.Since I dont want to end on a bad note I sandwich my negative points with something nice at the end:I absolutly love the variaty of new abilities. In the first Trilogy we had the magatama that helps us with the investigations.In this one we have SO MANY MORE. From body language perception, over our old friend magatama to emotion analysis and others (I dont want to spoil too much), this game is packed with "minigames" like that.As a final line I only hope we also get the Miles Edgeworth Investigation series to steam soon, but after that running low on Ace Attorney games to scratch our OBJECTION itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original trilogy for the Ace Attorney series back during my senior year of college during the pandemic. With an excess of time, I sorted through the highest rated games on steam and made the plunge into the series. The original trilogy had many positive traits going for it. The cast of characters were memorable & the plot lines that played out had many of us on the edge of our seats. It was a fantastic set of games that left a deep impression on the way I think about how information is presented in stories. A truly timeless series.Now, if you think that this is a review that will admonish the Apollo Justice trilogy in favor of the Phoenix wright trilogy, you'd be wrong. The original games, due to the time & budget constraints, recycled assets & characters in order to stretch their budget. However, the strength of writing is undeniable. The Apollo Justice trilogy finds itself in a different position entirely. For various reasons, each game in the AJ trilogy had a different director involved. Each game in the AJ trilogy feels distinctly different. The fact that this series is even called the Apollo Justice Trilogy is a hell of a red herring when the focus is split on three different defense attorneys in the series.  This lead to some confusion when you enter the name game & find that there's very little connecting everything except for the characters who even then tend to change. If you are willing to overlook what is undeniably a growing pain for the series, what you'll find is trilogy packed with a lot of charm, fresh ideas, and a stream of new characters to fall in love with. While not perfect,  I do appreciate the amount of effort & the willingness to make mistakes to take the series forward. I'm unbelievably excited to see what the future of this series holds.TL:DR Keep Cooking, 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy? Balancing Justice and Nostalgia! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)"It masterfully blends nostalgia with modern enhancements, offering an uneven yet richly rewarding legal adventure."The "Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy" emerges as a delightful treat for fans of courtroom drama and video game storytelling. This compilation, featuring rookie attorney Apollo Justice and his iconic mentor, Phoenix Wright, bundles together "Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney", "Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies", and "Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice". With a whopping 16 episodes, including two that were previously only available as DLC, this collection offers a comprehensive journey into the world of legal battles and intricate storylines. Language support spanning English, French, German, and several Asian languages ensures a broader appeal, inviting a global audience to partake in the thrill of courtroom action.Diving into the specifics, the trilogy shines in its presentation and extra content. The remastered graphics and soundtracks enhance the experience, with the Orchestra Hall and Art Library serving as delightful bonuses for fans. The Animation Studio adds a fun, interactive element, allowing players to recreate their favorite scenes. These extras are a testament to the developer's dedication to the series and its fans. However, the collection isn't without its shortcomings. While "Spirit of Justice" is often hailed as the standout game, offering depth and a chance for Apollo to truly shine, "Dual Destinies" receives mixed feelings. Some fans find it lacking compared to other entries, feeling it doesn't quite reach the heights of its predecessors. This disparity in quality between the games can lead to an uneven experience for players journeying through the trilogy.In terms of user engagement, the trilogy has been warmly received for its nostalgic value and replayability, even as a linear visual novel. Long-time fans appreciate the opportunity to relive these classic games on modern platforms, with HD graphics enhancing their experience. The extra content, including art and music, adds a layer of depth and appreciation for the series. However, there are critiques regarding the pacing and strength of some of the storylines in "Dual Destinies" and "Spirit of Justice". Some purists argue that these titles don't quite live up to the charm of the original trilogy. Nonetheless, even the less favored games in the collection are acknowledged as worthy of play, underscoring the enduring appeal of the Ace Attorney series.In conclusion, the "Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy" is a commendable effort in bringing classic games to a new generation of gamers and satisfying long-time fans. While not every game in the collection is equally celebrated, the overall package offers a rich, engaging experience that both honors its roots and embraces its evolution. This trilogy stands as a testament to the enduring charm and complexity of the Ace Attorney series, making it a worthy addition to any gamer's library.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: Despite giving this a negative score, i would still recommend at the very least one playthrough of each game. That being said, the games in this collection are so sub par with the rest of the series that it would make people who played the original trilogy (and the other collections), a BIG FRICKING MIGRAINE. Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney is the first game in this collection and it is the best one here simply because it's the last time Shu Takumi wrote a mainline Ace Attorney game (and the next games in this collection show just as much). While it is the shortest one here, i will say i had more fun playing the cases in this one than the other cases in the other games. A new cast of characters which are excellent in my opinion, and as for the cases themselves: Case 1 was excellent, Case 2 had fun investigation segments and some fun trial moments, Case 3 is takes logic and throws it out the window (i get the implications but... like... rly?), Case 4 while not the best finale out there, it is a very decent one at that.Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney: Dual Destinies is the game where they brought Phoenix back and it's not a bad idea at first glance until you realize they reversed his character development from Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney back to Phoenix from the first trilogy. This is also the first "3D game" and games like The Great Ace Attorney and Professor Layton vs Phoenix Wright showcased the 3D really well, so there is some potential here. However, the 3D here is just to be there. They don't really do any fun stuff with it like the examples i mentioned. The new characters here look pretty good however returning characters look HORRIBLE. And not to mention the returning characters here get MISCHARACTERIZED HARD! (or simply they didn't understand the character). As for the cases themselves, they get too handhold-y many times and for a game where you have to THINK, this is the worst thing you can ever do.Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney: Spirit of Justice is pretty much the same as Dual Destinies in terms of problems but it's not as bad as Dual Destinies.Honestly, i am dissapointed...

_childDocuments_.review: This trilogy is the weakest AA releases on Steam, but it’s still worth your play, nonetheless. AJ is a fun game, Apollo & Trucy’s chemistry makes the investigations fun, and I loved the return of Ema as a detective this time around, while Klavier Gavin fills in the prosecutor position here (really like him, especially compared to the other two in the trilogy).  The OST is easily among the best the mainline has to offer (along with the AA1’s). All cases are good, Turnabout Trump and Turnabout Succession obviously outshine the other two, but Turnabout Corner and Turnabout Serenade are definitely some of the better middle cases. Dual Destinies is hot garbage as far as AA goes imo. It almost feels like another team made it, without grasping the essence of the previous games and make it feel like a celebratory comeback, while discarding the entirety of Apollo Justice (ahem). The 3D looks horrific. I don’t know how DGS and the Layton crossover (which released before DD) can look this much better than Dual Destinies, all of them being released on the 3DS. The cases feel immature in a sense, not the crimes (and their depictions) themselves, but with the character designs and general dialogue. It’s even weirder that Turnabout for Tomorrow depicts the by far goriest and most disturbing murder that’s ever happened in Ace Attorney. All of that said most parts of cases 3-6 are still enjoyable, even if they don’t reach the heights the previous games did.I do like Spirit of Justice more than Dual Destinies, the change of setting and splitting of the cast for most of the game works in its favour as Phoenix being more like in the trilogy works better without Apollo and Athena next to him. The second case is really good and personally I loved the Khura’in cases. The 4th case is utterly misplaced and underdeveloped, the final is a bit of a mixed bag. I really enjoyed the first investigation (that felt more like Layton than like AA) and I liked the second trial, but the middle part is a bit rough, especially the foundation the first trial was built on was abysmal to say the least. The DLC was decent, even with Edgeworth returning to his AA1 character for whatever reason.I really hope they won’t let Ace Attorney die and release AA7 some time in the future, whatever that may bring.

_childDocuments_.review: While this trilogy doesn't quite match the quality of the original, I still believe that the Apollo Justice trilogy contains a fine set of titles.Apollo Justice was a bold new direction for the franchise, which is unfortunately still contentious to this day. With a time skip and a new protagonist, the game tried a lot of new things that a lot of fans didn't like, hence why a lot of it was undone in future titles. That said, I think that it's a strong set of characters and a good plot that's let down by weak cases. Overall, I think it's a good game and I would have liked to have seen more of what the creator had in mind when writing this game.Dual Destinies is unfortunately, not a title that lives up the rest of the trilogy. The playable character space is crowded by not only the return of Phoenix Wright but also a new protagonist, Athena Cykes. The cast struggle for screentime, reducing Athena to only having a single case in her debut game! The filler cases are weak and the overall plot is a tad predictable. It's also a lot easier than earlier titles, mostly due to the fact that the characters have a habit of hinting towards solutions to puzzles before you've even gotten a chance to answer.Spirit of Justice is definitely the best in the trilogy, with an engaging (if absurd at times) plot set in the foreign Kingdom of Khura'in. It introduces what I feel to be the best cross-examination mechanic in the series, the Divination Seance, where the last moments of the victim are analysed. My biggest criticism of this game is that the prosecutor, Nahyuta, lacks personality and only receives character development until near the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: These games play like homework. It's agonizing.AA4 gets a pass. It feels a little lost rather than outright bad, and it has some good ideas like the Mason system- It could have used a stronger thesis and more time to marinate on its ideas because of how... let's say "narratively dissatisfying" the motives of Zak Gramarye and Kristoph Gavin are, but I can see what it wanted to be. Valant and Klavier are great characters, and so is Hobo Wright.I genuinely don't understand what AA5 and 6 are going for other than "it's more ace attorney so we should raise the stakes without raising the stakes". They feel more kid friendly, and also are trying to have an overarching plot, but they're also not going into that plot... at all, sometimes. There would be substantial nuance if I were to go into individual cases of course, since there's plenty of below average quality cases in the first series as well, but those problems didn't feel systemic as a rule. To say as little as possible, 5's biggest issue is that it's definitely written for kids and gives its own game away literal hours before it lets Phoenix/Athena know what the player knows, and 6's biggest problem (of which it has many) is that the threat level is so comically unbelievable that you know that the heroes are going to win anyways. The Avengers Issue. I know we expect to win in all of the games, but it's absolutely catastrophic how nonsensical the situations presented are in this game- mostly due to the DC act and what an actual dictator would do in a situation where they have PW held at gunpoint. How did they think something like the DC act was a good thing to put in Ace Attorney? It's a good thing they made him forget about Matt Engarde. Nahyuta directly compounds practically every issue in the game somehow.There's a huge number of minor issues that I've frankly lost count of, but I can only say for sure that they're for a different audience.Oh, and they better kill off Apollo because these backstories all surely contradict each other.

_childDocuments_.review: Full transparency: I've bought these games on many different pieces of hardware before - DS, 3DS and Android specifically- so this isn't my first rodeo with any of these games. That said, this was a fantastic way to re-experience all these titles: the updates to the sprites were excellent, the presentation was phenomenal and the quality of life tweaks are great. I'd say of the 3 games, Spirit of Justice probably is my favorite: the overarching story, for me, remains a treat even on revisits and has some of the most emotional high points of the series. But the other two games are still phenomenal in their own right with some incredible cases: the most noteworthy for me being Turnabout Trump, Turnabout Succession and Turnabout for Tomorrow. If you're new to the series... while I'd say the Phoenix Wright Trilogy or the Great Ace Attorney Chronicles are overall better starting points, you could do worse than start here! But if you're already an Ace Attorney fan who's at least played the trilogy... well chances are, you were probably going to buy this anyways and are just reading the Steam reviews for fun. Either way, you're in for a fun set of mysteries that have been nicely updated for the modern day and make for great nighttime reading before bed! Especially if you own a Steam Deck.
