_childDocuments_.review: I originally played the Apollo Justice trilogy through iOS on my iPad, and was pleasantly surprised at how likeable Apollo and the new batch of characters you meet in these games are, as sometimes when the established main character takes more of a backseat, it can be the nail in the coffin for an at the time well loved game or TV show. This remake reminds me of Mass Effect Legendary Edition in a good way, as it seems most of the visual and gameplay improvements were focused on the first Apollo Justice game, as that one is the oldest out of the 3 games you can play here and when you play the OG now it seems very dated. Capcom did a great job breathing new life into the first game with this remake. I am currently playing through Dual Destinies and can't wait to start playing Spirit of Justice but kudos to Capcom on a job well done as I was hoping they would do this inevitable remake justice (hehe) and they sure did!

_childDocuments_.review: Apollo Justice - Great start to an awesome trilogy. Apollo is a nice character - even if he's surprisingly not the focal point of the game - and the story has some deliciously dark undertones.Dual Destinies - A sequel that tells its own story from Apollo Justice, but it really works. The writing is top-notch and brilliantly witty, the pacing is excellent and playing as 3 different lawyers helps to make the story feel so fleshed out. Plus Athena & Blackquill are just the best characters. In the whole series.Spirit of Justice - Big in scope and probably the longest game in the series yet the brilliant pacing never makes it feel dull. Khura'in is a very expansive, well-detailed environment and the artistry is breathtaking. The music may even be some of Noriyuki Iwadare's best work. It's also nice to see Maya again, even if what you expect might happen to her... happens to her.All in all, a brilliant trilogy that I'm so grateful I'm FINALLY able to play on other than my 3DS. And it has only made me more excited for what Ace Attorney 7 (Athena Cykes game plz!!) may bring.

_childDocuments_.review: The Ace Attorney series is my boo. I've played every single game on the first collection and this collection twice over. So is this trilogy just as good as the original? I'd say yeah. I know a lot of fans didn't like these games as much as the original three, but they felt to me like a new, more modern era of Ace Attorney that I enjoyed quite a lot. With the march of technology came new ways for these stories to create mystery and suspense, such as forensic analysis, psychological analysis, seeing through the eyes of the dead and stuff. The patented funny, witty but also suspenseful Ace Attorney writing is back in full force, and hey, that's what this is all about. Apollo Justice:This is the best game of the trilogy for me. It had the best music, fresh characters, and the most mind-blowing last case out of the trilogy that also ties nicely into the original Phoenix Wright trilogy.  Dual Destinies:Dual Destinies suffers from the "second game of a trilogy" problem of being relatively mid - like Justice For All was. Emphasis on relatively because it's still an Ace Attorney game - meaning it still blows most other mystery games on the market out of the water. It still has its fair share of trademark Ace Attorney moments and mind-bending plot twists. It just wasn't as memorable as Apollo Justice or Spirit of Justice for me. Spirit of Justice: Spirit of Justice is the climactic third game that caps off a trilogy. While its highs weren't as orgasmic as Trials and Tribulations, it was still really good. The new trial gimmick this game added was quite haunting, and I liked it a lot. TLDR: If you're a fan of the first trilogy, definitely get this one too. Everything you love about this series is still here plus a bunch of new stuff too. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy

Nothing beats the original Ace Attorney series but this one has great moments and lots of interesting characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review, I've just finished Apollo Justice. I know it's kind of controversial in the Ace Attorney fanbase, as it puts Phoenix aside. But I genuinely think it's one of Shu Takumi's best works, along with the Great Ace Attorney. It was fresh and interesting, even when playing the third case, the infamous Turnabout Serenade. Which is memed to death, but I still think it's one of the best third cases in the series.The only "fault" I see within the collection is that neither Dual Destinies nor Spirits of Justice really feel like Apollo's games. In fact, when opening the game you see Athena representing Dual Destinies and Phoenix representing Spirits of Justice. Even worse, Dual Destinies in particular feels like it misses the point of the original Apollo Justice, bringing back on the table the theme of a corrupt law system. Also, it's kind of not great as a game for Athena either, I think.But putting that aside, I think it's a good collection. The quality of life improvements are huge compared to the original games, and all the extra bells and whistles (like the whole museum) are great too. Even if Dual Destinies and Spirits of Justice aren't really my favourite, it was so worth it to finally see Apollo Justice in HD. So yeah if you enjoyed the first Ace Attorney trilogy you should give it a try

_childDocuments_.review: Another trilogy of Ace Attorney visual novels in collection with bonuses.  From the technical standpoint, the games are again a little more advanced with more animations and even animated (anime) cutscenes. They still remain text based, with absolute minimum of voice acting (as in few lines over 3 games).  The core game remains the same. There is some effort in the latter two games to make the experience smoother (fast travel can access all opened locations, list of objectives during investigation). The game is still  strictly linear, but at least some annoying hangups were avoided. New game mechanics are introduced as well, like the special abilities of each character. These are hit or miss: Appollo's search for tells can be sometimes grindy and tedious, while Athena's analysis is comparatively more complex and enjoyable. playing as an alternative to cross-examination.  The new main characters and their story are good. The other characters and the cases are in my opinion even more absurd than in previous games. This kind of humor is a staple of Ace Attorney series, but it seemed turned up two or three notches more in these games.  The games are still enjoyable, but at times the case were less about uncovering a mystery (which can be deduced fairly well from clues) and more like extracting teeth from unwilling subject (getting the rest of characters to accept it).
_childDocuments_.name: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy

_childDocuments_.review: This series never fails to subvert my expectations and engage me in every case. Although some cases are somewhat silly and a feel out of place with the storyline (SoJ 4....), all were fun and satisfying to complete. The design of things can seem ridiculous, but I think it ends up making this series unique and charming. My biggest issue with this game is the new mechanics they added that were along the lines of the psyche locks. Those were at best OK and were explained away by literal magic, but the two new ones they try to explain using "science" and are somehow allowed to be used in court. They weren't just mental blocks in people that you subconsciously overcame like the psyche locks, Apollo or Athena will literally say the witness is lying or whatever because their superpower said so and the judge just accepts it without any real evidence. I know the court system in this game is nonsense in the first place, but this was still really jarring every time it happened. But besides that, the story for almost every case is compelling, intricate and fun. I'd 100% recommend this to anyone who likes a good mystery or detective game. I wish I could play these games again for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a weaker trilogy than the original, the AJ:AA trilogy was still a (mostly) enjoyable experience. AJ:AA and Dual Destinies were both good games, introducing an interesting cast of new characters. Both prosecutors, Gavin and Blackquill, were great additions to the prosecutor roster, and Athena and Trucy turned out to be great sidekicks. Apollo was probably my least favorite main character, which is ironic given the name of this trilogy.In terms of the story, there were as many good cases as there were bad cases. Nonetheless, it was enjoyable to play through them, and the gameplay additions such as Athena's emotion matrix and the revisualization scenes were entertaining and brought some new life into the series.Sadly, the trilogy does end rather poorly with what may be the worst game in the series, Spirit of Justice. What an absolutely horrible experience, with both infuriating cases and a really despicable prosecutor. I legitimately couldn't bring myself to finish the third game; it was just too painful to play through, despite the new gameplay elements that were added.Overall, this trilogy is worth getting just for the first 2 games, for veterans of Ace Attorney and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent, definitive version of AA4 to 6 though I do have to wonder why it took so long to get a multiplatform release considering there were off-3ds mobile versions with redone art for AA4. Maybe it wasnt deemed worth it until TGAA sold well? Weird, one would think this would be done before TGAA, but I digress. Please give us the EDGEWORTH INVESTIGATIONS GAMES. CAPCOM.Apollo Justice is still excellent, but the problems with AA5 and 6 are especially evident if you play AA4 right before them. Seriously, playing this trilogy one after the other makes the drop in quality spectacular. It's immediately clear Shu Takemi did not write 5 and 6. The change in writing by having a fanboy write fanficition while takemi did TGAA combined with the mandate to keep Phoenix at the centre and make them more like 1 to 3, result in a massive regression of his character. Really. Watch the insane levels of sheer genius Phoenix displays in AA4, especially in the opening case, and tell me what we see after is the same character. The waste of potential, particularly on 5, is saddening. 4 started the idea of a troubling age of the legal system, and 5 keeps talking about this dubbing it a "dark age for the law" even though its barely used and conceptually wasted. The neat jury trial system introduced by 4, timely referencing a change in Japan's IRL system in '09, is also dropped forever.The fact that you can't just buy AA4 separately like you could on mobile irks me but I am glad 5 and 6 are being preserved despite the massive waste of potential they represent. And in the end they are passable amusements for those who wanted more like 1 to 3. My objections with the latter games aside, the collection has very neat extras for fans, it easily makes all the content accesible, including the DLC, so you can jump to whatever part in the story you want, runs on anything... It's the definitive verioin of these games. I only have one technical complaint. AA4's art looks slightly pixelated on resolutions above 1080p, but on 1440p and upwards rendering at 1080 looks better but makes the text slightly fuzzy. This can be easily solved if the devs let you render the UI at native and the game art at a different resolution.Now give me the Edgeworth games, darn it.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna do this game case by case, like with Great Ace Attorney Chronicles.AJ: 7/10----Already played this one and decided it wasn't worth a second playthrough especially since this collection is so long even with just Dual Destinies and Spirit Of Justice. From what I remember though, it's decent. Maybe I'll play it again at some point.DD: 6.5/10----This one's decent as well, not as good as AJ tho. The OST is good as always, and the fully animated cut scenes give a lot of life to a game where you otherwise have to imagine their interactions, but there's a lot to complain about. For starters, the cases are not that good. Also, the detective and the prosecutor are straight downgrades compared to their predecessors. The prosecutor is so edgy (more than Edgeworth and Godot) it feels forced, and the detective is an idiot. They did grow on me a bit in the end, but they're still low on the list. But at least the new attorney Athena Cykes is fun, probably the best new character.Case 1: Mid. I really liked Phoenix's return, and the new Payne is pretty funny. The murderer too (for a while). But the defendant is super annoying, and there's a piece of evidence that's a dumb stretch. This series has much better tutorial cases.Case 2: Pretty good. It felt nostalgic to play as Apollo again and to use his ability, and to see Trucy returning even as a minor character. I liked Athena's formal introduction to the story, and the theme for this case was a lot of fun. The murderer and his 'henchman' (sort of) are hilarious too. At first I thought one point of evidence was really dumb, but it came together nicely in the end. Also the revisualization portion is super cool. I hope it's a new mechanic!Case 3: Actual doodoo. The revisualisation of the case comes back which is good but this case sucks. Three super annoying characters are extremely obvious red herrings. One piece of evidence is a dumb play on words to pad for time that ultimately goes nowhere. The second part gets a little better with an interesting sub-plot but that's it. There's a story beat that pads for time (again). And finally, the culprit is SUPER OBVIOUS. The first two cases spoil it in a cut scene, so idk why they didn't do it here. The murderer pales in comparison to the other two, and breaks character so easily and so randomly. The murder scheme is a ridiculous stretch. The best part of this case is that the goat (not spoiling who) makes an appearance (voiced by Yuri Lowenthal aka PS4 Spider-Man in a cut scene, kinda funny). Case 4: Solid trial. The context for Trial 1 was nice, but nothing new. The defendant can be kind of annoying, though at times hilarious, and it did feel pretty rushed. But other than that this was good. The Psyche-Locks come back, which was a cool throwback. There's some actual character development. One character is an obvious red herring but he makes up for it because he's so funny. It ends on a crazy cliff hanger too. Case 5: It's ok. Starts out very strong, and has an amazing twist, but falls off because the final antagonist sucks. They try to give him some sort of nuance but it falls flat. It felt like they shoehorned in the mood detector for this exact character, or vice versa. Not to mention the plot hole that opens up with the  Again there's some really good parts especially the twist but that's the problem, only the twist is good, once the antagonist drops his act he becomes boring and ruins the tension of the trial.DLC Case: It's aight. It's not bad, it has a twist at the end that's pretty good, it's just that because it's a filler case that's 90% disconnected from the main story (10% because it takes place after case 2 but before case 3), there's nothing special about it, it's just regular Ace Attorney. The exact same premise could have taken place in any other AA game and almost nothing would have changed, save for some minor dialogue (except maybe GAA or Prof Layton or Investigations). Also, play it before the last case for story reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: I already played these games on the DS, but it's nice to have a big screen version.  The updated graphics are mostly good, though I miss the sprite work that made Apollo Justice look great.  After playing through these a second time, my opinion of Apollo Justice has improved, while I enjoyed Dual Destinies less.  Apollo Justice has several flaws with characterization and plot, but I appreciate that they tried to experiment.  Apollo didn't get enough development, which is a shame since it's his game.  I didn't mind "hobo" Phoenix and bitter Ema, however, since both of them went through serious career setbacks.  The new prosecutor Gavin Klavier is fun, but kind of a pushover though I love his character design. The tutorial case is excellent and the best of its kind in the series.  In contrast, the third case is my least favorite in the series due to its terrible logic and repeating animations, so Apollo Justice is the epitome of a mixed bag game.  Dual Destinies introduces Athena Cykes, who I find rather endearing even though she hasn't truly had a chance to shine in the series yet.  The real star of this game is Simon Blackquill, a snarky emo samurai who adds a ton of humor, especially when he banters with Athena and the Judge and sics Taka on people.  This game also has one of the most messed up cases, which is why it's the only entry with a Mature rating, though weirdly it's the easiest game with the most simplified mechanics.  The hand holding and overall lack of difficulty is my main gripe with this game, though the excellent bonus case adds back a few things like forensic science.  Spirit of Justice is the longest Ace Attorney game, though that's largely due to the addition of many animations.  I liked most of them, but some go on for too long and make the cases tedious.  Half of the cases take place in the fictional country of Khura'in, where defense attorneys are subject to one of the stupidest laws ever.  As a result, the stakes are a lot higher in this game than with the previous entries, though it feels a bit ridiculous.  I did, however, enjoy the new setting and the characters overall, though they went a bit too heavy on the pun names.  The bonus case is sweet with a really cool setting, but not as great as the Dual Destinies bonus case.  One of my favorite cases of all time is in this game and it involves Trucy, so Spirit of Justice is worth playing for this one alone.  Lastly, Prosecutor Nahyuta sucks and I wished that Taka had clawed his eyes out but that would give this game an M rating.  Overall, I'd say that this is the weakest Ace Attorney bundle, but there is still plenty to love so I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Apollo Justice: I really can't understand why this game catches so much heat. I loved this game. It has one of the best opening cases in the series. Case 2 while yes, isn't anything special, it's still a good case with a mildly annoying defendant. Case 3 deserves the hate it gets... I'm not gonna sugarcoat it. The leaps in logic for the defendant, the excruciating repeated video scenes, and the drawn out conclusion are all awful. Case 4 is certainly unique, but the way it wraps up the game is amazing. As for the game in its entirety, great music, mostly endearing cast, and overall pretty good writing (not you case 3). As for some of the characters: Apollo taking center stage was in fact pretty controversial, but I'm gonna be honest I like him better than Phoenix, he felt a lot more real. Klavier doesn't need much, his theme is great, and having a Prosecutor who wasn't a tool at pretty much any point through the entire game was a nice touch. As for our "new" detective Ema Skye, while this is probably the worst state she's been in as a character, I still really enjoyed seeing her back, and she's very far from being a bad character in this game. Kristoph is a fantastic character, but I won't spoil why here.Dual Destinies: This game has incredibly high highs, and God awful lows. Let's start with the biggest change overall, the 3D models. No this doesn't make the game better or worse. While I think Ace Attorney has more charm using the 2D sprites, the 3D models are undeniably an upgrade whether or not you like them better. As for the story... I'd argue the best case in the game doesn't even contribute to the main story... It's the special episode, which kinda makes it sound like cases 1-5 are bad, and they aren't. Well, except for case 2. Case 1 isn't anything special, it's just an average tutorial case. Case 2 was the first time throughout my experience of the mainline games where I genuinely considered just skipping to the next case. It's overly long, most of the characters are just downright headaches for ZERO reason, and whats more, they all just seem like their ENTIRE personality is their gimmick. Don't get me started on the total crapshoot logic they try to push. Case 3 had an incredible cast to go along with a pretty enjoyable story. While I'm not a total super fan of the whole "Dark Age of the Law" arc they went with in this game, this case was the one that actually got me to be decently into the story. Case 4 (and I'll loop 5 into this as well since they're pretty well connected) has a fair issue with being pretty long winded at times, but I can look past it thanks to it being an engaging story and enjoyable characters (albeit some of them overusing their character gimmicks at times). Some characters I'll mention from this game: Bobby Fulbright, while being my least favorite detective in the main series, (not a dig, that just spotlights how much I enjoy Gumshoe and Ema) was an absolute joy to have on screen. If there's one character group CAPCOM has yet to screw up on, it's the detective role. Simon Blackquill is a fantastic character and a great new addition to the cast, but I can't lie his "Silence!" interjection started to get a little old by the end of the game (please don't hate me). Athena Cykes was a welcome addition but I can't say I like or dislike her...because she does NOT get enough screentime to really develop. (Maybe SOJ will fix this......    :)  )Spirit of Justice: Ehh... I initially heard people say that Spirit of Justice was sort of like if Dual Destinies didn't have as many problems...I honestly see it as the opposite. First off, was giving Apollo ANOTHER backstory really needed?? As for the main story, this has been BY FAR the most sluggish I've ever felt playing an Ace Attorney game. We're headed to Khurain and everyone here hates defense attorneys so much they want them dead...Really??? This series is no stranger to absurd plots and motives, but this felt so random and just leads me to believe it was like a last minute decision. Getting into the cases, I mentioned how 5-2 almost got me skip to 5-3... 6-1 actually forced me to mute the game audio all together. This is easily my least favorite case in the ENTIRE series. You wanna talk about dragging on, repetitive dialogue, and leaping in logic? 6-1 is the poster child! Case 2 is a breath of fresh air, especially after the disaster that just took place. Athena and Trucy get some screentime, the plot is interesting, side characters are entertaining. My only gripe is that the trial section apparently just forgot to insert a to be continued screen. I get through dialogue pretty fast, and usually don't screw up presenting evidence, and this section still took me over 2 HOURS. I don't dislike long cases overall, 2-4 is one of my favorites in the series, and it's pretty frickin long. 6-2 however, for one, isn't a finale Case and doesn't even have THAT much relevance to the game's story. It basically just introduces Nahyuta (more on him later). Case 3 is alright overall, nothing really bad I can say about it, Maya returns, story flows good enough. Case 4 gives Athena some actual screentime (and is the end of that lol) so it's already good in my book. Then you add in some Simon Blackquill and you've got a really well put together case that actually builds off the previous game's development (by this game, and Dual Destinies for that matter, this seems to be a lost art for the most part). Case 5 is ok, it's really not anything special in terms of finale cases in my book, but I think that's just because I don't care for this games over-arching story in the first place. It's not bad by any means, I just didn't really experience the same level of payoff that I'm sure others would. The special case for this game is probably my favorite of the game (I won't let my bias get the better of me, it's not the best one). It has a good story, and it's literally just a giant throwback to the original game. Phoenix takes the defense, Edgeworth takes up the prosecution, and Larry screws everything up on the witness stand. What's not to love? I'm not a huge fan of the major characters this game introduces. Rayfa is a pretty good edition, she's probably the only "I hate defense attorneys character I enjoyed. Queen Ga'ran is one of the most underwhelming villains in the series in my opinion. Nahyuta has got to be the worst prosecutor I've ever seen, he's boring, relies on his gimmicks more than any actual development until he snaps during the finale, and his random voices lines during trials where he starts chanting are just downright annoying. Dhurke is an odd one. I don't dislike the idea behind him, but he suffers from the same problem as Clay from Dual Destinies. That being, here's a character that actually has this giant history with Apollo. Why? Well we needed you to feel invested in his story more so we drew this really awkward and uneven line connecting him to Apollo's new backstory.So yeah, I recommend this Trilogy, a LOT. However, I think these three installments fall very short of what the series has accomplished in both the past, (The Phoenix Wright Trilogy, and heck, even the Investigation Duology thanks to the sequel absolutely carrying it), and what it ended up accomplishing in the future, (The Great Ace Attorney Duology). This is by no means bad, not even close. But it's very clear this trilogy is littered with flaws, whereas the other installments are just more so sprinkled with them. If I had to rank the games overall:This Trilogy Only: AJAA > PWAA:DD > PWAA:SoJThe Mainline Series: 3>1>4>5>2>6The Entire Series: AAI2 > TGAA2 > PWAA:T&T > TGAA > PWAA > AJAA > PWAA:DD > PWAA:JFA > AAI > PWAA:SoJ

_childDocuments_.review: While this game certainly checks off all the usual marks like really bad puns, the most exaggerated characters you can imagine, and the iconic voice lines.… as someone whose only brush with the series was the Phoenix Wright trilogy I would recommend anyone but die hard fans of the series to pass on this.Compared to the first trilogy the "puzzles" in this one feel condescending.You know that moment when you figure something out, and you feel really good about figuring this out without getting a hint from the game? Yeah, this game often just doesn't give you that satisfaction.Often times when it could make the player feel smart about knowing something it just.… doesn't ask at all and presents the thing without any prompt whatsoever.Or when there's something that was okay-ish visible and that you could've figured out, it dumps about five dialogue pieces at you that each hint at the one thing.I guess a way to sum up this series is that one part of the special that I just finished so it's really fresh in my mind.Towards the end of a case you will often enter a "thinking" sequence where you have to figure out what really happened by answering a few questions that bring you to a result that "turns the case upside down" as they like to say.This should be a challenge.This is, after all, a game of deceit, riddles, and intrigue.So when you're presented with a question and three possible answers it's imperative to make it at least vaguely hard to answer.In the very last case of this trilogy, the SoJ special one of those questions is what the murder weapon is, something that was established within the first three minutes of the case both by Ema telling you as well as the follow-up autopsy report.This isn't hard to answer if you've paid the least bit attention to the case, or alternatively if you just go to the court record and read the autopsy report.There is no puzzle there.The first trilogy excelled at giving you a case that's hard to solve, with twists and turns.Now you get this one that still has twists (that can be seen from a mile away) and turns (that are impossible to predict not because they're unexpected but because the writing goes to lengths to hide the information from you that normally would be accessible but would render the story plain boring).I would like to refer to  which pretty much explains why it feels satisfying to have a story where the solution is visible if you look hard enough, but it's very much boring to go through a lengthy story that has a complicated make-up but only because it deliberately doesn't tell you things.I'm not saying the game is bad in its entirety.I particularly liked the Dhurke case of Spirit of Justice, i.e. game 6 episode 5 (yes, in Japanese the games are just numbered instead of named with the first trilogy comprising 1-3 and this one 4-6) because at some point you were able to figure out what the ♥♥♥♥ was going on to an extent. When he said he can't tell you something because it would betray someone you could know what he's talking about. You could piece it together a while before the game told you. And yes, the game more or less told you, without any fancy riddles or hard to guess answers.Of course I play a game with puzzles like this to feel smart about solving it.That's why Portal map creation and later workshop content took off so well, because people need new puzzles that puzzle them.It wasn't because of the first chamber that literally went "hey, put that cube on the receptacle".Sadly every single game in this trilogy have a strong habit of doing the latter whenever they could let you solve the puzzle.No matter how great the soundtrack is, how many in-jokes there are, how well they actually managed to put the 2D feel in a 3D render and how awesome the anime cutscenes are, the game feels condescending to me, and nothing can fix that.TL;DR: This game feels more like a visual novel than the first trilogy and I mean this in the worst possible way.If you like puzzles go play the first trilogy and then just stop. Trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: To get it out of the way up front, the Apollo Justice trilogy is generally regarded as being the lesser of the three Ace Attorney collections. Some of its cases go basically nowhere, it feels like they didn't really decide on it being the "Apollo Justice Trilogy" until the third game, Dual Destinies has some questionable character decisions, and frankly these days these games are probably more well known for that meme about the clown girl than anything else. But with all that said, being the "lesser" of what a lot of people would consider some of the best mystery games of all time is a distinction that only sounds bad on paper. They're still good games in their own right, even if you have to temper your expectations slightly compared to the rest, and the first game is severely underrated. In terms of port quality it's generally as good as you'd expect, but in particular (at least to my eyes) the updated 2D art of Apollo Justice looks a lot nicer than the original trilogy's HD release.Regarding the bonus content (which was mostly what I'm here for for now, since I've already played these games multiple times on the DS/3DS), it isn't as in-depth as The Great Ace Attorney's unused music vault and annotated concept art, but there is a lot of concept art for each character, alongside the usual suspects like the soundtrack and movie players and a silly animation studio that plays out like a more high quality version of that old objection maker website from the early 2000s. The Asinine Attorney bonus episodes unfortunately once again didn't make the cut, along with the Japan-exclusive collab costumes, but all of the other DLC is in, and it's still plenty content-complete and bonus-rich enough to consider this the definitive version of the games.

_childDocuments_.review: This trilogy is kind of weird.For people who don’t know, the original director of Ace Attorney made only the first game of this trilogy, and after that, Takeshi Yamazaki, the director of the Investigations games, directed the second and third games. So, the main problem people have with this trilogy is that it’s called the Apollo Justice Trilogy. None of the games really feel like they belong to Apollo Justice. In the first game, while he is the protagonist, he’s more like an observer of the events than a force that pushes the story forward. I have really mixed feelings about the second game of the trilogy, Dual Destinies. If I were to rate each game individually, it would probably be at the top of my list, but to be honest, it’s really self-contained, just like the third game. It’s underwhelming in this sense because, before that, the games had a narrative and arcs that could stretch across multiple games. And now we have what we have: Phoenix in the first game is a mastermind manipulator who’s always two steps ahead, and in Dual Destinies and Spirit of Justice, he’s the goofy character we know and love. In the first game, Apollo is a weird but well-meaning attorney, in the second he’s an edgelord, and in the third, he gets an actual arc and closure, so I guess that’s cool. I think the reason this happened is because nobody really expected this to be a cohesive trilogy. Takeshi Yamazaki didn’t even think about or want to work on another game after Dual Destinies.That said, while the story is a little weak compared to other games, it’s still REALLY good overall and has some of the best moments in the series. While it’s true that Apollo gets sidelined in favor of Phoenix and Athena, I would say that Athena is really worth it—she’s awesome. And having three playable attorneys means three times more interesting mechanics, which I think are really engaging. For all the minuses of these games, I would still highly recommend them. They’re really good. This trilogy is the perfect middle ground of all the games. There are fewer peak Ace Attorney moments, but there are also fewer cringe-worthy, weird, and dragged-out moments.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as tightly written and less narrative coherent then the original trilogy, nether the less Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy provides an interesting continuation of the Ace Attorney franchise, as this is a collection of 3 games, it makes sense to review them all by themselves.Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney - Story wise, this game has one of the most interesting set-ups in the entire franchise, 7 years after Trials and Tribulations you play as Apollo a new lawyer in a rapidly changing legal system linked with Phoenix Wright, a legendary attorney whose been disbarred, chilling stuff and the cases where it's the focus are amazing... the cases where it doesn't though lag a bit, both of which have interesting set ups but falling short in execution, for fans of the first 3 games I'd make the comparison to Justice for All as both of these games have amazing highs but really poor lows, also the music ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slapsAce Attorney: Dual Destinies - I wanted to like this one so much but it's just poor, it certainly has interesting moments and ideas but most of them feel at the cost of what was brought up in the previous game, it also feels like the writing quality takes a hit relying way more on pop culture references and being way more annoying with it's arching story beats (You can't go 5 seconds without hearing the phrase "Dark Age of the Law" or "Force their Biggest Smiles"), Dual Destines does have probably one of my favourite supporting cast of any game in the AA franchise with fun and emotional Athena and "takes no ♥♥♥♥" Blackquill, also the music ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slaps.Ace Attorney: Spirit of Justice - Rounding out the collection is the game I feel the most "meh" about in the entire series, a decent game that makes strives to fix the story issues of AA:DD giving one of the more epic-feeling over-aching plots in the series and the case quality (beside case 4 imo) is one of the more consistently good ones in the franchise, however, the characters take a considerable nose-dive in quality for me, some of the one-off characters are alright and I like Rahfa but I find Wright and Justice to feel and lot less interesting now and the wacky characters feel too reserved, you also cannot pay me to care about Sahdmadhi my god he's a boring prick, also the music ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slapsAs for the collection original content it's a fantastic celebration of the Ace Attorney franchise in the 2010's with original art music and a Objection.lol like animation viewer, it's a fantastic thing to see and should be a standard for any collection celebrating older titles, my only complaint is where was any of this love in Phoenix Wright Trilogy????All in all, despite not being a massive fan of these 3 games I would 100% recommend Apollo Justice Trilogy, this franchise is one of my favourite in the entire gaming landscape and the absolute goat in terms of visual novels, although please consider playing through Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney Trilogy if you want to get into the franchise for the first time.Also the music ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slaps.

_childDocuments_.review: The second trilogy in the Ace Attorney series, this collection picks up where the first left off in spectacular fashion. While I would say this trilogy is more disjointed narratively than the first trilogy, due to having to juggle significantly more characters than the last, it retains a compelling set of cases and overarching narratives throughout.In fact, this game has some of best cases in the series period, with Spirit of Justice and Apollo Justice having absolute bangers for their respective finales, with generally more engaging culprits (Though not necessarily prosecutors) than the originals. Oh, and the soundtrack is fire too.You can easily start the series right here if you're new and just want to get caught up to speed, or you can start with the original trilogy. Ultimately, it doesn't matter too much, as the new trilogy is designed for new players to be able to jump in without needing context from prior entries (One being the original trilogy anyway). That said, the last game in this trilogy, Spirit of Justice, does make some callbacks, so I would at least recommend you play the first two games in this trilogy before that one.All in all, this is an absolutely fantastic collection of some of the most consistently engaging and creative murder mystery games in the business, in a genre that this series pretty much created and to this day retains a sole monopoly over. If that's not an endorsement, I don't know what is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a hesitant recommend for me. I love the ace attorney series so I thought I would enjoy this trilogy immediately, but there is a lot going on here that honestly made me almost not recommend this game.To begin with these games are a heavy shakeup of the original trilogy, a whole new cast is constantly presented and the main focus is being put away from Phoenix wright towards his new apprentices. These new characters are generally quite enjoyable. The general story lines they have are fine and sometimes actually really enjoyable, the problem stems that everything you might have enjoyed about the previous trilogy feels dumbed down here. I will write an entire summary on it all in the bottom but I will first go step for step through each game. I am avoiding spoilers as much as possible in this review while still giving a general idea of my opinion on each game.Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney (4): The 4th main installment of ace attorney is the game I enjoyed the most of this collection, it feels like more of the original trilogy and the story here is generally fine, there are some moments that make made me feel the story is incomplete or that some things just didn't really make sense. But overall the gameplay mechanics, the story beats, the excellent music and art are all high quality and what I would expect of an ace attorney game. I loved the 2nd trail of this game and the way the game tries to tie everything up towards the end is a cool way of telling the story. I loved the prosecution of this game and I love the dynamic between the main character and their assistant. Overall I honestly could recommend this trilogy on sale just for this game alone. I can see why some people wouldn't like it but to me it was a nice change of pace from the previous games while still maintaining the quality of that original trilogy.Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies (5): The 5th main installment left me worrying at first. The game moves to a 3D art style with animated cutscenes and a bunch of new characters again. It gave me megaman X legacy collection 2 vibes, where it feels like they made so many games that they ended up just throwing stuff at the wall hoping it would stick. And while my worrying was overblown it still left a lot to be desired. The new mechanics and the new characters themselves didn't bother me, in fact towards the end of the game I really liked all of them, I also liked some of the trials. But going through the first 2 trials nearly made me quit this entire trilogy. The biggest problem I had was that I didn't feel like I was making choices, the game is extremely scared of losing the player, as a result it constantly gives you extremely obvious hints on what should be done. Not only that but the game doesn't want you to be confused. Ever. It feels like every trial everyone repeats the same things over and over again, and meanwhile there is a bunch of big background plot stuff going on and the game also makes sure it repeats it every trial over and over again. The anime cutscenes are cool but also often feel badly executed, stuff that is supposed to leave an impact just falls flat and it sometimes feels overly dramatic for no reason. In the end you start feeling extremely fatigued, there are some trials that still feel pretty good, and to me this game got better and better the more I played it, but that overwhelming sense of repetition and handholding stayed with me this entire game. Its a game that feels like it wanted to try doing a lot of new risky things but didn't always know how to execute on those things. Those new things generally ended up strong but still sometimes left something to be desired.  Its worth a playthrough but I wouldn't recommend the entire trilogy just for this.Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice (6): This is the one game in this collection that almost made me not recommend this entire trilogy. Its not that its bad, but it feels creatively bankrupt. All my problems of the previous games return here, but now the story and characters ended up frustrating me so much that I genuinely didn't feel like I was enjoying my time. I only finished it because I was hoping that I would end up liking it as much as Dual destinies towards the end. What makes it feel so bad? Not only does it feel handholdy and repetitive, but every step of the way I felt like I knew exactly what was happening in 80 % of the trials. From the motive, to who did it to how it was done, I felt like during the investigation I was able to figure it out almost immediately. The prosecution in this game is incredibly boring, it feels like they repeat the same lines and are rude for no reason except because ''I am bad guy''. It doesn't feel like the story is written by humans but by guidelines on how to create a ''good'' trial, as a result there are almost no surprises and it feels like you already know exactly how to build the puzzle but have to wait for the game to ask you to place the puzzle piece it wants you to play. But my frustrations didn't end there, I also felt like all characters just end up playing up their reaction a ton to create drama, it didn't feel like these characters I have seen grow in the last 5 games learned anything from the difficulties they have faced, instead of giving interesting dilemmas the game just forces drama on you to make you feel like the trial is important. It constantly tries to force the main characters to be relevant again, and that is disappointing to me because ace attorney has a giant cast of interesting characters that have matured and could offer interesting trials and perspectives, but instead we have to deal with the same like 7 characters these games love bringing back. In no other game did I feel that nostalgia baiting as much as in this game. In the end I didn't feel like I played an ace attorney game, I felt like I was playing a fan fiction of someone who was given very strict rules on how to write an ace attorney story. The risks 5 took feel absent here, as a result the qualities of that game feel lacking while the mistakes still feel present. The only thing I can say is that the new trial gimmick is pretty interesting and I liked what it offered to the trials. I would only recommend this game to someone that desperately wants more ace attorney, otherwise this game offers very little interesting or new.Summary and conclusion: I went into these games with high expectations. I loved the first trilogy and both great ace attorney games. Sadly I felt that ace attorney 5 and 6 left a lot to be desired, the further I went into this trilogy the more I felt disappointed. There is a lot still to love, most of the story lines here are at least acceptable, the art and music are still fantastic, and once the game has a good trial going it will completely absorb all of your attention. But in ace attorney 5 and especially 6 there will be a lot moments where you feel like the game doesn't respect you as a player, it doesn't trust you to make your own conclusions, it repeats information extremely often, gives you extremely guided information and often feels like it doesn't understand what it wants to do with its story anymore. I loved ace attorney 4 and there are a lot of things I enjoy about 5, 6 is the only game I wouldn't recommend. Overall I would still recommend this trilogy cause of 4 and 5, I love this series and I feel like these entries still add something new and interesting to this series.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who had played the original trilogy and Apollo Justice as a kid and then dropped off the series for years, I can say I had no particular nostalgia for this trilogy. The experience was fresh, it was unique and it reached the same heights as the OG AA trilogy did. In some aspects it can even surpass it. The convenience options and customization make the game experience far smoother than even in the previous trilogy release. Text box transparancy, text speed, even a story mode option that lets the game play itself so you can just enjoy it passively... it has it all. That's not even mentioning the bonus content, like the art gallery, the orchestral mode and the animation studio that allows you to play around with the poses of every character in the game.Now for the individual titles. - is the same game I played as a kid, but looking far more gorgeous and crisp. It is in fact better than I remembered it and I think people can appreciate it more now with some hindsight. Best tutorial case in the series, no contest. Apollo and Trucy have a great sibling like dynamic and hobo Phoenix Wright is a menace. Love it.As the only 2D entry in this trilogy it feels a bit like the odd one out, but as far as sprite based games go, this is the best looking in the franchise. This wasn't a simple resize job, the art was manually improved to work in better resolutions. - is the first 3D entry in the main line and boy does it show even in this remaster. Story wise I think it is far better than its reputation and the new attorney joining the Wright Anything Agency, Athena Cykes, is an absolute darling that improves every case she is in. The spectacle of the cases has been dialed up to 11, mostly thanks to its new 3D look and the anime cutscenes. It may not always hit the deeper writing of the games before, but it is a wild ride with many memorable and quotable moments. Blackquill is my favorite prosecutor in the series.The DD models are still very rudimentary and the new devs were still finding their footing, but the game still looks far better than on the 3DS obviously. Phoenix may be some kind of flesh golem, but his yaoi hands were preserved for pointing prowess.  - Despite its title this is very much an Apollo game just as much as a Phoenix entry and that's its strength. It rounds off Apollo's arc beautifully while also having the most daring and intense narrative of the franchise. The return of Maya and Ema is very much welcome and the cases all seem to have gotten the appropiate amount of time each, which means some will be very short, while some will be long and intense. The stakes have never felt higher and the character work is a marvel. Only praise from me.The 3D tech in this game has substantially improved and every model has been polished and made to shine. The 3DS game already looked amazing, but this is just on another level. In some regard I think SoJ looks better than even The Great Ace Attorney games. Bolstered by the best OST in the series, there is really no doubt in my mind that the trilogy is worth it just for this game already. : This trilogy is quite based, I assure you.

_childDocuments_.review: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney Trilogy presents new features and memorable faces, it's hard to pass for an Ace Attorney fan. Even though it's called the Apollo Justice Trilogy, it also revolves around Phoenix Wright and Athena Cykes (the latter for the latter 2 games). Let's start with the first game!A dark age of law has been ennui. Prosecutors are corrupt and would try to do anything to win. Defense attorneys use forged evidence to stake a victory, and the worst offense yet... Apollo Justice's two pronged cowlick... like seriously, that's a crime and a half from the fashion police. Joking aside, this game lets you play in the shoes of, you guessed it, Apollo Justice. He's in a similar position to Phoenix Wright, wanting to be a lawyer to protect the innocent. But it isn't a lawyer game without a cute assistant, and Trucy Wright, Phoenix's adopted daughter, fits the bill. Gameplay mechanics are fundamentally the same as your beloved Ace Attorney games, examine rooms, question people, become a lawyer, etc. etc. The gameplay mechanic used in this game is Apollo's Bracelet. Apollo is able to identify a person's unique tell if the bracelet reacts to it. Say, a person subconsciously scratching an area that they were hit before. This game mechanic, as well as Phoenix's Magatama will carry on in subsequent games. Also, the prosecutor for the game, Klavier Gavin, is probably my number 1 prosecutor now. Stories, while interesting, don't retain as much rememberability as compared to other cases. On top of that, usually when I play the games, I need a walkthrough because I'm a big dumbo, this game I found that I used it less, more logical. I also feel it's easier. Anyways, solid entry to the start of the trilogy. Phoenix is back as a lawyer. Oh look, he brought along a really f*cking annoying person, Athena Cykes. She's a young lawyer who studied the psychology side of law (hence Cykes like Psych), and will use it effectively in court cases. Magatama and Bracelet for Phoenix and Apollo respectively are now limited to use in investigations. Good news though, we moved to 3D character models! The game is pretty solid, and sees the return of another great prosecutor, Miles Edgeworth. But, the prosecutor of this game is also one that shouldn't be trifled with. Put behind bars because he was accused of a murder he never committed, it's Simon Blackquill! A samurai-esque emo aesthetic prosecutor, he knows how to shake up a witness. Fortunately, he's kept on a leash by everyone's favorite detective, Bobby Fullbright! Although, something's fishy with that guy. Good cases, great execution on investigation, although a shame that psychology was always used in every case.Let's go back to the roots, back to Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney... let us remember who was with us all along... and let her appear in the final game to end the trilogy. Maya Fey has returned! Well, kinda... 3 of the 6 cases uses a unique law feature: Divination Seance, a ritual which used to determine the accused fate, to see the last vision the victim had before dying. Unfortunately, the village of Khura'in has a strict policy, such that if lawyers fail to defend the accused, they will be subject to the same penalty as the accused... usually death. Fortunately, you're not just any 2 bit lawyer. You're Phoenix Wright/Apollo Justice/Athena Cykes, you can handle any defense case to find the truth!3 games bundled into one, this game is everything an Ace Attorney fan would enjoy. Put on a distinctly-colored suit, show everyone your attorney badge, and make sure you slam the table as hard as you can before saying the iconic word:

_childDocuments_.review: I had an absolute blast playing these games for the first time, I'm so glad Capcom brought them to PC with this collection. If you've played the Phoenix Wright Trilogy you know what you're getting into already. I can almost guarantee if you enjoyed those games you'll enjoy these too. (And if you haven't played those games, go play them first. I highly recommend them as well!)I know these 3 games in particular have a bit of a poor reputation among a lot of Ace Attorney fans, but there's really still a ton to love about them, especially if you're going in blind. 3 games for $50 is well worth the price in my opinion. You can see from my playtime that it took me over 100 hours to complete all 3 games (though you can probably subtract a few hours for a combination of dealing with game crashes in AJ:AA, plus me just being generally kinda bad at them). A few final notes:1. I did experience game crashes on launch and during a specific mandatory section in AJ:AA. The on-launch crash is an easy fix, the other one less so. If you experience either of these issues, other people have posted solutions on the Steam discussion page that will hopefully help you.2. Play the special case of Dual Destines between cases 2 and 3. The special case for Spirit of Justice actually goes after case 5 like you'd expect.3. _childDocuments_.review: I first thought this game was just Phoenix Wright but 10-15% worse. Apollo is just Phoenix but slightly worse, Trucy is just Maya but slightly worse, Klavier is just Edgeworth but slightly worse, etc. (Although I am a pretty big fan of Ema as the replacement for Gumshoe.) However, I really liked how the final case in this game tied together plot points from the first three cases, unlike the games in the original trilogy in which often only the first and last case of each game is relevant, aside from a few extremely minor points from the, for lack of a better word, "filler" cases. The last case in this game also deepened my appreciation for the "replacement" characters, even if I still ultimately think their original counterparts are better. In the end, I still think this is the worst game in the series up to this point, but that still means it's great, and I think it's almost on par with Justice For All.Apollo Justice: 8/10In many ways, worse than other entries in the series up to this point. The pacing throughout most of the cases is horrible; it feels like, in previous games, these cases would have been 70-80% as long as they are here. This is especially egregious in the second and third cases. Also, many of the side characters' defining traits are less quirky and fun like they are in previous games, and more just annoying. On top of that, I felt much less investment in the storyline of this Ace Attorney game compared to previous titles, and the culprit of the overarching mystery is simply not interesting. Still, at the end of the day, the core loop of investigating and pointing out contradictions is entertaining, and the mysteries on a case-by-case basis are more complex than previous cases in the series, in an engaging way, so I can't hate the game too much. It's disappointing as an Ace Attorney game, but not overall.Dual Destinies: 6/10It feels like I should like this game so much more than I do—the overarching storyline is awe-inspiring and incredible, many of the new characters are equally well-written as previous characters from the series who are mostly isolated to one title (especially Princess Rayfa), and I really like the political focus of this game's story—but there are still some issues that this new group of writers carries over from Dual Destinies. Primarily, the pacing is what drives down my enjoyment of Spirit of Justice. If this was a tighter read, about 20% shorter, I could easily bump up my rating by a point, but unfortunately, there are many instances where it just feels like a drag to get to the next plot point, as one character after another endlessly reiterates the same point. Additionally, there were two cases that were noticeably weaker than the rest in this game. They weren't nearly as better as the second cases from Dual Destinies, but both the first and fourth case in this game felt a bit lackluster compared to the others. Lastly, on a smaller note, I'm not a huge fan of the new insights feature; it feels like it could have worked much better, but its clunky implementation makes it bit frustrating to use. Overall, Spirit of Justice has excellent points all throughout, and feels like somewhat of a return to form from Dual Destinies, but it sadly also has a major pacing issue that hampers my enjoyment of it.Spirit of Justice: 7/10Overall, the second Ace Attorney is definitely weaker than the original trilogy. Admittedly, it would be difficult to live up to the masterpiece that is the first trilogy, but it still feels like the execution on this second trilogy could have been better. If you are a fan of the first trilogy, I would still definitely recommend this—I was able to find a lot of enjoyment from it, and I think you could, too—just don't expect it to be as excellent as the first trilogyApollo Justice: 8/10Dual Destinies: 6/10Spirit of Justice: 7/10Whole Trilogy: 7/10

Though he is certainly not as cutthrotting as Edgeworth in first game, nor vengheance seeking like Franziska in second. except... that makes fighting him in court less memorable, which is issue number 2. _childDocuments_.review: The trilogy's narrative is its crowning achievement. Each case is a novel waiting to be devoured, filled with twists that would make even the most seasoned mystery aficionados pause in awe. With his unwavering determination and innate sense of justice, Apollo Justice is a protagonist who grows on you and with you. The supporting cast is equally memorable, offering a spectrum of personalities that range from the hilariously eccentric to the deeply tragic, all contributing to a rich, immersive experience.The gameplay mechanics are a refined blend of the series' classic formula and innovative new features that elevate the experience. Thanks to the clever use of the DS's touchscreen and microphone, cross-examinations, evidence gathering, and courtroom showdowns feel more interactive and impactful. The 'Perceive' system in trials adds a layer of psychological depth, challenging players to analyze the facts and the subtleties of human behavior.Graphically, the trilogy is a standout, with vibrant character designs and beautifully rendered environments that breathe life into the world of Apollo Justice. The soundtrack deserves equal praise, with compositions that perfectly complement the highs and lows of the narrative, enhancing every moment of triumph, tension, and heartache.The Apollo Justice Trilogy is more than a collection of games; it's a landmark in storytelling and game design. It's a testament to the power of video games as a medium for conveying complex narratives and evoking deep emotional responses. Whether you're a long-time fan of the Ace Attorney series or a newcomer to the courtroom drama genre, this trilogy is an essential addition to your gaming library.In conclusion, the Apollo Justice Trilogy is a masterpiece that redefines what visual novels and adventure games can be. Its compelling story, engaging gameplay, and unforgettable characters set a new standard for the genre. This is not just a game you play; it's an experience you live, breathe, and ponder long after the credits roll. I cannot recommend it highly enough – it's an absolute must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has already experienced this trilogy, I can say without a doubt that these 3 games are all amazing! By the way, these games are so surprisingly replayable, even if they are linear visual novels. The cases are way too wacky to remember everything like the back of your hand whenever you replay, so I always get that great feeling of cornering a suspect pretty much every time I end up playing this series! name: Bleak Sword DX
detailed_description: Pure, thrilling, and wonderfully cruel, Bleak Sword DX is a dark fantasy action game challenging warriors to fight their way through compact, cursed diorama battlefields. Newly updated for PC, Bleak Sword DX expands on the critically acclaimed Apple Arcade version with elegant controls, three new game modes, and multiple gameplay and graphical improvements. Through twelve tense and deeply atmospheric chapters, you must lift the curse of the legendary Bleak Sword by striking down all manner of horrifying creatures across an oppressive world wielding fierce weaponry and powerful magic. This striking experience is scored by award-winning composer Jim Guthrie, with sound provided by famed designer Joonas Turner. BRUTAL NEW CHAPTERS DX includes all original Bleak Sword chapters plus the three DLC chapters complete with new level and enemy layouts. UNPREDICTABLE ADVENTURE A brand new Randomizer campaign modifier throws you into a remixed version of the original game where leveling up or facing bosses in order is not guaranteed. UNTOUCHABLE Jump into the brand new Boss Run gauntlet and face all 12 in-game bosses back to back with only one health bar. Make one wrong step and prepare to pay dearly! ENDLESS BATTLES The soul-crushing Arena mode throws you into a gladiator-style fight for survival. Fight increasingly difficult enemies and become a Bleak Sword legend. DYNAMIC GAMEPLAY IMPROVEMENTS New attacks, parries, and counters complement a streamlined control system designed specifically for PC & console, while enhanced enemy AI makes them more unpredictable. STUNNING GRAPHICAL ENHANCEMENTS New post-processing effects, adaptive depth of field, and a series of filters give Bleak Sword DX a fresh lick of paint, while particle effects, foliage, and weather enhancements bring a new level of atmosphere and immersion to the world.

_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Sword DX

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly put, Bleak Sword is really aesthetic—the random flashes of thunder, the eerie sway of the camera over the hand-crafted diorama below, the 3D/pixel mix, the satisfying kill animations and the music (done by Jim Guthrie!) all add to make an immersive grimdark fantasy setting where the hero must surmount impossible odds to rid the world of the evil which plagues it. That being said when I finished the game, that immersion I had when playing through the first couple chapters was already long gone. What happened in between? Well, what was a fun fast paced adventure became a grindy loveless chore.First off, the game needlessly has RPG elements which subtract from the game play. When finishing an encounter you are rewarded with EXP and upon level up you can increase up one of the three core stats; . This is the first issue:  Without high enough attack, enemies will pile up upon the screen and overwhelm the player, not to mention even with high defence and HP, you're still getting killed in only a few hits. That brings me to issue two, after combat you have a chance (15%ish) to receive an item. These items may increase your Attack or Defence, or be a consumable health item. While the items are no offender on their own (except for the items that provide permanent stat increases [which incentivize grinding]), their rarity makes them sorta lame. Especially since how the death mechanic works:  This is the single most grind-encouraging feature in the game and is INFURIATING. It adds such an artificial/chore-like level of difficulty in a game that is supposed to be fast-paced and fun. Almost level up'ed and died? Better grind those easy levels again. Lost your cool +3/+3 ring? You'll probably never see it again.However, upon dying you are presented with an opportunity, if you can first-try clear the level you died on without the items you had, you can reclaim your lost items and EXP. If you fail they are gone for good. While this feature is innocuous and seems kinda fun, it is actually a game-able mechanic which also promotes grinding:  Absolutely nonsensical. This also makes HP by far the worst stat to upgrade because it does not increase the amount healed between levels, just the cap itself.Besides the RPG elements, how is the combat? Well, its pretty good. The combat consists of attacking (which uses stamina), rolling and parrying (which dont use stamina). Combat is fluid and I-frames often feel generous. The early game really shines, and enemies really offer a fun experience when you learn to time your rolls and parries. Parrying specifically is one of the harder skills to master but it is incredibly rewarding/satisfying because you can stagger your enemy and unleash attacks that deal extra damage (and cost no stamina!). You probably think that learning to parry is the key to success:  WHY???? This was the single most ennauseating design choice this game could have. Why have this incredible mechanic and then slowly phase it out in favor of rolling like a hooligan all over a grim dark diorama???Speaking of, the enemies themselves scale off into the moon. Enemies that return from previous regions are buffed up with so much HP you run out of stamina trying to kill one (even after putting every level up possible into Attack). Their attacks drop you quickly even with good Defence too. Also fights become very repetitious too. The rare Big-Guy-With-A-Big-Sword-That-Cant-Be-Parried too quickly becomes the common Big-Guy-With-A-Big-Sword-That-Cant-Be-Parried. This is the end of my rant and I wish I could recommend it the game. However, the issues are so non core, that they could disappear from a single patch (Only lose items on death, heal fully after every fight, make consumables more common, tone down enemy HP scaling). One can only dream through the Bleakness.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Sword DX

_childDocuments_.review: First of all this is not a game for everybody. And after over 30 hours and multiple playthroughs, there are some problems with it. But I still can recommend the game for what it is.Bleak Sword DX has a beautiful and astonishingly design. A simple combat system and quick and short combat arenas which give the feeling of "just one more stage and I'm done". It is addicting even though it can be monotonous at some times.The first playthrough will take about 3-5 hours, and any subsequent about 2-3 hours (depending on difficulty and skill level). There are 3 difficulties and 2 campaign modes, DX and Classic. DX is ne new campaign which changes the arena fights a bit, mostly more enemies but overall feels a bit more polished, while the Classic campaign is straight from the original game on mobile, and a bit shorter. The combat is simple. Attack, Parryblock and Riposte, Dodge, Charge Attack, Heavy Attack and Stamina Management. Every enemy attack that doesn't have a red exclamation mark over the enemy, can be parried. Parries give you all your stamina back, which can make for great an quick chain kills. There is also simple Level Up system, and Item/Equipment system. And if you die, you lose all your currently aquired EXP and Items, but can get them back, by winning the Stage you previously died, but if you die a second time, the EXP and Items are gone. So don't get too attached to your Items. But this is in no way a problem, since you can always go back to earlier stages, play them again and reaquire new Items, or farm levels. So what are the problems then? The hitboxes can be a bit iffy sometimes, your hit doesn't register, or you get clipped where you probably shouldn't have. These are more minor nitpicks thought, since they are rare. Also turn down the lightning effect in the settings, all the way down, it can easily get you killed, if the screen suddenly FLASHES extremely in some stages, and you can't see what the enemies are doing. The same can be said about some stages, where trees or pillars can block your view, and enemies are invisible behind them. So always stay in an open field if possible.The biggest nitpick is more from an achievement collectors perspective. First, the "Collector" achievement: Please make an ingame list like the beastiary for items, and where to find them. So players can repeat the correct areas for the missing items they might have. Just playing the first area on Randomizer over and over for hours to just hope to find the missing items is currently the most effective method, and this shouldn't be.The Arena and the Randomizer.The Randomizer in itself is very fun to play. up until about 2/3 where suddenly you can get, and will get, bumrushed by multiple Bosses in almost every wave. Especially the Mine where normally the rats come in big groups of 5-8 rats, and suddenly you got yourself ~5 Bosses + the rest of the wave. It's very hard even on normal, and while it's still possible by farming Perma upgrades, playing very patiently and using recovery items, it's still way too annoying to be fun. A possible solution could be, by limiting the Boss spawn rate, to 1 Boss per wave, or maybe let the enemies hurt the other enemies, so a friendly fire for the enemies. I know the projectiles and the laser are already able to damage other enemies, I'm talking about their normal "melee" attacks. This could also be a new fun way to play the game, since you could play defensively and experience with a different approach to this different Playmode.The Arena and the achievement is the absolut worst I have every experienced. If you are a collector, have fun. In the Arena you get put against Waves of enemies, you can't level up and you can't go back to earlier waves, and once you die, you start from the VERY BEGINNING. No problem, if at the midpoint, about wave 30, you wouldn't get multiple bosses, and you have basically Level 1 stats. and it keeps getting worse and worse, and you are not even halfway to the 64 wave achievement. I couldn't do it, after multiple hours, I just couldn't do it, best was about 40. But I got intrigued, so I gave myself (shamelessy) infinite health, and checked out the rest of the waves. Which brings me to say. I find this impossible. if anyone can post me a run, please show me, I have no idea how you are supposed to win this. A possible fix for this would be enemy friendly fire, like mentioned in the Randomizer. Or not having to start from the very beginning, this can take up to 30+min just to have another attempt at the wave you died at. Or just removing the 64 wave achievement. 32 is definitely doable. The Bossrush mode was hard but I enjoyed it, if you got the no hit achievements for the bosses before, you should be able to win this mode. It's the same as Arena, no level ups and if you die you start at the beginning. But since it's only 12 stages, and only 1 Boss per Stage, you can do it.So even with these harsh things, I do recommend the game, it has a couple flaws, but overall the replayability is high for me, it's quick and fun. A game you can always come back to and play through again, while enjoying the simple and awesome visuals.So for some input on what could be improved for a game like this? Maybe give more options for environmental damage, like hitting a tree it falls and can damage enemies, or smashing a wall of a building makes it fall over and damage enemies. This would be cool and definitely a point for a more tactical approach. Thanks for making the game, I had fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the combat of a Dark Souls game but stripped down to the bare basics of rolling, walking, attacking and parrying.Actually, just imagine a Dark Souls game distilled to the bare basics, including graphics and levels.EDIT: This review was previously positive, but after beating the game I can no longer recommend it.There were numerous tiny issues that piled up, such as inconsistent hitboxes (especially when attack-dashing through projectiles) and parry punishes straight up not working 50% of the time.The lightning-obscures-your-entire-screen mechanic alone shifted my opinion massively, and the last zone has it in almost every single level - including the final boss. And the "lightning" slider in the options only changes the brightness of the screen-obscuring overlay.For such a simple and basic game, the main attraction - the combat - should be very crisp, which these issues and "features" prevent it from being.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda don't get this one... I liked the style and combat but there is no real customization between runs. I reached the 4th or 5th area on my first "life" (they give you multiple tries) and saw I still wasn't halfway through and just didn't feel interested in finishing it.To be more specific on why: you have 2 item slots to hold items which occasionally drop. Only 2 at once, and some items that drop have the exact same stats as others despite having different names for some reason. You rarely end up swapping items it feels so the item system is just boring. You level up every few levels and can choose Health, Strength or Defense, you can choose 1 of 2 of the options being offered. The level ups would be the only difference between runs but they BARELY make a difference and the choice is negligible. So another boring system I'm afraid.And that's it. _childDocuments_.review: The level up mechanic is straight unfair... When you die, you lose your items and all the XP you earned. But that's not the worst part: Souls-like as expected. The thing is, you only have one chance to retrieve both, by beating the stage you just failed. This becomes extremely problematic in later stages, because they naturally get harder and you probably won't succeed the first or second time. This means that if you constantly fail to beat a stage on your second try, you basically can't level up your character. You can go back to previous easier stages, but they only give you a fraction of the XP you got before,so it's not worth your time. As if that wasn't bad enough, some hit boxes are incomprehensible, especially your own when you dodge an attack and get hit anyway. Also, the shield blocking of some enemies is quite inconsistent. Sometimes you can hit them with the shield up, sometimes not, it's completely unclear when you land a hit and when it's blocked.
