_childDocuments_.review: 7/10It's a great game with lots of fun mechanics, but it's missing some things that would make it perfect. The story is above average with a world I'd like to know more about. They've done such a great job with laying foundation for a world that can multiple series to come. The game play is addictive, but frustrating at times. There are many instances later in the game where you are pin holed to play one way for the entire chapter. It moves the story along, but would be nice to have flexibility with strategy. Why it lost points:-Voice acting is hit or miss. The main characters are pretty good, but most of the side character acting is mediocre at best. That coupled with dialogue that seems extended and drawn out makes the game feel more tedious to listen to than entertaining. This is very apparent in later chapters where enemies have to wheeze between each...and...every...word.-Clarity of objective and tools. Early in the game the tool tips and descriptions are clear and perfect. As you get farther along, the utility of instance buildings and units become very unclear. This can lead you to play almost an hour or more before realizing the game wanted you to focus on a specific strategy revolving around a new mechanic given late game. That makes the game feel more repetitive and restrictive than challenging at times.-Lack of card diversity. The cards used for battle and city setup are essential to the strategy, but there aren't many unique cards per character. It would be nice to have more skill specific cards revolving around each character's strengths and weaknesses. As it is now, cards are mostly the same and unlocked at different character levels. It makes the gameplay dynamic in the beginning, but more dull near the end as each character has the same group of cards.Overall, amazing game especially for the price and time. I think with some minor tweaks it will be much more enjoyable to play the storyline. As far as replayability, I could see the multiplayer being fun, but the lack of card diversity make it less personal when it comes to strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're seeking a strategy game that prioritizes engaging gameplay over complex empire management, with simplified combat mechanics akin to a strategic rock-paper-scissors for unit placement, and is set in a beautifully rendered world rich with lore, then I recommend this game.However, if you're looking for a strategy game that delves into the intricacies of empire management, diplomacy, and resource gathering, this might not be the ideal game for you.I'm currently playing through the single-player campaign on the hardest difficulty, and it's providing a satisfying challenge. I've had to make numerous strategic decisions about unit composition and where I send my heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a Stylish and Polished combination of a few different strategy games.  Fusing a Total war map, Heroes of Might and Magic Hero/army management, and an Auto-battler/Card system, its juggling alot of things at once.  Draped over all of it is a fantastic Visual style with a unique fantasy aesthetic.  The current campaign offers eight missions, introducing a number of the games mechanics. I didn't find the writing anything exceptional, but the voice acting is done well and nothing stands out as too obnoxious.  There is a wide range of content to unlock for skirmish and multiplayer, with a huge range of hero classes and specialties.    I find that while the game lacks significant depth in any of the areas its exploring, it does a good enough job of tying it all together to warrant a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: There is something immensely charming about this game, something that makes it more than the sum of its parts. There is the strategic layer reminiscent of the Civilization and Endless series, there are the battles that are echoes of auto battlers, and a card ability crafting to make sure that you remain engaged during the battle. The artwork is evocative and beautiful, making every interaction feel premium in a wonderful way.You can dial up the difficulty for a greater challenge, or you can tune it down to enjoy the story in the campaign and take your time exploring the world and familiarizing yourself with the world and units. Overall it is a very enjoyable game and a very nice take on the genre!

_childDocuments_.review: First off the game is gorgeous so full marks there. Other then that there are some issues. This game's campaign reminded me of warcraft 3 which is a good thing but unfortunately instead of having a campaign for each faction you get 8 missions that blends a few together and the final missions are an unfun slog. MIddle of mission 8 on challegning and the concept is nice but the execution is aggravating. Combat is an autobattler which is nice so you dont have to do heavy micro.ProsArt - Top tier for this type of titleTurned Based - Personal preference since I like being able to stop at will without issue.Overworld leveling Card system - This is where you get some meaningful choice in your campaign choose between being able upgrade garbage tier units to elite cav or make any location a fortress that can heal and depost loot. Could of really done some cool stuff with this to increase replayability. Meh- Story. Standard endtimes affair. Not bad but not interesting- Units. While there are a host of units, there isnt really build diversity just ending up spamming the same high tier units and ignoring the rest. Not unusual in games like this but should be mentioned- Battle cards. Couldnt decide whether to put this in bad or not. The concept is good but they vary wildly in usefullness. When you level you can also pick battle cards which vary from useless to broken. The upgrades also vary from useless to meaningful. Ex Stun a group for 6 to 9 seconds with a shorter cd yay! vs units get +5 instead of +4. Stun duration is deadly. +1 is just technically an upgrade. Some of the Overworld upgrades are also hot garbage EX 80 resource to 75! You'd need to halve the 80 to 40 for even consideration but even then youll be swimming in resources at a certain point.Bad- AI. The AI is braindead. Im pretty sure they are just set to attack move. You can win 100% of the missions your allowed to build a base by making one hardpoint(fortress) and leaving a character there while the AI endlessly suicides into unwinnable battle vs a garrison+ your army. This leads tiresome battles while your other character goes to try to win the mission.- Mission structure. Outside of the base building missions there are the survive or do the thing missions. Incredibly aggravating. Most of the level up overworld cards are useless here making your limited levels pointless. Needlessly putting crucial units to survive in garrisons or in reserve. You are given two heroes on these missions you can only usefully use one so you have to stack the one hero and leave one sitting in a corner.Overall They game isnt bad. Its visually splendid and if they tweak the AI and combat there is real potential here. I enjoyed leveling the hero getting overworld cards that helped me jumpstart into the missions. It made the choice feel relevant. Unfortunately missions just devolved into make a fortress and watch AI suicide against it

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is fantastic, I think it has great potential to keep a series going. It's kinda like if Heroes of Might and Magic and Total War had a baby. I love it and its been a long time since I've played anything like those two.Here's my thoughts of the first 7 hours.- The soundtrack honestly is my top positive. I love it, it's a great mix of heroic and magical, I'm not a conductor by any stretch but they did a great job with the music.- Combat is good fun, love the use of cards etc but can be a bit repetitive and sometimes 'spammy'I wish there was a skirmish campaign with some RPG elements or even rogue-like as the card system can already potentially add that. I also wish there was an easier way to support your army 2v1 like in Total war, currently I believe you just retreat one army and attack with the other. However, that could just be user error or intentional by the devs. There's honestly just a good nostalgic vibe that I cant explain, but theres a demo so try it out! I wish more developers did this! what a great way to let people dip their toes before diving in (obviously can refund but still)

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence joins an incredible rooster of stylized War Games to drop recently; Songs of Conquest, Age of Wonders 4, Symphony of War, Unicorn Overlord  Graphics:Songs of Silence has an art direction that is easy on the eyes due to a ink and water color shader with vivid colors chosen by someone who understood color theory.I think Songs of Silence is the prettiest girl at the ball. Battles:The auto battles are beautiful to watch due to animation that looks better then Total War animations. Battles are engaging to watch due to fantastic hp/dmg pacing of random numbers. Best of all your given a hand of cards to play to turn the tide of the Auto Battle.   I think Songs of Silence has the best battles because its an auto battle that you can shove like a quarter machine. Overworld Map (4x portion):Closer to Unicorn overlord then Age of Wonders. Seems very simple but serves the purpose of filling out armies so you can get back into battle.  MusicSeems a bit over the top but its growing on me. StorySeems to take its milieu pretty seriously, I haven't played enough to say if its interesting or good. Difficultly:Seems to be very hard.Replay:Has a Campaign, has skirmish, has multiplayer, I would say there is a ton of game for the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Great strategy game. Mixes in elements of deck building with TBS/RTS and Auto Battler aspects. Art style is really nice. Has an interesting single player story and good skirmish modes. The game also has RPG elements with levelling up your characters. You will have to make strategic choices when you level up for example do you pick a new card you can deploy in battle, or do you instead pick an economy card that will help you on the world map stage, or do you skip both of those and instead power up a card you already have in your deck. Overall, I'm really enjoying it. It feels unique and refreshing. I don't really like deck building games so this game actually impressed me. It gives me enough of the RPG and RTS elements that I like in games that I can get onboard with the deck building aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a refreshing and unique entry in the turn-based strategy genre. Its mix of tactical battles, faction variety, and immersive worldbuilding makes it stand out.The gameplay is easy to pick up but offers plenty of depth for those who love to strategize. Each faction feels distinct, and the blend of narrative and mechanics adds extra layers of engagement.Visually, it’s stunning, with an art style that’s both beautiful and atmospheric. The music perfectly complements the game’s tone, enhancing every moment.If you’re a fan of strategy games and want something that feels fresh but familiar, Songs of Silence is definitely worth your time
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game with fresh, in depth worldbuilding. Gameplay is fairly simple but is more focused on strategizing before fights than mid-fight management. A few bugs/instances of typos in descriptions, but genuinely has not impacted my experience much. Really just buy it for the art/lore/gameplay and the rest falls in place.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game after the first couple of hours.The graphics are beautiful and it runs smoothly. The battles are fun and the campaign is also exciting but I have not come that far yet. I am excited to play more and try the multiplayer with a friend later. Really hope for the devs to develop this further and looking forward to new stuff in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: My initial impressions are very positive.  The art work is gorgeous, the developer has weaved an intriguing story and put a lot of effort in integrating it tightly into the game play.  The controls are intuitive and more advanced aspects, such as the card playing, well explained.  Looking forward to playing this one through.  I highly recommend this to players looking for a beautiful, fantasy strategy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: To me Songs of Silence is a unique game that tells its story through both dialogue and a powerful atmosphere. The beautiful art and music set a quiet, non-hectic and emotional mood, while the dialogue is short but meaningful. If you enjoy games that make you think and feel, this one is definitely worth playing. It stays with you long after you're done.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence isn’t the kind of game I usually play, but it surprised me in a good way. The best parts? The music and the art. The music makes the whole game feel alive. It really adds to the mood.The art style is awesome too—very unique and detailed. It makes the world feel real and interesting. The amazing music and art kept me hooked. If you’re looking for a game that’s beautiful to look at and listen to, Songs of Silence is definitely worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite Heroes, but it scratches the itch. Love the (pretty unique) art, love the cool units. Wasn't sure about the spell cards, but it works for the combat and it's entertaining.There's a lot of stuff to unlock and I think I'll be busy with this game for a lot of hours still.I hope they consider adding a coop story campaign to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I'd like to say that I am not an expert in the genre, and basically SOS was the first game I played. I really liked the art direction and the tactical part of the game. I reallly enjoyed playing it in a slow-paced maner, making it a great experience during a cosy winter night (or autumn). Didn't have time to play it after the release, but I am definitely returning back to it ASAP! Oh, and thank you for the Ukrainian localization <3
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo first and decided to purchase the full game yesterday. I can say that I fell in love with the art style and enjoy the relaxed and chill gameplay. The strategic part is deep enough for me so far but I know I only scratched the surface. Gonna finish the single player campaign first and will dive into the multiplayer aspects at a secon stage. I recommend this game for the story and the beautiful and unique presentation. It feels like reading a fantasy book I am completely immerse :-) Also the future roadmap will be full of surprises!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of silence is really good from what ive played so far. ive gotten to chapter 4 of the main story and played a bit of the skirmish mode which so far is really fun. it feels a lot like a heroes of might and magic game only its an auto battler as far as combat is concerned mixed with strategic card playing during the battles. its a nice mish mash of stuff that works suprisingly well together.My only complaint is the tutorial is kind of bad. Granted you can look up just about every game mechanic at any time with a built in wiki for the game but i still wish as a new player the tutorial was just a bit more streamlined than what it is. I found myself struggling the first two chapters with game mechanics even with reading the manual. The campiagn is really solid so far though and if you want endless enjoyment out of the game the skirmish mode alone is worth buying the game, not to mention it has multiplayer which i havent gotten to try. Im suprised more people dont know about this one. definitely a hidden gem of a game among strategy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool! Dude, the amount of love put into this game is just oozing out of it.The style, the artwork, the lore! It's a lot to dive into just in that alone. The gameplay is a lot of fun too. I'd say it's more casual (which is fine for me, because I usually suck at games like this). It's for sure more simple but it makes it addictive because things are happening so quick. And when I think I'm about to get completely wiped, I come back kicking ass!Yeah, I recommend. And like a year ago or so, I was talking to one of the devs on Facebook. Really nice. I can't remember who it was now.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: I love strategy games and this one was a standout experience with a special battling system I have never experienced in other games. The music and lore are incredibly captivating, drawing you deeper into its world with every turn. The campaign is filled with unexpected twists, keeping the story fresh and engaging from start to finish. Battles are genuinely challenging, requiring you to carefully plan and adapt to overcome a variety of foes, each with unique strengths.The battle system is especially cool: rather than controlling every move, you watch battles unfold and use cards based on your heroes to intervene at key moments. It’s a unique and enjoyable way to fight, blending strategy with suspense. Choosing the right heroes and troops before each battle is essential, but the turn-based format gives you plenty of time to strategize and experiment.The music is mesmerizing, sticking in my head long after I stopped playing, but it never felt repetitive or tiring. I also loved the game’s story and map, which is inspired by German folklore and mythical creatures, wich felt very original and adds a lot of charm and mystery to the world.Would recommend 100%
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much heart to it. The combat is pretty good, the characters are interesting, but what really drew me to this game was the style. The art direction for this game is beautiful, and playing it really brings you into this colorful and stylistic world.As for the price drop - if you are complaining about this then you should grow up! You made the assessment that the game would be worth your money for the price that you bought it when you bought it. Games have price drops all the time, and to complain about that is so petty.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Try the demo on Steam. A bit like Heroes of Might and Magic. Light cities management and auto-battler with battle cards to enhance, call or attack units with unique hero abilities. Fauna are not your typical medieval setting. Instead of elephants carrying your loot, you have giant aardvarks. The main hero rides a bull and there are flying bulls. Lovely art style, music, lore and fun game-play. Three factions to choose from.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually very careful with early access titles, however this one is a very solid experience and a must-have gem for any 4X fan.The art style is truly a standout, setting it apart with its unique and memorable aesthetic. It feels both modern and to some extent a slight reminiscent of Mucha’s iconic art (but in a very cool way). The card illustrations and UI design are beautifully crafted and animated. The game has high production values shining through in every aspect and is already quite polished for Early Access.The world is vibrant and filled with motion and life on every "little step" on the map. A pletora of subtle to bold VFX add depth to the world and create an atmosphere that truly brings the game to life. On the gameplay front, it feels fresh with a neat battle system, offering an innovative blend that nods to the Heroes franchise, but without the burden of repetitive city management and with much more dynamic combat experience.As a fan of many 4X games,  I am having a plenty of fun with this one and will continue to play it quite a lot. I especially like that is a bit different and not the next copy.Neat music with nice FX!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, BUT:1) need a reconnect button! ATM you can waste an hour or two just to get randomly disconnected and not have an option to join back;2) UI is clunky - right now you constanly occasionally misclick and ruin your turn. At least give options to customise keys;3) Seems to be some heavy balance issues with units and economy.As soon as these issues are at least partially fixed i'll change to recommend the game. RN it's only a SP version.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: My god, this game is brilliant! finaly i have time to check it, thanks to youtuber "Old Boy" thanks to whom i heard about it.Art design is troo masterpieceMusic in game is incredibleGame play is very nice, easy to undestend and very satisfiedFirst i thut it will be like Herouse of MaM but its very diferent and i relly like it. Campaign grabs attention from the first minutes. my first session was 4h and it was really hard to chenge attension.I wont more of this game, i want DLC to this game, i hope for the long support of this progect,PS thx for Ukrainian localization, you are the best!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome 4X game! It´s a turn based fantasy game like Heroes/Age of Wonders, but it´s much more enjoyable in multiplayer due to the faster play style and back and forth battles (no 3-8 hour snowballing until you fight the enemy hero and it´s all over then).I hope we will see a lot more players on release and much more different map layouts.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: In short: the game is good, it feels overloaded at first, but the gameplay and story are interesting and the graphics/visuals are incredible.I will continue to note "(1)" the problems and talk about most of them, but this game is cool and deserves its attention, don't be fooled by the fact that I write a lot about nuances there).Gameplay: I haven't played games like this and (1) at the beginning it felt overloaded, I think more in terms of UI/UX, because of its unique style it's hard to distinguish the UI right away, so it's confusing at first.The gameplay is pleasant, in some places it feels unpolished, I would like to skip the animation somewhere, speed it up a little or close some image, but these are all small improvements.Graphics: It's incredible, it covered up the lack of polish in the gameplay and made me want to keep playing to see more.Plot: at first the world feels a little too distant, like a fairy tale, but over time it becomes more engaging. (2) I would like the plot to somehow explain why "Silence" is so terrible, maybe it will be beyond the fourth chapter.The fourth chapter: I was tormented for several days in the evenings, because the previous stories gave plenty of time, here  you are immediately thrown into big and evil enemies with a (3) faction "old race" to play for which is not explained (units), it has expensive units and they need improvements (basic unit 60c→ warriors70c → "powerful improvements for the price of different resources"), and there are also constructs that require a large amount of resources, not to mention the additional goal of (4) finding people, which very quickly start to be killed, and you don't even know where they are and you have to save- scam to find everyone and then start playing normally.(5) It was also not clear at first, the new buildings destroy the existing world beam (building), that it is also a building in the old race cities.(6) Also here, in the middle of the game, the cards fell into a smaller pile and it was very difficult to choose them, especially as the city entered and the city improvement card was added.In conclusion, the chapter is interesting, but needs more explanations about the old race and some balance, maybe 2 moves after arriving in the city at the beginning of the chapter to prepare, can put some friendly village on top in the forests and come to help, also give the opportunity to save / find refugees .Although it was difficult, I am glad that I won.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, the game is difficult to access for several reasons:Lack of readability in interactions; there should be better details on hover to properly understand the options.Movement is consistently complicated; there is no path automation and no display of movement squares. As a result, in some cases, we are blocked by mountain passes, and it takes multiple attempts to get through.There is a lack of clear indications on the screen to discern whether we are in hero mode or city mode. This leads to many incorrect manipulations. Making the selection more apparent through colors or other means would simplify the system.Managing cities via a menu would be much clearer. A menu button that displays each city and its options would make it less cumbersome to navigate from city to city when we have several.Selecting a unit and hovering with the mouse to list actions, as well as receiving information on hover over an enemy or another object, would make the interface smoother and more user-friendly.Likewise, it is difficult to read battles and interactions. Clear icons on the units to indicate their status would be an improvement.Currently, it is really challenging to enjoy the game as we are forced to save repeatedly to avoid incorrect interactions.The game quickly becomes frustrating, and the pressure intensifies as the game progresses.Also, an options tree indicating future build possibilities and requirements would be a significant advantage.The game's concepts are very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: This game is interesting, beautiful, with intriguing word and campaign and with great voice acting.The real time auto-battles detract from the tactical experience typical of those kind of game, but in the same time makes them  faster to play. I haven't play enough, to decide for me if this is overall positive or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence is a treat to experience. The music and visuals of the game are way above the other games in this genre and it's certainly what hooked me initially since I'm not familiar with games in this genre. A clear and distinct visual style coupled with the blend of auto-battler and 4X genres turns this game into a fantastic introduction to this games in the same space. Cards feel satisfying to use when in battle as well as when your upgrading locations. Every action feels like something major that can change the course of the battle at any given moment. It gives you a glimpse into how nail bitingly tense and expansive these games can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: Songs of Silence delivers a captivating blend of strategy and action set in a fantasy world. With stunning artwork and innovative gameplay mechanics that strike the perfect balance between player involvement and strategic depth. Even though it's still early access, it's smooth as butter, feels like they've been working on it forever. Songs of Silence isn't just a game, it's shaping up to be a real adventure, and I'm totally hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: The game’s art style is truly fantastic: they are bright and engaging. The soundtrack and voice acting further enhance the overall experience. The gameplay is engaging, offering a unique mix of strategic planning and real-time decision-making that keeps you on your toes. However, combat can occasionally feel a little hands-off, and deciphering unit strengths and weaknesses can be slightly challenging. The stealth missions tend to drag, and managing the map with only a few heroes can be a bit frustrating. Despite these minor issues, Songs of Silence feels promising. It's an excellent pick for strategy enthusiasts; who value rich visuals, deep narrative, and innovative gameplay mechanics and for strategy newcomers who find this particular genre daunting, this game makes the on-boarding easy and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game's art style, and the soundtracks are enjoyable. In terms of gameplay, it's quite engaging and challenging, requiring strategic thinking. The user-friendly UI is a definite plus, making navigation hassle-free.For newcomers, there's enough guidance to ease you into the game without feeling lost. As someone who used to enjoy Command and Conquer (Generals & Zero Hour), I found myself drawn to this game despite the differences in gameplay style. The strategic aspect is what really stood out for me
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: A good introductory strategy game for someone who hasn't played a single one before. I found the game-play easy to understand and really fun when I got the hang of it. Watching the armies fight is really satisfying, though I would love it if there was a way we could fast forward through it as well.  Overall, it was an enjoyable experience for me. I also think the art-style and voice-acting impressively complement the story. I probably wouldn't have liked this game as much as I do without it!
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: As this just got relaeased EARLY ACCESS, I recommend the game for it having potential.Played through the campaign as far as it is available for now (4 Missions), took me around 5 hours. I kinda like the mass exodus vibes, but over all many missions were a bit puzzle like - challenging but you could see, with the right decisions, you get it done smoothly... I did not always take the best decisions and still managed to pass the missions. Just telling you, so you know what to expect.Then there is the random maps modus... which I tried out for around 2 hours. I think balancing might be a thing, which is no wonder for an Early Access Game, but I will try out more. Biggest issue here: you have to grind through various game plays to unlock factions and hero classes. I kind of would recommend the developers to reconsider to give more access to parts of the game sooner.... At the current state - 40 Euros for 4 campaign missions with an interesting story but partly okayish design... is quite something to consider. I think of it as an investment, I can see that the whole game looks beautiful and I would like to experience more depth in the game.In the end, it is a game with much potential but still somehow on the start of it's journey
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Silence

_childDocuments_.review: After a frustrating defeat in the Kampagne mode which lead me to wait for an easier difficulty I played a game on a random map and it was pretty good. I had alot of fun. I think the enemy AI is acting not really intelligent but difficultysettings will come so its fine for now.I love that you can unlock things through playing that is pretty cool too.The artstyle is just wonderful. I like the combat mechanic and I like that you don't have to walk on a grid.So thats many things I like. What I don't like are very specific things so I try to explain it a bit:You can right click on your hero when the Magnifying glass is shown to zoom in and manage your army. The hitbox for the magnifying glass is pretty small so often I misclicked and my character just walked a step. Luckily you can rightclick on the portrait of the hero to enter the managing screen but still.Which I also thought was exhausting is. When you clicked on a hero to walk with him but then click on another hero you dont select the new hero or new location etc. but you deselect your hero.So instead of selecting the other hero you deselect the hero you had selected at the time so that you have click again on a hero to select him which lead was often a bit frustrating.Like I said there are very specific thing.Besides that I had a funny little glitch on a random map where an enemy spawned at a place which I couldnt enter and he couldnt leave. It was in the corner of the map he was on kind of an island surrounded by rivers. Nothing terrible but more like funny. I think things like this happen at a random map and it was just this one enemy and this one time. Like 100 exp less.But at the moment I have to say the game is a clear YES! besides the price tag. I cant wait to see what comes next.

name: Tiny Glade
detailed_description: Tiny Glade is a relaxing free-form building game. Tap into the joy of making something pretty with no management, no combat, or wrong answers - just kick back, doodle some castles, and turn forgotten meadows into lovable dioramas. Explore gridless building chemistry , and watch the game carefully assemble every brick, pebble and plank, adapting to your whim. Draw a path through a building? A door pops up! Raise the building? Columns and beams line up to support it. There are no wrong answers or failure states. You can change your mind at any time, and whatever you make will look cozy out of the box. Let yourself unwind to the chill vibes , and escape into a world that feels alive. Ivy envelops your buildings, sheep waddle through your paths, and fireflies light up the night.

short_description: Tiny Glade is a small diorama builder where you doodle whimsical castles, cozy cottages & romantic ruins. Explore gridless building chemistry as the game adorns your glades with procedural detail. No management, combat or goals: just kick back and turn forgotten meadows into lovable dioramas.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the Demo, I was desperately waiting for the full release and the wait was worth it. It's the best game to relax (and maybe entertain during meetings). I love being able to freely create castles with a super easy process. Wish an option to enable grind lines was possible, just to get the perfect straight lines and corners. Overall 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I was afraid it's gonna lose its charm after one hour and that I'll get bored of it because I'll discover everything it has to offer. Almost 17 hours in and it didn't happen yet. It's true what they say, your only limit is your imagination. Also, this is the absolutely CUTEST game, I still can't get over how cute it is. It's so adorable it should be illegal.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: A very sweet, relaxing diorama builder.  I really enjoyed this more than I thought I would.  The camera mode is lots of fun to take pictures in after spending a while creating a little world.I can see easy potential upgrades for this - I wish it was possible to place "clutter" items by hand instead of having to rely on the randomization of the windows and doors, and I would love to be able to control some of the animals a little better, especially in photo mode.  Being able to place more objects to make these little creations feel more lived in would be my biggest want for the game right now.It would be amazing if we could also design indoors but I realize that is a pretty big ask technically speaking and I won't be shocked if that never happens.  The art style really lends itself to so many possibilities though.  I hope this continues to be developed and added to!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's so pretty and easy to build. I would recommend this game to anyone who wants a relaxing time making cute castles! <3 The worlds are a bit small and leave me wanting to build more and more. I would love to be able to make a cute rustic village. But other than that I adore the game! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all i ever wanted for a digital creation space. Thenly thing i am missing is a way to change the glade season type when i have an existing glade. i would like to be able to change it midway through building to see how it would affect stuff. hopefully if this is not too difficult to add, the amazing developers could implement this feature. Amazing work so far and i cannot wait until further updates to this awesome game! instant bought it when it came out!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely splendid game. This is perfect for someone who wants something to play when on a study break or just want something to unwind after schoolwork or work. I can also definitely see this as something someone can sink a lot of their time just because they want to make a work of art. Thank you Tiny Glade team for making an amazing and well made cozy cute game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: What a thoroughly enchanting game this is! Beautiful, cozy, and relaxing only begin to describe this game -- there's so much hidden complexity in its very simple design and rather basic tools. So much can be done with so little, it's genuinely incredible! I personally hope we get more tools down the line for the finer details (I'd love to place clutter myself, or adding some furniture here and there), but that's only a very small want amongst a list very big wins. This game is not for management, and doesn't feature any challenge whatsoever. It's more a mapping tool than a city manager; more sandbox than RPG; more relaxing than exhilarating -- but if you just want to create stunning and detailed glades, by all means try!I think as far as "uses", this could be a great way to ambient a scene for some kind of fantastical work. Maybe demonstrate building techniques and trends. Or anything along those lines, really. But I simply love making little scenes what can I say
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, it's a creativity game.  Simple in its controls but pleasantly unpredictable in some of its procedural generation.  As you decorate, little things like benches, wheelbarrows, potted plants, tools and other small items will randomly appear.  One of the most chill experiences in a game I've ever experienced.I can imagine some additions to this game.  Small details like fruit trees, idle animals, food gardens, other little decorations. This might be a stretch but maybe some very simply animated humans that perform simple tasks when placed next to a unique structure - put someone next to a row of carrots, maybe they're sitting on the ground with a basket of carrots next to them as they harvest the carrots(not actually harvest them, they just look like they are).  Place a person near a large door, a guard maybe?  No need to take care of them, just have them stay where they are and look nice.  So much creative potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a short on youtube and knew I had to have this. I got the demo. Fell in love. Kept coming back to the demo to try new things. And now, finally, the full game is out... and its beyond expectations. Its so relaxing. Love it as a "Diorama Doodler". Just helps one mellow out and just draw. Really wish there were more games like this, but at the same time, I'm glad Tiny Glade has finally done it. Can't wait to dive into all the different things I can do now in the full version. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing game. The visuals and music are fantastic, and I like how much you can make in a small sandbox. As people have mentioned in the reviews, I'd love to have more outdoor furniture that you can manually place, and I hope in the future we can add more environmental stuff like waterfalls.Overall, I love this game, and I will continue to play it and support it!

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are simply stunning, and you can really tell a lot of thought went into it. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly relaxing and I absolutely love casually creating without any resource restraints or worrying about quests or anything like that.  The visuals are beautiful, I love the camera mode for some an immersive opportunity. I can't wait to see what future updates will bring to this beautiful little gem of a game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: an absolutely delightful little game, deceptively simple but packed with the most intricate and gorgeous tiny details. intuitive to pick up, yet rewards deeper attention and experimentation. the visuals are stunning and the tiny sheep floats out of the way with an umbrella when you build under it, so basically perfection.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade just came out so it's important to keep in mind that there will likely be more features and additions in the future. The game is simple in its design but gives you the tools to push your creativity as far as you choose. Building and placing objects has a very solid and smooth feel to it, although the lack of tools like duplication, selecting multiple objects at once, and axis selection can make the game feel frustrating and tiring. The limitations for the size of buildings can feel very restricting, and the map size is pretty small if you want to create larger-scale projects. The game easily makes up for it with the  ambiance and vibes, the music is very charming and the visuals are stunning. The game provides you with the ability to add filters and change the direction and/or amount of sunlight, and there are 4 main themes (seasons) to choose from when you start a new project. I'd easily recommend Tiny Glade if you like cozy/relaxing games and want a cute escape from faster paced games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great, cozy, relaxing game that I've been eagerly awaiting for a long time now. It lives up to the hype! I dont write reviews often and this one deserves it.I cant wait to see what improvements will be made. Currently you are kind of stuck in mideval europe due to the architecture, I would love some more asian style roofs to make a Tibetan mountain village or recreate Ashina Castle from Sekiro or something. Some more urban features like metal lamp posts or fountains would also be great. Currently the biggest gripe I have is theres no way to copy and paste things. If I make a cool tower and want several of them I have to make it all over again every time and try to get it as close to the same as possible. I think stairs would also be a great addition, currently you can only get stairs by using paths on terrain differences, but stairs from one roof to another would greatly improve the flexibility in bigger city projects. There are so many things they can add, I'm excited for the future of this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews, but I felt I had to for this game as I am already obsessed with it and I barely have around 2 hours of playtime. This game is absolutely gorgeous and is very relaxing. I could see myself playing this everyday after work just to wind down! Not to mention the ASMR that comes with the sound effects is *chef's kiss*I do hope to see a future update where we're able to furnish the interiors and maybe even possibly add/move the objects on the exterior of the builds, but other than that, I highly recommend :)

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a delightful haven for anyone looking to unleash their creativity in a beautifully crafted environment. This charming sandbox game offers a whimsical escape, allowing players to build their own picturesque village at their own pace. The enchanting visuals create a serene atmosphere, perfect for immersing yourself in the joys of design and decoration.One of the standout features of Tiny Glade is its intuitive gameplay. The controls make it easy to pick up and play, encouraging you to experiment and explore your artistic instincts. With every house you construct and every garden you cultivate, there’s a sense of satisfaction that comes from watching your vision come to life. The game's design invites you to let your imagination run wild, creating unique dioramas that reflect your personal style.What’s particularly lovely about Tiny Glade is the absence of goals or time constraints. You can take your time to enjoy the process, making it an ideal choice for those cozy afternoons when you want to unwind. The community of fellow builders is also a fantastic resource, filled with inspiration and ideas that can enhance your own creations. It’s wonderful to see how others approach their designs, sparking new ideas and techniques that you might not have considered.Although the game currently has a limited selection of decorations, this only enhances the charm of Tiny Glade. It encourages players to think creatively and find innovative ways to make the most of the available options. Plus, there’s a palpable excitement about the potential for future updates, which could introduce even more delightful items and features to explore.In summary, Tiny Glade is a gem of a game that provides a cozy, fulfilling experience for anyone who loves to build and create. Its inviting atmosphere, charming visuals, and open-ended gameplay make it a perfect escape from the daily grind. If you’re looking for a game that celebrates creativity and relaxation, Tiny Glade is undoubtedly worth adding to your collection!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for my girlfriend and shes obsessed with it. This is the first PC game she has ever played and I think it's safe to say shes hooked. 10/10 to use her words: "I love how the longer you play, the more little fun things you find or figure out! As someone who struggles with most Platform games other than ACNH, this game is super fun and easy to learn."
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful little game, very calming and easy to play, with great attention to detail! What I love most is that with the lovely way the game adds vines and decor items, you can basically plop down anything and it'll look nice. The lighting is gorgeous in every time of day, and adjusting the time and angle of the light are simple, satisfying dials. I was lucky enough to playtest the game some months ago, and the amount of things that have been fixed and improved in such a short time, with such a small team, is incredible! The devs should feel very proud, and I hope to see this game continue to grow and be polished into an even brighter little gem than it already is!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the game I was waiting eagerly for release. Now it's in my hand (I mean in my PC) and I love to just escape the reality with this game. _childDocuments_.review: I have been looking for this type of game for a while, The possibilities with this game are "endless" and its just so cozy. I have currently only tried to make Hogwarts in it, and i must say it manages to do so very well. I also enjoy the possibility to view the project as a tabletop battlemap, makes it so useful for what im planning on building with it!Now there are a lot of features which i love with this, and there are some which could be adjusted to gain more possibilities with the building. For example i would love if the Terrain tool could create mountains too or at least much taller cliffs than is possible at the moment. I would also love a larger area to build on, (the one which is there now is big, but even bigger calls for more interesting and larger builds,) Also the ability to perhaps set the area at a coast side or by the sea would also be amazing! a few las things i would like adjusted is the ability to make steeper and taller roofs, especially when using the largest cylindrical tower, an own tool to make stairs would also be appreciated though we can do it already, and finally the abiltiy to use the "draw wall" tool on buildings higher up and not just at ground/terrain level.All in all, definitely recommends this game if you want a cozy, relaxing build experience or are looking to visualise your castle/town designs and let your creativity loose.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Summary 10/10. Tiny glade is extremely user friendly and personally I love the style they’ve gone for when it comes to the building mechanics, It’s not 100% perfect but I still love it I’ve obsessively played the demo and I’m super excited that the full game is here and it's amazing!   Gameplay wise it's super simple and while there are ways to make more complex buildings its  really easy to make simple cottages, castles, wizard towers ect. The little details you get from placing windows is extremely pleasing and typically always adds onto the charm of the buildings you make. At times this game feels like a Gamemasters dream, I’m genuinely using the glades I make for set pieces in D&D the style just fits perfect!   The camera mechanic is one of the best I’ve seen in my life from a game I genuinely love it. From the walking mode to the top down it’s partially got it all. My favorite mechanic from the camera mode is the walking as I get to just go in and Experience my glades after I’ve built them. While I do believe the game is Amazing there are some minor flaws I have with the game that I believe could be changed. For instance the water/pond creation, I understand for consistency keeping ponds always be at the original level of the ground. I really wish It worked with the ground raised. I'd really like to make down-stream rivers or just ponds in higher places.   Another flaw I find with the game is with the flower’s there’s no variation with the flowers you can have. I’d honestly really like to be able to have different colors and different sets of flowers.  I believe the idea of also being able to make little farms with like carrots or just other plants would be nice too but I understand that there’s only so much they can do with their game and they don't want things to be too complex  Regardless I do believe you should give Tiny Glade a try either via their Demo or just buying the game right out. I love the dev’s for what they’ve made and I will continue to support them and I hope they continue to make lovely games like Tiny Glade!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully presented game that annoyingly prevents me from doing what I want.Credit where credit is due: This game has one of the most pleasing sound and visual designs I've played.At this time, this game is too bare bones to be asking for $15. The replayability is low for me since there are a very limited number of materials and shapes to create and the game's prediction of where to place small details restricts my creative freedom. The play area is too small to really make anything truly expansive. There is limited terrain modification. Pathing being tied to entrances and support structures leads to frustrating moments. Combining structures is simply two of them clipping into one another.It feels like the whole concept is just generative AI but trained on the aesthetic that the game presents to the player. I often fought with the mechanics in order to get a result that was close but wasn't what I was trying to do. Refunded. Will be happy to revisit once there's more substance.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: BEWARE Radeon 5xxx users! You will experience constant crashes on many, many, many occasions! From the forum posts, user reports, i see there is a lot of us RX 5700 XT users. Forget about playing Fall theme: it's either instant reboot or, in better case, crash to desktop. Better wait until the story with AMD unfolds (dev is in contact with AMD).Daily Theme: Crash to Desktop. Update: that seems to work now, at least yesterday (3rd DT).Second day in the row since release, so already first 2 missed :). I thought the crash was specific to content inside it, but apparently it's the "daily" part that causes it, not the "theme" itself. There goes -15% price drop - to 15% of content. Now remember, the game loads automatically to last edited glade, so when it crashes on a freshly loaded daily theme, then you must be quick to hit escape, to open menu at the right moment before it crashes (and crashes, and crashes over and over again :).Anyhow... After playing the demo i am, like many other here, disappointed in how small the game actually is. Being able to zoom out and see the huge map, i thought building area will be much larger (or at least be able to see other, previously created glades from distance, created in the same theme).Of course the game itself is beautiful, music nice and chill, mechanics and all are great and i still like it. But in current state i would recommend just playing the demo for few days - there's just not much more in full version, especially given the price.I feel, that current -15% price should be the actual, target one. Then, i would still wait for a price drop (counting from current, discounted price). It's like Townscaper: beautiful but overpriced.Oh, and to top it off, discounted bundle with soundtrack wasn't available on day 1, which i would definitely buy (like i did with Foundation, which has absolutely best soundtrack for medieval genre AND was even updated with new tracks that came along).Definitely not worth the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is an in-depth city builder experience with various puzzle-like elements. As you continue playing the game, making new maps and creating new things, you learn more about how to use the game's tools to craft from your own unique perspective; that's what I enjoy most about this game.I would highly suggest spending your first ~5-10 hours playing this game entirely blind. Experiment with different things, and challenge your intuition to help you learn more about how to create what  want to create; this makes the game more rewarding and fulfilling to play. In turn, it gives your experience with the game a bit more replayability.I look forward to seeing what Ana and Tom are planning to do next, whether it be with Tiny Glade or other projects!

The things you make are only limited to your creativity.If you enjoy building little villages to grandiose castles, this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: an amazingly made and well thought out game even just from the technical perspective. they have different environment themes to set the mood, gradual day/night changes, and seemingly endless possibilities if you look beyond the menu. its so intuitive to just let yourself doodle and click around until you figure out how to do things. this game is like playing god in a cozy and warm way.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: "Hm, what's this? It looks nice and is pretty cheap. Maybe i'll try it out for a few minut- huh? It's 3 a.m. already!?"And that's going to be your experience, when you first play this game and any time you open it up.This game is a time machine. It transports you a few hours into the future without you even noticing.Tiny glade is a SUPER relaxing and creative game. You will enjoy it, even if you don't have a single artistic bone in your body. No matter what you do, the game will just compensate for your artistic incompetence and still make it look gorgeous.I'm also overwhelmingly impressed with the controls. It's very easy and intuitive, but also very precise. Moments of frustration simply don't exist here. That alone makes it a good game in my opinion. And it's crazy how much you can do with the few tools you are given. Playing around sometimes reveals some neat tricks/mechanics you didn't know about.I only have 3 noteworthy criticisms:-Decorative elements are very context dependent, which is perfectly fine, but it's kind of hard to make large flat roofs look appealing. -There is no collective selection tool or a copy and paste tool. If you like a structure you made and want to use it again, you will have to just build it again.-Water can't be placed on higher ground. It's always on the lowest level, even if you elevated the ground before, which results in a deep waterhole.tl;drIs it good?Yes.

But nonetheless it is still very fun and great the way the game is right now.Still, i wouldnt say no to updates ;)

_childDocuments_.review: (This isn't meant to be a negative review, it's a mixed one)Tiny Glade is absolutely gorgeous and adorable, there's a lot to love here but I'm really disappointed over the glaring lack of decorations and variety currently available. _childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a great game that excels at providing a cozy, creative game play experience. I've only played ~3 hours of the game (at time of review), but I could easily see myself sinking 100's of hours into it. I've been looking for a good chill game like this for a while and have really loved every second. It's the perfect unwinding game to play alone or with your significant other. TLDR - 8/10, it's an extremely relaxing game that allows your imagination to run wild, but can feel limited by the area it allows you to build in. I wish that were a few more options for items that you can add to your world to give it more of a unique feel and that the resizing controls were a bit better. But overall, there is way more to love about this game than there is to hate.From the start, Tiny Glade shows you everything it has to offer and says "have at it". There aren't any features hidden behind micro-transactions or progression systems, and the game outlines the tools that you have at your disposal via a short tutorial. Oh and you're also listening to some of the most tranquil and beautiful music while all this is going on. Like I could easily see myself falling asleep to it if I wasn't so hyper-fixated on finishing my town. Some features that I liked: -Tiny Glade offers 5 different environments to build in, each with their own aesthetic, as well as a daily theme which changes every 24hrs. -While creating your fantasy village/castle of your dreams, you can change the time of day and angle of the sun/moon to see how your creations look in different lighting. The lighting and visuals in this game are absolutely beautiful. No matter what you build, the game always has a soothing, inviting aesthetic. And the fact that you can get different colored lanterns and windows, really helps to amplify the atmosphere of whatever you build. -They allow you to change the color of practically everything so you can really find the right color to match the aesthetic that you're aiming for. Windows, lanterns, walls, roofs, fences, you name it. And objects like the buildings even have different textures you can pick from (brick or flat paint) that allow for some cool variation.-Camera mode is super cute and even allows you to walk through the world you made like someone that lives there. You can adjust depth of field, zoom, vignette, filters for the camera, while also providing such high quality shots of your creation.-The teraform and water tools are just great. The world that it gives you, at first, is basically flat and wooded, with an opening for your beginning creations. Within seconds you can transform it into town surrounded by hills of flowers with a cheeky little pond/river running through it. My first build was a tiny cabin surrounded by a brick wall, with a little creek behind it. I quickly learned that the water tool and be used to create arches in the wall, which I wasn't expecting at all.-Creating arches and doorways in a wall by using the path tool is always satisfying to me. And being able to have rows of arches in your building allows for some really interesting creations. -The animals that wander the world as you build are adorable. And you can pet them which is just what the game needs.Dislikes (a bit nit picky, but the game just launched i'm also trying to take that into consideration):-The area that it gives you to build in can get cramped pretty quickly. Even if you're not building massive castles, you'll hit the edge of the build area quicker than you'd expect. -I kinda wish there were more objects to place in the world. I know that the game just launched so i realize that this may come in future updates, but at the moment it feels like it needs a little more. You get two types of buildings (circle/square), a wall/fence, three types of windows (one of which is meh at best imo), a lamppost/lantern, and a flag/banner (changes depending on where its placed). The limitation can lead to very creative builds, but I feel like a tool for small objects like carts, wheels, or crates could go a long way.-When placing a building, occasionally objects like a wheelbarrow or crate will appear next to it, but you have no control over where it is placed or how it's oriented. It's seems to be tied to the size/positioning of the building. This kinda ties in with my previous point, in that I wish these were default objects that could be placed to accentuate a garden or something like that, rather than "flavor text" for the building. And when placing a tree in the Olden setting, it's REALLY difficult to get the creepy, leafless trees to appear. It seems like there's a radius around certain foliage that is generated in the world which allows for these kind of trees to be placed, but the spooky tree itself isn't selectible from the tool bar. (I could be wrong but I didn't find a way to easily place them)-Resizing tools and moving objects can be a bit tricky at first, and I've become best friends with the undo button bc of this. Learning what each of resizing options do and trying to match the dimensions of an other object, can feel a bit frustrating at times. What makes resizing so difficult, for me, is that you're doing it entirely by eye. Before i get too far into this point, I realize that the game is advertised with a "gridless building system" - however, objects don't snap together at a joined position or automatically center. This made building more difficult, in my experience, since there isn't a unit tied to an object's size or a "copy object" tool. If you're trying to match the dimensions of another object it can be pretty tedious to do so. I kinda wish there was an option for that allows you to know "this wall is X squares high, this tower is X spaces away from this object" so that making things proportional is less of a headache. Overall, there's so much to love about this game and it's future may include improvements to the things I was picky about, but that's no reason to hold out on getting this. Seeing your town slowly come to life, piece by piece, is incredibly satisfying and Tiny Glade has so many hidden tricks that you can learn to make your world feel that much more special. I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves sandbox building games, as this is without a doubt worth $15.

_childDocuments_.review: An ingenious town builder that relies on a compact toolset and clever procedural generation to create beautifully aesthetic towns and castles.It's simple to start building, almost like doodling, but there is delightful depth and surprises to be discovered as you begin to understand the way elements procedurally fit together to create new intricate structures.Everything from the sound and graphics exude charm and polish, with the lighting engine a particular marvel. _childDocuments_.review: Love the idea of the game, but as this game is not in early access (as far as I can tell), I sadly am disappointed with some of the mechanics and don't think this is as perfect as I would have wanted it to be.It has quite some good stuff going on though, so it's not all disappointing. But specially these few things make it hard for me to enjoy:- The map is way too small. Advertisement shows cities etc, but somehow, my map is just a tiny square? Am I doing something wrong, or is that really it? The way of building an entire city is what really sold me, and it just doesn't seem to be there.- Landscaping is terrible. The brush is teeny tiny, and there is no way to size it up. I would like a way bigger and smaller brush, but they limit it to a tiny one and gl making a nice landscape with that.-  Lack of tutorial - many things are hidden, and if I hadn't watched a YT video, I still wouldn't have known you can combine 2 windows and make a door by placing a window down (if on a tiny raised platform) or put a road (I had, but it was too tiny to make a door so no  doors for me made me think it didn't work that way).- No copy/paste for paint (/colors of walls/windows etc). i have to singlehandedly find the same color for ALL my windows and wall pieces. I get it's nice to be able to make them differently, but it's tedious. Why am I not able to copy one I select, and paste it on others I select with a click of a button?- Trees and flowers are poorly done. Each click just makes 1 tree. Why not add a brush so you can make an easy forest? make it tiny for 1, big for more? And it can be randomized just like the rest of the things are? Flowers are also in a bedding, and I have no idea why. I can't just plant flowers in my grass, because it looks man-made. disappointed me. I just want a flowerfield or some flowers in my surrounding area, not a man-made garden.That's about it for my disappointments. I think this game has a lot of potential, but for now, it feels incomplete. It  would be okay for an EA game, but as it isn't, it is a nice idea poorly implemented.

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is so easy to just open and lose time. The best part is that it's also satisfying to open and play for an hour or 2, and love what you make, but you can also throw in 8 hours and also feel accomplished. The games core mechanics are quite intuitive and are initially easy to get down, but you quickly see the vastness of the different possibilities with the tools provided, and that presents the challenge of learning building techniques to build even more intricate buildings and designs. While the game seems to have a decent depth to it, there are still some basic things missing like stairs, ladders, bridges, all of which have to be made tediously with other tools. Not necessarily a negative thing, but it can be quite a time consumer to get what seems to be basic village building tools. I don't know if this was by design, or it was just something they haven't yet incorporated and the procedural generation seems to be well optimized, so adding what seems to be rather simple and basic things can be quite difficult to get right. I can see the game blossoming into game of the year, and one of greatest building games of our generation, there is so much potential with additions, new styles, larger maps, more terrain control, etc. Excited to see where this game goes!

_childDocuments_.review: My second plot came from the daily in-game prompt, "Two Neighbours (I wouldn't have come up with any of this if not for it)." The neighbours have a hate/mostly love relationship, though they're currently fighting over whose house is taller. Blue's is sliiiightly taller thanks to their new flag, but Rose's  vision is a little wonky so Rose is convinced *they're* winning. Rose still comes over for tea at least once every day, judging from the very worn path in the snow between the covered bridge over the pond and each other's front doors. Rose knows it's hard for Blue to get out due to their freak accident so even when Blue's being troublesome and trollly on purpose, Rose still visits to make sure they're alright enough to ignore. I love this game. You can take the fence tool and scribble all over the ground, which I've done because it sounds cool and weird, then just undo. Or not undo, I guess, and make it all a  gigantic mess with flora and other random building parts. I have ~30 hours in, and maybe half is just from leaving the game open cuz it's pretty to look at and to listen to.
