And then suddenly out of nowhere, before you realize it, there are houses popping up, pathways, hills, ponds, flowers, trees, Cathedrals, town squares. Evrything built by YOU. Be ist a simple shack or the most impressiv Castles or rebuilds of Real castles, or Movie Locations ( i seen videos of someone building Helms dee and rivendell from Lord of the Rings. big thumbs up!! ).I have played the game nor for 12.3 Houres anbd already built 2 whole maps. 2 nice and relaxing villages. one in the beginners Map, a small town embedded in a valley. Then i built a quite bigger town in the Next map with a real market square, Inns, a monestary, houses, a big pond and what not.  And currently i am in the Progress of building a castle that takes up half the map. ( the other half is reserved for a smol Town)This game is THE BEST building simulator i have ever seen. Calm, relaxing and wonderfully made. The graphics are awsome, the sound is great. AND you can pet the sheeps and the ducks!!! (fish swim away from your mouse though X3 )And if you can't build it right the first time always remember what Bob Ross used to say: we don't make mistakes, we have happy accidents!The only thing I personally am missing is a bit of more ground dekoration for like roads or squares. You can build a market place, but you can't dekorate it with market stalls or something like this. just RNG deko that pops up when palcing trap doors on the floor or through windows or doors.BUT this game just released and it's got A LOT of potential!Recoomended 15/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: You don't get many build options in Tiny Glade, but the devs very cleverly programmed how different objects interact when you combine them, meaning that all kinds of amazing things can be done with a bit of imagination. What makes Tiny Glade really special is the graphics, particularly the colours and lighting, which are just mesmerising!  Birds, butterflies and sheep come to explore your places of wonder as you build, making the area feel alive.It's one of those games that's wonderfully simple, but so charming that you can't help but think of things that could be added.  Some devs might call it a day and rest of their laurels.  Others might add too much and somehow lose the special something that Tiny Glade undoubtedly possesses.  You can feel the love that devs Ana and Tom have put into their creation and, more than that, their good taste and pragmatic approach to the design.  So I feel quite safe that they will add more, but keep the heart of the game intact.  For me, I would love to see more life populate the landscapes I create but whatever they add, I just know it will be brilliant!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I only have a couple of hours in this game, but I can already wholeheartedly recommend it. It's easy to get the hang of most of the tools, although there are a couple of oddities. Doors and stairs only really attach to paths so you need to get creative to place them in the right spot. Then also, sometimes windows morph into doors on higher floors which is kinda... strange and not intuitive at all but it works... There's also some insanely whacky and over complicated ways to make stairs with building parts and walls and neither of these make intuitive sense either and is super tedious, but once you understand it it's fine... Overall it is a great game and I like it a lot. Even an uncreative person like me can feel creative in this. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderfully cozy. If you like essentially sculpting dioramas but in a digital space, this is perfect for you. It is also sheep and duck patting simulator in disguise (10/10 will pat again). The in game camera is FANTASTIC. I fall in love with this game the more I play it. It is a WONDERFUL destresser.There's a lot of really cool build content timelapsed or sped up out there on youtube if you're curious about this game's building limits.I played the free demo and after a few hours, was sold on getting this when it came out.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I just wanna start off by saying i was super hyped for this game and played the heck out of the demo.That being said I was a little underwhelmed by the game after release. It was still super relaxing, but only for the first 30 minutes and then you realize you ran out of things to mess with. The variation in build you can do is pretty lacking with only a few things that you can actually control. You cant choose decor, change flower or tree types, bridges and stairs are not easily created if they even can be, and overall the variation between build can be pretty lackluster. I can't even seem to figure out if there is a way to mass reset the Glade. And I know there are features I just haven't figured out how to take advantage of yet, but honestly i don't find myself motivated to with how dead the environment feels besides the occasional sheep or duck. Perhaps I got myself too excited  for the building possibilities in this sandbox. Overall i think i just got bored with the lack of direction and understanding of the mechanics of the building tools. I still love what this game is striving for and i will continue to follow its development if it continues to get any, I hope the developers keep adding features and designs in later updates of the game and expand on the great idea they have. i know they worked hard on what we've gotten so far at launch, but as of right now even on sale i kinda regret spending 13 bucks on a pretty barren sandbox.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: They should add a save or auto save feature to the game. I just spent over 2 hours on build that i was superrrrr happy with. Then i try and open photo mode and then, boom, my computer crashes and all progress lost. Idk if i am gonna play again but man that really sucks... So a auto save feature would be great.Otherwise great a chill game. worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good! ♡ I LOVE THE SHEEP AND THE BIRDS ON THEIR HEADS ♡♡♡ The cottage-core vibe really shines here, and I'm loving every bit of it. The fact that I can let my creativity run wild and design the place any way I want feels so freeing. Not to mention, everything is just so cute ♡ I hope they add more to the game soon, especially flowers, animals, and decorations!Thank you so much for this wonderful game ♡
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game, super relaxing and soothing. The art style in beautiful. Would love to see more stuff added in the future like livestock, tiny npc people that would roam the map, more types od windows and doors, the ability to make wheat fields, Korn fields or even sunflowers. Would be nice to see more flower and tree types. 8/10, great product.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the game I wanted for years. No risk, no recourse management, no currency to collect, no features to unlock with missions or challenges I don't wanna do.This is just pure, relaxing fun. Creating my own little worlds and everything just works and clicks together exactly in the way you'd expect it to! Could not ask for a better game for autumn and winter right now
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute game. I've followed this game's development on Twitter for a while and oh my god, it's perfect for when you just need... something to do. Something to have fun with, something to destress. It's perfect for letting your creativity run free despite a relatively "limited" palette of things. I really hope to see some more flower types maybe in future updates? Like being able to "paint" them with the painting tool in different "colors", that make them that color + a different type? :) That'd be super neat.Discussing some things about the game beneath so if you want absolutely 0 knowledge about the gameplay, you've been warned!I absolutely LOVE the charm this game has. It's.. just cute. The fact the sheep get parachutes if you build under them, the way the slopes adjust in a really realistic way?? You can even walk around using the camera settings in your own build!You can pet the ducks and the sheep (not the fish.. yet?), the fish actually swim away from you even in the frozen lake. Oh yeah this game also has different "seasons" for settings.I am OBSESSED with the "undo" button animations. It would've been so easy to just.. not.. do that? But it DOES. This game DOES go the extra mile for that character it has.I'm giving this game an honest 9/10 - because I know there will probably be patch updates with "added (900 new things) in the future, which will turn it into a 10/10. It's not trying to be any more than what it is and as a buyer, I'm grateful for that. Super intuitive and charming UI too.Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The complexity of what you can build is not immediately obvious which in my opinion adds to its appeal. You'll be going along thinking you can only do this or that and then, bam, you discover a new technique that opens up so many possibilities. Just go through some of the posts people have made and you'll get an idea of the wonders you can create. I hope more will be added in the future, but what is here is more than enough for the creative mind to run away with. It's just wonderful
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot lot of potential and I hope it will be added in the future. I am greatly enjoying building a fantasy world with an own story but I feel like there is also a lot missing.That said I will still play lots and lots of hours! Its also a good tool for DND Players, writers or artists who want to get a feel for a setting beforehand. Pros: • Artstyle, vibes, music and the feel for the building mechanism is amazing• if you get the hang of it you can do a lot of stuff • various scenarios and the photo area has also good variety in settings"Cons":• Feels like a really small game so far (but its new! so i'm hopeful for more content)• I wish for a few more options for customization with f.e. flowers, trees and decoration. Decoration is being added w/o me having control over it at first. It just plops up• If I set a door and put a path in front of it why is the door gone but a gate is being placed????(If its the case, that I have overseen something please tell me ;; )Havent played much so far, so this review can change, but I wholeheartly recommend it for people who just need to relax a bit !!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Overall mixed on the game. I think it's a solid foundation, but doesn't feel complete. Pros:- Beautiful graphics and art style- Building mechanics are decent- Relaxing and comforting experience- Feels like a lot of passion went into making it- The UI menu is simple to use and well executed- Photo mode is brilliantCons:- Despite the game’s stunning visuals, it's missing many essential features.- Limited variety of tools- Small map size with no option to choose different sizes- No copy-and-paste functionality- Inability to remove bushes or resize grass, which can obstruct windows or doors. The only workaround is to build a path - or raise the ground level.- Many features feel incomplete or missing. Objects don't align well, requiring you to manually adjust them due to a subpar - grid-lock system.- No ability to share your creations and/or maps with others. Even having community-made assets like buildings you can import from other players would be cool. Or having a system where you can save a specific building design so that you can paste into any world and re-use in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a cosy time sink. It is just SO good! I simply love it. It feels comfortable like an old coat. As if I've been playing it since forever. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks awesome. You can create almost every building from small cozy village to a giant spooky castle. One small minus is, that the game needs more decorations and more flowers and trees. But this is only a small problem, because the whole game is awesome. If you need more ispiration there are daily themes too in the game so you can build on a prepared map if you want. Just give this game a chance it is masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game! It's very cute, and relaxing. I've followed this game for a while now, and I am pleased to say it is super fun and sweet!Performance wise, it runs very well. Filling up a full map with stuff keeps a nice 120~ plus FPS at 4K on my rig (5800x, 7900xtx)I love it! Hopefully in the future with some more updates we get some more customization of small assets, the ability to possibly spawn animals (I'd love to make a sheep pen) and such. Hopefully this game is supported for a while! (Also, fully wooden houses/customization would be awesome!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing. Full of Potential (I've already built several buildings from my hometown). The hours fly by. I cant wait to see what might get added later on. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: fabulous, very cosy, very pretty, it's a super game if you want to do cute houses. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The most creative fun I've had in ages. While Tiny Glade does not have any objectives, quests, or tasks, it excels at building any kind of structure, town, castle that you can imagine. One fun detail about the game is the daily challenge (i.e. Build a Spooky Manor, Sun Temple, Library) which can help boost the imagination when needed. There is a little bit of a learning curve but you will pick things up as you play more. The music, sound effects, and graphics really create a cozy vibe that is perfect for a sandbox creator style game. I assume there will be further additions to the game in time as some of the options (windows, flowers, trees, fences) are slightly limited. 10/10 Recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game since I saw the creator(s) on TikTok posting their first videos. I have a couple hours in on the Demo and a few hours in on the full game now. So very happy with it. Great way to relax. Just throw on your favorite youtube or podcast and de-stress! 10/10 would recommend. Can't wait to see the creators next additions or ventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!! After building a huge city there are a few quality of life tools/things I'd love to see added in the future like being able to place the same color/design flag instead of having to change the color of every single one but for now, I had a blast building my city and I loved taking pictures of it in different lighting and times of day. There are a lot of tricks you can learn from youtube videos that make this game so much more fun. Before watching that video I was disappointed by the lack of customization but you'll be surprised what you can do!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: For the price, this cozy game is perfect for relaxing after some PvP games (and building with your chat if you stream.) However, there are some changes I'd really like to see come over time:1. A bit more life ie. more animals, humans. The game feels a little lifeless.2. More tools/a little more control over details of your glade3. An optional mode with really simple objectives and rewards to make it playable over time. Not a city builder, just the option to play a mode where we hit randomly generated goals & have a purpose.4. New atmospheres - spooky woods, holiday, etcOverall I think the game is super cute, and has gorgeous lighting. A tiny bit of a letdown as I thought we would get more from the full release, but still very cute' You can tell the devs really love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a great time playing this in the background while taking calls or listening to music/podcasts. _childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting on this game for a long time. now that it is here. i am beyond excited. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun doodle game, a bit like "townscaper" where you can build your fantasy castle/small town/other medieval style building. The customization is done in a really nifty way, and you can discover many new things, like if you put a window above a balcony it can become a door, you can merge windows to larger ones. Stack buildings to get interesting combinations.There is no "win" condition except when you say you like the result and declare the diorama complete, no competition, no resources, no structural integrity. just your fantasy and the mechanics.And the cute sheep you can pet of course!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Glade is a phenomenal addition to the cozy genre! I was instantly captivated by the demo and couldn't wait to dive into the full game.I thoroughly enjoy building villages and structures, crafting unique stories, and recreating nostalgic childhood gaming environments.If you delight in exploring creative freedom, setting personal objectives, and constructing breathtaking landscapes, then Tiny Glade is an absolute must-play.Highly recommended! _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It's cute, it's cozy, it's stress free and even better, I can use it for D&D! It also allows me to do a lot of environmental story telling with the assets and how things are placed. Fantastic, adorable, and really, really fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what was promised, the price is more than reasonable. It offers a peaceful exploration of one's imagination. The game allows you to explore and discover how to build different structures ect freely, refreshing in a "cosy city builder". And there are cute sheep and ducks that you can pet, 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I heard about the project that became this game long time ago, when I was looking for online courses about tools for the 3D software Houdini. If I remember correctly, one of the creators of this game made a online course about a lake house tool Houdini. I really liked the way that tool was made because when you changed a value it practically changed everything in the lake house accordingly. I really liked this aspect of Houdini (procedural tools) which can apply in FX and modelisation from what I know. When I heard that this game came out while being on sale from the start, I quickly bought it. I am pleased to see that the aspect of changing one thing changes everything nearby accordingly is still present. The daily different doodle is very present when you lack creativity. The music is very nice and relaxing. I wonder what this game would look like with a multiplayer aspect where each person makes their own take of the same environment at different places and that you could compare the differences. It is a great game regardless and very nice when you want to relax from the hardships of life or work.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. I have been wanting a game like this since I was 10 years old, playing minecraft creative mode. As far as building just for the fun of it goes, this is the best game I've ever played. There is SO much potential too, because of course no game is perfect (especially one made by TWO developers!!). I can imagine so much for this game, like having a much larger buildable area, more building/path/decoration features, more landscape designing features, maybe even adding people or indoor design, and being able to walk around in your little town!For how cheap this amazing game is, BUY IT BUY IT BUY IT. Not only is this an amazing game, but you will be supporting two outstanding indie developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really pleasant way to unwind, and occupy your mind for a bit. Its important to understand who this game is for. There is no economy, or management per se. It is limited completely by your own imagination/depth. If you're a '4K snap shooter' player, this game is not for you.If you want to enjoy burning up some time, with very pretty visuals and simple/intuitive procedural building, this game is for you.I have a super high stress job. To come home and play this for a few mins before bed is a real treat. If you are like me, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: So I just installed this game and have like 30 min so far.  I don't usually review games like this but I feel compelled because I didn't think I would like the game. My friend said it would be relaxing. I was worried because some games like this are complicated and overwhelming. Also I didn't see the point without other players or objectives or goals. Wow was I wrong.  Imagine having a paintbrush crafted by God himself. What I mean is that you feel like you are painting but also creating a living world on the fly.  Its hard to ever describe. I used the pond water brush and instantly there was a pond with ducks and fish swimming.  Making buildings and adjusting their dimensions is super intuitive.  The camera mode lets you be artistic and capture stunning photos. But more than that, its like a living zen garden that's alive and all of it is relaxing. The sounds of the minimalism whimsical music, the sounds of birds and water.  My wife loves the game since it is so relaxing compared to other games I play.  This game has so much to offer and anything they add to it will be really cool. Best 15 bucks I've ever spent on a game. Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The game already delivers more than enough for it's price, its chill, beautiful, well made and delightful. Played the Demo and the full version is like a dream to play with.It's a sandbox for happiness, just build, photograph, and even make a collection of your own Tiny worlds. - 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the demo of this sweet game that I played, I can say that you can lean back and build your dream medieval town in a limited way. The game could benefit from adding more small furniture items; for example, if you are building a city or town, the variety and detail of the elements related to those establishments could be increased. Currently, there is a significant lack of architecture and secondary elements in the game, but if we consider the graphics and the interactions between the elements, I believe it has the potential to be a great game.Yani gısacası sanatınızı konuşturacak yeterli eşya yok ammmıınaakeee
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: There is little I can't say that hasn't already been said, frankly. It's the 'creative mode' of building games I've always wanted, it's no-stakes, chill, and if you're like me and used to building games, it feels very intuitive, which is honestly what surprised me the most. I truly can lose hours to this game and at no point do I feel like any of it was wasted.I really love the daily theme too, it's really enjoyable and I love that little push and burst of inspiration it can give. I don't even have complaints, just as hopes for further expansion - even if only in cosmetics: I'd love for more wooden options for cosmetics, so buildings aren't just limited to stone & stucco; greater flower variety, and perhaps even the option to do non-flower options; different options for types of paths potentially. Actually, only one mechanical thing that isn't cosmetics: perhaps a (toggle) option for some guides... if only for when placing windows if nothing else lol.This is truly a gem of a game, and I hope studios - large and small - can truly look at this as proof that every game doesn't need nitty-gritty resource management or the like, especially if it's just to facilitate creative building (I say as someone who does also love nitty-gritty resource management games lol) or a farming sim.This game is going to fuel my creativity for ages, I can just tell. It's also going to give the players of my ttrpg campaigns some really awesome settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: After years of waiting, it's here! Tiny Glade is a cozy game for dreamers, builders, and anyone in need of a little peace.  It effortlessly combines creativity, tranquility, and immersion from head to toe. From the moment you step into its serene, verdant world, you're met with a sense of calm rarely found in video games. This is not your typical city builder or simulation game; Tiny Glade is more of a peaceful sandbox where your imagination can roam free without the stress of deadlines, failure states, or resource management.With just a few clicks, you can construct charming, organic structures that seem to grow naturally from the landscape. There's no grid, no harsh limitations—just you and your creative impulses.The soft, pastel-like colors and hand-drawn textures create a world that feels alive yet gentle, evoking the magic of a storybook come to life. The ambient sounds of chirping birds, rustling leaves, and flowing water further immerse you in the tranquil atmosphere, making this a perfect game for those looking to unwind and escape into a world of their own creation.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun and relaxing, and I keep discovering new things to do, or I'll see something in real life or something that someone else has done and be like: "I've gotta try that!"I know its just released, but I hope for more content in the future to keep things fresh. The "daily challenge" is a fun idea, and it makes me want to get on each day to see what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recomend, this game is so charming and there's features that are not necessary to give but give the charm an immense charm that brings the entire game together.And that's the key feature! the entire game is around combining things together to create an environment.The fish move away from your mouse.You can pet the sheep and if you try to make them fall they get a cute umbrella or an inflatable ring if you put them in water.The game is so charming and I'm only just scratching the surface of this amazing game
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I watched a YouTube video of someone playing this and I thought I might like to try it. 4 hours later and I am hooked. Tiny Glade is a deceptively simple building game. You can create buildings, plant flowers & trees, lay paths, build walls and fences, place lamp posts, squish the sheep and ducks, and before you know it your wife and kids have moved out from neglect and you've lost 30 pounds from not eating. Great job guys. Tiny Glade is so much fun. Try it now as the price is just right. Trust me, if you like to build in games, you will love this diorama builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I kept refreshing the page until I was able to buy it! I never have been this hyped up to buy and play a game as soon as it was available.This game is just perfect for when you feel tired, when you feel overwhelmed and when you need a warm and cozy hug by a beautifully crafted game. It feels awesome, it's fluid and it gives you a lot of options and freedom to decide what you want to build. Replayability is high considering the fact that it has daily prompts whenever you feel like you don't know what you want to build.The sound effects are just superb. Whenever you are building your walls, making ponds or just petting the sheep. Everything just feels satisfying, everything SOUNDS satisfying and it's peaceful. That's what the game is all about, just you and your sheep and your own creations. And that's the best part about the game. Whatever you do, you aren't doing it wrong, You can't do it wrong since anything looks good. All I can say is, buy it. Please- show the devs some love. Show them what we actually want from games. Because this is really it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: It's a typicall game who looks simple and cute but beat the hell out of you and ask you after a few hours: "That escalated quickly!" _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The best cozy game of all cozy games. I hope the developers add some more options in materials eventually and add some features that will make life easier, like bridges and stairs. Copy paste would be great too, and selecting multiple objects to move whole buildings instead of just part by part. But this is an amazing game as is and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The game is enjoyable and beautiful, but it soon loses its charm because once we finish our creation, there isn't much we can do with it.The building process is relaxing, and the game isn't meant for achieving specific challenges, but I would still like my creations to have a purpose when they're finished, not just for viewing and taking screenshots.Even though there are some animals in the game, I miss having more life. It would be nice if someone actually lived in these buildings and did something, so we could feel the satisfaction of having built something for someone.It doesn't deserve negative reviews, but it doesn't quite earn positive ones either. If I had the option, I would give the game a neutral rating due to the issues mentioned.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute game, but unfortunately, there isn't much to do in this game, given its price.What's the most perplexing is that there is a SIZE LIMIT in this game. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems so simple, but the depth of its building mechanics and the charm of its aesthetics really make it a worthwhile gem to invest hours upon hours of gameplay in. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game! I've been following it for a while, and I finally decided to get my hands on it. Best decision I've made in a while. I've only played for 30 minutes or so, but some games you just feel from the get-go.The game runs smoothly and the visuals are extremely satisfying, which, I believe, is exactly what the devs aimed for. You have plenty of tools to build your dreamy little corner, and just as many options for taking that killer shot after you finish building :)I love exploring game mechanics, and for Tiny Glade there are quite a few ways elements interact with each other, giving you customisability you didn't know you had. Right now I'm trying to figure out how to build thicker walls, and, for better or worse, I'm way too stubborn to search it online. Even though I find this fun, some people might appreciate an in-game guide for some of these 'out-of-sight' options, but the community will probably take care of this over time.Another suggestion would be giving players more control over placing decorations / add-ons (the likes of barrels, flower pots, lumber stacks, to name a few). Right now, these are automatically generated when certain structural elements interact (placing a window on the wall at ground floor level can generate a flower pot nearby, or a hanging cloth on the window sill), and they can be changed - cycled through - by clicking repeatedly on the element that generated them. It would be nice if we could place them independently.To conclude this review, I'd like to congratulate the developers and thank them for the love they put into this superb game. I cannot wait to see how it further evolves, because the potential is enormous. I'd also like to add a note for potential buyers: do not expect an architect simulator, as one of the game's core concepts is to take care of many of the details itself, making it a relaxing experience.

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Unpopular opinion, but: no.  The entire game is just building a castle, so I'm shocked at how little control you have over the build.  The build tool is so well designed and easy to use, but just missing so many key things.- You can't change the size of trees or customize them at all - this feels like a huge miss- The colour palette only has a few colours - for example, you can't build a white or light grey castle, or black...etc.- You can't change window/door sizes (or dormers, for that matter)- You can't build hex-style turrets (only circular)- You can't build triangles or other shapes as main buildings (only square)- You can't change the tile size of the move terrain up/down in height feature - can only do huge sections- You can't control customize vegetation:  vines on castle, or gardens, etc.- Multi-story buildings with different things on each story (e.g. a balcony on one level) might be possible - but I can't figure out how.  So basically you just have to have one square block as main building with all levels the sameIf this was an early access game I'd say this is fine, but this is a full launched "Overwhelmingly Positive" game, and I just don't see it.  I'm used to having FAR more control in any building games - which is really whack given the building tool is otherwise really great and intuitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply brilliant is the perfect way to describe this game because it's quite literally simple yet brilliant!It's fairly easy to learn how everything works, there's already heaps of videos that'll help if you're stuck on something but you won't have to follow a full on guide, you could watch someone build for maybe a few minutes and by then you'll know exactly what to do.While there's currently not that much variety in any of the toolbars, there's already a tonne of combinations you can create just with those few so it'll only get better as more content is added but there's plenty for the meantime.Personally I've experienced 0 bugs or crashes in both the demo and full release which is unheard of these days, all of my laptop's hardware is old and outdated too so it's had ample opportunity to do so but it's been flawless so far. Not bad at all especially for a tiny dev team!!!If you're unsure then I urge you to watch literally any video on Tiny Glade, you'll know pretty quick whether it's your type of game or not.Solid 9/10, if we get cobble pathways, rickety wooden bridges and a slightly larger build area in the future I'm changing that to a 10!

_childDocuments_.review: The building in this game is great. When I first played I thought the selection of tools was really limited but they come together in so many complex and small interactions that you can really use to make your builds come together. However, some of these tools can be a bit too fiddly for making certain things (Such as a suspended stair case or a bridge) that makes it feel like they should have their own tools. This game is really addicting and serene. This is really down to the complete absence of any kind of goals, quests, or management of any kind. It means when you boot up the game, you follow what is fun for you, not just the tiny quest markers the game wants you to follow.There are a few features I'd like to see that would bring this up from like an 8/10 to a 10/10. Such as the ability to place props myself (or at least move props already in the world), place crops like wheat (maybe just a painted version of flowers?) and I'd like to see the water features expanded (such as allowing you to place water on top of hills, and adding waterfalls when they fall off of them).

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks simple at a glance but it offers so much variety and the tools can make just about anything. It's yet another proof that small scale developers can make fantastic games and should be supported in the gaming industry. This is one of those games that will only get better with a thriving community and i hope it inspires more devs to populate this genre with games that focus more about relaxing creative outlets. There are an endless list of pros i can highlight but i think the most important one for my personal taste is actually the scale of it. The tools are intuitive and easy and its not . The last thing i want in 3D builder is for it to feel like i am trying to learn Blender again. When it comes to cons i don't think there's any lasting issues that won't be fixed since the devs seem to be very responsive and active. But if there is one issue I'd lift is the need for more optional keybind shortcuts or a copy paste style tool since more complex builds might require me to color in alot of different components one by one and the repetitive mouse motion puts a strain on the hand after a while. I don't mind the repetitiveness of it since it's part of the slow and calm experience of creating something it's just dragging mouse movements that will in the long run be taxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Here are my very early impressions after building my first house:I absolutely love how free flowing everything feels! It really does live up to the "no wrong answers" thing and it does a good job at filling in the blanks when aligning objects in certain places. I can see myself getting lost for days creating just one idea in the future. The controls are intuitive and the style is beautiful. I'm beyond excited to see what people come up with going forward! I expect some crazy castles and mansions that I can't even begin to imagine lol.My issues so far mainly lie within information and content to an extent. I really wish there was a guide or menu to show what types of structures you can create with each tool. For example, the window tool can be used to create doors and trap doors, but not on the ground level. Ground level doors can only be created by mashing the path tool against a wall. I wish these nuances were available to study instead of me trying and failing to find a door tool on the bar. I also wish you could choose what object the game generates to complement what you place (the flower pots, benches, etc). You kinda have to pick up and put down the object until it generates something you like. As for content, there is the right amount for people to experiment with and chew on for a new game. Unloading an insane amount of things at the start would be understandably daunting to most new players. I'm sure the devs plan to add more in the future, but I do wish there was a color picker to get exactly what you want as well as some new tools here and there.Despite my road bumps, I do think this game is an amazing pick up for the price that has endless possibilities! It is worth the hype for sure, but could benefit from more realized systems. I am thoroughly enjoying my time with the game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I've been faithfully waiting for it and yesss, it's finally here, and it's the most beautiful just-chill-and-be-creative type of game. Can't be happier. The lighting, the ray tracing, the atmosphere, ohh...I only wish there were a little more furniture items so that I can do an outdoors sitting area with benches, and a few more plant variations like pumpkins for autumnal builds, for example, or tree stumps, or even mushrooms. But that's definitely for the later updates.For now, it's perfect the way it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't bought this yet, why not? It deserves to be the game of the year, for sheer beauty, intuitive controls, and breathtaking attention to detail.The cosiest building game out there, but don't think the size limits you, you are only constrained by your imagination.11/10 would have paid twice the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! I love the concept! The tools are very user friendly and there are so many customization options for appearances and structure building. The game does a very good job not holding your hand and instead just lets you explore. It's such a refreshing experience to find little surprises that really add to building your own little cottage with an open field or an elaborate castle that towers over a cliffside. I've been following the development of this game for a few years now and I cannot recommend it enough. I was so excited when it launched! The team does a great job creating a beautiful, calm, and relaxing aesthetic to doodle. There is no goals, no challenges, no combat. Just a fun way to see what you can create with your imagination. I love the addition they made of having a daily inspirational creation for when you find yourself a little stuck. The team seems like they respond to feedback pretty well and they frequently put out updates to keep adding new ways to customize your castle or cottage.I can't say enough good things about it. I strongly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The beautiful world of Tiny Glades that you can shape to your liking.I am not a great fan of city-building games combined with sandbox elements since I struggle to come up with ideas about what I want to create and how I want to spend my time within such a game. Despite that I was very much looking forward to the release of Tiny Glades and my expectations were fully met. The game is beautiful and the controls are nice. Although I am not very creative when it comes to building stuff, I managed to create some lovely sceneries while being constantly inspired. One thing I found missing is the ability to add props (aside lanterns, flags). I would be nice to be able to add some carriages, boxes, chairs, tables, etc. I hope that the dev is working on something like that for the future. I also enjoy the ability to be able to jump in and out of the game without much hassle since I am a busy gamer and sometimes I can enjoy one game for only 20-30 minutes before having to do some chores. One thing that fascinated me the most is how well the game runs on the Steam Deck. Controller support is a bit strange, but it is very easy to get used to it and at the end of the day it is sufficient to enjoy the game without any stuttering or issues. Tiny Glades is easily one of the best games released recently in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a long time coming and the devs couldn't have done better, and while they are actively working on this game, if this was it I would love it completely. The ability to just sit back, relax, and build without needing to worry about the "management" that other games have is just what I needed. The fact that if you combine certain items you get a whole new decorative item is so cool. My friends and I are so inspired by this. Definitely recommend, will play for hours on end.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is surprisingly incredible. The amount of creativity you have access to with these simple tools is astonishing.  If there was an award for best UX (user experience) in a video game this would win it by a mile. Everything feels natural and satisfying to interact with. Photo mode options are numerous and useful. Music is pleasant and immersive.Even if it doesn't seem like you would get a lot of play time out of this, give it a shot anyway. It's hard to stop once you start.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I first heard about it on TikTok a few months ago and have been eagerly waiting for it's release. I played the demo and was immediately hooked. My bff got it for me release day and I've just built my first world. I see some negative reviews about how there's not much to do and there needs to be a tutorial. You have to remember, 1) it's a 2 person team and it just released. I'm sure they'll add more over time. 2) If you actually take the time to play around with the different items on the bar you'd be surprised at how much you can do. You just have to have some patience and creativity. It truly is free form and there's so much room for customizing your world just the way you like it. I also love the camera options. My favorite is the walking camera so you can actually walk around the world you created. Once again, I love this game and will be playing the heck out of it and I can't wait to what else the devs have in store for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I've recently been playing Tiny Glade, and I just want to express my admiration for this beautiful game. It's clear that so much love and care has gone into every aspect of it, and it truly shines through in the experience. To the two developers who have shared this amazing world with us: thank you for letting us be a part of your journey and for pouring your passion into something so delightful. It’s a joy to play and a reminder of the magic that small, thoughtful games can bring.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game soothes, you cannot make a mistake and if you do it doesn't feel punishing. All the sounds are satisfying to listen to, you can build whatever you want and you have the freedom to make whatever you want. Its charming in its style and its in a realm of its own. I hope more is added so we can make even more cute little details in our castles, towns and wizard towers. Also, whoever made the music and sound design needs plenty of credit as well. I love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect game for relaxing after a long day of stress. Something about it is just so satisfying...maybe it's the aesthetic graphics or how fluidly all the buildings interact with each other. Not to mention the cute sheep and duckies. Only one thing I haven't figured out...Why is this so perfect?
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: very nice cozy little game. feel free to go as crazy as you want in this sandbox builder.the mechanics are interesting to say none the less but its simple as is and nice to use.do hope the developer continue to add more stuff in the future along with more decorations/misc. i.e boats, animals, foliagerecommended: 4.5 sheep / 5graphics: cozy stylize / 5gameplay: your creativity is the limit / 5value: inner peace / 5music: soothing / 5

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely wonderful game.My list of 100% needed quality of life improvements:NEED STEAM WORKSHOP NOW!!!!Copy and paste function to structures.Way to adjust moonlight and daylight brightness, in essence, amount of clouds. (also different weather effects)Larger buildable map areas, the size it is at now is needlessly restrictive.and probably more requests to come since this is so coolAutomatic bridges with building road maybe?Indoors building some day?
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I find playing this game to be a calming experience. You make adorable little worlds, then photograph them, then tweak what you've created, then photograph again. You change the time of day, or apply a filter, and try again. You don't have a goal given to you by the game itself - you simply invent a scenic locale through play, like scribbling something on a page, and try to capture it from whatever angle feels best to you. The charm of this game is its simplicity
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The game have missing features that should be in the base game IMO:- No copy + paste. Let alone copy+paste selected group.- No group select feature.- Limited build-able land. (Personally it is too small.)- Stairs are incredibly difficult to build as you need to place each steps MANUALLY. Same exists in placing "level-3" windows.- The game need to include more different design/shape variant to their decoration (windows, doors, etc).This is not me bashing the game, I love it already and I recognize its great potential, however it needed just a little more dev time to make it truly great.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never play such kind of games, find them boring and exhausting. But Tiny Glade was the game that made me like this Genre 🙂 Simplicity of designing and compiling things together is so simple, I don't feel annoyed or frustrated.Game Visually is very pleasing too, managing to look detailed and so cartoony if it's the right way to put it :pWhat I believe is missing is modding. Game has okay amount of tools to be used, but it does feel like something else is missing. With mods, not only will people be able to make new, exciting additions for the game, it would drastically increase the player base too. People like to have access to more content if it's possible, that keeps them in the game for years if not longer,Otherwise, I am happy for what you have made at the moment 🙂 Keep going further, don't be afraid to experiment, and I hope to see this game become a classic in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fantastic game. It's entirely stress free, and worth every penny. I also think even the developers probably underestimated just how much detail people could jam into their builds. They've managed to build a game which has so few tools/mechanics that it remains intuitive, while being incredible flexible allowing for very complex and detailed creations. Absolutely excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I've just started to play this game and I already love it. Every time I build a new little cottage, I discover something new. It's fun to explore this game and I'm excited to continue to play it. It's a game that gives you a lot of creative freedom. Some downside to this game is that the controls are a little difficult to get down and it is lacking in a few aspects. I'm hoping they add more animals, even the potential of being able to place animals to build farms. With the game being just released, it's kind of what you should expect. There is a LOT of potential with this game and would recommend this game if building is your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Very little content.  No hedges or bushes, no variety of trees, no variety of paths, no varieties of flowers.  You get dirt paths, stone walls, wooden fences, rectangular buildings and round towers, windows, chimneys, wall/post lights, and flags. That's pretty much it, I'm not kidding.  There's a little bit of terrain stuff - water, and raised terrain which manifests as rock, but no variety.  The editing tools for what you do have are pretty slick I must say, I was impressed with that.But there are no bridges, no wooden stables, no benches, no campfires, no variety in lights, nothing to decorate meadows with such as boulders, wagons, horses, haybales / haystacks, scarecrows, leaf piles, farming implements, gravestones. No atmospheric effects, no moving water, no "city" decorations such as fountains, statues, signs.  No variety in construction materials - no log cabins, no wooden shanties, no metal fortresses.Tiny Glade is more of an idea than a completed product.  After about 15-20 minutes of play you've seen everything it has to offer.  And though you can do a lot with the extremely limited content in the game there simply isn't enough here to hold attention for very long.  This is not a product you can "explore".For what it does, this game should be priced somewhere between free and $2.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly smooth and intuitive controls. Photo mode is amazing. Only downside is once you have built a bunch of maps, there is no real reason to continue playing the game. I hope they add some new features like real bridges, alternatives to sand paths such as cobblestone and the ability to copy and paste (duplicate) buildings.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun chill game. If you're someone who likes to watching videos, listen to music or watch a stream while playing video games, you'd like this. If you're someone who like creating buildings, castles, villages, etc. you'd be very good at this game and have a lot of fun. Kinda a specific audience but for the audience, its top notch.Really cool art style, really fun building mechanics and overall layout to customization and controls and options. Overall, really sick game, but it is a bit limited with its options. what you see is MOSTLY what you get. (There are a few things you can get like doors, stairs, etc.) What i think could be improved is only 2 things:Add a wood style to buildings and walls, and instead of having decorations pop up around windows and doors (as fun as it is to have them pop up) have those decorations as a separate tab that you can manually place down. This would open up a LOT of options in terms of what you can decorate but also what you can also make on your own. If i want to make a scarecrow, training dummy, a market with a bunch of different barrels and boxes or any decoration that isn't apart of the base game, i cant. This would allow the people creating things to take it to the next level and create some really fantastic things.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to spend everyday in this game. Very immersive .I'm hoping they keep adding more stuff , the building stuff for now is excellent. Amazing sound design too. The theme idea is very cool too. I like to stick to og so I can get better with the basic builds first. Really easy to catch on. <3   10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The longer you play the more ways to build you can discover. It's very relaxing and easy to just start building and messing with the terrain. You can make nearly anything your heart desires or make something completely unexpected. I'm eager to see what is added to the game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cute graphics and adorable sheep and ducks - this is for you. If you just wanna spend some time playing a cozy game with great background-music building towns, manners, houses, churches, cottages etc. - this is for you.If you enjoy(ed) building Houses in Sims - this is for you. If you are wondering if you are gonna come up with enough ideas to make this game worth your while - dw, there's an inspirational theme to explore each day.Oh and if you think you have exhausted the limits of this game - I think you are wrong cause I keep coming across features I didn't know about.If you still don't think this game is for you - I'm sure you can think of somebody to recommend it to <3
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best, most relaxing sandbox builders i have ever played. i was concerned when i first opened the game and saw what looked like a very minimum and basic set of tools to work with. but i quickly realized that these tools do much more than what you see on the surface. certain combination of tools, stacking of basic structures, or merging certain things can create more than i ever imagined. i would recommend looking at the community screenshots and artwork sections to see just how much can be done with this seemingly simple builder. this is an absolute gem and is probably the best game i bought in the last 5 years, and 100% the best sandbox builder. i literally hit 24 hrs of game play in less than 3 days XD 100/10 recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I was very much anticipating the release of this game and it delivered! I enjoy finding all of the pop up decorations, and I appreciate the fluidity of the building. I am incredibly impressed and happy with this game! Definitely going to spend lots of time doing daily build 'challenges' and creating my own little worlds!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I had some expectations about this game but I’m a little on, there is no big difference with the demo version. But I think that the game can be greatly improved with simple additions (then a little more complicated to implement in a second part of my opinion) first, I would like there is more diversity in the ways (stone path, cobblestone, with a different style of earth...) and more decorations, even if there are by default that are automatically put when you build a building and add windows for example (the lines to linen, the loads full of straw...) but I would like to add a little everywhere (same for the lanterns, maybe more diversity).Now, a little more complicated, I would like to see two roofs of two different buildings connected. I would also like (even if it is more a wish than an improvement track) that we can merge several constructions build in separate worlds and then created a whole city! That’s it! Despite all this, I find the game relaxing and beautiful. Thanks to the developers for this game and to all of you for reading this review!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: For me, the game is too simplistic, not providing enough tools to be as creative as one would like.  The game has a good foundation.  However, it simply is not worth purchasing at this time, unless it receives more significant updates to game-play.  For those who do not mind this though, it can be very relaxing and enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I recommend it. Just know what you're getting though.It is NOT a game nor anything of the sort.It's more like a Puzzle with no goal or end.You can build buildings which start as quads and you keep pulling bits out, and you can run paths through them n add windows. That's pretty much it.For a De-stresser this I'd imagine is a good goto game I'm sure, but I just prefer something a bit more like Postal 2 after a bad day where I need to chill out. I think my nan might like this though.Conclusion:It's very Zen and very clever for what it does, but you can't get inside what you've made in the end. There's nothing beyond creating your beautiful little Glade thingy and that's actually what a lot of people want of course. This product just gives me mad cravings for Manor Lords.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for months, and bought it as soon as I could (on sale, too)! So far, it's been absolutely delightful. The graphics and style are gorgeous and really add to the ambience of the game. The soundtrack is smooth and relaxing and fits the atmosphere of the game. There is a top down view in the game that could be used as a good map builder for DMs or TTRPGs, alongside a photography mode for taking detailed screenshots of your creations. Right now, the build options are a bit limited, but I'm hoping the devs add more content in the future. It would be nice to add other structures like wells, fountains, barns, and aqueducts. Addition landscaping options like farms and different types of plants and fungi would be fun, too. I look forward to seeing how this game progresses and definitely recommend this to anyone looking to satisfy their castle building itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything I expected it to be and more! The daily prompts with their own unique landscapes is absolutely a winner and I've been checking back every day to see/build on each new one. I'd love if once we start cycling through what I assume is a limited number of prompts we could get the option to simply pick and choose them off a list or generate our own in some way. I'd also like to see a few new variations added to each build category like wrought iron fencing, full glass roofing/siding(greenhouses!) and more decor that isn't directly attached to doors/windows/etc. But overall these are small wishes and I'll be playing the game almost daily regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best calm building games i've played. it'd be an incredible game even through the lens of a year old release rather than having just launched! the building methods seem alot better at encouraging creativity than most games do, and i look forward to seeing where this goes! Has alot of potential for sure :3
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels really nice and I like what they did with it so far. Even in this state it feels good to play to a very large extent.That said, there is indeed room for improvement. Here are some features and components I'd like to see added in future patches:Quality of life: - Copy/duplicate a built component.- Paint all similar elements capability (think of roofs, walls, windows, etc.). It can be a pain to have to paint each and every one of them individually;- Distance indicators between elements so we can determine alignment, with the ability to snap an element if they are three ore more equidistant;- Add an ability to cycle through randomly generated features of a component. It's kind of annoying when you see a signpost appear next to the window of a house, or clothing racks appear on what I'd want to be the window of a stables or granary;New components that would improve gameplay:- Add actual bridges in the road section. I know you can sort of make a bridge using the block and adding roads underneath, but if I want a wood bridge for instance, we don't have that option at the moment. For bridges, straight and arched bridges;- Add a thicker version of the thin wall that we can drag and place. Make it so we can choose whether that thicker wall has crenelations or not;- Add religious symbols such as crosses, half moons, maybe even some random ones that don't pertain to any actual religion, like roosters, hawks, other totemic symbols, etc. I wanted to build a church in a fort and those normally have a cross on top but I didn't have an asset for it in the building options;- Add a drawbridge;- Add wind mill components;- Add statues;- Add hexagon tower/structure option, aside from round and square.Many of these features will make the current gameplay less painful. While I do enjoy it even as it is, I did find myself reluctant to come back to it, due to thinking how much of a chore it is to keep remaking the same component twenty times when I should be able to just duplicate it with a CTRL + MOVE action or something.Basically, I want to build things and enjoy the process. I don't want it to feel unnecessarily difficult. This is a creative mode game essentially and it does a lot of what it promises, but I feel some of these features would make the game feel way more polished and finished than it is at this moment.Still enjoyed it, hence the positive review, but again, there is a lot of room for improvement.I think it would have been more honest to say it is early access since some of the quality of life improvements I mentioned feel pretty essential to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I'd only just started, and within seconds was already immersed in the world of crafting and creation.  The interface is intuitive and requires no extra thought.  The options seem rather minimal, but the possibilities are endless.Yes, if you need a ton of different textures or styles or colors, you'll find this game lacking.  If, however, you're willing to overlook that, you can bask in the beauty and simplicity it all.The game is surprisingly quick to load, quick to start, and responsive.  The automatic visual settings were exactly what I would have otherwise chosen, though I know I can change them.  The music and sounds are appropriately soothing, and the atmosphere is just perfect for a relaxing time.This game is something you can pick up right away and either play for a few minutes or lose yourself for a few hours without any stress or strain.  I personally recommend this to anyone just for the opportunity to unwind in a creative way.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing game, I play this every day before going to sleep. hehe! I just love the aesthetics, I am someone who does not have artistic talents and it feels like you can't really do anything wrong or ugly on this game, just so beautiful, and it you need help with inspiration there's the Daily theme, or check the community for arts and screenshots. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: *This review is only a week into the original launch dateThis is the best and most intuitive creative building sim I have ever played! (And I have played quite a few over the years)If you enjoyed the games Summerhouse, TownScaper, Islanders, and you want that calming atmosphere but a more refined approach that does it's own thing and does it well... This is certainly THAT game. They created their own engine for this, it does what they wanted exactly how they wanted, and you can really feel that polish.I'd highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptionally well crafted entry into what I guess is the "Cozy builder" genre. There's a surprising level of depth in the small number of tools due to the way the game morphs elements together.It's all a matter of how you look at things. Is that a tower? Well not if you glue it to the side of a building and flatten it, now it's a balcony. Perspective matters a lot too, in the same space you can one big cottage that takes up half the map or you can make dozens of smaller buildings at a different scale and build a whole town.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: i enjoyed the level of creativity and freedom you are able to use in this game. Many little things to figure out and learn while playing so its kinda like a little gift every time u figure something else out. Could use some more building shape options. Could use some more color and texture options. Overall i for sure recommend this game to people who like games with freedom and many possible outcomes according to their actions.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the feedback around this game, and I get it - there are some limitations right now. But let’s not forget, this is a fresh concept created by just two people. Honestly, it’s a brilliant effort. These days, we often expect too much I feel. I've logged hours into this game, exploring every facet, and my 10-year-old son is right there with me.Sure, I hope for more tools and features in the future, but calling the game limited feels off to me. There’s plenty to dive into beyond what’s in the demo. It doesn’t just throw everything at you; you’ve got to think creatively and experiment to unlock its potential - and that’s a good thing.Visually stunning and genuinely relaxing, this game sparks creativity like nothing else. I’m impressed with what’s been released so far, and I’m excited to see how it evolves. Of course, there will always be critics, but take the feedback with a grain of salt. Keep pushing forward and improving! Great job!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is purely delightful. It's so beautiful, relaxing and fun. And the daily challenge is great if you aren't feeling creative and you might need a head start for an idea. I fell in love with the preview I saw for Tiny Glade ages ago and have been waiting for so long. It's worth it though. There are no timers, no fighting, no death, no scores, no struggling to beat off hordes of the undead. It's just peaceful, meditative building and creating. AND you can pet the three little sheep that wander about. They will baa when you do. And if you add a little pond, you can also pet the ducks and they will quack. It's so freaking cute and sweet.The controls are easy to learn. And I keep finding new things I can create. OH, and if you do something to disturb a sheep sometimes they will pop out an umbrella and float up for awhile to a new place. omg, that's just the most precious thing, lol.When you start a new build, there are some elements in place, which you can delete if you want, of course, but it's great because I keep finding things i didn't know I could create, and I can reverse engineer them to learn how to do it. If you like peaceful meditative games, this is for you. It's easy to get into a blissful creative flow with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is delightful! No stress, just putting down buildings, raising little hills and towers. There are sheep, and you can pet the sheep. Adding windows, changing the colour of the roof. If you add a stream or pond, ducks will come. You can pet the ducks!There are one or two tiny UI things that could be improved (eg. for flat topped buildings), but this game just came out, and they're still working on it.The camera feature is great! You can change from an aerial view to the perspective of someone walking around.  Everything always looks cute, even when I made an obviously haunted castle.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: It's a chill game. Just wish it had more to decorate with and also when walking into a building it's just empty with no floors. Needs more options to change around and maybe even an option to pick and choose what to put around the building rather than always something random. Also the buildings should be able to be a bit taller, needs different door options. Hopefully these will be updates later. Feels like it was meant to be released as early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: no stuff to decorate reallyThe game is truly cute and cozy.It has sweet graphics, the sound scape is really pleasant and it does what it promises as in being a castle builder without restrictions to story line process or money needed.But it doesnt have really anything to decorate the landscape around. There are no benches, flower beds, etc. which would make it so much cuter and nicer as we could use those to decorate the buildings & landscape. Rn the builds kinda feel like ruins or cute lost places.  I hope we will get more deco things so we can decorate our builds in the future. until then i wouldnt recommend to those who like to use clutter and more deco objects.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Really relaxing and fun to play with. You can get really lost in the details. Had 2 crashes at the beginning, but always saved everything and went smooth sailing after that. It definitely needs some more options for building in the future but playing around to get certain results, that arent quite obvious at the beginning is quite fun. Similar to how you put stuff together in Minecraft to simulate for instance a living room or a kitchen, you can play around with buildings and roofs to create for instance a bridge with a roof or a well.Its the small stuff, that makes it great: The music, the animals, how windows and doors change the surroundings in a natural way, the small stuff appearing when placing windows and doors, how you can turn any building instantly into a ruin by deleting a small portion of it.Its a game you can play for how long you want and then come back to it later or just start with a completely new map.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Played the Demo before release and rather enjoyed it then. The full game brings with it quite a few elements and definitely gives way to a lot of cool builds! Although things like bridges don't exist, the fact that the very next day after release they put out an update gives me hope that maybe that'll be a future thing.But even if nothing of any substance gets added, the game is worth $12 as is. I got it a little cheaper cause I already own House Flipper 2 so the bundle took a $1 off. Its super relaxing and just fun to play with as the generation adds a spice to the genre of peaceful building.(I would like to hope for the potential ability to maybe re-roll what gets randomly generated next to windows, doors, or walls. Would also like to see the option for farmland and broken/shuttered windows. Being able to add things like alleyway posters or signs (for shops) would be a really nice touch as well. Way down the line, signs for paths and chairs/tables to separate businesses from homes would be cool too!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: This game would be perfect if it wasnt for the fact that one thing about it was so incredibly wrong: It doesnt have post apocalyptic vibes.Ok ok, all joking aside, this game is a full on 10/10. But why did I make that joke above? Well I can explain that as I review the game so its a 2 for 1 journey right here.This game is what I wanted for years. A small game in which you get to create a small world space on your own. Make it immersive, make it pretty and most of all, make it your own. I had been craving this type of experience mostly with the aforementioned post apocalyptic vibes. a world reclaimed by nature. And while to a degree one can achieve this in Tiny Glade, its not exactly a modern world but very much medieval.And yet I could not love it more. Pounce Light is honestly very much underpricing this game. I know, many people probably would not pick it up at a higher price. I get that. But this game is very much easily worth double the price if not a flat out 30 bucks in terms of what it brings to the table.Not only do you have a full on manipulatable world space all for yourself, you have access to seasons, themes and heck a whole range of pallete swaps and colors to make your builds truly your own. From a small house in the wood, to a ruin inbetween the rocks. From a grand magnificent castle to a evil lair. Its honestly entirely up to you what you want to see.So whats there to really want more? Stairs that I can place. Yea I want to place stairs, sue me lol. The autogenerated ones are nice but I wanna place ones that go up the wall on the side and lead to a door. That would fit this game so well.And devs, if you should read this and I know you already seen my forum post much earlier: Thank you for this game. Its a super lovely experience. And while I have you, maybe I can put a post apocalypse version on the wishlist? Nah I doubt it, you got your hands full with having to support this game and for as much of a work of passion this truly was, you guys know what you can do best. So keep going. But you cant blame me for dreaming :P
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: I just bought Tiny Glade within the first hour of its launch.I highly anticipated this game as I already enjoyed the demo, but a few things are bothering me :- I thought the final product would let aus play in a much bigger area. It is fine for a little castle, but why not let us create a small village or even a city medieval like Carcassonne ? I really hope the area will expand.- It would be nice if the towers could expand at least twice higher. I understand there must be a limit but fantasy-like watchtowers are always nice.- Same with the elevation of the terrain. If it could be at least 4 times higher we could create some beautiful vertical castles and cities.Thanks for the good work, and I hope these requests will be considered : )
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: October 11, 2024Tiny Glade is a simple building game, it is simple and serene, yet you can create complex building and scenes.  I love the way parts and pieces can be combined to make something unique. The daily inspiration theme is one of my favorite parts of the game. The Daily theme keeps me coming back each day. There is nothing to dislike, I just want more parts and pieces. I can't wait to see what comes next as the Devs continue to develop Tiny Glade.To the Devs,Thank you for such a wonderfully simple, satisfying and sort of meditative game. After 30 hours of play I have created a wish list of sorts. I am sure you are planning most of this already but just in case here is my list.First, it would be nice to be able to add the items that show up when you had doors and windows (plants, benches, hay bales, sign posts, wood piles etc.) individually.Additional items:     Larger Area to build would like to make a whole village       Crumbling walls/buildings & piles of rubble to create ruins more easily      Stair cases (spiral and regular)      Boats       More animals (wild, farm, and pets)      Open doorways with no doors       Rotting wooden doors Enjoy your well deserved break. Congratulations on your nomination, and again thank you for such a wonderful game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great,  but I think there are some additional tools/features that should be added. A copy-and-paste tool would help a ton especially if you want a lot of the same structures. A select tool, specifically group select, is much needed for moving multiple items. It would also be nice if the height and width limit for structures should be higher. The water tool has a lot of potential, like it would be great if we could make a waterfalls and I think that we should be able to create a pond on elevated ground. I think the game feels a bit lonely. Maybe add some NPCs that will live in the structures. Lastly, just like other people have said maybe a feature that will allow us to customize the interior in the future? English is not my first language so I'm open for questions if some things are not clear.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: God its so refreshing playing something so simple and cute. I could not imagine writing a negative review on something like this. I don't even mess with cutsy games but this awesome. You guys made something truly special, well done.Edit: Currently, the game is a little bare bones. But with whats here, there's tons of building tech to be done. People that say "oh you can play for 40 mins and see everything" aren't really right. There's tons of little things you can do with just the bare bones stuff that it seems most of these negative reviews aren't doing yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! So dynamic how it adds decals and the world grows around your creations, this is incredible! I only just started playing, but I can tell this is going to take a huge amount of my life for the next few months. The only complaint I have is Wacom tablet support would be incredible! I got all excited and plugged mine in, and was disappointed the camera controls don't work with it. Minor complaint, I'm over it, this game is such an incredible feat for a small team, hats off to you! Way to go!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Glade

_childDocuments_.review: Been trying out to make my own Medieval Town built around a ruins of a former castle and I'm really happy i managed to pull it off greatly! It's definetly a cozy game to spend hours into, And I'm looking forward for the next thing to build, Maybe i be able to build a whole city next time or one cozy fishermen house!
