_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice small gem. Short but well built. Extremely pleasant graphics and well organised atmosphere, with slight 80s vibes. I didn't like that the story is pretty obvious shortly after the beginning (could have been some kind of a twist if done differently...)  but still enjoyable.Less than 7 hours to 100% it.For ultrawide users: the game is Vert- but if you use the usual Maintain_YFOV trick you can restore the correct FOV without any unusual fisheye effect and cutscenes are also scaled properly.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Gylt was a pleasant surprise to me. I initially thought it would be a game for children, but I was mistaken. Gylt showcases beautiful graphics with meticulous attention to detail in the art style that enhances the game's immersive nature and captivates players from start to finish. The search for Sally's missing cousin, Emily, drives the story forward, and the game successfully explores themes of guilt, fear, and friendship. The beautiful relationship between Sally and Emily is a significant aspect of Gylt, adding depth and emotional resonance to the game's narrative.It's worth mentioning that Gylt is remarkably polished, no glitches or bugs, providing a smooth gameplay experience. Additionally, all achievements can be unlocked without any issues. Gylt offers three distinct endings, including two bad endings and one good ending. The game allows you to obtain these endings without replaying it entirely; you can return to the campus after completing the game to collect any remaining items.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game!I played the whole game in one sitting (just under 6 hours first playthrough) and had to play more to get the collectables to get the secret ending.The story, the graphics, level designs and gameplay mechanics were great. It was a good balance on everything.Had an Alan Wake feel to it at some moments.I know some people have gotten annoyed and complained about dead ends in the game, but they are usually people who don't really enjoy or go for collectables in games, which is what some of the dead ends in the games were.If you use the map by looking in your backback with TAB, you can easily work out where you need to go next for the story or where you haven't been to find the missing keys etc for progression in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Good game but....The game it's good, but it's not comparable to RiME.The story it's heartwarming and the levels design are good enough. Visual style it's appealing while technically not so up to date, which doesn't actually worsen the quality of the game. Completing the full game finding every object takes some time which it's actually nice and accounts for about 10 hours.Sound wise, the music it's pretty awesome, just on par with RiME even though the later had some more memorable themes.The downside of this game it's the game mechanics itself. They aren't bad, but they are very repetitive. You haven't much to do but hiding over and over. I appreciate some stealth levels but in this game it's all you get. I would have preferred if the game mechanics changes a bit from level to level. There is also another thing that quite annoys me, and that's the extremely easy difficulty level. While not every game has to be a Dark Souls type, it's frustrating when you reach one of the few simple puzzles and suddenly you get the protagonist talking telling you exactly what the "puzzle" it's about. Puzzles are already extremely simple to have those kind of hints right when reaching one. I preferred RiME kind of puzzles and game mechanics by far.Obviously, GYLT and RiME are not the same game, but they do come from the same studio and this one feels like a step back in terms of quality.The game it's still good enough to put some time on it so I definitely recommend it but try to get it on sale. Because, even though the game it's not expensive, for the short life spam that it offers and the repetitive game mechanics, I feel it's worth a bit less than it's normal price.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting horror game, even though the art style is cartoonish/cute the subject matter is pretty heavy, as it deals with school bullying and the effects it has on children. Which is also what makes this game quite unique for a playthrough, because you dont see too many games touching on this subject of matter. Gameplay wise, this is a stealth action game, think an easier Metal Gear Solid. The story was what really kept me going, I was surprised by how polished this game is. Total game time is about 5 hrs 30 mins to 6 hours. I recommend this for someone who enjoys horror and interesting storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: This was my favorite Stadia exclusive so I was really excited to see it finally come to other platforms. I picked it up the second it went live on the store and I do not regret it. 7.5 hours later and I've got 2 of 3 endings, all the collectibles, and just have 9 more achievements to wrap up.To me, this game has a story that reminds me of Sea of Solitude, environments that remind of The Evil Within 1 & 2 with a little bit of Obscure thrown in, the cutscenes remind me of Deadlight (which was also by Tequila Works so that makes sense), and when you put all that together you get a fairly compelling horror game with a sad story. I really, really love this game. I loved it on Stadia and I love it even more now. I'm definitely going to buy the physical Collectors Edition for PS5 to add to my collection (the front of the CE looks like Sally's backpack !!!)Anyway, I got off track a tiny bit with the physical there but if you like games like the ones I mentioned above, definitely check this out. It's got exploration, stealth, puzzles, a great story, etc. I really think you'll love it if you give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Flawless. Just a classic game. Great story, graphics, and sound. Gameplay is good, but nothing too innovative. It's an adventure horror style with some light puzzles. The map is nice and you'll probably find most collectibles with a few left after you finish the game. Using a controller was perfect (it was the Stadia exclusive game, thankfully it could move on). Good length too. Perfect performance on Ultra, zero crashes.After you finish the main story you can go back and finish collecting stuff if you'd like.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Takes a masterful use of atmosphere, audio and level design to scare people without any cheap crap like jumpscares or gore. But this game manages. Incredible atmosphere, good story and well-acted protagonist more than make up for this game's simplistic stealth gameplay.The only thing I really didn't like is that you need to get all the rock people collectables to get the good ending to this game and those are really convoluted to obtain. For example you need to get 6 birds with your flashlight and that opens one unmarked room in the main building second floor without any prompt, cutscene or any indication that it happened. And afterwards you need to go to courtyard to the statue and activate the plaque to get to another one. And then you have to do some map cheating with the elevator to get a third hidden one. Without a guide there is no way players can be expected to figure something like that out by just exploring the level. At least most enemies don't respawn... When you make collectables this convoluted to find you should never make them have a significant impact on the story.Otherwise, I highly recommend this game. Just read a guide on all the rock people locations before you proceed to finale (you'll know when).
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Gylt is a good niche game: its got slight horror, puzzle, and combat along with  wonderful characters that gives a compelling people to root and feel sorry for. Only two characters have names in this game where as the rest our done in single entry journals that do a wonderful job in giving us a idea of what these nameless characters were like.Monster design is quite nice and simple, there's not to much going on and it works for this game.Spoilers AheadBosses, while interesting, do not have proper boss fights. Only one boss is actually fought and you fight him twice. There are two others, a stealth boss and a escape boss. the stealth one you can just ignore stealth for the most part if you have the healing to get through.There is a implied Fight or Stealth in most encounters but your resources are so plentiful that you would save yourself so much trouble by just fighting through everything.My biggest gripe is that the true ending requires you to get at least three  complete sets of collectibles that require each other for completion.I also hope that we can get a sequel to learn more about the dangers of the mountain and to either deal with them or bury them cause even though you escaped the evil the evil is still very much there. Its almost next door for crying out loud.This is a game worthy of trying out, i played it do to seeing a little bit on Superhorrorbro so if the devs wanna get games like this known they should check out you-tubers who play specific types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: People are drawing comparisons to Alan Wake and while I see it on a surface level, this isn't that at all. Nor is it as good as Alan Wake. - M+KB Lock-in is enabled by default. I don't think it is advisable to turn this off but then you lose some significant gameplay. Having it off also disables your crosshair from being red when aimed at a weakpoint so now you aren't sure what to "shoot"- AI placement and detection is questionable. The distraction and detecting leaves me a little confused but that may just me not having enough time in the game. With the distraction soda can tutorial, the enemy is placed in a questionable position. I threw the can to distract it and hid further along its path. Where I hid, the monster can detect me and there are no soda cans around. Turns out I can just run to the door and it'll sense but not detect me, even though the placement, how its facing, and the indicator all showing that if I come out then I'm screwed. - The AI (I don't think) can't see anything past its "zone". If there is an enemy patroling a specific hallway, if you are in a connecting room and you can stare at him through the window without him caring. The environmental design people drew blinds right next to the window but left the window completely bare. - The environmental and level design in my opinion is the worst offender for it being made that way because "video game". Looks completely unnatural and out of place as an actual real world location. - Less said about the writing in the story, the better. The overarching story is interesting but the actual storytelling from the writing and the environment leave something to be desired.I'm not entirely knowledgeable on the staff from Tequila Works but some of these issues seem to stem from a developer's first game. I know it's their first game as that studio label but not sure where Stadia got their employees from when they asked for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: When Emily is bullied at school she runs away, and her cousin Sally is out looking for her when she stumbles into an otherworldly place that seems to manifest the darkest thoughts of those it traps. As dark forces confront her will she be able to overcome them and rescue her cousin who is trapped too? Or is it all in Sallys mind, borne out of guilt (or GYLT if you prefer) for failing her?GYLT is essentially a young adult version of Silent Hill smooshed up with elements from Alan Wake, such as light being your main weapon against enemies and including some fairly generic chase sequences. In terms of the graphical style and narrative content it is very tweenage, with a cartoony Tim Burton-esque look to it and themes that are somewhat childish in nature, because its...uh..about children and for....uh.....children.Soooo, yeahhhh....not all that for anyone who isn't a child....This isn't like Coraline where its for the youth but is warped enough to be unsettling for adults.  This is pretty toothless, with simple combat, simple stealth, and basic set-pieces. Where it is more involving is the puzzles, which, whilst not head-scratchers, are pleasantly involving, and although I don't find it particularly rewarding as a story or experience, I'm not the age group its intended for.This isn't going to be Silent Hill 2 and that's okay (no sex-ee faceless but busty nurses here for those thirsty players ignorant to their meaning!), but you just have to know what you're getting isn't for adults. With game-play that's been done better elsewhere, and a life-lesson that's distinctly pre-teen / teen in its level, this is nothing more than an okay way to spend a few hours. Considering the generally high craft on display here that might be a harsh assessment, but it's an honest one, so there you go.Is it badly written? No. It won't win any awards but its not cringe because of the execution. The "message" is a worthy one, it's just nothing new to me and is at a level where you'd hope I've learned it by now, considering I'm old enough to have one foot in the grave at this point. Unless I happen to live to around 300, in which case I have one-sixth of a foot in the grave....(do the maths as to my age....)Bullying is bad m'kayyyyy?! But as the world gets ever more "woke", what exactly is bullying? Is it disagreeing with someone? "I like the colour blue" "I think blue is sh*t and that red is a much better colour" "Whah! Whah! You hurt my feelings disrespecting the colour blue, stop bullying me with your anti-blueisms. Respect my truth or reveal yourself to be a hater" (or some-such  bull-sh*t)"Get f*cked you snowflake!"It honestly feels like the world is one step away from such moronic entitled thinking, where everything the individual  believes and feels must have worth to it. Soon there might be a day where calling a flat-earther a "f*ck*ng idiot" is offensive, even though it's merely stating a truth you feel after formulating that opinion based on....um.....the scientific fact that the earth is round, and that to think otherwise is an indication of mental illness or massive stupidity. As an adult you get posed philosophical quandrys such as: an out of control train is hurtling down the tracks towards a switching junction, and ahead on one side is a woman with a baby in a pram, and on the other side is a group of people. You can give it a twist and say that the group is all old folks who have already lived a good portion of their lives,  thus adding in another moral question about ageism when it comes to worth, but essentially the point is whether the needs of the many outweigh the few and which side will you pick.In this game you are a bad person because you are emotionally immature....as a child yourself...and apparently DESERVE to be stuck FOREVER in an an evil dimension because you...uh...didn't want to play with your much younger cousin...?? Oof! I know life can be cruel, but that's a bit harsh considering it's natural to put away childish things as you mature and as such grow apart from your siblings. Because you didn't defend her from the bullies you are a bad person and DESERVE to be stuck in this horrible supernatural place FOREVER!!!! I mean, that's pretty harsh too, considering that your character isn't that old herself and gets bullied as well. But no! She's a piece of sh*t because she didn't either (a) get her head kicked in too, or (b) know that (as a child) she should be dealing with things that are generally overseen by adults. On the one hand you can understand Emily acting like a child, because she is one, but on the other hand:  She is a whiny little sh*t and honestly seems like she's destined for a life of prozac even before the bullying (which, to be fair, is horrific) and being "betrayed" by her cousin because she was moving away from her with age (which is bull-sh*t entitlement on her part as an immature kid)I get that these are the trials and tribulations of youth, those growing pains as we evolve into adults that are hopefully more reasoned and intelligent beings. But the truth of it is: The world just gets darker and deeper, and the "horrors" (such as it is here) of childhood pale in comparison. After, what? 30,000+ years of human development? People are still sh*t to one another no matter how old they are. Funnily enough, this isn't something the game feels the need to address....You even get an achievement called 'violence isn't the answer', which is very zen, yet sadly as a species that statement is a crock of sh*t when looking at our past, and..um...the present...and....er......our future. And also you earned this achievement by committing lots of acts of violence, so whilst it may not be the answer to bullying (reality seems to suggest that it very much is the answer) it was certainly quite helpful when it came to defeating demonic entities.According to this game, all we have to do is be "good to one another" a la 'Bill & Ted' and everything will be A-Okay. So: the next time you get bullied, try being nice to them. And then, when that doesn't work and they become emboldened by your perceived weakness, you realise that VIOLENCE IS THE ANSWER and you do your best to beat the sh*t out of them instead of getting beat-up yourself.  Here endeth the lesson when we're not in the la-la-land of twee make-believe that is young adult entertainment. Is it right to fight fire with fire? No (unless its an actual fire and you're burning things to make a fire-break). Will you stop being a victim? Probably. Until lobotomies become a cure for why people have been so sh*t for thousands of years, it's naive to think that a species which still has a primal pack mentality doesn't require alpha displays of power.This game has a very simplistic view of morality and personal responsibility, and as such is rather underwhelming by its conclusion. As entertainment it was a passable, somewhat enjoyable experience, but as a deep and thoughtful examination of the human condition.....well....that will depend on your age range as to its "complexity" in that regard.It's got a plucky, emotionally tortured young heroine! (female empowerment of the yoof!!) It's spooky and ookie and fwightening! (scary!!) It deals with "heavy themes"! (but then has nothing to say about them beyond neatly packaged outcomes for dramatic purposes) When you add it all together with the fairly average game-play it becomes a bit "meh!", but overall it did enough to hold my attention, so I give it a positive with some *coughs* caveats involved.  Bare in mind that I am a jaded arsehole and am perhaps being unreasonable about "a bit of fun", but then again: If you are doing a game about serious themes such as terrible bullying, doesn't it then invite more examination as to its worth? This has nothing to say, and given the topic, never could. Its not frightening or especially amazing as entertainment either. For the price its alright for a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Optimization seems to be a bit bad.  While the game runs rather gracefully it certainly puts a lot of pull on the CPU which feels kind've strange.  Obviously based on my hours played here, I did not finish the game.  Ultimately the puzzle aspects left me scratching my head trying to figure out how to solve at times, and I didn't want to jump in and out of Youtube to try to figure them out. _childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: GYLT is a very safe product that lacks depth in any department, be it gameplay, story, or else.It handles player with kid gloves, never forcing you to think about anything too much. The story is bland and characters, of which there are only three, are boring and uninteresting. The main protaginist is typical stoic character, the "villian" is misunderstood and simply needs love, and Guide is there so that the protagonist knew where to go, and to remind the player the motivation to go forward.The setting sometimes tries to be nightmarish and otherworldly, but majority of the time it mimics real world locations, be it classrooms, prison cells ect. There are only few locations where you get to appreciate the twisted nature of the world. Praise where praise is due, the graphics are very detailed and very snappy and pleasing to the eye. If you interested in exploration of topic of bullying, you will find none here. The game "shows" bullying through mannequins doing bad things to other mannequins, simply depicting as much as possible scenarios, throwing them at the player in a hopes something will stick. It's all straight forward with no nuance, and with how much these situations are depicted, considering the person who manifests these are ~10 years old, absurd. And the bullies are monsters. Thank you game, very cool.Speaking of game and its gameplay. Game allows the player to eirher sneak or fight their way through. Sneaking is ruined by rudimentary gameplay, mondane locations and aggresive UI that constantly shows AI awarness, rendering any sence of suspence obsolete. That leaves the player with more fun gamestyle of fighting, that the game also promotes by showering player with ammo and healthpacks. Despite very limited variety of enemy types - there are four monster types (not counting bosses), two of which you actually fight - they provide just enough engagement to vary the slog of playing this game. Enemies can dodge, hide their weak spots, rush you, teleport, and their attacks are dangerous. And even though I had to disable auto aim to have some fun, two and more monsters provide a good challange.That being said, enemy design is completely unfit for this game, specifically the level structure. Enemies usually patrol a small area, they cannot croutch and leave the floor they are standing on. But their locations often have many vents or highgrounds, which allows a player to simply camp monsters while they are dumbly stand right infront of the vent or small highground you may find yourself in. Vanquished enemies dissapear from the world, and that makes the locations feel empty afterwards. Puzzles are easy and straightforward, and at some point it made me realise that the game does not want the player to think, it urges you forward, but it also doesn't trust you with interesting puzzles as to not suspend your progress. This game is what happens when you take an interesting topic of bullying, streamline the story to be as simple and safe as possible, and put it on gameplay rails that are both easy and flawed, And while the graphics and high detail may attract few players to try it, I cannot see this game being a topic of discussion, fading away into obscurity not as some hidden gem, but as a very mediocre product.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that i need to shout this in all caps:YOU DO NOT LOCK THE ONLY DECENT ENDING BEHIND COLLECTING RANDOM GARBAGE, are you kidding me?!I could understand if it was plot-relevant diaries or something. It is not, you can miss them to your heart's content.  Instead here is what you need to do:- Collect 10 red rooks- Put 10 random (and I mean random) souls to rest using aforementioned 10 red rooks- Collect 6 birds.Some of that stuff is hidden in some asinine moon logic places. You do all that and your ending will be just abrupt and unsatisfying, and not, you know, infuriating. And that even not touching the fact that this game moonlights as anti-bullying PSA, with disclaimers and everything, and fails miserably at it. I'm serious, implications of the "normal" endings are insane, ill-advised and very irresponsible, just shy of The Medium and The Suicide of Rachel Foster (mostly because the subject matter is a little more tame). I'd recommend playing it with the achievement guide from the very beginning.The game itself is alright, I guess. It's like Silent Hill for the beginners. It looks mostly good if you don't count very rough comic cutscenes, The pacing was tight before it did a nosedive due to 1,5h of garbage collecting.I can VERY cautiously recommend it at 75% off or more.===================================================Is it just me or the grandpa in this game really looks like old Postal dude?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hesitant thumbs up.  More of a middle thumb, really.This game, overall, is passable.  It plays as it should, it looks okay and it sounds okay (ish).The thing is, I don't agree that the story is anything to write home about.  The themes here are very common at this point and there are other games that talk about them more adeptly.  Gylt has far too many moments of contrivance and clunkiness to tip over into "great" territory.On the technical side of things, this is yet another game built in Unreal that ships without DPI awareness.  If you are running your monitor with display scaling, you will have to edit the executable's compatibility flags.  This is something that can be easily fixed with a simple project setting toggle, but SO MANY Unreal developers miss it.The game is also strangely demanding despite not looking like it should be.Finally, the game has these pointless motion comic style cutscenes.  I say they're pointless because the game also contains real-time cutscenes that are fully voiced and animated.  The motion comic sequences are also heavily compressed, which sticks out like a sore thumb in 2024.Ultimately, this is an okay game to play through if you get it on sale, but you shouldn't pay full price.  You definitely shouldn't now that we have no idea where the money's going.

_childDocuments_.review: I do highly recommend Gylt. I was expecting some kind of adventure toonish-like kind of game but I found a entertaining, disturbing, creepy and fun horror game to play. The story was also surprisingly good: finding and reading the documents is really worth it. Overall a great surprise and will love it if you like horror, exploration, stealth and good story.

_childDocuments_.review: GYLT is a really good, beautiful and emotional horror, adventure game with so much to love and this is one of those types of horror games that's perfect for kids to play, but they have to be 10 and 11 as this is a great way to get them into horror, okay the story.The town of Bethelwood an old mining community located in Maine is where are little girl named Sally lives, unfortunately Sally's life is not easy dealing with bullies and generally just growing up, but it has become even worse since her little cousin Emily has disappeared having been missing for a month. Desperate to find her, Emily spends every day putting up missing poster flyers even when all hope seems lost and everyone has given up hope, but after being chased by a group of bullies Sally is soon dragged into some nightmarish and weird version of her hometown where her fears and worst memories are brought to life and twisted into a wicked monstrous forms, but all is not lost as she has found her little cousin, so despite the danger decides to save her and perhaps they can both escape this hell.Alright the likes, the story is absolutely fantastic it's beautifully written as it delves into its themes of bullying, depression, isolation and peer pressure and so much more, it feels like if Silent Hill was written by Ray Bradbury or Katy Towell, it just feels beautiful and heartfelt and almost made me cry. The graphics art style is really good and beautiful it has this stop motion feel to it like Coraline and ParaNorman, especially when it comes to its character designs. It also has incredible uses of color, scenery and character designs and just the overall design of the graphics.The levels in the game are really good it mostly takes place in a school and some of its surrounding areas and they are all incredibly well detailed from little potted plants to an arcade and generally the bizarreness of this twisted school, it's all incredibly good and quite visually distinct and makes you just want to stop, stare or just explore and see everything.The characters are really good, we only get three but each one is very well written, like Emily as she feels like an actual 7-year-old girl going through a difficult time in her life, Sally feels like an actual 11-year-old girl who's trying to be seen as mature but is still a little kid and you just want to hug them both.The mysterious old man is also well written as he has this mysterious air to him and you don't know if he's a good guy or a bad guy, but you do get a sense that he's trying to help and he's just very old and sad. The enemies and bosses are really good each one has their own unique design that really ties in with the story and it's themes, I think my favorite enemy has to be the dolls as they're really creepy looking with pretty good voices.The gameplay is really good it takes some inspiration from Alan Wake I.E using a flashlight to fight off enemies or sometimes distract them or blind them in order to get past them as you go around, explore and solve puzzles. The puzzles are very good, it’s all most all environmental puzzles and some wire puzzles, they can be quite tricky but not to the point where it's frustrating, it just takes a little brain work.The music was good with plenty of great haunting soundtracks that just takes you back to movies like Coraline. The voice acting is good not one character gives a wooden performance, each one is quite good. My favorites has to be the old man and the doll enemies, the dolls even those they has a few lines are repeated it's actually quite nice to listen to and the old man’s voice acting you could really hear/feel how sad, tired but still trying to help.The atmosphere is pretty good nice and spooky for first time players as you're wandering around dreading what's going to come out and get you. The notes are very good it really paints an interesting picture about the town and how this all started and there's also plenty of room for a sequel. Now then is the game scary, kind of yes but it’s mostly a general spookiness, sort of like Coraline or some of Ray Bradbury, RL Stine and Katy Towell’s works, we have the right level of scariness that kids and adults can enjoy.Alright the dislikes, now I would say this game is perfect, but there is a problem there's this game breaking bug that I encountered in my first playthrough for some reason when I was far in the game my stuff disappeared like all the notes and stuff, also the enemies like the eye stalks just reset, at first I didn't really care but then when I tried to meet the old man to get access to the mine, but I couldn't go through the main door due to the fact that the eye stalks were behind it that I destroyed previously and I could not fix it and was locked out of completing the game, so I had to start the whole game over. Alright then now that I told you all this GYLT is a really good, beautiful and emotional horror, adventure game with so much to love, with it absolutely fantastic story, really good characters and a really good and beautiful graphics art style.So I highly, highly, highly recommend this game you will definitely enjoy it, it's also the type of horror game I could safely recommend kids playing it granted they have to be 10 and 11 years old but still if you want to get your kids into horror games this is a good starting point sort of like introducing them to Ray Bradbury, RL Stine and Katy Towell’s works to get them into horror literature.

What's also weird is that this game was using 100% of my GPU and made the fans spin at max speed. I've never heard my GPU become so loud before with any other game. _childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: You play a young girl named Sally looking for her cousin Emily who's been missing for sometime. After being chased by some bullies, she tries to get back home but realises her town is destroyed and everyone is missing but strangely Emily is at the school. I had a great time through this, it's very well polished, the story was great and the voice acting was fantastic. I loved the little dialogue Sally says though-out the game and I made me jump a few times. Loved the art style and design of everything, it's so well detailed.Unfortunately, while I enjoyed the game and everything it offers, the game-play was simplistic. There are only four enemies in the game and it is very easy. The game follows modern day gaming trend where you have an awareness icon, item to distract, enemies can see you only at a certain distance (even if you're standing in their line of sight), enemies patrolling one area back and fourth or standing still in a certain location, stop chasing after you reach a certain area, no backtracking (only for collectables), follow the directed path given to you and very simple puzzles.I get it they wanted to tell a story but it is a horror game. I mean the game is liner but they still put an X on your map to tell you where you need to go, they don't let the player figure it out or even give an option to turn it off. Kinda feels like the developers were worried the game would be to hard or gamers wouldn't buy it and made easy for everyone. To get around you have your stealth and have a torch to fight back with. Considering how small the game is I wish they made the enemies much harder and opened up the game to travel different areas and paths to get around instead of holding your hand. You play as a young girl in a nightmare, so it would of made sense to only take a few hits and to be chased down, making the player find alternate routes because of how dangerous it is.There is no replay value apart from collectables and endings.Another thing that I didn't like is, they have real-time cutscenes but for some odd reason they use these still images as story content as well. Like they made the 3D scenes but realised they need more content or they ran out of time and just decided to do the images instead. It's jarring because there are some emotional scenes but you don't see the character animating these emotions you just get images which really ruins and takes you out of it.As I said, I did enjoy this game and do recommend it but it does have some missed potential. I hope they make another horror game like this but give options, open it a bit more, stop holding the players hand - let them figure it out, backtracking, and consider more survival horror gameplay. Playing the game I can saw these type of things in Gylt, would love them to go further with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly a stealth puzzle adventure game with a mental health story. It isn't really a horror game but more of a psychological thriller. The three endings are almost a let down after playing 7 to 8 hours. Still, it is fun to play and I enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: A game about an American mining town in which there is an alternate dark reality and you have to light enemies with a lantern to damage them. Yes, I'm talking about  Gylt.Story is pretty straightforward, and the game poses little challenge. It is a bit like Alan Wake but without the guns, just light the enemies to kill them. And with added stealth mechanics that fit great in the game. But there is plenty batteries and inhalers to comfortable traverse the game without having much problem. Puzzles are also quite easy, no Silent Hill piano puzzle here.Art direction is quite good, and although the game is not a graphics exhibition, it looks quite good. Music is good when it sounds, that is not quite often, most of the time you will be hearing only ambient sounds. And well, the ending is a bit disappointing: there are 3 endings and even the good "secret" ending could have been a bit more crafted.Anyway even with its flaws, I think it's a good experience for a 6-hour game. The stealth mechanics are fun, the story is plain but takes on an interesting topic and not being too long, it does not get repetitive or boring.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: "GYLT" really draws you in with its gorgeous, creepy visuals that'll remind you of "Little Nightmares." It’s a short but sweet horror game that packs in everything you’d expect, like sneaking around, using your flashlight to stun enemies (total "Alan Wake" vibes!), exploring secret spots, and solving puzzles that aren’t too tough. It took me about 7 hours in total to collect all blood stones to unlock the alternative ending.But the story? It feels a bit off to me. The game tries to set up this big reveal where you, playing as Sally, are supposed to realize that you’re actually the bully, and you need to make things right by saving your cousin, Emily. However, it doesn't quite land. Throughout the game’s seven hours, we see Sally busting her butt to find Emily, dealing with bullies herself before Emily disappears into this creepy, "Silent Hill"-esque place. And once they're both in that nightmare world, Sally’s trying super hard to save Emily from all sorts of monsters.Then there’s this weird old man who accuses Sally of being a bully and sort of manipulates the whole situation, (I feel like he tried to emotionally manipulate Sally to sacrifice herself) which feels pretty unpleasant. Honestly, Sally comes off more like she’s also a victim rather than the bully the game wants her to be. The title "GYLT" implies Sally is wracked with guilt all through this journey, and yes that how she feels, but let’s be real—a true bully wouldn’t be feeling that guilty in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: This game hooked me from the start, with the story and its thick atmosphere. But it's very short (I don't even have 8 hours registered on Steam), and as you make progress questions start to pile up. You find books containing "lore", but they mostly only repeat the questions, not answering them. When you finally reach the ending you'd naturally expect some answers, only to be disappointed.The gameplay is extremely simple and linear, with enemies that you either can kill with your flashlight, or avoid completely by sneaking. There are some easy puzzles here and there too, and that's it. It's good, but not great.Maybe the problem lies with me, being an adult playing children's games (because I try to find different games, hidden gems). But I'm not sure my kids (who span the right age, I guess) would think it's that great either.So... Should I recommend or not? I guess it's all about price. On sale for less than $10 maybe, but not otherwise.

Its a beautiful little gem and needs to be played by far more people than it has.  Music 10/10 Graphics 10/10  Story 10/10. Highly Recommended to everyone who loves the genre. _childDocuments_.review: It's alright I guess..And it does look adorable...but in the first two hours, nothing really happened. I'll give it another go soon to make sure I'm not wrong about this one, but all gameplay segments felt like filler between little tiny cutscenes that just send you to the next level. The story unfortunately is quite basic and things happen because the game needs them to happen.Gameplay consists of basic stealth and puzzles, tailored for a very young audience with little to no experience in playing games. The game presents you some more interesting stuff as you progress but all mechanics feel like they are included to hit a checklist - they don't feel organic or natural to the world.

_childDocuments_.review: a fairly standard stealth adventure game with light horror elements. It might spook you a bit for the first hour or so, but mercifully this is one of those modern horror games which don't try to scare you so much as unnerve you. Which is much better and the game does so wonderfully.All of the gameplay elements, the stealth, the puzzles, etc are all a bit undercooked. None of it's bad but none of it's particularly good, so most of your enjoyment will have to come from the story. which is actually pretty good. The game is on the shorter side so it doesn't need to parcel out its story sparsely, with frequent cutscenes that don't drag on beyond what's needed. You'll also be reading journal entries from various characters that further explain what's going on with your cousin and what's happening in the town.replayability is low however, apart from a few collectibles and different endings there's not much to the game. As afformentioned the gameplay is not particularly enticing by itself, so you can expect to be done and through with this game in a single playthrough. Which will take you about 6-7 hours. The are no difficulty modes or new game plus modes and the endings can be selected at the end and thus dont require seperate playthroughs.Some advice for your playthrough however, the 3 different endings are good, bad and secret. The good ending is not particularly satisfying, so unless you're going to watch the other endings on youtube like me, i suggest you to carefully collect all the clay people collectibles. There's about 10 total in the game. Don't worry too much about getting everything in your first go as you can backtrack later and you'll get a warning before the final stretch begins.Final rating: 7/10, its good but i'd wait for a sale unless the game really appeals to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Surpassed my expectations. I love the way our character is animated, great OST, smart ways of guiding the player so that we don't get stuck or waste time, the voice acting in french was good, variety in settings and enemies, simple but enjoyable puzzles, nice graphics like an animated movie, no bugs. It's cute and creepy at the same time. The only thing I didn't like much were the drawn cutscenes and the fact that the main theme was treated in a way that is too cliché and americanized. But all in all, very good surprise.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 .If you looking for an  alternative to a plague tale ,evil within, silent hill, outlast and resident evil  ,maybe it's a good choice to try this game.However,make sure to BUY IT AT SALE.In this game,a little girl Sally has to find her missing cousin Emily in a wired place and make a way to get both of them out of here.  Obviously Sally is  not a super soldier , so most of time you have to rely on STEALTH to avoid or stealth kill monsters .Also ,it feels good to use camera 's beam and fire ectinguisher  to fight back when it's necessary.Those  two weapons are also the tools to deal with puzzles, wich are quite easy and fun.Although ,players who have experience with  school bullying  may find this game traumatic ,so make sure not push yourself.And I have to admit it's quite hard to agree with some contents..And this is also the reason that  I may not recommend this game to kids.Overall , this game is fun and the art is cute ,the gameplay is satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Tackling a sensitive subject this game tries to empathize and transpose the player into a world imagined and derived from a place of refuge imagined by a bullied person.Very good overall story, hidden gems all over the place and a world full of "monsters" where you need to find your way around with courage and help your missing cousin who desperately needs your help and care.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually pretty enjoyable for a number of reasons: First, the designs of the character and enemies are very Tim Burton leaning, and the graphics overall are quite good. Secondly, there's tons of collectibles to locate as well as lore bits/diaries that give insight onto the events unfolding; I found the lore bits to be well written. Thirdly, the game is quite optimized and I didn't experience a single bug/glitch/frame drop during my entire playthrough. Lastly, the gameplay is a bit simple, but it doesn't overstay it's welcome which makes the story all that better. I'd say the game is more narrative driven, but regardless of the simplistic gameplay I enjoyed it all.Would recommend! Also, who the hell is the OLD MAN?

_childDocuments_.review: The main plot in centralized around childhood bullying, which for a grown man such as myself, left me caring very little for the outcome of the main characters (even though I've experienced bullying myself). _childDocuments_.review: Short and simple Alan Wake-style game that lasts about 5-6 hours to 100%. And do please 100%, the story is actually engaging enough to care about what happens to the characters and the true ending is the only one that isn't massively depressing, so please unlock it.Game play is solid, the graphics are way better than what you'd expect from a budget title, and even the cost-saving comic-style cutscenes have their own charm. If you want something sort and sweet for Halloween I'd fully recommend Gylt.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much love this version of childfriendly horror. One might think that means a fun cutsie halloween like experience like Luigi Mansion 3. But no, not at all. This game is more like the book series "Scary stories to tell in the Dark". Subject matter and visuals that are creepy and unsettling, but not so much that kids would be traumatized for days after. In other words, scary and serious enough that kids would be able to appreciate the thrill of fear the way adult horror media does for adults. And its brilliant. We need more movies and games like this.In terms of gameplay, its again, approaching that level of survival horror that isn't too taxing but enough so that you can tell if you were careless you would feel it. Its what easy mode should be in any game; not a braindead mode, but a mode that you have to take seriously but can easily enough bounce back if you got sloppy. But I will give one criticism to the gameplay. Due to the nature of the aim mechanic, being like og Resident Evil 4 with the laserpointer, the crosshair provided doesn't always line up to where the flashlight beam is aiming for combat or puzzle uses. With no option to turn off crosshairs, you just kinda have to learn to ignore it. Small thing, but still notable.  In terms of story, I LOVE that it feels so much like Silent Hill. So much so, that this game could EASILY fit in the Silent Hill universe with very VERY minimal changes to background lore that doesn't even need to be found. Unless you want the best ending.Thumbs WAY up on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I really enjoyed the story, atmosphere and gameplay. In my opinion, Gylt has Silent Hill vibes but a different stylistic and obvious gameplay approach (don't use guns) which I really enjoyed.Only real negative is, in my opinion, the final boss "fight"...it was a bit lackluster.I really wish Gylt was longer because I really enjoyed the story and atmosphere. I'm looking forward to other games that Tequila Works develops in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a surprisingly fun and simple little stealth adventure with a cool, if a little trite, story. It can easily be compared to Alan Wake but it's far easier and not nearly as dark. A lot of people have compared this to The Last of Us, but it isn't really like that at all in my opinion. The graphics are pretty good, the sound is okay, the enemy variety leaves a lot to be desired, and there aren't really a lot of things to do here. However, it's definitely worth the $15.00 that I paid for it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got that big, "Indie game that's a metaphor for depression" vibe going on. Well executed though, very little jank, lots of fun ways to bully the poor monsters into submission for having weak nerd arms. It's a fun romp, with good atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: Overall GYLT is a really nice and a bit creepy 3rd person action adventure game with some puzzles, a bit of stealth, relatively easy combat and a few boss fights. I wouldn't call it horror since it's not too scary overall.Level design is nice, controls work well, performance is good, puzzles are fair and well designed and the combat and stealth parts aren't too easy, but never frustrating. It feels like a good mixture of Little Nightmares, Alan Wake and Stray.There's just one thing i didn't like at all: To get the good ending you have to find a lot of optional collectibles which is a bit frustrating, especially since the game doesn't give you a warning and the chance to say "no, i still have things to do" when the last mission starts. But you can get back to the campus in freeroam mode after finishing the game, collect the missing items and finish the game again to get the good ending (that's how i did it). But i still think this isn't a prime example of good game design since the game doesn't warn you and getting the collectibles requires a lot of backtracking an possibly a guide to find some of the better hidden items.But overall i'd say: Really good game! Not a masterpiece, but except for the "finde certain collectibles to get the good ending" it's at least good in everything it does.
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: for $20 it was pretty good honestly. I'm not too good with puzzles but I only got stuck once or twice, the rest was pretty self-explanatory. some aspects of the gameplay are pretty annoying (one specific boss battle requires being stealthy while moving to various objectives but then seems to punish you for moving at all? not sure if I was dealing with it wrong or what.)they give you various ways to deal with enemies, which is pretty cool, but once you've gotten used to the gameplay it seems the easiest way is to just start gunning them down instead of being stealthy. they introduce various ways to "counter" this and force you to stealth but it ends up being annoying at times.the story/worldbuilding are honestly really awesome, I was able to predict a lot of things but I still had a lot of fun with it. the atmosphere is pretty spooky and fun. I actually enjoyed finding the collectibles because of how they expanded on the world and its characters. I also managed to find about 80% of the collectibles myself (which is a plus because I am very stupid and also very lazy, and some games go too crazy with hiding stuff.)they were very, VERY generous with items (healing and battery), it got outright humorous just how many extra things were laying around on the map that i didn't need but it was a good call, because on the off-chance that you managed to run out of items i think you might be screwed actually, depending on where you were lmao.there are multiple endings, but they make it really simple to go back and get different ones, thankfully. there are also apparently different achievements for beating bosses with no hits (i managed to get one on my first blind playthrough) and beating the game without killing any enemies (how????) so the replayability is there for anyone who.... feels like doing that? the stealth is way harder than just killing enemies so you won't catch me replaying the game for that lol.all in all, i'd say, if you can't decide whether or not to buy this game, watch the trailers or some gameplay online, just to see what you're getting into. the gameplay is basically the same through the whole thing so if it looks like fun, i'd say try it! if you're looking for an extremely challenging horror game, this may not be for you (unless you decide to play through with no enemy kills), but if the story seems interesting to you and you're interested in something comparatively chiller than other horror games out there, definitely give Gylt a shot :)
_childDocuments_.name: GYLT

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story. It really hits close to home for me as I was bullied relentlessly in middle school. It felt like no one would ever stick up for me. Close friends didn't help or mention it. Teachers ignored it and pretended like they cared but never actually helped. I ran into the guidance councilor's office crying once... just to have her kick me out and tell me to get back to class...I'm almost 30, now, and I have a tough shell... I confront things head on and I don't take anything from anyone... Push before they push you... Its not a good way to be. ... If you see bullying happening... please help stop it... doing nothing leaves scars that won't heal on their own.As for the game, itself:Great stealth mechanics, movement is fluid, controls are intuitive (though space for crouch is an odd choice, but you get used to it).A great survival horror game that had me panicking at times, but not so scary that it was hard to push forward.o.o ...but those manikins are pure nightmare fuel...

_childDocuments_.review: Short but nice.  As other people wrote, it really is a family friendly mix of Alan Wake and Silent Hill.  The required stealth is a little bit more than I would enjoy but nothing excessive, the overall balance between action, puzzles, stealth and lore is good.From a technical point of view I have zero complaints, the game is virtually bug free, graphics are nice and optimization is good.  If you want to spend 10 hours for mild horror, light puzzles and some action, I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla is your typical AAA open world RPG game with an overwhelming amount of collectibles and side activities to pad the game time along with a wide scope of gameplay mechanics to attempt to appeal to as many gamers as possible. This game has a Souls-like style of combat in that certain areas/encounters have a recommended player level, but that doesn't mean it can be done at a lower level however you'll have to spend more time in combat as you deal less and cannot take as much damage as your enemies.There are two main story lines that are active simultaneously. To complete the game you have to obviously take out all of the Knights Templar and kill the leader. However, in this game to do that you have to grind through a series of quests to identify underlings to expose the "Lieutenants" to take them out. Essentially, you have to take out 2 tiers of Templars (something like 15-20 in total) to get to the final boss.There's a "base building" feature where you plunder churches for their riches that in turn are used to upgrade/build new buildings in your settlement. Your items have a gear score/quality level that can only be upgraded with special/rare materials you get from exploration.I ultimately got fatigue of playing the game from all the stuff to do and stopped playing it. The game isn't bad, but the story is tedious and there's too much going on that for someone like me who tries to be a completionist it's overwhelming and exhausting to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Staving off the Odinsleep: A Sprawling Saga Marred by Monotony and Technical IssuesIntroduction:Assassin's Creed Valhalla, developed by Ubisoft Montreal, promised to deliver an epic Viking adventure set in the breathtaking landscapes of ninth-century England. With its ambitious scope, engaging narrative, and immersive open-world exploration, expectations were high for the latest installment in the long-running franchise. However, despite its strengths, Assassin's Creed Valhalla falls short in several key areas, ultimately leaving players with a mixed experience. In this critical review, we'll delve into the game's highs and lows, assessing its successes and shortcomings.Ambitious World Building and Narrative:Assassin's Creed Valhalla excels in its portrayal of the Viking Age and the clash of cultures between the Norse invaders and the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of England. The game's sprawling open world is richly detailed and filled with diverse landscapes, from verdant forests and snow-capped mountains to bustling cities and ancient ruins. Players take on the role of Eivor, a fierce Viking warrior, as they lead their clan on a quest for glory and conquest. The narrative explores themes of honor, betrayal, and the struggle for power, with branching storylines and multiple endings that offer players a degree of agency in shaping the fate of their character and their people.Repetitive Gameplay and Monotonous Activities:Despite its ambitious scope, Assassin's Creed Valhalla suffers from repetitive gameplay mechanics and monotonous activities that detract from the overall experience. The game's core loop of raiding enemy settlements, completing side quests, and gathering resources quickly becomes tedious and predictable, leading to a sense of repetition and grind. While the game offers a wide variety of activities and objectives, including hunting, fishing, and building settlements, many of these tasks feel shallow and lack meaningful rewards or incentives for completion. As a result, players may find themselves going through the motions rather than fully immersing themselves in the world of Valhalla.Technical Issues and Performance Problems:Assassin's Creed Valhalla is plagued by technical issues and performance problems that hinder the overall experience. From frequent crashes and game-breaking bugs to poor optimization and inconsistent frame rates, players may encounter numerous obstacles that disrupt their enjoyment of the game. These issues are particularly prevalent on older hardware and consoles, where performance may suffer due to hardware limitations. While Ubisoft has released several patches and updates to address these issues, they persist to varying degrees, detracting from the immersion and enjoyment of the game for many players.Conclusion:In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Valhalla offers a sprawling saga set in a richly detailed world filled with epic battles, political intrigue, and Norse mythology. However, its ambitious scope is undermined by repetitive gameplay mechanics, monotonous activities, and technical issues that detract from the overall experience. While the game has its strengths, including its ambitious world-building and engaging narrative, these are overshadowed by its shortcomings, leaving players with a mixed impression. Ultimately, Assassin's Creed Valhalla falls short of its lofty ambitions, delivering a flawed experience that fails to fully realize its potential.

_childDocuments_.review: ********** MAJOR ISSUES, READ THE UPDATE ***********I'm not recommending that people play this game for a very good reason... Crashes and major bugs are that reason.The game itself is enjoyable and I had already completed my original play-through on PS4 when the game first launched. I completely moved all my gaming to PC and have never looked back at consoles. Valhalla was fun when I played through the entire story originally, but the bugs are so bad that I don't want to risk anything happening to my PC. I bought this game last week ( 12-9-22 ), after the initial download and boot up I got about 2 minutes of gameplay before it crashed. After reading about issues it was recommended that all graphic settings be turned down. I went to relaunch the game and it was asking me to download the entire thing again...? Okay, I thought that was really strange, the game crashed and somehow deleted itself. I restarted my PC and what do you know, the game is back. I launched the game again and got about 30 minutes of play ( turned graphics down to medium ) before it crashed yet again. Okay, I guess the graphical settings need to be a potato quality to run on a high end PC. I go to relaunch and the game is asking to be downloaded again. I decided to search my storage and saw that my D drive was missing, with only the C drive showing as available. I restart the PC and guess what, the D drive is back. I launch the game again and turn the graphics far lower than they need to be for my PC. I get 2 hours of play time and it crashes yet again, and like every time before my D drive is missing.I'm not sure what would cause this as I can't seem to find anyone else having this issue, but the game crashes are somehow causing some kind of corruption on my new 4TB NVMe. M.2 SSD. The 6 months I've had this SSD, I have never had a single issue with it, Valhalla is the only game that has ever caused this issue and it scares me enough that I'm just done playing it until the issue is fixed.******** UPDATE ********Developer suggested I start a support ticket which I did. ( Case number 17556852 ). The rep asked for my MSINFO text file along with my DxDiag file, which I provided. Rep said that they would need to escalate the issue as it couldn't be resolved over chat and I completely understood that. I get an e-mail shortly after the conversation ( BTW I waited 2 hours in queue to chat with support ), and the e-mail says per the initial conversation that my $800+ newer NVME M.2 SSD is somehow at fault for the crashing when it was only Valhalla that caused this issue of my disappearing drive. This support rep said I should replace this drive and try the game again LOL. Not on your life, I'm not risking another $800 drive to try this game again. We even had that conversation in chat when they asked why I didn't try to re-download the game on to my  C drive. I said I wasn't willing to risk another drive.So basically the developer response has been less than helpful, I wasted 2 hours of my time to try and provide the suggested info for the rep to say they were escalating this, just to close the case and say my drive was faulty when everything points to this game crashing that caused this.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I can't stand it anymore. I need to write a review of this game and try playing one of the earlier games. Overall Game Score: 38/100Before I begin: This game has left such a sour taste in my mouth that I refuse to purchase another AC game, ever again. The problems with this game are both it and with the company behind it and it's clear they will not improve but decay. I'm not wasting money on the mindless 'developments' I can already foresee in this series's future. If you're reading this, I advise you to only purchase the earliest games for a quality experience. The audio in this game is good. The white noise of the ocean and surroundings is well done. The music is relatively decent for many locations. The weak link is the voices. The voice acting itself is often good but they aren't great because the dialogue they're given is dreadful (we'll get into that). Visuals are the greatest part of this game and that's not saying much. It doesn't have a heavy impact on your PC and plays well even on Very High settings. I won't get too much into it, however, but the FPS in the game isn't what it should be and plenty of other players have gone into it in much greater depth, so give their reviews a read too.Okay, positive stuff out of the way, let's dig into why this game is dreadful. There's so much to unpack. The game tries to do too much at once. It's quantity over quality. You can do so much in Valhalla, it's absurd but it's obviously going to lead to problems with dozens of unfixed bugs and controls not working like they're supposed to. You want to stab forward? You'll stab 90 degrees to the right at random. You want to dodge somebody's attack? Sometimes we'll listen to your inputs and sometimes we'll move you in front of the enemy attacking even if a split second ago you were rolling out of range of that attack. The more I play, the more I found the inputs get more complex and the lack of polish becomes apparent. (Shoutout to 'Redwall' for teaching me to parry when under-leveled, using a buggy system and to accept death comes for all, multiple times). The story in Valhalla is terrible. It's one of the weakest points of the game. Loose ends everywhere, illogical moments that lead nowhere, events that literally could be cut from the story because they do nothing for it and dialogue that feels like it starts and ends randomly at times. I feel like I'm watching inexperienced actors who forget who their character is meant to be in each scene and were whispered their lines just before it. Characters also don't appear to behave as they should, given the setting, being weirdly sensitive or dull at times that don't match with what they're going through. Furthermore on the writing part, historical accuracy is down the drain. The game says it's 'inspired' by historical events. Try more like they did a five minute google search and then just made up the rest. I get it's a work of fiction but the game acts like it's 90% based on reality when it's more like 15%. Honestly, the writing team should be fired immediately. Whatever group of writers put this mess together are not people I would consider writers because their incompetence shines so brightly, I can feel my eyes burning from a room over from where my PC is. I just can't let this go, can I? The modern day story line is terrible too. I think it's about time Ubisoft stop babbling in the corner and just get rid of the modern day story line from AC games. I've checked and a lot of people absolutely do not care about Layla or that part of the game. It's also incredibly frustrating to be in a viking world only to be dragged into the modern world to be reminded this character you don't care about exists. It worked fine in AC 1, 2 and maybe even 3 but I'd say after Black Flag, this just needs to stop. Nobody cares about the modern day view anymore. Ubisoft Connect is so poorly managed, I think some people would take malware over it or even see it as malware. Also, Ubisoft has plenty of time to pump out new releases but clearly not a single employee to fix bugs in their old games like Valhalla or even older games like the 'Kenway Fleet' bug from Black Flag...you know, the game that came out...about a decade ago? There's only two more things I want to point out and I bet it'll be relevant for Shadows in the near future too. This is the most IMPORTANT part, so I hope you survived my rambling to here. It's clear to anybody with a three digit IQ that the company is farming attention through controversy. Not getting into that can of worms but it's highly unethical and sickening. They've also proven with the design of specific characters in this game that they may be, how do I say this, 'people lacking empathy, moral integrity and a well-polished set of ethics'. Certain characters are given certain stereotypes based on certain characteristics that prove the developers see certain humans as 'lesser'. Furthermore, the developers have been actively engaging in censorship, so if you thought you had any credibility left, Ubisoft, that's cute. The second important point that I hope people remember going forward with future releases is that this game has been designed to be predatory of your time. It's manipulative. You're encouraged to take rivers everywhere, where they'll flash glowing points where you can raid constantly, making you want to spend time doing so. They've made the settlement construction based on finite resources you can only get from certain locations so if you want to build up your base, you need to hit all of them for raw materials. You won't be told clearly that some structures in the base don't give you access to something that's important or fun (like some buildings being purely for cosmetics), encouraging you to spend MORE time hitting specific locations. The grind in this game is designed maliciously. They want you to play as much as possible, to the point where instead of an open world where you can strike anywhere and do as you please, it's more like you're somebody in a viking costume with a shopping list and the promise of candy for checking off everything on the list. Thank you for reading all of this. I'm sure I missed some other problems but I think I've said enough to prove that this is not worth your time and money. Please do not feed a company that deserves to starve and do not support creators that actively help feed companies like this. There's a deep-seeded rot in Ubisoft, only when their sales tank will there exist even a slim chance of digging it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle to understand how reviews of this game are mixed! I think it's largely an AC fanbase that want games to be more closely tied to the Assassin storyline, and as someone who has only played Odyssey and Valhalla, I am not one of those people. Taking my perspective into account, I think this is a fantastic game! Yes, there is probably too much content. The sheer number of wealth/mystery/artifact locations in England is somewhat overwhelming and could have been cut back a bit. However, some of the mystery locations in particular are my favorite parts of this game. Much like Odyssey, they often have their own interesting or downright funny stories that add depth to the people outside of the main characters. I think there could have been fewer wealth or artifact locations without losing quality. But the combat in this game is satisfying, the adventuring is super fun, and the main stories are engaging. I have lost many hours in this game. I do wish Eivor had more of a personal investment in getting rid of the Order, like Kassandra did in Odyssey. It feels like Eivor is just doing Hytham a favor and you start to forget why some of the Order members are even that evil. But one of my favorite (albeit confusing) aspects of the game is the tie in with Norse mythology. I love that it isn't even DLC, but just part of the main story. It's incredibly cool to see different realms through Eivor's eyes. Overall, yes, it is not a traditional AC game and I understand that. But it's just a really good combat-heavy open world RPG and I fully recommend it.

Side missions were enough, but now a genuine story mission is buggered up, and I'm not even sure if the save I have was early enough. I am writing this now having uninstalled it, in no hurry to go back.Again: there's stuff to like. The combat is fun (though the stealth may be at a series low point), the little Roguelike mode is good, and England is actually kind of pretty. But for the AC die-hards who play this, I MEAN it, treat it like a damn minefield and save often.

The writing is decent, there are few memorable characters, but other questlines are boring and forgettable. Itemization is significantly improved. Stealth, on the other hand, is completely broken. Sometimes the enemies won't notice you in bright daylight, sometimes they spot you at night from far away. Enemies get alerted almost immediately and in the end you solve most of the situations with direct combat because it's faster and you eventually need to do it anyway. _childDocuments_.review: I have a weird relationship with the  franchise. I genuinely hated the first game, but the second drew me into what the series could be. Since then, I've spent the last 15 or so years, playing each entry with a mix of disappointment and elation. Some titles were good. Some were bad. They can't all be bangers. But even the bad ones at least felt playable. They were entertaining enough. With  and , the series got somewhat of a soft reboot, and the gameplay was engaging enough to get through some of the new drudgery that was introduced. While  is certainly beautiful, everything else about this game feels like a regression. Not many series survive as long as  and even the ones that do, or have survived longer, tend to have fewer entries. It's genuinely hard to keep something going for as long as  has, but one would expect that the developers and publishers would learn lessons along the way. Not so with Ubisoft and whatever studio they had pump out this game. After  and , Ubisoft was running the risk of putting out a third title that could have been more of the same. Rightfully, Ubisoft learned that this is not a good idea - See  or , two examples of when the formula gets too tired to carry on. It gets stale. So how could Ubisoft keep  from getting stale? After all, the previous two entries were both 100+ hour games, surely they shouldn't do that again, right?To be honest, it would have been better if Ubisoft had just copy/pasted the formula for one final entry. Instead, what they seemingly opted to do was take a grab bag of all the worst ideas ever introduced in the series and stuff them in here. Aside from the graphics, there is nothing really good to be said about this game.First off, the game has two prologues. One where Eivor (this entry's assassin), is a child, and then when they're grown up and deciding to go to England. Even after getting to England, and after 12 hours of playing, I still can't help but feel I'm in a tutorial. Point in case: I just learned the leap of faith, but I've been to several viewpoints already. The story is also all over the place. At its core, you are Eivor, a viking trying to make it in England in the 9th century. Sounds cool, right? Except there has to be assassin's, because it's , so they have something going on. Eivor also has visions of Ragnarok, and their own personal goals and motivations beyond that. So already, there is too much going on narratively. Should I care about Eivor's blood feud? The visions? The conquest of England? Should I care at all about King Harald (who doesn't seem like a bad guy) and Norway, or was that just to get us to England? And then there's whatever the modern day story, which they don't even attempt to connect to . The last game ends in Atlantis, with Layla making questionable decisions under the influence of the Staff of Hermes. This game picks up way after the fact, with Layla having connected with Shaun and Rebecca in New England, where there is a viking grave that they were drawn to by some message for some reason, because even though Desmond stopped the world from ending, now it's going to end again and its Layla's turn to stop it. I get it. It's hard to connect Ancient Greece to the Age of Vikings. "But Sony did it with !" is what I'm sure Ubisoft leadership said. Yes, but there wasn't really a throughline, other than Kratos destroyed Greece and moved on. When you're dealing with history, unfortunately, the series of events are kind of fixed. Without going down this rabbit hole, suffice it to say that once again, ditching the modern stay story would have saved Ubisoft a lot of headache trying to make this all fit. A lesson they learned by  and forgot by . The series has always been something of a mess when it comes to storytelling, and  really jumped the shark. But at least  was . Which brings me to...This game is not fun to play. At all. Movement feels stiff. Combat feels floaty and unruly. Whereas  gave you an ability to heal that required adrenaline to use,  has Eivor carrying food around, which is to be eaten when you get low on health. There is still adrenaline, but now it's used more similar to stamina in a Souls-like fashion. Successful attacks build adrenaline, but you have to use adrenaline to dodge and block. Missing attacks also drains adrenaline. Hypothetically, this makes combat more methodical, but that's only if you have tight execution. Again, I get it. The combat in the previous entries was kind of brain dead and button-mashy. But it was . The same cannot be said here. For example, enemies will flash a certain color before an attack. Orange means you can parry, and red means you should dodge. Except you shouldn't press the button when the color flashes. You should  so when the animation eventually does play, you can push the button at the right time. This mess led me time and time again to missing dodges or blocks, or wasting my adrenaline on them. I felt as though I was being punished for having reflexes. Exploring the world is also rough. Movement in the previous two games was quick and easy. In , it feels like they took the movement from  maybe? Running around feels like wading through a thick veil of molasses. Once again, I found myself getting stuck on random bits of geometry, preventing me from free running around. Whereas  removed a lot of movement restrictions to allow players to freely, and easily navigate the world,  decided to go with realism over fun, resulting in frustrating movement that I haven't seen since . Leveling also changed from a a boring skill tree to something more resembling the sphere grid from . Most nodes are just stat boots along the way to some ability. You don't have clear visibility as to where each branch of the grid goes. There are multiple ways in which you can choose to enhance Eivor, but none of them really feel like they impact the gameplay much.There are dozens of other subsystems the game decides to introduce, and I just couldn't be bothered to dive into any of them. If the core gameplay was engaging in any way, I might have felt so inclined, but it wasn't, so I didn't. I just really can't recommend this game. It's a mess. In an attempt to keep the series of getting stale, Ubisoft looked back to previous entries.  feels like Ubisoft was trying to make The Greatest Hits of the Worst Ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla can best be described as a 'shallow titan'.  In short, this game is massive, without a solid story to support the entire run-time of this 100+ behemoth.  With that said, there is a plethora of worthwhile side content to enjoy along the way.  The dev team has also perfected the placement of viewpoints along the map, and tied the game's story in well with the exploration; effectively minimizing backtracking.  As is the case with many releases, Valhalla's writing fluctuates in quality, with some arcs providing more engaging stories and characters.  Ah yes... Characters.  There's not a whole lot of good ones in this game unfortunately.  Some standouts are Basim, and Sigurd.  Most characters fall into some form of archetype, such as the young beta male king-to-be, the great warrior going mad, or the old king ready to die.  It is quite disappointing there aren't more well-written characters to get invested in, especially because the game's theme of loyalty is well portrayed with many of these generic archetype-bound 'characters'.To the game's credit there are some cute fan-service tie-ins to the lore to be found, though they are removed from the main-narrative.  Right... The Lore.  Valhalla, as was the case with Odyssey; relegates the Assassin's to a side role, with all mentions of the Hidden Ones being absent for 20-40 hours at a time... a few times.  Some, like myself may not mind too much the shift in focus, though it is a shame having lost great amounts of time with characters capable of carrying the game's disjointed story.I liked Valhalla.  I like the twists, exploration, viewpoints, mysteries/wealth/artifact system, and even the settlement system.  What I didn't like is how little substance the story had, and aside from two cut-scenes, how little your time spent in the world really matters.  Great potential, a decent ride, though not worth your time.
