_childDocuments_.review: Rather than go with quality, Ubisoft went with quantity. There are so many side quests and at least 50-60 hours of main story. But it isn't a compelling story. I didn't have any connection or real care for any of the characters or even enemies. Even the main character is just a mindless drone. There's not a lot to him, which is a shame since Odessey's MC was great and actually had depth. Lots of bugs especially with the arena type game mode for medals. They made stealth very optional/ obsolete and combat a lot of fun, so all I wanted to do was run around and fight everyone. You also have the ability to customize how much damage you do, how much damage you take, and how much health enemies have. I personally loved that addition. I had a lot of fun with the rune system, and there were a lot of different abilities to choose from. And there is no more getting garbage armor or weapons anymore, like in Odessey. All armor is part of sets, and all weapons can be fully upgraded. The environment is beautiful, but a little too spread out for my taste. Though, much better than Mirage. I haven't played the Siege of France DLC yet but I have played the other two. The Wrath of the Druids was alright, and the Dawn of Ragnarok is horribly boring and long.If its on sale, I would definitely recommend picking it up. At least 80-100 hours of gameplay without DLCs

Every compact area is a blessing, and with just as much to do, without the filler of riding my horse for 5 minutes to get there! This is from a completionist stand point, of course if you simply follow the quests, it would be a lot faster. I have reached a few moments though, such as in Jotunheim, where I was fighting a "boss" who was level 400. I was 337 at the time, and had a good set of gear and talents. I didn't have any issue. But so far it is the only instance that suggests needing to complete areas for the skill points. Every other aspect, is fine with whatever you get through the main story. I'm at 372 hours, and just read that i'm half way through the game... there is A LOT of small, hidden moments, that give more to the story of the land that you are travelling though. They can be a fun surprise!

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla is in many ways a terrific game, marred by unnecessary bloat and some questionable design choices. Criticisms include the seemingly complex but ultimately shallower RPG aspects compared to its predecessor, the lack of intricate character builds, the rather uneventful side content, and the main plot being stretched by some admittedly filler chapters. Where the game shines, however, is in its impeccable atmosphere, superb soundtrack and the most consistent writing since Black Flag. Flawed but undeniably interesting, Valhalla stands out for me as the most intriguing entry within the Assassin's Creed RPG era, because when it hits, it hits damn hard.

_childDocuments_.review: I've barely scratched the surface of this title, even at 27 hours, but I must say it's a real treat in the AC franchise. There's a lot of the Ubisoft bloat that's in just about all of their games, and it can be quite overwhelming a lot of the time. I will say though, the vast amount of activities you can take part in is very refreshing. Orlog is a blast. Flyting is fun. The drinking games bring you back to the days of house partying with your friends. And just when you think you done all there is to do, you construct a new building in your town and boom, new activity to go off and tackle.The Viking aesthetic is absolutely a gem to the series, and England has to be one of their best maps to date. You really get to live out your Norse fantasy here conquering a new land. Plus the fact that when you go into towns here, you have to disguise yourself or people will get frightened and run away is *chef's kiss*. Gives a new approach to the idea of trying to blend in like in older titles.My only real gripe with the game is that it will randomly crash from time to time. Not sure why? Probably a bad patch, and I'm sure it will never get fixed. Thankfully though, the game auto-saves regularly enough that even if you get a CTD, you don't lose much of your progress at all. I do have a second gripe, but it's just universal with Ubisoft as a whole. STOP with the micro-transactions already! I'm glad it's mostly cosmetic, but gating resources behind a paywall is a pretty gnarly move. Granted you can get resources in-game simple enough, but they make it just minor enough to be sort of irritating when it comes to some of the upgrade progression. More reason to get out and explore though, right? (I'm talking resources for upgrading gear early on. This has no effect on later upgrades, nor does it effect the progression of your settlement.)I definitely recommend really anyone to get their hands on this title, but I would say wait for one of Ubisoft's big sales so you can grab it for real cheap along with the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this, you're probably wonder whether or not to buy Assassin's Creed Valhalla. In fact, you will not be surprised by much at all, especially if you've played any of the more recent giant, sprawling Assassins Creeds.There's a lot more (kinda Souls-like) combat, with enemies signalling "dodge me" and "block me" attacks and boss fights against large health bars. Perhaps the biggest surprise is when, not long after the introduction, the game picks up and moves to England. Not just for a short bit of Viking-ing, but for a significant majority of the game; you're not going to spend dozens of hours exploring Viking Scandinavia here.If you loved Origins and Odyssey and like Vikings, then ignore the "Not Recommended". Other than that, it's hard to recommend this when there are plenty of better action/adventure games to be played out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I'm giving up on this game. I gave it more than it's fair shot. It's not an Assassin's Creed game, but I really tried to enjoy it as it's own Viking themed open world RPG game. The fabric of what makes an Assassin's Creed game has been forcefully and clumsily attached and the product suffers for it. Gameplay, story, fundamental themes, all of it is at odds with itself.The thing I was counting on carrying me through, the combat, eventually failed to keep me interested. I can't remember having a single fight that didn't have some jank to it. It was never satisfying. I'd hoped it was just me getting used to things, but I'm here to tell you now that it wasn't. It could be interesting, but it's mostly just i-framing around and left clicking; using adrenaline when you have it. I initially liked the light bow and hitting weak points into a finisher, but it's actually so much faster and reliable than anything else it became boring quickly. I made an effort to max my stealth/assassination damage in the hope of being able to use the not-so hidden blade in combat more, but landing a charged up stab, even from behind while in the smoke parry, never killed. In fact it would annoyingly knock them to the ground where I'd be forced to mash left click over them while they lay there. You'd think I'd be able to finish them. The insistence of using RPG "health bar to below or equal to zero" mechanics concerns the player with outputting more damage numbers rather than playing tactically. Sometimes you're forced to go loud, so forget about being...you know...AN ASSASSIN.There are some legitimately interesting skills in the progression tree, but that's only about 1/3rd of the tree. The other 2/3rds are uninteresting and bland. "You now passively generate adrenaline" Wow. Amazing high tier skill. And nevermind about the good ones I mentioned, they actually don't work half the time you're counting on them. Battleground Bolt: throw a slain enemies weapon. Cool, sounds awesome. Too bad it's on the same key as carry body and it takes priority. Not like there isn't already a secondary action button we could assign here. Counter Roll Mastery: dodge roll into a heavy attack to do a hidden blade attack. Wow awesome. Too bad you end up just dodging past the enemy still half the time. Also don't react as quickly as you can or it doesn't count.I could write a book of gripes but I think I'll leave it here and try Black Flag instead.Also I was stuck on CTDs at a few points and had to troubleshoot myself how to get out of the loop.-------------------------To the help desk response: I'm quite familiar with the basic troubleshooting steps and I've already done them. It's not on my end. It's the application.I'll tell you what did help: Capping my FPS to 60 and going from the automatically selected Ultra graphics to the step below it, although I'm pretty sure that the FPS cap was the real fix. There were two instances were I would consistently crash mid-combat. I was able to bandage this by leaving the area then coming back. What I'm going to take away from this response is that there's no mega-bug fix patch planned for the future, is there? I can think of plenty of instances of strange NPC behavior and graphical issues that can easily be recreated simply by walking around.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 12 hours of handholding BS, it finally starts to get funEDIT:  The only other Ass Creed game I ever played to full completion was Odyssey.  I'm only about 45 hours into this one, but by comparison I can say that Valhalla feels a whole lot less smooth and less polished overall than Odyssey.Leaving aside all the usual gripes and complaints about grind, in-game currency, 100% completionist stuff, and repetitive combat, THIS game compared to Odyssey has a significantly higher amount of bugs, buggy design, and just plain bad gameplay ideas poorly executed.Compared to Odyssey, where I was able to figure out most every puzzle reasonably, there have been multiple puzzles in Valhalla where the answer is basically impossible to discover without googling it.  One of these puzzles I googled only to find out it is a KNOWN BUG that there's basically no clues evident as to how to figure it out (the absolute worst of these is trying to get to the Sync point in the Thaelaerea Ruins).Other puzzles, including the new mushroom trips, often tell you to figure out which gate to go through based on "observable clues" only for there to be no observable clues.  The path to one gate is covered with leaves, the other covered with grass, the other covered with shields.  There's no indication what any of them is supposed to mean.  Another map spot gives you a rambling message and a three-circled icon, which is painted on three separate rocks.  At no point is it ever even hinted what you're supposed to do here.  I had to google it just to figure out you have to look at the rocks at a certain angle to where the paint lines line up to show the three-circled icon.Except doing that was literally the first thing I did, yet apparently I was an inch or two out of position so nothing happened and I kept on trying to figure out what else to do.Also there are random sidequest markers littered around the map that not only don't tell you what difficulty level it is, but are completely at odds with the difficulty level of the land itself.  East Anglia has a "recommended power" level of 55, yet there's a boss fight encounter with a boss at lvl 360.  This sort of thing happens constantly and it's incredibly stupid to have insanely high level boss fights hidden in what are basically newbie areas with absolutely no way of knowing they are not for newbies until you've triggered one and have a boss hunting you.Other bugs just keep coming in the most frustrating and stupid ways possible, such as fetch quests where the item you need to fetch is behind a locked door but the door key isn't spawned until an unrelated mission, or having to advance a quest by talking to someone, only for that someone to not have a Speak To prompt available.On top of that, there are some minor graphical glitches I encountered here that I never encountered in Odyssey, particularly in cutscenes where certain characters will flicker as if the lighting on them suddenly went out.  This made it almost laughably frustrating when I encountered an Anomaly Encounter, not realizing what it was, and thinking the graphics in the game were glitching yet again.It doesn't speak well for a game where an intended gameplay feature is basically indistinguishable from a bug.

_childDocuments_.review: I have such mixed feelings about this game because I'm a massive Assassin's Creed fan but I'm also a massive video game fan in general. This made it really hard to review this game because as an AC game this sucks, there's really no other way to say it. It leans too hard into the RPG aspects of itself and the story is nowhere near involved enough with the Hidden Ones/Brotherhood to really be considered an AC game. The only kind of AC aspect it has over the previous two entries in the series is the inclusion of social stealth, which to be honest I've rarely used because it feels kind of shoehorned in out of fear of more backlash from the community.With all that being said though, as a pure game not playing or reviewing it through the lens of it being an Assassin's Creed game, it's still quite a good game and is fairly enjoyable. It's not the best game I've ever played however I still did like it. It's story is quite engaging despite it tending to drag sometimes. The gameplay is sophisticated and mostly polished apart from some bugs and crashes that I've experienced here and there. I enjoyed it's combat from the start of the game to be honest and there's so many different routes you can go. It really leans into the RPG genre which when not thinking of it as an AC game is a good thing. It's expansive skill tree, wide range of abilities and vast selection of weapons and gear which can all be upgraded different ways really make for a unique playstyle for each different person.It's world and map are thoughtfully created and they are beautiful. Each different location has a unique feel and look and it makes exploring the map unlocking different secrets and solving puzzles not feel like a task or drag. I was continually impressed with how the game looked and the environmental building of the game.There's so much that I love about this game but also a lot bringing it down. So basically for anyone looking to play the game, as just a game without thinking about it being an AC game it's very good and I would recommend. For any hardcore AC fans wanting to play this, you'll be left sorely disappointed and upset. I'd still recommend the game to people but only buy it on sale, it doesn't have enough outstanding or exceptional elements to warrant this game being worth $90. The large majority of the game apart from the open world is either average or above average, so it's really only worth it while it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not recommending this game, even though I have 127 hours spent in it, and probably could have spent even more, since there is still a lot to explore, but I do not really have any motivation to do that.It is worse than Odyssey in my mind. One part of why is probably the setting and general tone. I remember someone analyzed Need for Speed games back in the day and it turned out that blue-ish and white-ish games in the series failed in sales because of the overall cold feel, and i think I see the same thing in Valhalla. One could argue, that "hey, there is Norway here, it is cold there", and yes, that is true, but most of your time you spend in England, and while it also has snow in northern region, it's... It is just not as welcoming as Greece was.And while again you can argue that "England is not Greece" (well, duh), the second part of why I think it is worse is the narrative. It sucks. Can't say I remember much from Odyssey now, but when I was playing it character felt alive. They felt natural. In Valhalla characters are flat, and most of them are completely forgettable. In fact, most of them look a like. I am a Caucasian, but I felt like I am not, because I could barely differentiate between some of the characters.The cutscenes are badly presented, too. Final Fantasy XIV has, arguably, way less complex engine for cutscenes, and yet any random one from FFXIV would be way more articulate and emotional than what Valhalla can offer. I did not care for anything or anyone on the screen till the very end of the game. I think only the Asgard DLC(s) were ok, because they were not supposed to "feel real" to begin with, so I guess suspension of disbelief worked better there.And yet I played 127 hours somehow. There is a lot to do here, probably more than in any of the previous games in the series. The quality of the side content is varying, but I the "world quests" certainly brought some sparkle sometimes. This feature I do approve, because it does make it interesting to explore... Unless it's England.I think they just went for something too big. The game is simply too large. Yes, it's not empty (which is good), but smaller areas from DLCs felt way more balanced and diverse enough for their size. Amount of stuff in England brings some anxiety to me personally. The scale of things is probably what ruined the story, too: if there were fewer characters, maybe  they could have been explored better.In terms of gameplay (besides exploration) - it is the same as the 2 previous games. Can't say if it's better or worse in any regard, to be honest, but if you liked it in previous games, you will probably like it here. Sieges could be a really cool thing, though, if only they had a bit more tactical stuff, like choices of how to progress in them. I think there was only 1, where there was 1 choice (which wall to destroy). But otherwise they were quite satisfactory.So... Yeah. Don't play this for story. For exploration, if you have lots of time - sure, but definitely not for story. And not for "intimate" assassinations.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that by the time I purchased this for PC I had nearly beat the game on PlayStation and the only reason I bought it for PC was because my data transferred over. Its a viking game in the AC universe. I went in expecting to be disappointed based on other peoples reviews trashing on it, but man I very happy I gave it a go because its fantastic. There's simply so much to explore here and I love watching my settlement grow. Evoir is a likable character that I care about and its interesting to see his culture clash with his curiosity and morals. The gameplay is fun and made to play at your own pace. If you're a completionist steer clear because there's simply so many things you can do that you'll never finish it all. You're meant to follow the main story and just do things on the side as you go along. If you try and do everything you come across you'll burn out and be like "why is this taking so long?". Follow the main story first, and then come do other stuff when you've beat it. My least favorite part of the game was the mythical portion (which is almost an entire other game that's optional), but I can see others enjoying it. The map itself is absolutely massive and gorgeous. Overall the amount of hate this game gets for not being a "true AC game" is ridiculous. Remove Assassins Creed from the title and you've got a fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Crashy, terrible loading times and glitch rich – but still worth it overallAs a long time fan of the AC series, and especially the preceding game, Odyssey, I’d been looking forward to getting my hands on AC:V for some time. The initial experience was…not great. The game frequently froze or crashed to desktop, cut scenes were populated by half-loaded textures and people moving like badly performed finger puppets and, oh my stars, the load times. But in the end, I’m glad I persevered to complete the game – albeit not to 100% because frankly after over 200hrs with it (of which I estimate maybe 25% was waiting for things to load) I’d had enough.Gameplay mechanics – these were a good development, and the joy of being able to keep the same weapon throughout much of the game rather than constantly replacing it with ‘upgrades’ was a good one. I also enjoyed turning off the auto-levelling so I could actually slowly begin to feel like the super-warrior Eivor was held up to be, rather than being slotted by every other random minor mook.The storyline was decent enough, although too long in places and after a while I did find myself thinking as I completed another region…’Oh no, is this not finished yet?!’ The acting, for the most part was solid throughout, and I enjoyed all the well-researched historical nods throughout. Although the ‘Robin Hood’ mission – urg. While (more or less) pointless, the dice game – Orlog – was rather fun to play, and I’d happily play this as a standalone.On the downside, some voice acting was…weak and often poorly recorded. One guard sounded like he’d recorded his dialogue in a small public bathroom, such was the echo, which ruined any degree of immersion. The game was also just far, far too long and at times grindy – if I wanted to play an MMO I’d play one – for a single player experience I want a tight and focused narrative. I contrast the 200+ hrs in AC:V to reach the end (and that’s not including any DLC) with the solid and brilliant 50hrs I spent playing Control, and it’s the latter game experience which will stay with me longer.Then, as mentioned there was the frequent and random crashing to desktop or freezing of system necessitating a Task Manager kill of the game. Textures outside in some regions loaded at a glacial pace, meaning my horse raced…then paused…then raced…then paused, although this might because the system expected me to be using an M2 SSD rather than the slower SATA ones. But oddly, it’s not been in an issue in any other games I’ve played in the same or similar engineer. On top of that, some cut scenes were just…broken, but thankfully skipable.So yes, a good game overall, if hobbled with some major tech and narrative issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a downgrade from AC Odyssey by quite a margin.1. The Main character is so much more bland, boring and forgettable than in Odyssey. Eivor just kinda exists, all the while being the most hypocritical character ever: wants peace and quiet - invades someone's land and is mad when they're angry and defend themselves. wtf is this ''Gentleman Viking'' bs?!? Vikings were morally reprehensible, and yet here we are glorifying their atrocities.2. Where's the depth???? Characters mostly seem bland and single issue motivated. Lines are meh at best. Sidequests are insanely short and meaningless when compared to Odyssey. The shallowness of the entire game is insulting, to be entirely honest.3. Choices: So far, choices seem meaningless. In 80% of cases, you're given three options, you pick one and get all three anyways. In about 20% of cases you're given a real choice to make, and even these seem superficial and meaningless, with only a small percentage seeming to have an effect. If not, the time delay to feel the consequences is so long that you'll have forgotten entirely about the story arc by the time they show up.4. Builds: There's barely any variety in Valhalla, and whichever build you opt for feels more or less like any other. Upgrading gear is an incredible chore which really just pushes you to pick one and stick with it for the entire game. 5. Movement: Eivor feels like an anvil being coaxed into movement, whereas Alexios/Kassandra feel light and agile, both in and out of combat.6. Emotions: Valhalla tries to be ''serious'' and 'dark' all of the time. This means that character deaths just don't have the same impact as in Odyssey. There is little to no contrast between the happy times and the sad times that they all mesh into a sort of unhappy middle7. Graphics in Valhalla feel like a noted regression from Odyssey. I play Odyssey on med-high and was generally impressed. I played Valhalla on Ultra (at the cost of frames) and was still thoroughly disappointed8. Music: Valhalla's music is alright, if a bit uninspired. The ''Shanties'' are utter bear excrements. They do not come from your crew, but a voice in your head just singing, as though someone put headphones on Eivor. The shanties stop as soon as you leave command or try and use a bow (which is immersion breaking as all hell) which was not the case in Odyssey. And the lyrics are.... let's just say LazyTown had better creative direction. 9. Sidequests: Odyssey's quests were fleshed out, with funny or interesting characters, and more often than not an unexpected ending. Valhalla's ''world events'' on the other hand are incredibly simplistic, rarely take you more than 50m from the quest giver and as a result are incredibly forgettable. No love or effort put into them, and it shows. 10. Settlements: Every settlement i've encountered in Valhalla seemed tiny and dead. Discovering Lunden was incredibly disappointing compared to arriving at Athens. As a whole, Valhalla felt smaller and deader than Odyssey. Valhalla has more maps, but they all feel significantly worse than any of the maps from Odyssey11. The maps: idk if it was on purpose, but Valhalla maps are an absolute pain in the posterior to traverse. England seems to be entirely made up of narrow valleys and towering hills with sheer rock cliff faces between them, making any straight line voyage unbearably long, in narrow, claustrophobic spaces. Asgard is even worse being entirely vertical, which led me to rage quit a few times (go down there, then go back up, then go back down over and over and over). Sightlines are generally bad, even from the top of hills everything is foggy. Valhalla's maps are somewhere between disastrous and passable.Overall Valhalla is a serious downgrade from Odyssey, in just about every way imaginable. It's a bad AC and an even worse Open World ''RPG''. Just play Odyssey instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried the game in the free weekend.I have played many previous AC games, but this one I found to be the least polished. Especially the beginning of the story has a lot of cut scenes, but the execution leaves something to be desired. Character's faces don't express well, I often cannot tell what emotion they're supposed to be feeling. Everyone is moving around awkwardly. Camera focuses on someone's face as if it's meaningful, while they're making some weird expressions.Or some of the ridiculous outfit designs, like someone wearing chainmail on bare skin, during a feast where no armor would be needed. Some outfits are completely unfit for the snowy cold environment of the beginning. It feels very much like a cartoon version of vikings.The game also just kind of dumps all of the systems on you and leaves them there. It felt a bit like it saying - it's on open world game, you know the drill, get on with it. All the marketing looked very polished so I was hoping that would be the case too with the game, but unfortunately I was pretty quickly disinterested.If I have to balance it out, I would say I did like the interface both visually and functionally. Clean, beautiful and plenty of options. And of course the music is incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, AC Valhalla represents the pinnacle of the Assassin's Creed series to date. A deep, well-thought-out plot, diverse gameplay, interesting characters, and their relationships create a complete gaming universe. Surprisingly, many players have a very restrained opinion of this game, giving it mediocre ratings. In my view, such assessments reflect not the quality of the game itself but the attitude towards the company Ubisoft. The desire to criticize Ubisoft has become a popular youth trend in recent years, a phenomenon that is also evident in attitudes towards games from other major companies. It's no wonder that this affects the companies' plans, as they strive to appeal to as broad an audience as possible in order to maintain profitability levels, consequently producing increasingly more casual games. In particular, it's noticeable that the recently released AC Mirage appears to be a mere shadow of its predecessors Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla itself. It would be quite regrettable if Ubisoft continues to drift in this direction.

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn't played any AC since brotherhood. But, I read over time how it was faring for each AC and the reviews.So when I had 2 wks of PTO, I thought I could get AC Valhalla, finish it in one week, and off to my life I go. Famous Last Words.The game is "amazing". That's a recurrent opinion I had, however it has some big issues, design and technically wise, so I'll list those off firstFirst off, the game is way too big for itself: If you want to plat it, you're going to be spending A LOT of time running around. Fast travels are available, sure, but it's going to be a lot of "FT, ride horse for 1km, grab trinket, repeat". Now do this in a map that's sprawling two regions (or 6 if you get the DLCs), and you're going to be dumping tons of time into the game. Add to the fact all that crappy shenanigan of connect and reda's shop, and you ain't going nowhereCombat isn't one of the things that ACV stellars in, and with all elites it's going to slightly seem repetitive at a certain point.Finally, technically-wise, there are some major bugs present either from the engine or rendering: Boats flying upwards because they touched eachother, bodies clipping into the ground, and the "very repeatable" nvidia driver crash. It gets infuriating, which could possibly be caught with better development.However, there are some good points: the story is amazing, I love the addition of a rogue-lite mode with niflheim, scenaries are really beautifully drawn and designed, and despite it all, the game made it a point to reward you for going out of your way and have fun.It's a really good game if you can overlook its flaws, however, it does indeed have its own big flaws. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: graphics: 10/10stealth gameplay: 9/10talent tree: 9/10gear/weapons: 8/10story: 6/10boss fights: 3/10sieges: 2/10I played 1 difficulty higher than default, with default guards and the intermediate amount of hints/directions.The scenery is beautiful and the world is clearly crafted with alot of effort and love to detail. I wish they had made the autopilot better tho, especially for the longship.The vikings in england part of the story was interesting, albeit a bit odd since it doesn't fit the assassin's creed theme too well in my opinion. However, I was positively surprised specifically by the ending of that story. The norse mythology part of the story was weird and had the characters behave in strange ways to accomodate it. Not a fan.When it comes to the (assassin) gameplay I'd say it was fun. There are some sieges that don't allow for much of a stealth approach, but the majority of time players can play fairly stealthy. Even when doing (river) raids the player can simply pre-clear the entire village/fort and then call in the crew to pickup the treasures (the NPCs are required to open certain doors and chests, which felt a bit awkward after clearing the camp alone, but at least I was able to choose between stealth or brute force).I really like that you can reset and redistribute your talents at any point. Gear is also easily reset and ressources refunded. The talent tree has much to offer and its worth investing some time to find appealing talents. The gear sets are usually incomplete until the later stages of the game, making the set boni of most sets not usable for most of the game which is a bummer in my opinion.There are plenty of boss fights in this game, however many of them did not feel great to me. Besides the number of noticable bugs during boss fights being uncomfortably high, the fights itself often times did not give me much satisfaction. Teleporting enemies are particularly annoying, but even generally avoiding strikes feels less skill based than it could/should be. There are fights where they "want you" to pick up "glowing orbs" in order to have an empored next strike, but unfortunately interacting with anything is often a pain in the butt and so are these orbs. Besides that there's almost no other mechanics, so the name of the game is dodging swings, many of which come at ridiculous speeds, from far away, seem to find you despite moving behind the enemy or deal damage in a cone/in an area. Dodging with propering timing gives you a slow-mo which allows you to get in a hit or two. Alternatively you can try to parry at higher risk (or with better reaction time).There are many collectible things, many of which require you to find your way inside a building/cave. They actually changed up the pattern little by little each time, but over time it felt tedious rather than fun and in many cases it felt unnatural. A building that's barred from the inside, needs to have a breakable stone wall destroyed with explosives, followed by destroying some empty wooden boxes in order to move a stone filled "closet" away from an knee high opening that allows entry into the house, all of that because all the windows are blocked by some wooden planks. Not only would no other person besides the protagonist ever manage to enter, nor would the wooden planks behind the windows be the bigger obstacle than the rest, especially because the roof is likely burnable (and thus should be the stuff blocking the windows).

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been thinking for a few hours before I finished the game whether to give it a positive or negative review but ultimately I enjoyed it more than I despised it.The main problem with Valhalla is that it is so. DAMN. Big. The story parts are mostly fine and yet there are so many different sagas, so many substories, that I had long forgotten about most of them by the time I finished. And the one issue I have with the main storyline is that it has no ending. It just stops. "You did all we asked and want some closure? ♥♥♥♥ you, free roam instead!"The game is filled to the brim with side-content and, well, it is the Ubisoft (duh) ♥♥♥♥♥♥ side-content all over the place. The first few hours are fun, later they become these annoying icons on your map that you know you will not bother with since the rewards are not worth it. As always.On the plus side, the music is absolutely incredible. Hearing the vikings sing on longships, in longhouses, or meadhalls was always a pleasure. The graphics are phenomenal as well albeit there were plenty of visual bugs.As for the gameplay - well, the fighting was kinda fun but not really. Nothing challenging, sometimes frustrating when a stick on legs with a spear blocks a viking with monumental posture who fights with double-handed swords in both hands. The longboat gameplay, so all the raids and such, started to bore me to death after four or five times.I have only beaten the base game and I have no intention to play the DLCs as I am just simply tired of it. Too much unnecessary content with too little meaning. However, I've seen it to the end and cared about the main characters, the main storyline was actually pretty good and engaging, I cannot give it a negative review; though, if there were ratings here, I would give it a solid 5+/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla is the twelfth main installment in Ubisoft’s renowned Assassin's Creed series. Set during the Viking Age, the game immerses players in the tumultuous era of Norse exploration and conquest. It follows Eivor Varinsdottir, a Viking raider whose story intertwines with the broader conflicts of 9th-century England. With a sprawling open world, intricate lore, and rich character development, Valhalla is a grand entry that continues the series' tradition of blending historical fiction with engaging gameplay. The game’s narrative is set in the late 800s, amidst the Viking invasions of England. Players assume the role of Eivor, who can be male or female, and lead their clan from Norway to England in search of a new home. The story is deeply rooted in Norse mythology and historical events, intertwining the Norse gods with the political and social upheaval of the time. The main storyline revolves around Eivor’s quest to establish a Viking settlement in England while navigating the complex politics of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms. The narrative is enriched by detailed character arcs, including alliances with historical figures like King Alfred of Wessex and legendary Norse heroes. The game’s story is divided into several acts, with major plot points involving epic battles, treacherous betrayals, and mystical elements tied to the Isu, an ancient civilization central to the series' lore.Valhalla boasts a vast and diverse open world that captures the essence of Viking-era Britain. The game world is divided into several regions, each reflecting the distinct culture and geography of medieval England—from the rolling hills of England’s countryside to the frost-bitten landscapes of Norway. The open world is teeming with activities, from main quests and side missions to hidden collectibles and environmental puzzles. The game's exploration is bolstered by a well-designed fast-travel system, horseback riding, and a longship for navigating rivers and coastlines. The dynamic weather system and day-night cycle add realism and depth to the exploration experience. The combat system in Valhalla is robust and satisfying, offering a mix of brutal melee combat and strategic use of abilities. Players can engage in visceral, cinematic battles that involve a variety of weapons such as axes, swords, and bows. The dual-wielding system allows for a high degree of customization, letting players create their own combat style. The game also retains the series' stealth elements, although combat often takes precedence. Eivor can use stealth to approach enemies silently, perform assassinations, and utilize various tools such as smoke bombs and tranquilizer darts. The stealth mechanics are less central than in previous installments, focusing more on blending combat with tactical approach. Valhalla incorporates deep RPG mechanics, including a detailed skill tree, character progression, and customization options. Players earn skill points by completing quests and defeating enemies, which can be spent to unlock new abilities and improve Eivor’s combat and exploration skills. The game also features a dialogue system that allows players to make choices influencing the narrative and relationships with other characters. The settlement-building feature is a key aspect of Valhalla. Players can upgrade and expand their Viking settlement, which provides various benefits such as new gear, resources, and gameplay enhancements. This system adds a layer of strategic depth and personal investment to the game. The game offers a wealth of quests and activities beyond the main storyline. Side quests range from solving local mysteries and assisting NPCs to engaging in mini-games and legendary hunts. Each activity is designed to enhance the immersive experience, providing additional lore and interaction opportunities. Visually, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is stunning, with detailed environments and character models that bring the Viking Age to life. The game’s graphical fidelity is particularly impressive on next-gen consoles, offering rich textures, realistic lighting, and atmospheric effects. The soundtrack complements the game’s setting with a mix of traditional Norse music and orchestral scores. Voice acting is robust and adds emotional depth to the characters and narrative, enhancing the overall storytelling experience.While Valhalla is a technical achievement, it is not without issues. Some players have reported bugs and performance hiccups, particularly on older hardware. However, Ubisoft has released several patches to address these concerns and improve the game’s stability.Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a monumental addition to the series, offering a captivating Viking adventure that blends historical intrigue with mythological elements. Its expansive open world, engaging combat, and deep RPG mechanics provide a robust and immersive experience. Despite some technical issues and a less pronounced focus on stealth, the game’s strengths make it a worthy journey for both longtime fans and newcomers to the Assassin’s Creed franchise. For those intrigued by Norse mythology, medieval history, and expansive RPGs, Valhalla delivers an epic and satisfying experience that stands out as one of the series' most ambitious entries.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, there is nothing wrong with this game. It's just that after 10 hours, you've done everything you will ever do going forward. Raids are the same with a different environment. The ships are the same.The combat is the same.The story isn't very engaging. Origins was a revenge story, Odyssey was a story about self, maturity, and the adventure to find these things. Valhalla is a story about... revenge? The challenges of starting a new home? Betraying your sibling when they are an idiot? I'm not sure. Traversing the English countryside is also boring. It's hills, some forests, and the occasional town / city. London and Winchester are not really all that interesting. Alexandria in Origins is a spectacle, Athens in Odyssey is a marvel, but the cities in Valhalla are empty and pointless. Your colony, Ravensthorpe, has everything you will ever need and while it's cool to watch it grow over time it's annoying that you have to keep going back to get goods, resources, and upgrades. Oh, and dear lord, the sudden induced coma missions that take you to Asgard are more annoying than anything. Basically we have the present day story with the chick (I forgot her name), the Viking era story with Eivor, and the Asgardian story with Odin. So more names, terms, and places are crammed into a single game. I think the team at Ubisoft tried to please way too many people and ended up creating a Frankenstein game that pleases no one. If you love Vikings you will probably love this - I know I do. But the gameplay itself is rather tiresome after a few hours and there's nothing else pushing you forward. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This game get a lot of undue criticism. Sure Odyssey is better in terms of it's beauty but that's only because the landscape is less dull and more vibrant. The part of the world Valhalla takes place in is genuinely less vibrant and colourful and therefore is accurate. The facial animations are also not as great as Odyssey nor are there as many stand out characters. But there are way more combat animations. There is more variety and depth to the combat in this game although it doesn't feel as finally tuned as Odyssey. The side quests aren't as varied and interesting as in Odyssey but the game does a better job of keeping you focused on the main story line, and I feel the main story line is better and has a longer duration than Odyssey. Odyssey has some great humour mixed in to break the tension and feels chilled, but Valhalla feels like a serious brooding Viking tale, which is as it should be. Valhalla also seems better optimised. It has more consistent and better performance than Odyssey on my rig and I think this is the case for most people. Although I still prefer Odyssey overall, I enjoy both of these games.They are both great in different ways and the strengths they share are great. Both are worth playing and enjoying. Just don't be in a rush, these games are both MASSIVE and take a long time to play through. They are best enjoyed when you are willing to take your time with them. Don't judge this review by game-play hours displayed as I originally played this game on a Series X console before jumping ship to PC.

_childDocuments_.review: I think giving this a thumbs down would be unfair considering how expansive the world is, the amazing graphics, scenes and landscapes, the mechanics of many things like sailing the boat, using the raven to scout and look out for treasure and so many other things.But despite all that, i couldn't wait to be done with this game, i thought since i finished Odyssey to perfection almost, i could do the same with this and i'd enjoy it till the end, but i didn't. Main quest was so drawn out, it sucked every bit of energy halfway through, uniting every kingdom in Britannia just to get to a very subpar ending (the normal ending) that's barely satisfying doesn't feel good. The game seems to use a lot "quantity over quality" in terms of most side quests, treasures, collectibles and the main quest. I won't even start talking about the repetitive sieges of castles at the end of every alliance made.I sincerely regret buying the DLCs, after i was done with the main quest, i couldn't even bring myself to start them even though i wanted to, that's how much the main quest killed my enjoyment. Uniting all kingdoms shouldn't be an obligation but an optional albeit more impactful decision. Also the DLC Dawn of Ragnarok seems to heavily imply that you're male, which is natural given that you'd be playing Odin's character in Female/Male Eivor, but that means less enjoyment for female players, at least to me it was.The romance is bad, how can such a game with so much to offer could make romance bad and barely done. Romance seems to be two types, committed (till the end) and flings, there's only 1 male romance option that's committed, Tarben, unlike more female committed options existing, he's cute, i liked him and all but really not the best. If you don't mind an extremely drawn out main quest and you think you can do all other things as well without being burnt out from the game then maybe you'd enjoy this or don't mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla is an outstanding game that offers a fantastic blend of action, adventure, and RPG elements. The game's graphics are breathtaking, with detailed and realistic landscapes that transport you to the Viking Age. The game's story is engaging and well-written, immersing players in the world of Eivor, the main character, and the struggles of the Viking people. The game's mechanics are smooth and intuitive, making it easy to get into the game and start playing right away. The game's AI is also highly advanced, providing a challenging and engaging experience that keeps players on their toes.The game's combat system is also noteworthy, it is highly tactical and allows players to use different strategies and tactics to defeat enemies. The game's open-world is huge and offers a lot to explore, from the beautiful landscapes of England and Norway to the different towns and villages that are full of life. The game's character creation and development system is also very robust, allowing players to create unique and powerful characters that can evolve and grow as they progress through the game.One thing that should have been included in the game is Steam Achievments, this would have added more replayability to the game and allows players to track their progress through the game.Overall, Assassin's Creed Valhalla is an excellent game that is an absolute must-have for fans of the series and action-adventure games in general. It's a game that will keep you entertained for hours on end and is sure to be one of the best games of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is not really an Assassins Creed game in terms of combat. I do however like the variety of weapons you can choose to use, whether it's sword and board, one hand weapon, two handers, dual wielding, or dual wielding shields.The story is what hooked me for most of my playtime through the base game and almost completing all the DLC. I may come back to finish off Dawn of Ragnarok, but for now I have to put this one back on the shelf for a while. I almost feel like I got blue balled by how the unlocking the last chapter works. After dumping 100hrs into this game I just can't be bothered to finish that "To Do" list they ask for just to get a proper conclusion, so I just watched some youtube videos of the cinematics. I wish they would have included more into the main story missions from the check list as it completely throws the pacing off in a horrible way.Overall a great experience but don't expect an Assassins Creed game here outside of story.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Odyssey, then you'll likely enjoy Valhalla.The series as a whole has moved away from the stealthy-assassin game play to allowing you play more combat oriented, but stealth play is still viable and one shots nearly everything.I'm a little baffled at the people who claim that there's TOO much to do. Are we supposed to be paying for 10-20 hrs of content tops? The main story quests are on point, and while they don't make me rethink my life or provide deep commentary on society, it's still a decent story set England's Viking era.The scenery is beautiful. I personally enjoy the large spaces between settlements since running from town to town within 30 seconds is just unrealistic. You can't get the rolling hills or marshlands if the next town is just seconds away. The towns themselves seem about right for the period and the one that you cultivate eventually goes from ruins to a little town.The downsides are that the river raid system - equivalent to Odyssey's battle system - is a little tedious after you do it a few times. The gearing system is a mixed bag. On one hand I'm glad I'm not getting spammed with a bunch of junk gear and there's a smaller set of gear that we can build up and upgrade. On the other hand, the bonuses seem minor, at least in the mid game. The combat is fine. You can swing your axe all day and do just fine, but to really excel it's encouraged to mix between your bow, melee, and special abilities/triggers.In terms of bugs, I've encountered some crashes, but in the 40 hours it's only been 1 CTD. There's some graphical glitches when boarding/leaving your longboat, but I wouldn't call it literally unplayable just because I'm not stumbling through around in a boat realistically enough.

I even found some enjoyment in it, despite the review. But, it would seem I have lost interest. So that requires some thought as to why.- Story: I don't find it very appealing, nor particularly interesting. No agency or feeling of importance.- Choices: While you can choose responses, they don't seem to matter.- Side-quests: there are too many, needless and boring, side-quests with silly writing and plots- Treasures: The map is "riddled" with treasures, and sadly you may have to gather them all- Voice acting: Nordic dialect. With few exceptions, diction and tone is off imo. I don't like the Anglicisation- Female Eivor: Her voice is, not very feminine. I believe it is more direction than the actor. Bad choice.- Female characters: I don't know, they look weird. Male characters I find mostly  look fine/normal.- Music: Music by Einar Selvik was mostly great, but beyond that I found little to admire.- Too big: I both love it, and dislike it. If you have limited time, find something else.I choose to focus on downsides, as it is a negative review after all. I'm sure many will disagree, which is both expected and fine. We all have different tastes. Have a great day!

_childDocuments_.review: Last night I started properly playing and I just finished my second, full session of several hours - one session on my desktop and one on my Steam Deck - and I'm having a lot of fun! I believe the "mixed" reviews are generally due to some (very fair) criticisms of Ubisoft (and their decisions and intransigence with player requests - especially regarding missing achievements on Steam) however the game itself is high quality and fun to play.The ancient Norse world is attractive and immersive. Likely because of it being so attractive, the game is technically challenging for your hardware. My Steam Deck in particular took some focus on the configuration to get it to an enjoyable state but I did get it to a very enjoyable 40FPS.The built in FSR works really well. I even use it set to Ultra Quality to get my desktop's RTX 3080 from an FPS in the upper 70s to just over 100FPS with Ultra High graphics settings outputting to my ultrawide monitor's 3440x1440 resolution.My Steam Deck, on the other hand, is set to a mix of low & medium graphics settings with FSR also set to Ultra Quality at 800p resolution with a mostly locked 40FPS with occasional dips into the 30s during cut scenes or with lots of characters on screen. Even with these occasional dips they are not noticeable unless the FPS counter is on the screen. And these settings look great on the Deck's small screen. I could alternatively set the resolution down to 720p if I wanted even more performance without giving much away.Ubisoft's cloud saves are set up by default and make for a seamless switch between my desktop and my Deck.I can definitely recommend this game for those either with a beefy system or for others, including Steam Deck owners, if you're willing to work on the graphics settings to get it running nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from a lifelong fan of the Assassin's Creed games, I have to say that AC Valhalla is quite a different direction that the franchise has taken. But is that really a bad thing?Veering off the long-beaten path, Valhalla presents an absolutely massive open-world map with breathtaking landscapes, and even additional realms of travel beyond the base-game's area (various trips to additional nations, locations, etc). This is quite a stark change from the founding games, and one that has been progressively added to since AC Origins. Another stark difference of Valhalla is the divorce between the traditional combat and stealth we've always known. No longer are the days where stealth is a requirement for an Assassin's Creed game. Now, you are a brute of a viking with a big, heavy ax, and subtlety is not exactly your strong suit. These two major changes were enough to scare off many AC traditionalist, but to put it frankly? The tradition AC format was getting old. How many times can you creep through a building and stalk rooftops to pounce on some dude until you get bored. For me, it was 15 years. I, for one, love the chance that has been made (so far) and look forward to the new face of the Assassin's Creed. Lets hope they don't f*** it up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times where the yes/no system of Steam Reviews is kinda limiting. As a score I'd give AC: Valhalla a 6/10, but if I have to pick between Yes/No, I'm leaning more towards "Do not recommend'.  This game has it's cool moments but they take up 5-10% of the total game time. I'm talking about the bosses, the main quests that are connected to The Order, the cave exploration side quests, as well as some fun main and side quests.  Everything else is boring, Yes - even the combat. Not that you'll be doing much combat. Majority of time you'll be doing boring "environmental puzzles" in order to get gear (aka spend 2-5 minutes looking for an oil jar, a key or a window from which you can break a barricaded door), boring side quests to get XP, and boring fetch quests to get clues for Order members. And unlike previous games, none of that is optional - you need new gear in order to get stronger, you need xp because of the level thresholds of the zones and you need to kill every Order member in order to have 100% story competition. Also if you want to upgrade your quiver or the amount HP rations you may carry - well then you also need to hunt down those small chests that RANDOMLY give you fabric - the material you need for the upgrades. Now to get back to the combat. It's outdated to say the least. You have normal attack, heavy attack, block, parry and dodge. Also you can shoot with the bow. With the help of abilities you can imbue your weapons with either poison or flame for a short time, which just gives you DOT damage. The other active abilities are just animations that do raw damage. They either kill a single soldier, or they do a tiny amount of damage versus a boss. In both cases they are useless. Not only is this combat worse than games like God of War, Marvel's Spider-Man and DMC V, but it's also worse than AC Odyssey - a game that actually had much bigger variety in weapons AND abilities that actually are woven into the combat instead of interrupting it. The main story is boring convoluted mess. It starts out pretty normal - you travel with your brother in order to establish a new home in England and gather allies. However the moment your brother starts talking about "his true destiny" it all goes to ♥♥♥♥. Aside from the main story, you have a small story for each England zone....and most of them are boring. Not only that, but they also recycle story points. More than once I had to uncover a traitor, more than once I had to help a boy king become a man, more than once I had to resolve a romance plot. Don't even start me on the story provided from the side quests. In one of the side quests I had to release some cats, in order to chase away some mice....I AM SUPPOSED TO BE A VIKING ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Even the interface in this game is designed to waste your time. You don't have a button to equip all set pieces at once, you need to visit an NPC in order to upgrade your gear, and you need a special building in order to have gear loadouts. The leveling system is needlessly presented in the form of several big nodes and much more smaller nodes with barely noticeable passive upgrades. When you do sync up the map reveals the locations of side quests and treasure locations but it doesn't tell you what kinds of side quests/treasures. Instead you have to either get close to them, buy a map or....buy a microtransaction that gives you the info. Even in that regard the game fails. The world is beautiful, but it there is nothing outstanding in it. Your either passing across vast green pastures or just land and mountains covered in snow. The audio is all over the place - sometimes combat music will stick around after the combat is done. Sometimes in cutscenes you will have loud dialogue ... and in the very next cutscene very loud music and quiet dialogue. If you want a better AC game - play any of the previous ones, they are better, yes - even the very first AC game is better than this one. If you want a better viking experience - I recommend watching the show "Vikings". Hopefully Valhalla is the last gigantic bland and bloated open world AC game. Ubisoft are trying to mimic the success of The Witcher 3, but even CDPR themselves admitted that TW3 was too long for most people and made a much more condensed adventure with Cyberpunk 2077. This is a special paragraph for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ oil jars. ♥♥♥♥ OIL JARS!  I hate whoever came up with them, I hate whoever had the idea to NOT make them higlitable by eagle vision and finally I hate whoever decided to not make a aim path visible when you are aiming to throw them. From my neary 100 hour playtime I probably spent 20 hours just searching for oil jars. Dear Ubisoft - if you're gonna have that many environmental puzzles you need to come up with more creative solutions. I also find it ridiculous that among all the weapons, talents and abilities there isn't a single one that allows me to break down breakable walls. Hell even in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Asgard section where I play as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Odin there are Oil Jar puzzles. If AC Mirage has a single Oil Jar puzzle within the first 2 hours, I'm refunding!

Yet if we compare this to games like Skyrim and Fallout, its LITERALLY the same type of stuff. - You do quests - You do side quests- You collect things- You do the story / story arcs.- Rinse. Wash. Repeat. The only reason people are so butt hurt about this game from what I can tell, and you see it in almost EVERY review, is because Ubisoft made it, and if you wanna be a cool bandwagon bro, you say what others are saying. oh and the whining about offline mode. Boohoo there's no offline mode. D'ont like it? Don't play it? Its really that simple.Game's got a lot going on for it, and its got a side story arc that's not too bad. i personally love vikings, and this game gives a good twist on the aspects of that. They've added things from previous AC games, and tweaked/improved on the others. You can choose different weapon variant types (one handed / two handed), and different armor classes and traits that go with them. Tech/skill tree for this game is massive, and gives some cool re-tweaked / new skills to use in combat.I don't know why they added romance as an options. Probably to just make some weirdo's happy, but its honestly unnecessary for a AC game.Glitch/crash wise, I've only crashed once in my entire 60+hours of playing this game when i tried to take a screenshot (but who wants to do that for a single player game anyways), so folks should probably turn their potatoes down graphic wise, if they want to avoid that. I wont give a rating grid like some people do on here, cause that comes off as super pretentious and like their scale actually equates to anything of value/relevance. Ill say this. If you like the Assassins Creed story line, this is a great addition to it. You don't like the price tag? Wait for a sale then. _childDocuments_.review: Gonna start this review by saying that the only reason I reinstalled this game was Assassin's Creed Mirage. That's all. AC Mirage was supposed to be a DLC for Valhalla, and somehow, as small as it was, it was better than Valhalla in every way.I really really had such a huge wall of negativity build around this game. I've watched dozen of videos with people hating on it. And yet, I had fun. And I have fun still. I don't hate this game. Eivor is likeable. I like her more than Kassandra from Odyssey. The gameplay is okay, it's fun, it lacks punch, though. But it's unique in its own way, as this is the only game in the series that has a small, yet, decent gore system. It's an okay game, really. The characters are okay, mostly boring, but okay. But for me, the real star is Basim. He's just so fascinating. Granted, he is the only assassin in this whole game, but he's just so interesting. And Mirage made me like him even more. I just wished he was the main character in Valhalla. Not gonna lie.What I don't like about Valhalla is just how big it is. Too big. When I open the map it literally lags because it's filled with icons. What I also don't like, is the parkour. The worst we've ever seen in any AC game. So heavy, so slow, so simple, lacks any real control or skill. Norway and England aren't built for parkour. Traversing on ropes isn't parkour. Nor is climbing huge rocks that shouldn't be able to be climbed on. Stealth is busted. Literally I try so hard to play stealthy, but the game doesn't allow me to. The real tragedy of this game, is that Mirage proved it could've been better. It proved parkour could've been better, it proved stealth could've been better. It's just a true shame. Because it's a good game, it's just too much, too much quantity and too little quality. I can't give it a negative review because I'll be back to play it in just a bit, but it's just a shame that it turned out to be like this.Also, again, Mirage > Valhalla.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommeneded on deep sale only.If you're interested in this game then be aware at least of how long it is. Im at 100 hours and i still haven't done everything there is to do, but that's not really a good thing because the vast majority of things to do (in typical UBISOFT fashion) are just time wasters. This game is gorgeous to look and the gameplay keeps you hooked aswell as the norse valhalla vibe, but beyond that it really does get boring over time. Im having a really hard time finishing this. Lots of icons on the map that really dont do much other than offer gimmick short games for silly rewards (like tatoos and ship parts that look stupid). Even the DLC isn't much more than simply weapon skins (as weapons are pretty much normalized no matter what you get). Im sure there are insane weapons with super cool bonus stats added to them, but by the time you get them they really dont offer anything to speak of over the normal weapons (and they dont add anything real in terms of cool new combat...just new bonuses that are mostly meh). The combat system is really not amazing (even with all the skills you get). You mash quick attack and heavy attack in 2-4 moves and thats about it. Heavy attack kills will grant executions which dont vary much so youll see the same animations over and over again.Your town for the most part is lame and utterly useless. I use maybe 3 buildings they want me to build. Cartographer, weapon blacksmith and tradepost. Maybe river raids, but river raiding get stupid quickly and most of your additions to the town dont add up to much youll really need to survive. Most add to a feast buff that youll never use. That or alternate DLC or expansion games added to make the game feel "cool" to those who like god of war. Its really not especially fun other than simply just existing as another thing to do. Most story lines are kill here kill there, investigate here and there, raid a giant castle (literally everytime it gets repetative) and then report back to your town for the next one. Rinse and repeat. But its not bad. Id say above average for what it is. Most stories are pretty good with simply too many bad ones in between to make the game good.Stealth is horrible as usual with armor set slots to switch between stealth and combat builds, but i never found myself needing to use them for much of anything as stealthing is silly unless you building specifically into stealth damage. Otherwise you wont be able to stealth kill your targets at all. Unless you want to keep jumping onto their backs w/ the assassination thing but that also gets nerfed over time and unless you keep up with it in skills (assassination damage) its pointless to do as youll never be able to kill anything with one hit (as the damage gets nerfed over time as you face higher power lvl enemies).What you do gather is mostly hidden behind timewaster activities that amount to find a key with your raven vision, or shoot a door open from a window in the back, climb in to a broken wall joint,  blow up a blocked entrance, or move a moveable shelf back or side to side. Literally thats about it or a variation of several of those. And that goes on for the entire game. Its so mind numbingly easy that it becomes a chore very quickly as it becomes "guess the gimmick" the devs thought of. Thankfully most of the games "achievements" are anything noteworthy so its pointless to do anything other than what you need to do (find ingots, iron, and leather, and weapon/armor upgrade materials). The rest you can leave alone and let it just sit there on your minimap. The game can really be won within 80 hours if you just play the storyline and skip most everything else.Right now im doing this on beserker difficulty and its still not really challenging. Combat is mostly just slow and dull with enemies just force interrupting you with parry moves that you have to wait for an attack to parry yourself so it can take a while. Forcing you to build into quick kills to make it go faster. The abilities aren't particularly amazing. I would have loved far better and cooler variation to keep combat more fresh, but its really gets stale no matter how many abilities you find. Abilities amount to just insane quick damage which makes you build adrenaline slots over time to keep combat moving faster. They really aren't that cool either. Literally nothing that adds extra cool moves to your combat. Its always extra kind of out of place stuff that doesnt really add up to the flow of things. Minus maybe a few abilities that is.Beyond that the game really is too long for what it is. They needed to end this far sooner with a far better finisher quest line. Im really having a hard time finding the will to finish it due to how lame most of the end is. I think im just gonna go for what i feel is the ending after i finish this last territory and see what happens.However if you love AC games for their length, then youll probably feel this game is a really nice addition and youll probably love it. However the combat is worse than previous games for sure.  Be warned and take what ive said to heart. This really is just a typical UBISOFT release. Nothing horribly new here.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an Assassin's Creed game in the slightest, and if you can get over that then I'm sure you would like this game. People say this game is really repetitive and to an extent I agree. However, in my view this game tells a large scale adventure story of a cool Vikings taking over an whole island, and you can't tell that story in an 18 hour game. My only issue with this game is that it can be prone to a lot of crashing. Once I crashed 6 times in a row within five minutes of each other. _childDocuments_.review: Snagged on sale, had many more hours on PS4.I can say that Valhalla's number 1 complaint on PC seems to be problems with it running. I've barely had any issues and none of which weren't corrected with some simple graphic tweaking, i've seen a few bugs but nothing really bothersome, sometimes combat feels janky but i realized long ago its just the animations sometimes being a little funky.Valhalla is a great entry in the creed franchise, its got a great story, good characters and the viking focus is one of the better choices in the series. Combat feels fun and engaging but its where one of our first hiccups comes in.Basically you the player will get used to 2 types of combat.Minion combat: many guys, they don't really stand a chance unless you are being dumb or are really out leveled. Its easy and your bread and butter alot of the time.Named character combat: These guys regularly have immense health pools or other sorts of defenses that puts them on a entirely different strata of difficulty for you, many of which can't be fought directly unless you utilize the various abilities you'll get throughout the game. If you find one of these guys and he wipes the floor with you get creative or come back later with different abilities.Naval combat has taken a step backward from other entries, its still there but is immensely streamlined, you'll spend your longboat time mostly just traveling with the occasional raid (raids are pretty cool tbh) The additon stories your crew can tell in addition to the songs keeps these segments or exploration.The world is HUGE, nothing we aren't used to by this point in the series but i always feel like its worth mentioning. of course like previous entries that huge world seems to be sparsely populated save for various areas. Valhalla's world is...probably one of the more boring ones of the franchise which might play a part in why this game is notorious for player retention.Valhalla is one of the last decent entries in the Creed franchise. Grab it if its on sale but you really shouldn't be paying more than 30 to 40 for the thing.

_childDocuments_.review: All-in-all, I thought I'd be way more bored with an Assassin's Creed game than I was. Pros and Cons listed below, but a 6/10 for basically being just slightly above average.Pros:-RPG like stat system allowing you to either shoot, assassinate, or fight your way through the game.-Various weapons to change your fighting style.-Different armor sets to improve your fighting style.-A good enough wealth of enemies to make you pay attention to what they're doing.-A big game with lots of scenic areas to enjoy exploring.Cons:-RPG like stat system falls off mid game, and challenges don't keep up, causing you to begin cheesing everything.-Weapons and armor sets aren't enough to justify needing them, as enemies will either 1 shot you or do nothing to you. Weapon variety has no clear advantage one way or another.-Enemy variety becomes stale at mid-game when you've seen it all and pretty much know what to expect.-Story is trite (more info in spoilers), and side-quests are insultingly dumb as opposed to be meaningful.-Choices don't matter.Spoilers BelowStory essentially follows a guy whose father died in a 'cowardly way' to his people and his surrogate brother who gets denied becoming a king. Surrogate brother explores the worlds, joins the assassins, they just so happen to like main character and give him the hand blade (the assassin order is /VERY/ loosely tied to this). Brother gets taken away, bunch of very skipable missions about straight forward betrayals ensues, brother comes back having been tortured but somehow learns about ancient ones' lab of technology. Go to lab of technology, its just a VR chamber that shows you whatever afterlife you want but its not perfect and main character figures it out. Pulls brother out of it, meanwhile assassins creed guy wigs out for unexplained reason and attacks main character. Essentially gets stuck in VR machine for thousands of years only to be resurrected by a magic staff, talks about wanting to find his family. VR machine also is responsible for gravity issues on planet so it gets tweaked because of magical AI thing inside, or something. Brother of main character steps down from leader because he's too effed up from torture, main character no longer believes in valhalla because of VR chamber. Game ends on cliffhanger to set up next years big, dumb, poorly written, uncompelling assassins creed game because Assassin's Creed guy stuck in VR machine gets revived by magical staff. Hopefully the next one actually involves the assassins and their creed.TL:DR- the story doesn't tell anything really compelling except "Afterlife is a myth, Order of Ancients (the enemy of the Assassin's Creed) = bad." It is kinda cool to see England during the Danish, Norwegian invasions, but it doesn't justify all the dumb story, lack of narrative point, bafflingly pointless and non-foreshadowed twists that have no meaning either, and stale gameplay at the 50% - 100% mark. Sadly, their in game expansion where you play as Odin has cooler enemies and characters, but its just a roguelite with not a lot of story nor connection to the main story or franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Roman EmpireThe Roman Empire ruled the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia and North Africa. The Romans conquered most of this during the Republic, and it was ruled by emperors following Octavian's assumption of effective sole rule in 27 BC. The western empire collapsed in 476 AD, but the eastern empire lasted until the fall of Constantinople in 1453.By 100 BC, Rome had expanded its rule to most of the Mediterranean and beyond. However, it was severely destabilized by civil wars and political conflicts, which culminated in the victory of Octavian over Mark Antony and Cleopatra at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, and the subsequent conquest of the Ptolemaic Kingdom in Egypt. In 27 BC, the Roman Senate granted Octavian overarching military power (imperium) and the new title of Augustus, marking his accession as the first Roman emperor. The vast Roman territories were organized into senatorial provinces, governed by proconsuls who were appointed by lot annually, and imperial provinces, which belonged to the emperor but were governed by legates. The first two centuries of the Empire saw a period of unprecedented stability and prosperity known as the Pax Romana (lit. 'Roman Peace'). Rome reached its greatest territorial extent under Trajan (r. 98–117 AD), but a period of increasing trouble and decline began under Commodus (r. 180–192). In the 3rd century, the Empire underwent a 50-year crisis that threatened its existence due to civil war, plagues and barbarian invasions. The Gallic and Palmyrene empires broke away from the state and a series of short-lived emperors led the Empire, which was later reunified under Aurelian (r. 270–275). The civil wars ended with the victory of Diocletian (r. 284–305), who set up two different imperial courts in the Greek East and Latin West. Constantine the Great (r. 306–337), the first Christian emperor, moved the imperial seat from Rome to Byzantium in 330, and renamed it Constantinople. The Migration Period, involving large invasions by Germanic peoples and by the Huns of Attila, led to the decline of the Western Roman Empire. With the fall of Ravenna to the Germanic Herulians and the deposition of Romulus Augustus in 476 by Odoacer, the Western Empire finally collapsed. The Eastern Roman Empire survived for another millennium with Constantinople as its sole capital, until the city's fall in 1453.Due to the Empire's extent and endurance, its institutions and culture had a lasting influence on the development of language, religion, art, architecture, literature, philosophy, law, and forms of government across its territories. Latin evolved into the Romance languages while Medieval Greek became the language of the East. The Empire's adoption of Christianity resulted in the formation of medieval Christendom. Roman and Greek art had a profound impact on the Italian Renaissance. Rome's architectural tradition served as the basis for Romanesque, Renaissance and Neoclassical architecture, influencing Islamic architecture. The rediscovery of classical science and technology (which formed the basis for Islamic science) in medieval Europe contributed to the Scientific Renaissance and Scientific Revolution. Many modern legal systems, such as the Napoleonic Code, descend from Roman law. Rome's republican institutions have influenced the Italian city-state republics of the medieval period, the early United States, and modern democratic republics.
