_childDocuments_.review: This is not a great Assassin’s Creed game. It is far too bloated with tedious things to do but if you just focus on the missions it still has the things which make Assassin’s Creed games fun.After really enjoying Odyssey I was rather disappointed by this one. To break this down I’ll look at the things I generally enjoy about Assassin’s Creed games.The combat was the fly in the ointment in Odyssey, it was far too drawn out and grindy. Here they have addressed this with a bunch of options to tune the combat to exactly how easy or difficult you want it to be. However the leveling up and upgrades are just an over complicated mess. Leveling up is a horrible spider web of upgrades, after a while I stopped caring and just auto assigned the skill points. The weapons no longer have the big red or green number to compare it to your current weapon so you have to scrutinise all the stats. Then not content with making you collect resources to upgrade your weapons you have to collect special resources to enhance you weapon to allow further upgrades. The engravings have been replaced with runes, so instead of being able to to put whatever engraving you want on whichever weapon you have an inventory filled with hundred of runes to dig through. A short while into the game I just gave up on all of this entirely, whacked the difficulty right down and just stuck with the equipment I had.I was glad to see the modern day plot feeling a bit more developed rather than feeling like they were just buggering about in the Animus for the sake of it. I liked how the story was broken down into distinct arcs that can be tackled in the order you choose. Overall the story had its good moments but a lot of it was pretty forgettable. In Odyssey they weaved in some Greek mythology with the Assassin’s Creed mythology that I ended up enjoying. They obviously wanted to do something similar here but they way they did it was to just have the protagonist get smashed out of their head on drugs and hallucinate about the Norse gods. It felt disconnected and irrelevant to the main plot so I ignored these side missions. Then later on in the main plot it feels like they arbitrarily selected a character to betray you at random which only makes sense if you have played these mythology arcs.I’ve always loved the sense of satisfaction of collecting things in games but this game pushed me over the edge. There are so many of them and they are designed to be just that little bit too annoying to be fun. A lot of the things to collect have a little extra step like finding a key or an explosive jar and the drinking game required a coordination that I just didn’t have. It was after spending a stupid amount of time trying and failing to stack a particular pile of rocks I suddenly had to ask myself, “What am I doing with my life?” The collectibles here are more like throwing seeds in front of a vampire; I am filled with a compulsion to cross off all the dots on the map rather than any sense of enjoyment. The rewards for collecting things are no reward at all; they are weapons I was never going to use or resources to enhance weapons that again I was never going to use.As ever the game has been made with excellent attention to detail. It still looks good and runs fine on my ancient graphics card.I liked being able to select the gender of the protagonist again and being able to change at will. I picked the option to let the game decide thinking it would be like Syndicate where it had a balance between both characters. However this option just uses female Eivor for the historical arcs and male Eivor for the mythology arcs. At first I didn’t even realise that was what was going on in the mythology arc, I thought it was just the character model for Havi. In Odyssey I chose Kassandra as I thought the voice acting was better but in this game I think male Eivor has the better voice acting, female Eivor sounds like a teenager trying to force their voice to be low and gravelly as they try and buy alcohol with a fake ID.I loved the Discovery tour when it was added in Origins and they have put a lot of effort into it to make it more game like; entirely missing the point of what made it so good back in Origins. I love the way Assassin’s Creed games mix historical events with fiction but it always left me unsure where the line between fact and fiction was. The discovery tour in Origins was great for authoritatively explaining the historical basis for the game and what was compromised for the sake of gameplay. By changing this to introduce more stories to play through again left me unsure of the historical basis of what was depicted.I bought the Ragnarok Edition and after completing the main game I started on the Ragnarok DLC but quickly lost all motivation to continue. I just lost all motivation to keep playing, there are too many arbitrary things to do in the main game without having to add more with the DLC. Okay so I’m still going to give this game a thumbs up. It is not a particularly good outing for the series but the things that tainted the game can be mostly ignored as long as you don’t get hung up on collecting everything.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:Okay, so my first review might have been a little hasty.  After seeing the repli from UbiKobold and noticing a few other oddities on my system I messed with a few settings and might have stumbled on my main problem.  It seems my freesync ultrawide isn't playing nice with gsync enabled and was what was preventing the game from running in fullscreen and generally being unstable.  I've disabled that in the monitor as well as nvidia settings and everything seems to be running great.  To be clear, this game really didn't like having freesync enabled with an nvidia gpu but there were a few other less noticeable issues on my system (both in windows and linux) that seem to be related to this as well.Changing my review to positive and recommended because I am genuinely enjoying the game.  Very early in the playtime so I can't comment on overall stability but so far this worked for me and might be worth a look if you're having a similar issue with the screen blacking out or the game only running in windowed mode.ORIGINAL REVIEW (please see above):Bought today because of the sale.  Huge download (which is fine) but then greeted with stutters, hitches, and a flashing black screen on first boot.  Had to edit the .ini file to activate windowed mode which worked but changing back to fullscreen or boarderless caused the game to go black any time the game window was in focus.Spent the evening troubleshooting to no avail.  I've yet to actually play any of the game since what's the point of a high refresh rate ultra wide if you're running in windowed mode...  Completely garbage on Windows 11 for me, requested a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 192 hours in: Grudging thumbs up, with lots of caveats.So Ive played through the main campaign, the DLCs (except Nilfheim), Ive maxed everything out (impossible - there is a stupid amount of stuff to max out, so Ive maxed out evertyhing I wanted to), done all the quests (ok, almost, I just cant be bothered with things like donating fish), and my net summary is that Valhalla isnt a bad game. It is even verging on a good one, But it is NOT a great one. There are some awesome moments which are great, eg the Odin storyline/worlds, but in general Valhalla is merely "fine". It is hugely addictive, and not a a in healthy way, Ive played ~200 hours on a game which is merely OK, and it quite annoying at times, but you cannot fault it for lack of content. I am actually quite impressed by the long game of Valhalla from a design and consumer value for money perspective: once youve done all the "quest storylines", you are left with 1/ cleaning up icons on the maps, 2/ river raiding until you go blind, 3/ niflheim rogue runs (and this is actually super well designed, I think I might continue to play this, its just a shame the actual gameplay isnt more fun/epic). God of War is a strictly better game in every regard, as is The WItcher 3, and I like AC Odyssey more, but all "end" which is a real shame (or a blessing, other games to play ya know!), and I would love it if they had the end game variety of stuff to do which Valhalla does.What else?- it sucks there is no steam achievements integration- the crashing really is terrible- the world largely feels soulless- the writing (outside of Odins quest) is not engaging- overwhelming majority of quests are boring and small- UBI connect is SUPER DUPER ULTRA flaky, frequently disconnects, struggles to connect at times, its all blegh- the game always "checks for additional content" on startup, and it wastes 30 seconds of your life. super ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scummy of ubi.Id rant more about crashing on the Steam Deck, but its not verified, so its kind of a draw - its good it plays on steam deck at all, and its super crashy on it (like once per hour).===============================================Update 80 hours in: Thumbs up/downI actually quite like it now. Maybe its Stockholm syndrome, but cest la vie. But its not a great game, its just designed to be very addictive.I moved to a one handed hammer, and combat is more fun now, more nimble, only two beers drunk, not completely ♥♥♥♥ faced drunk, but still the parry timing indicator is beyond unhelpful, even when it exists.The Odin stuff is EPIC. Riding a snow wolf, or hell cat. The Asgard storyline, fighting Fenrir, and the Jotunheim multiply connected spaces specifically. Odin himself is a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but at least he feels like a protagonist and a character. Its a real shame that the ability tree hasnt been replaced with some proper God powers, but the actual God Powers you get in the Svartlheim world are good, being a bird is awesome, and in general that storyline is good. They should have made an entire game of this. But its still nowhere near as good as God of War, if GOW is 10/10 (and it basically is), then the Odin storyline and gameplay is 7/10. Maybe 6.===============================================Original review 16 hours in: Thumbs down!Based on the way my brain associates things while playing AC Valhalla, I will compare it to the The Witcher 3 (look and feel of the world, broad game play similarities, etc). And in this comparison, ACV comes across as shallow and shabby, bland and boring, its sloppy instead of snappy.Whats funny, is that this is obviously the successor for ACO, which I loved. I loved the feel of the ancient Greek world, I loved Kassandra (who was funny, moral and kickass), and I even liked the combat better (it felt tighter and more snappy than ACV?!). Maybe Ive had a stroke, as I would have expected ACV to basically be ACO with a viking theme, but it doesnt feel like this at all, it feels sh*t. I played through ACO twice back to back, did all the DLC, loved it all and wanted more. THE BAD:The grimy mucky world of ACV isnt alive like in TW3, villages dont bustle, animals dont scurry, foliage doesnt sway (properly, it squeezes?).The combat in TW3 is sublime, light and heavy attacks, blocking and dodging feel like a wonderful ballet, while in ACV Eivor just swings (my 2 handed axe) like a drunk, and the timing for blocking, dodging, etc all feel sloppy. Obviously the stealth assassinations and body hiding etc in ACV are better since they are not present in TW3. The story line has not grabbed me in any way, I dont empathise with anyone and the story seems to be "build a village and kill the order", vs TW3 which has one of the best, most engrossing, most captivating story lines in video-game-dom, and makes even the most evil monsters feel understandable.Oh, and its ♥♥♥♥♥♥ crashy. Like take a screenshot-> crash. Use a synchronisation point -> Crash. Kill an enemy -> Crash. So tiresome.I guess I'll keep chuntering through this thing, on the basis that "surely it must get good at some point", but for now, Its a chore not a pleasure.THE GOOD:The graphics are nothing to write home about, Im running this with everything on a 3090, and it look blegh (vs ray traced games, vs Fenyx, Vs TW3 original, etc), and the lighting is mostly flat, but sometimes there is a beautiful vista, or the sun is low cutting through the clouds, and it looks pretty good. The archery is OK, but not as good as Fenyx (which I just played through), but its still quite well done, headshotting enemies never gets old. There is a decent amount of customisation of the gameplay (parrying windows in ms, FOV, etc, feels like O(100) options to customise) , this is really impressive actually and more games should do this. THE F*CKING UGLY:It is also F**KING ANNOYING that the game checks for additional content on startup - this takes 30sec whether you are online or offline, and as near as I can tell is some form of sh*te DRM. It cant be incompetence, as the same thing happens in Fenyx, so it must be malice. And if it doesnt take 30seconds, it might take a few minutes. F*CK OFF Ubisoft!!!

_childDocuments_.review: After eagerly awaiting its arrival on Steam, Assassin's Creed Valhalla delivers another open-world masterpiece from Ubisoft, following in the footsteps of its acclaimed predecessors, Odyssey and Origins. With a vast amount of content and a richly crafted world, Valhalla immerses players in an epic Viking adventure that is sure to captivate fans of the franchise.One of the standout features of Assassin's Creed Valhalla is the immense and meticulously designed open world. Ubisoft has once again outdone themselves, creating a breathtaking and expansive playground for players to explore. From the towering mountains of Norway to the lush fields of England, every corner of the world is teeming with detail and offers countless opportunities for discovery.Accompanying the vast world is the powerful and evocative soundtrack, highlighted by the epic composition "The First Departure" by Sarah Schachner. The music seamlessly blends with the gameplay, enhancing the immersive experience and adding an extra layer of grandeur to the Viking saga.While the main character's story is solid, it follows the familiar Assassin's Creed formula of being enjoyable but not particularly groundbreaking or unpredictable. However, the strength of Valhalla lies in its abundance of side content and exploration. Engaging in raids, building settlements, uncovering hidden secrets, and forging alliances provide hours upon hours of captivating gameplay.The sheer amount of content in Assassin's Creed Valhalla ensures that players will always have something new to discover and experience. The game offers a remarkable level of player agency, allowing them to shape their Viking saga and forge their own path through the richly detailed world.While the main storyline may not be the most groundbreaking aspect, the overall experience of Assassin's Creed Valhalla is undeniably amazing. The game captures the essence of the Viking era, immersing players in a world full of historical depth and breathtaking landscapes. From the awe-inspiring architecture to the intricate details of Norse mythology, Valhalla is a testament to Ubisoft's commitment to creating immersive open-world adventures.In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a remarkable addition to the franchise, showcasing Ubisoft's expertise in crafting open-world experiences. With its vast content, richly detailed world, and the captivating soundtrack, Valhalla offers players an unforgettable Viking adventure. While the main storyline may be familiar, the game more than makes up for it with its expansive exploration and rewarding gameplay. Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a must-buy for fans of the series and an immersive journey well worth embarking upon.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an AC game. But that's not necessarily a bad thing.This is essentially what would happen if Fable and Kingdoms of Amalur had a Danish Viking child who longs to raid Christian Settlements to appease their people and their Gods. Movement is my only gripe. Most of the time it isn't a problem but the second I want to go down I have to play ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ leapfrog with the gap 4-5times before the "c" registers that I want to drop.There are other moments where the auto-parkore mechanic decides you wanted to jump down a 100ft cliff face rather than try to jump to the ledge to the right.Other than that, everything is perfect. Plenty of loot to be discovered, many ways to play with an extensive talent tree that can eventually be 100%ed. Missions and side missions are extensive and full of unique features that make them each feel like an individual quest, rather than an exp grind and repeat. Microtransaction Store items can be earned in game for free, always a plus. Raiding is the only thing that really feels grindy, but not in a bad way. Having to carry a team of barely competent AI adds an element of danger to each run that I'm not upset at. Primarily because the alternative would be just you shredding through every settlement one after another in 1 long monotonous grindfest. Solid RPG, 90/100

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the Complete Edition of AC Valhalla for $40 as many people on the internet recommended it. One thing I took note of was the constant mixed reviews regarding the game play and the storyline that was given to the players which was repetitive and boring as compared to the earlier versions of Assassins Creed (E.g Black flag). So I decided to just play it with an unbiased view of the game as I have with other Assassins Creed games.Here's what I love about this game - The Long History of the game: Although they were straying far (hack and slash, assassinations, and the likes) from the original feels from the older versions like AC Unity or Black flag (that includes the dual axe wielding, long list of abilities you get to pick, etc...). This game puts you through a very long and a very exciting history lessons about various mythologies, Vikings, Iceland, Finland and Others. Because of this, I would recommend anyone who hates to sit through boring history lessons in class and play this instead, albeit it has been modified to fit the games objective so you need to research on the actual history to be more accurate, but my point still stands that it is a great game to learn about the history of other countries and mythologies through this game alone.The Graphics: My PC is well above the need to run this game at maximum graphics, but of course i wanted to save some VRAMs so that it runs smoothly, which made me put everything to High and Medium instead. Even so, the graphics on this game was amazing and immersive enough for me to not realize that I played for 3 hours (sometimes 5 if i really get myself into the character) without having the need to get off my computer and rest.The MAIN STORYLINE: This does not include the other packages that comes with the complete edition and just the Valhalla version itself. It took me 60+ hours just to complete the main storyline and another 80+ hours to complete the other storyline. This MAY seem long (or short if you are a speed runner) but it's such an immersive game that I took my time to enjoy everything this had to offer. If I had bought this game without the complete version at the original price, this would have been worth my time and money.Variety of Skills and abilities: This game provided with so much skills (either from skill trees, runic skills, Item abilities, Hugr-wrist, Abilities) that will suit the players game play experience. Although this again, strays off the original concept of the older games, I will probably find it boring if they kept using the original concept with no innovation put to it. Here's what I don't like about the game - The mechanics of the game: Back then the game mechanics were way more simpler and easier to understand (I play on keyboard and mouse), so learning the new mechanics of this game was complicated as there was alot of keybinds to remember, which sometimes cause me to press the wrong keybind and losing boss fights (especially with Sutr on Very Hard).The Falling Death bug: There are times where I get stuck in a falling animation during battles which just kills me instantly to make me get unstuck, which is frustrating since I was already almost done with the quest. This definitely needs to be fixed but other then that, the game is good and does not affect my overall experience or opinions of the game.TLDR: If you love immersive, historic and amazing graphics at medium settings, buy the original version, i recommend it. If you do not like to pay for full price, wait for another huge discount like i did and buy the complete edition for $40++.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the game at 80% discount and even then I don't find a good deal.The game opens very well and got me expecting a AC Odyssey (a game I liked a lot) with a viking theme, but it's a steep downhill from there.The movement isn't very fluid, the combat is stiff and we have a lot of "health bar" enemies, robbing the feeling of being a badass viking and prolonging almost every fight you start alone while still having "boss" fights.The story also starts well, but also declines fast because it just goes nowhere after the first part, a lot of escort missions, progress is unclear, we have modern times BS missions in the middle of the game, a lot of silly side missions and almost no impact of how you do a mission (I did a assassination without being detected and after the mission someone told me how great we both are at killing soldiers), and almost no characters are charismatic or interesting, not to mention noone having any hint of subtlety, if someone is hiding something they are always shifty right in your face, which breaks any interest in what may happen.The graphics are okay, same of Odyssey, but the charatcers are way worse, almost everyone looks like a generic NPC, and there's a lot of clipping in clothes, hair and beard.Exploration is tedious and the now more spaced fast travel points make it even worse.I don't even know if I will want to finish the game, it's not bad but it's boring and in a game this size this is a big negative trait.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed has had an identity crisis for a long time, and it's probably the most prominent in this game. I don't even know why Stealth was shoehorned into this title.The stealth mechanics are terrible in every way imaginable. It's incredibly easy to get spotted when cloaked or doing an assassination which should be obscured. When you do get spotted (and it is a when not an if), you'll be incentivized to just carve your way out rather than trying to find a place to hide because unless you run really, really far away, it's just easier to openly kill people with your axe than it is restarting a long sneaking mission from square one--having to patiently wait for guard patrols and the like.The stealth, in short, is not fun. Even with the return of blending into your environment, the feature comes across is a cheap way to appease players clamoring for a return to the franchise's roots. But the truth is, Assassin's Creed is so far removed from being a stealthy assassination game, it may as well just advertise on its face that it wants to be a high-powered button smasher. I honestly can't tell what this game is supposed to be. Witcher? God of War? Sniper Elite? It's like playing as Kratos in Skellige with X-ray kill shots but as a cheap knockoff of everything.This franchise shouldn't really exist anymore. I think what Ubisoft mostly wants is lowest common denominator stuff jammed into faux historical settings. You don't need Assassins and Templars for that. Both factions are a shadow of what they used to be in earlier games. The world building just isn't there. For me, it feels like some quickly slapped-together mumbo-jumbo to justify calling it "Assassin's Creed."I know people are always clamoring for open world this and that, but sometimes having too much of an open world is a bad thing. Stories happen out of sequence, you wind up with a LOT of empty space, and fetch quests/gathering materials are jammed into every nook and cranny to give the illusion of content. Witcher 3 is a brilliant open world game, but it feels cozy. Main quests are clustered together so you don't have to go wild distances just to pad runtime. AC Valhalla would benefit a LOT from a more concentrated, linear progression focused on story and stealth.If Ubisoft wanted to make an exclusive viking pillaging & raiding game in a giant soulless map, it should have just done that rather than shoehorn their hack & slash into  a franchise that's about stealth, hiding in the shadows, and striking only singular targets with precision.

_childDocuments_.review: far from smooth, with Eivor randomly jumping onto objects and canceling actions. Sailing is also unpleasant and unresponsive. Forgotten Saga, the free roguelite mode, where you're forced to use basic equipment, shows that the foundation isn’t bad, but in the main game, combat quickly becomes too easy or boring due to spongy enemies on higher difficulties. Slow-mo dodging stops being fun when it becomes a core fighting technique. Finishers are the worst design decision ever - exhausting, too long, repetitive, and disruptive to the pace., partly because of the setting. That Viking "honor-bound-warrior-odin-take-the-shield" theme gets bland quickly., leaning toward bombastic, fantasy aesthetics instead of historically accurate ideas... and while there are plenty to choose from, it’s not an overwhelming "scrap-fest". Each weapon is distinct enough to feel interesting. Great design decision. Say what you will, but Ubisoft remains unrivaled in historical sandbox open-worlds (Red Dead Redemption and Kingdom Come are both awesome but lack that “tourist” and historical reconstruction vibe.)Unlike many common opinions, for me, this is the first game in the franchise where the "assassin" theme loses relevance due to the Viking focus, and the Viking theme loses cohesion by trying to fit into the Assassin’s Creed universe. However, exploring the map, synchronizing viewpoints, and completing puzzles are as satisfying as ever if you enjoy that formula, and the stories are pleasant to follow. As always in AC games, it’s the historical setting, immersive world, and inimitable atmosphere that keep you engaged.P.S. Origins > Odyssey > Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, not bad, but my biggest gripe is that, as a massive Odyssey fan who put in well over 1,000 hours total, some things could be better.- Tons more unique features, but at the same time, the game has less. For example, you can no longer deck out your ship, but you have a settlement that you can customize and build up over time.- This really needs to stop, but it's Ubi we're talking about. This is a $60 game, so why are you putting in $20 outfits in a single-player game, for Odin's sake?- As much as you hate us, Ubi, can we please get achievements?- Once again, you'll be forced to use the Ubi-launcher. Having to open two launchers to play really sucks.- Like Red Dead 2's opening, I found the intro to be really mundane and boring. But once I pushed through that barrier, I'm finding myself enjoying this one. However, I'm sad a lot was cut. I loved customizing my ship, and hopefully, it'll return in Shadows.- Ubi have done something right, though. The graphics really are gorgeous, and the ocean is no different. The water physics here on max settings is really something to behold.- Skills unfortunately have taken a major nerf, gone are the fire arrow abilities or venom daggers Cassandra was known for instead we got 1% stealth dmg or 1% defense, don't get me wrong they're still here but you have significantly less of them and they're well meh.  Overall, it's entirely up to your preference. If you like Vikings and RPGs, go for it. However, if you hate the direction that the series has taken, then skip it, as you can't force yourself to like something. Personally, I prefer these over the older games. Be prepared, though, as like Bethesda, some bugs remain. During a cut scene, I saw a wolf pulling a Michael Jackson and moon walking. Nothing game-breaking, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought at discount. No spoilers. 8/10TLDR: I have thoroughly enjoyed this game, and while there are elements of grind, there is enough variation to make the experience worthwhile. A good blend of RPG, Action and adventure, this game does for Norse Mythology what Odyssey did for the Greeks. The story telling and hero/protagonist arc is quite compelling, although a little forced in places. Overall a great sequel/addition to the Assassins Creed Library (having played them all).The good:The story telling, building of the character over levels, and the skill tree seem well balanced, with a gradual progression through each area of the game making it challenging enough to encounter areas you're unfamiliar with, while not feeling too 'gamey' even at the higher levels and equipment against the low level enemies... Although, taking Thor's hammer at late-end game to some opening area enemies just to watch them fly is awesome.The visual aspects of the scenery are quite awesome, while climbing some of the mountains can be tedious, the view is worth it (just like IRL). The inventory management of weapons and armour is brilliant, it's worthwhile to play and watch as your equipment visuals and stats improve through upgrades as you progress. Take time to appreciate your gear go from wooden sticks to god-like armoury over the course of the game.(Almost all) The extra DLCs are quite a good addition to the game, and most support the gameplay well, with a few exceptions.The Bad:There are sections of the game where you must traverse large areas of the map, and without close proximity to the 'recon towers', or where mountainous terrain prevents horses. There is a LOT of mountainous climbing and running, and less urban parkour than I would prefer/expect. And finding those last remote chests/collectables can be a real grind. Having roads or even slight paths that make most of the map and mountains accessible, would have been simple to improve this game a lot.The story has elements where belief, even from a 'supernatural AC universe' point, must be completely suspended in order to follow the fundamental plot lines. There are elements where the protagonist would normally progress the story immediately, but instead is shuffled into a line of sub plots which add nothing to the ability of the protagonist to complete their primary objective.There is also a lot of 'woke agenda' nonsense that doesn't add anything, and only takes away from any realism. E.g. There were no non-white races in England pre-1000AD, the average temperature was much higher during the medieval period (when this was set) than today, (even viking) women would have very rarely fought in battles, while the Greeks were up for some SSMs, the Danes and Saxons/Celts were definitely hetros., etc.The Hildiran Trials. (They almost all suck - avoid if possible).The Reda quests. (They are almost all just 'find and kill' quests for tokens/opals to gear that aren't very useful, except early game, where they are quite difficult).Not so much a bad, but a huge missed opportunity to follow an actual historical viking (like Guthrum) through their adventures and conquests, and eventual peace in England.

_childDocuments_.review: HDR is broken, there is NO way to configure it right, you can tweak some parameters in game and windows and then tweak a perfectly fine calibrated tv's parameters to get somewhat reasonable result, but would you want to do that for every game? Doesn't make sense.  Then the graphics itself - I guess everyone who made a decision to post this game in production has severe myopia - the game is blurred so much it strains my eyes. You can, again, install mods on top of the game and tweak some videocard settings to improve it somewhat, but the sharp game picture gets blurred by the engine, then you try to re-sharpen it from the blur, but a lot of details are missing at that point and you get sharp but messy picture in the end and lose some frames just to get some eye relief. Be mindful that there is motion blur and depth of field stacked on top of this.Then there's haze, I mean this also should've been designed and approved by multiple people during production. In conclusion - game looks terrible on good hardware even 3 years after the launch and is not fixable. Gameplay wise - it is too  big and ambitious, the overall length of a game is strictly tied to the grinding of resources and microtransactions. which is unacceptable in full price game. This makes game boring after first couple of raids since you have to complete way too many repetitive actions just to move through the basic part of the story line. Regarding story line - if you got a DLC - it is implemented hideously, there are a lot of quests and tracking them can be tricky, but somehow the DLC starts without any explanation right in the beginning of the game without any story background or build up - you are simply thrown to the boss fight without any clue of who the characters are and what is the story.In conclusion: 1) A lot of questionable design choices 2) If you as a game designer add a graphical effect - make it possible to switch it off, bloom, blur, motion blur, depth of field, TAA, chromatic aberration, haze - are graphical game DEFECTS, nothing more3) Grinding is never welcome, never was, never will be4) The size of the game is too big both storage wise and in the actual game itself.5) DLC implementation is really bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the latest three RPG-style AC games, I prefer this one over the other two. I was originally not going to play Valhalla just based on everything I had heard about the game like the big map, long main story, settlement management etc. Also noticed that some of the controls were changed from the previous two games, but after getting started, the game started feeling more fluid compared to Odyssey and Origins. In the other two with location objectives, I felt the need to complete every single location right away, but in Valhalla with massively cut down looting, the game felt much better when you could just play and focus on the story instead of deviating to get some loot in the middle of a quest.Combat in Valhalla is easily the best of the three RPGs. Odyssey's problem was endless mathematics to figure out the best combination of perks in your gear and constantly changing some bits of armor just to get a few more points of damage in, and still yet you would find yourself fighting one basic opponent for multiple minutes. Origins was the most straight forward, just go with the type of weapon you like and pick the one with most damage. Valhalla had some customisation regarding what style you want to play and combat felt smooth and fluid while making the player feel like a strong warrior.When it comes to the much whined about size of the map and story, I admit, it did feel a bit overwhelming at some points. I primarily play FPS games and played ACs as a sort of cool down game when I didn't feel like grinding competitive games, but even then I had to take a few weeks of hiatus from Valhalla to come back to the game for it to feel fresh and rewarding again.I got myself the season pass with the two story extensions in Wrath of the Druids and Siege of Paris, but opted to not play Dawn of Ragnarök.- Wrath of the druids was packed with more world activities to grind, which felt like slowing down the tempo of the story, but overall a nice pack of content for the game. Good story and cool map in Ireland.- Siege of Paris was REALLY GOOD and far better than Wrath of the Druids. The story was well written and nicely paced and never felt like I was doing anything unimportant. I really liked the numerous bossfights that litter the storyine every so often and every assassination event with the setup phase and information gathering was a nice touch. All this made Siege of Paris seem more real in a way. Overall a great, fluid DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 4.5/5Visuals and Design: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a visual feast. The game’s recreation of Dark Ages England is breathtaking, with stunning landscapes, detailed architecture, and atmospheric weather effects. The character models, especially Eivor and the main cast, are well-crafted, bringing the Viking era to life with authenticity and flair.Gameplay: Valhalla builds on the RPG elements introduced in Origins and Odyssey, offering a rich and immersive experience. The combat is brutal and satisfying, with a variety of weapons and abilities that allow for different playstyles. The game also reintroduces some stealth mechanics, though the focus remains on open combat. The settlement system adds a layer of depth, giving players a sense of progression and investment in their Viking clan.Story: The narrative follows Eivor, a fierce Viking warrior, as they lead their clan from Norway to England in search of a new home. The story is engaging, with well-developed characters and meaningful choices that impact the game’s world. The relationship between Eivor and their brother Sigurd is particularly compelling, adding emotional weight to the journey. The game’s historical setting is rich with intrigue, political drama, and epic battles.Technical Performance: While Valhalla is impressive in many ways, it does suffer from some technical issues. There are occasional bugs and glitches, which can be frustrating, but they don’t significantly detract from the overall experience. The game runs smoothly on next-gen consoles, offering a visually stunning and immersive experience.Secrets and Hidden Loot: Exploration in Valhalla is highly rewarding. The game is filled with secrets, hidden treasures, and side quests that add depth to the world. From ancient ruins to hidden caves, there’s always something new to discover. The game’s world is vast and detailed, encouraging players to explore every corner.Final Thoughts: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a standout entry in the series, offering a rich and immersive Viking experience. The game’s stunning visuals, engaging story, and satisfying combat make it a must-play for fans of the series and newcomers alike. Despite some technical issues, Valhalla’s strengths far outweigh its flaws, making it one of the best Assassin’s Creed games to date.

_childDocuments_.review: in the first 30 hours thie game and the story felt great to me, but after this two big problems with the game revealed itself: repeatability and a bad ending to the story.The combat is decent at first. The weapon system is good and the ability system are really fun to use. The enemies are way to easy to beat though. You can keep on dodging the enemy attacks which refills your stamina bar and can keep you attacking for a good while. I have easily beaten bosses 150 levels above me. The fighting style of special enemies (zealots and other bosses) all feel too similar and quickly bores you. There were 1 or 2 enemies which were noticeably different from the pack, but that's it. If you want a stealth focussed game, this will not be your cup of tea. The AC II stealth style is ot really present here. YOu can stand in athin bush and the enemies will not notice you. This was also the case for AC Origins and Odyssey, but these two had more redeeming factors compensating for it than Valhalla. This game is also really easy compared to Odyssey, which makes going for a stealth character useless as you can clear out fortresses by barging in through the front door way more quickly. Clearing out fortresses will also feel like more of a chore since the way you do it doesn't really change throughout the game.I also was confused in a very bad way as to what the ending even is of this game. As you progress the game Eivor (the player chracter) will build alliances for the settlement. At first this makes good sense, but Eivor ends up allying the entirety of England, This seems really unecessary to me from a story perspective and could have been handled differently. /spoiler Eliminating the order was decent fun, but the end is rightout dull and very unrewarding. There is also a question as to what the ending really is. Is it when Eivor leaves Norway and the rest of the story is an epilogue? Is it when all regions in England are pacified? Is it when the Grand Maegester of the order is defeated?TLDR: This game starts out fun, but quickly turns into repeatable gameplay and story. I was confused as to what even the ending was. The game is very unrewarding and honestly felt like a waste of good gameplay hours. I even wouldn't recommend buying it on sale since you have to put a lot of hours into this game which you can put in to way better gaming experiences. Please don't invest your money and lots of time into this mediocre experience

At the beginning of the game a little message flashes across the screen claiming that they support everybody's sexual preference. The parkour system is stickier than ever before and I'd only compare it as slightly better than AC Syndicate's system. Although I'd much rather play Syndicate than this mess. If you want a game that feels like this game, then buy Elden Ring. Everything this game fails and succeeds at, Elden Ring does better. There is a shocking lack of customizable content to this game, which when taking into account it has a literal in-game micro(macro)-transaction store that is unacceptable. The AI are even more brain dead than before, instead of having a special method to attack certain enemy types like in previous AC's, most AI just throw up a straight unattackable block that in order to fight against you have to throw a heavy at them which doesn't damage them it just stuns them out of their stance. _childDocuments_.review: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla delivers a good mix of arc-driven storytelling and chaotic, open-world goodness. One thing I’ve really appreciated is how the story isn’t just one huge tangled mess—each arc is its own little narrative, which helps keep the pace on track. It’s way easier to stay focused when the main storyline isn’t competing with every side quest you stumble into.That said, I haven’t finished the game yet, but… Eivor feels kind of stale. I’m running with femme Eivor, and while she’s solid, I hear the male version might have a bit more oomph. Overall, Eivor gives me serious Connor vibes from AC3—kind of a grumpy hothead. I usually like my protagonists with more optimism, and she doesn’t bring that spark for me.Combat, though? Oh gosh. It’s fun. If you liked Odyssey’s combat (and I know that’s a hot take), this builds on it in all the right ways. The abilities add a lot to the flow—you can really get creative with how you fight, especially when facing big mobs. It’s the kind of action where you can experiment and feel rewarded for it.The skill tree is another win in my book. It’s node-based and gives you a little bit of everything—attribute boosts, new abilities every so often. It reminds me of Final Fantasy X’s Sphere Grid, which gave me those warm, nostalgic vibes. While it’s not as complex as something like Path of Exile, it’s straightforward in the best way.Now, the world design? It’s kind of hit or miss. England’s split into regions, and each one has its own thing going on—rock stacking, glitch puzzles, some artifact hunting. It’s fun, but it can get repetitive. There are also these cheeky mini-stories, like the guy in Worcestershire trying to perfect his special sauce with eels. You can’t help but chuckle at the lore behind Worcestershire sauce.But let me tell you, this world is HUGE. Beyond England, there’s Valhalla, Jotunheim, and more. It’s great value if you love lots of places to explore, but if you’re a completionist like me, it’s a little exhausting. The Valhalla side stuff, in particular, feels disconnected from the main story and drags on more than I’d like.If you like The Witcher 3 or other open-world games that are story-heavy and big on point-of-interest exploration, you’ll probably dig this. Just be ready for the long haul—there's a lot to do here.Overall, I’d give Valhalla a respectable 3 out of 5 stars. That might sound low, but 3 stars is still a solid 70%—and that feels right. My disconnect with Eivor as a character holds it back a bit for me. It’s a fun game, but the protagonist makes it tough to fully click with.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully constructed world with hundreds of (somewhat repetitive) hours of game play that I simply cannot recommend. Of over 200 games in my library this one has more bugs than all of them combined and crashes every 3-4 hours. The game has glitchy animations, poor pathing, "parkour" that seems an after thought, sound mixing that is laughably bad, and AI that will walk endlessly into walls,  go up and down ladders ad infinum, or simply walk in circles. There is frequent clipping, to which Ubisoft felt the best solution was to kill your character and force a reload, which often results in hours lost as this happens most often during river raids that dont allow saves until completion. Dialogue is choppy with odd and long silences, and is difficult to initiate, as the title character has to be standing in "just" the right spot (sometimes inches away, sometimes 6 feet away). There is loads of DLC, but the $ cost is high, and the devs made such a low effort to address the many bugs in the game (the majority of which have been present since launch) that it is a little insulting. I will likely continue sloshing through the muck of this game, because at its core, the hack and slash / exploration model is fun and I love all things Norse, but is far from polished, and at times infuriating.Ryzen 7 5800x, 64 GB RAM, Radeon RX 6800, Nvme M.2 with 200GB freeTLD: A buggy crash ridden shiny turd of a cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: Tbh thsi is my fav AC game so far. Comparing it to the Odyssey they improved a lot of game mechanics and story mission. The game does not feel so overwhelming like the previous one did. The custom village idea is 10/10 imo. Many new mechanics, like eating, leveling up mount's stats or even beeing able to finally !OPEN DOOR!People say its a long game, that takes even more time to fully finish the prologue. I dont see it. It was rly smooth for me. The story is catching and easy to follow. I LOVE that they "hide" map marks now, allowing me to better relax, instead of chasing every single question mark on my way, which was draining in previous games. Now even short 5min activities i find on my way are an adventure.  The mini games are super fun - i always participate whenever i have a chance - dice game is my fav! They got rid of a ton and ton of usless iteams we were getting from every dead body in AC Origin and Odyssey... They even reworked the numbers. Instead of collecting 173649924 coins for another usless weapon upgrade, they made it simple - we need 10-40, but we collect 1, sometimes maybe 2 from loot. Feels more real. They also got rid of the mercenary system!! (biggest + tbh)I know many people hate on skins in new AC games, but i have always been fan of those. The cosmetics in Vallhala deff are the peak so far (there are collabs as well! <3) I dont buy them, but collecting exotic currency from around the world is enough to get you what you want. I feel like noone talks about it, but you can easly get every single cosmetic skin for free, if you are patient enough. Ive got almost all of them in previous game, its much more rewarding too!Fans of the "old" AC games might feel cheated on, since its not a game about...well... assassins. Its a great viking game, with a great "follow-along" story. The game has brotherhood background with i would say - around 10% quests following that topic. The rest is pure viking expirience. TLTR: Great viking game with better mechanics from previous Assassins, tho without much of the "Assassin" expirience.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla offers an enjoyable gaming experience with its captivating gameplay and impressive visuals. The game has a well-crafted story that keeps players engaged throughout. However, there are a few aspects that could be better, such as the side quests, and the inability to dismantle found weapons for materials to enhance your own weapon. Additionally, the process of launching the game through Ubisoft Connect can be quite time-consuming, which can be frustrating.Let's start with the positives. Assassin's Creed Valhalla is undeniably fun to play. The gameplay mechanics are solid, and the game provides a satisfying sense of exploration and combat. The stunning graphics add a level of immersion, making the world feel alive and vibrant. Whether you're traversing the beautiful landscapes or engaging in intense battles, the visual quality truly enhances the overall experience.The main story of Assassin's Creed Valhalla is engaging and well-paced. It delves into the Viking era, allowing players to embody Eivor, a fierce warrior navigating the treacherous world of England. The narrative is filled with intriguing characters and plot twists, keeping you invested in Eivor's journey. The game strikes a fun balance between historical accuracy and fictional storytelling, creating a captivating blend of adventure and history, with fiction prevailing.However, the same cannot be said for the side quests. While the main storyline shines, some of the side quests can feel repetitive and lackluster. The objectives often lack depth and fail to provide meaningful rewards or significant impact on the overall narrative. This can dampen the overall enjoyment, especially for players who seek a more immersive and varied experience beyond the main story arc.One aspect that could greatly enhance gameplay is the ability to dismantle found weapons for materials. Unfortunately, Assassin's Creed Valhalla lacks this feature, which is a missed opportunity. Moreover, the process of launching the game through Ubisoft Connect can be tedious and time-consuming. It involves navigating through multiple platforms, starting from Steam and then proceeding to Ubisoft Connect before finally launching the game itself. This unnecessary sequence can be frustrating, particularly when you're eager to jump into the game quickly. A more streamlined and efficient launch process would greatly improve the overall user experience.Despite these shortcomings, Assassin's Creed Valhalla still offers a worthwhile experience. The game delivers on its promise of an engaging Viking adventure, with solid gameplay, impressive graphics, and a captivating main story.Final Score: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that takes some deliberate effort to be fun, but with some tweaks to the UI and difficulty it can hold its own against the other recent Assassin's Creed RPGs. First, it's worth mentioning that while the Uplay platform is still awful, its cross-platform cloud saves are an excellent feature. After putting 30 hours into my PS5 save, I was able to put another 10 hours in through Uplay+ before deciding to pick the game up on Steam and resuming my playthrough here. Just make sure you launch Uplay before launching the game through Steam for a seamless experience. As for the game itself, it's every bit as big and bloated as Odyssey, but it's also just as detailed and packed with things to see and do. If you enjoyed the Odyssey formula, or if you just enjoy the Viking age of history you'll probably enjoy this game too. In my opinion, the default gameplay settings for AC Valhalla are obnoxiously easy and make for Ubisoft's most generic and cluttered game yet. Fortunately, this can be mostly fixed through changing the following settings: Turn off the compass. Turn off 90% of the UI elements you can live without. Set the navigation mode to Pathfinder. Change the enemy damage taken and damage dealt modifiers to 200%. Set the level scaling to a difficulty you find comfortable. There are lots of other settings you can use to customize your experience, but by making these changes the game goes from baby's first video game to an immersive, viking age RPG that actually asks for some thought, strategy, and skill from the player.

_childDocuments_.review: The game-play is varied for an AC game, the aesthetics are great and the visuals are A+ as always, but graphics and pretty scenery have never been something AC games have failed at. The hero/heroine is more "swept" up in the events through trying to fulfill their own ends (loot and glory etc) rather than having a real stake in the long term mythos of the AC plot-line. While in Odyssey, the RPG choice element had a mostly meaningful impact, here it shows that such a system just does not fit into the very set and structured narrative of AC. Which is fine!  Not every game needs to be a choice-based rpg. All in all, If anything, this game serves as just as introduction to plot concepts the series will utilize in later installments.Despite the story pitfalls, I did still find the game enjoyable. I was one of the poor saps however who got saddled with the early game glitches that caused a major plot point to be unexplorable. Seems like they have fixed it now.

_childDocuments_.review: In the land of Valhalla, amidst the clash of steel and the roaring waves, there walks a warrior whose name resounds through the ages - Eivor Wolf-Kissed, a true Vikingr and Drangr of unmatched valor and cunning. From the fjords of Norway to the fields of England, Eivor's saga is one that shall be sung by skalds for generations to come.Eivor, with a heart as fierce as the tempest and a spirit as untamed as the wilderness, stands as a paragon of Viking strength and resilience. With axe and shield in hand, this warrior strikes fear into the hearts. It is said that Odin himself smiles upon Eivor's battles, for they fight with a ferocity born of the gods.But it is not just Eivor's prowess in combat that makes him a legend. His unwavering loyalty to his clan and allies is a testament to his character. Whether leading his fellow Vikingrs in raids or forging alliances with the Saxons, Eivor's leadership is a beacon of honor and integrity in a world of treachery and chaos.Among the many colorful characters of Eivor's saga, one cannot help but be captivated by the enigmatic Seeress Valka, whose mystical visions guide our hero on a path fraught with destiny. The irascible but endearing Bjorn the Berserker, a true berserker of the old ways, stands as a loyal and indomitable companion. And who could forget the jovial and ever-loyal Randvi, whose wisdom and counsel anchor Eivor in times of turmoil.Yet, it is Eivor's bond with his brother Sigurd, a man of vision and ambition, that defines his journey. Theirs is a complex and compelling relationship, filled with trials and triumphs, and it is this fraternal connection that adds depth to the epic saga of Eivor.In the world of Assassin's Creed Valhalla, Eivor stands as a living legend, a Vikingr of unmatched valor, surrounded by a cast of unforgettable characters. His tale is one of adventure, honor, and the unyielding spirit of a warrior who leaves an indelible mark upon the annals of history. Skål to Eivor and his legendary saga!

_childDocuments_.review: With 145 hours in...Valhalla isn't as good as Origins or Odyssey, but it's still pretty good. What I like. Big world. Nice weapons and armor selections. Continued emphasis on submerging the player in an historical timeline. Nilfheim.What I don't like. Historical timeline isn't as deep as previous versions. Going to Vinland should have been way more immersed in a story (as an example). Character gets overpowered too fast. In the timeline, I'm in 160 recommended territory and I'm already 250. I'm very disappointed how Ubisoft handled Eivor's interaction with Cassandra and the two relics I've seen so far. Those relics are the whole point of the game franchise, and as a player, I didn't even get a choice to interact with them, and the limited interaction that was scripted has no effect on storyline or character. Unbelievable. Enemy AI. The big boss knights that constantly chase you down (a fixture in Origins and Odyssey) aren't even a sure thing. You can get out of it. AND, one rode by while I was invading a fort, and he didn't even stop. Also, you don't need to hide kills anymore, None of these poor guards have friends. No one seems to care why they have an arrow sticking out of their heads. Nothing to see here. Don't sound the alarm (which very few places actually have - as opposed to Origins and Odyssey). Finally, just like all other version, we are set out to collect a litany of things that are useless. A rectangular block? That's what a guard has on him? A mouth harp? Nails? Like I said, lazy.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERSS!!!So I have spent around 50 hours in this game and I have beaten the main story quest which consists of going around like 10 sections of the map and doing a quest there in order to have a friendly relationship and acquire an alliance with them. These quests are incredibly repetitive and lack depth, they could've just reduced it to 6 and made them longer and more immersive. The ending and epilogue was incredibly lackluster, disappointing, and anti-climatic. I was hoping for a huge battlefield in the grasslands or something but for the ending you just explore the ruins and kill a boss and the epilogue you just fight in a village. There are also two other story lines which are Asgard and the Order of Ancients (Templars). I have not completed either of these but I did read that they contribute to the overall story but the main story was just so long and tedious, I just wanted to finish it instead of side-tracking. The enemy types only consists of footmen, rangers, heavy/brutes, and skirmishers. For each of them, you just use a combination of light, heavy, and ranged attacks and they fall easily. They are incredibly easy to beat even on the highest difficulty settings. They have this skill tree that increases your power level and looks like something from Path of Exile but lacks depth. You can't truly specialize in anything because if you were to specialize into melee skill nodes, you would still get ranged and stealth nodes along the way. The regions are separated by Power Level but you could still easily beat enemies in an area when your Power Level is 100 less than theirs. Due to this lack in difficulty, it doesn't make a huge difference what gear you have so I just started skipping all of the loot because it was just a waste of time. There is just so much freaking loot and they're always locked behind a door that you need to find a key for or stored above/below you where you need to find an entrance for the place. They have these quests called Mysteries which are just pseudo-side quests that take less than 5 minutes to complete. There are so many of them and they lack any depth or immersion but they do give a lot of EXP. There is only one quest that I remember that contributed to world building where a dude who describes food really well chases a kid chef who stole his pie and later on you get to see them open a pie shop in the town.I have gotten the DLC equipment sets (did not buy them) and for the most part they're cool since they also give you a different mount/raven/ship/etc. This leads to their equipment inventory which is just horrendous. You can sort your primary weapon by what type they are but you can't do the same for your off-hand which doesn't make sense. This problem is amplified by the fact that every piece of gear that you pick up is a unique piece and you are unable to sell/dismantle/get rid of them so it just takes up place even when its an equipment you got 49 hours ago. You can't group them into sets either so if you have a 5 piece set, you have to manually look through all your gear and put all 5 pieces on.Despite having a high-end PC running on max settings and getting 70-80 fps consistently, I would still crash from time to time. There is also a boss fight in Asgard where you fight a wolf that burrows underneath and apparently if you have over 60 fps, the wolf never unburrows so you can never hit him so you're stuck in the fight unless you kill yourself or quit. If you enjoyed Odyssey and Origins with the RPG style and with a Vikings theme then this game might be for you. Otherwise if you were hoping that Valhalla would return to AC's roots, this is absolutely not for you. They dove even deeper into the RPG elements and gave you a huge map with collectibles and lootables every 10 seconds.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla, one of the latest additions to the venerable Assassin's Creed franchise, is a regrettable departure from the series' established identity. This installment, ostensibly set against the backdrop of the Viking Age, exhibits a profound divergence from the core tenets that once defined the essence of the Assassin's Creed experience.One cannot help but be disheartened by the abandonment of the franchise's intrinsic focus on stealth and subtlety. Valhalla, in its misguided attempt to infuse Viking aesthetics, forsakes the delicate dance of shadows and precision that were once the hallmarks of Assassin's Creed titles. The subtlety of the assassins has been supplanted by a brazen, brute-force approach that undermines the very foundation upon which this franchise was built.The narrative, which was once a tapestry interwoven with historical intrigue and the enigmatic struggle between the Assassins and Templars, has been reduced to a mere backdrop. The epic tales of conspiracy and secrecy that characterized earlier entries have been diluted, giving way to a generic Viking saga that fails to capture the nuance and depth of its predecessors.Furthermore, the open-world structure, while expansive in scope, lacks the refined design seen in earlier titles. The immersion of traversing historical cities has been replaced by the vast, often monotonous landscapes of medieval England, diminishing the sense of awe and discovery that was integral to the Assassin's Creed experience.The combat mechanics, while competent, deviate significantly from the elegant, skill-based engagements that typified earlier entries. Valhalla's combat embraces a more hack-and-slash approach, forsaking the finesse and strategic depth that once defined the franchise's distinctive feel.In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Valhalla stands as a testament to the perils of deviating too far from a franchise's established identity. The abandonment of key elements, such as stealth, narrative intricacy, and refined combat, results in a game that, despite its technical prowess, fails to resonate with the essence that endeared the Assassin's Creed series to its fanbase. Regrettably, Valhalla represents a departure that compromises the very soul of this storied franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Yup. I guess I should have checked this beforehand, but I expected a big title to have achievements. I know, strange right? We're off to a great start. Oh, no NewGame+ either, but there's a gamemode to compensate for that a bit.England isn't that interesting. There's more locations of course and there's something to be said about how big the total playable area is, especially if you include the forgotten saga, the DLCs and river raids. That's probably the biggest selling point of this game, so lets get that out of the way first. It's an EPIC sized game and the mythical locations are fun enough. However, the big maps feel empty. Very empty. There's clusters of collectibles and objectives but there's oh so much  terrain. Low to no NPC activity, too many repeated assets, horrible navigational quality, etc. And then you have too many fantastical elements in the real world equivalent locations and the 'map clearing simulator' part of the game going wild to compensate for all the aforementioned holes. Odyssey and Origins did it way better.About movement and combat. Parry, block, light & heavy attack buttons are counter-intuitive. Remapping on controller is a pain. Movement itself  a lot slower than Odyssey and Origins did. Not sure if it's because of the way the terrain and the assets were modeled in a haste (without much testing) or because of a new movement system, but it sucks. I've never had an AC game make me fall when I didn't want to and not fall when I did want to . For a game that lets you crawl through small or triangular windows this much, they could have at least made the climbing behavior match that. Frustrating beyond belief. Neither movement nor combat is fun. And this sort of ties into movement and combat abilities a bit, so...Instead of carefully catered abilities that help you move and fight better, like Odyssey and Origins did so well and all the AC games before that, the stinking pile of a mess I wouldn't even call a skilltree anymore pretends to let you choose a path of skills that doesn't even matter because you can just remap everything at all times. Skills are locked behind incredibly repetitive stat upgrades that don't even make sense anymore (like crit chance upgrades that are superfluous because all your weapons have +150% crit chance already) and give you an illusion of choice that ultimately doesn't matter. Origins abilities just  right. Buildcrafting was near perfect in Odyssey. This game has nothing going for it in this department. Everything is worse. The only abilities worth getting are the ones that make up for features that should have been part of default combat in the first place. Don't even get me started on stamina.The UI is a serious downgrade from Odyssey and Origins. The changes made to the loot system forced a new UI design that didn't get playtested enough. Upgrading items is a pain. I scrolled more in this game than on facebook, youtube and instagram combined. Poor mousewheel. I don't have much to say about the overall design and functionality of the UI, but it's just not that great.I think it says enough that I initially wanted to play this game for the story but got caught up in clearing the map so much that I ended up not caring about any storyline whatsoever (except the parts taking place in the mythical locations). Ironically, the game calls you out for it, but it's the game's own fault. Both the mechanics (map clearing and such) and the character motivations (conflict between ambition and family) lend themselves to you playing in such a way. The ambition/family conflict is sort of the best part of this game, but then again it doesn't matter because you know who.- Real places are boring, surreal places are less boring but not enough content overall. Big and empty.- Everything except the size is worse than Odyssey and Origins, combat, movement, UI, abilities, story, etc.- Oh I forgot, it's the most GRINDY AC game yet.

Creed: Valhalla .. despite the beautiful world creation, the great character story and general historical attention to detail .. fails to hit the amazing high standard of Assassin's Creed: Odyssey in _childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla" is a remarkable addition to the Assassin's Creed series, offering a deep dive into the Viking era. The game stands out with its stunning open-world design, capturing the rugged beauty of medieval England and Norway. The landscapes are breathtaking, with meticulous attention to historical details, making exploration a delight for players.The game's narrative is compelling, weaving a rich tapestry of Viking culture and mythology with the familiar Assassin's Creed lore. Eivor's journey, customizable as either male or female, is filled with gripping storylines and complex characters that bring the world to life. The voice acting and character animations add depth to the immersive experience.Combat in "Valhalla" is brutal and satisfying, reflecting the ferocity of Viking warfare. The game introduces new mechanics, such as raiding and settlement building, which add layers to the gameplay and provide a sense of progression. The skill tree and gear customization are extensive, allowing players to tailor their playstyle.However, the game is not without its flaws. Some players might find the pacing slow at times, and the sheer size of the game can be overwhelming. There have also been reports of bugs and performance issues, though patches have addressed many of these concerns.In conclusion, "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" is a must-play for fans of the series and newcomers alike. It offers an expansive, beautifully crafted world filled with adventure, intrigue, and the raw appeal of Viking legend. Despite some minor drawbacks, the game is a testament to Ubisoft's ability to keep the series fresh and engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a proper RPG game with a gameplay loop that was greatly improved from its RPG predecessors (Origins & Odyssey). There is a great Assassin's Creed story to be found here, perhaps one of the best ones in the franchise, written by Darby McDevitt who has expanded and fixed many inconsistent lore of the entire franchise. Plus beautifully composed music by AC Origin's Sarah Schachner, the man Jesper Kyd himself, collaborating with Wardruna's vocalist Einar Selvik who have breathed much of Norse's soul into this game.All this praising seems contradictory with some opinions coming from the AC's fanbase. This is because Valhalla is the most polarized game in the franchise, but I would like to add that AC's fanbase is similar to Star Wars: there are those who seek to replicate the unending nostalgia of the past, and those who seek things that are familiar but also new. Valhalla does not contain a white hood and a protagonist with similar personality to Ezio Auditore, but what it has is a story told similar to a Norse saga with many arcs focused on different subjects. Though in the end, all these arcs would come down to one focus: the ISU lore and the modern day story - a subject that is not favored by some of the fan, but one can easily argue that these are the staples of the franchise and it wouldn't be an Assassin's Creed game without the modern story and the ancient astronauts element.Similar to AC Black Flag - also the black sheep of the franchise that was frowned upon its release due to not being "Assassin's Creed enough." I believe that given time, most will also come to appreciate Valhalla, for there is a mature story and a philosophical experience to be found here.Valhalla's biggest problem would be its pacing which is familiar to Blade Runner: it is a slow burn. This game is not for those who don't have time. The base game can easily take up 100 hours, and another 100 if you play the expansions. And there is no skipping the side arcs, you have to do and read much in this game to digests its narrative.For the expansions, I would say Siege of Paris and Dawn of Ragnarok are both worth the time and investment, whereas Wrath of the Druids is a waste of time and potential due to its inconsistent narrative with everything else.

The game tells about the Vikings and their campaigns in England, Denmark, France. Unlike previous parts, Assassin's Creed Valhalla offers a large open world filled with quests, opportunities for exploration and freedom of movement. It reminds me of games like Black Flag and Odyssey where the players can go their own way and influence the story as they please. The combat system of Valhalla has also been changed. The game now has a more realistic combat feel due to the fact that it has become more dynamic and interesting. This is different from the play style of other episodes, where the main combat mechanics were dodge, parry and stealth kill. But Assassin's Creed Valhalla does not ignore its beginning. Like the other titles in the series, it has a compelling storyline rife with mystery and intrigue, and gives you the opportunity to fully immerse yourself in the historical setting. Overall, Assassin's Creed Valhalla offers an epic adventure in the world of the Vikings, combining the best elements of the Assassin's Creed franchise with new innovations and providing both Assassin's Creed series enthusiasts and newcomers alike have an amazing gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Build your own Viking Legend. Become Eivor, a Viking raider raised to be a fearless warrior, and lead your clan from icy desolation in Norway to a new home amid the lush farmlands of ninth-century England. Find your settlement and conquer this hostile land by any means to earn a place in Valhalla. England in the age of the Vikings is a fractured nation of petty lords and warring kingdoms. Beneath the chaos lies a rich and untamed land waiting for a new conqueror. Will it be you? Write Your Viking Saga. Blaze your own path across England with advanced RPG mechanics. Fight brutal battles, lead fiery raids or use strategy and alliances with other leaders to bring victory. Every choice you make in combat and conversation is another step on the path to greatness. Lead Epic Raids. Lead a crew of raiders and launch lightning-fast surprise attacks against Saxon armies and fortresses. Claim the riches of your enemies' lands for your clan and expand your influence far beyond your growing settlement. ENGAGE IN VISCERAL COMBAT. Unleash the ruthless fighting style of a Viking warrior as you dual-wield axes, swords, or even shields against relentless foes. Decapitate opponents in close-quarters combat, riddle them with arrows, or assassinate them with your Hidden Blade. Grow Your Settlement. Your clan's new home grows with your legend. Customise your settlement by building upgradable structures. Unlock new features and quests by constructing a barracks, a blacksmith, a tattoo parlour, and much more. Share Your Custom Raider. Recruit mercenary Vikings designed by other players or create and customise your own to share online. Sit back and reap the rewards when they fight alongside your friends in their game worlds. A Dark Age Open World. Sail across the icy North Sea to discover and conquer the broken kingdoms of England. Immerse yourself in activities like hunting and drinking games or engage in traditional Norse competitions like flyting – or, as it's better known, verbally devastating rivals through the art of the Viking rap battle. name: Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes - Definitive Edition
detailed_description: Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes is a unique mix of puzzle, strategy and RPG: Plan your every move and combine your attacks to defeat your enemies in matching puzzle inspired battle scenarios, upgrade your heroes and creatures to unleash increasingly devastating attacks onto your opponents, and let the strategic thinker in you lead your troops to victory. Originally developed by Capybara Games, Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes is getting a Definitive Edition including its DLC, refreshed character portraits, many quality-of-life improvements and an expanded, fully reworked and re-balanced online mode! Taking place 40 years before the Heroes of Might & Magic V saga, Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes tells the tale of five heroes scattered across five different regions of Ashan. Each must travel their own dangerous paths to grow in strength, unravel a demonic plot, and ultimately save their world from devastation. ● A unique mix of genres : Be creative, always be one step ahead of your opponent. The more combos you make, the more damage your enemy will take! ● Be the leader of your army… : Choose the perfect combination of units for your troops, artifact and spell for your hero and lead them to victory! ● … and get stronger : Gain XP after every battle and level up your hero and their attributes! ● Single player mode : Put your tactical skills to the test in the 20+ hour-long story mode. It will not be an easy journey but you’ll have to succeed and save the world from devastation. ● Multiplayer mode : A very addictive and extensive multiplayer mode. 1v1, 2v2, against bots or other players, online or offline, it doesn’t matter, your goal remains the same: lead your army to the top of the ladder! ● Included in this definitive version, the I Am the Boss DLC: Switch to the side of Chaos and play as one of the 4 villains of the game in any mode other than the campaign! A newly-created exclusive Multiplayer boss (Euny the Archdruid) is included in this DLC! The unique puzzle/strategy battle gameplay of Clash of Heroes will put your tactical skills to the test in the 20+ hour-long story mode and against players in offline and online PvP. Adopt the perfect strategy , let the leader in you guide your troops to victory! Be creative , find the perfect combination of units, artifacts and spells. Piece together crazy combos and break the enemy lines. Every additional combo can be decisive! Gain XP after each battle, level up your hero and units in order to get an unbeatable team. Find artifacts and hire mercenaries, it will help you on your quest to save the world from devastation. An addictive and intense PvP mode! Whether 1v1 or 2v2, online or offline, against bots or real players , the slightest misstep could be fatal! Climb the ladder and try to be on top of the world! Select the character you’ve mastered among the 15 heroes of 5 different factions. In a 1v1 matchup, choose the combination of artifacts, spells and units carefully and enhance the power of your troops! In 2v2 , work on and build up the synergy between you and your teammate to be the best duo! Combine and make a maximum of devastating combos to beat your enemies and take as many W’s as you can!

_childDocuments_.review: the original is one of my absolute favourite PvP puzzlers and i dreamt about a sequel or expanded version with more units or factions for over a decade....but sadly this is just a quick cashgrab: somehow worse art, promised rebalancing nowhere to be found, original taken off the store.edit:to be fair there are very minor stat changes on few(3) units and the two most OP artifacts have been nerfed/disabled repectively ....so some rebalancing has actually been found now; the strongest spells&units have not been touched though. also the core gameplay beneath it all still is fantastic, still a strong recommend if you don't own one of the previous releases!
