_childDocuments_.review: Europa is an enjoyable, emotional journey along the likes of games like Jusant and GRIS. The artwork of each level is beautiful and the pacing and length is just right. There was no point where I felt frustrated or unable to go on, and I'm happy to see that there is now a newly added zen mode should I want to re-experience the story and try to get all of the collectibles without any "threats" in the game. Thank you for this experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a few hours of a beautiful, relaxing, ghibli-inspired (not to limit it here) experience, PLEASE play Europa. You can feel the passion that went into every single area and it's a great break from the AAA multiplayer slop.Congrats to the team and creator on a fantastic little gamed that put a big smile on my face.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: A Solid 7/10. Pros: feels like a playable ghibli story, a la Castle In The Sky- amazing, graphics, music, and a story that will make anyone search their soul just a little.Cons: the gameplay, while good,  feels lacking in some areas, especially those focused on puzzles- to put it simply, the game feels too linear in some open world segments, and too vast in the puzzle areas, forcing the devs to limit your movement abilities in order to create arbitrarily hard or long puzzles for the player.Overall, a game worth an afternoon of your time, with a story worth telling. if you can overlook the issues above, than you will find this game extremely enjoyable. I know I did
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on Europa since the day it was revealed and I'm pleased to say that the game met my expectations.It's clear to see that they were going for a relaxing, cozy type of experience. The main character of this game is just as much the world as it is Zee. As you explore and find journal entries left by his father you see the budding of a utopia, and then the seeds of its demise. I found myself as eager to find the next journal entry as I was to explore the world.Speaking of exploration, there is some, here, but it is not as vast and open as the landscape my lead you to believe, but I would hope no one was expecting such. This is an india game by a small studio and in my opinion, they delivered on the experience they set out to provide. The lands are lush and vibrant, animals run and scamper about as well as the remnants of the previous age that humans contributed to destroying. The game leaves you with a moral question of what decision you might make, given all that transpired. I thought this was well done.Action: This is a cozy game about learning of the past and discovering the world around you. It is a tight experience with a small amount of exploration that I found to be fun and a worthy addition to my library. Will definitely revisit this again one day. There is no combat, but there are threats posed by the roving machines or stationary sentry guns. Taking damage merely leaves you dazed and seeing stars, so there is no death or real threat. This isn't meant to be that type of experience, and you can even turn the danger off if you just want to kick back and enjoy exploring without having to take cover at times and avoid the dangerous machines.On the technical side, the jumping mechanics are a tad floaty and feel imprecise, but it is a minor thing that you get used to. The hovering and gliding are fun and make traversal easier and quicker at times. I encountered one minor glitch toward the end of the game when I came out of a wind tunnel to an elevated structure and Zee wouldn't move forward. After a moment or two it worked itself out and I continued on. I give a happy thumbs up for Europa. It was a quick 3.5-4 hour experience that I hope you'll enjoy as much as I did.Thank you for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Like Studio Ghibli movies?Like to be emotionally invested in things?Like a narrative style that will take you on a journey?Get. This. Game.It's stunning. Not just visually but in every sense of the word. From the moving music to the rolling landscapes, there is nothing I disliked about this experience. I got SO invested in the story, I actually sobbed my little eyes out at the ending even though I kind of knew how it'd end. At every 'level' I was wowed. I audibly gasped at a lot of the scenery, and even just stood there to soak it all in. While it is a 'short' game (completion time around 5 hours ish) it's worth every single penny, every single second. LOVED it.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Europa! The movement was satisfying and fun, and the environments that you glide around in are absolutely gorgeous. I loved seeing the game's different influences peek through in different sections, all while maintaining its own distinct identity. Without spoilers, the story handles its subject matter well and with the appropriate weight, much of which is very close to my heart and it ultimately left me with a lot to think about. I typically prefer to play games with a controller (and that is an option here) but I decided to use mouse+keyboard and found it intuitive and easy to pick up! The main downside for some might be the game's length, as it is on the shorter side, but personally I enjoyed this about it. I really love when I'm able to play through the entire experience in one afternoon, and then come back to it later for any missed collectables or just to revisit some favorite moments (or the whole thing!) I am very glad that I got to spend time with this game, and I am happy to see it released! Genuinely beautiful, in both content and visuals!
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: What a stunning game. I have been left speechless, in tears really. I was moved all the way until the very end. This game is a masterpiece. The music scores are emotion provoking. The puzzles reminiscent of gentle Zelda games. The graphics are as if you are watching a beautifully lush movie. The narration is by far one of my favorites in games. You are captivated by a moving, tragic, but hopeful story. If you are looking for a narrative, adventure atmospheric experience, please play this game!My review of the game:
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eyeing this game for a while and just got it today. I love the world and the general design of the game. It's a very short game though with some simple mechanics. I really enjoyed playing it and completed the whole game in 4,5 hours. I'm not a gamer or anything, but just played through for fun. I gave me a vibe of "castle in the sky" from Studio Ghibli which I really enjoyed and the bioms were super cute and I loved the detail and animation style. I think I would give it 6 out of 10 stars due to the simpel mechanics and quick game through. The ending I'm a bit unsure too and I would have liked a bit more story at the end. I don't think I would play it again since it  got a little boring doing the same over and over again just a little bit more difficult each time, but I would definately recommend this for a rainy day.Super cute game that you can complete in an afternoon <3
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty chill game if you want to get off your head after a long stressful day. It's colorful and vibrant. Music is beautiful. Story is simple but good. Gameplay is also simple and encourage you to explore around the different maps.I think what i was looking forward the most in the game is the narrated journals, if it wasn't for them i would probably got bored of the game within the first hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Comfy walking simulator/platformer with a cute artsyleTook me a while to understand the developers vision (expected more of a platformer but got something more akin to Journey) but it clicked around 30mins~ 1hr inStory was good if not abit generic, only issue is there's no indicator on chapter select for which levels you've missed emeralds/chests or zephyr upgrades so the 100% will be a bit tedious but it'll be worth.7/10 would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: The game does not start all the time. It start with the black screen and error in graphics. I bought the game twice and all two times had to turn it back. What is interesting is the fact that demo version I could start and play from Steam but the original game did not even start. I think that the developers manually limited the game with range of DirectX dll-s to work on and with.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game with a well told story where you learn more of it as you progress further.The way you can move is nicely done with sliding around on water or gliding in the sky.The art style is very nice and the music fits very well.It is not a very long game if you just want to have a game to play through during the day.Can for sure recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: This beautiful adventure games had my heart from the start. The graphics, the storyline, the gameplay... It was such a wonderful time and I'm happy I got to experience it. The puzzles are very approachable while still remaining a challenge. My advice would be to look EVERYWHERE before going to a new space, I missed half of the emeralds which means I'll have to play again to 100% it haha. Enjoy!!
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Cute! Relatively short, perfectly pleasant, it gets in its own way a few times like needing to stop fully to read journal entries or sketch creatures, interrupting the pretty good flow of drifting along through environments, but it's a good way to pass a few hours for folks who like meditative journeys like, uh, Journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Literally one of the prettiest games I've played. The vibes were immaculate and it really feels like you're in a Studio Ghibli movie. The story was beautiful and the art was legitimately stunning. Every time I crested a hill, I stopped and was genuinely amazed at the view. I kept finding myself saying how gorgeous it was. Would very much recommend getting the game if you can. The puzzles were challenging but not frustrating and the travel in the game felt good as a player. It was also nice, in my opinion, to have a game that doesn't feel the need to go on forever. It's play time felt very good for what the game is.And the music was actually stunning. There were times where I stopped playing just to listen to the music.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Ill start by saying, a game has never given me goosebumps before. The story was great. I loved the photo mode, some games make it way too complicated or just very lack luster but this was very easy to control. I can't tell you how many pictures I took. XDI don't think I can think of any cons to this at all. I was bummed when it wasn't released in April when it was originally supposed to be, but I can't even hold a grudge because they took the time the needed to make an EXCELLENT game. Artstyle = amazing.Music = AmazingVoice actor = I want to play any game that you speak in.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous contemplative game with a focus on beauty and quiet. The visuals are the strong suit, where Breath of the Wild meets Laputa Castle in the Sky. Relaxing, not very challenging gameplay (reminds me of Journey a whole lot) that asks of the player to take a seat and think about humankind and the mark we leave wherever we go. Very good little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Europa is a gorgeous studio Ghibli art-style adventure set well into the future after humans have colonized Jupiter's moon Europa. But a war between man and machine has changed the course of humanity's future. You play as Zee, a young child who might be humanity's last hope. I very much enjoyed the adventure, it took me about 3 hours to complete since I took time to poke around. I thank the team for the Steam review key! Here are my top takeaways:1. Relaxing vibe with no fall damage. And gliding from place to place feels so freeing!!!! Stamina can run out easily but there are lot of crystals to replenish yourself. 2. The story is told through journal writings. Zee has been left behind and his father is guiding him along the way through the writings. The journals are pretty easy to find, I didn’t have to go out of my way too much to find them so you’re sure to catch on to the story.3. The little creatures are really adorable and it's nice to have other leaving beings along there with Zee as he travels through this empty world. Although some get a bit aggressive near the end but if you show them a little love, they’ll show you some love right back.4. Puzzles are pretty simple, perhaps a bit too simple... I know cozy and chill is the vibe but it doesn’t really ramp up much in difficulty. This does, however, make it a good game for younger gamers and non-gamers. Something that's not too overwhelming but also really fun. 5. For a game that appears so open, not a whole lot to explore, which was a bit disappointing, but climbing to the top of ruins and cliffsides gives you a lot of time to take in the beautiful views!
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully stunning, stunningly beautiful.  Either way this game looks amazing!  I'd been following Helder on twitter for a while, eagerly waiting for Europa's release.  Purchased on release day, I was not let down!  Initially taken in by the "Zelda" look, I held off trying the demo as I prefer not to spoil anything form the full release.  While the game is relatively short, I couldn't stop playing and completed it on 2nd day of play.  "We're here for a good time, not a long time" comes to mind.While the initial reaction on seeing Europa is surly "looks amazing", there is a lot more to this game.  Game mechanics and controls are probably different than what you'd expect but are quickly learnt and have some refreshing ideas behind them.  Puzzles are relatively easy but fun and I think that fits in with the over all style of the game.  Chilled music, beautiful world and a chilled gaming experience.Then there is the story, narrated by Zee's father Adam through a series of diary pages which you collect in each section of the world.  It's been a long time since a game has provoked any emotion like this in me and during this short but excellent adventure, I really did get to feel for Zee and Adam.Helder has done a fantastic job here and you can really see the passion the team have put into Europa.  Titles like this just show that indie games can give you just as good (if not better) experience than any AAA game.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME!First, the art concept and style is absolutely gorgeous. It looks like water color come to life and I enjoy just looking at it so much. All of the environments are special and unique, especially the one that looks like it's underwater. The game mechanics are easy and fun! You can fly and slide basically anywhere. The one con I have is sometimes the jumping is a little glitchy and I'll miss my landing but other times I'll make it. The puzzles are easy, which is good because I hate puzzles lol And lastly the story is touching, deep, and well thought out. I teared up multiple times as the story was revealed through excellent voice acting. I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me just say this is one of the most visually impressive indie games I have ever played. I would even go as far as to say it rivals some AAA game titles. It deserves a nomination for Best Art Direction at the 2024 Game Awards at the very least. The music is also excellent. The piano melodies fit the relaxed nature of this game perfectly. The story, as short as it is, is pretty touching and has heart. I won't expand any further to prevent spoilers. What would I change? I wish Zee (the main character) controlled better. I wasn't a big fan of how slippery his movement was or how imprecise his movements could be. This was most evident during the platforming sections. It was also a mixed bag while dodging hazards. Sometimes, it actually helped while other times, it hindered. Despite the my minor beef with the controls, I enjoyed my time with the game, and I would recommend it to any one who is looking for a short and relaxed game play experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly very well made with very good details of arts and epic design in level design especially the level tutorial and camera guidance. Actually surprised by such a small team but generated a high quality game.The game itself  is more like a Ghibli style of "journey" even the story are kind of similar and it has the battery UI on the player character itself its more like "Deadspace", I found some assets that were from synty studio's polygon environment pack.  Some details are similar to legend of zelda, but these are not important. Making 3D platformer is very hard to make the game interesting now days because there were so many of them. but this game shows a very attractive puzzle solving and parkour, when I saw it on steam store page.I like the Devs use different time to separate different level, even the player are in the envrionment, but it gives compeletely different feel.  As a small team indie game I can give 9/10. took me almost 3 hours to finish it but the game is comprehensive enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a soothing story book experience with some very light puzzling and an amazing atmosphere, this is the right kind of game. Otherwise, if you expect a lot of gameplay or challenge, then maybe skip this one. As a narrative driven game or visual novel, I would give it 3 out of 5 stars. It's missing more variety in puzzles and I would have wished for more lore. While I realise this is a budget-constrained indie product, a few more scattered pages describing Europa or what the relationship between the main characters is like wouldn't have hurt. By the 2/3 mark I was waiting for the experience to be over, which is sad since the game is really gorgeous. Maybe this could be a DLC to give it some replay value? Also, quite a few of the aesthetic cues seem to be borrowed from the recent two Zelda games, which can be either a good or tired, depending on your taste. Would be great to see what this very talented team could do with more time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Europa is one of those games that nails its core movement mechanic to the point that it's consistently fun to play. Floating around with the Zephyr "jetpack" is so much fun, only occasionally hindered by the crystal-powered creatures that ground you (for puzzle reasons.)It took me 2.8hrs to beat, all on Steam Deck, but there are plenty of achievements to aim for so I'll be diving back in soon enough.The game feels reminiscent of artistic platformers like Ico, Shadow of the Colossus, and Journey, but it has a gorgeous style of its own. Strange to recognise developer HP from my teen obsession with the Max Payne modding scene, but thrilled to see him launch Europa after following its development on socials (congratulations!)Beautiful game. Well worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: No combat, just puzzles and vibes. Would have loved to pet the animals, especially the fox. I guess you can sort of "pet" them if you're close enough and Zee naturally reaches his hand out and it looks like petting. Also would be helpful to add a emerald count to each area (ex: 2/5 found), so people know if they've found all in the area before moving on. Story and music were fantastic and reminded me of Castle in the Sky and Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind. Absolutely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with amazing graphics, music and sweet story. It's a platformer with nice exploration however it's abit too peaceful, even the hazards have no real downside, which is a shame as the game is very easy - even if this fits the peaceful post-war narrative. Collectables aren't too hard to find/get and playtime + achievement hunting will net you around 4 hrs of game time.  Puzzles are simple and easy. Basically, this game is a good introduction to those new to platformers or who want a peaceful emotional experience similar to Journey, Abzu or Omno.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game! The art, musical score, narration, story... all of it. Absolutely stunning. I'm not a finisher of games, but i played through this is four and a half hours. I didn't want to stop!I wasn't sure about it at first because I'm not a a fan of puzzle-y type games, but the mechanics are gently fed to you through gameplay at a comfy pace. This is the first game where I managed to complete jump challenges without raging out!It was a comfortable game to play, physically. I have joint issues in my hands, but had no issues with movement or key bindings, which was a relief. There are a lot of bright white scene transitions though, so if you have sensitive eyes, be on the lookout for those.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: This is a BEAUTIFUL game.  You glide and float around the grass pains and the blue lakes with a small engine, you can slide down every hill and skate on the water, it's really fun! this game is a short beautiful emotional story about a planet, similar Journey and Abzu. If you liked Journey, definitely get this one!10/10 you can pet the turtles
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review: Getting the obvious out of the way first, Europa is a game I wholeheartedly recommend to those who like environmental/document-based storytelling, some nice floaty platforming, and a beautiful world. There are a couple of issues keeping it from absolute perfection, but going in forewarned should help a lot.Following the android Zee as he follows his late creator's guiding notes across the terraformed Europa to the remains of humanity on the ark, the story is simple, but engaging and very touching. The mood is helped by gorgeously soft aesthetics that feel like a melding of Studio Ghibli's Castle in the Sky and Journey, and a beautiful soundtrack by Matthew Thomason.The gameplay is where some might end up losing their way, though it's not bad by any means. The controls and simple and intuiative, the movement is solid if occasionally floaty, and there are a couple of collectable types that can be challenging to find. There are "enemies" which end up proving frustrating in places as they interrupt the flow of exploration. The puzzles aren't anything brain-bending, just environmental and platform-based challenges that require some awareness.Overall, this is a good game. Is it a perfect game? No. But it's an excellent game for an indie developer who worked with a very small team to create something that is twice as long and just as engaging as Journey. Indeed, there are so many headnods to Journey that you might want to play through a few times just to catch them. If you enjoy a sweet story, engaging platforming and beautiful visuals and music (and don't mind some occasionally frustrating mechanics), then please give this game a chance.8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

_childDocuments_.review:
On the moon Europa, a lush terraformed paradise in Jupiter’s shadow, an android named Zee sets out in search of answers. Run, glide and fly across the landscape, solve mysteries in the ruins of a fallen utopia, and discover the story of the last human alive.

Europa is a peaceful game of adventure, exploration and meditation. As you travel you’ll gradually upgrade the capabilities of your Zephyr jetpack, boosting yourself further through the air until you can flow freely into the sky.
_childDocuments_.name: Europa

name: Colossal Cave
detailed_description: SteamVR Solo App ㅤ Experience the enchanting realm of 'Colossal Cave' in VR without breaking the bank! Explore our discounted standalone SteamVR version - the same riveting adventure, at a price that's irresistibly compelling! About the Game ㅤ Embark on a timeless journey through a sprawling cave system packed with treasures, creatures, mazes, and wits-defying puzzles. The great grandpappy of adventure games will test you and tickle your problem-solving skills as you unearth its plot and secrets. Through cunning trial-and-error you will crawl through tight squeezes, encounter impressive caverns, collect inventory, locate treasure, thwart dwarf attacks, all while keeping your eye on the score before your lamp goes out. Dust off your vintage Colossal Cave maps from the 70s or 80s, they'll still work like a charm. This is a faithful, unchanged tribute to the original game design. Need a little nudge? Stuck on the dragon? Call our classic hint line at 1-206-207-9017 for a helping hand. Can't seem to make progress? Search online for hints and tips that have been shared for decades. Any tips or tricks regarding the original game play will still work here. Or, join our Discord for even more support! Developed in the mid-1970’s by amateur cave spelunker, this classic text-adventure was originally crafted as a way for a father to entertain his two young daughters. Will Crowther based his design on detailed cave maps he’d made with his wife, Patricia, of the Bedquilt section of Kentucky’s Mammoth cave. Family cave exploration is at the heart of this game. Shortly thereafter, the code-prankster, Don Woods, discovered the game on the ARPANET and expanded the cave. He layered in more fun, fantasy, puzzles, and a vexing 350-point system. Years later, Don’s expansion became the most accessible and the definitive version of Colossal Cave Adventure . Enter Roberta Williams. She first played the game in 1979 and was instantly hooked. She spent weeks playing the game, taking notes and mapping out the cave, as it was revealed through the textual descriptions in game. Her mind was filled with imaginary neon mushrooms, misty underground lakes, a snappy bivalve mollusk, and a noticeably absent giant. After finishing the game, and all 350 points achieved, she was ready for another adventure – a dilemma in 1979. If it was another adventure she wanted, she’d have to make her own! And, indeed she did. In 1980 she designed and developed the world’s first graphic computer game, Mystery House . This groundbreaking game is considered one of the most influential in history, establishing conventions that have become standard in the adventure game genre. It has been ported to just about every computer and console, played by millions, and inspired many other games, books, movies, and TV series. Relive the golden age of adventure gaming. Immerse yourself in a timeless exploration through a sprawling cave system filled with treasures, creatures, and brain-teasing puzzles. Transport back to a more innocent time and experience the retro-cool of point-and-click mechanics, accompanied by an art style that harkens back to the golden age of adventure games. This lovingly and respectfully assembled tribute is brought to you by boutique studio, Cygnus Entertainment. Ken and Roberta Williams are committed to sharing and preserving the spirit of classic adventure games. With its challenging and mind-bending puzzles, this explorative game will keep you enthralled. Explore 14 distinct regions filled with magic, hidden secrets, breathtaking views, and cave-dwelling creatures of all types. Each area offers a unique and enchanting experience. And with over 20 individual achievements to find and accomplish, you'll be hooked for hours. Simple, intuitive, point-&-click controls Captivating, colorful, and immersive regions Challenging, logic-driven puzzles A perfect blend of challenge and reward Scenic subterranean vistas with hidden secrets Over 20 individual achievements to accomplish A game that is incredibly fun and engaging A game experience unlike any other And, as much as this game is steeped in gaming history and lore, there’s also a reason it’s stood the test of time and become so richly intertwined with gaming culture. It’s fun! It is also thought provoking and challenging. It is both simple and complex. It's creative - and, as Roberta says, it’s a fantastic design. Venture down into Colossal Cave and explore its depths. Don’t forget your lamp! Finally, embark on a thrilling journey with us on Discord, a space where you can get the latest game updates, seek technical support or valuable game hints, and .

short_description: Acclaimed game designer Roberta Williams revives Colossal Cave as a retro, point-&-click, cave exploration puzzler. Based on the original 1970’s design by Will Crowther & Don Woods this 3D update maintains its vintage charm, while revitalizing it for modern gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: I am Roberta Williams – about Colossal Cave, Release 2.0Since the latest release of our game (2.0), I have been so very pleased by the enjoyment that gamers are having with it! A year ago, our first release of Colossal Cave received a well-deserved ‘cool’ reception, but it was our first game to develop after a very long hiatus. Believe me, Ken and I had some ‘learning’ to do. Since then, we have been unceasing in our efforts to address every dismay or issue we saw in any review. We made a huge list of updates! The newest improvements: additional modes of locomotion, integrated tutorials, autosave, new and enhanced graphics, more sound effects including footsteps, performance enhancements, and much more. The game today is not the same as that initial release. I wish to thank everyone who has played Colossal Cave 2.0 or will give it a go. It was a passion project, and we are very proud of it. I hope you will enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is special, not only because it marks the most welcome return of Ken and Roberta Williams to game design, but also playing it makes me feel like I did as a kid experiencing King's Quest for the first time  - a sense of wonder while exploring a world full of surprises round every corner. The objective of the game is simple - find all the treasures hidden in the cave - but finding your way through its mazelike passages and great caverns is far from simple. Fortunately there's an automap feature that maps your progress as well as any items you've dropped, as unlike most other adventure games you can't put an infinite number of items down your pants ;) I was thrilled to play the game as it was being developed and got totally hooked exploring every nook and cranny of the cave, and even when you reach the end it feels like there's something else to discover. I would have liked to see more NPC interaction or expansion in certain areas, and my main criticism is that it's sometimes too faithful to the original and players may not fully appreciate it without any knowledge of the text adventure. I'll be playing it again to try and get maximum points but for now my one word review is COLOSSAL :D

_childDocuments_.review: Colossal Cave is a faithful remake of the eponymous first-ever popular text adventure from the mid-70s, now with first-person 3D graphics. It adds some much-needed quality-of-life features, but leaves the gameplay untouched - which makes it authentic, but also probably hard to appreciate for a modern audience.Your task is to explore a cave, survive its dangers, and bring 15 treasures back to the surface. Collecting treasures and solving puzzles earns you points. That's all the story there is - the original Colossal Cave was written at a time when programmers hadn't fully realized yet that this new medium could be used to tell actual stories. The game originally started as a text-based cave exploration simulation with some fantasy elements such as a dragon, dwarves, and magic added to it.While the game is advertised as the return of adventure game design veteran Roberta Williams (of King's Quest fame), it is important to understand that this product, due to being a faithful recreation of a game that is older than her career, has practically nothing inside that would remind her fans of her stories, characters, or puzzle design. Nevertheless, it's always nice to see designers of classic games complete new works.Gameplay consists of exploring the cave system, solving puzzles, and occasionally fighting dwarves.There is ample room for exploration as the game features about 80 rooms, each individually designed, plus some 35 rooms in mazes that are basically just variations on two templates. The artists succeeded in keeping the game visually interesting by adding a bit of clutter and giving many rooms their own, unique look. However, it often makes no sense that a room of the given type would appear in a cave system. Also, apart from a general description of the room, none of the clutter items can be interacted with, they do not have individual descriptions either. In lots of rooms, there simply isn't anything to do other than traversing them.The puzzles are mostly inventory-driven and not particularly logical. Some trial-and-error may be required, but players familiar with inventory-driven puzzles shouldn't have much trouble. It's noteworthy that some of the treasures also have uses within the puzzles, and some can be lost unrecoverably (for the current playthrough).By far the most challenging aspect of the original Colossal Cave, was finding your way around. Passages may bend and twist, so if you leave a room to the west, and want to go back, then you can't rely on just going east - you may need to go north, for example. The game also includes not just one, but three mazes, and in many rooms, the same exits may randomly loop back on themselves, or (with a small chance) lead to a new room. The game's automap feature is a godsend here, as it depicts the complex topography accurately and also helps you find passages that you haven't explored yet. The map also persists between playthroughs (but you can erase it manually).The "combat" with the dwarves is very simple - you just click on a weapon in your inventory, click "Use", and then click on the enemy. However, enemies may randomly spawn out of nowhere, and - true to the original game - they have a random chance of killing you before you even get to react. You can get resurrected three times in any given playthrough, but that reduces your score.Another feature that the game retains from the original, is a hard limit on the time you can spend exploring, as your lantern will eventually run out and leave you helpless in the dark. The game is a bit more generous with the lamp than the original though, provided that you play with "instructions".While several of these mechanics feel really ancient by now and are hardly fun, the main gameplay loop of exploring the cave and solving puzzles is still enjoyable and feels rewarding. I appreciated the quality-of-life features, though I think that more could have been done in that regard, such as a way to switch off the random unpreventable instadeaths.Graphics are a mixed bag. Most of the game is held in a stylized, low-poly look, but most of the textures looked still nice on my 4k screen. That said, the area that you start in is full of issues, from clunky pixels in the shadows and the skybox to broken geometry on the props and a water texture that flows in several directions at once and, depending on view angle and lighting, looks like quicksilver. These problems only occurred in the small overworld area, though - the cave interiors do not have these issues.For an indie game with stylized graphics, I found the visuals quite nice. The animations of creatures and dwarves are especially well-done. On the other hand, there's an animation of a lava fountain that looks really crude, like something from 20 years ago.Sound effects are mostly okay and fit the respective action, with some notable exceptions (for example, the sound effect of wading through the river in the overworld area sounds nothing like the real thing). Ambiance sounds like air drafts or dripping water contribute to the atmosphere. On the other hand, you almost never hear your footsteps. This could have been done better.Music is used very sparingly. The game just plays a few short, well-known, classical tracks in specific situations, such as a few chords of "Hall of the Mountain King" when you enter one particular room for the first time. I'm fine with that, I don't think continuous music would have fit the theme of solitary cave exploration very well.The game features a narrator who reads room descriptions from the original game, describes any actions taking place, comments on some, and also occasionally makes suggestions. All these lines are voiced by a very competent actor whose voice doesn't get old even though you keep hearing it throughout the entire game.The game offers very limited graphics settings (resolution, fullscreen, vsync), 3 separate volume sliders (music, speech, FX), and a subtitle toggle.You can choose between two different input methods (mouse and keyboard, or mouse only), which is nice in principle, but unfortunately neither works very well. There is no key for "interact", instead there is a giant icon in the center of the screen, which you can switch between an "eye" (look), "hand" (interact), or "feet" (move). The main difference between the two control methods is that one uses mouse buttons in the "feet" mode for movement, while the other uses WASD keys. Regardless of which option you choose, you'll have a giant black icon obstructing the center of the screen.Keys cannot be rebound, so players with AZERTY keyboards, Dvorak keyboards, or certain disabilities may want to use the mouse-only controls. Even if you use WASD, you keep having to break your immersion and looking down on your keyboard, because the map key ("M") is impossible to blind-type when your fingers rest on your mouse and WASD. Basic PC functionality like rebindable keys should not have been lacking for a game that constantly wants you to switch between movement, looking around, inventory, and map. The game provides 21 save slots, which is more than enough for one playthrough.I encountered one game-breaking bug (falling through the map in an endless loop upon loading a save), but it only occurred in one room (cobble crawl). There were no gameplay bugs and no crashes.While this is not a game for everyone, it should be quite enjoyable for people who want to relive (or discover for the first time) an incredibly influential piece of computer gaming history. Some archaic mechanics may be hard to like for players who were never used to them, but features like the automap or the increased lantern duration help a lot. The $25 base price is a bit steep though for what's being offered, I recommend getting it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone younger than 40 prepare to be shocked, or at least startled a bit by the ironman-style design and gameplay rules that hearken back to a time when most people weren’t playing games or if they were maybe only a few each year.  Everything from the simplistic yet still charming graphics, awkward interface, and a point reward system that modern adventure games have moved past are on full display here.  By design, the game is meant to played multiple times, especially if you are going for the coveted 350 max award.  Perfecting the game will require lots of memorization and prep work and the ability to avoid accepting help of any kind including tutorials and mid-game hints, which all cost points.  After two or three passes you might be ready to take your notes and maps and go for that perfect 350 score, but make sure you have plotted the best path through the game, as your lantern only has half its life when going for this prize.There are 15 treasures to locate in order to win the game, but most serious gamers will want to go for that 350-point secondary objective, so plan to replay the game at least 2-3 times unless you go straight for a walkthrough guide.  I had the chance to play Colossal Cave on both PC and PS5 and found both versions nearly identical given the limiting style and complexity of the visual design.  There is a definite indie vibe about the presentation, and many times I felt I was playing somebody’s final submission in their college-level game design course.  Don’t get me wrong; the game looks great for what it is, but unless you are really going to go for those 350 points, I think $40 might be a bit much.  This feels more like a $20-30 game, which I’m sure it will be in an upcoming sale. As big a fan as I am of the Williams and adventure games, Colossal Cave just doesn’t bring as much to the table as it should for a $40 game.  It’s a fun adventure that can get grindy and a bit frustrating at times, mostly because its staying true to its hardcore 70’s design roots, so I totally encourage everyone to check it out on whatever system you own, but you may want to wait for a sale before you venture into this Colossal Cave.Read full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: The cave is aptly dubbed colossal! It's quite massive, but luckily there is a map that updates as you explore. I dig the atmosphere a lot. I was pulled in immediately, though do mind I've only just started playing. I've never played the original text adventure, so I come fresh to this experience.While visually it's not the most polished game, there's plenty to love about the aesthetics, and it's clear great efforts have been made to make the different parts / rooms of the cave distinct. Sound wise, there aren't many songs from what I can tell, and it is sound effects and ambiance that are front and center.The game has a number of small bugs but I haven't encountered anything serious so far.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I´ve played through the game on the Meta Quest 2  (VR Standalone Version). I´ve also bought the Steam PC Version. So, actually I´ve spend ~80U$ on the game. If you are interested in my review for the Meta Quest 2 VR Version, check out my 30 min Deepdive Youtube Video review (no spoilers!):I´ve checked the Steam Version after playing through the game in VR on the Quest 2. Graphics look a little bit better on the PC (better shadow/particle effects, higher resolution of textures etc.). Also the interface is a little bit more comfortable compared to the Quest 2 solutions, but that doesn`t mean the Quest controls are bad. It features also a point&click interface on the quest.About the game:I'm really torn on this one, but I think that's what Ken and Roberta Williams were expecting from most players when they made some of the decisions nearly 2 years ago. In any case, they & the whole team have my utmost respect for having managed and delivered the project under their own steam in this short time (basically they developed and finished the game within 1 1/2 years). Unlike many "Kickstarter" zombie projects from old veterans they delivered self-financed a graphical re-master of an text adventure from the 70s. Ken obviously still knows how to produce a game. I really hope they have the energy to create one more unique game, not just some kind of "remaster" or "re-make".At least Roberta, the original game designer of Sierra Online (Mystery House, King´s Quest series, Phantasmagoria) - managed to create an atmosphere in the game – heavily limited by its original design mechanics tho - that makes you want to go on a journey of discovery. At the end, there is one real goal besides reaching the maximum of 350 points. And at least in this aspect, the old gameplay scored with me: I stayed motivated and always wanted to find a solution.  For Roberta, Colassal Cave was her first computer game and it strongly influenced her development as a game designer. So this late work of hers and Ken's is probably a late homage to the game that launched her career in the 70s.Colossal Cave 3D is essentially the same as the original text adventure game with its puzzles, flow and world design. Only in 3D.  I think that's a smart decision on one hand, and a bit "cowardly" on the other.Because this way the design performance of Roberta - apart from the visualization - can practically not be rated. Not only are the original texts translated into images, they are recited. Thus Colossal Cave is not a new game, but only some kind of "remaster", another variant that fits into the series of already existing versions of Colossal Cave.In terms of gameplay, your task is to find a way through the cave maze by solving mini-quests and collecting treasures. You will then receive points for the achievements. You will also receive points if you drop your treasures at the wellhouse.Like in most classic adventure games, you have to think around corners or simply try things out. Unfortunately, the puzzles didn't always seem logical to me (same as in the original). On the other hand, it was fun to play a game where not everything is presented in a logical and bite-sized way. While the initial puzzles are easy, they quickly become more difficult as the game progresses. Colossal Cave is NOT an easy game. It is something for puzzle freaks and those who are not always looking for a logical solution.The graphics of Colossal Cave are not ugly, but  remind me of an early 2000s game. The game takes place mostly in an underground cave complex, and I would have liked to see a more spectacular presentation. As I understand it, the main goal of the remaster was the graphical interpretation according to Roberta's imagination. Well regarding the graphics there is nothing beautiful or special about the cave. Therefor the "reimagination" part comes a little bit short. At least for my taste.The sound design is much better than the graphics. I love the narrator. He does a great job. He basically reads to you the original text adventure while you explore and click on stuff with the "eye"-Cursor. You should really use the eye, otherwise you miss stuff.Did the Williams deliver what they promised? I think they did. It´s a graphic reinterpretation of the original game. But it´s certainly not a beautiful game. Is it still fun for puzzle fans? Yes! Old school adventure fans will like the flashback and the nostalgia. This remastered version stays true to the original as much as possiible. My rating of the PC Version:Gfx: 65/100Sound: 72/100Story: 45/100 Gameplay: 80/100 (old school puzzles!)Interface: 80/100--Total: 75/100Is it worth 40$? Well that´s something you have to decide for yourself. I think this should be a ~20$ title. In overall sales the title would probably perform better if it would be offered at a cheaper price. But maybe sale comes soon. I hope to see one more unique title from the Williams in the coming years before they are too old.Thanks for reading! Cheers.
_childDocuments_.name: Colossal Cave

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I didn't realize I didn't go back and update this, and am swapping it to Recommended now. The game has made a lot of strides forward, addressing many of the concerns in one way or another.The VR is very well done, the textures are good, the perspective is good, and while it might need a bit of work in controls (specifically holding items, picking things up, etc. things that are user addressable based on your specific type of controller) - it goes very well with the pancake version, only adding and not taking away, with a few minor adjustments for the player to get used to. The included documentary is really good and well done in it's addition/integration. As originally: the game still runs very well, even on VR I had zero frame issues, no crashes, no problems.The game now offers more hints in exchange for points in more parts of the game (ie: How to get out of one of the mazes, how to work with a flighty creature). It doesn't offer the hint once after you've already solved it, or once you enter an area - if you fail enough time it'll prompt again, just in case.The game itself has no technical issues, and any further concerns I might have with it is more of a genre thing. There isn't much more that can be done with the story until the end as it would have spoilers or deviate from the original - so just know that going inOriginal review:Beat the game tonight, first time playing any version of Colossal Cave. People in the know told me this was a very faithful version of the original - which is great and all, but... didn't the original come with a manual? Something for players to reference for any info? (Edit: per comments, no... it did not. So I guess I slightly understand, but I'm not giving this one a pass. She was 're-imagining it' and definitely could have come up with something to make the story exist or provide some sort of help/clue/direction for players as to who, what, where, when, why, and how.)Going to be honest, I bought this immediately because of Roberta/Ken Williams. I've been playing their games since I was a child and walking walking next door after school to play Kings Quest 1 on my neighbors PC. I love almost every game they've done and immediately was hyped when I saw this project (not even overly annoyed that it went on sale after I bought it for 10% off). But this game is different from what I've run into from them before: we have no manual, no hints, no story, no details to even begin going off of, and while there are very good aspects, the bad are kind of painful.Good:The music is good when it's playing. The narrator's voice acting is good.The caves themselves look pretty decent (though I didn't understand the trash until the end).The scenic areas look great.The auto-map is a life saver.Bad:The narrator gets REALLY aggravating, very quickly. "You can't do anything with that" as I try to climb ladders.Naming everything in my inventory as I mouse over it.Repeating the same voice line for room descriptions, so no voice lines or descriptions of anything IN the room - just the room as a whole. The world border areas are really sharply enforced. No story. We literally just are on an island, take over a shack, and start looting people who are just working. I actually thought that we were being attacked because we stole stuff, not just because we existed. Some indication or story would have been great.Absolutely zero hints for the players. I spent the first hour just ignoring the attackers because of the pause when they attacked and then them vanishing, so I figured "I guess I can't do anything about it."The inventory system clears your item when you change maps or press I again, so you have to go back in and select something to have it ready for right click. That also didn't help my confusion about 'fighting back.'Lack of music for the large part. Most of the time we wander in silence.The hint system popping up at bad times for things I've already figured out but gone into again. Why can't we turn this off? Again, I know. I KNOW it's a remake of an original from long ago, but we were missing key portions that originally came with the purchase back then that could... and SHOULD ..  have been added or weaved in. Can I recommend this? Not if you are not a fan and greatly remember the original. If you are like me and just jumping in because the Williams' are just amazing at game design and creation, then in this instance I need you to consider "Do I want to blindly go along for a bit and then consult a guide for most of it?" because you'll need to. For instance there is no indication of how to even begin the ending part of the game. Without a person in chat pointing me in the right direction a couple of times, I'd honestly have had zero clue on even trying to end this after I found all the treasures. I'd have just wandered until I stopped playing.In the end, I ended up missing 15 points for a perfect score, and I just have no real desire to go in and do it again. I don't even know how I lost 10 points (5 points for the coins). So I'm not even sure what I can do different. And honestly I just don't want to. I've replayed most of their games over and over and am able to safely get max scores in their other games, but I really feel let down by this one in so many ways. It was a passion project by Roberta and so I don't want to vote it down, but as a fan of their work... this was disappointing. So I have to mark it no, and that sucks. I really, really, wanted to like this. I'm really sorry that I just can't.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Ken and Roberta since my childhood playing Sierra games, so obviously I was excited to hear they were making a new game.  I was then a bit disappointed to learn it really wasn't a new game but a remake.  That said, it's a remake of THE original adventure game and one I have never played.  So why not give it a try?  And I've had a blast so far.  I intended to just try it out for a few minutes, but I've already spent four hours exploring the cave.  I'm hoping to get some friends involved too, just like I did as a kid.  (After all, some of these puzzles seem pretty tough!)  The "older" graphics look pretty nice to me, a child of the 80s and 90s.  That's not to say I would accept any old thing.  I don't think I could play this game without the automap or (shudder) in text form.  The twisty passages are way too alike for that.  But I'm having a blast.  I'm so happy Ken and Roberta got to do this passion project, and I hope it spurs them on to new, exciting adventure games in the years to come.

I'm a little confused on the dwarves fight mechanic as there's little to no control over if you can hit them or they hit you.  Seems random and you just need to reload your last save so the next encounter they might miss and you can move on.  Played on my PC first night and steam deck the next day. _childDocuments_.review: I was excited to hear that Ken and Roberta Williams were developing a new game.  When I found out it was a remake of Colossal Cave, some of that excitement waned as I was hoping for an original story or concept from them.  Now that I've played Colossal Cave 3D for several hours, I'm pleasantly surprised.  The game is a lot of fun, but it took me a while to get to that point.The very first time I played the game, I found it frustrating.  The controls were awkward and it wasn't clear how the game was played.  After making some adjustments to the controls (mouse + keyboard was much better than mouse-only) and adjusting the camera and movement speed, it felt much better.  I also went back and went through the tutorial, and also opted to take instructions.  Both of these helped understand things better.Once I started to explore the cave more and better understood the mapping system, things started to make a lot more sense and I started having fun playing the game.  This truly feels like a classic text adventure updated for today.  I've only made it to about 100 points so far (out of a possible 350), but I find myself wanting to play the game and I plan to go for the full 350.Some of the other reviews I read criticize the graphics.  I don't share this same criticism.  The graphics are not going to amaze you, but they are entirely appropriate for this style of game.Overall, this is one of the most fun adventure games I've played in many years, and I highly recommend it to anyone that is a fan of the adventure game genre.  If things don't make sense at first, give it some time.  Once you figure out how things work, it becomes very enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I could never finish ADVENTURE. It feels like ADVENT meets Zork: Grand Inquisitor in the best way possible. :) Thanks Roberta and everyone who worked on this great reimagining!
_childDocuments_.name: Colossal Cave

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time streaming this game on my Twitch channel (@Cobra_Commanda) having never played the original text adventure but as a Roberta Williams fan since 1992 or '93 when I played through King's Quest VI for the first time. I can't speak for everyone, I know there are critics, and it's not the cheapest game out there, but I wanted to support Roberta & Ken in hopefully continuing to make games into the future. You have to look at your own personal financial situation and make decisions that work for you. Maybe you want to wait until the game goes on sale, and that's fine too.As far as gameplay goes, I've heard people complain that CCA3D doesn't "hold your hand" the way most modern games do, but that's exactly what I liked about it. You can die in the game in true classic Sierra style! I also loved that it wasn't dripping with irony and overly philosophical/naval-gazing writing; it was just good old-fashioned spelunking adventuring fun with a touch of irreverence here and there. I didn't feel like there was forced deeper meaning or messaging that I was supposed to take away about (usually) depression or whatever. I got to just explore a cave and solve puzzles. Honestly, it was refreshing!There were a couple of times when I *definitely* would have gotten stuck without the help of a couple of people in my chat (that one maze... omg), but we perservered! I hear people saying the graphics are bad, but I'm a classic pixel art lover first and foremost so they looked fine to me, and personally I prefer them to the art of a certain other adventure game from another legacy developer that came out in recent months. ;-)  But I digress...Maybe I'm a bit biased, but seeing Roberta's face on the back of the KQVI box did inspire me as a pre-pubescent girl in the early 90s who loved fantasy, adventure, storytelling, writing, and video games, and I do hope she'll keep making more (maybe some beautiful pixel art ones?). I was in a position where I could afford to purchase this, and I'm happy I did so. It was extremely fun for me to stream on my channel. Is it for everyone? Of course not. But if you share some of the sentiments I've expressed in this review, there's a good chance that you'll have a lot of fun with it. Happy spelunking!
_childDocuments_.name: Colossal Cave

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a remake, and was surprised to find out it's just a modern implementation of the original game.  And that's a pretty important thing for me to say cause I never liked the original, but I did like this one. That's it, really. It's graphics are not the prettiest, but do work. It's animations are not the fluidest, but they work. The game does have some quality of life implements that help players and the narration is quirky and funny. I'm really happy to see Roberta and Ken Williams back into the videogame business, and I'm really eager to see a new adventure game designed by Roberta. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Colossal Cave

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it to you with all my heart. This is a Classic Car of gaming. It's for the collector. It's for the old-schooler and aficionados of finely-reworked digitial artisinal crafts. It's for those new to gaming but experienced in VR. Yeah, you can start here! This is instruction-worthy. It's close to where it all began!This game is not for those into instant gratification. Unless you have a real knack for puzzles and problem-solving and don't mind literally feeling your way around in the dark (with lamplight alone, in some cases) to find your way. This is from the old days. This is a walk through time as much as it is a the space of a cave. It's originally from a very different time. So it deserves observance, respect and appreciation for what it was as well as what it is now. This a most respectful treatment.It is an adventure game for the patient and persistent, for the curious and brave! But also for the wise and determined! It takes time to find your way in the dark and only by lamplight. I hope you're ready for an adventure!If you've played classic Point-and-Click adventures many of which were made by the creators of this remake you'll know how it works already. Ironically enough, VR works on basically the same principles of interactivity. So not just veterans of those games will know their way how to get started. For me, I never actually got too far in the original. I began in the King's Quest era of gaming. Traditional text adventures, like this one that was maybe the first required time, patience and persistence. You were unlikely to sit and finish text adventure games in one sitting. It was sometimes a months-long, on-and-off, grief-and-exaltation-inducing affair. Sometimes coming back to it months or years later. It's like,... you couldn't get it. No way to solve the puzzle!. You could never get it! Until you could. You figured it out. Typed the right instruction/command and then it clicked. When you did though it was glorious. I didn't get too far in the original. That doesn't mean I forgot the experience. It was enchanting but one I never mustered the courage to see through. Roberta and Ken Williams through Cygnus have re-ignited the fire and inspired me to re-light my lamp. To go back down into that cave I could never fully stomach exploring before via text. One day I will go back to the text-game, probably armed with the knowledge and experience I gained here in this 3D, narrated version of that game. I probably will do pretty well in it too. But what matters to me is I get to experience it at all, and if not for the remade version of it in 3D with CHEESE controls compared to having to type EVERYTHING in the original, well, I might have not made it back any too soon if ever. Now I know I will. On a personal note I want to thank Ken and Roberta. You made my childhood much brighter. Mom bought the Sierra games I enjoyed playing, but to tell the truth, I actually played a lot more of them! As far as I am concerned you are rescuing a priceless gem from the obscurity of time and evolving platforms. What's more, you're doing it in VR. Sierra was an innovator back when few dared to try to make games for computers. One can see how that happened then. I appreciate you now lending your hands to this game and choosing such a worthy candidate to bring into contemporary cultural currency.I would not put any price on the experiences the Williams's and their talented, dedicated teams past and present have brought us. $25 is a small price to pay for what you're getting. This is a 3D, live-action, FPS-style (soon VR) recreation of a game that you could have originally played in only very limited circumstances. It's an interactive museum exhibit and it is a darn good take on the original concept too. Executed well-enough to make it endure for as long as people are playing computer games. That's a worthy investment, and one I'd hasten anyone who loves the artform to make. It's also a neat exploration puzzle game in its own right.This is art that means to be art. So to those reading, please enjoy and appreciate it accordingly. I bid Ken and Roberta continued success and the best of luck in their future endeavors whatever they may be. I'd be remiss not to mention that I do hope to see further, and different kinds of installments of works from them in the future. You've certainly brought a whole lot of enjoyment to my life and that's something I will always be grateful for. Thank you so much.

_childDocuments_.review: This graphically-rich re-imagining of the 1977, 350-point Don Woods edition of Will Crowther's famous text adventure is an extremely faithful adaptation of an important game in gaming history. Roberta Williams' vision and her team's efforts bring a multi-sensory presentation to what was previously the imagination's purview, as players explore the various caverns and their secrets. Each space is detailed, with colors and textures to give them a unique feel. The trek is not without its hazards: dwarves, dragons, darkness, and time itself all pose problems that must be overcome with a combination of wit, wisdom, and luck. While games have improved and iterated on more player-friendly design patterns over the decades, it's a valuable view into the past, to how Roberta and Ken (and many others) were inspired to make an industry in part thanks to stories like this one. The greatest value, though, is in endeavoring to present Colossal Cave in a way that will attract newer audiences, like a carefully-crafted museum expo. Spelunkers willing to master these dangers and scour every corner of the subterranean world will be rewarded with much more than a wheelhouse full of treasures.

_childDocuments_.review: A nearly perfect adaptation of the original text game! I was mesmerized as a world that I had first explored 40 years ago appeared before my eyes for the first time ever. I took 0 hints in/on this 2023 Colossal Cave game. I got through the entire game using my memory of the original text game and a few hints in regard to the original text game. That tells you that this game is 100% loyal to the original.My memory in regard to the original text game had faded a lot, and that enabled me to have a truly thrilling experience playing this game. I felt real terror the first time that the bear growled at me in the cave. And I felt real terror the first time that I heard the giant speaking and pounding on something. And the giant, troll, and bear puzzle, which was always brilliant, was implemented brilliantly.Adventure (Colossal Cave), Adventure in Serenia, and a game named Decathlon were the first 3 games that I ever played. _childDocuments_.review: This game delivers exactly what it promises: an old-school adventure experience wrapped inside a modern-day game. It's a faithful recreation of the classic text adventure, with all the quirks & frustrations intact. Don't play it expecting more (or less!) than that. It's about exploring & replaying until you find all the treasures, solve the puzzles & get the max score. It's not for everybody. But for those who enjoy the genre, it's a fun experience, with some laughs and surprises along the way.In terms of style, I think the creators nailed the feel of playing through a text adventure with full visuals and sound. The narrator has a great voice, and if he ever gets annoying, you can turn him off. It's certainly not cutting-edge in terms of graphics (possibly held back by the need to support VR?) but I enjoyed the overall style and atmosphere. I wish I could have played it on a VR setup; that seems the ideal way to play this. I encountered a few technical "hiccups" but no major bugs. I shared a few QoL wishes with a member of the dev team, who said they might be included in a future patch. An overall 8/10, but with a big asterisk: IMO, it's overpriced. For hardcore adventure fans, it might be worth paying the full price. For more general gamers and who aren't sold by the nostalgia of this title, it's probably best to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I have stayed up WAY too late playing this.  I'm absolutely delighted.  I grew up on Sierra games and am familiar with text-based adventures (though never played the original Colossal Cave).  It's important to know that though this game is fully 3D, it still PLAYS like a text adventure.  Compass directions are important, and you will be managing your inventory space and using items on different things.  Even the VR version doesn't have immersive interaction (like grabbing a door handle to open a door).  That's not a deal-breaker for me though.  Once you get used to the simple way to interact with the game, it's easy to fall into the sense of adventure and exploration.  I can't wait to get back to this after work tomorrow and play some more!

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original text version on a Kaypro II computer back in the early 1980's and I remember the world in my mind vividly.  When I started this game, I was pleased to see that it offered every type of game control - mouse only, mouse and keyboard, and gamepad.  I'm using an Xbox controller, so in I went.  I chose to not use hints, thinking I was already good at this game.  Well, I was wrong.  I instantly got lost in the caves.  So I will be restarting the game with hints.  From what I see so far, this game will definitely appeal to anyone who played the text game.  For those who never played this before, I am guessing this version might be slightly frustrating.  The graphics are not mind-blowing modern stuff - more like something you would see in games from maybe 10 years ago.  Moving around is pretty fast and it's easy to get disoriented.  Interacting with items and surroundings is a sort of hybrid point & click, and text game style.  Takes some getting used to.  But it's worth it for the fact that this game is one of the milestones in adventure gaming.  You have to give it a little effort.  It's so amazing to see this game come to life visually, so I am going to give it my all to play this to the end and get the ultimate 350 point finish.  I recommend this to all Colossal Cave veterans who are here on Steam and are looking at this game.  You need this in your collection.  To the newcomers, I can't say if this will be your cup of tea.  But you can't go wrong trying this out.  It's a piece of gaming history.  The term XYZZY has been in my life for the past 30 plus years, and this game brings it full circle.  It makes me wish a bunch of the early text games like Infocom's Wishbringer could be brought to life this way, I would totally be into it, too.  I was a huge fan of Sierra games, and the fact that the founders of Sierra made this?  It couldn't get any better.
_childDocuments_.name: Colossal Cave

_childDocuments_.review: Colossal Cave is wonderful!  I absolutely love it.   The voice narration is perfect.  The ambiance and small details bring the game to life.   The entire text of the original game is captured in the audio and subtitles.  I think the Cygnus team really captured what they were aiming for: it's a classic adventure game, with challenging and fun puzzles, and with a streamlined user interface.  So many references in computer lore originated in Colossal Cave that older gamers will enjoy seeing.  Twisty passages, all alike and XYZZY are not Easter eggs: this is their natural habitat!  I fully recommend this.  My daughter and I are having a blast playing it together and it's a great bonding experience.  No adult themes or violence.  It's fun to explore every nook and cranny of the caves.  Thank you, Roberta!!!

_childDocuments_.review: PSA for fellow Steam Deck users: You should consider this Verified! The only Deck-related problem is that the game does not have Cloud Save support, so you can't just continue playing your save files on your computer unless you transfer the save file manually between each system. Bummer!!As for the game, it's far too early for me to make a judgement. All I can say as a non-VR player is that the game still feels incredibly immersive. I am not into VR since it gives me a headache, but the effect of being inside the game world is absolutely here. The environments in the game are nice (don't get it twisted, it may be a cave but I've already seen beautiful places in there) but it's the sounds that really makes you feel you are there. Love the narrator but he is being too nice!!!It's frustrating to have to wait a while before I can continue testing my ridiculous theories out of fear of activating a hint.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEW: I originally had a hard time recommending this game due to some very unintuitive puzzles and a price that felt too high. But since then, Cygnus has made enough changes to the experience (including a very reasonable new $25 price tag) that I now can give it a thumbs up — with just a few caveats.Colossal Cave is a faithful remake of a really antiquated, often frustrating, game design from the 1970s that requires tons of playthroughs to beat (or probably a walkthrough). Puzzles and exploration rely on too much random chance, just like the original.However, the folks behind this remake have made a few changes recently to give more context and allow for players to have a better shot of beating the game without turning to the internet. The original Colossal Cave offers “instructions” that leave out some pretty key information players kinda need. Thank goodness then, that the 2023 remake now finally offers (for lack of a better phrase) “instructions for the instructions” that give players MUCH better context about how the game really works. Yes, someone could look this info up online, but it’s so much more elegant when it’s built into the game like this.I’m still not a big fan of some of the underlying puzzle design (which Cygnus Entertainment leaves intact for good reason), but exploring the cave is still a treat. It’s pretty dang cool to see a formative piece of adventure game history brought up to much more modern standards. Just beware: many cave passages will not always take you where they’re supposed to, and sometimes change where you end up at random. I really don’t like this mechanic, but it’s hard to fault this edition for keeping the game design unchanged — at its core, Colossal Cave is game preservation, not a top to bottom redo.My biggest complaint of the remake is that the music and sound is very sparse, and the lack of hearing your own footsteps makes the journey feel disconnected and a bit barren. But the narrator’s terrific and adds a lot of life and zest to the journey — this remake wins big here.Overall: it’s good! Falls a little short of being “great,” but it’s much much more solid now than it was at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: When the Williams mentioned that they were starting a new project that Sierra fans would probably enjoy, remaking the game that kicked everything off for them seemed like the perfect answer.  Come see the granddaddy of adventure games where it all started and how it shaped Sierra's early adventure games.I'd played a bit of the original text adventure game from the 1970s, but didn't make it too far.  Of the text adventures I had played, the interface for the original Colossal Cave Adventure (CCA) was a little too unwieldy and clunky for what I expected, so half of the challenge was fighting with the parser.  Fortunately, this proper remake of the original strips away most of the frustrations of the original and allows the player to explore and get lost within the caves.The team did a great job in bringing this game to modern devices.  However, this version remains very true to the original, warts and all.  Because of this faithful reproduction, it does come with the same moon logic and random navigation issues that were in the original.  Still, there are a couple of clever puzzles I enjoyed, especially the use of the magic words.It is easy to see how the original game was a massive influence on the first crop of computer adventure games, many which involved hunting for treasures.  Consider the first couple of Sierra games like Mystery House, Wizard and the Princess, and the first two King's Quest games borrowed a lot of similar ideas from searching for treasure, getting past bridge trolls, dwarves, having your inventory stolen (and then you steal it back again), etc.That this game has also been ported to pretty much every modern gaming interface of today is amazing.  However, this was not just a one-and-done release, but the team responded to feedback and continued to improve upon this game,  Looking back at an early preview of this game from a year ago, one can see improved graphics, enhancements, descriptions, and additions.  If you played this game when it was first released in January 2023, give it another spin to see how things have gotten even better.Carry on intrepid adventurer, let's go spelunking!

_childDocuments_.review: [Updated review, after significant patches shipped since launch]It's important to understand what this game is and is not before playing. This is a faithful visual translation of the first text-based adventure game ever made. As such, it still contains everything that made it significant, along with much of what made it frustrating. In other words, this is essentially a time capsule created without the benefit of nearly 40 years of development in the genre. Before Mystery House and King's Quest, and even longer before Myst, there was ADVENT, a.k.a. Colossal Cave Adventure. Through those decades, Sierra, Cyan, and others defined and incrementally shaped what "Adventure" means to gaming, but it all started here—before you could point or click.If you're able to harness the nostalgic fantasy nerd inside you, go in with an open mind and lots of patience. There is fun and wonder to compliment the confusion deep in the caverns. As you take advantage of saving early and often, give thanks that you can do so, and that you're not sending "LOOK DRAGON" to a remote computer that eventually responds via teletype on physical paper :) (But seriously, save early and often.)

_childDocuments_.review: Having never played the original Colossal Cave Adventure, I didn't know if I would enjoy this remake. The first night I played it was thrilling (I got jump scared by dwarves, a pirate, and a snake many times) and was able to progress through the game organically through discovery and trial and error, just like the old adventure games I know and love. It took a while to get used to these particular point-and-click controls, and the game lacks some features I hoped it would have (more voice acting, more music, more interactivity in general) but I've played this game every day since I've purchased it and I plan to keep up that habit until I hit the max score. Happy to have Roberta and Ken back in the game industry, and hope there are more projects to come!
