_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun arcade racer, but I feel like the AI is just programmed unfairly.  Once you get behind 5 or 6 seconds from a leader it just seems like you cannot catch them no matter what.  Even using the boost which should be a pretty cheap way to get there, but just useless.  I feel like driving the track well just isn't rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Looks kinda cute and there's a certain wit to the game, but unfortunately it completely fails at what it wants to be: a racing game. Now, maybe I'm just not getting the 90s games homage, but the least I can ask for is *racing*. All I get though is teabagging. The AI can't seem to pour out a bucket of water, and despite the bulletpointed "adaptive difficulty", that just never changes. I went 13 GP into the career and unless I manage to run out of fuel or hit the inside walls too often on Cote d'Azur, I dump the AI by 15+ seconds at every 6-lap race. I would complain about how the AI doesn't even seem to change the finishing order between themselves a lot, and how I'm not sure why the game doesn't go for 2-car teams and slightly larger grids, but if you're running away that hard it doesn't even matter.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Has a ton of potential, and I bought it for the Virtua Racing vibe... but the controls are too touchy for me unfortunately.  They are like a light switch, either on or off.   But if I see thats fixed at a later date I will come back as the game looks pretty neat.I am saying NO to recommend it... but keep in mind the controls may not bug others... so its up to you.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was something else. Seems all the people into it are more into the team building management part of the game. The actual driving falls short from what I wanted. All I was expecting was something in the ballpark of Virtua Racing but this is extremely basic, more like you generally guide the car around the track and match the corner speed to what is expected. No physics model to speak of at all, arcade or realistic.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but almost everything about it annoys me. There's two good things about this game, for starters it runs great on Linux through proton, but that's more of a nod to proton, and second, the amount of texture detail in the splash screen in contrast to the rest of the game gives me a good chuckle, likely unintentional. Now for the bad, the menus look like it was pulled from a mobile game, the noises your pit crew dude make are stupid(awkward phoned-in voice overs from the devs would at least be endearing), the arcadey nature of the game paired with fuel and tire strategy is perplexing at best, doubly so when there is no manual transmission option, and don't you even think about cutting a corner, because this arcade game is serious business and will slow you down. It sucks that I can't get past all this to experience the effort that was put into the career mode.I went into this expecting Virtua Racing, but with more courses and extra stuff, but what I got was a $30 mobile game. Guess that's what happens when all the reviews I watched were from easily impressed switch-guys who have been stricken with the faux-nostalgia cancer of thinking low poly games equal good.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game's core career mode concept of starting in the past and working your way forward through time to the present day is something I've always wanted from a NASCAR game. F1 is obviously the exact opposite of that, but it's still cool to see someone finally make this type of game. It's also exceptionally rare for an arcade racer to have a proper career mode, so that's doubly cool. I don't really vibe with is the flat textured graphical style, but that's entirely subjective. The multiplayer is a little confusing, my friend and I had a hard time getting a lobby set up, and we didn't know that you have to unlock content in multiplayer because the game doesn't tell you, so we wasted a lot of time trying to figure out how to change the track layouts. We both bought the game mainly for career mode though, so it's not that big of a deal, just something worth mentioning. Oh yeah, the game actually has wheel support too, but there's no FFB, just centering spring. I don't think a game like this needs FFB at all, but I know for a lot of people that's a deal breaker, so there's your heads up.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to learn, fiendishly difficult to master, brutal on the joints in your fingers if you play for long enough with a controller, this is '90s sim/arcade hybrid racing right out of a PS1 game or the old Virtua Racing family of arcade machines. But it doesn't coast on nostalgia, even if you're way too young to remember the '90s there's a lot to love even in the present day. A change of pace from the full-sim F1 or Assetto Corsa experience or a "daily driver" in its own right, there is a LOT to love here. One of the best games I've played in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Retro graphics that look good and work extremely well at high frame rates, and fast paced racing with an addictive career makes this one an instant classic. The game has character and atmosphere that is lacking in many higher budget and higher fidelity racing games, and the player is presented with good racing action with meaningful strategic choices despite the short length of the races. Good stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. Quite funny in naming people and circuits. Personally prefer this over the hyperrealism of other racing games. Only annoyance I could find is having to re-do an entire season before progressing to another era in carreer mode. I get that that's sort-of the game, but I'd like the option to just re-do the races I didn't finish in first.It's not really a game for the big race-game fans, but a silly little racing game for those who just enjoy playing a silly little game from time to time. 6/7 would reccommend.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooooo good. Controls rock and the racing is fun. The graphics look awesome but what surprised me was how great the audio is. The sound of the race cars, the track ambience, and the music are superb. The simple car upgrades and the team management is fun too.There’s a few things I wish this game had, but I don’t think it’s getting updates anymore. A replay mode and a photo mode would be nice. Manual gearbox would be fun too. The writing is funny, but it would do well with some additional lines to make it less repetitive. BUT!! It’s really really fun. I am glad I bought this video game :3
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great racing game that captures a lot of the thrill and the amazing moments of F1 racing.Not too arcadey - but certainly not a simulation. As a non-wheel racing gamer, this was just the right mixture.The career mode is fun and it's really enjoyable to go through the decades of F1, even though the "difficulty increase" throughout the decades feels more forced than needed.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent F1 game in the same vein as Virtua Racing from the 90s. If you remember that you'll like this a lot. Especially given how well the computer controlled NPCs are programmed to respond and block, tail, and evade you. Also the little emoticons that pop up above the NPCs gives you a good idea of how they're driving/responding to how the race is going.  Ironically better programmed that a lot of supposed triple A racing games, where not a single one tries to cut you off, almost like they're too embarassed! Whereas here they'll tailgate into corners, touch fenders, and even have spectacular blowouts midway through the race and you have to avoid their cars which have subseequently spun out. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Man.... i gotta say, this game took me completely by surprise. i think i discovered this game from some random youtube video and decided to give this a shot, especially since it was on sale. Let me just say this game wowed me! This genre of retro racers sadly has been cursed with developers not delivering on whats promised or being stuck in development hell or games getting cancelled out right. But this game, im glad saw the light of day. Its polished, its straight to the point, its got depth and inspiration from modern games, its surprisingly lengthy and cars have some levels of customization. This was totally worth every penny and if these devs take on another racing game ill absolutely keep and eye on it, Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun, an engaging combo of retro-esque graphics, recognisable yet legally-distinct-to-real-life tracks, and a surprisingly in-depth career mode - permanent and temporary upgrades, staff management, car wear and damage, and AI that will fight back if you hit them into the wall one too many times through a season. It's a bit on the easier side if you have experience with racing games, but if the microtransaction-riddled hellscape of modern big-budget racing games is getting you down, this is a great game to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is a very good looking and sounding Arcade type racing game. It took me a few hours to get used to the steering and braking using my x box controller. I have just finished 99/99 laps of Naples GP and that gave me lots of experience of the steering and how the car behaves and pitting and fitting new tyre types and re fuel and servicing the shocks and engine and brakes.Also the weather changes and it looks very colourful and lots of gorgeous detail, like the on screen map of the course and the lap time and caution messages to warn me I need to pit and re fuel or change tyres.I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS GAME FOR A ARCADE TYPE RACING EXPERIENCE.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. One of the most fun racing game I've played in years. I enjoy the arcade physics; there is a lot of depth to them.It's a great pick up and play game, you can just hop on for a race or two.They did a great job with the tracks. Each track has a unique feel that carries over from the real life track.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: 55 hours of solid entertainment in the hardest difficulty. Got this game because I had a bad F1 itch and I'm still saving up for good sim racing gear, this definitely scratched that F1 itch. Fuel and Tires make a difference in the outcome, teaches F1 strategy, great physics, reminds me of the Early F1 games that I used to play as a kid. Great game to practice proper racing line, and reflexes as well.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches that Virtua Racing aesthetic itch, with a nice layer of upgrades on top. Also features team social dynamics that are a bit weird, like you get an option of going to the cinema with the commercial manager or the pit boss and one of them is gonna get pissed and might leave the team if too unhappy... weird, but charming and manageable. Very arcade-y handling, but in a good way. Lots of races and different types of events too, not just GPs. Recommended especially for Deck owners, it's a great 15min at a time game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic arcade style F1 game, that has a surprising amount of depth to it. I love this game since I find Codemasters F1 games to be a lot more fun on wheel, and have been looking for racing games that are designed for game pads that still have some level of depth to it. Really love how you can feel the car become sluggish with higher fuel loads, or how you lose grip as tyres or the bodywork degrades. The rival system is also a really awesome addition that makes it so other drivers you bump wheels with on track become more aggressive to you.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I like racing games, used to play sims but now I just want to play arcade racing from time to time without a sweat. This game is good for that. It can require some skills and knowledge if you play on pro difficulty. But there is also normal difficulty which is quite simple to beat. There are also rewinds if you are too bad :) Maybe this game is not for tryhards. - Car handling is basic but I like it in general although there is no manual gearing. There is a speed boost that you can use- You can upgrade your car in the career mode- There are also perks that you can also use that can improve slip streams, starts and whatnot.- You doing pits and choosing pit strategy here- Circuits are mini versions of real tracks, so you can recognize some corners- There are quite a lot to do in a career mode (although I'm not used to play for long in one game and I playing short sessions so for some it wouldn't seem a lot maybe).- In the career mode you obviously racing gran prix but without qualification (you are starting last), there is also few more mods like: hot laps, check points, elimination mode that goes before gran prix and will prepare you to it kind of.- There is also hot lap competition with real players I believe but I didn't try it.All in all - nice racing game to chill, have fun and also have some challenges if you will.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is a near perfect blend of arcade racing with a sim mindset. While sparse in some areas, it is well fleshed out and considered in all the right places. 4 player couch co-op is so much fun! Somehow my friends and I were evenly matched despite our varying skills at racing and/or video games. Online multiplayer would beyond the Hot Lap mode would put this game on another level.I would love to know more information about the mechanics of the game be it in the descriptions menu or a wiki. On this note, more flexibility in setting up championship races would also be cool. Things like saved racer profiles, keeping rain on for the whole race, number of cars on track, and a reverse version of both short and long tracks would be great. The ability to modify tire deg. would also be blessed. Sometimes I want to race 20 laps but I don't want to pit 7 times on softs.The campaign menus are a bit un-intuitive but I got used to them. Some more flexible car/helmet customization would also be cool. Think bare-bones version of Forza. All in all this is a fantastic game and will keep you booting it up for some casual fast laps well into the 10's of hours after you've finished the Campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, the graphics are fun, it's light. It's not an intensive game to run, i'm currently running it on my Windows PC, BUT also on my Mac M1 using Crossover. Runs a treat, with my configured 8BitDo controller. I'm only talking career here, I have never played a racing game before in my life, for real. I wanted to pick up something light to have a story mode on. So everything below here is career based. I'm currently 10 hours in, and have just begun the 2000 season (So probably 40%? Through career)The decades as season progression is great, it makes sense. I really like that with the phone call tunes changing and the vehicle chassis changing, fantastic little elements in there.It's easy to pick up and play, there's not much confusing mechanics/buttons to remember. You don't need to know any technical details to play the game. Heck, I didn't and it's great to play. The modes are fun and keep it fresh for each map, in each season. The driver relationships are great, these should be involved in the phone call options. Where you can choose to hang out/do something with one of the other drivers, if you look at F1 motorsports (Real life that is), those drivers are friends and some are rivals. So yeah, introduce them into the phone call options a bit more to build/reduce relationships. Customisation is fun, I wish there was more sponsorship decals really, because F1 cars are plastered in decals. With so many helmet styles in player customisation, probably worth clicking/selecting the helmet styles to open another sub-menu which tiles into squares, with a small thumbnail for each design. There's too many to flick through one at a time and I would've forgotten the number or design I liked without having to scroll through -aaaallll- of them again.Things for the dev to work on so far, the 1990 season, Canada, Quebec track. Exiting the pit lane forces the player to break as it's on 'auto-pilot' until dropping you off to face a barrier. Nah. No. That shouldn't happen, something needs sorting out there. A player shouldn't have to break as a first instinct coming out of the pit. Auto-drive it past the first bend maybe? Because you can't change the track or release them from the pit sooner, that defeats the object of it being like the tracks. Qualifying... I get it's a light-hearted formula' genre game. But starting 10th every time sort of sucks. A perk get's you to 9th but is really useless with other perks being better and boosting at the start to pass 9th anyway. I think there should be some time trial to qualify and then the perk could be remade to +1 starting position to whatever you qualified for. And it could also be random, you could qualify and not know other's times and at the end there could be some % chance that a player beat you. (So you're not always 1st qualifying and 1st winning as that would get boring)Other than that though, i'm seriously loving this game. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: really cool f1 racing with some light management elements. there's staff that provide buffs to race day, on the track or in the active pit lane, or engage with your  sponsors to boost your income. the racing is tight and responsive from the jump and steadily gets faster as you progress through the decades kind of like mario kart CC difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun Arcade F1 Racing game. I love how it gets more difficult after your first season in each decade. The AI becomes more advanced, some AI drivers admire you and wont drive dirty, some AI despise you and will ram you to ruin a podium position. Some AI drivers suddenly get the car upgrades they need and leave you 6 seconds behind with no hopes of catching up. There's tire changing, parts repair, and re-fueling in the pit stops. You have to be wise of when to pit, how much fuel you're carrying, tire conditions, weather. It's all a lot of fun and somewhat immersive after you get your first season out of the way. I would love to see the Devs make a Rally game with the team management from this game and maybe more upgrade/downgrade options for your car, and see their take on snow and muddy roads. I think they would crush it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Hi everyone,Should this game be in your Steam collection ? YES and a thousand times YES !.I haven't encountered any bugs. The graphics are great and the gameplay is incredible, I have a lot of fun beating my own times / playing in career mode or custom championship.This game is well worth the asking price, the quality is impeccable, the cars from 1980 to 2020 and the sound is top too, the circuits are quite detailed, the developers are attentive to updates .There is already a lot of content but I hope that, in the future, there will be even more!  American competition ? karting? Manager mod ? nascar ? more race ? i hope.I'm a complete fan and I admit that I'm probably not very objective, however I really don't have any faults to highlight, it 's just a VERY GOOD game !Buy it for dozens of hours of fun against decent AI and players from around the world !!!Have fun ! sorry for my basic english !
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unbridled unmitigated good fun. The racing is not SUPER technical but it's really rewarding. Definitely you don't need to be some sim racing guru to play it and pretty much anyone can pick up a controller and have a great time. But as someone who DOES own a full racing rig and is really into my driving, I also still find it really fun and a blast. Basically, New Star just really know what they're doing and this is definitely worth the money. Would be great to see some online multiplayer in there, too, any maybe some longer endurance racers and definitely some harder AI. But honestly even just for a casual pick and play it's really great.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I must say this all I wanted for a arcade racing game for my steamdeck. Not overly complicated, quick and action packed races, tire wear, pit stops, easy to learn but hard to master. I wish more people would notice this game. As a motorsports fan, I'm actually surprise how long I took to notice this. This game is amazing. Props to the devs, you made something special here,
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: When i booted this game up I really had no idea how damn hooked I'd get.I played the whole first campaign of races and came to 4 hours later realizing this game was probably the most fun i'd had racing in a long time, if not ever.Controls are less sim, more arcade; however theres light sim touches light improved parts, managing the team to get money/pit stop/engineer perks.Cannot recommend enough.Scratches the F1 Itch SO GOOD
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches all the right itches. It's a great racing game without being too far on either end of the Arcade/Simulator spectrum. The cars feel fun to drive and are quite responsive. The game doesn't take itself too seriously, you'll see the headlines between a few races here and there and the content is pretty funny. If you find that EA's F1 is a bit more than you can stomach on the Simulation side, this game tones it down to a digestible level. They start you off with very little complexity and then steadily increase it.I would say i'm surprised that this isn't more popular, but this game doesn't have actual online multiplayer - which, to me, is likely a large contributor to its lesser popularity. However, it does have split-screen PVP which can be hard to find these days, especially for PC games.If you enjoy racing on your own, pick this game up. It's worth every dime.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly pretty great. It is F1 racing for casuals. And with that in mind, it features something that is missing in a lot of other racing games - FUN! I've just been having pure fun playing this. Hats off to the team. I'd love to see them come out with a GT3 racing game just like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the price of entry. Incredibly underrated.My rival started getting madder and madder at me because I bumped him ONCE on the first GP. Fast forward 5 GP's and he challenges me to a 1 on 1. He loses badly. In retribution, he repaints my car the night before the final into a beautiful white/pink which I took 1st in. He finished the season with 0 points.Mustachioed prick lmao. Everyone else on the grid admired me.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are finicky at best. The pit stop could use some reworking. The idea of a boost is fun but takes away from the F1 simulator aspect of things. I like that the AI tries to 'defend' the corner but not much is done for when they're 'attacking' the corner. The pit-stop strategizing seems to have little to no effect or any real benefits for one or the other in the end. Slip-streams shouldn't be a perk but just an overall aspect. Overall, a fun game to pick up, mess around with, and practice racing lines when you're bored, but, not something I can see myself sinking tons of hours on.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Big time recommend from me. It's kind of like a rogue-like f1 arcade racing game. The meta game (game outside of the racing) is cool, the way it sets up different events for each race weekend in career mode is really fun. The racing is a really nice blend of simulation and arcade, and introduces some light f1 racing strategy in a fun way that's easy to learn even if you don't follow the sport. The local split screen is great too.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game for F1 fans that just want to zone out and relax. Literally the only 2 complaints I have is that the 2 eras I played had the exact same engine noise, and there is no option for manual shifting (which would be amazing if the devs add it). Otherwise a genuinely fun game for something so simple
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I own Horizon Chase Turbo with Sena. I think it would be the same so I did not need this game.For fun I also own Hotwheels.I must admit that all three games are fine. Even if you own Horizon Chase Turbo, you have in New Star GP (1) the Pit management and (2) much more detailed circuits and in more numbers (than Horizon Chase Turbo) (3) without headhaches (In Horizon you can soon become sick if you play to much due to the game speed on screen). New Star GP remains an arcade game with a mini simulation touch.(4) Another big advantage : this is easily playable without any jerk on an old PC (7 Years old) using an NVidia GTX 1060 6GB RAM, on triple screen configuration (3 x 2560*1440 aka WQHD) using Apple Cinema LED Diplay at 60 Htz refresh rate.(5) More important : this is fun. Do you need a simulation game after a hard day's work ? For my part no. I just need to relax without any hassle.(6) Graphically speaking, this is really top, an arcadish look but this remains pretty to look at.Developpers said it was compatible with a Logitech Wheel. I own a G29, this is not ideal since you cannot set up the wheel in game (OK I could use Logitech profiler but developpers instructions would be welcome...) and you are forced to use the keyboard in menus. Use a gamepad, this is what the game is designed for (keyboard is never needed). WIth Microsoft Elite 2 gamepad, this works flawlessly.Purchase the game for 20 € max, then you make a profitable investment.Sole regrets : a) the game needs an update since the game asks you to use A button instead of X button in menus, so it is not 100% perfect.b) the impossibility to select a circuit and to do a race out of career mode (in solo mode, unless I have missed something). You need to enter career mode to play it but once done, this is over you cannot start again, you have to play the 9 other races of the season..., only then the circuit becomes playable again in solo mode.c) The rewind mode is not clear even with a pad (you click on a button for Rewind, then you have toi use the mouse to go back exactly where you wanted). I would have preferred a button to restart a race, period.But this is a funny game which will bring you fun even on low end hardware (even if a 7 years old PC is not totally obsolete).
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mixture of elements that work better as the sum of their parts. Each of the aspects of the game is greatly simplified, but that allows for a fun and engaging experiecing that you can pick up for a little while or for a long sitting. In essence, in this game you act as the manager of a F1 team and also as their driver, so yuo execute everything: from upgrades to the car, to the overtakes on track. But since none of it is really complex, what sounds complicated in turn is very easy and fun.I love that you can trash talk other drivers and then they will mad with you and try to crash you (Nigel Mansgwen who?), or you can have a respectable rivarly with them. I also love that with the upgrades you do feel the car being faster and faster throughout the season, which also adds a bit of difficulty spike.Perhaps the aspect I like the least about the game is the driving. It's fun and arcadey but I almost never feel in danger during the races. The opponents are very slow, and I can end up winning a GP by 20 seconds. Perhaps this was my fault for choosing the normal difficulty rather than the Pro one, so developers should add the option to change difficulty once you start the carreer mode!!!All in all a fun game that's perfect on the Steam Deck (and I will probably get it for my phone as well lol)
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to racing games, I mostly play management/sim style but have played a few where you are driver like this (Circuit Superstars and Project Cars come to mind).  With that in mind, I'm not judging the management/development part of this game since it's obviously very simple in an arcade driving game like this.The steering is super easy which I appreciate, and even on the harder mode it's pretty easy to do well.  The game looks okay, and if you're looking for an arcade-y open-wheel racing game, you could certainly do worse.  Don't expect much depth, and do expect arcade-style action (there is a boost button and a rewind button), but I've had some fun with it.  This will probably be a steam-deck game for me for short plays, but if you like arcade racers then it's worth a shot (preferably on sale - I got for $17.99 which feels just a bit high until I think about how that wouldn't buy a McDonalds meal, and then it seems like a fair price :-P).
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hell of a lot of fun and I enjoyed playing this - this is my first time with the game and true first impressions (  ).Glad I brought this and if you like Virtua Racing, you are going to love this on the PC.Controls are really good, game is really good and it have a lovely mode that eases you into how it works with the tutorial.My video does not show the current patch that released, it was recorded a day or so before that.  I highly recommend this if you want a tight arcade racing game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: its fun, the controls are tight and upgrading/customizing your car is fun despite lacking depth. supposedly there's adaptive difficulty as you play through the career but im not seeing any improvement from the ai.after three races, i stopped doing the events and racing the track blind. im still blasting everyone. i dont think the ai even uses boost.so .. knowing you're gunna win every single race with little to zero resistance makes this a no from me. even the neat features like dynamic events and perks and stuff kind of fall flat, they're not as cool as they sound.id keep this game for 9.99 or even 14.99 but i paid 17.99 on sale and im considering refunding it, it's definitely not worth the full 29.99
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: You should know that by being a racing driver you are under risk all the time. Being a racing driver means you are racing with other people and if you no longer go for a gap that exists you are no longer a racing driver because we are competing, we are competing to win and the main motivation to all of us is to compete for the victory, it is not to conserve for a fifth or sixth place.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this a try on the strength of the endearing retro visual style, and found a deeper open-wheel racing game than I expected, while being thoroughly accessible. Altogether, a breath of fresh air in the circuit racing genre.The driving, set to some great original music, feels good and definitely leans toward arcade racing. For instance, while real-world F1 cars have a Kinetic Energy Recovery System that provides a short-duration burst of power, the equivalent here works much more like your typical boost button. There is a racing line displayed to guide the player. And while crashes will damage the car and impact performance, they're far more forgiving than in the really diehard racing simulations.But what surprised me is how, without any of it seeming like a chore, the game works in details like fueling, tire, and pitting strategy. And racing team management, which is accomplished with a very intuitive menu interface. Feeling, even to someone like me who has never engaged with a racing team management sim, just like something you naturally do between races.At the moment, I'm dominating the early GP races in the career mode, which spans from the 1980s to the 2000s and from what I've read, may be expanded further. While I've largely been relying on an aggressive one-pit strategy, the game has already cautioned me that the difficulty is adaptive, so the better I perform, the more competitive other teams will get on the track and in the paddock. Reflecting rather well the automotive arms race that is classic F1 racing.This also means that, quite surprisingly, I find myself investing more in my crew and less in upgrades to the car. Building a team to last, rather than squeezing every last drop of performance out of the car to pad out my margin of victory. Which is very much not what I expected going in. But it was a pleasant surprise to find such depth in a game with these lovely retro arcade visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely banging game. I bought this because of the positive reviews on a whim and was not disappointed. I love the arcadey physics but with pit stops, fuel loads, tyre wear and all that it still gives the feeling and relative flow of an F1 race. The championship mode is great.The tracks are incredible, despite being unique they are still excellent representations of the actual tracks, with certain corners, whole sectors, or even just a vibe being so accurate to the game. And playing at my home track you could really see the attention to detail in the tracks.I hope this game gets the support it deserves, I can see this game and these devs building a strong community. Hopefully there is plenty more to come out of this game and these devs!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: For the same price as Le Mans Ultimate, you get a proper, fun game. Which LMU isn't. Seriously though, despite it's unashamedly arcade style, New Star GP has everything that should be included in 'real' sims: Full Career mode, hotlaps with leaderboards, and individual championships.Then there's the management side: hiring and firing staff, and trying to keep them happy (an impossible task), press conferences and full customisation of cars. The rivalry idea is fun: if you trash talk an opponent in the press conference, or run them off the road, they'll come after you in a big way. All in all, a great title that every sim could learn from.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: having loads of fun with this. great little f1 game that simulates all the aspects of that type of racing, from crew management to sponsorship to pitstops in an arcadey and quick, non time consuming way (eg: short ~6 lap races but the tires wear out in only a couple laps)my one major gripe to the devs: make the dials and mirrors in work in cab view!!!!!super lightweight on memory and graphics as well so great for low budget low spec which i appreciate greatly
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic racing game. The art style is fun and the game's atmosphere is really upbeat thanks to the soundtrack. The overall experience with a controller is pretty flawless. I am using a Logitech F710 wireless.The game play is simple, gas, brake, go. FYI, there is currently no manual transmission option as this was designed as an arcade racer. I know, arcade racers do sport MT but, that where this game is and seems like it will stay. I'm good with that, if I want more realism i can play one of the racing sim games I have. Where this game becomes more is in the perks you select for your crew, managing your winnings to upgrade your car and be prepared for random events that pop up. Pit strategy also plays a role. Will you select hard or soft tires? How well can you handle your car on a full tank? Handling deteriorates with a heavier fuel load. Also, check the weather before a race, is that rain on the horizon? When should you pit to switch to wet tires? Also, can you hit the gas at the right moment to have a perfect start off the grid?If you are looking for a fun and simple F1 racing game, this is the one.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, everything I want in a retro racing game.  It plays and feels like a 1980's racer game but is so much better with career mode, upgrades and smother but retro graphics.I absolutely love it.  I am half way through the first season in the career mode.  I can't say enough about how awesome it is.  I have only played on arcade settings and don't know if I care to try realistic since arcade is so good.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game all round. Makes you feel like Ayrton Senna!Nice meta game with fast pace chunks of progression and fun little decisions to make between events. Very nice graphics, giving that proper Virtua Racing vibe through and through. Polished and quick loading so the action never lets up. Plays wonderfully on the Steam Deck too. It’s very arcadey (obviously) but you still need to drive it properly, just that it’s quite forgiving but none the less satisfying for it. The complexity is pitched perfectly for the aim of the atmosphere of the game, with enough depth and nuance to the handling and the races without being frustrating or feeling dumbed down. Very nicely done. Nice selection of events to mix it up (with changing weather + puddles that you need to adapt your strategy and driving to, as well as look after your tyres and consider the best time to use the KERS boost) and confidently presented overall. Above all, it’s just plain FUN and I’m excited to progress through the next years in the game and see how it pans out. I have not even arrived at “Monaco” yet in the first year (and there is TONS more content here to explore) but I felt completed enough to write this review, so it must be good!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I want to refund this game so I can buy it back at full price because they deserve my money.  After a few hours of this (and 36 seasons Retro Bowl) I don't know if New Star Games gets me, or just gets gaming in general.  They definitely hit that sweet spot of an easy learning curve, but enough depth to keep you coming back.  It's hard to put your finger on exactly what New Star does so well, but there's something fundamental that they understand about what makes games fun that so many companies miss.  It's that magic that Nintendo captured during the Wii era:  yes, you can make phenomenally good games that are wildly technologically inferior to everything else out there.  I absolutely hate the low-poly aesthetic of the mid-90's graphics, but somehow I don't even notice it when I'm playing, because it just fits.  Everything about the game is polished and considered.  Every element was clearly chosen and created by people who actually play games, not a bunch of boardroom clowns with marketing degrees.  I haven't played EA's F1 (the most common comparison), but I'd way rather be playing this than Forza.  Sure, Forza wins the beauty contest.  Hundreds of cars...but how many are actually enjoyable to drive?  Hundreds of tracks...how many are actually fun to race on?  And don't get me started on the train wreck of a menu system, seasons (welp, it's winter again, guess I'll have to wait till next week to play), broken physics, and awful grinding.  I guess the moral of the story is that something simple, done correctly, is vastly superior to something complex, but done poorly.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game!After hundreds of hours in the official F1 games, as well as Motorsport Manager and its mobile variants, I think I finally found a new kick. Sure, New Star GP is no simulation but it’s still a lot of fun. The game combines driving with managing your own F1 Team through the decades. You start in the 80s and work your way up to the modern era of F1. The driving is not very challenging but mistakes are punished, so it’s quite appealing still and can lead to occasionally exciting races. The AI is not helping sometimes, pulling unforseeable (and also quite illegal) moves but all in all the racing is fun. The other part is the management aspect, which you could describe as F1 Manager LIGHT. It’s not very deep but you can I.e. determine strategies, upgrade your aero, engine, suspension, or even do occasional publicity stunts with the help of your public relations manager. While we are at the point of crew members, they can provide the team with helpful perks, that make your racing easier or earn you more money after a victory. All in all this is a really fun game, that will surely keep me playing for the next 20-50 hours. It’s also very light on resource consumption, so it can run several hours on the steam deck. Tl;dr:Can recommend this for every arcade racing and gp team management fan.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying it a lot so far, there are not many good arcade racers out there now and this is a good one. I like the aggressive AI and the general feel of the game gives me nostalgic flashbacks to the early Micropose Grand Prix series, which is no bad thing. I'm only two hours in and although I'm enjoying the game, a full price of £24.99 I do wonder if it is priced about £5 too high. I bought it on offer at £14.99 and at that money it is definitely fair.Improvements on my wish list are, in the following order: 1) Online multiplayer 2) Bigger grid sizes in a race/bigger circuits to accommodate them.   3) More intelligent/gambles from AI on strategy.  4) The ability to change the names of teams and drivers
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Really really fun! Delivers on being a retro styled arcade racer with a lot more depth than I was expecting. The more I play the more I'm sold on the game.If i had to have a gripe it would be for more cosmetic customization for the cars in a future update (like sponsorship text color or helmet colors). Would also love to change difficulty during the career mode, I realized after one season I needed to switch to the higher difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Arent the devs of Wreckfest going to be upset that these devs stole the AI programming?Seriously though, its a fun update on a retro style arcade racer. Enough depth to the in-between-race choices to keep you engaged and the races can become chaotic enough to make you want to get back to the in-between stuff before you tear your hair out in frustration over the ludicrous AI shenanigans. Balanced...as all things should be.Its fun having decades of cars that actually feel dynamic in their era, 80s feel planted but a bit slow, 90s ultra-fast and slightly unwieldy in a fun way, etc.Will it satisfy hardcore sim racers? Shut up, nerd. Pick up a controller and embrace this arcady break from soul crushing realism and actually have some fun.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Love when games balance "sim" aspects into an arcade base, this game brings that together with an entertaining career mode where you manage your team and sometimes watch chaos ensue as well a custom championship mode for replay value afterwards. Basically you can kick back after a long day but still feel like you are actually racing, nice presentation, has some pit strategy mixed in, and best of all it's funny. Full recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I had been looking for a good racing game for a long time and there just weren't that many good options (imo) until this one came out earlier this year. It is exactly what I was looking for and been one of the games I pick up to play whether I have 30  minutes, or a few hours. The racing is fun, and goes to show that you don't need an exact replica of real life to get the excitement of a good race. It's fairly arcadey, so if you're more into the sim aspect, it's probably not for you, but there is a surprising amount of depth in the main game mode, and with only 6 laps per GP, it makes you want to do just one more race. Highly recommend - have not found a game by this dev that I do not like yet.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Very good arcade F1 career game. In career you go through 80s cars, then 90s and all the way to 2020. There's a multiplayer race option but it's only local or with Remote Play Together.The races are quick and the gameplay is very simple and sometimes silly - in a good way. You will be able to recognize all the tracks and they have multiple layouts. To upgrade your car you not only need to do the GPs but also side events. For example an elimination race, checkpoints time trial, reverse track race, etc.All in all I would recommend this. Plays very well also on Steam Deck. For $30 it is a bit steep. I got it for $18 and I'd say it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a refreshing game, it has a surprising amount of depth to the gameplay. Most importantly though, it's never boring.I love all the on track action, the short races with pit stops, the fact that tire temps, wear, and fuel weight is simulated.There is just so much packed into this game, worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Believe the hype from the reviews, this game is insanely fun. Think the arcade thrill of Virtua Racing with a great campaign mode that lets you upgrade your car, manage crew, unlocking perks, weather such as rain, and pit choices such as tire and fuel strategy. Multiple camera options is the cherry on top. Definitely worth a purchase. With that said, be prepared for the difficulty to rise considerably as you progress further.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game It's already one of my favorite racing games of all time. It's EXACTLY what I was looking for in an Arcade Racing game. A surprisingly good amount of depth in a fun arcade racer package, nuanced with some realistic sim-style characteristics. The career mode is great with progression through different eras and building rivalries with the AI characters (who have comically similar names to real life F1 icons), and there is a nice focus on car development and team management to boot too.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is more than just a racing game, it's a celebration and a heartfelt tribute to the world of Formula 1. It's clear that the developers are fans themselves, and their love for the sport is evident in every aspect of the game. It's the game F1 fans deserve, and it's an absolute joy to experience.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, defnitely recommend. However for the devs just a couple things to make it a bit better. Unfortunately right now there is no manual gearbox so a setting for that would be great. There is also no option to change the bindings for controller. Fixing those two things I believe would make it pretty much a perfect game.Thank you New Star for never failing us xoxo
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Amazing Idea. The cars and gameplay are insteresting and a lot of good Ideas. But pleeaase... seriously? reverse races? It´s a anti-pattern for racing games, even arcades. Worse on a f1 one... is a signal that's something is wrong. You got one race more of gameplay time for track... in a incredible horrible event, with the AI hitting you all the time, bad pit entrances and exits and you even won't give me 100% of the credits for the race if I use flashback? Now if the AI hits me in a corner that surely was not made to be run in that direction in the last lap I need to restart the entire thing. Great. Let´s do it like 10 times, shaw we? Every...time... It became the type of event it´s not fun to do. I'm a completionist but I'm gonna start skipping those or I will stop playing the game.And the crew is like the most needy and tiresome ever. Play it for laughs then if you must but in the way it is now is just bad. It´s better than before, but surely it has space to improvments. Like events and bonuses. Not only well paid adults in a winning team crying and leaving all the time.This game is too good to have such idiotic problems. Please Devs, keep the development. Would love to have manual shift for the gears too.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Something strange happens in this game: it happens that you might like rough steering.I asked for a refund twice because the steering didn't convince me and today I repurchased it for the second time (bought for the third time) and I am convinced that this steering is perfect in this game. I never thought I would like On/Off steering.I never even thought I would like turbo in a game.No element of this game was placed by chance, everything comes together beautifully. Nothing is out of place.Everything is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little arcade F1 racer with suprisingly good handling and depth. The main things i like about it:- presentation.- sound design.- how the career mode is set up.- you can upgrade your cars and the upgrades are noticable.The main things i dislike:- nemesis system isnt implemented in a fun way.- perk system is due for a qol fix, its kinda unclear how it works at first.- the addition of a perk that allows GP restarts is a serious negative point for me, this takes away from the immersion in a big way, i really hate it.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A fun racing & management game with just enough simulation elements to make it immersive and challenging. One thing I've always loved about New Star Games is their approach to teaching new players: the tutorial is built into the game so you can learn as you go. No need to read walls of text or complete a separate tutorial "mission" beforehand.At $30 it's not the cheapest game, but it's worth it. Many different tracks and racing eras to explore (even though I'm mainly a fan of the 90s - yes, I'm getting old).
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Pretty good, Very grippy physics. Pit strategy is kinda interesting but feels extremely rigid as in 99% of the time it's pit on laps 2 and 4 or once on lap 3, It's almost never a good idea to try to push an extra lap. I feel like it would be a bit more interesting if there were 7 laps and there was a bit more pit strategy flexibility maybe adding medium tire compound would help. Tracks are based on real life tracks which I found charming.I don't think it's perfect but it's a very solid and unique arcade racer with light management aspects which is quite enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: This game is VERY fun. I like how you progress through the eras. I like how  its realistic, but has some details that arent. The only thing that I dont like is that if you go off the track, all your speed is gone. You can go from 150 to 75 in a second. This also happens when you are fighting someone and you barley dip a tire in the grass. But, overall, the game is very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome hommage to Formula 1 - you feel how much love has been put into this game, I really love it! The tracks are so greatly designed, that you know very fast which original track it should be. Same for the fake drivers - very funny! :)The only thing I hope to be worked on is the difficulty. Started with the normal difficulty, the first season was way too easy. Won every race by more than 20 seconds. Hoped that the second season gets more difficult, but same for the first race. So I started a new career in the pro mode and well, it's not that harder. Winning is pretty easy, now with around 5 to 10 seconds in front. It still makes a lot of fun to me, but would be greater if the races were more challenging, as the rest of the game is soo great!Some little bugs / general things:- KI drivers are breaking / slowing down for the pit entrance, where I can simply go full speed into the box. This is one big problem regarding the easiness of the game I guess, because every pit stop you can save a lot of time against the KI- Saw some cars crashing in the box in rainy conditions- Tyres: Wet tyres in dry conditions didn't feel like a time loss at all. Of course this is an arcade game, but I think the tyres in general could influence the cars behaviour more
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A fun retro looking arcade F1 racing game that looks simple on the surface but has some deeper mechanics that you wouldn't expect. Such as damage, fuel weight, a nemesis/rival system, crew choices, random events during the seasons, interactive pit stops, wear on parts other than just the tires, and dynamic weather. It's not perfect, but I can't think of anything that it's "bad" at.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of Super Monaco GP on the Megadrive and also F1 Exhaust Heat on the SNES. Loving this game, very fun to just pick up and play and very reminiscent of arcade racers of old. Highly recommended. It could do with a bit more pace though and a sense of more speed, without boost, the cars can feel quite slow, but the visuals are just so awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice arcade racing game with an unexpected depth in racing and strategy. Its more fun to play than most auf the current racing games with a good humor.Its still in development and im excited for the upcoming addations. I hope there will be some more mechanics for racing, the career and more general content.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Played this one at the Gameforce Indie-boot and immediately purchased it afterwards!It not only brings back the feeling of the original Grand Prix 2 all the way from '96 but also incorporates today's features like events, upgrades, crew interaction etc.Enjoying the Early Access and looking forward to what's next to come!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game does so many things right. I love the graphics. They take me right back to the 90's arcades when I played Virtua Racing and Daytona USA. Driving is great. You can upgrade your car. Career mode is awesome. There's just enough sim (fuel, tires, pitting) to feel like real Formula 1/2/4 without taking away from the arcade aesthetic or gameplay. The game is so polished I can't even tell it's early access.My one gripe is my comms chief is mad at me and about to quit the team because I didn't take her to the movies, and honestly I'm not sure what that has to do with racing.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, loving it so far. Great mix of retro arcade style racing plus management. Loving the graphics styling and the racing is really fun. Really easy to pick up for short periods which I love as I often don’t have time to game for long periods. Can’t wait for the future updates but even now it’s well worth the purchase
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Can't wait to see the finished product! Even in just the first 2 playable series this game is addicting fun. Brings a fresh arcade feel to open wheel racers while still having rpg levels of depth that you'd see in main line titles. This game is woefully underrated and is easily one of the best games I've played all year
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, it is a fun little arcade racer to enjoy alone or with friends.The artstyle is perfect, a good resemblance to the old arcade racers on the arcade machines.The car handling is clean and intuitive, there is a good weight to the cars.Damage model is simple but does the job.Pit Stops were implemented well with a minigame.There is a really big track selection with manyy different layouts of many iconic racetracks.The career mode is better than the one on the EA F1-Games, ngl.Overall it is an already great game with good ideas and great potential. The roadmap looks really promising.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Its a really fun and cute arcade F1 game and i´m excited to see whats to come but holy *#%& the ai is annoying its so aggressive a lion in heat wouldn't come to close to it they just ram you of the course and cut in front of you where you cant do anything except crash they really need to implement a penalty  system.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Works best on controller, full support for a xbox one controller. Also, lower your sensitivity settings for steering.Fun game, it is challenging, you have to watch both fuel and tires, and AI is really defensive.Reccomend to play it in cockpit mode.It feels like a sipler version of the F1 games, it even has some team managing involved.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: For those with a craving for racing games that can balance Arcade with a little bit of simulation, I would highly recommend this game. If you grew up playing Virtua On this game will hit just the spot. So with the ambitious Roadmap they have ahead it only makes me happy that I've found this game and I'm more than glad with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Add replays!  Night time races with lights would be cool too.  Option to go back and change you helmet/looks. More paint options would be more fun too, car numbers, etc. Problem:  I got a DNF on Adriatic Sea GP and it won't let me try again. Awesome game! Hope to see lots of add-ons n updates! The pits makes it fun. Glad I decided to get it! Hope to see some improvements tho
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, good fun.  Very much like the retro arcade race games of the late 90s and early 2000s but with slightly updated graphics.  Thats not to say it looks or feels old, it just replicates it well.  Race physics and AI are fun and challenging too.   Enough depth to make it the career mode fun without being overly detailed and somewhat tiresome like the F1 games.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun Racer with way more depth than expected. Pit Tactics are especially fun.The Crew Management Part is the one like the least so far, as it is really hard to keep the mood up, imho the Team should be happy when i win race after race and not moan about perks not being used. But we'll see, we are in early access after all.Coloring the car and the race tracks changing over the time periods is also fun!Also the game runns on every potatoe that can run unity, nice!
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: Love the thing to bits. The game is a casual version of the codemasters F1 games, with a carrer mode, letting you upgrade your car as the season goes along.It's just short races of 6 laps, but it garantees you can pick up and play for a bit and still do 2 or 3 races.The AI is surprisingly decent. They try to close the door when you approach to make an overtake and they actually give you room once you're side by side with them, so it's already better than the F1 games in that department.It's on the easy side of things, even if you choose the pro difficulty the AI drivers will have little chance if you're just an average racing game player, but I wouldn't increase the difficulty too much. Love the artstyle, it remind me of that old arcade game Virtua Racing. I wish it had some special long duration event, like LeMans or Indy500.

_childDocuments_.review: As a 90's kid growing up watching the likes of Senna, Prostell, and Mansell on the TV and pretending (poorly) to be them on Pole Position, Final Lap, and finally Virtua Racing at the arcade, I'm blown away by New Star GP and the work that's been done with the early access version.The presentation is great as well as the gameplay, but it's the attention to detail that sets this one apart in my book. One can tell the cars and tracks that inspired what's in the game, but the team has taken care to tweak things for entertainment value (ie, no super long flat out straights yet maintaining the look and feel of circuits) and added in touches between races to keep things interesting in team building decisions the New Star team is known for. All my gripes are small and inconsequential, but he's a couple to put on the back burner- unless I've missed it, can you edit your helmet and appearance after the initial setup?  My bald guy needs a cap :)- Could there be another way to distinguish tire compounds other than the pirelli style bands for the 80's and 90's cars?  Maybe white vs. yellow lettering?  Just picking nits :)Beyond that, really looking forward to the next updates
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: I started following this game when it was first teased in the Retro Bowl and Retro Goal subreddits, and I'm pretty pleased that I did. It's a good game at release and I think if it wanted to, it has a solid base of game play mechanics to implement a manager mode or even be more realistic in some of its driving. Highly recommend if you just want to chill and race. A few cons that I have noticed so far:I'm not a racing guru, and I haven't consistently played a racing game in years, but I felt the races were easy once you made it past the pack even if you haven't upgraded your car or used your rewinds. The battles with other drivers were fun during the few short minutes you stay racing with them.it is *really* difficult to break your car, I tried a few times and I couldn't get it into the red or break any of my parts. I also noticed that even if you run out of fuel, I was able to still complete an entire lap going at 60 MPH. I could stop entirely and then start accelerating again, but 60 MPH was the cap until I refueled. Another note: it'd be helpful to know how much fuel = 1 lap when fueling.Due to the graphic design of the game I also kind of find it hard to see the end of a road just due to the textures, and this also makes spotting the pitting lane a pain sometimes. These problems are exemplified when you use the driver POV camera.Pros:Cool driver events and relations. Keep your team happy or risk having someone leave and their perks with them, the random events that can improve relations or give you funds, just the all around flavor of them even if it's an event that gives you nothing, it's pretty cool.The idea of managing your relationship with other drivers is still kinda barebones and isn't like the old NASCAR games just yet, but I was able to pretty clearly notice when a driver liked me or not -- if they liked me I could pass easily and if they didn't I'd have to undercut them because they were always blocking my path. It's fun. Also, seeing driver events such as their gearbox breaking down mid-race or seeing news about a certain driver not being able to have topspeed potential due to engine problems before the race was AWESOME.The overall racing gameplay is solid, again I'm not a racing guy so I don't have a steering wheel or anything like that but using my dualshock 4 everything felt responsive and I was pretty happy with it overall.The Eras is a great idea and moving from the 80s to 90s was awesome.What you pay for this game is pretty much worth it, especially with this dev team and their tendency to expand their games past their original goals once completed.
_childDocuments_.name: New Star GP

_childDocuments_.review: New Star GP is the F1 97 Arcade Mode with beautiful and highly detailed retro graphics, an excellent soundtrack, accessible high grip downforce driven gameplay that is superb for a 1980s-2010s Formula One/Indycar arcade title.Era driven seasons with different car specs and tracks, a wide variety of parody race drivers with their own personalities, likes, dislikes, and skill levels. Your crew similarly has the need to feel wanted and appreciated, and will resign if they feel like they are being mistreated. Wide selection of upgrades for your car and some team buffs, some light management features with interviews and team decisions to make. Dynamic and randomised weather makes pit stop strategies a critical element of every race, which could make or break your chance for the top of the podium. Some AI issues right now with rivals overly willing to turbo punt you off the track, and often your backstage choices or lack of can mess up your team management, but this should be addressed in time.Excellent wear and tear damage model with everything from your suspension and brakes to gearbox and spoilers that will degrade as a race goes on, especially if you hit too much of a curb or into the gravel. Doesn't feel like crashes harm you that much mechanically, only making the punting rivals even more annoying as they can get away with just a slight loss of speed, while you are spinning through the gravel trap and getting your car components worn down extra fast.Fantastic feel, tracks based on real world counterparts, and a surprising amount of depth for a arcade based pad racer. More games should be this accessible while still having this amount of complexity to them. Some humour, great music, beautiful scenery and lots going on during a race, really makes the stadiums feel alive.One of the courses looks a bit phallic, so there is that, too.Is it perfect? No.Is it incredible? YES. YES. ALL THE YES.8 Green Starting Lights/10 Grid spots.Vroom.

_childDocuments_.review: For those looking for a faithful low wattage (for steam deck folk) homage to classic F1 racing, this looks to be the one! Ditto for the cars, which are grouped by decade. While I've not played this on my wheel, it's a beauty on the steam deck! I'll match this one up with any recent licensed option.One minor issue, love it or hate it, there seems to be annoying orange smoke popping up at various spots on the track.

Choose one of many hero characters and descend into the deadly Halls of Torment. Fight unholy horrors from beyond and survive wave after wave of enemies until you face one of the tormented Lords. Explore various underground expanses and find new powerful items that enable you to venture even deeper into the abyss. _childDocuments_.review: I played Vampire Survivors to death so when I saw this game and the raving reviews I was sure I was going to love this.Except I didn't. If you enjoyed VS for the ridiculous power spike ride/power fantasy thing, skip this game. This is a numbers game. The level ups here just feel so underwhelming. An 8% attack speed is boring. A 20% crit damage increase when you have like 15% crit chance in the beginning is laughable. 40 HP increase is boring. 9% move speed is boring. In VS a level up can be the difference between getting swarmed to death or coasting, here it's just.. you deal 3dps on average more or you run 0.2m/s more, how fun.Then there are the powers, which are exactly as boring. I don't feel like any power I've selected in 3 hours of play mattered at all because everything hits like wet noodles anyway. I've leveld them, I've gotten the achievements for that, I couldn't even tell you if the levels made a difference.But HoT has items, and from all 3 components, these seem the most impactful. For example an amulet that gives up to +50% bonus damage depending on enemies around you. You'd think +50% bonus damage must be amazing, but it isn't either. I honestly don't even know how being +50% stronger can not feel impactful but it actually does.So I regret the purchase, as none of the concepts that made VS fun are in this. So beware if you come from VS, this is nothing alike.

_childDocuments_.review: HoT is carried by its strong aesthetics. I think almost everyone will dig the visual style, and for many people it'll be really good at pushing nostalgia buttons in the brain. This visual association I think drives the positive ratings, because mechanically the game offers literally nothing new, or even slightly novel. No significant improvements or twists are made to the Vampire Survivors recipe and indeed it has less complexity and build variety than many. Upgrades you get from leveling up are  boring fodder like extra x% crit chance or x% attack speed increases. Rarely you may get lucky with a 'good' level up upgrade choice that may offer 2 substantial stat boosts instead of one mediocre one.The meaningful upgrades are the ability drops and these only come from bosses or are spread out really far in the levels - so during a 30 minute run you really only make a small handful of impactful decisions. Even if you get the 'best' drops the runs still miss that feeling of gamebreaking insanity that the best of this genre is so good at evoking.Making this problem even more troublesome is the fact that many of these ability drops are locked behind quests so you wont even see them until after completing certain criteria. Furthermore, getting an ability drop that actually works with your current class is only half the issue - you must then also get the appropriate ability upgrade because the upgraded abilities are without exception so much better than their base counterparts. These upgrades must of course also be first unlocked via quests, and then you must hope that the right one happens to be one of the handful of drops you get in any run.This is just putting the most fun the game can offer behind too much RNG, and even at its best HoT is still just a mid Survivors clone that admittedly looks pretty sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Having followed the game since the very first public announcement, it is very nice to see Halls of Torment reaching its Early Access release.Halls of Torment is the answer to "what would happen if Vampire Survivors and old-school Diabolo had a baby?"While many might look at this and sigh "yet another VS clone", HoT is much more interactive and poses much more of a challenge compared to VS.It sports a unique set of levels, characters, enemies and bosses.Each enemy has a unique visual style, attack pattern and damage type.As you play through the 30-minute runs in the levels, you earn coins to unlock permanent upgrades, which help you to kill enemies more quickly and which in turn adds to the satisfaction factor.There's also a ton of challenges/missions you can complete which unlock abilities and collectables, each of which increases your attack power.A small heads-up I'd like to give to new players is that it can be a bit grindy at times, as the levels' final bosses pose an interesting challenge to anyone surviving for that long.TLDR: Chasing Carrots hits the mark yet again with a very good game. Despite the "Early Access" label, Halls of Torment is surprisingly polished and definitely worth a try.edit: it also runs well on deck! :)

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank B- (70-75%)Nice game - try if you are interestedSee my profile for more details about my reviews.I give around 74% of rating to Halls of Torment - a very decent game that will attract all the gamers who love Vampire Survivors (VS) and want something new or different around that genre. Bonus point if you love the old tacky but cosy isometric 3D looking style from Diablo 2, Baldur's Gate 1/2 and such. The tribute to that era is obvious and very well done.Halls of Torment brings a nice little variation on VS, with a few twists such as (spoiler!) the end of each level not being about death (the end) but... a boss! That makes sense, and that is pretty cool. Also you will find all the tropes from games such as Diablo and the like from that era: the items, the dungeons, the dialogues, etc.There is a fine amount of content in there to keep you entertained for a good week, however personally this game did not have the richness and variety that VS brought to me. The characters, the levels, the skills, the weapons, the enemies... all were fine and very respectful of this Diablo tribute, yet overall lacked what makes VS so crazy and rich.I would say try this if you are interested to tackle more indie games in that exploding genre at the moment - it is a very nice B- game. If you did not like VS in the first place, I doubt this would make you change your mind about the concept. is  on

_childDocuments_.review: The game is early access, so there's hope and potential for it, but in a market that's HEAVILY and I mean HEAVILY saturated right now, this game launched (TB was right, EA is launch) in a state that failed to bring anything new to the table and failed to really compete with other games in this space. There's SO many survivors-like rogue-like "kill waves of baddies and get randomized loot or powerups" games out and coming out regularly.  This game didn't give me a single reason to play it more than a few runs compared to the countless other options I've demo'd and bought. Starting out with "Sword Guy" and having to swing at everything in melee range is just zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz.  The interaction between "Pickup Range" and "My Melee Range" and "The waves of enemies that come out" just makes early game and un-upgraded gameplay an extreme chore. Vampire Survivors and other Survivors-Likes also have these issues sometimes. But it felt pretty bad here. No ultrawide support and no proper resolution options. Early game is ponderous, monotonous, and slow. The options I had for powerups were really boring.  Lightning.  Orbs.  Needles.   Makes me feel like I'm doing a D&D campaign with a DM that really hates magic and tries to run "low magic" worlds.  Very bland and boring. I feel like this is going to be particularly egregious in terms of having to grind the crap out of it to get anywhere and having to upgrade all your baselines before things stop feeling like total garbage. The only unique thing this game has done so far is that you have RNG chests with RNG equipment that you equip mid-run as you get them from bosses. But there is no dopamine here yet, in fact it kinda put me to sleep for real, like I need to go take a nap now, I don't feel like playing anything anymore. So many aspects of this game feel really halfbaked. The low-fi low resolution vibe feels like 50% design intent and 50% copout to not have to have the UX be polished.

_childDocuments_.review: I love vampire survivors, I tried it on my computer, and finished it on my phone and enjoyed it a lot. I also played 20 minutes till dawn, which was another great game. However, Halls of Torment features some of the best aspects of vampire suvivor, like its chests, length of a run, upgrades, and so on, while adding its own game-changing features. The new features in Halls of Torment, in my opinion, only improved the game in a positive way and thus made it slightly better than the aforementioned games.+ different heroes that are unlocked the more you play.+ purchasable (with in-game gold of course) upgrades that are unlocked the more you play.+ each quest you achieve gives a %0.5 xp bonus for your runs, while rewarding you with gold or unlockables.+ why are we limited to only 3-4 items per run??? Ooh, now I see, this wellkeeper (stage 2) guy allows us to have them permanently and use a loadout for each hero. But we need to retrieve the items and buy them for once first, meaning, every run we make now has even more value.+ permanent potions with the help of a new guy, but again, you need to retrieve them and buy them back from the wellkeeper first. + By following the two blood trails in stage 1 and do what it requires you to do, you will get a huge help for the boss, which is a good way of making player do something during a run and not just stay there and wait for 30 minutes.+ For the same reason of my last point, there are papers(?) on the map that you can acquire and get free skills, and there is also another thing(?) that you can get which makes you collect all xp on the map, this exists at all runs from stage 1 to 3, I don't know about other stages though.+ The atmosphere is well expressed to the player with a great graphic design and background musics.+ The sounds of enemies (like skeletons) dying is so satisfying to listen to.     I am yet to see any other feature the game has, since I have only played for 8 hours at the time I am reviewing this game; However, I have a strong feeling that this game will not dissappoint. If you like survivor type games, then I can guarantee that you will enjoy this game.
