_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Bullet-heaven game with lots of content if you like experimenting with builds and unlocking achievements. Graphics evokes memories of late-90's PC games like Diablo which really plays on my nostalgia (this is a good thing). Sound mostly consists of dark and gloomy tunes, which really fits the rest of the game. One of the unironically greatest things is that the experience gain sound pitches up the closer you are to a level up which fires off all kinds of neurons in my brain (another good thing).The game manages to have lots of classes that still feel kind of unique, although I wouldn't mind even more differences. The shared abilities will most likely be a large part of your build, abilities aren't really modified at all by the class which means that they feel the same independant of your class choice. To my knowledge there isn't really any "combine X class with Y skill for great results" besides some minor things like a class's attack being short range therefore lending itself to close range abilities.The item system feels like it's in a good place and lets you modify both your characters and gameplay to a greater degree than the class selection. Some items are kind of uninteresting stat gains, but they have been around since early access and are kind of good when starting off so it's no big deal. The end-game agony mode introduces stronger, run-only items with  randomness added and I kind of wonder if that design would be even better to make repeated runs feel more rewarding, but that might be PoE-brain talking here.Each map contains a few quests or unlockable content like NPCs or bonuses that makes the end-boss easier, both of which is kind of fun to go for. I love the retro way that the NPC talking animations are done which feels on point with the rest of the game's art style.Overall, for the asking price this is just an insane amount of value and if you enjoyed any other games in the genre you will enjoy this one. Very recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to say a lot about a game that is exactly what it's look like : it's a Vampire Survivor inspired game that really wanted to look more like Diablo 2 than its counterpart.And it obviously does work, those type of game have always been closer to hack & slash than bullet hell so it's nothing surprising to see them borrowing more from them. This one in particular is extremly specific about the stats and much less about the attacks, this results in a more flexible game that usual where on the spot decision is more natural than trying hard to stick the build. There's sure archetypes and playing arround them is probably a good idea but because there's so much more option available it really discourage badly chasing one option. The interesting flipside of this is the randomness doesn't hit too hard but also it gives value to defensive options, something that's pretty rare to achieve in very stat heavy game.But having said that, it's not that much of departure either and the main appeal of this game in particular over any other one is its presentation. Now I did stop at what looked like a conclusion but there's obviously more to, there's exactly 500 achievement to unlock and a few of them does require some effort, two different mode gradual difficulty, a few different grind and I have barely foudn any artifact outside the obvious so there's a time sink element to it I haven't touched and probably won't bother too much with and while the game itself isn't extremly difficult it does seem to scale pretty viciously. Combined with ennemies that have pretty varied behaviors, none of this is a completly mindless grind while also being entirely optional.In any case, there's nothing wrong with this game that isn't relative to what type of game it is, that is to say a pretty repetitive time sink.

_childDocuments_.review: I find myself rather perplexed by the effusive praise lavished upon this game. However, within this game, the progression is rather more subtle, even imperceptible. As you amass upgrades, their contribution to your potency feels barely noticeable, while the relentless waves of adversaries seem to gain strength at an accelerated pace that significantly outpaces your own. The sense of tangible growth in power, so integral to these games, appears conspicuously absent. Each venture into the game's world feels like a rerun of the previous, devoid of any thrilling combination or synergistic possibilities. Can anyone explain what I might be missing here?

_childDocuments_.review: I'd seen this game called many things before I bought it: "Bullet Heaven" "Walking Simulator" "Diablo Survivors." Hell, I'd even seen someone call the well for saving items (a dangling pail that descends from Earth into the underworld) the "lotion bucket." After four hours, which I find is a relative wealth of time with games like these, I've come up with my own way to describe Halls of Torment: Podcast Companion. It's the perfect thing to do while listening to Sanderson wax poetic about speculative fiction, or Rich Roll sit down with Arnie for a discussion about coddling kids a little less, or--if you're really in the mood for torment--Rogan or Peterson going on with their inane drivel of the week. Whatever you're into, HoT is a great way to feel like you're doing something while you're doing another something. It's fun on its own, too. Even if you prefer, for some reason, just listening to the sounds of the game (at least put on some music, you serial killer) it stands on its own two feet so that you can sit there on your own one butt and enjoy killing skeletons, and blobs (one of the more anemic enemy types, but hey, it makes me hate them and want to kill them even more, so mission accomplished, right?).TL;DR Its fun, but it ain't no ear porn. Learn to utilize the lotion bucket.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 8/10Halls of Torment is a very fun survivors game that gets a lot of things right. The enemies are varied and interesting, the gameplay is smooth as butter, hitboxes feel fair, the weapons are interesting with cool evolutions to em. The game offers a deep progression system that allows for many, many builds. You can really cook some cool stuff up in this game and as somebody that recently 100%'d the game's achievements, I really enjoyed being able to theorycraft and come up with solutions for some of the more involved achievements. It was almost like solving a puzzle. The game does get some things wrong though. The balancing is all over the place, some of the characters are much stronger than others. The same can be said about the powers, one in particular is about 4x stronger than the next best power. Items are also in the same boat, once I got a specific item the game became piss easy even on Torment 15. Progression is also pretty slow, it can take a long time to collect all the items you want. The game also has some bugs, none of which are overly impactful but they're definitely noticeable. The ice map is pretty terrible and the boss there is deceptive, his attacks go much further than their animations. Not something that matters when you're comically strong but definitely noticeable when you aren't. Another very specific gripe I have is that 100%ing the game is a pain in the ass. 500 achievements is pretty hefty but that isn't even my real issue. My issue is that artifacts aren't guaranteed drops, once you have collected around 24 it becomes an RNGfest to collect the ones you are missing with no way for you to influence it. You have to finish an entire run for a chance at getting one of the remaining artifacts you need which is super tedious. Definitely didn't appreciate that my last 12 achieves took hours longer than necessary because of this. Was gonna knock the score down a point for this but decided against it because of how specific of a problem this is. Super lame and frustrating though, devs should fix this arbitrary and unnecessary wall. TLDR: Game is very fun and does a lot right. Also does some stuff wrong and 100%ing the achieves devolves into an RNGfest for the last 10-20 achieves which is pretty awful. Would definitely recommend the game for its price!

_childDocuments_.review: This purchase is aging like a fine wine. The developer reminds me of old Blizzard in their approach and i am dying of curiosity how they will tie this up and hat the future may hold.The game itself i would describe as DIablo meets Vampire survivors. The developer is taking their time and is already innovating on the formula with creative little solutions. To give and example. They cut down the RNG reliance when it comes to lvl up choices by relegating some of that RNG to unique versions of items (you have items) that can only be used that run. Meanwhile you can subvert that RNG during the run with potions and careful planning and even before the run depending what marks you choose (far better choice than how many weapons will i use this run). This way every run can still be a new experience without frustrating the player to much. Its is less rogue like, If that's your only appeal in these sort of games, it might not be for you. Still i would risk it if i were you at this price. Chances are you will still like it. Definitely not just another Vampire's Survivor's clone. The RPG element is greatly enhanced.  You want debuffs? You got them. You want items? Very well implemented and plenty of possible builds to try. You want single damage, cc, aoe spam, trickster build, tank build, pet build? You got all of that. You want unique heroes that can do different thing. Well guess what, you got that to. TALKING HEADS? You bet they got talking heads!. Another thing that impresses me is the amount of thought put into how the ai moves. And the atmosphere is just the cherry on top. My only regret is that I've done it all and need to wait for more content to come out

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best game in its category.The feeling of progression is pretty well balanced.Items are good in general but some would benefit a bit of a buff to make them competitive with others.Talents are very interesting!Overall a great game, with depth of itemisation and talents.Sad to think that this game has 10 times the depth of Diablo 4.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: I like the Horde Slayer genre.It allows one to dip into and out of a game quickly instead of needing to dedicate hours to playing (although i can spend hours playing these games anyway).It's also quite addictive, keeping me playing to unlock that next weapon/ upgrade/ stage/ character.I discovered Halls of Torment from a demo play-through by SplatterCatGaming, and thought it interesting enough to try out.It is one of the more fun examples of the Horde Slayer genre I have played.Regarding the above-mentioned staples of the genre, it does it quite well.In addition, I love the Diablo-esque art direction. I am fond of the darker atmosphere.The music suits the mood nicely too.This is the first Horde Slayer game where I've had to pay attention to a variety of character stats.This is because the game is designed in such a way that the base stats of each character make a big difference to the effectiveness of the stat boosts provided by the various weapons, items, and abilities.Stat boosts can work much better for some characters, and for some others not at all.I enjoy the quest-unlock record - it allows you to know what quest goals have been achieved and what other related quests can be further pursued after a particular goal has been achieved, which allows you to plan for what next quest to tackle, giving you a little bit of control over your chosen path to end-game.Aside from the general common quest-record, there is a different set of quest-goals for each character, and one for each stage.I would love to see a much larger variety of stages, enemies, weapons/items/abilities, and also hear a larger variety of music tracks, but i assume that these will come in time, as it is still early access days.Regarding some quality-of-life improvements (at the time of this review, 3rd June 2023),1) It would be nice to be able to see the character stats outside the dungeons where character & equipment selection happens - you can only see character stats after you've started a run.2) Although stat boosts for a current run are recorded inside the menus in the order they were chosen, there are some mutations to abilities/weapons that can be chosen during a run which don't show up in the stats and abilities menus, and many times I don't remember exactly what the choice i made did to the character, and it would be nice to be able to refer back to it when entering the menus.3) Some info needs to be less opaque specifically in regard to how some stat values interact with stat boosts and items (eg. base stats vs  Shrine of Blessings boosts vs in-run boosts, base stats of 0% and the interaction with percentage multipliers, and so on... ) - and related to this,if some types of stat boosts have no effect on the character's stats, it would be useful if those stat boosts did not appear in the choices offered (unless, of course, this is meant to be a feature of the game).I am having a blast playing Halls of Torment.I recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: A year ago I stumbled into this game looking for something fresh coming out of being bored & overpowered in Vampire Survivors and bored & disappointed with Diablo 4.Several milestones later, today, I have once again capped out the achievements.While metas developed, I felt that this game always offered variety and rewarded creativity.I want more. Perhaps in the form of another installment, as this game is packed to the brim as it is.Would love to see a multiplayer experience in the future.But otherwise the game scratched every itch; lucky loot, grinding, big numbers, build diversity, plenty of challenge.Best 5 dollars spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment is a pretty solid, although maybe a bit bland, bullet heaven game.The art style is fantastic; reminds me of the days when I'd get up at 4am before school to get on the PC to play Diablo, and a couple years later Diablo 2. Judging from the other reviews, it seems like I'm far from the only one feeling nostalgic because of the graphics!The gameplay is quite fun; it's your typical bullet heaven kinda thing where there's huge swarms of enemies and you destroy them all before they reach you. There's many classes to choose from, and each one of them feels very unique. Where it falls a bit short for me is the abilities; unfortunately none of them feel particularly impactful or flashy, I guess? The upgrades and abilities definitely give you massive power boosts, but to me they felt a bit bland. This might be because a lot of the other games in this genre tend to have very flashy abilities, and here they feel a lot more toned down in comparison. Still, that's my only complaint about the game; everything else is fantastic! It is being actively developed and I'm very excited to see what comes next! As of writing this review, it took about 38 hours to 100% so there's already lots of content, and absolutely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually really enjoy this game. I like the graphics and character variation. I bought it a long time ago and didn't even realize it was in my inventory until I started playing all the games I've never even installed.I didn't expect much. If you're coming into it just wanting to chill and just smack around some skellys, you'll have a good time.EDIT: After playing the game a bit more, it has nothing to offer after you have beaten each level and played with each character once. You could experience most everything in 5-7 hours, and has nothing else. Further still, after you have unlocked gear, universal stat upgrades, character stat upgrades, potions, etc., it becomes a boring collection of enemy death animations with no input from the player. I tried getting artifacts to make the game interesting and different, but they didn't add enough of a challenge to keep me playing. If you made all the enemies damage sponges, it wouldn't make it anymore fun. The game would just become superficially frustrating instead of effortlessly dull. I even had that moment where I said to myself "Why am I playing this video game? Like, no one cares if I've beaten this game. I don't care if I've beaten this game. I'm never going to talk about this game to another person. I should stop playing video games." If you ever start questioning why you play video games at all because of the game you're currently playing, it probably means the game is a time sink with no benefit. While there is a narrative, it could be replaced by latin filler and it would not effect your experience. The enemy types differ in two ways: movement and range. Enemies swirl, lurk close and far, roll, flip, zig zag, and more. Doesn't change a thing. The only thing that may get difficult is if there are ranged enemies, and enemies that leave aoe in the ground. If you move in a circle, you probably won't get hit. At the end of all this, I don't hate the game. It has nice graphics, sounds, and character variations. I just wouldn't recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Slash and hack, auto or on precise aim, as you desire. Epic boss fights, critical rewards, 30 minute sessions, which you most likely won't survive for the first 5-10 hours,Instant recommendation if you enjoyed previous Hack and Slash games, and want more out of vampire survivors. The ability to automate attacks, and auto-lock on to enemies is but a click away, during the game, OR you can aim, and attack, on command, when you want.The cooldowns are real. The  level ups are intense, and will require many times to figure out a good strategy.You start off with the Barbarian, with more heroes to unlock as you keep playing. Next comes Archer, Exterminator the fire-casting hero, next a cleric, and their abilities have everlasting level ups on the eternal upgrades for all heroes that enter the halls of Torment.It's a small purchase for many hours of fun,If you know you enjoyed 20 minutes till Dawn, Vampire Survivors, The Boneraisers, Rogue Genesia, you will enjoy this without a doubt :) What makes Halls of Torment Unique: No Dashing unless with a specific hero, it's an ability, not a commodity. Your evasion of enemies comes from zig zagging, while attacking The attacking itself, is customizable, and not fixed, like VS, [auto attacking :on/off auto-aim :on/off]  Up to you. [] First two heroes have their work cut out for them,Melee- Great difficulty, after you play with Archer™,  but once you find the balance of level ups, and your intended build, you will have better control of your fights.You can add Crit chance to attacks, you modify crit amount, you get applied force,By level 14 already, you're being swarmed so hard, that if you proceed, you need both damage, and area-of-effect for your weapon to get you where you need to be.The levels seem to be more difficult than the other, so for example, Level 1 is fighting on earth, but level 2, you're in the depths of hell, the enemies feel stronger, the swarms look and feel bigger, when these enemies shield up on their first wave it's like 3 hits to wear down the shield,The way you level up your character needs to be focused, - You need to think about it every time because you do not get re-rolls :) like in other games. You get  4 options every level up, which is more than fair, so it's something to work with,Enemy-Boss-Kills - Are intense, especially because they can summon more creeps into the spawns, they're super boss-fights actually, melee can't even reach the boss if you don't build for swarm-protection first.Archer breezes the first 1 or 2 bosses in a level,The reward from a boss fight, is sometimes a choice of 1 of 3 equipment items, a super rare spell that triggers and now has a chance to feature in your level up abilities. Negatives, Avoidable, with extra skill, and visionLand-blending, enemies don't really get stuck into the terrain's objects like we do, [Fixable but at the same time, it makes sense that it camouflages because it's part of the terrain] -= Can't wait to see what the new engine does for the game! <3Much love to this great success, and it's a game that lasts for a long time,There are also 243 achievements :) in-game quests help attain them,After 3 hours, I have just kept enjoying it, and upon reaching the 30th minute with barbarian, I was actually beaten by the first level's end boss, - I kept trying to get health from barrels, which can either contain, vegetables, or potions +70 HP, or a level up helps give HP when you need it most, I had 14 minutes left on the barbarian run earlier, and went as low as 8HP from 952-max - and recovered all the way to the end of the level getting to 30 minutes, and 200+HP for the boss fight. This was not enough,Learning to dodge - as if you're tapping movement keys, is a skill, If you use a controller, then it's even easier, because you can use the analog's pressure, of how fast/slow you move, it's not just a 100% on, or off movement, which is like some of these games in this genre.The Auto-attack actually shows you how far your upgrades have come , toggling it, off, accidentally, can have some level-ending consequences... but it's part of the learning curve ;)The next really epic thing about this is statistics, from always scrolling./moving across a level, the 5000 meters in one run is achieved, small things like this shows deep love for the underlying structure of this game.It's a real gem! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from Vampire Survivors, this game feels like the next step in the right direction. This game has enough of a different feel, different mechanics, different leveling system, and different character functions to feel very distinct while offering a familiar gimmick and gameplay experience. This game also may be genuinely more difficult than Vampire Survivors, which isn't necessarily a huge feat, but the game makes you work for the power spikes you'd normally feel in Vampire Survivors, definitely requiring more technical skill to strafe enemies and more game sense to know which upgrades will best suit your character for the run. The game's progression is easy to pickup, as unlocks and objectives can be found before starting each new run, as well as permanent upgrades and equippable gear that modifies stats and abilities. I do have a small gripe with this game; the game does not hold your hand or help you understand much outside of the fundamental controls. I could see this being a rather frustrating learning curve, since the game expects you to learn a lot through trial and error or through repetition. This works for some and won't work for others; it is a bit hard to get into, but once the ball starts rolling and you start engaging with the content, understanding how the game works, the game becomes a lot more enjoyable. Only time will tell, but I think this game has the potential for me to like it even more than its other contemporaries. Another bonus are the plethora of achievements to collect, giving any player something to strive for and major satisfaction when obtaining many at a time. I would recommend this game to anyone, especially since the price is generous for the potential fun to be had. However, do some research to see if this game will be a good fit, it definitely will not be for everyone and the difficult learning curve could turn people away.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for the price, plenty of stuff to do and I bet the developer will bring more stuff with time. Its and easy buy, you won't regret it!Abilites are fun, traits are very good and well balanced for the most part (will talk more about that later) and you have A LOT of unique characters to choose from, each one completely changing the way you play the game.Visuals are nice, animations are good and sound is well developed. Boss fights are unique and challenging and throughout the maps you learn a few of the attacks the final boss will use, very nice touch of game design there.Improvements needed:-Some traits seems useless, incrementing 0.05 of any base stats its a waste 99% of the time even with all the percentages upgrades applied on top of it.-The "course" traits are also useless (like the one that gives you fragility and something else), it would be nice to gain some buff at the cost of getting the debuff, maybe after each course, all traits multipliers could be increased by X% or something like that.-We should be able to open the inventory from the trait selection menu, some times I can't remember if I need 10% critical rate or if I already reached my desired %, or I can't remember if an ability is affected by a certain trait.-Some items should display what buff they are giving when you hover over it on the main interface in the right side, for example the Mask of Madness, I need pause the game and hover over crit rate, crit dmg, attack speed, multistrike... to see the % stats provided by the mask.-Boss items collected on each stage by completing a small quest should give a description of what that item do when you hover over it. That is a REALLY cool design that gives you a purpose and a little help on each map but after you get the item you don't really know what that item does.-Its easy to get bosses stuck behind walls (specially on chamber of dissonance) allowing you to cheese some of the fights.-After you finish the final boss fight you should immediately be teleport out of the map, you can cheese some quests like the Golem total rolling time and archer walking distance.-Maybe a little buff to Dragon Breath (or maybe I wan't able to use it properly) but it seems like the ability does not follow the same progression as the others. Maybe a speed buff to the wave is enough because a lot of the time the enemy is killed before the wave get to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Among the best 'survivor'-like entry with some technical issues.  I hope devs never stop adding maps, characters, and new content/features/QoL.PROS:- There's much more game content than what initially appears on the surface.  Keep playing!- Game design is clever and creative in how you unlock the various things it has to offer; also nice surprises.- Progression pacing is well balanced when it comes to perma upgrades and unlocks.- Quest structure execution is well done and rewarding.- Decent sound - skeleton bones satisfying!  Soundtrack can seem a little repetitive at times but not really an issue.- High boss HP can make battles feel like more of a drag than they need to be, but they are interesting and unique.  Be nice to see lower HP and perhaps slightly increased difficulty a little to compensate.- Gameplay momentum holds up well; you can choose your 'level up' option pretty quickly since all the details are right thereCONS:- Run length is too long; would like to see it reduced to 20 minutes.- Some tooltips are missing, like for pierce.  Unclear how it works depending on character.- Building on previous point, it can be confusing understanding how the different level up powers affect weapons.  Like what does piercing mean for electrical attack?- Would be nice if the item retrieval mechanism had a 5 minute cooldown rather than only being limited to 1 item retrieval per run.  Though I guess this slows progression pacing so the player doesn't unlock too much too fast which isn't necessarily a bad thing.TECHNICAL:- MAJOR: Crash to desktop incident when playing as sorceress on Ember map with 7 minutes left. :( Fortunately only occurred once in my 7h playtime.  Sure be nice to have more confidence that this won't happen again.- Game doesn't let you set resolutions or remember how your window was sized from previous session, requiring manual window resizing every time you launch the game.- Playing with a mouse felt quite buggy but didn't look into controls much.  I only play this with a controller now.- MINOR: It'd be nice to see animations smoothed out a little more or the game frame rate capped to its render rate.  Even at 144hz the animations are quite stuttery.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is okay. 5/10. Right at average. The graphics are nastolgia bait for me. I love that oldschool pc style CRPG look. Obviously, it's inspired by the Diablo I art style, but it also reminds me of my old favorite - Baldur's Gate (the actual first version not the EE version). The gameplay is a bit ... meh. It's your typical survivor game where you have nothing but movement to control. Though, they do let you toggle your auto-aim and your auto-fire - which DID become useful.They actually have the best dodge (Block) mechanic I've seen. In short - it actually complements your armor stat (Defense). In most games of this nature, a dodge mechanic would just be consisting of adding number to some sort of logarithmic equation, which they do a bit here; the logarithmic equations to determine their stats. (e.g.) 20 Defense actually equals an 18% damage reduction and there's a point of diminishing returns. Like 40 defense would only be 28% resistance not 36%. However, their dodge mechanic is structure with the equation like normal but it break it down like this: "Damage from 0-X has a 100% damage block chance; Damage from X-Y; Has a 50% chance; And Y-Z has a 10% chance." This is actually BRILLIANT! They work WITH armor instead of 'despite' armor, which is how most games (even the greats) use the dodge mechanic. I cannot give this game enough praise for this mechanic. Everything else however, is ... just meh. The way you get your skills/abilities/equipment is just underwhelming. Almost all bonuses are either super weak, or come with a pretty big penalty to use it. ...Just meh. You are FORCED to replay maps to unlock the ability to buy your equipment. Because, the mechanic they have is if you pick up a piece of equipment you don't own, you need to put that item in a 'well' that sends it to 'the base camp camp' where you can buy it from an NPC to have as a permanent equipment.  It sounds cool, but in-effect it becomes a slog because you can only send ONE PIECE back during a run.... which is the other issue that makes this g ame feel incredibly meh. A Run...by default... is 30 minutes. These games bennefit from not being tied to the timer. I believe they're best when you're given a goal that isn't related to time such as: Defeat 5 bosses and those bosses are triggered by killing X amount  of Mini-Bosses, which are triggered by y amount of normal enemies. So, these games are designed to lost 30 minutes and to be fair on the game - the game is entertaining enough that you can accidentally spend way more time on the game than intended. It's just by having the time limit, you're not really encouraged to do many-many runs to collect all the items. The information given in the game is awful. They do have tool tips ... for SOME THINGS... to let you know what it does, but it's not consistent. There's many abilities I don't know if they effect a skill or not - even though some of the skills label their stats with the 'normal' stat name if it's being used for something weird. (e.g.) Force would be next to the word "Chaining" to signify how many hops a chain will get, or it'll be next to "Piercing" for how many enemies a projectile pierces through.  But, it's not consistent with that, it also appears there's a heavy amount of skills that don't work with many abilities and only benefit from 3-4 of the abilities you can put points into. The character all play different.... but holy crap are some over tuned than the others. Archer - best class in the game I have unlocked. BAR NONE. Nothing can compete with its' dps, range and speed. The summoner class is almost unusable because its' dps is just so insanely low and it has no other utility. Hell, the summoner class barely is a summoner class - it just has projectiles shaped like birds (ghosts actually, but they look like birds if you aren't paying attention). And a weird thing, this is the first survivor game where they try and NOT let you get your full equipment load out - unless you're doing the 'Agony" mode which is their challenge mode. (e.g.) You have 6 skill slots and a main weapon. You start with the main weapon, and only get skills from defeating bosses, which seems to have a similar timer to Vampire Survivors, being; at 5 minutes in a mini boss shows up, 10-12 minutes another one, 18-20 another, and 25 another. BUT these bosses will drop 2 items, instead of skills, so out of the 4 mini-bosses you get 2 skills and 2 items. SO, you can go on a map and find scrolls which will give you another skill per scroll (the most i've seen on a map is 2). So... this is also the way you give your skils their 'fully leveled special traits'.... so you either have 3 at max or 1-2 with one being beefed. <-This is TERIBLE - this is actually what makes the game not all that fun to play. Normally, I would put 40+ hours into these games, but 12 hours in... I'm bored, tired, and annoyed. I don't feel like the game WANTS ME to play it. It always punishes you and says "play again, nerd!" Without making the game better the next time through. Oh.... I do like how you have to complete quests to unlock some of you permanent skill buffs, but .... the quests aren't really prominent enough to make that a great way of doing it. Oh yeah, and in this game - the maps scale in difficulty... so, in order to grind for gold ... you end up playing the  first map over and over and over because the other ones are rather difficult. Oh yeah... the boss at the end of the map... progressively gets faster... to the point where unless you're spending a lot of level up points on speed, it will just literally walk on top of you, until you get an invulnerability bonus, which comes with a speed boost too. This gets so frustrating, because it ruins MOST builds- you either have to be a tank or super fast, because glass cannons will almost never survive.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game with an abysmal end game, meta and balance. I want to say this is a 10/10 game but in reality it is a 7/10 survivor roguelite. I could not fit everything I wanted to say.-Gameplay: It is unfortunately very boring. I have to admit, I truly did not have much fun compared to other roguelites I have played and I have played a lot of roguelites. To sum it up for you, you struggle to survive the first 5-10 minutes, then start stabilising and killing until enemies cannot reach you then you sit in one spot and wait for the next 10-15 minutes to be over. It is a slog-fest if you ask me. I enjoyed the first 40 hours of the game because you had to be on your toes at any given moment. Now with patch 1.0, I literally play another game on my phone while I wait for my Halls of Torments run to finish. It is not engaging at all especially with the broken items that are now available from the start. I truly believe it was a mistake to allow players to bring up green items because balance is now absurdly broken.-Progression: Long grind. Requires a lot of runs to get started for equipment, potions and gold, then even more hurdles to get artefacts, tormented souls, green equipment and even more gold. Honestly it takes too long that the rewards do not seem like rewards. It has been rewarding to be able to do +28 artefacts but the cost was too much in my opinion. There is also no gold sink at the moment, so you will eventually end up hoarding up gold since there is nothing you can use it for other than the vault, which is useless in my mind.The quest system is abysmal. XP is directly linked to the quests you have completed which means you cannot have an efficient run unless you start completing quests. There are 500 quests for a total of 150% XP. Some quests require you to be able to achieve a certain level or power spike, meaning you cannot do them until you have completed the rest of the quests or at least some that you require. Also some quests have traits or upgrades attached to them making them important to complete for power spikes. Not having any of these in your arsenal means your runs are severely hindered. Why is this terrible? Because it hinders your gameplay and forces you to do gimmicky quests so you are able to have efficient runs. I really like the quest system as a tracker since I am a completionist. What I despise and hate is the way they hide traits and powers that should be in my arsenal behind a stupid quest. I would have not minded if they said "Complete +15 artefact with Warlock" and get Trait V or something like that. That is a good challenge which would probably drive me crazy until I achieve it. "Get 25 move speed. Get warlock to 1 health. Reach 50% critical chance with exterminator". These are more irritations than challenges. They are "waste my time" quests. Sure, they are easy and probably good enough to teach players how to use potions to maximise traits and stats.-Game Length: Not having a x2 or a short version of a run is a massive negative. Most of the time I was AFK. I would reach unkillable status very quickly and had to wait extensive periods of time for the run to finish. I would prefer a 15 min game mode or even 10 min of chaos than a 30 min run. Usually 30 min is 30 plus 10-15 min of clicking through stuff. It is just too long and does not give a good incentive to keep playing. What helped me power through the game was the achievements.-End game: Not good. Ran out of space.-Equipments: Blood Catcher (Enhancement). That is all I have to say about items. If you are not wearing this, you are a fool. This item needs to be removed or nerfed to the ground. I am pretty sure this is the only item that allows you to do +30 artefact runs. I have not tried duellist's spark which seems it could be good, regardless Blood Catcher not only heals you, it increases your damage per stack. In one of my runs, I had 5000% extra damage because of that stupid amulet. No other equipment compares.Ignoring blood catcher, there are loads of fun equipment to use and this patch allows you to double up and rings so I usually get both green echo band. Also allows you to streamline builds that were previously was not possible or not viable. There are load of builds you can do and mostly they will be decent. I caution people to actually see what damage types their character's have as I have seen people using Echo band (Reach) without having any physical damage to proc it, wasting a good ring slot for nothing.-Characters: Good amount of different characters with each having their own unique set of skills. Some of them are tedious to play with since they have a specific build to even be viable, some not good at all. For example, Norseman and shield maiden are the best characters in the game because of their shield block. Some of you might not understand this but at +15 artefacts you basically need massive amounts of defence and shield block to even survive the early onslaught. Any innate bonuses to defence makes you able to resist damage plus the mark of shield maiden makes your damage scale with shield block and then gives you the option for even more shield block. You can try to make builds without shield block but I think you would need to be insanely good at this game to even succeed. Ultimately, fragile characters fail to even survive the first few seconds of the hardest challenges this game has to offer.Regardless of endgame, all characters seem to have a decent play style and can derive some fun from them. Some characters like sage and warlock can be exceedingly fun to use and push quite a bit of the challenges ahead of you. Since they are not balanced appropriately, they can do loads of crazy stuff. On the other hand, Exterminator and Beast huntress are quite bland and not really entertaining, not really achieving much and not fun at all. Overall, there is definitely a character for everyone, even though I would welcome more characters and different playstyles.-Abilities: Massive problem here. All skills suck except ring blades, transfixion,  phantom needles and morning star. The rest are utter garbage, do not even pick them and if you get them randomly do not bother levelling them up. Lightning strikes and astronomer's orbs might be decent to level up but really depends the type of build you are going with. What matters in this game is damage output. How quickly can you kill and where. Ring blades is the best at this and the rest are not even comparable. Getting cyclone and range upgrades allows you to not only kill everything with ease, it usually happen off screen. This means as soon as they spawn on the map, they will die and spawning a new set and those will die, repeating the cycle. This means highest kill count in the game. With Ring Blades maxed out, I had a lvl 154 shield maiden in one of my runs with almost 70k kills. It is absolutely broken and it should be balanced. At the moment, there is literally no reason to get any other abilities other than for a smaller additional damage output or doing some gimmicky build like a spark build or projectiles. Also your FPS will drop to single digits with too many abilities. My favourite build is maxed out morning star with tinctured chain, making it hit everything on my screen which works very well if I make a physical damage build. Certainly I am being pessimistic about abilities as they surely all work in some fashion early stages of the game but once you start hitting the harder challenges, you will never pick radiant aura or meteor strikes again. I hope new abilities are coming and balancing.-Theme: Love the Diablo-like theme, dark and gritty. I even like the blurring option to make it more retro. Love the fact that each level has its own dangerous creatures to send hordes at you and are distinctive. The hellish theme is fantastic and the soundtrack really adds to the atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - An amazing game with stellar design quality, easily one of the best of its whole genre.Great oldschool pixelart style and music. Very good difficulty progression, every single ability viable from easiest to hardest stage on both normal and agony.Good characters with enough versatility and diversity to keep them unique from each other. Absolutely stellar item and ability traits diversity that allows a ton of builds for both massive optimized damage or plain old niche-but-amazingly-fun gameplay.Great looking levels with distinct geometry, altering the flow of gameplay in a unique way per stage.But even despite all these points, the TRUE genius of Halls of Torment lies in its enemy diversity and the movement AI unique to every type of enemy. They will walk up to you, some will circle around you in different patterns, some will charge and retreat, they will have shields, some will shoot conal projectiles, or AoE projectiles, they will leave hazardous puddles or spawn minions upon death.The developers did a fantastic job at forming waves of enemies whose unique style of movement will subvert the player's expectations and forces them to rethink the concept of what it means to kite a horde of enemies - keeping them at bay is no longer a matter of "Just walk in an oval" when certain enemies are specifically designed to counteract this style of motion.An additional honorable mention to the quest design. Ive completed all 301 quests the game offers to the player, also resulting in 100% steam achievements. Theres really not a single quest that I would consider out of the ordinary difficult, combined with the fact that quests unlock new characters, ability traits/upgrades and gold, its a simple but very elegant way of motivating the player in a genuine way to pursue 100%.While theres certainly arguments to be had about specific characters and builds being too overpowered (which is pretty much the case for every one of these types of games EVER, so its really not an argument at all), this game does almost nothing straight up wrong, but does almost everything straight up right. Its quite simply amazingly designed, will never insult the player's intelligence or hold your hand, and is incredibly fun.After having played Vampire Survivors and Holocure, Halls of Torment is definitely my new personal genre-defining standard in many aspects.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played the 1.0 yet, but would highly recommend getting this game.Well balanced meta-progression, fun abilities, satisfying mid-run upgrades and you can make any ability into a fun build.Does not require the use of a wiki either. Grinding is sane and mostly comes in the form trying to complete character-specific achievements for new upgrades or new abilities on all your subsequent runs.Difficulty does spike quick in the final areas, but by that point you unlocked most of the characters and you've figured out some of the stronger builds, so those areas act mostly as testing grounds for your ideas.

Alt F4 after one round though.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has been improved with more characters, locations, and content, but I still don't really care much about the gameplay loop.The runs are too long, the enemies to similar -within their given location-, and at the end of the day, I just think is too boring. It lacks the dynamism and power fantasy aspect of other survivor-like games; the runs never really evolve too much and most of the power ups are just incremental to your stats, rather than abilities that produce other effects.You can get more weapons and spells, but this is usually limited to only a few per level, so it never really gets too crazy or fun. I think in their attempt of trying to keep the game challenging and "balanced" the developers hindered their ability to experiment and make the game much more chaotic. As an end result, it's this kind of mix between Diablo, and a survivor’s clone, but without really coming to its own identity. This ends up hurting the game, and making the runs feel too reiterative and boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Devs ban folks who critique the game and encourage others to harass them. Don't support harmful market practices, folks, no matter how good the game seems.---8/15/2023 review below for archival purposes:'Halls Of Torment' beats pretty much every other horde shooter by a mile and is still being actively developed; all the others I played or saw were content to plop out a quick clone, grab people's money, and run for it.HoT features multiple characters with drastically different stat spreads and projectiles, equipment sets with equipment catering to multiple playstyles, abilities that you can pick up mid-game for additional attacks, branching upgrade paths, and multiple levels with entirely different enemy sets. There's a lot to see and do, which is both a good and bad thing. The whole package is wrapped up in a charming early 90s RPG graphics set.I only have two gripes with the current state of the game:First of all, the music is incredibly dull and forgettable. It is the embodiment of "generic fantasy battles".Secondly, the grind to get new equipment is pretty painful, since you have to get a new piece of gear unlocked as a drop via completing achievements, then receive it as an RNG drop from certain mid-bosses, manually walk to a special point on the map to send it up via a bucket, and then pay gold to unlock it for future runs once your current run ends. So, a special run dedicated to completing the achievement, a luck check to get that new gear, and then grinding to get enough gold to buy it; 3 unlocking grinds with 1 part of it being totally luck-based.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors by way of Diablo 1, by way of Smash TV. The circling and kiting gameplay is still at its core, but the different character classes have their own quirks that require a more in-depth approach to leveling and making builds. Also BUILDS are very much more at the forefront, as meta-progression involves acquiring gear and equipping your class before a run. Also, different mobs have different pathing behaviors and abilities that change how you deal with them. I also like that as you unlock more stuff, the game actually becomes harder because abilities you acquire come from a much larger pool, and so your goto build becomes harder to guarantee and you're forced into rolling with what you get and figuring out how to make it work. It very much becomes more of a roguelike the deeper you get into it. Overall, a great progression of the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: Diablo style visuals meets Vampire Survivors gameplay, I usually don't go for genre hype clones, but this is in a different league.  Definitely worth the $5 price tag.Just to be clear, this is NOT an equipment looter game. While you do pick up items/equipment to unlock and start runs with (as well as upgraded versions of the same loot to be found) there's roughly only 10 pieces of equipment per slot, HoT plays more like VS and an achievement farm game.  That's not a negative in my opinion, but I had the wrong impression initially on the storefront pictures and trailer.It's easy to pick up and play, and a single run takes 30 mins (with a faster mode unlocked in late game), so it's great if you only have an hour.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright let's start with the most important things. I disliked this genre before playing this game. Diablo bullet hell sounds like a terrible time to me. _childDocuments_.review: Decent enough, but some of the endgame stuff is just WAY too tedious. No, I don't want to grind out new gear two or three at a time per run, or grind out new artifacts one at a time per run, or sit in the Vault for a literal hour. I should've just stopped at finishing the main story.EDIT: Okay, after some rest, I've got a little more distance. I'm keeping this review as negative because I do want to make sure to caution people about what I DON'T like, but if you either don't intend to bother with or don't mind the grind, then it's definitely one of the better bullet heavens around, with a lot of room for interesting builds between the wide variety of classes, skills, and collectible equipment.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: For somebody like myself who enjoys vampire survivors, this game follows fairly hot on its heels and offers some welcome game play changes by comparison.- Cheap price- Plenty of replayability- No bugs or issues to speak of that I encountered in thirteen hours of play.- Intuitive game play that jumps straight into the action with no need for explanation even to those new to the genre.- Fantastic balance (as of this review) where every build in the game plays differently, yet at the same time do not feel definitively better or worse than other characters.- Chalk full of plenty of bosses and mini bosses that are unique. Unlike in other games of this nature this is not a blink and you'll miss it sorta deal when they show up. Most of them have unique attack patterns in addition to appearance and stand out quite well. Only a few of them seem like bigger versions of the regular monsters.- A money system with plenty of things to spend your gold on, from permanent in-game buffs that apply to all your characters (unlockable by doing certain things with certain characters), to items and equipment you can find and retrieve using a well. Note - The well is something you'll unlock after finding someone trapped in a cage on level 2 and freeing him. You'll then unlock the well in the main hub, and from that point on, he will lower a bucket down into each mission area, allowing you to permanently recover a single item or potion per run for continued and infinite use. It's pretty cool.This way you can outfit your characters with the best items you find before starting your next mission.- Every session is a thirty minute commitment, with no way to speed it up, adjust it, or increase monster difficulty.- There is a lack of mission locations and not enough secret unlocks or hidden items to find in any of the missions or hub world.- Given that this game has the aforementioned hub area, it would benefit greatly from some added lore and interactions which most games of this genre lack.- There needs to be some kind of a bestiary.- The well can only except one item per mission (this may be for balancing reasons but it makes little sense and frankly encourages one to reset the mission the moment they put an item in the well instead of committing). Special note - I believe most of the above cons are a result of this being in early access, and thus most of my complaints may be addressed in the future.----------------As of this time, you're getting more than enough content to justify five bucks, even if the developer were to abandon this game the price tag would be worth it for what's already there, let alone the upcoming content.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's make this quick. As in all my reviews I focus on the good and the bad. And let's make it clear, everyone asks is this better than Vampire Survivors or not. As such I will give my honest opinion, being a fan of both games.The Good:1. More engaging gameplay than Vampire Survivors, and more meaningful bosses.2. Classes do their own stuff Diablo-style, instead of being one trick pony, but you make it work a-la Vampire Survivors.3. More meaningful unlocks than Vampire Survivors - here everything you worked for is actually meaningful and helps every run that follows afterwards.4. More skillful than Vampire Survivors - everything poses a challenge, especially in the first 10 hours, whilst VS... Give me Gennaro without upgrades and I will get to the 30th minute. Granted I do have experience with the game... Extensive at that.5. More meaningful map items - unlike VS, the map items have very specific uses and are way worth going for them.6. More meaningful equipment items - in HoT you will remember that item you got 5 (or 15) runs ago that made all your consecutive play-throughs better and easier. In VS, any combo wins, if you play it properly. Yes, even the super defensive ones - including making yourself un-killable.7. More meaningful boss kills - you will remember your first boss kill way longer than your first Reaper kill in VS - which most people googled anyway. Here, you actually did something for it, and it is memorable.8. Let's face it, 2,5D is more fun than 2D.9. The Soundtrack is way more atmospheric and worth not turning off after numerous hours of VS.The BAD:1. On the average, Vampire Survivors is the more fun and accessible game. If you want to have good fun, you go for VS, not HoT, as HoT is the more challenging one.2. The RNG in VS works better than HoT. In HoT you can do nothing wrong, play to the best of your ability, and still lose through no fault of your own. In VS, that is way less likely.3. 2D works better for "You are the bullet hell" types of games, as it is very difficult to meander through 2,5D enemies to avoid damage than it is through 2D ones.4. VS was the first and it did it really, really, really good. This point cannot be overstated enough. This makes every other game of this type being forced to innovate enough, in order to be fun. (EDIT: Not first in the Bullet Hell genre, but the first one on steam to gain amazing traction and get many people hooked into)5. A lot of fans of the "You are the bullet hell" genre may not necessarily go for a darker, and more difficult game.6. Here comes my general Early Access warning - although this one has too much promise to be an abandonware.Conclusion:Both games are a win for me, as they tickle two types of itches - the fun one, and the I really earned what I got one. As such, both games are very welcome in the Bullet Hell genre. and both of them deserve to be played thoroughly. If you are on the fence, and the summer sale until 13.07 is going, grab it and give it a whirl. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has potential, but it isn't there yet.  These are deceptively simple games, but getting the balance of brutally punishing and rewarding is difficult.  This one merely feels grindy.  The hoards are damage sponges and dish out a lot of damage in return so it is far to easy to find yourself surrounded and overwhelmed at any point in the run.  Further the rewards do not feel substantial and the powers as you get them feel like wet farts.  Eventually all of my runs boiled down to running and hoping to accidentally killing a few leaving behind the experience until I could get lucky enough to find a magnet.  I believe it will eventually find the sweet spot and balance, but it hasn't yet.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought the game a few months back, it was a blast and had tons of fun. Each character plays differently enough to keep the game fresh. I loved working through the blessings and quests. The music and characters are top notch, especially coming from a $5 title.The last 2 updates (including the one from today) have taken a lot of the fun away. I'm not 100% sure on details for what was changed. Experience seems to be nerfed into the ground which leveling up was a lot of the fun. I use to get to around level ~105 on the 3rd stage. After the last 2 updates, I can't even complete the stage now using similar 'tried and true' builds. On the first stage, I end up at around level ~60, previously was ~90. I know the jade xp amulet was nerfed (warranted but give the xp elsewhere?).I thought the game was about a power fantasy and slowly getting to the point where you can make any build/skill work and be fun. From other comments and posts, it seems this game is no longer for me and is meant to be a bit more on the hardcore side instead of just blasting through enemies.I guess I've gotten my money's worth at 52 hours so I can't complain too much. I would not recommend this game anymore to people like me who are looking for a bit more casual power fantasy experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun I have had with a game in a while. The first night I played this I played for 7 hours straight without looking away. I have't been this captivated by a game in a long time. Great game play loop, amazing art, solid progression, and  solid maps. If they devs decide to update this game more I think they could have one o the best games on steam.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best "horde shooters" I have played up to now. It looks great, sounds great and plays great. There is a nice amount of content to keep you entertained for a long time. Achievements' difficulties seem to be on point and they are fun to work for. I would really love it if they expanded upon this with updates and/or dlcs. Maybe workshop support would be good too.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't actually played 68 hours...just left my PC on. Anyways, this game is just a less flashy, less creative, less "heart" clone of Vampire Survivors. I'm about 6 runs in (I know, not a lot) but c'mon, I was hoooked on VS after my first run. This game is so damn slow. Damage sucks, speed sucks, enemies are spongy. etc...etc...Maybe it gets better? _childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this because the gameplay loop is very fun. Unfortunately I find that this game is improperly labeled as being verified for Steam Deck. The game crashes frequently enough that you start to hesitate before playing another 30+ minute round. I play with a PS5 controller and there's a random but frequent bug where the joysticks only register a tilted joystick as a single input preventing any movement beyond the first step. Some dialogs don't respond to controller input and require use of a mouse. Additionally, some UI elements are displayed incorrectly, such as the buy potion screen and sometimes the item vendor.Once the bugs are squashed this will be a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely see an Early Access title come out as sturdy as this one, don't let the tag scare you away, because you'll be walking into a ton of content!Halls of Torment is an enjoyable, pleasantly addictive game in a retro jacket reminiscent of classics like Fallout and Diablo that'll always have you pushing forward with a healthy 'alright, just one more run' mentality.This game knows it doesn't have to reinvent the wheel, with its incredibly solid base systems, like its combat, movement and impressive, unique character variety with their own play styles, but it is not afraid to add bells and whistles. Unique, meaningful upgrades and a great variety of enemies and skill paths will keep every trip through the Halls fun and memorable, yet also satisfyingly challenging, which I personally feel these type of games oftentimes lack.Every new character you unlock will have you experimenting and getting used to new ways to play, with a new, shiny weapon to use and fresh skills to spice up their respective tools.I highly recommend Halls of Torment and I can't wait to see where it'll go!

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Vampire Survivors but want a more involved experience this is it. It's a twin-stick setup (though WASD/Mouse works obviously) so you have to move and aim. Outside of each run there are permanent upgrades.This goes a very Diablo 2 aesthetic and looks fantastic. Character/Enemy design is a little uninspired but as a whole the game looks on point.

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment is a little like what might happen if you made Diablo 1 and cut all the boring parts out. The music is not as good as the original Diablo.But if that sounds good to you, then this is highly worth it. I'm getting a lot of entertainment out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A Captivating Descent into DarknessRating: ★★★★☆Review:Halls of Torment delivers a dark and atmospheric dungeon-crawling experience that will enthrall fans of the genre with its immersive world and challenging gameplay.From the moment you step foot into the foreboding halls of this twisted realm, you're enveloped in an atmosphere of dread and despair. The game's grim aesthetic and haunting soundtrack set the stage for a journey into the depths of darkness, where every corner holds new horrors to confront.One of the game's standout features is its procedurally generated dungeons, which offer endless replayability and a fresh challenge with each playthrough. The layout of each dungeon is dynamically generated, ensuring that no two runs are ever quite the same. This adds a layer of unpredictability to the gameplay, keeping players on their toes as they navigate the treacherous corridors and confront the malevolent denizens that lurk within.Combat in Halls of Torment is fast-paced and satisfying, with a variety of weapons and abilities at your disposal to dispatch your foes. The game's intuitive control scheme makes it easy to execute precise attacks and dodge incoming threats, adding a layer of depth to the gameplay that rewards skillful play.While the game's graphics may not rival those of AAA titles, they effectively convey the dark and oppressive atmosphere of the game world. The eerie lighting and detailed environments help to immerse players in the haunting setting of the Halls of Torment, heightening the sense of tension and foreboding as they explore its depths.That said, there are some areas where the game could be improved. The difficulty curve can be steep at times, particularly for newcomers to the genre, and some players may find themselves frustrated by the relentless onslaught of enemies. Additionally, while the procedurally generated dungeons offer replay value, they can also feel somewhat repetitive after extended play.In conclusion, Halls of Torment is a captivating dungeon-crawling experience that delivers thrills and chills in equal measure. With its atmospheric world, challenging gameplay, and endless replayability, it's sure to delight fans of the genre looking for their next dark adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Combine Diablo with your favorite Vampire Survivor type game and you have Halls of Torment. This game is absolutely fantastic. It has wonderful progression  that keeps you coming back for more, and is just hard enough that you feel like it's challenging but not impossible. I highly recommend this game. You will not find a better value for $5 (but if you have $10, buy this AND Rogue Genesia- HoT and RG are the best in the Vampire Survivor genre that i've played).Edit: The big difference in this game and almost all the other VS type games i've played is that you control your attacks. It seems like a simple thing but it makes a world of difference imo. I think it makes the game feel much more responsive and I wish others in the genre would take note. It really is a perfect mix of Diablo and the VS genre. Speaking of Diablo... (I know I've mentioned it a ton)... the art style is PERFECT.  This game is a true gem. I cannot wait to see what all they do between now and the rest of EA.Edit # 2 (after beating alost all that EA has to offer short of some quests):-After 18 hours of play time it's safe to say I LOVE this game. Some notes for those who like the game and/or need some help to get more out of it:-Use the Warrior early and often until you unlock the well guy. -Once you unlock the Pyro guy, use him to plow throw the early stages of the Fire area and the Aqueduct, Basically I used him to unlock as much as I could until I got the sorcerer then used her and switched between her and the archer to finish off the bosses when those were my final sticking points.-Once you are able to use more items than the starter set the game really takes off customization wise.-Personally, as I said above, I found the archer and sorcerer to be the strongest late game characters when focusing on Attack Speed and Crit. -I completely ignored health/defense/health regen (health regen only because I found a torso piece that heals you for every 3% of your kills- which actually adds up extremely quick to heal you when you are destroying thousands per minute)This game is AMAZING!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on a 201/201 100% completion on build version 2023/06/28 (Not sure why the game uses the date for game version instead of a build number but that's all I could find.)  Yes I do recommend the game, stating that now because some people don't care for the details about what I do and don't like and just want to know that.  It may look like I am critiquing the game more than praising it but that's only because it's easier to find faults in something than praise it. Despite the things I say below I did enjoy the game.What I liked: The games artistic direction and setting is very reminiscent of Diablo which I'm pretty sure everyone pointed out, Even the music has a similar feel to it along with the little camp you can wander around in to set stuff up before runs. The classes while not overly unique do encourage different skill builds, The game has achievement based progression so to unlock features, characters, upgrade types, potions and so on requires you to complete specific achievements in game, then you usually have to find them and purchases them with gold as well. As of this build the game currently has 3 maps and while that doesn't sound like a lot if nothing else is added to the game after this (which more has already been announced) The amount of game-play you get for the price is more than enough.  What I didn't like:    The rough truth is many of the systems in game I liked the idea of more than the actual execution. For example.- Having to find the gear in game and send it back to town so you can use it in future runs. Great, but I didn't like only being able to send one piece back per run, you lose the use of it during the run you are on, and then you have to pay with gold to unlock it even though you sent it back. It requires more runs to send everything back (over 40 items and 10 potion bottles) than it does to get all achievements.- Having a variety of skill choices that appear at random during a run to make each run different. Great, but the skills themselves aren't balanced at the start let alone after various upgrades so a few skill choices will always distantly outshine the rest making the runs more similar than intended, unless you are trying to unlock a specific achievement for skill or damage type.- Having various equipment choices to design a build around once you've unlocked them. Great, but the majority of the items are uninspired and really add nothing and are out shined by the few that do like a helmet that increases attack speed by 1% per kill for several seconds up to 50% vs a helmet that adds 3 defense, or the amulet that increases EXP gain by 50% which is practically required if you want to get to level 100.  - Leveling up to become more powerful. Good, but the experience points aren't balanced properly. Currently the only map you can get to level 100 and above (around 110) is map 3 and doing so requires you to have around 90% achievement completion to boost exp gain, wear the necklace that gives 50% exp boost, and as high of a kill speed as possible. But balance is the bigger issue with this. With those things killing 17k - 18k enemies will get you to level 100 and possibly over on map 3, but killing 30k enemies on map 1 with the same set up wont even get you to level 85. With full completion of 201 achievements which gives 100.5% exp boost, and the 50% exp boost amulet, and EXP boosts you can buy with gold from the upgrade shop. 30k kills still wont get you to level 85 on map 1 but 17k will now get you to 110 on map 3. Making map 3 the only map many achievements can be completed on.- Using gold earned in run to unlock upgrades. Great, but the gold you earn isn't enough to unlock everything by a long shot by the time you've completed the game, If you don't want to grind an extra 40 or so runs you can refund all of your upgrades and just buy potion bottles to finish up the purchases 40 items achievement but doing so leaves a lot of items still locked (not that you would use them usually anyways) and a few of the upgrades wont be fully unlocked anymore (Not that you should ever need the 25k upgrade to give you a second revive.) Grinding money is one of the least pleasant aspects of this game. -Potions to change choices being required to alter level up choices for attributes and skills. Great, but having to find 3 ingredients for each potion and send up the potion bottle then buy the bottle isn't worth the time investment I had less than 10 achievements left to unlock before I even got everything together to use potions and that's with only a few flasks. Overall I think many things need to be re balanced in the long run so there isn't such a heavy dependency on the 3rd map, and specific skills over others. Summoning in its entirety is just mostly bad over all, It sounds great but in its current state it's not. In the end I enjoyed my time with the game and will probably come back to it with future updates if only because I want to keep it at 100% completion but honestly the grind for the last 15 or so achievements just  burned me out and that's without moving on to the gold grind, and while i hope at least some systems are re-balanced in the future for the price the game is more than worth it already and most people probably wouldn't burn out as easily as I do. This is one of the top games in this genre right now and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment is one of the best games in the vampire survivors genre.The gameplay is enjoyable and simple, whether using a mouse and keyboard or a controller. Game design, environment, and soundtrack give off Diablo vibes. Progression is fun, challenging, and rewarding. Currently, HoT has to offer a huge variety of items, characters, zones, potions, and upgrades to unlock, along with a plethora of combinations and synergies when combining said items and potions with a wide selection of spells for each character.Considering the low price, extensive content, replay value, and amount of free updates, there is no reason not to give this game a go. I strongly recommend trying this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: Great value for money and surprisingly relaxing game to play after days work, if you are into games where minute to minute gameplay can be very mind numbing (sometimes you afk, sometimes its more involved), but working towards the next challenge or item unlock keeps you playing.I was ready to drop the game after few initial hours, but things open up once you unlock some supporting game mechanics (and unlock 20 minute runs). I was also ready to drop it later on due to extreme repetition, but kept going just for the Quests/Challenges that flow pretty nicely through the game showing every aspect of it.Hopefully developers keep working on the game, because it definitely could use more of everything (well, maybe not more damage visual effects): item and ability balancing is all over the place making certain items and abilities feel just useless, characters and builds do not feel that much different from each other, level design could be much more varied, endgame could be expanded in many ways, UI and QoL are lacking on certain things and so on.

_childDocuments_.review: It is remarkable how great this game is. There are tons of clones for Vampire Survivors (VS), some actually good, but this stands out for many reasons. It follows the same formula of a rogue-lite, just as VS did, but adds some noteworthy changes with the inclusion of equipment slots that you acquire more armors through playing. The equipment actually make a huge difference too over time.Equal to note is how the game visually feels playing. It's like going from Castlevania on the NES to Diablo 1 (and other games of the time) on the PC. The similarities between both games' visuals to their respective influences is a work of perfection. It really does give a nostalgic feel like I had as a kid, moving up in the gaming tech world. The visuals and aesthetic feel really add to this being a worthy successor to the genre, if you're looking for a bit of a change.

_childDocuments_.review: After the 31/8/23 patch the devs have walked back some of the changes and made the game feel fun again.. with some newly added difficulty. but the main issue was it was just a grind and not fun I feel this was corrected as I'm having fun again and picking crazy combos.. although there is still some meta needed with different classes, I can only hope this will be corrected ..  its nice to see the devs are listening to the feed back. I can once again recommend this game in its current state but as changes will come and change the game till full release so will my review.

There's a lot of content and achievements in spite of it being early access and I look forward to coming back to the game every time it gets an update or I'm just in the mood to fight hoards of monsters. If not, you wont.HoT has very basic progression where you hunt achievements to increase your XP multiplier. Some achievements require tailored builds, so you get to experiment.There are only a few very effective builds so you will find yourself running the same one over and over.The builds themselves may start out different but in last third of the run must of them devolve into you running around in circles while your abilities clean the screen for you and you just enjoy the absolute mayham that unfolds on said screen.While that might sound bad, it might be just what you look for. _childDocuments_.review: After trying one of the best demo ever (savegame can be ported on the full game), I bought it. So here it is, another Vampire Survivors clone, this time with a Diablo theme and RPG elements put in. You can feel, from the first minutes of play, this game has been made with love (they even let you set autofire on or off on the fly).Lots of different characters to choose from, each with different abilities and play style. Lots of equipment to find. Lots of quests that adds for the replay value. Runs are 30 minutes each (if you last that long!).Only con I can find, I still don't fully understand how upgrades on level up work: % doesn't add up (or it does?), there is a misterious "force" stat (what for?), "defense" is different from "block", "multistrike" is not always applied... seems like a different little world only devs knows about. Not as easy as in similar games. Upgrades seem also not so big.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun rogue like, bullet hell, JRPG-esque game.If I had to describe it, it's like vampire survivors mixed with Diablo 1The game starts very, very slow. It offers a fairly decent challenge. Eventually you begin to get items and permanent stat upgrades for gold. This helps you progressYour scaling is much slower than vampire survivors. In vampire survivors you eventually become a giant blob of destruction. In this game you become strong but you always have to be mindful of where you're running or have something to dodgeI haven't reached end game yet so I'll update if that changesAs for new armor items you find during a run, towards the end of the run or any point you can put the items "somewhere" and make them available for purchase for your next run. When the levels end there is always a boss and you can leave when you want. Each level has notes which help share an secret or important information. After you beat a level you unlock an "agony" mode which is harder. You unlock more classes as well. There is a big 1.0 content releasing soon so now is a perfect time to start. If you've played deep rock galatic survivors, vampire survivors, then you may like this game.So far I've found it a little harder than vampire survivors. It's getting easier with upgrades now though. Very fun.
