_childDocuments_.review: Halls of torment is surprisingly good, once again, it's another clone of  Vampire Survivors which at this point is basically its own genre. It takes many good ideas from several games and inspiration from things like old school Diablo to make a really solid new game. The gameplay, progression, visuals and overall experience is awesome. The gameplay here is solid, it's a Vampire Survivors like game, it's got awesome new ideas on top of mixing in new ideas. You start off as one of a few characters and you survive for 30 minutes while hordes of enemies come towards you. You gain XP upon killing your enemies that level you up and with each level you gain new enhancements to your character. These enhancements can be things like attack speed, extra health or even adjustments to how your attacks function. You can also find these scrolls on the map which provide you with extra attacks to add to your character. The enemy design here is great, they move in really cool patterns and the game fills the screen with things to kill all the time. Even the bosses are good, everything here keeps you moving and keeps the game exciting. That's pretty much it, that's the loop of the game. What makes it even greater is the progression outside of the runs you do. You have tons and tons of quests and objectives to do. These tasks are pretty simple but they provide you with new abilities and content and also gold which is the currency for upgrades. These upgrades really make a big difference to the difficulty in the game, there's a fair amount of grinding but after some play time the game does get much easier. There is also this armour system, similar to something you would see in diablo or other RPG games. You collect armour and gear which improves your base stats, so far I have not found anything extremely special but that might change as I progress through the game. The level design is great, there is currently a good amount of levels to play on with plenty of objectives. Most importantly they have very good level design which makes them feel very unique each time you do a run. On top of all of this, there are tons of achievements and all kinds of extra bits. One point of feedback is currently quests do not show up anywhere while you are in a run which can be quite tedious to figure out what you should do next, it would be great if the game allowed you to see the current main quest while you are in the middle of a run. The art in the game is awesome, it's very reminiscent of Diablo and other dark fantasy themes. It's got a very solid retro style and everything from the levels, UI, attacks and enemies look great. The music here is great, it all just sounds perfect, spooky and grim is the best way to describe it. There aren't too many varied tracks but what exists is solid and coming from such a small studio I would expect much less. As for performance, the game runs pretty solid, I didn't notice any temperature issues, however I did have some very minor FPS drops when the action got a little hectic. It did not hinder my experience but hopefully in time we can see some improvements. There was not a single bug that I experienced during my play time. In conclusion the game is off to an amazing start, it's still in early access and it has so much promise, what already exists is a near perfect game and with some more time it could be one of the best in the genre. I love how much style the game has and it really captures the dark fantasy feel. The gameplay is great, progression is really fun and there is tons of content for the price, i would very much recommend you give this game a try. I am looking forward to further updates!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must-play! It masterfully blends the best elements of Diablo and Vampire Survivor while carving out its own unique style. The more you play, the more engaging it gets. One of its standout features is the freedom to develop your own play style, with characters that evolve based on your choice of weapons and class. This ensures every playthrough feels fresh and personal. You won't get bored—each boss fight pushes you to keep going, leveling up and perfecting your skills. It innovates within the Bullet Hell, Roguelike, and ARPG genres by taking the best aspects from previous hits and enhancing them.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing.I bought this game after trying out the demo and expecting there to be more to it given the current "overwhelmingly positive" rating on steam. The game is bland. Every playthrough feels the same. Most of the characters have essentially the same attack (some variation of doing damage in a cone). Only the sorceress and the one with the dog stand out a bit for me, since one can use a bit more positional play with them. The incremental impact of in-game upgrades is so small that they make no difference to the gameplay -- what you are doing feels the same whether it is minute 1 or minute 30 (e.g. one usually needs 4-5 upgrades in multistrike just to get a second projectile...). The abilities bring in a bit of much-needed variety, but their upgrades are only slightly better than the standard upgrades.One can gather items to equip as one progresses. Some are decent, but I ended up staying with what I found in the beginning (mostly stacking block) because there was no incentive to change it really and it was good enough to clear all levels with any character (on agony too). The sense of progression in general is lacklustre in the game. Maybe things could still be changed, but it does not sound like the devs are planning to do so.I come to this game after having played Vampire Survivors. VS is hardly a game (you just move around), but at least it is fun and has a sense of mystery (lots of things to discover). HoT has moving around and aiming, but it just feels tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good entry into the increasingly crowded Vampire Survivor like game market. I will say that VS is still the better game overall, and if you don't have that, then get it now!While this has a lot in common with VS, it manages to be its own thing, and it feels like it has a lot of Diablo DNA in it. The runs aren't as varied or fun as VS as it is more about character improvement and you will play the same class a lot and you don't get many new weapons during a run. A key difference over VS is the ability to manually aim at targets, which is crucial sometimes. You can toggle autoaim/autofire while playing.The controls are very tight and allows you to thread the needle between mobs of enemies with precision. The game feels a lot more skillful to play than VS where the weapons are doing the hard work rather than the player.This is an easy recommendation for fans of VS who are looking for a different take on the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I'm going to change my review. I (mostly) recommend the game now.I went back and played some more and got into it all over again. The problem I had before was that I went to the new content and just got destroyed. I felt in control before but now I was a newb. But I tried out the Agony system and I like it. I see the logic behind some of the changes and can see where they're going. It still feels really fun in the first two acts.The difficulty does ramp up too quickly though. When you die to swarms of enemies that have too much health it feels bad. Even if you think you're not making any mistakes, you will die to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But there's too much good here to leave this a bad review.I'll leave my old review here for transparency...____Two days ago I was forming my glowing review of this game in my head. It was better than VS I was to declare, mainly because it was harder and required more skill, and the enemies were more varied, 'meaty', and fun to kill. After the latest patch those words don't fit anymore. There are two new classes and a new zone introduced, but also new bugs. And the game moved from 'hard' to 'frustrating'. Enemies are bullet sponges, and exp gain has been nerfed.The devs seem to have misunderstood their own game. Players do not want a dark souls-like challenge requiring patience and persistence to complete. We (or at least I) want to gain power, kill lots of stuff, and make steady progress at unlocking all the goodies. I want to have fun. This is a passing dalliance, not a new part of my life. Give me a 20-30 hour ride to 80% completion and wake me up when you have DLC. Which I will buy. I have no doubt the devs will reconsider their changes, but until then I have to give this a bad review.

_childDocuments_.review: ‘Halls of Torment’ sets itself apart in the very ‘hands-off’ genre of auto-battler rogue-like RPGs, or as I like to call them: “Survivor-like’s”. It does this by adding stage dependent quests, as well as armor/jewelry that you equip in a Diablo-esque character menu. Each game you can only get a few pieces of armor, but you’ll soon unlock the town's merchant, allowing you to pass 1 item down a well per game, which you can then buy from him as a permanent upgrade/equipable. Bosses also function as proper bosses in Halls of Torment, with AoE and projectile based abilities that you have to dodge. This in conjunction with the ability to aim your attacks, Halls of Torment sometimes functions as a more “traditional” ARPG, than just an auto battler. On top of all this, you don’t ever have the issue of running out of level upgrades, unlike ‘Vampire Survivors’, which usually caps your damage off - this makes picking the right upgrades important, for example, you might not get enough movement speed or damage for the final boss. Each class here feels truly unique, and it is definitely the case of quality over quantity, with each character having their own specific main weapon, which will change what equipables you might bring, as well as what upgrades you might choose. It doesn’t vary too much, but it does benefit replayability. The main thing that Halls of Torment does differently, and the thing that sets itself apart, is its visuals, audio, and music, which all mimic ‘Diablo’ 1 and 2. This overall aesthetic/theme bolsters up those who are nostalgic for those games, while for those who haven’t played them, will at the very least be charming/unique. I personally love this overall style, and wish more games would use it, similar to how we have a plethora of ‘Doom’-inspired games nowadays. Overall, Halls of Torment is great, and there is a lot here already despite being an ‘early-access’ title. The price point is very reasonable, there aren’t any bugs or poor optimisation issues - it’s a solid product with no glaring downsides.

(and not in a good way)This is all especially apparent in the newly added area and the new hard mode called Agony, where a lot of characters and builds don't even function properly. _childDocuments_.review: Currently, this is the best game in the "Bullet Heaven" genre. Everything from the art style, to the sound design, to the itemization and gameplay is cohesive. This is what we imagined Diablo 1 was actually like, back when it came out in 1997. Each class you pick has their own unique weapon that tends to be the primary focus, rather than selecting spells or weapons that are accessible to every class in Bullet Heaven games. Non-unique spells do play an important role in complementing your offense, but they tend to be the dressing or sides. Upgrades, whether from leveling up or finding gear somewhere in the level, feel meaningful. You will notice distinct builds and playstyles for each class, greatly differentiating how even the early portion of runs start. This developer needs all of the support they can get. It would be an injustice for this game to not get more thoroughly crafted and considered content.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just another horde survival game, but one of the better ones. Superior to Vampire Survivors imo. It's up there alongside Boneraiser Minions as an equal-best of the genre.The game excels primarily in presentation: it really feels like a 90's ARPG, like Baldurs Gate or Diablo, in terms of game-feel, animations, sounds, music and cutscenes.I found the gameplay to be addictive, and the progression was satisfying.There is a large array of characters to play and skills/spells to learn, and they all feel quite unique, as you plunge into the three large levels on offer. I'm looking forward to the dev adding more content. I finished all of the stuff currently available in about 18 hours.Most powerful of all is the fact that you can aim your spells/attacks, so it feels much more like an ARPG, as opposed to many games in this genre which end up feeling more like idle games.

_childDocuments_.review: Unquestionably the best game for the price point. Couldn't have asked for a better experience nor updates for the game with the current price tag as it stands. GOTY material right here.If you guys want to take something to improve on; continue optimizing the game until you get so much head-room with the frame-times so you can gradually keep on increasing the amount of concurrent enemies on the screen (assuming you're hitting 300+ enemies 5 times/s in a cone-area, while dealing DOT and AOE, doing all those calculations while moving).This would definitely allow you guys (the best Devs<3) to expand and flesh out your own visions (also the players', when required) for the future capabilities and game modes. I'm kind of hoping that this game will keep its' perfect and simplicit design, but make it possible for the player to keep engaged for a longer period of time, resulting in replayability.If you're asking for something concretely analogous to my previous point; I'd throw out something along the lines of Diablo III:s `Torment` -difficulties.I'm not saying you "SHOULD" implement that exact system, but something along the general idea of what that system is designed to achieve -- it's not intrusive, nor game breaking. Nor is it trying to sell you something which takes away from the player or from the overall game experience. That system achieves at giving more headroom for increased play-time and thus more opportunities to get even more hooked to explore and try out new things, like builds.The next idea which would totally make the game "endless" and exciting would be procedurally-generated maps from the assets. Going beyond that, maybe having some mip-mapping so that you could have "biomes" that interpolate smoothly from one map style to the other, which would then trigger biome-specific mob spawning in the early game. Maybe even put a rare cartography table as an item somewhere hidden inside the "starting" chunk-zone so that you can open an overlayed map to show the outlines where you've been, but I'd say -don't- display locations of any crates, items, etc.After this, I would argue to incorporate endless waves/hordes/survival -mechanic where the timer goes reversed (how long can you survive). Also probably a good idea to disable the revive blessing and the ring from this game-mode (or make it an option to disable it, by which you could for example, give the player +x% XP gain while revive is turned off, or post-increment the torment score by a factor of some percentage that seems fair and balanced [thinking of leaderboards]). A substitute for this could be having a generic "Hardcore" mode which would achieve just the same, which might better suit the perfect simplicit game-logic design.Thank you so much for this game<3

_childDocuments_.review: "A Nostalgic Journey with a Fresh Twist."If you're a fan of classic Diablo games and looking for a fresh alternative to Vampire Survivors, Halls of Torment is a must-try. This game beautifully combines elements of nostalgia with its own unique aesthetic, offering a captivating experience for dungeon-crawling enthusiasts.One of the first things that struck me about Halls of Torment is its visual style. It's a delightful throwback to the classic Diablo era, with pixel art that oozes charm and nostalgia. Every corner of the game world feels meticulously crafted, drawing you deeper into its dark and atmospheric setting.But Halls of Torment isn't just a visual homage to the classics—it brings its own flair to the table. The gameplay is engaging and addictive, with challenging dungeons to explore and foes to vanquish. Each encounter feels satisfyingly strategic, requiring careful planning and quick reflexes to succeed.And let's not forget about the music. It's nothing short of fantastic, setting the perfect mood for your journey through the halls of torment. From haunting melodies to adrenaline-pumping beats, the soundtrack elevates the entire experience to new heights.Of course, no game is without its flaws, and Halls of Torment is no exception. There are occasional bugs and balancing issues that can detract from the immersion, but these are minor inconveniences in an otherwise stellar experience.In conclusion, if you're craving a dose of nostalgia with a fresh twist, look no further than Halls of Torment. With its classic Diablo-inspired visuals, engaging gameplay, and fantastic music, it's a journey well worth embarking on.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: A unique take on the VS genre, Halls of Torment takes Diablo mechanics and mixes them with horde based survival. The game is highly replayable, and each run feels like you are progressing more in the meta game, from unlocking new equipment, to upgrading your blessings. This game is very heavy on the meta progression side of things, but it feels extremely nice. There was nearly 0 times I had to grind, besides to get the last achievements needed for 100%, which took a few extra runs. The game feels very fair, as you unlock up to 10 rerolls for abilities, among other upgrades to your level up selection. at the time of this review, there are 12 characters, each with unique attacks and traits, making the game feel fresh each time you unlock a new one. I highly recommend this game for people who are seeking a new take on the genre.

Diablo aesthetic with graphics and music.Intensity starts out higher than VS and keeps escalating. Manual aiming adds engagement and challenge. There is an option for auto-aim but I didn't have it enabled.Sound and music are good. Mowing down hordes of skeletons and hearing their clinking bones crumble to the ground is very satisfying.Enemy variety is good and new enemy types keep coming at you throughout the run. There are boss characters to focus down while managing enemy hordes coming at you. Very engaging.Native Linux client. Full controller support.Looking forward to playing more and seeing where this game goes!

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - Amazing 7 hours (At time of EA review)	- Game is Survivors-like (Action Roguelike Reverse-Bullet Hell), of similar kin to 'Vampire Survivors' with the flavour of 'Diablo 2'.	- Combat is simple and autonomous yet satisfyingly addictive, focusing on balancing a variety of upgrade abilities and strategies to employ against a massive horde enemies.	- The puzzle of making it through to 30 minutes in each level without dying is challenging without being overly frustrating, providing a good balance between difficulty and enjoyment.	- The upgrades strewn across the map encourages exploration and rewards players.	- Multiple characters with their own quests and expansive traits for additional replayability.	- Finding a items and taking it back to a well for one-time purchase and permanent use in future runs adds depth to the gameplay experience, offering additional content beyond the main storyline.	- The graphics in Halls of Torment are faithfully themed to the Pixel Art of 'Diablo 2'.	- The upward trend of enemies and your ability upgrades fill the screen with effects, causing the feeling of both pressure and power.	- Make sure to balance XP to upgrade with retrieving scrolls to add additional abilities.	- Focus on using gear and upgrading abilities that complement the character that you've picked.Perfect game for when you want to mindlessly waste 30 minutes+ and not have to think too much.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll compare this to vampire survivors as that's where most people will come from.- Vampire survivors is a bit more addictive and fun, but that's because this game is not even done yet while VS even has DLCs now. Halls of Torment will catch up, I'm quite confident of that.- The focus is a little less on epileptic exploding screens with hordes of enemies at all times, and more on steady progression after runs and boss fights.- I'm missing the regular loot box drops from VS, this game relies more on upgrades after leveling up. That is fine, but a bit less interesting.- The equipment system is a nice addition and something VS lacks.- The tone of the game is less humorous and quirky, and more "Diablo 1 and 2". Some NPCs having voice lines and some (hidden) story elements are also very reminiscent of Diablo.- Final level bosses turn a round from an undead genocide simulator to a bullet hell. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do, but I just find it dull... at least for now. I know roguelites can sometimes take a long time to get going due to the long-term progression/unlocks, but weapon varieties, items, and character abilities really don't seem to have all that much variety yet in my 5+ hours. Weapon "evolutions" are very basic and uninteresting, like adding a shock effect to the lightning strike... I have yet to see ones with total changes to how the skill works and looks. In-round upgrade choices are VERY basic and boring, like +10% damage and +6% movement speed. The long-term progression is the same: incremental percentage upgrades. Enemies and projectiles swarm you constantly and damage ticks super fast even with a lot of the long-term progression leveled up. Maps are largely just endless variations of the same few tiles.As someone who has played the vast majority of these bullet heaven style games, I think there are a lot better options as of right now. Rogue Genesia, Nordic Ashes, Boneraiser Minions, Brotato, Vampire Survivors, 20 Minutes Til Dawn, and Soulstone Survivors are all better more nuanced games in the genre. That said, I will keep an eye out for updates to core systems and content and update my review accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game used to be better but there was a patch kind of "streamlining" it. I just did an experimental run on agony ("hard") difficulty frozen depths where I picked all the first passives/abilities that came up essentially making the run random. It did not matter at all, you can pick anything and still win easily. Considering that due to the nature of the game the only inputs from the player are your leveling and ability decisions aside from some simple strafing mechanics, this then becomes a boring idle game.I also think the buffs you can get to start out with after a while are way too strong especially since starting stronger makes you kill and level up faster, further cementing your advantage. It is much more fun to get horizontal progression and try out new builds and find new combinations to beat hard content instead of just getting giga raw stat buffs and plowing through everything. It is bad game design to make a game easier as you progress through.Ideally such a game as this is balanced by exponentially synergistic elements, interesting passives and finding some fresh combo of traits/abilities each run. That is completely absent as each run and character is basically the same. Also there is almost nothing on the maps but the same layout repeated. I wish there were certain events or quests or something to spice it up a little besides just running in circles on spawn after getting the two scrolls.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the demo literally to DEATH! The Full game is AWESOME! Plays like the demo but with more quality of life changes, and more items, maps, and characters.I do own Vampire Survivors and many of it's clones, but this feels fresh, looks GREAT and plays even better!It is an isometric game where you survive hordes of enemies until you face the boss of that map. Being able to aim makes the game All the more fun, and challenging, yes, the game is tough! I am VERY happy that it FINALLY came out and is as good, or better than the demo in so many ways!!! I love the graphics, the feel of the game, and the freedom to move and shoot by aiming, you can set it to auto shoot, or manually shoot with the right stick almost twin stick style.This game is a steal at it's current price, and WAY better than most AAA titles out there! If you like Vampire Survivors with Original Diablo/Diablo 2 type graphics, BUY THIS!*EDIT* One thing however, there is a boss that shoots a curse at you, two in it's second form, no matter if you are fully leveled, or are godlike, he can curse you twice, many are HATING this, there is a way around this however, and it will take patience, and work!You can unlock the sorceress(check the in game pillar on how to unlock her) and melt him before the curse kills you, you can also get two revives that you can unlock with in game currency(in the buffs pillar), and you can get a revive ring in game. These types of games are about taking many steps to the goal, and they aren't designed to be beaten on your first run by everyone, most of these games are punishing and take awhile to figure out, and vibe with. Don't give up, and keep trying! I've done it and I am not very good at most games, just keep trying!

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review:The game had its official 1.0 release.  I had previously not recommended this game.  Have I changed my mind?No.It's still unbalanced.  It crashes or bugs out more than ever.  The challenge modifiers aren't fun.  I think if you play for less than 15hrs you will probably enjoy yourself.  If you want to try and unlock most of the content or try for most of the achievements then you are in for pain.Previous Review:I had a lot of fun with this.  Why am I not recommending it?  The big August 2023 update that added new characters, new spells, a new map, and new features is just not good.  One of the new characters is ok, the other (spear+dog) is darn near unplayable.  The new spells are meh and tend to have very poor damage output.  The golem spell, which used to be the game's 'never take' spell now looks darn right reasonable next to the fire strike ability.  That's not hyperbole: the fire strike spell was so bad I thought it was bugged, and then I saw the damage levels for the achievements were like half that of the other spells.  So they know its bad, they just don't care to fix it.What it boils down to is that I have no confidence these balance problems will be fixed.  If you're fine with paying a few dollars, playing until the novelty wears off, and that's fine with you, then go for it, it's a fine game.  If you want to unlock everything...you're in for a painful grind that will rub your nose in the game's flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an over rated and over hyped rip off of Vampire Survivors.  I do not understand this genre and fans' response to it.  In any way. In fact, 20 minutes to Dawn, a game which wasnt fortunate enough to randomly get covered by a streamer, did BOTH of those things (also wasnt the first in any way).   Yet that game doesnt get the wonderful reviews this one gets.Point is...its under $5 so it's o.k. for what it is...but it IS another rip off of Vampire survivors (which is actually a rip off of a mobile game). _childDocuments_.review: If one likes games with good gloomy mood and well-balanced progression -- e.g., diablo 2 -- one might also like Halls of Torment. I would summarize the *positive* aspects as follows:- Good progression. Game is divided into 30-minute runs. In each run, one starts from level 1 and gain traits by levelling up. In the beginning, even the easiest 30-minute dungeons are impossible to complete. However, one gains items, gold for blessings, elixirs, and complete milestones that all yield permanent advantages that last between runs.- Good build diversity. There are several different classes and each can be built in a lot of different ways by selecting different items and opting for different so-called abilities (spells, really).- Great soundtrack. It makes the game immersive.- Well-tuned. The game never feels too easy or too difficult.- Fun gameplay. Gameplay is similar to diablo or similar games. The developers have managed to capture a feeling of helplessness, as you try to avoid monsters and kill your way towards an escape.There are also a few *negative* aspects:- Descriptions, e.g. of traits, are sometimes unclear.- Game is not as long as, e.g., Elder scrolls games. There is a magnitude or so difference in price though. But it would be nice with more maps.- Graphics is not great. The game looks rather retro, and I imagine many -- myself included -- appreciate this. However, the character appearance does not change at all from equipping items or anything else really. Moreover, monster sprites are quite often reused. It would be nice with more monsters with different appearance and if items made some difference on the appearance.Overall, this is a great game that I strongly recommend. Another recommendation is to not read too much about builds or so. A major aspect of the game is trying out different builds (and it takes only 30 minutes to try one out).

_childDocuments_.review: New York styled Pizza:Pizza dough:14 g instant yeast617g water - 95F950g all-purpose flour19g fine sea salt25g granulated sugarAmerican Pizza Sauce and Toppings:1 tablespoon (14g) butter1 tablespoon (9g) extra virgin olive oil6 cloves garlic, rough chopped2 teaspoons (4g) red pepper flakes28 oz (794g) can of crushed tomato2 teaspoons (2g) dried oregano1.5 tablespoons (21g) granulated sugarsalt and pepper to tasteSplash of olive oil2 cups (227g) low moisture mozzarella, fresh grated2 cups (200g) Monterey jack cheese, fresh grated1/2 cup (26g) parmigiano reggiano, fresh gratedAmerican Pizza Dough:Preheat the oven and a baking steel or pizza stone at 500F for 45 minutes before utilizing it.Whisk yeast and sugar into your water, and allow it to sit for 5 minutes. In a separate bowl, add flour and salt and mix by hand to combine. Pour your water mixture into your flour and mix by hand until you get a rough dough, then transfer to a work surface and knead until it starts to pull away from the work surface and is relatively smooth.Place your dough in a greased bowl, then cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 1 - 2 hours at room temperature or until double in size.Punch down your dough and dive into 300g pieces. Form those pieces into balls and place them in a floured proofing pizza box, cover with a lid, and proof at room temperature for 3 - 4 hours. (If you do not have a proofing pizza box, you can use a floured baking sheet, cover it with an inverted baking sheet and wrap it in plastic wrap.)American Pizza Sauce and Toppings:In a medium sauce pot, add butter and olive oil. Set that over medium-high heat; once the butter melts add garlic, cook until fragrant, add pepper flakes, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the garlic begins to brown on the edges.Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, salt, and a splotch of olive oil, boil over medium-high, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally or until thickened and viscous—season with salt to taste and let it cool down.Assembly.- Place one of your pizza doughs onto a floured pizza peel, and flour your dough generously.Punch your dough down in the center, working your way out to create a ¼” wide. Pick up your dough, place it over your closed fists, and rotate it around, gently stretching to 13” to 14”.Place a couple of spoons of your sauce, starting in the center, spreading in little circles, and working your way to the edge until it gets evenly spread out.In a medium-size mixing bowl, place mozzarella cheese, Monterey Jack, and Parmigiano; mix until combined. Sprinkle your cheese mixture to your desire and place in the oven onto your baking steel and bake for 5 - 7 minutes or until the edge gets golden brown and the cheese melts.Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Can recommend this game. It's a genuinely cool twist on the genre Vampire Survivors pioneered, adding unique weapons for each Character alongside Equipment loadouts for even greater customisation before you even step into the Halls. Once you do, you have myriad abilities to choose from as you progress, each with their own upgrade paths which you unlock and choose from as you progress through the game and it's challenges. Challenges which test your ability to get the most out of every character and every ability.My only snag with this game, as is likely something somewhat personal, is I had sound issues the entire time I played Halls of Torment. Apparently, having done a bit of research, this has something to with users of Focusrite external audio devices. It results in the audio lagging behind and becoming distorted, either gradually as you play or pretty much immediately. I'm hopeful this is something that can be fixed, considering this is still an Early Access title, but something to be aware of potentially.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically Vampire Survivors with a Diablo coat of paint.  If you loved VS than you'll definitely love this game.Like VS your characters start of very weak which means you will likely die a lot.  But there is a tonne of meta progression which will make you ever stronger.  Speaking of characters, you only start out with two, but fear not, as there are currently 5 more that you can unlock by performing certain feats in game.  The meta progression are tied to achievements and there is a lot them (200 atm), that adds MUCH replay value.Aesthetic wise, the game looks amazing as it has a dark Gothic tone which is very reminiscent of Blizzards Diablo.A nice feature that this game has is that it allows the player to toggle on/ off the auto aim and auto attack of your characters.  So if you're someone that prefers to have more direct control of what your character is doing, well you have that option.As of writing this review I have just over 23 hours of game time and yet I've only completed 60% of the game.  And Halls of Torment is only in early access, so there is no telling how much more content that will be added in the future. _childDocuments_.review: I gotta admit I'm a sucker for any game of this genre that allows retrieving gear from runs and thus upgrading your characters and changing the way they can be played but with the 1.0 release HoT really gave it their all and made an already great game even better.The possibility to now also bring back uncommon items allows for even more build diversity while Torment Shards are a possible way to actually get away from some typical BiS items and exchange them for more utility focused gear if one so desires. At the same time the 500 quests in this game at least partially make you play characters in ways you usually wouldn't, giving you incentive to try new things and maybe even find a character playstyle you prefer. Anything you have to do in the game can be done without Torment Shards btw, it's just a nice way to give you an additional power boost if you feel like you're in need of it. Artifacts and the Vault are the final 2 things allowing you to challenge yourself, with the former modifying your runs to make them harder while the latter can indeed become pretty crazy if you spend enough gold on a run. Only thing I really wish this had is an option to tell the game to always automatically pick gold or potions on level up after you've run out of upgrades for the current run (thank you, Vampire Survivors) but the game must be pretty good if that's the only 'issue' I can think of right now. x)Either way this game offers plenty of replayability and in my eyes is very close to the top, maybe even the best of the genre right now - and for the asking price there's nothing you can do wrong here.

_childDocuments_.review: The legions of the Burning Hells spill forth in numbers not seen since the Lord of Terror and his foul brothers walked among us. Wait, it this not Diablo? Halls of Torment nails the early Diablo atmosphere so well, from the rattling of innumerable skeletons to the scotched ground beneath your feet, that you'll swear you've loaded up a remake of the first two games. The gameplay is obviously completely different, especially early on where you'll be losing constantly to make small bits of progress towards conquering a stage. As with any good roguelite, you'll soon be overcoming challenges you couldn't imagine meeting before with your quickly stockpiling strength. After enough quests are completed, blessings are purchased, and equipment is discovered, you'll even start to find those once insurmountable hordes trivial. Blessings can be refunded at any time and equipment can be swapped or removed, but it'll be a lot harder to ignore the more powerful traits coming each level or the increased experience pouring from the quest bonus to return to the place on the power creep arc you enjoyed the most. The stages will grow a little too long for the 'just one more run' rhythm of the early game as you routinely reach the end of the 30 minute timer and face off against the Lord of whatever horrible thing is waiting for you there. You'll look down and realize that an entire night has passed in the span of just a few “30 minute” runs that went far longer. It gets hard to commit to sitting down with the game at that point, but it's even harder to complain about still wanting to. Early Access only seems to mean a limited number of stages, characters, and abilities at this point. The game is already plenty stable. I only saw two crashes in about 40 hours and while there is a bit of slowdown each time the screen fills with monsters and wildly triggering effects, that never made it any harder to guide my character through the gaps in the monster hordes. The visualizations of many of those effects, however, did often make it very difficult to actually see my next move. Information isn't as obvious as it should be with some traits not meshing with the particularities of some characters and others affecting abilities in surprising ways. Not that there's any more room for information during the runs as level ups and hordes constantly descend upon you. But this can make designing builds a bit frustrating, something not made any easier by the randomness of traits and abilities. Though adapting on the fly is part of the fun with these sorts of games.There's currently more than enough possibilities to keep anyone entertained, especially for the current asking price. Even if the promised updates, one of which is planned to hit the beta branch on this very day, never came, it'd still be awfully hard to complain about all the Halls of Torment have to offer.Autumn Sale Update: The previously mentioned planned update has been live for a good amount of time now. It brought a new stage, two new characters, several new abilities, and several new items. These have all been interesting and varied bits of content to explore, but the most important addition since the above review is the new Agony Mode. This mode solves the issue of challenge disappearing with power progression by upping the difficulty based on how well you're doing in a stage. Better yet, this is an optional mode that can be toggled on or off at the start of a stage. The absolute flood of enemies and effects brought about by doing well in this mode can be a severe drain on frame rate and have caused a few more crashes while playing on the Steam Deck. But that is the cost of an ever increasing amount of mayhem, now isn't it?Information is a lot more explicit now as well. The various stats of individual characters can be viewed before selecting them which is a huge help in noting the non-basic differences between them. Your first ability is also now selectable from the full list of unlocked abilities, removing a frustrating source of randomness at the start of each run. Most of my issues with the game have already been resolved and there's more content slated for release early next year. The future of Halls of Torment is looking bright and it has never failed to capture me in the same way it first did every time I return to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I so very much want to give this a thumbs up because they're this close to greatness.For context I've got 100+ hrs in Vampire Survivors and I imagine many other people leaving a review here do as well. I've put in 50 or so hours into this, unlocked pretty much everything there is to unlock at this point in EA, and have about 4 achievements left that I can't be bothered getting at this point.Aesthetically, this game is neat. They've gone after the Diablo 1 vibe, and it probably looks better than what D1 actually looks like - so hats off to them for that. Stilted animations and dialog - all good. Inventory and loot for persistent upgrades? Also cool. So far there are, like, two characters to meet and, well, that's it. If you're expecting "Stay a while and listen", you're out of luck.As for "everything else" - this game and a lot of others like it I feel have fundamentally misunderstood what VS did and I'm not sure that enough people understand this, so I'm going to tell you, because I played that game in its EA phase as well.VS at its core is extremely concerned with a slow but controlled burn for the player, in that it is strict in how characters grow from level to level, how often unique/boss-type enemies appear, when weapon ascendencies can happen and just when the sessions start to feel like they get too long or dull, VS will then offer up a variety of options and mutators to make the game harder and even speed things up. By the time you reach VS' "endgame", yes, a lot of the challenge is trivialized and it's mostly a matter of nuking everything until the time runs out, but up to that point VS does a stupidly good job of controlling the "just one more minute" tension-and-release cycle. Essays can and should be written about what that game does because I am not doing justice to how VS' mechanics overlap to create a stupidly compelling experience. It should not come as a surprise that the developer of that game used to make gambling apps.You'd think HoT would offer the same sort of progression and understanding of VS' systems, but it simply doesn't. For whatever reason, a lot of the upgrades feel pathetic, with the most expensive one (the revive) only being truly worthwhile to a run, with damage and walk speed being the big game changers a distant second. The best thing HoT does on this front is actually make the achievements system boost the XP earned, which is a cool idea... but to have 98% of the things unlocked and have that boost, and wear the +50% xp amulet and *still* not be able to ding level 100 with either the Cleric or the Shieldmaiden by the 30th minute on the hardest area despite multiple attempts? At that point I truly give up, because I think what may have happened is HoT only concerns itself with the first few minutes of play, and not the totality of the run.There are numerous QoL fixes that are (apparently) coming, such as fast restart, being able to reroll scrolls of mastery and so on, but none of are going to fix the inherent problem in the endgame's design, in that there either is none, or it's kinda just down to luck, I guess? This is apparent in the finale of each zone - each boss (or "lord") is an enormous damage soak that, once you get used to their patterns (or just invest enough in walk speed), becomes an exercise in tedium because it just a massive HP pool to drain each time. VS by contrast spends most of its time killing you immediately on the 30 minute mark until you've worked out how to beat the reaper, rather than running away from the reaper until one of you dies of boredom.Don't get me wrong: I don't regret the time spent, and maybe you'll find enjoyment out of this - but don't expect the same arc as you got from VS.

_childDocuments_.review: is a dark fantasy Rogue-lite horde survival game that faithfully re-creates the retro look of the popular 1990s isometric RPGs such as Diablo, Planescape, Baldur's Gate, etc, has a solid progression system and difficulty curve, and implements a few unique things that make it stand out from other games in the genre.Overall, I recommend it because, despite not adding many new innovative things to the genre, it's a solid game which is simply addictive and fun to play. Although the gameplay is typical for the genre, its unique sub-systems make the journey enjoyable and I always found myself wanting to complete the next quest, get another piece of gear, and become stronger via the meta upgrades and equipment to the point where I became unstoppable.Note: this review is current as of the 1.0 patch released on 10 October 2024.- The gameplay is standard among the genre, though it does add a few unique and thematically-appropriate sub-systems (quests and equippable gear) which make progress more tangible;- The replay value is quite high as there are a huge number of classes to unlock, equipment to collect, and meta upgrades to purchase;- The bosses and mini-bosses are varied, well-designed, and engaging (although they can have an excessive number of hit points on the "Agony" setting and take eons to kill);- The graphics look quite nostalgic due to their intentionally low-res and polygonal nature;- The soundtrack is composed of generic atmospheric dark fantasy songs which gets lost among the sound effects;- The voice acting is surprisingly good in quality and adds some charm to the game; and- The story is non-existent and there isn't even anything listed on the store page.The game has 500 achievements which provide good milestones to strive for and help keep you engaged in the game. None of them require any extra grinding and they will all be acquired as you play through the game casually which will take anywhere from 60-80 hours depending on your proficiency in, and experience with, the genre. That being said, around one achievement per class and stage of the 190 new ones that were added in the 1.0 release are asinine and simply not fun as they force you to play the classes in a way that is antithetical to their natural playstyle or play the stages in a way that just isn't enjoyable such as not being able to attack or move for x minutes.The gameplay is typical for the horde survival genre: you die during a run due to being too weak, return to the hub to purchase gear and meta upgrades, and repeat this process numerous times until you are powerful enough to complete a stage. You eventually unlock an optional "Shrine of Torment" mode for which, when enabled, spawns extra mini-bosses every few minutes and has a variable difficulty level that scales based on your performance during the current run.There are 11 different classes that offer very distinct playstyles from one another since they each specialize in a certain set of stats, have a unique starting ability, and have access to upgrades which are exclusive to them. There are also 18 abilities to choose from, of which you can have up to six per run, and each one has three upgrades which considerably increases the build diversity and replayability in general.The bosses are easily one of the highlights of the game because of the way they telegraph their attacks: they mark locations on the ground that will be affected by their attack a second later which gives you ample time to react to and dodge them while also keeping the combat relatively engaging. Unfortunately, one downside is that the bosses tend to have an excessive amount of hit points when playing in the Shrine of Torment mode which unnecessarily extends the length of the boss fights unless you have most of the meta upgrades, have gear which synergizes well with your class, and optimize your build during the run.The bosses also sometimes drop equippable gear which can come in the form of a torso piece, helmet, necklace, ring, boots, or gloves, and is very similar to Diablo-style games. Furthermore, many pieces of equipment offer special passive abilities that you can't get via the meta upgrades or level-up choices which is a fantastic design choice that expands the gear beyond just increasing various stats. Some examples include the ability to summon minions, create hazards on the battlefield, and unusual stat increases which typically have a specific trigger but also a downside to counteract it to make you consider how good it is for your character and build and the overall risk versus reward of using said piece of gear.Like most games in the genre, grinding ends up being ubiquitous but is at least handled in a unique way that gives you palpable milestones to pursue: each stage and class has its own set of quests for you to complete which give you a large variety of rewards and a minor experience bonus for each one that you complete. You also acquire gold throughout a stage, for completing a stage, and through the completion of certain quests, which allows you to purchase meta upgrades and equippable gear.The graphics accurately re-create the retro look of the 1990s isometric RPGs that were popular at the time, to the point where the game looks a little low-res and you can make out the polygonal shapes. In fact, some of the finer details seem like they were ripped straight from the Diablo series such as the red orb which represents health and some of the pieces of equipment. The three character portraits in the game look especially polygonal which actually adds a certain level of charm to the game.The soundtrack is made up of atmospheric dark fantasy songs that suit the area they are played in but are otherwise forgettable and often get lost among the sonorous sound effects; however, there is only one final boss theme in the entire game for five of the six stages and it becomes extremely repetitive when you are playing on the Shrine of Torment mode and the final bosses have a copious amount of hit points. Additionally, there is voice acting for the three characters that you can interact with which is surprisingly good.The story is completely non-existent and there isn't anything in-game or even on the Steam store page which is odd because developers usually put at least some sort of backstory in the description on the store page.The developers have been doing an outstanding job with the game so far by releasing frequent updates to the game in order to balance the game and add new classes, quests, gear, abilities, quality of life features, and many other things since its Early Access release. In fact, most of the qualms that I had with  have been assuaged as they added most of the missing quality of life features that I listed in my review of it (which you can find  if you're interested). Additionally, the developers added a feature which checks if you have a save file from  and carry over its data if you do which is very convenient and generous.Overall, I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of the horde survival genre as it's one of the best ones on the market: it's well-executed, polished, fun, engaging, and it even manages to deliver a hint of nostalgia. If you're not sure whether the game is for you then you can always try out the free Prelude which I linked above to see if you like the core concept of the game but be aware that it's missing a lot of content compared to the main game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the current endgame boss—although there's tons of quests to finish and achievements still to unlock, and I'm definitely not done playing. I've got to say this is my favorite Vampire Survivors-like of all time.I love the art style—it's retro, but in a tasty nostalgic way that doesn't sacrifice variety and has some pretty cool animations thrown in. Very old-school dungeon crawl monster manual kind of aesthetic. There are a lot of very different and cool characters, lots of weapons and abilities, and there's a lot of room to craft unusual builds that work.But the best part is the pacing and balancing. You know that feeling of definitely being screwed this time, and you're absolutely not going to make it, but you might as well keep struggling? And then the tide imperceptibly turns and you wriggle out of your doom yet again? To me that's the perfect balance of difficulty, and at least for me, this game has served it up consistently. It's something you can very much tweak to your preferences. Whenever I feel like I'm winning just a bit too easily, it's simple to add a couple more modifiers (with quests and rewards attached) and right back to barely mostly squeaking by.At the price, if you like bullet heaven games with lots of meta progression and a consistent aesthetic (which I think this game does WAY better than Vampire and most of its descendants), it's super easy to recommend. The demo is generous with its content and free, give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Dont launch this expecting to just win because you've played Vampire survivors or some other bullet heaven.This game is great though. Some enemies block attacks, some enemies dont walk straight at you, some react to your movement.The sound design in this is great, hits feel good when they connect with enemies. Skeletons rattle or clank when you hit them, the sound of them dying sounds like bones falling on each other. Getting hit is responsive, picking up XP is ASMR.Items come in a good bit of variety. Some are basic stat buffs, some are passives that go off when you're hit, some are based on elements (like fire, ex +2% damage per burning enemy). You can just pick up some nice stats or even build completely around a mechanic. I love the wind crown, 1% attack speed per kill lasting 5 seconds, up to 50%. Abilities might seem a little odd at the start. Just play with them and discover how good they can be. Some characters are best to focus on their main weapon, some can excel with abilities. Level them to level 3 and you can get special augments. Game goes hard. Its fun. Yes it plays on your diablo 2 nostalgia, but it actually improves on this genre in a direction that I like. The sound design and visuals coming off diablo 2 are genuinely nice. It just sets a great tone for the game and my GOD do I love the animations. The shield maiden looks a lot like the warrior from diablo 1 but that's honestly a nice thing, its a great animation set.There's lots of room for improvement. Lots of room for growth, more variety, new characters, abilities, augments and items.Its fun stuff and as usual in the genre, it's not expensive. Highly recommend if it looks like something you'd like or has some of the genres you enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment stands tall in the survival game arena, bearing echoes of Vampire Survivors and Diablo 2 in its retro aesthetic and thrilling, horde-battling gameplay. The game's strategic depth, with myriad hero characters and abilities, engrosses you from the get-go. However, the boundary between this hauntingly fascinating underworld and the reality begins to blur, as days and nights melt into one another.The charm quickly turns into a comedic tragedy as the game seeps into the real world. Seemingly innocuous objects turn sinister, children's toys transform into menacing enemies, and a trip to the grocery store feels like a dungeon crawl. No place feels safe; every corner conceals potential adversaries.To shake off these visions, you turn to alcohol and pills, but the monsters merely sway, refusing to fade away. The final blow comes when, in a well-meaning but misguided attempt to protect your territory, you wage war on your children's toys in the yard. What was once an amusing decline spirals into a crisis, leading to a week-long stay in the local hospital.So while Halls of Torment offers a thrilling and engaging gaming experience, it also serves as a comedic, yet cautionary tale of how deeply a game can permeate the walls of our reality. Enjoy the descent into the abyss, but remember to keep a firm foot in the real world, lest you find yourself swinging at imaginary foes in your backyard.

You can reroll abilities on scrolls. You can reroll equipment in chests. And more!Many many achievments, each with meaningful unlock.The basic gameplay is similar to Vampire Survivors. This is more in depth with combat, elements, play style, and upgrades ie damage, speed etc.Agony is actually very difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Jeez this game stole so many hours from me. I didn't even know that I had 20 hours to give while studying 13 hours a day. This is an awesome rogue like. I still feel like though these genres should allow u to change the time limit in the game cuz 30+min run can get long when ur trying to squeeze them in ur schedule.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 : One of the best survivor-like at the moment.+ Progression is fun and rewarding : Retrieving new pieces of armor, buying potions and bonus stats for your characters, earning new characters by completing levels.. There is a lot to do.+ Builds you want to try with rare and fun ways to upgrade your chosen abilities.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Initially it seems like a rather shallow, slower-paced Survivors game, but the deeper you get, the more the complexity comes out. "Winning" isn't particularly difficult, but there's a lot (200+ as of now, still in EA) of in-game challenges (which are also achievements) that have rewards and unlocks associated with them - those are the real game. Some of them are fairly easy, but others require some real effort to 'solve'.The unlockable potions are also surprisingly deep. They let you affect the upgrades you're offered in various ways - rerolling them, saving one for later, doubling the effects of one, or removing one from the pool entirely; this is a much more important system than it initially looks like, too. The 'save an upgrade for later' one actually lets you take two normally mutually exclusive upgrades, and choosing what to double is a very important decision for some builds.There's a lot of characters (who all have unique achievements and who all play differently), and at the current time 5 maps, and a 'hard mode' on each map, as well. Really, there's a lot of content here, and it's well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment is a game that lovers of moody journeys must play. It offers a unique gaming experience because to its breathtaking visuals, captivating gameplay, and captivating story. Get ready to be mesmerized by the eerie beauty that the Halls of Torment have in store for you.Love love love 10\10
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't bad. It's okay. But it's nothing but a pretty mediocre grind to the endgame. And once you get there.. there is nothing to do.However it has an aesthetic that reminds you of D2, it's fun for a bit to try certain things and some of the milestones (achievements) require a bit of figuring out how to get them. Its fine to kill a few days. But you'd be better off doing something for your real life.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Feels bad man. I appreciate the style and vibe the devs are going for, but the gameplay is sour. So many better bullet heavens out there. Boring level up options (6% range, woo), Boring items (one item drop every like, ten minutes, "+10% Defense and Health", yay...), horrendous screen readability (I get hit by enemies more often just due to the fact that I couldn't see them for the spell effects, color palettes, and attack animations), poorly explained mechanics (half the stats change based on which character you pick and also per spell you pick up; you pick up temporary boons of which I have no idea what they do), Boring and unbalanced secondary spells (some do literally 20-30% of the damage of others over the course of a run), the list goes on.Don't worry though, once per full mission you can send one of the two items you got that run up a well to use in future runs. That means you get to send up three pairs of gloves even though you've been playing for two hours and you already have better gloves in the first place, because RNG. Then you have to pay a full run's worth of metacurrency collected to actually use it. Great first-impression experiences there...
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: First Time for me enter these halls of bullet hell type of games. Played pretty much 8+ hours straight and had so much fun.Roguelite / RPG elements with old school Diablo style graphics is so good combination. Classes feels good in their own way (11 of them). Worlds have unique touch & monsters (5 worlds). Music is good, have the same vibe. It's fun to find new items. Make interesting combinations for builds with armors and such. Payed 3,74e for it. It would deserve 5e though in my opinion.For small game, and maybe small team. This game is delivering of what it tries to be. Can see though it can get boring very quick from here. Wish there be future DLC for more Worlds to explore, new gear and maybe classes. So far, do not regret my purchase. Willing to support this game more in future if they add more content. For sure its so fun and addicting already.If you enjoy these kind of games and are fun of the "Vibe". Get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid Survive-Rogue. Ironically by being one of the most "return to form" variants out there, it's also one of the more unique as it handles in a much different way than your usual Survival-like. This is a plus for me but some people may just want the stack abilities on abilities until everything is dead approach compared to Halls' more traditional hack and slash build.Upgrades are meaningful and there are a lot of achievements and unlock for you completionists like me who crave the dopamine hit of seeing that little rectangle box at the bottom of the screen. Each character is vastly different functionally due to the weapon they have equipped so in my short play each run has been a little different. It's a little harder than some other Survival-likes I feel but that's a bit of a plus. Highly recommend it for fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: If  you like this genre and ideally own steam deck, worth purchasing even in EA.Game is ok and summarized already in reviews before mine. What I can't imagine is to play this on PC after regular work (programmer) ... Simply not happening. But on steam deck or console - yeah. I personally play this only on steam deck, so dunno how it works on pcIt has Diablo 2 feeling, but I'd preffer to have variable play time. 30 mins per run is quite a lot. I dislike this even for other alternative games out there. Why I can't choose time scaling by my own is simply bad design choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry but it really didn't get to me... The leveling up is really underwhelming and the abilities are just... "ok".Also the enemies are tooooooooo bullet spongy from the start of the run.I didn't like that you can't change the game's resolution and that everything is soooo old-looking... Yes it may have it's charm, but I also don't want to look at a game made in 2023 that looks like it was made in 1996... Or if you really want to give that impression, at least let the player decide the resolution, so it doesn't destroy its eyesight.The good part is that there are many quests and unlocks which is really good for a game like this since it greatly increases the replay value, but yeah other than that the gameplay loop is ehhhhhhhh...If I may give a suggestion, make getting abilities easier and more impactful, because having only one or two abilities other than the basic attack for the first 8 - 10 minutes of the game is just boring
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Its like Vampire Survivors but looks like DiabloHas some small differences compared to Vampire Survivors.- Everyone has an unique Attack (that can be clicked and aimed). You can put the settings on "auto" and it will attack automatiicaly for you, however, there are passives that icrease the damage of your main attack if you dont permanently auto-spam it.- Every other boss drops equipment that is comparable to typcial RPG equipment (Either pure statboost, an additional passive effect for your build or an unique ability).- After 30 Minutes, the run doesn't just end. A Boss pops up that has to be killed (Comparable to MMORPG bosses (run out of the damage zone and kill it).All in all, the game is great and feels different enough to give it a try if you like Vampire Survivors (or the genre in general). Furthermore as of this Review, the game is still in early access. There might be more to come making it standing out even more.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after watching some streams and seeing something fairly similar to Vampire Survivors. I was mistaken. This is not a "reverse bullet hell", this is a grueling, very grindy, twin-stick rogue-like, which makes you suffer for a long time before grudgingly giving you just enough tools to start climbing the next mountain and suffer more. While this game is definitely really long in terms of time needed to do anything, and it has a lot of tasks to do (such as "earn a million of gold", "walk 100 kilometers", "kill a hundred thousand enemies", "inflict 750000 damage in one run with this ability, then five more similar ones", "debuff a hundred thousand enemies"), it's not... well, fun, I guess. You have to grind in the same two first areas for hours just to get enough gold to buy first upgrades and stop dying in the first few minutes (check the achievements - there is one for surviving six minutes, and not everyone has it), and it gets boring quite rapidly.I'm sure this game has a loyal following, and I'll probably keep grinding very slowly, but it's absolutely not a Vampire Survivors clone, and it's unpleasantly grindy - you have to work a lot doing the same things to make every single small step forward.No big issues in the execution - it's reasonably playable, not a lot of bugs, reasonable graphics and sound.Update after about 5 months and 54 hours played, with 255 achievements of 310: sadly, no, it's not a skill issue. I've already finished most skill-based achievements completed by top 10% players, and it's still a sad and boring grind fest to be dragged on for the next 60 hours. Reasonably well made, and even somewhat enjoyable if not played too often, but still not recommended to people without masochistic tendencies.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm having a good time with Halls of torment.Let's hope the devs keep adding content, balancing and refining mechanics (more importantly  please oh please) and bless us with ever so divine Quality Of Life features.- Cheap, fun and addictive.- I like the slower pace combined with the old school diablo vibe (visuals and sound). Runs are a bit on the longer side (30m + time spent selecting level ups if you didn't die).- You can send back and buy items (one per run) to be able to equip your characters for future runs in addition to buying the tipical metagame buffs (+HP, Attack, Gold etc...).- Controller friendly, autoattack and autoaim. When active, autoaim will take control if you dont aim manually.- Neither too easy nor too hard except for the final bosses.- No ultrawide support.- The game doesn't explain how things work. What does/affects what? What does this character do? Nope, pure guesswork and i loathe opaque mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I'm usually on the fence about Early Access games, but boy does this one VERY much deserve its current Overwhelmingly Positive status even without the finale out quuuite yet. I was already tempted by the early Diablo-style art combined with the bullet heaven playstyle, but the in-map quest system, multistage/tier bosses, coupled with a fun equipment hunting/recovery system on top of general character quest progression improvement, AND clean map drop indicators and auto aim/auto fire in-game on the fly toggles? Chefs kiss. Get in on this if you like the admittedly saturated bullet heaven/VS style gameplay, this one stands out and made more impressive by the team involved. At the least, try the demo they have: I was pleasantly surprised to find out that even after uninstalling the demo, my progression there carried over to the main game!

I really enjoy it.In other games there often comes a point when you're just standing in the middle of a sea of enemies and pushing against it. _childDocuments_.review: This is a 'hold off for now' type of review:I'm not exactly sure why this game is getting such high reviews, other than it's clear "Diablo 2 baiting" in the style of the graphics. The items are nice, but don't seem to do very much, the graphics are...a throwback, and quite muddy, making it extremely difficult to see just what the heck is taking off my health, The weapons are boring, feel weak as all get out, don't scale very well, and the level-up abilities are just flat-out boring; the weapon system needs a very large overhaul if this game is going to be fun in the long run.
