_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: goodplay it blind for best experience ; something unknown is better discovered than farmed and rushed for. refreshing and strange to see a game that has achieved (at the time of writing)- no best in slot gearing ; all of it is playstyle optional choice (VERY DIFFICULT TO DESIGN -- Path of Exile did this with it's skill tree, in a 5$ game, something functionally the same and far simpler is a very big surprise.)- distinct tradeoffs that do not feel punishing for not playing a certain way ; get the item that supports it , or the item that covers other aspects so it makes what you do viable- everything is unlocked through natural gameplay , never felt "I needed a wiki / google or I missed this entirely". it does give optional quests as guidance.- bosses feel good and can be played around regardless of build.- characters and items are different enough from eachother that runs feel influenced by it.some things can be a bit odd, and feel like they were thrown in for fun in an otherwise punishing game.there's a potion that lets you 2x a level up ability you can get fairly early on, when progression is gated into trees - getting a capstone twice is huge. it's fun, so it's fine.it can be odd to use this potion to break linear , like Proficient Stance 1 ( Wide Attack ) giving 20% range, 50% area mainhand weapon, which is supposed to be in three parts normally,  instead effectively 6 times. When other upgrades are in the +8% area global, 5% range global as a norm ; being able to do this is massive. It's the only way to do "whole screen" damage I found.Without the potion it is 1 Proficient Stance  - damage orientated, 2 PS - defensive orientated, 3 PS - utility. With potions, you can stall this and freeze a proficient stance progression point to get it more than once. This probably isn't a bug, but it doesn't feel intended either with how the rest of the pacing is. You can do similar things to all abilities. It enables creativity by rewarding thinking, and it is something you somewhat pick up as something you can do intuitively over time - so it's fine, and I wouldn't want it changed, but maybe expanded on in a way that fits the theme of the game, everything seems very intuitive as a choice can make. This is very vague, and you have to really pay attention to the names of the skills and how they work to think to do this. I would like to see a mode that makes the game harder, and one that reduces the amount of time spent as I don't always have 30 minutes to set aside. Runs are also not saved and have to be completed in 1 sitting; you can pause indefinitely but not exit the game. probably to allow more to happen and not be cached / periodically saved in any way which is hardware taxing.The only item I believe needs a change is the Jade Amulet - a flat 50% experience boost is too much acceleration. Completing quests each give 1% each to bonus gained experience, and there's over 300 quests, so effectively completing 50 quests at the cost of an item slot is very strong compared to what the other items offer in the early game when it's unlocked. Eventually this item falls off naturally and you pick the other items because 50% gain isn't very noticeable when you complete 100+ quests; and the other amulets are actually introducing new playstyle methods - which this doesn't, other than offering you a way to seemingly overlevel yourself out of the monsters you're fighting very quickly, which becomes unnecessary, and arguably always is, because it's alleviated without it with the same results by playing better with the other amulets instead; so this amulet enables lethargic gameplay by giving similar results for less effort, while feeling unbalanced when the effort is present.The only downside of the Jade Amulet is the choice to not take any of the other amulets, which isn't enough when they're not yet unlocked, and that experience is capped. which, hitting the cap means experience gain becomes a dead stat with no effect.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: I got bored on the very first run. Two runs total and zero fun. Even the boss-type enemies with unique attack patterns couldn't get me engaged. Autobattlers are inherently mindless but shouldn't feel boring. Circle strafe, select upgrade, and repeat.Reviews seem to be stacked with people who dislike Diablo IV because they thought it would be an autobattler.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: It's doable up to the regular dungeon and the first trial. It's hard to clear from difficulty level 3 and the treasure dungeon, so the game becomes dependent on the difficulty level thereafter. You lose the fun from then on.It's not in the quest, but I cleared the Ghost Cave without taking damage before the boss appeared. Try it if you're bored.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most addicting "survivor" games out there. It is VERY easy to lose hours to this game, and the devs are still steadily adding content. With this said, there are a handful of traits and mechanics which are not properly explained (especially in the UI) which makes the first few hours of this game very trial and error. "Force" is the most notably confusing trait on first go, so I do hope that there are better metric visuals added in the future.There are things missing which are staples from other games of this genre - most glaringly the total lack of turbo. Combined with the ramping up necessity for the first 10 minutes of gameplay, the later half of the matches can tend to feel underwhelming as you progress further through the quests. This is usually an issue with these bullet hell type top down games and long-term progression. However, I do feel that with new additions to exploration (potentially with merchants and secret areas) and with modifications available for the in game timer/speed that Halls of Torment will solidify itself as one of the top dogs in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, if you're a fan of bullet-heavens, survivor-likes, or horde-modes, whatever you call them.It's very much Vampire Survivors meets Diablo 1. A bit less chaotic, a bit more methodical, a bit darker, etc. I enjoy it a lot though. There's depth in the item recovery mechanic, the extra weapon evolutions, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little relaxing game where you can also express a lot of your skills in movement. I'd say I prefer this over the other "Vampire Survivor-likes". It's got an amazing pace, and the upgrades always feel huge and meaningful. It also has a charming retro dungeon crawling artstyle, which I adore.For the price it's a definite recommend, a lot of bang for your buck.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best survivors type games I've played. I'd rank it 2nd place right under the OG vampire survivors. The pacing is fantastic and it always feels like I'm gaining *something* with every run. The characters are varied and the equipment effects are interesting. There are a lot of options and builds you can make!Only gripes I have currently is that there's no way to know what my other potential options are for the tiered upgrades so unless I memorize everything or wait until all of them cycle through, I'm just guessing. And that the levels are kind of big and empty and there's no map to tell me how far away stuff is. And lastly that the abilities don't show up when you look at your stats in the pause menu so you have no idea if certain stats are affecting them at all or how (force?). All in all, highly recommend and can't wait for more updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the worst VS game I've played. You can select a character class, but your character class has exactly 1 ability that differentiates it from every other class. For example, the archer of course shoots arrows and the swordsman swings a sword in a cone, and those abilities can be upgraded, but that's the extent of variety other than RNG during game. And chances are, your RNG isn't even going to have much variety either, because I can count the number of abilities you can get on one hand during a run, at least for the first four hours. When you level up, you can pick a stat increase, like 8% attack speed or something. The only interesting thing about it is the art style.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: 16 hours in and I can barely scavenge enough gold to get the basic meta stats. yet you need the basic meta stats to complete the ridiculous quest lines that half of which don't even make any sense. Quest says to deal 33,333 damage in one hit. I dealt up to 100,000 and it still didn't count.Progression is far too slow and most the abilities either suck or are completely unfun to play with. Where vampire survivors rewards you for playing, this game punishes you. Upgrading ability quest lines just adds more clutter to that ability upgrade path. You're far too weak until you upgrade all the meta stats and you get so few gold from actually playing vs completing quests. Most quests require the meta stats to be upgraded to achieve. There is some good to this game. The blue potion is an amazing new addition to this style of game that gives players the choice of dramatically improving one of their abilities. The equipment system is also a nice addition, although it is also a drag to collect the gear. On top of that it costs gold to obtain. Something which the meta stats also need. If you have a lot of time on your hand, then go for it.But for me, it was just too much of a slow burn.
_childDocuments_.name: Halls of Torment

_childDocuments_.review: I've got all the achievements as of now(12th July 2023) and I think I can write my review now.First of all - great game. Fun to create builds, fun to run around, fun to dodge stuff, just fun altogether.That said game needs some QoL's and rebalancing. - straight up sucks. Roll build is terrible and dps build is hindered by golem being late to the party all the time, even when he's not he doesn't do what he is supposedly capable of. I had 36 Attacks per second 100% crit 500% crit damage 174 base golem which is supposedly 32k dps (on single target, not even counting his cone) do 3 attacks and stand around in a boss. The roll really hinders dps build by resetting his position and taking him out of combat.Remove roll entirely, I don't even feel like it fits the ability. If not, make the DPS evolution remove roll entirely and rework AI/make it faster/make it teleport to the target.Really lackluster, even with both evos it does decently but it's overshadowed by other abilities and doesn't really do anything better than the others, maybe clearing offscreen, but the Ring Blades do it better.Make it physical? At least some synergy with the splash ring.Also pretty lackluster, it does fine but lacks in other departments. I tried full orb extravaganza build(14 orbs with a lot of movespeed) and it didn't really do anything. I do understand that I severely cut on its damage but what's the point of increasing orbs then.Buff roughness and base movespeed? Maybe add movespeed scale with a fraction(like .2) of attack speed? I also don't really feel like they need the crit build path in general.I feel like this is the only truly balanced ability which is not too op but is just good and has a great diversity in build paths all of which work nicely.Jack of all trades master of none. Speccing into anything will probably do worse than any other ability. Lightning strike is just plain better option. Base damage is laughably low, only decent build is stacking electrify with it I guess, but even at that it's not really reliable.Remove the damage branch or rework it and pivot into something else, maybe like thunder crown. In general also a bad thing to have crit build path on.Decent abilities, can work in a lot of situations, but really hindered by being unreliable. Dragon's breath needs some other evolution instead of the push one and its constant evolution really suffers from the burn limit.Can benefit from buffs in anything really, AS/Area/Base damage.The best abilities in my opinion. While Phantom needles and Ring blades are S-tier, Transfixion is SSS-tier. Does it all and does it great. Stacking fragile for single target DPS, screen clearing, great AS for stragglers or killing banshees, great range, great area, scales with anything you throw at it.I feel like they are really neatly balanced and fun, maybe except the Warlock, for me personally he really lacks single target damage. Also summon rings are kind of worthless, doing full summon build isn't that fun and your main weapon will oudamage all your summons combined by like 3x. Summoned units suffer same fate as golem as in coming too late, that's why main weapon is that good for clears. I feel like characters that can't crit can get some alternative scaling from crit and crit damage i.e. 5% crit = 0.05 Attacks and 20% crit damage = 10% cone/area or whatever.There is some decent variety and room for creating builds but some of them are just straight BIS. Like in most situations you can't really go wrong with AS head, projectile gloves and XP necklace. The real fun build-changing things drop too late for you to care as you are way too overpowered by that point, like the standing still armor/def increase armor and the AS/MS ring. The unlock point same as the 66% ability gloves would benefit them. Some items like the 1%hp boots, and the 100x damage necklace are just plain bad. Honestly a lot of boots are just plain bad. The elemental rings are also kind of useless as I only found myself using them when I wanted to increase burn/elec on characters already using fire/electricity already. For physical users the splash ring is too good to pass and cleric/warlock do fine regardless.The 100k recovery quest is really tedious, I suggest it be cut to a lower number, as for others they pose a nice amount of challenge.Fun in general but really tedious to recover through well. I suggest well have two slots, one for potions only and second for items or potions. I am done with the game and still need like 6 potions and 5-10 items. Maybe make some crafting bench to make an oblivion potion from 2 reroll potions and vice-versa and so on. The ingredients part I feel like was really minor and didn't really constitute the amulet and search minigame but I guess its fine.Please let us see what alternatives are available for that trait level in-game. It's really annoying to consult wiki when making a specific build to check if, say, lvl 5 orbs have AS increase trait available at this level. This is my main gripe.First boss is way too hard without quest, I can see why there is quest but considering this is first area you are basically playing until you unlock cleric to kill him if not using quest. Also, since there are no quests on following maps might as well just nerf first boss and remove quest from it since it kinda creates expectation of quests being a thing per area. All in all first area is well designed.Decent up in challenge but harbors just plain annoying mobs and a lot of visual clutter. The breathing worms are annoying, absolute abundance of green zone slimes and a lot of exploding imps/slimes just make it marginally less strategical, you basically must stand in one place and hope you have enough range to kill the worms from where you are standing. Second boss is the hardest of three both because of the spinny blades and the orbs he spawns ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up your abilities' targeting/splitting damage. Also very tanky. _childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute standout in the burgeoning Bullet Heaven subgenre that got kickstarted back with Vampire Survivors, and of these games that I've played at time of review I'm confident in calling this one my personal favorite of the bunch so far. I fully recommend it to anyone even curious about this genre or the game itself, and for its asking price it's incredibly hard to go wrong with.   An early aside worth pointing out is it features the options to toggle Auto-Aiming and Auto-Attacking as simple button clicks mid-run. While I generally don't use accessibility features myself, I'm appreciative when I see them nonetheless being made available for those that do frequently need and use them. More accessibility like this is always a good thing.    It does an excellent job of not just solely blending the surface-level aesthetic of late 90s Diablo and contemporary dungeon crawling ARPGs with the Bullet Heaven gameplay loop but also actively demonstrates an understanding of just how important variety and distinction is within its playable classes as well as subsequent synergies with abilities and unique items that can be obtained throughout runs and the meta-progression. For instance with two of the eleven classes: the Warlock and Beastmaster at a surface level are very similar, both focusing on controlling the horde with assistance from summons/companions rather than their strength and abilities alone. However, they become very different in active play when it becomes apparent that Warlock's answer to this problem is to fight the horde with another horde at the expense of his own durability and the quality of his army, while Beastmaster takes the opposite approach of investing exclusively into a single companion (her hunting dog, excluding additional summon abilities or items that grant summons) and greatly buffing the quality of both her and her pet's attacks for crowd control. Item synergies play a role here too though, as with the Warlock it's a fun build to add rings and abilities throughout a run that create an ever expansive army, while for Beastmaster I like to prioritize gear and upgrades that focus on the individual quality like crit rate/damage and attack speed. Differences like these even across surface-level similar classes really makes for a lot of replay value, and that's before we even get into the meta progression.    Its meta progression and achievements are tied together much like other games in the genre or Risk of Rain 2 where every quest you do to earn or complete something is in itself an achievement (which is why this has, at time of writing, 500 of them). Like most of these games and other roguelites you start out with few upgrades, poor gear, and slow progression and over the time of your runs become an absolute monster steamrolling your way into endgame (represented here with the Agony system and the Vault). An artistic touch I very much enjoy though with the Quest/Achievement board ingame is how each segment is itself a piece of low resolution pixel art; The Haunted Caves a Skull, the Swordsman's quest tree is... a Sword. The Cleric's, a Cross, Archer's - a Bow & Arrow, and so on. Beyond that, as you buy upgrades and gear through the three vendors during the meta-run, their areas will slowly become more detailed and overflowing with materials. I just love details like these that elevate the experience even if they arguably aren't otherwise necessary, and they definitely add to tone of the game.    In terms of performance, I've been exclusively playing this on my Steam Deck thus far and I'm happy to say that at least so far it runs pretty well. It consistently maintains 50-60 for me even at 20-30 minutes in and my battery life doesn't drain that fast, very high recommend for that platform.    I could go on in higher detail for much longer in an already long review, but in short this Diablo-Vampire Survivors mashup of a game is an excellent Bullet Heaven that's well worth your time and deserves to stand alongside best entries in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment is a shining example of everything I love about this genre of games!I went looking for games similar to Vampire Survivors, because after I finished the available content I was desperate for something to fill the void in my heart.Halls of Torment was one of the top recommendations, and for good reason, in my opinion! I think it takes a lot of what Vampire Survivors does within the genre and adds other elements to it that truly elevate the gameplay experience, and make it one of my favorite games to have played.The gameplay loop feels rewarding, and while it feels challenging, it never feels unattainably so. You are able to make good use of the tools available to you, and make consistent improvements to your gear as the game goes on. By the end of Vampire Survivors, as much as I loved it, I felt like many of the challenges and levels felt trivial; yes, they required a specific sequence of actions from me, but I was able to become so powerful that little could stop me besides the lag of my FPS. Playing Halls of Torment, though, I found myself needing to consistently make a game-plan for what challenges I wanted to tackle, and even when I had built a solid loadout, I needed to continue to adapt and prepare. It felt really rewarding, and I was overjoyed to work towards the last achievements for this game.Sincerely, 10/10, would highly recommend this game if you're interested in anything resembling the Vampire Survivors/roguelike survival/bullet hell games.

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment is a game I feel may be propped up a bit harder than appropriate, by rabid Diablo fans and contrarian Vampire Survivors detractors. Overall, it's alright and competently made, though it's easily the least fun game in its genre. I went in expecting to love it, but here we are.I usually have a fair tolerance for boredom and grind, but Halls of Torment is kind of devoid of any amazing discoveries or engaging unlockable content. Just about every single achievement is an uninteresting grind milestone. Nearly all upgrades and progression are slight percentage increments on the stats of a basic attack. Passive damage, passive regeneration, passive health, passive range, passive crits, passive blocks, and such. If you want an interesting rogue-like, you need to give the players a more creative assortment of stats, attacks, effects, modifications, and amplifications, to make playthroughs far more varied.The really simple abilities you can pick up are... Mostly not at all interactive or fun. Many merely provide some passive damage around you. You'll find a few choices for each item slot, but end up with a best-in-slot for most, anyway. There's only a few progression mechanics, only a few stock Diablo characters, and only three maps. Unlike its inspiration games, the randomisation will never provide you with a broken run, but will occasionally give you a weaker than usual run, and that's just less fun. Many achievements only offer gold, so you don't have that many new features to keep you playing. This all adds up to make a rather stale experience.It's a moderately challenging experience, sure, but you always end up strong enough to clear screens anyway. The first final boss has a poorly implemented charge attack, and the other two final bosses didn't hit me once on my first encounters of each. And even with a high damage build you will find they've got way, waaay too much health, so be wary of the mechanical complexity of dying of old age. Checking their health every so often feels like watching the clock too closely while you're at work. So ultimately the game never gets that brutally hard, you just need to figure out what stats don't apply to your character, then concentrate to conserve your health for half an hour, and finally slap some meat for a handful of minutes at the end.I've always found Diablo 1 & 2 to be utterly, headache-inducingly hideous, but Halls of Torment's cloning of its art style actually works pretty well for this style of game. The main drawback is that enemy projectiles can be very easily lost underneath the spell effects for your own attacks. Placing enemy projectiles on a higher layer would greatly aid clarity. Despite what I think of the graphics of Diablo, I do actually love ARPGs and horde survival games, and was really trying to like this one. I'm not even totally done playing it yet, though I'm finding it very easy to quit out to go do some of my more tedious household errands instead. At a point where I've seen most of the content, I must concede it's a let downSound design and music are wonderful and authentic, too. Other than that, and the baseline addiction of "Smacking more skeletons with an incrementally stronger character", there's little reason to recommend Halls of Torment over contemporaries like Vampire Survivors, Brotato, and 20 Minutes Till Dawn.

_childDocuments_.review: This is still in early access, so obviously there are some issues to deal with, and changes are being made to the game to hopefully improve it. Like the store page says, it's a relatively simple game to get into, like a lot of bullet heaven games. The more complicated elements that set it apart from say, Vampire Survivors, are that you can equip gear, and you are constantly tweaking varying stats in the game with far fewer level-ups on average (versus VS, where you can hit a certain point and just level up constantly). Gold is also harder to come by. All in all, it's a bullet heaven game that looks like old Diablo games. At its best, it's engaging without being overwhelming, and it can be fun to see how powerful your character amps up, and the character classes are neat. A number of the attacks are also quite neat, visually, and the character designs can be fun. If you have a third party guide that advises you how best to make use of characters and stats, the game can be quite enjoyable. But it's a problem that third party guides feel indispensable. There's a difference between needing help with some of the many achievements, and needing help to avoid dying all the time/figuring out how specific mechanics work because the game doesn't explain them. So while, with the removal of Agony decay, I have changed this to a recommend, it is only with the caveat that you need a third party guide to enjoy it.One issue I have is that there is also no map for some reason, making at least one landmark impossible to find except by luck and googling, because the game doesn't explain it to or let you know what it is you're looking at. If you're distracted by staying alive and collecting XP and loot, you won't see the markers to go there. If there are any other landmarks on any other levels, I have no idea. For now, I assume there are none. Why there seemingly isn't something LIKE that level 1 landmark, which helps with the final level boss, on all the other levels, I have no idea. It's a bizarre game level change.A third party guide is particularly indispensable for Agony mode. Agony mode is a neat idea but it is not explained at all (or at least it was not when I started, perhaps it's developed since with their numerous changes). The basic concept is that enemies are harder to kill, and the higher the agony level, the more and harder the enemies are to kill, and the better XP they drop. There is a limit to agony, but the game doesn't (or at least didn't) tell you until you hit it. It's also not at all clear what precisely makes agony go up, though allegedly it's you hitting harder and faster and killing enemies quickly. The developers thankfully removed Agony decay, which is great, because it was one of the dumbest aspects of the game, particularly given Agony is required for progression.Minor quibble, but it's very weird that you have to select a character just to buy stat increases that benefit everyone. I don't know why that's a thing, other than you have to choose a character to do everything else in the campsite. Also the gold % increase seems kind of useless. I seem to be earning less now than I did before I bought all the upgrades. Movement speed can also be downright punishing: on the fourth level, no matter how fast I made my character, they were always too slow to get out of certain AOE attacks, which was ridiculous. And for some reason to equip rings properly you have to unequip both rings because the game will randomly decide which to replace, which is ridiculous. I'm also not entirely sure what the point of four alternate armor outfits is when you have 9 characters with different stats and abilities and they all share the same alternate armor slots, and this isn't something you can use while on a run. In World of Warcraft, the same mechanic is used so you can easily switch between builds, particularly during dungeons and raids. Here, each character has different needs for optimization. Even if you wanted, say, a gold gathering set, each character is going to have different needs based on their stats, but you only have four places and so can only pre-arrange for four characters. It's not a bad idea in concept, it's just executed very weirdly. Why not just give each character four alternate armor slots?It's a decent enough premise with some interesting design choices. The levels are basic but that's not exactly a problem, although getting stuck on objects I don't realize are objects is frustrating. I would also like it if there was something like the trinket on level 1 in the other three levels that made the final boss easier, but if there already is I have no idea. This game seriously needs a map and maybe a bestiary or codex or something. The music is okay mostly, and even nice in places, but the sound effects, particularly the warlock's, can be very annoying. I wish there was an option to manually change the music. An option on death but with remaining revives should also be added to allow you to quit the game. As is, the revive screen seems so silly. Why are you giving me the option to revive as if it's an option? The only choice I have is to click yes.When it's fun, it's very fun, and obviously I put in a lot of hours for it because I enjoy it to some respect (especially after I've upgraded everything and found and bought all the armor). It is still very clunkily designed. Look up community discussions and guides and check out the subreddit, which also has useful info for progression and achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: Slow, boring and repetitive.Pros:- lots of classes with unique basic attack and it's unique upgrades- choose starting equipment that suits your play-style for specific classCons:- terrible level-up upgrades: on each level you choose a trait like +5% damage (or attack speed or range etc) or +10% with with specific ability. So you get like x3 base dps and x2 survival by the end of a run.- You get ~5 abilities during run (like orbs flying around you or lightning strikes at random enemies), ability upgrade counts as an ability and is almost useless (orbs deal additional minor electricity damage with low chance of micro-stun etc). Most abilities don't benefit from most stats (or just general traits are too weak to see difference), there are no synergies (some have low chance to slightly increase vulnerability to physical/magical damage or status effects like burn but that's all)- slow meta progression - per run you can resurface only one gear piece to add it to starting gear pool for a huge price, there are some permanent stat boosts with increasing gold costs and you don't earn much per run. To unlock new gear, abilities and traits you need to complete quests like deal gazillion damage with specific ability requiring  you to get and max it asap ignoring other upgrades and using that ability as a primary source of damage = boring an extremely annoying run. And there are so damn many of them- low number of maps with tremendous "difficulty" spikes - complete 20 runs to get enough gold to get +10% to all stats to be able to pass dps check on next map, there are ~5 maps so you will be mostly playing 1-2 maps to gather gold and complete quests- enemies have long death animation and you will want to have high movement speed and you will be wondering whether you step over dead enemies or are they still alive and will damage you- music is ambient and most sounds are indistinctive - it is slightly atmospheric but mostly makes gameplay quite boring- no map - there are icons to sow direction to pick-ups but it's hard to tell far they are, and they are mostly in different directions from starting point so no way to calculate optimal path, this gets even worse on diagonal maps- very limited statistics in character menu - no way to check burn chance of flamethrower, can't understand whether it's worth upgrading without knowing base value.You will be mostly playing same map each time with another calss or maxing specific abilty to grind unlocks/upgrades. Each time there will be a lack or ability synergies, your stats at the end of the run will be just slightly higher than at the start of the run - no interesting builds or characters that devastate everything using fun strategy. Just circle around monsters  while auto-attacking for half an hour to unlock some minor garbage. Repeat x200 times.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played more than ten bullet heaven games at this point - I like the genre, and I tend to be forgiving in my reviews. Bullet heaven games are cheap, simple, and you know what you're getting - a few hours of fun for a few bucks, perhaps double digits if it's really good.This is my first negative review of a bullet heaven game. I disliked pretty much everything about Halls of Torment.The graphics are bad. The quality is bad (pixelated), the style is bad (fugly), the color palette is a monotonous litany of grays and browns, the skill animations are underwhelming and in some cases (the needles) barely visible, the character models are tiny and unimpressive, the menu buttons, the items, everything is just profoundly uncool. It's one big old pile of meh.There is no skill variety - over the course of three hours, I only saw the same four unimpressive secondary skills. Don't worry, they are all equally bland and underpowered.The upgrades are generic and repetitive as well. There is nothing even remotely interesting or creative - it's all just incremental changes of basic stats. I didn't see a single cool thing in the entire game. The only thing that impresses in Halls of Torment is its commitment to blandness. Save your five bucks. If you buy this game, you are encouraging unapologetic mediocrity.

_childDocuments_.review: DEFINITELY worth the price. Almost played for 4 hours straight first time. If you loved the OG Diablo II then you will like this game. It really feels like that had a lot of influence on this game. The replayability of this is awesome. You have multiple characters to play as, all have different skills and you will never choose the same build twice. It takes a little bit to figure out exactly where you are supposed to go and what does what but you will figure it out quickly. My main advice is do not waste any skill points into "Long Fingers" that increases the range that you can grab fallen objects. The reason is because throughout the level there will be these hands that drop on the ground, and it shows you where they are to run to. If you pick up the hand it will grab EVERY SINGLE DROP on the map and give it to you no matter how much you killed and how far away it is. So killing a bunch and running for one of those hands or trying to find one in a barrel or something is key to getting massive levels quickly. The boss fights are intense as hell. I've only beaten the first 2 areas but Jesus that first boss. For 4 bucks this game is a steal. I've purchased games for 20-40 dollars that I didn't enjoy as much as this. Thanks Game Developers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game triggers my dopamine in a way not unlike crack cocaine. My monkey brain sees Damage numbers and small percentage modifiers increase and i am instantly elated. The constant dopamine and the exponential growth makes my zoomer brain happy. After a couple of hours though it gets repetitive, to the point .With the right level up PERKS you can afk large portions of rounds and take a cigarette break. It loses its replayability. But for the 5 dollars it is definitely worth it. 9/10 Get if you want something you can play while you watch solo leveling in the background.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game that could be better!It's a little slow. Collecting gear & potions feels like a real slog and there's little variation in these departments. Winning a run with new items doesn't grant you access to said items and you feel a touch cheated. Winning runs often takes 40+ minutes, reward me I say! Also the balance feels slightly off in favour of magic users. HOWEVERThe tone is marvellous. The art direction is delicious. The few animations coupled with some voice acting is PERFECT. Enemy variety is on point and the levels genuinely have environments that are fun to explore. There are heaps of power ups and the character selection screen is stacked once you have unlocked them all. I often unlocked two characters at once, why not implement the same philosophy with gear and potions?With a little more variety and fine tuning this could go from good to great!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: new update bad, no fun, everything feels nerfed excepted for the enemy *cries*This game was fun before this new updateEverything feels off with damage, I'm somehow getting hit more too, new area is tough and pretty much requires you to go full damage. the ability that could help deal damage was heavily nerfed, i can see it needing to be nerf but this much nerfed where it feels useless, nah. XP gain was nerfed, leveling up feels slow but yet overall stats feel slow around that level too somehow? Monsters i usually know i can mostly ignore after a certain time i cannot anymore. , i can't reach lvl 100 anymore, cant even get lvl 90 for achieve......ment, nevermind you have to reach "agony III", okay? lets try it.... the mobs scale with you and then outpace  it feels like you have to go full DPS, i tried to go somewhat all round but that does not work as you won't do enough damage while everything becomes more deadly, tanky, etc. Mini-bosses feel like they have more HP then a Boss on normal mode and I'm 8 minutes into a run?? There is a new or combined stat "Force"? what is that? i don't know, m looking for the stat to help my sorcerer's chain lightning chain more (pierce). sorcerer feels nerfed to now that her lightning bolts go to one point rather then spread out  with more lightning bolts you get.New area is also a DPS check, new ability that spawns mines on the floor that you have to stand in to activate is a pain, but not to hard to use  if you aren't swarmed....but you need to get 3 million damage in one run with it for an achievement and all you have so far is 1.3 mil and 2900 DPS and there is 11 minutes left in the run out of 30 min....New hero's feel under powered , but after testing older characters they all feel under powered so I cannot say if these guys are badly balanced or not except for one of them, their pet is pretty bad, borderline useless. tho i did get the only achievement for it (damage dealt with it) so I guess its working as intended? he feels weird to play, it has relatively high alpha damage and slow reload but it doesn't feel like it scales well with damage, reload and crit buffs, you would think it would do well against single targets but it actually does better (relatively) with expendable mobs and scales poorly with mini-bosses and bosses.Yes they  have a revive mechanic and you get 2 free revives after purchasing them and now i have to use both or 1 per run while before i was playing with my life for fun not really going below half HP. The maps are balanced now i have to use skill right?? doesn't feel like that with everything being more tanky,, more damage, unable to get xp fast enough,  you moving means less mobs spawn in a game that inherently makes enemies swarm you meaning you take more damage that you cannot dodge, just get speed you say, i tried but then i don't do the damage i need now i got 2 minibosses at once. but that ain't the best part, before the update introducing new achievements, i had 3 or so left to go, and i've collected everything i want. but you as a NEW player? guess what! in order to get abilities, passive buffs, more powerful buffs on level up and so on you can only get them through achievements! congrats, i cannot imagine a newbie now actually getting far due to frustration, so all i can say is have fun to all the masochists out there. there is now 243 achievements, you can only get a +100% xp boost by completing them all, and another 30% now from the necklace that was necessary to get level 100 (before it was 50% xp buff)There are a lot of things still needed in this game that i overlooked in till now because it WAS fun, was . You cannot check all your abilities or hero stats before you start a run, some relevant stats aren't even shown in a run either, but your characters general stats are shown even ones that aren't relevant to the character (they did before Aug 31st 2023 update).Some stats need a description in the stats area rather then just when you hover over the buff you want to choose when you level up. lets use force for example.Force:"improves all stats and Abilities in different ways. Usually it increases duration, piercing, knock back, and others"Others? what others? im playing this new spear hero with dog it has a base force stat of 10 and a total of 14 due to a shrine blessing. Okaaay what is force buffing? I know from before this update, duration is for summons, pierce is obvious but this weapon has infinite pierce it seems so its not that, knock back? I don't know lets play with it and find a mob i cant one shot....i guess it is knock back but is it only affecting knock back? i do not know because there is no stat description for what "Force" does for this specific character, is just knock back ? i mean it affects "others" stats as well.....i would not buff my force stat (as example).Again there is no wiki of sorts in game, no necronomicon to figure out what spells do what. play and find out basically and make a mental reminder yes, your radiant aura does get affected when you buff area even though it does not show that in the stats tab.This update feels half done, every achievement has a unique icon, but the 42 new achievements and the ones they changed all have just "Q" as the icon. if you can get an older version play that it is a ton of fun, there is some QoL changes and overall new content, but more cons enough to not make this fun anymore, so watch and not play it yet if you think it is fun, it was, but not at the moment.I'm writing this out of frustration so sorry for everything being everywhere, I hope the devs scale back the nerfs and buff the under-powered stuff rather the bringing everything down to the under-powered stuffs level.

_childDocuments_.review: It's bizarre how well the developers managed to emulate so much soulful detail. The logo, the entry screen, the music, the interface, the cursor, the buttons, and the unforgiving, anti-handholding gameplay. I had to double check whether the game I just booted up wasn't some boomer game studio from before 2000 making their one final game, or whether this was a 20 year old PC port. Nope, it's a fresh game from 2023. Wtf?Besides all that, the game is insanely fun too. That alone would get it a positive review, all the other stuff is merely very delicious cherries (or carrots) on top. I wasn't even aware this was an early access game until 20 hours in, since this was gifted to me. Now I fell for the trap of dying to get updates for this.Don't let the early access part scare you, though. This game easily already has 30+ hours you can put into it for only €5. This game deserved to be at least double or triple that, even right now in its "unfinished" state.

_childDocuments_.review: Halls of Torment is a fantastic roguelike that offers many unique elements and draws players in for hours of fun. Below are the pros, cons, and ratings in various categories:Pros:+Variety of characters – Each with unique abilities, allowing for different play styles.+Atmospheric visuals – Retro pixel art inspired by classic 90s games.+Excellent music and sound design – Builds a dark, gothic atmosphere.+Character upgrade system – Very satisfying, with numerous abilities and progression paths.+Diverse enemies – A variety of monsters that force you to think and adapt your strategies.Cons:-Repetitive levels – Some levels may feel similar over time.-Lack of deep story – The game focuses more on gameplay than narrative depth.Future Expectations:*Adding more bosses and story-driven quests to bring even more variety.*Expanding the locations and mechanics to reduce the sense of repetitiveness.Ratings (1-5):Graphics: 4.5/5Music and sound: 5/5Gameplay: 4.5/5Character and mechanic complexity: 4/5Replayability: 4/5

Halls of Torment is a horde survival game in a pre rendered retro look reminiscent of RPGs from the late 90s.

Choose one of many hero characters and descend into the deadly Halls of Torment. Fight unholy horrors from beyond and survive wave after wave until you face one of the tormented lords. Advance your hero with character traits, abilities, and items. Create a new powerful build during each run. Explore various underground expanses and find new powerful items that enable you to venture even deeper into the abyss.

_childDocuments_.review: Other games: "Sorry, you can't go there right now. You could run into sequence breaking content, or unbeatable enemies, or puzzles that are impossible with your current abilities."Immortals Fenyx Rising: "Do what you want, I ain't your dad."The game's an absolute blast. It offers a level of freedom and power you just don't see in other modern games. It offers cleverly designed puzzles, but gives you options to blow through them using your divine powers. It offers challenging combat, but lets you become so powerful you'll be able to take down most enemies in a couple hits. It makes you earn your upgrades, but is generous with materials and currency. It deals with some weighty themes and surprisingly detailed Greek mythology, but does so in a way that's consistently good-natured and hilarious throughout. Basically, it prioritizes fun over everything else, and it absolutely succeeds.I wholeheartedly recommend giving this one a play.

_childDocuments_.review: Phoenix rising is not just a tale. Its journey to your heart. Play as mystical hero and a Greece world where you have to find your life path to become a champion of lands. This time a different take but welcomed one. Not a natural one but a creative one. I might say this is one of the best games Ubisoft produced in a long run. Not to shy away spot lights from other games but this one for me is truly the one you have to play it. Beautifuly crafed open world that doesn’t overtake its welcome or overshadows with bombastics maps like Assassin creed does sometimes. Smaller scales and at the same time so dense and so busy in every corner. You will not be disappointed cause there are lot of secrets and puzzles and chest to do. Everything is done in welcoming manner that you want to spend those moments to clear them out. Some puzzles are crafter very creative and make your choice matter how you solve it. Rewards are always waits for you either there be a fashion armor sets to impact your gameplay style or collect yourself into better version. I played a lot of games and saw harsh and warm but just wanted to say that this is one of the most beautiful games out there. From early morning sun lights to dark evening shadows and lightnings in the skies this game art is worth your eyes to be hugged. The combat and fun factor is doing what is should do to serve a purpose of having fun. Either it be to challenging or to easy this hits the right note. If you find it to easy you can always try to push yourself to the limit and play without leveling up and see how that goes well. Everything calculated mark to mark and still the combat is engaging and fun for the new comers and professionals. I was heartbroken when I did find out Ubisoft cancelled Phoenix rising sequel. Cant understand this decision but I do know that this game will track more and more new fans cause this game worth every second spend in it. Its just pure light of joy.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this is a hard one to review given it's age. But I hope you have the time to read it. For one, this game was not released in 2022. So the release date can be confusing in the steam store. The original release date is December 3, 2020. I did play this on more than 1 platform hence I'll be reviewing on this platform given it's state today and with the Steam Deck available on my hands. I will say that the lore of this game does require you to understand the world of mythology. Especially Greek Mythology in order to get some of the character back stories. But these stories are mostly well known if you've ever been out of high school. Thus, there's expectations that you know them. Hence that's the only requirement you actually really need to know to have a good laugh on the comedy of things.Undoubtedly this game is a blend of Assassin's Creed and Breath of the Wild which was only exclusive to the Nintendo Switch (not anymore thanks to the community hehehe...). And as an avid Open world type of player, I will say this was a joy to play on with the comedic effect in place giving it a nice touch for those who like comedy. If that's what you're looking for then this will not disappoint. Game content, open world structure, points of interest, etc. are just a good experience in this game. None of the points of interest are pointless. Actually, each one has it's point of progress for your character. Treasure chests, Zeus' Bolts, Ambrosia, Charon's Coins, and etc. are all part of progressing your character's strength.HOWEVER, I will say that character customization is RESTRICTED. It's not as vast as AC Odyssey for that matter. You can choose what to upgrade but once you hit the end of each tree, you pretty much realize that everyone will hit this point once they get to this point as well. Thus, there's no point in customizing play style. You have what you have and the only thing that can make things unique to your playthrough is just which gear you choose to use. Oh and the gear is mostly visual. You'll notice it when you complete at least 1-2 sections of the world map.Enemy variations could do better though. I notice almost all enemies are the same. Even bosses don't have much uniqueness to them once you face them. Kinda a bummer at part but once you face crowds, I do hope you have DMC skills in your hands cause they can be pretty annoying. Just a lack of unique enemy design. Puzzle designs are interesting but there are puzzles that are annoying. There are points in a puzzle where, in your head, it's so easy to solve but for some damn reason the game makes the puzzle difficult to solve and there's no solution skip to these terribly designed puzzles. For one, there's a PINBALL puzzle where you have to basically pinball a fireball into a hole... which borders some luck that relies on the Physics engine of the game. Another is a jump the ball into the other side of the platform which also borders some luck and precise timing in order to get the ball to the other side. In other words, there are puzzles that are not straight forward in solution despite the solution having some randomizer to take effect. Even though you're standing in the solution, the game basically forces you to pray to the Physics gods to solve something ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ basic into the equation. And yes, this is the weakest part of the game. The puzzles. Innovative, but annoying. I decided to split this review into two parts. 1 for the PC and the other for the STEAM DECK. Why? I won't lie, I have pretty badass PC but my experience with both is just SIGNIFICANTLY different. If you plan to play on PC (at this time and age), I really do hope you have an AMD GPU. This game just crashes randomly and quite commonly on my Nvidia PC with the latest drivers. I tried 537.xx drivers and it still crashes. Discussion forums have also said to downgrade your drivers down to 528.xx but I say.. ♥♥♥♥ it... To do all that for one game is NOT RECOMMENDED. I genuinely do not know who's responsible for a fix to the random crashing but I 100% absolutely can confirm that this game crashes commonly in 2024 and no it's not my hardware as I can literally play all my other games without crashing. It's only this and mostly other Ubisoft games. Does it suck? yeah... it sucks. But this is all I can say about the PC review. It's bad and unfortunately makes me want to switch to the other device I have to just play it... and speaking of which... For a game that's older than the deck itself, I will say this game was NOT optimized for the Steam Deck. Hence don't expect it to be. I did the numbers and had at least 5-10 hours of gameplay on this in the deck and will say that my experience was WAY better than my PC (which has an RTX3070 btw). Game doesn't crash (unless I smash my deck with a hammer), decent frame pacing (not perfect frame pacing, just decent), highly acceptable quality, and completely comfortable to play on. Just one issue, you need to set your controls to gamepad mode manually. I don't know why but that's how it is. Concerning the FPS, it does drop a lot at medium settings at 800p. Hence it's not perfect 60 fps but it's at least better than having it crash every now and then. It goes down to about 40fps and lowest I got is 30 fps so you might want to stick to NSW framerate if you know what I mean. But it does hit 60 fps at certain sections. Either way, devs never made any optimization for the deck so you'll just have to make do with raw performance as stock. If and only if you want to, you can try using 3rd party upscalers such as FSR if you want to make it really hit 60fps flat. I don't need to say it but I used SteamOS for my experience and not Windows so you know exactly m experience. This game is definitely 7/10 for me. I wouldn't give it a decimal point higher given the flaws of the game. But hey, it's a better game than a lot of other games right now. Recommended if you really like open world game and comedy. I would only say that you shouldn't play this on an Nvidia PC because of the crashing issue that it has. But if you have a Steam Deck, fire away. It's the best alternative experience to BOTW from the NSW without sailing the 7 seas.

_childDocuments_.review: It started really good, but that did not last for me, unfortunately.First of all, a bit of context: I have not played "Breath of The Wild", which inspired this game, but I did play "Genshin Impact", which is supposed to be (and is) quite similar gameplay wise. This means, that some of my complaints may be intrinsic to this type of games in general, not this game specifically. I also finished "Assassin's Creed Odyssey", which is somewhat similar both in terms of open-world and general Greek mythology theme.The prologue of the game felt quite nice. There was a lot of humor, but it was well-paced and [usually] well-placed. The way you were introduced to mechanics through the story was good, even though the "mystery" of the first quest chain ended up to be a bit contrived. The quest chain also did not feel as if it was forcing you to just follow it, providing you enough time to wander about, if you wanted. The combat was simple, but fun, although I do not understand why most of the monsters were flying away from me at high speeds almost on every kill: that felt out of place. It was quite a good experience overall. But then I reached the point, when the game truly became open-world, and everything collapsed.The humor in dialogues started feeling stale and even annoying. There was too much of it, even though there were moments of silences during free-roaming. I honestly became tired of it pretty soon, because almost every line of dialogue tried to be a joke of some kind. Furthermore the gods did not differ that much from each other, essentially just voices and some theme for jokes, that carried over from dialogue to dialogue. They were annoying and utterly pointless in their existence. To me this also ruined the story, which obviously did not try to invent anything to begin with.The combat became stale pretty fast, too. It was quite repetitive, and I honestly did not see much point in skills, that you can buy with coins here. There was not that much depth to it. Perhaps, if I played on higher difficulty, that would have been different, but I think it would have just made me use dodge more often. Although, it did bring a little bit of satisfaction when I tried to keep the combo meter high and succeeded, which did not seem to do anything in terms of rewards. I also did not like the fact that 3 or 4 of the skills (godly powers) were unlocked through coins without any story behind them, as the rest of them. I find this a wasted opportunity, because they are god powers, not regular physical skills as in latest Assassin's Creed trilogy, so some short story would have been nice. It could have benefited from elemental effects, too, because they can make fighting a bit more diverse.What's worse, the open world felt pointless, or rather it was here to stretch out the experience. A very good example is a quest, where you need to move a large pearl into the sea. First you need to walk quite a distance towards the pearl, and then you need to push it towards the sea for like 10 minutes, if not more. It felt like a chore, and not because of monsters forced on you along the path: it was slow and uninteresting. Before this I completed a vault where you needed to push balls to solve a puzzle and even that was much more interesting.But even if that was not the case, I did not feel inspired to walk around this world. Yes, it looks quite beautiful, no argument from me there, and there is stuff to do there, which is mostly puzzles and vaults (which are kind of puzzles, too), but that's not enough. When I played Genshin, I was progressing slowly through the story, because I was constantly noticing something interesting a bit off the path I had to follow and I went there to investigate, even if there was nothing interesting, in the end. Things were placed on the map in right places to specifically trigger your curiosity. There were not things like this in Fenyx Rising, most of the things I noticed when looking around were generic or just mountainy landscapes.Even if there were more things picking my curiosity, I do not think I would have went for them, because traversal of the world was boring, too. Or maybe just because I did not like quite a few things about it:1. To jump higher you can hold jump button, but there is not that much difference in height. And it's mostly pointless, since you unlock double-jump pretty earlier in the game, too (as part of main story).2. To glide you need to press jump button and then press glide button, which is a separate one. For me it often resulted in losing just a little bit of height, because I needed to switch to a different button. I would prefer to start gliding by holding jump button, and I believe this is how it worked in Genshin.3. There is not that much difference between running horse and running you. There is a small difference in speed, but it's like 10 vs 11 meters/second. Maybe 10 vs 12. The only real benefit from a horse is that it's a secondary stamina meter, meaning that you can move at this speed longer, but this gets ruined by the fact that you need to summon the horse and then to drop off of it.4. There is a lot of  mountains that you just have to climb, and climbing is slow. Of course, I would not expect the speed of AC Odyssey here, but... No, scratch that, here it would have made much more sense, because this is a fairy tail, while AC Odyssey is, technically, not. Increasing speed even at the cost of stamina would have been a godsend here. Or at least a way to speed it up through upgrades.I remember playing AC Odyssey and just loving to go around checking those question marks on map. It did not have the design filled with curious things "along the way" as Genshin had, but the feeling that traversal of the world had was really good. Not as good as web-swinging in Spider-Man games or even in AC Unity, but good enough for me to get satisfaction just from running around.Overall, I think this game suffered from its ambitions. If this was a more linear experience with somewhat smaller world, which is open more in a sense of Bioshock type of games, rather than true open-world, with traversal having feeling closer to Assassin's Creed games, with elemental effects in combat, a bit less humor, but more detailed characters - it could have been a really good game. But I guess I am describing something really different, so maybe this is just not a game for me. Good thing, that I, at least, got it at a discount.

Follow the main story for a bit, get your wings, the ability where you do spears upward (also handy for a triple jump), upgrade your stamina and health and go from there. Yes, the game is puzzle heavy, but you can actually adjust them to make it easier by some toggles in the options as well as switching the difficulty down to easy or story if you wish. I started on normal, but after a few hours it felt kinda difficult so i switched to easy for the rest of the game with all puzzle assistants on. Yes, there are some puzzles that are really dumb and/or annoying. But there's also a lot I liked too.Story was good, some funny humor here and there. I'd love to see some sequels but do it like Prince of Persia Warrior Within and make it more angry, add some blood and gore, etc. However that's one bad thing about the game- the puzzles and combat are tied to the same adjustment. You cant make the puzzles easy and the combat difficult for example. I did all the main quests, side quests and about 23 vaults. I also upgraded my character to about 80-85% abilities. There's also new game plus.You can switch difficulty at any time. Got about 35 hours total. I just played the base game, no dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like this is the game ubisoft wanted to make all the time, but they werent confident enough to create a new IP instead they created assassins creed origins, assassins creed odyssey and assassins creed valhalla. But now they build up enough confidence and dared to create a new IP: Immortals Fenyx RisingI was surprised that the game was made by ubisof, because it was such a fun game.This truly feels like a work of passion.There are only a few flaws: being "forced" to manually spot the treasure chests and the enemy variety.The idea to spot everything manually is alright if you do it once in the tutorial, after that it is just annoying, but you dont have to collect every treasure chest etc if you dont want to, so you are not forced to use the mechanic.Regarding the enemy variety, there arent too many types, so you encounter nearly always the same enemies just different colors, indicating how strong that enemy is.But this is just nitpicking.It runs very smooth, the story is enjoyable, I can only recommend the game.And for the future, hopefully ubisoft will keep their newfound confidence to create new IPs for their various new ideas instead of forcing them into already existing IPs (e.g. Assassins Creed) just because they fear it won't sell well enough.That being said:Congratz Ubisoft, you created a really nice game

This mean you never get the feeling to become actually stronger, because everywhere is always scaled to your power level. Everything is running pretty smoothly. But I do get a problem when I close the game. IF I exit the game with ''Exit to Desktop''. The game will close but Steam will still mark it as running. So I cannot start any other games or even close my computer because it is saying a program is still running. The only way to close my computer was to override it (holding 3 sec the power button). The solution I found was to exit to the main title first, then exit to desktop. Pretty annoying.NEUTRAL :- Puzzles are too easy. I put that as neutral comment, because it depend of people. They could put some very easy and more challenging puzzles, but they didn't. The challenging one are about that you don't have the necessaries Godly Power. This is not a challenge, this is a prerequisite.Overall :For a 80 $ game (92 $ with taxes), this is a fail. Don't get it full price.I got it on sale for 15 $. For that price this is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising continually impressed me with the creativity of its design. The world, the characters, the gameplay, the enemies, the story, the music, and especially the puzzles are so full of thoughtful, clever creation. It is truly special and is among my favorite titles of all time.One complaint I see is that "tHeRe aRe tOo mAnY PuZzLeS". The puzzles are a big part of what this game *is*. They're really not too difficult, but are apparently far beyond the limited capability of some (often rude) players. The puzzles are truly interesting and fun which sets them apart from so many puzzles you see in lots of other similar games.The biggest valueless complaint I see often is that "It uSeS ThE UbIsOfT LaUnChEr". I don't love launchers either, but to ding this title because of that publishing mechanism is stupid. Many other Ubisoft titles have similar useless "reviews" for the same reason. It says nothing of the game itself which is what I want to know about when I read a review. It's like a one-star review for something on Amazon because the shipping was slow.  Immortals Fenyx Rising is an excellent title that is interesting, compelling, and fun. It is worth your time..

_childDocuments_.review: 1) I think I could never take this game seriously (when it first came out) due the name 2) It's under Ubisoft which means I generally stay away from their games due to their extra drm crudI picked this game up during a recent sale due to a friend's recommendation. So far I'm about 37 hours in, maybe halfway through the main story and it's been a blast. Yes, it's open world, has combat and small dungeons - and there's a lot of puzzles - I get the Breath of the Wild (BOTW) similarities and can only say: BOTW feels both large and sometimes empty. This game is both big AND there's generally SOMETHING around a corner, some sort of activity or fighting area or something else going on. While I It has fighting: A few different combo variations with reactive combat - more of a watch for 15 seconds on new enemies to "see what they'll do" than just run up and pound everythingIt is Metroidy: It takes a variety of abilities to access all the content in the game. Even some treasure chests may require a specific ability (or set of) to unlock.It has puzzle dungeons: some logic, some manuvering (yourself / objects), time based, etc. Powering up some abilities can be VERY useful in either solving these areas, most puzzles are open enough to allow some taking advantage of the abilities / area to perhaps not solve them in the intended fashion - I have actually bugged out a couple of dungeons due to unforseen results occasionally to "alternate" solutions to solving the puzzleIt has equipment upgrading - and many "types" of equipment which can give perks that reward a variety of playstylesIt has decent respawn allowances: You don't feel like you just wasted 30 minutes because you walked off an edge instead of jumpingIt has big boss fights - where paying attention to mechanics can greatly shorten the encounter (hit: learn how to parry - it's way too useful not to abuse as much as possible)It has backstory being told primarily via some rather good Voice acting which has some pretty funny riffs against Greek Mythology. It flows behind you as you play rather than interrupting playI can't say that I've had any issues with Ubisoft Connect. I did see that the in (cash?) store where you can spend electrum was completely non-functional for me. Wasn't too surprised but it didn't keep the game from being functional

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game, but I don't *not* recommend it. If there was an "Eh" option, this would be a low Eh. If you like Greek mythology, pick this up while it's on sale, but let me spin you a story first:So it's winter 2020 or something. I had a laptop, bought this game, and it ran like ♥♥♥♥ because the game insists on having, like, literally an entire solar system worth of stars fully rendered on every character. (I'm not kidding, look up the opening cutscene, Zeus just inexplicably has the entire milky way galaxy on him for no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason)Fast forward to autumn 2023. I buy the game *again* and now I can run it because new laptop. And it's... Fine? Something about me. When it comes to mythology games, I will always play them, but I have a VERY high standard. You need to make something really special if you're stepping into my territory of mythology. And this game is not special. The game has zero identity, the world is incredibly bland. You know how in Zelda BOTW there are like 10 different biomes spread across the world, and each one also has tons of interesting stuff to find in it? Well this game has five biomes. Tutorial, grassy plain, grassy plain (but there is brick and ♥♥♥♥ everywhere and the grass is orange), snow, and lava. 100% this game and tell me if you remember a single pixel of the world. If you've got a PC that can run this game and want an ancient Greek game, just get Assassin's Creed Odyssey. The dialogue is fine. I like the occasional interactions between Zeus and Prometheus. The twist at the end, no spoilers, was really dumb and didn't really add anything to the experience.Speaking of endings, let's talk about the final boss. And speaking about the final boss, let's talk about bosses. And speaking of bosses, let's talk about the combat. It's meh. Your abilities don't work because the controls are very unresponsive most of the time, so you'd quickly press the buttons for an ability and have Fenyx just stand there while like four minotaurs beat her like she owes them money. The game loves to arbitrarily crank up difficulty and completely ruin the flow of the game. Like, 11 or so hours in I was ready to face the final boss. Beat the boss, got the twist, beat the final dungeon, fought the *real* final boss, and got my ass kicked because all of his attacks are screen-clearing instakills that cannot be anticipated or avoided in any way because the game locks your camera to some random direction for no reason whenever it feels like. So the only way to beat him is to tank him with like 20 billion potions. So fast forward to like *20* hours into the game, I finally had enough potions to tank him. Why is that a feature? Why do I need to ruin the game for myself just to finish it? Why can't completing the main storyline for the game adequately prepare me for the ending? Why do I need to slop 10 hours of grinding on top of that? It's a 5 hour game that gets stretched to 20 hours because it randomly throws roadblocks that require hours of tedious grinding in your way. Other than that, upgrades don't feel meaningful (Upgrading your weapons increases damage, but whenever you upgrade them, the enemies in the world become stronger so you're just dealing the exact same percentage of damage to them, the numbers are just slightly bigger). There's a lot of "Now go do this thing!" questing instead of "You did this, which caused this, so therefore you need to do this!". It feels less like a story, and more like a laundry list of pointless chores. If you react to seeing mythological characters the same way Marvel fans react whenever some dude named PeepeePoopoo Man shows up in the post-credits scene of Avengers, then you'll get a kick out of the constant "Now go slay this random mythological monster that was completely unrelated to the questline until now!" You'll definitely struggle to find motivation to play this game. But if you push through it, you have a middling and slightly charming open world game waiting for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a light-hearted cartoony take on Assassin’s Creed Odyssey and much like that game I loved this. It is one of those games with a big map full of things to systematically tick off that are like crack to me. It looks great, there is a great range of character customisation and weapons. The upgrade system is not too complex and you unlock some fun mechanics as you progress.  The story is fun, the slightly silly take on Greek mythology is excellent, I like the commentary by Zeus and Prometheus; almost like Statler and Waldorf. The gameplay is a nice mix of exploration, puzzles and combat. The combat is nice and easy. The puzzles are mostly satisfying however a few of the puzzles are annoyingly difficult. They put in a few puzzles to sell the DLC that are clearly meant to be played near the end of the game once you have got used to the mechanics, but some of them are in the starting areas. So don’t get disheartened if you think you are just doing an easy early game side mission and find yourself stumbling into a seemingly unfair really difficult puzzle. The other annoyance is how you find things on the map. Instead of the nice viewpoints in Assassin’s Creed you have to stop every once in a while and tediously scan all round you to find things to get them marked on the map. It breaks the fun fast flow of the game with its tedium, I really don’t know how they thought it was a good idea. But these are just a few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in an otherwise excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Immortal Fenyx Rising a year ago on Ubisoft+ and had to buy it as soon as it reached Steam. _childDocuments_.review: Game that was started developing by game designer and finished by effective manager. Good ideas wrapped into "oh look how many activities do we have" Ubisoft open-world. I'd recommend to buy it only when it is on sale (without Season Pass).I've spent 100+ hours in a game and 90 hours of them I was thinking "why am I continue playing?" and I can't find an answer. It's not a bad game, but Ubisoft really tried to make it bad. It starts good, you have a desire to explore this world, but after 2-3 hours you understand the core concepts and realize that you'll need to do the same thing over and over for 20-40 hours depends on difficulty and how many activities you're focusing on. You can check other reviews for more information about "good parts", but I wanted to focus on "controversial" design decisions.Personally, the story is the weakest part of the game. Have you ever heard a story about "the only one who can save us all"? This is it with exact same twists. You're the mortal who should fight Typhon and his servants, because other gods lost the battle . The game is about Greek mythology? Yes, but from mythology you'll get "legendary beasts" as a common enemies and short myths retailing in a humorous manner. Game just points out "Hey, here is Daedalus Wings. Here is Odyssey. And this is Cyclops. Want to know more? Go to wiki".There are a lot of them in this game:As I said, the game isn't bad, visual style is good, combat feels dynamic (but don't expect to much from it), movement is not restricted, so you can get pretty much everywhere in measurable amount of time, some puzzles are interesting to solve, builds (via combination of armor and weapons) may provide a small variety of gameplay (Ubisoft was trying to provide a balance for all builds, but as usual the choice between "45% damage if you have full health", "45% damage for 6 seconds after you perfectly avoid *and make exact two attacks with a hammer after double-jump and left-right strafe" and "30% to sword damage passively" is pretty much obvious).Mostly, doesn't worth it:So for me it looks like someone wanted to make a good relaxing game for 8-12 hours, but effective manager said "I need an involvement for 40 hours" so we just copy-paste \ scale all those ideas 4 times. I'd recommend to get this game on sale, set a normal difficulty (it doesn't really change anything except the time you spent fighting and solving time puzzles), play a bit, choose activities you like, get through the story and don't really focus on grinding everything (as I do). In this case, you'll enjoy the game (most likely)
