_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenix Rising is a game that unfortunately was a bit overshadowed by Assassin's Creed Valhalla, a game in Ubisoft's cash cow franchise. In my opinion, it should’ve been the other way around because this is one of my favorite Ubisoft titles. AC Valhalla uses that typical Ubisoft open-world formula, which is getting more and more stale. Immortals was developed by the AC Odyssey team, but it’s a completely new IP, and more importantly, a breath of fresh air.The best way to describe this game is what would happen if AC Odyssey and Zelda: Breath of the Wild had a child since it combines the best parts from both titles.It uses Greek mythology as its setting, but has a more light-hearted tone and lots of humor, reminding me of some PS2 platformers. The graphics are stylized and colorful, and work really well for this style. The story is alright: it's simple and to the point. Enjoyable, but nothing special.Gameplay is simple but fun. It's mostly an action-platformer RPG, with a lot of simplified features. Combat is enjoyable, although nothing special in the end. It's simple but fluid, with some build customization.Exploration is also a big part of the game. It's open-world, but it's quite small, and this size felt perfect to me. Content is more packed, so there’s always something new to find if you look around. It's much better than having a big, empty map.The closest this gets to the Ubisoft formula is scouting around for nearby locations, marking places on the map for you to clean. You can explore naturally, but even if you want to find everything, it doesn’t feel like a chore.And the main reason for that is that this title, like Zelda, has a lot of puzzles. There're other locations like guarded chests, but the vast majority is environmental puzzles. And while there aren’t a lot of mechanics, each puzzle is unique. I really enjoyed the puzzles, although since they are physics-based, sometimes they are annoying because they don't feel consistent.Now, if you don’t like puzzles, then maybe this game isn’t for you. There’re also a lot of small dungeons to find, with a lot more puzzles to solve! Even if you just want to play the main story, puzzling is still a big part of the game.Some things are limited by stamina, like special-moves, sprinting and climbing. Some special moves can even aid in moving around, although those are more advanced techniques and aren’t required, unless you aim for 100%.Loot is mostly gear with different cosmetics and stats, without levels. You can level up gear, but it’s streamlined in the sense that when you upgrade a type of gear everything levels up at the same time. And I prefer it this way. Besides chests, there’re also other items to find that allow you to upgrade stats like health and stamina. It’s not hard to upgrade everything, and there’s even a mastery system to level up further, especially if you’re going for a new game plus.The soundtrack is enjoyable, and I really enjoyed the transitions when combat ended. A small touch, but I like these details. Like the random chest opening animations, those were a nice touch as well. You can see this game has more passion, since the devs had more freedom and weren't shackled to the Ubisoft formula. The result is a fun and enjoyable title.There’re also 3 DLCs available, and they’re all played independently, although it’s recommended you finish the main game first.The first DLC is basically a post-game epilogue, with a heavy focus on dungeon puzzles. They are harder, and will require some of the advanced techniques, but they are taught to you. You even level up further, but it’s contained here. And it should, otherwise it would break the main game. It’s more of the same, so I’m not complaining.The second DLC tells a new story in an eastern setting, and gameplay-wise it’s basically the entire main game condensed into just a few hours. The map is much smaller, but it has the same design and upgrades, just on a smaller scale. Once again, more of the same, and after the first DLC, I preferred starting progression from the beginning.The third DLC is the weirdest one. For the most part, gameplay is similar, but there’s one crucial difference: the game is played with an isometric perspective, severity limiting your visibility. The game is designed around that, but I wasn’t a fan of that. You also need to gather resources, and the combat has way more enemies but with a lot of customization. I think these two elements alone would make this DLC feel unique, without the restrictive camera. It wasn’t terrible to play, just meh.So, I really enjoyed the game and can easily recommend it on sale if you enjoy the genre. However, I have some criticisms, all related with Ubisoft and their stupid launcher.For a single player game, the game has a lot of unnecessary microtransactions, even if they’re all cosmetic. The game already has a lot of options, but most of the cool skins are unfortunately locked behind the in-game store, which sucks and it’s only an attempt for Ubisoft to get more money.There’re daily challenges that reward you with premium currency that can be used to buy those exclusive items, but only a selection of items is available per week. It’s a live service model that has no place in here.The Ubisoft launcher has a LOT of bugs. You can’t check your stats in-game, only on the launcher. When I started playing, they were available in the overlay, but disappeared a few weeks later. I can check them of the desktop launcher, but it’s extra steps for something that should be in-game.It’s the same for the achievements. They’re available only in the desktop launcher and at least unlock correctly, but there’s no way to check them in-game, and worst of all, there’s no notification when you unlock one. It wasn’t like this some years ago, so definitely a stupid regression.The new unit system is dumb. Before, at least you could get all exclusive rewards by doing all the in-game challenges, since you would get enough units, with a few exceptions. Now, even if you complete all challenges, including the DLCs, you’ll only get around half the units you need to unlock everything. I could even get more stuff if my previous units hadn’t expired…The only way to get everything now is to get points from another game (and giving up rewards there), or grinding weekly challenges for years… And even worse, the community challenges are bugged during the time I played this. Just unnecessary and annoying BS Ubisoft decided to put in all their newer titles.And those are my main criticisms, none related to the game itself. These doesn’t ruin the experience, but this game would be better without all this BS.And to top it all off, Ubisoft cancelled a sequel, moving the developing team for yet another Assassin’s Creed title, something I was extremely disappointed with.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very realistic Beta Testing Simulator. The game realistically simulates the job of a beta tester dealing with an unstable and unfinished software. Basically the mechanic of the game consists of tweaking settings and other things I won't say not to spoiler the game, in order not to crash the software. Sometimes the game is also interrupted by some kind of a mini-game about greek mythology, but these are short intermissions that don't distract by the main purpose of the game. I particularly liked the meta-game of having to access actual forums and rollback actual drivers (oops, I spoiled part of the game, but this was during the prologue so you'll pardon me). Like "Outer Wilds" the main mechanic is a repeating cycle (start game, tweak, play, crash, repeat). Sometimes all this could feel frustrating, but fortunately at the start of each "cycle" there is half a minute meditation exercise showing a nice picture of a temple with nice waterfalls, inviting you to "check additional contents" which I guess means that there is more to life than all this, and you should check inside yourself... at least this is my interpretation.All in all, whatever price you paid, it's too much for this Beta Software Simulation game.I liked the mini-games, though, and I would like that some publisher - other than Ubisoft - would take the idea and extrapolate it into a standalone game, which I would call Zelda Creed.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on steamdeck. Wow this game is the highest possible 9 out of 10 I can give.. I had no clue this game existed.... what perfect way to wash away the sadness of beating Elden Ring. Also.. everyone says it "copies" BOTW.. like shut up.. no seriously shut your stupid mouth... no really, look at me.. shut up and stay shut up.This game has its own very strong identity.. the graphic are incredible aided by an insane Elden Ring esque draw distance.. Now combat is good and challenging, but holy dog feces do I hate the fact there is a 2 button parry.. what a cheap way to make the game more difficult.. I immediately made it a 1 button back grip button press on Steamdeck.. also I do not agree with a lot of reviewers here that the player character is slidy or stiff.. not my experience.. however I do find gliding to be unnecessarily hard to control and it's irritating how the character can start climbing stuff in the battle.. and if you try to dash and jump you usually screw it up.. and stamina seems limited at times but you can pump it up whenever with plentiful mushrooms and potions. It's also super irritating that a lot of people see Ubisoft on the cover and immediately think oh it has too much collectibles.. but those very same people have no problem with the ridiculous complex crafting and leveling mechanics of a fromsoft game... I personally found the collecting of a bunch of different elements to level up many different types of abilities to not be a grind as the world is so dense with stuff to do that you are constantly collecting enough stuff to level up something. People also complain how it's a map marker collection where you just go from icon to icon on the map.. but really you don't have to reveal the map icons, it's a mechanic if you want it but you don't need to use it.. I preferred mostly exploring on my own.. seeing stuff in the distance and going "that's cool.. let's go there" or "I don't think I've ever been there before" just like Elden Ring.I like the setting and extremely densely packed world tons.. the puzzles are good and consistently get more interesting and difficult as the game opens up. I found the humor mostly on point and entertaining.. the music for the most part is amazing though some songs or musical cues can get quite repetitive... And I said it before the graphics are increadible.. but it does sometimes look too cartoony.. while other times it looks like the most beautiful game ever.. usually when you are high up and seeing the whole world.. and at 15$ or 80% off this game was a steal. at 50$ there is still enough here to make it worthwhile and had I known it was going to impress me so much I would've gladly thrown more money at it to snatch it up. Its a beautiful, fun, funny, rough around the edges colorful adventure well worth the asking price!

_childDocuments_.review: =Probably my last update=With about 10 hours in, I can definitively say that this game is more of a comedic lighthearted open world UBI game similar to Assassin's Creed.  The world is broken into sectors with a "tower" you must scale in order to remove the fog-of-war, there are the bosses for those sectors, and basically every other mechanic UBI has shoved into ALL of their open world games.  So, if you enjoy that very formulaic gamestyle, this is for you.  If you're tired of UBISoft's rehashing of this genre, you may want to pass.=End of updates====UPDATE 2===Now, a new issue.  Can't launch the game - click play, a few seconds later the play button lights up again.  Check task manager, and it definitely ISN'T running.  Click play again, same thing.Wow, the technical issues just keep coming and I'm quite sure it has to do with the launcher (UBI) and nothing to do with Steam.I actually just confirmed this minutes after posting the above - the UBISoft launcher never registered me quitting the game previously.  I went to shut it down, and received the notice that quitting the launcher while the game was active could cause issues - needless to say, the game was already shut down.  I restarted the launcher, and lo-and-behold, the game launched properly.===END UPDATE 2=====UPDATE===Sadly, after more hours in the game, I can say that it isn't a horrible game, but what brings it down are all of the technical issues most likely associated with UBISofts launcher and overlay.  Still getting errors on cloud saves, the game sometimes hangs when exiting, having to start the game multiple times - but when it is working, the game is pretty fun.===END UPDATE===On the fence still, but for $6, anyone could give it a go.- Initial play attempt = four or five UBI pop-ups, then nothing after it installed the UBISoft launcher on top of my current launcher and stalled.  Had to re-install the launcher after downloading it from their site, but then the game initially wouldn't register to my account.  Ran the game again and it worked, but cloud saves fail every time you exit the game.  I also have to start the game twice, as the first time it again tells me the game isn't registered to my account, but the second time it launches with no issues.- It seems they weren't sure how to handle the story - seriously or lightheartedly, so it fluctuates back & forth in a very painful manner.- Despite what Steam says, it does work with a controller after you turn off Steam input - it even natively supports controllers, so not sure what that was about.- Unlike some comments I've seen, you CAN choose your gender, but character customization is barebones+ Runs okay so far, no crashes, stutters, or anythingAt $6/$10 I can recommend the game, at this point, but definitely not at the normal $50+ cost.

_childDocuments_.review: IFR is a quality open world game in all the right ways. I did everything that I encountered but I know it’s not 100% due to some Ubisoft achievements (missing about 8-9 from the main game). Steam shows over 72 hours but in-game it shows around 65 hours. I played it blindly with no concern for efficiency. I enjoyed the puzzles and the overall variety with the challenges, moves/skills and combat.Sometimes you NEED to take a break due to its open world nature where tasks can feel repetitive, lots of asset re-use and there could have been more variety with the enemies. But it’s comparable to other open world games, nothing against this game in particular. Also the game has a lighthearted and funny atmosphere with the jokes and art style. I’m not against that but not all the jokes landed well. Some involve cheating and having weird s*x kinks between gods etc. It’s a bit weird when the game is trying to be cartoony. I’m still not a fan of launchers and this is no exception, but it didn’t give me any issues at least. My biggest problem is the lack of Steam achievements. Yes, you have them in their launcher but it’s just not the same. It’s demotivating and the reason why I didn’t go for 100%. I’m hopeful we’ll still get them like with Assassin’s Creed Valhalla and we know they can unlock retro actively based on previous examples. So all that I did is not wasted, I’m planning on getting 100% when we get Steam achievements.I usually ignore games without Steam achievements and I understand if others do it but I still highly recommend getting the game. I would even say that the normal price of €40 is worth it if you like open world games. The game is on sale often though, so you don’t have to pay that price. It’s awesome being able to get such a great game for a good price. I have all the DLC, I will be playing them in order next.

_childDocuments_.review: Fenyx Rising is a clone of the Zelda. With own bad and good sides. First of all, is an Ubisoft game. With all the consequences that entails. For almost 20 years, they still didn't change the template of game making. Grind times grind. Endless chests, items to collect and ctrl+c\ctrl-v activities. If you're a collector, get ready for a nearly endless gameplay. And this is a positive and the same time a negative moment. I mean, many side-activities are interesting to explore, but a lot (A LOT) aren't. Sometimes riddles are unclear to understand. That's why it is difficult to solve them. Sometimes you can meet similar riddles which you already solved many times before. For example, murals on the floor where you have to make a picture from its pieces.I liked graphics and art here. It's wonderful in my opinion. The game looks flamboyant and bright. The world is big and alive. Everything moves - trees, grass, birds in the sky, particles in the air. A mesmerizing sight. Enemies are different with their own abilities. Monsters from an antic mythology, and you easily can recognize them.But the battle system for me wasn't so interesting. Because once I found two-three overkill patterns to attack and didn't use others. And this is not about attacks only. I didn't use a bow and a sword at all. Only an axe with a regeneration health ability. A bow was a tool for riddle solving. Like in the Zelda you can climb, craft, fly, ride mounts and many classical things. Probably, the biggest problem for me here was a storytelling. Characters are faceless, annoying and boring. Specially narrators -Zeus and Hephaestus. I hate when powerful entities, like gods, in games turn into clowns in a circus. And yes, antic gods here are pathetic clowns. They make references to a modern culture. Characters all the time desperately try to joke, but this completely unfunny. The cringe parade in the flesh.  This may be funny only for kids. And it should be Greek kids, 'cause from time to time narrators remember a myth and discuss it without the context. I mean, all of us know the most famous myths about the twelve feats of Hercules or The Trojan Horse, but there are a lot of not so famous myths, which we don't know (or only me). My point is when narrators discuss something, they often don't give a context. Not only they. Even the game doesn't give a historical note. Nobody cares if you're understanding or not what they're talking about. And all the story comes that way. The plot here, as simple and dull as it can be. Came Typhoon and took the Olympus from gods. So help those helpless hipsters gods and take their place back. But I believe they don't deserve it.A very uneven game. You can enjoy some elements of it and hate others. Is it a good game or bad? I don't know. Buy on sale and if you REALLY want it. I played IFR for 40 hours half on a year ago and dropped it. After such a big pause, I had come back to it. And finally did it. The game completed. And the final part was the best. P.s. You can find all my short reviews .

_childDocuments_.review: Inevitably this game will get compared to The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, and fair enough because it's clearly heavily inspired by it, but this game does not have the weapon durability system. In my opinion this game is probably the definitive "Breath of the Wild experience" for PC gamers. For me personally, this game really does knocked it out of the park in almost every way. Immortals Fenyx Rising is an open-world adventure/action/hack and slash/puzzle game that really does make you feel like a hero in a Greek myth. The characters are endearing and well-performed. The humor is full of amazingly awful dad jokes and self-awareness about how messed up a lot of Greek mythology really is. The humor, gameplay, and art style reminds me a lot of older PlayStation 2 games like Jak & Daxter and Sly Cooper. The banter between Zeus and Prometheus that you overhear while running around fighting minotaurs and gorgons is really something special. (Jokingly) my only issues with the game is that there isn't more of it. I'd love to see sequels made by the same team take on Norse and Egyptian mythologies and more. Realistically though I'd say this game has a few small flaws that you can avoid if you know what you're doing, which most new players won't. First and foremost, don't try to 100% the game on your first playthrough. I tried to do that and ended up being way too strong and I had accidentally optimized myself into boredom. The stun system is way too easy to exploit once you get a handful of items and if you have enough stamina you can basically stunlock every single enemy and boss without even trying. My second issue is that the whole "play any way you want" as advertised with the incredibly diverse gear system gets left behind once you realize there are like two or three dominant strategies and 90% of the gear is pretty irrelevant. There are three main weapons which are the sword, axe, and bow. A lot of items buff different weapons differently. However the bow will never be as good as the sword (especially since you can jump and sort of hover in the air while you attack), and you never need to use the axe for stun damage when it's so much slower than the sword, and your special powers like Athena's Dash will deal way more stun damage than the axe can ever dream of. Sure, you can build a character who focuses on aerial combat and stunlocks enemies out of the sky but that's probably not as effective as just equipping the right armor and spamming Ares's Wrath while chugging stamina potions. My third issue is the Difficulty scales both the puzzle and combat difficulty at the same time. Combat difficulty is self-explantory, and just changes numbers like your health regen speed and enemy damage output. This game has a lot of puzzles that are based on timers, like you flip a switch, a door opens, and you have to run across a complicated room to get through that door before the timer expires. So increasing difficulty lowers the length of the timers, requiring much higher skill to complete. Now if you're like me and you're really good at combat but really bad at puzzles, you're out of luck because you either get bored from the combat or you lock yourself out of doing any puzzles. It's not a big deal but it basically requires you to be a big fish in a small pond by intentionally avoiding making yourself overpowered for combat. Like I explained above it's very easy to accidentally "over-level" and cheese the game to hell. These are issues that are pretty easily remedied and avoided but only after you've sunken a few dozen hours into the game. My advice would be to play on Normal, focus on the actual quests, and don't try to 100% the game the first time around. There's New Game+ and a "Nightmare Difficulty" which will give you a nice victory lap to 100% the game on and I definitely think you should because there are so many clever puzzles and Zeus and Prometheus have little conversations based on the smallest things you do in the game. I think this game really deserves a lot of attention for how great it is.

Some fraction of this time was spoiled by poorly designed puzzles, not working controls, bugs with physics or targeting issues. But otherwise it's a solid game.I wish there were no DLCs, but more base game content, more weapons/armors, various enemies and some sort of end-game. I wish there were Steam achievements so I'd spend some extra time trying to complete them.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to the mostly negative recent reviews I feel like I should share my experience with the game as well. For me there were only some minor performance issues. In 40 hours playtime the game froze 3 times and crashed once. Which obviously was annoying, but tolerable since I was back in-game after literally one minute with almost zero progress loss.Besides that I had a great time playing this game. The story was centered around greek mythology and narrated in a comedic kind of way. You are supposed to free 4 gods and defeat the final boss Typhon, who stole the essences of the gods.The puzzles of the game are fun and the vaults (dungeons) are really great. Combat is also very fun and the world is beautiful. If you want to do everything on the map I guess you could spend around 60-90 hours. I got it on sale for 11.99€ and would definitely recommend it for that price. 59.99€ might still be a little too expensive.7.5/10edit: I had full controller support with my xbox controller after disabling the steam input in properties.

The world is dense in Immortals Fenyx Rising, with puzzles to solve and monsters to fight around every hill and valley. _childDocuments_.review: Oh, Ubisoft, can you just make a good game a good game and not ruin it for a while?.. Immortals Fenyx Rising is a Greek mythology based action adventure in an open world that attempts to marry The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild to the Assassin’s Creed formula from Origins to today. And the concept is genuinely solid as are the basics, but… Well. It’s Ubisoft, so despite liking the game a lot, I’m writing this exhausted and after deciding not to play the DLCs.To get it out of the way first – I have not played Breath of the Wild yet myself. I’ve not found Switch comfortable enough to own or even borrow, so I’ve avoided that title and, if I’m going to be honest to myself – I doubt that I will like it that much. The promise of a completely free open map with no little handholding, systemic approach to design sounds both impressive and also super boring to me. I just tend to prefer more guided titles, even if they leave a lot of freedom to what I can do, I just don’t particularly care about games that want me to wander around and find entertainment for myself.That’s one of the reasons why I thought Immortals Fenyx Rising might click with me – it’s a far more guided experience. To the point where it’s a more traditionally story-driven game. It has a lot of similar basics as BotW, but most of the systems are simplified and you get a lot of what you expect to find in a modern AC instead. So, unlike BotW, it’s not a question of – you can fight the final boss from the start, it’s just going to be stupid hard unless you get better gear and upgrades by doing the rest of the game. It’s more of a – you can do most of the game in any order, but you cannot get to the ending without going through all linear story arcs.And I’m mostly fine with that. The story is… I’m sure a lot of people will roll their eyes at the approach to writing in this game, as it basically takes the Ancient Greek mythology and tells it as a fourth-wall breaking somewhat anachronistic “modern” story, with social media lingo and memes included. But it manages to do it well enough to not sound like “how do you do, fellow kids”, and on top of that the underlying story is good and the voice acting performances are fun.Plus it doesn’t usually get in the way of gameplay, which (unlike AC games) is more central here. As mentioned, it’s far closer to modern AC, so while you do get limited stamina, just like in BotW, the climbing itself is basically lifted from Odyssey as is. And you don’t get any additional systemic elements on top of that – there are no rains to make things slippery or lightning to strike metallic things or anything like that. But still, just adding stamina, making the world full of small and bigger puzzles that are fun to solve and which are very varied, makes the game feel entirely unlike modern AC titles and, gameplay-wise, much more interesting.But then they Ubisofted all over the map with Stuff To Do. As mentioned – I’ve not played BotW myself and neither did I watch anyone ever 100% it. But finding treasures and solving optional puzzles in Immortals feels very un-Zelda and extremely Ubisoft. There’s just way too much crap, most of it is useless (no really, most of the rewards are just skins for equipment), simple upgrade materials are measured in thousands just so you must get more of them… The quality of a lot of puzzles and puzzle dungeons suffers greatly from it too. Like – for example, there’s a fun little one-off puzzle dungeon which suddenly turns the game into pinball. Fun and unexpected, but it’s so unrefined and random that instead of having fun, you’ll be wasting several dozens of minutes trying to achieve the goal the game set because everything is slow and random. That, or do it very quickly because again – totally random. And it’s just one example among dozens of icons on the map screen you’ll get if you mark them (you can decide not to mark them, though).And if the game had about half of it simply cut while the rest better refined, I’d be singing praises for the game right now. Well, no, first I’d be playing DLCs that I, otherwise, just had no patience for right now, then singing praises. Instead, I consciously understand that I’ve enjoyed the game and I love what they were doing here. But also I don’t want to play it anymore.Then again, it’s not the only thing cooling my excitement. Despite clearly being a lower budget (not as low budget as poor Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands got, mind you), Ubisoft wanted to double dip hard into this release, so the store and microtransactions are pushed hard down your throat from the start… Even though all of them are purely decorative. The Steam release is also clearly a throwaway thing for the company as they didn’t even bother to make a proper compatibility check for Steam Controller system, so without additional (if simple) tweaks, the game won’t properly work for you. It also loads super slowly, because it “checks for additional content” every time you have to get into main menu for about half a minute. And after you close the game, Ubisoft Connect (ex-Uplay) throws a million errors at you. Just – no care for the title whatsoever.It’s a real shame, because I did like this game. And I would’ve liked it much much more, and maybe the DLCs too, if it knew when to stop and not Ubisoft its pants. But no, sadly it does the exact same mistakes all recent Ubisoft titles do. I’d say – it’s still worth checking out. It’s fun, funny, with some good puzzles, descent combat… And it feels more fresh than what you usually expect from the developers. Plus, this feels like a passion project, reminding me of how exciting Origins felt. Like all of the nerdy fun things the team learned from Ancient Greece research finally could be shared with the world, because it sure as hell wasn’t in Odyssey which was just sterile and boring in comparison. But do expect it to get stale and you stopping playing it not because you finished it, but because you got bored.

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals: Fenyx Rising is a near-perfect game in my eyes. As Fenyx, you are the protagonist in the tale of Prometheus, exploring the lands of the gods to free and unite them against Typhon. As a fan of anything mythology-related, the greek mythology is represented very well in this game. You are constantly being told new small tales from greek mythology, even when just exploring and happening upon some ruins, or fighting a legendary foe. The story is told very tongue-in-cheek; the game does not take itself too seriously and remembers that it is, first and foremost, a game. Not all of the humor lands, but most of it got a good chuckle out of me and helps keep the game light and fun while teaching you lots of cool mythology. I don't get some of the negative reviews; I had no problem with crashes, the Ubisoft Client works fine (surprisingly) and it DOES work on the Steam Deck without any setup necessary or any problems; I played it on there for a while.The gameplay consists of exploring the lands of the gods; 5 main areas and 2 small side areas. The combat system is active, with light and heavy attacks you can mix and match. The more you explore, the more you can upgrade your stats, learn the powers of the gods and obtain their blessings, which power you up further. The game's power curve is excellently done - while fighting against a simple bear at the beginning can prove fatal, you will feel like a god by the end of the game yourself, effortlessly cutting swaths throughout the enemy hordes. The game also has a fantastic artstyle and looks downright gorgeous, though the optimization could be slightly better.Exploring the areas is typically Ubisoft, though this time, there aren't really any collectibles - anything you find serves you in some way. Chests give new equipment and cosmetic variations as well as upgrade ingredients while splinters and ambrosia upgrade your weapons and health. The landscape is also dotted with tons of vaults - small puzzle side areas which, I thought, were surprisingly well done. There are a lot of puzzle ideas in this game, from moving boxes around to playing pinball with heavy balls and using controllable arrows to light fires. 50 hours and I never, ever got bored and the game never got repetitive, which is honestly a feat in my eyes. I heard the game being compared to Zelda: BotW at times, and while I have never played that, after reading up on it, the gameplay loop does seem to be very similar. It's high quality stuff, never too hard but can make you think at times.The only two downsides I can find is that, first, you have to "mark" things on the map yourself by entering far sight mode and hovering over the treasures, like in Mad Max for example. Far Sight has a limited range though, so you have to sometimes stop and scan your surroundings. It takes only a minute though and its cool to populate and check off your map. The other thing is that there is an ingame store - it's all cosmetics, though, and the game has daily / weekly quests that give you a currency for cosmetics you can't find by playing the game normally. That currency is very easy to obtain and by the end of the game, you will have unlocked several of those extra cosmetics, on top of every cosmetic equipment variation you can find just by playing. A single player game having an in game store can be argued about, but it's all cosmetic stuff and I never bought anything. Since the game does use the Ubisoft launcher, you will also get experience in their Ubisoft Connect system, which also allows you to unlock some cosmetics. You can ignore all of that, though, if you want, but it should be mentioned; game is awesome, though.Finishing the main game, with exploring everything and finding all the things, took me about 50 hours. The DLCs are very solid as well - I reviewed those separately. Either way, this game has an insane bang for your buck if you are at all interested in epic open world adventures with a tongue-in-cheek story, addictive gameplay and lots of things to do and find, including a ton of secrets. This is a true gem and one of the best games I ever played, simply because it knows that it's a game and is pure fun. A definite recommendation!( As mentioned, the game works fine on Steam Deck; if you logged into it on a PC before, you don't even need to enter your UPlay credentials. It doesn't use Steam Cloud Save though; your saves are automatically backed up through the Ubisoft launcher after closing the game, so they are there when switching to / from the Deck.)

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, it felt a bit weird helping these gods instead of slaughtering them. Heard the name “Hermes” and I immediately clenched my fists in anger.It looks like Zelda and Assassins’s Creed finally had a baby. The game is flawless, and creative in every way. This game is definitely one of the best sleeper hits of 2020. The story is a blast and hiding the pretty factual lore behind two bantering narrators was genius. Honestly, I absolutely loved this game. Even though I joked about it, I feel those that call it a "clone" of AC or Breath of the Wild were giving it an incomplete assessment. It's WAY different than both of those games, despite being clearly inspired by them.My biggest gripe with BOTW is that there was very little story and no structure as far as where to go and what to do. This game remedies both of those and makes for a more engaging experience.BOTW is about exploring a vast world with stuff to do spread out over a largely empty map. Fenyx is about exploring a smaller, denser world with a lot more (and better) stuff to do condensced into a very full map.I had a blast playing it and actually spent the time to almost 100% it because it was that fun to me. It’s not a deep game, and the comedy falls flat 90% of the time, but I have no regrets in buying it.I love when a game doesn’t take itself too seriously just like this one, all those jokes and “deliberately” corny narration is just nice laughing material, it’s like playing Monty Python’s Greek version.I will admit my dumb monkey brain did struggle with a few puzzles which felt a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to me, but most of them felt super rewarding after completing them.Combat was pretty neat. I liked all the special abilities you could get as well as the combination of aerial combat to combo into different things. Ubisoft games in general tend to have kinda repetitive combat to me so this was a nice change of pace.I also loved how bright and vibrant everything is. I know the cartoony art style is hit or miss for a lot of people but I found it charming. The enemy designs were also super cool too.The only real gripe that I had with it (besides the occasional frustrating puzzle) is that towards the end it got a bit easy. It may be down to me just getting better naturally but in the last 1/3 of the game, enemies felt super easy and I could do entire rooms of fights without getting hit at all.Overall, it's great and definitely worth picking up on a sale. A shame that everything went against it, including being launched a week before Cybercrap 2077.This game would have been way more popular with a better name and not stuck on Ubisoft's launcher.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This was a hard one to give a thumbs up to. It shouldn't have been, because the game-play was great, it was interesting and kept your attention all the way through, which is really rare in today's market. Graphics were decent, though it could have used better texturing in a lot of areas. All the characters were likable. Plays a lot like Breath of the Wild on the Switch, which was a nice touch.HOWEVER, just like turn-on's and turn-off's, I absolutely hated the plugs for the 'new age' hyped political BS over gender identity, non-binary (Yes, I got the joke about Hermaphroditus. Did you?), etc,.. I mean, it's the Roman era, which was famous of course for it's recorded history of incest and homosexuality, so you should expect that going in and accept that those events as they happened. But why include all our current day identity crisis nonsense this? It doesn't help the character, it's not comedic, it doesn't contribute to the story, it's forced and doesn't fit the narrative, it certainly doesn't HELP the sales of the product, so why?At least there wasn't that many references to it. But still, simply existing was off-putting and really killed the mood for me. The game would have been all the better (and would have a better shelf life) if you kept this out.

_childDocuments_.review: Really, this game is quite amazing for what it is.  It is trying it's best to have an open world like Zelda:BotW, but have more to do it in than BotW offered.  To be clear, I am not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on BotW, it's an amazing game.  But so is this.  It's not as thoughtful, it's doing its best to lean more towards humor, and it's successful.Throughout the adventure, you will often hear the continued tale and discussions between Zeus and Prometheus.  It's funny and heartwarming.  The tale is meant to show Zeus he is a bad father while saving humanity and preventing the Titan called Typhon from killing the gods and taking over the world, remaking it in his own image.  The Voices:  The voice acting is truly great in this game.  Everyone is speaking English (in the English version), but they have thick Greek accents and it adds more levity to it as they discuss the various transgressions that Zeus has committed against his own family.  At one point they are talking about Herakles and Zeus interrupts asking "why are you saying it like that?".  To which Prometheus responds by saying, "Because that is how it's pronounced".  The joke here being that everyone refers to the Greek Hero Herakles as "Hercules", which is a Romanized version of the name.  It really leans hard into it's Greek roots and I truly loved that about the game.  Nor is it filled with the fluffy, childish version of Greek Mythology, it's the gritty kind of Greek Mythology with all the nastiness they contain, and all the wonder as well.  You also come across and regularly speak to the likes of Hermes, Hephaestus, Ares, Athena, and Aphrodite, all of which are excellently voiced.  Story:  Story is fine.  It was never going to win any awards on this front.  It wouldn't be a game about Greek Mythology if it wasn't your basic heroes journey story.  And it is that in spades.  A man/woman (you get to choose what Fenyx is), who is a shield bearer and story teller, but no great warrior, must come to realize that he/she is a hero because that is what they need to be.  Who they were will mean something to who they are becoming, but a hero is someone who is called to duty and answers when the call comes, not necessarily someone who is born warrior.Gameplay:  This is where the game really really shines.  As the game goes on, you will unlock more and more powers to fight in a world that is becoming ever more harsh.  The map is riddled with gateways to Tartaros (think the puzzle dungeons of Zelda:BofW).  And these are a lot of fun.  You always get from them a piece of Zeus's lightning bolt which is used to enhance Fenyx as the game goes on.  You also expand the health pool by finding Ambrosia around the map.  The combat is exciting, it is on the ground and in the sky, and the ever broadening of Fenyx's abilities really opens up what you can and cannot do in the world.  Some of those same abilities will also enable you have an easier time solving all the puzzles around the world.  Each one of the aforementioned gods will need to brought back to their full godhood through what are essentially trials on Fenyx's heroes journey.  They also grant blessings which can enhance your gameplay in subtle ways.  For example, Ares blessings will enhance combat, even adding a new combo stage to your combo meter.  These things can change what weapons you decide to use.  Each weapon does something different.  Perhaps it improves the damage your sword does.  But there are others that will restore health when you reach a new combo stage, while others may offer enhanced stun for a few seconds after a perfect dodge.  All the equipment works like this.  You can forge your equipment to enhance the bonuses and do more damage or give better defense.  All equipment, when enhance to level 4, will unlock another bonus you get for using it.  All the upgrades are to gear slots, and not specific gear, so you don't have to worry about enhancing all the swords, your upgrades count for all swords/axes/armors.Beyond Tartaros, the world is riddled with challenges that each offer further enhancement to Fenyx.  They unlock more weapons/armors, or offer more upgrade materials, or offer cosmetic changes to equipment you already have, or Coins of Charon.  The coins are vital as they are used a currency to upgrade your powers.  Some will offer a charge to a godly weapon ability, others though will enhance the ways you can navigate the world or the battle field.  For example, you get the Wings of Daidolas, but one of the first abilities worth getting is the one that allows you to glide faster and use less stamina.  Herakles Gauntlets allow you to move heavy objects, but an enhancement not only allows you to pick up heavier blocks, but pull enemies towards you, or you towards enemies, on the battle field.The map is absolutely massive.  Each God is in a certain part of the world, each section of the map is very different from each other.  Aphrodite lives in an incredibly lush, natural land.  Athena resides in a beautiful but more developed area with many large temples and landmarks.  Hephaestus lives in a land that is more barren, as befitting a god that uses a forge to make things.  It's littered with broken down automatons.  Ares land is blasted by War, barren, and really only has half destroyed structures besides his massive keep.The game does support ultrawide and run great for me.  It's a huge world and it feels even larger at 5120x1440.  All of this is delivered by consistent frame rates.  The draw distance is pretty impressive because at points you are high enough to see every inch of the Golden Isle, and it all looks quite good in my opinion.  Also, there is a day/night cycle and it feels like a different world at different times of day.  In the northernmost land, at night, you will see Aurora Borealis in the night sky and night will also offer a few combat challenges that only become available at night.All of this is great, it's easily a 9/10 game for me.  It's compelling and fun to play, nothing feels forced.  There is one downside though, and that is Ubisoft Connect.  When you start the game it will always "Check for more content...", and this will always take 30-60 seconds with no way to shut it off.  Hermes main point in the game, besides comedy relief, is offer to lighten your burden of Electrum (real money currency for the game, which only offers you cosmetic or shortcut items).  As soon as you get back to home base, his first inquiry is about you spending Electrum.  It's an annoying live service thing they added to an otherwise fantastic single player game.  You can get Electrum by doing daily or weekly quests, but it's really immersion breaking to hear Hermes offer to let you buy some premium skin or crafting gear goody bag.I did not play the DLC, the reviews overall were disappointing for them so I didn't really feel a need or want to do them.  The main game also offers a New Game + option, which I may come back to at a later time.

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising is a perfectly cromulent open world icon hoovering sim. What makes it different from the million and one other icon hoovering titles is that it's cartoonish and light-hearted. You never have to kill any real people because all the baddies are ghostly monsters conjured up by the big bad. The story does not take itself seriously at all. The jokes are bad, barely even dad joke quality, but they're not offensive. They're just kinda... there.In fact the whole game is just kinda... there. The movement and combat is a bit janky, but not unplayably so. There are some tedious parkour and platforming sections, but most of them are optional. The puzzles are polished versions of lever and trapdoor, Sokoban, that sort of thing. They're actually pretty decent if you like casual puzzling, and really push this game from "meh" up to "solid way to spend a bunch of hours".You're a hero. You explore Greece. You help the gods. You save mankind. Do not expect a compelling story or an unforgettable multimedia experience. It's just cheerful, harmless fun. Sometimes that's all you need.

_childDocuments_.review: I never fully embraced Ubisoft’s open world games until I played Immortals: Fenyx Rising. Don’t sleep on this game! It’s different, and in a good way.Immortals: Fenyx Rising has a similar look to Zelda: Breath of the Wild, but the colors in Immortals: Fenyx Rising are more vibrant; and the textures are more consistent. Zelda: Breath of the Wild includes some more realistic textures along with its cartoony look; Immortals: Fenyx Rising does not.A word about the comparison with Zelda: Breath of the Wild. I never understood why gaming journalists criticized the similarities. Obviously Immortals: Fenyx Rising was inspired by Zelda, but why should this be a bad thing? Nobody would say that a Souls-like game is “too similar” to Dark Souls either.The gameplay in Immortals: Fenyx Rising encompasses three major areas: exploring, puzzle solving, and combat. Minor gameplay features include role-playing mechanics, i.e. leveling up, gathering materials, and crafting potions. Exploration is fun, as the open world is reasonably sized and offers an unusual but welcome amount of verticality. Fenyx, our protagonist, is equipped with the wings of Daidalos – and gliding through the air is just so much fun in this game. Solving puzzles may sound boring at first; aren’t minigames and puzzles in most games? Yes, I think so, but Immortals: Fenyx Rising is different because the puzzles never exhaust you. While playing through the game, I never once felt the need to look up any solutions online. Even after more than 40 hours into the game, the puzzles will still introduce new mechanics. Don’t expect Portal or The Talos Principle, but I’m sure that some of the puzzles in Immortals: Fenyx Rising will surprise you. In short, the puzzles will demand your wits, but they will rarely, if ever, frustrate you.The combat is pleasantly over the top as your abilities are more than just human. You have superhuman abilities, such as Hephastios’ hammer, my favorite: a giant hammer appears in your hand and you simply smash your foes. It never gets boring. The only bad thing I can say about combat in Immortals: Fenyx Rising is the lack of variety in your enemies. Then again, you spend more time exploring and solving puzzles anyway; so every fight feels like a welcome change of pace. Also, dodging or blocking enemy attacks is an effective and fun way to make sure you get the upper hand in every fight.The soundtrack is another big plus. Previous works by Gareth Coker, who composed the soundtrack for Immortals: Fenyx Rising, include the soundtracks of Ori and the Blind Forest and Ori and the Will of the Wisps. If you want to get an idea of how well done the soundtrack is, just listen to the main track “Heart of the Hero”.Fenyx’ story is told by two narrators: the always smug, boastful Zeus and the more thoughtful, idealistic Prometheus. They comment on many of the events in the background and I personally find their dialog hilarious. You will understand many of the jokes and even more if you are somewhat familiar with Ancient Greek mythology. For example, at one point Zeus comments: “The sincerest form of flattery is kidnapping someone so you can get some alone time, just ask Ganymede.” I laughed my head off. The other gods are fun, too. Ares, for example, [minor spoiler:]  He is helplessly in love with Aphrodite, but doubts his chances: “Oh, so a gorgeous goddess in love with a ? I’m sure that’s illegal.” Zeus only comments in the background: “Definitely not illegal!” There are also wholesome moments, like Prometheus saying: “Fenyx couldn’t help but reflect on what the god of war had taught her. That true courage isn’t the absence of despair. But triumph over it.” So, yeah, I enjoyed the dialogue quite a bit in this game.You won’t pass a test on Ancient Greek mythology by playing Immortals: Fenyx Rising, but Ubisoft Québec has done a really good job integrating Ancient Greek mythology into their game. If you’re unfamiliar with it, you will learn many stories on your adventure; and if you already know them, your knowledge will be refreshed and you’ll understand the insiders.You can grab the Gold Edition of Immortals: Fenyx Rising for like $15 during a big sale and it’s definitely worth it. Another reviewer here called this game “criminally underrated”; I agree.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real treasure. A huge amount of content awaits you in a really big open world, which you can freely explore.The story is set in Greek mythology and right at the beginning I have to say that as an classical archaeologist I was very pleasantly surprised by the accuracy, details and references that the game offers. The whole thing has a more light-hearted tone and lots of humor, which is really perfect. Especially the chemistry between Zeus and Prometheus is very good. A huge advantage for me is that the game doesn't seem repetitive to me at all. Puzzles, vaults and also enemies are original and except for a few basic units, they are not repeated at all. The combat system is enjoyable, the game offers multiple fighting styles that you can use at the same time. Quick short sword, a long heavy axe or a long  distance bow. A stealth option is also present and the whole thing is further enriched by a large number of special attacks. Finally, I would like to mention flying, which is really amazing. Yes, the ubisoft launcher isn't perfect, it would be great to have achievements on steam and there is also an in-game store with microtransactions, but I personally didn't notice it at all while playing. Definitely give this game a try, it´s worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually not bad. It's very clearly inspired by BOTW, both in shading (very bright colors and cell shaded cartoony shaders for bodies of water) as well the way combat pans out. Unfortunately it's nowhere near as "free" as the aforementioned due to the lack of meaningful interactions with the terrain. It basically copied weaponized rigidbodies and stopped there.First and foremost I want to mention very clearly that this game is Ubisoft. It RADIATES Ubisoft. Progression is tied to, and I kid you not, 8 different currencies of gems. It has in-game real money cosmetic purchases, including horse armor (again, this is not a joke). It has a season pass for its DLC. It tries to tie the story into having you buy aforementioned microtransactions in a completely offline single player game. Whoever came up with the design here made the marketing lead at Ubitrash jizz their pants. Over half the available space is in the main menu is dedicated to advertisements for in-game purchases. It's so unbelievably greedy it's almost like satire.Fortunately these can be fairly easily ignored, and the remainder of the game is quite nice. Aside from your starting gear new equipment that you find are actual sidegrades; which is exactly how I like it. On the flipside there is still linear power progression, only it is tied to currencies. The overworld is actually beautiful, but also feels very devoid of life and more like ambient set-pieces. Enemies live somewhere in the realm of "decently dynamic"; some of them actively react to the environment by picking up rigid bodies. Other simply spawn rigidbodies to throw. Enemies seem to have different attack patterns based on the proximity to the player. It's too little to be impressive, but it's much more than most modern games can be given credit for.The gameplay loop is decent. There is a very strong state economy going on due to neither health nor stamina regenerating during combat (technically it does, but VERY slowly). Hitting stunned targets regenerates stamina. Parrying regenerates stamina - more so the closer you are to the active frames. Enemies have a stun-bar, which once filled, causes them to be, well... stunned. The game effectively rewards you for alternating in your strategy, which is of course great. The flipside is once again that it implements parrying without trying to reduce it; implying that you just have to learn the animations for each enemy to be effective. Outside the rigidbodies projectiles can be hard to read. You have heavy attacks, light attacks and a bow - all of which can be transitioned between seamlessly. You also have aerial attacks for each (which seem to be extremely overpowered). They're just simple three or four hit combos, which is a true and tested implementation and completely fine as is.One of my primary gripes is actually with the traversal; stamina regenerates faster outside combat, but you still spend it way too fast in my opinion. This means that you can't just run anywhere. You randomly have to halt and wait for it to regenerate. This makes sense for vertical traversal (which is great in this game by the way; you can climb ANY piece of geometry, only limited by your stamina), but not for running around.The story is annoying. The game has this whole "you guys know, like, greek mythology???? Here is a funni reference to it1!" theme going that's amusing for maybe 1 minute and then starts to overstay its welcome. It makes very obvious references to the Odysseus and paints the pantheon through the most obvious "comical" caricatures. Especially Zeus they reduce to a pompous numbskull (they really go to town on Zeus, it's almost like a vendetta).Overall it's all quite good, and a pretty surprising game to have developed by Ubitrash. I presume this was greenlit to try and cash in on that BOTW hype - which clearly failed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 65% through the main game. And so far as I can recommend...don't play this on PC if you have the option.The story is enjoyable enough, the narration (literal) is amusing, and something of a unique concept. The Greek mythos is quite well researched. 4.5/5Game play  and combat in particular is somewhat spotty, but still decent. I'm sure you can adjust the controls to make it a little more streamlined, but it's clearly more intended for console. 3/5Puzzles are...well not entirely puzzles? I mean, there is some cleverness there but overall not terribly difficult. If you're here for the puzzles don't expect to be overwhelmed. 2.5/5Exploration is...really a let down to be honest. You climb up to a high point to reveal a map section and then you go into first person and scout out every single secret the map has. It's not exactly engaging to know what you're going to find at that weird temple in the distance. 2.5/5There are no steam achievements and Ubisoft Connect is a serious pain the ass. Keep in mind that Connect will run in the background, so keep that in mind if you have a borderline system. Also, there is a not insignificant cash grab feature for skins and such that isn't terribly subtle but thankfully not completely in your face. 0/5If you still want to play the game, and it is fairly enjoyable (but could be much more so with little effort on their part, seriously Ubisoft). Then my recommendation is not to play it on PC but on console. The game was VERY CLEARLY designed for console. The port isn't exactly a bad one per se...but play it on console is my recommendation. Coming from a PC master race it's annoying to say that, but eh...Overall, it's a solid 3/5 on the PC. And enjoyable enough. But I wouldn't pay $60 for it. Right now it's on sale 75% off. That's good for the time waster this has proven to be. But full price? Nope.EDIT (08JAN2023) :: The game also occasionally crashes. Possibly something to do with the autosave?EDIT (10JAN2023) :: Ubisoft Connect overlay must be enabled for daily quests.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game. There is a good atmosphere, a decent moveset, good progression, interesting armor/weapon builds, loads of playtime, and exploring is fun. About 40 hours to 100% the game, and another 30 in the DLCs.But there are too many things that irk me to leave a good review. -I bought the upgraded version with all the DLC, and the menu screen is 80% covered with ads for the DLC and store. -The ubisoft app integration is super bad, about half of the time I launch the game, it cannot verify my ownership and won't let me play. -Anytime you enter a cutscene, it will hardlock all your inputs at that time. So if you are opening the map when it starts, you will continually open the map afterwards. As soon as you close the map it re-opens. You can't access the menus because the map opens in 0.5 seconds. You have to alt+f4 the game to fix it. Completely unreasonable for a game that's been out this long.-Many of the bonus rewards in the puzzle vaults just require you to spend 10 extra minutes ferrying around heavy objects and don't do anything interesting. Just a super tedious chore.-The enemy AI is really simple, even bosses seem to only have 3 moves. And they have a very long projection to the point there is no danger. Combat is made too easy with high stun god-moves that you can spam. And I'm not even abusing the completely broken potions that basically negate combat (100% protection, reflect all projectiles, return 2k damage in a single defense potion that lasts the entire fight).-Scripting and voice acting is super cringy. The characters are supposed to have Greek accents, but Zeus sounds more like a jewish grandmother. The dialogue is sometimes straight Greek mythology and okay, but other times it's over the top youth-speak, trying to be relevant to Gen Z or something. The two contrast so much and just doesn't make sense.-They decided to put online player screenshots all over the map, so when you try to fast travel or select a quest on the map, you often have to navigate your way around player screenshots to select the actual thing.-Cutscenes are in 30 fps, but don't appear to be pre-rendered because they use player cosmetics, so why are they so low? Same with menus, opening menu sections can sporadically drop your fps if there is a video preview of an ability in action.DLC Review:A New God was just a castle with vaults of tartaros-style puzzle rooms. There were something like 25 puzzle/platforming rooms that took a bit of time to work through. Some were okay, some were really tedious, none really added anything beyond the main game. Definitely not worth a purchase, even if you liked the vaults of tartaros.Eastern Realms seems like it was the initial development of a sequel game, but is super unpolished. Voice acting is super bad, some of the character recordings are echoey and poorly done. Puzzle rooms are very poorly crafted, many can be easily cheated by flying under the level to the final lift. Would have been a much better setting for the game than the original Greek mythology. Really seems like they were working on a sequel and then just dumped it as a DLC for a quick payout before layoffs.Lost Gods is a top-down version of the game that removes all of the best features of the original game, like stamina based climbing, gliding, and being able to see more than 20 feet away from you.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually a pretty good game - mythology, puzzle solving, nice music, a lush world to explore. I think the impressive part is that it manages to be good  being an Ubisoft game, and you can see where the Ubisoft middle managers have had their hand in the pie, with the currencies and 'map vomit' of activities. But somehow the developers have, thankfully, contrived to push those to the side as much as possible so that you can actually forget it's there. The 'map vomit' is more of a 'sneeze' and is actually more spread out and manageable, and the currencies are just something you can easily forget about or ignore and doesn't make itself known too much. As for the game itself, it's a decent story, about as much as you can expect from an open world one. The best part for me is that it doesn't take itself seriously, there's a good dose of seriousness and humour everywhere.  The mechanics are fun and build up slowly so that you get that sense of empowerment as you progress. There are plenty of activities on the side that help you build up your power, the vaults were especially fun for me. I didn't face any of the technical issues mentioned so it always pays to be a patient gamer. I'd recommend it if you're a fan of open world and puzzles and something that isn't trying too hard to please.Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game that I definitely recommend to anyone who is on the fence. Ran perfect, plenty of PC friendly options and controlled great with KB/M. The graphic design was great and made for some awesome areas on the map. I absolutely loved the story, the narration and comedy as you move throughout the world was so well done that it kept a great flow. Plenty of variety in puzzles without being overly difficult. Fun combat, again without being too overly difficult. The game is very forgiving if you die, during mid combat after I took down a huge mob I died and it respawned me on the last boss with the mob already cleared out. I loved the challenge without the annoyances of “starting all over”. I did not 100% this game but there is plenty to do and what I did explore I was always rewarded with some kind of upgrade or items I needed. I really hope they make sequel and expand on the Greek Mythology because there is plenty to work with. I never really found an “armor set” that suited my playstyle but by the end of the game I was cleaning house. It was nice to be very powerful for quite sometime before finishing the game. One common annoyance with these types of games is that as soon as you become powerful…the game ends. WHAT THE HELL???? I wanted to play a little while in full kick ass mode and this game allows that.BUY IT AND PLAY IT

_childDocuments_.review: An above average game that could of been great if wasn't open world. If it just had a linear story and cut out all the filler content it would of been a masterpiece. Yes this is a legit zelda alternative but it lacks the awesome physic puzzles or robust crafting freedom of that game. On top of that we get lots of padding including a 3 hour intro/prelude and many things like double jump and basic moves like air dash locked behind a skill tree. I personally loved the puzzles but i felt like they should of just put the best parts of the puzzle temples instead of having lot of repetitive filler. How many times do have to find a hidden rock to put down on a pressure plate for crying out loud. The combat is basic as well and the harder difficulties only make the already too long game even more torturous with there cheap bullet sponge ways. I personally loved the beautiful graphics and titan quest vibes and despite me not having enough interest to finish i'll recommend it on sale. But ubisoft's open world ways really got in their way of delivering what could of been a fun little romp.  Instead it becomes just another tiresome open world game that you will never finish due to eventual boredom.

Those make the combat more interesting.  I will take a break for a while, but will come back for a nightmare play through.  I do recommend this game as it's a fun time killer.  oh, and it ran beautifully on highest settings, which is great considering my middle of the road Graphics card.

Absolutely.The game is like Zelda: BOTW made by minimum-wage employees. There are puzzles, but they aren't fun and repeat themselves all the time. There is dynamic combat, but target switching is the worst, enemies are damage sponges, and most of the skills are useless. There is an open world, yet there is no exploration - you just mark objectives on your map and navigate to them afterward. There are several layers of leveling systems, yet nothing excites you about leveling up - you just kill damage sponges faster.The story is not bad, and the humor is... Well, it's there, but basically, the story of the game is a big Manzai of Zeus (who plays "funny" (a.k.a. cringe) man) and Prometheus (who plays the straight man). It can be really funny sometimes, but most of the time, it's just mediocre stand-up. There are also other guys, but in their cases, it's even worse...Overall, I would give the game 6/10. It could have been around 7.5/10 if the game were shorter and more focused, but I just felt really, really tired at the end. Maybe worth checking out, but that's it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was approaching Fenyx Rising as a "typical Ubisoft game" or a "cartoonish Odyssey". Just finished it, and I find this statement so unfair - this is really an underrated, hidden gem.Narrative approach is clever and well-executed. The plot itself is surprisingly good. Light, but never trivial, and underneath the goofy vibes and horny jokes (which totally make sense in the light of Greek mythology), it delivers a really nice story about family and identity.Exploration is extra fun. Using "eagle vision" to mark places of interest can quickly turn the game into a boring to-do list, but you can spot most of interesting things from afar on your own, so you don't need to rely on it. And this made it one of my most enjoyable exploration experiences in recent years.Combat is really fun and smooth. Seems very simple at first, but has some surprising depth and it's very satisfying and engaging.Puzzles are great! Built on simple ideas, but impressively creative. Perfectly balanced for a relaxing game - not too easy, and never too hard to get you stuck for hours. Art style and graphics are fantastic. For some reason, trailers and screenshots don’t do it justice - the game looks much better in motion and avoids feeling overly “sweet”. Traversing a deserted kingdom on horseback, exploring colossal temples and castles with silhoutes of tormented ghosts haunting the land, brings to mind... Elden Ring. The soundtrack is also surprisingly amazing! Perfectly complements the atmoshpere and themes of the game, and fits its relaxing aura.Towards the end, looks like I've got only praises to give, and most of them are "surprising". And yeah, honestly Fenyx deserves them. Everything it tries to do, it does great, or at least very solid. It might be partly because it isn't the type of game I usually play, and I haven't played Breath of the Wild, which apparently Fenyx is a clone of, but it's easily one of the best games I played this year. It's not revolutionary in any way, but delivers something special, really stands out from other titles and I love it. Big thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising looked neat and I have heard great things, so I decided to pick it up. Unfortunately, It’s a pretty mediocre game. It is clearly inspired by Nintendo’s Breath of the Wild, but they made the smart decision to not make weapons break, which is nice to see.To start with the good, the combat is fun. It’s relatively simple, but it’s fun. You got a light and heavy attack, a bow attack, and a doge. The doge slows time if timed right, which is not anything original, but it works well and it’s fun. Enemies can feel pretty tanky at times, but you can upgrade your weapons and gear using a very confusing system that has something like 10 different currencies.The game is filled with puzzles. They are not the hardest puzzles, but I enjoyed doing many of them. The story is comedic, which I liked, but I do not find it particularly interesting or engaging. The world and graphics look good and the game runs well enough, although not what I would call great. You can explore the world, which is interesting enough, but you can also just use your magic telescope that has a very far range and sees through walls to see where the loot is, but is pretty finicky to use. The game would have been better if they did not have that and maybe made loot areas more visible from a distance, or if they just went the normal approach and showed you everything when you were nearby.The controls feel like they could have used an extra bit of polish, mainly in the gliding and climbing.There are no Steam achievements for some reason, which is really annoying, especially since it has achievements on console, but not a deal breaker for me. Cloud saves and controller support are broken, which is annoying, but this is not really a controller game, so lack of controller support does not bother me. Cloud saves not working does. They’ve chosen to use some Ubisoft system, which errors every single time, instead of just using Steam Cloud which works perfect 99.99% of the time.Every time you open the game, it spends several minutes verifying that you own that game, which is very annoying and really makes me not want to even open the game, especially when it isn’t anything amazing. The main menu greets you with a cash shop where you can buy items. I did not look too carefully, but they looked to only be cosmetics. Not the worst thing in the world, but still very annoying to see in any game, especially a game it has absolutely no place being in, like a full priced single player only game.Immortals Fenyx Rising is not good, it's not bad, it’s just mediocre. It’s a decent way to pass some time, but nothing about it makes me want to open it, so I end up playing other, better, games.

_childDocuments_.review: I played through Immortals Fenyx Rising on console and had a pretty good time! There's a lot of reviews about how the game crashes. And there's been some developer responses, which is super cool! I didn't play a ton, but did experience one crash. Otherwise, the game ran great. The comparisons to Zelda: Breath of the Wild are totally fair. But I do think Immortals Fenyx Rising has it's own personality and style. It's clear that a lot of care and thought went into the game. There are A TON of puzzles. So many of the points of interests involve solving some kind of puzzle. If you enjoy puzzles, this is fantastic. If you're like me and typically lean on guides to get through puzzles, just be cognizant that you're likely to be looking at guides quite often. Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys exploration, puzzles, Greek mythology, or open-world games. ⚡

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of content, lots of world to explore, lots of rewards to find, though some of them are just visual upgrades and don't change your gear stats. If you're a completionist, there's plenty here to grind on, though that's not necessary to complete the game. You can just focus on the main quests. There are aspects of this game I appreciate the relative simplicity of, versus other games. For example, there is no durability system to weapons. Once you have a new weapon, it won't break, and you have it forever, thankfully. There are lots of ability upgrades, based on collectible items. There are also a lot of potion upgrades based on brewing, but mercifully no complicated recipes. The game simply tells you if an upgrade is available based on what's in your inventory. Most of the NPCs are baddies, so the world and the story does feel a bit sparse. There are however, many nods to Greek mythology, with the less family friendly parts alluded to subtly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is actually pretty fun and if you get it on discount like me its a great value proposition. I could make a list of Pros and Cons, but the TLDR is that while noticeably flawed, it's a genuinely fun game to play.I'm still downvoting this on general principle for its completely insane technical state, this is the first game in like the last 10 years that genuinely manages to crash my entire system, forcing me to outright *powercycle* my PC. It happens regularly when I close the game and if this isn't something related to Ubisoft's dumpster fire of a launcher, I'm eating my left shoe.EDIT after 20 hours:Yeah, while the game showed significant promise in the beginning, it gets really monotonous rather quickly and the bosses are giant letdowns (the main story boss and the superboss of Aphrodite's area are literally just the same reskinned harpy creep).The vaults also become boring rather quickly and they fail to bring anything truly surprising or interesting to the table like in BotW/TotK. Fighting also becomes boring due a merely decent (not bad by any means but nothing to write home out) combat system combined with bosses that are both from a moveset and visual perspective nothing special.After 20 hours I'm kind of bored and the only nice thing I have to say is that the game is genuinely funny a lot of the times.If you really want to play this game, I'd advise you to skip all the open world side stuff and just beeline the quests (which is honestly a pretty brutal thing to say about a BotW clone or open world game in general).

_childDocuments_.review: Clash of the Titans meets Titan Quest meets Cartoons meets Adult films meets God of War meets Devil May Cry... pretty much sums up the game. Visual - simple but very nice and very romantic atmosphere throughout whole game, made a lot of screenshots, really nice art design, eyecandy. Story - solid, despite the known Greek mythology it was about the family and really impactful in some way - shows real world problems in fairy tale adaptation, sometimes I was touched as themes as betrayal, rejection, depression, hopelessness, low self-esteem, no success etc occured. Really recommend the game for adult audience, game is not really suitable for kids despite the visual. Dialogues - between Prometheus and Zeus its interesting how they comment every action in the game, so it feels like narration is alive whole time, you dont have the feeling of being only watching main hero to progress but those characters too. But... whole game is insanely thirsty, its like writer/s were horny whole the time, other way I cant explain why this game has so much of double-meaning texts which I am not fan of, in my past life I was like that, but now its not that funny anymore, because they bring serious topics around it and I am not fan of adultery and betrayal of your spouse, its not funny and never should be taken lightly as it destroys too many lives. Gameplay - great gameplay, its fun to upgrade every time your char with powers, new tricks, never gets old, because if you do all side missions and collectibles you get better and more interesting equipment, there was always reward and game feels rewarding in terms of combat and combination of your suit/weapons, where you can be really overpowered as I was in the last 1/4 of the game, where I was really too strong and even boss fights were like 30 seconds to 1 minute speedrun shots. World - living world with enemies and animals, its all hostile but still you have sense of life and uncover something interesting. This game has really good approach as it offers variety of puzzles, mostly special tombs which are from beginning quite simple and bit of repetitive but after time they get more interesting and harder, but still nothing you cant beat after few tries. Platforming is solid, you can run, jump, climb with endurance meter and use horse/unicorn etc animals for quicker travel. Upgrades - it has some RPG elements, but its Action Adventure game in core, so yes you upgrade sword, axe, bow, armor, helmet and potions, but you dont have to be necessarily over the top to beat the game, yet, I wanted to be as strong as possible but still theres a plenty of room because I returned to game after more than month and didnt want to play it more, so I just quickly finished the game. Music - fine, sometimes good, sometimes not so special, moody. Replayability? - I would say yes, it has really catchy combat, fights are the best in the game and to me it never got old, as you upgrade over time fights are even more entertaining. Rating: Its game on its own from Ubisoft, Its epic action-adventure with really visually stunning world, would recommend if you are fan of greek mythology or epic adventure with fast paced hacknslash combat. TL;DR - Epic Action-Adventure with powers and upgrades where you kill monsters from greek mythology, got OP later, enemies got rekted.
