_childDocuments_.review: A bit like BOTW but not restricted to poor hardware. Overall a very chill, relaxing and fun experience aside for the second dlc. Beautiful world,  lots of humor, nice puzzles, and a fun enough fighting system, and it doesn't feel too big or long. Seems to be the exception for an Ubisoft game lately.  Lots of small drops of greek mythology by the narrators here and there is also nice !   Having played on Hard, it quickly became very easy once the small learning curve is passed and equipements and stats have been upgraded. Difficulty is clearly not the goal here.Though the humor is not for all ages, the game itself is very accessible for everyone.I really liked the artstyle, very pleasing to the eye. Some animations too are really funny, especially the cyclops.  Sounds design is good, and both the ambient and combat music are good enough too.  Oh and the story, is quite good. One of the main point here is how its told through the two narrators that you hear talk and banter during the whole game.  I wish there was more of it, and that there was more gods in the based game, that would have been even better, more greek gods drama !                                 Some bad points :  Far too many chests everywhere. And most of them only offer colour variation of armors or weapons. Once stats are maxed, you can keep grinding to go over the max which gives very smalls % benefits that aren't worth it except if you're a completionist. So skipping normal chest becomes usual once you have done 2 zones.Hermes taskboard also takes a bit to complete but to my surprise, completing all tasks doesn't give anything special. Some vaults or even locked chests have puzzles that are time based with very precise timings, which brings a bit of frustration.The last area, the mountain, is annoying to move around.About the DLCS : _A new god :  more and almost only puzzles, a bit more challenging than the base game but fun enough and worth it._Lost Gods :  the problematic one , isometric view that doesn't translate well for some things, far less story content, combat is far more difficult , too difficult at times because of other changes, which made it extremely frustrating. Which is too bad, the main _Myth of eastern realms : i'll skip this one for now,  since it is completely unrelated, maybe one day !

_childDocuments_.review: Game doesn't have native controller support, of any kind at all on Steam. Apparently the Ubisoft Connect version works fine with controller, but over here, the prompts remain to be KB/M. Tried it on Big Picture mode, with and without DualSenseX (as I'm using my DualSense for this), and myriad of other ways.Even if you look past the prompts being in KB/M, the game's sensitivity is built around mouse. And there's no controller option or prompt setting in-game, and sensitivity built around mouse doesn't translate well to a controller, so adjusting that won't bring you the same controller sensitivity feel that you'd normally get.Such a shame that Ubisoft would drop a ball like this for a game in 2022. One hand, glad that they're bringing back their games to Steam, on the other hand, can't support their mediocre measures for this game.Instant refund.Edit: if you disable PS controller support from Steam settings, and keep DualSenseX running, then your controller is picked up as DS4 in the game and it works fine then. But other than that, no native support for DualSense. Not sure what's the case for Xbox controllers on Steam, as others are reporting the same problem as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game would be so so so much better if it WAS a clone of Breath of the Wild. I honestly wish they had ripped Nintendo off completely, what they’ve scraped together here pales in comparison and fails in so many ways the newer Zelda games never could. It isn’t a carbon copy, it’s more like the scribbled notes of someone seeing Breath of the Wild played on a CRT through a crack in the door. They ripped the constant narration and bad "humor" from other annoying games, threw in some RPG-lite upgrading, stuffed the rest with a confused replication of the newest Zeldas’ mechanics, and set that all over an overdone, uninspired setting. Following the trend of most AAA games, it feels like nobody playtested this game at all, or someone would have mentioned that it does NOT feel good to play. The game is exceedingly clunky, every action has a full animation that has to play out every single time before any other action can even be attempted. There is a big delay from when you press a button in combat and when your character actually carries it out, and that also extends to gliding, climbing, platforming, puzzle solving, etc. There is no fluidity between actions like the newest Zelda games, if you press a button on your controller when your character is in one of the MANY animations for any little thing in the game, nothing will happen. This makes every action you take seem like you’re fighting the game to make happen, especially: climbing upwards, dropping from ledges, vaulting up ledges, opening/closing your glider, diving while gliding, sprinting at all, jumping combined with anything else, the list goes on. In another page out of Nintendo’s book: every chest, collectible, and puzzle has an unskippable animation, wasting hours of your life over the course of the game. Player upgrades in the hub also incur a lengthy, detestable cutscene each time, which incentivizes redeeming upgrades in batches to avoid watching it.You have no idea what a button in the world is going to do before pressing it, and a lot of the time even after pressing it you don’t know what it did. No blue lines connecting the switch to what it affects, no camera change to show what’s being powered or moved, and you definitely can’t see or hear the results of your actions in way too many cases. Any given door could have a puzzle to unlock it AND a button to unlock the puzzle, and both could be in completely different zip codes, with no way to tell what goes with what. Most of the puzzle solutions are trivially intuitive, the rest are oblique purely because you literally can’t see what you are supposed to do. It should go without saying that all of this is antithetic to good puzzle design.Luckily they give you two or three dozen ways to speed up traversal across the exceedingly large map. Unfortunate for us that they needed to. It would have been more than enough to make a smaller world packed with the same amount of filler (or less), but instead we have featureless landscapes to completely bypass in the sky, or by a mount that can’t jump, or fast traveling instead of seeing the world on the way to the actual playable content. A small, tightly designed world doesn’t align with “bigger number better”, so to our detriment we are stuck with this AAA status quo of an ever increasing map size. Not a surprise given the devs also worked on AC Odyssey, a poster child for map bloat. Combat is fairly simple, some strategies are better than others I guess but the system is so restrained you don’t have a choice but to fight enemies exactly how the devs decided you would. Generous windows for the dodge (and parry) and small enemy hurtboxes makes defense trivial, but not getting hit doesn’t shorten the high time-to-kill on these large health pools of some enemies. I’m not positive that combat actually gives you anything worth the time taken, maybe a few resources you are going to get from the mandatory combat or open world anyway. Which means that you are best off avoiding combat entirely when you can help it, and you certainly can. There’s also a suspicious amount of input reading, enemies will stand passively with you and attack only after you do. Doesn’t make the game difficult, just annoying.And that wraps up all of the traditional gameplay pillars, with not a single one done half as well as this game’s obvious sources of inspiration. I saw a post somewhere saying that the best way to play the game would be to NOT tag all the points of interest from the synchronize points, and to instead discover everything naturally while on your way to the next quest marker. That honestly makes sense, it’s less like a list of tasks to work down and more like you’re actually exploring the world, and that’s how BOTW worked. Unfortunately, nothing you come across is actually fun enough for that to be worth doing, so I can’t recommend playing this game like that or at all. Also, they added this cool mechanic that causes a “local” (mapwide) debuff after you do some very low number of objectives (sometimes none at all). As if you needed another reason to NOT play the game, they’ve included a deterrent built right in.

_childDocuments_.review: I had never even heard of this game and my brother gave it to me as a gift because he felt I would like it after we had a discussion about games.  Boy was he right.The way I would describe this game is that is Breath of the Wild meets Assassin's Creed Odyssey.  The inspiration from Odyssey is in a lot of the design of the buildings which made me smile every time I came across something that made me think of Odyssey since it has to be my favorite Assassin's Creed game of all time mostly because of the Greek Mythology aspect.  The BotW inspiration is ALL over this game but while I always felt BoTW felt empty, this game does not feel empty at all.Enter Immortals Fenyx Rising.The story is fun.  The characters are interesting.  Exploring the world is fantastic and you never know what you are going to find over the next hill or at the bottom of a cliff or under water.  I like the mount system and how easy it is to catch the various mounts all over the world.  It isn't time consuming at all and you can have as many mounts as you want and switch them out any time.The puzzle aspects are great.  Sometimes it takes a bit to figure it out but nothing is too terribly difficult or time consuming.The variety of enemies is quite nice and the skills and powers you pick up along the way become quite helpful in ways I didn't quite expect.The myth challenges are fun.  The only one I am not really a fan of yet (mostly because I have been avoiding them) are the navigating challenges.  I can be quite clumsy with my gliding/wing usage.My only real complaint about this game is that (and this only happens to me with Ubuisoft games)  sometimes when I quit the game, it is still running in the background and trying to stop it can be a real pain in the butt and in most cases requires a reboot of my system.  But considering just how much fun I am having playing it?  I will deal with that minor annoyance and just enjoy the hell  out of this title.  I see many many more hours of game play ahead and I am very much looking forward to it.  As for you, the one reading this review, give the game a try if you like snarky commentary and fun stories with a lot of time spent in a rather cool world based in Greek Mythology.

_childDocuments_.review: I had great fun playing this game. The art style is beautiful and the combat fun. I loved exploring and solving the puzzles that are dotted everywhere. Yes, this game has the typical Ubisoft symptom of dotting the landscape with icons but, personally, I don't mind it. I think it's done better here than in most of their other games. The mini puzzles that need to be solved give a great sense of reward as some require careful observation of the environment to figure out.I also loved the vaults and the levels of puzzles they presented. There are some mild frustrations with some of them where a whole section needs to be restarted to try again after a failed attempt, which can get tedious. Overall, the vaults are brilliant in engaging the player with some longer, more complex puzzles as presented on the Golden Isle.As mentioned, combat is fun, flashy, and satisfyingly responsive. The story is pretty well done and the writing is very competent as well, with many parts having me genuinely chuckle -- rare for the video game format.I will say though, the climbing feels incredibly slow... Knowing that this same engine is used for the latest Assassin's Creed games where climbing is fast and fluid, it makes no sense. Yea, maybe they want to limit it more to fit in with the stamina system but, later in the game, when you can have loads of stamina, climbing is just tedious and I found myself avoiding it when possible. It's usually quicker going around a tall climb, than actually climbing it. Maybe that was the intention.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever want to play The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild but you don’t own the necessary Nintendo console? Ubisoft got you covered.The story: The game has actually two stories. One is Zeus seeking help against the monstrous Typhon and Prometheus starts to tell him the story of Fenyx, a shield-bearer who tries to lift the curse of the petrified humans and step out of the shadow of her heroic brother. To do so she needs to restore the Olympian gods to their former glory.  While Fenyx story is more serious Prometheus and Zeus act as light-hearted commentators, often pointing out what kind of horrible father Zeus is and what terrible stuff the Greek gods did according to mythology.The gameplay:  It is a mix of combat, exploration an riddles. Each activity gives you different kind of materials to increase your health, stamina, upgrade your skills or your equipment. Each part neatly meshes into the others. Combat is surprisingly fun. Try to keep you combat multiplier high by skilful evade enemy attacks. The game also offers a new game plus mode which lets you upgrade your character further.The graphic: Vivid colours and lush landscapes, especially in Aphrodite’s domain.  Plus Fenyx, who is canonical female, looks like she is right out of Disney’s latest animated movie. I was seriously waiting for her to turn out to be a princess.The problems: Boy, where to start? There are a lot of small things and feels it like bad management decisions are to blame:Personally I think all the negative reviews here don’t do the game justice and are more due to the rejection of Ubisoft.

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to premise this review that I usually don't play games that involve puzzles as an integral part of the gameplay, but Immortals Fenyx Rising made every moment enjoyable. Thanks to my time in Assassin's creed games, the control layout was familiar, though it took some doing for me to master the moves necessary to win consistently. What can I say, it seemed straightforward enough, though the interplay between Prometheus and Zeus was absolutely hilarious. Few games have made me chuckle and laugh out loud this many times. The idea that the old Titan Typhon has ripped the gods from their essences and it was your job to restore them was a really fun concept to me. _childDocuments_.review: I will help this game out a bit because it honestly deserves more love. I picked it up upon completing Assassin's Creed Odyssey. Devs took a lot of inspiration from AC series and BOTW Zelda, there's no doubt about it. As to why you SHOULD give it a go despite a lot of people complaining about Ubisoft Connect... read below.- BAD: If you want to play Ubi games, you have to install their official Ubisoft Connect app. I've had UPlay then Ubisoft Connect since Assassin's Creed IV Black Flag, and it's something that you need to launch in order to play the game online. Yes, it's not always reliable and takes forever to open - but it NEVER crashed my games or made them unplayable in any way. The more Ubi games you play, the less of a big deal it becomes, because you automatically launch it and don't really think about it.- The GOOD thing about it however, is that the app has a Rewards system, which means that through completing weekly challenges (that are optional) you end up earning credits on the Connect app, which then can be exchanged for cosmetic DLCs such as Legendary/Epic skins in game, weapons, mounts, armour, sometimes additional missions in game, etc. Ubisoft Connect offers you free adds-on as well.To sum it up: Yes, installing extra apps is annoying, but no, it shouldn't ruin the gaming experience in overall.(Based on over 100 hours of gameplay accumulated on Epic Games and Steam together - finished the game and replaying it for the 2nd time)+ Combat is easy to learn, lots of combos to master, different weapons to choose from, different modes of difficulty meaning that you can enjoy the story and explore the world at your own pace or go hardcore and choose to die to everything that moves.+ Soundtrack is fantastic. Period.+ All the characters are likeable, and may I say that Zeus who co-narrates everything in the game... is so cringe that it's so good. He throws around dad jokes at every opportunity, and a lot of them hint at the Greek mythology and how he screwed everyone over. I mean, there are moments when I just want to quit the game because of that fella. But he still cracks me up in a good way.+ The humour may not be everyone's cup of tea, but the whole game feels like a joke at times, and it's not meant to be taken seriously. There are a lot of memes and references to other media as well.+ The world is filled with Vaults of Tartaros which are basically domains of varied difficulty, that include mini boss fights, a lot of platforming, and tons of puzzles to solve. I personally love those, because they are the most rewarding part of the game.+ Completing Daily challenges awards you with weapon skins and materials used for ascention; Weekly challenges give you coins that you can use as in-game currency to buy cosmetic DLCs (microtransactions). That means that you can either pull out your wallet, sit back and enjoy sets of skins OR put in some effort, grind for the coins and then exchange them for the same items for FREE (mind you that in the second case, those skins appear in the game randomly and you may need to wait for them a bit longer). - strictly technical issues. The game itself is fine.- Controllers are not supported for this game for some reason. Whilst a lot of people prefer a keyboard/mouse, I am not one of those people and to make it even worse, I use a PlayStation controller. Because yes, I like Sony more.Thankfully, Steam offers controller support so all you have to do is choose which layout you want to use for the game, and just play. Ubisoft, git gud.- No Steam Achievements. I mean, come on u guys. You gave us achievements for Origins and Odyssey then you just gave up. We Gamers like to collect those on Steam. Don't ask why, we just do. So please copy pasta them from your app to Steam. Make your fans happy again.- The game is very resource pack heavy. It can lag even on low graphic settings. But I will blame it on my old potato PC and partly on the game being POORLY optimised.- Ubisoft Connect throwing a tantrum every now and then asking me 1000 times to log in then not recognising my password and repeat. I once tried to log on too many times in a row and my account got locked. Upon contacting Ubisoft customer support I was told that I have to wait 24 hours to log in again. It could always get worse than this, right? :)The game is 90% off on sale now, so grab it and give it a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: The game-play is great! The combat is fun and exciting at first and slowly becomes a chore. The game throws the same 4-5 enemies at you with more and more health as you progress through the game. When you do find a new enemy, it becomes common around the world and merges with the others. When killing enemies, it gives you bare-minimum and sometimes no rewards.The first few hours of the game are magical! I had so much fun exploring Vaults and other activities around the map. Exploration rewards you with chests and some underwhelming gear but it gives you some reasons to explore. Again, after a while, they lose their charm and become a drawn out mechanic. They add very little differences between points of interests (POI) and Vaults, eventually the puzzles become time wasters.The story is a great idea but it does not live up to it. The characters are weak and act dumb. The first hour of the game made me question if the main character knew anything. The gods all act the same and are somewhat boring. They are cowards and are depressed with nothing to live for, but the main character comes in and saves the day with pitiful cheer-me-ups. However, the gods aren't themselves and that does make it entertaining. The game is told like a story with narration over it. It is a fantastic way to tell the story. It has funny lines and the voice actors for the narrators are the best in the game. Overall, the story is really intriguing and had fun comedic moments, but it was executed poorly.A few things I want to congratulate the game on are: narration, skip-ables, and humor.One of the best parts of the game is the narration! The game benefits a lot from  (Names of people talking) talking over the gameplay. They have fun jokes and they sound like best buds. They also have great tone's for different events, unlike every other character that is the same bland monotone conversation. The narration makes me stop my music to listen to every word they say.This game lets you skip every cut-scene! Story cut-scene or minor animations. It is amazing. I personally have not skipped any story cut-scene but I have skipped a lot of the boring repeated animations. Very very nice feature.The humor in the game is safe enough for most children but also hides adult humor in it! With these little additions, it makes it more fun! It made me laugh some and smile and it did not go farther than any modern PG13 film. I can only recall it saying "badass" once.A few game play mechanics I want to complain about are: far-sight, stamina, enemy attacks, and treasures. This mechanic sucks. It is a "mini-game" of sorts that makes you find all the objectives around the map. You have to look at each objective, press E and then it will show up on the map. This is terrible. There is no information on how many you can see, the indicator only shows when you are an inch or so from it, and this is the worst part of the game. Massive time waster.This game is a clone of Breath of the Wild (BOTW), no doubt, with its copying of stamina and game play. This is awesome! I really wanted a game like BOTW on PC. But the stamina in this game is a burden to play with. If I am in combat, I think it is fair to enforce the stamina drain on every action but this game forces it on you throughout the whole game. Carrying an object stops all stamina regain, unless your not moving, and slows the pacing of all the puzzles and tedious work already in the game.Some enemy attacks are truly unfair. The combat in this game is simple: block/roll then attack. The fighting is easy and not difficult, but there are moments in this game where a projectile will change on a dime and hit you or a enemy is not facing you but instant turns to attack you with an unshockable attack. It is unfair and happens every couple fights. Not a big issue but it is there.This game is fun! I really enjoyed it (still have the ending to do, but wanted to write this before hand). I have never heard about this game and luckily saw it on the day of release. I picked it up for $15 and I really enjoyed it. If you want BOTW on PC, this is a great game for it! It took me the whole game to get invested, still a little withdrawn, but I am happy with the experience I had with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let's get the obvious out of the way.  This is an unabashed, shameless rip-off of Breath of the Wild in every conceivable way.  However, it's not a cheap rip-off.  A lot of time and effort went in to developing what makes this game good, and for that reason I can recommend it.  There are a few things holding back from being a fantastic game, though.First off, the combat is satisfying, with some cool combos and fun weapons.  Also, the world is detailed, the models are diverse, the assets unique, and the animations are very well done.  Those at the grunt level tasked with bringing this game to life took great care to make it high quality, and it shows.  It definitely looks like a AAA game. The problem I have, is it often feels more like the production of a corporation capitalizing on a popular game than a project lovingly crafted by passionate developers.  What do I mean by this?Well, it's obvious that a lot of elements of this game were designed by committee and doled out to various programming departments who probably didn't communicate with each other.  My foremost example of this is one of the earliest labyrinths.  It is designed to teach you how to use your newfound magnesis, err, I mean, godly power that lets you pick up objects and manipulate them from a distance.  The person who designed this particular labyrinth apparently didn't collaborate with the the overworld designer, because the puzzle in the overworld you need to solve to access the labyrinth is the exact same puzzle that's in the labyrinth, but without any tutorial.  So, by the time you get to the official tutorial inside the labyrinth you've already had to figure out how to use the powers by yourself and now it's almost laughable that the tutorial was placed here.There's a lot of having to figure out stuff yourself, too.  They drop powers on you without even telling you have them, much less how to use them.  Sure, there's a tutorial screen you scroll through, but I found myself spending a lot of time and even Google searches on how to do the most basic things.  How was I supposed to know that as soon as I got the bow I could remote control my arrows like they were some kind of drone?  Took me way too long to solve that puzzle.Anyway, I wanna get back to that overworld I mentioned in passing a moment ago.  It's detailed and brought to life with extreme precision and care, but it seems more like a collection of evenly dispersed locations stuffed chalk-full of random items.  Most of the time, it doesn't seem designed to fill you with wonder or the desire to explore, it's simply designed to keep you occupied.  The most egregious example of this is climbing up high to get an overview of the land.  Instead of getting excited about the places you might be able to visit from your breathtaking vista, you're invited to scan the entire area with a tool and muck up the horizon in every direction with decals of where each power-up and pick-up item you can find is located.  It undermines the desire to explore and turns travel into an exercise involving an itemized checklist.  It has every mark of corporate game design all over it.  This is a shame, too, because the overworld is beautifully crafted and the locations a delight to look upon, and this game could have easily become so much more with the correct vision and guidance.But, there are advantages that come with big corporate game design, and that's deep pocket books to bank roll things like 100% voice acting for most of the characters.  And to be sure, the voice acting is top notch, all the actors did a fantastic job.  Unfortunately, I found the writing pretty bad, the story bland and uninteresting, with no personal stake for the main character.  Because of this, most of the cut scenes seemed filled with unnecessary and sometimes cringy dialogue, redundant information, or without a lot of direction or purpose.All that being said, though, they did copy one of the greatest games of all time, and not only did they do a good job in copying someone else's homework, they added a lot of fun things to the mix.  Perhaps, if Breath of the Wild didn't exist, I might think of this as a fantastic game.  But after seeing what a truly great game can do with a better version of its idea, Fenyx falls  short of achieving the same level of greatness, but it's definitely worth the full $15 I paid for it on sale.  I'd probably even pay more.

_childDocuments_.review: Think of Assassins' Creed Odyssey, make it with cartoon graphics, lower the age of the MC and make the whole game more playful and less engaged, remove the part of the murders and add a lot of puzzles for which you need to know how to reason, enemies worthy of a fantasy game, five Greek gods plus a villain as evil and arrogant as he is too sure of himself,  a lot of skill tests, a lot of activities that serve to lengthen the game but that give you little in terms of character growth, a lot of grinding and you will have an idea of what this game is.First, I clarify that I had fun playing it, but Ubisoft continues to churn out titles that take too long. It is not true that 80 hours of play are better than 50 or 30, we must not confuse longevity with the ability of a game to entertain. A game should not last as long as possible, but just enough to not become too boring.That said, if you want to do everything you can go beyond 100 hours, at some point I decided I had reached the limit and I aimed to finish it.The fights are not challenging, they are all easy... And I repeat all of them, even the bosses are too easy to be defeated. The only thing that can push you to do everything is puzzles and skill tests, but you must be good at these things.

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising is on sale right now for $8 and for that price it's a no-brainer.  Imagine a recent Zelda game done in the Ubisoft way and this is what you're imagining.  The voice acting and writing here are just fantastic.  I don't want to oversell it and have you be disappointed, but honestly it's the most entertained I've been by the dialogue and narration in a game... maybe ever?  I certainly can't think of anything else that made me chuckle so often.  The constant banter between Zeus and Prometheus is worth the price of admission all by itself.  Combat in the game is quick and responsive, and just feels good.  The difficulty options make it easy to decide if you're just playing for fun or if you want a challenge.  Puzzles are about like you'd expect from a Zelda-style game, not too challenging but fun enough.  The open world is very pretty and exploration is constantly rewarded.  Honestly, there's nothing here to dislike.  I bought it at full price and I have no regrets, so when it's on sale you should not pass it up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not good. I tried to give it a chance, but the uncanny valley graphics that were meant for Xbox 360 Civilization advisors kills all I can even attempt to put into this game. Everything looks like it was made with free assets off of the unity store. Most enemies are obnoxiously boring sponges that you chip damage off of until you fall asleep. The dialogue is peak millenial writing, with every single character being a quirky little fellow that has something very funny to say! Hey Zeus, Typhon gave me some epic odyssian zaza! Etc, just garbage dialogue meant to get likes on Twitter. None of the characters feel like they give a ♥♥♥♥, instead everyone is in on this "hilarious" meta view of this world. Like I'm going to fall over laughing at the truly gutbusting lines of Zeus and Prometheus exchanging witty quips about what they're smoking and how they need to get back into shape. Instead, I'm going to cringe in disgust as I turn off the game and uninstall permanently.It's really like the creators of AC Odyssey were like "Hey Ubisoft, we'd like to make the last game but with more fantasy elements." And the Ubisoft corporate guys gave them a budget of $500,000 instead of the 500 million for the last game. Everything feels cheap, the UI feels like an embarrassing mobile game, and the dialogue/story is so mind numbing I just turned it off during the middle of a cutscene. Ultimately, this is a game devoid of passion and creativity. To me, this game perfectly represents everything that is horrid about the game industry in it's current stage. Please, devs, ubisoft, whoever was truly responsible for this waste of time and space, look to games like God of War or even your last game Odyssey for inspiration. Stop making this bloatware trash just to fit in with the rest of the industry. You can do better.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 - It's good if you get it on significant sale, I paid $15 and I'm okay with that price for what I got. Biggest Pro - The combat is pretty fun once you get the timing and your fingers get used to the control scheme, the weapons are interesting and they upgrade in an interesting way.Biggest Con - It is an ambitious BotW-inspired exploration and collection game design that heavily leans on Metroidvania concepts of unlocking movement skills to gatekeep content and upgrades... implemented with poorly-configured camera algorithms and frustratingly sloppy movement controls.EDIT: What other people say about the game being designed purely according to what marketing department felt would maximize profits (this is Ubisoft after all) and built by incredibly bad (cheap?) coders is true.  Be prepared for random crashes but also signs revealing the pure stupidity of the devs such as sound randomly not working at all until you restart the game a couple times.  Again, get it on sale and hope that it works for you, but refund at the very first sign of problems.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to respond to some of the things I have seen in recent reviews that I do not feel are entirely accurate. 1. Comparisons to BOTW: Aside from the obvious visual style they are not even remotely similar.  This game actually descends from Assassin's Creed Odyssey and it shares many game mechanics with that game.  2. Voice Acting: the acting in this game is of the same quality of any ubisoft game and is exactly what I would expect.  Depending on your perspective that could be good/bad/Neutral.  Personally I don't mind it at all, it's pretty good for what it is.  3. Humor: The dialog and narration in this game are pretty funny.  Yes they are campy but they are supposed to be.  This game will not replace a recording of George Carlin on stage, But it's not supposed to.   It's exactly as funny as it needs to be.  Stop taking everything so seriously.  4. Ubisoft - Connect : Every Ubisoft game requires you to run their software and have an account.  This game is no exception.  Why is that a surprise to some people ?  I don't like it, it's entirely stupid and serves to do nothing but irritate paying customers and make them not want to buy Ubisoft titles in the future.  Blame Ubisoft for their stupid anti-consumer practices if you want to but it has nothing what so ever to do with this game specifically.  5. Controller support - I read a review from this month saying that Controller Support was completely broken.  That simply isn't true, it works just fine for me.  I used my Guillikit Bluetooth Controller from the first time I fired up the game and it's been flawless.  6. Too much content/takes too long to finish -  Seriously ?  Shut the hell up and go play asteroids, your opinion is invalid.  7.  Crashes : I ran into a situation where I was crashing over and over at the same area of the map.  I traced it back to the nvidia driver crashing (I was using the latest "Game Ready" driver.)  I removed it and installed the "Studio Driver" instead which is slightly older and according to nvidia more stable.  I haven't had a crash since.  Don't know who to blame for the crashing but the driver I was using just came out a week ago and the devs obviously could not have tested the game with that driver and using an older one did fix the issue.  I expect that it's a bug that will be resolved sooner or later.  I did send in several crash reports to help with that.   I'll continue to update this review as I make my way through the game, so far it's been a blast!

_childDocuments_.review: It's your typical Ubisoft game. Massive open world full of pointless busy work only now it's combined with the annoyance of the stupid puzzles from the last couple of Zelda games.Stamina is a big deal as you need it for attacks, swimming, jumping, gliding etc. How do you level your stamina? You have to do these 'rifts' (think Zelda temples only more annoying) full of jumping, gliding, moving blocks and shooting puzzles. Then you get a 'lightning bolt of Zeus' at the end. The fun part is each stamina bar requires multiple bolts to upgrade on an ever increasing scale.The jumping puzzles would only rate as annoying if the keyboard controls weren't utter dog sh*te. Want to double jump? Yeah, good luck with the game responding to you on a very random basis. This makes the jumping crap utterly frustrating at times. The same can be said for the dodging controls....one option is a double tap of the direction button but the game just fails to respond to this on a regular basis making those 'flashing red attacks' unavoidable. (It is NOT my KB as both by corsair and razor KB get the same results).Want to upgrade your weapons to d a bit more damage? Yeah, you need red and blue crystals. Blue are fairly easy to get by killing mobs or opening chests. The red come from specific types of chests and the very rare outcropping in the overworld. But you need LOADS of the damn things and the upgrades just feel so MEH....it might turn a 30 shot enemy into a 25 shot one......Want to open the map up? Climb a statue and gave from the top with a 'vision' setting that allows you to scan the map pixel by pixel to highlight points of interest. It's just another innovation free Ubisoft radio tower..WARNING FOR HIGH END CPU USERS:: The game starts with an unlocked frame rate. Your CPU WILL say "hold my beer!" and boost itself to maximum frequency to see how many FPS it can achieve. mY I7 13700kf PEAKED AT 260FPS before I realised and limited the fps to that of my monitor in the game settings. No CPUs were harmed but lets just say i didn't need a kettle to make my coffee even with very good water cooling!I am 22.7 hrs in as of writing and am on the verge of giving up because its just a boring grind with no positive outcome.I loath the jumping puzzles and the combat is just about average thanks to the iffy key press recognition.If you want to try it i'd recommend waiting for a deep, deep sale!PS Every start up requires it to 'check for additional content, and the start screen constantly pushed the Ubisoft store..... (cosmetics only I believe but still....)

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked BotW, this is pretty similar, but the Mythological aspect gives it originality and uniqueness. The combat system is cool, although it's not that deep and it could reach the point of just smash a button and use potions. The dialogs are pretty well done, although they might get a little crigey from time to time, but it's nothing too bad. What I liked the best was the landscapes and the visual style, it's very lush and colorful, it makes you want to keep exploring.The campain is short and 100% doesn't take that long (around 50-60 hours). The difficulty isn't a big deal, I played on hard and it wasn't. I didn't try the next one because the description sounded like just spamming more attacks. I'm currently playing the DLCs and they seem quite long, with lots of stuff to do. I liked how they created a new Asian map and changed just enough to seamlessly go from Greece to China. A solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has way more negative reviews than it deserves because it requires Ubisoft Connect. And yea, that can be a real struggle to deal with.You can find instructions and guides to how to play without Ubisoft Connect though, and I recommend looking into that, if you struggle with Ubisoft.The game itself is great though, and it really is a shame that reviews don't make that clear. I have this on Switch and played it there for 90 hours when it first came out, and now am replaying it here.The world is big and colorful, though exploring it is nothing super original for someone used to open world games. You can choose your difficulty, so it can offer quite a challenge, but is also very accessible.Controls feel pretty good to me, and I do love that you can climb and glide (after playing Botw every game that doesn't let me climb stuff is such a bummer).Where Immortals Fenyx rising really shines though is the storytelling. Not necessarily the plot, but the narration and the humor. I often tend to skip cutscenes and not pay attention when narrators in game explain things, but in this game every word was a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, I spent 41 hours on this game, so it was absolutely fine.The good: - "cartoonish" graphics are usually a plus for me- Neat movement for traversal imo (for the most part, see the nitpicks)- combat is fast paced and mostly fun- massive collect-a-thon world- The constant dialogue between Zeus and Prometheus was enjoyable for the most parts. I also do enjoy greek mythology overall, so it was nice to listen to.The bad:- Now, I'm not here for the challenge too much in this case. But I played the latter half of the game on nightmare, the highest difficulty. I expected *some* amount of challenge, but the final boss battles only required roughly 4 health potions (and 1-2 attack/def potion). For reference, you have 20 of each in the end-game.- After you get off "tutorial island", you unlock 3 dlc-preview quests. Although the game doesn't tell you this until you're inside one of them, and they look identical to other main story quests. While they give you a predetermined "loadout" of powers, potions etc, they still expect you to do them towards the end of your gameplay. But one of them **is located in the tutorial zone**. 2 of the godly powers can be used for mobility purposes, but chances are you haven't acquired them in your playthrough yet, let alone have never had any reason to use them for mobility. So here the game is throwing one of the hardest "challenge runs" in the game at you with little warning. Just a tiny warning or something in the quest description would've helped a lot.- This might mainly be a keyboard issue, but the "godly powers", 2 of which are used for mobility, are always hidden behind at least 2 button presses: you have to hold down one key to bring up the menu, and then one extra button press to perform the action. With the default binds it makes sense: 1-4 is mapped to potions, and they're also used for godly powers. but even if you map them to something completely different that doesn't share a binding, you still have to hold the context button. When you're asked to chain 2+ godly powers in a row, *and* also have to use a stamina potion in the middle, it feels extremely clunky, and is easily messed up. There's no "stance" or anything tied in to holding the context button, you can instantly use it. So there's 0 reason to not allow it on PC.The nitpicky:- The way you reveal objectives on the map feels kinda "meh". You're supposed to use it from high up above, but there's no line of sight requirement or anything. So you can just awkwardly "scan" a wall until your cross-hair reacts and you can reveal something. I guess this is a band-aid fix due to some objectives being placed in caves/cliff walls where most people might not scan for stuff.- Small anti-frustration measures in "vaults" (Usually puzzle areas) would have gone a long way. Why does dying to a laser reset you waaay further back than if you'd died by falling off a cliff? (yes, even if you do not have the hp to "recover")- Inconsistencies in how godly powers interact with physics objects, namely spheres. The Dash + uppercut does absolutely 0 to a sphere, but the hammer sends it flying. This mechanic is used in a total of **two** vaults in the entire game, and I was stuck for 5+ minutes, because I only checked with the abilities I use often: uppercut and dash. These didn't affect the sphere, so I figured none of them did. - Small stuff like this crops up all over the place, where some things are granted pages in the tutorial pages, and some are even on-screen prompts. But mostly things are not explained. I'm fine with experimentation, but there's such a weird arbitrary line of what's described and what isn't.- Not being able to rotate "in place" while hovering. More than a few "deaths" took place due to that.- I didn't touch the real money shop, but I did browse the one where you could do "dailies" to get a currency to be spent on cosmetics. I genuinely do not get why there's a week long timer before it changes. Do they expect people to stick around in this game for more than like... 4 weeks, ever? I took a rather completionist approach, and did practically everything available in the "main land" (minus the 5th zone, was getting a bit same-y at this point). If I didn't, I could probably easily shave off 25 hours of my runtime. Despite my long lists of complaints, they are mostly nitpicks. Had a good time, that was somewhat interrupted by small frustrating moments, which does drag down the score a fair bit.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Immortals Fenyx Rising is an incredibly well made game, completely undone by the decisions made at the top level, and it is a shame.  IFR is an open world adventure taking place in ancient Greece, steeped in the lore of the Greek Gods.  Its cartoony graphics, and much of its gameplay seems inspired by mashing together traditional Ubisoft "climb the towers" open world traits, and Nintendo's Zelda Breath of the Wild.  That is a pretty solid combo!  The game looks fantastic and feels great, it is clear there were many talented people involved in making the game.  At the macro level, the problem with the game is that it can't decide what it wants to be, and in trying to be everything to everyone, completely loses its way.  This manifests in a number of ways, the first thing I noticed was how mixed up the narrative is.  The game is framed by a sequence between Zeus and Prometheus, where they are discussing you, the human that is their last hope, and your adventures.  As they speak about the adventures, you experience them in realtime, doing hero things and interacting with others characters.  There is a massive tone gulf between the two viewpoints.  The Zeus/Prometheus parts are written in that Pixar all ages sort of way, where it would be appropriate for a young person, but there are winks and jokes for the adults too.  It doesn't always hit the mark, but it is not terrible.  The writing in the parts you are actually experiencing is unbearable.  It is seemingly written for children, the dialog is utterly banal, and the tone is inexplicably goofy, even when dealing with deadly serious matters.  Every conversation with Hermes and the other Gods that you rescue is painful, and the vast majority of the attempts at humor fall completely flat.  It is a totally fine thing to make a game for children, only aimed at children, but based on both the Zeus parts, and the marketing for this game, I do not think that is Ubisofts intention, and if it was and was known, I would not have bought and played it.  Gameplay-wise, the game has tight controls and feels very good in both exploration and combat.  Again, taking its cues from Breath of the Wild, you can glide long distances over the open world, and climb most any surface, as long as you have enough stamina and stamina potions.  The game world manages to feel both overstuffed with tasks and empty and devoid of life at the same time.  The enemies just seem to be magically "there", they don't feel like they actually reside in the environments.  The tasks you complete are engaging at first but there are so many of them stuffed into the map that all of them eventually feel like a chore.  The combat is excellent, but by the time you are halfway through the game you have unlocked all your powers and moves, and have fought all the main enemy archetypes so much that combat becomes a slog as well.  It feels like the enemies, and especially the bosses, could have been more challenging and interesting, but were dialed back a bit to keep the game accessible to everyone.  There are Zelda-like shrines scattered throughout the map, some of them are combat arenas but most of the them are puzzle based.  They range from boring to miserable.  The worst offenders are the ones that try and use the physics engine in a BOTW-like way, and frankly, the game is just not made for it.  There was on puzzle where you have to hit a switch to make a spot on the ground spring up and send a large stone ball rolling over it up onto a ledge.  I tried to do it at least ten times and couldn't get it to get all the way up there.  It would get very close some of the times, and not close at all on others.  Eventually I got it by doing the exact same thing I had been doing the whole time.  That is unforgivably bad game design.  Many of the puzzles involve getting a box or a stone block, and getting it somewhere else without it breaking.  There is nothing enjoyable about them.  I stopped playing IFR at the 20-ish hour mark, I think I was 65-70% done with everything.  I had really enjoyed the first few hours of the game, but it got to the point where almost everything in the game felt like a chore and I couldn't stand it anymore.  I also want to note that the Ubisoft does a very poor job of releasing their games on Steam.  Not having Steam Achievements and not using Steams cloud infrastructure are terrible decisions, and forcing me to use Ubisoft Connect makes me want to avoid Ubisoft games in the future whenever possible.  3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Unironically the best Souls-lite Assassin's Creed game. It uses all the same gameplay mechanics as Odyssey but cuts out the pretenses and is just a good fantasy action game. The only thing it lacks is social gameplay, but the Souls-lite AC games sucked at that until Valhalla anyways.It has the same climbing and combat mechanics of the Souls-lite AC games, but a much better gear system that's more constrained where all gear is upgraded by type, such as upgrading all light weapons, all heavy weapons, or all bows with a single click. You don't have to manage too many resources or collect hundreds of items to unlock every cosmetic.And all the gear and cosmetic unlocks are tied to Vaults and heroic chests specifically, so you always know you're going to find a totally unique and new piece of gear in every vault, and that every heroic chest you find will give you a new cosmetic for your gear.The crafting/upgrade system is straightforwards and incentivises exploration, with all upgrade materials for skills, gear, and consumables being stuff you find in the open world. And you loot everything in a wide radius when you find it, so no need to pick up individual nectars or pomegranates, you can loot an entire patch in a single button press.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game, here are my final thoughts: The story is engaging, and Zeus's humorous commentary adds to the enjoyment. The combat system is well-developed and satisfying, and the puzzles, while occasionally challenging, provide a sense of accomplishment upon completion.One aspect I dislike is the platforming segments, which can be frustrating since some of them can be very hard. For those finding the platforming too challenging, I recommend skipping them and moving on to the next trial, challenge, or story element.Another drawback is the absence of Steam achievements, making me less motivated to clear the entire map and complete trials. Regarding bugs, I've hardly encountered any, even after completing the entire story.Overall, I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys puzzles and exploration. The game offers a lot of hours to finish, especially if you want to clear the entire map from chests, puzzles, and trials.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game to (almost) 100% on Stadia (RIP) and I REALLY liked it there - gorgeous world, solid combat, fun puzzles and exploration, nice itemization. It's *heavily* inspired by Breath of the Wild, but that's really not a bad thing here. Especially since it does away with a lot of the things that annoyed me in BotW, such as weapon durability and cumbersome crafting. I even liked the story - it's silly, yes, but at least I found it memorable; that's more than I can say about many other games these days.If you look at other reviews, you'll see two recurring complaints - that you have to use Ubisoft Connect and that each time you launch the game it spends a fair bit of time on "checking for additional game content", whatever that is. These are real problems and are indeed annoying, but overall the launcher thing is just a one-time setup, and the "checking" stage is 35 seconds - which is exactly 33 seconds too long for my taste, but I'm willing to wait that long once per session.As for downsides in the game itself, my main complaint is that it has a "survey" mode that allows you to detect (and mark) points of interest on the map, which really take away a lot of the fun inherent in the exploration. The game does a decent job of also making these points of interest visually distinct, though, so I highly recommend just never using the "survey" feature and instead relying only on pure exploration to find these points of interest. Yes, you'll probably miss a bunch of stuff, but you'll have much more fun exploring!Oh, and one more thing - while I really like this game, I don't recommend the DLCs at all. Stick with the awesome main game.
_childDocuments_.name: Immortals Fenyx Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Insofar Immortal Fenyx Rising feels like a chore, without the any kind of satisfaction that actual chores give you. It's an open world game with POI icons all over the place, you travel to them (mind-numbingly boring & time-wasting), do the (not particularly fun) activity at the location , get a miniscule amount of resource that you accumulate to get a miniscule upgrade, then you open the map and do it all over again.Shallow and basic, hit enemies and make numbers appear until they die, with occasional parrying/dodging. There doesn't seem to be any significant benefit to parrying as opposed to negating damage by just dodging, both just slows down time (unless the equipment has parry bonus damage). Dodging distance seems poorly implemented as it sometimes doesn't go far enough to escape attacks. All combat options(sword for quick, axe for heavy, bow for range) are given pretty early and does not evolve as you progress - thus it gets stale pretty quickly. Range attacks sucks, the guided arrows do most damage but also slows combat to a crawl. Your damage numbers also becomes ♥♥♥♥ very early in the game unless you go around doing time-wasting chores for upgrades, making enemies damage-sponges that makes boring combat last even longer.Exploration is slow, worse in the early game where stamina is limited, which not just limits sprinting but swimming and climbing distance. Later you might upgrade the stamina resource, but while spending stamina to sprint of boost glide does increase movement speed, it still takes too long to get to places - take into account how many ♥♥♥♥♥♥ POIs are marked around the map, a big chunk of your playtime is just slowly getting to places.The world is huge, and manages to feel pretty empty despite the ♥♥♥♥-ton of POI icons it litters all over the place. There's the usual open world game mechanic of climbing up a vantage point to reveal map and POIs, except in this one you have to manually identify each POI with your cursor, but 1)there's annoyingly far too many of them, 2) the identification ring isn't particularly sensitive enough, 3) most of the POIs aren't visually identifiable without the ring, thus you end up simulating a seizure and fast clicking to get as many of them out of the way as possible. I honestly groan every time I open up the map screen and see how many chore icons are on it. Quite a lot of the icons are just treasure chests or ambrosia, but I wouldn't exactly count travelling to chest or ambrosia to simply collect them "gameplay". Some of the collectibles might be locked behind puzzles/combat/platforming, but it isn't particularly engaging, as it seems to be made to be very accessible to children. Within the first few hours of the game, you would have seen a dozen iteration of box-on-button puzzles, which gets old really fast, made worse with how slow you are at pushing large boxes (in one case, pushing a dumb pearl long distance). Vaults similarly provide puzzle/combat/platforming challenges, just with a different upgrade resource at the end. Perhaps the reason the game gets old really quickly is that regardless whether you travelled to a treasure chest/ambrosia/vault POI, you're basically doing the same few activities. and always rewarded with 1/6th to 1/???th of an upgrade.I have never played Zelda:BOTW, but I have played Middle Earth: Shadow of War and I recommend that instead: it has the same tower vantage point to reveal POIs with cursor mechanic (which I didn't like then either) - except there's only 6-10 POIs instead of the dozens in Fenyx; combat's inifinitely better in depth and mechanics, as are the enemies (Nemesis system!); the upgrade tree is far more interesting, and the process of earning them is more fun/less of a chore; you can enslave orcs to your side; writing and graphics are also better...  I can't think of any aspect of Fenyx that is more appealing that Shadow of War, except if you want a more kid-friendly game (which it is), or enjoy listening to Zeus and Prometheus constantly bickering as narrators to the story, rather than hanging out with one grumpy elf-ghost.I would definitely refund this game if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: Very light hearted story around the Greek mythology, its gods and heroes. Decent amount of foes to pluck from their miserable life under the rule of Typhon, who drove the golden isle into the darkest of ages. Despite the criticism I actually enjoyed the visuals, the plot and the fighting. I also liked the easy to solve puzzles, which sometimes gave it a nice platformer touch.Sure, the dialogues are quirky, Fenyx is quite cheeky and the gods are as flawed as legends depict them. The open world approach with a myriad of tasks to solve and quite some grinding if you'd like to explore every inch of the playable area gives you a lot of freedom about what to tackle next.It's a fun adventure with some beautiful spots and locations to discover and explore. I loved the skill tree and developing Fenyx into an almost unstoppable force of god. Prometheus narrating the story to Zeus is hilarious in itself and made me chuckle more than I'd be ready to admit. The whole feels a bit as if Assassin's Creed, Tomb Raider and Super Mario had a crossover and I genuinely enjoyed the journey - and can therefore only recommend!Edit: Typos, many

Lo and behold, an update that addresses the crashing issue was quietly released a few months ago (nearly 3 years too late in my opinion), so I immediately updated to the latest version of my driver and the crashing issue is fixed!So, apart from that annoying little thing, I can truly say this game is amazing! People do like to compare this game to BOTW and accuses it of copying many of the elements. So, no, I haven't played BOTW, because I don't see the point in owning a Switch, so the only other reference I have that compares to this is AC Odyssey. _childDocuments_.review: Good art style. The crisp, vibrant greens and golden yellows really elevate the otherwise simple approach. The swaying tall grass, the cotton candy clouds, the glowing fruit in the trees, the galaxy in the night skybox. It's all great stuff and very pleasing to the eyes. It's easily the best part of the whole game.Unfortunately, it's all wasted on one of the most shamelessly derivative games ever conceived. Well, not conceived. Phrasing it that way implies it's the result of love and passion. More like manufactured in a factory. A factory that's clearly harmful to the environment. Ubisoft game releases are like watching security camera footage of a truck dumping hazardous chemicals into a freshwater stream.A cabal of soulless, faceless, nameless bean-counters who don't play video games and don't care about artistry or integrity or the industry at large, underpaying a team of regretful programmers and animators, making everything into a financial decision and training themselves to smile in an interview because that's what they've noticed real humans doing, are the kinds of people responsible for a game like this.There is not one single original idea in this game, and they were all done better in other games. I only played the first two islands, and there are maybe three or four more, I don't know for sure because I forgot to check before I Alt-F4'd out of the game, so maybe it gets better. Maybe things change dramatically and the combat gains some much needed depth, or maybe the characters stop being off-brand Illumination rejects, maybe the puzzles actually start requiring thought and aren't just pointless speed-bumps to a chest, but given the track record of a company like Ubisoft, it's far more likely that the game gets even worse.But hey, if it sounds like I'm being too hard on it, let me also mention that the entire game is narrated. The game is framed as a story that one person is telling another person. These two people will chat and joke and bicker at every single possible moment. Discover a "new" location, time for some chatter. Make progress in the "story," time for some chatter. It's so clear that this game was "designed" to be appealing to little tiny children. They are just so unfunny and uninteresting and they insert themselves constantly. Sometimes, just to say out loud the very thing you're watching happen. "Fenix reached out her hand..." I know that, I'm watching it happen! Games like this would have you think that something for children can't have merit or quality or be enjoyed by older gamers. But that's just yet another failing of the Ubisoft approach.Because this is Ubisoft, a game being made for children doesn't stop them from having a shop! In it, you can buy all sorts of cosmetics and useless junk. You can buy horse armor! Because even their micro-transactions have to borrow from better games.There was one moment when I heard an NPC say to another NPC "your weapon keeps breaking! Are you sure you're using it right?" Ubisoft making such unoriginal drivel, and using an electrified talking pile of garbage to make a jab at a ZELDA GAME, is outrageous to me. Ubisoft is incapable of coming up with original video game mechanics, incapable of writing interesting stories, incapable of creating lovable characters, incapable of innovating their own formula, and most certainly incapable of innovating the genres their games stink up. They bring nothing to the table and create risk free, assembly line products for an audience of people I cannot relate to.I bought this game on a deep discount because I saw so many people online hype it up to be a breath of fresh air for their map marker approach. It certainly wants to be a breath of something, but there's nothing fresh here. I already gambled away my money with this game, I won't gamble any more of my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons: The game is Zelda-inspired. However, quite a few problems emerged across my first 18 hrs of gameplay (clearing 2.5 regions out of 6). Lack of interactions between the character and the world, it still has the shape of the previous AC open world games. Bad physics, it is very hard to turn around airborne, and sometimes items don't drop at supposed location when trying to solve a puzzle. Repetitive gameplay like most other Ubisoft games. Getting 3 items across the map, push a ball from A to B, shoot an arrow across a few specific location blah blah blah. The puzzle is only hard for the sake of it, like you have to start all the way back if you miss a point during a platformer challenge, or a switch to open a door is hiding god knows where (I suspect they want to prolong people's game hour that way). The puzzle can give you a real headache combining with the game physics problem I talked about before. Solving a puzzle in Zelda makes you feel smart and proud, solving a puzzle in this game makes you feel whoever design these is stupid. Pros: Fun dialogue and cute graphics. I like how Zeus is ranting about everything when Prometheus is ranting about Zeus. The other gods are also quite funny (they are the only motivation I am still playing).  Very good combat system. The rewards from all those repetitive puzzles are quite helpful instead of some trash items in AC Odessey or Hogwarts Legacy. You also don't have to spend tons of time upgrading an individual item.In general: One of the better games from Ubisoft's industrial assembly line, gameplay wise consider it as a way better version of Hogwarts Legacy.

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly enjoyable open world exploration game, like Assassins Creed, but not so full of itself and considerably more fun.Combat and puzzles are casual-friendly, (even on hard difficulty), although there are optional dungeons that are harder. _childDocuments_.review: (( Pay no mind to the hours played. I almost finished the game when Ubi gave me a few weeks or month trial of Ubisoft+! ))This game isn't that bad! It plays like Darksiders meets Assassins Creed: Origin or Odyssey with a touch of Zelda. So it can be a bit repetitive combat wise but its OK for its Hack/Slash combat. The games controls are fine, I'm using a controller this time but have used Keyboard and Mouse when I played it with Ubi+. The game has a good sized map and lots of content to explore and discover. There is also a good amount of gear and cosmetics to find as well and also to be able to unlock more skills along your journey to help freeing the other Gods. _childDocuments_.review: What baffles me is that there are people who played Zelda BotW, Genshin Impact and this game. They immediately compare the games to Zelda, fair enough as it was the original concept before the other two, but somehow... just somehow... I don't comprehend how... they tend to rate this game as the worst of the three.In terms of characterization, open-world, moment to moment game play of exploration and combat, and overall quality of the three games, I'll have to say: BotW > IFR >>>>>>>>> your cat putting a dead rat too close to your foot >>>>> Genshin Impact. Anyone who talks down at IFR and, in the same breath, praises Genshin cannot be trusted. That or they just didn't play the game for more than an hour. The free demo alone has more game play and depth than all of Genshin.I have like 400 hours in BotW (600 if you count TotK too), 160 hours in Genshin and about 80 in IFR (I started the DLCs so I'll easily get to over 100).Turns out, I like open world games. I bought this game to experiment if I like them and it seems to have been fairly successful. My first attempt to play this game resulted in my computer overheating and shutting down, hence my deleted old review and I refunded the game; but after figuring out that it's not IFR but it's actually my computer, I fixed my computer I tried again. It works no problem.If you don't have a Ubisoft account thing, make one -> link it to Steam (there is an option for that) and no more problems. Steam launches the ubisoft app thing without any additional inputs (after I hit play) and I face no problems.The game never crashed on me once and I was playing with high settings. As for controls: M&K is fine, but I didn't like it. I played the game with my PS5 controller; and to do that, I went into the Steam Options and turned OFF this game's steam controller thing (there's a guide for this) AND I used DS4 to emulate a PS4 controller. That worked perfectly.The biggest things that I want to complain about at this moment are:1) climbing in this game can use some polish. It has a realistic approach to it, better than all other BotW-ripoffs, but it comes at the cost of making it less fun. Case in point: the moment I hit circle to drop, the moment the character needs to let go (unless she is mid-climbing-jump). 2) Basic Shield enemies starting tier 2 (so, blue and beyond) are the most annoying enemies in the game. I don't like the "you can't parry this" mechanic, but that's a skill issue (though, I swear perfect dodging in this game is really weird. I can perfect parry for days but perfect dodge just doesn't work as well), but they run up to you and start charging up a shield bash that you can't knock down with an axe swing. Sure, I can use a power to remove this problem entirely, but I'm trying to combo man. Getting my combo into triple digits and having blue flashy lights is what I'm going for. On top of that stupid thing that should be just deleted, seriously, just delete it, if I do Axe -> Sword -> Sword, the second sword hit here is Fenyx's extra long start-up finisher which the Shield enemy just blocks. This is also incredibly stupid. Frankly, just delete this enemy and bring in a different enemy.So... overall, not so bad. It took me a while to get used to Fenyx's voice and Greek Mythology is... well, if you're unaware of how the Greek deities are humongous jerks, especially Zeus, then prepare yourself because oh boy this game kinda holds back, it isn't rated M, but you'll learn quite a bit. If you wanna smack any of them, then you're not alone.I, for one, appreciated the commentary during game play, especially since it isn't intrusive, and I found it funny. Zeus's voice actor specifically did a fantastic job. As far as in-app purchases, it's all cosmetic. All proper gear is only obtainable in-game and, importantly, upgraded together. For example: If you upgrade your armor to level 3 -> all new armor you find afterwards is already level 3. Sure there is grinding but it isn't more than BotW. I say this as someone who maxed out all armor in BotW (thrice) and TotK: this game's grind isn't bad at all; it is just less varied as in BotW where you have to collect specific loot for each upgrade of each armor piece; while in IFR, you need blue things + red or purple things. Also yellow things for potion pouch and arrow pouch upgrades.Puzzles are fine. With a big ol' open world, you gotta have stuff for players to do as an empty open world is a failure. BotW fills this with Korok Seeds for puzzles and they are quite the copy-paste going around and TotK is in this same boat. IFR's least fun puzzle is the sliding block puzzle but it has an upside that they're almost always locked and there is a puzzle to solve to unlock them. The game does this to add some variety and I appreciate it. There is one unique puzzle that's only used once where you cover a statue's eyes with rocks nearby that I had to look up, so there was someone on the team trying to add more variety but it didn't seem to work out that well.I've seen a lot of people complain about the mechanic of going to a high place, entering first person mode and marking nearby stuff, like chests, puzzles, challenges, etc, but I wanna comment that this mechanic is kinda IFR's equivalent to Zelda's sensor mechanic. If you don't like it, then don't do it. If you're like me and enjoy wandering, then you'll just trip over chests, enemy groups, puzzles, challenges, etc all on your own. They're not invisible unless you mark them so I don't get why people complain about this mechanic. Furthermore, and this is important: you don't need to go to a high place to mark stuff with this mechanic. You can enter first person mode at any time and mark stuff through walls, so if you see a chest in the distance and you don't wanna lose track of it, you can just mark it right there. It's like dropping pins in BotW but upgraded significantly. One last thing I want to mention is how IFR respects your time more than BotW (and TotK). When it comes to finishing a shrine in Zelda, skipping as fast as possible will still waste like 10 seconds. Meanwhile in IFR, if I mash circle to skip, I'm out in less than a second. That's one example and there are a whole bunch more but this is long enough and no one is going to read all this anyway. If you did, well, trust me, there are other ways IFR respects your time by not wasting it on unskippable bits like Zelda loves to. Not to mention my computer >>> the nintendo switch, so the load times of entering and exiting shrines is super fast that I don't get to read the snarky Zeus comments on the tips that show up during the loading screens. I'm not going to say IFR is better than BotW but IFR is 100% much much better than Genshin. If you finished TotK recently and you're looking to scratch that itch some more until TotK gets some DLC or something, then this game is very much worth the $20 on sale to get it + the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello friends! Today i will review the game Immortals Fenyx Rising. This game has some issues on steam, but if you can get it to work, it works very well. It is a open worldgame similiar to other ubisoft games, except this one is more greek mythology related. It features a hero who must save the gods and lands from evil. There is also a decent story the game follows when saving the gods, and some twists and turns. Many puzzles are also in teh game, so you can play many puzzles througth the game. So if you do not like action rpgs with lots of puzzles, you may wish to avoid this game. Also, seems the current nvidia driver version causes lots of issues with this game. A poster on the forum says using a older version driver can fix this issue. You can see the information here on the driver version to rollback to which is driver version #528.19. If you wish for them to have a permanenet fix, i suggest people contact nvidia and explain the issue with the current patch with them and this game to have a long term fixing solution.Other people have reported crashing in the game. Although i did not personally experience crashing inside the game, i do have issues when closing the game. The crashing could be related to the steam overlay and the cloud saving, as i think this is the issue that is causing them. I have contacted ubisoft connect support about this issue too. Anyways,here are my pro and con list for the game. Crashing maybe also caused by settings from nvidia/amd settings, so the player may have to fool around with them to find the best solution to the crashing issues.PROS:- A story based around greek mythology.- Lots of side quests to do.- Many collectibles to find.- Lots of puzzles.- Controller support for my logitech f310.- Legendary beasts and mythical monsters to find roaming the open world.- Ability to go wherever you want in the open world.CONS:- Some technical issues associated with the game, such as the currrent nvidia drive causing crashing, and other things. This can cause everything from crashing or not properly shutting down correctly.- Many individuals are mad there is not achievements on steam. You can achievements being connected to ubisoft connect and on their platform, not steam.- Some people have said their controllers are not working. I am using a f310 logitech controller fine and it worked right away with no fooling around.- Some of the quests feel repetitive and doing vaults almost feel the same. Also many puzzles in the game.- This requires ubisoft connect to play, and i see this as a negative.- A in game money store in a single player game. Usually these are only cosmetic, but they also have upgrades to stuff in the game. This takes real money to buy this stuff.NOTE: To fully enjoy the game with the dlc's, there is a certain order you should play them in. The order is: The main game (beat it), then play A new god (beat it), then playThe Lost gods (beat it). The eastern gods should be treated as a seperate entity as it features a new hero and new places. Make sure to play eastern gods last.Do i recommend the game? Yes, if you can get over the bugs in the game and can actually play it. It is quite fun action rpg with many many puzzles. If you do not enjoy puzzles though, avoid this game at all costs. If you like the full base game, consider getting the DLC's as they add more storyline to the game about fenyx. Make sure to follow my method of playing above or else the story will be out of order.

_childDocuments_.review: I wonder how many times Ubisoft higher ups intervened during development and said "Now how can we make this part waste people's time more".This game does not respect your time at all. It has a good foundation (obviously since it's just ripping off breath of the wild) but then they sprinkle on the good ol' Ubisoft secret recipe of making the game worse. Not everything is worse, I will say I enjoy the sword, axe, stamina, skill combat system (sometimes). Flying bosses are the worst, even when I spec my equipment into airborne. You can't grab the treasure chest you missed in a dungeon and then warp out, you have to complete the entire dungeon AGAIN. You can't even go to the entrance of the dungeon to leave or you'll lose progress, Ubisoft purposefully implemented you needing to redo the entire dungeon to waste people's time. Gliding parkour is the worst since it's incredibly sluggish. Collecting health ingredients which is probably the most important is the most tedious and time consuming to grab, needing to get off your horse, hit the tree with the axe, then back onto your horse instead of just running past ingredients with auto-grab on horse. Amber in tree trunks require you to wait for the trunk to topple over for no reason so you just stand around waiting. They copy the Breath of the Wild scouting mechanic more or less but there's so much busy work and the environment is done so terribly that you're just going to be manually panning the entire screen to get any hits. There's puzzles in the dungeons that aren't even puzzles and are a lot of busy work. There's a puzzle in the open world where you need to find lettuce in a village type area so you'd think maybe you go the market for the lettuce. Nope, it's just locked inside building the size of a large cage whose sole purpose is to have the lettuce locked up inside. So many puzzles are exploration puzzles where it's usually wander around and hope you find the thing you need to find rather than actually thinking. I don't know, there's far more things that make this game, in my opinion, more egregious than the other Ubisoft sandbox games or maybe it's the only one I've bothered playing a good amount of recently. Also the main antagonist is some stupid overbite looking fool that Ubi actually tries to push as menacing even though the rest of the game is lighthearted.Edit: Oh and also it's appalling how aggressive they are pushing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ live service paid cosmetic daily quest model. It's also incredibly disgusting that it is okay nowadays for a game to heavily advertise their new game or DLC in the game you already bought. It's awful for DLC since 99% of games always make it REALLY obvious you're missing out on the actual intended experience of the game because you're too stingy to give them more money. Ubisoft does the same with advertising their DLC everywhere and also as a "quest" on the map. It is incredibly disengengous as they advertise what you'll get in the DLC but maxing your stats out completely. This will make endorphins rush as power fantasies usually do, especially when contrasted versus when you weren't, but that's because they are trying to trick you to thinking the DLC is better than it actually is. As example, a normal enemy without special heapth probably takes 2 hits + 5 hit combo on Nightmare difficulty. The gold bordered enemies in the trial took 1. Despicable.
